## firestore.rules

```rules
// The live ruleset for this project — see docs/FIRESTORE_RULES.md.
//
// EDITING THIS FILE CHANGES NOTHING UNTIL IT IS DEPLOYED. It is deployed by
// `npx firebase-tools deploy --only firestore:rules`, which reads firebase.json
// and targets the project's NAMED database (not `(default)`). CI does not do it.
//
// This file having drifted ahead of what was actually deployed is what made
// establishing a player's Home impossible: the `home` field was permitted here
// and rejected in production, so the first-run house placement failed on every
// attempt and its tutorial — whose condition is "no home yet" — asked forever.
// Any new UserProfile field needs BOTH a clause in isValidUser and an entry in
// the update whitelist below, and then a deploy.
//
// 2026-08-31 — 寵物照護 added NO new field, on purpose. Its state lives at `islandState.pet.care`,
// inside a map already validated here as 「a map」, so the feature writes correctly against a ruleset
// deployed before it existed. Its one new write shape (a feed: `inventory` + `islandState` together)
// is spelled out in its own clause below, but the fallback whitelist already covered it — so this
// edit is documentation rather than a gate, and nothing about 寵物 is waiting on a deploy.
//
// 2026-08-29 — `utilityCards` (功能卡) and `limitedShop` (限時商店 purchase records) are the two
// newest such fields. Each has a shape clause in isValidUser and appears in the update whitelist
// below: `utilityCards` in six clauses, because six writes can touch it (a card grant, a card use,
// a limited-shop purchase, and the three payout paths that may spend a use-based card's charge),
// and `limitedShop` in the purchase clause and the catch-all. If cards are being bought and the
// count never moves, THIS FILE NOT BEING DEPLOYED is the first thing to check.
//
// 2026-08-25 — `wallet` (碎片, and every currency added after it) is the newest such field. It has
// a shape clause in isValidUser and appears in five update clauses below, because five different
// writes touch it: a purchase, a daily-login claim, 摸摸寵物, a standalone reward grant, and the
// catch-all. If 碎片 are being granted and the balance never moves, THIS FILE NOT BEING DEPLOYED
// is the first thing to check — see docs/FIRESTORE_RULES.md for what that failure looks like from
// the player's side (it is not a rejected write; it is a blank save).
rules_version = '2';
service cloud.firestore {
  match /databases/{database}/documents {
    // 0. Default deny catch-all
    match /{document=**} {
      allow read, write: if false;
    }

    // --- Global Helpers ---
    function isSignedIn() {
      return request.auth != null;
    }
    
    function isOwner(userId) {
      return isSignedIn() && request.auth.uid == userId;
    }

    function isValidId(id) {
      return id is string && id.size() <= 128 && id.matches('^[a-zA-Z0-9_\\-]+$');
    }

    function incoming() {
      return request.resource.data;
    }

    function existing() {
      return resource.data;
    }

    // --- Entity Validations ---
    function isValidUser(data) {
      return data.userId == request.auth.uid
        && data.displayName is string && data.displayName.size() <= 100
        && data.level is number && data.level >= 1 && data.level <= 1000
        && data.balanceGold is number && data.balanceGold >= 0
        // 錢包 — every currency that is NOT 金幣 (src/constants/currency.ts). One nested map, for
        // the reason `islandState` and `workoutRewards` are one: it is ONE clause here and ONE
        // whitelist entry below, so adding a third currency later is a row in CURRENCY_SPECS
        // rather than another rules deploy.
        //
        // 金幣 deliberately stayed at the top level as `balanceGold`. It is required
        // unconditionally by this function, the daily-login server increments it inside a
        // transaction, and every save in the wild carries it — moving it would be a migration of
        // the one number a player would notice going missing.
        //
        // Validated for SHAPE and floor, not for amount: what a player is OWED is decided by the
        // reward service and (for 每日登入) by the server, and rules cannot re-derive that. What
        // they can do is refuse a negative balance and a non-number, which is what stops a
        // hand-crafted write from minting or from corrupting the field for every later increment.
        && (!("wallet" in data) || (
          data.wallet is map
          && (!("fragments" in data.wallet) || (
            data.wallet.fragments is number && data.wallet.fragments >= 0
          ))
        ))
        && (!("currentXp" in data) || (data.currentXp is number && data.currentXp >= 0))
        && (!("territoryLevel" in data) || (data.territoryLevel is number && data.territoryLevel >= 1))
        && (!("inventory" in data) || data.inventory is list)
        && (!("equippedItems" in data) || data.equippedItems is list)
        && (!("lastUpdated" in data) || data.lastUpdated is string)
        && (!("avatar" in data) || (data.avatar is string && data.avatar.size() <= 100))
        && (!("lastLoginDate" in data) || data.lastLoginDate is string)
        && (!("loginStreak" in data) || (data.loginStreak is number && data.loginStreak >= 0))
        // 每日登入 board mirror (types.ts UserProfile / constants/dailyLogin.ts). The server owns
        // `daily_login_claims`; these three are the client's copy so the panel can draw a board
        // without a round trip. The anchor is a civil date written once, the cycle id is
        // `cycle-YYYY-MM-DD`, and the claimed days are 1-based indices into one round — so the
        // list can never be longer than the round is. Deliberately NOT size-capped tighter than
        // that: over-tight validation here is what breaks a save silently.
        && (!("loginAnchorDate" in data) || (data.loginAnchorDate is string && data.loginAnchorDate.size() <= 10))
        && (!("loginCycleId" in data) || (data.loginCycleId is string && data.loginCycleId.size() <= 32))
        && (!("loginClaimedDays" in data) || (data.loginClaimedDays is list && data.loginClaimedDays.size() <= 31))
        && (!("lastPetDate" in data) || data.lastPetDate is string)
        && (!("petCountToday" in data) || (data.petCountToday is number && data.petCountToday >= 0))
        // 每日登入獎勵 (constants/dailyLogin.ts). The round is a seven-day tile counted from
        // `loginAnchorDate`; `loginCycleId` names the tile a claim belongs to and
        // `loginClaimedDays` is which of its seven days are collected. `dailyLoginAnchor` is the
        // server's own copy of the anchor (src/server/dailyLoginApi.ts), written by the Admin SDK.
        //
        // The day list is bounded here rather than trusted: without the size cap a client could
        // grow it without limit, and without the value range it could name a day that is not in
        // the round. It cannot police WHICH days are in the list — that is the check only the
        // server can make, and is why the API exists.
        && (!("loginAnchorDate" in data) || data.loginAnchorDate is string)
        && (!("dailyLoginAnchor" in data) || data.dailyLoginAnchor is string)
        && (!("loginCycleId" in data) || (data.loginCycleId is string && data.loginCycleId.size() <= 64))
        && (!("loginClaimedDays" in data) || (data.loginClaimedDays is list && data.loginClaimedDays.size() <= 7))
        // 商品碎片 (src/constants/fragments.ts). `itemFragments` is a map of catalog id -> count: one
        // entry per item the player has actually collected toward, which is why it is a map and not
        // a list — a fragment belongs to exactly one product, and the storage is what makes that
        // true rather than a rule some later write has to remember.
        //
        // Validated for SHAPE and size only. Rules cannot check that a count is one the player
        // earned any more than they can check a gold balance is, and an over-tight bound here does
        // not reject one field — isValidUser runs against the WHOLE merged document, so it would
        // fail every other write in the same load too (see docs/FIRESTORE_RULES.md). The cap is set
        // well above the catalog's size so a growing shop cannot silently break existing saves.
        && (!("itemFragments" in data) || (data.itemFragments is map && data.itemFragments.size() <= 500))
        && (!("raffleTickets" in data) || (data.raffleTickets is number && data.raffleTickets >= 0))
        // 免費轉盤次數 (src/types.ts, paid by 每日登入 第 7 天). A plain non-negative count, checked
        // for SHAPE and floor only — rules cannot know how many turns a player has earned any more
        // than they can know a gold balance, and what they CAN refuse is a negative or a non-number,
        // which is what stops a hand-crafted write from corrupting the field for every later spin.
        && (!("freeWheelSpins" in data) || (data.freeWheelSpins is number && data.freeWheelSpins >= 0))
        && (!("raffleTicketProgress" in data) || (data.raffleTicketProgress is number && data.raffleTicketProgress >= 0))
        && (!("migrationVersion" in data) || data.migrationVersion is string)
        && (!("interiorData" in data) || data.interiorData is map)
        // The player's single Home. Null means "not placed yet"; a map must carry a style id,
        // and the one-per-player guarantee is structural - it is an object, not a list.
        && (!("home" in data) || data.home == null || (
          data.home is map
          && data.home.currentStyle is string && data.home.currentStyle.size() <= 64
        ))
        && (!("islandPlacements" in data) || data.islandPlacements is list)
        // 離線回歸 (src/constants/islandReturn.ts). One nested map holding: `lastSeenAt`, the ISO
        // instant the absence is measured from; `sprouts`, the overgrowth currently standing on
        // the island; and `pet`, the companion's mood. All three are decoration and mood — nothing
        // under this key can grant an item, move a currency or alter progress, which is why it is
        // validated for SHAPE and size and not for content.
        //
        // The list cap is deliberately looser than the client's own ceiling (OVERGROWTH_MAX, 26):
        // an over-tight bound here does not reject one field, it fails the whole write and — via
        // isValidUser running against the merged document — every other write in the same load.
        // See docs/FIRESTORE_RULES.md.
        && (!("islandState" in data) || (
          data.islandState is map
          && (!("lastSeenAt" in data.islandState) || data.islandState.lastSeenAt is string)
          && (!("sprouts" in data.islandState) || (
            data.islandState.sprouts is list && data.islandState.sprouts.size() <= 40
          ))
          && (!("pet" in data.islandState) || data.islandState.pet is map)
        ))
        // 健身獎勵 (src/constants/workoutRewards.ts). One nested map holding: `claims`, the rewards
        // this account has already been paid, keyed by trigger id; `completedCount`/`lastCompletedAt`,
        // the training record a future 連續／里程碑 rule would read; and `processedIds`, the recent
        // completion ids that make a redelivered event a no-op.
        //
        // Unlike `islandState`, this one CAN grant an item — a claim is written in the same update
        // as the `inventory` entry it paid for. That is deliberate and it is why the two share a
        // whitelist clause below: they must land together or not at all. What the rules can check
        // is SHAPE and size, not whether the item was deserved; deciding that is the client's job
        // today and the fitness service's job once there is one to ask (see docs/workout-rewards.md).
        //
        // The id list is capped at four times PROCESSED_ID_LIMIT (12) rather than at it: an
        // over-tight bound here does not reject one field, it fails the WHOLE write and — via
        // isValidUser running against the merged document — every other write in the same load.
        // See docs/FIRESTORE_RULES.md.
        && (!("workoutRewards" in data) || (
          data.workoutRewards is map
          && (!("claims" in data.workoutRewards) || data.workoutRewards.claims is map)
          && (!("completedCount" in data.workoutRewards) || (
            data.workoutRewards.completedCount is number && data.workoutRewards.completedCount >= 0
          ))
          && (!("lastCompletedAt" in data.workoutRewards) || data.workoutRewards.lastCompletedAt is string)
          && (!("processedIds" in data.workoutRewards) || (
            data.workoutRewards.processedIds is list && data.workoutRewards.processedIds.size() <= 48
          ))
        ))
        // 功能卡 (src/constants/utilityCards.ts). One nested map holding: `owned`, how many of each
        // card is in the bag; `active`, the effects currently running; and `usedTotal`, a lifetime
        // counter. One key here and one whitelist entry below, so the SECOND card — and the first
        // effect that needs a new field — needs no rules change at all.
        //
        // Like `workoutRewards`, this one CAN pay: an active effect multiplies a currency grant
        // (src/constants/rewardEffects.ts), and a `uses`-based card is spent in the same write as
        // the reward it boosted. What rules can check is SHAPE and size, not whether the effect was
        // deserved — deciding that is the client's job today and a service's job when there is one.
        //
        // The list cap is deliberately loose: an over-tight bound here does not reject one field,
        // it fails the WHOLE write and — via isValidUser running against the merged document —
        // every other write in the same load. See docs/FIRESTORE_RULES.md.
        && (!("utilityCards" in data) || (
          data.utilityCards is map
          && (!("owned" in data.utilityCards) || data.utilityCards.owned is map)
          && (!("usedTotal" in data.utilityCards) || data.utilityCards.usedTotal is map)
          && (!("active" in data.utilityCards) || (
            data.utilityCards.active is list && data.utilityCards.active.size() <= 24
          ))
        ))
        // 限時商店 (src/constants/limitedShop.ts). Only the player's own purchase counts are stored
        // — the rotation itself is derived from the clock and never saved, so there is nothing here
        // a client could forge into a different shelf. The map is pruned to the recent periods on
        // every write (see `recordPurchase`), which is what keeps the cap below comfortable.
        && (!("limitedShop" in data) || (
          data.limitedShop is map
          && (!("purchases" in data.limitedShop) || (
            data.limitedShop.purchases is map && data.limitedShop.purchases.size() <= 200
          ))
        ))
        // 每週任務 (src/constants/weeklyTasks.ts). One nested map holding a single list of task
        // DEFINITIONS — a name, a metric, a target and the weeks that target was met. One key here
        // and one whitelist entry below, for the same reason `workoutRewards` and `utilityCards`
        // are one: a new metric is a row in METRIC_SPECS rather than a schema change plus a rules
        // deploy.
        //
        // Notably absent: progress. It is recomputed from `workout_logs` on every read, so there is
        // no number here a client could inflate and no field that could fall out of step with the
        // exercise it claims to represent. That is a stronger guarantee than any rule could give:
        // rules can check that a number is a number, not that it was earned.
        //
        // The cap is MAX_WEEKLY_TASKS (8) with headroom, and it is deliberately loose for the
        // reason spelled out over `workoutRewards`: an over-tight bound here does not reject one
        // field, it fails the WHOLE write and — via isValidUser running against the merged
        // document — every other write in the same load. See docs/FIRESTORE_RULES.md.
        && (!("weeklyTasks" in data) || (
          data.weeklyTasks is map
          && (!("tasks" in data.weeklyTasks) || (
            data.weeklyTasks.tasks is list && data.weeklyTasks.tasks.size() <= 32
          ))
        ));
    }

    function isValidAppSettings(data) {
      return data.userId == request.auth.uid
        && data.bgmVolume is number && data.bgmVolume >= 0.0 && data.bgmVolume <= 1.0
        && data.isMuted is bool
        && data.voiceGuideEnabled is bool
        && data.warmupEnabled is bool
        && (!("currentTrackIndex" in data) || data.currentTrackIndex is number)
        && (!("youtubeMusicEnabled" in data) || data.youtubeMusicEnabled is bool);
    }

    function isValidWorkoutLog(data) {
       return data.keys().hasAll(['logId', 'userId', 'type', 'duration', 'counts', 'calories', 'goldEarned', 'timestamp'])
        && data.userId == request.auth.uid
        && data.logId is string && data.logId.size() <= 100
        && data.type is string && data.type.size() <= 100
        && data.duration is number && data.duration >= 0
        && data.counts is number && data.counts >= 0
        && data.calories is number && data.calories >= 0.0
        && data.goldEarned is number && data.goldEarned >= 0
        && data.timestamp is string;
    }

    // --- Path Rules ---

    // Connection Health Check
    match /test/connection {
      allow read: if true;
    }

    // Global Shop Catalog items
    match /shop_items/{itemId} {
      allow read: if true; // Accessible by anyone to view the store items
      allow write: if false; // Only system admin directly
    }

    // User Profile matching
    match /users/{userId} {
      allow get: if isOwner(userId) && isValidId(userId);
      
      // Strict structural validation on Creation
      allow create: if isOwner(userId) && isValidId(userId)
        && isValidUser(incoming());

      // Tiered Action-based Updates matching expected application updates
      allow update: if isOwner(userId) && isValidId(userId)
        && isValidUser(incoming())
        && incoming().userId == existing().userId   // Immutable user reference identifier
        && (
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly(['displayName', 'avatar', 'lastUpdated']) ||
          // Buying. The three fragment keys are in here because a gold purchase SETTLES the
          // fragments collected toward the item it just bought, in the same write (see
          // context/useShopActions.ts) — hasOnly is a subset test, so an ordinary purchase that
          // touches none of them still matches this clause unchanged.
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly([
            'equippedItems', 'inventory', 'balanceGold', 'wallet',
            'itemFragments', 'raffleTickets', 'raffleTicketProgress', 'lastUpdated'
          ]) ||
          // 商品碎片's own two writes: a grant (運動結算 / 每日簽到 / 轉盤) which touches only the
          // fragment keys, and a 碎片解鎖 which spends a stack and appends the item to the
          // inventory. Neither may move gold — the fragment route costs no currency, and leaving
          // `balanceGold` out of this clause is what enforces that rather than a comment saying so.
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly([
            'itemFragments', 'raffleTickets', 'raffleTicketProgress', 'inventory', 'lastUpdated'
          ]) ||
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly(['interiorData', 'balanceGold', 'territoryLevel', 'lastUpdated']) ||
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly(['level', 'currentXp', 'balanceGold', 'lastUpdated']) ||
          // The 每日登入 writes, all three of them: the once-a-day bookkeeping in
          // AppContext (lastLoginDate/loginStreak/anchor, plus cycle+claims when the round
          // rolls over), the server-claim mirror, and the offline claim that pays out
          // locally (useEconomyActions). hasOnly is a subset test, so one clause covers all.
          // 'wallet' is in this list because the round now PAYS 碎片 while a 補簽 still charges
          // 金幣, so one claim write touches both halves of the wallet at once. `hasOnly` is a
          // subset test, so the same clause still covers the mirror write that touches neither.
          // 'utilityCards' is in this clause and the two below it for one reason: a 功能卡 whose
          // duration is counted in USES is spent by the very grant it boosted, and that spend has
          // to land in the same write as the payout — otherwise a failed save either pays twice or
          // charges a use for nothing. See src/constants/rewardEffects.ts.
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly([
            'lastLoginDate', 'loginStreak', 'loginAnchorDate', 'loginCycleId', 'loginClaimedDays',
            'balanceGold', 'wallet', 'currentXp', 'utilityCards', 'lastUpdated'
          ]) ||
          // 每日登入獎勵's NON-CURRENCY half (src/context/useDailyLoginPrize.ts). The round stopped
          // being a ladder of one currency on 2026-09-17: a day can now pay 商品碎片, 抽獎券, a
          // 功能卡, a whole product, or a free turn of the 幸運轉盤, and this is the ONE write that
          // lands whichever of those the day rolled.
          //
          // It is its own clause rather than more keys on the one above, and that is the whole
          // point of `hasOnly` being a subset test: the claim write moves money and marks the day
          // off, this one hands over goods and moves no balance at all. Keeping them apart means
          // `balanceGold` is absent HERE — so a prize write can never move gold, which is enforced
          // by this list rather than by a comment saying it does not.
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly([
            'itemFragments', 'raffleTickets', 'raffleTicketProgress', 'inventory',
            'utilityCards', 'freeWheelSpins', 'lastUpdated'
          ]) ||
          // 摸摸寵物 — the daily counter and its 碎片/經驗值 payout, in one write so the limit
          // cannot be raced. See context/useEconomyActions.ts (petDog).
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly([
            'lastPetDate', 'petCountToday', 'wallet', 'currentXp', 'utilityCards', 'lastUpdated'
          ]) ||
          // The Economy / Reward Service's standalone grants (grantReward): one currency, or XP,
          // and nothing else. 島嶼秘寶 and the 管理員測試 supply buttons are the callers today.
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly([
            'wallet', 'balanceGold', 'currentXp', 'utilityCards', 'lastUpdated'
          ]) ||
          // 功能卡's own two writes: a grant (a 輪盤 drop, 管理員測試) and a use, which spends a copy
          // and starts an effect. Both touch this one nested map and nothing else — the same
          // property that makes 離線回歸's clause a single line, and the reason a second card needs
          // no rules change. See context/useUtilityCards.ts.
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly(['utilityCards', 'lastUpdated']) ||
          // 幸運轉盤 (context/useWheelActions.ts). ONE write: the turn spent — a free one
          // (`freeWheelSpins`) or a 抽獎券 — and whatever the wedge paid, which is fragments, more
          // tickets, an item or a card. They must land together or the wheel either charges for
          // nothing or spins for free.
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly([
            'raffleTickets', 'raffleTicketProgress', 'freeWheelSpins', 'itemFragments',
            'inventory', 'utilityCards', 'lastUpdated'
          ]) ||
          // 限時商店 purchase (context/useLimitedShop.ts). ONE write: the charge, the goods and the
          // per-period purchase record. The goods are either a 功能卡 (`utilityCards`) or a catalog
          // item (`inventory`, plus the fragment settlement a purchase strands), which is why both
          // appear here — hasOnly is a subset test, so one clause covers both kinds of product and
          // both currencies. Splitting it would let a charge land without the goods.
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly([
            'limitedShop', 'utilityCards', 'inventory', 'balanceGold', 'wallet',
            'itemFragments', 'raffleTickets', 'raffleTicketProgress', 'lastUpdated'
          ]) ||
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly(['territoryLevel', 'migrationVersion', 'lastUpdated']) ||
          // 離線回歸's four writes — the arrival, the 「我還在」 heartbeat, a 整理, and the pet
          // greeting its owner. All of them touch this one nested map and nothing else, which is
          // the whole reason the state is a map rather than five top-level fields: one clause here
          // covers the feature, and a fifth kind of write later needs no rules change at all.
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly(['islandState', 'lastUpdated']) ||
          // 寵物照護 (src/constants/petCare.ts, src/context/usePetCare.ts). A feed spends one bag of
          // 寵物用品 AND restores the animal, and those cannot be two writes: a failure between them
          // either takes the food without feeding the pet or feeds it for free, and the player has
          // no way to tell which happened. Same reasoning as 健身獎勵's clause below.
          //
          // Note what this clause does NOT add: a field. The care state lives at
          // `islandState.pet.care`, inside a map `isValidUser()` already validates as 「a map」, so
          // no shape clause changed and the feature is writable against a ruleset deployed before
          // it existed. That was a deliberate choice at the data-modelling stage — see the `care`
          // field's own note in src/constants/islandReturn.ts. This clause is therefore
          // documentation of a write that the fallback whitelist already permits, not a gate the
          // feature is waiting on.
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly(['islandState', 'inventory', 'lastUpdated']) ||
          // 健身獎勵's two writes: the bookkeeping a valid completion produces, and the grant that
          // pays a reward. The grant touches BOTH keys in one update on purpose — the item and the
          // record that it was given have to land together, or the save ends up either marked-and-
          // unpaid or paid-and-unmarked. hasOnly is a subset test, so this one clause covers the
          // bookkeeping-only write as well. See context/useWorkoutRewards.ts.
          // 'balanceGold'/'currentXp' joined this clause when the workout PAYOUT moved out of the
          // fitness screen and into the reward service (context/useWorkoutRewards.ts): the coins,
          // the XP and the replay guard (`processedIds`, inside `workoutRewards`) now ride in ONE
          // write, which is what makes a redelivered completion unable to pay twice.
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly([
            'workoutRewards', 'inventory', 'balanceGold', 'currentXp', 'utilityCards', 'lastUpdated'
          ]) ||
          // Establishing the Home consumes the Starter House from the inventory in one write;
          // re-skinning it touches 'home' alone.
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly(['home', 'inventory', 'lastUpdated']) ||
          // 每週任務 — building, editing, deleting a goal, and recording that a week's target was
          // met. All four touch the one key, and none of them may move anything else: a task is a
          // goal the player set for themselves, and it has never been a thing that pays out.
          // Keeping it in its own clause rather than folding it into the fallback whitelist is
          // what makes that true by construction (see context/useWeeklyTasks.ts).
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly(['weeklyTasks', 'lastUpdated']) ||
          // Fallback whitelist ensuring any partial updates in standard User attributes are fully permitted
          incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly([
            'displayName', 'level', 'currentXp', 'territoryLevel', 'balanceGold',
            'inventory', 'equippedItems', 'lastUpdated', 'avatar', 'home',
            'lastLoginDate', 'loginStreak', 'loginAnchorDate', 'loginCycleId', 'loginClaimedDays',
            'lastPetDate', 'petCountToday', 'dailyLoginAnchor',
            'itemFragments', 'raffleTickets', 'raffleTicketProgress',
            'interiorData', 'islandPlacements', 'islandState', 'workoutRewards', 'migrationVersion',
            'wallet', 'utilityCards', 'limitedShop', 'weeklyTasks'
          ])
        );
      
      // Sub-collections under User Profile
      match /inventory/{itemId} {
        allow read: if isOwner(userId) && isValidId(userId);
        allow create, update: if isOwner(userId) && isValidId(userId) && isValidId(itemId);
      }

      match /workout_logs/{logId} {
        allow list, get: if isOwner(userId) && isValidId(userId);
        allow create: if isOwner(userId) && isValidId(userId) && isValidId(logId)
          && isValidWorkoutLog(incoming());
      }

      // 每日登入的領取紀錄與稽核 (src/server/dailyLoginApi.ts).
      //
      // Readable by the owner so the panel can show its own history; NOT writable by anyone. The
      // server writes these with the Admin SDK, which bypasses rules entirely — so "no client
      // writes" costs nothing and is what makes the claim record trustworthy: a document here can
      // only have been created by the transaction that also moved the wallet.
      match /daily_login_claims/{claimId} {
        allow list, get: if isOwner(userId) && isValidId(userId);
        allow write: if false;
      }

      match /daily_login_audit/{entryId} {
        allow list, get: if isOwner(userId) && isValidId(userId);
        allow write: if false;
      }

      match /settings/{settingId} {
        allow get: if isOwner(userId) && isValidId(userId) && isValidId(settingId);
        allow create, update: if isOwner(userId) && isValidId(userId) && isValidId(settingId)
          && isValidAppSettings(incoming());
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## scripts/audit-catalog.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 商品資料稽核 — `npm run audit:catalog`.
 *
 * The guard behind the rules that constants/items.ts and constants/rarity.ts assert but cannot
 * enforce on their own. TypeScript already makes a MISSING field impossible; what it cannot see is
 * whether the catalog still means anything — whether a tier is unique where it must be, whether the
 * ladder still narrows towards the top, whether two shelves quietly grew a duplicate id.
 *
 * Every check here is a rule written down somewhere else in prose. If one of them fails, the fix is
 * usually the catalog, occasionally the rule — but never this file quietly, because a guard that is
 * loosened whenever it complains is not a guard.
 *
 * Exit code 1 on any failure, so it can sit in front of a build.
 */

import { ALL_ITEMS, type ItemDefinition } from '../src/constants/items';
import { RARITY_LADDER, type Rarity } from '../src/constants/rarity';
import { getDisplayCategory } from '../src/utils/categoryUtils';

const failures: string[] = [];
const warnings: string[] = [];

const fail = (msg: string) => failures.push(msg);
const warn = (msg: string) => warnings.push(msg);

// --- §19: every item has the fields the rest of the game assumes -------------------------------

const seen = new Map<string, ItemDefinition>();
for (const item of ALL_ITEMS) {
  const where = `${item.id} (${item.name})`;

  if (!item.id) fail(`商品缺少 id：${item.name}`);
  if (seen.has(item.id)) {
    fail(`重複的商品 id：${item.id} — 「${seen.get(item.id)!.name}」與「${item.name}」`);
  }
  seen.set(item.id, item);

  if (!item.name) fail(`${where} 缺少 name`);
  if (typeof item.price !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(item.price)) {
    fail(`${where} 的 price 不是有效數字：${item.price}`);
  } else if (!Number.isInteger(item.price) || item.price < 0) {
    fail(`${where} 的 price 必須是非負整數：${item.price}`);
  }
  if (!item.category) fail(`${where} 缺少 category`);
  if (!item.shopCategory) fail(`${where} 缺少 shopCategory`);
  else if (!getDisplayCategory(item.shopCategory)) {
    fail(`${where} 的 shopCategory「${item.shopCategory}」不在 DISPLAY_CATEGORIES 裡`);
  }

  // The one shape a 0-price item is allowed to have: it is EARNED, not free. See utils/unlock.ts
  // and constants/houseStyles.ts (毛胚屋 is granted, never sold).
  if (item.price === 0 && !item.xpUnlock && item.id !== 'house-starter') {
    fail(`${where} 的 price 是 0，但沒有 xpUnlock — 免費商品必須有解鎖條件`);
  }
  if (item.xpUnlock !== undefined && item.price !== 0) {
    fail(`${where} 同時有 xpUnlock 與 price ${item.price} — 解鎖條件取代價格，不是疊加`);
  }

  // Required by the type, checked anyway: `ALL_ITEMS` is partly GENERATED (artwork.ts,
  // houseStyles.ts), and a generator that maps a field through can drop it without the literal
  // ever looking wrong.
  if (!item.rarity) fail(`${where} 缺少 rarity`);
  else if (!RARITY_LADDER.includes(item.rarity)) {
    fail(`${where} 的 rarity「${item.rarity}」不是有效的稀有度`);
  }
}

// --- The ladder still has to narrow towards the top --------------------------------------------

const counts = new Map<Rarity, number>(RARITY_LADDER.map((r) => [r, 0]));
for (const item of ALL_ITEMS) counts.set(item.rarity, (counts.get(item.rarity) ?? 0) + 1);

// 神話 is capped at ONE item in the entire game — rarity.ts and DESIGN_SYSTEM.md both say so, and
// it is the single hardest rule in the file: a second one does not make two special items, it
// makes the tier mean nothing.
const mythic = counts.get('mythic') ?? 0;
if (mythic > 1) {
  const which = ALL_ITEMS.filter((i) => i.rarity === 'mythic').map((i) => i.id).join('、');
  fail(`神話 只能有 1 件，目前有 ${mythic} 件：${which}`);
}

// 史詩 stays scarce. This used to guard 傳說 with a flat 「single figures」, which stopped being a
// meaningful bound the moment 傳說 merged down into 史詩 (rarity.ts, 2026-08-28) and the rung
// inherited its stock: 12 items would have failed a rule that was written about 3.
//
// A share rather than a count, because what this rule protects is the FEELING that a purple frame
// is unusual, and that is relative to how much else is on the shelf. 12% is a ceiling with room in
// it — the catalog sits at ~8% — so it fails on a drift, not on the next graded shelf.
const epic = counts.get('epic') ?? 0;
const epicShare = epic / ALL_ITEMS.length;
if (epicShare > 0.12) {
  fail(`史詩 佔 ${(epicShare * 100).toFixed(1)}%（${epic}/${ALL_ITEMS.length}），超過 12% 上限`);
}

// The distribution must be a pyramid: each rung no bigger than the one below it. This is what
// stops the ladder inverting one item at a time — the failure that turns 稀有 into the default.
for (let i = 1; i < RARITY_LADDER.length; i++) {
  const lower = RARITY_LADDER[i - 1];
  const upper = RARITY_LADDER[i];
  const lo = counts.get(lower) ?? 0;
  const up = counts.get(upper) ?? 0;
  if (up > lo) fail(`稀有度分布倒掛：${upper} 有 ${up} 件，多於它下面的 ${lower}（${lo} 件）`);
}

// --- Price and rarity must stay SEPARATE properties ---------------------------------------------

/**
 * The rule 「不要用價格決定稀有度」 (§5), checked the only way it can be: if rarity were derived
 * from price, the two would be perfectly rank-correlated. So the catalog must contain at least one
 * counter-example in BOTH directions — a cheap item outranking an expensive one, and vice versa.
 * This does not prove nobody derived it, but it does fail the moment someone re-sorts the whole
 * catalog by price, which is how the derivation actually creeps back in.
 */
const priced = ALL_ITEMS.filter((i) => i.price > 0);
const rank = (r: Rarity) => RARITY_LADDER.indexOf(r);
const cheapButRarer = priced.some((a) =>
  priced.some((b) => a.price < b.price && rank(a.rarity) > rank(b.rarity)),
);
if (!cheapButRarer) {
  fail('目錄裡沒有任何「便宜但更稀有」的商品 — 稀有度看起來是從價格推導出來的（見 §5）');
}

// --- Report -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

const pct = (n: number) => `${((n / ALL_ITEMS.length) * 100).toFixed(1)}%`;
console.log(`商品總數：${ALL_ITEMS.length}`);
console.log('稀有度分布：');
for (const tier of RARITY_LADDER) {
  const n = counts.get(tier) ?? 0;
  console.log(`  ${tier.padEnd(10)} ${String(n).padStart(3)}  ${pct(n).padStart(6)}`);
}

for (const w of warnings) console.warn(`⚠ ${w}`);
if (failures.length > 0) {
  console.error(`\n✗ ${failures.length} 項商品資料問題：`);
  for (const f of failures) console.error(`  - ${f}`);
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log('\n✓ 商品資料稽核通過');

```

## scripts/audit-character-parts.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * DOES THE IMPORTED CHARACTER STILL AGREE WITH THE RIG?
 *
 *   npm run audit:character
 *
 * The model layer's whole design rests on one agreement: the CONTROLLER places joints from
 * `AUTHORED_SKELETON`, and the GEOMETRY under each joint was cut about that same point. Nothing
 * at runtime re-checks it. When the two drift — a part re-exported from Blender without
 * re-pasting the numbers, a number tuned by hand without re-cutting the parts — the game does
 * not throw. It draws a character that is subtly wrong: soles under the grass, a head that
 * floats, a hat sized for a skull that is no longer there. Those are hard to see on purpose
 * and easy to measure, which is what this script is for.
 *
 * It reads only what SHIPS — the six .glb files and the rig constants — so it is checking the
 * thing players get rather than the Blender file it came from. Re-cutting the parts is
 * `npm run split:character`; this says whether the result and the rig still describe one
 * character.
 *
 * Exits non-zero on any failure, so it can be put in front of a build.
 */

import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';
import { CHARACTER_MODEL_BUDGET, CHARACTER_MODEL_FILES } from '../src/constants/characterAssets';
import {
  AUTHORED_ARM_REST_Z,
  AUTHORED_ATTACHMENTS,
  AUTHORED_SKELETON,
  LEGACY_WEARABLE_FIT,
  RIG_ENVELOPE,
  crownY,
  toWorld,
} from '../src/constants/characterRig';

const ROOT = path.dirname(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)));
const PUBLIC_DIR = path.join(ROOT, 'public');

/**
 * How far a measurement may sit from the number the rig states, in LOCAL units.
 *
 * 0.0005 local is ~1 mm of world, and the rig constants are written to four decimal places, so
 * anything inside this is rounding rather than drift. `RIG_ENVELOPE.toleranceWorld` is the same
 * idea one layer up and is used directly for the envelope checks below.
 */
const TOLERANCE = 0.0005;

/** The legacy torso capsule, which every imported torso is a scaled copy of. */
const LEGACY_TORSO = LEGACY_WEARABLE_FIT.torso;

const failures: string[] = [];
const notes: string[] = [];

const fail = (message: string) => failures.push(message);
const note = (message: string) => notes.push(message);

/** Reports a measured number against the one the rig promises. */
function expect(label: string, measured: number, expected: number, tolerance = TOLERANCE) {
  const drift = Math.abs(measured - expected);
  if (drift > tolerance) {
    fail(
      `${label}: the parts measure ${measured.toFixed(4)} but the rig says ${expected.toFixed(4)} ` +
        `(off by ${drift.toFixed(4)} local / ${toWorld(drift).toFixed(4)} world).`,
    );
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// LOAD THE SIX PARTS
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const loader = new GLTFLoader();

async function loadPart(url: string): Promise<THREE.Object3D> {
  const file = path.join(PUBLIC_DIR, url.replace(/^\//, ''));
  if (!fs.existsSync(file)) {
    throw new Error(
      `missing. Expected ${path.relative(ROOT, file)} — the paths are stated in ` +
        `constants/characterAssets.ts, and the files are produced by \`npm run split:character\`.`,
    );
  }
  const buffer = fs.readFileSync(file);
  const array = buffer.buffer.slice(buffer.byteOffset, buffer.byteOffset + buffer.byteLength);
  const gltf = await new Promise<{ scene: THREE.Object3D }>((resolve, reject) => {
    loader.parse(array as ArrayBuffer, '', resolve as never, reject);
  });
  gltf.scene.updateMatrixWorld(true);
  return gltf.scene;
}

type PartId = 'head' | 'torso' | 'leftArm' | 'rightArm' | 'leftLeg' | 'rightLeg';

const PART_FILES: Record<PartId, string> = {
  head: CHARACTER_MODEL_FILES.head,
  torso: CHARACTER_MODEL_FILES.torso,
  leftArm: CHARACTER_MODEL_FILES.leftArm,
  rightArm: CHARACTER_MODEL_FILES.rightArm,
  leftLeg: CHARACTER_MODEL_FILES.leftLeg,
  rightLeg: CHARACTER_MODEL_FILES.rightLeg,
};

const parts = {} as Record<PartId, THREE.Object3D>;
for (const [id, url] of Object.entries(PART_FILES) as [PartId, string][]) {
  try {
    parts[id] = await loadPart(url);
  } catch (error) {
    fail(`"${id}" (${url}) ${(error as Error).message}`);
  }
}

if (failures.length > 0) {
  report();
  process.exit(1);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MEASURE
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const box = (object: THREE.Object3D) => new THREE.Box3().setFromObject(object);
const partBoxes = Object.fromEntries(
  (Object.keys(parts) as PartId[]).map((id) => [id, box(parts[id])]),
) as Record<PartId, THREE.Box3>;

const s = AUTHORED_SKELETON;

// --- The two envelope rules, checked on the assembled character ------------
//
// This is the pair the checklist calls the 鐵則, and the only pair that can put the character
// through the floor or through a doorway. Everything else is proportion; these two are contract.
const assembled = new THREE.Box3();
const place = (id: PartId, position: THREE.Vector3, restZ = 0) => {
  const joint = new THREE.Group();
  joint.position.copy(position);
  const pose = new THREE.Group();
  pose.rotation.z = restZ;
  joint.add(pose);
  pose.add(parts[id]);
  joint.updateMatrixWorld(true);
  assembled.union(box(joint));
};

place('head', new THREE.Vector3(0, s.head.y, 0));
place('torso', new THREE.Vector3(0, s.torso.y, 0));
place('leftArm', new THREE.Vector3(-s.shoulder.x, s.shoulder.y, 0), AUTHORED_ARM_REST_Z);
place('rightArm', new THREE.Vector3(s.shoulder.x, s.shoulder.y, 0), -AUTHORED_ARM_REST_Z);
place('leftLeg', new THREE.Vector3(-s.hip.x, s.hip.y, 0));
place('rightLeg', new THREE.Vector3(s.hip.x, s.hip.y, 0));

expect('sole (assembled)', assembled.min.y, s.soleY, RIG_ENVELOPE.toleranceWorld / 2.25);
expect('crown (assembled)', assembled.max.y, crownY(s), RIG_ENVELOPE.toleranceWorld / 2.25);
note(
  `assembled ${(assembled.max.y - assembled.min.y).toFixed(4)} local tall ` +
    `(${toWorld(assembled.max.y - assembled.min.y).toFixed(4)} world), sole ${assembled.min.y.toFixed(4)}`,
);

// --- The skeleton's own numbers, against the geometry they describe ---------
expect('head.crownRise', partBoxes.head.max.y, s.head.crownRise);
expect('head.halfWidth', Math.max(-partBoxes.head.min.x, partBoxes.head.max.x), s.head.halfWidth);
expect('torso.halfWidth', Math.max(-partBoxes.torso.min.x, partBoxes.torso.max.x), s.torso.halfWidth);

// --- The sockets that are MEASURED off the body rather than chosen ----------
//
// `foot` is the one anchor that has to land on the ground plane: a shoe is drawn at the sole,
// so if this drifts every shoe in the game sinks or floats by the same amount, on both feet, in
// a way that reads as a shoe bug rather than as a rig one.
expect('attachments.foot', AUTHORED_ATTACHMENTS.foot.position[1], partBoxes.leftLeg.min.y);
expect('attachments.ankle', AUTHORED_ATTACHMENTS.ankle.position[1], partBoxes.leftLeg.min.y + 0.035);

// The head sockets are all stated relative to the SKULL's centre, not the neck joint the part
// hangs from — legacy gets away with conflating the two only because its head is a sphere
// centred on its own joint. Checking one of them keeps that offset honest.
const skullCentreY = (partBoxes.head.min.y + partBoxes.head.max.y) / 2;
expect('head sockets centred on the skull', AUTHORED_ATTACHMENTS.hair.position[1], skullCentreY);
expect(
  'attachments.halo keeps its 0.07 clearance',
  AUTHORED_ATTACHMENTS.halo.position[1],
  s.head.crownRise + 0.07,
);

// --- Does the cloth actually clear the limb? -------------------------------
//
// The three wrap-around wearables — sleeve, trousers, shoes — enclose a limb rather than
// hanging off a point, so each carries the limb it was drawn for baked into its geometry (see
// LEGACY_WEARABLE_FIT). On a re-proportioned body they fail by INTERSECTING, which no other
// check here would notice: the parts are still the right size, the joints are still in the
// right place, and the character still stands 2.1639 tall with a limb sticking through its
// clothes.
//
// Both checks are measured against the geometry that shipped, not against the numbers the
// splitter happened to print, so re-cutting the model without re-pasting the sockets fails
// here rather than on someone's screen.
{
  const clearance = (measured: number, needed: number, what: string) => {
    if (measured < needed) {
      fail(
        `${what}: the cloth reaches ${measured.toFixed(4)} but the limb is ${needed.toFixed(4)} ` +
          `across — the limb comes through by ${toWorld(needed - measured).toFixed(4)} world. ` +
          `Widen the socket's scale in AUTHORED_ATTACHMENTS.`,
      );
    } else {
      note(`${what}: ${toWorld(measured - needed).toFixed(4)} world of clearance`);
    }
  };

  // SLEEVE. Two failures, and the second is the one legacy's numbers cause on this arm: a
  // sleeve wide enough but sat too low leaves the shoulder ball bare above it.
  const { sleeve } = AUTHORED_ATTACHMENTS;
  const sleeveScale = sleeve.scale ?? 1;
  const sleeveRadius = LEGACY_WEARABLE_FIT.sleeve.radius * sleeveScale;
  const sleeveCentreY =
    sleeve.position[1] + LEGACY_WEARABLE_FIT.sleeve.y * sleeveScale;
  const sleeveTop =
    sleeveCentreY + (LEGACY_WEARABLE_FIT.sleeve.length / 2 + LEGACY_WEARABLE_FIT.sleeve.radius) * sleeveScale;

  // The upper arm is the arm mesh nearest the shoulder; the other one is the hand.
  //
  // Measured off each mesh's own GEOMETRY, not `setFromObject`: by this point the parts have
  // been reparented into joint groups for the envelope check above, so a world-space box would
  // silently return root-space numbers and compare a sleeve in arm space against an arm in
  // character space. The part files put every mesh at its root untransformed, so the geometry
  // box IS the part-space box.
  const armBoxes: THREE.Box3[] = [];
  parts.leftArm.traverse((node) => {
    const mesh = node as THREE.Mesh;
    if (!mesh.isMesh) return;
    mesh.geometry.computeBoundingBox();
    armBoxes.push(mesh.geometry.boundingBox!.clone());
  });
  const upper = armBoxes.sort(
    (a, b) => a.getCenter(new THREE.Vector3()).length() - b.getCenter(new THREE.Vector3()).length(),
  )[0];
  const upperCentreX = (upper.min.x + upper.max.x) / 2;
  const upperRadius = Math.max((upper.max.x - upper.min.x) / 2, (upper.max.z - upper.min.z) / 2);

  clearance(sleeveRadius, Math.abs(upperCentreX) + upperRadius, 'sleeve vs upper arm (width)');
  clearance(sleeveTop, upper.max.y, 'sleeve vs upper arm (shoulder end)');

  // TROUSERS and SHOES. One number sizes both — Pants.tsx's floor is the snugger of the two,
  // and `foot` deliberately takes the same scale as `leg` so the hem and the boot shaft meet.
  const legScale = AUTHORED_ATTACHMENTS.leg.scale ?? 1;
  const legRadius = Math.max(
    -partBoxes.leftLeg.min.x,
    partBoxes.leftLeg.max.x,
    -partBoxes.leftLeg.min.z,
    partBoxes.leftLeg.max.z,
  );
  clearance(LEGACY_WEARABLE_FIT.trouserFloor * legScale, legRadius, 'trousers vs leg');

  // WHERE THE TOP AND THE TROUSERS MEET, which is the seam neither of them owns.
  //
  // Between the top's hem and the trousers' waistband there is a stretch of leg that BOTH
  // garments can disclaim, and on this character the thigh is nearly as wide as the chest, so
  // the top's cap has narrowed past it by the time it reaches hip height. Left to the top
  // alone, a band of bare leg shows right round the hips: not a poke-through, a hole between
  // two garments that each look correct on their own.
  //
  // Either side may close it, so the check is on the UNION. The trousers close it by rising
  // past their waistband (`trouserRise`) — which is the better half of the deal, because a top
  // inflated until it happens to reach is a top that no longer fits the chest.
  const trouserTop =
    s.hip.y + Math.max(LEGACY_WEARABLE_FIT.trouserWaistY, AUTHORED_ATTACHMENTS.trouserRise) * legScale;
  const legTop = s.hip.y + partBoxes.leftLeg.max.y;
  if (trouserTop >= legTop) {
    note(
      `trousers cover the whole leg (to ${trouserTop.toFixed(4)}, leg ends ${legTop.toFixed(4)}) — ` +
        `nothing left for the top to reach`,
    );
  } else {
    const top = AUTHORED_ATTACHMENTS.torso;
    const topScale = top.scale ?? 1;
    const topCentre = s.torso.y + top.position[1];
    const topR = LEGACY_WEARABLE_FIT.top.radius * topScale;
    const topStraightHalf = (LEGACY_WEARABLE_FIT.top.length / 2) * topScale;
    const dropBelowCap = topCentre - topStraightHalf - trouserTop;
    const topReach = Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, topR ** 2 - Math.max(0, dropBelowCap) ** 2));
    const thighOuter = s.hip.x + Math.max(-partBoxes.leftLeg.min.x, partBoxes.leftLeg.max.x);
    clearance(topReach, thighOuter, 'top vs thigh where the trousers stop');
  }

  // …and however it is sized, the top still has to reach the shoulders. Checked separately
  // from the seam above because the two pull in opposite directions: whatever closes the hip
  // by making the garment bigger also risks pushing its collar up past the neck, and a fix for
  // one that quietly broke the other is precisely what this pair exists to prevent.
  const shoulderScale = AUTHORED_ATTACHMENTS.torso.scale ?? 1;
  const shoulderTop =
    s.torso.y +
    AUTHORED_ATTACHMENTS.torso.position[1] +
    (LEGACY_WEARABLE_FIT.top.length / 2 + LEGACY_WEARABLE_FIT.top.radius) * shoulderScale;
  if (shoulderTop < s.torso.y + partBoxes.torso.max.y) {
    fail(
      `the top reaches ${shoulderTop.toFixed(4)} but the torso's own top is at ` +
        `${(s.torso.y + partBoxes.torso.max.y).toFixed(4)} — the shoulders show through it.`,
    );
  }
  if ((AUTHORED_ATTACHMENTS.foot.scale ?? 1) !== legScale) {
    fail(
      `attachments.foot is scaled ${AUTHORED_ATTACHMENTS.foot.scale ?? 1} but attachments.leg is ` +
        `${legScale}. They must match: the trouser hem and the boot shaft meet at the ankle, and ` +
        `two different sizes open a gap there.`,
    );
  }
}

// --- Does the buried part of the leg STAY buried while walking? ------------
//
// A leg's mesh runs up inside the torso so the thigh has something to pivot from without
// opening a seam at the hip. That hidden length is free while the character stands still — and
// it is the first thing to betray a model in motion, because the controller swings the leg
// about the hip and whatever is buried swings OUT of the body's back or front.
//
// Nothing else here can see it: every other check measures the character at rest, where the
// geometry is correct by construction. So this one poses the leg.
//
// The torso is recovered as the legacy capsule under a non-uniform scale — which is what the
// part actually is — so containment can be tested exactly rather than against a bounding box
// that would call the corners of the body solid.
{
  /** `walkSwingRange` in Avatar.tsx. The everyday extreme; the somersault's 1.7 is a stunt. */
  const WALK_SWING = 0.6;

  const torsoHalf = {
    x: Math.max(-partBoxes.torso.min.x, partBoxes.torso.max.x),
    y: Math.max(-partBoxes.torso.min.y, partBoxes.torso.max.y),
    z: Math.max(-partBoxes.torso.min.z, partBoxes.torso.max.z),
  };
  const scale = new THREE.Vector3(
    torsoHalf.x / LEGACY_TORSO.radius,
    torsoHalf.y / (LEGACY_TORSO.radius + LEGACY_TORSO.length / 2),
    torsoHalf.z / LEGACY_TORSO.radius,
  );

  /** How far OUTSIDE the torso a point is, in torso-local units. Negative means inside. */
  const outside = (p: THREE.Vector3) => {
    const u = new THREE.Vector3(p.x / scale.x, p.y / scale.y, p.z / scale.z);
    const capY = THREE.MathUtils.clamp(u.y, -LEGACY_TORSO.length / 2, LEGACY_TORSO.length / 2);
    return Math.hypot(u.x, u.y - capY, u.z) - LEGACY_TORSO.radius;
  };

  const legVerts: THREE.Vector3[] = [];
  parts.leftLeg.traverse((node) => {
    const mesh = node as THREE.Mesh;
    if (!mesh.isMesh) return;
    const position = mesh.geometry.getAttribute('position');
    for (let i = 0; i < position.count; i += 1) {
      legVerts.push(new THREE.Vector3().fromBufferAttribute(position as THREE.BufferAttribute, i));
    }
  });

  /** A leg vertex in TORSO space, with the leg swung by `angle` about its hip. */
  const posed = (v: THREE.Vector3, angle: number) =>
    v
      .clone()
      .applyAxisAngle(new THREE.Vector3(1, 0, 0), angle)
      .add(new THREE.Vector3(-s.hip.x, s.hip.y - s.torso.y, 0));

  let worst = 0;
  let worstAngle = 0;
  for (const v of legVerts) {
    if (outside(posed(v, 0)) >= 0) continue; // Visible at rest — its business, not ours.
    for (const angle of [-WALK_SWING, -WALK_SWING / 2, WALK_SWING / 2, WALK_SWING]) {
      const d = outside(posed(v, angle));
      if (d > worst) {
        worst = d;
        worstAngle = angle;
      }
    }
  }

  if (worst > 0.001) {
    // The two numbers that explain it, because the obvious remedy is the wrong one. Trimming
    // the leg's top barely helps: what governs this is how deep the BODY is where the leg
    // swings, and whether the pivot is inside it at all. A point ON the pivot does not move
    // under rotation — so a hip buried in the torso is self-covering, and a hip below it has
    // nothing over the leg to begin with.
    const torsoBottom = s.torso.y + partBoxes.torso.min.y;
    const legDepth = Math.max(-partBoxes.leftLeg.min.z, partBoxes.leftLeg.max.z);
    fail(
      `the leg swings OUT of the torso: ${toWorld(worst).toFixed(4)} world units proud at ` +
        `${THREE.MathUtils.radToDeg(worstAngle).toFixed(0)}deg, which the walk cycle reaches every ` +
        `step. Shortening the leg's top does NOT fix this — the cause is the two numbers below, ` +
        `and legacy passes because both go the other way.\n` +
        `      hip ${s.hip.y.toFixed(4)} vs torso bottom ${torsoBottom.toFixed(4)}: the pivot is ` +
        `${toWorld(torsoBottom - s.hip.y).toFixed(4)} world BELOW the body (legacy's is 0.0788 INSIDE), ` +
        `so almost nothing is buried to stay buried.\n` +
        `      leg half-depth ${legDepth.toFixed(4)} against a torso only ` +
        `${Math.max(-partBoxes.torso.min.z, partBoxes.torso.max.z).toFixed(4)} deep — ` +
        `${((legDepth / Math.max(-partBoxes.torso.min.z, partBoxes.torso.max.z)) * 100).toFixed(0)}% ` +
        `of the body's own thickness (legacy: 41%), so the thigh fills the hip front-to-back and ` +
        `any swing takes it outside.`,
    );
  } else {
    note(
      `leg stays buried through a ${THREE.MathUtils.radToDeg(WALK_SWING).toFixed(0)}deg swing ` +
        `(${toWorld(-worst).toFixed(4)} world to spare)`,
    );
  }
}

// --- Left/right symmetry ---------------------------------------------------
//
// The right limbs are mirrored from the left by the splitter, so any asymmetry here means a
// mirror went wrong rather than that the model is asymmetric.
for (const [left, right] of [
  ['leftArm', 'rightArm'],
  ['leftLeg', 'rightLeg'],
] as [PartId, PartId][]) {
  const l = partBoxes[left];
  const r = partBoxes[right];
  expect(`${right} mirrors ${left} in x`, r.max.x, -l.min.x);
  expect(`${right} mirrors ${left} in y`, r.min.y, l.min.y);
  expect(`${right} mirrors ${left} in z`, r.min.z, l.min.z);
}

// --- The eyes the controller drives ----------------------------------------
for (const name of ['Eye_L', 'Eye_R']) {
  if (!parts.head.getObjectByName(name)) {
    fail(
      `head.glb has no "${name}" node, so the controller cannot blink or squint this face ` +
        `(GlbHeadPart binds it by name). Re-cut with \`npm run split:character\`.`,
    );
  }
}

// THE BOUND NODE MUST SIT AT ITS PARENT'S ORIGIN.
//
// The controller ASSIGNS the eye's height rather than offsetting it —
// `eyeL.position.y = lerp(0, 0.012, squint)`, which is 0 at rest. So a bound node that carries
// the eye's own position has that position destroyed on the first frame, and the eyes jump to
// the neck joint. This shipped once: the eyes sat 0.08 below the joint and flew 181 mm of world
// upward the moment the game ran.
//
// It is checked HERE and not in a preview, because a harness that renders the model without the
// controller's useFrame cannot see it — the model is correct until something writes to it.
for (const name of ['Eye_L', 'Eye_R']) {
  const bound = parts.head.getObjectByName(name);
  if (bound && Math.abs(bound.position.y) > 1e-6) {
    fail(
      `"${name}" sits at y ${bound.position.y.toFixed(4)} in its parent, but the controller ` +
        `overwrites that with 0 every frame — the eye will jump ${toWorld(Math.abs(bound.position.y)).toFixed(4)} ` +
        `world units up in the game while looking correct in any static preview. The height ` +
        `belongs on a parent node (see Eye_L_Socket in split-character-glb.mjs).`,
    );
  }
}

// …and the eyes must be level with each other.
//
// The source places them 12 mm of world apart in x, and the splitter centres the pair
// (SYMMETRISE_EYES). Checked here because it is the one adjustment the splitter makes to how
// the character LOOKS: if that flag is ever turned off, or a re-export moves an eye in y or z
// where the splitter's x-only correction cannot reach it, the face goes crooked again — and a
// crooked face is the kind of thing that reads as "something is off" long before anyone can
// name which eye moved.
//
// Measured on the SOCKET, which is where the position now lives.
{
  const left = parts.head.getObjectByName('Eye_L_Socket');
  const right = parts.head.getObjectByName('Eye_R_Socket');
  if (left && right) {
    const drift = new THREE.Vector3(
      left.position.x + right.position.x,
      left.position.y - right.position.y,
      left.position.z - right.position.z,
    );
    if (drift.length() > TOLERANCE) {
      fail(
        `the eyes are not symmetric: L ${left.position.toArray().map((v) => v.toFixed(4)).join(', ')} ` +
          `vs R ${right.position.toArray().map((v) => v.toFixed(4)).join(', ')} ` +
          `— off by ${toWorld(drift.length()).toFixed(4)} world.`,
      );
    } else {
      note(`eyes symmetric at ±${Math.abs(right.position.x).toFixed(4)}`);
    }
  } else {
    fail('head.glb has no Eye_L_Socket/Eye_R_Socket — re-cut with `npm run split:character`.');
  }
}

// --- Triangle winding ------------------------------------------------------
//
// A mirror is a negative-determinant transform: it flips triangle winding, and a
// wound-backwards closed mesh is culled from the outside and visible from the inside. On a
// character that shows up as a limb that is there in the model viewer and invisible in the
// game — so it is worth measuring rather than eyeballing. Signed volume by the divergence
// theorem is positive exactly when a closed mesh is wound outward.
for (const id of Object.keys(parts) as PartId[]) {
  parts[id].traverse((node) => {
    const mesh = node as THREE.Mesh;
    if (!mesh.isMesh) return;
    const volume = signedVolume(mesh.geometry);
    if (volume <= 0) {
      fail(
        `${id} / "${mesh.name}" is wound inside-out (signed volume ${volume.toFixed(6)}). ` +
          `It will be invisible from outside. This is the mirror step in split-character-glb.mjs.`,
      );
    }
  });
}

function signedVolume(geometry: THREE.BufferGeometry): number {
  const position = geometry.getAttribute('position');
  const index = geometry.getIndex();
  const count = index ? index.count : position.count;
  const a = new THREE.Vector3();
  const b = new THREE.Vector3();
  const c = new THREE.Vector3();
  let total = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 3) {
    const [ia, ib, ic] = index
      ? [index.getX(i), index.getX(i + 1), index.getX(i + 2)]
      : [i, i + 1, i + 2];
    a.fromBufferAttribute(position, ia);
    b.fromBufferAttribute(position, ib);
    c.fromBufferAttribute(position, ic);
    total += a.dot(b.clone().cross(c)) / 6;
  }
  return total;
}

// --- Budget ----------------------------------------------------------------
let triangles = 0;
let meshes = 0;
let missingMaterial = 0;
const materials = new Set<THREE.Material>();
for (const id of Object.keys(parts) as PartId[]) {
  parts[id].traverse((node) => {
    const mesh = node as THREE.Mesh;
    if (!mesh.isMesh) return;
    meshes += 1;
    const position = mesh.geometry.getAttribute('position');
    triangles += mesh.geometry.index ? mesh.geometry.index.count / 3 : position.count / 3;
    for (const material of Array.isArray(mesh.material) ? mesh.material : [mesh.material]) {
      if (material) materials.add(material);
      else missingMaterial += 1;
    }
  });
}

if (missingMaterial > 0) fail(`${missingMaterial} mesh(es) have no material; they render as default white.`);
if (triangles > CHARACTER_MODEL_BUDGET.triangles) {
  fail(`${Math.round(triangles)} triangles against a budget of ${CHARACTER_MODEL_BUDGET.triangles}.`);
}
if (meshes > CHARACTER_MODEL_BUDGET.meshes) {
  fail(`${meshes} meshes against a budget of ${CHARACTER_MODEL_BUDGET.meshes} — each one is a draw call.`);
}
if (materials.size > CHARACTER_MODEL_BUDGET.materials) {
  fail(`${materials.size} materials against a budget of ${CHARACTER_MODEL_BUDGET.materials}.`);
}
note(`cost ${Math.round(triangles)} tris / ${meshes} mesh / ${materials.size} mat`);

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// REPORT
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

report();
process.exit(failures.length > 0 ? 1 : 0);

function report() {
  console.log('');
  console.log('  character parts vs. AUTHORED_SKELETON');
  console.log('');
  for (const line of notes) console.log(`  · ${line}`);
  if (notes.length > 0) console.log('');
  if (failures.length === 0) {
    console.log(`  OK — ${Object.keys(parts).length} parts agree with the rig.`);
    console.log('');
    return;
  }
  for (const line of failures) console.error(`  ✗ ${line}`);
  console.error('');
  console.error('  Re-cut the parts and re-paste the printed numbers: npm run split:character');
  console.error('');
}

```
