## scripts/audit-ground-contact.ts

```ts
/**
 * `npm run audit:ground`
 *
 * Do the character's feet meet the surface the character is standing on — everywhere?
 *
 * WHY THIS IS A STANDING CHECK. "How high are the feet" is answered in three different places for
 * three different reasons: the island samples its terrain, the interior has one flat floor, and
 * the dressing room stands the avatar on a stage. Each of them looks right in isolation and
 * nothing fails when one is wrong; the character just hovers, and a hover of a few centimetres is
 * only visible when the camera comes close. So it went unnoticed that:
 *
 *   - `resolveCollisions`'s INTERIOR branch never assigned `terrainY` at all. It inherited the
 *     initialiser it happened to share with the island branch — 0.35, which is the outdoor grass
 *     height plus the outdoor foot lift — and the player therefore stood a third of a unit above
 *     an interior floor that is at 0. That is a sixth of the character's own height, clear over
 *     every rug and every furniture base in the house.
 *   - outdoors, FOOT_LIFT held the root 0.05 above the ground, on top of the 11 mm the soles are
 *     already authored BELOW the root — so the visible gap under both feet was ~39 mm on every
 *     surface in the game.
 *
 * The reference the game already gets right is the DRESSING ROOM: DressingRoomView puts the stage
 * group and the avatar group at the same y, and StudioFloor draws its disc at its own y = 0, so
 * the avatar's root lands exactly on the floor plane there — and that is the one place the
 * character is looked at close up. This audit asserts the rest of the game does the same thing.
 *
 * Pure arithmetic plus the real `resolveCollisions`. No renderer, no browser.
 */

import * as THREE from 'three';
import {
  AUTHORED_SKELETON,
  CharacterSkeleton,
  LEGACY_SKELETON,
  LEG_LENGTHEN,
  V2_SKELETON,
  toWorld,
} from '../src/constants/characterRig';
import { soleAnchorY } from '../src/components/Three/Shoes';
import { FOOT_LIFT, footLevelAt, resolveCollisions } from '../src/components/Three/characterMovement';
import {
  ISLAND_SURFACE_Y,
  ISLAND_TERRAIN,
  MOUND_BASE_SINK,
  getTerrainInfo,
} from '../src/constants/terrain';
import { INTERIOR_FLOOR_Y } from '../src/constants/interiorShell';
import { ROOM_DEFS } from '../src/constants/rooms';
import { ALL_ITEMS, getStandableSurface } from '../src/constants/items';
import {
  getFurnitureInteractions,
  interactionAnchoring,
  interactionPosture,
  poseRootHeight,
} from '../src/constants/furnitureInteractions';
import { getPosture } from '../src/constants/interactionPostures';
import { resolveInteractionSpot } from '../src/lib/furnitureInteraction';
import { getFootprint, measureFootprint, registerFootprint } from '../src/lib/furniturePlacement';
import { ItemCategory, PlacedItem, UserProfile } from '../src/types';
import {
  DODECAHEDRON_INSPHERE,
  PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS,
  getResolvedRockPositions,
  getRockScale,
} from '../src/utils/placementRules';
import { ISLAND_SCALE, buildModelObject3D, footprintOf } from './lib/measureFurnitureModel';

let failures = 0;
let checks = 0;

function check(name: string, ok: boolean, detail: string) {
  checks++;
  if (!ok) failures++;
  console.log(`${ok ? '  ok  ' : ' FAIL '} ${name}`);
  console.log(`        ${detail}`);
}

const mm = (v: number) => `${(v * 1000).toFixed(1)}mm`;

/**
 * How far the soles may be from the surface and still read as standing on it.
 *
 * Asymmetric on purpose, because the two directions are not the same mistake. A sole a little
 * INSIDE the ground is invisible — it is what the rig's negative `soleY` is deliberately for.
 * A sole ABOVE the ground is the bug this file exists to catch, and it is visible from the first
 * millimetre, so nothing is allowed there at all.
 */
const MAX_SINK = 0.02;
const MAX_FLOAT = 0;

/** World Y the lowest drawn point of the body reaches when the root is at `rootY`. */
const soleWorldY = (rootY: number, s: CharacterSkeleton) => rootY + toWorld(s.soleY);

/** Assert the body standing at `rootY` meets a surface drawn at `surfaceY`. */
function checkContact(name: string, rootY: number, surfaceY: number, s = LEGACY_SKELETON) {
  const gap = soleWorldY(rootY, s) - surfaceY;
  check(
    name,
    gap <= MAX_FLOAT + 1e-9 && gap >= -MAX_SINK - 1e-9,
    `root ${rootY.toFixed(4)}, surface ${surfaceY.toFixed(4)}, soles ${
      gap >= 0 ? `${mm(gap)} ABOVE it` : `${mm(-gap)} into it`
    }`,
  );
}

const island = (placements: PlacedItem[] = []) =>
  ({ islandPlacements: placements } as unknown as UserProfile);

/** resolveCollisions, with everything this audit does not care about defaulted away. */
function footLevel(x: number, z: number, isInterior: boolean, profile: UserProfile | null) {
  return resolveCollisions({
    testPos: new THREE.Vector3(x, 0, z),
    isInterior,
    islandScale: 1,
    profile,
    home: null,
  }).terrainY;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 1. The character's own envelope: where IS the bottom of the model?
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
//
// Everything below asserts that the root origin is put on the surface. That is only the right
// thing to do because the rig's first invariant says the root origin IS the ground contact point,
// so this part checks that claim against the model actually being drawn before trusting it.

console.log('\n=== part 1: the rig contract the rest of this audit stands on ===');

// The legacy leg is a capsule hanging off the hip pivot, and Shoes.tsx already derives where its
// bottom cap lands (it has to, to put a shoe there). If that derivation and the skeleton's own
// `soleY` ever disagree, every "the feet are on the ground" statement in the game is off by the
// difference — silently, because nothing raycasts the mesh to check.
const legacySoleFromModel = LEGACY_SKELETON.hip.y + soleAnchorY(LEG_LENGTHEN);
check(
  'the drawn leg ends where the skeleton says the sole is',
  Math.abs(legacySoleFromModel - LEGACY_SKELETON.soleY) < 1e-9,
  `leg capsule bottom cap ${legacySoleFromModel.toFixed(4)} vs soleY ${LEGACY_SKELETON.soleY} (LOCAL)`,
);

for (const [name, s] of [
  ['legacy', LEGACY_SKELETON],
  ['v2', V2_SKELETON],
  ['authored', AUTHORED_SKELETON],
] as const) {
  const depth = -toWorld(s.soleY);
  check(
    `${name}: soles are authored just inside the ground, not above it`,
    depth > 0 && depth <= MAX_SINK,
    `soles sit ${mm(depth)} below the root origin — a body on the surface buries them by that much`,
  );
}

check(
  'the walk resolve adds no lift of its own on top of that',
  FOOT_LIFT === 0,
  `FOOT_LIFT ${FOOT_LIFT} — anything above 0 is daylight under both feet, on every surface`,
);

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 2. Outdoors
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

console.log('\n=== part 2: the island ===');

// The plateau is drawn as one flat disc at exactly ISLAND_SURFACE_Y (Three/Island.tsx's
// PlateauSurface), so out on the flat the surface height is not an approximation — it is that
// number, and the feet have to be on it.
for (const [x, z] of [[1.5, -2], [2.5, 2.5], [3.5, -1]] as const) {
  const y = footLevel(x, z, false, island());
  const drawn = getTerrainInfo(x, z, 1).targetY;
  check(
    `flat grass at (${x}, ${z}) stands on the plateau disc`,
    Math.abs(y - ISLAND_SURFACE_Y) < 1e-9 && Math.abs(y - drawn) < 1e-9,
    `foot level ${y.toFixed(4)}, plateau drawn at ${ISLAND_SURFACE_Y}`,
  );
  checkContact(`flat grass at (${x}, ${z}): soles meet the ground`, y, drawn);
}

// The mound is the only raised ground on the island, and the one place the walk height and the
// drawn geometry are two different descriptions of the same slope rather than one shared number —
// so it is checked against the FRUSTUM, rebuilt here from what Island.tsx draws.
for (const m of ISLAND_TERRAIN.mounds) {
  const baseY = ISLAND_SURFACE_Y - MOUND_BASE_SINK;
  /** Height of the drawn cone at radius d, or the plateau where the cone is buried under it. */
  const drawnMoundY = (d: number) => {
    if (d <= m.radiusTop) return m.topY;
    if (d >= m.radiusBottom) return ISLAND_SURFACE_Y;
    const t = (d - m.radiusTop) / (m.radiusBottom - m.radiusTop);
    return Math.max(ISLAND_SURFACE_Y, m.topY + (baseY - m.topY) * t);
  };

  for (const d of [0, m.radiusTop * 0.6, m.radiusTop, 2.53, 2.6, m.radiusBottom + 0.1]) {
    const x = m.cx + d;
    const y = footLevel(x, m.cz, false, island());
    check(
      `mound at ${d.toFixed(2)} from centre: the feet are on the slope that is drawn`,
      Math.abs(y - drawnMoundY(d)) < 1e-9,
      `foot level ${y.toFixed(4)}, frustum surface ${drawnMoundY(d).toFixed(4)}`,
    );
  }
}

// The outcrops are the other raised ground, and they were the worst offender in the game: the
// step-up ramped to `rockTop - 0.1` ABOVE the plateau, which at the centre of a rock is a fifth
// of a unit over its own summit. Checked against the drawn solid, which is a dodecahedron — so
// the bar is its INSPHERE (entirely inside the rock: the feet may sink, never hover).
for (const [i, rPos] of getResolvedRockPositions(1, null).entries()) {
  const scale = getRockScale(i);
  const summit = rPos[1] + scale * DODECAHEDRON_INSPHERE;
  for (const [label, d] of [['summit', 0], ['flank', scale * 0.5], ['clear of it', scale + 0.5]] as const) {
    const y = footLevel(rPos[0] + d, rPos[2], false, island());
    const drawn = d === 0
      ? Math.max(getTerrainInfo(rPos[0], rPos[2], 1).targetY, summit)
      : Math.max(
        getTerrainInfo(rPos[0] + d, rPos[2], 1).targetY,
        rPos[1] + Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, (scale * DODECAHEDRON_INSPHERE) ** 2 - d * d)),
      );
    check(
      `rock ${i} (${label}): the feet are on the rock, not over it`,
      y <= drawn + 1e-9,
      `foot level ${y.toFixed(4)}, rock surface ${drawn.toFixed(4)}`,
    );
  }
}

// The beach is a slope rather than a plane, so the check that matters there is that the feet
// follow the SAMPLED height rather than any constant — the slope is where a constant would show.
for (const [x, z] of [[6.2, 0], [0, -6.6]] as const) {
  const y = footLevel(x, z, false, island());
  const drawn = getTerrainInfo(x, z, 1).targetY;
  check(
    `beach at (${x}, ${z}) follows the sampled slope`,
    Math.abs(y - drawn) < 1e-9 && Math.abs(y - ISLAND_SURFACE_Y) > 1e-6,
    `foot level ${y.toFixed(4)} = sampled ${drawn.toFixed(4)}, and it is NOT the grass height`,
  );
  checkContact(`beach at (${x}, ${z}): soles meet the sand`, y, drawn);
}

/*
 * DECKS —— 「玩家站上去，腳有沒有踩在木板上」。
 *
 * A deck is ground that was placed rather than generated, and it is the one outdoor surface whose
 * height is MEASURED off a model. Standing on it must be the same statement as standing on grass.
 *
 * ## Why this check was rewritten
 *
 * It used to test ONE item (木製平台) and it registered that item`s footprint as a hand-built box
 * whose top was the model`s `maxY`. So it asserted that the feet land on `maxY` — against a
 * footprint it had just declared to have that `maxY`. It was self-consistent and empty: when
 * 小型觀景平台 shipped with railings, the feet went to the top of the RAILS, 840 mm above the
 * boards, and this file stayed green.
 *
 * The rewrite fixes both halves of that:
 *
 *  1. **Every standable item**, not one, and through the real `measureFootprint` on the real
 *     model rather than a box typed out here.
 *  2. **An independent verification.** Where the shipping code scans a coverage grid
 *     (lib/furniturePlacement.ts` measureStandTop), this fires real rays straight down inside a
 *     player-sized disc and demands they all land on the surface the player was put on. Two
 *     different methods have to agree, so the check cannot be satisfied by the bug it guards.
 */
const CONTACT_SAMPLES = 24;

/**
 * How far below the foot level a downward ray may land and still count as the same surface.
 *
 * Decks are laid as separate boards with visible seams (they must be — two coplanar faces is the
 * z-fighting the placement system exists to avoid), so a ray dropped at random inside a
 * player-sized disc sometimes falls through a seam and hits the sub-deck below. 小型觀景平台`s
 * seams show 43 mm of sub-deck. This is the same allowance `STAND_GAP_TOLERANCE` makes on the
 * other side, and it is still an order of magnitude below the failure being guarded (840 mm).
 */
const SEAM_ALLOWANCE = 0.12;

for (const item of ALL_ITEMS) {
  if (!getStandableSurface(item.id)) continue;

  const model = buildModelObject3D(item.id, ISLAND_SCALE);
  if (!model) { check(`${item.name} could be measured`, false, `${item.id} returned no model`); continue; }
  measureFootprint(item.id, model);
  const fp = getFootprint(item.id);
  if (!fp) { check(`${item.name} could be measured`, false, `${item.id} produced no footprint`); continue; }

  const placed: PlacedItem = {
    instanceId: `deck-${item.id}`,
    itemId: item.id,
    position: [0, ISLAND_SURFACE_Y, 0],
    rotation: 0,
  };
  const y = footLevel(fp.cx, fp.cz, false, island([placed]));

  // (1) the surface lookup uses the MEASURED walking surface, not the top of the model.
  const expected = ISLAND_SURFACE_Y + (fp.standY ?? fp.maxY);
  check(
    `${item.name}: feet land on the measured walking surface`,
    Math.abs(y - expected) < 1e-9,
    `foot level ${y.toFixed(4)}, walking surface ${expected.toFixed(4)}` +
      (fp.standY !== null && fp.maxY - fp.standY > 1e-6
        ? ` — ${mm(fp.maxY - fp.standY)} below the top of the model, which is where the railings are`
        : ` — this piece has nothing above its deck, so it is also the top of the model`),
  );
  checkContact(`${item.name}: soles meet the boards`, y, expected);

  // (2) INDEPENDENT: rays straight down inside a player-sized disc must all land on that surface.
  //     This is what makes the check unable to pass while the player floats.
  model.updateMatrixWorld(true);
  const ray = new THREE.Raycaster();
  const down = new THREE.Vector3(0, -1, 0);
  let worstDrop = 0;
  let misses = 0;
  const localTop = y - ISLAND_SURFACE_Y;
  for (let i = 0; i < CONTACT_SAMPLES; i++) {
    // A spiral over the disc, so the samples cover its area rather than one ring of its edge.
    const t = (i + 0.5) / CONTACT_SAMPLES;
    const r = PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS * Math.sqrt(t);
    const a = i * 2.399963; // golden angle
    ray.set(
      new THREE.Vector3(fp.cx + Math.cos(a) * r, localTop + 0.5, fp.cz + Math.sin(a) * r),
      down,
    );
    const hit = ray.intersectObject(model, true)[0];
    if (!hit) { misses++; continue; }
    worstDrop = Math.max(worstDrop, localTop - hit.point.y);
  }
  check(
    `${item.name}: there is solid deck under every part of the player`,
    misses === 0 && worstDrop <= SEAM_ALLOWANCE,
    misses > 0
      ? `${misses}/${CONTACT_SAMPLES} rays inside the player\u2019s own radius hit NOTHING — the body is over a hole`
      : `worst gap under the soles ${mm(worstDrop)} across ${CONTACT_SAMPLES} rays (allowance ${mm(SEAM_ALLOWANCE)} for board seams)`,
  );
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 3. Indoors — the branch that used to answer with the island's height
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

console.log('\n=== part 3: the interior ===');

const [livingX, livingZ] = ROOM_DEFS.living.pos;
const interiorY = footLevel(livingX, livingZ, true, null);

check(
  'the interior branch answers with the interior floor',
  Math.abs(interiorY - INTERIOR_FLOOR_Y) < 1e-9,
  `foot level ${interiorY.toFixed(4)}, floor at ${INTERIOR_FLOOR_Y}`,
);
// Stated separately and in the negative, because this is the exact regression: the number the
// interior used to return was the ISLAND's, inherited through a shared initialiser.
check(
  'the interior floor does not come from the island',
  Math.abs(interiorY - (ISLAND_SURFACE_Y + FOOT_LIFT)) > 0.1,
  `interior ${interiorY.toFixed(4)} vs island grass ${(ISLAND_SURFACE_Y + FOOT_LIFT).toFixed(4)}`,
);
// The floor plane is drawn a hair below the walkable height on purpose (z-fighting), so contact
// is measured against the plane the player can actually see.
checkContact('interior: soles meet the floor', interiorY, INTERIOR_FLOOR_Y - 0.01);

check(
  'footLevelAt agrees with the full resolve, indoors and out',
  footLevelAt(livingX, livingZ, true, 1, undefined) === interiorY
    && footLevelAt(0, 0, false, 1, []) === footLevel(0, 0, false, island()),
  'the pose code and the walk code read the same floor',
);

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 4. Sitting and lying still happen ABOVE the floor
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
//
// The floor level is an input to the seated pose: the legs reach DOWN from the seat toward it
// (lib/interactionPosture.ts's floorAngle). While it was the island's 0.35, an indoor chair whose
// cushion is 0.535 above the floor looked like it was only 0.185 below the hip, and the character
// sat with its legs swung ~70deg forward — nearly horizontal — reaching for a floor that was not
// there. The invariant that catches it needs no pose maths: a seated body's root is above the
// floor it would otherwise be standing on, never below it.
//
// WHICH PART of the body that invariant is about depends on where the legs go, and the bathe
// posture is what made the difference visible. The root origin is the GROUND CONTACT POINT — it
// means "where the soles are" only while the soles are under the body:
//
//   reachFloor / side   the legs hang down toward the floor, so the root IS the lowest point and
//                       comparing it to the floor is exactly right.
//   extendForward       the legs go straight out at hip level, so there is no body at the root
//                       at all — it sits a third of a metre under the tub, which is bookkeeping,
//                       not a character through the floorboards. The lowest thing that actually
//                       exists is the torso resting on the tub floor.
//
// So the check asks for the lowest REAL part in both cases, which is the thing the invariant was
// always a proxy for, and still fails a bath anchored below the floor it stands on.

console.log('\n=== part 4: a body on furniture is above the floor it came from ===');

for (const item of ALL_ITEMS) {
  for (const interaction of getFurnitureInteractions(item.id)) {
    // Only the postures that put the body ON a piece have a root height to check. An acting
    // posture is played standing on the floor, which is what part 1 of this audit already covers.
    const anchoring = interactionAnchoring(interaction);
    if (anchoring === 'stand') continue;
    const posture = interactionPosture(interaction);

    // Outdoor pieces sit on the island; indoor pieces sit on the interior floor. Either way the
    // piece's own base is on that floor, which is what `surfaceY` is measured from.
    const outdoor = item.category === ItemCategory.BUILDING;
    const floorY = outdoor ? ISLAND_SURFACE_Y + FOOT_LIFT : INTERIOR_FLOOR_Y + FOOT_LIFT;
    const placement: PlacedItem = {
      instanceId: `probe-${item.id}`,
      itemId: item.id,
      position: [0, floorY, 0],
      rotation: 0,
    };
    const spot = resolveInteractionSpot(placement, interaction, LEGACY_SKELETON);
    if (!spot) continue;

    const rise = poseRootHeight(anchoring, interaction.surfaceY ?? 0, LEGACY_SKELETON, interaction.give);
    // The lowest part of the body that is actually there — see the note above.
    const legsGoForward = getPosture(posture).legs === 'extendForward';
    const lowest = legsGoForward
      ? spot.y + toWorld(LEGACY_SKELETON.torso.y - LEGACY_SKELETON.torso.halfWidth)
      : spot.y;
    check(
      `${item.name} (${posture}): the body settles above the floor`,
      lowest >= floorY - 1e-9,
      `${legsGoForward ? 'torso underside' : 'root'} ${lowest.toFixed(4)}, floor ${floorY.toFixed(4)}`
        + ` — ${mm(rise)} of ${posture} rise off the piece's base`,
    );
  }
}

console.log(
  failures === 0
    ? `\nPASS — ${checks} checks, the character's soles meet every surface it stands on.\n`
    : `\n${failures} of ${checks} check(s) failed.\n`,
);
process.exit(failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);

```

## scripts/audit-ground-cover.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 地被層與地表變化場的品質下限 —— made into a check that can fail.
 *
 *   npm run audit:groundcover
 *
 * ## What this is guarding
 *
 * The lawn pass replaced 520 identical boxes with a layered, field-driven scatter, and both
 * halves of that are easy to break silently later:
 *
 *   THE BUDGET. Every layer is one InstancedMesh, so adding detail costs no draw calls and is
 *     therefore tempting without limit. The first build of this system drew 82 000 triangles —
 *     more than the entire rest of the island scene — and nothing anywhere failed. A number that
 *     only shows up in a GPU profile is a number nobody checks.
 *   THE FIELD. `lib/groundField.ts` is a noise function with a remap window tuned by measuring
 *     percentiles (see the comment there). Nudge the window and the lawn goes uniformly mid-green
 *     with no patches at all — which is the flat lawn the pass existed to remove, reintroduced by
 *     a one-character edit that looks harmless.
 *
 * So this measures the geometry the game actually builds and runs the scatter the game actually
 * runs, then asserts the things that must stay true. No renderer, no browser — everything under
 * test is in `lib/groundCoverBuild.ts` and `lib/groundField.ts`, which import neither.
 */

import * as THREE from 'three';

import { GROUND_COVER_LAYERS, type GroundCoverLayer } from '../src/constants/groundCover';
import {
  LAYER_HEIGHT,
  buildLayerGeometry,
  groundCoverSeed,
  makeGroundCoverRng,
  scatterLayer,
} from '../src/lib/groundCoverBuild';
import { sampleGroundField } from '../src/lib/groundField';
import { GRASS_RADIUS, ISLAND_TERRAIN, getIslandSurfaceY } from '../src/constants/terrain';
import { HOUSE_FOOTPRINT } from '../src/constants/houseStyles';
import type { HomeObstacle } from '../src/utils/placementRules';

const failures: string[] = [];
const fail = (m: string) => failures.push(m);
const ok = (label: string, detail: string) => console.log(`  ok   ${label}\n        ${detail}`);

/**
 * The whole ground cover's triangle ceiling, at any territory level.
 *
 * Set from the measurement that motivated it rather than from taste: the rest of the island
 * scene measured ~64 000 triangles per render with the lawn excluded (a guest island, territory
 * level 1, no placements). A lawn allowed to reach 60 000 is a lawn that can be most of the
 * frame's geometry, which is where this went wrong the first time. It currently lands near
 * 47 600 at level 1; the headroom is for a fourth layer, not for inflating the three that exist.
 */
const TRIANGLE_CEILING = 60_000;

/**
 * Draw calls the ground cover may add. One per layer, plus one more per layer that casts a
 * shadow.
 *
 * The point of the whole instancing design is that this number does not grow with detail, so it
 * is worth failing on: an accidental per-instance `<mesh>` would sail past every other check here
 * while costing a thousand draw calls.
 */
const DRAW_CALL_CEILING = 6;

/** Per-instance triangle ceilings. A plant that needs more than this is not a low-poly plant. */
const PER_INSTANCE_CEILING: Record<GroundCoverLayer['id'], number> = {
  tuft: 40,
  clump: 80,
  frond: 40,
};

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ geometry */

function trianglesOf(geometry: THREE.BufferGeometry): number {
  const index = geometry.getIndex();
  return (index ? index.count : geometry.attributes.position.count) / 3;
}

console.log('\n地被層 GEOMETRY\n');

let totalTrisL1 = 0;
let totalTrisMax = 0;
let drawCalls = 0;

const geometries = new Map<GroundCoverLayer['id'], THREE.BufferGeometry>();

for (const layer of GROUND_COVER_LAYERS) {
  const geo = buildLayerGeometry(layer.id);
  geometries.set(layer.id, geo);

  const tris = trianglesOf(geo);
  const verts = geo.attributes.position.count;

  if (!Number.isFinite(tris) || tris <= 0) {
    fail(`${layer.id}: the merged geometry is empty — mergeGeometries returned null (indexed and non-indexed parts mixed?).`);
    continue;
  }
  if (tris > PER_INSTANCE_CEILING[layer.id]) {
    fail(`${layer.id}: ${tris} triangles per instance against a ceiling of ${PER_INSTANCE_CEILING[layer.id]}.`);
  } else {
    ok(`${layer.id} costs ${tris} triangles per instance`, `${verts} vertices, ceiling ${PER_INSTANCE_CEILING[layer.id]}`);
  }

  /**
   * The geometry must sit ON its declared height, rooted at zero. The vertex shader divides by
   * `LAYER_HEIGHT` to get its 0..1 bend parameter, so a mismatch does not look like a bug — the
   * plant simply bends from the wrong place, or clips through the ground when it does.
   *
   * The floor is one-sided. A plant whose lowest vertex is ABOVE y=0 hovers, and on the slope of
   * the mound it hovers visibly. Dipping BELOW zero is expected and fine — every blade is leaned
   * about its own base, which tilts its bottom ring under the root plane, and the instance is
   * seated `GROUND_BITE` into the ground anyway. It only has to stay shallow enough that the
   * plant is not half buried.
   */
  geo.computeBoundingBox();
  const box = geo.boundingBox!;
  if (box.min.y > 0.002) {
    fail(`${layer.id}: geometry starts ${box.min.y.toFixed(4)} ABOVE its own root plane, so every instance hovers.`);
  }
  if (box.min.y < -0.08) {
    fail(`${layer.id}: geometry reaches ${box.min.y.toFixed(4)} below its root plane — that much of the plant is buried.`);
  }
  if (Math.abs(box.max.y - LAYER_HEIGHT[layer.id]) > 0.02) {
    fail(
      `${layer.id}: geometry tops out at ${box.max.y.toFixed(3)} but LAYER_HEIGHT says ${LAYER_HEIGHT[layer.id]} ` +
        `— the shader's bend parameter would be wrong by ${(box.max.y / LAYER_HEIGHT[layer.id]).toFixed(2)}x.`,
    );
  }

  totalTrisL1 += tris * Math.min(layer.maxCount, layer.baseCount);
  totalTrisMax += tris * layer.maxCount;
  drawCalls += 1 + (layer.castShadow ? 1 : 0);
}

console.log('\n預算 BUDGET\n');

if (drawCalls > DRAW_CALL_CEILING) {
  fail(`the lawn costs ${drawCalls} draw calls against a ceiling of ${DRAW_CALL_CEILING}.`);
} else {
  ok(`${drawCalls} draw calls`, `${GROUND_COVER_LAYERS.length} layers, ${GROUND_COVER_LAYERS.filter((l) => l.castShadow).length} of them casting`);
}

if (totalTrisMax > TRIANGLE_CEILING) {
  fail(
    `the lawn peaks at ${Math.round(totalTrisMax)} triangles (every layer at its cap) against a ceiling of ${TRIANGLE_CEILING}. ` +
      `Lower a maxCount, or make a plant cheaper — do NOT raise the ceiling without re-measuring the rest of the scene.`,
  );
} else {
  ok(
    `${Math.round(totalTrisL1)} triangles at territory level 1`,
    `${Math.round(totalTrisMax)} at the caps, ceiling ${TRIANGLE_CEILING}`,
  );
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the field */

console.log('\n地表變化場 FIELD\n');

/**
 * What the lushness distribution has to look like for the lawn to read as patchy.
 *
 * Percentiles rather than a mean, because a mean cannot tell a field with real bare patches and
 * real deep patches apart from a uniformly mid-green one — and those two look completely
 * different on screen. Sampled inside r 4.5, i.e. clear of the rim fade, so this measures the
 * NOISE and not the shoreline.
 */
const inner: number[] = [];
const rng = makeGroundCoverRng(4242);
for (let i = 0; i < 40_000; i++) {
  const r = Math.sqrt(rng()) * 4.5;
  const th = rng() * Math.PI * 2;
  inner.push(sampleGroundField(r * Math.cos(th), r * Math.sin(th)).lush);
}
inner.sort((a, b) => a - b);
const pct = (p: number) => inner[Math.floor(p * (inner.length - 1))];

const p05 = pct(0.05);
const p50 = pct(0.5);
const p95 = pct(0.95);

if (p05 > 0.25) fail(`the field has no bare ground: its 5th percentile is ${p05.toFixed(3)}, so nowhere on the lawn is thin.`);
if (p95 < 0.75) fail(`the field has no deep ground: its 95th percentile is ${p95.toFixed(3)}, so nowhere on the lawn is lush.`);
if (p50 < 0.3 || p50 > 0.7) fail(`the field's median lushness is ${p50.toFixed(3)} — the lawn reads as uniformly ${p50 < 0.3 ? 'thin' : 'deep'} rather than patchy.`);
if (failures.length === 0 || (p05 <= 0.25 && p95 >= 0.75 && p50 >= 0.3 && p50 <= 0.7)) {
  ok('lushness spans bare to deep', `p05 ${p05.toFixed(3)} · p50 ${p50.toFixed(3)} · p95 ${p95.toFixed(3)}`);
}

/**
 * The shoreline. Grass has to be GONE before the plateau's own edge, or the lawn ends as a drawn
 * circle against the sand — which is the seam the whole rim-fade exists to remove.
 */
let maxAtRim = 0;
for (let i = 0; i < 720; i++) {
  const th = (i / 720) * Math.PI * 2;
  const r = ISLAND_TERRAIN.plateauRadius - 0.05;
  maxAtRim = Math.max(maxAtRim, sampleGroundField(r * Math.cos(th), r * Math.sin(th)).lush);
}
if (maxAtRim > 0.02) {
  fail(`the lawn still has lushness ${maxAtRim.toFixed(3)} at the plateau's rim; it must fade to nothing before the sand.`);
} else {
  ok('the lawn fades out before the sand', `peak lushness at r ${(ISLAND_TERRAIN.plateauRadius - 0.05).toFixed(2)} is ${maxAtRim.toFixed(4)}`);
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the scatter */

console.log('\n撒點 SCATTER\n');

/** A Home parked where the placement system would accept one, to test the keep-out. */
const HOME: HomeObstacle = {
  position: [2.4, 0, -1.6],
  rotation: 0.6,
  footprint: HOUSE_FOOTPRINT,
};

for (const layer of GROUND_COVER_LAYERS) {
  for (const islandScale of [1, 1.8, 2.6]) {
    const instances = scatterLayer(layer, islandScale, HOME, makeGroundCoverRng(groundCoverSeed(layer, islandScale)));
    const wanted = Math.min(layer.maxCount, Math.round(layer.baseCount * islandScale * islandScale));

    // Everything must be on the flat walkable plateau. Anything past it is on the sloped sand,
    // where a plant seated at the plateau height floats or sinks.
    for (const inst of instances) {
      const r = Math.hypot(inst.x, inst.z);
      if (r > GRASS_RADIUS * islandScale + 1e-6) {
        fail(`${layer.id} @${islandScale}: an instance stands at r ${r.toFixed(3)}, past the plateau's ${(GRASS_RADIUS * islandScale).toFixed(3)}.`);
        break;
      }
      const surface = getIslandSurfaceY(inst.x, inst.z, islandScale);
      if (inst.y > surface + 1e-6) {
        fail(`${layer.id} @${islandScale}: an instance is seated ${(inst.y - surface).toFixed(4)} ABOVE the ground under it.`);
        break;
      }
    }

    // Nothing may stand inside the Home, where the floor would slice it.
    const solidHalfWidth = HOUSE_FOOTPRINT.halfWidth;
    const solidHalfDepth = HOUSE_FOOTPRINT.halfDepth;
    let inside = 0;
    for (const inst of instances) {
      const rx = inst.x - HOME.position[0];
      const rz = inst.z - HOME.position[2];
      const cos = Math.cos(-HOME.rotation);
      const sin = Math.sin(-HOME.rotation);
      const lx = rx * cos - rz * sin;
      const lz = rx * sin + rz * cos;
      if (Math.abs(lx) < solidHalfWidth && Math.abs(lz) < solidHalfDepth) inside++;
    }
    if (inside > 0) fail(`${layer.id} @${islandScale}: ${inside} instance(s) stand inside the Home's footprint.`);

    // The scatter is allowed to come up short — that is how a thin field thins rather than piles
    // up — but a layer that cannot fill even half its budget is misconfigured, not sparse.
    if (instances.length < wanted * 0.5) {
      fail(
        `${layer.id} @${islandScale}: only ${instances.length} of ${wanted} instances found a spot (${Math.round((instances.length / wanted) * 100)}%). ` +
          `Its lushThreshold/lushExponent/spacing exclude most of the island.`,
      );
    } else if (islandScale === 1) {
      ok(`${layer.id} places ${instances.length} / ${wanted}`, `keeps clear of the Home and stays on the plateau at scale 1, 1.8 and 2.6`);
    }
  }
}

/**
 * Determinism. The lawn is rebuilt whenever the Home moves, and a scatter that re-rolled would
 * shuffle every blade on the island the moment the player nudged their house.
 */
for (const layer of GROUND_COVER_LAYERS) {
  const a = scatterLayer(layer, 1, null, makeGroundCoverRng(groundCoverSeed(layer, 1)));
  const b = scatterLayer(layer, 1, null, makeGroundCoverRng(groundCoverSeed(layer, 1)));
  if (a.length !== b.length || a.some((inst, i) => inst.x !== b[i].x || inst.z !== b[i].z)) {
    fail(`${layer.id}: two scatters with the same seed disagree — the lawn would reshuffle on every rebuild.`);
  }
}
if (!failures.some((f) => f.includes('reshuffle'))) {
  ok('the scatter is deterministic', 'the same island always grows the same lawn');
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ verdict */

console.log('');
if (failures.length === 0) {
  console.log('PASS — the lawn is inside its budget and the field still has patches in it.\n');
  process.exit(0);
}
for (const f of failures) console.error(`  ✗ ${f}`);
console.error(`\nFAIL — ${failures.length} problem(s).\n`);
process.exit(1);

```

## scripts/audit-hair.ts

```ts
/**
 * `npm run audit:hair`
 *
 * Does every hairstyle still sit on the head?
 *
 * WHY THIS IS A STANDING CHECK. The reported bug was not one bad hairstyle - it
 * was five, because nothing in the code knew where the skull ended. A style
 * declared raw head-local offsets and the renderer drew them, so `fall.y = -0.28`
 * reaching the character's ankles was indistinguishable from a correct value.
 * src/constants/hair.ts now derives placement from HEAD_ANCHOR and clamps into
 * HAIR_ENVELOPE; this script is what makes that guarantee testable rather than
 * merely intended. Add a hairstyle with a 10-unit curtain and this fails instead
 * of the player finding it.
 *
 * HOW. It runs the real `buildHairLayout` - the same function the avatar renders
 * from - over every entry in HAIR_SPECS, bare-headed and under a hat, then
 * measures the resulting geometry. No renderer needed: the layout is arithmetic.
 *
 * Part 1 self-tests the envelope check against a deliberately broken spec, so a
 * check that had quietly stopped detecting anything cannot make part 2 pass for
 * the wrong reason.
 *
 * Part 3 walks the element tree `HairPiece` actually returns and re-measures it
 * with three.js, closing the gap between "the layout is in bounds" and "the mesh
 * that gets drawn is in bounds" - a layout mapped onto the wrong geometry argument
 * would otherwise pass part 2 and still cover the player's face.
 *
 * Exit code 1 on any failure, so it can gate a commit.
 */
import * as THREE from 'three';
import React from 'react';
import {
  HAIR_SPECS,
  HAIR_ENVELOPE,
  HEAD_ANCHOR,
  HAIR_SHELL_RADIUS,
  buildHairLayout,
  measureHairBounds,
  findFloatingPieces,
  buriedInSkull,
  coversFace,
  scalpVertex,
  SCALP_COLUMNS,
  SCALP_ROWS,
  HairSpec,
} from '../src/constants/hair';
import { HAT_BRIM, HairPiece } from '../src/components/Three/character/legacy/wardrobe';
import type { HatKind } from '../src/components/Three/character/types';

/** Avatar.tsx mounts the head group here; used only to report avatar-space heights. */
const AVATAR_HEAD_Y = 0.68;

const eps = 1e-6;

/**
 * How wide a gap still counts as two pieces touching.
 *
 * 0.004 on a head of radius 0.26 whose locks are around 0.02 thick, so under a
 * quarter of a lock's own width: close enough that the pieces really are in
 * contact, loose enough that the tangent approximations the solvers make (a ring
 * read at a lock's midpoint standing in for its whole length) do not trip it.
 */
const CONTACT_TOLERANCE = 0.004;

let failures = 0;

function fail(msg: string) {
  console.error(`  FAIL  ${msg}`);
  failures++;
}

/**
 * Every head this audit measures: bare, and then wearing each hat in turn.
 *
 * Per HAT and not just "hatted", because a hat is no longer a boolean to the hair. It
 * presses the shell onto the skull and hands back where its own brim is, and 貝雷帽's
 * brim is TILTED - so the five hats give five different bands of shell, and only one
 * of them was ever going to be the one that folds a column over itself.
 */
const HEADS: Array<[string, HatKind | null]> = [
  ['bare    ', null],
  ...(Object.keys(HAT_BRIM) as HatKind[]).map(
    kind => [`${kind}`.padEnd(8), kind] as [string, HatKind | null],
  ),
];

function check(label: string, spec: HairSpec, hat: HatKind | null): void {
  const layout = buildHairLayout(spec, { hat: hat ? HAT_BRIM[hat] : null });
  if (!layout) {
    console.log(`  ${label}  (hidden)`);
    return;
  }
  const b = measureHairBounds(layout);
  // A style that is nothing BUT a scalp (吋頭) legitimately emits no geometry at
  // all under a hat. Saying so beats printing an empty bounding box as Infinity.
  if (!Number.isFinite(b.minY)) {
    console.log(`  ${label}  (no geometry - fully covered)`);
    return;
  }
  const avatarLow = (b.minY + AVATAR_HEAD_Y).toFixed(3);
  const avatarHigh = (b.maxY + AVATAR_HEAD_Y).toFixed(3);
  console.log(
    `  ${label}  y ${b.minY.toFixed(3)}..${b.maxY.toFixed(3)} ` +
      `(avatar ${avatarLow}..${avatarHigh})  r<=${b.maxRadius.toFixed(3)}  ` +
      `face corridor floor ${Number.isFinite(b.lowestInFaceCorridor) ? b.lowestInFaceCorridor.toFixed(3) : 'clear'}`,
  );

  if (b.minY < HAIR_ENVELOPE.minY - eps) {
    fail(`${label}: hangs to ${b.minY.toFixed(3)}, below the envelope floor ${HAIR_ENVELOPE.minY} (reaches the torso)`);
  }
  if (b.maxY > HAIR_ENVELOPE.maxY + eps) {
    fail(`${label}: rises to ${b.maxY.toFixed(3)}, above the envelope ceiling ${HAIR_ENVELOPE.maxY}`);
  }
  if (b.maxRadius > HAIR_ENVELOPE.maxRadius + eps) {
    fail(`${label}: reaches radius ${b.maxRadius.toFixed(3)}, wider than ${HAIR_ENVELOPE.maxRadius}`);
  }
  if (b.lowestInFaceCorridor < HAIR_ENVELOPE.faceClearY - eps) {
    fail(
      `${label}: geometry reaches y=${b.lowestInFaceCorridor.toFixed(3)} in the corridor in front of ` +
        `the face (must stay above ${HAIR_ENVELOPE.faceClearY}) - this covers the eyes`,
    );
  }
  if (layout.scalp) checkScalpWinding(`${spec.id} ${label}`, layout.scalp);
  if (layout.scalp) {
    if (layout.scalp.radius <= HEAD_ANCHOR.radius) {
      fail(`${label}: scalp radius ${layout.scalp.radius} does not clear the head sphere ${HEAD_ANCHOR.radius} (z-fighting)`);
    }
    // The other end of the same rule. The rim is supposed to finish INSIDE the
    // skull - that is what stops the shell ending in a floating lip over the
    // temple - and a rim that stopped level with the head sphere would z-fight it
    // all the way round instead.
    if (layout.scalp.rimRadius >= HEAD_ANCHOR.radius) {
      fail(`${label}: scalp rim ${layout.scalp.rimRadius} does not tuck under the head sphere ${HEAD_ANCHOR.radius}`);
    }
  }

  // 「頭髮不要有那種莫名其妙懸浮出來的頭髮，都要有關聯」. Reach and attachment are
  // independent properties: a lock floating a centimetre off the back of the head
  // is inside every bound above and still obviously wrong. See findFloatingPieces.
  const loose = findFloatingPieces(layout, CONTACT_TOLERANCE);
  if (loose.length) {
    const worst = [...loose].sort((a, b) => b.gap - a.gap).slice(0, 4);
    fail(
      `${label}: ${loose.length} piece(s) connect to nothing - ` +
        worst
          .map(g => `${g.key} (nearest ${Number.isFinite(g.gap) ? g.gap.toFixed(3) : 'nothing'})`)
          .join(', '),
    );
  }
}

/**
 * Is the scalp shell wound the right way out, all the way round?
 *
 * A triangle whose normal points INTO the head is invisible from outside and visible
 * from inside, so a patch of them is hair that appears and disappears as the camera goes
 * round the character - 「轉動角色的時候，頭髮和頭的連接處會突然有點不見」. It is also
 * exactly the kind of thing the shell can grow by accident, because the shell is SOLVED:
 * change how the rim is fitted, or how rows are spread down a column, and two neighbouring
 * columns can end up disagreeing enough to fold the surface over on itself. The layout
 * bounds in part 2 would not notice - a folded mesh is still inside the envelope.
 *
 * Also reports how close the worst triangle comes to standing edge-on, because a face at
 * 0.03 is one rounding error from being at -0.03, and because a strip of near-edge-on
 * faces is what made DoubleSide necessary on the shell in the first place.
 */
function checkScalpWinding(label: string, part: NonNullable<ReturnType<typeof buildHairLayout>>['scalp']) {
  if (!part) return;
  const v = (i: number, j: number) => new THREE.Vector3(...scalpVertex(part, i, j));
  let flipped = 0;
  let worst = 1;
  let worstAt = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < SCALP_COLUMNS; i++) {
    for (let j = 0; j < SCALP_ROWS; j++) {
      const a = v(i, j);
      const a1 = v(i, j + 1);
      const b = v(i + 1, j);
      const b1 = v(i + 1, j + 1);
      // The two triangles wardrobe.tsx emits for this quad, in its winding order.
      for (const [p, q, r] of [[a, a1, b], [b, a1, b1]] as const) {
        const n = new THREE.Vector3().subVectors(q, p).cross(new THREE.Vector3().subVectors(r, p));
        if (n.lengthSq() < 1e-18) continue;
        const out = new THREE.Vector3().add(p).add(q).add(r).multiplyScalar(1 / 3).normalize();
        const facing = n.normalize().dot(out);
        if (facing < 0) flipped++;
        if (facing < worst) {
          worst = facing;
          worstAt = `column ${i} (yaw ${((part.yaw[i] * 180) / Math.PI).toFixed(1)}deg) row ${j}`;
        }
      }
    }
  }
  if (flipped) {
    fail(`${label}: ${flipped} scalp triangle(s) wound inside out, worst at ${worstAt} - these vanish from outside the head`);
  }
  scalpFacing.push(`  ${label}  shell winding ok, closest to edge-on ${worst.toFixed(3)} (${worstAt})`);
}

const scalpFacing: string[] = [];

console.log('PART 1 - the envelope check itself');
{
  const broken: HairSpec = {
    id: 'broken', label: 'broken', color: '#000', silhouette: 'long',
    cap: true, fall: { length: 4 }, curls: { count: 4, length: 4 },
  };
  const b = measureHairBounds(buildHairLayout(broken)!);
  if (b.minY >= HAIR_ENVELOPE.minY - eps) {
    console.log(`  ok    a 4-unit curtain is clamped to ${b.minY.toFixed(3)}, not drawn to ${(-4).toFixed(3)}`);
  } else {
    fail(`clamping is not working: a 4-unit curtain reached ${b.minY.toFixed(3)}`);
  }

  // The pre-fix geometry, reconstructed: a full-azimuth dome and a closed
  // curtain. If the measurement is sound it must flag both.
  const legacy = measureHairBounds({
    color: '#000', sway: false, fringe: [], fringeSheets: [], crest: null, locks: [], spikes: [], perm: [],
    ribbons: [],
    mass: { shellRadius: 0.28, curtain: null },
    // The full-azimuth dome, expressed as a shell whose rim is the same everywhere
    // and never tucks: exactly the surface HairPiece used to draw.
    scalp: {
      key: 'legacy', y: 0.026, radius: 0.28, rimRadius: 0.28, occiput: 0,
      yaw: Array.from({ length: SCALP_COLUMNS }, (_, i) => (2 * Math.PI * i) / SCALP_COLUMNS - Math.PI),
      rim: Array.from({ length: SCALP_COLUMNS }, () => Math.PI / 1.6),
      tuck: Array.from({ length: SCALP_COLUMNS }, () => 0),
    },
    curtain: { y: -0.28, args: [0.28, 0.31, 0.71, 32, 1, true, 0, Math.PI * 2] },
  });
  if (legacy.lowestInFaceCorridor < HAIR_ENVELOPE.faceClearY && legacy.minY < HAIR_ENVELOPE.minY) {
    console.log(
      `  ok    the old geometry is still detected as broken ` +
        `(face corridor blocked down to ${legacy.lowestInFaceCorridor.toFixed(3)}, hangs to avatar y ${(legacy.minY + AVATAR_HEAD_Y).toFixed(3)})`,
    );
  } else {
    fail('the check no longer detects the original defect - it would pass anything');
  }
}

console.log('');
console.log('PART 2 - every shipped hairstyle');
console.log(
  `  envelope: y ${HAIR_ENVELOPE.minY}..${HAIR_ENVELOPE.maxY}, r<=${HAIR_ENVELOPE.maxRadius}, ` +
    `face corridor |x|<${HAIR_ENVELOPE.faceClearHalfWidth} z>${HAIR_ENVELOPE.faceClearMinZ} clear below ` +
    `y=${HAIR_ENVELOPE.faceClearY} (hair opens +-${((HEAD_ANCHOR.faceHalfArc * 180) / Math.PI).toFixed(0)}deg at the front)`,
);
console.log(`  head r=${HEAD_ANCHOR.radius}, hair shell r=${HAIR_SHELL_RADIUS.toFixed(3)}`);
console.log('');

for (const spec of Object.values(HAIR_SPECS)) {
  console.log(`${spec.id} (${spec.label})`);
  for (const [label, hat] of HEADS) check(label, spec, hat);
}

console.log('');
console.log('PART 2b - the scalp shell faces outward everywhere');
for (const line of scalpFacing) console.log(line);
console.log('');
console.log('PART 3 - the mesh HairPiece actually returns');
{
  /** Builds the real three.js object for one JSX geometry element. */
  const GEOMETRY: Record<string, (args: unknown[]) => THREE.BufferGeometry> = {
    sphereGeometry: a => new THREE.SphereGeometry(...(a as [number])),
    cylinderGeometry: a => new THREE.CylinderGeometry(...(a as [number])),
    capsuleGeometry: a => new THREE.CapsuleGeometry(...(a as [number])),
    coneGeometry: a => new THREE.ConeGeometry(...(a as [number])),
    boxGeometry: a => new THREE.BoxGeometry(...(a as [number])),
  };

  /**
   * Walks the JSX HairPiece returned, accumulating <group>/<mesh> transforms, and
   * feeds every vertex through `visit` in head-local space. HairPiece is hook-free,
   * so it can be invoked directly with no renderer.
   */
  function walk(node: React.ReactNode, parent: THREE.Matrix4, visit: (v: THREE.Vector3) => void) {
    React.Children.forEach(node as React.ReactElement, child => {
      if (!React.isValidElement(child)) return;
      const props = child.props as Record<string, unknown>;
      const type = child.type;

      if (typeof type === 'string' && GEOMETRY[type]) {
        const geo = GEOMETRY[type](props.args as unknown[]);
        const pos = geo.getAttribute('position');
        const v = new THREE.Vector3();
        for (let i = 0; i < pos.count; i++) {
          visit(v.fromBufferAttribute(pos, i).applyMatrix4(parent));
        }
        geo.dispose();
        return;
      }

      const local = new THREE.Matrix4();
      if (typeof type === 'string' && (type === 'group' || type === 'mesh')) {
        const p = (props.position as [number, number, number]) ?? [0, 0, 0];
        const r = (props.rotation as [number, number, number]) ?? [0, 0, 0];
        // The occiput patch is the one mesh that carries a scale - see
        // HairSpec.occiput. Ignoring it here would have this walk measure a sphere
        // where the renderer draws an ellipsoid, i.e. silently stop checking it.
        const s = (props.scale as [number, number, number]) ?? [1, 1, 1];
        local.compose(
          new THREE.Vector3(...p),
          new THREE.Quaternion().setFromEuler(new THREE.Euler(...r)),
          new THREE.Vector3(...s),
        );
      }
      const world = new THREE.Matrix4().multiplyMatrices(parent, local);
      // The scalp shell is the one mesh that brings its own BufferGeometry rather
      // than a <xGeometry args={...}> child - see wardrobe.tsx `scalpGeometry`. It
      // still has to be measured, and measuring the built buffer (rather than the
      // layout it came from) is the entire point of this part.
      if (props.geometry instanceof THREE.BufferGeometry) {
        const pos = props.geometry.getAttribute('position');
        const v = new THREE.Vector3();
        for (let i = 0; i < pos.count; i++) {
          visit(v.fromBufferAttribute(pos, i).applyMatrix4(world));
        }
      }
      if (typeof type === 'function') {
        walk((type as (p: unknown) => React.ReactNode)(props), world, visit);
      } else {
        walk(props.children as React.ReactNode, world, visit);
      }
    });
  }

  for (const spec of Object.values(HAIR_SPECS)) {
    for (const [head, hat] of HEADS) {
      const label = `${spec.id} ${head}`;
      const swayRef: React.RefObject<THREE.Group | null> = { current: null };
      const tree = HairPiece({ spec, hat, swayRef });
      const layout = buildHairLayout(spec, { hat: hat ? HAT_BRIM[hat] : null });
      if (!tree || !layout) {
        if (layout) fail(`${label}: HairPiece drew nothing for a style that has a layout`);
        continue;
      }

      if (!layout.scalp && !layout.fringe.length && !layout.fringeSheets.length && !layout.locks.length &&
          !layout.spikes.length && !layout.perm.length && !layout.crest && !layout.curtain) {
        console.log(`  ${label}  (no geometry - fully covered)`);
        continue;
      }

      let minY = Infinity, maxY = -Infinity, maxRadius = 0, lowFace = Infinity;
      walk(
        React.createElement(React.Fragment, null, tree),
        new THREE.Matrix4(),
        v => {
          minY = Math.min(minY, v.y);
          maxY = Math.max(maxY, v.y);
          maxRadius = Math.max(maxRadius, Math.hypot(v.x, v.z));
          // Same exemption measureHairBounds makes, and for the same reason: the
          // scalp shell finishes its rim INSIDE the skull on purpose, and hair the
          // head sphere stands in front of is not hair in front of a face.
          if (!buriedInSkull([v.x, v.y, v.z]) && coversFace([v.x, v.y, v.z])) {
            lowFace = Math.min(lowFace, v.y);
          }
        },
      );

      // Tessellation tolerance: a sampled hull sits marginally inside the true
      // surface, so the drawn mesh may read a hair smaller than the analytic bound.
      const tol = 0.01;
      const predicted = measureHairBounds(layout);
      const drifted: string[] = [];
      if (minY < predicted.minY - tol) drifted.push(`minY drawn ${minY.toFixed(3)} vs predicted ${predicted.minY.toFixed(3)}`);
      if (maxY > predicted.maxY + tol) drifted.push(`maxY drawn ${maxY.toFixed(3)} vs predicted ${predicted.maxY.toFixed(3)}`);
      if (maxRadius > predicted.maxRadius + tol) drifted.push(`radius drawn ${maxRadius.toFixed(3)} vs predicted ${predicted.maxRadius.toFixed(3)}`);
      if (drifted.length) fail(`${label}: drawn mesh does not match the layout - ${drifted.join('; ')}`);

      if (minY < HAIR_ENVELOPE.minY - tol) fail(`${label}: drawn mesh hangs to ${minY.toFixed(3)}, past the envelope floor`);
      if (maxRadius > HAIR_ENVELOPE.maxRadius + tol) fail(`${label}: drawn mesh reaches radius ${maxRadius.toFixed(3)}`);
      if (lowFace < HAIR_ENVELOPE.faceClearY - tol) {
        fail(`${label}: drawn mesh reaches y=${lowFace.toFixed(3)} in front of the face - this covers the eyes`);
      }

      console.log(
        `  ${label}  drawn y ${minY.toFixed(3)}..${maxY.toFixed(3)}  r<=${maxRadius.toFixed(3)}  ` +
          `face corridor floor ${Number.isFinite(lowFace) ? lowFace.toFixed(3) : 'clear'}`,
      );
    }
  }
}

console.log('');
if (failures > 0) {
  console.error(`${failures} failure(s).`);
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log('All hairstyles sit within the head attachment envelope.');
```

## scripts/audit-hud-scale.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * Guards the one duplication the responsive HUD size system cannot avoid.
 *
 * The four device tiers live in TWO places by necessity: as media queries in
 * `src/index.css` (which sizes the chrome) and as numbers in
 * `src/hooks/useHudTier.ts` (which picks the LAYOUT and the fold's default).
 * Nothing in the language ties them together, and the failure mode when they
 * drift is silent and awful: the card would switch to its compact ARRANGEMENT
 * at one width while its PADDING, avatar and type switched at another, so a
 * band of widths renders a one-line card with desktop-sized parts in it —
 * which is exactly the "sized for one screen, forced onto another" problem the
 * system exists to end.
 *
 * So: parse both files and assert they agree.
 *
 *   1. every tier's min-width in useHudTier.ts has a matching `@media
 *      (min-width: Npx)` block in index.css,
 *   2. the `tablet:` / `laptop:` / `desktop:` Tailwind variants are declared at
 *      those same widths (a variant is how other components will spend this
 *      scale — one declared at the wrong px is a trap for every future user),
 *   3. the `short:` height variant matches HUD_SHORT_MAX_HEIGHT,
 *   4. every --hud-* token introduced at the base tier still exists (a rename
 *      that misses one leaves `var(--hud-gone)` resolving to nothing, which
 *      renders as a zero-width, zero-padding card rather than as an error).
 *
 * Run: `npm run audit:hud-scale`
 */

import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { HUD_TIER_MIN_WIDTH, HUD_SHORT_MAX_HEIGHT, type HudTier } from '../src/hooks/useHudTier';

const css = readFileSync('src/index.css', 'utf8');
const failures: string[] = [];

// --- 1. tier min-widths present as media queries ---------------------------
const mediaWidths = new Set(
  [...css.matchAll(/@media\s*\(min-width:\s*(\d+)px\)/g)].map((m) => Number(m[1])),
);
for (const [tier, min] of Object.entries(HUD_TIER_MIN_WIDTH) as [HudTier, number][]) {
  if (min === 0) continue; // `mobile` is the base tier — it has no query.
  if (!mediaWidths.has(min)) {
    failures.push(
      `tier "${tier}" starts at ${min}px in useHudTier.ts, but index.css has no ` +
        `@media (min-width: ${min}px). Widths in the CSS: ${[...mediaWidths].sort((a, b) => a - b).join(', ')}`,
    );
  }
}

// --- 2. the Tailwind tier variants agree with the same table ---------------
for (const tier of ['tablet', 'laptop', 'desktop'] as const) {
  const declared = css.match(
    new RegExp(`@custom-variant\\s+${tier}\\s*\\(@media\\s*\\(width\\s*>=\\s*(\\d+)px\\)\\)`),
  );
  if (!declared) {
    failures.push(`no \`@custom-variant ${tier}\` declared in index.css`);
  } else if (Number(declared[1]) !== HUD_TIER_MIN_WIDTH[tier]) {
    failures.push(
      `\`${tier}:\` is declared at ${declared[1]}px in index.css but the tier starts ` +
        `at ${HUD_TIER_MIN_WIDTH[tier]}px in useHudTier.ts`,
    );
  }
}

// --- 3. the height variant ------------------------------------------------
const short = css.match(/@custom-variant\s+short\s*\(@media\s*\(height\s*<=\s*(\d+)px\)\)/);
if (!short) {
  failures.push('no `@custom-variant short` declared in index.css');
} else if (Number(short[1]) !== HUD_SHORT_MAX_HEIGHT) {
  failures.push(
    `\`short:\` is <=${short[1]}px in index.css but HUD_SHORT_MAX_HEIGHT is ${HUD_SHORT_MAX_HEIGHT}`,
  );
}

// --- 4. no token is referenced after being renamed away --------------------
// Base-tier declarations are the authority: a token must be declared there (so
// it always resolves) and, if any component spends it, it must still exist.
const declaredTokens = new Set([...css.matchAll(/^\s*(--hud-[a-z-]+):/gm)].map((m) => m[1]));
const usedTokens = new Set<string>();
for (const file of ['src/index.css', 'src/components/UI/TopBar.tsx', 'src/components/UI/HudFrame.tsx']) {
  for (const m of readFileSync(file, 'utf8').matchAll(/var\((--hud-[a-z-]+)/g)) usedTokens.add(m[1]);
}
for (const token of usedTokens) {
  // --hud-gutter is declared inside `.hud-scroll-gutter`, not at :root.
  if (token === '--hud-gutter') continue;
  if (!declaredTokens.has(token)) failures.push(`${token} is used but never declared in index.css`);
}

if (failures.length) {
  console.error('audit:hud-scale FAILED\n');
  for (const f of failures) console.error(`  • ${f}`);
  console.error(
    '\nThe device tiers are documented in the "RESPONSIVE HUD SIZE SYSTEM" block of\n' +
      'src/index.css and mirrored in src/hooks/useHudTier.ts. Change both together.',
  );
  process.exit(1);
}

console.log(
  `audit:hud-scale OK — ${Object.keys(HUD_TIER_MIN_WIDTH).length} tiers ` +
    `(${Object.entries(HUD_TIER_MIN_WIDTH).map(([t, w]) => `${t}>=${w}`).join(', ')}), ` +
    `short<=${HUD_SHORT_MAX_HEIGHT}px, ${usedTokens.size} --hud-* tokens in use, all declared.`,
);

```

## scripts/audit-interior-shell.ts

```ts
/**
 * `npm run audit:interior`
 *
 * Do the interior room shell's collision rules still agree with the geometry
 * that is actually drawn?
 *
 * WHY THIS IS A STANDING CHECK. The shell used to be described in four
 * independent places — the meshes in BuildingInteriorView, the walkable
 * rectangles in characterMovement, and two separate wall descriptions in
 * CameraController — each re-deriving it from ROOM_HALF_SIZE plus its own
 * literals. They drifted, and the drift was invisible: every rule was written
 * against the wall's CENTRE LINE while the wall is 0.35 thick with a baseboard
 * standing 0.22 proud of it, so the player's body sat 0.22 inside the wall and
 * the camera could be pushed clean through it. Nothing failed loudly; it just
 * looked wrong.
 *
 * They now all read constants/interiorShell.ts, and this asserts the two
 * properties that made the single source of truth worth having:
 *
 *   1. The constants still reproduce the meshes exactly. If someone retunes a
 *      wall's thickness or moves the ceiling beams, the meshes change and the
 *      collision follows — but only as long as the meshes are still derived
 *      from these numbers, which is what part 1 pins down.
 *
 *   2. The margins each system reserves are at least the margins it is allowed
 *      to spend. This is the invariant that was actually violated:
 *      applyObservationFloor may render up to CAMERA_COLLIDER_RADIUS past the
 *      collision limit, on the understanding that the limit reserved that much
 *      clearance to a real surface. Reserve less than you spend and the camera
 *      ends up outside the house.
 *
 * Pure arithmetic over the exported constants — no renderer, no browser.
 */

import {
  BASEBOARD_THICKNESS,
  CEILING_BEAM_HEIGHT,
  CROWN_HEIGHT,
  CROWN_TOP_Y,
  DOORWAY_CLEAR_HEIGHT,
  DOORWAY_HALF_WIDTH,
  DOORWAY_PANEL_THICKNESS,
  INTERIOR_CEILING_Y,
  INTERIOR_FLOOR_Y,
  ROOM_INNER_HALF_SIZE,
  WALL_BASEBOARD_INSET,
  WALL_CROWN_INSET,
  WALL_SURFACE_INSET,
  WALL_THICKNESS,
  buildWalkableRects,
  buildWallSegments,
} from '../src/constants/interiorShell';
import { ROOM_GRID_SIZE, ROOM_HALF_SIZE } from '../src/constants/rooms';
import * as THREE from 'three';
import {
  CAMERA_COLLIDER_RADIUS,
  MIN_OBSERVATION_DISTANCE,
  FURNITURE_CAMERA_CLEARANCE,
  buildFurnitureContainmentBoxes,
  solveBoxContainmentLimit,
  type CameraContainmentBox,
} from '../src/lib/cameraCollision';
import { PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS } from '../src/utils/placementRules';
import { LEGACY_SKELETON, bodyClearanceRadius } from '../src/constants/characterRig';

/** clampFrameDelta's ceiling and the interior canvas' near plane, mirrored for the checks below. */
const MAX_FRAME_DELTA = 0.1;
const INTERIOR_NEAR_PLANE = 0.3;
const MIN_CAMERA_DISTANCE = 0.35;
/** Avatar.tsx's walk speed, before the (post-step) animation modifier. */
const PLAYER_SPEED = 3.8 * 1.2 * 1.2;

const EPS = 1e-9;
let failures = 0;

function check(name: string, ok: boolean, detail: string) {
  if (!ok) failures++;
  console.log(`${ok ? '  ok  ' : ' FAIL '} ${name}`);
  console.log(`        ${detail}`);
}

const near = (a: number, b: number) => Math.abs(a - b) < 1e-6;

console.log('\n1. Constants still reproduce the drawn geometry');
check(
  'solid wall panel + baseboard',
  near(WALL_THICKNESS, 0.35) && near(WALL_BASEBOARD_INSET - BASEBOARD_THICKNESS / 2, 0.18),
  `panel ${WALL_THICKNESS} thick, baseboard centred ${WALL_BASEBOARD_INSET - BASEBOARD_THICKNESS / 2} in`
);
check(
  'doorway panels, opening and header',
  near(DOORWAY_PANEL_THICKNESS, 0.2) &&
    near((ROOM_GRID_SIZE - DOORWAY_HALF_WIDTH * 2) / 2 + 0.2, 4.7) &&
    near(DOORWAY_CLEAR_HEIGHT + (5 - DOORWAY_CLEAR_HEIGHT) / 2, 4.4),
  `opening ${DOORWAY_HALF_WIDTH * 2} wide, clear to ${DOORWAY_CLEAR_HEIGHT}, header centred 4.4`
);
check(
  'ceiling beams hang where the ceiling limit says',
  near(INTERIOR_CEILING_Y + CEILING_BEAM_HEIGHT / 2, 4.86),
  `beam centre ${INTERIOR_CEILING_Y + CEILING_BEAM_HEIGHT / 2}, underside ${INTERIOR_CEILING_Y}`
);
check(
  'crown moulding sits under the beams and clear of every doorway',
  // Its top must not reach into the beams (which would z-fight along the whole top edge of
  // every wall), and its underside must stay above the doorway's clear height, because the
  // moulding runs unbroken across a doorway wall's header rather than stopping either side of
  // the opening. Both are what let it be one band per wall instead of one band per panel.
  CROWN_TOP_Y <= INTERIOR_CEILING_Y + EPS && CROWN_TOP_Y - CROWN_HEIGHT > DOORWAY_CLEAR_HEIGHT,
  `crown ${CROWN_TOP_Y - CROWN_HEIGHT}..${CROWN_TOP_Y}, beams from ${INTERIOR_CEILING_Y}, doorway clear to ${DOORWAY_CLEAR_HEIGHT}`
);
check(
  'wall surface is the deepest thing on the wall',
  WALL_SURFACE_INSET ===
    Math.max(WALL_THICKNESS / 2, DOORWAY_PANEL_THICKNESS / 2, WALL_BASEBOARD_INSET, WALL_CROWN_INSET),
  `inset ${WALL_SURFACE_INSET} -> inner face at ${ROOM_INNER_HALF_SIZE} (centre line ${ROOM_HALF_SIZE})`
);

console.log('\n2. Player is contained by the wall SURFACE, not its centre line');
const rooms = [
  { cx: 0, cz: 0 },
  { cx: ROOM_GRID_SIZE, cz: 0 },
  { cx: 0, cz: ROOM_GRID_SIZE },
];
/**
 * The radius the PLAYER is actually walled off at, which is not the general collision radius.
 * The character is widest at the skull, and a wall is the only obstacle tall enough for the
 * difference to be visible — see characterRig.ts's bodyClearanceRadius. Everything below is
 * therefore checked against the widest part of the body, not against the torso-sized collider.
 */
const WALL_CLEARANCE = bodyClearanceRadius(LEGACY_SKELETON);
const rects = buildWalkableRects(rooms, WALL_CLEARANCE);
const room = rects[0];
check(
  'the WIDEST part of the body never crosses the wall surface',
  room.maxX + WALL_CLEARANCE <= ROOM_INNER_HALF_SIZE + EPS,
  `centre capped at ${room.maxX.toFixed(3)}, head reaches ${(room.maxX + WALL_CLEARANCE).toFixed(3)}, surface at ${ROOM_INNER_HALF_SIZE}`
);
check(
  'and the head is what that clearance is measuring',
  WALL_CLEARANCE > PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS + EPS,
  `wall clearance ${WALL_CLEARANCE.toFixed(3)} against the body collider's ${PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS}`
);

const inside = (x: number, z: number) =>
  rects.some((r) => x >= r.minX && x <= r.maxX && z >= r.minZ && z <= r.maxZ);
let northGap: number | null = null;
let eastGap: number | null = null;
for (let t = 0; t <= ROOM_GRID_SIZE; t += 0.01) {
  if (northGap === null && !inside(0, t)) northGap = t;
  if (eastGap === null && !inside(t, 0)) eastGap = t;
}
check(
  'walkable union stays connected through both doorways',
  northGap === null && eastGap === null,
  northGap === null && eastGap === null
    ? 'no gap walking north or east into the adjoining room'
    : `gap north at ${northGap}, east at ${eastGap}`
);

const step = PLAYER_SPEED * MAX_FRAME_DELTA;
const solidGap = ROOM_GRID_SIZE - ROOM_INNER_HALF_SIZE + WALL_CLEARANCE - room.maxX;
check(
  'one frame cannot tunnel through a wall into the next room',
  step < solidGap,
  `max step ${step.toFixed(3)} < solid separation ${solidGap.toFixed(3)}`
);

console.log('\n3. Camera reserves at least the margin it is allowed to spend');
const segs = buildWallSegments(rooms);
check(
  'wall segments sit on the inner face',
  segs.some((s) => near(s.z1, ROOM_INNER_HALF_SIZE) && near(s.z2, ROOM_INNER_HALF_SIZE)),
  `north face at ${ROOM_INNER_HALF_SIZE} (was ${ROOM_HALF_SIZE}, i.e. inside the wall)`
);

// Worst case: the player hugging a wall with the camera aimed straight into it. Anywhere
// further out and MIN_OBSERVATION_DISTANCE never binds, so this is the only case worth testing.
const pivot = room.maxZ;
const tSurface = ROOM_INNER_HALF_SIZE - pivot;
const collision = tSurface - CAMERA_COLLIDER_RADIUS; // deliberately NOT floored - see CameraController
const solved = Math.max(0, Math.min(11, collision));
let rendered = Math.max(solved, Math.min(11, MIN_OBSERVATION_DISTANCE, collision + CAMERA_COLLIDER_RADIUS));
rendered = Math.max(rendered, Math.min(11, MIN_CAMERA_DISTANCE));
const cameraWorld = pivot + rendered;
check(
  'camera never renders past the wall surface',
  cameraWorld <= ROOM_INNER_HALF_SIZE + EPS,
  `camera at ${cameraWorld.toFixed(3)}, surface at ${ROOM_INNER_HALF_SIZE}`
);
check(
  'near plane never clips the whole wall panel away',
  cameraWorld + INTERIOR_NEAR_PLANE < ROOM_HALF_SIZE + WALL_THICKNESS / 2 - EPS,
  `near plane ${(cameraWorld + INTERIOR_NEAR_PLANE).toFixed(3)} < panel far face ${(ROOM_HALF_SIZE + WALL_THICKNESS / 2).toFixed(3)}`
);
check(
  'MIN_CAMERA_DISTANCE cannot reach past a surface',
  MIN_CAMERA_DISTANCE <= PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS + EPS,
  `floor ${MIN_CAMERA_DISTANCE} <= the ${PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS} the walk rects keep the pivot clear by`
);
check(
  'ceiling limit + full overrun stays under the beams',
  INTERIOR_CEILING_Y - CAMERA_COLLIDER_RADIUS + CAMERA_COLLIDER_RADIUS <= INTERIOR_CEILING_Y + EPS,
  `limit y ${INTERIOR_CEILING_Y - CAMERA_COLLIDER_RADIUS}, beams at ${INTERIOR_CEILING_Y}`
);
check(
  'floor limit - full overrun stays above the floor',
  INTERIOR_FLOOR_Y + CAMERA_COLLIDER_RADIUS - CAMERA_COLLIDER_RADIUS >= INTERIOR_FLOOR_Y - EPS,
  `limit y ${INTERIOR_FLOOR_Y + CAMERA_COLLIDER_RADIUS}, floor at ${INTERIOR_FLOOR_Y}`
);


// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
console.log("\n4. Furniture is a volume the camera stays out of, not an obstacle it backs away from");
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
//
// The two halves of that sentence are what this section holds apart. A piece the arm merely passes
// OVER must cost nothing — that is the property whose loss put the camera on the player's head the
// last time furniture was made camera-relevant — while a piece the camera would come to REST in
// has to push it out. Both are answered by solveBoxContainmentLimit; these are the cases.

const wardrobe: CameraContainmentBox = {
  x: 0, z: 3, rotation: 0, halfWidth: 0.6, halfDepth: 0.35, baseY: 0, topY: 2.2,
};
const rug: CameraContainmentBox = {
  x: 0, z: 3, rotation: 0, halfWidth: 1.2, halfDepth: 0.9, baseY: 0, topY: 0.02,
};

const dirTo = (dx: number, dy: number, dz: number) => new THREE.Vector3(dx, dy, dz).normalize();

// The camera arm ending INSIDE the wardrobe: pivot at head height in front of it, aimed at it,
// and short enough to stop in the middle of the piece.
{
  const pivot = new THREE.Vector3(0, 1.8, 0);
  const dir = dirTo(0, -0.2, 1);
  const armIntoIt = 3.2;
  const limit = solveBoxContainmentLimit(pivot, dir, armIntoIt, wardrobe, FURNITURE_CAMERA_CLEARANCE);
  const resting = pivot.clone().addScaledVector(dir, limit);
  const face = wardrobe.z - wardrobe.halfDepth;
  check(
    'an arm that would end inside a wardrobe is shortened to stand outside it',
    limit < armIntoIt - EPS && face - resting.z >= FURNITURE_CAMERA_CLEARANCE - EPS,
    `arm ${armIntoIt} -> ${limit.toFixed(3)}, camera z ${resting.z.toFixed(3)}, box face ${face.toFixed(3)}`
  );
  check(
    'the near plane then clears the wardrobe rather than cutting into it',
    face - resting.z >= INTERIOR_NEAR_PLANE - EPS,
    `standoff ${(face - resting.z).toFixed(3)} >= near plane ${INTERIOR_NEAR_PLANE}`
  );
}

// The same wardrobe, GRAZED: a longer arm that passes through it and lands beyond the far side.
{
  const pivot = new THREE.Vector3(0, 1.8, 0);
  const dir = dirTo(0, -0.2, 1);
  const armPastIt = 8;
  check(
    'an arm that passes clean through and lands beyond it is left alone',
    solveBoxContainmentLimit(pivot, dir, armPastIt, wardrobe, FURNITURE_CAMERA_CLEARANCE) === armPastIt,
    'a graze costs nothing, which is what keeps a furnished room from moving the camera on its own'
  );
}

// A rug never reaches the camera at all — and never gets a box in the first place, since
// buildFurnitureContainmentBoxes drops anything under its minimum height.
{
  const pivot = new THREE.Vector3(0, 1.8, 0);
  const dir = dirTo(0, -0.75, 1);
  const arm = 2.4;
  check(
    'a flat piece cannot shorten the arm even if one were built for it',
    solveBoxContainmentLimit(pivot, dir, arm, rug, FURNITURE_CAMERA_CLEARANCE) === arm,
    `camera floor y ${(INTERIOR_FLOOR_Y + CAMERA_COLLIDER_RADIUS).toFixed(2)} clears the rug's inflated top ${(rug.topY + FURNITURE_CAMERA_CLEARANCE).toFixed(2)}`
  );
  check(
    'and a flat piece is never given a box at all',
    buildFurnitureContainmentBoxes(
      [{ itemId: 'rug', position: [0, 0, 3], rotation: 0 }],
      () => ({ cx: 0, cz: 0, halfW: 1.2, halfD: 0.9, minY: 0, maxY: 0.02 }),
    ).length === 0,
    'under the minimum height, so it is dropped before it can matter'
  );
}

// A rotated piece's box turns with it: a wall shelf's footprint centre hangs off to one side, and
// that side has to follow the placement rather than staying in world space.
{
  const [box] = buildFurnitureContainmentBoxes(
    [{ itemId: 'shelf', position: [5, 1, -2], rotation: Math.PI / 2 }],
    () => ({ cx: 0.4, cz: 0, halfW: 0.5, halfD: 0.2, minY: -0.3, maxY: 0.4 }),
  );
  check(
    'a rotated placement carries its off-centre footprint round with it',
    !!box && Math.abs(box.x - 5) < 1e-6 && Math.abs(box.z - (-2 - 0.4)) < 1e-6,
    box ? `centre (${box.x.toFixed(2)}, ${box.z.toFixed(2)}) for a +0.4 local x at 90 degrees` : 'no box built'
  );
}

console.log(
  failures === 0
    ? '\nInterior shell OK — geometry and collision agree.\n'
    : `\n${failures} check(s) failed.\n`
);
process.exit(failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);

```
