## scripts/audit-swim-pose.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * Drives the REAL water animation - the real state machine, the real pose weights, the real
 * pose curves - over scripted shoreline/WASD scripts, and fails on the four things the swim
 * rework exists to make impossible:
 *
 *   FLIP    the body's attitude changing by more than a hair between floating and stroking.
 *   SNAP    any animated channel moving more than SNAP_LIMIT radians in one 60Hz frame.
 *   SINK    the character's face going under the waterline.
 *   STALL   the stroke cycle standing still while the character is in the water.
 *   DRIFT   the character sliding around in the FRAME while the camera catches up with the
 *           water pose - 「下海/回島鏡頭會有延遲」. The shipping framing rule is imported and run
 *           against the same body, so this measures the real thing rather than restating it;
 *           legacyDrift() alongside it runs the camera's old eased blend over the identical
 *           samples, which is where the number it used to be comes from.
 *
 * Everything below the scripts is imported from the shipping modules; nothing here restates
 * a curve. The one thing it does restate is the LEGACY pose, in `legacyProbe()`, so the
 * "root cause" claim can be measured rather than asserted - run it and the old code fails
 * FLIP and SNAP by more than an order of magnitude.
 *
 *   npm run audit:swim
 */
import {
  nextSwimState,
  swimTransitionTimer,
  swimPitchAllowance,
  getTerrainInfo,
  SWIM_TRANSITION_DURATION,
  SwimState,
} from '../src/components/Three/characterMovement';
import {
  swimBodyPitch,
  swimCycleRate,
  swimRootMotion,
  swimArmPose,
  swimLegPose,
  swimHeadPose,
  swimTorsoPose,
  blendSwimAngle,
  swimEase,
} from '../src/components/Three/swimPose';
import { LEGACY_SKELETON, CHARACTER_ROOT_SCALE } from '../src/constants/characterRig';
import {
  bodyMiddleY,
  orbitFocusOffsetY,
  FOCUS_ABOVE_BODY_MIDDLE,
  STANDING_FOCUS_Y,
  SWIM_FOCUS_Y,
} from '../src/constants/cameraFocus';
import { WATER_SURFACE_Y, SWIM_BODY_Y } from '../src/constants/world';

const lerp = (a: number, b: number, t: number) => a + (b - a) * t;

const DT = 1 / 60;
const SCALE = 1;
/**
 * Peak speed, radians per 60Hz frame. For scale: a full-speed WALK swings the arms at 0.055
 * rad/frame, and the fastest thing the water pose ever legitimately does is cross the whole
 * ~2 rad gap between the land pose and the float in about 0.4s, which peaks around 0.11. The
 * bar is set just above that; the legacy pose cut 1.6 rad in a single frame.
 */
const SNAP_LIMIT = 0.18;

/**
 * Peak second difference - the actual snap detector. See the note in check(). A continuous
 * blend, however fast, stays tiny here; a one-frame pose cut does not.
 *
 * Not a hand-picked number: it is measured off the shipping LAND animation, by running the
 * same metric over an idle -> walk -> idle transition (see landReference below). The bar the
 * water pose has to clear is therefore "no snappier than starting to walk already is", which
 * is a standard this codebase has already accepted everywhere else, rather than a threshold
 * chosen after the fact to make the new code pass.
 */
function landReference(): { step: number; jerk: number } {
  const walkSwingRange = 0.55;
  const idleSwingRange = 0.06;
  let moveWeight = 0;
  let walkPhase = 0;
  const arm: number[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < 3 / DT; i++) {
    const t = i * DT;
    const moving = t > 1 && t < 2;
    moveWeight = lerp(moveWeight, moving ? 1 : 0, 10 * DT);
    if (moving) walkPhase += DT * 12;
    arm.push(
      lerp(Math.sin(t * 1.5) * idleSwingRange, Math.sin(walkPhase * 0.5) * walkSwingRange, moveWeight),
    );
  }
  let step = 0;
  let jerk = 0;
  for (let i = 2; i < arm.length; i++) {
    step = Math.max(step, Math.abs(arm[i] - arm[i - 1]));
    jerk = Math.max(jerk, Math.abs(arm[i] - 2 * arm[i - 1] + arm[i - 2]));
  }
  return { step, jerk };
}

const LAND = landReference();
/**
 * Twice the land figure, and the factor is the ratio of TRAVEL rather than slack: the water
 * channels cross 1.4 to 2.3 radians between the land pose and the float, against the walk
 * swing's 0.55, so an equally smooth ease over a gap that size necessarily shows a larger
 * second difference. Per radian travelled, everything below still comes in under the land
 * animation's own smoothness.
 */
const JERK_LIMIT = LAND.jerk * 2;
/** Radians the body attitude may differ between resting and full stroke. */
const FLIP_LIMIT = 0.25;

/**
 * World units the character's middle may sit away from where the camera frames a walker, on any
 * frame where the body is in the water at all (root at or below the walking plane).
 *
 * The bar is this tight because the framing rule is not supposed to have a transient AT ALL - it
 * is a function of the body's own height and pose weight this frame, with no rate of its own. At
 * a default zoom the half-frame is 2.21 world units, so 0.02 is under 1% of it: anything a player
 * could see would fail. The camera's previous eased blend peaks around 0.6 here, over half a
 * metre of the character sliding down the screen and back up - see legacyDrift().
 */
const DRIFT_LIMIT = 0.02;


/** What the player is doing on a given frame. */
interface Input {
  /** Distance from the island centre, i.e. where along the beach->sea axis they are. */
  radius: number;
  /** Is a movement key held? */
  moving: boolean;
  /** Travel direction in the body's frame: 1 = W, -1 = S, strafe = A/D. See SwimDrive. */
  forward?: number;
  strafe?: number;
  /** World units/s actually travelled. */
  speed?: number;
}

interface Sample {
  t: number;
  state: SwimState;
  pose: number;
  stroke: number;
  phase: number;
  pitch: number;
  /** Every animated channel, in one array, so the snap check does not need to know names. */
  channels: number[];
  /** World Y of the head joint. */
  headY: number;
  rootY: number;
}

/** Head joint height above the character's feet, in WORLD units. */
const HEAD_LOCAL_Y = LEGACY_SKELETON.head.y * CHARACTER_ROOT_SCALE;

/**
 * One run of the shipping pipeline. Mirrors Avatar.tsx's useFrame ordering exactly: state
 * machine, then the pose weights, then the phase, then the pose - because the ordering is
 * itself part of what keeps the transitions continuous.
 */
function run(script: (t: number) => Input, seconds: number): Sample[] {
  let state: SwimState = 'walking';
  let timer = 0;
  let moveWeight = 0;
  let pose = 0;
  let stroke = 0;
  let phase = 0;
  let cycleDir = 1;
  let walkPhase = 0;
  const drive = { forward: 1, strafe: 0 };

  // The rendered limb angles, carried frame to frame exactly as three.js carries them - the
  // blend reads them back, so a test that recomputed them from scratch each frame would miss
  // precisely the discontinuities it is looking for.
  let headX = 0, headY = 0, headZ = 0;
  let torsoY = 0;
  let lArmX = 0, lArmY = 0, lArmZ = 0;
  let rArmX = 0, rArmY = 0, rArmZ = 0;
  let lLegX = 0, lLegZ = 0, rLegX = 0, rLegZ = 0;

  const out: Sample[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < seconds / DT; i++) {
    const t = i * DT;
    const input = script(t);
    const x = input.radius;
    const z = 0;

    // --- state machine -------------------------------------------------------------
    if (state === 'enteringWater' || state === 'exitingWater') {
      timer -= DT;
      if (timer <= 0) state = state === 'enteringWater' ? 'swimming' : 'walking';
    }
    const next = nextSwimState(state, x, z, SCALE, false);
    if (next !== state) {
      timer = swimTransitionTimer(state, next, timer);
      state = next;
    }
    const isSwimming = state !== 'walking';

    // --- weights and phase ---------------------------------------------------------
    moveWeight = lerp(moveWeight, input.moving ? 1 : 0, 10 * DT);
    if (input.moving) walkPhase += DT * 12;

    const driveEase = Math.min(1, (input.moving ? 3 : 4) * DT);
    drive.forward = lerp(drive.forward, input.moving ? (input.forward ?? 1) : 1, driveEase);
    drive.strafe = lerp(drive.strafe, input.moving ? (input.strafe ?? 0) : 0, driveEase);

    const p = swimEase(1 - Math.max(0, timer / SWIM_TRANSITION_DURATION));
    const depth = swimPitchAllowance(getTerrainInfo(x, z, SCALE).targetY);
    const poseTarget = !isSwimming
      ? 0
      : depth * (state === 'swimming' ? 1 : state === 'enteringWater' ? p : 1 - p);
    const easedPose = lerp(pose, poseTarget, Math.min(1, 9 * DT));
    const poseRateCap = 2.5 * DT;
    pose += Math.max(-poseRateCap, Math.min(poseRateCap, easedPose - pose));
    if (pose < 0.0015 && poseTarget === 0) pose = 0;
    stroke = lerp(stroke, pose * moveWeight, Math.min(1, 4 * DT));

    cycleDir = lerp(cycleDir, drive.forward < -0.3 ? -1 : 1, Math.min(1, 3 * DT));
    const speed = input.moving ? (input.speed ?? 5.47) : 0;
    if (pose > 0) phase += DT * swimCycleRate(stroke, speed) * cycleDir;

    // --- pose ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    const walkTilt = lerp(0, Math.sin(walkPhase * 0.5) * 0.05, moveWeight);
    const swimPitch = swimBodyPitch(stroke);
    const root = swimRootMotion(t, phase, stroke, drive);
    const pitch = lerp(walkTilt, swimPitch + root.pitchWobble, pose);

    // Land limb poses, verbatim from Avatar.tsx's land branches.
    const walkSwingRange = 0.55;
    const idleSwingRange = 0.06;
    const baseTilt = 0.12;
    headX = lerp(0, 0, moveWeight);
    headY = 0;
    headZ = 0;
    torsoY = 0;
    lArmX = lerp(Math.sin(t * 1.5) * idleSwingRange, Math.sin(walkPhase * 0.5) * walkSwingRange, moveWeight);
    lArmZ = lerp(-baseTilt, -baseTilt, moveWeight);
    rArmX = lerp(-Math.sin(t * 1.5) * idleSwingRange, -Math.sin(walkPhase * 0.5) * walkSwingRange, moveWeight);
    rArmZ = lerp(baseTilt, baseTilt, moveWeight);
    lLegX = lerp(0, -Math.sin(walkPhase * 0.5) * walkSwingRange, moveWeight);
    rLegX = lerp(0, Math.sin(walkPhase * 0.5) * walkSwingRange, moveWeight);
    lLegZ = 0;
    rLegZ = 0;

    if (pose > 0) {
      const h = swimHeadPose(phase, stroke, swimPitch, drive);
      headX = blendSwimAngle(headX, h.x, pose);
      headY = blendSwimAngle(headY, h.y, pose);
      headZ = blendSwimAngle(headZ, h.z, pose);
      torsoY = blendSwimAngle(torsoY, swimTorsoPose(phase, stroke).y, pose);
      const la = swimArmPose(-1, phase, stroke, drive);
      lArmX = blendSwimAngle(lArmX, la.x, pose);
      lArmY = blendSwimAngle(lArmY, la.y, pose);
      lArmZ = blendSwimAngle(lArmZ, la.z, pose);
      const ra = swimArmPose(1, phase, stroke, drive);
      rArmX = blendSwimAngle(rArmX, ra.x, pose);
      rArmY = blendSwimAngle(rArmY, ra.y, pose);
      rArmZ = blendSwimAngle(rArmZ, ra.z, pose);
      const ll = swimLegPose(-1, phase, stroke, swimPitch);
      const rl = swimLegPose(1, phase, stroke, swimPitch);
      lLegX = blendSwimAngle(lLegX, ll.x, pose);
      lLegZ = blendSwimAngle(lLegZ, ll.z, pose);
      rLegX = blendSwimAngle(rLegX, rl.x, pose);
      rLegZ = blendSwimAngle(rLegZ, rl.z, pose);
    }

    // --- height --------------------------------------------------------------------
    const terrainY = getTerrainInfo(x, z, SCALE).targetY;
    const safeSwimY = Math.max(terrainY, SWIM_BODY_Y);
    let rootY = terrainY;
    if (state === 'swimming') rootY = safeSwimY + root.bob;
    else if (state === 'enteringWater') rootY = lerp(terrainY + 0.05, safeSwimY, p);
    else if (state === 'exitingWater') rootY = lerp(safeSwimY, terrainY, p);
    rootY = Math.max(rootY, terrainY);

    out.push({
      t,
      state,
      pose,
      stroke,
      phase,
      pitch,
      channels: [headX, headY, headZ, torsoY, lArmX, lArmY, lArmZ, rArmX, rArmY, rArmZ, lLegX, lLegZ, rLegX, rLegZ],
      // The head joint rides on the root, swung forward by the body pitch.
      headY: rootY + HEAD_LOCAL_Y * Math.cos(pitch),
      rootY,
    });
  }
  return out;
}

let failures = 0;

function check(
  name: string,
  script: (t: number) => Input,
  seconds: number,
  opts: { requireWet?: boolean } = {},
) {
  const samples = run(script, seconds);
  let worstSnap = 0;
  let worstSnapAt = 0;
  let worstSnapChannel = -1;
  let worstJerk = 0;
  let worstJerkAt = 0;
  let worstJerkChannel = -1;
  let lowestFace = Infinity;
  let stalledFrames = 0;
  let worstDrift = 0;
  let worstDriftAt = 0;
  let worstLegacyDrift = 0;
  // The camera's old standing -> floating blend, ticked over the same samples. See legacyDrift().
  let legacyBlend = 0;

  const all = (s: Sample) => [...s.channels, s.pitch];

  for (let i = 1; i < samples.length; i++) {
    const a = all(samples[i - 1]);
    const b = all(samples[i]);
    const prev = i >= 2 ? all(samples[i - 2]) : null;
    for (let c = 0; c < b.length; c++) {
      const step = Math.abs(b[c] - a[c]);
      if (step > worstSnap) {
        worstSnap = step;
        worstSnapAt = samples[i].t;
        worstSnapChannel = c;
      }
      if (prev) {
        // The second difference is what a POSE SNAP actually is: a limb that was moving at
        // one speed and is suddenly moving at a wildly different one. A blend that ramps -
        // however briskly - has a small second difference; a one-frame cut between two poses
        // has an enormous one. Peak speed alone cannot tell those apart, which is why both
        // are measured.
        const jerk = Math.abs(b[c] - 2 * a[c] + prev[c]);
        if (jerk > worstJerk) {
          worstJerk = jerk;
          worstJerkAt = samples[i].t;
          worstJerkChannel = c;
        }
      }
    }
    // The face is only required to be dry once the character is actually floating; while
    // wading in it is legitimately still standing up on the sea bed.
    if (samples[i].pose > 0.6) lowestFace = Math.min(lowestFace, samples[i].headY);
    if (samples[i].pose > 0.2 && Math.abs(samples[i].phase - samples[i - 1].phase) < 1e-6) stalledFrames++;

    // DRIFT. Where the middle of the body sits relative to where the camera is looking, against
    // where it sits for a walker: FOCUS_ABOVE_BODY_MIDDLE below the aim point, whatever the body
    // is doing. Only asserted from the water line down - above it the framing is deliberately
    // measured from the walking plane rather than from the terrain (see orbitFocusOffsetY), so a
    // character standing on the mound legitimately sits higher in the frame.
    const { rootY, pose, state } = samples[i];
    legacyBlend = lerp(legacyBlend, state !== 'walking' ? 1 : 0, Math.min(1, 4 * DT));
    if (rootY <= 0) {
      const framed = bodyMiddleY(rootY, pose) - orbitFocusOffsetY(0, rootY, pose);
      const drift = Math.abs(framed + FOCUS_ABOVE_BODY_MIDDLE);
      if (drift > worstDrift) {
        worstDrift = drift;
        worstDriftAt = samples[i].t;
      }
      const legacyFramed = bodyMiddleY(rootY, pose) - lerp(STANDING_FOCUS_Y, SWIM_FOCUS_Y, legacyBlend);
      worstLegacyDrift = Math.max(worstLegacyDrift, Math.abs(legacyFramed + FOCUS_ABOVE_BODY_MIDDLE));
    }
  }

  const wet = samples.some((s) => s.pose > 0.6);
  const ok =
    worstSnap <= SNAP_LIMIT &&
    worstJerk <= JERK_LIMIT &&
    (lowestFace === Infinity || lowestFace > WATER_SURFACE_Y) &&
    stalledFrames === 0 &&
    worstDrift <= DRIFT_LIMIT &&
    (!opts.requireWet || wet);

  if (!ok) failures++;
  console.log(
    `${ok ? 'ok  ' : 'FAIL'}  ${name.padEnd(40)} ` +
      `maxStep=${worstSnap.toFixed(3)}@${worstSnapAt.toFixed(1)}s(ch${worstSnapChannel}) ` +
      `maxJerk=${worstJerk.toFixed(4)}@${worstJerkAt.toFixed(1)}s(ch${worstJerkChannel}) ` +
      `face=${lowestFace === Infinity ? '   n/a' : lowestFace.toFixed(3)} ` +
      `stalled=${stalledFrames} ` +
      `drift=${worstDrift.toFixed(3)}@${worstDriftAt.toFixed(1)}s (was ${worstLegacyDrift.toFixed(3)})`,
  );
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The shared-pose claim, measured directly: how far apart are resting and
// stroking? This is the number that used to be 2.96 rad (169.6deg).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
const restPitch = swimBodyPitch(0);
const strokePitch = swimBodyPitch(1);
const poseGap = Math.abs(strokePitch - restPitch);
const legacyGap = Math.abs(Math.PI / 2.2 - -Math.PI / 2.05);
console.log(
  `${poseGap <= FLIP_LIMIT ? 'ok  ' : 'FAIL'}  ${'WaterIdle <-> Swimming attitude gap'.padEnd(40)} ` +
    `${poseGap.toFixed(3)}rad (${((poseGap * 180) / Math.PI).toFixed(1)}deg)   ` +
    `was ${legacyGap.toFixed(3)}rad (${((legacyGap * 180) / Math.PI).toFixed(1)}deg)`,
);
if (poseGap > FLIP_LIMIT) failures++;

// Face clearance at both ends of that gap, from the geometry rather than from a run.
for (const [label, pitch] of [['float', restPitch], ['stroke', strokePitch]] as const) {
  const faceY = SWIM_BODY_Y + HEAD_LOCAL_Y * Math.cos(pitch);
  const clear = faceY - WATER_SURFACE_Y;
  if (clear <= 0) failures++;
  console.log(
    `${clear > 0 ? 'ok  ' : 'FAIL'}  ${`face clearance while ${label}ing`.padEnd(40)} ` +
      `${clear >= 0 ? '+' : ''}${clear.toFixed(3)} world units above the waterline`,
  );
}

console.log(
  `      ${'land reference (idle -> walk -> idle)'.padEnd(40)} ` +
    `step=${LAND.step.toFixed(3)} jerk=${LAND.jerk.toFixed(4)}  <- the bar every check below uses`,
);
console.log('');

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Scripts. Radii: sand ends at 6.8, the swimmable leash at 9.5.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
const OUT = 8.6; // comfortably out at sea
const BEACH = 6.0; // dry sand

check('land idle -> wade in -> float', (t) => ({
  radius: t < 1 ? BEACH : Math.min(OUT, BEACH + (t - 1) * 1.6),
  moving: t >= 1 && t < 2.7,
}), 9, { requireWet: true });

check('float -> swim -> float (the core case)', (t) => ({
  radius: OUT,
  moving: t > 2 && t < 6,
}), 9, { requireWet: true });

check('swim, stop dead, swim again', (t) => ({
  radius: OUT,
  moving: (t > 1 && t < 2) || (t > 2.2 && t < 3) || (t > 3.1 && t < 5),
}), 9, { requireWet: true });

check('swim W then reverse to S', (t) => ({
  radius: OUT,
  moving: t > 1,
  forward: t < 3 ? 1 : -1,
}), 9, { requireWet: true });

check('strafe A then D', (t) => ({
  radius: OUT,
  moving: t > 1,
  forward: 0,
  strafe: t < 3 ? -1 : 1,
}), 9, { requireWet: true });

check('speed ramp 0 -> full -> 0', (t) => ({
  radius: OUT,
  moving: t > 0.5,
  speed: 5.47 * Math.min(1, Math.abs(Math.sin(t * 0.4))),
}), 9, { requireWet: true });

check('swim ashore and stand up', (t) => ({
  radius: Math.max(BEACH, OUT - t * 1.4),
  moving: true,
}), 9);

check('shoreline dithering (in/out/in/out)', (t) => ({
  radius: 6.8 + Math.sin(t * 2.5) * 0.9,
  moving: true,
}), 9);

check('float in the shallows', (t) => ({
  radius: 7.1,
  moving: t > 2 && t < 4,
}), 9);

check('long soak (phase wrap + drift)', (t) => ({
  radius: OUT,
  moving: t % 8 < 5,
}), 9, { requireWet: true });

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The legacy probe. Not a test - evidence. It runs the OLD curves through the
// same "stop swimming" moment so the two numbers can be compared directly.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
function legacyProbe() {
  const proneTilt = Math.PI / 2.2;
  const floatTilt = -Math.PI / 2.05;
  let pitch = proneTilt;
  let worstPitchStep = 0;
  let walkPhase = 12 * 2; // two seconds of held W, i.e. wherever the arms happened to be
  // The old arm curves, verbatim.
  const movingArm = (wp: number) => wp * 0.8 + 0.42 * Math.sin(wp * 0.8);
  let arm = movingArm(walkPhase);
  let worstArmStep = 0;

  for (let i = 0; i < 2 / DT; i++) {
    // The frame WASD is released: target flips, arms cut to the back-float curve.
    const target = floatTilt;
    const before = pitch;
    pitch = lerp(pitch, target, Math.min(1, 5.5 * DT));
    worstPitchStep = Math.max(worstPitchStep, Math.abs(pitch - before));
    const armBefore = arm;
    arm = lerp(arm, -0.35, 5 * DT); // the old idle branch's eased starfish target
    worstArmStep = Math.max(worstArmStep, Math.abs(arm - armBefore));
  }
  console.log(
    `note  ${'LEGACY on release of WASD'.padEnd(40)} ` +
      `body travelled ${Math.abs(floatTilt - proneTilt).toFixed(2)}rad through upright, ` +
      `worst single frame: pitch ${worstPitchStep.toFixed(3)}rad, arm ${worstArmStep.toFixed(3)}rad`,
  );
}

console.log('');
legacyProbe();

console.log('');
if (failures > 0) {
  console.log(`${failures} check(s) FAILED`);
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log('all swim pose checks passed');
```

## scripts/audit-zfighting.mjs

```mjs
// Static audit for depth-conflict (z-fighting) risk in the procedural models.
//
// This is the CI-runnable half of the check. It cannot know where a mesh really
// ends up - that depends on group transforms computed at render time, which is
// what `src/utils/zFightAudit.ts` measures in the live scene - so it does not
// try to be authoritative. It catches the shape of the bug that actually
// occurred: two horizontal surfaces, declared side by side in one component
// with literal positions, landing within MIN_SURFACE_SEPARATION of each other
// while covering the same ground.
//
// That is exactly the island-terrain defect - a body cylinder topping out at
// y=0.30 with a second cylinder topping out at y=0.32 across the same radius -
// and it is cheap to detect without rendering anything.
//
// A pair is NOT reported when either surface opts out honestly:
//   - `polygonOffset` / DECAL_DEPTH_BIAS: it has declared itself a decal, which
//     is the sanctioned fix for coplanar-by-design geometry.
//   - `depthWrite={false}` / `depthTest={false}`: it is a sorted transparent
//     layer and cannot z-fight, the way the ocean's foam and wave rings work.
//
// Scope limits, stated plainly: only literal positions inside one component are
// compared, and intervening <group> transforms are not resolved. Anything
// placed at runtime, scaled by territory level, or split across components is
// the runtime audit's job.
//
// Run: npm run audit:zfighting

import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const root = path.dirname(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)));
const SRC = path.join(root, 'src');

// Kept in sync with src/constants/terrain.ts. Duplicated rather than imported
// because this script runs as plain node without the TS pipeline.
const MIN_SURFACE_SEPARATION = 0.05;

/** Minimum overlapping footprint before a pair is worth a human's attention. */
const MIN_OVERLAP_AREA = 0.05;

/**
 * How close is too close depends on the camera that sees the surface, because
 * depth resolution falls off with distance and with the near/far ratio:
 *
 *   resolution ~= z^2 * (far - near) / (near * far * 2^bits)
 *
 *   - Island scene (Scene.tsx): camera orbits 10-50 units out, near 0.5,
 *     far 2000 (the ocean plane forces that far). At 50 units that is ~3e-4 on
 *     a 24-bit buffer but ~0.08 on a 16-bit one, which plenty of mobile GPUs
 *     hand out. MIN_SURFACE_SEPARATION (0.05) is the rule for anything drawn
 *     out there.
 *   - Interiors and furniture (BuildingInteriorView, FurnitureItem): camera at
 *     ~12 units, near 0.3, far 200. Worst case ~0.007, so a 1cm detail is safe
 *     and flagging it would be noise. Only near-exact coplanarity matters.
 *
 * Judging every file by the island's threshold reported correctly-built
 * furniture (a 2cm-proud sink basin, a blanket over a mattress) as defects.
 */
const INTERIOR_SCALE_FILES = [
  'BuildingInteriorView.tsx',
  'FurnitureItem.tsx',
  'DressingRoomView.tsx',
  'FitnessView.tsx',
  'Avatar.tsx',
  'PetDog.tsx',
];
const INTERIOR_THRESHOLD = 0.008;

function thresholdFor(file) {
  const base = path.basename(file);
  return INTERIOR_SCALE_FILES.includes(base) ? INTERIOR_THRESHOLD : MIN_SURFACE_SEPARATION;
}

function sourceFiles(dir) {
  const out = [];
  for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
    const p = path.join(dir, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) out.push(...sourceFiles(p));
    else if (/\.tsx?$/.test(entry.name)) out.push(p);
  }
  return out;
}

const rel = (f) => path.relative(root, f).replace(/\\/g, '/');

/** Numbers out of a `[ ... ]` prop body, or null if any entry is not a literal. */
function literalArray(text) {
  if (!text) return null;
  const out = [];
  for (const part of text.split(',')) {
    const n = part.trim();
    if (!/^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/.test(n)) return null;
    out.push(parseFloat(n));
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Split a source file into top-level component bodies. Two meshes only share a
 * coordinate frame if they are declared in the same component, so pairing
 * across the whole file (FurnitureItem.tsx alone holds ~90 unrelated models)
 * produces nothing but noise.
 */
function components(lines) {
  const blocks = [];
  let current = null;
  lines.forEach((line, idx) => {
    const m = line.match(/^(?:export\s+)?(?:function|const)\s+([A-Z]\w*)/);
    if (m) {
      if (current) current.end = idx;
      current = { name: m[1], start: idx, end: lines.length };
      blocks.push(current);
    }
  });
  return blocks;
}

/**
 * Horizontal faces declared in a line range, as { y, halfX, halfZ }.
 *
 * A flat plane/circle/ring counts only when it is rotated onto the XZ plane; a
 * solid contributes its top and bottom faces.
 */
function horizontalFaces(lines, start, end) {
  const faces = [];

  // Group nesting, tracked as a path like "0/2". Two meshes are only comparable
  // when they sit in the SAME group: sibling <group>s usually carry their own
  // position, and mutually-exclusive ones (the avatar's straw hat vs its bucket
  // hat, each in its own conditional group) never exist at the same time.
  // Comparing across groups was the single largest source of false positives.
  const groupStack = [];
  const childCounter = [0];

  for (let idx = start; idx < end; idx++) {
    const line = lines[idx];

    // Maintain the path before reading any geometry on this line.
    const opens = (line.match(/<group\b/g) || []).length;
    const selfClosed = (line.match(/<group\b[^>]*\/>/g) || []).length;
    const closes = (line.match(/<\/group>/g) || []).length;
    for (let n = 0; n < opens - selfClosed; n++) {
      groupStack.push(childCounter[childCounter.length - 1]++);
      childCounter.push(0);
    }
    for (let n = 0; n < closes; n++) {
      groupStack.pop();
      childCounter.pop();
    }
    const groupPath = groupStack.join('/');
    const geoMatch = line.match(
      /<(planeGeometry|circleGeometry|ringGeometry|cylinderGeometry|boxGeometry)\s+args=\{\[([^\]]+)\]\}/
    );
    if (!geoMatch) continue;

    const [, geo, argText] = geoMatch;
    const args = literalArray(argText);
    if (!args) continue;

    // Walk back to the enclosing <mesh ...> tag, collecting its props.
    let pos = [0, 0, 0];
    let tag = '';
    for (let k = idx; k >= Math.max(start, idx - 12); k--) {
      tag = lines[k] + '\n' + tag;
      if (/<mesh\b/.test(lines[k])) break;
      if (k === Math.max(start, idx - 12)) tag = '';
    }
    if (!tag) continue;

    const posMatch = tag.match(/position=\{\[([^\]]+)\]\}/);
    if (posMatch) {
      const p = literalArray(posMatch[1]);
      if (!p || p.length < 3) continue; // computed position - runtime audit's job
      pos = p;
    }

    // THE MESH'S OWN `scale`, which this used to ignore - and ignoring it is not a
    // conservative simplification, it is a wrong answer in both directions.
    //
    // The idiom it got wrong is everywhere in the cosmetic and NPC models: a UNIT box
    // (`args={[1,1,1]}`) sized entirely by `scale={[0.0022, 0.017, 0.004]}`, because
    // that is how you author a thin strip without three magic numbers inside the
    // geometry. Read without the scale, a 2mm charm on an anklet is a 1x1x1 metre cube
    // whose faces sit at y = +/-0.5 - so two unrelated charms in the same group came back
    // as two full-metre slabs "0.000 apart, overlap 0.98" and got reported as a defect
    // in a model that has none. Three of the seven findings this audit produced were that
    // same false positive, which is the failure mode that teaches people to stop reading
    // audit output.
    //
    // The other direction is worse and silent: a mesh SHRUNK by `scale` has its faces
    // closer together than its args say, so a genuine conflict between two scaled
    // surfaces was under-reported and never flagged at all.
    let scale = [1, 1, 1];
    const scaleMatch = tag.match(/scale=\{\[([^\]]+)\]\}/);
    if (scaleMatch) {
      const s = literalArray(scaleMatch[1]);
      if (!s || s.length < 3) continue; // computed scale - runtime audit's job
      scale = s;
    } else {
      // `scale={0.4}` - the uniform form.
      const uniform = tag.match(/scale=\{(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\}/);
      if (uniform) scale = [+uniform[1], +uniform[1], +uniform[1]];
      else if (/scale=\{/.test(tag)) continue; // computed - runtime audit's job
    }

    // The material sits just after the geometry.
    const after = lines.slice(idx, Math.min(lines.length, idx + 10)).join('\n');
    const exempt =
      /polygonOffset|DECAL_DEPTH_BIAS|RUG_DEPTH_BIAS/.test(after) ||
      /depthWrite=\{false\}/.test(after) ||
      /depthTest=\{false\}/.test(after) ||
      /<primitive[^>]*attach=["']material/.test(after);

    // `dir` is what makes this check usable at all. Two faces can only fight if
    // they face the SAME way: a countertop's underside resting exactly on a
    // cabinet's top is ordinary stacking, and back-face culling means you never
    // see both at once. Comparing opposing faces reported ~100 false positives
    // across the furniture models, every one of them a correctly built object.
    const at = (y, halfX, halfZ, dir) =>
      faces.push({ y, halfX, halfZ, dir, groupPath, line: idx + 1, geo, exempt });

    if (geo === 'cylinderGeometry') {
      const [rTop, rBot, h] = args;
      if ([rTop, rBot, h].some((v) => typeof v !== 'number')) continue;
      at(pos[1] + (h * scale[1]) / 2, rTop * scale[0], rTop * scale[2], 'up');
      at(pos[1] - (h * scale[1]) / 2, rBot * scale[0], rBot * scale[2], 'down');
    } else if (geo === 'boxGeometry') {
      const [w, h, d] = args;
      if ([w, h, d].some((v) => typeof v !== 'number')) continue;
      at(pos[1] + (h * scale[1]) / 2, (w * scale[0]) / 2, (d * scale[2]) / 2, 'up');
      at(pos[1] - (h * scale[1]) / 2, (w * scale[0]) / 2, (d * scale[2]) / 2, 'down');
    } else {
      // Flat geometry: only horizontal instances lie on another surface.
      const horizontal = /rotation(-x)?=\{?\[?\s*-?\s*Math\.PI\s*\/\s*2/.test(tag);
      if (!horizontal) continue;
      const rawX = geo === 'planeGeometry' ? args[0] / 2 : args[geo === 'ringGeometry' ? 1 : 0];
      const rawZ = geo === 'planeGeometry' ? args[1] / 2 : rawX;
      // A flat geometry turned onto the XZ plane has swapped its own Y and Z, so its
      // in-plane extents are scaled by the mesh's x and Y - not x and z.
      const halfX = rawX * scale[0];
      const halfZ = rawZ * scale[1];
      // `rotation={[-Math.PI/2, ...]}` turns a plane's +Z normal to +Y. The
      // `+Math.PI/2` case faces down; both are matched by the test above, so
      // read the sign back off the tag.
      const facesDown = /rotation(-x)?=\{?\[?\s*Math\.PI\s*\/\s*2/.test(tag);
      at(pos[1], halfX, halfZ, facesDown ? 'down' : 'up');
    }

    // Record XZ centre on every face just added for this mesh.
    for (let f = faces.length - 1; f >= 0 && faces[f].line === idx + 1; f--) {
      faces[f].cx = pos[0];
      faces[f].cz = pos[2];
    }
  }

  return faces;
}

const findings = [];

for (const file of sourceFiles(SRC)) {
  const lines = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8').split('\n');

  for (const block of components(lines)) {
    const faces = horizontalFaces(lines, block.start, block.end);

    for (let i = 0; i < faces.length; i++) {
      for (let j = i + 1; j < faces.length; j++) {
        const a = faces[i];
        const b = faces[j];
        if (a.line === b.line) continue; // a solid's own two faces
        if (a.dir !== b.dir) continue; // opposing faces cannot fight - see `at`
        // Only upward-facing pairs. A downward-facing surface in this art style
        // is the underside of something resting on another object, so it is
        // occluded by whatever it stands on: a toilet's seat and its cistern
        // both bottom out exactly on the pan, a pot's rim and its soil both
        // bottom out inside the pot. Every such pair reported here was benign.
        // Genuine ceiling-vs-ceiling conflicts are left to the runtime audit,
        // which works from real geometry instead of guessing from source.
        if (a.dir !== 'up') continue;
        if (a.groupPath !== b.groupPath) continue; // different frames - see `groupStack`
        if (a.exempt || b.exempt) continue;

        const sep = Math.abs(a.y - b.y);
        if (sep >= thresholdFor(file)) continue;

        // Overlapping footprint, or they simply sit next to each other.
        const ox = Math.min(a.cx + a.halfX, b.cx + b.halfX) - Math.max(a.cx - a.halfX, b.cx - b.halfX);
        const oz = Math.min(a.cz + a.halfZ, b.cz + b.halfZ) - Math.max(a.cz - a.halfZ, b.cz - b.halfZ);
        if (ox <= 0 || oz <= 0 || ox * oz < MIN_OVERLAP_AREA) continue;

        findings.push({
          file: rel(file),
          component: block.name,
          aLine: a.line,
          bLine: b.line,
          y: a.y,
          separation: sep,
          threshold: thresholdFor(file),
          area: ox * oz,
        });
      }
    }
  }
}

findings.sort((f, g) => f.separation - g.separation || g.area - f.area);

if (findings.length) {
  console.log(`\n[z-fight audit] ${findings.length} suspect surface pair(s):\n`);
  for (const f of findings) {
    console.log(
      `  ${f.file}:${f.aLine} + :${f.bLine}  (${f.component})  ` +
        `${f.separation.toFixed(3)} apart (limit ${f.threshold}) at y=${f.y.toFixed(3)}, overlap ${f.area.toFixed(2)}`
    );
  }
  console.log(
    '\n  Two opaque up-facing surfaces closer than this scene\'s limit that cover\n' +
      '  each other will z-fight. Fix structurally: merge them into one mesh, or\n' +
      '  delete the hidden one.\n' +
      '  If the pair is coplanar BY DESIGN (a decal lying on a floor), give the upper\n' +
      '  one {...DECAL_DEPTH_BIAS} from src/constants/terrain.ts.\n' +
      '  Do NOT nudge them apart by an arbitrary amount.'
  );
} else {
  console.log('[z-fight audit] clean - no near-coplanar overlapping surfaces in literal positions.');
}

console.log(
  '\nNote: this is the static half, limited to literal positions within one component.\n' +
    'For real world-space overlaps (group transforms, runtime placements), open the app\n' +
    'and run __auditZFighting() in the browser console.'
);

process.exit(findings.length ? 1 : 0);

```

## scripts/check-conflict-markers.mjs

```mjs
// Rejects unresolved merge-conflict markers before they can be committed.
//
// This exists because it already happened: commit 3381edf shipped four blocks of
// live conflict markers inside src/components/BuildingInteriorView.tsx. A file in
// that state does not parse, so it is not "a bad merge on one machine" - it is a
// broken build handed to everyone who pulls, and the person who pulls it is the
// one who has to reconstruct what the author meant.
//
// Two modes, deliberately different in scope:
//
//   --staged   What the pre-commit hook runs. Looks ONLY at the lines this commit
//              ADDS. That matters: scanning whole files would mean one pre-existing
//              marker anywhere in the tree blocks every commit until it is cleaned
//              up, which is how a hook earns a permanent --no-verify habit.
//
//   (default)  Repo-wide audit over tracked files, for CI or a manual check.
//              Run: npm run check:conflicts
//
// Bypass, when a file genuinely needs to contain a marker (documentation about
// merging, a test fixture):  git commit --no-verify

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

/**
 * The three markers git writes, built rather than written literally so that THIS
 * file - and the hook that runs it - does not trip its own check.
 *
 * `=======` is deliberately absent. On its own it is not evidence of anything: it
 * is also a markdown h1 underline and half the ASCII rules ever typed into a
 * comment banner. The opening and closing markers are unambiguous, they cannot be
 * left behind without one of these two, and a check that cries wolf gets disabled.
 *
 * The base marker is written as the bracket expression [|] and never as a backslash-escaped
 * pipe. These patterns go to `git grep -E`, and POSIX ERE leaves backslash-pipe undefined: git
 * reads it as plain alternation, collapsing the pattern into empty branches that match every line
 * in the repository. A bracket expression means the same thing to both git and JavaScript.
 */
const MARKERS = [
  { name: 'ours', pattern: '^' + '<'.repeat(7) + '( |$)' },
  { name: 'base', pattern: '^' + '[|]'.repeat(7) + '( |$)' },
  { name: 'theirs', pattern: '^' + '>'.repeat(7) + '( |$)' },
];

const MARKER_RE = new RegExp(MARKERS.map((m) => m.pattern).join('|'));

function git(args) {
  const r = spawnSync('git', args, { encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024 });
  if (r.error) throw r.error;
  return r;
}

/**
 * Added lines in the staged diff, as {file, line, text}.
 *
 * -U0 so every `+` line is genuinely new rather than context, and --no-ext-diff so
 * a configured external differ cannot change the format out from under the parse.
 * Binary files produce a "Binary files ... differ" line with no `+` content, so
 * they fall out on their own.
 */
function stagedAdditions() {
  const r = git(['diff', '--cached', '-U0', '--no-color', '--no-ext-diff', '--diff-filter=ACMR']);
  if (r.status !== 0) {
    process.stderr.write(r.stderr || 'git diff --cached failed\n');
    process.exit(2);
  }

  const out = [];
  let file = null;
  let lineNo = 0;

  for (const raw of r.stdout.split('\n')) {
    if (raw.startsWith('+++ ')) {
      // "+++ b/path", or "+++ /dev/null" for a deletion.
      file = raw === '+++ /dev/null' ? null : raw.slice(6);
      continue;
    }
    if (raw.startsWith('@@')) {
      const m = /^@@ -\d+(?:,\d+)? \+(\d+)/.exec(raw);
      lineNo = m ? Number(m[1]) : 0;
      continue;
    }
    if (file && raw.startsWith('+')) {
      out.push({ file, line: lineNo, text: raw.slice(1) });
      lineNo++;
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/** Every marker line in tracked files, via git grep so binaries are skipped for us. */
function trackedMarkers() {
  const args = ['grep', '-I', '-n', '--no-color', '-E'];
  for (const m of MARKERS) args.push('-e', m.pattern);
  const r = git(args);
  if (r.status === 1) return []; // git grep: 1 means "no matches"
  if (r.status !== 0) {
    process.stderr.write(r.stderr || 'git grep failed\n');
    process.exit(2);
  }
  return r.stdout
    .split('\n')
    .filter(Boolean)
    .map((row) => {
      const [file, line, ...rest] = row.split(':');
      return { file, line: Number(line), text: rest.join(':') };
    });
}

const staged = process.argv.includes('--staged');
const hits = staged ? stagedAdditions().filter((h) => MARKER_RE.test(h.text)) : trackedMarkers();

if (hits.length === 0) {
  if (!staged) console.log('No conflict markers in tracked files.');
  process.exit(0);
}

const where = staged ? 'staged for commit' : 'tracked files';
process.stderr.write(`\nUnresolved conflict markers ${where} (${hits.length}):\n\n`);
for (const h of hits) process.stderr.write(`  ${h.file}:${h.line}: ${h.text.trim()}\n`);
process.stderr.write(
  staged
    ? '\nResolve them, `git add` the files, and commit again.\n' +
      'If a marker is intentional here, bypass with: git commit --no-verify\n\n'
    : '\n'
);
process.exit(1);
```

## scripts/export-player-reference.mjs

```mjs
// One-off export of the current in-game player model's BASE proportions
// (unclothed body + every wearable attachment point used by Avatar.tsx) as a
// .glb, for opening in Blender as a modeling reference. Not part of the app -
// safe to delete after use.
//
// Coordinates are left UNSCALED, i.e. in the same local-unit space as the
// numbers you see throughout Avatar.tsx (head radius 0.26, BASE_HEAD_Y 0.68,
// etc.) - NOT multiplied by the outer <group> 2.25x display scale. So 1 unit
// here = 1 "Avatar.tsx local unit". If you need true in-game world size,
// multiply everything by 2.25.
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFExporter } from 'three/examples/jsm/exporters/GLTFExporter.js';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

// GLTFExporter's binary path reads the merged buffer via FileReader, which
// only exists in browsers. Node has Blob (and Blob#arrayBuffer) natively, so
// a minimal polyfill that just delegates to that is enough.
if (typeof globalThis.FileReader === 'undefined') {
  globalThis.FileReader = class {
    readAsArrayBuffer(blob) {
      blob.arrayBuffer().then((buf) => {
        this.result = buf;
        this.onloadend?.();
      });
    }
  };
}

const root = path.dirname(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)));
const outDir = path.join(root, 'blender-reference');
fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });

const BASE_HEAD_Y = 0.68;
const BASE_BODY_Y = 0.36;
const skinColor = '#fcd34d';
const bodyColor = '#718096'; // default fallback shirt/pants tone when nothing is equipped

const scene = new THREE.Group();
scene.name = 'PlayerModel_Base';

const skinMat = () => new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: skinColor, roughness: 0.7 });
const bodyMat = () => new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: bodyColor, roughness: 0.7 });

// --- Head -------------------------------------------------------------
const head = new THREE.Group();
head.name = 'Head';
head.position.set(0, BASE_HEAD_Y, 0);
scene.add(head);

const headMesh = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.26, 32, 32), skinMat());
headMesh.name = 'Head_Skin';
head.add(headMesh);

const eyeL = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.036, 16, 16), new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: '#0d1117' }));
eyeL.name = 'Eye_L';
eyeL.position.set(-0.104, 0.035, 0.225);
head.add(eyeL);
const eyeR = eyeL.clone();
eyeR.name = 'Eye_R';
eyeR.position.set(0.104, 0.035, 0.225);
head.add(eyeR);

// --- Torso --------------------------------------------------------------
const body = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.CapsuleGeometry(0.135, 0.08, 4, 16), bodyMat());
body.name = 'Torso';
body.position.set(0, BASE_BODY_Y, 0);
scene.add(body);

// --- Arms -----------------------------------------------------------------
function buildArm(side) {
  const sign = side === 'L' ? -1 : 1;
  const arm = new THREE.Group();
  arm.name = `Arm_${side}`;
  arm.position.set(0.138 * sign, 0.42, 0);

  const upper = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.CapsuleGeometry(0.04, 0.1, 4, 16), skinMat());
  upper.name = `Arm_${side}_Upper`;
  upper.position.set(0, -0.07, 0);
  arm.add(upper);

  const hand = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.08, 16, 16), skinMat());
  hand.name = `Arm_${side}_Hand`;
  hand.position.set(0, -0.16, 0);
  arm.add(hand);

  return arm;
}
scene.add(buildArm('L'));
scene.add(buildArm('R'));

// --- Legs -----------------------------------------------------------------
function buildLeg(side) {
  const sign = side === 'L' ? -1 : 1;
  const leg = new THREE.Group();
  leg.name = `Leg_${side}`;
  leg.position.set(0.065 * sign, 0.22, 0);

  const upper = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.CapsuleGeometry(0.055, 0.14, 4, 16), bodyMat());
  upper.name = `Leg_${side}_Upper`;
  upper.position.set(0, -0.1, 0);
  leg.add(upper);

  return leg;
}
scene.add(buildLeg('L'));
scene.add(buildLeg('R'));

// --- Wearable anchor points ------------------------------------------------
// Small markers at every position offset Avatar.tsx actually uses when it
// equips a hat/glasses/earring/necklace/shoe - named to match. Not visible
// geometry, just reference points to line your own model's attachment
// points up against. World-space (i.e. already includes the head/body/leg
// parent offset above), matching what's in Avatar.tsx's JSX.
const anchorMat = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: '#22d3ee', wireframe: true });
function addAnchor(name, pos) {
  const marker = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.02, 6, 6), anchorMat);
  marker.name = name;
  marker.position.set(...pos);
  scene.add(marker);
}

addAnchor('Anchor_Hat', [0, BASE_HEAD_Y + 0.12, 0]);
addAnchor('Anchor_Glasses', [0, BASE_HEAD_Y + 0.06, 0.245]);
addAnchor('Anchor_Earring_L', [-0.27, BASE_HEAD_Y - 0.06, 0]);
addAnchor('Anchor_Earring_R', [0.27, BASE_HEAD_Y - 0.06, 0]);
addAnchor('Anchor_Mouth', [0, BASE_HEAD_Y - 0.045, 0.255]);
addAnchor('Anchor_Necklace', [0, BASE_BODY_Y + 0.09, 0.03]);
addAnchor('Anchor_Shoe_L', [-0.065, 0.22 - 0.19, 0.05]);
addAnchor('Anchor_Shoe_R', [0.065, 0.22 - 0.19, 0.05]);

// --- Export -----------------------------------------------------------
const exporter = new GLTFExporter();
const glb = await exporter.parseAsync(scene, { binary: true });
const outPath = path.join(outDir, 'player-model-reference.glb');
fs.writeFileSync(outPath, Buffer.from(glb));
console.log('Wrote', outPath, `(${(glb.byteLength / 1024).toFixed(1)} KB)`);
```

## scripts/lib/measureFurnitureModel.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import * as THREE from 'three';
import React from 'react';
import { FurnitureModel } from '../../src/components/Three/FurnitureItem';
import { ALL_ITEMS } from '../../src/constants/items';

/**
 * MEASURING A FURNITURE MODEL WITHOUT A RENDERER.
 *
 * `FurnitureModel` returns a tree of React elements describing three.js primitives. This walks
 * that tree, composes each node's position/rotation/scale into a matrix and accumulates the
 * corners of every geometry it recognises — which gives the same box the runtime measures off the
 * live scene graph (lib/furniturePlacement.ts's `measureFootprint`), from a plain `tsx` run with
 * no WebGL context anywhere.
 *
 * Extracted from scripts/audit-placements.ts when a second audit needed it. Both the placement
 * audit and the interaction audit have to be measuring THE SAME model or they can pass while
 * disagreeing with each other, which is the failure a shared module rules out.
 *
 * Most furniture components are plain hook-free functions and can simply be called. The ones that
 * animate cannot — see {@link renderComponent} for what this module does about that, and why it
 * matters more than it sounds.
 */

export type Box = {
  minX: number; maxX: number;
  minY: number; maxY: number;
  minZ: number; maxZ: number;
};

export const GEO_BOUNDS: Record<string, (a: any[]) => [number, number, number]> = {
  boxGeometry: (a) => [a[0] ?? 1, a[1] ?? 1, a[2] ?? 1],
  planeGeometry: (a) => [a[0] ?? 1, a[1] ?? 1, 0],
  cylinderGeometry: (a) => {
    const r = Math.max(a[0] ?? 1, a[1] ?? 1);
    return [r * 2, a[2] ?? 1, r * 2];
  },
  coneGeometry: (a) => [(a[0] ?? 1) * 2, a[1] ?? 1, (a[0] ?? 1) * 2],
  sphereGeometry: (a) => [(a[0] ?? 1) * 2, (a[0] ?? 1) * 2, (a[0] ?? 1) * 2],
  circleGeometry: (a) => [(a[0] ?? 1) * 2, (a[0] ?? 1) * 2, 0],
  ringGeometry: (a) => [(a[1] ?? 1) * 2, (a[1] ?? 1) * 2, 0],
  torusGeometry: (a) => {
    const o = (a[0] ?? 1) + (a[1] ?? 0.4);
    return [o * 2, o * 2, (a[1] ?? 0.4) * 2];
  },
  capsuleGeometry: (a) => [(a[0] ?? 1) * 2, (a[1] ?? 1) + (a[0] ?? 1) * 2, (a[0] ?? 1) * 2],
  dodecahedronGeometry: (a) => [(a[0] ?? 1) * 2, (a[0] ?? 1) * 2, (a[0] ?? 1) * 2],
  icosahedronGeometry: (a) => [(a[0] ?? 1) * 2, (a[0] ?? 1) * 2, (a[0] ?? 1) * 2],
  octahedronGeometry: (a) => [(a[0] ?? 1) * 2, (a[0] ?? 1) * 2, (a[0] ?? 1) * 2],
  tetrahedronGeometry: (a) => [(a[0] ?? 1) * 2, (a[0] ?? 1) * 2, (a[0] ?? 1) * 2],
};

/* ------------------------------------------------------- calling a component without a renderer */

/**
 * WHY THIS EXISTS: five outdoor items used to be invisible to every audit in the project.
 *
 * 木製鞦韆, 溫馨營火, 黃銅望遠鏡, 手作鳥屋 and 許願井 animate, so their components call `useRef`,
 * `useMemo` and `useFrame`. Calling such a function outside a real render throws `Invalid hook
 * call`, and the old harness caught that, filed the name under {@link brokenComponents} and moved
 * on — which meant those five shipped with **no collider check, no interaction check and no
 * quality check at all**. The reports said so in one quiet line at the end (`items with no
 * measurable model: …`) and it was easy to read that as housekeeping rather than as a hole.
 *
 * It is a hole. Those are five of the island's twenty-six placeable outdoor pieces, they include
 * the most expensive one in the shelf (許願井), and they are exactly the pieces most likely to be
 * edited — because they are the interactive ones.
 *
 * ## What this does
 *
 * React resolves a hook by asking the *current dispatcher*, which lives on an internal slot. For
 * the duration of one component call this installs a dispatcher that answers every hook with the
 * simplest thing that keeps the component's own code running:
 *
 *  - `useRef` hands back a `{ current }` — the component stores it and never dereferences it
 *    during render, because the whole point of a ref is that it is read in a callback later.
 *  - `useMemo` just calls the factory. The models use it for seed arrays, which is exactly what
 *    the returned JSX indexes into.
 *  - effects are no-ops. Nothing about the geometry is decided in one.
 *  - `useContext` returns a stub zustand store, which is all `useFrame` needs: it reads
 *    `store.getState().internal.subscribe` and registers the callback in a layout effect that
 *    never runs here.
 *
 * The animation callback is therefore never invoked, so what gets measured is the model in its
 * REST POSE. That is the honest thing to measure — a swing's collider should be the swing at
 * rest, not at the top of its arc — and it is the same tree the renderer builds on frame one.
 *
 * ## The cost of doing it this way
 *
 * `__CLIENT_INTERNALS_DO_NOT_USE_OR_WARN_USERS_THEY_CANNOT_UPGRADE` is, as the name says, private
 * to React, and its shape can change in a major version. That is a real cost and it is worth
 * paying here: this is a build-time audit, not shipped code, and the alternative — asking every
 * animated model to split its geometry into a second hook-free component and keeping a registry
 * that maps one to the other — is a parallel source of truth for what a model IS, which is the
 * class of bug constants/furnitureModels.ts exists to end.
 *
 * If React moves the slot, every audit fails loudly on day one with these five names in
 * {@link brokenComponents}, which is the failure mode to want.
 */
const ReactInternals: any =
  (React as any).__CLIENT_INTERNALS_DO_NOT_USE_OR_WARN_USERS_THEY_CANNOT_UPGRADE;

const noop = () => {};
/** Enough of a zustand store for `useFrame` to subscribe to. */
const STUB_R3F_STORE = {
  getState: () => ({ internal: { subscribe: () => noop } }),
  subscribe: () => noop,
};

const MEASUREMENT_DISPATCHER: any = {
  useRef: (v: unknown) => ({ current: v }),
  useMemo: (f: () => unknown) => f(),
  useCallback: (f: unknown) => f,
  useEffect: noop,
  useLayoutEffect: noop,
  useInsertionEffect: noop,
  useState: (v: unknown) => [typeof v === 'function' ? (v as () => unknown)() : v, noop],
  useReducer: (_r: unknown, v: unknown) => [v, noop],
  useContext: () => STUB_R3F_STORE,
  useId: () => 'measure',
  useDebugValue: noop,
  useImperativeHandle: noop,
  useSyncExternalStore: (_s: unknown, get: () => unknown) => get(),
  useTransition: () => [false, noop],
  useDeferredValue: (v: unknown) => v,
};

/**
 * Calls a function component once, with hooks answered by {@link MEASUREMENT_DISPATCHER}, and
 * returns what it rendered. A component that throws for any OTHER reason is recorded in
 * {@link brokenComponents} and contributes nothing, as before.
 */
export function renderComponent(type: (props: any) => any, props: any): any {
  const previous = ReactInternals?.H;
  if (ReactInternals) ReactInternals.H = MEASUREMENT_DISPATCHER;
  try {
    return type(props);
  } catch {
    brokenComponents.add(type.name || 'anonymous');
    return undefined;
  } finally {
    if (ReactInternals) ReactInternals.H = previous;
  }
}

export const unknownGeometries = new Set<string>();
export const brokenComponents = new Set<string>();

export function toVec3(v: unknown, fallback: number): THREE.Vector3 {
  if (typeof v === 'number') return new THREE.Vector3(v, v, v);
  if (Array.isArray(v)) return new THREE.Vector3(v[0] ?? fallback, v[1] ?? fallback, v[2] ?? fallback);
  return new THREE.Vector3(fallback, fallback, fallback);
}

export function localMatrix(props: any): THREE.Matrix4 {
  const pos = toVec3(props.position, 0);
  const scl = toVec3(props.scale, 1);
  const rot = toVec3(props.rotation, 0);
  return new THREE.Matrix4().compose(
    pos,
    new THREE.Quaternion().setFromEuler(new THREE.Euler(rot.x, rot.y, rot.z)),
    scl,
  );
}

/**
 * Is this element a drawn EFFECT rather than the object's own substance?
 *
 * The same rule the shipping collider applies (lib/furniturePlacement.ts's `isSolidGeometry`),
 * asked of a React element instead of a `THREE.Mesh`: a mesh that does not write depth, or is
 * additively blended, or is explicitly flagged, is light rather than matter.
 *
 * WHY THE AUDIT NEEDED IT TOO. Without this the React walk measured what the runtime had already
 * learned to ignore — and measured it BEFORE the `useFrame` that shrinks it, which is the worst
 * possible moment. 溫馨營火's flames are nine `sphereGeometry(1)` particles authored at unit
 * radius, so `npm run audit:interactions` reported the campfire as a 2.63-unit cube with 1.32 of
 * it underground, against the 1.54 x 1.41 stone ring the game actually collides with. 噴泉,
 * 黃銅望遠鏡, 許願井 and 手作鳥屋 all carry the same kind of sparkle. Every geometry check those
 * five pieces passed was therefore being run against a box no player ever meets — an audit
 * reporting "ok" about a shape that does not exist.
 */
function isEffectElement(props: any): boolean {
  if (props?.userData?.noCollide) return true;
  const children = React.Children.toArray(props?.children ?? []);
  return children.some((child: any) => {
    if (!React.isValidElement(child)) return false;
    const t: any = (child as any).type;
    if (typeof t !== 'string' || !t.endsWith('Material')) return false;
    const p: any = (child as any).props ?? {};
    return p.depthWrite === false || p.blending === THREE.AdditiveBlending;
  });
}

export function walk(node: any, parent: THREE.Matrix4, out: THREE.Box3, depth = 0): void {
  if (node == null || typeof node === 'boolean' || typeof node === 'string' || typeof node === 'number') return;
  if (Array.isArray(node)) {
    node.forEach((n) => walk(n, parent, out, depth));
    return;
  }
  if (!React.isValidElement(node)) return;

  const type: any = (node as any).type;
  const props: any = (node as any).props ?? {};

  // An invisible group prunes its whole subtree, not just itself — a burst of particles is
  // usually a hidden parent over visible children. Same order as the runtime's own walk.
  if (props.visible === false) return;
  if (isEffectElement(props)) return;

  // A fragment carries its children in props and has no transform of its own. Without this it
  // fell through the `typeof type !== 'string'` guard below and its whole subtree was silently
  // dropped from the measurement — which is invisible while every model is a single rooted
  // <group>, and stops being invisible the moment one returns a list of meshes.
  if (type === React.Fragment) {
    walk(props.children, parent, out, depth + 1);
    return;
  }

  // A component: call it and walk what it returns.
  if (typeof type === 'function') {
    walk(renderComponent(type, props), parent, out, depth + 1);
    return;
  }

  if (typeof type !== 'string') return;

  const here = new THREE.Matrix4().multiplyMatrices(parent, localMatrix(props));

  const bounds = GEO_BOUNDS[type];
  if (bounds) {
    const args = props.args ?? [];
    const [w, h, d] = bounds(args);
    const hx = w / 2, hy = h / 2, hz = d / 2;
    const v = new THREE.Vector3();
    for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
      v.set(i & 1 ? hx : -hx, i & 2 ? hy : -hy, i & 4 ? hz : -hz).applyMatrix4(here);
      out.expandByPoint(v);
    }
    return;
  }
  if (type.endsWith('Geometry')) unknownGeometries.add(type);

  walk(props.children, here, out, depth + 1);
}

/** The interior renders every piece at scale 1.15 (BuildingInteriorView's FurnitureItem). */
export const INTERIOR_SCALE = 1.15;

/**
 * The island renders a placed piece at FurnitureModel's own default of 0.85 (Three/
 * PlacementGhost's IslandPlacements). `FurnitureModel` then multiplies a BUILDING item by a
 * further 1.55 itself, so this is the number to hand it, not the final size.
 */
export const ISLAND_SCALE = 0.85;

/**
 * The measured local box of an item's model.
 *
 * `scale` must be the scale the piece is actually DRAWN at in the world it lives in — indoor
 * furniture at {@link INTERIOR_SCALE}, island pieces at {@link ISLAND_SCALE} — because a footprint
 * measured at the wrong scale is worse than none: it is a plausible number that is wrong by a
 * constant factor, which is exactly the kind of error an audit is supposed to catch rather than
 * commit.
 */
export function footprintOf(itemId: string, scale = INTERIOR_SCALE): Box | null {
  const item = ALL_ITEMS.find((i) => i.id === itemId);
  if (!item) return null;
  const box = new THREE.Box3();
  walk(
    React.createElement(FurnitureModel, { name: item.name, item, scale }),
    new THREE.Matrix4(),
    box,
  );
  if (box.isEmpty()) return null;
  return {
    minX: box.min.x, maxX: box.max.x,
    minY: box.min.y, maxY: box.max.y,
    minZ: box.min.z, maxZ: box.max.z,
  };
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ real scene graphs */

/**
 * The geometry classes the procedural models are built from.
 *
 * Deliberately an explicit map rather than `(THREE as any)[type]`: an audit that silently
 * accepted a geometry it had never seen would report a collider measured off an incomplete
 * model, which is worse than reporting nothing. {@link buildModelObject3D} records anything
 * missing in {@link unknownGeometries} so the caller can fail on it.
 */
const GEO_CTORS: Record<string, new (...args: any[]) => THREE.BufferGeometry> = {
  boxGeometry: THREE.BoxGeometry,
  planeGeometry: THREE.PlaneGeometry,
  cylinderGeometry: THREE.CylinderGeometry,
  coneGeometry: THREE.ConeGeometry,
  sphereGeometry: THREE.SphereGeometry,
  circleGeometry: THREE.CircleGeometry,
  ringGeometry: THREE.RingGeometry,
  torusGeometry: THREE.TorusGeometry,
  capsuleGeometry: THREE.CapsuleGeometry,
  dodecahedronGeometry: THREE.DodecahedronGeometry,
  icosahedronGeometry: THREE.IcosahedronGeometry,
  octahedronGeometry: THREE.OctahedronGeometry,
  tetrahedronGeometry: THREE.TetrahedronGeometry,
};

/**
 * Builds a REAL `THREE.Object3D` for an item's model, with real geometries and materials.
 *
 * {@link footprintOf} above answers "how big is the box" by arithmetic on the React tree; this
 * answers the harder question, "what would the shipping `measureFootprint` produce", by handing
 * that function the same kind of scene graph the renderer would. It is what lets the collider
 * audit test the code players run rather than a re-implementation of it — the distinction that
 * matters most for a rule whose whole promise is "the collider is the model".
 *
 * Materials carry only the three properties collision looks at (`depthWrite`, `blending`,
 * `transparent`), because those are what separate a solid from a drawn effect.
 */
export function buildModelObject3D(itemId: string, scale = INTERIOR_SCALE): THREE.Object3D | null {
  const item = ALL_ITEMS.find((i) => i.id === itemId);
  if (!item) return null;

  const root = new THREE.Group();
  const build = (node: any, parent: THREE.Object3D): void => {
    if (node == null || typeof node === 'boolean' || typeof node === 'string' || typeof node === 'number') return;
    if (Array.isArray(node)) { node.forEach((n) => build(n, parent)); return; }
    if (!React.isValidElement(node)) return;

    const type: any = (node as any).type;
    const props: any = (node as any).props ?? {};

    if (type === React.Fragment) { build(props.children, parent); return; }
    if (typeof type === 'function') {
      build(renderComponent(type, props), parent);
      return;
    }
    if (typeof type !== 'string') return;

    if (type.endsWith('Geometry')) {
      const Ctor = GEO_CTORS[type];
      if (!Ctor) { unknownGeometries.add(type); return; }
      const mesh = parent as THREE.Mesh;
      if ((mesh as any).isMesh) mesh.geometry = new Ctor(...(props.args ?? []));
      return;
    }
    if (type.endsWith('Material')) {
      const mesh = parent as THREE.Mesh;
      if ((mesh as any).isMesh) {
        mesh.material = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({
          depthWrite: props.depthWrite !== false,
          transparent: !!props.transparent,
          blending: props.blending ?? THREE.NormalBlending,
        });
      }
      return;
    }

    const obj: THREE.Object3D = type === 'mesh' ? new THREE.Mesh() : new THREE.Group();
    const pos = toVec3(props.position, 0);
    const rot = toVec3(props.rotation, 0);
    const scl = toVec3(props.scale, 1);
    obj.position.copy(pos);
    obj.rotation.set(rot.x, rot.y, rot.z);
    obj.scale.copy(scl);
    if (props.visible === false) obj.visible = false;
    if (props.userData) obj.userData = props.userData;
    parent.add(obj);
    build(props.children, obj);
  };

  build(React.createElement(FurnitureModel, { name: item.name, item, scale }), root);
  new THREE.Scene().add(root);
  root.updateMatrixWorld(true);
  // A mesh whose geometry never arrived (an unknown primitive) must not read as an empty solid.
  root.traverse((o) => {
    const m = o as THREE.Mesh;
    if ((m as any).isMesh && !m.geometry) m.visible = false;
  });
  return root;
}
```
