## scripts/pack-game.mjs

```mjs
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * Packs the whole game into a single downloadable .zip that another person -
 * or another AI - can open, understand and actually run without hitting bugs.
 *
 * Supersedes the older pack-for-ai.cjs / bundle-for-ai.cjs pair. What those
 * missed, and why this exists:
 *
 *   1. They packed whatever was on disk, including a tree with unresolved git
 *      merge-conflict markers in it - the resulting zip could not build at all.
 *      This script REFUSES to pack unless the tree typechecks and builds.
 *   2. They stripped every binary by extension, which silently dropped
 *      blender-reference/player-model-reference.glb (a real source asset).
 *   3. They packed firebase-applet-config.json verbatim, leaking the project's
 *      real Firebase credentials into a file meant to be handed out.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node scripts/pack-game.mjs                 # verify, then pack
 *   node scripts/pack-game.mjs --skip-build    # skip vite build (still typechecks)
 *   node scripts/pack-game.mjs --keep-secrets  # pack the real Firebase config
 */

import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const ROOT = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
const OUT_DIR = path.join(ROOT, 'package-out');
const BUNDLE_NAME = 'island-fitness-ai';

const argv = new Set(process.argv.slice(2));
const SKIP_BUILD = argv.has('--skip-build');
const KEEP_SECRETS = argv.has('--keep-secrets');

/** Directories never worth shipping: installed deps, VCS, build scratch, prior outputs. */
const EXCLUDE_DIRS = new Set([
  'node_modules', '.git', 'dist', 'package-out', 'temp_ai_pack', '.vscode', '.idea',
]);

/**
 * Files excluded by exact name. `.env` variants hold real API keys; the
 * project-source.zip / project-full-source.md / pack-for-ai.cjs family are
 * stale artifacts of the superseded scripts and would just confuse a reader
 * about which entry point is current.
 */
const EXCLUDE_FILES = new Set([
  'project-source.zip', 'project-full-source.md', 'pack-for-ai.cjs',
  'pack-for-ai.js', 'bundle-for-ai.cjs', 'README_AI.md', '.env', '.env.local',
  '.DS_Store',
]);

/** Extensions that are real source assets and must survive packing (see reason #2 above). */
const BINARY_KEEP_EXTS = new Set(['.glb', '.gltf', '.png', '.jpg', '.jpeg', '.ico', '.woff', '.woff2', '.ttf', '.mp3', '.wav', '.ogg']);

/** Extensions that are text and therefore safe to inline into FULL_SOURCE.md. */
const TEXT_EXTS = new Set(['.ts', '.tsx', '.js', '.jsx', '.mjs', '.cjs', '.css', '.html', '.json', '.md', '.rules', '.example', '.txt', '.yml', '.yaml']);

/**
 * Hand-written notes on the files a newcomer needs oriented first. Anything not
 * listed still gets packed and inventoried, just without a description - this
 * is a reading order, not a manifest of everything.
 */
const FILE_ROLES = {
  'index.html': 'Vite HTML entry. Mounts #root and loads src/main.tsx.',
  'server.ts': 'Express host. In dev it wraps Vite as middleware on port 3000; in prod it serves dist/. Also owns POST /api/shop/chat, the Gemini-backed shop assistant.',
  'vite.config.ts': 'Vite config. Note the usePolling watcher (the repo lives on OneDrive, where native FS events are unreliable) and the manual vendor chunk split.',
  'src/main.tsx': 'React root. Wraps <App/> in an ErrorBoundary that renders the error + component stack on screen instead of a blank page.',
  'src/App.tsx': 'Top-level view router and persistent HUD chrome. Chooses between Scene and the full-screen views (Shop, Fitness, Tracker, Dressing Room, Building Interior).',
  'src/types.ts': 'Shared domain types: UserProfile, ShopItem, PlacedItem, WorkoutLog, View enum, ItemCategory.',
  'src/index.css': 'Tailwind entry AND the authoritative GLOBAL Z-INDEX LAYER SYSTEM. Read the comment block at the top before positioning anything.',
  'src/context/AppContext.tsx': 'Global state: profile, inventory, equipped items, current view, UI flags. Backed by Firestore or localStorage depending on auth mode.',
  'src/lib/firebase.ts': 'Firebase wrapper AND a full localStorage-backed Firestore shim. When the config is a placeholder or anonymous auth fails, the app transparently runs in Local Guest Mode - this is why it boots with no credentials.',
  'src/lib/playerBus.ts': 'Non-React per-frame state bus between the 3D layer and HUD overlays, plus clampFrameDelta() - the tab-resume delta guard that stops the camera spinning after a tab switch.',
  'src/lib/soundUtils.ts': 'All audio. Every effect is synthesized live with the Web Audio API (no sound files at all), including the layered swim ambience.',
  'src/constants/world.ts': 'Single source of truth for ocean surface / swim body world-Y. Ocean, Avatar, Weather and Fish must all read these, never re-literal them.',
  'src/components/Three/Scene.tsx': 'The R3F Canvas and scene graph root: lighting, island, ocean, sky, weather, and every 3D actor.',
  'src/components/Three/Avatar.tsx': 'Player character: procedural mesh plus the movement/animation state machine (walk, run, several swim poses, hammock, emotes).',
  'src/components/Three/CameraController.tsx': 'Camera. First/third-person blending, collision, and the free-fly build-mode rig.',
  'src/components/Three/characterMovement.ts': 'Input-to-motion math shared by the avatar: acceleration, terrain and water height sampling, collision.',
  'src/components/Three/Fish.tsx': 'Instanced fish schools circling the island shallows.',
  'src/components/Three/Ocean.tsx': 'Ocean surface: custom GLSL wave displacement, shoreline foam, depth tinting.',
  'src/components/UI/MiniMap.tsx': 'Canvas-drawn minimap. Reads live position from playerBus (or the build-mode camera when that is active).',
  'src/components/UI/HudFrame.tsx': 'Layout primitive that assigns HUD elements to the shared safe-area regions.',
  'firestore.rules': 'Deployed Firestore security rules. DRAFT_firestore.rules is a work-in-progress variant, not what is live.',
  'metadata.json': 'AI Studio applet manifest: display name, requested camera permission, server-side Gemini capability flag.',
  'firebase-applet-config.json': 'Firebase client config. Sanitized to placeholders in this bundle so the app boots straight into Local Guest Mode.',
};

const log = (msg) => console.log(msg);
const fail = (msg) => { console.error(`\n[FAIL] ${msg}\n`); process.exit(1); };

/** Walks the project, honouring the exclude sets. Returns repo-relative POSIX paths. */
function collectFiles(dir = ROOT, acc = []) {
  for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
    if (entry.isDirectory()) {
      if (EXCLUDE_DIRS.has(entry.name)) continue;
      collectFiles(path.join(dir, entry.name), acc);
    } else if (entry.isFile()) {
      if (EXCLUDE_FILES.has(entry.name)) continue;
      const rel = path.relative(ROOT, path.join(dir, entry.name)).split(path.sep).join('/');
      acc.push(rel);
    }
  }
  return acc;
}

function isTextFile(rel) {
  const ext = path.extname(rel).toLowerCase();
  if (TEXT_EXTS.has(ext)) return true;
  // Extensionless dotfiles like .gitignore are text too.
  return ext === '' && path.basename(rel).startsWith('.');
}

/**
 * Guard #1 - the bug that made the previous bundles unusable. An unresolved
 * merge leaves `<<<<<<<` / `=======` / `>>>>>>>` at column 0; esbuild dies on
 * them, so a zip containing them can never run.
 */
function assertNoConflictMarkers(files) {
  const marker = /^(<{7}|={7}|>{7})( |\r?$)/m;
  const dirty = [];
  for (const rel of files) {
    if (!isTextFile(rel)) continue;
    const body = fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, rel), 'utf8');
    if (marker.test(body)) dirty.push(rel);
  }
  if (dirty.length) {
    fail(`Unresolved git merge-conflict markers found in:\n  - ${dirty.join('\n  - ')}\n`
      + `A bundle containing these cannot build. Resolve the merge first.`);
  }
  log('  [ok] no merge-conflict markers');
}

/** Runs an npm script through the local toolchain, streaming output on failure only. */
function runNpm(script, label) {
  const npmCli = path.join(path.dirname(process.execPath), 'node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js');
  const args = fs.existsSync(npmCli) ? [npmCli, 'run', script] : null;
  try {
    if (args) execFileSync(process.execPath, args, { cwd: ROOT, stdio: 'pipe' });
    else execFileSync('npm', ['run', script], { cwd: ROOT, stdio: 'pipe', shell: true });
    log(`  [ok] ${label}`);
  } catch (err) {
    const out = `${err.stdout ?? ''}${err.stderr ?? ''}`.trim();
    fail(`${label} failed:\n${out}`);
  }
}

function rmrf(p) { fs.rmSync(p, { recursive: true, force: true }); }

function copyInto(rel, stageRoot) {
  const dest = path.join(stageRoot, rel);
  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(dest), { recursive: true });
  fs.copyFileSync(path.join(ROOT, rel), dest);
}

/** Renders an indented directory tree from the packed file list. */
function renderTree(files) {
  const root = {};
  for (const rel of files) {
    let node = root;
    for (const part of rel.split('/')) node = (node[part] ??= {});
  }
  const lines = [];
  const walk = (node, prefix) => {
    const keys = Object.keys(node).sort((a, b) => {
      const aDir = Object.keys(node[a]).length > 0;
      const bDir = Object.keys(node[b]).length > 0;
      if (aDir !== bDir) return aDir ? -1 : 1;
      return a.localeCompare(b);
    });
    keys.forEach((key, i) => {
      const last = i === keys.length - 1;
      const isDir = Object.keys(node[key]).length > 0;
      lines.push(`${prefix}${last ? '└── ' : '├── '}${key}${isDir ? '/' : ''}`);
      if (isDir) walk(node[key], prefix + (last ? '    ' : '│   '));
    });
  };
  walk(root, '');
  return lines.join('\n');
}

function detectStack() {
  const pkg = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'package.json'), 'utf8'));
  const deps = { ...pkg.dependencies, ...pkg.devDependencies };
  const pick = (name, label) => (deps[name] ? `${label} ${deps[name].replace(/^[\^~]/, '')}` : null);
  return [
    pick('react', 'React'), pick('typescript', 'TypeScript'), pick('vite', 'Vite'),
    pick('three', 'Three.js'), pick('@react-three/fiber', 'react-three-fiber'),
    pick('@react-three/drei', 'drei'), pick('tailwindcss', 'Tailwind CSS'),
    pick('firebase', 'Firebase'), pick('express', 'Express'),
    pick('@google/genai', '@google/genai'), pick('@mediapipe/tasks-vision', 'MediaPipe Tasks Vision'),
    pick('motion', 'Motion'), pick('recharts', 'Recharts'),
  ].filter(Boolean);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

log(`\nPacking ${BUNDLE_NAME}\n`);
log('Verifying the tree is shippable...');

const files = collectFiles();
assertNoConflictMarkers(files);
runNpm('lint', 'typecheck (tsc --noEmit)');
if (SKIP_BUILD) log('  [skip] vite build (--skip-build)');
else runNpm('build', 'production build (vite build)');

log('\nStaging files...');
const stageParent = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'pack-game-'));
const stage = path.join(stageParent, BUNDLE_NAME);
fs.mkdirSync(stage, { recursive: true });

let binaryCount = 0;
for (const rel of files) {
  copyInto(rel, stage);
  if (BINARY_KEEP_EXTS.has(path.extname(rel).toLowerCase())) binaryCount++;
}
log(`  [ok] ${files.length} files (${binaryCount} binary asset${binaryCount === 1 ? '' : 's'} preserved)`);

// Sanitize the Firebase config so the bundle boots into Local Guest Mode and
// carries none of this project's real credentials. firebase.ts recognises these
// exact placeholder values and skips its connection probe entirely.
if (!KEEP_SECRETS) {
  const placeholder = {
    projectId: 'remixed-project-id',
    appId: 'remixed-app-id',
    apiKey: 'remixed-api-key',
    authDomain: 'remixed-project-id.firebaseapp.com',
    firestoreDatabaseId: '(default)',
    storageBucket: 'remixed-project-id.firebasestorage.app',
    messagingSenderId: '000000000000',
    measurementId: '',
  };
  fs.writeFileSync(
    path.join(stage, 'firebase-applet-config.json'),
    `${JSON.stringify(placeholder, null, 2)}\n`,
    'utf8',
  );
  log('  [ok] firebase-applet-config.json replaced with placeholders');
} else {
  log('  [WARN] --keep-secrets: real Firebase credentials are in this bundle');
}

// Ship the compiled output too, so the game can be viewed with a static server
// and no build step. Named prebuilt-dist/ so it never shadows a fresh `dist/`.
if (!SKIP_BUILD && fs.existsSync(path.join(ROOT, 'dist'))) {
  fs.cpSync(path.join(ROOT, 'dist'), path.join(stage, 'prebuilt-dist'), { recursive: true });
  log('  [ok] prebuilt-dist/ included');
}

log('\nGenerating AI-readable docs...');
const stack = detectStack();
const tree = renderTree(files);

const manifest = {
  name: 'Motu',
  description: JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'metadata.json'), 'utf8')).description,
  generatedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
  entryPoints: {
    html: 'index.html',
    client: 'src/main.tsx',
    clientRoot: 'src/App.tsx',
    server: 'server.ts',
    scene3d: 'src/components/Three/Scene.tsx',
  },
  runCommands: {
    install: 'npm install',
    dev: 'npm run dev',
    devUrl: 'http://localhost:3000',
    typecheck: 'npm run lint',
    build: 'npm run build',
    servePrebuilt: 'npx serve prebuilt-dist',
  },
  techStack: stack,
  requiresCredentialsToRun: false,
  authMode: 'Falls back to Local Guest Mode (localStorage) when Firebase is unconfigured.',
  optionalCredentials: {
    GEMINI_API_KEY: 'Enables POST /api/shop/chat (the AI shop assistant). Without it that one endpoint returns 500; everything else works.',
    'firebase-applet-config.json': 'Replace placeholders to persist to a real Firestore instead of localStorage.',
  },
  files: files.map((rel) => {
    const abs = path.join(ROOT, rel);
    const stat = fs.statSync(abs);
    const entry = { path: rel, bytes: stat.size };
    if (isTextFile(rel)) {
      entry.lines = fs.readFileSync(abs, 'utf8').split('\n').length;
    } else {
      entry.binary = true;
    }
    if (FILE_ROLES[rel]) entry.role = FILE_ROLES[rel];
    return entry;
  }),
};
fs.writeFileSync(path.join(stage, 'PROJECT_MANIFEST.json'), `${JSON.stringify(manifest, null, 2)}\n`, 'utf8');
log('  [ok] PROJECT_MANIFEST.json');

const readingOrder = Object.entries(FILE_ROLES)
  .filter(([rel]) => files.includes(rel))
  .map(([rel, role]) => `| \`${rel}\` | ${role} |`)
  .join('\n');

const aiDoc = `# AI_START_HERE — Motu

Read this file first. It is written for an AI or developer who has never seen
this project, and it covers everything needed to run the game and change it
without breaking it.

${manifest.description}

## 1. Run it

Requires Node.js 20+ (developed on 24.x). Nothing else — no database, no API
key, no account.

\`\`\`bash
npm install
npm run dev          # http://localhost:3000
\`\`\`

\`npm run dev\` starts \`server.ts\`, an Express host that mounts Vite as
middleware, so the API route and the client are served from the same origin and
port. Running bare \`vite\` also works for pure front-end changes, but then
\`POST /api/shop/chat\` 404s.

To view the shipped build with no build step:

\`\`\`bash
npx serve prebuilt-dist
\`\`\`

Do **not** open \`index.html\` or \`prebuilt-dist/index.html\` from the
filesystem. It is an ES-module app; \`file://\` origins block module loading and
you get a blank page. Always go through a server.

## 2. It boots with no credentials — that is intentional, not a bug

\`firebase-applet-config.json\` in this bundle holds placeholder values. On
detecting them, \`src/lib/firebase.ts\` skips its connection probe and the app
runs in **Local Guest Mode**: a hand-written localStorage shim implements the
Firestore surface the app uses (\`doc\`, \`getDoc\`, \`setDoc\`, \`updateDoc\`,
\`onSnapshot\`, \`increment\`, \`arrayUnion\`, \`arrayRemove\`). Progress persists in
the browser instead of the cloud.

So expect these on a clean run, and do not "fix" them:

- Console: \`Firebase is not configured. The app will run in Local Guest Mode using localStorage.\`
- Google sign-in fails — use the guest option on the auth screen.
- \`POST /api/shop/chat\` returns 500 unless \`GEMINI_API_KEY\` is set (copy
  \`.env.example\` to \`.env\`). Only the shop chat assistant depends on it.
- One \`https://cdn.pixabay.com/...mp3\` request at first click. It is a
  throwaway used to unlock the browser audio context; offline it fails
  silently and is caught.

To point at a real backend, fill in \`firebase-applet-config.json\` with your own
Firebase web config and deploy \`firestore.rules\`.

## 3. Tech stack

${stack.map((s) => `- ${s}`).join('\n')}

## 4. Where things live

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
${readingOrder}

## 5. Invariants worth knowing before editing

These are the project's real footguns — each one has already caused a bug.

1. **Z-index is a global system, not per-component.** \`src/index.css\` opens with
   a \`GLOBAL Z-INDEX LAYER SYSTEM\` block defining Background / Game View / HUD /
   Floating Panel / Toast / Modal / Loading. Use those classes. Raising a whole
   Game View above HUD is exactly what once made the minimap invisible indoors;
   components needing to beat HUD portal to \`document.body\` instead.
2. **World heights come from \`src/constants/world.ts\`.** \`WATER_SURFACE_Y\` and
   \`SWIM_BODY_Y\` were once duplicated literals across Ocean / Avatar / Weather /
   Fish, drifted apart, and left the swim splash FX rendering below the water.
   Never re-hardcode \`-0.5\`.
3. **Per-frame cross-component state goes through \`playerBus\`, not React state
   and not \`window\`.** Player position, rotation, camera yaw, dog state and the
   interaction prompt update every frame; routing them through React would
   re-render the tree 60×/s.
4. **Always clamp \`useFrame\` deltas with \`clampFrameDelta()\`.** A hidden tab
   throttles rAF, so the first frame back can report a multi-second delta. Feeding
   that raw into a rotation rate spun the camera several full turns — that is the
   bug the helper exists to prevent.
5. **Audio is fully synthesized.** There are no audio files. \`soundUtils.ts\`
   builds every effect from Web Audio primitives (noise buffers, oscillators,
   filters). Add sounds the same way, and keep failures silent — audio is
   blocked until the first user gesture.
6. **The file watcher polls on purpose.** This project lives in a OneDrive
   folder where native FS events are unreliable, so \`vite.config.ts\` sets
   \`server.watch.usePolling\`. Removing it causes stale modules that survive a
   hard refresh.

## 6. Verifying a change

\`\`\`bash
npm run lint     # tsc --noEmit — must be clean
npm run build    # vite build — must succeed
\`\`\`

There is no test suite; these two commands are the gate. \`npm run lint\` also
catches stray git merge-conflict markers (TS1185), which is how a previously
shipped bundle turned out to be unbuildable.

## 7. Also in this bundle

- \`PROJECT_MANIFEST.json\` — machine-readable inventory: every packed file with
  size, line count and, for key files, its role.
- \`FULL_SOURCE.md\` — every text source file concatenated into one document, for
  pasting into a model with a large context window.
- \`prebuilt-dist/\` — the compiled app, ready for any static server.
- \`README.md\` — the original human-facing setup guide.
- \`security_spec.md\`, \`firestore.rules\` — data model and access rules.

## 8. Full tree

\`\`\`text
${BUNDLE_NAME}/
${tree.split('\n').map((l) => (l ? `  ${l}` : l)).join('\n')}
\`\`\`
`;
fs.writeFileSync(path.join(stage, 'AI_START_HERE.md'), aiDoc, 'utf8');
log('  [ok] AI_START_HERE.md');

/**
 * Kept in the bundle (npm ci needs it) but never inlined into FULL_SOURCE.md:
 * a quarter-megabyte of resolved dependency hashes is pure noise in a document
 * whose entire purpose is to be read into a model's context window.
 */
const NO_INLINE = new Set(['package-lock.json']);

let full = `# Motu — full source\n\n`
  + `Generated ${manifest.generatedAt} by scripts/pack-game.mjs.\n`
  + `Every text source file in the project, concatenated. Binary assets are listed but not inlined,\n`
  + `and ${[...NO_INLINE].map((f) => `\`${f}\``).join(', ')} is omitted as noise (it is still in the .zip).\n`
  + `Start with AI_START_HERE.md for orientation.\n`;
const textFiles = files.filter((f) => isTextFile(f) && !NO_INLINE.has(f));
for (const rel of textFiles) {
  const body = fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, rel), 'utf8');
  const lang = path.extname(rel).replace('.', '') || 'text';
  full += `\n\n---\n\n## ${rel}\n\n\`\`\`${lang}\n${body.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n').replace(/\`\`\`/g, '\\`\\`\\`')}\n\`\`\`\n`;
}
const binaries = files.filter((f) => !isTextFile(f));
if (binaries.length) {
  full += `\n\n---\n\n## Binary assets (not inlined)\n\n`
    + binaries.map((b) => `- \`${b}\` (${fs.statSync(path.join(ROOT, b)).size} bytes)`).join('\n')
    + '\n';
}
fs.writeFileSync(path.join(stage, 'FULL_SOURCE.md'), full, 'utf8');
log(`  [ok] FULL_SOURCE.md (${textFiles.length} files inlined)`);

log('\nCompressing...');
fs.mkdirSync(OUT_DIR, { recursive: true });
// Local time, not toISOString() - the stamp is read by a human looking for the
// file they just produced, and a UTC name is off by the timezone offset.
const now = new Date();
const pad = (n) => String(n).padStart(2, '0');
const stamp = `${now.getFullYear()}${pad(now.getMonth() + 1)}${pad(now.getDate())}`
  + `-${pad(now.getHours())}${pad(now.getMinutes())}`;
const zipPath = path.join(OUT_DIR, `${BUNDLE_NAME}-${stamp}.zip`);
rmrf(zipPath);

try {
  if (process.platform === 'win32') {
    execFileSync('powershell', [
      '-NoProfile', '-NonInteractive', '-Command',
      `Compress-Archive -Path '${stage.replace(/'/g, "''")}' -DestinationPath '${zipPath.replace(/'/g, "''")}' -Force`,
    ], { stdio: 'pipe' });
  } else {
    execFileSync('zip', ['-qr', zipPath, BUNDLE_NAME], { cwd: stageParent, stdio: 'pipe' });
  }
} catch (err) {
  fail(`Compression failed: ${`${err.stdout ?? ''}${err.stderr ?? ''}`.trim() || err.message}`);
}

// Also drop the generated docs beside the zip, unzipped. Uploading a .zip to a
// chat assistant does not work - nothing extracts it - so the file you actually
// hand to a model has to be reachable without unpacking anything first.
const LOOSE_DOCS = ['FULL_SOURCE.md', 'AI_START_HERE.md', 'PROJECT_MANIFEST.json'];
for (const doc of LOOSE_DOCS) fs.copyFileSync(path.join(stage, doc), path.join(OUT_DIR, doc));

rmrf(stageParent);

const mb = (p) => (fs.statSync(p).size / 1024 / 1024).toFixed(2);
const rel = (p) => path.relative(ROOT, p).split(path.sep).join('/');
log(`\nDone.`);
log(`  ${rel(zipPath)} (${mb(zipPath)} MB)  <- the whole runnable project`);
for (const doc of LOOSE_DOCS) {
  const p = path.join(OUT_DIR, doc);
  log(`  ${rel(p)} (${mb(p)} MB)`);
}
// ~3.6 chars/token is a reasonable estimate for source code.
const tokens = Math.round(fs.statSync(path.join(OUT_DIR, 'FULL_SOURCE.md')).size / 3.6 / 1000);
log(`\nFULL_SOURCE.md is roughly ${tokens}k tokens - feed that one to a model, not the .zip.\n`);

```

## scripts/setup-hooks.mjs

```mjs
// Points git at the version-controlled hooks in scripts/hooks.
//
// Run automatically by the `prepare` npm lifecycle script, so a fresh clone gets the hooks from
// its first `npm install` with nothing to remember. That indirection is the whole point:
// .git/hooks is not version controlled, so hooks written there guard one working copy while
// everyone else commits unchecked - which is how four blocks of conflict markers reached main.
//
// Idempotent, and silent about being unable to run: `npm install` inside a tarball or a CI cache
// warm-up has no .git, and that is not a failure worth breaking an install over.

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

const HOOKS_PATH = 'scripts/hooks';

const inRepo = spawnSync('git', ['rev-parse', '--git-dir'], { encoding: 'utf8' });
if (inRepo.status !== 0) {
  console.log('setup-hooks: not a git repository, skipping.');
  process.exit(0);
}

const current = spawnSync('git', ['config', '--get', 'core.hooksPath'], { encoding: 'utf8' });
if (current.status === 0 && current.stdout.trim() === HOOKS_PATH) {
  process.exit(0);
}

const set = spawnSync('git', ['config', 'core.hooksPath', HOOKS_PATH], { encoding: 'utf8' });
if (set.status !== 0) {
  console.log('setup-hooks: could not set core.hooksPath, skipping.');
  process.exit(0);
}

console.log(`setup-hooks: core.hooksPath -> ${HOOKS_PATH}`);

```

## scripts/split-character-glb.mjs

```mjs
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * SPLIT THE HAND-MADE CHARACTER into the six part files the model layer loads.
 *
 *   npm run split:character
 *
 * IN   blender-reference/authored-character-source.glb   — the whole body, one .glb, as
 *                                                          exported from Blender
 * OUT  public/models/character/{head,torso,arm-left,arm-right,leg-left,leg-right}.glb
 *      plus a block of rig numbers printed to stdout for constants/characterRig.ts
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * WHY A SCRIPT AND NOT SIX MANUAL EXPORTS
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 *
 * The six parts are not six independent assets — they are one body cut along its joints, and
 * every cut has to agree with the rig about where that joint is. Cutting by hand means
 * re-doing six pivot placements, two mirrors and one unit conversion every time the body is
 * touched, and getting one of them wrong is the import bug the checklist calls out: a limb
 * that looks correct standing still and detaches the moment the character walks.
 *
 * Doing it here means the source stays ONE Blender file, the cut is reproducible, and the
 * numbers the rig needs are MEASURED off the asset instead of typed twice.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * WHAT IT DOES, AND WHY EACH STEP EXISTS
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 *
 * 1. NORMALISE THE HEIGHT. `RIG_ENVELOPE` says the character is 0.9617 LOCAL from sole to
 *    crown, and every door, camera offset and piece of furniture on the island was tuned
 *    against that. The source model is whatever height it happens to be, so a single uniform
 *    scale + a lift puts its sole on `soleY` and its crown on the envelope. Uniform, so the
 *    modeller's proportions survive untouched — this is a change of units, not of design.
 *
 * 2. RE-PIVOT ONTO THE JOINT. Each part is re-based so its origin is the point the
 *    controller rotates. Head and torso take the empties as authored. Limbs take the empty
 *    moved onto the limb's OWN axis: the source arm and leg meshes sit a couple of
 *    centimetres inboard of their empties, and a joint off the limb's axis both swings wrong
 *    and — the visible half — puts every lathed wearable (trousers, sleeves, shoes) beside
 *    the limb instead of around it. The geometry is compensated by the same amount, so the
 *    rest pose on screen is identical; only the pivot moves.
 *
 * 3. MIRROR THE RIGHT SIDE FROM THE LEFT. The source carries hand-duplicated right limbs
 *    that are a few millimetres off a true mirror. Deriving them here makes the character
 *    symmetric and halves what has to be modelled.
 *
 * 4. FLATTEN THE REST ROTATION OUT OF THE ARMS. The arms are authored splayed. That angle is
 *    a POSE, not geometry: the controller writes `rotation` on the arm joint every frame and
 *    would overwrite it. It is therefore reported here and lives in slots.tsx as the part's
 *    `transform`, which is applied to the mesh AND to anything worn on the arm — one number,
 *    one place. The exported arm .glb is in plain shoulder space, hanging straight down.
 *
 * Nothing here is destructive: the source .glb is only read.
 */

import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';
import { GLTFExporter } from 'three/examples/jsm/exporters/GLTFExporter.js';

// GLTFExporter's binary path reads its merged buffer through FileReader, which only exists
// in browsers. Node has Blob#arrayBuffer natively, so delegating to it is enough — same
// shim as scripts/export-player-reference.mjs, which wrote the reference this model started
// from.
if (typeof globalThis.FileReader === 'undefined') {
  globalThis.FileReader = class {
    readAsArrayBuffer(blob) {
      blob.arrayBuffer().then((buf) => {
        this.result = buf;
        this.onloadend?.();
      });
    }
  };
}

const ROOT = path.dirname(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)));
const SOURCE = path.join(ROOT, 'blender-reference', 'authored-character-source.glb');
const OUT_DIR = path.join(ROOT, 'public', 'models', 'character');

/**
 * The envelope, restated. Deliberately duplicated from constants/characterRig.ts rather than
 * imported: that file is TypeScript with a module-load assertion in it, and this script has
 * to be runnable with plain `node`. Two numbers, and the script prints what it produced so a
 * drift between them is visible in the output rather than silent.
 */
const TARGET_LOCAL_HEIGHT = 0.9617;
const TARGET_SOLE_Y = -0.005;

/** The one node in the source scene that is the real body. See the duplicate note below. */
const BODY_ROOT = 'PlayerModel_Base';

/**
 * Whether to centre the two eyes on the face's centreline. See {@link placeEyes}.
 *
 * The one step in this script that changes how the character LOOKS rather than what space it is
 * in, so it is the one step that is a flag. Turn it off to get the face exactly as authored.
 */
const SYMMETRISE_EYES = true;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// LOAD
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const buffer = fs.readFileSync(SOURCE);
const arrayBuffer = buffer.buffer.slice(buffer.byteOffset, buffer.byteOffset + buffer.byteLength);

const gltf = await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
  new GLTFLoader().parse(arrayBuffer, '', resolve, reject);
});

const scene = gltf.scene;
scene.updateMatrixWorld(true);

/**
 * The body, picked by exact name.
 *
 * The source file also contains a scatter of `PlayerModel_Base.001` … `.009` copies — the
 * leftovers of duplicating limbs while modelling, most of them empty. Selecting the one
 * un-suffixed root is what keeps those out, and is why the parts below can simply walk the
 * hierarchy instead of naming individual meshes.
 */
const body = scene.getObjectByName(BODY_ROOT);
if (!body) {
  console.error(`[split] no object named "${BODY_ROOT}" in ${path.relative(ROOT, SOURCE)}.`);
  console.error('[split] the source must keep the reference export\'s hierarchy — see docs/character-authored-model.md.');
  process.exit(1);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MEASURE
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Every mesh under an object, in scene order. */
function meshesUnder(object) {
  const out = [];
  object.traverse((node) => {
    if (node.isMesh) out.push(node);
  });
  return out;
}

/** World-space bounds of a set of meshes. */
function boundsOf(meshes) {
  const box = new THREE.Box3();
  for (const mesh of meshes) box.expandByObject(mesh);
  return box;
}

const bodyMeshes = meshesUnder(body);
if (bodyMeshes.length === 0) {
  console.error(`[split] "${BODY_ROOT}" contains no meshes.`);
  process.exit(1);
}

const bodyBox = boundsOf(bodyMeshes);
const sourceSole = bodyBox.min.y;
const sourceCrown = bodyBox.max.y;
const sourceHeight = sourceCrown - sourceSole;

/**
 * The unit fix, as one uniform scale and one lift.
 *
 *   y_out = SCALE * y_in + LIFT      (and x/z simply scale, the centreline does not move)
 *
 * Solved from the two things the rig actually promises: the sole lands on `soleY` and the
 * total height is the envelope's. Everything else about the model's shape is left alone.
 */
const SCALE = TARGET_LOCAL_HEIGHT / sourceHeight;
const LIFT = TARGET_SOLE_Y - SCALE * sourceSole;

/** Source-space point → normalised LOCAL space. */
const toLocal = (v) => new THREE.Vector3(v.x * SCALE, v.y * SCALE + LIFT, v.z * SCALE);

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// PARTS
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * A joint's world frame: position and rotation, and DELIBERATELY not scale.
 *
 * A joint is a rigid frame, so the part space it defines has to be one too. Inverting the
 * node's full `matrixWorld` instead would be right for a bare empty and silently wrong the
 * moment the pivot node carries the geometry as well — the torso empty in this source IS the
 * torso mesh, scaled 0.77, and dividing that scale back out again exports a torso 30% too
 * wide with nothing to show that anything happened.
 */
function jointFrame(node) {
  return new THREE.Matrix4().compose(
    node.getWorldPosition(new THREE.Vector3()),
    node.getWorldQuaternion(new THREE.Quaternion()),
    new THREE.Vector3(1, 1, 1),
  );
}

/**
 * Where a part's joint sits, given the empty the modeller placed and the meshes that hang
 * off it.
 *
 * `onLimbAxis` is step 2 of the header note: for an arm or a leg, the returned joint is the
 * empty slid along its own local X onto the centre of the limb it drives. For the head and
 * the torso the empty is already right — a neck pivot is not on any axis and the torso's
 * empty IS its centre.
 */
function jointFor(pivotNode, meshes, { onLimbAxis }) {
  const world = new THREE.Vector3().setFromMatrixPosition(pivotNode.matrixWorld);
  if (!onLimbAxis) return { world, axisOffsetX: 0 };

  // The limb's own axis, measured in the PIVOT's local frame so a splayed arm is measured
  // along the arm rather than along the world.
  const toPivotLocal = jointFrame(pivotNode).invert();
  const box = new THREE.Box3();
  for (const mesh of meshes) {
    const geo = mesh.geometry.clone();
    geo.applyMatrix4(new THREE.Matrix4().multiplyMatrices(toPivotLocal, mesh.matrixWorld));
    geo.computeBoundingBox();
    box.union(geo.boundingBox);
    geo.dispose();
  }
  const axisOffsetX = (box.min.x + box.max.x) / 2;
  return {
    world: world.clone().add(
      new THREE.Vector3(axisOffsetX, 0, 0).applyQuaternion(
        pivotNode.getWorldQuaternion(new THREE.Quaternion()),
      ),
    ),
    axisOffsetX,
  };
}

/**
 * One part's geometry, in normalised PART space: origin on the joint, the pivot's rest
 * rotation taken out, the unit fix applied.
 *
 * Returns plain THREE.Mesh objects with fresh materials — the source ones are re-created
 * rather than reused so the six output files do not share mutable state, and so the
 * duplicate materials in the source (three identical skins, two identical cloths) collapse
 * into one per colour per file.
 */
function bakePart(pivotNode, meshes, axisOffsetX, { mirror = false } = {}) {
  const toPivotLocal = jointFrame(pivotNode).invert();
  const materials = new Map();

  return meshes.map((mesh) => {
    const geo = mesh.geometry.clone();
    geo.applyMatrix4(new THREE.Matrix4().multiplyMatrices(toPivotLocal, mesh.matrixWorld));
    geo.translate(-axisOffsetX, 0, 0);
    geo.scale(SCALE, SCALE, SCALE);
    if (mirror) {
      // A mirror is a negative-determinant transform: three fixes the normals through the
      // normal matrix, but nothing fixes the triangle winding, and a wound-backwards face is
      // culled — the classic "the right arm is invisible from outside" export.
      geo.scale(-1, 1, 1);
      flipWinding(geo);
    }
    repairOrientation(geo, mesh.name);
    geo.computeBoundingBox();

    const source = Array.isArray(mesh.material) ? mesh.material[0] : mesh.material;
    const name = materialName(source);
    if (!materials.has(name)) {
      materials.set(
        name,
        new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({
          name,
          color: source.color.clone(),
          roughness: source.roughness,
          metalness: source.metalness,
        }),
      );
    }
    const out = new THREE.Mesh(geo, materials.get(name));
    out.name = mesh.name;
    return out;
  });
}

/**
 * Every surface that had to be turned right side out, for the warning at the end.
 * @type {string[]}
 */
const repairs = [];

/**
 * Changes to how the character LOOKS, as opposed to defects repaired.
 *
 * Kept apart from `repairs` deliberately. A defect is always wrong and the script is entitled to
 * fix it; an adjustment is a decision someone made, and reporting the two in one list would let
 * a judgement hide inside a maintenance message.
 * @type {string[]}
 */
const adjustments = [];

/**
 * Turns an inside-out surface the right way round — and says so.
 *
 * A mesh mirrored in Blender with a negative scale that was applied without recalculating
 * normals comes out inverted in BOTH senses, and each has its own symptom, which is why they
 * are two separate checks rather than one:
 *
 *   WINDING   decides which side is the front face. Backwards, the surface is culled: it is
 *             there in the model viewer, invisible in the game, and visible again from inside
 *             the head. Signed volume by the divergence theorem is negative exactly when a
 *             closed mesh is wound inward, so this is measured rather than guessed.
 *   NORMALS   decide the shading. Backwards, the surface is lit from the wrong side and reads
 *             as a black hole where a feature should be. Tested against the winding itself —
 *             the face normal the triangle order implies — so it needs no assumption about the
 *             shape being convex.
 *
 * Repaired here rather than left faithful because an invisible eye is not a design decision.
 * It is still REPORTED, because the real fix is in Blender (Mesh ▸ Normals ▸ Recalculate
 * Outside) and a defect silently patched by a build step is one that comes back.
 */
function repairOrientation(geo, label) {
  const position = geo.getAttribute('position');
  const index = geo.getIndex();
  const count = index ? index.count : position.count;
  const at = (i) => (index ? index.getX(i) : i);

  const a = new THREE.Vector3();
  const b = new THREE.Vector3();
  const c = new THREE.Vector3();

  let volume = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 3) {
    a.fromBufferAttribute(position, at(i));
    b.fromBufferAttribute(position, at(i + 1));
    c.fromBufferAttribute(position, at(i + 2));
    volume += a.dot(b.clone().cross(c)) / 6;
  }
  if (volume < 0) {
    flipWinding(geo);
    repairs.push(`${label}: triangles were wound inside-out`);
  }

  const normal = geo.getAttribute('normal');
  if (!normal) return;

  const face = new THREE.Vector3();
  const stored = new THREE.Vector3();
  let disagreeing = 0;
  let triangles = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 3) {
    const [ia, ib, ic] = [at(i), at(i + 1), at(i + 2)];
    a.fromBufferAttribute(position, ia);
    b.fromBufferAttribute(position, ib);
    c.fromBufferAttribute(position, ic);
    face.copy(c).sub(b).cross(a.clone().sub(b));
    stored.set(0, 0, 0);
    for (const v of [ia, ib, ic]) {
      stored.x += normal.getX(v);
      stored.y += normal.getY(v);
      stored.z += normal.getZ(v);
    }
    triangles += 1;
    if (face.dot(stored) < 0) disagreeing += 1;
  }
  if (disagreeing > triangles / 2) {
    for (let i = 0; i < normal.count; i += 1) {
      normal.setXYZ(i, -normal.getX(i), -normal.getY(i), -normal.getZ(i));
    }
    normal.needsUpdate = true;
    repairs.push(`${label}: normals pointed inward`);
  }
}

/** Reverses every triangle, indexed or not. */
function flipWinding(geo) {
  if (geo.index) {
    const a = geo.index.array;
    for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i += 3) {
      const t = a[i];
      a[i] = a[i + 2];
      a[i + 2] = t;
    }
    geo.index.needsUpdate = true;
    return;
  }
  for (const attr of Object.values(geo.attributes)) {
    const { array, itemSize } = attr;
    for (let i = 0; i < array.length; i += itemSize * 3) {
      for (let c = 0; c < itemSize; c += 1) {
        const t = array[i + c];
        array[i + c] = array[i + itemSize * 2 + c];
        array[i + itemSize * 2 + c] = t;
      }
    }
    attr.needsUpdate = true;
  }
}

/**
 * A material's job, from its colour. The source names are Blender's (`Material_3.002`), which
 * say nothing; these say what the surface is, which is what someone opening a part file wants
 * to know — and what a future skin-tone or shirt-colour override would key off.
 */
function materialName(material) {
  const { r, g, b } = material.color;
  const luminance = 0.2126 * r + 0.7152 * g + 0.0722 * b;
  if (luminance < 0.02) return 'Eye';
  return g > b ? 'Skin' : 'Cloth';
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// WRITE
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async function writeGlb(object, file) {
  const exporter = new GLTFExporter();
  const glb = await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    exporter.parse(object, resolve, reject, { binary: true });
  });
  fs.writeFileSync(file, Buffer.from(glb));
  return fs.statSync(file).size;
}

fs.mkdirSync(OUT_DIR, { recursive: true });

const report = [];

/** Builds, writes and records one part file. */
async function emit({ id, file, rootName, meshes, cost }) {
  const root = new THREE.Group();
  root.name = rootName;
  for (const mesh of meshes) root.add(mesh);
  root.updateMatrixWorld(true);

  const size = await writeGlb(root, path.join(OUT_DIR, file));
  const box = boundsOf(meshesUnder(root));
  report.push({ id, file, size, box, ...cost });
}

/** Triangles and mesh count, for the budget line at the end. */
function costOf(meshes) {
  let triangles = 0;
  for (const mesh of meshes) {
    const pos = mesh.geometry.getAttribute('position');
    triangles += mesh.geometry.index ? mesh.geometry.index.count / 3 : pos.count / 3;
  }
  return { triangles, meshes: meshes.length };
}

// --- head ------------------------------------------------------------------
//
// The one part that is not a flat list of meshes. Its eyes are bound to `rig.eyeL`/`rig.eyeR`
// so the controller can blink and squint them, and the controller writes `scale.y` and an
// absolute `position.y` on those refs — which means each eye has to be its OWN node, sitting
// at the eye's centre with its geometry re-based about it. An eye left inside the head mesh
// would scale about the neck.
const headPivot = body.getObjectByName('Head');
const headMeshes = meshesUnder(headPivot);
const headJoint = jointFor(headPivot, headMeshes, { onLimbAxis: false });
const headBaked = bakePart(headPivot, headMeshes, 0);

const eyes = headBaked.filter((m) => m.material.name === 'Eye');
const skull = headBaked.filter((m) => m.material.name !== 'Eye');
for (const mesh of skull) mesh.name = 'Head_Skin';

const eyeNodes = placeEyes(eyes);

/**
 * Puts each eye on its own node, and puts that node SYMMETRICALLY about the face's centreline.
 *
 * The source has the two eyes at x -0.0882 and +0.0786 — mirror images of each other in every
 * other respect (same size, same y, same z, vertex-for-vertex reflections), so the whole of the
 * asymmetry is one eye sitting further out than the other. Each is moved half the difference,
 * which centres the pair without favouring either eye's position.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * WHY THIS IS HERE AND NOT LEFT TO THE MODELLER
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 *
 * It is a JUDGEMENT, unlike the winding repair below it — an inside-out eye is invisible and
 * therefore always wrong, but a face is allowed to be asymmetric if that is what someone drew.
 * This runs because it was ASKED for. It is not a rule the splitter is entitled to on its own,
 * which is why it is a flag rather than an unconditional step: set `SYMMETRISE_EYES` to false
 * and the eyes come through exactly as authored.
 *
 * It reports what it moved, for the same reason the winding repair does: the source file still
 * has the offset, so the alignment is re-applied on every re-cut until Blender is fixed too.
 */
function placeEyes(meshes) {
  const centres = meshes.map((mesh) => {
    mesh.geometry.computeBoundingBox();
    return mesh.geometry.boundingBox.getCenter(new THREE.Vector3());
  });

  let targets = centres;
  if (SYMMETRISE_EYES && centres.length === 2) {
    // The pair's own average, mirrored: |x| from the two half-widths, y and z shared outright.
    // Averaging rather than copying one eye onto the other keeps the correction as small as it
    // can be — each eye moves half the error instead of one of them moving all of it.
    const halfWidth = (Math.abs(centres[0].x) + Math.abs(centres[1].x)) / 2;
    const y = (centres[0].y + centres[1].y) / 2;
    const z = (centres[0].z + centres[1].z) / 2;
    targets = centres.map((c) => new THREE.Vector3(Math.sign(c.x) * halfWidth, y, z));
    for (const [i, c] of centres.entries()) {
      const moved = c.distanceTo(targets[i]);
      if (moved > 1e-5) {
        adjustments.push(
          `eye at x ${c.x.toFixed(4)} moved ${moved.toFixed(4)} ` +
            `(${(moved * 2.25 * 1000).toFixed(0)} mm world) to sit at ±${halfWidth.toFixed(4)}`,
        );
      }
    }
  }

  return meshes.map((mesh, i) => {
    const centre = centres[i];
    const side = centre.x < 0 ? 'Eye_L' : 'Eye_R';
    mesh.geometry.translate(-centre.x, -centre.y, -centre.z);
    mesh.name = `${side}_Mesh`;

    /**
     * TWO nodes, not one, and the second one is the whole point.
     *
     * The controller does not offset the eye — it ASSIGNS its height outright, every frame:
     *
     *     eyeLRef.current.position.y = lerp(0, 0.012, squintAmount)
     *
     * which is 0 whenever the character is not squinting. So the node the rig binds cannot be
     * the node that carries the eye's position: on the first frame its y is overwritten with
     * zero and the eyes jump to the neck joint's height. Legacy gets this right by accident of
     * how it is written — its eye groups sit at y = 0 inside a parent that holds the height —
     * and an imported head has to reproduce that shape deliberately.
     *
     *   Eye_L_Socket   holds WHERE the eye is. Nothing writes to it.
     *   Eye_L          holds nothing, sits at the socket's origin, and is what the rig binds.
     *                  `position.y = 0` is then a no-op, and `scale.y` for the blink scales
     *                  about the eye's own centre because the geometry was re-based to it.
     */
    const socket = new THREE.Group();
    socket.name = `${side}_Socket`;
    socket.position.copy(targets[i]);

    const bound = new THREE.Group();
    bound.name = side;
    bound.add(mesh);
    socket.add(bound);

    return { socket, centre: targets[i] };
  });
}

await emit({
  id: 'head',
  file: 'head.glb',
  rootName: 'Head',
  meshes: [...skull, ...eyeNodes.map((e) => e.socket)],
  cost: costOf(headBaked),
});

// --- torso -----------------------------------------------------------------
const torsoPivot = body.getObjectByName('Torso');
const torsoMeshes = meshesUnder(torsoPivot);
const torsoJoint = jointFor(torsoPivot, torsoMeshes, { onLimbAxis: false });
const torsoBaked = bakePart(torsoPivot, torsoMeshes, 0);
for (const mesh of torsoBaked) mesh.name = 'Torso_Body';
await emit({ id: 'torso', file: 'torso.glb', rootName: 'Torso', meshes: torsoBaked, cost: costOf(torsoBaked) });

// --- arms ------------------------------------------------------------------
const armPivot = body.getObjectByName('Arm_L');
const armMeshes = meshesUnder(armPivot);
const armJoint = jointFor(armPivot, armMeshes, { onLimbAxis: true });

/**
 * The arm's rest pose, read off the empty rather than assumed.
 *
 * `Arm_L`'s own rotation is the splay the modeller gave the arm. Taken out of the geometry by
 * `bakePart` (which works in the pivot's local frame) and reported here for slots.tsx — see
 * step 4 of the header note for why it cannot live on the joint group.
 */
const armRest = new THREE.Euler().setFromQuaternion(
  armPivot.getWorldQuaternion(new THREE.Quaternion()),
);

/**
 * The UPPER arm on its own — the piece a sleeve has to fit over, as opposed to the hand.
 * Picked as the mesh nearest the shoulder; `handSocket()` picks the far one by the same rule,
 * so the two cannot both choose the same mesh.
 */
function upperArmBounds(meshes) {
  let nearest = null;
  for (const mesh of meshes) {
    mesh.geometry.computeBoundingBox();
    const centre = mesh.geometry.boundingBox.getCenter(new THREE.Vector3());
    if (!nearest || centre.length() < nearest.centre.length()) {
      nearest = { centre, box: mesh.geometry.boundingBox.clone() };
    }
  }
  return nearest;
}

const armLeft = bakePart(armPivot, armMeshes, armJoint.axisOffsetX);
const armRight = bakePart(armPivot, armMeshes, armJoint.axisOffsetX, { mirror: true });
await emit({ id: 'leftArm', file: 'arm-left.glb', rootName: 'Arm_L', meshes: armLeft, cost: costOf(armLeft) });
await emit({ id: 'rightArm', file: 'arm-right.glb', rootName: 'Arm_R', meshes: armRight, cost: costOf(armRight) });

// --- legs ------------------------------------------------------------------
const legPivot = body.getObjectByName('Leg_L');
const legMeshes = meshesUnder(legPivot);
const legJoint = jointFor(legPivot, legMeshes, { onLimbAxis: true });
const legLeft = bakePart(legPivot, legMeshes, legJoint.axisOffsetX);
const legRight = bakePart(legPivot, legMeshes, legJoint.axisOffsetX, { mirror: true });
await emit({ id: 'leftLeg', file: 'leg-left.glb', rootName: 'Leg_L', meshes: legLeft, cost: costOf(legLeft) });
await emit({ id: 'rightLeg', file: 'leg-right.glb', rootName: 'Leg_R', meshes: legRight, cost: costOf(legRight) });

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// THE RIG NUMBERS
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const head = toLocal(headJoint.world);
const torso = toLocal(torsoJoint.world);
const shoulder = toLocal(armJoint.world);
const hip = toLocal(legJoint.world);

const headBox = report.find((r) => r.id === 'head').box;
const torsoBox = report.find((r) => r.id === 'torso').box;
const legBox = report.find((r) => r.id === 'leftLeg').box;

/** Crown and half-width, measured off the exported part rather than off the source. */
const crownRise = headBox.max.y;
const headHalfWidth = Math.max(Math.abs(headBox.min.x), headBox.max.x);
const torsoHalfWidth = Math.max(Math.abs(torsoBox.min.x), torsoBox.max.x);
const soleFromHip = legBox.min.y;

/**
 * How much a wearable authored for the legacy head has to shrink to sit on this one. Same
 * mechanism as V2_ATTACHMENTS' 0.81 — the ratio of the two half-widths, so the whole existing
 * wardrobe arrives at the new head's size instead of hanging off it.
 */
const LEGACY_HEAD_HALF_WIDTH = 0.26;
const LEGACY_TORSO_HALF_WIDTH = 0.135;
const headScale = headHalfWidth / LEGACY_HEAD_HALF_WIDTH;
const torsoScale = torsoHalfWidth / LEGACY_TORSO_HALF_WIDTH;

/** The head sphere's centre, which is NOT the neck pivot — every head socket hangs off it. */
const headCentreY = (headBox.min.y + headBox.max.y) / 2;

/**
 * Where the FACE is on that sphere, which is not where legacy's was. Glasses and the mask are
 * drawn around legacy's eyes (y 0.035 above its skull centre), so they follow this head's eyes
 * rather than its skull: `faceDrop` is how much lower this face sits once legacy's is scaled.
 * Glasses also move out to the sphere's surface at the new latitude, keeping legacy's inset.
 */
const LEGACY_EYE_Y = 0.035;
const eyeCentre = eyeNodes[0]?.centre ?? new THREE.Vector3(0, headCentreY + LEGACY_EYE_Y * headScale, 0);
const faceDrop = eyeCentre.y - (headCentreY + LEGACY_EYE_Y * headScale);
const glassesY = headCentreY + 0.06 * headScale + faceDrop;
const glassesInset = (Math.sqrt(0.26 ** 2 - 0.06 ** 2) - 0.245) * headScale;
const glassesZ = Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, headHalfWidth ** 2 - (glassesY - headCentreY) ** 2)) - glassesInset;

/**
 * The torso's SHAPE, for the garment warp (TorsoShape in characterRig.ts). The chest is a
 * capsule flattened front to back, so half-width, half-depth and the cap height are measured
 * separately; the straight section is where the section stops shrinking.
 */
const torsoHalfDepth = Math.max(Math.abs(torsoBox.min.z), torsoBox.max.z);
const torsoStraightHalf = (() => {
  const pts = [];
  for (const mesh of torsoBaked) {
    const pos = mesh.geometry.getAttribute('position');
    for (let i = 0; i < pos.count; i++) pts.push([pos.getX(i), pos.getY(i)]);
  }
  const full = pts.filter(([x]) => Math.abs(x) >= torsoHalfWidth - 1e-4).map(([, y]) => Math.abs(y));
  return full.length ? Math.max(...full) : 0;
})();
const torsoCapHeight = torsoBox.max.y - torsoStraightHalf;

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * FITTING THE TWO WEARABLES THAT ARE LATHED AROUND A LIMB
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 *
 * Sleeves, trousers and shoes are the wearables that do not simply hang off a point: they are
 * drawn AROUND a limb whose thickness they had to assume, and legacy's assumptions are baked
 * into their geometry. On a re-proportioned body those assumptions stop holding, and the
 * symptom is the limb coming through the cloth.
 *
 * Rather than re-model any of them, each is brought in at THIS body's size through the socket
 * it already mounts on — the same mechanism that fits a legacy hat to a smaller skull. The
 * numbers below are what those sockets have to be, derived from the parts that were just cut.
 *
 * `MARGIN` is how much daylight to leave between limb and cloth. ~9 mm of world at this scale:
 * enough that the trouser's own crease displacement (which pushes the surface INWARD, see
 * Pants.tsx) cannot reach the leg, and small enough that nothing looks baggy.
 */
const MARGIN = 0.004;

/** Legacy's sleeve capsule, from LegacyArmWearables: `capsuleGeometry(0.048, 0.04)` at y -0.03. */
const SLEEVE = { radius: 0.048, capOffset: 0.02, halfHeight: 0.068, drawnAt: -0.03 };

/** The snuggest radius each leg wearable puts against the leg, from Pants.tsx and Shoes.tsx. */
const LEGACY_TROUSER_FLOOR = 0.0575; // Pants.tsx MIN_CLEARANCE
const LEGACY_SHOE_COLLAR = 0.058; //   Shoes.tsx, the shaft/collar cylinders

/** How high above the hip the trousers reach. Pants.tsx `WAIST_Y`. */
const LEGACY_TROUSER_WAIST = 0.035;

/** Legacy's torso garment, from LegacyTorsoWear: `capsuleGeometry(0.138, 0.08)` at the socket. */
const TOP = { radius: 0.138, capOffset: 0.04, halfHeight: 0.178 };

const upper = upperArmBounds(armLeft);
/** The upper arm as a capsule: how thick it is, where its axis is, and where its top ends. */
const armRadius = Math.max(
  (upper.box.max.x - upper.box.min.x) / 2,
  (upper.box.max.z - upper.box.min.z) / 2,
);
const armAxisX = upper.centre.x;
const armTop = upper.box.max.y;

/**
 * The sleeve socket, solved rather than tuned.
 *
 * Two conditions, and they are the two ways a sleeve fails:
 *   RADIUS  it must clear the arm everywhere, including the arm's own offset from the joint.
 *   CAP     its shoulder end must ENCLOSE the arm's shoulder end. Aligning the two capsules'
 *           top-cap centres reduces that to the radius condition, which is why the position
 *           below is derived from the cap rather than from the sleeve's midpoint — a sleeve
 *           sized correctly but sat too low leaves the shoulder ball bare, which is exactly
 *           what the legacy numbers did to this arm.
 */
const sleeveScale = (Math.abs(armAxisX) + armRadius + MARGIN) / SLEEVE.radius;
const sleeveCentreY = armTop - armRadius - SLEEVE.capOffset * sleeveScale;
const sleeveY = sleeveCentreY - SLEEVE.drawnAt * sleeveScale;

/**
 * One scale for BOTH leg wearables, taken from whichever of the two is snuggest against the
 * leg. Shared deliberately: a trouser hem and a boot shaft that came in at different sizes
 * would part company at the ankle, and no one would be able to say which of the two was wrong.
 */
const legRadius = Math.max(
  Math.max(-legBox.min.x, legBox.max.x),
  Math.max(-legBox.min.z, legBox.max.z),
);
const legWearScale = Math.max(
  (legRadius + MARGIN) / LEGACY_TROUSER_FLOOR,
  (legRadius + MARGIN) / LEGACY_SHOE_COLLAR,
);

/**
 * THE TOP's socket, which has to satisfy two things at once — and the second is the one that
 * gets missed, because it is not about the torso at all.
 *
 *   A. COVER THE TORSO'S TOP, or the shoulders show through the shirt.
 *   B. COVER THE LEG WHERE THE TROUSERS DO NOT. The trousers only reach `WAIST_Y` above the
 *      hip; above that the leg is bare and the TOP has to cover it. On this body the thigh is
 *      nearly as wide as the torso, so the top's own cap has already narrowed past the leg's
 *      outer edge by the time it gets down there — and a band of bare leg shows between hem
 *      and waistband, all the way round the hips.
 *
 * B is why this is not simply the chest ratio any more. Sized to the chest, the top is 6 mm of
 * world clear of the body and 46 mm SHORT of the leg at the waistband. So the scale is searched
 * upward from the chest fit until B holds, with the position pinned so A stays exactly met —
 * the smallest top that closes the gap, rather than the roundest one that obviously would.
 *
 * Everything is in ROOT space here, because the constraint spans three parts (torso, leg,
 * trousers) and only the root is common to all three.
 */
const torsoTopRoot = torso.y + torsoBox.max.y;
const legOuterX = Math.abs(hip.x) + Math.max(-legBox.min.x, legBox.max.x);
const trouserWaistRoot = hip.y + LEGACY_TROUSER_WAIST * legWearScale;

/** Radius of the top's capsule at a root height, for a given scale and centre. */
const topRadiusAt = (scale, centreY, y) => {
  const capCentre = centreY - TOP.capOffset * scale;
  const straightTop = centreY + TOP.capOffset * scale;
  if (y <= straightTop && y >= capCentre) return TOP.radius * scale;
  const d = y > straightTop ? y - straightTop : capCentre - y;
  return Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, (TOP.radius * scale) ** 2 - d * d));
};

/**
 * How far the trousers are carried up PAST their waistband, so the leg is never bare.
 *
 * This is the answer to B, and it is a better answer than growing the top was. The bare band
 * appears because the trousers stop at the waistband while the leg carries on up inside the
 * body; covering that stretch with TROUSER closes it at the source, and the top can then go
 * back to simply fitting the chest instead of being inflated until it happened to reach.
 *
 * Stated in the TROUSERS' own space — divided by the leg socket's scale — because that is the
 * space PantsModel draws in, and it is drawn inside that socket.
 */
const trouserRise = (legBox.max.y + MARGIN) / legWearScale;

/**
 * THE TOP'S HEM (TorsoShape.hem). Where a top stops following the belly in and hangs over the
 * trousers instead: at the waistband, wide enough to cover the widest cut's hips (日系寬褲's
 * 0.082 at this leg's scale, either side of the hip joint), and at least as deep as the chest.
 * `HEM_EASE` is the daylight between the hem and the waistband under it.
 */
const WIDEST_TROUSER_HIP = 0.082; // constants/pants.ts, `wide`
const HEM_EASE = 0.006;
const hemY = trouserWaistRoot - torso.y;
const hemHalfX = Math.abs(hip.x) + WIDEST_TROUSER_HIP * legWearScale + HEM_EASE;
const hemHalfZ = Math.max(torsoHalfDepth, WIDEST_TROUSER_HIP * legWearScale) + HEM_EASE * 2;

/** The top is back to what it should be: the chest's own ratio, sat where the torso sits. */
const topScale = torsoScale;
const topY = 0;

const n = (v) => Number(v.toFixed(4));
const p3 = (x, y, z) => `[${n(x)}, ${n(y)}, ${n(z)}]`;

console.log('');
console.log('  source        ' + path.relative(ROOT, SOURCE));
console.log(`  measured      sole ${sourceSole.toFixed(4)}  crown ${sourceCrown.toFixed(4)}  height ${sourceHeight.toFixed(4)} (source units)`);
console.log(`  unit fix      y_out = ${SCALE.toFixed(6)} * y_in + ${LIFT.toFixed(6)}  →  height ${TARGET_LOCAL_HEIGHT}, sole ${TARGET_SOLE_Y}`);
console.log('');
for (const r of report) {
  const size = r.box.getSize(new THREE.Vector3());
  console.log(
    `  ${r.id.padEnd(9)} ${r.file.padEnd(14)} ${String(Math.round(r.size / 1024)).padStart(4)} KB   ` +
      `${Math.round(r.triangles)} tris / ${r.meshes} mesh   ` +
      `bounds ${size.x.toFixed(3)}x${size.y.toFixed(3)}x${size.z.toFixed(3)}`,
  );
}
console.log(
  `  ${'TOTAL'.padEnd(9)} ${''.padEnd(14)} ${String(Math.round(report.reduce((s, r) => s + r.size, 0) / 1024)).padStart(4)} KB   ` +
    `${Math.round(report.reduce((s, r) => s + r.triangles, 0))} tris / ${report.reduce((s, r) => s + r.meshes, 0)} mesh`,

/** The hand's centre in ARM space, for `attachments.hand`. */
function handSocket() {
  // The hand is the outermost mesh on the arm: the one whose centre is furthest from the
  // shoulder. Named rather than indexed so re-ordering the source cannot silently pick the
  // upper arm instead.
  let best = null;
  for (const mesh of armLeft) {
    mesh.geometry.computeBoundingBox();
    const centre = mesh.geometry.boundingBox.getCenter(new THREE.Vector3());
    if (!best || centre.length() > best.length()) best = centre;
  }
  return [best.x, best.y, best.z];
}
```

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 每日登入 — rules tests.
 *
 * Run with `npm run test:daily-login`. Written in the same tsx-script style as the `audit:*`
 * checks because that is the test runner this repo has; there is no vitest/jest here, and adding
 * one is a bigger decision than this feature should make on its own.
 *
 * These cover the DECIDABLE half of the spec: cycle tiling, day boundaries in Asia/Taipei, the
 * state machine, make-up pricing and the affordability edges. The concurrency cases from the
 * brief (double-claim, simultaneous free+make-up, retry after a lost response) are properties of
 * the WRITE path, not of these functions — see docs/daily-login.md for which of those the current
 * architecture can actually guarantee and how they are enforced.
 */

import {
  CivilDate,
  DAILY_LOGIN_CURRENCY,
  DAILY_PRIZE_COINS,
  DAILY_PRIZE_FRAGMENTS,
  DAILY_PRIZE_ITEM_RARITIES,
  DAILY_PRIZE_PLAN,
  DAILY_PRIZE_SPINS,
  MAKEUP_SURCHARGE,
  addCivilDays,
  buildSquares,
  canClaim,
  civilDateAt,
  civilDaysBetween,
  dailyPrizeFor,
  makeupCostForDay,
  resolveCycle,
} from '../src/constants/dailyLogin';

let failures = 0;
let checks = 0;

function eq(name: string, got: unknown, want: unknown): void {
  checks++;
  const ok = JSON.stringify(got) === JSON.stringify(want);
  if (!ok) {
    failures++;
    console.log(`FAIL  ${name}\n        got  ${JSON.stringify(got)}\n        want ${JSON.stringify(want)}`);
  } else {
    console.log(`PASS  ${name}`);
  }
}

/** A boolean check, for the properties that are not an equality. Same shape as test-economy's. */
function ok(name: string, condition: boolean, detail = ''): void {
  checks++;
  if (!condition) {
    failures++;
    console.log(`FAIL  ${name}${detail ? `  ${detail}` : ''}`);
  } else {
    console.log(`PASS  ${name}${detail ? `  (${detail})` : ''}`);
  }
}

/** An instant, written as Taipei wall-clock time so the boundary cases read as what they test. */
function taipei(iso: string): Date {
  return new Date(`${iso}+08:00`);
}

console.log('\n-- the prize table ---------------------------------------------------');

/**
 * The round stopped being a ladder on 2026-09-17.
 *
 * It used to be seven amounts of one currency (4 / 6 / 10 / 16 / 24 / 36 / 60 碎片) and the tests
 * here pinned that it only ever climbed. There is nothing to climb now: a day is a KIND of thing,
 * four of the seven days are a coin flip between two kinds, and two of them pay no number at all.
 *
 * So what is pinned instead is the SHAPE of the week, the odds, and the one property the old ladder
 * tests were really protecting — that a prize is decided before the day arrives and never re-rolls.
 * That last one is not a nicety: the board previews all seven days, and the server names its claim
 * document after the prize's kind, so a roll that moved would be a second claim document for the
 * same day and therefore a second payout.
 */
eq('seven days', DAILY_PRIZE_PLAN.length, 7);
eq('the round mints 金幣 and nothing else', DAILY_LOGIN_CURRENCY, 'coins');

eq(
  'days 1, 3, 4 and 6 are a coin flip between 商品碎片 and 金幣',
  [1, 3, 4, 6].map((day) => [...DAILY_PRIZE_PLAN[day - 1]]),
  [1, 3, 4, 6].map(() => ['item-fragments', 'coins']),
);
eq(
  'day 2 is three ways',
  [...DAILY_PRIZE_PLAN[1]],
  ['utility-card', 'raffle-ticket', 'coins-and-fragments'],
);
eq('day 5 is a whole product', [...DAILY_PRIZE_PLAN[4]], ['item']);
eq('day 7 is a free spin', [...DAILY_PRIZE_PLAN[6]], ['free-spin']);

/**
 * The odds, measured rather than declared.
 *
 * A thousand rounds is enough to catch a draw that is uniform-in-name-only — an off-by-one in the
 * index, a seed that correlates the day with the option, a `Math.floor` that can reach `length`.
 * The tolerance is deliberately loose (±6 points): this is a check that the branch is roughly even,
 * not a test of the hash's distribution, and a tight bound here would fail on a harmless change to
 * the seed string.
 */
{
  const rounds = 1000;
  const tally = (day: number) => {
    const counts = new Map<string, number>();
    for (let i = 0; i < rounds; i++) {
      const kind = dailyPrizeFor(`cycle-2026-03-${String((i % 28) + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${i}`, day).kind;
      counts.set(kind, (counts.get(kind) ?? 0) + 1);
    }
    return counts;
  };

  const even = (day: number, expected: number) => {
    const counts = tally(day);
    const options = DAILY_PRIZE_PLAN[day - 1];
    const share = 100 / options.length;
    const off = options.map((kind) => Math.abs(((counts.get(kind) ?? 0) / rounds) * 100 - share));
    ok(
      `day ${day} draws its ${expected} options evenly`,
      counts.size === expected && Math.max(...off) < 6,
      [...counts].map(([k, n]) => `${k} ${((n / rounds) * 100).toFixed(1)}%`).join('、'),
    );
  };

  even(1, 2);
  even(2, 3);
  even(5, 1);
  even(7, 1);
}

/**
 * The four coin-flip days must be independent OF EACH OTHER, not merely 50/50 when averaged over
 * rounds — and this is a regression test for a bug that shipped and was caught by looking at the
 * board rather than at the numbers.
 *
 * The four days seed on strings that differ only in their LAST character (`...:1` … `...:6`).
 * FNV-1a mixes from the low end and the fraction is read off the top bits, so those four seeds came
 * out within a couple of 256ths of each other: in four rounds out of five all four days landed on
 * the same side of the flip, and a week of 「碎片 or 金幣」 was in practice all one or all the other.
 * Every per-day check above still passed, because each of them varies the ROUND.
 *
 * See constants/seed.ts's `avalanche` for the fix. What this pins is the property, not the fix: a
 * round whose four flips always agree is a broken draw however it got that way.
 */
{
  const rounds = 400;
  let unanimous = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < rounds; i++) {
    const id = `cycle-2026-0${(i % 9) + 1}-${String((i % 28) + 1).padStart(2, '0')}`;
    const kinds = [1, 3, 4, 6].map((day) => dailyPrizeFor(id, day).kind);
    if (kinds.every((k) => k === kinds[0])) unanimous++;
  }
  // Four independent coin flips agree 1 time in 8. Anything past a quarter of all rounds is the
  // seeds moving together rather than luck.
  ok(
    'the four coin-flip days do not move together within a round',
    unanimous / rounds < 0.25,
    `${((unanimous / rounds) * 100).toFixed(1)}% of rounds were unanimous (獨立時約 12.5%)`,
  );
}

/**
 * Deterministic, which is the property everything else in the feature is built on: the board can
 * preview it, the server can name a document after it, and a retried claim is the same claim.
 */
{
  const first = dailyPrizeFor('cycle-2026-03-10', 4);
  const again = dailyPrizeFor('cycle-2026-03-10', 4);
  eq('the same round and day always roll the same prize', first, again);
  ok(
    'a different round rolls independently',
    [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7].some(
      (day) => dailyPrizeFor('cycle-2026-03-10', day).kind !== dailyPrizeFor('cycle-2026-03-17', day).kind,
    ),
    'a seed that ignored the cycle id would make every week identical',
  );
}

/** What each kind actually hands over. The amounts are the brief, restated where they can be read. */
{
  const kindsOf = (day: number) => DAILY_PRIZE_PLAN[day - 1];
  ok(
    'a 碎片 day pays 10 商品碎片 and no money',
    kindsOf(1).includes('item-fragments') &&
      DAILY_PRIZE_FRAGMENTS === 10,
  );
  ok('a 金幣 day pays 15', DAILY_PRIZE_COINS === 15);
  eq('day 7 pays exactly one free spin', dailyPrizeFor('cycle-2026-03-10', 7).spins, DAILY_PRIZE_SPINS);
  eq(
    'day 5 always names a tier',
    DAILY_PRIZE_ITEM_RARITIES.includes(dailyPrizeFor('cycle-2026-03-10', 5).itemRarity!),
    true,
  );
  ok(
    'and never a tier above 史詩',
    !DAILY_PRIZE_ITEM_RARITIES.includes('mythic'),
    '神話 is not something a login may hand out',
  );
}

/**
 * The make-up is a flat PRICE in 金幣.
 *
 * It used to be `reward + 500`, back when the day and the fee were the same currency and a make-up
 * had to be a wash plus a fee to be neither a trap nor a reason to skip days. A day does not have
 * one value any more — four of the seven pay no money at all — so there is nothing to add a fee to.
 * Hence flat, and hence identical on every day of the round.
 */
eq('make-up price is flat', makeupCostForDay(3), MAKEUP_SURCHARGE);
eq('the same on every day', makeupCostForDay(7), makeupCostForDay(1));
console.log('\n-- civil dates and the 00:00 boundary --------------------------------');

eq('23:59:59 belongs to that day', civilDateAt(taipei('2026-03-10T23:59:59')), '2026-03-10');
eq('00:00:00 belongs to the next', civilDateAt(taipei('2026-03-11T00:00:00')), '2026-03-11');
eq('one millisecond before midnight', civilDateAt(taipei('2026-03-10T23:59:59.999')), '2026-03-10');
// The device's own zone must not enter into it: both instants below are the same moment, and one
// of them is "yesterday" in UTC.
eq('UTC evening is already tomorrow in Taipei', civilDateAt(new Date('2026-03-10T16:00:00Z')), '2026-03-11');
eq('UTC just before that is still today', civilDateAt(new Date('2026-03-10T15:59:59Z')), '2026-03-10');
eq('month rollover', civilDateAt(taipei('2026-03-31T23:59:59')), '2026-03-31');
eq('year rollover', civilDateAt(taipei('2027-01-01T00:00:01')), '2027-01-01');
eq('leap day', civilDateAt(taipei('2028-02-29T12:00:00')), '2028-02-29');
eq('civil arithmetic crosses months', addCivilDays('2026-03-31', 1), '2026-04-01');
eq('civil arithmetic crosses years', addCivilDays('2026-12-28', 7), '2027-01-04');
eq('civil difference', civilDaysBetween('2026-03-10', '2026-03-17'), 7);

console.log('\n-- cycle tiling -----------------------------------------------------');

const ANCHOR: CivilDate = '2026-03-10';

eq('first login is day 1', resolveCycle(ANCHOR, taipei('2026-03-10T09:00:00')).currentDayIndex, 1);
eq('cycle id is derived from the start date', resolveCycle(ANCHOR, taipei('2026-03-10T09:00:00')).cycleId, 'cycle-2026-03-10');
eq('day 7 is the last of the cycle', resolveCycle(ANCHOR, taipei('2026-03-16T23:59:59')).currentDayIndex, 7);
eq('cycle end date', resolveCycle(ANCHOR, taipei('2026-03-10T09:00:00')).endDate, '2026-03-16');

{
  // Day 7 ends -> the next server day opens a new cycle at Day 1, with a new id.
  const next = resolveCycle(ANCHOR, taipei('2026-03-17T00:00:00'));
  eq('new cycle starts the next day', next.currentDayIndex, 1);
  eq('new cycle has a new id', next.cycleId, 'cycle-2026-03-17');
  eq('new cycle is numbered', next.cycleNumber, 1);
}

{
  // Cycles are calendar-driven, not claim-driven: a player who vanishes for five weeks comes back
  // to a fresh cycle rather than to where they left off.
  const later = resolveCycle(ANCHOR, taipei('2026-04-15T08:00:00'));
  eq('long absence lands in a later cycle', later.cycleNumber, 5);
  eq('long absence still starts at some day of it', later.currentDayIndex >= 1 && later.currentDayIndex <= 7, true);
}

{
  // Device clock rolled BACK before the anchor. Must not produce a negative cycle or open a day.
  const back = resolveCycle(ANCHOR, taipei('2026-03-01T09:00:00'));
  eq('clock rolled back stays in cycle 0', back.cycleNumber, 0);
  eq('clock rolled back opens no later day', back.currentDayIndex, 1);
}

console.log('\n-- the state machine ------------------------------------------------');

{
  // Day 3 of the cycle, nothing claimed yet.
  const cycle = resolveCycle(ANCHOR, taipei('2026-03-12T10:00:00'));
  const squares = buildSquares(cycle, new Set(), true);
  eq('today is available', squares[2].state, 'available');
  eq('yesterday is buyable', squares[1].state, 'makeup_available');
  eq('day 1 is buyable', squares[0].state, 'makeup_available');
  eq('tomorrow is future', squares[3].state, 'future');
  eq('day 7 is future', squares[6].state, 'future');
  eq('future squares still show their prize', squares[6].prize.kind, 'free-spin');
  eq('future squares carry no price', squares[6].makeupCost, null);
  eq('buyable squares carry a price', squares[1].makeupCost, MAKEUP_SURCHARGE);
}

{
  // THE SPEC'S "skipped day 2" CASE. Claimed day 1, skipped day 2, now on day 3.
  const cycle = resolveCycle(ANCHOR, taipei('2026-03-12T10:00:00'));
  const squares = buildSquares(cycle, new Set([1]), true);
  eq('claimed day is terminal', squares[0].state, 'claimed');
  eq('skipping day 2 does not hold day 3 back', squares[2].state, 'available');
  eq('the skipped day is only buyable', squares[1].state, 'makeup_available');
  eq('a claimed day can never be re-claimed free', canClaim(squares[0], 'free'), false);
  eq('a claimed day can never be bought back', canClaim(squares[0], 'makeup'), false);
  eq('free claim is only for today', canClaim(squares[1], 'free'), false);
  eq('make-up is only for a missed day', canClaim(squares[2], 'makeup'), false);
}

{
  // Day 7 is the round's PRIZE, not merely its last day: it opens only once the six under it have
  // been collected. Without this a 補簽 buys nothing — see isGrandPrizeUnlocked.
  const cycle = resolveCycle(ANCHOR, taipei('2026-03-16T12:00:00'));
  const squares = buildSquares(cycle, new Set(), true);
  eq('day 7 stays shut while the round is incomplete', squares[6].state, 'future');
  eq('the other six are all buyable', squares.slice(0, 6).every((s) => s.state === 'makeup_available'), true);

  const earned = buildSquares(cycle, new Set([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]), true);
  eq('day 7 opens once the six are in', earned[6].state, 'available');
  eq('and it is claimable free', canClaim(earned[6], 'free'), true);

  // A make-up on the last outstanding day is what unlocks it, which is the whole point of the fee.
  const oneShort = buildSquares(cycle, new Set([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]), true);
  eq('one day short leaves the prize shut', oneShort[6].state, 'future');
  eq('and the missing day is buyable', oneShort[5].state, 'makeup_available');
}

{
  // A finished cycle: unclaimed squares are missed, and nothing in it is actionable.
  const old = resolveCycle(ANCHOR, taipei('2026-03-12T10:00:00'));
  const squares = buildSquares(old, new Set([1, 2]), false);
  eq('past cycle keeps its claims', squares[0].state, 'claimed');
  eq('past cycle unclaimed is missed', squares[2].state, 'missed');
  eq('missed cannot be bought back', canClaim(squares[2], 'makeup'), false);
  eq('missed carries no price', squares[2].makeupCost, null);
  eq('nothing in a past cycle is claimable', squares.some((s) => canClaim(s, 'free') || canClaim(s, 'makeup')), false);
}

console.log('\n-- affordability edges ----------------------------------------------');

{
  const cost = makeupCostForDay(3); // 750
  const afford = (balance: number) => balance >= cost;
  eq('exactly enough is enough', afford(cost), true);
  eq('one coin short is not', afford(cost - 1), false);
  eq('one coin over is fine', afford(cost + 1), true);
  // No longer 「price minus the day's value」: the two are different currencies, so the cost IS the
  // price. What still has to hold is that it does not vary with the day.
  eq('the price is the whole cost', cost, MAKEUP_SURCHARGE);
}

console.log(
  failures === 0
    ? `\nALL PASS (${checks} checks)\n`
    : `\n${failures} of ${checks} checks FAILED\n`
);
process.exit(failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);
```
