## scripts/test-offline-return.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 離線回歸 — rules tests.
 *
 * Run with `npm run test:offline-return`. Same tsx-script style as `test:daily-login` and the
 * `audit:*` checks, because that is the test runner this repo has.
 *
 * The properties pinned here are the ones the brief states as requirements and that are cheap to
 * get wrong months later:
 *
 *  §2/§15  a first sighting is never a long absence, and a short one grows nothing
 *  §2      growth is gradual and monotonic in time away, never a cliff
 *  §4      藤蔓 and 蜘蛛網 are capped, so a long absence is never a jungle
 *  §11/§12 logging in twice from ONE absence adds nothing the second time, and a patch the
 *          player tidied does not grow back until MORE time has passed
 *  §6/§7   nothing anywhere in the resolved state can reduce gold, XP, inventory or a pet
 *  §1/§2   the environment state is gradual and monotonic, and its worst case is still a lit,
 *          coloured island rather than a dark one
 *  §7      clearing the island restores it — the grading is derived from what is standing on it,
 *          so tidying and recovery are the same act
 *  §14     growth prefers the sheltered corners, but the preference can never stop it growing
 *  §1/§2   the colour drain is continuous in hours away, reaches true greyscale, and no single
 *          hour of absence is ever a visible step
 *  §6/§8   the recovery starts drained, ends exactly neutral, and the bloom leads the lift
 *  §12     nothing about a recovery is stored, so being interrupted is an ordinary state
 *
 * The siting rules (lib/islandOvergrowth.ts) are exercised through the real solver, so a change
 * to the island's keep-outs shows up here as sprouts that fail to find a home rather than as
 * weeds in a doorway nobody notices until they are on screen.
 */

import {
  CLEAR_COLOUR_STATE,
  COLOUR_FULL_DAYS,
  COLOUR_MIN_DRAIN,
  COLOUR_STAGES,
  ISLAND_GRADES,
  NEUTRAL_AMBIENCE,
  OVERGROWTH_KINDS,
  OVERGROWTH_MAX,
  PET_HOME_STATE,
  PET_MOODS,
  QUIET_HOURS,
  RECOVERY_HOLD_SECONDS,
  RECOVERY_SECONDS,
  colourDrainForHours,
  colourStageForDrain,
  getOvergrowthKind,
  hoursForColourDrain,
  makePetState,
  overgrowthBudget,
  overgrowthMix,
  resolveIslandAmbience,
  resolveIslandColour,
  resolveOfflineReturn,
  resolvePetMood,
  stageForHours,
  vitalityForHours,
} from '../src/constants/islandReturn';
import { findTidyTarget, growOvergrowth, tidyOvergrowthAt } from '../src/lib/islandOvergrowth';
import { HOUSE_FOOTPRINT } from '../src/constants/houseStyles';
import type { HomeObstacle } from '../src/utils/placementRules';

let failures = 0;
let checks = 0;

function eq(name: string, got: unknown, want: unknown): void {
  checks++;
  const ok = JSON.stringify(got) === JSON.stringify(want);
  if (!ok) {
    failures++;
    console.log(`FAIL  ${name}\n        got  ${JSON.stringify(got)}\n        want ${JSON.stringify(want)}`);
  } else {
    console.log(`PASS  ${name}`);
  }
}

const HOURS = 3_600_000;
const NOW = new Date('2026-08-22T12:00:00Z');
const hoursAgo = (h: number) => new Date(NOW.getTime() - h * HOURS).toISOString();

/** A Home placed off-centre and rotated, so nothing below can pass by axis-aligned accident. */
const HOME: HomeObstacle = {
  position: [1.4, 0, -1.1],
  rotation: 0.7,
  footprint: HOUSE_FOOTPRINT,
};

const world = { home: HOME, islandScale: 1, placements: [] };

console.log('\n-- reading an absence ------------------------------------------------');

eq('no timestamp is a first sighting', resolveOfflineReturn(undefined, NOW).isFirstSighting, true);
eq('a first sighting is never a return', resolveOfflineReturn(undefined, NOW).shouldGreet, false);
eq('a first sighting reports no time away', resolveOfflineReturn(undefined, NOW).hours, 0);
eq('garbage is a first sighting, not a long one', resolveOfflineReturn('not-a-date', NOW).isFirstSighting, true);
eq('a clock set forward cannot go negative', resolveOfflineReturn(hoursAgo(-50), NOW).hours, 0);
eq('two days away reads as two days', resolveOfflineReturn(hoursAgo(48), NOW).days, 2);

console.log('\n-- the stage ladder --------------------------------------------------');

eq('an hour away is home', stageForHours(1).id, 'home');
eq('overnight is still not a return', stageForHours(11).greets, false);
eq('half a day is a breeze, and still silent', stageForHours(12).greets, false);
eq('three days is the first greeting', stageForHours(72).greets, true);
eq('a week climbs', stageForHours(168).id, 'climbing');
eq('a fortnight slumbers', stageForHours(336).id, 'slumber');
eq('a year is still only slumber', stageForHours(24 * 365).id, 'slumber');
// 「不要每次都顯示相同文字」 — a stage that greets and has one line would say the same thing every
// time, which is the one thing the brief asks this copy not to do.
eq(
  'every greeting stage has more than one line',
  [72, 168, 336].every((h) => stageForHours(h).lines.length > 1),
  true,
);

console.log('\n-- the growth curve --------------------------------------------------');

eq('nothing grows inside the quiet window', overgrowthBudget(QUIET_HOURS - 1), 0);
eq('nothing grows at the boundary itself', overgrowthBudget(QUIET_HOURS), 0);
eq('a day away is a handful', overgrowthBudget(24) <= 5, true);
eq('a week away is legible but not a jungle', overgrowthBudget(168) < OVERGROWTH_MAX, true);
eq('the ceiling holds at a year', overgrowthBudget(24 * 365), OVERGROWTH_MAX);

{
  // Monotonic and gradual: more time away is never LESS growth, and no single day is a cliff.
  let previous = 0;
  let biggestJump = 0;
  let monotonic = true;
  for (let day = 1; day <= 90; day += 1) {
    const budget = overgrowthBudget(day * 24);
    if (budget < previous) monotonic = false;
    biggestJump = Math.max(biggestJump, budget - previous);
    previous = budget;
  }
  eq('growth never goes backwards', monotonic, true);
  eq('no single day more than doubles a small island', biggestJump <= 4, true);
}

console.log('\n-- what grows, and when ----------------------------------------------');

{
  const day1 = overgrowthMix(24);
  eq('a day away is leaves only', [...day1.keys()], ['leaf']);

  const day3 = overgrowthMix(72);
  eq('three days has grass', day3.has('weed'), true);
  eq('three days has no vines yet', day3.has('vine'), false);

  const week = overgrowthMix(168);
  eq('a week is climbing', week.has('vine'), true);
  eq('a week has no cobwebs yet', week.has('web'), false);

  const long = overgrowthMix(24 * 40);
  eq('a long absence cobwebs', long.has('web'), true);
  eq('vines stay a detail', (long.get('vine') ?? 0) <= getOvergrowthKind('vine').cap, true);
  eq('cobwebs stay a detail', (long.get('web') ?? 0) <= getOvergrowthKind('web').cap, true);

  for (const kind of OVERGROWTH_KINDS) {
    eq(`${kind.id} never exceeds its cap`, (long.get(kind.id) ?? 0) <= kind.cap, true);
  }
  eq(
    'the mix never exceeds the ceiling',
    [...long.values()].reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) <= OVERGROWTH_MAX,
    true,
  );
}

console.log('\n-- topping up, never re-rolling (§11/§12) -----------------------------');

{
  const first = growOvergrowth({ existing: [], hours: 168, ...world });
  eq('a week away actually grows something', first.length > 0, true);

  // The same absence, resolved a second time — this is the "logged in twice" case.
  const again = growOvergrowth({ existing: first, hours: 168, ...world });
  eq('a repeat login adds nothing', again.length, first.length);
  eq('a repeat login returns the same list', again === first, true);

  // A LONGER absence tops up rather than starting over, and keeps what was already there.
  const later = growOvergrowth({ existing: first, hours: 24 * 30, ...world });
  eq('more time away grows more', later.length > first.length, true);
  eq('nothing already standing is replaced', first.every((s) => later.includes(s)), true);

  // What the player cleared stays cleared.
  //
  // The guarantee is stated against the CLOCK, not against a "已整理" flag, and this is the pair
  // of checks that says which: arriving stamps `lastSeenAt`, so the very next login measures its
  // absence from that moment and is worth nothing. A player who tidies and comes back tomorrow
  // finds their work still done. A player who tidies and then leaves for another two months finds
  // the weeds back — which is the system working, not the tidy being undone.
  const cleared = tidyOvergrowthAt(later, later[0].x, later[0].z, HOME);
  eq('tidying removes something', cleared.removed.length > 0, true);

  const nextLogin = growOvergrowth({ existing: cleared.sprouts, hours: 2, ...world });
  eq('the next login grows nothing at all', nextLogin === cleared.sprouts, true);
  eq('so the island stays as the player left it', nextLogin.length < later.length, true);

  const muchLater = growOvergrowth({ existing: cleared.sprouts, hours: 24 * 60, ...world });
  eq('another two months away does grow again', muchLater.length > cleared.sprouts.length, true);
  eq('and still never past the ceiling', muchLater.length <= OVERGROWTH_MAX, true);
}

console.log('\n-- where it is allowed to grow ---------------------------------------');

{
  const grown = growOvergrowth({ existing: [], hours: 24 * 45, ...world });
  const ground = grown.filter((s) => getOvergrowthKind(s.kind).surface === 'ground');
  eq('a very long absence still spawns a full island', grown.length >= 20, true);

  eq(
    'nothing grows on the player spawn point',
    ground.every((s) => Math.hypot(s.x, s.z) > 2),
    true,
  );
  eq(
    'nothing grows off the grass',
    ground.every((s) => Math.hypot(s.x, s.z) < 5.7),
    true,
  );
  eq(
    'nothing grows inside the house',
    ground.every((s) => {
      const rx = s.x - HOME.position[0];
      const rz = s.z - HOME.position[2];
      const cos = Math.cos(-HOME.rotation);
      const sin = Math.sin(-HOME.rotation);
      return (
        Math.abs(rx * cos - rz * sin) > HOUSE_FOOTPRINT.halfWidth ||
        Math.abs(rx * sin + rz * cos) > HOUSE_FOOTPRINT.halfDepth
      );
    }),
    true,
  );
  eq(
    'no two sprouts share a spot',
    ground.every((a, i) => ground.every((b, j) => i === j || Math.hypot(a.x - b.x, a.z - b.z) > 0.3)),
    true,
  );
  eq(
    'every wall sprout has its own anchor',
    new Set(grown.filter((s) => s.slot >= 0).map((s) => s.slot)).size ===
      grown.filter((s) => s.slot >= 0).length,
    true,
  );
}

console.log('\n-- with no Home placed yet -------------------------------------------');

{
  const homeless = growOvergrowth({ existing: [], hours: 24 * 40, home: null, islandScale: 1, placements: [] });
  eq('the ground still grows', homeless.length > 0, true);
  eq('nothing clings to a house that is not there', homeless.every((s) => s.slot < 0), true);
}

console.log('\n-- tidying ------------------------------------------------------------');

{
  const grown = growOvergrowth({ existing: [], hours: 24 * 40, ...world });
  const target = grown.find((s) => getOvergrowthKind(s.kind).surface === 'ground')!;

  eq('standing in a patch offers a tidy', !!findTidyTarget(grown, target.x, target.z, HOME), true);
  eq(
    'what the prompt offers is what the action takes',
    findTidyTarget(grown, target.x, target.z, HOME)!.count,
    tidyOvergrowthAt(grown, target.x, target.z, HOME).removed.length,
  );

  // Far out to sea: nothing in reach, and therefore no prompt and no write.
  eq('an empty corner offers nothing', findTidyTarget(grown, 200, 200, HOME), null);
  const nothing = tidyOvergrowthAt(grown, 200, 200, HOME);
  eq('and tidying it removes nothing', nothing.removed.length, 0);
  eq('and returns the very same list, so no save is triggered', nothing.sprouts === grown, true);

  // At the house, one press takes the vines and cobwebs with the weeds.
  const atHome = tidyOvergrowthAt(grown, HOME.position[0], HOME.position[2] + 3, HOME);
  eq('tidying at the house clears its walls too', atHome.sprouts.every((s) => s.slot < 0), true);

  // Tidy everywhere, and the island comes back clean — nothing can be un-clearable.
  let left = grown;
  for (const sprout of grown) left = tidyOvergrowthAt(left, sprout.x, sprout.z, HOME).sprouts;
  left = tidyOvergrowthAt(left, HOME.position[0], HOME.position[2], HOME).sprouts;
  eq('everything that grows can be cleared', left.length, 0);
}

console.log('\n-- the pet ------------------------------------------------------------');

eq('an hour away leaves a lively pet', resolvePetMood(1), 'lively');
eq('overnight leaves a lively pet', resolvePetMood(11), 'lively');
eq('a few days quietens it', resolvePetMood(72), 'calm');
eq('a fortnight has it waiting', resolvePetMood(336), 'waiting');
eq('coming back is a reunion', resolvePetMood(336, { justReturned: true }), 'reunion');
eq('coming back from an hour out is not', resolvePetMood(1, { justReturned: true }), 'lively');
eq('vitality never bottoms out', vitalityForHours(24 * 3650) > 0, true);
eq('vitality is full at home', vitalityForHours(0), 1);
eq(
  'every mood still walks — none of them is a stopped pet',
  Object.values(PET_MOODS).every((m) => m.pace > 0 && m.liveliness > 0),
  true,
);
eq(
  'only the quiet moods put the bed out',
  Object.values(PET_MOODS).filter((m) => m.showsNest).map((m) => m.id),
  ['calm', 'waiting', 'reunion'],
);

console.log('\n-- nothing written may be `undefined` --------------------------------');

{
  // Firestore rejects an `undefined` field SYNCHRONOUSLY, before the request is sent — so one
  // optional field written as `{ x: undefined }` fails every write in the feature, and does it
  // with `invalid-argument`, whose generic "try again later" message points nowhere near the
  // cause. This is the check that stops the next optional field on PetLifeState repeating it.
  const hasUndefined = (value: unknown): boolean =>
    typeof value === 'object' && value !== null
      ? Object.values(value).some((v) => v === undefined || hasUndefined(v))
      : false;

  eq('a never-greeted pet omits lastGreetedAt entirely', 'lastGreetedAt' in makePetState('calm', 0.7), false);
  eq('a never-greeted pet carries no undefined', hasUndefined(makePetState('calm', 0.7)), false);
  eq('a greeted pet keeps the timestamp', makePetState('lively', 1, '2026-08-22T00:00:00.000Z').lastGreetedAt, '2026-08-22T00:00:00.000Z');
  eq('a greeted pet carries no undefined', hasUndefined(makePetState('lively', 1, '2026-08-22T00:00:00.000Z')), false);
  eq('the resting state carries no undefined', hasUndefined(PET_HOME_STATE), false);
  eq(
    'nothing the grower produces is undefined',
    hasUndefined(growOvergrowth({ existing: [], hours: 24 * 40, ...world })),
    false,
  );
}

console.log('\n-- 環境狀態 (the one calculation everything reads) ---------------------');

{
  const at = (count: number) =>
    resolveIslandAmbience(Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) => ({
      id: `t${i}`,
      kind: 'weed' as const,
      x: 0,
      z: 0,
      slot: -1,
      seed: 0.5,
    })));

  // §7 — a clean island is not "nearly normal", it is EXACTLY normal, and it is the shared
  // constant, so the common case allocates nothing.
  eq('a clean island is the neutral constant itself', resolveIslandAmbience([]) === NEUTRAL_AMBIENCE, true);
  eq('so is a save with no sprout list at all', resolveIslandAmbience(undefined) === NEUTRAL_AMBIENCE, true);
  eq('and nothing about it is graded', NEUTRAL_AMBIENCE.wildness, 0);

  // §1/§2 — more time away means a more overgrown island means a duller one. Monotonic across the
  // whole range, so there is no count at which tidying one weed makes the island look WORSE.
  let monotonic = true;
  let biggestStep = 0;
  for (let count = 1; count <= OVERGROWTH_MAX; count += 1) {
    const prev = at(count - 1);
    const here = at(count);
    if (here.wildness < prev.wildness) monotonic = false;
    if (here.saturation > prev.saturation) monotonic = false;
    if (here.brightness > prev.brightness) monotonic = false;
    biggestStep = Math.max(biggestStep, here.wildness - prev.wildness);
  }
  eq('wildness only ever rises with the sprout count', monotonic, true);

  // §2/§23 — 「不要使用硬切換」. One more weed is never allowed to be a visible event; the whole
  // range is 26 objects, so any single step worth more than a few percent is a cliff.
  eq('no single sprout moves the island more than 5%', biggestStep < 0.05, true);

  // §2 — 「不要做成黑暗恐怖風格」, pinned as a number rather than as a comment. Whatever anyone
  // retunes later, the most overgrown island the game can produce stays a lit, coloured island.
  const worst = at(OVERGROWTH_MAX);
  eq('the worst case is still bright', worst.brightness >= 0.8, true);
  eq('the worst case is still exposed', worst.exposure >= 0.85, true);
  eq('the worst case still has its colour', worst.saturation >= 0.7, true);
  eq('the worst case is fully wild', worst.wildness, 1);
  eq('and it reads as needing a tidy, not as a ruin', worst.grade.id, 'wild');

  // A ceiling that cannot be exceeded, however the list got that long.
  eq('an over-full island cannot go past the ceiling', at(OVERGROWTH_MAX + 40).wildness, 1);

  // §5 — the named grades cover the range in order, and the first one starts at zero.
  eq('the grade ladder starts at zero', ISLAND_GRADES[0].fromWildness, 0);
  eq(
    'the grade ladder only ever climbs',
    ISLAND_GRADES.every((g, i) => i === 0 || g.fromWildness > ISLAND_GRADES[i - 1].fromWildness),
    true,
  );
  eq('a clean island is 整潔', at(0).grade.id, 'fresh');

  // §4 — vines are the last thing to appear and they LENGTHEN; they must be worth nothing on an
  // island that is barely grown, or a five-day absence hangs full-length ivy on the house.
  eq('a barely-grown island has no vine growth', at(3).vineGrowth, 0);
  eq('a fully overgrown one has all of it', worst.vineGrowth, 1);
  eq(
    'vine growth is always a fraction',
    Array.from({ length: OVERGROWTH_MAX + 1 }, (_, i) => at(i).vineGrowth).every((v) => v >= 0 && v <= 1),
    true,
  );
}

console.log('\n-- 環境會恢復 (§7 — tidying is the recovery) ---------------------------');

{
  // The property the whole design turns on: the grading is derived from what is STANDING on the
  // island, not from the clock, so clearing the island IS restoring it. If this ever fails, a
  // player who tidies every weed is left in a garden that is still dim for reasons they cannot see
  // and cannot act on — which is the failure mode the clock-driven version has by construction.
  const grown = growOvergrowth({ existing: [], hours: 24 * 30, ...world });
  const before = resolveIslandAmbience(grown);
  eq('a month away leaves a visibly overgrown island', before.wildness > 0.6, true);
  eq('and a visibly duller one', before.saturation < 1 && before.brightness < 1, true);

  // Clear half of it and the island must already be measurably brighter — recovery is continuous,
  // not something that only lands once the last weed is gone.
  const half = grown.slice(0, Math.floor(grown.length / 2));
  const midway = resolveIslandAmbience(half);
  eq('clearing half brings the light part-way back', midway.brightness > before.brightness, true);
  eq('but not all the way', midway.brightness < 1, true);

  // Clear all of it, through the real tidy path, and the island is exactly as it was.
  let left = grown;
  for (const sprout of grown) left = tidyOvergrowthAt(left, sprout.x, sprout.z, HOME).sprouts;
  left = tidyOvergrowthAt(left, HOME.position[0], HOME.position[2], HOME).sprouts;
  eq('tidying everything empties the island', left.length, 0);
  eq('and the environment is neutral again', resolveIslandAmbience(left) === NEUTRAL_AMBIENCE, true);
}

console.log('\n-- 短暫離線不改變任何東西 (§1 Stage 0) --------------------------------');

{
  // An overnight break has to be invisible — not "subtle", invisible. This runs the real grower at
  // the quiet threshold and asserts the island is untouched all the way through to the grading.
  const overnight = growOvergrowth({ existing: [], hours: QUIET_HOURS, ...world });
  eq('twelve hours grows nothing', overnight.length, 0);
  eq('and changes nothing on screen', resolveIslandAmbience(overnight) === NEUTRAL_AMBIENCE, true);

  // And the first day is present but nearly nothing, which is what the eased curve is for.
  const day = growOvergrowth({ existing: [], hours: 24, ...world });
  const dayAmbience = resolveIslandAmbience(day);
  eq('a day away grows a little', day.length > 0, true);
  eq('but barely dims the island', dayAmbience.brightness > 0.98, true);
  eq('and still reads as a tidy island', dayAmbience.grade.id, 'fresh');
}

console.log('\n-- 生成位置 (§14 — a preference, never a constraint) -------------------');

{
  // The shelter bias spends siting attempts being fussy about where growth lands. If it is ever
  // allowed to become a hard rule, the island quietly grows FEWER things than the curve authorised
  // — and because the grading reads the sprout list, a month away also stops looking like a month
  // away. This is the check that keeps the two halves honest; it caught exactly that regression
  // when the bias was first added on top of an eight-attempt siting loop.
  let worst = Infinity;
  for (let i = 0; i < 60; i += 1) {
    worst = Math.min(worst, growOvergrowth({ existing: [], hours: 24 * 30, ...world }).length);
  }
  eq('a long absence actually fills the island', worst >= OVERGROWTH_MAX - 4, true);

  // And the bias does what it is for: growth favours the corners beside the house over the open
  // middle of the lawn. Aggregated over many runs, because one run is a handful of dice rolls.
  let sheltered = 0;
  let total = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < 40; i += 1) {
    for (const sprout of growOvergrowth({ existing: [], hours: 24 * 30, ...world })) {
      if (getOvergrowthKind(sprout.kind).surface !== 'ground') continue;
      total += 1;
      const d = Math.hypot(sprout.x - HOME.position[0], sprout.z - HOME.position[2]);
      if (d < 4.5) sheltered += 1;
    }
  }
  eq('most growth comes up in the sheltered corners', sheltered / total > 0.62, true);
  // Not ALL of it, though — a perfectly clean lawn reads as level design rather than as neglect.
  eq('but the open lawn still gets a scattering', sheltered / total < 0.95, true);
}

console.log('\n-- 離線褪色 (§1/§2 — a slide, never a switch) --------------------------');

{
  const left = (days: number) => 1 - colourDrainForHours(days * 24);

  // §2 — 「不要使用突然切換」, and the strongest possible form of it: sample the ENTIRE range at
  // hourly resolution and assert that no single hour of absence is ever a visible event. A
  // stepped implementation (「離線超過 X 天 → 直接變黑白」) fails this on the hour it steps.
  //
  // The step is measured only across the range that is actually DRAWN. The curve is steepest at
  // its own origin — the first hour past COLOUR_QUIET_HOURS is worth about 2%, because a power
  // curve below 1 leaves zero with an infinite slope — but every value there is under
  // COLOUR_MIN_DRAIN, where the veil is not mounted and the screen is untouched. Measuring
  // through the dead band would pin a number no player can see, and would push the tuning toward
  // a flatter curve to satisfy it; the assertion below is the requirement, and the one after it
  // is what makes the unmeasured part safe.
  let monotonic = true;
  let biggestStep = 0;
  let biggestHiddenDrain = 0;
  for (let hour = 1; hour <= COLOUR_FULL_DAYS * 24 + 48; hour += 1) {
    const prev = colourDrainForHours(hour - 1);
    const here = colourDrainForHours(hour);
    if (here < prev) monotonic = false;
    if (here < COLOUR_MIN_DRAIN) {
      biggestHiddenDrain = Math.max(biggestHiddenDrain, here);
      continue;
    }
    biggestStep = Math.max(biggestStep, here - prev);
  }
  eq('colour only ever drains, never comes back with time', monotonic, true);
  eq('no visible hour of absence is a jump', biggestStep < 0.01, true);
  eq('and everything below the threshold really is off screen', biggestHiddenDrain < COLOUR_MIN_DRAIN, true);

  // §1 — the ladder the brief spells out, as numbers. Not thresholds in the code (nothing branches
  // on these); this is the curve being held to the shape it was asked for, so a later retune that
  // makes a week away look like a month shows up here rather than on a player's screen.
  eq('an overnight break changes nothing at all', left(0.5), 1);
  eq('nor does a full day', left(1), 1);
  eq('three days is slightly faded', Math.abs(left(3) - 0.8) < 0.03, true);
  eq('ten days is halfway', Math.abs(left(10) - 0.5) < 0.03, true);
  eq('three weeks is nearly grey', Math.abs(left(21) - 0.2) < 0.04, true);
  eq('a month is black and white', left(COLOUR_FULL_DAYS + 1), 0);

  // §1 — 「完全黑白」 has to be reachable and then STAY reachable. A curve that merely approaches
  // zero never delivers the thing the brief asks for, and one that is not clamped would invert.
  eq('a very long absence stays black and white', left(365), 0);
  eq('and cannot go past it', colourDrainForHours(365 * 24 * 10) <= 1, true);

  // §15 — the short absences that make up almost every session produce no effect at all, which is
  // what keeps the veil unmounted and the common login free.
  eq('a same-day return is below the mount threshold', colourDrainForHours(20) < COLOUR_MIN_DRAIN, true);
  eq('so is a full day', colourDrainForHours(24) < COLOUR_MIN_DRAIN, true);
  eq('two days is not', colourDrainForHours(48) >= COLOUR_MIN_DRAIN, true);

  // Nonsense in, neutral out. `hours` comes from a parsed timestamp, so a clock set backwards or
  // a corrupt save must produce a normal-looking world rather than a NaN in a CSS filter.
  eq('a negative absence drains nothing', colourDrainForHours(-500), 0);
  eq('an unreadable absence drains nothing', colourDrainForHours(NaN), 0);

  // §14 — the admin presets are generated by inverting this same curve, so every level the panel
  // can show is a real point on it. If the inverse ever drifts, the panel starts demonstrating a
  // world no absence can produce.
  for (const stage of COLOUR_STAGES) {
    const hours = hoursForColourDrain(stage.previewDrain);
    eq(
      `preview 「${stage.label}」 round-trips through the real curve`,
      colourStageForDrain(colourDrainForHours(hours)).id,
      stage.id,
    );
  }
  eq(
    'and every preview except 正常彩色 is actually visible',
    COLOUR_STAGES.slice(1).every((s) => s.previewDrain >= COLOUR_MIN_DRAIN),
    true,
  );
  eq('the colour ladder starts at zero', COLOUR_STAGES[0].fromDrain, 0);
  eq(
    'and only ever climbs',
    COLOUR_STAGES.every((s, i) => i === 0 || s.fromDrain > COLOUR_STAGES[i - 1].fromDrain),
    true,
  );
}

console.log('\n-- 恢復演示 (§6/§7/§8 — the world comes back) --------------------------');

{
  const MONO = (COLOUR_FULL_DAYS + 1) * 24;
  const at = (t: number) => resolveIslandColour(MONO, t);

  // §6 — 「不要只是直接瞬間恢復正常彩色」. The world the player walks back into is the drained one,
  // and it is still drained a moment later; the recovery is something they watch happen.
  eq('the player arrives to a black and white island', at(0).saturation, 0);
  eq('and it is still black and white a beat later', at(RECOVERY_HOLD_SECONDS * 0.9).saturation, 0);
  eq('nothing is finished at arrival', at(0).done, false);

  // §7 — smooth all the way home, checked the same way the drain is: no frame of the animation
  // may be a jump. At 60fps a step of 4% would be a visible band.
  let smooth = true;
  let rising = true;
  let biggest = 0;
  let previous = at(0);
  for (let frame = 1; frame <= 600; frame += 1) {
    const here = at(frame / 60);
    if (here.saturation < previous.saturation - 1e-9) rising = false;
    if (here.bloom < previous.bloom - 1e-9) rising = false;
    biggest = Math.max(biggest, here.saturation - previous.saturation);
    previous = here;
  }
  smooth = biggest < 0.04;
  eq('the recovery only ever moves toward colour', rising, true);
  eq('and never in a visible step', smooth, true);

  // §8 — the colour arrives somewhere before it arrives everywhere. The bloom has to LEAD the
  // uniform lift through the middle of the animation, or the effect reads as a brightness slider
  // rather than as colour spreading out of the island.
  const mid = at(RECOVERY_HOLD_SECONDS + RECOVERY_SECONDS * 0.3);
  eq('colour is back in the middle of the frame first', mid.bloom > mid.saturation, true);
  eq('while most of the frame is still drained', mid.saturation < 0.5, true);

  // §13 — the effect must be a no-op BEFORE the element is removed, or the last frame flashes.
  // Both terms are checked because either one left short would do it on its own.
  const end = at(RECOVERY_HOLD_SECONDS + RECOVERY_SECONDS);
  eq('the recovery ends on exactly full colour', end.saturation, 1);
  eq('with the bloom past the whole frame', end.bloom, 1);
  eq('and reports itself finished', end.done, true);
  eq('and stays finished', at(9999).done, true);

  // §11 — 「數秒內」. Pinned so a later retune cannot quietly turn this into a cutscene.
  eq('the whole demo is a few seconds', RECOVERY_HOLD_SECONDS + RECOVERY_SECONDS <= 10, true);

  // §12 — a player who leaves mid-recovery. There is no stored progress to reconcile: the next
  // login measures a SHORTER absence and therefore arrives at a shallower drain, all the way down
  // to no effect at all. This is the property that makes the missing 「正在恢復」 flag safe.
  const interrupted = resolveIslandColour(MONO, RECOVERY_HOLD_SECONDS + RECOVERY_SECONDS * 0.5);
  eq('leaving halfway is a legal state, not an error', interrupted.done, false);
  eq('and coming back an hour later drains almost nothing', colourDrainForHours(1) < COLOUR_MIN_DRAIN, true);
  eq(
    'the second visit is always gentler than the first',
    colourDrainForHours(48) < colourDrainForHours(MONO),
    true,
  );

  // An absence too short to show is not a zero-length animation, it is no animation: the veil
  // reads `done` and never mounts. Identity, so the common case allocates nothing.
  eq('a short absence resolves to the shared neutral state', resolveIslandColour(20, 0) === CLEAR_COLOUR_STATE, true);
  eq('held previews of a short absence are neutral too', resolveIslandColour(20, null) === CLEAR_COLOUR_STATE, true);

  // §14 — the admin hold. Frozen at the arrival state and never `done`, so it stays on screen to
  // be looked at instead of curing itself while the tester reads the readout.
  const held = resolveIslandColour(MONO, null);
  eq('a held preview sits at the arrival state', held.saturation, 0);
  eq('and never completes on its own', held.done, false);
  eq('and shows no bloom, because nothing is recovering', held.bloom, 0);
}

console.log('\n-- 兩半互不干涉 (the clock half and the sprout half) --------------------');

{
  // The one structural claim the whole design rests on: the permanent grading knows nothing about
  // time, and the transient one knows nothing about the island. If either ever starts reading the
  // other's input, 「整理完島還是灰的」 (or 「恢復完之後又變灰」) is back.
  const grown = growOvergrowth({ existing: [], hours: 24 * 30, ...world });
  const ambience = resolveIslandAmbience(grown);

  // The permanent half stays inside its gentle band no matter how long the absence was — it is
  // the SPROUTS that dim it, and there are only ever OVERGROWTH_MAX of those.
  eq('a month away still leaves the light coloured', ambience.saturation >= 0.7, true);
  eq('the drain is the only thing that can reach greyscale', colourDrainForHours(24 * 31), 1);

  // And tidying, which is the permanent half's recovery, is untouched by any of this.
  let left = grown;
  for (const sprout of grown) left = tidyOvergrowthAt(left, sprout.x, sprout.z, HOME).sprouts;
  left = tidyOvergrowthAt(left, HOME.position[0], HOME.position[2], HOME).sprouts;
  eq('tidying still returns the island to neutral', resolveIslandAmbience(left) === NEUTRAL_AMBIENCE, true);
  // …and the colour drain does not care either way, because it never looked at the list.
  eq('and the drain is unchanged by tidying', colourDrainForHours(24 * 31), 1);
}

console.log(
  failures === 0
    ? `\nALL PASS (${checks} checks)\n`
    : `\n${failures} of ${checks} checks FAILED\n`,
);
process.exit(failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);

```

## scripts/test-pet-care.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 寵物照護 — rules tests.
 *
 * Run with `npm run test:pet-care`. Same tsx-script style as `test:offline-return` and the
 * `audit:*` checks, because that is the test runner this repo has.
 *
 * The properties pinned here are the ones the brief states as REQUIREMENTS — the things that would
 * still typecheck, still run, and still be wrong:
 *
 *  §6/§20  nothing can reach zero, nothing is irreversible, and one bowl always brings an animal
 *          all the way back. There is no death mechanic and no state a player cannot recover from.
 *  §3/§15  the response to activity is CONTINUOUS and monotonic — no single point on the range is a
 *          visible step, so the animal changes gradually instead of switching.
 *  §16     time is measured, not counted: settling once over a long gap equals settling many times
 *          along it, and settling twice at the same instant changes nothing. This is the property
 *          that makes the offline case free and the one a refactor is most likely to break.
 *  §4      not being fed lowers activity, and lowered activity is what sends the animal to its bed.
 *  §7/§22  the behaviour decision is a pure function of a context — every behaviour is reachable,
 *          and an owner who walks away is always followed.
 *  §9      a resting spot is found from a DECLARED capability, never from an id or a name, and a
 *          bed the player placed always beats the improvised one.
 *  §11/§12 pet food is an ordinary stacking catalog item, and its declared summary matches what it
 *          actually does.
 */

import {
  ALL_PET_BEHAVIORS,
  PET_BEHAVIORS,
  PET_CARE_TUNING,
  PET_CONDITION_BANDS,
  PET_FOOD_EFFECT_RANGE,
  PET_LEASH_DISTANCE,
  applyPetCareEffects,
  combinePetMotion,
  decidePetBehavior,
  newPetCareState,
  petActivityResponse,
  petCondition,
  readPetCareState,
  readPetCareStates,
  settlePetCare,
  withPetCare,
  type PetBehaviorContext,
  type PetBehaviorId,
  type PetCareState,
} from '../src/constants/petCare';
import {
  consumableAcceptsSpecies,
  getConsumablesFor,
  getPetFoodsFor,
  petEffectsFrom,
} from '../src/constants/consumables';
import {
  ALL_PET_HABITAT_KINDS,
  PET_HABITAT_KINDS,
  getHabitatItems,
} from '../src/constants/petHabitats';
import { ALL_PET_SPECIES, PET_SPECIES, PET_SPECIES_TABLE } from '../src/constants/pets';
import { isPetSupplyItem, speciesServedBy } from '../src/lib/petCompatibility';
import { PET_MOODS } from '../src/constants/islandReturn';
import { ALL_ITEMS, getItemById } from '../src/constants/items';
import {
  getCategoryPlacementScope,
  getDisplayCategory,
  getPlacementCategoriesIn,
} from '../src/utils/categoryUtils';
import { collectRestingSpots, resolveRestingSpot } from '../src/lib/petRestingSpots';
import type { PlacedItem } from '../src/types';

let failures = 0;
let checks = 0;

function eq(name: string, got: unknown, want: unknown): void {
  checks++;
  const ok = JSON.stringify(got) === JSON.stringify(want);
  if (!ok) {
    failures++;
    console.log(`FAIL  ${name}\n        got  ${JSON.stringify(got)}\n        want ${JSON.stringify(want)}`);
  } else {
    console.log(`PASS  ${name}`);
  }
}

const HOURS = 3_600_000;
const NOW = Date.parse('2026-08-31T12:00:00Z');
/** A care state stamped `h` hours before NOW, so settling it to NOW measures exactly that gap. */
const stateAgo = (h: number, nutrition = 1, energy = 1): PetCareState => ({
  nutrition,
  energy,
  updatedAt: new Date(NOW - h * HOURS).toISOString(),
});

const round = (n: number) => Math.round(n * 1e6) / 1e6;

console.log('\n-- nothing can be lost (§6, §20) --------------------------------------');

{
  // A YEAR away. If any state in this system can be reached that a player cannot walk back from,
  // this is where it is.
  const abandoned = settlePetCare(stateAgo(24 * 365), NOW);
  eq('a year away never empties the bowl', abandoned.nutrition >= PET_CARE_TUNING.nutritionFloor, true);
  eq('a year away never stops the animal', abandoned.energy >= PET_CARE_TUNING.energyFloor, true);
  eq('and both are still real numbers', Number.isFinite(abandoned.nutrition + abandoned.energy), true);

  // One bowl of the game's actual food, on the game's actual worst case.
  const food = getItemById('petfood-basic')!;
  const fed = applyPetCareEffects(abandoned, petEffectsFrom(food.consumable!.effects), NOW);
  eq('one bowl visibly moves the worst case', fed.delta.nutrition > 0.4, true);
  // Two bowls, because one is deliberately not a full bowl (§15: no instant switch).
  const twice = applyPetCareEffects(fed.state, petEffectsFrom(food.consumable!.effects), NOW);
  eq('two bowls fill it completely', round(twice.state.nutrition), 1);

  // …and the activity climbs back on its own once nutrition is up, which is what makes the
  // consequence of neglect fully reversible rather than merely survivable. Half a day, because
  // energy is deliberately lagged behind food (§15 — no instant switch).
  const rested = settlePetCare(twice.state, NOW + 12 * HOURS);
  eq('a fed animal is lively again by the next day', rested.energy > 0.8, true);
  eq('and it is far above where it was', rested.energy - abandoned.energy > 0.4, true);
  eq('right back to the top of the ladder', petCondition(rested).band.id, 'thriving');

  // The lowest band is a real, reachable state — and it is the LOWEST one. A ladder whose bottom
  // rung is unreachable is one whose copy nobody ever reads.
  eq('the worst case lands on the lowest band', petCondition(abandoned).band.id, 'drowsy');
  eq('the lowest band is where the ladder starts', PET_CONDITION_BANDS[0].fromActivity, 0);
}

console.log('\n-- time is measured, never counted (§16) ------------------------------');

{
  // The property the whole offline story rests on: one settle over a gap equals many settles along
  // it. If this fails, a player who left the tab open gets a different pet from one who closed it.
  const start = stateAgo(0, 0.9, 0.8);
  const once = settlePetCare({ ...start }, NOW + 72 * HOURS);

  let stepped = { ...start };
  for (let h = 1; h <= 72; h++) stepped = settlePetCare(stepped, NOW + h * HOURS);

  eq(
    'one long settle ≈ many short ones (nutrition)',
    Math.abs(once.nutrition - stepped.nutrition) < 1e-9,
    true,
  );
  // Energy is solved exactly rather than approximated, so this is not merely 「close enough」: the
  // two agree to floating-point noise. An approximation would drift with how often it was applied,
  // which is the same as saying a background tab would produce a different animal.
  eq('one long settle == many short ones (energy)', Math.abs(once.energy - stepped.energy) < 1e-9, true);

  // Idempotent at the same instant: every reader settles freely, and none of them has to coordinate.
  const settled = settlePetCare(stateAgo(30), NOW);
  eq('settling twice at the same instant is a no-op', settlePetCare(settled, NOW), settled);

  // A clock that went backwards must never be a way to restore an animal.
  const rewound = settlePetCare(stateAgo(-100, 0.3, 0.3), NOW);
  eq('a backwards clock restores nothing', rewound.nutrition, 0.3);

  // Junk out of the document store is a healthy animal, not NaN walking into the movement code.
  const junk = readPetCareState({ nutrition: 'lots', energy: null, updatedAt: 42 }, NOW);
  eq('unreadable stored state reads as healthy', [junk.nutrition, junk.energy], [1, 1]);
  eq('an absent state is a brand-new pet', readPetCareState(undefined, NOW), newPetCareState(NOW));
}

console.log('\n-- neglect lowers activity, gradually (§3, §4, §15) -------------------');

{
  // Monotonic in time away: more neglect is never MORE activity.
  let previous = 2;
  let monotonic = true;
  for (let days = 0; days <= 30; days++) {
    const activity = petCondition(settlePetCare(stateAgo(0), NOW + days * 24 * HOURS)).activity;
    if (activity > previous + 1e-9) monotonic = false;
    previous = activity;
  }
  eq('activity never rises with more neglect', monotonic, true);

  // And it visibly falls: a system where nothing changes is also monotonic.
  const day1 = petCondition(settlePetCare(stateAgo(0), NOW + 24 * HOURS)).activity;
  const day7 = petCondition(settlePetCare(stateAgo(0), NOW + 7 * 24 * HOURS)).activity;
  eq('a week of neglect is plainly quieter than a day', day1 - day7 > 0.2, true);

  // §15: no single step across the whole range is a visible jump. This is the check that would
  // catch someone replacing the interpolation with a threshold ladder.
  let biggestStep = 0;
  for (let i = 1; i <= 200; i++) {
    const a = petActivityResponse(i / 200);
    const b = petActivityResponse((i - 1) / 200);
    biggestStep = Math.max(
      biggestStep,
      Math.abs(a.pace - b.pace),
      Math.abs(a.liveliness - b.liveliness),
      Math.abs(a.nestPull - b.nestPull),
    );
  }
  eq('the motion response has no visible step anywhere', biggestStep < 0.02, true);

  // Pace never reaches zero. A pet that stops dead reads as broken, not as tired.
  eq('even a listless animal still walks', petActivityResponse(0).pace > 0.5, true);
  eq('a well-fed animal is not slowed at all', petActivityResponse(1).pace >= 1, true);

  // Nutrition reaches behaviour THROUGH energy — the causal chain the whole system is built on.
  const starved = settlePetCare(stateAgo(0, 0.2, 1), NOW + 48 * HOURS);
  const full = settlePetCare(stateAgo(0, 1, 1), NOW + 48 * HOURS);
  eq('low nutrition drags activity down with it', starved.energy < full.energy, true);

  // Neither system may overwrite the other: a quiet mood and a hungry animal compose.
  const quiet = combinePetMotion(PET_MOODS.waiting, petActivityResponse(0.2));
  eq('mood and care multiply rather than replace', quiet.pace < PET_MOODS.waiting.pace, true);
  eq('and the stronger pull toward the bed wins', quiet.nestPull >= PET_MOODS.waiting.nestPull, true);
}

console.log('\n-- the behaviour layer (§7, §21, §22) --------------------------------');

{
  const base: PetBehaviorContext = {
    activity: 0.9,
    nestPull: 0,
    ownerDistance: 2,
    ownerMoving: false,
    restDistance: 8,
    ownerNearRest: false,
    previous: 'follow',
  };

  // Sampling with a fixed sweep of rolls rather than Math.random, so this is a statement about the
  // distribution rather than about one lucky draw.
  const sample = (ctx: PetBehaviorContext) => {
    const counts = new Map<PetBehaviorId, number>();
    for (let i = 0; i < 400; i++) {
      const id = decidePetBehavior(ctx, i / 400);
      counts.set(id, (counts.get(id) ?? 0) + 1);
    }
    return counts;
  };

  // An owner who walks off is followed, whatever the animal would rather do. Otherwise a player
  // reads a resting pet as one that is broken.
  eq(
    'an owner past the leash is always followed',
    decidePetBehavior({ ...base, activity: 0, nestPull: 1, ownerDistance: PET_LEASH_DISTANCE + 1 }, 0.99),
    'follow',
  );

  // A lively animal mostly follows, and explores sometimes — 「有正常 Idle 行為、可以探索」.
  const lively = sample(base);
  eq('a lively pet mostly follows', (lively.get('follow') ?? 0) > 150, true);
  eq('a lively pet also explores', (lively.get('wander') ?? 0) > 0, true);
  eq('a lively pet never takes itself to bed', (lively.get('goToBed') ?? 0) + (lively.get('rest') ?? 0), 0);

  // A neglected animal, owner elsewhere: it heads for its bed. This is 「躲在窩裡」, and it is the
  // consequence the whole feature is built to produce.
  const tired = sample({ ...base, activity: 0.15, nestPull: 0.9, ownerDistance: 10, previous: 'idle' });
  eq('a listless pet heads for its bed', (tired.get('goToBed') ?? 0) > 100, true);
  eq('a listless pet rarely explores', (tired.get('wander') ?? 0), 0);

  // …and gets up the moment its owner comes over. This needs no code of its own — it is what
  // happens when the resting weights go to zero.
  const noticed = sample({ ...base, activity: 0.15, nestPull: 0.9, ownerDistance: 1.5, restDistance: 0.2 });
  eq('a resting pet gets up when you come to it', (noticed.get('rest') ?? 0) + (noticed.get('goToBed') ?? 0), 0);

  // Resting happens IN the bed, never on the way to it — §21's 「不要 teleport 到寵物窩」 expressed
  // as the property that actually prevents it.
  const enRoute = sample({ ...base, activity: 0.1, nestPull: 1, ownerDistance: 10, restDistance: 6 });
  eq('a pet only rests once it has arrived', enRoute.get('rest') ?? 0, 0);

  // Every declared behaviour is reachable. A table entry nothing can select is dead data that
  // still reads like a feature.
  const reachable = new Set<PetBehaviorId>();
  for (const activity of [0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1]) {
    for (const ownerDistance of [1, 5, 10]) {
      for (const restDistance of [0.3, 1, 6]) {
        for (const ownerMoving of [false, true]) {
          for (const nestPull of [0, 0.5, 1]) {
            for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
              reachable.add(
                decidePetBehavior(
                  { ...base, activity, nestPull, ownerDistance, restDistance, ownerMoving },
                  i / 20,
                ),
              );
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
  eq('every behaviour in the table is reachable', reachable.size, ALL_PET_BEHAVIORS.length);

  // The anchors have to be honoured by the mover, so at least assert the table is coherent: the
  // two resting behaviours aim at the bed, and following aims at the owner.
  eq('goToBed and rest both aim at the bed', [PET_BEHAVIORS.goToBed.anchor, PET_BEHAVIORS.rest.anchor], ['rest', 'rest']);
  eq('following aims at the owner', PET_BEHAVIORS.follow.anchor, 'owner');
  eq('only the two settled behaviours are settled', ALL_PET_BEHAVIORS.filter((b) => b.settled).map((b) => b.id), ['idle', 'rest']);
}

console.log('\n-- resting spots are declared, never named (§9) -----------------------');

{
  const HOME = { position: [2, 0, -1] as [number, number, number], rotation: 0.6 };
  const bed: PlacedItem = {
    instanceId: 'bed-a',
    itemId: 'petbed-outdoor-basic',
    position: [7, 0, 3],
    rotation: 0,
  };
  const notABed: PlacedItem = {
    instanceId: 'tree-a',
    itemId: 'deco-campfire',
    position: [7.1, 0, 3.1],
    rotation: 0,
  };

  const none = resolveRestingSpot({ placements: [notABed], home: HOME, islandScale: 1 });
  eq('with no bed placed, the improvised spot is used', none.source, 'default');

  const withBed = resolveRestingSpot({ placements: [notABed, bed], home: HOME, islandScale: 1 });
  eq('a placed bed wins over the improvised spot', withBed.source, 'item');
  eq('and it is where the player actually put it', [withBed.x, withBed.z], [7, 3]);
  eq('the reach comes from the item, not from a constant', withBed.radius, getItemById('petbed-outdoor-basic')!.petRest!.radius);

  // Nothing is found by id or by name: the ONLY thing that makes a placement a resting spot is the
  // declared capability. A campfire sitting 10cm from the bed is not one.
  eq('a piece with no petRest is never a resting spot', collectRestingSpots({ placements: [notABed], home: HOME }).length, 0);

  // Two beds resolve to a stable winner, on every device and every reload — an order that depended
  // on where the pet happened to be standing would have it change its mind mid-garden.
  const farther: PlacedItem = { instanceId: 'bed-b', itemId: 'petbed-outdoor-basic', position: [20, 0, 20], rotation: 0 };
  const forwards = resolveRestingSpot({ placements: [bed, farther], home: HOME, islandScale: 1 });
  const backwards = resolveRestingSpot({ placements: [farther, bed], home: HOME, islandScale: 1 });
  eq('the same bed wins whatever order the placements are in', forwards.instanceId, backwards.instanceId);
  eq('and it is the one nearest the Home', forwards.instanceId, 'bed-a');

  // Every declared resting spot must actually be REACHABLE FROM A BUILD RAIL, or it is a bed the
  // player can own and never put down — which is the exact bug `placementScope` exists to prevent
  // (utils/categoryUtils.ts). Asserted against the rail's own resolver rather than against the shop
  // section, because the two are deliberately allowed to differ: 寵物窩 is browsed under 寵物 and
  // placed outdoors. Anything that stops it appearing in a rail fails here.
  for (const item of ALL_ITEMS.filter((i) => i.petRest)) {
    const category = getDisplayCategory(item.shopCategory)!;
    eq(`${item.name} is a placeable object`, category.kind, 'placeable');
    const scope = getCategoryPlacementScope(category);
    eq(
      `${item.name} is on the build rail it is scoped to`,
      getPlacementCategoriesIn(scope, ['placeable']).some((c) => c.id === item.shopCategory),
      true,
    );
  }
}

console.log('\n-- pet food is an ordinary item (§11, §12) ----------------------------');

{
  const foods = getConsumablesFor('pet');
  eq('there is at least one pet food in the catalog', foods.length >= 1, true);

  for (const food of foods) {
    const spec = food.consumable!;
    const category = getDisplayCategory(food.shopCategory);

    // It stacks and is spent — not worn, not placed, not applied. That is what `consumable` means
    // in the taxonomy, and it is what puts the bag in the ordinary inventory rather than in one of
    // its own (§12).
    eq(`${food.name} lives on a consumable shelf`, category?.kind, 'consumable');
    eq(`${food.name} is bought with gold like anything else`, food.price > 0, true);

    // Amounts stay inside the sanity range: a mistyped 4 in a catalog row can only ever be a bowl
    // that fills the animal, never one that does something impossible.
    for (const effect of spec.effects) {
      eq(
        `${food.name}'s ${effect.kind} is a sane amount`,
        effect.amount >= PET_FOOD_EFFECT_RANGE.min && effect.amount <= PET_FOOD_EFFECT_RANGE.max,
        true,
      );
    }

    // The written summary has to be true. It is hand-written on purpose (a generated one reads like
    // a spreadsheet), which is exactly why it needs a guard against drifting away from the numbers.
    const applied = petEffectsFrom(spec.effects);
    if (applied.nutrition > 0) {
      eq(
        `${food.name}'s summary mentions the nutrition it gives`,
        spec.effectSummary.includes(`${Math.round(applied.nutrition * 100)}%`),
        true,
      );
    }
    if (applied.energy > 0) {
      eq(
        `${food.name}'s summary mentions the activity it gives`,
        spec.effectSummary.includes(`${Math.round(applied.energy * 100)}%`),
        true,
      );
    }

    // Feeding a full animal must never be able to take a bag for nothing — the caller refuses it,
    // but the maths must agree that there was nothing to give.
    const full = applyPetCareEffects({ nutrition: 1, energy: 1, updatedAt: new Date(NOW).toISOString() }, applied, NOW);
    eq(`${food.name} gives a full animal nothing`, [round(full.delta.nutrition), round(full.delta.energy)], [0, 0]);
  }
}

console.log('\n-- 休息處按物種適配，不是按名字 (§1, §3, §4, §5) ----------------------');

{
  // The compatibility system in one assertion per row: a home says which shapes it is and which
  // animals it takes, and the SHAPE bounds the animals. A 「鳥也能睡的狗屋」 typo — the exact thing
  // §1 exists to prevent — fails right here rather than shipping as a bird standing in a kennel.
  const habitats = ALL_ITEMS.filter((i) => i.petRest);
  eq('the catalog sells more than one kind of home', habitats.length >= 6, true);

  for (const item of habitats) {
    const spec = item.petRest!;
    const kind = PET_HABITAT_KINDS[spec.kind];
    eq(`${item.name} declares a real habitat kind`, !!kind, true);
    eq(`${item.name} is for at least one species`, spec.species.length > 0, true);
    eq(
      `${item.name}'s species all fit a ${kind.label}`,
      spec.species.every((s) => kind.suitableFor.includes(s)),
      true,
    );
    // §9's constraint, as data. A raised resting place is only reachable by something that flies:
    // this game has no climbing, so a dog bed at height 1 would be a bed the dog stands under
    // forever. Only the perch postures may declare a height, and they must.
    if (kind.posture === 'perch') {
      eq(`${item.name} is somewhere a bird can land on`, (spec.height ?? 0) > 0, true);
    } else {
      eq(`${item.name} is on the ground, where a walker can reach it`, spec.height ?? 0, 0);
    }
  }

  // Every species the game sells has somewhere to sleep. A species with animals and no homes is
  // the state this whole change was made to get out of.
  for (const species of PET_SPECIES) {
    eq(
      `${PET_SPECIES_TABLE[species].label} has homes it can use`,
      getHabitatItems(species).length >= 2,
      true,
    );
  }

  // And the filtering is real, not decorative: put one of everything on the island and each animal
  // resolves only its own.
  const HOME = { position: [0, 0, 0] as [number, number, number], rotation: 0 };
  const placements: PlacedItem[] = habitats.map((item, i) => ({
    instanceId: `h-${i}`,
    itemId: item.id,
    position: [i * 3, 0, 0] as [number, number, number],
    rotation: 0,
  }));

  for (const species of PET_SPECIES) {
    const seen = collectRestingSpots({ placements, home: HOME, species });
    eq(
      `a ${PET_SPECIES_TABLE[species].label} sees only homes that accept it`,
      seen.every((spot) => getItemById(spot.itemId!)!.petRest!.species.includes(species)),
      true,
    );
    eq(`a ${PET_SPECIES_TABLE[species].label} sees some`, seen.length > 0, true);
  }

  // The specific failure §1 names: a bird with only a dog bed placed has NO owned spot and falls
  // back to the improvised nest — it does not claim the kennel.
  const kennelOnly: PlacedItem[] = [
    { instanceId: 'k', itemId: 'pethome-dog-cabin', position: [4, 0, 0], rotation: 0 },
  ];
  eq(
    'a bird never settles in a dog house',
    resolveRestingSpot({ placements: kennelOnly, home: HOME, islandScale: 1, petItemId: 'pet-bird-budgie' }).source,
    'default',
  );
  eq(
    'but a dog does',
    resolveRestingSpot({ placements: kennelOnly, home: HOME, islandScale: 1, petItemId: 'pet-dog-shiba' }).source,
    'item',
  );

  // A bird's own home carries the height it lands at, all the way through to the resolved spot —
  // the number Three/IslandPet.tsx flies to.
  const perch: PlacedItem[] = [
    { instanceId: 'p', itemId: 'pethome-bird-perch', position: [2, 0, 0], rotation: 0 },
  ];
  const landed = resolveRestingSpot({ placements: perch, home: HOME, islandScale: 1, petItemId: 'pet-bird-canary' });
  eq('a perch is somewhere off the ground', landed.height > 0.5, true);
  eq('and the bird grips it rather than lying on it', landed.posture, 'perch');
  // The label is the item's own name, never a second copy of it written on the spec.
  eq('a spot is called what the item is called', landed.label, getItemById('pethome-bird-perch')!.name);
}

console.log('\n-- 飼料按物種適配 (§10, §11, §17) --------------------------------------');

{
  const foods = getConsumablesFor('pet');
  eq('there is a real shelf of food, not one bag', foods.length >= 6, true);

  for (const species of PET_SPECIES) {
    const label = PET_SPECIES_TABLE[species].label;
    const forSpecies = getPetFoodsFor(species);
    // Two each at minimum — one meal and one treat — so 「餵食」 is a choice rather than a button.
    eq(`${label} has at least two things it can eat`, forSpecies.length >= 2, true);
    // §17, stated as the property that matters: nothing a player could be shown for this animal is
    // a food this animal cannot have.
    eq(
      `nothing offered to ${label} is incompatible with it`,
      forSpecies.every((f) => consumableAcceptsSpecies(f.consumable!, species)),
      true,
    );
    // …and the filter actually removes things. A filter that returns everything is not a filter.
    eq(`${label}'s list is narrower than the whole shelf`, forSpecies.length < foods.length, true);
  }

  // The universal foods really are universal, and the species-specific ones really are not.
  const universal = foods.filter((f) => !f.consumable!.species);
  eq('there is at least one food every animal can eat', universal.length >= 1, true);
  for (const food of universal) {
    eq(
      `${food.name} is offered to every species`,
      PET_SPECIES.every((s) => getPetFoodsFor(s).some((f) => f.id === food.id)),
      true,
    );
  }
  const dogOnly = getItemById('petfood-dog-stew')!;
  eq('a dog food is invisible to a cat', getPetFoodsFor('cat').some((f) => f.id === dogOnly.id), false);
  eq('a dog food is invisible to a bird', getPetFoodsFor('bird').some((f) => f.id === dogOnly.id), false);

  // Meals and treats are told apart by their NUMBERS, not by a 「食物類型」 field — there is none.
  // What has to hold is that the shelf actually contains both shapes for every species, or
  // 「不同食物應在恢復效果上有差異」 (§12) is a claim the data does not back.
  for (const species of PET_SPECIES) {
    const applied = getPetFoodsFor(species).map((f) => petEffectsFrom(f.consumable!.effects));
    eq(
      `${PET_SPECIES_TABLE[species].label} has a proper meal to eat`,
      applied.some((a) => a.nutrition >= 0.5),
      true,
    );
    eq(
      `${PET_SPECIES_TABLE[species].label} has a treat, not just meals`,
      applied.some((a) => a.energy > a.nutrition),
      true,
    );
  }
}

console.log('\n-- 一隻寵物一份狀態 (§6, §21) -----------------------------------------');

{
  const dog = 'pet-dog-shiba';
  const cat = 'pet-cat-orange';
  const hungry: PetCareState = { nutrition: 0.2, energy: 0.25, updatedAt: new Date(NOW).toISOString() };
  const full: PetCareState = { nutrition: 1, energy: 1, updatedAt: new Date(NOW).toISOString() };

  const before = { [dog]: hungry, [cat]: full };
  const fed = applyPetCareEffects(before[dog], petEffectsFrom(getItemById('petfood-dog-stew')!.consumable!.effects), NOW);
  const after = withPetCare(before, dog, fed.state, NOW);

  eq('feeding one pet feeds that pet', after[dog].nutrition > before[dog].nutrition, true);
  // The assertion the whole per-pet map exists for. A missing spread here would read as a feature
  // working perfectly — every pet would just quietly share one appetite.
  eq('feeding one pet leaves the others exactly as they were', after[cat], before[cat]);
  eq('and does not invent animals nobody owns', Object.keys(after).sort(), [cat, dog].sort());

  // Junk out of the document store must not become a phantom pet in the household.
  const cleaned = withPetCare({ [dog]: hungry, '': full, bad: 42 }, cat, full, NOW);
  eq('an unreadable entry is dropped rather than repaired', Object.keys(cleaned).sort(), [cat, dog].sort());
  eq('a map that is not a map reads as an empty household', readPetCareStates('nope', NOW), {});
}

console.log('\n-- 新增一種寵物不需要改程式 (§6, §24) ---------------------------------');

{
  // The claim this whole design makes, checked as far as data can check it: every species in the
  // table is fully described BY the table, so nothing downstream needs a branch to handle one.
  for (const species of PET_SPECIES) {
    const def = PET_SPECIES_TABLE[species];
    eq(`${species} is in the species table`, def?.id, species);
    eq(`${species} has a word for a shelf`, def.label.length > 0, true);
    eq(`${species} has a word for a sentence`, def.companionNoun.length > 0, true);
    eq(`${species} says how it gets around`, ['ground', 'air'].includes(def.locomotion), true);
    // The shelf its animals are sold on has to be real, or 「去買一隻」 links nowhere.
    eq(`${species}'s animals have a shelf`, !!getDisplayCategory(def.shopCategory), true);
    eq(
      `${species}'s shelf actually has animals on it`,
      ALL_ITEMS.some((i) => i.shopCategory === def.shopCategory),
      true,
    );
  }
  eq('every species in the table is one the id parser knows', ALL_PET_SPECIES.length, PET_SPECIES.length);

  // Every habitat kind is reachable from the catalog. A kind nothing is sold as is dead vocabulary
  // that still reads like a feature — the same rule the behaviour table is held to above.
  const kindsSold = new Set(ALL_ITEMS.filter((i) => i.petRest).map((i) => i.petRest!.kind));
  eq('every declared habitat kind is actually sold', kindsSold.size, ALL_PET_HABITAT_KINDS.length);
}

console.log('\n-- 寵物用品都在寵物分頁 (§23) -----------------------------------------');

{
  // §23: 狗窩 / 貓飼料 / 鳥籠 must not be scattered through 家具 / 飾品 / 特殊商品. Every pet supply
  // in the catalog is asserted to be on a 寵物 shelf, so a new one filed under 花園 fails here
  // rather than being found by a player who went looking in the wrong section.
  for (const item of ALL_ITEMS.filter(isPetSupplyItem)) {
    const category = getDisplayCategory(item.shopCategory);
    eq(`${item.name} is browsed under 寵物`, category?.mainSection, 'PET');
  }

  // And the shop's species chips are derived from the shelf rather than hard-coded: both pet
  // shelves serve all three species, so both get the full row.
  for (const shelf of ['PetSupplies', 'PetHomes']) {
    const items = ALL_ITEMS.filter((i) => i.shopCategory === shelf);
    eq(`${shelf} offers a chip for every species`, speciesServedBy(items), [...PET_SPECIES]);
  }
}

console.log(
  failures === 0
    ? `\nALL PASS (${checks} checks)\n`
    : `\n${failures} of ${checks} checks FAILED\n`,
);
process.exit(failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);

```

## scripts/test-pet-interactions.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 寵物互動 — rules tests.
 *
 * Run with `npm run test:pet-interactions`. The sibling of `test:pet-care`: that one pins how an
 * animal's condition moves over hours; this one pins what it does in the seconds after its owner
 * does something to it — and above all that every one of those things ENDS.
 *
 *   反應   every reaction starts and ends at rest (no pop into or out of it), stays within a
 *          gentle amplitude, and 「開心」 is hops and a wag rather than the old spin
 *   餵食   the bowl goes in front of the owner toward the animal, never under the owner's feet;
 *          the animal eats from behind it, facing the owner
 *   玩耍   the toy follows the owner's facing, never dips below the ground at any instant of its
 *          flight or bounce, and comes to rest where it says it will
 *   生命週期 one activity per animal; feeding outranks play; everything expires on its own clock;
 *          two animals never share one; a reset clears it all
 */

import { PET_SPECIES } from '../src/constants/pets';
import { PET_FEED_CELEBRATION_SECONDS } from '../src/constants/petCare';
import {
  PET_FEED,
  PET_PETTING,
  PET_PLAY,
  PET_PLAY_STYLE,
  PET_REACTIONS,
  type PetReactionId,
} from '../src/constants/petInteractions';
import {
  addPetReaction,
  bowlSpot,
  eatStandSpot,
  emptyReactionFrame,
  reactionSpecFor,
  throwLanding,
  toyFlightPosition,
  toyRestPoint,
} from '../src/lib/petReaction';
import {
  currentPetActivity,
  currentPetReaction,
  endPetActivity,
  finishPetActivity,
  patPet,
  petActivityCount,
  petActivityExpired,
  playPetReaction,
  resetPetActivities,
  startEating,
  startPetting,
  startPlay,
  sweepPetActivities,
} from '../src/lib/petActivity';

let failures = 0;
let checks = 0;

function ok(name: string, condition: boolean, detail = ''): void {
  checks++;
  if (!condition) {
    failures++;
    console.log(`FAIL  ${name}${detail ? `\n        ${detail}` : ''}`);
  } else {
    console.log(`ok    ${name}${detail ? `  (${detail})` : ''}`);
  }
}

const near = (a: number, b: number, eps = 1e-6) => Math.abs(a - b) <= eps;

console.log('\n== 寵物互動 ==========================================================');

// --- 反應 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
console.log('\n-- 反應: rest at both ends, gentle in between ----------------------------------');

for (const id of Object.keys(PET_REACTIONS) as PetReactionId[]) {
  for (const airborne of [false, true]) {
    const spec = reactionSpecFor(id, airborne);
    const where = `${id}${airborne ? ' (air)' : ''}`;
    const at = (t: number) => {
      const f = emptyReactionFrame();
      addPetReaction(f, id, t, airborne);
      return f;
    };
    const start = at(0);
    const end = at(spec.seconds);
    const restStart = Math.max(Math.abs(start.hop), Math.abs(start.pitch), Math.abs(start.drop), Math.abs(start.roll), Math.abs(start.spin));
    const endSpinRemainder = Math.abs(Math.sin(end.spin / 2));
    const restEnd = Math.max(Math.abs(end.hop), Math.abs(end.pitch), Math.abs(end.drop), Math.abs(end.roll), endSpinRemainder);
    ok(`${where} · starts at rest`, restStart < 1e-6, restStart.toExponential(1));
    ok(`${where} · ends at rest (a spin ends on a whole turn)`, restEnd < 1e-6, restEnd.toExponential(1));

    let maxHop = 0;
    let maxPitch = 0;
    let maxDrop = 0;
    let maxRoll = 0;
    let minHop = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i <= 120; i++) {
      const f = at((i / 120) * spec.seconds);
      maxHop = Math.max(maxHop, f.hop);
      minHop = Math.min(minHop, f.hop);
      maxPitch = Math.max(maxPitch, Math.abs(f.pitch));
      maxDrop = Math.max(maxDrop, Math.abs(f.drop));
      maxRoll = Math.max(maxRoll, Math.abs(f.roll));
    }
    ok(`${where} · never hops below the ground`, minHop >= 0);
    ok(`${where} · stays gentle`, maxHop <= 0.4 && maxPitch <= 0.4 && maxDrop <= 0.16 && maxRoll <= 0.3,
      `hop ${maxHop.toFixed(2)} pitch ${maxPitch.toFixed(2)} drop ${maxDrop.toFixed(2)} roll ${maxRoll.toFixed(2)}`);
  }
}
ok('開心 is hops and a wag, not the old spin on the spot', !PET_REACTIONS.happy.spin && (PET_REACTIONS.happy.wag ?? 0) >= 1);

// --- 餵食 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
console.log('\n-- 餵食: where the bowl goes and where the animal eats from ------------------');
{
  const owner = { x: 2, z: -1, yaw: 0.4 };
  const pet = { x: 4, z: 0.5 };
  const bowl = bowlSpot(owner, pet);
  const fromOwner = Math.hypot(bowl.x - owner.x, bowl.z - owner.z);
  ok('the bowl is set down at arm\'s length in front of the owner', near(fromOwner, PET_FEED.bowlAhead, 1e-9),
    fromOwner.toFixed(3));
  const toPet = [pet.x - owner.x, pet.z - owner.z];
  const toBowl = [bowl.x - owner.x, bowl.z - owner.z];
  const cos = (toPet[0] * toBowl[0] + toPet[1] * toBowl[1]) / (Math.hypot(toPet[0], toPet[1]) * Math.hypot(toBowl[0], toBowl[1]));
  ok('…on the animal\'s side', cos > 0.999);

  const underfoot = bowlSpot(owner, { x: owner.x + 0.05, z: owner.z });
  const facing = [Math.sin(owner.yaw), Math.cos(owner.yaw)];
  const dir = [(underfoot.x - owner.x) / PET_FEED.bowlAhead, (underfoot.z - owner.z) / PET_FEED.bowlAhead];
  ok('an animal standing on the owner\'s feet gets its bowl in front of the owner, not underneath', near(dir[0], facing[0], 1e-9) && near(dir[1], facing[1], 1e-9));

  for (const height of [0.45, 0.9]) {
    const stand = eatStandSpot(bowl, owner, height);
    const standFromOwner = Math.hypot(stand.x - owner.x, stand.z - owner.z);
    ok(`an animal ${height} tall eats from BEHIND the bowl, facing its owner`, standFromOwner > fromOwner
      && near(stand.yaw, Math.atan2(bowl.x - stand.x, bowl.z - stand.z), 1e-9));
  }
  ok('eating lasts exactly as long as the care system says a meal does', PET_FEED.eatSeconds === PET_FEED_CELEBRATION_SECONDS);
}

// --- 玩耍 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
console.log('\n-- 玩耍: the toy follows the owner and never goes underground ----------------');
{
  const landings = new Set<string>();
  for (let deg = 0; deg < 360; deg += 45) {
    const yaw = (deg * Math.PI) / 180;
    const land = throwLanding({ x: 0, z: 0, yaw }, 3);
    landings.add(`${land.x.toFixed(3)},${land.z.toFixed(3)}`);
    const heading = Math.atan2(land.x, land.z);
    let delta = heading - yaw;
    while (delta > Math.PI) delta -= Math.PI * 2;
    while (delta < -Math.PI) delta += Math.PI * 2;
    if (Math.abs(delta) > 1e-9) ok(`throw at ${deg}° goes the way the owner faces`, false, `off by ${delta}`);
  }
  ok('eight facings, eight different landings — the direction comes from the owner', landings.size === 8);

  const from = { x: 0, y: 1.4, z: 0 };
  const to = { x: 3, y: 0.3, z: 1 };
  let lowest = Infinity;
  let landedEarly = false;
  let sawLanded = false;
  const total = PET_PLAY.flightSeconds + PET_PLAY.bounces * PET_PLAY.bounceSeconds + 0.5;
  for (let i = 0; i <= 600; i++) {
    const t = (i / 600) * total;
    const { point, landed } = toyFlightPosition(from, to, t);
    lowest = Math.min(lowest, point.y);
    if (landed) sawLanded = true;
    if (landed && t < PET_PLAY.flightSeconds) landedEarly = true;
    if (sawLanded && !landed) landedEarly = true;
  }
  ok('the toy is never below the ground at any instant', lowest >= to.y - 1e-9, `lowest ${lowest.toFixed(4)} vs ground ${to.y}`);
  ok('it lands once and stays landed', sawLanded && !landedEarly);
  const start = toyFlightPosition(from, to, 0).point;
  ok('it leaves from the hand', near(start.x, from.x) && near(start.y, from.y) && near(start.z, from.z));
  const firstTouch = toyFlightPosition(from, to, PET_PLAY.flightSeconds).point;
  ok('its first touch is the landing point', near(firstTouch.x, to.x) && near(firstTouch.z, to.z) && near(firstTouch.y, to.y, 1e-6));
  const rest = toyFlightPosition(from, to, total).point;
  const said = toyRestPoint(from, to);
  ok('it comes to rest exactly where toyRestPoint says it will', near(rest.x, said.x) && near(rest.z, said.z) && near(rest.y, to.y));
  ok('the arc clears a knee-high animal', PET_PLAY.arcHeight > 0.8);
}

console.log('\n-- every species has a way to play, and they differ -------------------------');
ok('every species has a play style', PET_SPECIES.every((s) => !!PET_PLAY_STYLE[s]));
ok('the species do not all play the same way', new Set(Object.values(PET_PLAY_STYLE)).size === PET_SPECIES.length);

// --- 生命週期 -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
console.log('\n-- 生命週期: one at a time, outranked correctly, always ends -------------------');
{
  resetPetActivities();
  const t0 = 100000;
  const dog = 'pet-dog-shiba';
  const cat = 'pet-cat-orange';

  ok('petting starts', startPetting(dog, t0) && currentPetActivity(dog)?.kind === 'petting');
  patPet(dog, t0 + 500);
  ok('a pat plays a reaction', currentPetReaction(dog)?.id === 'pat');
  ok('play may take over from petting', startPlay(dog, 'fetch', t0 + 600) && currentPetActivity(dog)?.kind === 'play');
  startEating(dog, t0 + 700);
  ok('feeding outranks play (a meal that was saved must be shown)', currentPetActivity(dog)?.kind === 'eat');
  ok('play cannot interrupt a meal', !startPlay(dog, 'fetch', t0 + 800) && currentPetActivity(dog)?.kind === 'eat');
  ok('petting cannot interrupt a meal either', !startPetting(dog, t0 + 800));

  ok('two animals keep separate activities', startPetting(cat, t0) && currentPetActivity(cat)?.kind === 'petting'
    && currentPetActivity(dog)?.kind === 'eat');

  const meal = currentPetActivity(dog)!;
  finishPetActivity(dog, t0 + 5000);
  const doneAt = meal.kind === 'eat' ? meal.doneAt : null;
  finishPetActivity(dog, t0 + 5300);
  ok('finishing twice does not restart the fade', meal.kind === 'eat' && meal.doneAt === doneAt);
  ok('a finished meal lingers while its bowl fades', !petActivityExpired(meal, t0 + 5000 + PET_FEED.fadeSeconds * 500));
  ok('…and expires when the fade is done', petActivityExpired(meal, t0 + 5000 + PET_FEED.fadeSeconds * 1000 + 1));
  ok('a finished meal can be followed by play', startPlay(dog, 'fetch', t0 + 5100));

  const playing = currentPetActivity(dog)!;
  ok('play that never finishes expires on its own', petActivityExpired(playing, playing.startedAt + (PET_PLAY.maxSeconds + PET_PLAY.fadeSeconds) * 1000 + 1));
  const petting = currentPetActivity(cat)!;
  ok('petting nobody continues expires', petActivityExpired(petting, t0 + PET_PETTING.idleTimeout * 1000 + 1));
  startEating(cat, t0);
  const stuck = currentPetActivity(cat)!;
  ok('a meal whose bowl can never be reached still expires', petActivityExpired(stuck, t0 + (PET_FEED.approachTimeout + PET_FEED.eatSeconds + 2) * 1000 + 1));

  sweepPetActivities(t0 + 60000);
  ok('a sweep long afterwards leaves nothing behind', petActivityCount() === 0 && currentPetReaction(dog) === null);

  startPetting(dog, t0);
  playPetReaction(dog, 'happy', t0);
  endPetActivity(dog);
  ok('ending an animal clears its activity and its reaction at once', !currentPetActivity(dog) && !currentPetReaction(dog));

  startPetting(dog, t0);
  startPlay(cat, 'pounce', t0);
  resetPetActivities();
  ok('a reset clears every animal', petActivityCount() === 0);
}

console.log('');
if (failures > 0) {
  console.log(`FAIL — ${failures} of ${checks} checks failed.`);
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log(`PASS — ${checks} checks.`);

```
