## scripts/test-placement-precision.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 佈置／建造 —— 移動精度、選取鎖與堆疊 的規則測試。
 *
 * Run with `npm run test:placement`. Same tsx-script style as `test:pet-care` and the `audit:*`
 * checks, because that is the test runner this repo has.
 *
 * ## What it is guarding, and why each property is here
 *
 * Two player-visible faults produced this system, and both of them would still typecheck, still
 * run, and still be wrong:
 *
 *  §1/§2  **移動跨度過大.** A piece could only stand on a 0.5 grid, so a small pointer movement
 *         moved nothing at all and then moved half a metre. The property that replaces it is not
 *         "the constant is smaller" — it is that the mapping from pointer to world is CONTINUOUS
 *         and MONOTONIC at the scale a player nudges at, which is what the ray tests below state.
 *  §4/§5  **移動 A 卻選到 B.** Selection was re-derived from whatever the raycast hit on every
 *         pointer event, so a drag that passed over another model handed the gesture to it. The
 *         property is that the Active Object survives every pointer event that is not the player
 *         explicitly choosing something else — including the release that ends the drag, which is
 *         delivered as a click and is the one the old code could never have distinguished.
 *  §7/§8  **堆疊.** Contact must not read as collision, and a support must not read as an obstacle
 *         to the thing standing on it — indoors AND outdoors, through the same rule.
 *  §3     **Floating point.** Quantising is what makes a saved position survive a round trip; a
 *         quantiser that returns 0.30000000000000004 has done nothing useful.
 *
 * Everything here runs against the real modules the game ships. Footprints are registered through
 * the real `registerFootprint`, so a collider change shows up here rather than being re-implemented
 * in this file.
 */

import {
  ALIGN_STEP,
  DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX,
  PRECISION_STEP,
  TOUCH_DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX,
  canSelect,
  clearClickGuard,
  consumeCancelKeyGuard,
  dragThresholdFor,
  endSession,
  exceedsDragThreshold,
  getPlacementStep,
  guardCancelKey,
  guardNextClick,
  isClickGuarded,
  isManipulating,
  beginMove,
  endGesture,
  getPlacementSession,
  quantize,
  rayHitHorizontal,
  selectSubject,
  setAlignModifier,
  translateRayXZ,
  type PointerRayLike,
} from '../src/lib/placementSession';
import {
  boxFootprint,
  clampOntoSupport,
  getFootprint,
  makeObb,
  placementsCollide,
  registerFootprint,
} from '../src/lib/furniturePlacement';
import { resolveInteriorPlacement, type WallFace } from '../src/lib/interiorPlacement';
import type { ShellRoom } from '../src/constants/interiorShell';
import { PlacedItem } from '../src/types';

let failures = 0;
let checks = 0;

function eq(name: string, got: unknown, want: unknown): void {
  checks++;
  const ok = JSON.stringify(got) === JSON.stringify(want);
  if (!ok) {
    failures++;
    console.log(`FAIL  ${name}\n        got  ${JSON.stringify(got)}\n        want ${JSON.stringify(want)}`);
  } else {
    console.log(`PASS  ${name}`);
  }
}

function ok(name: string, condition: boolean, detail = ''): void {
  eq(detail ? `${name} — ${detail}` : name, condition, true);
}

// --- Fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Two pieces of furniture, registered exactly as the game registers a measured model.
 *
 * A wide low table that declares a top, and a small vase. Deliberately a plain box each: the point
 * of these tests is the placement rule, and the collider's own fidelity is `audit:colliders`'s job.
 */
const TABLE = 'item-22';        // 熱帶木桌 — declares `tabletop` in constants/items.ts
const VASE = 'deco-bonsai';     // 海島盆栽 — an ordinary ornament, so it takes DEFAULT_PLACEMENT

registerFootprint(TABLE, boxFootprint({
  cx: 0, cz: 0, halfW: 0.9, halfD: 0.5, minY: 0, maxY: 0.7, walk: null,
}));
registerFootprint(VASE, boxFootprint({
  cx: 0, cz: 0, halfW: 0.15, halfD: 0.15, minY: 0, maxY: 0.4, walk: null,
}));

/** A ray from above, aimed straight down at (x, z) — the simplest well-defined pointer. */
const downAt = (x: number, z: number, fromY = 6): PointerRayLike => ({
  origin: { x, y: fromY, z },
  direction: { x: 0, y: -1, z: 0 },
});

/** A ray from a slanted camera, which is what the game actually produces. */
function slantedAt(x: number, z: number): PointerRayLike {
  const len = Math.hypot(0.4, -1, 0.6);
  return {
    origin: { x: x - (0.4 / len) * 8, y: 8, z: z - (0.6 / len) * 8 },
    direction: { x: 0.4 / len, y: -1 / len, z: 0.6 / len },
  };
}

const NO_WALLS: WallFace[] = [];
/** One room at the origin. These cases are all about the floor and tabletops, but the resolver
 *  needs the house's shape to answer a ceiling mount, so it is stated rather than empty. */
const ONE_ROOM: ShellRoom[] = [{ cx: 0, cz: 0 }];

console.log('\n-- 一、量化是精確的，不是「大概」 (§3) --------------------------------');

{
  // The whole reason to quantise is that the SAME logical spot must be the same number every time
  // it is reached — otherwise nothing downstream can compare two positions, and a save/load round
  // trip slowly grows digits. `Math.round(v / step) * step` alone does not give you that.
  eq('a grid point is spelled exactly', quantize(0.06, 0.02), 0.06);
  eq('and so is a negative one', quantize(-0.06, 0.02), -0.06);
  eq('half a step rounds up, once', quantize(0.01, 0.02), 0.02);
  eq('zero stays zero, not -0', Object.is(quantize(-0.004, 0.02), 0), true);

  // Reached from below and from above, the same cell must produce one number — this is the
  // property that a naive multiply loses, and the one every `a === b` short-circuit depends on.
  for (let i = -50; i <= 50; i++) {
    const target = quantize(i * PRECISION_STEP, PRECISION_STEP);
    const fromBelow = quantize(i * PRECISION_STEP - PRECISION_STEP * 0.3, PRECISION_STEP);
    const fromAbove = quantize(i * PRECISION_STEP + PRECISION_STEP * 0.3, PRECISION_STEP);
    if (fromBelow !== target || fromAbove !== target) {
      ok('every cell has exactly one spelling', false, `cell ${i}`);
      break;
    }
    if (i === 50) ok('every cell has exactly one spelling', true, '101 cells, approached both ways');
  }

  // Re-quantising must be a no-op, or a position that goes through save → load → drag → save
  // drifts by half a step per round trip.
  let v = 1.234567;
  const once = quantize(v, PRECISION_STEP);
  for (let i = 0; i < 200; i++) v = quantize(quantize(v, PRECISION_STEP), PRECISION_STEP);
  eq('quantising is idempotent over 200 round trips', v, once);
}

console.log('\n-- 二、步進夠細，而且格線只是輔助 (§1, §2) ----------------------------');

{
  // The number the complaint was about. 0.5 was a quarter of a table's width; the replacement has
  // to be small enough that one step is invisible, and the align grid has to be smaller than what
  // it replaced or it is the same complaint with a modifier key in front of it.
  ok('the default step is fine enough to read as continuous', PRECISION_STEP <= 0.05,
    `PRECISION_STEP = ${PRECISION_STEP}`);
  ok('the align grid is coarser than the default', ALIGN_STEP > PRECISION_STEP);
  ok('but still finer than the 0.5 grid it replaced', ALIGN_STEP < 0.5,
    `ALIGN_STEP = ${ALIGN_STEP}`);

  endSession();
  eq('free movement is the default, not the exception', getPlacementStep(), PRECISION_STEP);
  setAlignModifier(true);
  eq('holding the modifier is what engages the grid', getPlacementStep(), ALIGN_STEP);
  eq('and the dock can see it', getPlacementSession().align, true);
  setAlignModifier(false);
  eq('releasing it goes straight back to free movement', getPlacementStep(), PRECISION_STEP);
}

console.log('\n-- 三、滑鼠小幅移動 → 物品小幅移動 (§1, §2, §15.1–15.3) ----------------');

{
  endSession();

  // THE REGRESSION TEST FOR THE ORIGINAL BUG. Walk the pointer across a room in 1 cm steps and
  // watch what the placement rule does with it. Under the old 0.5 grid this produced 49 samples
  // of no movement at all followed by one jump of 0.5; the requirement is that it produces small
  // movements throughout, and never a jump larger than one step.
  const positions: number[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i <= 120; i++) {
    const resolved = resolveInteriorPlacement({
      itemId: VASE,
      instanceId: 'drag',
      rotation: 0,
      ray: downAt(-1 + i * 0.01, 0),
      faces: NO_WALLS,
      rooms: ONE_ROOM,
      placements: [],
    });
    positions.push(resolved.placement.position[0]);
  }

  const jumps = positions.slice(1).map((v, i) => Math.abs(v - positions[i]));
  const biggest = Math.max(...jumps);
  ok('no single 1 cm pointer step moves the piece more than one grid step',
    biggest <= PRECISION_STEP + 1e-9, `largest jump ${biggest.toFixed(4)}`);

  // "It responds at all" is a separate claim from "it does not lurch", and the old code failed
  // this one: over any short window of pointer travel the piece has to actually move.
  const stalls = jumps.filter((j) => j === 0).length;
  ok('the piece is not frozen for long stretches', stalls <= jumps.length / 2,
    `${stalls} of ${jumps.length} samples were stationary`);

  // Monotonic: dragging right never moves the piece left.
  ok('dragging one way never moves the piece the other way',
    positions.every((v, i) => i === 0 || v >= positions[i - 1] - 1e-9));

  // End to end, the piece travels the distance the pointer did.
  ok('120 cm of pointer travel is 120 cm of piece travel',
    Math.abs((positions[positions.length - 1] - positions[0]) - 1.2) <= PRECISION_STEP);

  // And the same walk under the align modifier is the coarse grid — deliberately steppy, because
  // that is what the player asked for by holding it.
  setAlignModifier(true);
  const aligned = resolveInteriorPlacement({
    itemId: VASE, instanceId: 'drag', rotation: 0,
    ray: downAt(0.37, 0.61), faces: NO_WALLS, rooms: ONE_ROOM, placements: [],
  });
  eq('the align modifier snaps to its own grid',
    [aligned.placement.position[0], aligned.placement.position[2]],
    [quantize(0.37, ALIGN_STEP), quantize(0.61, ALIGN_STEP)]);
  setAlignModifier(false);
}

console.log('\n-- 四、抓取點：拿住哪裡就是哪裡 (§2) ----------------------------------');

{
  // The other half of "it jumps": with no grab offset the object's ORIGIN went to the cursor, so
  // taking hold of a table by its corner threw the table a metre before the mouse had moved.
  //
  // The offset is applied by translating the ray, and the claim that makes that correct is exactly
  // this: for any horizontal plane, moving the ray's origin in XZ moves the hit by the same
  // vector. It has to hold for a slanted camera ray, not just a straight-down one.
  for (const [name, ray] of [['straight down', downAt(2, -1)], ['slanted camera', slantedAt(2, -1)]] as const) {
    const before = rayHitHorizontal(ray, 0.35)!;
    const after = rayHitHorizontal(translateRayXZ(ray, 0.7, -0.4), 0.35)!;
    ok(`the grab offset moves the hit by exactly itself (${name})`,
      Math.abs(after.x - before.x - 0.7) < 1e-9 && Math.abs(after.z - before.z + 0.4) < 1e-9);
  }

  // Which means: grab a piece anywhere on itself, and the first sample of the drag leaves it
  // exactly where it already was. A drag that starts by moving the object is the bug.
  const origin: [number, number, number] = [3, 0, -2];
  const grabRay = slantedAt(3.6, -1.5);          // taken hold of 60cm along, 50cm across
  const hit = rayHitHorizontal(grabRay, origin[1])!;
  const grab: [number, number] = [origin[0] - hit.x, origin[2] - hit.z];
  const settled = rayHitHorizontal(translateRayXZ(grabRay, grab[0], grab[1]), origin[1])!;
  ok('grabbing a piece by its edge does not move it',
    Math.abs(settled.x - origin[0]) < 1e-9 && Math.abs(settled.z - origin[2]) < 1e-9);
}

console.log('\n-- 五、Active Object：移動 A 時不會變成 B (§4, §5, §6, §15.6–15.9) -----');

{
  endSession();
  ok('nothing held means anything can be selected', canSelect('B'));
  eq('and nothing is being manipulated', isManipulating(), false);

  selectSubject('A');
  eq('choosing A makes A the Active Object', getPlacementSession().activeId, 'A');
  ok('merely holding A still allows an explicit switch to B', canSelect('B'),
    'SELECTED is not a lock — §13');

  beginMove('A');
  eq('a drag is the locked phase', isManipulating(), true);
  ok('the cursor passing over B does not let B be selected', !canSelect('B'));
  ok('nor C, nor D', !canSelect('C') && !canSelect('D'));
  ok('A itself is still selectable, so the held piece is not the one thing you cannot click',
    canSelect('A'));
  eq('and the Active Object has not moved', getPlacementSession().activeId, 'A');

  endGesture();
  eq('releasing returns to SELECTED, still holding A', getPlacementSession().phase, 'selected');
  eq('A is still the subject', getPlacementSession().activeId, 'A');

  // THE EVENT-ORDERING CASE. The release that ends a drag is also delivered as a click, AFTER the
  // gesture has ended — so the phase lock alone can never catch it. This is the exact sequence
  // that used to hand the table to the player who was dragging a book across it.
  clearClickGuard();
  beginMove('A');
  guardNextClick();   // what usePlacementDrag does when a drag that MOVED is released
  endGesture();
  ok('the release that ended a drag is not a selection', !canSelect('B'));
  ok('and the ground click it also produces is refused', isClickGuarded());
  clearClickGuard();  // what the next pointerdown does
  ok('but the very next press restores ordinary selection', canSelect('B'));

  // A press and release that never moved is an ordinary click and must still select.
  beginMove('A');
  endGesture();       // no guardNextClick: the drag never moved
  ok('a tap that did not drag still selects', canSelect('B'));

  endSession();
  eq('ending the session releases the Active Object', getPlacementSession().activeId, null);
  eq('and clears any outstanding claim', isClickGuarded(), false);
}

console.log('\n-- 五之二、點擊 vs 拖曳：門檻在哪裡 (§8, §11) --------------------------');

{
  /*
    The click/drag boundary, as arithmetic.

    The property under test is not "there is a constant" — it is that the SAME press produces
    different verbs depending only on how far the hand travelled, and that a finger is given more
    room than a mouse. Both placement modes read this one function (usePlacementDrag), so a change
    here is a change to 室內 and 室外 together, which is the whole point of pulling it out of the
    hook and into the session module.
  */
  ok('a mouse press that does not move is a CLICK', !exceedsDragThreshold(0, 0, 'mouse'));
  ok('and so is the pixel or two a real mouse reports between down and up',
    !exceedsDragThreshold(2, 2, 'mouse'), `${Math.hypot(2, 2).toFixed(2)}px < ${DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX}`);
  ok('a deliberate pull is a DRAG', exceedsDragThreshold(0, 12, 'mouse'));
  eq('the boundary itself counts as a drag, so there is no dead value',
    exceedsDragThreshold(DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX, 0, 'mouse'), true);

  // Diagonal travel is measured as distance, not per-axis: 3px right and 3px down is 4.24px of
  // hand movement and must read the same as 4.24px in a straight line.
  ok('travel is measured as a distance, not per axis', exceedsDragThreshold(3, 3, 'mouse'));

  // A fingertip never lands still. At the mouse threshold every tap on a piece of furniture would
  // be a small drag — and on touch there is no hover, so a tap is the only way to LOOK at
  // something.
  ok('the same wobble from a finger is still a tap', !exceedsDragThreshold(6, 4, 'touch'),
    `${Math.hypot(6, 4).toFixed(2)}px < ${TOUCH_DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX}`);
  ok('but a real swipe on glass drags', exceedsDragThreshold(0, 24, 'touch'));
  ok('touch is given more room than a mouse',
    dragThresholdFor('touch') > dragThresholdFor('mouse'));
  eq('a pen is held to the mouse\'s precision', dragThresholdFor('pen'), dragThresholdFor('mouse'));
  eq('and an unknown device too, rather than falling through to nothing',
    dragThresholdFor(undefined), DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX);

  /*
    The gesture the threshold buys, end to end.

    An armed press that never crosses the threshold must leave the session exactly as an ordinary
    click would: no lock while the button is down, and no claim on the release. That is what makes
    「點一下＝選取」 survive a hand that is not perfectly still.
  */
  endSession();
  selectSubject('A');
  ok('an armed press does not lock the session before the threshold', canSelect('B'));
  eq('and nothing is being manipulated yet', isManipulating(), false);
  beginMove('A');       // what crossing the threshold does
  eq('crossing it is what enters the locked phase', isManipulating(), true);
  endGesture();
  endSession();
}

console.log('\n-- 五之三、ESC 的兩個意思 (§10, §11) -----------------------------------');

{
  /*
    Escape means two different things and both placement modes bind it on the window:

      mid-drag → 取消這次搬動 (usePlacementDrag puts the object back; the piece stays held)
      at rest  → 放下這個東西 (the mode drops the whole session)

    The drag takes the key in the capture phase and stops it, which settles a real keypress. This
    flag is what settles the case `stopPropagation` cannot: an event dispatched AT the window has a
    one-node path, so every listener on that node runs regardless. Without the flag the drag
    cancelled correctly and the mode then closed the editor anyway — one Escape doing both jobs,
    which is the one outcome neither meaning wants.
  */
  ok('an Escape nobody claimed reaches the mode handler', !consumeCancelKeyGuard());

  guardCancelKey();
  ok('an Escape the drag spent is refused to the mode handler', consumeCancelKeyGuard());
  ok('and it is spent exactly once, so the NEXT Escape still puts the piece down',
    !consumeCancelKeyGuard());
}

console.log('\n-- 六、堆疊：接觸不是碰撞 (§7, §8, §15.10–15.14) -----------------------');

{
  const table: PlacedItem = { instanceId: 't1', itemId: TABLE, position: [0, 0, 0], rotation: 0 };
  const tableTop = getFootprint(TABLE)!.maxY;

  // Resting ON the table: the two occupy the same ground but not the same height, and the vertical
  // band test is what has to say so. Getting this wrong is "花瓶碰到桌面就說不能放".
  const onTable: PlacedItem = { instanceId: 'v1', itemId: VASE, position: [0, tableTop, 0], rotation: 0 };
  ok('a vase resting on a table is not colliding with it', !placementsCollide(onTable, table));

  // Sunk INTO the table is a real overlap and must stay one, or the distinction is meaningless.
  const insideTable: PlacedItem = { instanceId: 'v2', itemId: VASE, position: [0, tableTop - 0.3, 0], rotation: 0 };
  ok('a vase sunk into the table still is', placementsCollide(insideTable, table));

  // Side by side on the floor, touching but not interpenetrating.
  const beside: PlacedItem = { instanceId: 'v3', itemId: VASE, position: [1.15, 0, 0], rotation: 0 };
  ok('a vase standing beside the table is not colliding', !placementsCollide(beside, table));

  // Indoors, the resolver has to actually PUT it on the table when the player points at the table,
  // and put it on the floor when they point past the edge. Nearest surface wins, no mode switch.
  const ontoTable = resolveInteriorPlacement({
    itemId: VASE, instanceId: 'v', rotation: 0,
    ray: downAt(0.2, 0.1), faces: NO_WALLS, rooms: ONE_ROOM, placements: [table],
  });
  eq('pointing at a table stands the piece on the table', ontoTable.mount, 'surface');
  eq('and names what it is standing on', ontoTable.supportId, 't1');
  eq('at the height of the top, not sunk into it', ontoTable.placement.position[1], tableTop);
  eq('and the spot is legal — the support is not an obstacle to what stands on it', ontoTable.ok, true);

  const pastTheEdge = resolveInteriorPlacement({
    itemId: VASE, instanceId: 'v', rotation: 0,
    ray: downAt(4, 0), faces: NO_WALLS, rooms: ONE_ROOM, placements: [table],
  });
  eq('pointing past it puts the piece on the floor behind', pastTheEdge.mount, 'floor');
  eq('with nothing under it', pastTheEdge.supportId, null);

  // The clamp: aimed at the very corner of the top, the piece slides back on rather than being
  // left hanging over the edge.
  const atTheEdge = resolveInteriorPlacement({
    itemId: VASE, instanceId: 'v', rotation: 0,
    ray: downAt(0.88, 0.48), faces: NO_WALLS, rooms: ONE_ROOM, placements: [table],
  });
  eq('a piece aimed at the corner of a table still lands on the table', atTheEdge.mount, 'surface');
  const [cx, , cz] = atTheEdge.placement.position;
  const vase = getFootprint(VASE)!;
  ok('and wholly on it, not hanging over the edge',
    Math.abs(cx) + vase.halfW <= 0.9 + 1e-9 && Math.abs(cz) + vase.halfD <= 0.5 + 1e-9,
    `landed at (${cx.toFixed(3)}, ${cz.toFixed(3)})`);
}

console.log('\n-- 七、堆疊的夾取規則是共用的 (§14) ------------------------------------');

{
  // The clamp indoors and the clamp outdoors are the same function — this is the shared half of
  // "室內外統一" for surface placement. Checked directly so that a change to one is a change to
  // both by construction rather than by review.
  const support = makeObb(getFootprint(TABLE)!, 0, 0, 0);
  const candidate = makeObb(getFootprint(VASE)!, 5, 5, 0);
  const slide = clampOntoSupport(candidate, support)!;
  ok('anything aimed off the support is pulled back onto it', !!slide);
  ok('and lands inside its top face',
    Math.abs(candidate.cx + slide.dx) <= 0.9 - 0.15 + 1e-9 &&
    Math.abs(candidate.cz + slide.dz) <= 0.5 - 0.15 + 1e-9);

  const alreadyInside = makeObb(getFootprint(VASE)!, 0.1, 0.1, 0);
  const noSlide = clampOntoSupport(alreadyInside, support)!;
  eq('a piece already wholly on the support is not moved', [noSlide.dx, noSlide.dz], [0, 0]);

  // A support smaller than the thing being put on it is a refusal, not a clamp — otherwise a deck
  // would be dragged to wherever a table happened to be.
  eq('a support too small to hold the piece refuses instead of dragging it',
    clampOntoSupport(support, makeObb(getFootprint(VASE)!, 0, 0, 0)), null);

  // Rotation is not a special case: the clamp works in the support's own frame.
  const turned = makeObb(getFootprint(TABLE)!, 0, 0, Math.PI / 4);
  const diagonal = clampOntoSupport(makeObb(getFootprint(VASE)!, 3, 3, 0.6), turned)!;
  ok('a rotated support clamps in its own frame', !!diagonal);
  const px = 3 + diagonal.dx;
  const pz = 3 + diagonal.dz;
  const u = (px - turned.cx) * turned.ux + (pz - turned.cz) * turned.uz;
  const v = (px - turned.cx) * turned.vx + (pz - turned.cz) * turned.vz;
  ok('and the result really is on the turned top face',
    Math.abs(u) <= turned.halfW + 1e-9 && Math.abs(v) <= turned.halfD + 1e-9);
}

console.log(
  failures === 0
    ? `\nALL PASS (${checks} checks)\n`
    : `\n${failures} of ${checks} checks FAILED\n`,
);
process.exit(failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);

```

## scripts/test-utility-cards.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 功能卡 / 輪盤機率 — rules tests.
 *
 * Run with `npm run test:utility-cards`. Same tsx-script style as `test:economy`,
 * `test:workout-rewards` and the `audit:*` checks, because that is the test runner this repo has.
 *
 * The properties pinned here are the ones the brief states as requirements and that are cheap to
 * break months later — most of them are properties of the DATA as much as of the code, so this is
 * also the check that catches somebody pricing the 雙倍金幣券 at 30 金幣 or giving the 輪盤's card
 * slot a fatter weight than its 碎片 slot:
 *
 *  §1/§4   a card is granted, accumulates, is capped, and is spent by being used
 *  §2/§3   the ×2 happens in ONE layer, applies to the right currency only, and never twice
 *  §15     Inventory → Use → Active Effect → Effect End, including expiry
 *  §5      the 輪盤 draws from a weighted table, cards are the rarest outcome, and a draw is a pure
 *          function of the spin id (so a re-render cannot re-roll it)
 *  §1/§5   a card declares its own channels honestly — every table that sells or drops it agrees
 *
 * The 限時商店 used to be tested here too. It is its own shop now, with its own pools, its own
 * rotation and its own bundle pricing, so it has its own suite: `npm run test:limited-shop`
 * (scripts/test-limited-shop.ts). What stayed behind is the one assertion that spans both — a
 * card's `channels` list against the shop pool that actually sells it.
 *
 * What it deliberately does NOT test: the write paths and the React layer. Those need a Firestore
 * and a DOM; what is testable without either is every rule that decides WHAT happens, which is the
 * half that silently rots.
 */

import {
  ALL_UTILITY_CARDS,
  UTILITY_CARDS,
  activeEffects,
  describeDuration,
  getOwnedCardCount,
  getUtilityCard,
  grantCards,
  isEffectLive,
  pruneUtilityState,
  useCard,
  type UtilityCardState,
} from '../src/constants/utilityCards';
import { MAX_REWARD_MULTIPLIER, settleReward } from '../src/constants/rewardEffects';
import { checkGrant, type Reward } from '../src/constants/rewards';
import {
  WHEEL_ENTRIES,
  WHEEL_SLOTS,
  drawWheelSlot,
  utilityCardChance,
  wheelOdds,
} from '../src/constants/wheelRewards';
import { pickWeighted, totalWeight, weightedChance } from '../src/constants/rewardPools';
import { SPECIAL_CARD_POOL } from '../src/constants/limitedShop';

let failures = 0;
let checks = 0;

function eq(name: string, got: unknown, want: unknown): void {
  checks++;
  const ok = JSON.stringify(got) === JSON.stringify(want);
  if (!ok) {
    failures++;
    console.log(`FAIL  ${name}\n        got  ${JSON.stringify(got)}\n        want ${JSON.stringify(want)}`);
  } else {
    console.log(`PASS  ${name}`);
  }
}

function ok(name: string, condition: boolean, detail = ''): void {
  eq(name + (detail ? ` (${detail})` : ''), condition, true);
}

const T0 = Date.parse('2026-08-29T10:00:00.000Z');
const coins = (amount: number): Reward => ({ kind: 'currency', currency: 'coins', amount });
const fragments = (amount: number): Reward => ({ kind: 'currency', currency: 'fragments', amount });

console.log('\n-- the card catalog (§1) ------------------------------------------------');

ok('there is at least one card', ALL_UTILITY_CARDS.length > 0);
ok(
  'every card keys itself by its own id',
  ALL_UTILITY_CARDS.every((card) => UTILITY_CARDS[card.id] === card),
);
ok(
  'every card has copy, a tier, an icon and a cap',
  ALL_UTILITY_CARDS.every(
    (card) => !!card.name && !!card.description && !!card.effectSummary && !!card.rarity && card.maxOwned > 0,
  ),
);
ok(
  'every card declares a duration that can end',
  ALL_UTILITY_CARDS.every((card) =>
    card.duration.kind === 'timed' ? card.duration.seconds > 0 : card.duration.count > 0,
  ),
);
ok(
  'every multiplier is greater than 1 — a card that changes nothing is not a card',
  ALL_UTILITY_CARDS.every((card) => card.effect.multiplier > 1),
);
eq('an unknown card id resolves to null', getUtilityCard('no-such-card'), null);
eq('雙倍金幣券 doubles 金幣', UTILITY_CARDS['double-coin'].effect, {
  kind: 'currency-multiplier',
  currency: 'coins',
  multiplier: 2,
});
ok('its duration reads as a sentence', describeDuration(UTILITY_CARDS['double-coin'].duration).length > 0);

console.log('\n-- inventory: grant, accumulate, cap (§4) -------------------------------');

let state: UtilityCardState = {};
eq('a fresh bag holds none', getOwnedCardCount(state, 'double-coin'), 0);

state = grantCards(state, 'double-coin', 1).state;
eq('one grant is one card', getOwnedCardCount(state, 'double-coin'), 1);

const two = grantCards(state, 'double-coin', 2);
eq('grants accumulate', getOwnedCardCount(two.state, 'double-coin'), 3);
eq('and report what landed', [two.granted, two.dropped], [2, 0]);

const capped = grantCards({ owned: { 'double-coin': 98 } }, 'double-coin', 5);
eq('the cap holds', getOwnedCardCount(capped.state, 'double-coin'), UTILITY_CARDS['double-coin'].maxOwned);
eq('and the overflow is reported rather than silently kept', [capped.granted, capped.dropped], [1, 4]);

eq(
  'a grant of an unknown card changes nothing',
  grantCards(state, 'nope' as never, 1).state,
  state,
);
eq('a grant of zero changes nothing', grantCards(state, 'double-coin', 0).granted, 0);

console.log('\n-- use → active effect → end (§15) --------------------------------------');

const bag: UtilityCardState = { owned: { 'double-coin': 2 } };
const used = useCard(bag, 'double-coin', { nowMs: T0, activationId: 'act-1' });
ok('using a card succeeds', used.ok);
if (used.ok) {
  eq('it spends exactly one copy', getOwnedCardCount(used.state, 'double-coin'), 1);
  eq('it records the use', used.state.usedTotal?.['double-coin'], 1);
  eq('one effect is running', activeEffects(used.state, T0).length, 1);
  eq('the effect names the card and nothing else about it', used.effect.cardId, 'double-coin');
  ok('a timed card gets an expiry', !!used.effect.expiresAt);
  ok('and no use counter', used.effect.usesLeft === undefined);

  const halfway = T0 + 15 * 60 * 1000;
  ok('it is still live halfway through', isEffectLive(used.effect, halfway));
  const after = T0 + 31 * 60 * 1000;
  ok('and dead once the window passes', !isEffectLive(used.effect, after));
  eq('an expired effect is not returned as active', activeEffects(used.state, after).length, 0);
  ok('and the sweep removes it', pruneUtilityState(used.state, after)?.active?.length === 0);
  eq('a clean state needs no sweep', pruneUtilityState(used.state, halfway), null);

  // §15's 「已使用 / 效果進行中」: a second copy exists, but the card refuses to stack with itself.
  const again = useCard(used.state, 'double-coin', { nowMs: T0 + 60_000, activationId: 'act-2' });
  eq('a card with stacking: reject refuses while its own effect runs', again, {
    ok: false,
    error: 'already-active',
  });
  eq(
    'and once it has ended, the second copy can be used',
    useCard(used.state, 'double-coin', { nowMs: after, activationId: 'act-3' }).ok,
    true,
  );
}

eq('using a card you do not hold is refused', useCard({}, 'double-coin', { nowMs: T0, activationId: 'a' }), {
  ok: false,
  error: 'none-owned',
});

console.log('\n-- the reward calculation layer (§2/§3) ---------------------------------');

const live: UtilityCardState = used.ok ? used.state : {};
const ctx = { cards: live, nowMs: T0 + 60_000 };
const settled = settleReward(coins(40), ctx);

eq('金幣 is doubled', settled.reward, coins(80));
eq('the BASE is preserved, not overwritten', settled.base, coins(40));
eq('the multiplier is reported', settled.multiplier, 2);
eq('and so is which card did it', settled.applied.map((note) => note.cardId), ['double-coin']);
eq('a timed card is not consumed by being applied', settled.cardsAfter, null);

eq('碎片 are untouched by a 金幣 card', settleReward(fragments(40), ctx).reward, fragments(40));
eq('經驗值 is untouched by a 金幣 card', settleReward({ kind: 'xp', amount: 40 }, ctx).reward, {
  kind: 'xp',
  amount: 40,
});
eq(
  'an item grant is never multiplied',
  settleReward({ kind: 'item', itemId: 'item-5', quantity: 1 }, ctx).reward,
  { kind: 'item', itemId: 'item-5', quantity: 1 },
);
eq(
  'a 功能卡 grant is never multiplied',
  settleReward({ kind: 'utility-card', cardId: 'double-coin', quantity: 1 }, ctx).reward,
  { kind: 'utility-card', cardId: 'double-coin', quantity: 1 },
);

eq('with nothing running, the reward is returned unchanged', settleReward(coins(40), { cards: {}, nowMs: T0 }).reward, coins(40));
eq(
  'an expired card pays nothing extra',
  settleReward(coins(40), { cards: live, nowMs: T0 + 31 * 60 * 1000 }).reward,
  coins(40),
);
eq(
  'the multiplier does not depend on the size of the reward',
  settleReward(coins(1), ctx).multiplier,
  settleReward(coins(999), ctx).multiplier,
);

// 「不會在多個地方重複 ×2」 — settling an ALREADY settled reward is what a second multiplication
// site would look like, and the guard is that there is only one call site. What can be pinned here
// is that one settlement never applies the same activation twice.
eq('one activation multiplies once', settleReward(coins(40), ctx).multiplier, 2);
eq(
  'and re-settling the OUTPUT is what a duplicated layer would look like',
  settleReward(settled.reward, ctx).reward,
  coins(160),
);

// A duplicated activation record in the save (a corrupt write) must not compound without limit.
const doubled: UtilityCardState = used.ok
  ? { ...used.state, active: [...(used.state.active ?? []), { ...used.state.active![0], activationId: 'dup' }] }
  : {};
ok(
  'stacked effects are capped',
  settleReward(coins(40), { cards: doubled, nowMs: T0 + 60_000 }).multiplier <= MAX_REWARD_MULTIPLIER,
);

// A `uses`-based card is the other duration shape, and the one whose consumption has to ride in the
// same write as the reward.
const usesCard: UtilityCardState = {
  active: [{ activationId: 'u-1', cardId: 'double-coin', activatedAt: new Date(T0).toISOString(), usesLeft: 2 }],
};
const spent = settleReward(coins(10), { cards: usesCard, nowMs: T0 });
eq('a uses-based effect still multiplies', spent.reward, coins(20));
eq('and reports the state to persist', spent.cardsAfter?.active?.[0]?.usesLeft, 1);
eq(
  'a reward it does not apply to never spends a use',
  settleReward(fragments(10), { cards: usesCard, nowMs: T0 }).cardsAfter,
  null,
);
const lastUse = settleReward(coins(10), { cards: spent.cardsAfter ?? {}, nowMs: T0 });
eq('the final use ends the effect', lastUse.cardsAfter?.active?.length, 0);

console.log('\n-- the policy still governs (constants/rewards.ts) ----------------------');

ok(
  '輪盤 may not pay 金幣, cards or not',
  !checkGrant({ reward: coins(10), source: 'wheel' }).ok,
);
ok(
  'a 功能卡 grant of a whole quantity is allowed',
  checkGrant({ reward: { kind: 'utility-card', cardId: 'double-coin', quantity: 1 }, source: 'wheel' }).ok,
);
ok(
  'a 功能卡 grant of zero is not',
  !checkGrant({ reward: { kind: 'utility-card', cardId: 'double-coin', quantity: 0 }, source: 'wheel' }).ok,
);

console.log('\n-- the wheel (§5) ------------------------------------------------------');

ok('the table has weight', totalWeight(WHEEL_ENTRIES) > 0);
ok('every slot has copy and a positive weight', WHEEL_SLOTS.every((slot) => !!slot.label && slot.weight > 0));
ok('a 功能卡 is reachable', WHEEL_SLOTS.some((slot) => slot.prize.kind === 'utility-card'));
ok(
  'every card slot names a card that exists',
  WHEEL_SLOTS.every((slot) => slot.prize.kind !== 'utility-card' || !!getUtilityCard(slot.prize.cardId)),
);
ok(
  'no wheel slot pays 金幣 — the policy would refuse it anyway',
  WHEEL_SLOTS.every((slot) => slot.prize.kind !== 'currency' || slot.prize.currency === 'fragments'),
);

const cardChance = utilityCardChance();
const otherChances = WHEEL_SLOTS
  .filter((slot) => slot.prize.kind !== 'utility-card')
  .map((slot) => weightedChance(WHEEL_ENTRIES, slot));
ok('a card is rarer than every ordinary prize', otherChances.every((chance) => chance > cardChance), `card ${(cardChance * 100).toFixed(1)}%`);
ok('and rare in absolute terms', cardChance > 0 && cardChance <= 0.05);

// §19's 「不會因 UI 重渲染重新抽獎」: the draw is a pure function of the spin id.
const spin = 'spin-abc';
eq('the same spin id always draws the same wedge', drawWheelSlot(spin)?.id, drawWheelSlot(spin)?.id);
ok(
  'different spins do not all land on the same wedge',
  new Set(Array.from({ length: 400 }, (_, i) => drawWheelSlot(`spin-${i}`)?.id)).size > 1,
);

// The distribution has to actually follow the weights, or 「權重」 is decoration.
const draws = new Map<string, number>();
const SAMPLES = 20000;
for (let i = 0; i < SAMPLES; i++) {
  const slot = drawWheelSlot(`sample-${i}`);
  if (slot) draws.set(slot.id, (draws.get(slot.id) ?? 0) + 1);
}
for (const { slot, chance } of wheelOdds()) {
  const observed = (draws.get(slot.id) ?? 0) / SAMPLES;
  ok(
    `${slot.id} lands near its weight`,
    Math.abs(observed - chance) < Math.max(0.01, chance * 0.25),
    `${(observed * 100).toFixed(2)}% vs ${(chance * 100).toFixed(2)}%`,
  );
}
ok('the card slot is actually drawn at all', (draws.get('card-double-coin') ?? 0) > 0);
eq('an empty table draws nothing', pickWeighted([], 1), null);
eq('a table of zero weights draws nothing', pickWeighted([{ value: 'a', weight: 0 }], 1), null);

console.log('\n-- where a card can come from (§1/§5) -----------------------------------');

// A card's declared channels have to match the tables that actually sell or drop it. The 限時商店
// half now means 「有一列組合包在賣它」 — see scripts/test-limited-shop.ts for everything about
// how that shelf behaves.
for (const card of ALL_UTILITY_CARDS) {
  const inShop = SPECIAL_CARD_POOL.some(
    (source) => source.content.kind === 'utility-card' && source.content.cardId === card.id,
  );
  const inWheel = WHEEL_SLOTS.some(
    (slot) => slot.prize.kind === 'utility-card' && slot.prize.cardId === card.id,
  );
  eq(`${card.id} declares its 限時商店 channel honestly`, card.channels.includes('limited-shop'), inShop);
  eq(`${card.id} declares its 輪盤 channel honestly`, card.channels.includes('wheel'), inWheel);
}

console.log(
  `\n${failures === 0 ? 'ALL PASS' : `${failures} FAILURE(S)`} — ${checks - failures}/${checks} checks\n`,
);
process.exit(failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);

```

## scripts/test-weekly-tasks.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 每週任務 — rules tests.
 *
 * Run with `npm run test:weekly-tasks`. Same tsx-script style as the other `test:*` checks, for the
 * same reason test-daily-login.ts gives: this repo has no vitest/jest and adding one is a bigger
 * decision than one feature should make.
 *
 * These cover the DECIDABLE half of the spec — the week's tiling and its boundaries in Asia/Taipei,
 * how progress is measured from real activity records, the remaining-days wording at each edge,
 * validation including every invalid input the brief names, and what a corrupt save is normalised
 * into. What they deliberately do NOT cover is the WRITE path (creating a task while another write
 * is in flight, a refused save): those are properties of context/useWeeklyTasks.ts and of Firestore,
 * not of these functions — see docs/weekly-tasks.md.
 */

import {
  COMPLETED_WEEKS_LIMIT,
  DAYS_PER_WEEK,
  MAX_WEEKLY_TASKS,
  METRIC_SPECS,
  TASK_NAME_MAX,
  applyWeeklyTaskEdit,
  availableMetrics,
  computeWeeklyTaskProgress,
  cycleFromWeekStart,
  getMetricSpec,
  hasErrors,
  makeWeeklyTask,
  markWeekCompleted,
  measureActivity,
  normalizeWeeklyTaskState,
  sortProgress,
  summariseWeek,
  unsupportedMetrics,
  validateWeeklyTaskDraft,
  weekStartFor,
  weeklyCycleAt,
  type HealthActivity,
  type WeeklyTaskDefinition,
} from '../src/constants/weeklyTasks';
import { civilDateAt } from '../src/constants/civilTime';
import { activityFromWorkoutLog, WORKOUT_LOG_METRICS } from '../src/lib/healthData';

let failures = 0;
let checks = 0;

function eq(name: string, got: unknown, want: unknown): void {
  checks++;
  const ok = JSON.stringify(got) === JSON.stringify(want);
  if (!ok) {
    failures++;
    console.log(`FAIL  ${name}\n        got  ${JSON.stringify(got)}\n        want ${JSON.stringify(want)}`);
  } else {
    console.log(`PASS  ${name}`);
  }
}

function ok(name: string, condition: boolean, detail = ''): void {
  checks++;
  if (!condition) {
    failures++;
    console.log(`FAIL  ${name}${detail ? `  ${detail}` : ''}`);
  } else {
    console.log(`PASS  ${name}${detail ? `  (${detail})` : ''}`);
  }
}

/** An instant, written as Taipei wall-clock time so the boundary cases read as what they test. */
function taipei(iso: string): Date {
  return new Date(`${iso}+08:00`);
}

/** A task, with everything the tests do not care about filled in. */
function task(overrides: Partial<WeeklyTaskDefinition> = {}): WeeklyTaskDefinition {
  return {
    taskId: 'wt-test',
    name: '每週運動',
    metric: 'workout_count',
    target: 3,
    createdAt: '2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z',
    startWeek: '2026-09-14',
    completedWeeks: [],
    ...overrides,
  };
}

/** One activity, at a Taipei wall-clock instant. */
function activity(at: string, overrides: Partial<HealthActivity> = {}): HealthActivity {
  return {
    activityId: `a-${at}`,
    completedAt: taipei(at).toISOString(),
    type: '開合跳',
    durationSeconds: 600,
    reps: 40,
    calories: 112,
    ...overrides,
  };
}

console.log('\n-- the week, and where it starts -------------------------------------');

// 2026-09-21 is a Monday. Every case below is anchored on that fact.
eq('a Monday is its own week start', weekStartFor('2026-09-21'), '2026-09-21');
eq('a Sunday belongs to the week that began six days earlier', weekStartFor('2026-09-27'), '2026-09-21');
eq('a Wednesday looks back to Monday', weekStartFor('2026-09-23'), '2026-09-21');
eq('the week is seven days long', DAYS_PER_WEEK, 7);
eq('a cycle runs Monday to Sunday', cycleFromWeekStart('2026-09-21').weekEnd, '2026-09-27');

// Month and year boundaries, because a week that cannot cross one is a week that breaks four times
// a year and once more on new year's eve.
eq('a week may start in one month and end in the next', cycleFromWeekStart('2026-09-28').weekEnd, '2026-10-04');
eq('a week may cross a year boundary', weekStartFor('2027-01-01'), '2026-12-28');
// 2028 is a leap year; 2028-02-29 is a Tuesday.
eq('a leap day resolves to its own Monday', weekStartFor('2028-02-29'), '2028-02-28');

console.log('\n-- timezone: the same instant is the same week for everybody ---------');

{
  // 23:30 Taipei on the final Sunday and 00:30 Taipei on the following Monday are 60 minutes apart
  // and must land in DIFFERENT weeks — the case that a `toISOString().slice(0, 10)` gets wrong for
  // every player east of UTC.
  const lateSunday = taipei('2026-09-27T23:30:00');
  const earlyMonday = taipei('2026-09-28T00:30:00');
  eq('23:30 Sunday is still the old week', weeklyCycleAt(lateSunday).weekStart, '2026-09-21');
  eq('00:30 Monday is the new week', weeklyCycleAt(earlyMonday).weekStart, '2026-09-28');
  ok(
    'the two are one hour apart in real time',
    earlyMonday.getTime() - lateSunday.getTime() === 60 * 60 * 1000,
  );
  // And the civil date agrees with the cycle, which is what stops the history list and the task
  // cards from disagreeing about which day a late-night workout happened on.
  eq('the civil date of 23:30 Sunday', civilDateAt(lateSunday), '2026-09-27');
}

{
  // The window is half-open: the first instant of Monday is IN, the first instant of the next
  // Monday is OUT. An inclusive end would count one workout in two consecutive weeks.
  const cycle = cycleFromWeekStart('2026-09-21');
  eq('the window opens at Monday midnight', cycle.startMs, taipei('2026-09-21T00:00:00').getTime());
  eq('the window closes at the NEXT Monday midnight', cycle.endMs, taipei('2026-09-28T00:00:00').getTime());
}

console.log('\n-- progress comes from the records, and only from them ---------------');

{
  const now = taipei('2026-09-23T12:00:00'); // Wednesday
  const activities = [
    activity('2026-09-21T09:00:00'),
    activity('2026-09-22T09:00:00'),
    // Last week's — must not count.
    activity('2026-09-20T09:00:00'),
    // Next week's — must not count either. A future-dated record is not impossible: an API can
    // report a completion with its own clock.
    activity('2026-09-28T09:00:00'),
  ];
  const progress = computeWeeklyTaskProgress(task(), activities, now);
  eq('only this week counts', progress.current, 2);
  eq('the target is the one the task names', progress.target, 3);
  eq('the percentage is rounded', progress.percent, 67);
  eq('not yet complete', progress.completed, false);
  eq('status is active', progress.status, 'active');
}

{
  const now = taipei('2026-09-23T12:00:00');
  // A record with an unparseable timestamp must be skipped, not turned into NaN. A NaN progress bar
  // does not throw — it silently renders empty, which is the worst kind of wrong.
  const broken: HealthActivity = { ...activity('2026-09-22T09:00:00'), completedAt: 'not a date' };
  const progress = computeWeeklyTaskProgress(task(), [activity('2026-09-22T09:00:00'), broken], now);
  eq('a broken timestamp is skipped', progress.current, 1);
  ok('and the ratio is still a number', Number.isFinite(progress.ratio));
}

{
  const now = taipei('2026-09-23T12:00:00');
  const activities = [
    activity('2026-09-21T09:00:00', { durationSeconds: 600, reps: 40, calories: 100, type: '深蹲' }),
    activity('2026-09-22T09:00:00', { durationSeconds: 900, reps: 60, calories: 150, type: '開合跳' }),
  ];
  eq('workout_minutes sums the durations', computeWeeklyTaskProgress(task({ metric: 'workout_minutes', target: 60 }), activities, now).current, 25);
  eq('workout_reps sums the reps', computeWeeklyTaskProgress(task({ metric: 'workout_reps', target: 200 }), activities, now).current, 100);
  eq('calories sums the calories', computeWeeklyTaskProgress(task({ metric: 'calories', target: 500 }), activities, now).current, 250);
  eq(
    'activity_type_count counts only the named type',
    computeWeeklyTaskProgress(task({ metric: 'activity_type_count', activityType: '深蹲', target: 3 }), activities, now).current,
    1,
  );
  eq(
    'a type nobody did counts zero',
    computeWeeklyTaskProgress(task({ metric: 'activity_type_count', activityType: '游泳', target: 3 }), activities, now).current,
    0,
  );
}

{
  // 「完成度不應超過 100% 的視覺上限」 AND 「原始進度資料仍應正確保存」 — both, at once.
  const now = taipei('2026-09-23T12:00:00');
  const activities = Array.from({ length: 7 }, (_, i) => activity(`2026-09-2${1 + (i % 3)}T0${i}:00:00`, { activityId: `a${i}` }));
  const progress = computeWeeklyTaskProgress(task({ target: 5 }), activities, now);
  eq('the raw count is not clamped', progress.current, 7);
  eq('the raw percentage is not clamped', progress.rawPercent, 140);
  eq('the bar ratio IS clamped', progress.ratio, 1);
  eq('the displayed percentage is clamped', progress.percent, 100);
  eq('and it is complete', progress.completed, true);
  eq('status reflects it', progress.status, 'completed');
}

{
  // 步數 has no data source, so a steps task measures zero — not a plausible-looking invented number.
  const stepsTask = task({ metric: 'steps', target: 30000 });
  eq('a steps activity contributes nothing', measureActivity(activity('2026-09-22T09:00:00'), stepsTask), 0);
}

console.log('\n-- remaining days are computed, never hardcoded ----------------------');

{
  const cycle = cycleFromWeekStart('2026-09-21');
  const on = (day: string) => computeWeeklyTaskProgress(task({ target: 99 }), [], taipei(`${day}T12:00:00`), cycle);

  eq('Monday: the whole week is left', on('2026-09-21').daysRemaining, 7);
  eq('Monday says so', on('2026-09-21').remaining, { kind: 'days', days: 7 });
  eq('Friday', on('2026-09-25').daysRemaining, 3);
  eq('Saturday has today and tomorrow', on('2026-09-26').daysRemaining, 2);
  // The one the brief singles out: 「當天到期：顯示適當的當日提示」.
  eq('Sunday is the last day, not "1 day left"', on('2026-09-27').remaining, { kind: 'due_today' });
  eq('and Sunday still counts as one day remaining', on('2026-09-27').daysRemaining, 1);
  // 「已過期：顯示已過期」 — only reachable for a PAST cycle, which is what a history view asks for.
  eq('the Monday after is expired', on('2026-09-28').remaining, { kind: 'expired', daysAgo: 1 });
  eq('expired has no days remaining', on('2026-09-28').daysRemaining, 0);
  eq('an expired, unmet task says so', on('2026-09-28').status, 'expired');
  eq('three days later', on('2026-09-30').remaining, { kind: 'expired', daysAgo: 3 });
}

{
  // A task created THIS week is not retroactively expired for the weeks before it existed.
  const later = task({ startWeek: '2026-09-28' });
  const thisWeek = computeWeeklyTaskProgress(later, [], taipei('2026-09-23T12:00:00'));
  eq('a task starting next week is upcoming', thisWeek.status, 'upcoming');
}

console.log('\n-- crossing a week boundary -----------------------------------------');

{
  const activities = [activity('2026-09-22T09:00:00'), activity('2026-09-23T09:00:00'), activity('2026-09-24T09:00:00')];
  const done = computeWeeklyTaskProgress(task({ target: 3 }), activities, taipei('2026-09-25T12:00:00'));
  eq('the week it was earned in: complete', done.completed, true);

  // The SAME records, one week later. The new cycle starts empty — no write, no reset, no scheduled
  // job: the window simply moved.
  const nextWeek = computeWeeklyTaskProgress(task({ target: 3 }), activities, taipei('2026-09-30T12:00:00'));
  eq('the next week starts at zero', nextWeek.current, 0);
  eq('and is active again', nextWeek.status, 'active');
  eq('with a new period', nextWeek.cycle.weekStart, '2026-09-28');
}

{
  // The completion RECORD survives the crossing, which is what makes last week's achievement
  // still true after the progress that earned it has rolled off the window.
  const marked = markWeekCompleted(task(), '2026-09-21');
  eq('a week is recorded', marked.completedWeeks, ['2026-09-21']);
  eq('recording twice is a no-op', markWeekCompleted(marked, '2026-09-21').completedWeeks, ['2026-09-21']);
  ok('and returns the same object', markWeekCompleted(marked, '2026-09-21') === marked);

  const last = computeWeeklyTaskProgress(marked, [], taipei('2026-09-23T12:00:00'), cycleFromWeekStart('2026-09-21'));
  eq('a recorded week reads as celebrated', last.celebrated, true);
  const other = computeWeeklyTaskProgress(marked, [], taipei('2026-09-30T12:00:00'));
  eq('a different week does not', other.celebrated, false);

  // The list is capped, and it is the OLDEST that goes.
  let many = task();
  for (let i = 0; i < COMPLETED_WEEKS_LIMIT + 4; i += 1) {
    const week = `2026-01-${String(1 + i).padStart(2, '0')}`;
    many = markWeekCompleted(many, week);
  }
  eq('the record is capped', many.completedWeeks?.length, COMPLETED_WEEKS_LIMIT);
  eq('and it keeps the newest', many.completedWeeks?.[COMPLETED_WEEKS_LIMIT - 1], `2026-01-${COMPLETED_WEEKS_LIMIT + 4}`);
}

console.log('\n-- validation: the invalid inputs the brief names --------------------');

{
  const existing = [task({ taskId: 'a', name: '每週運動' })];
  const valid = { name: '每週深蹲', metric: 'workout_count', target: '3' };

  eq('a valid draft passes', validateWeeklyTaskDraft(valid, existing), {});
  ok('an empty name is refused', !!validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, name: '' }, existing).name);
  ok('whitespace alone is refused', !!validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, name: '   ' }, existing).name);
  ok('an over-long name is refused', !!validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, name: 'x'.repeat(TASK_NAME_MAX + 1) }, existing).name);
  ok('a duplicate name is refused', !!validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, name: '每週運動' }, existing).name);
  ok('a duplicate ignoring surrounding space is still a duplicate', !!validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, name: '  每週運動  ' }, existing).name);
  // 「重複操作」 — editing a task must not collide with its own name.
  eq('editing a task keeps its own name', validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, name: '每週運動' }, existing, 'a'), {});

  ok('an empty target is refused', !!validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, target: '' }, existing).target);
  ok('a non-numeric target is refused', !!validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, target: '三次' }, existing).target);
  ok('zero is refused', !!validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, target: '0' }, existing).target);
  ok('a negative target is refused', !!validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, target: '-5' }, existing).target);
  ok('a fractional target is refused', !!validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, target: '2.5' }, existing).target);
  ok('an absurd target is refused', !!validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, target: '99999' }, existing).target);
  ok('NaN is refused', !!validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, target: 'NaN' }, existing).target);
  ok('Infinity is refused', !!validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, target: 'Infinity' }, existing).target);

  ok('an unknown metric is refused', !!validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, metric: 'vibes' }, existing).metric);
  // 「不要使用虛假的固定數值冒充實際運動紀錄」 — a metric with no data source cannot be created at all.
  ok('an unsupported metric is refused', !!validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, metric: 'steps', target: '30000' }, existing).metric);
  ok(
    'activity_type_count needs a type',
    !!validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, metric: 'activity_type_count' }, existing).activityType,
  );
  eq(
    'and passes once given one',
    validateWeeklyTaskDraft({ ...valid, metric: 'activity_type_count', activityType: '深蹲' }, existing),
    {},
  );

  const full = Array.from({ length: MAX_WEEKLY_TASKS }, (_, i) => task({ taskId: `t${i}`, name: `任務 ${i}` }));
  ok('a full list refuses a new task', !!validateWeeklyTaskDraft(valid, full).form);
  eq('but still allows editing an existing one', validateWeeklyTaskDraft(valid, full, 't0'), {});
  ok('hasErrors agrees', hasErrors(validateWeeklyTaskDraft(valid, full)) && !hasErrors(validateWeeklyTaskDraft(valid, existing)));
}

{
  // Building and editing both trim, round, and keep the things that must not move.
  const built = makeWeeklyTask({ name: '  每週深蹲  ', metric: 'workout_count', target: '4' }, taipei('2026-09-23T12:00:00'));
  eq('the name is trimmed', built.name, '每週深蹲');
  eq('the target is an integer', built.target, 4);
  eq('the start week is this week', built.startWeek, '2026-09-21');
  eq('it starts with no completed weeks', built.completedWeeks, []);
  ok('and gets an id', built.taskId.startsWith('wt-'));

  const edited = applyWeeklyTaskEdit(markWeekCompleted(built, '2026-09-21'), {
    name: '每週深蹲加量',
    metric: 'workout_reps',
    target: '300',
  }, taipei('2026-09-24T12:00:00'));
  eq('editing keeps the id', edited.taskId, built.taskId);
  eq('editing keeps the start week', edited.startWeek, built.startWeek);
  eq('editing keeps the completion record', edited.completedWeeks, ['2026-09-21']);
  eq('editing changes the metric', edited.metric, 'workout_reps');
  ok('and stamps an update time', !!edited.updatedAt);

  // Switching AWAY from activity_type_count must drop the type, or a later switch back would
  // silently resurrect a stale one.
  const typed = makeWeeklyTask({ name: '深蹲週', metric: 'activity_type_count', target: '3', activityType: '深蹲' });
  eq('a typed task keeps its type', typed.activityType, '深蹲');
  const untyped = applyWeeklyTaskEdit(typed, { name: '深蹲週', metric: 'workout_count', target: '3' });
  eq('switching metric drops the type', untyped.activityType, undefined);
}

console.log('\n-- a corrupt save is normalised, not rendered ------------------------');

{
  eq('undefined becomes an empty list', normalizeWeeklyTaskState(undefined), { tasks: [] });
  eq('null becomes an empty list', normalizeWeeklyTaskState(null), { tasks: [] });
  eq('a non-list becomes an empty list', normalizeWeeklyTaskState({ tasks: 'nope' }), { tasks: [] });

  const dirty = normalizeWeeklyTaskState({
    tasks: [
      task({ taskId: 'good' }),
      // Every one of these is a shape the UI would render as NaN or a blank card.
      { taskId: 'no-name', metric: 'workout_count', target: 3 },
      { taskId: 'string-target', name: 'x', metric: 'workout_count', target: '3' },
      { taskId: 'zero-target', name: 'x', metric: 'workout_count', target: 0 },
      { taskId: 'nan-target', name: 'x', metric: 'workout_count', target: Number.NaN },
      { taskId: 'bad-metric', name: 'x', metric: 'vibes', target: 3 },
      { name: 'no id', metric: 'workout_count', target: 3 },
      null,
      'a string',
      // A duplicate id would give two cards one React key and make editing one edit both.
      task({ taskId: 'good', name: 'duplicate id' }),
    ],
  });
  eq('only the sound one survives', dirty.tasks?.map((entry) => entry.taskId), ['good']);

  const overLong = normalizeWeeklyTaskState({
    tasks: Array.from({ length: MAX_WEEKLY_TASKS + 5 }, (_, i) => task({ taskId: `t${i}`, name: `任務 ${i}` })),
  });
  eq('the list is capped at the maximum', overLong.tasks?.length, MAX_WEEKLY_TASKS);
}

console.log('\n-- the week summary and the list order -------------------------------');

{
  const now = taipei('2026-09-24T12:00:00');
  const activities = [
    activity('2026-09-21T09:00:00', { durationSeconds: 600, reps: 40, calories: 100 }),
    activity('2026-09-23T09:00:00', { durationSeconds: 300, reps: 20, calories: 50 }),
    activity('2026-09-19T09:00:00', { durationSeconds: 999, reps: 999, calories: 999 }), // last week
  ];
  const entries = [
    computeWeeklyTaskProgress(task({ taskId: 'a', target: 2 }), activities, now),
    computeWeeklyTaskProgress(task({ taskId: 'b', target: 9 }), activities, now),
  ];
  const summary = summariseWeek(activities, entries, now);
  eq('only this week is summed', summary.workouts, 2);
  eq('minutes', summary.minutes, 15);
  eq('reps', summary.reps, 60);
  eq('calories', summary.calories, 150);
  eq('completed tasks', summary.tasksCompleted, 1);
  eq('active tasks', summary.tasksActive, 2);

  // An upcoming task is not counted against this week's tally — it has not started.
  const withUpcoming = summariseWeek(
    activities,
    [...entries, computeWeeklyTaskProgress(task({ taskId: 'c', startWeek: '2026-10-05' }), activities, now)],
    now,
  );
  eq('an upcoming task is not part of the tally', withUpcoming.tasksActive, 2);
}

{
  const now = taipei('2026-09-24T12:00:00');
  const done = computeWeeklyTaskProgress(task({ taskId: 'done', target: 0 }), [activity('2026-09-22T09:00:00')], now);
  const active = computeWeeklyTaskProgress(task({ taskId: 'active', target: 9, createdAt: '2026-09-02T00:00:00.000Z' }), [], now);
  const later = computeWeeklyTaskProgress(task({ taskId: 'later', startWeek: '2026-10-05' }), [], now);
  eq('unfinished tasks come first', sortProgress([done, later, active]).map((e) => e.task.taskId), ['active', 'later', 'done']);
}

console.log('\n-- the health data adapter ------------------------------------------');

{
  // The one place that knows `counts` means reps. A log missing half its fields must still produce
  // a usable activity rather than a set of undefineds.
  const full = activityFromWorkoutLog({
    logId: 'log-1',
    userId: 'u',
    type: '深蹲',
    duration: 300,
    counts: 25,
    calories: 44,
    goldEarned: 10,
    timestamp: '2026-09-22T09:00:00.000Z',
  });
  eq('a full log translates', full, {
    activityId: 'log-1',
    completedAt: '2026-09-22T09:00:00.000Z',
    type: '深蹲',
    durationSeconds: 300,
    reps: 25,
    calories: 44,
  });

  const sparse = activityFromWorkoutLog({ timestamp: '2026-09-22T09:00:00.000Z' });
  eq('missing numbers become zero, not NaN', [sparse?.durationSeconds, sparse?.reps, sparse?.calories], [0, 0, 0]);
  ok('and it still has a type', !!sparse?.type);

  eq('a log with no timestamp is dropped', activityFromWorkoutLog({ logId: 'x' }), null);
  eq('a log with a junk timestamp is dropped', activityFromWorkoutLog({ timestamp: 'yesterday' }), null);
  eq('a negative duration is floored at zero', activityFromWorkoutLog({ timestamp: '2026-09-22T09:00:00.000Z', duration: -5 })?.durationSeconds, 0);
}

{
  // The adapter's declared support and the metric table must agree, or the form offers a goal
  // nothing can feed.
  const declared = [...WORKOUT_LOG_METRICS].sort();
  const marked = availableMetrics().map((spec) => spec.id).sort();
  eq('the adapter feeds exactly the metrics marked available', declared, marked);
  eq('步數 is the one that is not', unsupportedMetrics().map((spec) => spec.id), ['steps']);
  ok('and it says why', unsupportedMetrics().every((spec) => !!spec.unavailableReason));
  ok('every metric has a spec', METRIC_SPECS.every((spec) => getMetricSpec(spec.id) === spec));
  ok('an unknown metric has none', getMetricSpec('vibes') === null);
  ok(
    'every available metric has a default inside its own bounds',
    availableMetrics().every((spec) => spec.defaultTarget >= spec.minTarget && spec.defaultTarget <= spec.maxTarget),
  );
}

console.log(
  failures === 0
    ? `\nALL PASS (${checks} checks)\n`
    : `\n${failures} of ${checks} checks FAILED\n`
);
process.exit(failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);

```

## scripts/test-workout-rewards.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 健身獎勵 — rules tests.
 *
 * Run with `npm run test:workout-rewards`. Same tsx-script style as `test:daily-login`,
 * `test:offline-return` and the `audit:*` checks, because that is the test runner this repo has.
 *
 * The properties pinned here are the ones the brief states as requirements and that are cheap to
 * get wrong months later — most of them are properties of the CATALOG as much as of the code, so
 * this is also the check that catches somebody pricing a 神話 item at 200 gold:
 *
 *  §3/§4  nothing expensive, graded, premium, limited or earned can ever be in the newbie pool
 *  §4     the pool is derived from the catalog, never enumerated — it must be non-empty and every
 *         member must be a wearable from a declared category
 *  §5     Filter → Random, never Random → Check: a draw can only ever return a pool member
 *  §6/§13 one account claims 首次健身獎勵 exactly once, and a replayed completion changes nothing
 *  §11    an invalid completion is not a completion
 *  §19    the rules table drives everything; nothing branches on a specific trigger id
 *
 * What it deliberately does NOT test: the write path and the React layer. Those need a Firestore
 * and a DOM; what is testable without either is every rule that decides WHAT is granted, which is
 * the half that silently rots as the catalog grows.
 */

import { ALL_ITEMS, getItemById } from '../src/constants/items';
import {
  getLastWorkoutCompletion,
  makeWorkoutCompletion,
  reportWorkoutCompletion,
  resetWorkoutCompletionBus,
  subscribeWorkoutCompletion,
} from '../src/lib/workoutCompletion';
import { getDisplayCategory } from '../src/utils/categoryUtils';
import { rarityRank } from '../src/constants/rarity';
import {
  NEWBIE_PRICE_CEILING,
  NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL,
  PROCESSED_ID_LIMIT,
  WORKOUT_REWARD_RULES,
  WORKOUT_VALIDITY,
  appendProcessedId,
  buildRewardPool,
  drawReward,
  hasClaimed,
  hasProcessed,
  isEligibleForPool,
  isValidWorkout,
  pickRewardFrom,
  resolvePendingRewards,
  seedFrom,
  type WorkoutCompletion,
  type WorkoutRewardState,
} from '../src/constants/workoutRewards';

let failures = 0;
let checks = 0;

function eq(name: string, got: unknown, want: unknown): void {
  checks++;
  const ok = JSON.stringify(got) === JSON.stringify(want);
  if (!ok) {
    failures++;
    console.log(`FAIL  ${name}\n        got  ${JSON.stringify(got)}\n        want ${JSON.stringify(want)}`);
  } else {
    console.log(`PASS  ${name}`);
  }
}

function ok(name: string, condition: boolean, detail = ''): void {
  eq(name + (detail ? ` (${detail})` : ''), condition, true);
}

const completion = (over: Partial<WorkoutCompletion> = {}): WorkoutCompletion => ({
  workoutId: 'wk-1',
  userId: 'u-1',
  completedAt: '2026-08-24T10:00:00.000Z',
  workoutType: '開合跳',
  durationSeconds: 90,
  repCount: 12,
  source: 'prototype',
  ...over,
});

console.log('\n-- what counts as a workout (§11) -------------------------------------');

ok('a normal workout is valid', isValidWorkout(completion()));
ok('nothing is not a workout', !isValidWorkout(null));
ok('an id-less completion is refused', !isValidWorkout(completion({ workoutId: '' })));
ok('a user-less completion is refused', !isValidWorkout(completion({ userId: '' })));
ok('an unparseable timestamp is refused', !isValidWorkout(completion({ completedAt: 'soon' })));
ok(
  'opening and closing the screen is not a workout',
  !isValidWorkout(completion({ durationSeconds: 2, repCount: 0 })),
);
ok(
  'long enough counts even with no reps reported (a run)',
  isValidWorkout(completion({ durationSeconds: WORKOUT_VALIDITY.minDurationSeconds, repCount: undefined })),
);
ok(
  'enough reps counts even when it was quick (a set)',
  isValidWorkout(completion({ durationSeconds: 1, repCount: WORKOUT_VALIDITY.minReps })),
);
ok(
  'a NaN duration cannot pass as effort',
  !isValidWorkout(completion({ durationSeconds: Number.NaN, repCount: 0 })),
);

console.log('\n-- the pool is derived, and it is not empty (§4) -----------------------');

const pool = buildRewardPool(NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL);
ok('the newbie pool has items in it', pool.length > 0, `${pool.length} 件`);
ok(
  'the pool is a strict subset of the catalog',
  pool.every((item) => ALL_ITEMS.includes(item)),
);
ok(
  'every pool member is in a declared category',
  pool.every((item) => !!getDisplayCategory(item.shopCategory)),
);
ok(
  'every pool member is worn, not placed or applied',
  pool.every((item) => getDisplayCategory(item.shopCategory)?.kind === 'wearable'),
  'kind === wearable',
);
ok(
  'every pool member belongs to 人物外觀',
  pool.every((item) => getDisplayCategory(item.shopCategory)?.mainSection === 'PERSON'),
);

console.log('\n-- nothing valuable can get in (§3) ------------------------------------');

ok(
  'nothing above the ceiling',
  pool.every((item) => item.price <= NEWBIE_PRICE_CEILING),
  `<= ${NEWBIE_PRICE_CEILING}`,
);
ok('nothing free', pool.every((item) => item.price >= NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL.minPrice));
// Was 「no rarity tier at all」 (`item.rarity === undefined`) until 2026-08-25, when rarity became
// REQUIRED on every catalog item. That assertion was testing the OLD way of spelling 「這是一件普通
// 商品」 — an absent field — and there is no such state any more, so it is restated in the tier's
// own name rather than deleted. The INTENT is identical and is the thing worth keeping: the newbie
// pool hands out ordinary goods and nothing else. See constants/rarity.ts.
ok('nothing above 普通', pool.every((item) => item.rarity === 'common'), 'rarity === common');
ok('nothing earned by 經驗值', pool.every((item) => (item.xpUnlock ?? 0) === 0));
ok('nothing retired', pool.every((item) => !!getItemById(item.id)));
ok(
  'no 特殊飾品 / 寵物 / 寵物飾品',
  pool.every((item) => !['SpecialFx', 'Dogs', 'Cats', 'Birds', 'PetGear', 'Pets'].includes(item.shopCategory)),
);
ok(
  'no furniture, art, house styles, floors or walls',
  pool.every((item) => {
    const section = getDisplayCategory(item.shopCategory)?.mainSection;
    return section !== 'INDOOR' && section !== 'OUTDOOR';
  }),
);

// The other direction: every item the rules SHOULD admit is in fact admitted, so the filter cannot
// quietly narrow to nothing while still passing every exclusion test above.
const expected = ALL_ITEMS.filter(
  (item) =>
    NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL.categories.includes(item.shopCategory) &&
    item.price >= NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL.minPrice &&
    item.price <= NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL.maxPrice &&
    (item.xpUnlock ?? 0) === 0 &&
    // `maxRarity` is nullable and `null` now means 「不設上限」 rather than 「只收未標記的」, so the
    // comparison has to be guarded the same way isEligibleForPool guards it. Reading it as a plain
    // `<=` against `rarityRank(null)` (-1) would make an unbounded pool admit nothing.
    (NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL.maxRarity == null ||
      rarityRank(item.rarity) <= rarityRank(NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL.maxRarity)),
);
eq('the pool is exactly what the rules describe', pool.map((i) => i.id), expected.map((i) => i.id));

// A synthetic item per exclusion, so the gate is tested rather than merely observed to hold on
// today's catalog — the catalog could stop containing a counter-example at any time.
const base = pool[0];
ok(
  'an expensive item in an allowed category is refused',
  !isEligibleForPool({ ...base, id: 'x-expensive', price: NEWBIE_PRICE_CEILING + 1 }, NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL),
);
// Same restatement, in the other direction: 普通 is what the pool ADMITS now, so the synthetic
// item that must be refused is the rung above it. This is the check that catches the pool's
// ceiling being widened by accident.
ok(
  'an item one rung above the ceiling is refused',
  !isEligibleForPool({ ...base, id: 'x-rare', rarity: 'rare' }, NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL),
);
ok(
  'an ordinary item at a newbie price is admitted',
  isEligibleForPool({ ...base, id: 'x-common', price: 100, rarity: 'common' }, NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL),
);
ok(
  'a 神話 item at a newbie price is still refused',
  !isEligibleForPool({ ...base, id: 'x-mythic', price: 100, rarity: 'mythic' }, NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL),
);
ok(
  'an XP-unlock item is refused',
  !isEligibleForPool({ ...base, id: 'x-xp', price: 100, xpUnlock: 100 }, NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL),
);
ok(
  'a cheap sofa is refused',
  !isEligibleForPool({ ...base, id: 'x-sofa', price: 100, shopCategory: 'Living' }, NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL),
);
ok(
  'an item in a category that no longer exists is refused',
  !isEligibleForPool({ ...base, id: 'x-ghost', shopCategory: 'NoSuchCategory' }, NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL),
);

console.log('\n-- filter, then draw (§5) ----------------------------------------------');

ok('an empty list draws nothing', pickRewardFrom([], 12345) === null);
ok(
  'every seed lands inside the pool',
  Array.from({ length: 500 }, (_, i) => pickRewardFrom(pool, i)).every((item) => !!item && pool.includes(item)),
);
ok(
  'the same seed always draws the same item',
  pickRewardFrom(pool, 9_999)?.id === pickRewardFrom(pool, 9_999)?.id,
);
ok(
  'the same completion id always draws the same item (a retry cannot re-roll)',
  drawReward(NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL, [], seedFrom('wk-abc')).ok &&
    JSON.stringify(drawReward(NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL, [], seedFrom('wk-abc'))) ===
      JSON.stringify(drawReward(NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL, [], seedFrom('wk-abc'))),
);
ok(
  'different completions do not all draw the same item',
  new Set(
    Array.from({ length: 60 }, (_, i) => {
      const draw = drawReward(NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL, [], seedFrom(`wk-${i}`));
      return draw.ok ? draw.item.id : 'none';
    }),
  ).size > 1,
);

const ownedAllButOne = pool.slice(0, -1).map((item) => item.id);
const lastLeft = drawReward(NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL, ownedAllButOne, seedFrom('wk-owned'));
ok(
  'an owned item is skipped while anything else is left',
  lastLeft.ok && lastLeft.item.id === pool[pool.length - 1].id,
);
const allOwned = drawReward(NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL, pool.map((item) => item.id), seedFrom('wk-all'));
ok(
  'owning the whole pool still yields a reward rather than nothing',
  allOwned.ok && allOwned.fromOwnedFallback,
);

console.log('\n-- once per account (§6) ----------------------------------------------');

const fresh: WorkoutRewardState = {};
eq('a fresh account is owed the first-workout reward', resolvePendingRewards(fresh).map((r) => r.id), ['first_workout']);
ok('a fresh account has not claimed it', !hasClaimed(fresh, 'first_workout'));

const claimed: WorkoutRewardState = {
  claims: {
    first_workout: { itemId: pool[0].id, grantedAt: '2026-08-24T10:00:00.000Z', workoutId: 'wk-1', source: 'prototype' },
  },
  completedCount: 1,
};
ok('a claimed account has claimed it', hasClaimed(claimed, 'first_workout'));
eq('a claimed account is owed nothing', resolvePendingRewards(claimed), []);
eq(
  'still owed nothing after a hundred more workouts',
  resolvePendingRewards({ ...claimed, completedCount: 101 }),
  [],
);

console.log('\n-- replay protection (§13) --------------------------------------------');

ok('an unseen completion has not been processed', !hasProcessed(fresh, 'wk-1'));
const afterOne: WorkoutRewardState = { processedIds: appendProcessedId(fresh, 'wk-1') };
ok('a seen completion has been processed', hasProcessed(afterOne, 'wk-1'));
eq('recording the same id twice does not duplicate it', appendProcessedId(afterOne, 'wk-1'), ['wk-1']);

let ring: WorkoutRewardState = {};
for (let i = 0; i < PROCESSED_ID_LIMIT + 5; i++) ring = { processedIds: appendProcessedId(ring, `wk-${i}`) };
eq('the id list is capped', ring.processedIds?.length, PROCESSED_ID_LIMIT);
ok('the newest id is kept', hasProcessed(ring, `wk-${PROCESSED_ID_LIMIT + 4}`));
ok('the oldest id has aged out', !hasProcessed(ring, 'wk-0'));

console.log('\n-- the completion interface (§8) ---------------------------------------');

// The bus is what keeps the prototype and a future API interchangeable, so its contract is pinned
// here rather than left to the one component that happens to call it today.

resetWorkoutCompletionBus();
const built = makeWorkoutCompletion({
  userId: 'u-1',
  workoutType: '開合跳',
  durationSeconds: 90.4,
  repCount: 12.6,
  source: 'prototype',
});
ok('a built completion gets an id', !!built.workoutId);
ok('a built completion gets a timestamp', !Number.isNaN(Date.parse(built.completedAt)));
eq('duration and reps are whole numbers', [built.durationSeconds, built.repCount], [90, 13]);
ok(
  'two builds do not share an id',
  makeWorkoutCompletion({ userId: 'u', workoutType: 'x', durationSeconds: 60, source: 'prototype' }).workoutId !==
    built.workoutId,
);
eq(
  "a service's own id is passed through, never replaced",
  makeWorkoutCompletion({ workoutId: 'api-42', userId: 'u', workoutType: 'run', durationSeconds: 60, source: 'external-api' })
    .workoutId,
  'api-42',
);
ok(
  'reps stay absent when the source does not report them',
  !('repCount' in makeWorkoutCompletion({ userId: 'u', workoutType: 'run', durationSeconds: 60, source: 'external-api' })),
  'a run has no reps',
);

resetWorkoutCompletionBus();
const heard: string[] = [];
const stop = subscribeWorkoutCompletion((c) => heard.push(`a:${c.workoutId}`));
reportWorkoutCompletion(completion({ workoutId: 'wk-bus-1' }));
eq('a subscriber hears a completion', heard, ['a:wk-bus-1']);

// The case the replay exists for: a listener that mounts AFTER the announcement still gets it.
subscribeWorkoutCompletion((c) => heard.push(`b:${c.workoutId}`));
eq('a late subscriber is replayed the last completion', heard, ['a:wk-bus-1', 'b:wk-bus-1']);
eq('the bus remembers the last completion', getLastWorkoutCompletion()?.workoutId, 'wk-bus-1');

stop();
reportWorkoutCompletion(completion({ workoutId: 'wk-bus-2' }));
eq('an unsubscribed listener hears nothing more', heard, ['a:wk-bus-1', 'b:wk-bus-1', 'b:wk-bus-2']);

// A broken UI subscriber must never be able to stop the reward service from being told.
resetWorkoutCompletionBus();
const survived: string[] = [];
subscribeWorkoutCompletion(() => {
  throw new Error('a broken subscriber');
});
subscribeWorkoutCompletion((c) => survived.push(c.workoutId));
reportWorkoutCompletion(completion({ workoutId: 'wk-bus-3' }));
eq('one throwing subscriber does not stop the next', survived, ['wk-bus-3']);
resetWorkoutCompletionBus();

console.log('\n-- the rules table (§19) ----------------------------------------------');

const rules = Object.values(WORKOUT_REWARD_RULES);
ok('every rule names a pool that exists', rules.every((rule) => !!buildRewardPool(NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL) && rule.poolId === NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL.id));
ok('every rule keys itself by its own id', rules.every((rule) => WORKOUT_REWARD_RULES[rule.id] === rule));
ok('every rule has copy to show', rules.every((rule) => !!rule.title && !!rule.message));

console.log(
  `\n${failures === 0 ? 'ALL PASS' : `${failures} FAILURE(S)`} — ${checks - failures}/${checks} checks\n`,
);
process.exit(failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);

```
