```tsx
// Shared white, read every frame by the lightning flash below. Allocating it inside useFrame
// made one throwaway THREE.Color per frame purely to hold a constant.
const FLASH_COLOR = new THREE.Color('#ffffff');

/**
 * The weather's own lighting, before an absence is taken into account.
 *
 * Lifted out of the component so {@link SceneLighting} can state its grading in one place instead
 * of threading a multiplier through seven switch arms. These are the numbers the island has always
 * used; nothing here changed when 離線環境 arrived.
 */
function weatherLighting(weather: WeatherType) {
  switch (weather) {
    case WeatherType.SUNNY:
      return {
        ambInt: 0.5,
        hemiInt: 0.6,
        hemiCol: new THREE.Color('#ffffff'),
        dirInt: 1.4,
        dirCol: new THREE.Color('#fffbeb'), // Warm golden sun
      };
    case WeatherType.RAINY:
      return {
        ambInt: 0.28,
        hemiInt: 0.35,
        hemiCol: new THREE.Color('#94a3b8'),
        dirInt: 0.5,
        dirCol: new THREE.Color('#cbd5e1'), // Overcast dim teal-grey
      };
    case WeatherType.STORM:
      return {
        ambInt: 0.15,
        hemiInt: 0.2,
        hemiCol: new THREE.Color('#475569'),
        dirInt: 0.25,
        dirCol: new THREE.Color('#334155'), // Dark stormy blue-slate
      };
    case WeatherType.SNOW:
      return {
        ambInt: 0.7, // Snow bounce reflection
        hemiInt: 0.5,
        hemiCol: new THREE.Color('#e2e8f0'),
        dirInt: 0.85,
        dirCol: new THREE.Color('#f8fafc'), // Light frozen color
      };
    case WeatherType.TWILIGHT:
      return {
        ambInt: 0.35,
        hemiInt: 0.5,
        hemiCol: new THREE.Color('#c084fc'), // Purple twilight bounce
        dirInt: 0.95,
        dirCol: new THREE.Color('#f97316'), // Fiery sunset orange directional
      };
    case WeatherType.MIDNIGHT:
      return {
        // Dark, but deliberately not as dark as STORM: the island still has to
        // be readable enough to walk around and place furniture on at night.
        ambInt: 0.3,
        hemiInt: 0.34,
        hemiCol: new THREE.Color('#1e3a8a'), // Deep blue night bounce
        dirInt: 0.5,
        dirCol: new THREE.Color('#a5c4ff'), // Pale moonlight
      };
    default:
      return {
        ambInt: 0.5,
        hemiInt: 0.5,
        hemiCol: new THREE.Color('#ffffff'),
        dirInt: 1.2,
        dirCol: new THREE.Color('#ffffff'),
      };
  }
}

/** The colour a long absence leans the light toward. Built once — see constants/islandReturn.ts. */
const SHADE_COLOR = new THREE.Color(AMBIENCE_SHADE_TINT);

/** Scratch for the HSL round-trips below, so grading a colour allocates nothing extra. */
const HSL = { h: 0, s: 0, l: 0 };

/**
 * 離線環境的顏色 — one weather light colour, aged by however overgrown the island is.
 *
 * ## Why this is not a post-processing pass
 *
 * 「畫面稍微變暗、飽和度降低」 reads as a job for a colour-grading pass over the finished frame, and
 * that is what it would be in a project that already had an EffectComposer. This one does not: the
 * island renders straight to the canvas, and adding a composer means a new dependency, a
 * full-screen render target, and at minimum one extra full-screen draw every frame on hardware
 * that the brief explicitly says has stuttered before. For a *subtle, permanent* tint that is a
 * very large bill for a very small effect.
 *
 * Desaturating the LIGHT instead buys nearly the same picture for nothing at all. Everything on
 * the island is lit by these three lights, so pulling the saturation out of their colour pulls it
 * out of every surface they touch — no new pass, no new material, no per-object shader, and not a
 * single extra draw call. It differs from a true post-process only on emissive and unlit surfaces
 * (the sky dome, the fireflies), and leaving those alone is arguably the better picture anyway:
 * an overgrown garden is shaded, not overcast.
 *
 * The lightness the weather chose is restored at the end on purpose. Dimming is the intensity
 * term's job ({@link IslandAmbience.brightness}) and the exposure's; if the tint were allowed to
 * darken as well, the three would compound invisibly and 「稍微變暗」 would quietly become 「變黑」.
 */
function gradeLightColor(base: THREE.Color, ambience: IslandAmbience): THREE.Color {
  base.getHSL(HSL);
  const lightness = HSL.l;
  const out = new THREE.Color().setHSL(HSL.h, HSL.s * ambience.saturation, lightness);
  out.lerp(SHADE_COLOR, ambience.shade * AMBIENCE_SHADE_MAX);
  out.getHSL(HSL);
  return out.setHSL(HSL.h, HSL.s, lightness);
}

// Performance-optimized lighting sub-component to interactively lerp lights on frame
function SceneLighting() {
  const { weather, profile } = useApp();
  const gl = useThree((state) => state.gl);
  const ambientRef = useRef<THREE.AmbientLight>(null);
  const hemiRef = useRef<THREE.HemisphereLight>(null);
  const dirRef = useRef<THREE.DirectionalLight>(null);

  /**
   * 島嶼目前的荒廢程度 — resolved ONCE, here, from the list the scene is already drawing.
   *
   * Not from `lastSeenAt`, and not per-component: this is the brief's 「不要讓不同 Component 各自
   * 計算離線天數」 line, and the reason the calculation lives in constants/islandReturn.ts rather
   * than in either of the two files that read it. It costs a length lookup and returns a shared
   * constant for the overwhelmingly common case of a clean island.
   *
   * Because it is derived from the sprouts rather than from the clock, the light comes back as the
   * player tidies — the same array shrinks, the same number falls, and the lerp below carries the
   * island home over the next second or so with no recovery logic anywhere. See §7 of the brief
   * and the long note on {@link IslandAmbience}.
   */
  const ambience = resolveIslandAmbience(profile?.islandState?.sprouts);

  /**
   * HOW WINDY IT IS, published out of React for the outdoor animation system.
   *
   * Every swaying plant, the mobile and the hammock read the weather's wind multiplier, and none
   * of them can call `useApp()` to get it: those models are also rendered by the build-time
   * audits through a stub hook dispatcher with no providers above them
   * (scripts/lib/measureFurnitureModel.ts), where a context read throws and the model is filed as
   * unmeasurable. One publish from the component that already has the weather, read as a module
   * value by lib/outdoorMotion.ts, keeps the models context-free.
   */
  useEffect(() => { setWindWeather(weather); }, [weather]);

  // Keyed on the grading SCALARS rather than on the ambience object, so this recomputes when the
  // island actually changes and not merely when some unrelated part of the profile is patched.
  const targets = useMemo(() => {
    const base = weatherLighting(weather);
    return {
      ambInt: base.ambInt * ambience.brightness,
      hemiInt: base.hemiInt * ambience.brightness,
      hemiCol: gradeLightColor(base.hemiCol, ambience),
      dirInt: base.dirInt * ambience.brightness,
      dirCol: gradeLightColor(base.dirCol, ambience),
    };
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [weather, ambience.brightness, ambience.saturation, ambience.shade]);

  const updateLightning = useLightningFlicker();

  useFrame((state) => {
    const elapsed = state.clock.getElapsedTime();

    // Lightning strike timing synced dynamically with SkyDome
    const flash = updateLightning(elapsed, weather === WeatherType.STORM, 0.9, 0.15);
    const flashAmbient = flash * 0.9;
    const flashDir = flash * 2.8;

    // Lerp direct and indirect lighting values for realistic ambient density shifts
    if (ambientRef.current) {
      ambientRef.current.intensity = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(
        ambientRef.current.intensity,
        targets.ambInt + flashAmbient,
        0.03
      );
    }
    if (hemiRef.current) {
      hemiRef.current.intensity = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(
        hemiRef.current.intensity,
        targets.hemiInt + flashAmbient * 0.5,
        0.03
      );
      hemiRef.current.color.lerp(
        flashAmbient > 0 ? FLASH_COLOR : targets.hemiCol,
        0.03
      );
    }
    if (dirRef.current) {
      dirRef.current.intensity = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(
        dirRef.current.intensity,
        targets.dirInt + flashDir,
        0.03
      );
      dirRef.current.color.lerp(
        flashDir > 0 ? FLASH_COLOR : targets.dirCol,
        0.03
      );
    }

    /**
     * 光線稍微變弱 — the last of the four grading terms, and the only one that is not a light.
     *
     * One scalar on the renderer, so it costs nothing and reaches everything the lights cannot
     * (the sky, the ocean's own tint), which is what keeps a heavily overgrown island from looking
     * like a dim garden under a bright sky.
     *
     * It rides the SAME 0.03 lerp as the lights above, and that is the whole of the brief's §15:
     * a returning player's first seconds are the exposure and the three lights easing from where
     * they were toward what the absence is worth — 「數秒內逐漸套用」 — rather than the island
     * being dim on frame one. There is no transition timer anywhere in this feature, because the
     * lighting rig was already a smoothing filter and an absence is just another input to it.
     *
     * Per-renderer, so it cannot leak: the house interior and the shop mount their own <Canvas>
     * and are never touched by this.
     */
    gl.toneMappingExposure = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(gl.toneMappingExposure, ambience.exposure, 0.03);
  });

  return (
    <>
      <ambientLight ref={ambientRef} intensity={0.4} />
      <hemisphereLight ref={hemiRef} intensity={0.5} color="#ffffff" groundColor="#4a4a4a" />
      {/* The island's sun, and the only shadow caster outdoors.

          The four `shadow-*` settings below the camera box were added with the 地表/人物 quality
          pass, and they are what make the shadow map usable for CONTACT shadows rather than only
          for the big soft blobs the terrain was getting:

          near/far — the default range is 0.5 to 500 over a scene whose content sits between 15
            and 45 units from this light. Depth precision is spent across the whole range, so
            999 parts in 1000 of a 16-bit depth buffer were describing empty space beyond the
            island. Tightening it to 5..70 is a straight ~7x gain in usable precision, for free.
          bias/normalBias — required the moment anything self-shadows. The character's meshes now
            receive shadows (see character/bodySurface.ts), and a curved surface lit at a grazing
            angle is where depth-map acne appears: without these, the skull's own shadow lands on
            the skull as a band of stripes. normalBias (offsetting the lookup ALONG the surface
            normal) is the one that matters on spheres and capsules; the constant bias handles
            what is left, and is kept small so contact shadows do not detach from their caster. */}
      <directionalLight
        ref={dirRef}
        position={[20, 20, 10]}
        intensity={1.2}
        castShadow
        /* 1024, down from 2048. The shadow camera below spans 40 world units, so this
           is still ~26 shadow texels per unit - far finer than a stylised island with
           PCF filtering can show - while the map itself is a quarter of the pixels.
           It is not a one-off cost: a shadow map is a full extra render of every
           castShadow object in the scene, EVERY frame, and at 2048 that pass was
           writing four megapixels of depth per frame to resolve edges that the filter
           then softens away again. */
        shadow-mapSize={[1024, 1024]}
        shadow-camera-left={-20}
        shadow-camera-right={20}
        shadow-camera-top={20}
        shadow-camera-bottom={-20}
        shadow-camera-near={5}
        shadow-camera-far={70}
        shadow-bias={-0.0004}
        shadow-normalBias={0.028}
      />
    </>
  );
}

/**
 * Everything inside the island's <Canvas>.
 *
 * Its own component purely so it can be memoised, and it deliberately takes NO props, so after
 * mount React never walks it again. That is the point: <Scene /> is a direct child of AppContent,
 * which consumes AppContext, and R3F's own <Canvas> subscribes to the same context to bridge it
 * across the renderer boundary - so every context change (a coin awarded, the weather cycling, a
 * proximity flag flipping) used to re-render this entire 3D element tree, hundreds of elements
 * reconciled against state almost none of them read.
 *
 * Nothing is lost. The pieces that DO depend on context - SceneLighting, Avatar, Island, and the
 * rest - call useApp() themselves and re-render on their own, which is where that work belongs.
 */
/**
 * The cosmetic field, plus the one thing it needs that only AppContext can answer.
 *
 * Its own component so SceneContents above can stay free of context and stay memoised: the ground
 * lookup is the only piece in that tree which has to be rebuilt when the island's placements or
 * territory level change, so it is the only piece that subscribes.
 *
 * groundAt is "how high is the ground at (x, z)" for ground-conforming cosmetics — the same lookup
 * the player's own feet use (characterMovement's resolveCollisions calls getSurfaceAt too).
 *
 * Sharing it is the point: a ring of light drawn around someone standing on a deck sits ON the
 * deck, and it does so with no knowledge of decks, because the one function that knows where
 * the top of anything is already answers for both.
 */
function GroundedCosmeticField({ children }: { children?: React.ReactNode }) {
  const { profile } = useApp();

  const groundAt = useMemo(() => {
    const placements = profile?.islandPlacements ?? [];
    const islandScale = 1 + ((profile?.territoryLevel ?? 1) - 1) * 0.4;
    return (x: number, z: number) => getSurfaceAt(x, z, placements, islandScale).y;
  }, [profile?.islandPlacements, profile?.territoryLevel]);

  return <CosmeticEffectField groundAt={groundAt}>{children}</CosmeticEffectField>;
}

const SceneContents = React.memo(function SceneContents() {
  return (
    <>
        <SkyDome />
        {/* 深夜's moon, stars and shooting stars. Always mounted; it fades
            itself in and out with the weather (see NightSky.tsx). */}
        {/* No drei <Stars> here, and that is the other half of the 破圖 report.
            It was mounted unconditionally with no weather gate of any kind, so 2000
            additively-blended white points were drawn into the sky at HIGH NOON - a
            permanent scatter of pale specks over the blue that reads as dead pixels
            rather than as anything in the world. Its field is a full SPHERE, so about
            half of those points sat BELOW the waterline; Ocean's surface planes are
            transparent with depthWrite off and therefore cannot occlude anything, so
            they came through the sea as well. Diffing two renders of the same frame
            with and without it put 37 changed pixels in the sky and 9 in the water,
            with the lowest 260px under the horizon.
            深夜's stars are NightSky.tsx's own StarField, which is gated on the night
            ramp, confined to the upper hemisphere for exactly this reason, and
            twinkles per star. Nothing is lost by deleting this line. */}
        <Fireflies count={40} />
        {/* Self-hosted HDR rather than drei's `preset="sunset"` - see
            constants/environmentMaps.ts. */}
        <Environment files={HDRI_SUNSET} />
        
        <SceneLighting />

        {/* Special cosmetic effects. Wraps the world group because the player and the pet are
            both inside it and both register their ornaments through this provider; the pooled
            particle meshes it mounts alongside them live in untransformed world space, which
            this group is (it has no transform of its own). One per Canvas — see
            Three/effects/EffectField.tsx. */}
        <GroundedCosmeticField>
        <group>
          <Ocean />
          {/* The sea floor and everything growing on it. Mounted here rather
              than inside Ocean.tsx because that component's contents live in an
              already-rotated group where local Z is world up - reasoning about
              seabed depth in that frame is needlessly confusing. */}
          <OceanDecorations />
          {/* Sits below Ocean's surface planes - drawn opaque, so the
              translucent water blends over it and tints the shoal */}
          <Fish count={32} />
          <Clouds />
          <Island />
          <Avatar isInterior={false} />
          {/* The player's one Home, drawn separately from IslandPlacements so no code path can
              ever produce a second dwelling. */}
          <PlayerHomeView />
          <IslandPlacements />
          <PlacementGhost />
          {/* The equipped 寵物 walking beside its owner - or, with nothing equipped, the island's
              own stray. See IslandPet.tsx for which of the two is mounted. */}
          <IslandPet />
          {/* 拿著鏟子在島上到處走的餅乾兔園丁。掛在 Island 之後，因為她每一步的腳下高度
              都是問地形要的（見 IslandNpcs.tsx）。另一位居民（河馬管家）在屋子裡，掛在
              BuildingInteriorView 那個 Canvas 上。 */}
          <IslandNpcs />
          {/* 島邊的訪客 —— 旅行商人與他的小船（Three/MerchantVisitor.tsx）。掛在世界
              group 裡而不是 Ocean 裡面：Ocean 的內容活在一個已經轉過的 group（local Z 是
              世界的上）裡，而這艘船是照世界座標航行的。他在不在，是限時商店的檔期算出來
              的（constants/merchantVisit.ts），不是這裡決定的。 */}
          <MerchantVisitors />
          <IslandDecorations />
          {/* 離線回歸 — whatever grew while nobody was here (Three/IslandOvergrowth.tsx).
              Drawn after the island own decorations and as a SIBLING of PlayerHomeView: it is
              temporary world state rather than art or furniture, it carries no collider and no
              pointer handlers, and nothing in the build/placement system can see it. */}
          <IslandOvergrowth />
          <Weather />
        </group>
        </GroundedCosmeticField>

        {/* No <ContactShadows> here. It re-rendered the ENTIRE scene into an
            offscreen depth target plus two blur passes on every single frame
            (drei's `frames` prop defaults to Infinity), which profiling put at
            ~100x the cost of every other per-frame subscriber combined - and it
            bought nothing, because its plane sits at y=0 while the island's
            opaque walkable surface is at ISLAND_SURFACE_Y (0.3), so it was
            buried under the terrain and never visible. Ground shadows come from
            the directional light's real shadow map above (castShadow +
            receiveShadow on the terrain), which is what was actually being seen
            all along. */}

        <CameraController minDistance={10} maxDistance={35} />
        <InteractionPromptTracker />
        <ZFightAuditBridge label="island" />
    </>
  );
});

/**
 * The island.
 *
 * Holds nothing but the <Canvas> and the one piece of state that has to reach it as a PROP:
 * whether to keep rendering at all.
 *
 * `frameloop='never'` stops the island entirely while a full-screen view is covering it. Going
 * into the house does not replace this Canvas - BuildingInteriorView mounts a SECOND one on top
 * (App.tsx's View Overlays block), so without this the island kept drawing every frame, shadow
 * map and all, behind an opaque interior: two live WebGL scenes competing for the same GPU and
 * the same main thread, which is what made crossing the threshold hitch. The same holds for the
 * shop, the dressing room and the rest - each covers the island completely, or (Settings,
 * Tracker) behind a stack of two heavy backdrop blurs that nothing recognisable survives.
 * BUILD_MODE is deliberately NOT covered: it decorates the island through this very Canvas.
 *
 * It has to be the PROP and not an imperative `setFrameloop` from inside the Canvas. R3F
 * re-applies this prop on every render of <Canvas>, and <Canvas> re-renders on every AppContext
 * change (it consumes the context in order to bridge it across the renderer boundary) - so a
 * child calling setFrameloop was overwritten again within a tick, and the island never actually
 * stopped. Driving it from the prop makes React's value the only one there is.
 *
 * Note setFrameloop resets the render clock. That is fine here precisely because it can only
 * happen while the scene is hidden, so no time-driven animation is ever seen jumping.
 */
export function Scene() {
  const { currentView } = useApp();
  const covered = currentView !== View.HOME && currentView !== View.BUILD_MODE;

  /**
   * How many pixels the island is drawn at — see Three/AdaptiveResolution.tsx.
   *
   * State here rather than a constant on the <Canvas> below, and measured from inside the
   * renderer rather than guessed from the hardware, because this scene's frame time is almost
   * entirely a function of the drawing buffer's area (the measurements are in that file). A
   * fixed cap has to be chosen for the weakest machine or the sharpest display and is wrong for
   * the other; letting the number follow the frame time it actually produces is right for both.
   *
   * It has to live at this level for the same reason `frameloop` does: <Canvas> re-applies its
   * own props on every render, and it re-renders on every AppContext change, so a value set
   * imperatively from a child is overwritten within a tick.
   */
  const [dpr, setDpr] = React.useState(initialDpr);

  return (
    <div className="w-full h-full absolute inset-0 z-background cursor-crosshair">
      {/* `near` is set explicitly because the default (0.1) throws away almost
          all of this scene's depth precision. Depth resolution scales with
          near/far ratio, and the ocean's far plane forces far=2000, so a 0.1
          near gives a 20000:1 range - at the ~50 units this camera orbits at,
          that leaves surfaces under ~0.4 apart unresolvable on any 16-bit depth
          context, which is where the terrain flicker was visible worst.

          0.5 is free: CameraController clamps the orbit to minDistance 10, and
          the only world content that can come nearer than that is a rain
          particle passing through the lens, which is a full-screen artifact
          either way. This is a supporting fix - the coplanar surfaces it used
          to expose have been merged in Island.tsx regardless, so nothing here
          depends on it. */}
      <Canvas
        frameloop={covered ? 'never' : 'always'}
        shadows={{ type: THREE.PCFShadowMap }}
        camera={{ position: [30, 12, 40], fov: 25, near: 0.5, far: 2000 }}
        /* THE SINGLE BIGGEST LEVER ON THIS SCENE'S FRAME TIME, and it was not set.
           With no `dpr` R3F renders at `window.devicePixelRatio`, so a laptop at
           Windows' default 150% scaling was drawing 2.25x the pixels of the canvas it
           displays, and a 4K panel 4x. That is paid in full by the one thing this
           scene has most of: BLENDED FULL-SCREEN LAYERS. Sky dome, far sea, near sea,
           the reflection smear, the wave crest, the foam, 200 transparent cloud puffs
           and the weather particles all overdraw the same pixels, none of them can
           early-Z out (they discard), and every one of them costs proportionally more
           the more pixels there are. 1.5 keeps the edges of the HUD-free 3D art
           smooth on a HiDPI panel while capping the worst case at 2.25x fewer
           fragments than an uncapped 4K display was doing.

           That cap is now the STARTING rung rather than the whole answer: `initialDpr()` picks
           exactly the number the old `[1, 1.5]` range would have produced, and
           <AdaptiveResolution> walks down from it on a machine that is missing frames at it.
           A 1x panel is now reachable too, which a floor of 1 could never help. */
        dpr={dpr}
        onCreated={({ gl }) => tuneRenderer(gl)}
      >
        <AdaptiveResolution dpr={dpr} onChange={setDpr} />
        {/* A Suspense boundary INSIDE the canvas, around everything that can suspend (the HDR
            <Environment>, the character's GLB parts). Without one, R3F forwards the suspension
            out by making <Canvas> itself suspend, and with nothing above it that paused the WHOLE
            app at the root: no commits for 20-140 s, a frozen loading bar, and the entire HUD
            re-rendering every frame while it waited (captured: deepest Incomplete fiber was
            CanvasImpl). It must be in here, not around <Canvas>: bounding it outside hides the
            committed canvas, which stops R3F's own root, so the island never drew at all. */}
        <React.Suspense fallback={null}>
          <SceneContents />
        </React.Suspense>
      </Canvas>

      {/* 離線褪色 — the desaturating sheet, and the recovery that lifts it (UI/IslandColourVeil).
          A SIBLING of the <Canvas> and inside this wrapper on purpose. Inside, so the frame it
          desaturates is the island and nothing else: every HUD tier is z-game-view and above, so
          the shop, the buttons and every modal stay in full colour over a black-and-white world.
          A sibling rather than a child, because it is a DOM element — it costs the R3F tree
          nothing, and it renders literally nothing at all unless this session began with a long
          absence. It cannot reach input: pointer-events are off and there is no path from it to
          the camera, a collider or a raycast. */}
      <IslandColourVeil />
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { memo, useMemo } from 'react';
import * as THREE from 'three';

/**
 * Q-version footwear for the avatar.
 *
 * The 3D shoe used to be one `boxGeometry` per foot with a single flat colour, while the shop
 * icon for the same item was a fully articulated drawing - so a shoe that looked detailed in the
 * grid turned into a monotone brick once equipped. This module fixes that side of the gap: every
 * shoe is built from a stack of parts (outsole / midsole / upper / heel / trim) and takes its
 * palette straight from the matching branch of QVersionIcon, so the worn shoe and its icon read
 * as the same object.
 *
 * LOCAL SPACE - the whole component is authored in one convention, and every number below is in
 * it. Get this wrong and the shoe either floats or sinks into the terrain:
 *
 *   y = 0   the ground / underside of the outsole. Everything is built UPWARD from here.
 *   z = 0   the ankle's centre line. +z is forward (toes), -z is back (heel).
 *   x = 0   the centre line of the foot. The models are symmetric, so one component serves
 *           both feet and there is no left/right variant to keep in sync.
 *
 * The caller is responsible for putting that origin on the ground - see `soleAnchorY()`.
 *
 * ENCLOSING THE LEG - the leg is a capsule of radius LEG_RADIUS whose bottom cap rests at y = 0,
 * and it is NOT trimmed when a shoe is on. So any closed part of a shoe that sits at a height
 * where the leg is already at full width has to be wider than LEG_RADIUS, or the leg pokes out
 * through the side of it. That is why the collars and shafts here are cylinders of radius ~0.058
 * and up rather than something snugger: at chibi scale the leg is nearly as wide as the foot.
 * Open shoes (sandals, flip-flops) dodge this entirely - they have no closed upper, and the
 * skin-coloured foot slab they do draw simply merges with the leg it overlaps.
 */

export type ShoeType = 'sport' | 'leather' | 'heels' | 'boots' | 'sandals' | 'flipflops';

/** Radius of the avatar's leg capsule. Mirrors the value in Avatar.tsx. */
const LEG_RADIUS = 0.055;

/**
 * Where the shoe group has to sit in LEG-LOCAL space for its y=0 to land on the ground.
 *
 * The leg capsule hangs off the hip pivot at -0.10 - legLengthen/2 with a straight section of
 * 0.14 + legLengthen, so its bottom cap is at -(0.10 + legLengthen/2) - (0.14 + legLengthen)/2
 * - LEG_RADIUS, which reduces to -0.225 - legLengthen. Deriving it rather than hard-coding it
 * keeps the shoes glued to the sole if the legs are ever lengthened again.
 */
export const soleAnchorY = (legLengthen: number) => -0.225 - legLengthen;

/** Half-width of a normal shoe body. Comfortably clear of LEG_RADIUS - see the header note. */
const W = 0.060;

/**
 * A rounded slab - the workhorse shape for soles and uppers.
 *
 * It is a capsule laid on its side and squashed: `rotation.x = 90deg` maps the capsule's own +Y
 * axis onto world +Z (so the straight section runs heel-to-toe) and its local +Z onto world -Y,
 * which is why the vertical squash is `scale.z` and not `scale.y`. The result is a shape with
 * rounded ends and a flat-ish top, which is what a chibi sole wants - a plain box reads as a
 * brick, and that brick is exactly what this file exists to replace.
 *
 * `y` is the slab's BOTTOM, not its centre, because every shoe here is stacked bottom-up.
 */
function Slab({
  r,
  len,
  h,
  y,
  z = 0,
  color,
  roughness = 0.6,
  metalness = 0,
  castShadow = false,
}: {
  /** Half-width, and also the radius of the rounded heel/toe ends. */
  r: number;
  /** Length of the STRAIGHT section. Total depth is len + 2r. */
  len: number;
  /** Finished height of the slab. */
  h: number;
  y: number;
  z?: number;
  color: string;
  roughness?: number;
  metalness?: number;
  castShadow?: boolean;
}) {
  return (
    <mesh
      position={[0, y + h / 2, z]}
      rotation={[Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]}
      scale={[1, 1, h / (2 * r)]}
      castShadow={castShadow}
    >
      <capsuleGeometry args={[r, len, 4, 20]} />
      <meshStandardMaterial color={color} roughness={roughness} metalness={metalness} />
    </mesh>
  );
}

/** An upright tube - ankle collars and boot shafts. `y` is its bottom. */
function Tube({
  rTop,
  rBot,
  h,
  y,
  z = 0,
  color,
  roughness = 0.6,
  castShadow = false,
}: {
  rTop: number;
  rBot: number;
  h: number;
  y: number;
  z?: number;
  color: string;
  roughness?: number;
  castShadow?: boolean;
}) {
  return (
    <mesh position={[0, y + h / 2, z]} castShadow={castShadow}>
      <cylinderGeometry args={[rTop, rBot, h, 20, 1, true]} />
      <meshStandardMaterial color={color} roughness={roughness} side={THREE.DoubleSide} />
    </mesh>
  );
}

/**
 * A capsule stretched between two points - straps, laces and the flip-flop's Y.
 *
 * Straps run diagonally in all three axes, and hand-authoring Euler angles for those is how you
 * end up with a strap that floats off the foot. Deriving the rotation from the endpoints instead
 * means the ends always land exactly where the design says they do.
 */
function Strut({
  from,
  to,
  r,
  color,
  roughness = 0.5,
}: {
  from: [number, number, number];
  to: [number, number, number];
  r: number;
  color: string;
  roughness?: number;
}) {
  const [ax, ay, az] = from;
  const [bx, by, bz] = to;
  const { position, quaternion, straight } = useMemo(() => {
    const a = new THREE.Vector3(ax, ay, az);
    const b = new THREE.Vector3(bx, by, bz);
    const dir = new THREE.Vector3().subVectors(b, a);
    const length = dir.length();
    return {
      position: new THREE.Vector3().addVectors(a, b).multiplyScalar(0.5),
      // Capsules are born pointing up +Y; rotate that onto the strut's direction.
      quaternion: new THREE.Quaternion().setFromUnitVectors(
        new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0),
        dir.normalize(),
      ),
      // capsuleGeometry's first length arg is the straight part only, so the caps have to be
      // subtracted or the strap overshoots its anchors by one radius at each end.
      straight: Math.max(length - 2 * r, 0.001),
    };
  }, [ax, ay, az, bx, by, bz, r]);

  return (
    <mesh position={position} quaternion={quaternion}>
      <capsuleGeometry args={[r, straight, 4, 10]} />
      <meshStandardMaterial color={color} roughness={roughness} />
    </mesh>
  );
}

/**
 * A strap arching over the foot. A torus in the XY plane, squashed to an oval so it hugs a foot
 * that is much wider than it is tall. Its lower half is buried inside the footbed on purpose -
 * that is what tucks the strap ends out of sight without modelling them.
 */
function ArchStrap({
  y,
  z,
  r,
  tube,
  color,
  scaleX = 1.35,
  scaleY = 0.85,
}: {
  y: number;
  z: number;
  r: number;
  tube: number;
  color: string;
  scaleX?: number;
  scaleY?: number;
}) {
  return (
    <mesh position={[0, y, z]} scale={[scaleX, scaleY, 1]}>
      <torusGeometry args={[r, tube, 8, 24]} />
      <meshStandardMaterial color={color} roughness={0.55} />
    </mesh>
  );
}

/** Three toe bumps peeking out of an open shoe. The single clearest "this shoe is open" cue. */
function Toes({ y, z, color }: { y: number; z: number; color: string }) {
  return (
    <>
      {[-0.026, 0, 0.026].map((x, i) => (
        <mesh key={i} position={[x, y, z - Math.abs(x) * 0.28]} scale={[1, 0.8, 1.1]}>
          <sphereGeometry args={[0.011, 10, 8]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial color={color} roughness={0.75} />
        </mesh>
      ))}
    </>
  );
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *
 * The six shoes. Palettes are lifted from QVersionIcon's shoes-* art. *
 * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

/** Runner: chunky two-tone foam stack, blue heel counter, swoosh and laces. */
function SportShoe() {
  return (
    <>
      <Slab r={W} len={0.04} h={0.014} y={0} z={0.028} color="#1F4E7A" roughness={0.85} castShadow />
      <Slab r={W + 0.001} len={0.038} h={0.024} y={0.013} z={0.028} color="#F4F7FB" roughness={0.75} />
      <Slab r={0.058} len={0.03} h={0.036} y={0.034} z={0.032} color="#FFFFFF" roughness={0.55} castShadow />
      {/* Reinforced panels: heel counter at the back, lighter cap over the toe. */}
      <Slab r={0.059} len={0.004} h={0.034} y={0.035} z={-0.03} color="#2E7FD4" roughness={0.55} />
      <Slab r={0.052} len={0.004} h={0.026} y={0.034} z={0.09} color="#DCE9F5" roughness={0.5} />
      <Tube rTop={0.06} rBot={0.06} h={0.03} y={0.048} z={-0.012} color="#FFFFFF" roughness={0.55} />
      {/* Padded collar rim closing the top of the cylinder. */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.077, -0.012]} rotation={[Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]}>
        <torusGeometry args={[0.058, 0.009, 8, 24]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#7CB8EB" roughness={0.6} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Swoosh sweeping up out of the midsole on both flanks. */}
      {[-1, 1].map((s) => (
        <mesh key={s} position={[s * 0.058, 0.046, 0.03]} rotation={[0.28, 0, 0]}>
          <boxGeometry args={[0.005, 0.014, 0.075]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial color="#2E7FD4" roughness={0.5} />
        </mesh>
      ))}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.068, 0.026]} rotation={[0.25, 0, 0]}>
        <boxGeometry args={[0.05, 0.012, 0.032]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#FFFFFF" roughness={0.6} />
      </mesh>
      {[0.014, 0.03].map((z) => (
        <mesh key={z} position={[0, 0.079, z]}>
          <boxGeometry args={[0.052, 0.005, 0.006]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial color="#2E7FD4" roughness={0.45} />
        </mesh>
      ))}
    </>
  );
}

/** Oxford: tan welt, stacked heel, long polished toe cap, pale laces. */
function LeatherShoe() {
  return (
    <>
      <Slab r={0.058} len={0.04} h={0.012} y={0} z={0.03} color="#C89A64" roughness={0.7} castShadow />
      {/* Stacked heel sits ON the welt rather than under it - dropping it below would push the
          shoe through the ground, since y=0 is already the terrain. */}
      <Slab r={0.042} len={0.006} h={0.009} y={0.011} z={-0.03} color="#8A5A38" roughness={0.7} />
      {/* Low roughness plus a touch of metalness is the polish - cheaper and better looking
          than painting a specular streak on as extra geometry. */}
      <Slab r={0.056} len={0.03} h={0.034} y={0.018} z={0.034} color="#4A2C1A" roughness={0.28} metalness={0.15} castShadow />
      <Tube rTop={0.058} rBot={0.058} h={0.024} y={0.04} z={-0.012} color="#4A2C1A" roughness={0.28} />
      <mesh position={[0, 0.062, -0.012]} rotation={[Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]}>
        <torusGeometry args={[0.057, 0.006, 8, 24]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#3A2113" roughness={0.35} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Toe-cap seam. */}
      <Slab r={0.05} len={0.002} h={0.028} y={0.02} z={0.082} color="#3A2113" roughness={0.3} />
      {/* Lace facing across the throat. */}
      {[0.012, 0.028].map((z) => (
        <mesh key={z} position={[0, 0.052, z]} rotation={[0.2, 0, 0]}>
          <boxGeometry args={[0.032, 0.004, 0.005]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial color="#D9B98C" roughness={0.6} />
        </mesh>
      ))}
    </>
  );
}

/**
 * Pump: pointed toe, satin vamp, chunky block heel with a dark tap.
 *
 * A true stiletto would need the foot pitched forward, and the leg it attaches to cannot be
 * tilted from here - the result is a floating shoe with the ankle poking out under the arch. The
 * item description covers block heels too ("細跟或粗跟"), so this takes the block: it keeps
 * ground contact honest at both ends and still reads unmistakably as a heel.
 */
function HeelShoe() {
  return (
    <>
      <Slab r={0.052} len={0.024} h={0.012} y={0} z={0.034} color="#C4134F" roughness={0.4} castShadow />
      {/* Pointed toe: a cone squashed to the sole's height, apex forward. */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.006, 0.111]} rotation={[Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} scale={[1, 1, 0.24]}>
        <coneGeometry args={[0.05, 0.028, 16]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#C4134F" roughness={0.4} />
      </mesh>
      <Slab r={0.03} len={0.006} h={0.046} y={0} z={-0.036} color="#C4134F" roughness={0.4} castShadow />
      <Slab r={0.03} len={0.006} h={0.005} y={0} z={-0.036} color="#7A0C36" roughness={0.7} />
      <Slab r={0.056} len={0.018} h={0.034} y={0.01} z={0.02} color="#E11D64" roughness={0.3} castShadow />
      <Tube rTop={0.057} rBot={0.057} h={0.036} y={0.032} z={-0.024} color="#E11D64" roughness={0.3} />
      <mesh position={[0, 0.068, -0.024]} rotation={[Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]}>
        <torusGeometry args={[0.056, 0.005, 8, 24]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#C4134F" roughness={0.35} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Gem at the throat. */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.046, 0.05]}>
        <sphereGeometry args={[0.011, 12, 10]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#FFD84D" roughness={0.15} metalness={0.4} />
      </mesh>
    </>
  );
}

/** Tall boot: lug sole, tan welt, high shaft, folded cuff and a buckled ankle strap. */
function BootShoe() {
  return (
    <>
      <Slab r={W + 0.001} len={0.038} h={0.016} y={0} z={0.026} color="#2A2E36" roughness={0.95} castShadow />
      <Slab r={W + 0.002} len={0.038} h={0.008} y={0.015} z={0.026} color="#D9A566" roughness={0.7} />
      <Slab r={W} len={0.03} h={0.032} y={0.022} z={0.03} color="#3F4550" roughness={0.6} castShadow />
      <Slab r={0.054} len={0.004} h={0.026} y={0.024} z={0.086} color="#4C525E" roughness={0.55} />
      <Tube rTop={0.063} rBot={0.063} h={0.1} y={0.045} z={-0.006} color="#3F4550" roughness={0.6} castShadow />
      {/* Folded-over cuff, deliberately wider than the shaft. */}
      <Tube rTop={0.07} rBot={0.068} h={0.026} y={0.132} z={-0.006} color="#A97C50" roughness={0.65} />
      <mesh position={[0, 0.158, -0.006]} rotation={[Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]}>
        <torusGeometry args={[0.069, 0.006, 8, 24]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#8A5A32" roughness={0.7} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Ankle strap and its buckle. */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.072, -0.006]} rotation={[Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]}>
        <torusGeometry args={[0.064, 0.007, 8, 24]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#2A2E36" roughness={0.7} />
      </mesh>
      <mesh position={[0, 0.072, 0.058]}>
        <boxGeometry args={[0.017, 0.017, 0.009]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#FFC94D" roughness={0.25} metalness={0.5} />
      </mesh>
    </>
  );
}

/** Slide sandal: cork footbed on a rubber outsole, coral straps, gold medallion, bare toes. */
function SandalShoe({ skinColor }: { skinColor: string }) {
  return (
    <>
      <Slab r={W} len={0.04} h={0.01} y={0} z={0.028} color="#A9743E" roughness={0.85} castShadow />
      <Slab r={W + 0.001} len={0.04} h={0.014} y={0.009} z={0.028} color="#EFD3A4" roughness={0.8} />
      {/* The foot itself, not a shoe part - an open sandal has to show one. */}
      <Slab r={0.052} len={0.026} h={0.03} y={0.021} z={0.03} color={skinColor} roughness={0.75} />
      <Toes y={0.03} z={0.088} color={skinColor} />
      <ArchStrap y={0.024} z={0.03} r={0.04} tube={0.008} color="#FF7A59" />
      <ArchStrap y={0.024} z={-0.018} r={0.038} tube={0.006} color="#FF9E7A" scaleX={1.3} scaleY={0.9} />
      <mesh position={[0, 0.056, 0.03]}>
        <sphereGeometry args={[0.011, 12, 10]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#FFC94D" roughness={0.2} metalness={0.4} />
      </mesh>
    </>
  );
}

/**
 * Flip-flop: thin two-tone foam and a Y strap.
 *
 * The sandal above is also "strap over a sole", so the two have to be told apart by build, not
 * colour: this one gets a thin sole instead of the sandal's chunky cork stack, and a Y off a
 * single toe post instead of two bands across the foot.
 */
function FlipFlopShoe({ skinColor }: { skinColor: string }) {
  return (
    <>
      <Slab r={W} len={0.04} h={0.008} y={0} z={0.028} color="#17B8B0" roughness={0.8} castShadow />
      <Slab r={W + 0.001} len={0.04} h={0.012} y={0.007} z={0.028} color="#FFFDF5" roughness={0.8} />
      <Slab r={0.052} len={0.026} h={0.03} y={0.018} z={0.03} color={skinColor} roughness={0.75} />
      <Toes y={0.027} z={0.088} color={skinColor} />
      {[-1, 1].map((s) => (
        <Strut
          key={s}
          from={[0, 0.034, 0.072]}
          to={[s * 0.05, 0.018, 0.016]}
          r={0.005}
          color="#17B8B0"
        />
      ))}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.036, 0.072]}>
        <sphereGeometry args={[0.009, 12, 10]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#8AE6DF" roughness={0.4} />
      </mesh>
    </>
  );
}

/**
 * Draws one shoe. Both feet render the same model - see the LOCAL SPACE note about symmetry.
 *
 * Memoised because none of this geometry animates: the feet are swung by their parent hip
 * pivots, so re-running the whole stack on every avatar state change would be pure waste.
 */
export const ShoeModel = memo(function ShoeModel({
  type,
  skinColor,
}: {
  type: ShoeType;
  skinColor: string;
}) {
  switch (type) {
    case 'sport':
      return <SportShoe />;
    case 'leather':
      return <LeatherShoe />;
    case 'heels':
      return <HeelShoe />;
    case 'boots':
      return <BootShoe />;
    case 'sandals':
      return <SandalShoe skinColor={skinColor} />;
    case 'flipflops':
      return <FlipFlopShoe skinColor={skinColor} />;
    default:
      return null;
  }
});
```

## src/components/Three/SkyDome.tsx

```tsx
import React, { useMemo, useRef } from 'react';
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { useFrame } from '@react-three/fiber';
import { useApp } from '../../context/AppContext';
import { WeatherType } from '../../types';
import { useLightningFlicker } from '../../hooks/useLightningFlicker';

/**
 * Lightning's white, and the two scratch colours the flash is mixed into.
 *
 * Module scope because the storm branch below runs every frame while a flash is up and used to
 * build three fresh THREE.Color objects each time it did. That is small, but it is small garbage
 * produced at 60Hz in the middle of a stutter report, and there is nothing here that has to be
 * new - the values are overwritten from `targets` before they are read.
 */
const FLASH_TOP = new THREE.Color('#f1f5f9');
const FLASH_BOTTOM = new THREE.Color('#ffffff');
const flashTopScratch = new THREE.Color();
const flashBottomScratch = new THREE.Color();

export function SkyDome() {
  const { weather } = useApp();

  const topColorRef = useRef(new THREE.Color('#bae6fd'));
  const bottomColorRef = useRef(new THREE.Color('#e0f2fe'));
  
  const material = useMemo(() => {
    return new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
      uniforms: {
        uTopColor: { value: topColorRef.current },
        uBottomColor: { value: bottomColorRef.current },
      },
      vertexShader: `
        varying vec3 vWorldPosition;
        void main() {
          vec4 worldPosition = modelMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
          vWorldPosition = worldPosition.xyz;
          gl_Position = projectionMatrix * modelViewMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
        }
      `,
      fragmentShader: `
        varying vec3 vWorldPosition;
        uniform vec3 uTopColor;
        uniform vec3 uBottomColor;
        void main() {
          float h = normalize(vWorldPosition).y;
          // The gradient has to span the SKY, not the first three degrees of it.
          //
          // This was smoothstep(0.0, 0.05, h). h is the sine of the elevation angle, so 0.05 is
          // 2.9 degrees: the entire horizon-to-zenith blend finished within three degrees of the
          // waterline and everything above it was one flat, unshaded colour. That is what the
          // 破圖 report is looking at - a hard-edged pale stripe pasted along the horizon under a
          // dead blue ceiling, with the seam between them landing in the same few pixels as the
          // sea's own horizon line.
          //
          // It is worst zoomed out, which is exactly where it was reported: the third-person
          // camera's lens is 35 / uiScale, so pulling back to uiScale 0.5 opens the FOV from
          // 35 to 70 degrees and roughly doubles how much sky is on screen - a band that was
          // half-off the top of the frame becomes a stripe across the middle of it.
          //
          // 0.42 puts the zenith colour at ~25 degrees of elevation, so the pale horizon haze now
          // occupies a believable slab of sky and arrives at the sea as a gradient rather than as
          // an edge. Both endpoint colours are untouched: this changes the SHAPE of the ramp, not
          // the palette, so every weather's identity survives.
          float factor = smoothstep(0.0, 0.42, h);
          gl_FragColor = vec4(mix(uBottomColor, uTopColor, factor), 1.0);
        }
      `,
      side: THREE.BackSide,
    });
  }, []);

  const targets = useMemo(() => {
    switch (weather) {
      case WeatherType.SUNNY:
        return {
          top: new THREE.Color('#4fc3f7'), // Gorgeous deep sky blue
          bottom: new THREE.Color('#e0f2fe'), // Very light pastel horizon
          sunPos: new THREE.Vector3(120, 140, -150),
          sunScale: 1.0,
          sunColor: new THREE.Color('#ffffff'),
          glow1: new THREE.Color('#fcd34d'),
          glow2: new THREE.Color('#fbbf24'),
          opacity: 1.0,
        };
      case WeatherType.RAINY:
        return {
          top: new THREE.Color('#5a6a80'), // Foggy grey-teal
          bottom: new THREE.Color('#94a3b8'), // Misty wet horizon
          sunPos: new THREE.Vector3(120, 100, -150),
          sunScale: 0.7,
          sunColor: new THREE.Color('#e2e8f0'),
          glow1: new THREE.Color('#94a3b8'),
          glow2: new THREE.Color('#64748b'),
          opacity: 0.12, // Sun dimmed substantially behind clouds
        };
      case WeatherType.STORM:
        return {
          top: new THREE.Color('#1e293b'), // Storm dark slate
          bottom: new THREE.Color('#334155'), // Deep heavy cloud color
          sunPos: new THREE.Vector3(120, 80, -150),
          sunScale: 0.5,
          sunColor: new THREE.Color('#cbd5e1'),
          glow1: new THREE.Color('#475569'),
          glow2: new THREE.Color('#1e293b'),
          opacity: 0.02, // Barely visible sun
        };
      case WeatherType.SNOW:
        return {
          top: new THREE.Color('#9fc3df'), // Overcast soft winter blue
          bottom: new THREE.Color('#f1f5f9'), // Frosted bright horizon
          sunPos: new THREE.Vector3(120, 120, -150),
          sunScale: 0.95,
          sunColor: new THREE.Color('#ffffff'),
          glow1: new THREE.Color('#e2e8f0'),
          glow2: new THREE.Color('#cbd5e1'),
          opacity: 0.45, // Diffused pale winter sun
        };
      case WeatherType.TWILIGHT:
        return {
          top: new THREE.Color('#4c1d95'), // Sunset deep royal purple
          bottom: new THREE.Color('#ea580c'), // Horizon orange glow
          sunPos: new THREE.Vector3(140, 18, -150), // Low sunset disk
          sunScale: 1.9, // Aesthetic sunset magnification
          sunColor: new THREE.Color('#f97316'), // Deep orange low sun
          glow1: new THREE.Color('#ea580c'), // Twilight crimson glow
          glow2: new THREE.Color('#9d174d'), // Dark pink halo
          opacity: 0.9,
        };
      case WeatherType.MIDNIGHT:
        return {
          top: new THREE.Color('#060d24'), // Near-black zenith, so stars read
          bottom: new THREE.Color('#1b2a52'), // Faint indigo horizon glow
          // The sun is put below the horizon and faded out entirely; the moon in
          // NightSky.tsx is the light source in the sky at night.
          sunPos: new THREE.Vector3(140, -80, -150),
          sunScale: 1.0,
          sunColor: new THREE.Color('#1e293b'),
          glow1: new THREE.Color('#1e293b'),
          glow2: new THREE.Color('#0f172a'),
          opacity: 0.0,
        };
      default:
        return {
          top: new THREE.Color('#bae6fd'),
          bottom: new THREE.Color('#e0f2fe'),
          sunPos: new THREE.Vector3(100, 150, -150),
          sunScale: 1.0,
          sunColor: new THREE.Color('#ffffff'),
          glow1: new THREE.Color('#fcd34d'),
          glow2: new THREE.Color('#fbbf24'),
          opacity: 1.0,
        };
    }
  }, [weather]);

  const sunRef = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);
  const sunGlobeRef = useRef<THREE.Mesh>(null);
  const glow1Ref = useRef<THREE.Mesh>(null);
  const glow2Ref = useRef<THREE.Mesh>(null);
  
  // Dynamic lightning state
  const updateLightning = useLightningFlicker();

  useFrame((state) => {
    const elapsed = state.clock.getElapsedTime();

    // Smoothly interpolate uniform colors (Lerp)
    let currentTop = targets.top;
    let currentBottom = targets.bottom;

    // Handle random lightning flashes during STORM (high frequency double-flicker feel)
    const flashVal = updateLightning(elapsed, weather === WeatherType.STORM, 0.8, 0.2);
    if (flashVal > 0) {
      currentTop = flashTopScratch.copy(targets.top).lerp(FLASH_TOP, flashVal * 0.7);
      currentBottom = flashBottomScratch.copy(targets.bottom).lerp(FLASH_BOTTOM, flashVal * 0.95);
    }

    material.uniforms.uTopColor.value.lerp(currentTop, 0.03);
    material.uniforms.uBottomColor.value.lerp(currentBottom, 0.03);

    // Update Sun positioning & appearance
    if (sunRef.current) {
      sunRef.current.position.lerp(targets.sunPos, 0.03);
    }
    
    if (sunGlobeRef.current) {
      const gMat = sunGlobeRef.current.material as THREE.MeshBasicMaterial;
      gMat.color.lerp(targets.sunColor, 0.03);
      gMat.opacity = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(gMat.opacity, targets.opacity, 0.03);
      gMat.transparent = true;
      
      const targetScale = targets.sunScale * (1 + Math.sin(elapsed * 2) * 0.03); // Breathing sun
      sunGlobeRef.current.scale.setScalar(targetScale);
    }

    if (glow1Ref.current) {
      const gMat1 = glow1Ref.current.material as THREE.MeshBasicMaterial;
      gMat1.color.lerp(targets.glow1, 0.03);
      gMat1.opacity = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(gMat1.opacity, targets.opacity * 0.4, 0.03);
      gMat1.transparent = true;
      glow1Ref.current.scale.setScalar(targets.sunScale * 1.5 + Math.sin(elapsed * 3) * 0.05);
    }

    if (glow2Ref.current) {
      const gMat2 = glow2Ref.current.material as THREE.MeshBasicMaterial;
      gMat2.color.lerp(targets.glow2, 0.03);
      gMat2.opacity = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(gMat2.opacity, targets.opacity * 0.15, 0.03);
      gMat2.transparent = true;
      glow2Ref.current.scale.setScalar(targets.sunScale * 2.5 + Math.cos(elapsed * 2.5) * 0.08);
    }
  });

  return (
    <group>
      {/* Sky Sphere.
          32x32 is enough, and that is a MEASURED answer rather than an assumption. The gradient
          is evaluated per fragment from `normalize(vWorldPosition)`, and a world position
          interpolates along the chord rather than along the sphere, so in principle the ramp
          creases along every triangle edge. In practice it does not show: rendering the same
          gradient at 32x32 and at 64x40, aimed straight down the band where the ramp actually
          varies, came out pixel-identical to within a rounding step (max channel-sum delta 2 of
          765) with the same peak second derivative down the centre column. There is no faceting
          here to fix, so there is no reason to pay for the vertices. */}
      <mesh>
        <sphereGeometry args={[500, 32, 32]} />
        <primitive object={material} attach="material" />
      </mesh>
      
      {/* Sun Group */}
      <group ref={sunRef} position={[100, 150, -150]}>
        {/* Core Sun */}
        <mesh ref={sunGlobeRef}>
          <sphereGeometry args={[15, 32, 32]} />
          <meshBasicMaterial color="#ffffff" transparent />
        </mesh>
        {/* Glow Halo 1 */}
        <mesh ref={glow1Ref}>
          <sphereGeometry args={[15, 32, 32]} />
          <meshBasicMaterial color="#fcd34d" transparent opacity={0.4} />
        </mesh>
        {/* Glow Halo 2 */}
        <mesh ref={glow2Ref}>
          <sphereGeometry args={[15, 32, 32]} />
          <meshBasicMaterial color="#fbbf24" transparent opacity={0.15} />
        </mesh>
      </group>
    </group>
  );
}
```

## src/components/Three/StickFigure.tsx

```tsx
import React, { useRef } from 'react';
import { useFrame } from '@react-three/fiber';
import * as THREE from 'three';

interface StickFigureProps {
  type: 'jumping-jacks' | 'squats' | 'idle';
  scale?: number;
}

export function StickFigure({ type, scale = 1 }: StickFigureProps) {
  const groupRef = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);
  const leftArmRef = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);
  const rightArmRef = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);
  const leftLegRef = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);
  const rightLegRef = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);

  useFrame((state) => {
    const time = state.clock.getElapsedTime();
    
    if (type === 'jumping-jacks') {
      const cycle = Math.sin(time * 4);
      const angle = (cycle + 1) * (Math.PI / 2.5); // 0 to ~72 degrees
      
      if (leftArmRef.current) leftArmRef.current.rotation.z = angle;
      if (rightArmRef.current) rightArmRef.current.rotation.z = -angle;
      
      const legAngle = (cycle + 1) * (Math.PI / 8);
      if (leftLegRef.current) leftLegRef.current.rotation.z = legAngle;
      if (rightLegRef.current) rightLegRef.current.rotation.z = -legAngle;
      
      if (groupRef.current) {
        groupRef.current.position.y = Math.abs(cycle) * 0.2;
      }
    } else if (type === 'squats') {
      const cycle = Math.sin(time * 2);
      const squatDepth = (cycle + 1) * 0.3; // 0 to 0.6
      
      if (groupRef.current) {
        groupRef.current.position.y = -squatDepth;
      }
      
      if (leftArmRef.current) leftArmRef.current.rotation.x = -Math.PI / 2;
      if (rightArmRef.current) rightArmRef.current.rotation.x = -Math.PI / 2;
    }
  });

  const boneColor = "#ffffff";
  const jointColor = "#e2e8f0";

  return (
    <group ref={groupRef} scale={scale}>
      {/* Head */}
      <mesh position={[0, 1.6, 0]}>
        <sphereGeometry args={[0.2, 16, 16]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color={boneColor} />
      </mesh>

      {/* Torso */}
      <mesh position={[0, 1.1, 0]}>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.05, 0.6, 4, 8]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color={boneColor} />
      </mesh>

      {/* Shoulders */}
      <mesh position={[0, 1.4, 0]} rotation={[0, 0, Math.PI / 2]}>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.04, 0.4, 4, 8]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color={boneColor} />
      </mesh>

      {/* Left Arm */}
      <group ref={leftArmRef} position={[-0.2, 1.4, 0]}>
        <group position={[-0.2, 0, 0]} rotation={[0, 0, Math.PI / 2]}>
          <mesh castShadow>
            <capsuleGeometry args={[0.04, 0.3, 4, 8]} />
            <meshStandardMaterial color={boneColor} />
          </mesh>
        </group>
      </group>

      {/* Right Arm */}
      <group ref={rightArmRef} position={[0.2, 1.4, 0]}>
        <group position={[0.2, 0, 0]} rotation={[0, 0, -Math.PI / 2]}>
          <mesh castShadow>
            <capsuleGeometry args={[0.04, 0.3, 4, 8]} />
            <meshStandardMaterial color={boneColor} />
          </mesh>
        </group>
      </group>

      {/* Hips */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.8, 0]} rotation={[0, 0, Math.PI / 2]}>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.04, 0.2, 4, 8]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color={boneColor} />
      </mesh>

      {/* Left Leg */}
      <group ref={leftLegRef} position={[-0.1, 0.8, 0]}>
        <group position={[0, -0.3, 0]}>
          <mesh castShadow>
            <capsuleGeometry args={[0.05, 0.5, 4, 8]} />
            <meshStandardMaterial color={boneColor} />
          </mesh>
        </group>
      </group>

      {/* Right Leg */}
      <group ref={rightLegRef} position={[0.1, 0.8, 0]}>
        <group position={[0, -0.3, 0]}>
          <mesh castShadow>
            <capsuleGeometry args={[0.05, 0.5, 4, 8]} />
            <meshStandardMaterial color={boneColor} />
          </mesh>
        </group>
      </group>
    </group>
  );
}
```

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { useMemo } from 'react';
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { DECAL_DEPTH_BIAS } from '../../constants/terrain';

/**
 * 更衣室 — the tiled stage the character stands on.
 *
 * The floor used to be one white disc, which read as an empty void the avatar happened to be
 * floating over: nothing gave the eye a sense of scale, and the feet had no surface to sit on.
 * It is a laid tile floor now — a grid of two warm creams with grout, a border course and an
 * inlaid ring — which is what turns the space into a room the character is standing in.
 *
 * Everything is drawn on ONE canvas texture rather than assembled from meshes. A tile floor made
 * of geometry is ~100 draw calls for something that never moves and is seen from one fixed angle,
 * and stacking 100 coplanar quads on a disc is exactly the z-fighting the DECAL_DEPTH_BIAS note
 * below exists to avoid.
 *
 * Palette is the app's own (index.css): island-cream / island-cream-2 / island-sand for the
 * tiles, island-line for grout, island-teal for the inlay. Nothing new is invented here, so the
 * 3D stage and the 2D panel beside it stay the same room.
 */

export const STAGE_RADIUS = 1.5;

/**
 * Deliberately further apart than the palette's own neighbouring creams.
 *
 * This stage is lit by three 70-intensity point lights and a 400 spotlight — the studio bulbs the
 * character is meant to be shown off under. Any pattern painted in adjacent creams is blown flat
 * white by that lighting: the first cut of this floor used the tokens verbatim and read as the
 * plain white disc it was replacing. The values below are what survives the exposure.
 */
const CREAM = '#FBF8F2';
const CREAM_2 = '#E2D8C2';
const SAND = '#D8CCB2';
const GROUT = '#BFB7A2';
const TEAL = '#2A9D8F';

/** Tiles across the full width of the stage. 9 keeps each tile a hand-span at avatar scale. */
const TILES = 9;

/**
 * The floor's whole appearance, drawn once.
 *
 * `circleGeometry` maps its UVs so the disc fills the [0,1] square with the centre at (0.5, 0.5),
 * so canvas space IS floor space: the disc's rim is the inscribed circle, and anything drawn in
 * the canvas corners is clipped away by the geometry and never seen.
 */
function tileTexture(): THREE.CanvasTexture {
  const S = 1024;
  const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
  canvas.width = S;
  canvas.height = S;
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d')!;
  const c = S / 2;
  const step = S / TILES;

  ctx.fillStyle = CREAM;
  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, S, S);

  // The field: a two-tone check. The darker square is island-sand rather than a grey, so the
  // contrast stays warm — a neutral grey check made the whole stage look dirty.
  for (let row = 0; row < TILES; row++) {
    for (let col = 0; col < TILES; col++) {
      ctx.fillStyle = (row + col) % 2 === 0 ? CREAM : CREAM_2;
      ctx.fillRect(col * step, row * step, step, step);
    }
  }

  // Grout. Drawn as lines over the tiles rather than as gaps between them, so the tiles stay on
  // an exact grid and the accents below can be placed straight onto the intersections.
  ctx.strokeStyle = GROUT;
  ctx.lineWidth = 6;
  for (let i = 0; i <= TILES; i++) {
    const p = i * step;
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.moveTo(p, 0);
    ctx.lineTo(p, S);
    ctx.moveTo(0, p);
    ctx.lineTo(S, p);
    ctx.stroke();
  }

  // A small teal lozenge on each interior intersection — the tile-spacer detail that reads as a
  // laid floor rather than a printed grid. Kept tiny: at four times this size they tile the eye
  // and start competing with the character.
  for (let row = 1; row < TILES; row++) {
    for (let col = 1; col < TILES; col++) {
      const x = col * step;
      const y = row * step;
      if (Math.hypot(x - c, y - c) > c * 0.9) continue;
      ctx.save();
      ctx.translate(x, y);
      ctx.rotate(Math.PI / 4);
      ctx.fillStyle = TEAL;
      ctx.globalAlpha = 0.8;
      ctx.fillRect(-8, -8, 16, 16);
      ctx.restore();
    }
  }

  // A border course just inside the rim, laid over the check: real floors change pattern at the
  // edge, and it is what stops the grid from simply being sliced off by the disc.
  ctx.globalAlpha = 1;
  ctx.strokeStyle = SAND;
  ctx.lineWidth = c * 0.1;
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.arc(c, c, c * 0.945, 0, Math.PI * 2);
  ctx.stroke();

  // Two inlaid rings bounding that course.
  ctx.strokeStyle = TEAL;
  ctx.globalAlpha = 0.85;
  ctx.lineWidth = 5;
  for (const r of [0.995, 0.895]) {
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.arc(c, c, c * r, 0, Math.PI * 2);
    ctx.stroke();
  }

  // Vignette: the stage is lit from above its centre, so the tiles have to fall off towards the
  // rim or the lighting of the floor and the lighting of the character disagree.
  ctx.globalAlpha = 1;
  // No white lift in the middle: the studio bulbs already over-expose the centre, and adding to
  // it there was what bleached the tiles out of existence in the first cut.
  const vignette = ctx.createRadialGradient(c, c, c * 0.3, c, c, c);
  vignette.addColorStop(0, 'rgba(38,70,83,0)');
  vignette.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(38,70,83,0.16)');
  ctx.fillStyle = vignette;
  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, S, S);

  const tex = new THREE.CanvasTexture(canvas);
  tex.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;
  tex.anisotropy = 8;
  return tex;
}

/* ============================================================================================
   THE CYCLORAMA — the wall the character is photographed against.
   ============================================================================================
   WHY IT EXISTS. 更衣室 used to be a transparent canvas over a white-to-cream HTML gradient, so
   every ornament was shown against a near-white field. That is fine for a navy jacket and quietly
   ruinous for a whole class of goods: 泡泡髮飾 is transparent glass, 星星髮飾 is pale cream,
   結霜光環 is white ice, 精靈光環 is a thin bright ring. On white they do not read as "subtle",
   they read as absent, and a player who cannot see what they bought asks for their money back.

   It is fixed HERE, once, for every item — present and future — rather than by giving the
   offending ornaments a darker colour or the preview panel a per-item background. A photographer
   with this problem does not repaint the subject; they hang a backdrop. So the stage gets one: a
   graded cyclorama that separates BOTH ends of the value range, light goods against the deeper
   top and dark goods against the brighter floor, and is a single unlit surface either way.

   Three properties it has to have, and why:

   · A SPHERE, drawn from the inside. The preview is a turntable — the player drags the character
     round 360 degrees — so a flat plane behind them would swing out of frame the moment they
     turned it. There is no direction here that is "behind".
   · UNLIT (`meshBasicMaterial`). The stage is lit by three 70-intensity point lights and a 400
     spotlight, which is exactly the exposure that already flattened the tile floor into white
     (see CREAM/CREAM_2 above). A lit backdrop would be blown out by the same lights it exists to
     protect the subject from.
   · GRADED, deepest at the top. The character's head — where the ornaments in question live —
     sits a little below the middle of the frame, and the floor is bright, so the gradient puts
     its strongest value change exactly where the hair ornaments are and leaves the stage reading
     as a lit floor rather than as a dim room.
   ============================================================================================ */

/** Inside radius of the cyclorama. Well past the stage and well inside the camera's far plane. */
const BACKDROP_RADIUS = 14;

/**
 * The gradient, top to bottom.
 *
 * On the app's own family (index.css): a cool grey-teal at the top, island-sand through the
 * middle, and cream where it meets the floor. Nothing new is invented, and nothing here is
 * saturated — a coloured backdrop would tint every item shown against it, which is the opposite
 * of what a preview is for.
 *
 * THE RAMP IS COMPRESSED INTO THE MIDDLE ON PURPOSE, and the flat plateaus at either end are not
 * padding. A sphere's v runs pole to pole, but the camera here is nearly level with a 35-degree
 * field, so it only ever sees a band about a fifth of the way either side of the equator. Stops
 * spread evenly from 0 to 1 put the whole interesting part of the gradient somewhere the player
 * never looks, and the first cut of this backdrop was measurably flat on screen for exactly that
 * reason. The ramp sits where the frame is; the plateaus cover the turntable's pitch range.
 */
const BACKDROP_STOPS: ReadonlyArray<readonly [number, string]> = [
  [0, '#9BADAB'],
  [0.3, '#9BADAB'],
  [0.5, '#C6C2B4'],
  [0.7, '#EFEADF'],
  [1, '#EFEADF'],
];

function backdropTexture(): THREE.CanvasTexture {
  const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
  // One pixel wide: the gradient only varies with height, and a 1x512 strip stretched round the
  // sphere costs nothing and cannot band the way a small square would.
  canvas.width = 1;
  canvas.height = 512;
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d')!;
  const grad = ctx.createLinearGradient(0, 0, 0, canvas.height);
  // Row 0 is the top of the image, and three maps that to v = 1, i.e. the sphere's north pole.
  BACKDROP_STOPS.forEach(([at, colour]) => grad.addColorStop(at, colour));
  ctx.fillStyle = grad;
  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);

  const tex = new THREE.CanvasTexture(canvas);
  tex.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;
  return tex;
}

/**
 * The graded wall the stage stands in. Mount as a sibling of the character, NOT inside the stage
 * group — it is the room, not something standing on the floor.
 */
export function StudioBackdrop() {
  const gradient = useMemo(backdropTexture, []);

  return (
    <mesh renderOrder={-1}>
      <sphereGeometry args={[BACKDROP_RADIUS, 32, 24]} />
      {/* `depthWrite={false}` so nothing is ever ordered against a surface fourteen metres away;
          `renderOrder={-1}` keeps it first in the queue, which is what makes that safe. */}
      <meshBasicMaterial map={gradient} side={THREE.BackSide} depthWrite={false} toneMapped={false} />
    </mesh>
  );
}

/**
 * The stage disc, its tiles, and the rim rings that sit on top of it.
 *
 * Caller places this at the stage's height — the floor is drawn at its own y = 0.
 */
export function StudioFloor() {
  // Built on first mount and kept: the drawing above is deterministic, and re-running it on
  // every render would rebuild a 1024² canvas for a floor that never changes.
  const tiles = useMemo(tileTexture, []);

  return (
    <group>
      <mesh rotation-x={-Math.PI / 2} receiveShadow>
        <circleGeometry args={[STAGE_RADIUS, 64]} />
        {/* Rougher than the old mirror-glossy disc: tile has a soft sheen, and at 0.1 the
            highlight washed the pattern straight back out to white. `color` multiplies the map,
            so this also pulls the whole floor down out of the blown-out top of the range. */}
        <meshStandardMaterial map={tiles} color="#E9E4D8" roughness={0.65} metalness={0} />
      </mesh>

      {/* Outer glowing ring for feet-visibility contrast — island-teal. This and the rim shadow
          lie ON the disc, so they take the shared decal bias rather than relying on a 5mm lift
          the depth buffer cannot resolve reliably. */}
      <mesh rotation-x={-Math.PI / 2} position={[0, 0.005, 0]}>
        <ringGeometry args={[STAGE_RADIUS - 0.05, STAGE_RADIUS, 64]} />
        <meshBasicMaterial color={TEAL} transparent opacity={0.4} {...DECAL_DEPTH_BIAS} />
      </mesh>

      {/* Subtle rim shadow */}
      <mesh rotation-x={-Math.PI / 2} position={[0, 0.01, 0]}>
        <ringGeometry args={[1.15, 1.2, 64]} />
        <meshBasicMaterial color="#000000" transparent opacity={0.02} {...DECAL_DEPTH_BIAS} polygonOffsetUnits={-6} />
      </mesh>
    </group>
  );
}
```

## src/components/Three/Torch.tsx

```tsx
import React, { useRef, useMemo } from 'react';
import { useFrame } from '@react-three/fiber';
import * as THREE from 'three';
import {
  OUT_CHARRED, OUT_DRY, OUT_METAL, OUT_STONE_DARK, OUT_WOOD_DARK,
} from '../../constants/outdoorPalette';
import type { LightingSpec } from '../../constants/lighting';
import { FixtureLight } from './FixtureLight';

/**
 * 火把 —— 一根有箍環與繩結的木柄，頂上是燒黑的燃料杯。
 *
 * 兩件商品共用這一個模型（constants/furnitureModels.ts 的 SHARED_FURNITURE_MODELS）：
 * 室外的 火把 放大 1.8 倍，室內的 部落火把 放大 1.2 倍。所以這裡的每一個細節都必須對
 * 「插在草地上」和「立在房間裡」兩種情境都成立 —— 這就是底部做成一個外擴的腳座、而不是
 * 一根插進土裡的尖樁的原因：尖樁在戶外對，在室內就是一根戳進地板的釘子。
 *
 * 改版前這裡只有兩個 mesh：一根圓柱、一個黑色套環。
 */
export function Torch({ item }: { item?: { lighting?: LightingSpec } | null } = {}) {
  return (
    <group>
      {/* 腳座。室內立得住、室外看起來像壓進土裡的那一圈。 */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.035, 0]} castShadow receiveShadow>
        <cylinderGeometry args={[0.075, 0.09, 0.07, 8]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color={OUT_STONE_DARK} roughness={0.95} />
      </mesh>

      {/* 木柄，上細下粗。

          柄的下端必須埋進腳座裡。改版前它從 y=0.16 起算，而腳座的頂面在 0.07 —— 中間有 0.09
          個局部單位的空氣。火把在島上的縮放是 0.85 × 1.55（BUILDING）× 1.8（TorchModel）=
          2.37，所以那個縫在畫面上是 213mm：一根浮在石座上方的棍子，兩者之間看得到草。

          現在柄從 y=0.02 起算，穿過整個腳座。錐度維持原本每單位 0.0203 的收縮率，所以兩道綁繩
          的半徑不用跟著改。 */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.41, 0]} castShadow>
        <cylinderGeometry args={[0.045, 0.061, 0.78, 8]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color={OUT_WOOD_DARK} roughness={0.9} />
      </mesh>

      {/* 兩道綁繩。木柄上唯一的第三層細節，也是「手作」讀感的來源 —— 一根光溜溜的棍子
          看起來是量產的，綁了兩圈繩子的棍子看起來是有人做出來的。
          半徑是照著木柄在那個高度的實際粗細算的：柄從 y=0.16 的 0.058 收到 y=0.80 的 0.045。 */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.30, 0]} rotation={[Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} castShadow>
        <torusGeometry args={[0.053, 0.013, 5, 8]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color={OUT_DRY} roughness={1} />
      </mesh>
      <mesh position={[0, 0.66, 0]} rotation={[Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} castShadow>
        <torusGeometry args={[0.047, 0.012, 5, 8]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color={OUT_DRY} roughness={1} />
      </mesh>

      {/* 燃料杯與它的金屬箍。 */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.855, 0]} castShadow>
        <cylinderGeometry args={[0.078, 0.05, 0.15, 8]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#262626" metalness={0.7} roughness={0.35} />
      </mesh>
      <mesh position={[0, 0.912, 0]} rotation={[Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} castShadow>
        <torusGeometry args={[0.076, 0.013, 5, 10]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color={OUT_METAL} metalness={0.55} roughness={0.4} />
      </mesh>

      {/* 杯子裡燒到一半的木柴。火焰是粒子，粒子沒有形狀；有三根實體的柴，火才有東西可燒。 */}
      {[0, 1, 2].map((i) => {
        const a = (i / 3) * Math.PI * 2 + 0.5;
        return (
          <mesh
            key={i}
            position={[Math.cos(a) * 0.028, 0.955, Math.sin(a) * 0.028]}
            rotation={[Math.sin(a) * 0.3, 0, -Math.cos(a) * 0.3]}
            castShadow
          >
            <cylinderGeometry args={[0.016, 0.022, 0.14, 5]} />
            <meshStandardMaterial color={OUT_CHARRED} roughness={1} />
          </mesh>
        );
      })}

      {/* 火。實體火心（白天讀得出來的那一朵）＋ 粒子（夜裡的火光與火星）。 */}
      <FlameCore position={[0, 0.985, 0]} height={0.36} radius={0.095} />
      <FlameParticles position={[0, 0.99, 0]} />

      {/* 火光。透過共用的 FixtureLight 掛出去（Three/FixtureLight.tsx），所以強度、範圍與顏色
          跟其他每一件會發光的家具一樣，寫在商品資料裡（constants/lighting.ts）。

          它的 behaviour 是 `always`：火把燒的是自己的燃料，牆上那個開關沒有一條線接到它，
          關了燈之後還亮著的正是這種光 —— 一個只點著火把的房間是玩家蓋得出來的東西。

          不投影：一盞會投影的點光源等於每幀從六個方向重畫整個場景，而火把是玩家最容易在同一
          個房間裡放上好幾支的東西，在弱一點的 GPU 上這曾經是全遊戲最貴的一件可放置物品。 */}
      <FixtureLight item={item} position={[0, 1.3, 0]} />
    </group>
  );
}

// Reused across all particles/frames instead of `new THREE.Color()` inside the per-frame
// loop below - with many torches placed at once (a common decorating choice), that used to
// allocate up to 60 Color objects per torch, every frame, purely for GC to immediately collect.
const FLAME_CORE_COLOR = new THREE.Color('#ffffcc');
const FLAME_INNER_COLOR = new THREE.Color('#ffcc00');
const FLAME_OUTER_COLOR = new THREE.Color('#ff4500');

/**
 * 火焰的實體核心 —— 兩個錐體，外橘內黃，會呼吸但不會消失。
 *
 * 為什麼火需要一個**不透明**的形狀：原本火把與營火的火焰只有加色混合（additive）的粒子。
 * 加色混合是把自己的顏色**加到背後的畫面上**，所以在夜裡的深色天空前它是一團橘光，在白天
 * 的亮草地前它加到已經很亮的底色上就直接飽和成白色 —— 商店縮圖畫的是一朵橘紅色的火，玩家
 * 白天放下去看到的是一團白色的棉花。這正是「縮圖跟實際物品不一致」最嚴重的一種：不是細節
 * 少了，是東西認不出來了。
 *
 * 解法不是把粒子調暗（那樣夜裡就沒有火光了），而是給火一個**畫得出輪廓的身體**：兩個低面數
 * 的錐體，白天讀成一朵橘黃色的火，晚上被粒子與燈光包起來仍然是火心。粒子留著，但可以少幾顆
 * —— 加起來 mesh 數是往下的。
 *
 * 兩個錐體，不是四個：low poly 的火本來就該是一個尖形色塊，多加的層只會讓輪廓變模糊。
 */
export function FlameCore({
  position, height = 0.30, radius = 0.085, speed = 6.2, phase = 0,
}: {
  position: [number, number, number];
  height?: number;
  radius?: number;
  speed?: number;
  phase?: number;
}) {
  const outer = useRef<THREE.Mesh>(null);
  const inner = useRef<THREE.Mesh>(null);

  useFrame((state) => {
    const t = state.clock.getElapsedTime() * speed + phase;
    // 一團火的擺動是「抽高又落下」，不是整體放大：y 拉伸與 xz 收縮反向，火才會舔。
    const stretch = 1 + Math.sin(t) * 0.16 + Math.sin(t * 2.3) * 0.07;
    if (outer.current) {
      outer.current.scale.set(1 / Math.sqrt(stretch), stretch, 1 / Math.sqrt(stretch));
      outer.current.rotation.y = Math.sin(t * 0.6) * 0.25;
    }
    if (inner.current) {
      const s = 1 + Math.sin(t * 1.4 + 1.1) * 0.13;
      inner.current.scale.set(1 / Math.sqrt(s), s, 1 / Math.sqrt(s));
    }
  });

  return (
    <group position={position}>
      <mesh ref={outer} position={[0, height / 2, 0]}>
        <coneGeometry args={[radius, height, 6]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#ff7a18" emissive="#ff5a05" emissiveIntensity={0.85} roughness={0.6} />
      </mesh>
      <mesh ref={inner} position={[0, height * 0.34, 0]}>
        <coneGeometry args={[radius * 0.55, height * 0.62, 6]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#ffd24a" emissive="#ffc020" emissiveIntensity={1.1} roughness={0.5} />
      </mesh>
    </group>
  );
}

function FlameParticles({ position }: { position: [number, number, number] }) {
  // Was 60 individual meshes (each its own draw call) - cut to a quarter since the additive
  // blending already makes individual particles blend into one continuous flame shape at
  // normal viewing distance, and this is the item players place the most of per room.
  // Cut again to 10 once `FlameCore` above took over the job of BEING the flame: the particles
  // are now the halo around a shape that is already there, so fewer of them costs nothing to
  // read and pays for the two solid cones twice over.
  const count = 10;
  const mesh = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);
  
  const particles = useMemo(() => {
    const temp = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        temp.push({
            t: Math.random() * 10,
            factor: 20 + Math.random() * 100,
            speed: 0.01 + Math.random() / 50,
            xFactor: -5 + Math.random() * 10,
            yFactor: -5 + Math.random() * 10,
            zFactor: -5 + Math.random() * 10,
            mx: 0,
            my: 0,
        });
    }
    return temp;
  }, [count]);

  const pointRefs = useRef<THREE.Mesh[]>([]);

  useFrame((state) => {
    const time = state.clock.getElapsedTime();
    pointRefs.current.forEach((ref, i) => {
        if (!ref) return;
        const p = particles[i];
        p.t += p.speed;
        
        // Loop position
        const life = (time * 0.5 + i / count) % 1;
        
        // Scale and shape logic for "water droplet"
        // At the bottom (life = 0), it's bulbous. At the top (life = 1), it's pointy.
        const t = life;
        // Droplet shape approximation: wide at bottom, sharp at top
        const spreadFactor = (1 - t) * Math.sqrt(t + 0.01) * 0.4;
        
        // 0.34, not 0.8: the particles used to climb more than twice the height of the flame they
        // belong to, so the torch wore a tall column of pale dots with the fire down at its foot.
        // They are the flicker around `FlameCore` now, so they live inside its envelope.
        const y = t * 0.34;
        const x = Math.cos(p.xFactor + t * 2) * spreadFactor;
        const z = Math.sin(p.zFactor + t * 2) * spreadFactor;

        ref.position.set(x, y, z);
        // Smaller than they were (0.12 + 0.02): the solid `FlameCore` is the flame now, and an
        // additive halo wider than the shape it surrounds is exactly what turned this into a
        // white puff against a bright sky.
        ref.scale.setScalar((1 - t) * 0.075 + 0.012);
        
        // Color transition - copy from a shared preset instead of allocating a new Color
        if (ref.material instanceof THREE.MeshStandardMaterial) {
            const preset = t < 0.2 ? FLAME_CORE_COLOR : t < 0.5 ? FLAME_INNER_COLOR : FLAME_OUTER_COLOR;
            ref.material.color.copy(preset);
            ref.material.emissive.copy(preset);
            ref.material.opacity = (1 - t) * 0.55;
        }
    });
  });

  return (
    <group position={position} ref={mesh}>
      {Array.from({ length: count }).map((_, i) => (
        <mesh key={i} ref={(el) => { if (el) pointRefs.current[i] = el; }}>
          <sphereGeometry args={[1, 8, 8]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial 
            transparent 
            blending={THREE.AdditiveBlending} 
            depthWrite={false} 
            emissiveIntensity={2}
          />
        </mesh>
      ))}
    </group>
  );
}
```

```tsx
/**
```
