```tsx
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import React, { useRef, useMemo, useSyncExternalStore } from 'react';
import { useFrame } from '@react-three/fiber';
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { useApp } from '../../context/AppContext';
import { WeatherType } from '../../types';
import { WATER_SURFACE_Y } from '../../constants/world';
import { usePlayerHome } from '../../hooks/usePlayerHome';
import { getHouseRoofSplashHeight } from './HouseModel';
import { getTerrainInfo, isLandTerrain } from '../../constants/terrain';
import {
  getFootprint, getFootprintVersion, makeObb, obbContainsPoint, subscribeFootprints,
  type Obb2,
} from '../../lib/furniturePlacement';
import type { ResolvedHome } from '../../hooks/usePlayerHome';

/**
 * The round dot every weather particle is drawn with.
 *
 * A bare `<pointsMaterial>` with no `map` rasterises each point as a hard-edged SQUARE, and that
 * is the second half of the 破圖 report: on a clear day this system is 300 pollen motes at 0.15
 * opacity, which showed up as a scatter of pale squares sitting on the sky, plus - whenever one
 * drifted within a metre of the lens, since `sizeAttenuation` scales points by distance - a single
 * flat square the size of a HUD icon parked in mid-air. Neither reads as weather; they read as
 * broken pixels, which is exactly how they were reported.
 *
 * Drawn once into a canvas rather than loaded, so it costs no network request and cannot 404 the
 * way the CDN sound clips did. The material keeps tinting it per weather (`color` is multiplied
 * with the map), so rain stays blue and pollen stays amber - this only decides the SHAPE.
 */
function createParticleSprite(): THREE.CanvasTexture {
  const size = 64;
  const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
  canvas.width = size;
  canvas.height = size;
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d')!;
  const gradient = ctx.createRadialGradient(size / 2, size / 2, 0, size / 2, size / 2, size / 2);
  // Solid core, then a soft shoulder - a hard-edged circle would just trade square aliasing for
  // round aliasing on the near-camera motes, which are the ones that got noticed.
  gradient.addColorStop(0, 'rgba(255,255,255,1)');
  gradient.addColorStop(0.35, 'rgba(255,255,255,0.92)');
  gradient.addColorStop(0.72, 'rgba(255,255,255,0.28)');
  gradient.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(255,255,255,0)');
  ctx.fillStyle = gradient;
  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, size, size);
  const texture = new THREE.CanvasTexture(canvas);
  texture.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;
  return texture;
}

/**
 * One placed decoration, reduced to the only two things a raindrop needs to know about it.
 *
 * Built once per island change rather than once per drop per frame - see {@link Weather}'s
 * `obstacles` memo, and the note on {@link splashHeightAt}.
 */
interface SplashObstacle {
  box: Obb2;
  topY: number;
}

/**
 * How high a drop landing at (px, pz) stops.
 *
 * Module scope, and taking its obstacles pre-built, because this is the hottest function in the
 * scene: in 暴風雨 it is called 3500 times a FRAME. It used to be a closure declared inside
 * useFrame that re-derived the world for every one of those calls - `getFootprint` plus a fresh
 * `makeObb` for every placement, every drop. On an island with fifteen decorations that was
 * 52,500 throwaway objects per frame, which is not a rendering cost at all: it is a garbage
 * collector being fed ~3 million short-lived allocations a second, and the pauses it takes to
 * clear them are exactly the 卡頓 being reported. The boxes do not move between frames, so they
 * are now built once and merely read here.
 */
function splashHeightAt(
  px: number,
  pz: number,
  islandScale: number,
  home: ResolvedHome | null,
  obstacles: readonly SplashObstacle[],
): number {
  // 1. Terrain base height. Read from the shared terrain contract rather than from a local
  //    copy of the island's radii, so a drop cannot land at a height the ground isn't at.
  const info = getTerrainInfo(px, pz, islandScale);
  // Shallow and open water both land on the surface itself - rain/snow splashes on the water,
  // it doesn't sink to the seabed depth getTerrainInfo reports for a swimming body.
  let height = isLandTerrain(info.terrain) ? info.targetY : WATER_SURFACE_Y;

  // 2. Splash on the player's Home roof. Tested as a rotated box rather than a circle so
  //    rain doesn't visibly stop short of the corners of a wide house.
  if (home) {
    const rx = px - home.position[0];
    const rz = pz - home.position[2];
    const cos = Math.cos(-home.rotation);
    const sin = Math.sin(-home.rotation);
    const localX = Math.abs(rx * cos - rz * sin);
    const localZ = Math.abs(rx * sin + rz * cos);

    if (localX < home.footprint.halfWidth && localZ < home.footprint.halfDepth) {
      height = Math.max(height, getHouseRoofSplashHeight(home.style));
    }
  }

  // 3. Splash on placed decorations, against the measured box of whatever is actually drawn.
  //    The footprint the placement rules use answers both "how wide" and "how tall" at once,
  //    correctly under rotation, and needs no entry when a decoration is added.
  for (let i = 0; i < obstacles.length; i++) {
    const o = obstacles[i];
    if (o.topY > height && obbContainsPoint(o.box, px, pz)) height = o.topY;
  }

  return height;
}

/** Cell size of {@link SplashHeightCache}, in world units. */
const SPLASH_CELL = 0.2;
/** The box drops can be in: the ±30 spawn box, widened for the storm's +12 spawn offset and drift. */
const SPLASH_MIN_X = -44;
const SPLASH_MAX_X = 48;
const SPLASH_MIN_Z = -32;
const SPLASH_MAX_Z = 32;

/**
 * {@link splashHeightAt}, answered once per 20 cm cell instead of once per drop per frame.
 *
 * In 暴風雨 the particle loop asks 3500 times a frame, and every ask walks the terrain rings, the
 * roof box and every placed decoration's OBB. Profiled on the island that loop was ~3 ms of main
 * thread EVERY frame on its own - the single largest JS cost in the scene, and on an Intel UHD
 * laptop enough by itself to push frames past the 16.7 ms deadline, which is what drops them to
 * 33 ms and reads as 卡頓. Nothing a drop lands on moves while it falls, so the answer for a spot
 * is the same every frame: it is filled lazily (NaN = not asked yet) so building the cache is
 * never a hitch of its own, and a new cache is made whenever the island's shape changes.
 *
 * Sampling at the cell centre shifts a splash by at most 10 cm - a drop that lands a hair outside
 * a roof edge may splash at roof height - which is invisible at rain-particle size.
 */
class SplashHeightCache {
  private readonly cols = Math.ceil((SPLASH_MAX_X - SPLASH_MIN_X) / SPLASH_CELL);
  private readonly rows = Math.ceil((SPLASH_MAX_Z - SPLASH_MIN_Z) / SPLASH_CELL);
  private readonly heights = new Float32Array(this.cols * this.rows).fill(NaN);

  constructor(
    private readonly islandScale: number,
    private readonly home: ResolvedHome | null,
    private readonly obstacles: readonly SplashObstacle[],
  ) {}

  at(x: number, z: number): number {
    const cx = Math.floor((x - SPLASH_MIN_X) / SPLASH_CELL);
    const cz = Math.floor((z - SPLASH_MIN_Z) / SPLASH_CELL);
    if (cx < 0 || cz < 0 || cx >= this.cols || cz >= this.rows) {
      return splashHeightAt(x, z, this.islandScale, this.home, this.obstacles);
    }
    const i = cz * this.cols + cx;
    let h = this.heights[i];
    if (h !== h) {
      h = splashHeightAt(
        SPLASH_MIN_X + (cx + 0.5) * SPLASH_CELL,
        SPLASH_MIN_Z + (cz + 0.5) * SPLASH_CELL,
        this.islandScale, this.home, this.obstacles,
      );
      this.heights[i] = h;
    }
    return h;
  }
}

export function Weather() {
  const { weather, profile } = useApp();
  const maxParticles = 3500;
  const particleSprite = useMemo(createParticleSprite, []);

  // Terrain parameters from the user's profile
  const territoryLevel = profile?.territoryLevel || 1;
  const islandScale = 1 + (territoryLevel - 1) * 0.4;

  // Rain lands on the Home's roof and on placed decorations rather than passing through them.
  const home = usePlayerHome(profile);
  const placements = profile?.islandPlacements;

  /**
   * The decorations rain can land on, as world-space boxes.
   *
   * Rebuilt when the island's furniture changes and not once per drop per frame - see
   * {@link splashHeightAt} for what that used to cost. Keyed on the footprint version as well as
   * on the placements, because a model's box is MEASURED the first time it is drawn
   * (lib/furniturePlacement.ts): a memo watching only `placements` would cache the empty answer
   * from before the measurement landed and rain would fall straight through that piece forever.
   * This is the same subscription CameraController and PlacementGhost use for the same reason.
   */
  const footprintVersion = useSyncExternalStore(subscribeFootprints, getFootprintVersion);
  const obstacles = useMemo<SplashObstacle[]>(() => {
    const list: SplashObstacle[] = [];
    for (const p of placements || []) {
      const fp = getFootprint(p.itemId);
      if (!fp) continue;
      list.push({
        box: makeObb(fp, p.position[0], p.position[2], p.rotation || 0),
        topY: p.position[1] + fp.maxY,
      });
    }
    return list;
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [placements, footprintVersion]);

  const splashHeights = useMemo(
    () => new SplashHeightCache(islandScale, home, obstacles),
    [islandScale, home, obstacles],
  );

  // Generate initial random particle states including splash state and coordinates
  const [positions, offsets, speeds, splashStates, splashProgress, impactCoords, splashVelocities] = useMemo(() => {
    const pos = new Float32Array(maxParticles * 3);
    const offs = new Float32Array(maxParticles * 3);
    const spds = new Float32Array(maxParticles);
    
    const states = new Uint8Array(maxParticles); // 0 = falling, 1 = splashing
    const prog = new Float32Array(maxParticles); // 0.0 -> 1.0 progress
    const impact = new Float32Array(maxParticles * 3); // (x,y,z) of impact
    const vels = new Float32Array(maxParticles * 3); // (vx,vy,vz) of splash splatter

    for (let i = 0; i < maxParticles; i++) {
      // Spawn within a generous 3D box covering the whole island bounds
      pos[i * 3] = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 60;     // X
      pos[i * 3 + 1] = Math.random() * 30;         // Y
      pos[i * 3 + 2] = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 60; // Z

      // Unique random wave offsets for natural horizontal sway/float paths
      offs[i * 3] = Math.random() * Math.PI * 2;     // Phase X
      offs[i * 3 + 1] = Math.random() * Math.PI * 2; // Phase Y
      offs[i * 3 + 2] = Math.random() * Math.PI * 2; // Phase Z

      // Speed variance
      spds[i] = 0.06 + Math.random() * 0.16;
      
      states[i] = 0;
      prog[i] = 0;
      
      impact[i * 3] = 0;
      impact[i * 3 + 1] = 0;
      impact[i * 3 + 2] = 0;
      
      vels[i * 3] = 0;
      vels[i * 3 + 1] = 0;
      vels[i * 3 + 2] = 0;
    }
    return [pos, offs, spds, states, prog, impact, vels];
  }, []);

  const pointsRef = useRef<THREE.Points>(null);
  const materialRef = useRef<THREE.PointsMaterial>(null);

  // Styling targets based on active weather state
  const styleTargets = useMemo(() => {
    switch (weather) {
      case WeatherType.SUNNY:
        return {
          size: 0.05,
          color: new THREE.Color('#FEF08A'), // Amber golden summer pollen motes
          opacity: 0.15,
          activeCount: 300,
        };
      case WeatherType.RAINY:
        return {
          size: 0.08,
          color: new THREE.Color('#93C5FD'), // Clear atmospheric blue raindrops
          opacity: 0.65,
          activeCount: 1600,
        };
      case WeatherType.STORM:
        return {
          size: 0.12,
          color: new THREE.Color('#E2E8F0'), // Thick slate grey rain streaks
          opacity: 0.85,
          activeCount: 3500,
        };
      case WeatherType.SNOW:
        return {
          size: 0.18,
          color: new THREE.Color('#FFFFFF'), // Pure white fluffy snow flakes
          opacity: 0.9,
          activeCount: 1500,
        };
      case WeatherType.TWILIGHT:
        return {
          size: 0.09,
          color: new THREE.Color('#F97316'), // Glowing warm orange/red embers
          opacity: 0.8,
          activeCount: 600,
        };
      case WeatherType.MIDNIGHT:
        return {
          size: 0.07,
          color: new THREE.Color('#C7D2FE'), // Cool pale-indigo night dust
          opacity: 0.5,
          activeCount: 280,
        };
      default:
        return {
          size: 0.05,
          color: new THREE.Color('#93C5FD'),
          opacity: 0.0,
          activeCount: 0,
        };
    }
  }, [weather]);

  /**
   * How many particles were live last frame.
   *
   * The pool is 3500 entries but only `activeCount` of them belong to the current sky - 300 on a
   * clear day. The loop below used to step all 3500 regardless, dragging the other 3200 downward
   * a fixed 0.5 a frame so they would sit out of sight under the terrain, and then re-uploading
   * the whole 42,000-float buffer to the GPU. Ten out of every eleven particles on a sunny island
   * were being simulated and uploaded purely in order to be invisible.
   *
   * `setDrawRange` says the same thing to the renderer directly and much more honestly - the
   * inactive tail is simply not drawn, so it needs no hiding place, no per-frame nudge and no
   * upload. This ref is what makes that safe in the other direction: when the sky turns and the
   * active range GROWS, the newly-uncovered entries still hold wherever they were parked the last
   * time they were live, so they are respawned into the sky rather than blinking in mid-fall.
   */
  const activeRef = useRef(0);

  useFrame((state) => {
    if (!pointsRef.current || !materialRef.current) return;

    const time = state.clock.getElapsedTime();
    const posAttrib = pointsRef.current.geometry.attributes.position as THREE.BufferAttribute;
    // The raw buffer, not getX/setXYZ. Three method calls per axis per particle is real overhead
    // at this count, and every value here is written straight back.
    const pos = posAttrib.array as Float32Array;

    // Smoothly transition material color, size, and opacity values
    materialRef.current.opacity = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(
      materialRef.current.opacity,
      styleTargets.opacity,
      0.04
    );
    materialRef.current.color.lerp(styleTargets.color, 0.04);
    materialRef.current.size = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(
      materialRef.current.size,
      styleTargets.size,
      0.04
    );

    // The live count RISES at once and FALLS gradually, which is what keeps the draw range from
    // being visible as a cut. A sky turning to 暴風雨 wants its rain immediately (and the
    // material's opacity is still fading in underneath it), but a storm ending must not delete
    // 3200 drops between two frames: the tail eases out over roughly the same second the opacity
    // lerp takes, so the downpour thins to a drizzle and then to nothing. The old loop got this
    // for free by dragging the surplus underground; this states it instead of hiding it.
    // The floor of one guarantees progress - a proportional step alone stalls once the gap is
    // small enough to round away.
    const target = styleTargets.activeCount;
    let active = activeRef.current;
    if (target > active) {
      // Newly-live entries get a fresh position in the same box the pool was seeded in.
      for (let i = active; i < target; i++) {
        pos[i * 3] = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 60;
        pos[i * 3 + 1] = Math.random() * 30;
        pos[i * 3 + 2] = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 60;
        splashStates[i] = 0;
        splashProgress[i] = 0;
      }
      active = target;
    } else if (target < active) {
      active = Math.max(target, active - Math.max(1, Math.ceil((active - target) * 0.06)));
    }
    activeRef.current = active;
    pointsRef.current.geometry.setDrawRange(0, active);
    if (active === 0) return;

    // Active frame processing
    for (let i = 0; i < active; i++) {
      const o = i * 3;
      let x = pos[o];
      let y = pos[o + 1];
      let z = pos[o + 2];
      const speed = speeds[i];

      if (weather === WeatherType.RAINY) {
        if (splashStates[i] === 1) {
          // Progress the splash animation
          splashProgress[i] += 0.08;
          if (splashProgress[i] >= 1.0) {
            splashStates[i] = 0;
            y = 30 + Math.random() * 5;
            x = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 60;
            z = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 60;
          } else {
            const t = splashProgress[i];
            x = impactCoords[o] + splashVelocities[o] * t;
            y = impactCoords[o + 1] + splashVelocities[o + 1] * t - 4.0 * t * t; // simple downward gravity parabola
            z = impactCoords[o + 2] + splashVelocities[o + 2] * t;
          }
        } else {
          y -= speed * 1.9; // Standard rainfall velocity

          const colY = splashHeights.at(x, z);
          if (y <= colY) {
            splashStates[i] = 1;
            splashProgress[i] = 0.0;
            impactCoords[o] = x;
            impactCoords[o + 1] = colY;
            impactCoords[o + 2] = z;

            // Random outwards semi-hemispherical trajectory for the rebound splash
            const angle = Math.random() * Math.PI * 2;
            const r = 0.2 + Math.random() * 0.4;
            splashVelocities[o] = Math.cos(angle) * r;
            splashVelocities[o + 1] = 0.7 + Math.random() * 1.0;
            splashVelocities[o + 2] = Math.sin(angle) * r;

            y = colY;
          }
        }
      } else if (weather === WeatherType.STORM) {
        if (splashStates[i] === 1) {
          splashProgress[i] += 0.10; // Rapid splash during fierce storm
          if (splashProgress[i] >= 1.0) {
            splashStates[i] = 0;
            y = 30 + Math.random() * 5;
            x = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 60 + 12; // spawn offset right to compensate wind drift
            z = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 60;
          } else {
            const t = splashProgress[i];
            x = impactCoords[o] + splashVelocities[o] * t;
            y = impactCoords[o + 1] + splashVelocities[o + 1] * t - 5.0 * t * t;
            z = impactCoords[o + 2] + splashVelocities[o + 2] * t;
          }
        } else {
          y -= speed * 2.9; // Fast diagonal torrent
          x -= speed * 0.9; // Wind angled drift

          const colY = splashHeights.at(x, z);
          if (y <= colY || x < -30) {
            if (y <= colY) {
              splashStates[i] = 1;
              splashProgress[i] = 0.0;
              impactCoords[o] = x;
              impactCoords[o + 1] = colY;
              impactCoords[o + 2] = z;

              // Blown sideways by the raging storm wind
              const angle = Math.random() * Math.PI * 2;
              const r = 0.3 + Math.random() * 0.5;
              splashVelocities[o] = Math.cos(angle) * r - 0.6; // strong wind drag to the left
              splashVelocities[o + 1] = 0.8 + Math.random() * 1.3;
              splashVelocities[o + 2] = Math.sin(angle) * r;

              y = colY;
            } else {
              // Off-screen reset
              y = 30 + Math.random() * 5;
              x = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 60 + 12;
              z = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 60;
            }
          }
        }
      } else {
        // Reset splash states for other non-rainy weather types
        splashStates[i] = 0;

        if (weather === WeatherType.SNOW) {
          y -= speed * 0.42; // Float downwards slowly
          x += Math.sin(time * 0.9 + offsets[o]) * 0.028; // Harmonic wind sway
          z += Math.cos(time * 0.6 + offsets[o + 2]) * 0.022;

          const colY = splashHeights.at(x, z);
          if (y < colY) {
            y = 30;
            x = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 60;
            z = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 60;
          }
        } else if (weather === WeatherType.TWILIGHT) {
          y += speed * 0.35; // Combustion embers floating upwards
          x += Math.sin(time * 1.3 + offsets[o]) * 0.018; // Fluttering heat rise
          z += Math.cos(time * 1.1 + offsets[o + 1]) * 0.018;
          if (y > 30) {
            y = 0;
            x = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 60;
            z = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 60;
          }
        } else {
          // SUNNY / MIDNIGHT: relaxed atmospheric drift - golden pollen by day,
          // cool night dust after dark. Same lazy motion, different palette.
          y += Math.sin(time * 0.25 + offsets[o]) * 0.006;
          x += Math.cos(time * 0.18 + offsets[o + 1]) * 0.004;
          z += Math.sin(time * 0.12 + offsets[o + 2]) * 0.004;

          if (y < 0) {
            y = 30;
          }
          if (y > 30) {
            y = 0;
          }
        }
      }

      pos[o] = x;
      pos[o + 1] = y;
      pos[o + 2] = z;
    }

    // Only the live prefix is dirty, so only that prefix is re-uploaded. On a clear day this is
    // 300 particles' worth of floats instead of the whole 3500-entry pool.
    posAttrib.clearUpdateRanges();
    posAttrib.addUpdateRange(0, active * 3);
    posAttrib.needsUpdate = true;
  });

  return (
    <points ref={pointsRef}>
      <bufferGeometry>
        <bufferAttribute
          attach="attributes-position"
          args={[positions, 3]}
        />
      </bufferGeometry>
      <pointsMaterial
        ref={materialRef}
        size={0.05}
        color="#93C5FD"
        map={particleSprite}
        alphaTest={0.01}
        transparent
        depthWrite={false}
        opacity={0.4}
      />
    </points>
  );
}
```

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { useThree } from '@react-three/fiber';

import { installZFightAudit } from '../../utils/zFightAudit';

/**
 * Registers the <Canvas> it is mounted in with `window.__auditZFighting()`, so the depth-conflict
 * check can be run against the real scene graph — with every group transform, territory scale and
 * runtime placement resolved — rather than guessed at from source. `npm run audit:zfighting` is
 * the static counterpart that runs in CI.
 *
 * Mounted in BOTH canvases: the island's (Scene.tsx) and the house interior's
 * (BuildingInteriorView.tsx). They are separate renderers with separate scene graphs, and while
 * this lived as a private component inside Scene.tsx the audit could only ever see the island —
 * so "clean" meant "clean outdoors", and every wall, floor, doorway and piece of furniture in the
 * house had never been looked at. `label` is what the report calls each one.
 *
 * Also exposes the scene as `window.__scene<Label>`, which is the companion to a finding: the
 * audit names a pair, and that handle is how you go find those two meshes in the live graph.
 *
 * Renders nothing — this is a logic-only Canvas child, like CameraController. Stripped from
 * production by the `import.meta.env.DEV` guard.
 */
export function ZFightAuditBridge({ label }: { label: string }) {
  const scene = useThree((state) => state.scene);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!import.meta.env.DEV) return;
    const handle = `__scene${label.charAt(0).toUpperCase()}${label.slice(1)}`;
    (window as unknown as Record<string, unknown>)[handle] = scene;
    return installZFightAudit(label, () => scene);
  }, [scene, label]);

  return null;
}
```

## src/components/Three/character/Attachment.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import type { AttachmentPoint } from '../../../constants/characterRig';

/**
 * Mounts a wearable at a socket.
 *
 * The entire reason this exists rather than each wearable carrying its own offsets: a
 * wearable that positions itself is a wearable that knows the shape of the body under it,
 * and that is the coupling section 十一 of the brief is about. Here the wearable draws at
 * its own origin, and WHERE that origin lands is the model's answer.
 *
 * `mirror` flips the socket across the character's centreline, which is how a single
 * authored ear/hand/foot socket serves both sides — a model cannot accidentally put its two
 * earrings at different heights, because there is only one number.
 */
export function Attachment({
  point,
  mirror = false,
  children,
}: {
  point: AttachmentPoint;
  mirror?: boolean;
  children: ReactNode;
}) {
  const [x, y, z] = point.position;
  const scale = point.scale ?? 1;
  return (
    <group
      position={[mirror ? -x : x, y, z]}
      rotation={point.rotation ? [...point.rotation] : [0, 0, 0]}
      scale={[scale, scale, scale]}
    >
      {children}
    </group>
  );
}
```

## src/components/Three/character/AuthoredCharacterModel.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { Suspense } from 'react';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import type { RefObject } from 'react';
import type * as THREE from 'three';
import { localHeight } from '../../../constants/characterRig';
import { Attachment } from './Attachment';
import {
  LegacyArm,
  LegacyArmWearables,
  LegacyGroundWearables,
  LegacyHead,
  LegacyHeadWearables,
  LegacyLeg,
  LegacyLegWearables,
  LegacyTorso,
  LegacyTorsoWearables,
} from './legacy';
import { CharacterPartBoundary } from './partLoader';
import { AUTHORED_PARTS } from './slots';
import type { AuthoredPart, CharacterPartId } from './slots';
import type { CharacterModelProps } from './types';

/**
 * THE AUTHORED CHARACTER MODEL — hand-made 3D assets, one part at a time.
 *
 * Select it with `?character=authored`. With no parts registered it renders exactly the
 * legacy character, which is the point: the import path is walkable and testable BEFORE the
 * first asset exists, so a finished head can be checked the day it is made rather than the
 * day the whole body is.
 *
 * The composition rule, per part:
 *
 *   registered   →  the authored mesh, inside a joint group this file owns
 *   not yet      →  the legacy procedural part
 *
 * The joint group, its position and its rig ref are ALWAYS owned here, never by the part.
 * That is what makes a half-imported character animate correctly: an authored head and a
 * legacy leg are bound to the same rig by the same code, so the controller cannot tell them
 * apart and the walk cycle does not care which is which.
 *
 * Each authored part gets its OWN Suspense boundary with the legacy part as the fallback,
 * so an asset still streaming in shows the old limb for a frame instead of unmounting the
 * rig — a suspended avatar would drop every ref mid-frame and stall the animation.
 *
 * And its own ERROR boundary, with the same fallback, for the case Suspense does not cover: a
 * part that arrives BROKEN rather than late. A missing file or a bad export throws, and
 * without a boundary per part that throw unwinds to the app root and replaces the whole game
 * with an error screen. With one, a bad asset costs exactly one limb and says so in the
 * console. See CharacterPartBoundary.
 */

/**
 * A joint the controller drives, with whatever geometry belongs inside it.
 *
 * Every authored part goes through here, so there is exactly one place that decides what a
 * joint is, and a part physically cannot set its own joint height.
 */
function Joint({
  bind,
  position,
  part,
  children,
}: {
  bind: RefObject<THREE.Group | null>;
  position: readonly [number, number, number];
  /** The pivot correction, if the asset needed one. See AuthoredPart.transform. */
  part: AuthoredPart;
  children: ReactNode;
}) {
  return (
    <group ref={bind} position={[position[0], position[1], position[2]]}>
      {part.transform ? <Attachment point={part.transform}>{children}</Attachment> : children}
    </group>
  );
}

/**
 * Everything worn on a part, as a thunk, so `part()` below can decide whether to draw it
 * without every caller having to know which wearables belong to which slot.
 *
 * A thunk and not an element for the same reason `legacy` is one: it may go unrendered, and
 * building it eagerly would run the hairstyle's and the wreath's memos for a part that has
 * declared it cannot host them.
 */
type Wearables = () => ReactNode;

export function AuthoredCharacterModel(props: CharacterModelProps) {
  const { rig, skeleton, attachments, outfit } = props;

  /**
   * Renders one part: the authored asset if it exists, the legacy part if it does not.
   *
   * `legacy` is passed as a thunk rather than an element because it is used twice — once as
   * the no-asset fallback and once as the Suspense fallback while an asset loads — and the
   * legacy part binds a rig ref, so handing the same element to both would bind that ref
   * from two places at once.
   */
  const bodyLocalHeight = localHeight(skeleton);

  /**
   * `wearables` is rendered INSIDE the joint AND inside the part's `transform`, next to the
   * imported mesh — not beside the joint. Both halves of that matter:
   *
   *   inside the joint      a hat has to nod with the head; trousers have to swing with the leg.
   *   inside the transform  a sleeve has to hang the way the arm hangs. The arm's rest splay
   *                         lives in `transform`, so anything outside it wears the pose the
   *                         model does not have.
   *
   * It is drawn only when the part says it can host the wardrobe. The default is that it
   * cannot — an unfitted hat floating beside a new skull is worse than an honest bare head —
   * so `wearsWardrobe` is a claim each asset makes for itself once it has been checked.
   */
  const part = (
    id: CharacterPartId,
    joint: readonly [number, number, number],
    bind: RefObject<THREE.Group | null>,
    legacy: () => ReactNode,
    wearables: Wearables,
  ) => {
    const authored = AUTHORED_PARTS[id];
    if (!authored) return legacy();
    const { Component } = authored;
    return (
      <CharacterPartBoundary label={id} fallback={legacy}>
        <Suspense fallback={legacy()}>
          <Joint bind={bind} position={joint} part={authored}>
            <Component outfit={outfit} partId={id} bodyLocalHeight={bodyLocalHeight} rig={rig} />
            {authored.wearsWardrobe ? wearables() : null}
          </Joint>
        </Suspense>
      </CharacterPartBoundary>
    );
  };

  return (
    <>
      {part(
        'head',
        [0, skeleton.head.y, 0],
        rig.head,
        () => <LegacyHead rig={rig} skeleton={skeleton} attachments={attachments} outfit={outfit} />,
        () => <LegacyHeadWearables rig={rig} attachments={attachments} outfit={outfit} />,
      )}
      {part(
        'torso',
        [0, skeleton.torso.y, 0],
        rig.torso,
        () => <LegacyTorso rig={rig} skeleton={skeleton} attachments={attachments} outfit={outfit} />,
        () => <LegacyTorsoWearables attachments={attachments} outfit={outfit} />,
      )}
      {part(
        'leftArm',
        [-skeleton.shoulder.x, skeleton.shoulder.y, 0],
        rig.leftArm,
        () => <LegacyArm side="left" rig={rig} skeleton={skeleton} attachments={attachments} outfit={outfit} />,
        () => <LegacyArmWearables attachments={attachments} outfit={outfit} />,
      )}
      {part(
        'rightArm',
        [skeleton.shoulder.x, skeleton.shoulder.y, 0],
        rig.rightArm,
        () => <LegacyArm side="right" rig={rig} skeleton={skeleton} attachments={attachments} outfit={outfit} />,
        () => <LegacyArmWearables attachments={attachments} outfit={outfit} />,
      )}
      {part(
        'leftLeg',
        [-skeleton.hip.x, skeleton.hip.y, 0],
        rig.leftLeg,
        () => <LegacyLeg side="left" rig={rig} skeleton={skeleton} attachments={attachments} outfit={outfit} />,
        () => <LegacyLegWearables side="left" attachments={attachments} outfit={outfit} />,
      )}
      {part(
        'rightLeg',
        [skeleton.hip.x, skeleton.hip.y, 0],
        rig.rightLeg,
        () => <LegacyLeg side="right" rig={rig} skeleton={skeleton} attachments={attachments} outfit={outfit} />,
        () => <LegacyLegWearables side="right" attachments={attachments} outfit={outfit} />,
      )}

      {/* The ground cosmetics, which hang off the ROOT rather than off any part — so unlike
          every slot above they are not any part's to render, and this model has to mount them
          itself exactly as LegacyCharacterModel does. Left out, an aura would disappear the
          moment the authored model was selected, with nothing to point at as the cause. */}
      <LegacyGroundWearables attachments={attachments} outfit={outfit} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## src/components/Three/character/CharacterModelV2.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { RoundedBox } from '@react-three/drei';
import type { CharacterModelProps } from './types';

/**
 * Player character model v2 - the remodel drawn from the design sketch.
 *
 * WHAT THIS FILE IS NOT: it is not a character controller. It owns no state, no useFrame and no
 * refs of its own. Avatar.tsx keeps every one of those and passes the refs in, so v2 and the
 * legacy model are driven by the exact same animation code, terrain sampling, swim state machine,
 * emote table and footstep VFX. Swapping models cannot change how the character behaves, only
 * what it looks like - which is the whole reason the remodel is safe to land next to the shipped
 * one instead of replacing it.
 *
 *
 * READING THE SKETCH
 *
 * The reference is a ~2-heads-tall mascot; the shipped legacy build is ~1.85. Beyond the head
 * ratio the sketch asks for five things the sphere-headed model does not have:
 *
 *   1. a rounded-CUBE skull - flat-ish crown, squared jaw, wider than deep - not a sphere;
 *   2. ears, which the legacy head has none of (its only side geometry is earring jewellery);
 *   3. thin arms ending in oversized round mitt hands;
 *   4. thin legs, noticeably longer than the legacy stubs;
 *   5. real oval feet pointing forward, rather than a leg capsule that just stops.
 *
 * It is deliberately NOT a 1:1 tracing. Measured against its own head, v2 stands ~2.2 heads tall
 * where the sketch is ~2.0 and legacy is 1.85. The extra tenth is because a 2D outline has no
 * volume: the head here is 0.50 WIDE against 0.44 tall - wider than it is tall, as drawn - so it
 * carries far more visual mass in perspective than its height alone predicts, and matching the
 * sketch's height ratio exactly reads as a bigger head on screen, not a smaller one. Same reason
 * the limbs, drawn as single strokes, are given enough radius here to survive being lit.
 *
 *
 * WHAT IS FIXED, AND WHY
 *
 * Two numbers are load-bearing for systems outside this file and are reproduced EXACTLY:
 *
 *   - the sole sits at local y = -0.005. groupRef's origin is the character's ground contact
 *     point, so terrain height, the "not sunk into the sand" invariant, shadow contact and every
 *     footstep VFX spawn are all quoted against it.
 *   - the crown sits at local y = 0.94 + LEG_LENGTHEN, giving the same ~2.16 world units the
 *     legacy model stands at. Legacy reaches it as head centre 0.68 + radius 0.26; v2 as head
 *     centre 0.72 + half-height 0.22. Identical totals, so nothing downstream that was tuned
 *     against the character's HEIGHT has to move: door clearance, the camera's 1.9-unit
 *     avoidance cylinder, the +1.2/+1.65/+1.8 camera focus offsets, furniture scale.
 *
 * The shoulder (0.42) and hip (0.22) pivots are unchanged too, so the arm and leg swing arcs the
 * animation writes are the same arcs on the same joints. The head centre is the ONLY joint that
 * moves (0.68 -> 0.72) and it moves so the smaller skull can keep the crown where it was - see
 * CHARACTER_RIG_METRICS in constants/characterModel.ts.
 *
 * All coordinates below are LOCAL units. Multiply by Avatar.tsx's baseScale (2.25) for world.
 */

/**
 * Head half-extents. Head centre 0.73 + HEAD_HALF_H = the legacy crown, 0.94 (+ LEG_LENGTHEN).
 *
 * WIDTH is the number that decides whether this reads as a new character at all. The first cut
 * of v2 ran 0.50 wide against the legacy sphere's 0.52 - four percent - and spent its whole
 * proportion change on head HEIGHT and torso length instead. Both of those are things the head
 * hides at normal camera distance, so the silhouette came out indistinguishable from legacy: the
 * head still filled it end to end. At 0.42 the skull is ~19% narrower than legacy's, which is
 * the first change big enough to actually see from the third-person camera.
 *
 * That puts v2 at ~2.3 heads tall against legacy's 1.85 and the sketch's ~2.0. Deliberately past
 * the sketch: a drawn outline carries no volume, and the head still has to lose enough mass in
 * 3D to stop dominating. If it ends up reading too slender, HEAD_HALF_W/H/D and the rig's headY
 * are the only knobs that need touching - raise the halves and drop headY by the same amount, so
 * the crown stays put.
 */
const HEAD_HALF_H = 0.21;
const HEAD_HALF_W = 0.21;
const HEAD_HALF_D = 0.21;

/**
 * Corner rounding on the skull. Tightened along with the shrink: at 0.115 on a 0.42 box the flat
 * facial plane reaches |x|,|y| <= 0.095, and the corners stay square enough that the rounded-CUBE
 * silhouette the sketch draws survives at distance. Rounding much past 0.16 collapses the head
 * back into the sphere v2 exists to replace - which is half of why the first cut looked unchanged.
 */
const HEAD_ROUND = 0.115;

/** The flat facial plane the eyes, mouth and blush are registered against. */
const FACE_Z = HEAD_HALF_D;

/** Shared with the legacy build so a skin tone reads identically across the two models. */
const SKIN_ROUGHNESS = 0.7;

/**
 * The head numbers Phase 2 will need when it refits the wardrobe to this skull. The SOCKETS
 * themselves now live in constants/characterRig.ts as `V2_ATTACHMENTS`, which is what the
 * wearables actually mount through; these are the raw measurements behind those offsets, kept
 * here next to the geometry they describe so the two cannot drift apart.
 */
export const V2_HEAD_METRICS = {
  crownY: HEAD_HALF_H,
  halfWidth: HEAD_HALF_W,
  halfDepth: HEAD_HALF_D,
  faceZ: FACE_Z,
} as const;

/** One arm. Mirrored by `side`: -1 is the character's left (-x), +1 its right. */
function V2Arm({ side, skinColor }: { side: -1 | 1; skinColor: string }) {
  return (
    /* The outward hang is on an INNER group. The outer group is leftArmRef/rightArmRef, whose
       rotation the animation overwrites every frame - a rest pose written there would be erased
       on the first useFrame. Nesting it means the swing arc composes ON TOP of the rest pose,
       which is also how the sketch reads: arms angled slightly away from the body even at idle. */
    <group rotation={[0, 0, side * 0.16]}>
      {/* Upper arm. r 0.028 against the legacy 0.040 - the sketch's arms are strokes, and the
          mitt hand below is what carries the visual weight. The outward tilt is up at 0.16 so
          there is visible daylight between arm and torso, which is how the sketch reads and
          what stops the arms from merging into the body's outline at distance. */}
      <mesh position={[0, -0.09, 0]} castShadow>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.028, 0.14, 4, 12]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color={skinColor} roughness={SKIN_ROUGHNESS} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Mitt hand. Oversized on purpose - at 0.072 it is well over twice the arm's radius,
          which is the mascot proportion the sketch draws and the thing that keeps a 0.028 arm
          from reading as a stick. Now that the head has shrunk, the hands are a much larger
          share of the silhouette, which is exactly the read the reference has. */}
      <mesh position={[0, -0.205, 0]} scale={[1, 1.04, 0.92]} castShadow>
        <sphereGeometry args={[0.072, 16, 12]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color={skinColor} roughness={SKIN_ROUGHNESS} />
      </mesh>
    </group>
  );
}

/** One leg. `side` mirrors nothing geometrically yet; it is here for Phase 2's trouser seams. */
function V2Leg({ skinColor }: { side: -1 | 1; skinColor: string }) {
  return (
    <>
      {/* Shin/thigh as one tapered limb. Its top reaches +0.005, just inside the torso box's
          lower edge, so the joint never opens a gap when the leg swings forward. */}
      <mesh position={[0, -0.095, 0]} castShadow>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.038, 0.13, 4, 12]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color={skinColor} roughness={SKIN_ROUGHNESS} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Foot. An ellipsoid rather than a capsule so it reads as the sketch's flat forward oval.
          Its BOTTOM is the number that matters: -0.250 below the hip pivot, against a hip that
          sits at 0.2283 + LEG_LENGTHEN, puts the sole at local -0.005 - the same ground contact
          the legacy leg capsule resolves to, and the reason the character stands ON the terrain
          rather than floating above it or sinking into it.
          Pushed +0.034 forward so the toe leads, and its top overlaps the limb by 0.022. */}
      <mesh position={[0, -0.208, 0.034]} scale={[0.075, 0.042, 0.125]} castShadow>
        <sphereGeometry args={[1, 16, 12]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color={skinColor} roughness={SKIN_ROUGHNESS} />
      </mesh>
    </>
  );
}

/**
 * v2 renders BARE: no hair, hats, outfits, pants, shoes, necklaces, glasses or masks.
 *
 * Not an oversight and not a bug in the dressing room — every one of those is authored
 * against the legacy 0.26 sphere head and 0.135 capsule torso, and would render detached on
 * this body. `V2_ATTACHMENTS` in constants/characterRig.ts is the table that will refit them;
 * until something actually reads it, the honest thing is to draw nothing, which is why the
 * registry marks this model `wearsWardrobe: false` so the UI can say so.
 */
export function CharacterModelV2({ rig, skeleton, outfit }: CharacterModelProps) {
  const { skinColor, bodyColor } = outfit;

  return (
    <>
      {/* ---------------------------------------------------------------- HEAD */}
      <group ref={rig.head} position={[0, skeleton.head.y, 0]}>
        {/* The skull. Wider (0.50) than deep (0.46) and flatter (0.44) than either, which is
            what separates a rounded cube from a rounded sphere at a glance. */}
        <RoundedBox
          args={[HEAD_HALF_W * 2, HEAD_HALF_H * 2, HEAD_HALF_D * 2]}
          radius={HEAD_ROUND}
          smoothness={5}
          castShadow
        >
          <meshStandardMaterial color={skinColor} roughness={SKIN_ROUGHNESS} />
        </RoundedBox>

        {/* Ears - new to v2; the legacy head has no side geometry at all. Squashed on x so they
            sit flush against the skull rather than sticking out as spheres, and pushed slightly
            back (-0.02) so they read behind the cheek line from a three-quarter camera. */}
        {([-1, 1] as const).map((side) => (
          <mesh key={side} position={[side * 0.212, 0.015, -0.012]} scale={[0.5, 1, 0.85]} castShadow>
            <sphereGeometry args={[0.062, 12, 10]} />
            <meshStandardMaterial color={skinColor} roughness={SKIN_ROUGHNESS} />
          </mesh>
        ))}

        {/* Eyes. Kept as spheres on eyeLRef/eyeRRef because the animation blinks by writing
            `scale.y` on exactly these meshes - changing their shape here would change blinking
            for free, and not in a good way. Inset 0.018 into the flat face so ~0.02 protrudes,
            matching how the legacy eyes sit proud of the sphere.
            NOTE: the saved preference for angled crescent HAPPY eyes is a Phase 2 item - it needs
            an expression signal the animation does not currently expose. See the handover. */}
        <group position={[0, 0.005, FACE_Z - 0.017]}>
          <group ref={rig.eyeL} position={[-0.082, 0, 0]}>
            <mesh>
              <sphereGeometry args={[0.035, 16, 16]} />
              <meshStandardMaterial color="#0d1117" roughness={0.1} />
            </mesh>
          </group>
          <group ref={rig.eyeR} position={[0.082, 0, 0]}>
            <mesh>
              <sphereGeometry args={[0.035, 16, 16]} />
              <meshStandardMaterial color="#0d1117" roughness={0.1} />
            </mesh>
          </group>
        </group>

        {/* Mouth. Same torus-arc construction and same rotation as legacy, because the smile
            animation writes `mouthRef.current.scale.set(s, s, 1)` and that only reads correctly
            on an arc lying in the XY plane. Widened 0.036 -> 0.040 for the sketch's broader grin,
            and held at y -0.065 so it stays inside the flat facial plane (|y| <= 0.07). */}
        <group ref={rig.mouth} position={[0, -0.062, FACE_Z - 0.004]}>
          <mesh rotation={[0, 0, Math.PI * 1.275]}>
            <torusGeometry args={[0.036, 0.0044, 8, 24, Math.PI * 0.45]} />
            <meshStandardMaterial color="#0d1117" roughness={0.5} />
          </mesh>
        </group>

        {/* Blush. Embedded deep enough (z 0.170 against a 0.23 face) that it cannot protrude in
            profile, which is the same trick the legacy cheeks use. */}
        {([-1, 1] as const).map((side) => (
          <mesh key={side} position={[side * 0.122, -0.046, 0.152]}>
            <sphereGeometry args={[0.050, 12, 12]} />
            <meshStandardMaterial color="#fda4af" transparent opacity={0.28} roughness={0.9} />
          </mesh>
        ))}
      </group>

      {/* --------------------------------------------------------------- TORSO */}
      {/* A rounded box where legacy uses a capsule. Spans 0.2467..0.5067 local, and is now TALLER
          than it is wide (0.26 against 0.24) - the sketch's torso is an upright rounded rectangle,
          and the earlier wider-than-tall version read as a squat block once the head above it
          shrank. Ending at 0.2467, just above the 0.245 hip, is what lets the full length of each
          leg show instead of burying its top third the way the legacy capsule does. */}
      <group ref={rig.torso} position={[0, skeleton.torso.y, 0]}>
        <RoundedBox args={[0.24, 0.26, 0.20]} radius={0.075} smoothness={4} castShadow>
          <meshStandardMaterial color={bodyColor} roughness={SKIN_ROUGHNESS} />
        </RoundedBox>
        {/* Neck. Spans 0.4567..0.5967, bridging the 0.03 between the torso's top (0.5067) and the
            head's underside (0.5367). The sketch draws a short neck there, so the gap is wanted,
            but it has to be filled or head TILT shows daylight through it. Riding inside the
            torso JOINT means the idle breathing scale carries it, so it can never drift away
            from the torso it is plugging. */}
        <mesh position={[0, 0.15, 0]}>
          <cylinderGeometry args={[0.065, 0.070, 0.14, 16]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial color={skinColor} roughness={SKIN_ROUGHNESS} />
        </mesh>
      </group>

      {/* ---------------------------------------------------------------- ARMS */}
      {/* Shoulders at +-0.135, just outside the 0.12 torso half-width, so the arms hang clear of
          a torso that is narrower than the legacy capsule's 0.135 radius made it. */}
      <group ref={rig.leftArm} position={[-skeleton.shoulder.x, skeleton.shoulder.y, 0]}>
        <V2Arm side={-1} skinColor={skinColor} />
      </group>
      <group ref={rig.rightArm} position={[skeleton.shoulder.x, skeleton.shoulder.y, 0]}>
        <V2Arm side={1} skinColor={skinColor} />
      </group>

      {/* ---------------------------------------------------------------- LEGS */}
      {/* Hips at +-0.055 - closer together than the legacy 0.065 and much narrower than the
          torso, which is what gives the sketch's two-thin-strokes read. */}
      <group ref={rig.leftLeg} position={[-skeleton.hip.x, skeleton.hip.y, 0]}>
        <V2Leg side={-1} skinColor={skinColor} />
      </group>
      <group ref={rig.rightLeg} position={[skeleton.hip.x, skeleton.hip.y, 0]}>
        <V2Leg side={1} skinColor={skinColor} />
      </group>
    </>
  );
}
```

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { useLayoutEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { LEGACY_TORSO_SHAPE } from '../../../constants/characterRig';
import type { TorsoShape } from '../../../constants/characterRig';

/**
 * 服裝貼身 — carrying garments drawn on one torso onto a torso of a different SHAPE.
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * WHY A WARP AND NOT A SCALE
 * ============================================================================
 *
 * Every torso garment is drawn hugging legacy's circular capsule. A socket scale fixes SIZE and
 * nothing else, and the authored chest differs in shape three ways at once: it is shallower
 * front-to-back than it is wide, its straight section is shorter, and its caps are flatter. No
 * one number fits all three, so a uniformly scaled shirt floated 2 cm off the chest and hung its
 * rounded bottom 2 cm under the body — the pointed bib the wardrobe was reported for.
 *
 * So each vertex is moved instead, by a map that sends legacy's torso SURFACE exactly onto this
 * one's (see {@link warpTorsoPoint}). Anything drawn ON the legacy body lands on this body;
 * anything drawn N mm off it lands N mm off this one. That second half is the point: clearance
 * is what stops a garment z-fighting the skin or the layer under it, so it is carried over in
 * absolute terms instead of being scaled down with the body.
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * WHAT IT COSTS AND WHAT IT LEAVES ALONE
 * ============================================================================
 *
 * The garments are small (a few thousand vertices for the busiest outfit), and the warp runs
 * once per mesh when the outfit changes — never per frame. Geometry is CLONED before it is
 * moved: R3F's `<capsuleGeometry>` elements and the necklace's memoised tube are owned by their
 * components, and the shop's thumbnails may share them, so the originals are never touched.
 * Clones are disposed when their mesh leaves the subtree or the fit unmounts.
 *
 * A mesh is re-fitted if its geometry is replaced (an `args` change) or its transform relative to
 * the fit root changes; otherwise a re-render is a traversal and two comparisons per mesh.
 */

/**
 * Where on a torso's DRESSED surface a bearing (cx, cz — a unit vector in plan) meets height `y`.
 *
 * Without a hem that is the body itself. With one, the lower cap is replaced below the straight
 * section: the section eases out to the hem's size by the hem line — smoothstep, so the chest
 * does not crease where the flare starts — and only closes underneath past it.
 */
function surfaceRadius(shape: TorsoShape, y: number, cx: number, cz: number): number {
  const over = Math.abs(y) - shape.straightHalf;
  const hem = shape.hem;
  if (over <= 0 || !hem || y > 0) {
    const k = over <= 0 ? 1 : Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, 1 - (over / shape.capHeight) ** 2));
    return k / Math.hypot(cx / shape.halfX, cz / shape.halfZ);
  }
  const u = over / shape.capHeight;
  const uHem = (-hem.y - shape.straightHalf) / shape.capHeight;
  const t = Math.min(1, u / uHem);
  const ease = t * t * (3 - 2 * t);
  const hx = shape.halfX + (hem.halfX - shape.halfX) * ease;
  const hz = shape.halfZ + (hem.halfZ - shape.halfZ) * ease;
  const k = u <= uHem ? 1 : Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, 1 - ((u - uHem) / (1 - uHem)) ** 2));
  return k / Math.hypot(cx / hx, cz / hz);
}

/**
 * Height on `to` of height `y` on `from`: the straight sections match, each cap is stretched onto
 * the other's cap, and anything past the pole keeps its distance from it.
 */
function mapHeight(from: TorsoShape, to: TorsoShape, y: number): number {
  const a = Math.abs(y);
  const sign = y < 0 ? -1 : 1;
  if (a <= from.straightHalf) return y * (to.straightHalf / from.straightHalf);
  const fromPole = from.straightHalf + from.capHeight;
  if (a <= fromPole) {
    return sign * (to.straightHalf + ((a - from.straightHalf) * to.capHeight) / from.capHeight);
  }
  return sign * (to.straightHalf + to.capHeight + (a - fromPole));
}

/**
 * The warp, torso-local in and out. Keeps bearing; maps height as above; and in plan:
 *
 *   inside the body  scales with the body, so an inner lining stays inside;
 *   outside it       keeps its absolute distance off the surface.
 *
 * The two agree ON the surface, so the map is continuous. Past a pole the body has no surface
 * (radius 0 on both sides) and the point is carried over unchanged, which is also continuous.
 */
export function warpTorsoPoint(from: TorsoShape, to: TorsoShape, p: THREE.Vector3, out: THREE.Vector3): THREE.Vector3 {
  const r = Math.hypot(p.x, p.z);
  const y = mapHeight(from, to, p.y);
  if (r < 1e-9) return out.set(0, y, 0);
  const cx = p.x / r;
  const cz = p.z / r;
  const rb = surfaceRadius(from, p.y, cx, cz);
  const re = surfaceRadius(to, y, cx, cz);
  const r2 = rb > 1e-9 && r <= rb ? r * (re / rb) : re + (r - rb);
  return out.set(cx * r2, y, cz * r2);
}

const sameShape = (a: TorsoShape, b: TorsoShape) =>
  a.halfX === b.halfX && a.halfZ === b.halfZ && a.straightHalf === b.straightHalf &&
  a.capHeight === b.capHeight && !a.hem && !b.hem;

interface FitRecord {
  /** The geometry the component owns — what every re-fit starts from. */
  source: THREE.BufferGeometry;
  /** The warped clone currently on the mesh. */
  fitted: THREE.BufferGeometry;
  /** Mesh-to-root matrix the clone was built under. */
  matrix: THREE.Matrix4;
}

const FIT_KEY = 'torsoFit';

/**
 * The geometry a mesh was given BEFORE it was fitted — its own if it has never been fitted,
 * otherwise the source the clone on it is carrying.
 *
 * Asked instead of assuming, because a fitted clone can outlive this component's record of
 * it: every time the subtree is torn down and put back — React's StrictMode does exactly
 * that on each mount in development, and a Suspense boundary does it whenever it hides and
 * re-shows its content — the cleanup below empties the map while the clones are still on
 * their meshes. Taking one of those as a source warps an already-warped garment: the second
 * pass reads its clearance off LEGACY's wider chest, so the shirt lands ~2 cm INSIDE this
 * body and the torso is left looking bare. See the fix's counterpart in the cleanup.
 */
function sourceOf(mesh: THREE.Mesh): THREE.BufferGeometry {
  return (mesh.geometry.userData?.[FIT_KEY] as THREE.BufferGeometry | undefined) ?? mesh.geometry;
}

const _p = new THREE.Vector3();
const _q = new THREE.Vector3();
const _a = new THREE.Vector3();
const _b = new THREE.Vector3();
const _n = new THREE.Vector3();
const _j = new THREE.Matrix3();
const _nm = new THREE.Matrix3();
const _nmInv = new THREE.Matrix3();
const EPS = 1e-4;

function warpGeometry(
  source: THREE.BufferGeometry,
  toRoot: THREE.Matrix4,
  from: TorsoShape,
  to: TorsoShape,
): THREE.BufferGeometry {
  const geometry = source.clone();
  // The clone carries the geometry it was made from, so a fit can always be undone by
  // whoever finds the clone — see sourceOf. A fresh userData object and not the cloned
  // one: BufferGeometry.clone() hands the copy the SOURCE's userData BY REFERENCE, so
  // writing the mark straight onto it would mark the original as fitted as well.
  geometry.userData = { ...source.userData, [FIT_KEY]: source };
  const fromRoot = toRoot.clone().invert();
  const position = geometry.getAttribute('position') as THREE.BufferAttribute;
  const normal = geometry.getAttribute('normal') as THREE.BufferAttribute | undefined;
  _nm.getNormalMatrix(toRoot);
  _nmInv.getNormalMatrix(fromRoot);

  for (let i = 0; i < position.count; i++) {
    _p.fromBufferAttribute(position, i).applyMatrix4(toRoot);

    if (normal) {
      // The normal goes through the inverse-transpose of the warp's Jacobian, taken numerically:
      // the map is piecewise and not worth differentiating by hand, and three central differences
      // on a few thousand vertices is nothing.
      const cols: number[] = [];
      for (let axis = 0; axis < 3; axis++) {
        _q.copy(_p).setComponent(axis, _p.getComponent(axis) + EPS);
        warpTorsoPoint(from, to, _q, _a);
        _q.copy(_p).setComponent(axis, _p.getComponent(axis) - EPS);
        warpTorsoPoint(from, to, _q, _b);
        _a.sub(_b).multiplyScalar(1 / (2 * EPS));
        cols.push(_a.x, _a.y, _a.z);
      }
      // Matrix3.set is row-major; the columns above are the partial derivatives.
      _j.set(cols[0], cols[3], cols[6], cols[1], cols[4], cols[7], cols[2], cols[5], cols[8]);
      if (Math.abs(_j.determinant()) > 1e-12) {
        _j.invert().transpose();
        _n.fromBufferAttribute(normal, i).applyMatrix3(_nm).applyMatrix3(_j).applyMatrix3(_nmInv).normalize();
        normal.setXYZ(i, _n.x, _n.y, _n.z);
      }
    }

    warpTorsoPoint(from, to, _p, _q).applyMatrix4(fromRoot);
    position.setXYZ(i, _q.x, _q.y, _q.z);
  }

  position.needsUpdate = true;
  if (normal) normal.needsUpdate = true;
  geometry.computeBoundingBox();
  geometry.computeBoundingSphere();
  return geometry;
}

/**
 * Wraps torso garments and fits them to `shape`. Children are drawn in LEGACY torso space, exactly
 * as they always have been; nothing inside needs to know this is here.
 */
export function TorsoFit({ shape, children }: { shape: TorsoShape; children: ReactNode }) {
  const root = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);
  const clones = useRef(new Map<THREE.Mesh, FitRecord>());

  // Every render, after the children have committed: R3F has attached any new geometry by the
  // time a parent's layout effect runs, so this sees the finished subtree.
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const group = root.current;
    if (!group) return;
    const from = LEGACY_TORSO_SHAPE;
    const identity = sameShape(from, shape);

    group.updateWorldMatrix(true, true);
    const rootInverse = group.matrixWorld.clone().invert();
    const seen = new Set<THREE.Mesh>();

    group.traverse((object) => {
      const mesh = object as THREE.Mesh;
      if (!mesh.isMesh || identity) return;
      seen.add(mesh);
      const toRoot = rootInverse.clone().multiply(mesh.matrixWorld);
      const record = clones.current.get(mesh);

      if (record && mesh.geometry === record.fitted && record.matrix.equals(toRoot)) return;

      // A geometry that is not our clone is a new one from the component: fit that. Otherwise the
      // mesh moved, and the fit is rebuilt from the geometry it was originally given.
      const source = record && mesh.geometry === record.fitted ? record.source : sourceOf(mesh);
      if (record) record.fitted.dispose();
      const fitted = warpGeometry(source, toRoot, from, shape);
      mesh.geometry = fitted;
      clones.current.set(mesh, { source, fitted, matrix: toRoot });
    });

    for (const [mesh, record] of clones.current) {
      if (seen.has(mesh)) continue;
      // Gone from the subtree (or the fit became the identity): release the clone, and hand the
      // mesh its own geometry back if it is still alive somewhere.
      if (mesh.geometry === record.fitted) mesh.geometry = record.source;
      record.fitted.dispose();
      clones.current.delete(mesh);
    }
  });

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const map = clones.current;
    return () => {
      for (const [mesh, record] of map) {
        // Same restore as the removal loop above, and for the same reason: this cleanup also
        // runs when the subtree is only being HIDDEN, and a mesh left holding a clone this
        // component has forgotten is one that gets warped a second time when it comes back.
        if (mesh.geometry === record.fitted) mesh.geometry = record.source;
        record.fitted.dispose();
      }
      map.clear();
    };
  }, []);

  return <group ref={root}>{children}</group>;
}
```

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { useMemo } from 'react';

import { PANTS_PALETTES } from '../../../constants/pants';
import { getCharacterForm, type BodyFill } from '../../../constants/characterForm';
import type { CharacterModelId, CharacterOutfit } from './types';

/**
 * Draws the joins a model declares in `constants/characterForm.ts`.
 *
 * A model renders `<BodyForm joint="torso" .../>` inside each joint group it has, and gets
 * whatever that model's spec puts there — nothing at all, for a model with no spec. The component
 * is therefore safe to mount unconditionally: it is the DATA that decides whether anything is
 * drawn, which is what keeps a future imported model from inheriting legacy's anatomy.
 *
 * It holds no state and runs no frame callback, exactly like every other part of a model (see
 * character/types.ts). A fill is geometry, and geometry is all a model owns.
 */
export function BodyForm({
  modelId,
  joint,
  outfit,
  side = 'right',
}: {
  modelId: CharacterModelId;
  joint: BodyFill['joint'];
  outfit: CharacterOutfit;
  /** Which limb this instance is inside. Ignored for `head` / `torso`. */
  side?: 'left' | 'right';
}) {
  const fills = useMemo(
    () => getCharacterForm(modelId).filter((fill) => fill.joint === joint),
    [modelId, joint],
  );

  if (fills.length === 0) return null;

  return (
    <>
      {fills.map((fill) => {
        const x = fill.mirrorX && side === 'left' ? -fill.position[0] : fill.position[0];
        return (
          <mesh
            key={fill.name}
            position={[x, fill.position[1], fill.position[2]]}
            scale={fill.scale ? [fill.scale[0], fill.scale[1], fill.scale[2]] : undefined}
            castShadow
          >
            <sphereGeometry args={[fill.radius, fill.segments ?? 16, (fill.segments ?? 16) / 2]} />
            <meshStandardMaterial color={fillColor(fill, outfit)} roughness={0.7} />
          </mesh>
        );
      })}
    </>
  );
}

/**
 * What colour a fill takes.
 *
 * The `leg` rule is lifted verbatim from the legacy thigh capsule's own lining, and sharing it is
 * the point: the pelvis and the thigh under it have to be the same colour or the hips read as a
 * separate garment. Trousers over bare legs is the common case (the shipped trousers are lathed
 * OVER the capsule rather than replacing it), so the lining colour is what shows through any gap
 * — including the one between the two trouser legs that the pelvis now fills.
 */
function fillColor(fill: BodyFill, outfit: CharacterOutfit): string {
  switch (fill.tint) {
    case 'body':
      return outfit.bodyColor;
    case 'leg':
      return outfit.pants ? PANTS_PALETTES[outfit.pants].body : outfit.skinColor;
    case 'skin':
    default:
      return outfit.skinColor;
  }
}

/** Re-exported so a preview harness can enumerate what a model declares. */
export { getCharacterForm };
export type { BodyFill };
```

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 角色表面 —— how the character is LIT, as opposed to what it is made of.
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * THE PROBLEM THIS SOLVES
 * ============================================================================
 *
 * Every surface on the character was `<meshStandardMaterial color roughness={0.7} />`. Under the
 * island's rig (one ambient, one hemisphere, one directional) that is a plain Lambert ramp on a
 * sphere and four capsules, and it produces three specific failures that read as 「立體感不足」:
 *
 *   1. NO SILHOUETTE. Against the lawn, a mid-tone body has nothing separating its outline from
 *      the ground behind it. The character sits IN the picture instead of standing in front of it.
 *   2. A HARD, FLAT SHADOW SIDE. Lambert falls to the ambient term and stops. Real diffuse
 *      surfaces — skin especially — carry light a little way past the terminator, and drawn
 *      characters exaggerate that into a warm band. Without it the dark side of every limb is one
 *      dead value.
 *   3. NO CONTACT SHADING. Nothing was darker where two parts meet. The underside of the chin,
 *      the inside of an arm against the ribs, the top of a thigh under the hips — all exactly as
 *      bright as the outside of the same part, which is precisely what makes a body read as
 *      「零件拼接」: separately lit primitives sitting near each other.
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * WHY IT IS A TRAVERSAL AND NOT A MATERIAL FACTORY
 * ============================================================================
 *
 * The obvious design is a `skinMaterial()` / `clothMaterial()` pair that the model calls instead
 * of `<meshStandardMaterial>`. It was rejected for the reason section 六 of the character brief
 * exists: **a future character arrives as an imported model, and an imported model brings its own
 * materials.** A factory only reaches surfaces whose authors remembered to call it, so the day a
 * GLB head is dropped in, the head stops being shaded like the body — and nothing fails, it just
 * looks wrong.
 *
 * This walks whatever is under the character root and upgrades every standard material it finds.
 * Legacy's capsules, v2's, an imported GLB's, the wardrobe's sixty-odd pieces, a hat added next
 * year — all of them, with no cooperation required from any of them. That is also why it lives
 * here rather than inside `legacy/`: it is a property of THE CHARACTER, not of one model.
 *
 * ### What it does not touch
 *
 * A material that already carries an `onBeforeCompile` of its own is left alone. That is not
 * politeness, it is correctness: the hair system (legacy/hairShading.ts) caches its materials at
 * MODULE scope and shares them with the shop's thumbnails, so patching one here would both
 * destroy its root-to-tip gradient (there is one `onBeforeCompile` slot) and leak character
 * lighting into the shop. Same for anything else that grows its own shader later.
 *
 * ============================================================================
 * COST
 * ============================================================================
 *
 * One traversal of ~100 objects per render of the character (NOT per frame), and each material is
 * patched exactly once — `needsUpdate` is set on the first visit only, so the recompile happens
 * once per material rather than once per render. Every material built by this file shares ONE
 * `onBeforeCompile` function object, which is how three keys its program cache, so the whole
 * character adds a single compiled program however many materials it ends up with.
 */

import * as THREE from 'three';

/**
 * The key light, world space — restated from Scene.tsx's `<directionalLight position={[20,20,10]}
 * />`, which aims at the origin.
 *
 * A constant rather than a lookup for the same reason hairShading.ts keeps its own copy: the warm
 * bounce below is an ART effect with a deliberately wide falloff, so it wants the scene's light
 * DIRECTION (fixed) and not its per-frame intensity (which the day/night cycle already drives
 * through the light itself). Indoors the interior rig aims its key from much the same quarter, so
 * the same vector serves both canvases.
 */
const KEY_DIR = new THREE.Vector3(20, 20, 10).normalize();

/**
 * How dark a fully downward-facing surface goes, and where the ramp ends.
 *
 * THIS IS THE CONTACT SHADING, and it is worth being clear about why a normal-direction term is
 * the right tool rather than a hack. Everything on this character that reads as "joined" has the
 * same geometry: an overhang. The skull overhangs the shoulders, the jaw overhangs the neck, the
 * arm's underside faces the ground, the hips overhang the thighs. Ambient light in the real world
 * arrives overwhelmingly from the sky, so a surface whose normal points DOWN receives almost none
 * of it — which is exactly the cue that says "there is something above this".
 *
 * The hemisphere light already does a weak version of this (sky colour above, ground colour
 * below), but at 0.5 intensity against a 0.5 ambient it is far too subtle to build form with.
 * This is the same physical idea, drawn like an illustrator: strong enough to see.
 *
 * The floor is deliberately not black. A chibi's underside in shadow should still be its own
 * colour, not a silhouette.
 */
const AO_FLOOR = 0.74;
const AO_RAMP_LOW = -0.85;
const AO_RAMP_HIGH = 0.35;

/**
 * The warm bounce carried past the terminator, and how wide the band is.
 *
 * A narrow warm band exactly where the light dies is the single most recognisable thing about
 * drawn character shading, and on skin it is also literally true — red light scatters furthest
 * under the surface, so the last lit millimetres of a face go warm before they go dark.
 *
 * Added AFTER lighting rather than folded into the BRDF, for the reason hairShading.ts spells out
 * at length: this is a drawing decision about WHERE on the form it sits, not a physical lobe, and
 * a physical approximation on geometry this simple just widens the highlight.
 */
const BOUNCE_COLOR = new THREE.Color('#ffb37a');
const BOUNCE_STRENGTH = 0.11;

/**
 * The rim: a cool sky-toned fresnel, and the only term here whose job is the SILHOUETTE.
 *
 * Physically it is the sky wrapping round the edge of a rounded body, which is why it is a fixed
 * cool tone rather than a shift of the surface's own colour — keeping it independent of what it
 * is drawn on is what makes it work as separation. It cannot come out the same colour as the
 * lawn behind it.
 *
 * Kept low. A strong rim on a soft, low-poly character reads as a plastic toy under a studio
 * light, which is the opposite of this island's 「柔和、溫暖」 direction. At 0.16 it is invisible
 * as an effect and obvious as an improvement — the character simply stops merging into the grass.
 */
const RIM_COLOR = new THREE.Color('#cfe6ff');
const RIM_POWER = 2.8;
const RIM_STRENGTH = 0.16;

const f = (n: number) => n.toFixed(4);
const rgb = (c: THREE.Color) => `vec3(${f(c.r)}, ${f(c.g)}, ${f(c.b)})`;
const xyz = (v: THREE.Vector3) => `vec3(${f(v.x)}, ${f(v.y)}, ${f(v.z)})`;

/**
 * Injected just before `<tonemapping_fragment>`.
 *
 * WHERE this goes is not free, and it is the same trap hairShading.ts documents: that is the last
 * point at which `gl_FragColor` is still LINEAR. One chunk later `<colorspace_fragment>` has
 * encoded it to sRGB, and adding a linear colour to an encoded one double-brightens the addition
 * and clips it. `<dithering_fragment>`, the obvious end-of-shader hook, is on the wrong side of
 * exactly that line.
 */
const SURFACE_GLSL = /* glsl */ `
{
  vec3 N = normalize(normal);
  vec3 V = normalize(vViewPosition);
  // viewMatrix is orthonormal, so multiplying a vector by it on the RIGHT applies its transpose
  // — i.e. its inverse. That turns the shading normal back into world space, which is the frame
  // "which way is up" is a question about.
  vec3 Nw = normalize((vec4(N, 0.0) * viewMatrix).xyz);

  // 1. Ambient occlusion by facing. Everything that overhangs something else darkens under it,
  //    which is what turns six primitives into one body.
  gl_FragColor.rgb *= mix(${f(AO_FLOOR)}, 1.0, smoothstep(${f(AO_RAMP_LOW)}, ${f(AO_RAMP_HIGH)}, Nw.y));

  // 2. Warm bounce, in a band straddling the terminator.
  vec3 L = normalize((viewMatrix * vec4(${xyz(KEY_DIR)}, 0.0)).xyz);
  float ndl = dot(N, L);
  float band = smoothstep(-0.55, 0.1, ndl) * (1.0 - smoothstep(0.08, 0.62, ndl));
  gl_FragColor.rgb += ${rgb(BOUNCE_COLOR)} * (band * ${f(BOUNCE_STRENGTH)});

  // 3. Cool rim, for separation against whatever is behind.
  float fres = pow(1.0 - clamp(abs(dot(N, V)), 0.0, 1.0), ${f(RIM_POWER)});
  gl_FragColor.rgb += ${rgb(RIM_COLOR)} * (fres * ${f(RIM_STRENGTH)});
}
`;

/**
 * ONE function for every material on the character — see the cost note above. It closes over
 * nothing and reads nothing off the material, so three compiles it once for the whole body.
 */
function patchCharacterSurface(shader: THREE.WebGLProgramParametersWithUniforms) {
  shader.fragmentShader = shader.fragmentShader.replace(
    '#include <tonemapping_fragment>',
    `${SURFACE_GLSL}\n#include <tonemapping_fragment>`,
  );
}

/** Marks a material as already handled, so repeat traversals cost a property read. */
const MARK = 'characterSurface';

/**
 * Opt a material OUT of the treatment.
 *
 * For surfaces that are not BODY — a glowing cosmetic, a lens, anything whose look is its own
 * statement. Call it where the material is built; the traversal will then skip it forever.
 */
export function excludeFromCharacterSurface<T extends THREE.Material>(material: T): T {
  material.userData[MARK] = 'excluded';
  return material;
}

/**
 * Whether three's no-op `onBeforeCompile` has been replaced on this instance.
 *
 * `Material.prototype.onBeforeCompile` is an empty function, so a material that has never been
 * patched inherits it and has no OWN property of that name. Anything with one has a shader of its
 * own to protect — see the hair note above.
 */
function hasOwnShader(material: THREE.Material): boolean {
  return Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(material, 'onBeforeCompile');
}

/**
 * Applies the treatment to everything under `root`.
 *
 * Idempotent and cheap to repeat: a material is patched at most once, and every later call is a
 * walk plus one property read per material. Call it whenever the character's subtree may have
 * changed — which in practice means on every render of the component that owns the root, since
 * that is exactly when React has added or removed a wearable.
 */
export function applyCharacterSurface(root: THREE.Object3D | null | undefined): void {
  if (!root) return;

  root.traverse((object) => {
    const mesh = object as THREE.Mesh;
    if (!mesh.isMesh) return;

    /**
     * SELF-SHADOWING, and it is a bigger part of this pass than the shader below.
     *
     * Every body mesh in the game set `castShadow` and NONE of them set `receiveShadow`. The
     * character therefore threw a shadow on the lawn and received none at all — not from the
     * house, not from a tree, and, most visibly, not from ITSELF. No shadow under the chin where
     * a skull overhangs the shoulders by 11 cm; none from an arm swinging across the chest; none
     * under the hips. That is the other half of 「零件拼接」: parts that overlap in space but
     * never in light.
     *
     * Set here rather than on each mesh for the same reason the material patch is: an imported
     * model's meshes come out of a loader with three's defaults (both flags false), so a
     * per-mesh `receiveShadow` in the legacy JSX would be one more thing a new model silently
     * fails to inherit.
     *
     * It costs nothing to draw — a mesh that receives shadows is a shadow-map LOOKUP in a shader
     * that is already doing them for the terrain, not an extra pass. What it does need is the
     * bias tuning on the light (see Scene.tsx), because self-shadowing on curved surfaces is
     * exactly where acne shows.
     */
    mesh.receiveShadow = true;

    const materials = Array.isArray(mesh.material) ? mesh.material : [mesh.material];
    for (const material of materials) {
      if (!material) continue;
      // Standard-lit surfaces only. A MeshBasicMaterial has no lighting to extend and is used
      // here exactly where a flat, unlit look is the point (ripples, splash, VFX).
      if (!(material as THREE.MeshStandardMaterial).isMeshStandardMaterial) continue;
      if (material.userData[MARK]) continue;
      if (hasOwnShader(material)) {
        // Remember the decision, so the next traversal does not re-test it.
        material.userData[MARK] = 'skipped';
        continue;
      }

      material.onBeforeCompile = patchCharacterSurface;
      material.needsUpdate = true;
      material.userData[MARK] = 'applied';
    }
  });
}
```
