## src/components/Three/outdoorAnimation.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import React, { useCallback, useEffect, useMemo, useRef } from 'react';
import { useFrame, useStore } from '@react-three/fiber';
import * as THREE from 'three';
import {
  SuspendedTimeline,
  WindSample,
  advanceWindClock,
  sampleWind,
  seedRange,
  windClock,
  windRotorAngle,
} from '../../lib/outdoorMotion';
import type { WindNodeSpec, WindRotorSpec } from '../../constants/outdoorAnimation';

/**
 * THE OUTDOOR ANIMATION RUNTIME — one loop, one wind sample per object, and a cull.
 *
 * ## What was here before, and why it could not be extended
 *
 * Every animated outdoor piece owned a `useFrame` with its own copy of the same four lines:
 * read the clock, work out how long since the player poked it, lerp a boost, write a rotation.
 * Five pieces did it (swing, campfire, telescope, birdhouse, wishing well) and the pieces the
 * brief is about — the palm, the fountain, the mobile, the hammock — did not move at all,
 * because "add another `useFrame` with another set of magic numbers" is not a thing anyone wants
 * to do for the twentieth object.
 *
 * ## The three things this buys that a per-object `useFrame` cannot
 *
 *  1. **ONE update pass.** R3F already runs a single `requestAnimationFrame` loop and every
 *     `useFrame` is a subscription to it — so the old code was never N loops. What it WAS is N
 *     callbacks each re-deriving the shared state (the clock, the weather's wind multiplier, the
 *     camera). Here that work happens once and the per-object callback receives it.
 *  2. **DISTANCE AND FRUSTUM CULLING.** A palm forty units behind the camera does not evaluate.
 *     This is only safe because every animation in lib/outdoorMotion.ts is a pure function of
 *     time: a culled object is not paused, it is simply not asked, and the frame it comes back it
 *     is instantly at the right pose. There is no state to catch up and nothing pops.
 *  3. **A DETAIL LADDER.** Between "full rate" and "not at all" there are two strides, and
 *     entries are spread across frames by index so a grove of palms never all update on the same
 *     one.
 *
 * ## Why the loop is owned by an entry rather than by a driver component
 *
 * The obvious shape is `<OutdoorAnimationDriver />` mounted once in Three/Scene.tsx. It was
 * rejected because these models are also rendered where no such component exists — the placement
 * ghost, the shop's 3D preview, and (crucially) the build-time audits, which walk the same JSX
 * with a stub hook dispatcher (scripts/lib/measureFurnitureModel.ts). A driver that has to be
 * remembered in four places is a driver that will be forgotten in the fifth.
 *
 * Instead, the FIRST registered animation elects itself owner and runs the pass for everyone;
 * when it unmounts the next one takes over. Every other entry's `useFrame` is an integer compare
 * and a return. Nothing has to be mounted anywhere, and the system works the moment one animated
 * object exists.
 *
 * The one assumption that buys: every registered entry is in the SAME canvas as the owner, since
 * the owner's camera is what the cull is measured against. True by construction here — everything
 * that registers is an outdoor placeable, and outdoor placeables only ever render in the island
 * canvas. The house interior mounts its own Canvas over the island's for ~0.18 s during the door
 * crossfade, and registers nothing.
 */

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the registry */

/** What one animated object is handed each time it runs. Reused in place — never held. */
export interface OutdoorFrame {
  /** The shared wind clock, seconds. Weather-scaled and continuous across weather changes. */
  time: number;
  /** Seconds since THIS entry last ran — already correct under striding. */
  delta: number;
  /** The object's own world position, for sampling the wind field. Reused; copy if you keep it. */
  position: THREE.Vector3;
  /** Distance to the camera, world units. */
  distance: number;
  /** 1 at full rate, 0.5 or 0.25 when strided. Fade an expensive flourish out with it. */
  detail: number;
}

interface Entry {
  token: object;
  anchor: React.RefObject<THREE.Object3D | null>;
  update: (frame: OutdoorFrame) => void;
  radius: number;
  cullDistance: number;
  /** Wind-clock time this entry last ran at, for the delta. */
  last: number;
  /** Fixed slot so entries in the same stride bucket land on different frames. */
  slot: number;
}

/**
 * ONE REGISTRY PER CANVAS, not one per game.
 *
 * This used to be a single module-level `entries` array with a single elected owner, and the
 * module note above justified it with an assumption that has since stopped being true:
 * 「everything that registers is an outdoor placeable, and outdoor placeables only ever render in
 * the island canvas」. The house interior mounts its own `<Canvas>` (BuildingInteriorView.tsx) and
 * registered nothing — so one array WAS one canvas, and the assumption held by accident.
 *
 * The object-interaction pass (Three/objectAnimation.tsx) is what ends that: it puts indoor
 * furniture in here too. With one shared array the two canvases' entries would be culled against
 * whichever camera happens to belong to the elected owner — walk into the house and every indoor
 * drawer is measured against the island camera standing outside the wall, so it either never
 * animates or always does. Neither is a crash, which is exactly why it would have been found late.
 *
 * Keying on the R3F store — one store per `<Canvas>`, by construction — makes the partition
 * structural rather than remembered. The owner election, the frame counter and the stride slots
 * are all per-registry for the same reason.
 */
interface Registry {
  entries: Entry[];
  owner: object | null;
  frameIndex: number;
  slotCounter: number;
}

const registries = new Map<object, Registry>();

function registryFor(store: object): Registry {
  let r = registries.get(store);
  if (!r) {
    r = { entries: [], owner: null, frameIndex: 0, slotCounter: 0 };
    registries.set(store, r);
  }
  return r;
}

/**
 * Inside this, an object always animates at full rate regardless of the frustum.
 *
 * The frustum test asks "is it on screen", and the honest answer for a shadow-caster is "not
 * necessarily the same as: does it matter". A palm just off the left edge of the screen still
 * throws a moving shadow across ground the player CAN see. Rather than reconstruct the shadow
 * camera's own frustum here, everything near the player is exempt — which is where the shadow
 * map has any resolution anyway.
 */
const FRUSTUM_EXEMPT_DISTANCE = 14;
const FULL_RATE_DISTANCE = 22;
const HALF_RATE_DISTANCE = 40;
const DEFAULT_CULL_DISTANCE = 70;

const _camPos = new THREE.Vector3();
const _pos = new THREE.Vector3();
const _projScreen = new THREE.Matrix4();
const _frustum = new THREE.Frustum();
const _sphere = new THREE.Sphere();
const _frame: OutdoorFrame = { time: 0, delta: 0, position: _pos, distance: 0, detail: 1 };

function runPass(reg: Registry, camera: THREE.Camera, delta: number): void {
  const time = advanceWindClock(delta);
  reg.frameIndex++;

  _camPos.setFromMatrixPosition(camera.matrixWorld);
  _projScreen.multiplyMatrices(camera.projectionMatrix, camera.matrixWorldInverse);
  _frustum.setFromProjectionMatrix(_projScreen);

  for (let i = 0; i < reg.entries.length; i++) {
    const e = reg.entries[i];
    const obj = e.anchor.current;
    if (!obj) continue;

    // Read the matrix rather than `getWorldPosition`, which walks and recomposes every ancestor
    // on every call. One frame of staleness is nothing to a cull test, and this is the only
    // per-object cost paid by an object that is about to be skipped.
    _pos.setFromMatrixPosition(obj.matrixWorld);
    const distance = _pos.distanceTo(_camPos);
    if (distance > e.cullDistance) continue;

    if (distance > FRUSTUM_EXEMPT_DISTANCE) {
      _sphere.center.copy(_pos);
      _sphere.radius = e.radius;
      if (!_frustum.intersectsSphere(_sphere)) continue;
    }

    const stride = distance < FULL_RATE_DISTANCE ? 1 : distance < HALF_RATE_DISTANCE ? 2 : 4;
    if (stride > 1 && (reg.frameIndex + e.slot) % stride !== 0) continue;

    _frame.time = time;
    _frame.delta = e.last === 0 ? delta : Math.min(0.25, time - e.last);
    _frame.distance = distance;
    _frame.detail = 1 / stride;
    e.last = time;
    e.update(_frame);
  }
}

export interface OutdoorAnimationOptions {
  /** Bounding radius for the frustum test, world units. Generous is cheap; mean is a pop. */
  radius?: number;
  /** Beyond this the object does not animate at all. */
  cullDistance?: number;
}

/**
 * Registers one animated object.
 *
 * `anchor` is whatever object's world position decides how important this animation is — for a
 * piece of furniture, the model's own root. `update` is called with {@link OutdoorFrame} at
 * whatever rate the cull decides, and must be a pure function of `frame.time` (see the module
 * note): if it integrates, culling will show.
 */
export function useOutdoorAnimation(
  anchor: React.RefObject<THREE.Object3D | null>,
  update: (frame: OutdoorFrame) => void,
  options: OutdoorAnimationOptions = {},
): void {
  const token = useRef<object>({}).current;
  const updateRef = useRef(update);
  updateRef.current = update;
  const { radius = 3, cullDistance = DEFAULT_CULL_DISTANCE } = options;
  // Which canvas this entry belongs to. `useStore` is R3F's own context read, so the audit
  // harness's stub dispatcher (scripts/lib/measureFurnitureModel.ts) answers it like every other
  // hook here — and a MODEL still never touches it, which is the rule that keeps these components
  // callable outside a renderer.
  const store = useStore() as unknown as object;

  useEffect(() => {
    const reg = registryFor(store);
    const entry: Entry = {
      token,
      anchor,
      update: (f) => updateRef.current(f),
      radius,
      cullDistance,
      last: 0,
      slot: reg.slotCounter++,
    };
    reg.entries.push(entry);
    if (reg.owner === null) reg.owner = token;
    return () => {
      const i = reg.entries.indexOf(entry);
      if (i >= 0) reg.entries.splice(i, 1);
      if (reg.owner === token) reg.owner = reg.entries.length > 0 ? reg.entries[0].token : null;
      // The last entry out closes the registry, so a house interior visited fifty times does not
      // leave fifty empty maps behind.
      if (reg.entries.length === 0) registries.delete(store);
    };
  }, [anchor, radius, cullDistance, token, store]);

  useFrame((state, delta) => {
    const reg = registries.get(store);
    if (!reg || reg.owner !== token) return;
    runPass(reg, state.camera, delta);
  });
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ wind rigs */

/** A wind rig node, plus the rest pose the model's own geometry needs it to hold. */
export type WindRigNode = WindNodeSpec & {
  /** The node's own rotation with no wind — a trunk section's lean, a frond's droop. */
  /**
   * The pose the node holds with no wind — a trunk’s lean, a frond’s droop.
   *
   * Only X and Z are used. Yaw belongs to the model (see the write in the frame callback), so
   * a part that has to point somewhere states that with an ordinary `rotation={[0, a, 0]}` in
   * its own JSX and the rig will not touch it.
   */
  rest?: readonly [number, number, number];
};

export interface WindRigOptions extends OutdoorAnimationOptions {
  /**
   * Per-instance variation, from the placement's instance id.
   *
   * 「避免畫面中所有椰子樹像複製貼上一樣同時移動」 has FOUR independent answers, and this is
   * only one of them — the wind field itself is spatial, so two plants standing apart are already
   * reading different parts of the same gust. The seed adds the rest: a phase offset, a rate and
   * a gain, so two plants standing in the SAME place (the shop preview, a tight cluster) still
   * differ.
   */
  seed?: string | number;
  /** Scales every node's bend — a small palm should not sway as far as a big one. */
  gain?: number;
}

export interface WindRig<K extends string> {
  /** Attach to the group this node bends. Stable across renders. */
  ref: (key: K) => (o: THREE.Object3D | null) => void;
}

const ZERO_REST = [0, 0, 0] as const;
const _wind: WindSample = { sway: 0, cross: 0, gust: 0 };

/**
 * A chain of groups that bend in the wind, driven as ONE registry entry.
 *
 * The nodes are a plain object because that is what makes a plant readable at the call site:
 * `{ trunkA: …, trunkB: …, crown: …, frond0: … }` next to the JSX that uses them. One entry for
 * the whole plant matters — a palm has thirteen bending parts, and thirteen registry entries per
 * tree would put a grove of twenty back where it started.
 *
 * The key SET is read once. A model's rig is a fixed piece of its own structure, so a node table
 * that grew or shrank between renders would be a bug rather than a feature.
 */
export function useWindRig<K extends string>(
  anchor: React.RefObject<THREE.Object3D | null>,
  nodes: Record<K, WindRigNode>,
  options: WindRigOptions = {},
): WindRig<K> {
  const nodesRef = useRef(nodes);
  nodesRef.current = nodes;
  // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  const keys = useMemo(() => Object.keys(nodes) as K[], []);
  const targets = useRef<Partial<Record<K, THREE.Object3D | null>>>({});
  const setters = useRef<Partial<Record<K, (o: THREE.Object3D | null) => void>>>({});

  const ref = useCallback((key: K): ((o: THREE.Object3D | null) => void) => {
    const existing = setters.current[key];
    if (existing) return existing;
    const setter = (o: THREE.Object3D | null) => { targets.current[key] = o; };
    setters.current[key] = setter;
    return setter;
  }, []);

  const { seed, gain = 1, radius = 3, cullDistance } = options;
  // Three seeded constants, resolved once. `rate` is applied as a time-varying lag rather than by
  // scaling a clock: sampling the shared field at `(1 - rate) * t` seconds in the past IS running
  // at `rate` times its speed, and it keeps the whole system a pure function of one clock.
  const variation = useMemo(() => ({
    phase: seedRange(seed, 1, 0, 7),
    gain: seedRange(seed, 2, 0.82, 1.2) * gain,
    rate: seedRange(seed, 3, 0.86, 1.18),
  }), [seed, gain]);

  useOutdoorAnimation(anchor, (frame) => {
    const drift = variation.phase + (1 - variation.rate) * frame.time;
    for (let i = 0; i < keys.length; i++) {
      const key = keys[i];
      const node = targets.current[key];
      if (!node) continue;
      const spec = nodesRef.current[key];
      if (!spec) continue;

      sampleWind(frame.position.x, frame.position.z, (spec.lag ?? 0) + drift, _wind);
      const bend = spec.bend * variation.gain;
      const cross = bend * (spec.cross ?? 0);
      const rest = spec.rest ?? ZERO_REST;
      // Y IS THE MODEL’S, NOT THE RIG’S.
      //
      // Bending is a lean — it lives entirely in X and Z (`bend` and `cross` write nothing
      // else). Yaw is how a model LAYS ITS PARTS OUT: the eight blades of a 草叢, the four
      // fronds of a 蕨類, the four leaves of a 小型葉片植物 and the three tufts of a
      // 野生植物叢 are all one shape repeated at `rotation={[0, a, 0]}` around the stem.
      //
      // Writing the whole Euler triple used to overwrite that yaw with `rest[1]`, which is 0
      // for every node in the project — so on the first animated frame all eight blades, all
      // four fronds and all four leaves snapped to the SAME heading and stacked on top of one
      // another. The plants were drawing a quarter of the parts they were built from, and the
      // build-time audits could not see it: they measure the React tree, where the JSX rotation
      // is still there, so every count and every collider was right. Only the running game was
      // wrong, and it read as "these plants are sparse" rather than as a bug.
      //
      // Assigning the two axes the rig actually drives leaves yaw where the model put it. No
      // rig node in the project has ever declared a non-zero `rest[1]`, so nothing that was
      // working depends on the old behaviour.
      if (spec.axis === 'x') {
        node.rotation.x = rest[0] + _wind.sway * bend;
        node.rotation.z = rest[2] + _wind.cross * cross;
      } else {
        node.rotation.x = rest[0] + _wind.cross * cross;
        node.rotation.z = rest[2] + _wind.sway * bend;
      }
    }
  }, { radius, cullDistance });

  return { ref };
}

/**
 * A part the wind TURNS rather than bends — the mobile's arms, and any future windmill or vane.
 *
 * The angle comes from `windRotorAngle`, which is the gust envelope integrated in closed form, so
 * the rotor accelerates in a gust and coasts nearly to a stall in a lull while remaining a pure
 * function of time. `tilt` adds a small wobble on the two other axes so the thing reads as hung
 * rather than as bolted to a motor.
 */
export function useWindRotor(
  anchor: React.RefObject<THREE.Object3D | null>,
  target: React.RefObject<THREE.Object3D | null>,
  spec: WindRotorSpec,
  options: WindRigOptions & { tilt?: number } = {},
): void {
  const { seed, radius = 3, cullDistance, tilt = 0 } = options;
  const variation = useMemo(() => ({
    phase: seedRange(seed, 4, 0, 7),
    offset: seedRange(seed, 5, 0, Math.PI * 2),
  }), [seed]);
  const specRef = useRef(spec);
  specRef.current = spec;

  useOutdoorAnimation(anchor, (frame) => {
    const node = target.current;
    if (!node) return;
    const s = specRef.current;
    const angle = windRotorAngle(frame.position.x, frame.position.z, s.turnsPerSecond);
    node.rotation.y = variation.offset + angle * (s.direction ?? 1);
    if (tilt !== 0) {
      sampleWind(frame.position.x, frame.position.z, variation.phase, _wind);
      node.rotation.x = _wind.cross * tilt;
      node.rotation.z = _wind.sway * tilt;
    }
  }, { radius, cullDistance });
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ occupancy */

/**
 * WHEN THE PLAYER GOT ON THIS PIECE, and when they got off.
 *
 * The sibling of the press-driven object reactions (Three/objectAnimation.tsx's
 * `useObjectAnimation`), and the reason it could not just be one of them: a press is an INSTANT
 * (the player pressed E and the telescope chimed), while an occupancy is an INTERVAL, and a swing
 * needs to know how long it has been ridden rather than how long ago it was poked.
 *
 * The timestamps travel ON the event rather than being sampled here, so the model and
 * Three/Avatar.tsx — which dispatches it — are working from the identical number rather than from
 * two `performance.now()` calls that happen to be close. That is what makes the seat and the body
 * exactly, not approximately, in step.
 */
export function useFurnitureOccupancy(instanceId: string | undefined): React.RefObject<SuspendedTimeline> {
  const timeline = useRef<SuspendedTimeline>({ mountedAt: null, releasedAt: null, rode: 0 });

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!instanceId) return;
    const onOccupy = (e: Event) => {
      const d = (e as CustomEvent<{ instanceId?: string; at?: number }>).detail;
      if (d?.instanceId !== instanceId) return;
      timeline.current.mountedAt = d.at ?? performance.now();
    };
    const onRelease = (e: Event) => {
      const d = (e as CustomEvent<{ instanceId?: string; at?: number }>).detail;
      if (d?.instanceId !== instanceId) return;
      const at = d.at ?? performance.now();
      if (timeline.current.mountedAt != null) {
        timeline.current.rode = (at - timeline.current.mountedAt) / 1000;
      }
      timeline.current.mountedAt = null;
      timeline.current.releasedAt = at;
    };
    window.addEventListener('furniture-occupy', onOccupy);
    window.addEventListener('furniture-release', onRelease);
    return () => {
      window.removeEventListener('furniture-occupy', onOccupy);
      window.removeEventListener('furniture-release', onRelease);
    };
  }, [instanceId]);

  return timeline;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ water */

/**
 * WATER, as three composable pieces rather than as one fountain.
 *
 * The brief asks for a fountain and rules out a fluid simulation, so what is left is the question
 * of what the CHEAPEST honest reading of falling water is. The answer these three settle on: a
 * viewer believes water when they can see where it comes from, where it goes, and that the
 * surface it lands on notices. Three components, one for each of those, and any future stream,
 * spout or pond gets them without a line of new animation code.
 *
 * Every mesh they draw declares `depthWrite={false}`, which is not only correct for stacked
 * translucent water — it is also the flag both the shipping collider (lib/collisionShape.ts) and
 * the quality audit (scripts/audit-outdoor-quality.ts) already use to tell "a drawn effect" from
 * "a part of the object". Water therefore cannot change where the player is allowed to stand, and
 * cannot inflate a model's structure score.
 */

const WATER_LIGHT = '#bae6fd';

export interface WaterJetProps {
  /** The nozzle mouth. */
  from: readonly [number, number, number];
  /** How far above the mouth the arc peaks. */
  rise: number;
  /** Radius the droplets land at, measured from the mouth. */
  spread: number;
  /** The height they land on — a bowl's water, the pool. */
  landY: number;
  /** Droplets in flight at once. Four reads as a jet; more is a cost with no picture behind it. */
  count?: number;
  /** Flights per second. */
  rate?: number;
  size?: number;
  color?: string;
}

/**
 * Water thrown up out of a nozzle and falling back into a bowl.
 *
 * The arc is a straight line from mouth to landing point plus a parabolic bump, rather than a
 * ballistic solve. A real projectile whose apex is where a garden fountain's looks would have to
 * be launched hard enough to overshoot the model entirely; stating the apex directly is both
 * cheaper and the only way to keep the water inside the piece — which is the brief's
 * 「水落點明顯不合理」 in reverse.
 */
export function WaterJet({
  from, rise, spread, landY, count = 4, rate = 1.1, size = 0.045, color = WATER_LIGHT,
}: WaterJetProps) {
  const groupRef = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);
  const drops = useRef<(THREE.Mesh | null)[]>([]);
  const seeds = useMemo(
    () => Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) => ({
      azimuth: (i / count) * Math.PI * 2 + 0.4,
      offset: i / count,
    })),
    [count],
  );

  useOutdoorAnimation(groupRef, ({ time }) => {
    for (let i = 0; i < seeds.length; i++) {
      const mesh = drops.current[i];
      if (!mesh) continue;
      const s = seeds[i];
      const p = (time * rate + s.offset) % 1;
      const r = spread * p;
      // Linear fall from mouth to landing, plus a bump that peaks halfway. `4 * p * (1 - p)` is
      // the unit parabola through (0,0) and (1,0) with a maximum of 1 at the middle.
      const y = from[1] + (landY - from[1]) * p + rise * 4 * p * (1 - p);
      mesh.position.set(from[0] + Math.cos(s.azimuth) * r, y, from[2] + Math.sin(s.azimuth) * r);
      // Fades out as it lands rather than vanishing — 「避免水流突然消失」.
      const fade = p > 0.78 ? (1 - p) / 0.22 : 1;
      mesh.scale.setScalar(size * (0.7 + 0.3 * Math.sin(p * Math.PI)) * fade);
    }
  }, { radius: 2 });

  return (
    <group ref={groupRef}>
      {seeds.map((_, i) => (
        <mesh key={i} ref={(el) => { drops.current[i] = el; }}>
          <sphereGeometry args={[1, 6, 5]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial
            color={color}
            emissive={color}
            emissiveIntensity={0.45}
            transparent
            opacity={0.75}
            depthWrite={false}
          />
        </mesh>
      ))}
    </group>
  );
}

export interface WaterFallsProps {
  /** Where each stream leaves its rim. */
  spouts: readonly (readonly [number, number, number])[];
  /** The height the streams land on. */
  landY: number;
  /** Radius of the splash ring at each landing point. */
  splash?: number;
  size?: number;
  rate?: number;
  color?: string;
}

/**
 * Streams running off a rim, and the rings they make where they land.
 *
 * One droplet per stream, not a column of them: the static tapered cylinder in the model already
 * IS the stream, and what a low-poly falling stream is missing is not more water, it is EVIDENCE
 * OF MOTION. A single bead running down it at a believable speed supplies that for one draw call.
 */
export function WaterFalls({
  spouts, landY, splash = 0.16, size = 0.05, rate = 0.85, color = WATER_LIGHT,
}: WaterFallsProps) {
  const groupRef = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);
  const drops = useRef<(THREE.Mesh | null)[]>([]);
  const rings = useRef<(THREE.Mesh | null)[]>([]);

  useOutdoorAnimation(groupRef, ({ time }) => {
    for (let i = 0; i < spouts.length; i++) {
      const s = spouts[i];
      const offset = i / spouts.length;
      const p = (time * rate + offset) % 1;

      const drop = drops.current[i];
      if (drop) {
        // Accelerating, because water does: `p * p` puts the bead slow at the lip and quick at
        // the pool, which is most of what reads as "falling" rather than "sliding".
        const fall = p * p;
        drop.position.set(s[0], s[1] + (landY - s[1]) * fall, s[2]);
        drop.scale.setScalar(size * (0.75 + fall * 0.45) * (p > 0.9 ? (1 - p) / 0.1 : 1));
      }

      const ring = rings.current[i];
      if (ring) {
        // The splash belongs to the bead that just landed, so it runs on the same phase shifted
        // by one flight — the ring opens exactly when a bead reaches the water.
        const rp = (p + 0.06) % 1;
        const grow = rp < 0.5 ? rp / 0.5 : 0;
        ring.scale.setScalar(0.0001 + splash * grow);
        const mat = ring.material as THREE.MeshStandardMaterial;
        mat.opacity = grow > 0 ? 0.5 * (1 - grow) : 0;
      }
    }
  }, { radius: 2.5 });

  return (
    <group ref={groupRef}>
      {spouts.map((s, i) => (
        <React.Fragment key={i}>
          <mesh ref={(el) => { drops.current[i] = el; }}>
            <sphereGeometry args={[1, 6, 5]} />
            <meshStandardMaterial
              color={color}
              emissive={color}
              emissiveIntensity={0.4}
              transparent
              opacity={0.8}
              depthWrite={false}
            />
          </mesh>
          <mesh position={[s[0], landY + 0.02, s[2]]} rotation={[-Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} ref={(el) => { rings.current[i] = el; }}>
            <ringGeometry args={[0.62, 1, 12]} />
            <meshStandardMaterial
              color={color}
              emissive={color}
              emissiveIntensity={0.5}
              transparent
              opacity={0}
              depthWrite={false}
            />
          </mesh>
        </React.Fragment>
      ))}
    </group>
  );
}

/** One still water surface a ripple opens on. */
export interface WaterSurface {
  /** Its centre, at the water's own height. */
  at: readonly [number, number, number];
  /** How far a ring opens before it fades — the surface's own radius, near enough. */
  radius: number;
}

export interface WaterRipplesProps {
  /**
   * Every surface this one entry animates.
   *
   * Per-surface radius rather than one shared number, so a fountain's pool and its upper bowl —
   * which differ by a factor of three — are ONE registry entry rather than two. A future pond
   * with a birdbath beside it is the same call.
   */
  surfaces: readonly WaterSurface[];
  /** Rings in flight per surface. */
  count?: number;
  rate?: number;
  color?: string;
}

/** Rings opening and fading on a still surface — the 「水面有輕微動態效果」 half of the brief. */
export function WaterRipples({
  surfaces, count = 2, rate = 0.32, color = WATER_LIGHT,
}: WaterRipplesProps) {
  const groupRef = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);
  const rings = useRef<(THREE.Mesh | null)[]>([]);
  // Flattened once so the per-frame loop is a straight walk rather than two nested ones.
  const plan = useMemo(
    () => surfaces.flatMap((s, si) => Array.from({ length: count }, (_, ci) => ({
      at: s.at, radius: s.radius, phase: (ci / count) + si * 0.37,
    }))),
    [surfaces, count],
  );

  useOutdoorAnimation(groupRef, ({ time }) => {
    for (let i = 0; i < plan.length; i++) {
      const mesh = rings.current[i];
      if (!mesh) continue;
      const p = (time * rate + plan[i].phase) % 1;
      mesh.scale.setScalar(0.0001 + plan[i].radius * p);
      const mat = mesh.material as THREE.MeshStandardMaterial;
      // Opens from nothing and fades to nothing, so a ring never appears or disappears with an
      // edge — the same reason the jet's droplets fade rather than being switched off.
      mat.opacity = 0.34 * Math.sin(p * Math.PI) * (1 - p * 0.4);
    }
  }, { radius: 2.5 });

  return (
    <group ref={groupRef}>
      {plan.map((r, index) => (
        <mesh
          key={index}
          position={[r.at[0], r.at[1] + 0.012, r.at[2]]}
          rotation={[-Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]}
          ref={(el) => { rings.current[index] = el; }}
        >
          <ringGeometry args={[0.78, 1, 16]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial
            color={color}
            emissive={color}
            emissiveIntensity={0.4}
            transparent
            opacity={0}
            depthWrite={false}
          />
        </mesh>
      ))}
    </group>
  );
}

export { windClock };
```

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * Shared GLSL noise, injected into the procedural surface materials.
 *
 * This block used to live inside floorMaterial.ts. It moved here when
 * wallMaterial.ts needed exactly the same four helpers: two copies of a hash
 * function is two copies that can be tuned apart, and a floor and the wall
 * above it drifting to different grain would be visible in one glance.
 *
 * Cheap value noise + fbm, enough for grain, mottle and veining, plus a
 * softened line used for grout, plank joints and mortar.
 */
export const NOISE_GLSL = `
  float fHash(vec2 p) {
    p = fract(p * vec2(123.34, 456.21));
    p += dot(p, p + 45.32);
    return fract(p.x * p.y);
  }
  float fNoise(vec2 p) {
    vec2 i = floor(p), f = fract(p);
    f = f * f * (3.0 - 2.0 * f);
    return mix(
      mix(fHash(i), fHash(i + vec2(1.0, 0.0)), f.x),
      mix(fHash(i + vec2(0.0, 1.0)), fHash(i + vec2(1.0, 1.0)), f.x),
      f.y
    );
  }
  float fFbm(vec2 p) {
    float v = 0.0, a = 0.5;
    for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) { v += a * fNoise(p); p *= 2.03; a *= 0.5; }
    return v;
  }
  // Softened line: 1 on the line, 0 off it. Half-width w is in world units.
  float fLine(float d, float w, float soft) {
    return 1.0 - smoothstep(w, w + soft, abs(d));
  }
`;
```

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * THE WATER POSE.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Why this file exists
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 *
 * The water animation used to be two poses, not one. Avatar.tsx held a `proneTilt` of
 * +PI/2.2 (+81.8deg, face down in the water) for "moving" and a `floatTilt` of -PI/2.05
 * (-87.8deg, flat on your back) for "idle", and every limb chain picked between two
 * completely unrelated curves with a bare `if (isMoving.current)`. Letting go of WASD
 * therefore asked the body to travel 169.6deg - through upright - while the arms cut in
 * one frame from a full-circle freestyle windmill to a starfish back-float. That is the
 * flip, the lie-down and the limb snap, and no transition duration can hide it: the two
 * endpoints simply were not the same character.
 *
 * So the fix is not a blend rate. It is that THERE IS ONLY ONE WATER POSE. Floating and
 * swimming share a single body attitude, a single head angle, a single limb rest pose and
 * a single surface bob; the ONLY difference between them is how big the arms and legs
 * move, which is a continuous 0..1 amplitude. Starting to swim adds motion. It never
 * re-orients anything.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * The two weights and the one phase
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 *
 * Everything here is driven by exactly three numbers, all owned by Avatar.tsx:
 *
 *   pose   0..1  How much water pose there is at all. 0 = the land pose, 1 = fully
 *                floating. Land <-> water enter/exit rides this, and so do the shallows:
 *                it is the transition progress TIMES swimPitchAllowance(), so a character
 *                wading in ankle-deep is a partial pose rather than a special case.
 *   stroke 0..1  How hard the character is swimming: pose * moveWeight. Amplitude only -
 *                it must never appear in a base angle, because a base angle that moves
 *                with it is exactly the flip this file exists to delete.
 *   phase  rad   The stroke cycle. ALWAYS advancing while there is any water pose, at a
 *                rate that eases between a slow idle scull and the actual travel speed.
 *                Never frozen and never reset, so no state change can land the limbs on a
 *                stale angle.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Sign conventions (all verified against the rig, do not guess these)
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 *
 * ROOT PITCH  Positive is face-down. The root's origin is the character's FEET, so a
 *             pitch of `t` swings the whole body forward about the ankles and leaves the
 *             head at `headJointY * cos(t)` above the feet. t = PI/2 is exactly
 *             horizontal; LESS than that is head-up, which is the whole point of
 *             SWIM_BODY_PITCH below.
 * ARM / LEG   The limb hangs along -Y from its joint, so `rotation.x = p` puts the hand at
 *             (0, -cos p, -sin p) in body space. In the pitched water frame body +Y points
 *             the way the character swims and body +Z points down into the water. So
 *             p = -PI/2 is the hand straight down into the water, p = -PI is reaching
 *             ahead, p = 0 is back at the hip. For the legs the same axis means POSITIVE
 *             lifts the feet toward the surface.
 * HEAD        Negative rotation.x looks UP, i.e. it gives back the body's forward pitch.
 * TORSO       rotation.y rolls the shoulders about the spine once the body is horizontal.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Blending against the land pose
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 *
 * Each channel is returned as a `{ base, osc }` pair rather than one angle, and that split
 * is load-bearing. `base` is where the limb rests in the water and is blended against the
 * land value along the SHORTEST ARC (see blendSwimAngle); `osc` is the stroke motion and
 * is simply scaled by the pose weight. Collapsing the two into a single angle before
 * blending would make the shortest arc depend on where in the stroke cycle the character
 * happened to be when it entered the water - and near the +-PI wrap that flips the
 * direction the arm travels, which is a windmill on the way into the sea.
 */

/**
 * The shared body attitude, radians of forward pitch, applied at pose = 1.
 *
 * 1.24 rad is 71deg: 19deg off horizontal, head end up. With the shipped rig (head joint
 * 0.68 LOCAL x 2.25 = 1.53 world above the feet) that carries the face
 * 1.53 * cos(71deg) = 0.50 world above the root, and the root floats at SWIM_BODY_Y
 * (0.1 below the waterline), so the face rides ~0.4 above the surface and the shoulders
 * ~0.19 above it. Chest higher than the legs, face clear of the water, body still reading
 * as horizontal - which is the brief.
 *
 * The old prone value (81.8deg) put the face 0.12 above the root, i.e. AT the waterline
 * with the skull mostly under it. That is the "face down, sunk" pose, and it came from
 * copying competitive freestyle, where the swimmer breathes to the side. A cozy swim does
 * not do that; it keeps its face out.
 */
export const SWIM_BODY_PITCH = 1.24;

/**
 * Extra forward lean at stroke = 1, added to SWIM_BODY_PITCH.
 *
 * Deliberately tiny. This is the ONLY base angle in this file allowed to move with the
 * stroke weight, and 0.10 rad (5.7deg) is about the limit of what can move without reading
 * as a change of pose - it lands the face 0.25 above the surface instead of 0.4, so the
 * character still never gets its face wet. It exists because "leans in slightly as it sets
 * off" is what the transition into swimming should look like, and because the alternative -
 * the body doing nothing at all when you press W - reads as the arms being detached from
 * the character.
 */
export const SWIM_STROKE_LEAN = 0.10;

/**
 * The absolute angle from vertical that the legs trail at, whatever the body is doing.
 *
 * The legs are stated in WORLD terms and converted to a hip angle by subtracting the body
 * pitch, so that the extra stroke lean tips the legs UP by exactly as much as it tips the
 * chest DOWN and the legs keep skimming the same depth. Stated as a hip angle instead, the
 * lean would drive the feet 0.1 rad deeper every time the player pressed W.
 *
 * 1.44 rad is 82.5deg, i.e. 7.5deg below horizontal: the feet sit ~0.16 world below the
 * hips, just under the surface, which is where a floating pair of legs actually hangs.
 * Exactly horizontal (PI/2) would lift them clear of the water.
 */
export const SWIM_LEG_LINE = 1.44;

/**
 * How far below horizontal the face is left pointing, once the head has given back the
 * body's pitch. The direct analogue of CRAWL_HEAD_GAZE in Avatar.tsx, and for the same
 * reason: the pitch is applied to the whole group, head included, so without this the face
 * points wherever the spine does.
 *
 * 0.30 rad (17deg down) looks a body length or two ahead along the surface. Zero would
 * crane the neck fully back; the old +0.12 (a chin TUCK, on top of an 82deg body pitch)
 * aimed the face straight into the sea floor.
 */
export const SWIM_HEAD_GAZE = 0.30;

/**
 * Stroke cycle rate, radians/second.
 *
 * IDLE is the floating scull - one full cycle every ~5.5s, slow enough to read as resting.
 * The moving rate is the travel speed times PER_SPEED, clamped: the brief's "animation
 * speed follows movement speed, with a sane minimum and maximum". At the shipped swim speed
 * (5.47 world units/s) that lands at 3.39 rad/s, one arm cycle per 1.85s - a relaxed
 * touring stroke. For reference the old code ran the arms off walkPhase at 9.6 rad/s, a
 * stroke every 0.65s, which is a large part of why swimming read as frantic.
 */
export const SWIM_IDLE_CYCLE = 1.15;
export const SWIM_CYCLE_PER_SPEED = 0.62;
export const SWIM_CYCLE_MIN = 2.2;
export const SWIM_CYCLE_MAX = 5.4;

/** Flutter kick rate as a multiple of the arm cycle. Two-and-a-bit beats per stroke. */
export const SWIM_KICK_RATIO = 2.5;

/** Surface bob: amplitude in WORLD units, rate in rad/s. Identical in both states. */
export const SWIM_BOB_AMP = 0.05;
export const SWIM_BOB_RATE = 0.9;

const clamp01 = (v: number) => (v < 0 ? 0 : v > 1 ? 1 : v);
const lerp = (a: number, b: number, t: number) => a + (b - a) * t;

/** One channel of the pose: a resting angle plus the stroke motion riding on it. */
export interface SwimChannel {
  /** Where the limb rests in the water. Blended against the land pose by shortest arc. */
  base: number;
  /** Stroke motion about `base`. Scaled by the pose weight, never blended as an angle. */
  osc: number;
}

const ch = (base: number, osc: number): SwimChannel => ({ base, osc });

/**
 * Which way the character is actually travelling, in its OWN frame - the whole of this
 * file's answer to "the animation must not assume the character only ever swims forward".
 *
 * In third person these are always (1, 0): the controller yaws the body to face the
 * movement direction, so W/A/S/D are already correct and these terms vanish. They earn
 * their keep in first person and at high zoom, where the yaw is locked to the camera and
 * S genuinely means "swim backwards" and A/D genuinely mean "swim sideways".
 *
 * Nothing here writes to the controller. This is read off the movement vector the
 * controller already produced.
 */
export interface SwimDrive {
  /** +1 travelling the way the body faces, -1 straight backwards. */
  forward: number;
  /** +1 travelling to the body's right, -1 to its left. */
  strafe: number;
}

export const SWIM_DRIVE_FORWARD: SwimDrive = { forward: 1, strafe: 0 };

/**
 * Radians the stroke cycle advances per second.
 *
 * `speed` is the character's ACTUAL horizontal speed this frame, not a constant, so any
 * future swim-speed feat or slowdown moves the arms with it for free. The clamp is what
 * stops that becoming "the faster you go the more the character vibrates".
 */
export function swimCycleRate(stroke: number, speed: number): number {
  const travelling = Math.min(SWIM_CYCLE_MAX, Math.max(SWIM_CYCLE_MIN, speed * SWIM_CYCLE_PER_SPEED));
  return lerp(SWIM_IDLE_CYCLE, travelling, clamp01(stroke));
}

/** The body's forward pitch for a given stroke weight. The one shared attitude. */
export function swimBodyPitch(stroke: number): number {
  return SWIM_BODY_PITCH + SWIM_STROKE_LEAN * clamp01(stroke);
}

/**
 * Root motion: the surface itself. Present identically whether floating or swimming, so
 * that starting and stopping never changes the rhythm the body rides on.
 *
 * `roll` carries the stroke's shoulder dip (locked to the arm phase, so the body rotates
 * toward whichever hand is pulling) plus a slow swell that is there even at rest, plus a
 * lean into the direction of travel when strafing. All three are small on purpose - the
 * brief's "rotation amplitude should be very small" - and they sum to well under 0.12 rad.
 */
export function swimRootMotion(time: number, phase: number, stroke: number, drive: SwimDrive) {
  const s = clamp01(stroke);
  return {
    /** WORLD units, added to the float height. */
    bob: Math.sin(time * SWIM_BOB_RATE) * SWIM_BOB_AMP,
    /** Radians, added to swimBodyPitch(). */
    pitchWobble: Math.sin(time * 0.73) * 0.018,
    /** Radians about the body's own forward axis. */
    roll:
      Math.sin(phase) * lerp(0.022, 0.055, s) +
      Math.sin(time * 0.55) * 0.02 +
      drive.strafe * 0.16 * s,
  };
}

/**
 * The arms. One formula for floating and for swimming - only the numbers it interpolates
 * between change, which is what makes "start swimming" an amplitude ramp instead of a cut.
 *
 * The hand traces an ELLIPSE, not a line: `x` (fore-aft) and `z` (out-in) run in
 * quadrature, so over one cycle the hand goes forward, down, back along the body, then out
 * and around to the front again. That circulation is what reads as a stroke rather than as
 * sculling, and it is what lets the same curve serve the idle - shrink the ellipse and the
 * hand simply drifts in a small slow oval by the hip.
 *
 * Base angles are stated in the NEGATIVE representation (-1.33 rather than its equivalent
 * 4.95) so that the shortest arc from the land pose is unambiguous - see the module note.
 *
 * @param side -1 for the left arm, +1 for the right.
 */
export function swimArmPose(side: -1 | 1, phase: number, stroke: number, drive: SwimDrive) {
  const s = clamp01(stroke);
  // Arms alternate. Half a cycle apart is the whole of "never let both arms do the same
  // thing at the same time" - one reaches while the other pulls.
  const p = side < 0 ? phase : phase + Math.PI;

  // Resting angle: -1.33 rad hangs the hand below the chest (the treading-water scull),
  // -2.13 carries it forward into the middle of a pull. Under 0.8 rad apart, so even the
  // base shift between floating and swimming is a small, believable reach.
  const centre = lerp(-1.33, -2.13, s);
  // Sweep: 0.16 rad is a lazy drift, 0.72 a compact cozy pull. The old freestyle ran a
  // full unbounded revolution, which cannot be faded out at all.
  const sweep = lerp(0.16, 0.72, s);
  // Out from the body: wide and relaxed while floating, tucked in while stroking.
  const spread = lerp(0.40, 0.22, s);
  const flare = lerp(0.06, 0.26, s);

  // Strafing: the arm on the side being travelled toward reaches wider, the trailing one
  // pulls harder - a lopsided scull, which is what sculling sideways looks like.
  const asym = 1 + drive.strafe * side * 0.3 * s;

  // `side` IS the sign of rotation.z: negative is outboard on the left, positive on the
  // right, which is the convention the land pose states as `rotation.z = -baseTilt` on the
  // left and `+baseTilt` on the right. Both terms therefore carry it - an outboard amount
  // multiplied by the side - rather than being written out per arm.
  return {
    x: ch(centre, sweep * Math.sin(p) * asym),
    // The cos runs NEGATIVE: most outboard where the hand is swinging FORWARD (recovery,
    // elbow leading) and most tucked where it is pulling back along the body.
    z: ch(side * spread, -side * flare * Math.cos(p)),
    y: ch(0, side * 0.14 * Math.cos(p) * s),
  };
}

/**
 * The legs. A small flutter, and deliberately not the main event: the brief asks for the
 * legs to sell "is swimming" from the corner of the eye and nothing more.
 *
 * @param pitch The body pitch actually in use, so the trail line stays put - see
 *              SWIM_LEG_LINE.
 */
export function swimLegPose(side: -1 | 1, phase: number, stroke: number, pitch: number) {
  const s = clamp01(stroke);
  const kick = phase * SWIM_KICK_RATIO + (side < 0 ? 0 : Math.PI);
  return {
    x: ch(SWIM_LEG_LINE - pitch, Math.sin(kick) * lerp(0.045, 0.20, s)),
    z: ch(side * lerp(0.14, 0.05, s), 0),
  };
}

/**
 * The head. The single most visible thing in the old pose and the one the brief is most
 * insistent about: the face comes out of the water and stays out.
 *
 * The base gives back all but SWIM_HEAD_GAZE of the body pitch, so the face points along
 * the surface however the body is leaning. The oscillation is a small yaw with the stroke
 * (the head turning slightly toward the pulling arm) and nothing on the pitch axis at all,
 * because bobbing the head up and down is exactly what makes a swim look like drowning.
 */
export function swimHeadPose(phase: number, stroke: number, pitch: number, drive: SwimDrive) {
  const s = clamp01(stroke);
  return {
    x: ch(-(pitch - SWIM_HEAD_GAZE), 0),
    // Look where you are going: in first person a strafe means the character is genuinely
    // travelling sideways, so the head leads it.
    y: ch(drive.strafe * 0.25 * s, Math.sin(phase) * 0.14 * s),
    z: ch(0, Math.sin(phase) * 0.05 * s),
  };
}

/**
 * The torso. A small counter-roll to the root's, which is what turns "the whole avatar
 * tips" into "the shoulders rotate with the stroke".
 */
export function swimTorsoPose(phase: number, stroke: number) {
  const s = clamp01(stroke);
  return { y: ch(0, Math.sin(phase) * lerp(0.05, 0.16, s)) };
}

/**
 * Blends one channel against the land pose.
 *
 * The base takes the SHORTEST arc, so a limb never travels the long way round on the way
 * into or out of the water; the stroke motion is faded in by weight rather than blended,
 * for the reason given in the module note.
 */
export function blendSwimAngle(landValue: number, channel: SwimChannel, weight: number): number {
  const w = clamp01(weight);
  let diff = channel.base - landValue;
  while (diff < -Math.PI) diff += Math.PI * 2;
  while (diff > Math.PI) diff -= Math.PI * 2;
  return landValue + diff * w + channel.osc * w;
}

/**
 * Smoothstep for the enter/exit water progress.
 *
 * The state machine hands out a LINEAR 0..1, and a linear ramp has corners: velocity
 * appears and disappears in one frame at both ends, which is visible on a whole-body pitch
 * change however short it is. Easing it is not "increasing the transition duration" - the
 * duration is unchanged, this is the shape.
 */
export function swimEase(p: number): number {
  const t = clamp01(p);
  return t * t * (3 - 2 * t);
}
```

```tsx
/**

import { memo, useRef } from 'react';
import { useFrame } from '@react-three/fiber';
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { PetSpec, getPetBreed, getPetSpec, getPetSpecies } from '../../constants/pets';

/**
 * 寵物 — the companion that stands beside the character once its rack entry is switched on.
 *
 * Built from primitives in the same Q-version language as the rest of the avatar's wardrobe, and
 * coloured from constants/pets.ts — the same table the shop icon draws from, so the dog on the
 * card and the dog on the stage are the same animal.
 *
 * LOCAL SPACE — every number in this file is authored in ONE convention, and the whole model is
 * normalised so that:
 *
 *   y = 0   the ground the paws stand on. Everything is built UPWARD from here.
 *   y = 1   the top of the head. The model is drawn to a unit height and the caller scales it by
 *           the breed's `height`, so re-tuning how big a dog is against the character is one
 *           number in constants/pets.ts rather than a rebuild of the geometry here.
 *   z = 0   the middle of the body. +z is forward (nose), -z is back (tail).
 *   x = 0   the centre line. Both sides are drawn from the same numbers mirrored, so there is no
 *           left/right variant to keep in sync.
 *
 * The three breeds are separate builds rather than one parameterised body because the silhouette
 * IS the breed — 臘腸's body is longer than it is tall on legs that barely clear the ground,
 * 紅貴賓 is a stack of fleece pom-poms, 柴犬 is a compact barrel with prick ears. A single shape
 * with enough knobs to cover all three would be harder to read than the three shapes.
 */

/** Low segment counts on purpose: 圓潤低多邊形, not a smooth render-quality sphere. */
const SPHERE = [16, 12] as const;
const CAP = [8, 12] as const;

/** Every part shares one matte finish — no gloss anywhere on a plush low-poly pet. */
function Fur({ color }: { color: string }) {
  return <meshStandardMaterial color={color} roughness={0.92} metalness={0} />;
}

/** The eyes and nose all three breeds share, sized and placed by the caller's muzzle. */
function Face({
  spec, eyeX, eyeY, eyeZ, noseY, noseZ, noseR,
}: {
  spec: PetSpec; eyeX: number; eyeY: number; eyeZ: number; noseY: number; noseZ: number; noseR: number;
}) {
  return (
    <>
      {[-1, 1].map(s => (
        <mesh key={s} position={[s * eyeX, eyeY, eyeZ]} castShadow>
          <sphereGeometry args={[0.045, ...SPHERE]} />
          <Fur color={spec.dark} />
        </mesh>
      ))}
      <mesh position={[0, noseY, noseZ]} castShadow>
        <sphereGeometry args={[noseR, ...SPHERE]} />
        <Fur color={spec.dark} />
      </mesh>
    </>
  );
}

/**
 * Four legs standing on y=0, the far pair shaded so the near pair reads in front of them.
 *
 * `top` is where the leg ENDS UP, not how long it is — and it has to be set above the belly at
 * the leg's own x/z, not at the body's centre line. That is the whole reason this takes a top
 * rather than a length: a leg sized to clear the lowest point of the body still hung in mid-air,
 * because a capsule's underside curves up towards its sides and the legs are out at the sides.
 * The overshoot is buried inside the body, so overshooting costs nothing and stopping short
 * costs the dog its legs.
 */
function Legs({
  spec, radius, top, x, frontZ, backZ,
}: {
  spec: PetSpec; radius: number; top: number; x: number; frontZ: number; backZ: number;
}) {
  const length = Math.max(0, top - radius * 2);
  const y = radius + length / 2;
  return (
    <>
      {([[-1, backZ], [1, backZ], [-1, frontZ], [1, frontZ]] as const).map(([s, z], i) => (
        <mesh key={i} position={[s * x, y, z]} castShadow>
          <capsuleGeometry args={[radius, length, ...CAP]} />
          <Fur color={s < 0 ? spec.shade : spec.coat} />
        </mesh>
      ))}
    </>
  );
}

function DachshundModel({ spec }: { spec: PetSpec }) {
  return (
    <>
      {/* Short legs, reaching well up into the barrel. Short is relative: the breed's legs are
          still about a third of its height — what makes it read as 臘腸 is that the BODY is
          nearly three times as long as those legs, not that the legs are stumps. */}
      <Legs spec={spec} radius={0.055} top={0.36} x={0.14} frontZ={0.32} backZ={-0.32} />

      {/* Long low body. Slimmer and longer than the other two breeds: this is the one shape that
          has to say "臘腸" before any of the detail does. */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.46, 0]} rotation={[Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} castShadow>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.19, 0.6, ...CAP]} />
        <Fur color={spec.coat} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Paler underside, sat low enough to actually show below the barrel — at the body's own
          centre height it is swallowed whole and paints nothing */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.3, 0]} rotation={[Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} scale={[0.85, 1, 0.4]} castShadow>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.17, 0.5, ...CAP]} />
        <Fur color={spec.accent} />
      </mesh>

      {/* Tail, thin and carried up off the long back */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.58, -0.52]} rotation={[-0.75, 0, 0]} castShadow>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.034, 0.22, ...CAP]} />
        <Fur color={spec.coat} />
      </mesh>

      {/* Neck. Without it the head sphere merges into the barrel and the whole dog reads as one
          blob with a snout stuck on the end. */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.62, 0.34]} rotation={[0.8, 0, 0]} castShadow>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.105, 0.16, ...CAP]} />
        <Fur color={spec.coat} />
      </mesh>

      {/* Head, held up and clear of the back */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.75, 0.44]} castShadow>
        <sphereGeometry args={[0.245, ...SPHERE]} />
        <Fur color={spec.coat} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Long tapered muzzle */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.7, 0.66]} rotation={[Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} castShadow>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.072, 0.2, ...CAP]} />
        <Fur color={spec.accent} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Long ears, hanging well past the jaw — the breed's other signature, so they are drawn
          big enough to be read from across the stage */}
      {[-1, 1].map(s => (
        <mesh key={s} position={[s * 0.2, 0.72, 0.4]} scale={[0.36, 1.65, 0.85]} rotation={[0, 0, s * 0.1]} castShadow>
          <sphereGeometry args={[0.165, ...SPHERE]} />
          <Fur color={spec.dark} />
        </mesh>
      ))}
      <Face spec={spec} eyeX={0.115} eyeY={0.82} eyeZ={0.6} noseY={0.7} noseZ={0.87} noseR={0.05} />
    </>
  );
}

function PoodleModel({ spec }: { spec: PetSpec }) {
  return (
    <>
      <Legs spec={spec} radius={0.05} top={0.38} x={0.14} frontZ={0.2} backZ={-0.2} />
      {/* Ankle poms, the give-away of a clipped poodle */}
      {([[-1, 0.2], [1, 0.2], [-1, -0.2], [1, -0.2]] as const).map(([s, z], i) => (
        <mesh key={i} position={[s * 0.14, 0.09, z]} castShadow>

          <sphereGeometry args={[0.155, ...SPHERE]} />
          <Fur color={spec.shade} />
        </mesh>
      ))}

      <mesh position={[0, 0.71, 0.4]} scale={[1, 0.85, 1]} castShadow>
        <sphereGeometry args={[0.125, ...SPHERE]} />
        <Fur color={spec.accent} />

    </>

}

function ShibaModel({ spec }: { spec: PetSpec }) {
  return (
    <>
      <Legs spec={spec} radius={0.062} top={0.39} x={0.15} frontZ={0.22} backZ={-0.2} />
      {/* Cream front socks, the breed's urajiro reaching down the legs */}
      {[-1, 1].map(s => (
        <mesh key={s} position={[s * 0.15, 0.075, 0.22]} castShadow>
          <capsuleGeometry args={[0.063, 0.02, ...CAP]} />
          <Fur color={spec.accent} />
        </mesh>
      ))}

      {/* Sturdy barrel body */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.47, 0]} rotation={[Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} castShadow>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.23, 0.26, ...CAP]} />
        <Fur color={spec.coat} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Cream chest and belly */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.34, 0.08]} rotation={[Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} scale={[0.85, 1, 0.5]} castShadow>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.21, 0.24, ...CAP]} />
        <Fur color={spec.accent} />
      </mesh>

      {/* Tail curled over the back — a torus stood on edge, which is the one primitive that
          keeps an even thickness the whole way round the curl */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.72, -0.24]} rotation={[0.3, Math.PI / 2, 0]} castShadow>
        <torusGeometry args={[0.115, 0.062, 8, 20, Math.PI * 1.6]} />
        <Fur color={spec.coat} />
      </mesh>

      {/* Neck, so the head reads as a head rather than a bulge on the barrel */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.56, 0.17]} rotation={[0.7, 0, 0]} castShadow>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.115, 0.1, ...CAP]} />
        <Fur color={spec.coat} />
      </mesh>

      {/* Head */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.71, 0.26]} castShadow>
        <sphereGeometry args={[0.29, ...SPHERE]} />
        <Fur color={spec.coat} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Cream mask: cheeks either side of a short broad muzzle */}
      {[-1, 1].map(s => (
        <mesh key={s} position={[s * 0.16, 0.63, 0.42]} castShadow>
          <sphereGeometry args={[0.115, ...SPHERE]} />
          <Fur color={spec.accent} />
        </mesh>
      ))}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.66, 0.47]} scale={[1.15, 0.85, 1]} castShadow>
        <sphereGeometry args={[0.135, ...SPHERE]} />
        <Fur color={spec.accent} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Triangular prick ears. Flattened front-to-back and left broad at the base: a full cone
          reads as a horn, and a tall splayed one turns the head into a fox's — the one animal
          this breed must not be mistaken for. */}
      {[-1, 1].map(s => (
        <mesh key={s} position={[s * 0.16, 0.93, 0.2]} rotation={[0.12, 0, s * -0.14]} scale={[1, 1, 0.55]} castShadow>
          <coneGeometry args={[0.115, 0.18, 3]} />
          <Fur color={spec.coat} />
        </mesh>
      ))}
      <Face spec={spec} eyeX={0.13} eyeY={0.76} eyeZ={0.48} noseY={0.69} noseZ={0.6} noseR={0.055} />
    </>
  );
}

/**
 * 貓 — one build for all three, where the dogs get one each.
 *
 * That asymmetry is the point rather than a shortcut: 臘腸/紅貴賓/柴犬 are breeds, and their
 * silhouettes are what name them, so three shapes. 橘/虎斑/賓士 are not breeds at all — they are
 * coat patterns on the same cat, and swapping one for another in life changes nothing but the
 * markings. So the body is shared and `breed` only decides what is painted on it.
 *
 * Against the dogs a cat is slimmer through the barrel, stands on thinner legs, and carries a long
 * smooth tail up off the croup where every dog here has a curl, a sweep or a pom.
 */
function CatModel({ spec, breed }: { spec: PetSpec; breed: string }) {
  const isTuxedo = breed === 'tuxedo';

  return (
    <>
      <Legs spec={spec} radius={0.048} top={0.42} x={0.13} frontZ={0.2} backZ={-0.2} />
      {/* The tuxedo's white socks, on all four — the marking it is named for */}
      {isTuxedo && ([[-1, 0.2], [1, 0.2], [-1, -0.2], [1, -0.2]] as const).map(([s, z], i) => (
        <mesh key={i} position={[s * 0.13, 0.075, z]} castShadow>
          <capsuleGeometry args={[0.049, 0.03, ...CAP]} />
          <Fur color={spec.accent} />
        </mesh>
      ))}

      {/* Body, slimmer through the barrel than any of the dogs */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.5, 0]} rotation={[Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} castShadow>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.2, 0.26, ...CAP]} />
        <Fur color={spec.coat} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Pale underside — on the tuxedo this is the white bib and belly, carried in one piece from
          the chest back, which is how the pattern actually sits */}
      <mesh
        position={[0, isTuxedo ? 0.4 : 0.37, isTuxedo ? 0.12 : 0.04]}
        rotation={[Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]}
        scale={isTuxedo ? [0.75, 1, 0.62] : [0.8, 1, 0.45]}
        castShadow
      >
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.185, 0.22, ...CAP]} />
        <Fur color={spec.accent} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Mackerel bars, as rings round the barrel. A ring is the one primitive that keeps an even
          width all the way over a curved flank — stripes drawn as flat patches pinch at the sides
          and stop reading as stripes at all. The tuxedo has none. */}
      {!isTuxedo && [-0.09, 0, 0.09].map(z => (
        <mesh key={z} position={[0, 0.5, z]} castShadow>
          <torusGeometry args={[0.201, 0.022, 6, 18]} />
          <Fur color={spec.shade} />
        </mesh>
      ))}

      {/* Tail: long, smooth and lifted, in two segments so it curves rather than sticking out
          straight. The second starts exactly where the first ends, so there is no join to see. */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.55, -0.32]} rotation={[-0.9, 0, 0]} castShadow>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.043, 0.22, ...CAP]} />
        <Fur color={spec.coat} />
      </mesh>
      <mesh position={[0, 0.715, -0.431]} rotation={[-0.25, 0, 0]} castShadow>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.04, 0.2, ...CAP]} />
        <Fur color={spec.coat} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Ringed tail on the tabbies, white tip on the tuxedo */}
      {isTuxedo ? (
        <mesh position={[0, 0.815, -0.457]} castShadow>
          <sphereGeometry args={[0.043, ...SPHERE]} />
          <Fur color={spec.accent} />
        </mesh>
      ) : (
        ([[0.52, -0.29], [0.63, -0.36]] as const).map(([y, z], i) => (
          <mesh key={i} position={[0, y, z]} rotation={[-0.9 + Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} castShadow>
            <torusGeometry args={[0.044, 0.016, 6, 14]} />
            <Fur color={spec.shade} />
          </mesh>
        ))
      )}

      {/* Neck, so the head reads as a head rather than a bulge on the barrel */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.58, 0.16]} rotation={[0.7, 0, 0]} castShadow>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[0.1, 0.09, ...CAP]} />
        <Fur color={spec.coat} />
      </mesh>

      {/* Head — rounder and smaller against the body than any of the dogs' */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.73, 0.24]} castShadow>
        <sphereGeometry args={[0.26, ...SPHERE]} />
        <Fur color={spec.coat} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Ears: taller and set wider than the shiba's prick ears, which is most of what separates a
          cat's head from a dog's at a glance. Flattened front-to-back so they read as triangles. */}
      {[-1, 1].map(s => (
        <mesh key={s} position={[s * 0.17, 0.95, 0.2]} rotation={[0.1, 0, s * -0.2]} scale={[1, 1, 0.5]} castShadow>
          <coneGeometry args={[0.105, 0.22, 3]} />
          <Fur color={spec.coat} />
        </mesh>
      ))}
      {/* Muzzle: two small cheek pads, short and round where every dog here has a snout that
          projects forward */}
      {[-1, 1].map(s => (
        <mesh key={s} position={[s * 0.072, 0.655, 0.44]} castShadow>
          <sphereGeometry args={[0.078, ...SPHERE]} />
          <Fur color={spec.accent} />
        </mesh>
      ))}
      {/* The tuxedo's blaze, running up the bridge of the nose between the eyes */}
      {isTuxedo && (
        <mesh position={[0, 0.79, 0.44]} scale={[0.3, 1.2, 0.42]} castShadow>
          <sphereGeometry args={[0.1, ...SPHERE]} />
          <Fur color={spec.accent} />
        </mesh>
      )}
      <Face spec={spec} eyeX={0.12} eyeY={0.78} eyeZ={0.44} noseY={0.7} noseZ={0.52} noseR={0.042} />
    </>
  );
}

/**
 * 鳥 — one build for all three, in the same sense the cats share one: a budgerigar, a Java sparrow
 * and a canary are all small perching birds of near enough the same size, and drawing three
 * separate skeletons for them would be inventing differences that are not there.
 *
 * What IS there, and what this switches on, are the two parts that actually differ between them —
 * the bill (a parrot's hook, a finch's heavy cone, a canary's fine pin) and the tail (the budgie's
 * is nearly as long as its body; the other two are short) — plus which colour goes where. That is
 * the whole table below.
 *
 * The birds fly rather than stand (see {@link HoveringBird}), so this model has no legs under it:
 * the feet are tucked up against the belly the way a bird in the air holds them, and the wings are
 * on their own pivots so they can beat. A perched pose would need legs and would be the wrong pose
 * — the player asked for a companion in the air beside them.
 */
type BirdBill = 'hook' | 'cone' | 'pin';
/** A slot of {@link PetSpec}, including the two 鳥-only ones, named so the table below can point at it. */
type Tone = 'coat' | 'shade' | 'accent' | 'dark' | 'beak' | 'mark';

interface BirdForm {
  bill: BirdBill;
  /** How far the tail reaches back, in this file's local units where the bird is 1 tall. */
  tailLength: number;
  /** The skull and throat: the 虎皮鸚鵡's yellow mask, the 文鳥's black hood, or just the coat. */
  head: Tone;
  belly: Tone;
  wing: Tone;
  tail: Tone;
  /** 文鳥 only: a black eye on a black hood is invisible, and in life the red ring is what you see. */
  eyeRing: boolean;
  /** 虎皮鸚鵡 only: the barring the bird is named for, on the wing and over the nape. */
  barred: boolean;
}

const BIRD_FORMS: Record<string, BirdForm> = {
  budgie:      { bill: 'hook', tailLength: 0.62, head: 'accent', belly: 'coat',   wing: 'accent', tail: 'mark',  eyeRing: false, barred: true },
  javasparrow: { bill: 'cone', tailLength: 0.30, head: 'dark',   belly: 'mark',   wing: 'shade',  tail: 'dark',  eyeRing: true,  barred: false },
  canary:      { bill: 'pin',  tailLength: 0.34, head: 'coat',   belly: 'accent', wing: 'shade',  tail: 'shade', eyeRing: false, barred: false },
};

/** Bill by shape: how fat, how long, where it sits on the face and how far it tips down. */
const BIRD_BILLS: Record<BirdBill, { r: number; len: number; y: number; z: number; pitch: number }> = {
  // A parrot's beak is short, deep and curls back under itself — the one profile no finch has.
  hook: { r: 0.085, len: 0.18, y: 0.775, z: 0.38, pitch: 0.55 },
  // A Java sparrow's is enormous for its head; scaled down to polite it stops being the bird.
  cone: { r: 0.115, len: 0.26, y: 0.735, z: 0.42, pitch: 0.06 },
  pin:  { r: 0.065, len: 0.20, y: 0.745, z: 0.40, pitch: 0.08 },
};

/** The 鳥-only slots fall back, so a bird added to PET_SPECS without them still renders in colour. */
function tone(spec: PetSpec, t: Tone): string {
  if (t === 'beak') return spec.beak ?? spec.shade;
  if (t === 'mark') return spec.mark ?? spec.accent;
  return spec[t];
}

function BirdModel({ spec, breed }: { spec: PetSpec; breed: string }) {
  const form = BIRD_FORMS[breed] ?? BIRD_FORMS.budgie;
  const bill = BIRD_BILLS[form.bill];
  const head = tone(spec, form.head);
  const keratin = tone(spec, 'beak');
  const mark = tone(spec, 'mark');
  const wings = useRef<THREE.Group[]>([]);

  // The wingbeat. Fast and shallow rather than slow and wide: a hovering bird's wings blur, and at
  // the size this renders next to the character a lazy albatross flap reads as the bird falling.
  // Both wings are driven off one value, mirrored — see the sign note below.
  useFrame(({ clock }) => {
    const beat = 0.22 + Math.sin(clock.getElapsedTime() * 7.2) * 0.55;
    // A wing pointing -x lifts on a NEGATIVE rotation about z and one pointing +x on a positive
    // one, so the mirrored pair takes the mirrored sign and the two beat together.
    if (wings.current[0]) wings.current[0].rotation.z = -beat;
    if (wings.current[1]) wings.current[1].rotation.z = beat;
  });

  return (
    <>
      {/* Tail: a flattened cone so it tapers to a point rather than ending in a square. Its axis is
          rotated onto -z (backwards) and the squash is on the axis that lands vertical, which is
          what makes it a flat fan instead of a spike. */}
      <mesh
        position={[0, 0.4, -(0.26 + form.tailLength / 2)]}
        rotation={[-Math.PI / 2 - 0.12, 0, 0]}
        scale={[1, 1, 0.3]}
        castShadow
      >
        <coneGeometry args={[0.12, form.tailLength, 6]} />
        <Fur color={tone(spec, form.tail)} />
      </mesh>

      {/* Body, an egg lying front-to-back */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.44, 0]} scale={[0.86, 0.94, 1.16]} castShadow>
        <sphereGeometry args={[0.27, ...SPHERE]} />
        <Fur color={spec.coat} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Underside — the 文鳥's pink belly, the 金絲雀's cream vent, the budgie's plain green */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.34, 0.03]} scale={[0.8, 0.6, 1]} castShadow>
        <sphereGeometry args={[0.24, ...SPHERE]} />
        <Fur color={tone(spec, form.belly)} />
      </mesh>
      {/* The 金絲雀's warm breast, which is the only thing separating it from a plain yellow shape */}
      {breed === 'canary' && (
        <mesh position={[0, 0.52, 0.22]} scale={[0.9, 0.8, 0.6]} castShadow>
          <sphereGeometry args={[0.16, ...SPHERE]} />
          <Fur color={mark} />
        </mesh>
      )}

      {/* Feet, tucked up under the belly the way a bird in flight carries them */}
      {[-1, 1].map(s => (
        <mesh key={s} position={[s * 0.09, 0.23, 0.02]} rotation={[0.9, 0, 0]} castShadow>
          <capsuleGeometry args={[0.028, 0.1, ...CAP]} />
          <Fur color={keratin} />
        </mesh>
      ))}

      {[-1, 1].map((s, i) => (
        <group key={s} ref={(el: THREE.Group | null) => { if (el) wings.current[i] = el; }} position={[s * 0.17, 0.55, 0]}>
          <mesh position={[s * 0.13, -0.03, -0.04]} scale={[0.28, 0.85, 1.25]} castShadow>
            <sphereGeometry args={[0.2, ...SPHERE]} />
            <Fur color={tone(spec, form.wing)} />
          </mesh>
          {form.barred && [-0.13, 0, 0.13].map(z => (
            <mesh key={z} position={[s * 0.192, -0.03, z - 0.04]} castShadow>
              <boxGeometry args={[0.012, 0.26, 0.05]} />
              <Fur color={spec.dark} />
            </mesh>
          ))}
        </group>
      ))}

      {/* Throat, bridging the head into the body. Painted the head's colour, not the coat's, because
          on all three of these the mask or hood carries on down under the chin. */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.63, 0.1]} castShadow>
        <sphereGeometry args={[0.19, ...SPHERE]} />
        <Fur color={head} />
      </mesh>
      {/* Head */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.76, 0.17]} castShadow>
        <sphereGeometry args={[0.225, ...SPHERE]} />
        <Fur color={head} />
      </mesh>
      {/* 虎皮 again, over the crown and nape where the barring actually starts */}
      {form.barred && [0.86, 0.79, 0.72].map(y => (
        <mesh key={y} position={[0, y, 0.02]} scale={[1, 1, 0.35]} castShadow>
          <torusGeometry args={[0.185, 0.018, 6, 16, Math.PI]} />
          <Fur color={spec.dark} />
        </mesh>
      ))}
      {/* The 文鳥's white cheeks, the mark it is picked out by at any distance */}
      {breed === 'javasparrow' && [-1, 1].map(s => (
        <mesh key={s} position={[s * 0.15, 0.735, 0.235]} scale={[0.7, 1, 0.7]} castShadow>
          <sphereGeometry args={[0.095, ...SPHERE]} />
          <Fur color={spec.accent} />
        </mesh>
      ))}
      {/* The budgie's violet cheek patches and its row of throat spots */}
      {breed === 'budgie' && (
        <>
          {[-1, 1].map(s => (
            <mesh key={s} position={[s * 0.145, 0.7, 0.29]} castShadow>
              <sphereGeometry args={[0.05, ...SPHERE]} />
              <Fur color={mark} />
            </mesh>
          ))}
          {([[0, 0.6, 0.33], [-0.09, 0.615, 0.3], [0.09, 0.615, 0.3]] as const).map(([x, y, z]) => (
            <mesh key={x} position={[x, y, z]} castShadow>
              <sphereGeometry args={[0.03, ...SPHERE]} />
              <Fur color={spec.dark} />
            </mesh>
          ))}
        </>
      )}

      {/* Bill. The cone's axis is +y, so a quarter turn about x lays it along +z and the form's own
          `pitch` tips it down from there — a parrot's a long way, a finch's barely at all. */}
      <mesh position={[0, bill.y, bill.z]} rotation={[Math.PI / 2 + bill.pitch, 0, 0]} castShadow>
        <coneGeometry args={[bill.r, bill.len, 10]} />
        <Fur color={keratin} />
      </mesh>
      {/* The budgie's cere, sat on top of the beak where it meets the face */}
      {form.bill === 'hook' && (
        <mesh position={[0, 0.835, 0.33]} castShadow>
          <sphereGeometry args={[0.06, ...SPHERE]} />
          <Fur color={keratin} />
        </mesh>
      )}

      {/* Eyes, set toward the sides of the skull as a bird's are — further out than any of the
          mammals in this file, which is most of what makes a round head read as a bird's. */}
      {[-1, 1].map(s => (
        <group key={s} position={[s * 0.155, 0.81, 0.26]}>
          <mesh castShadow>
            <sphereGeometry args={[0.05, ...SPHERE]} />
            <Fur color={spec.dark} />
          </mesh>
          {form.eyeRing && (
            <mesh position={[0, 0, 0.01]} rotation={[0, s * 0.5, 0]}>
              <torusGeometry args={[0.07, 0.018, 6, 16]} />
              <Fur color={keratin} />
            </mesh>
          )}
        </group>
      ))}
    </>
  );
}

/**
 * The pet itself, drawn to a unit height at the origin and facing +z.
 *
 * `itemId` is the catalog id (`pet-dog-shiba`); an id with no spec renders nothing rather than a
 * placeholder, so a save holding a pet that has since left the catalog just shows no companion.
 */
export const PetModelOld = memo(function PetModelOld({ itemId }: { itemId: string }) {
  const spec = getPetSpec(itemId);
  const breed = getPetBreed(itemId);
  const species = getPetSpecies(itemId);
  const bodyRef = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);

  // Standing idle: a slow breathing rise, and enough sway that the dog reads as alive next to an
  // avatar that has its own idle. Deliberately tiny — a companion that bounces pulls the eye off
  // the character whose outfit this screen exists to show.
  //
  // 鳥 get none of it. They are already beating their wings and riding a hover path, and a third
  // motion on top of those two is the difference between a bird in the air and a jittering one.
  useFrame(({ clock }) => {
    if (!bodyRef.current || species === 'bird') return;
    const t = clock.getElapsedTime();
    bodyRef.current.position.y = Math.sin(t * 1.6) * 0.012;
    bodyRef.current.rotation.z = Math.sin(t * 0.8) * 0.02;
  });

  if (!spec || !breed) return null;

  return (
    <group ref={bodyRef}>
      {/* Species first, because the cats and the birds each share one build while every dog has its
          own — see the comment on CatModel for why the halves of this are shaped differently. */}
      {species === 'cat' && <CatModel spec={spec} breed={breed} />}
      {species === 'bird' && <BirdModel spec={spec} breed={breed} />}
      {species === 'dog' && (
        <>
          {breed === 'dachshund' && <DachshundModel spec={spec} />}
          {breed === 'poodle' && <PoodleModel spec={spec} />}
          {breed === 'shiba' && <ShibaModel spec={spec} />}
        </>
      )}
    </group>
  );
});

/**
 * The equipped pet, placed beside the character: a step out to the character's right and half a
 * step FORWARD, turned slightly inward so it reads as accompanying them rather than standing to
 * attention. Scaled to the breed's height in the avatar's own local units, so it is mounted in
 * the same space the avatar is and needs no second scale factor to stay in proportion.
 *
 * Forward, not behind. Standing it behind the character was the natural reading of "右側後方半步"
 * and it put the dog behind the very thing the camera is pointed at — from this screen's fixed
 * front-on view the owner's body cut across the pet's face. In front of the shoulder line nothing
 * occludes it, and it is still far enough out sideways to leave the outfit — the reason this
 * screen exists — completely clear.
 *
 * Offsets are in the avatar's LOCAL units, where the character's own torso is ~0.14 wide.
 */
export const AVATAR_PET_OFFSET = { x: -0.36, z: 0.2 } as const;

/**
 * Where a 鳥 flies, in the same avatar-local units as {@link AVATAR_PET_OFFSET}.
 *
 * `y` puts it between the character's shoulder (0.44) and the crown (0.945): high enough to be
 * plainly airborne rather than hopping about the floor, low enough that it is never mistaken for a
 * hat. It is out at the same `x` as the dogs stand, so the outfit — the reason this screen exists —
 * stays as clear as it is with a dog on the stage.
 *
 * The drifts are the "移動一點點的距離就盤旋" of it: a tenth of a unit sideways is a bit less than
 * the character's own torso width, so the bird visibly wanders forward, back and side to side
 * without ever leaving the owner's side or crossing in front of the clothes.
 *
 * The three speeds are deliberately not multiples of one another. On round ratios the path closes
 * into the same visible loop every few seconds and reads as a mechanism on a track; left
 * incommensurate, the three sines take minutes to line up again and the bird never quite repeats
 * itself — which is the difference between hovering and orbiting.
 */
const BIRD_HOVER = {
  x: AVATAR_PET_OFFSET.x, y: 0.58, z: 0.24,
  driftX: 0.1, driftY: 0.045, driftZ: 0.085,
  speedX: 0.55, speedY: 0.9, speedZ: 0.37,
} as const;

/**
 * How hard the bird turns into its own drift.
 *
 * Facing the direction of travel outright is what a bird does and what looks worst here: half of
 * the path is backwards, so half the time the player would be shown the tail of the bird they just
 * bought. Steering the yaw by the sideways speed against a fixed forward bias keeps the turn honest
 * — it banks and points where it is sliding — while capping it at roughly 42°, so the bird is
 * always still facing out of the screen. Its other virtue is that it cannot wrap: an angle blended
 * from atan2 snaps by a full turn the moment the bird drifts straight backwards.
 */
const BIRD_FORWARD_BIAS = 0.062;

const HoveringBird = memo(function HoveringBird({ itemId, height }: { itemId: string; height: number }) {
  const ref = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);

  useFrame(({ clock }) => {
    const g = ref.current;
    if (!g) return;
    const t = clock.getElapsedTime();
    const h = BIRD_HOVER;

    g.position.set(
      h.x + Math.sin(t * h.speedX) * h.driftX,
      h.y + Math.sin(t * h.speedY) * h.driftY,
      h.z + Math.sin(t * h.speedZ + 1.1) * h.driftZ,
    );

    // The drift's own derivative, so the attitude is the motion's rather than a second animation
    // guessing at it — the bird can never bank one way while sliding the other.
    const vx = Math.cos(t * h.speedX) * h.speedX * h.driftX;
    const vz = Math.cos(t * h.speedZ + 1.1) * h.speedZ * h.driftZ;

    g.rotation.y = 0.3 + Math.atan2(vx, BIRD_FORWARD_BIAS);
    // Bank into the turn: sliding left drops the left wing, as it must to be turning at all.
    g.rotation.z = -vx * 3.5;
    // And nose down a little when pressing forward, up when backing off.
    g.rotation.x = vz * 5;
  });

  return (
    <group ref={ref} scale={height}>
      <PetModelOld itemId={itemId} />
    </group>
  );
});

export const CompanionPet = memo(function CompanionPet({ itemId }: { itemId: string }) {
  const spec = getPetSpec(itemId);
  if (!spec) return null;

  // 鳥 fly beside the owner instead of standing next to them — see BIRD_HOVER.
  if (getPetSpecies(itemId) === 'bird') {
    return <HoveringBird itemId={itemId} height={spec.height} />;
  }

  return (
    // A gentle turn toward the owner, not a full one: much past this and the dog is in profile,
    // and the face the player just bought stops facing the player.
    <group position={[AVATAR_PET_OFFSET.x, 0, AVATAR_PET_OFFSET.z]} rotation={[0, 0.3, 0]} scale={spec.height}>
      <PetModelOld itemId={itemId} />
    </group>
  );
});
```
