## src/components/UI/FragmentProgress.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { useId } from 'react';
import { useApp } from '../../context/AppContext';
import { ownsItem } from '../../utils/inventory';
import { getItemById } from '../../constants/items';
import {
  FRAGMENTS_PER_TICKET,
  FRAGMENTS_TO_UNLOCK,
  collectsFragments,
  fragmentName,
  getFragmentCount,
  getFragmentsRemaining,
  getRaffleTickets,
  getTicketProgress,
  isFragmentItem,
} from '../../constants/fragments';
import { QVersionIcon } from '../QVersionIcon';

/**
 * The 商品碎片 vocabulary every surface shares — the mark, the meter and the ticket chip.
 *
 * Same job as UI/ItemStock.tsx does for 庫存/購買: the shop card, the purchase dialog, the daily
 * board and the workout settlement all lay fragments out differently, and a player has to be able to
 * read 「我還差多少」 the same way in all four. The answer lives here so a new surface gets it right by
 * using it, not by re-deriving 200-minus-what-I-have and re-writing the copy.
 *
 * ## Colour — a prism, anchored on teal
 *
 * Fragments are NOT gold. Gold is reserved for currency (index.css says so at the token), and a
 * fragment is not money: it cannot be spent on anything but the one item it belongs to, and it is
 * earned rather than held. So the ramp starts on island-teal, the colour this game already uses for
 * its other earned track (經驗值's bolt), and that is the only colour a nearly-empty stack ever
 * shows.
 *
 * From there it splits, the way a shard of glass splits light: teal → 水藍 → violet → 珊瑚
 * (`--fragment-ramp`, index.css). The ramp is painted across the whole TRACK and clipped to the
 * fill, never stretched to fit it, so **how colourful the bar is IS how full it is** — a stack at
 * 30% is teal and sky, and only 200/200 has the coral in it. That is the entire reason the colour
 * was added: it gives the same number a second reading that works at thumbnail size, across a shelf,
 * without being read. Stretch the ramp to the fill instead and every stack looks identical again.
 *
 * 抽獎券 ARE money and take the gold family — but a torn stub rather than a disc, so the two never
 * read as the same thing sitting in the same header.
 */

/** The ramp's stops, mirrored from index.css so the SVG mark below can use them inline. */
const PRISM = {
  teal: '#2A9D8F',
  aqua: '#35C6B4',
  sky: '#4FB9E8',
  violet: '#8E8CEB',
  orchid: '#CE84D8',
  coral: '#E8836A',
} as const;

/**
 * The fragment mark: a chipped shard with the light broken across it. Never a coin, never a gem.
 *
 * Three faces, three parts of the ramp — the lit top-left in orchid-to-white, the body running aqua
 * to coral, and an edge that is itself graded from teal-dark to plum so the outline stays crisp
 * against both ends of the fill it sits on. Gradient ids are `useId`-scoped because this mark
 * renders a dozen times on one shelf and duplicate SVG ids resolve to whichever landed first.
 */
export function FragmentShard({
  size = 14,
  className = '',
  /** 集滿 — adds the halo. The shard is otherwise identical at every count. */
  lit = false,
}: {
  size?: number;
  className?: string;
  lit?: boolean;
}) {
  const uid = useId().replace(/:/g, '');
  const body = `frag-body-${uid}`;
  const facet = `frag-facet-${uid}`;
  const edge = `frag-edge-${uid}`;

  return (
    <svg
      width={size}
      height={size}
      viewBox="0 0 24 24"
      fill="none"
      className={`${lit ? 'fragment-shard-lit' : ''} ${className}`}
      aria-hidden
    >
      <defs>
        <linearGradient id={body} x1="4" y1="3" x2="19" y2="21" gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
          <stop offset="0" stopColor={PRISM.aqua} />
          <stop offset="0.4" stopColor={PRISM.sky} />
          <stop offset="0.72" stopColor={PRISM.violet} />
          <stop offset="1" stopColor={PRISM.coral} />
        </linearGradient>
        <linearGradient id={facet} x1="2.6" y1="10" x2="12.6" y2="2.3" gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
          <stop offset="0" stopColor={PRISM.orchid} />
          <stop offset="1" stopColor="#F2FCF8" />
        </linearGradient>
        <linearGradient id={edge} x1="3" y1="3" x2="20" y2="21" gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
          <stop offset="0" stopColor="#1F7A70" />
          <stop offset="1" stopColor="#9B5578" />
        </linearGradient>
      </defs>

      <path d="M12.6 2.3 21 9.1l-4.2 12.2-9.6-1.1L2.6 9.5z" fill={`url(#${body})`} />
      {/* The lit face — the one catching the light, and the reason the mark reads as a broken piece
          of something rather than as a pentagon. */}
      <path d="M12.6 2.3 9.6 12 2.6 9.5z" fill={`url(#${facet})`} opacity="0.92" />
      {/* The second face, a half-tone between the two, so the shard still has depth at 11px. */}
      <path d="M12.6 2.3 21 9.1 9.6 12z" fill="#FFFFFF" opacity="0.22" />
      <path
        d="M12.6 2.3 21 9.1l-4.2 12.2-9.6-1.1L2.6 9.5z"
        stroke={`url(#${edge})`}
        strokeWidth="1.5"
        strokeLinejoin="round"
      />
      <path
        d="M12.6 2.3 9.6 12l7.2 9.3M9.6 12 2.6 9.5"
        stroke={`url(#${edge})`}
        strokeWidth="1.1"
        strokeLinejoin="round"
        opacity="0.5"
      />
    </svg>
  );
}

/**
 * The 抽獎券 mark: a torn stub with a punched bite on each side. Gold, because it is spendable.
 *
 * The same ticket as the 64px one in QVersionIcon.tsx, one detail level down — that file's own
 * comment already promised 「兩者是同一張票的兩個尺寸」, and this is that promise paid. What was
 * missing was everything that makes paper look like paper: the body was one flat fill with square
 * corners, which at 11px in a wallet chip is a gold pill with a dotted line on it.
 *
 * Three things carry the shrink, and each one is chosen because it survives being small:
 *
 *  1. **The silhouette** — rounded corners and the two half-round bites at the waist. Same trick as
 *     the big icon: the corners sweep 1 (convex), the bites sweep 0, and that single digit is the
 *     whole difference between a bump and a notch.
 *  2. **The stub as a BAND, not a hairline.** A dashed line alone is the first thing to disappear;
 *     a deeper gold field behind it still says 「這張票有票根」 down to about 8px.
 *  3. **A raking gradient** across the body, so the card stock has a lit edge and a shaded one.
 *
 * The big icon's little wheel and its star are deliberately NOT here. They are 8px features on a
 * 64px drawing, which is 1.3px on the size this mark actually spends its life at.
 */
export function RaffleTicket({ size = 14, className = '' }: { size?: number; className?: string }) {
  const uid = useId().replace(/:/g, '');
  const paper = `ticket-paper-${uid}`;
  const clip = `ticket-clip-${uid}`;

  /** One ticket's outline. Corners sweep 1; the two waist bites sweep 0, which is what bites them in. */
  const outline =
    'M5 7.4H19A2 2 0 0 1 21 9.4V10.5A1.8 1.8 0 0 0 21 14.1V15.2A2 2 0 0 1 19 17.2H5'
    + 'A2 2 0 0 1 3 15.2V14.1A1.8 1.8 0 0 0 3 10.5V9.4A2 2 0 0 1 5 7.4Z';

  return (
    <svg width={size} height={size} viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" className={className} aria-hidden>
      <defs>
        <linearGradient id={paper} x1="4" y1="7" x2="11" y2="18" gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
          <stop offset="0" stopColor="#FCE3A6" />
          <stop offset="0.5" stopColor="#F3C566" />
          <stop offset="1" stopColor="#DFA236" />
        </linearGradient>
        <clipPath id={clip}>
          <path d={outline} />
        </clipPath>
      </defs>

      <path d={outline} fill={`url(#${paper})`} />
      {/* Stub and highlight, both clipped to the ticket so their ends are the ticket's own rounded
          corners rather than two rectangles poking out of it. */}
      <g clipPath={`url(#${clip})`}>
        <rect x="14.2" y="6" width="8.4" height="12.4" fill="#E2A63E" />
        <path d="M5.5 9.1H12.6" stroke="#FFFFFF" strokeWidth="1.3" strokeLinecap="round" opacity="0.6" />
      </g>
      <path d={outline} stroke="#C98A24" strokeWidth="1.5" strokeLinejoin="round" />
      {/* The perforation: a pale groove with the punch holes dashed over it. Two strokes, because a
          row of dark dashes on gold reads as dirt, and the light line under them reads as a fold. */}
      <path d="M14.2 8.3v8" stroke="#FFEFC8" strokeWidth="1.9" strokeLinecap="round" />
      <path d="M14.2 8.3v8" stroke="#C98A24" strokeWidth="1.2" strokeLinecap="round" strokeDasharray="1.5 1.7" />
    </svg>
  );
}

/**
 * The bar itself — the one place the prism is actually assembled.
 *
 * Shared by the meter and the gain card so a stack cannot look 40% full in the shop and 40% full in
 * a different colour on the settlement screen.
 *
 * The nesting is what makes 「顏色＝進度」 work and is not incidental:
 *
 *   track (the full width)
 *     └ fill      width = pct%          ← clips
 *         └ ink   width = 100/pct×100%  ← always exactly the track's width, so the ramp is laid
 *                                         across the WHOLE bar and the fill reveals a prefix of it
 *
 * Sizing the ink to the fill instead would stretch the whole ramp into whatever is filled, and every
 * stack from 5% to 100% would show the identical run of colour.
 */
function FragmentBar({
  pct,
  ready,
  height = 'h-2',
  className = '',
}: {
  pct: number;
  ready: boolean;
  height?: string;
  className?: string;
}) {
  const clamped = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, pct));
  // 100/pct of the fill's own width == the track's width. Capped so a 1-fragment stack does not ask
  // the browser for a 20000%-wide element.
  const inkWidth = clamped > 0 ? `${Math.min(6000, (100 / clamped) * 100)}%` : '100%';

  return (
    <div className={`fragment-track ${ready ? 'fragment-ready' : ''} w-full ${height} ${className}`}>
      <div className="fragment-fill" style={{ width: `${clamped}%` }}>
        <div className="fragment-ink" style={{ width: inkWidth }} />
        {/* The gloss needs something to travel across; under ~6% there is no bar to catch it and it
            reads as a flicker at the left edge instead. */}
        {clamped > 6 && <div className="fragment-sheen" />}
      </div>
      {/* Quarter marks — 「還差多少」 as a shape, for the glance that never reads the number. */}
      {[25, 50, 75].map(mark => (
        <span key={mark} className="fragment-notch" style={{ left: `${mark}%` }} aria-hidden />
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}

/**
 * 碎片進度 — the bar, the count and the 還差 line for one item.
 *
 * Renders NOTHING for an item that has no fragment of its own (經驗值 rewards, 毛胚屋), and nothing
 * for an item whose race is genuinely over. Both are deliberate: a bar under a finished race is a
 * progress readout for nothing.
 *
 * ## 「已擁有」 is not 「結束了」
 *
 * The gate here used to be `owned && held === 0`, which quietly made those two the same sentence.
 * They are not. An own-once item (a hat) is finished the moment it is owned. A STACKABLE one is not:
 * a second sofa is a real purchase, so its fragments still buy something and the bar has to keep
 * standing. {@link collectsFragments} is that distinction, and it is the same predicate the drop
 * roll, the unlock and the purchase settlement now ask — a bar that shows is a bar that can be
 * filled and spent, in all four places or none.
 *
 * The one case it still draws on a finished item is a leftover stack — which should not exist,
 * because buying an own-once item with gold settles it (context/useShopActions.ts). Drawing it
 * anyway means a save that somehow holds one says so instead of hiding it.
 *
 * It sits in a tinted well (`.fragment-well`) rather than loose on the card, because on a shop card
 * this is not one more line of copy — it is the SECOND offer, standing next to the gold price, and a
 * player has to be able to see that this card has two prices without reading either.
 */
export function FragmentMeter({
  itemId,
  className = '',
  /** Drops the 還差 line and shrinks the type — for a card that has little room to give. */
  compact = false,
}: {
  itemId: string;
  className?: string;
  compact?: boolean;
}) {
  const { profile } = useApp();
  if (!isFragmentItem(itemId)) return null;

  const held = getFragmentCount(profile, itemId);
  const owned = ownsItem(profile, itemId);
  const collecting = collectsFragments(itemId, owned);
  // Nothing left to collect AND nothing left over: the race is finished and there is no bar to draw.
  // A leftover stack on a finished item still draws, so the save can say so.
  if (!collecting && held === 0) return null;

  const remaining = getFragmentsRemaining(profile, itemId);
  const ready = remaining === 0;
  const pct = Math.min(100, (held / FRAGMENTS_TO_UNLOCK) * 100);
  // 「再一件」 rather than 「解鎖」 once one is already owned — the bar is the same bar, but what it
  // buys is a second copy, and the copy says so rather than leaving the player to work out why a
  // progress meter is sitting under a card marked 已擁有.
  const again = owned && collecting;

  return (
    <div
      className={`fragment-well w-full ${ready ? 'fragment-well-ready' : ''} ${
        compact ? 'px-2.5 py-2' : 'px-3 py-2.5'
      } ${className}`}
    >
      <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 mb-1.5">
        <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-1 text-island-navy-soft/85 font-bold text-[10px] min-w-0">
          <FragmentShard size={compact ? 12 : 14} lit={ready} className="flex-shrink-0" />
          <span className="truncate">{fragmentName(itemId)}</span>
        </span>
        {/* `tabular-nums` and the fixed bar height below keep a card the same size as the number
            grows — the shelf must not reflow every time a workout pays out. */}
        <span
          className={`font-black tabular-nums flex-shrink-0 ${compact ? 'text-[10px]' : 'text-[11px]'} ${
            ready ? 'fragment-ramp-text' : 'text-island-navy-soft/85'
          }`}
        >
          {held.toLocaleString()}
          <span className={ready ? '' : 'opacity-55'}> / {FRAGMENTS_TO_UNLOCK}</span>
        </span>
      </div>

      <FragmentBar pct={pct} ready={ready} height={compact ? 'h-1.5' : 'h-2'} />

      {!compact && (
        <p className={`mt-1.5 text-[10px] font-bold ${ready ? 'fragment-ramp-text' : 'text-island-navy-soft/60'}`}>
          {ready
            ? (again ? '碎片已集滿，可再免費解鎖一件' : '碎片已集滿，可直接解鎖')
            : `還差 ${remaining.toLocaleString()} 個碎片${again ? '可再換一件' : ''}`}
        </p>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

/**
 * 抽獎券 balance, with the fraction of the next one showing underneath.
 *
 * The carry is drawn as a hairline rather than a second number: it is not a currency the player
 * spends, it is the promise that 多出來的碎片 are not being thrown away, and it only has to be
 * visible enough to answer 「那剩下的幾個去哪了」.
 */
export function RaffleTicketChip({ className = '' }: { className?: string }) {
  const { profile } = useApp();
  const tickets = getRaffleTickets(profile);
  const carry = getTicketProgress(profile);

  return (
    <span
      className={`inline-flex flex-col gap-1 px-3 py-1.5 rounded-full bg-island-gold/12 border border-island-gold/35 text-island-navy font-black text-xs ${className}`}
      title={
        carry > 0
          ? `抽獎券 ${tickets}　再 ${FRAGMENTS_PER_TICKET - carry} 個多餘碎片可換下一張`
          : `抽獎券 ${tickets}`
      }
    >
      <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 leading-none">
        <RaffleTicket size={13} />
        <span>{tickets.toLocaleString()}</span>
      </span>
      {carry > 0 && (
        <span className="h-[3px] w-full rounded-full bg-island-gold/25 overflow-hidden" aria-hidden>
          <span
            className="block h-full rounded-full bg-island-gold"
            style={{ width: `${(carry / FRAGMENTS_PER_TICKET) * 100}%` }}
          />
        </span>
      )}
    </span>
  );
}

/**
 * One 「+N 碎片」 announcement, with the item it is for.
 *
 * Used by the surfaces that PAY fragments rather than the ones that spend them — the workout
 * settlement and the daily claim. It shows the item's own artwork because that is the whole point of
 * a per-item fragment: the reward is not "some fragments", it is 「離那盞燈更近了」, and a player who
 * cannot see which lamp has been handed a number rather than a reward.
 */
export function FragmentGainCard({
  itemId,
  amount,
  overflow = 0,
  className = '',
}: {
  itemId: string;
  /** How many landed on the item. */
  amount: number;
  /** How many had nowhere to go and became 抽獎券 instead. */
  overflow?: number;
  className?: string;
}) {
  const { profile } = useApp();
  const item = getItemById(itemId);
  if (!item) return null;

  const held = getFragmentCount(profile, itemId);
  const remaining = getFragmentsRemaining(profile, itemId);
  const ready = remaining === 0;

  return (
    <div className={`fragment-well flex items-center gap-3 p-3 ${ready ? 'fragment-well-ready' : ''} ${className}`}>
      <div className="w-12 h-12 rounded-xl bg-white border border-island-line flex items-center justify-center flex-shrink-0 overflow-hidden">
        <QVersionIcon itemId={item.id} size={40} />
      </div>
      <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
        <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-2">
          <span className="text-xs font-black text-island-navy truncate">{fragmentName(item)}</span>
          {amount > 0 && (
            <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-1 font-black text-sm flex-shrink-0">
              <FragmentShard size={14} lit={ready} />
              <span className="fragment-ramp-text">+{amount}</span>
            </span>
          )}
        </div>
        <FragmentBar pct={Math.min(100, (held / FRAGMENTS_TO_UNLOCK) * 100)} ready={ready} className="mt-1.5" />
        <p className="text-[10px] font-bold text-island-navy-soft/70 mt-1">
          {held.toLocaleString()} / {FRAGMENTS_TO_UNLOCK}
          {ready ? '　·　可解鎖' : `　·　還差 ${remaining.toLocaleString()}`}
          {overflow > 0 && `　·　多出的 ${overflow} 個已轉為抽獎券`}
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## src/components/UI/HairSpinPreview.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { useRef } from 'react';
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { Canvas, useFrame } from '@react-three/fiber';
import { RotateCw } from 'lucide-react';
import { HairSpec, AVATAR_SKIN_COLOR } from '../../constants/hair';
import { HairPiece } from '../Three/character/legacy/wardrobe';
import { LEGACY_SKELETON } from '../../constants/characterRig';
import { playSound, SoundEffect, triggerHaptic } from '../../lib/soundUtils';

/**
 * Turntable preview of a hairstyle on a head, for the purchase confirmation.
 *
 * A hairstyle is the one thing in the shop whose back matters as much as its front - the flat
 * thumbnail deliberately shows the front only, so a player buying 大波浪 has never seen what the
 * fall actually does behind the head. This spins the real thing: it mounts the same `HairPiece`
 * the avatar wears, on a head built from the same sphere, tones and landmarks, so what turns here
 * is the model the player is buying rather than a second illustration of it that could drift.
 *
 * Deliberately not OrbitControls. The only useful axis is yaw - a hairstyle inspected from
 * underneath tells you nothing and looks broken - so the interaction is a turn button plus
 * horizontal drag, and pitch is simply not offered.
 */

/** Yaw state, shared between the DOM controls and the r3f frame loop. */
interface SpinState {
  yaw: number;
  /** Radians still owed to the turn button; drag cancels it (see the drag handler). */
  remaining: number;
}

/** A full turn in a little under two seconds - long enough to read the back, short enough to sit through. */
const SPIN_SPEED = Math.PI * 1.15;

/** Radians of yaw per pixel dragged. Tuned so a full turn is roughly one screen-width swipe. */
const DRAG_SENSITIVITY = 0.012;

function PreviewHead({ spec, spin }: { spec: HairSpec; spin: React.MutableRefObject<SpinState> }) {
  const group = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);
  // HairPiece animates its hanging pieces through this ref. Nothing drives it here - the preview
  // has no walk cycle to follow through from - so the hair simply hangs at rest, which is the
  // shape the player is actually choosing between.
  const swayRef = useRef<THREE.Group>(null!);

  useFrame((_, delta) => {
    const s = spin.current;
    if (s.remaining > 0) {
      const step = Math.min(s.remaining, delta * SPIN_SPEED);
      s.yaw += step;
      s.remaining -= step;
    }
    if (group.current) group.current.rotation.y = s.yaw;
  });

  return (
    <group ref={group}>
      {/* Head. These are the legacy model's numbers, not lookalikes: the same skull HEAD_ANCHOR
          is measured against, and the same eye/mouth/blush landmarks. The hair is fitted to that
          anchor, so any drift here would show up as hair sitting wrong on the preview only.
          The radius is READ from the rig rather than retyped, so a remodel cannot leave this
          preview quietly fitted to a head the game no longer draws. */}
      <mesh>
        <sphereGeometry args={[LEGACY_SKELETON.head.halfWidth, 32, 32]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color={AVATAR_SKIN_COLOR} roughness={0.7} />
      </mesh>
      <group position={[0, 0.035, 0.225]}>
        <mesh position={[-0.104, 0, 0]}>
          <sphereGeometry args={[0.036, 16, 16]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial color="#0d1117" roughness={0.1} />
        </mesh>
        <mesh position={[0.104, 0, 0]}>
          <sphereGeometry args={[0.036, 16, 16]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial color="#0d1117" roughness={0.1} />
        </mesh>
      </group>
      <mesh position={[0, -0.045, 0.255]} rotation={[0, 0, Math.PI * 1.275]}>
        <torusGeometry args={[0.036, 0.0043, 8, 24, Math.PI * 0.45]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#0d1117" roughness={0.5} />
      </mesh>
      <mesh position={[-0.122, -0.029, 0.18]}>
        <sphereGeometry args={[0.056, 16, 16]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#fda4af" transparent opacity={0.3} roughness={0.9} />
      </mesh>
      <mesh position={[0.122, -0.029, 0.18]}>
        <sphereGeometry args={[0.056, 16, 16]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#fda4af" transparent opacity={0.3} roughness={0.9} />
      </mesh>

      <HairPiece spec={spec} hat={null} swayRef={swayRef} />
    </group>
  );
}

export function HairSpinPreview({ spec, size = 160 }: { spec: HairSpec; size?: number }) {
  const spin = useRef<SpinState>({ yaw: 0, remaining: 0 });
  const drag = useRef<{ active: boolean; x: number; moved: number }>({ active: false, x: 0, moved: 0 });

  const turn = () => {
    // Ignore a second press mid-turn rather than queueing another lap: a player tapping twice
    // wants to see the back again, not to sit through two full rotations.
    if (spin.current.remaining > 0) return;
    triggerHaptic('light');
    playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
    spin.current.remaining = Math.PI * 2;
  };

  const onPointerDown = (e: React.PointerEvent) => {
    drag.current = { active: true, x: e.clientX, moved: 0 };
    (e.currentTarget as HTMLElement).setPointerCapture(e.pointerId);
  };

  const onPointerMove = (e: React.PointerEvent) => {
    if (!drag.current.active) return;
    const dx = e.clientX - drag.current.x;
    drag.current.x = e.clientX;
    drag.current.moved += Math.abs(dx);
    // A drag takes the wheel off the button: continuing a scripted turn under the player's finger
    // fights them for the same axis.
    spin.current.remaining = 0;
    spin.current.yaw += dx * DRAG_SENSITIVITY;
  };

  const onPointerUp = (e: React.PointerEvent) => {
    (e.currentTarget as HTMLElement).releasePointerCapture?.(e.pointerId);
    drag.current.active = false;
  };

  return (
    <div
      style={{ width: size, height: size }}
      className="rounded-2xl relative overflow-hidden flex-shrink-0 border border-island-line bg-island-cream-2 touch-none cursor-grab active:cursor-grabbing"
      onPointerDown={onPointerDown}
      onPointerMove={onPointerMove}
      onPointerUp={onPointerUp}
      onPointerCancel={onPointerUp}
    >
      <Canvas
        camera={{ position: [0, 0, 1.75], fov: 32 }}
        gl={{ alpha: true, antialias: true }}
        style={{ background: 'transparent' }}
      >
        <ambientLight intensity={1.15} />
        <directionalLight position={[2, 3, 2.5]} intensity={1.5} />
        <directionalLight position={[-2, 1, -1.5]} intensity={0.55} />
        {/* Rim from behind. Without it the near-black styles lose their outline against the
            cream tile at exactly the angle the turn exists to show. */}
        <directionalLight position={[0, 1.5, -3]} intensity={0.9} />
        {/* Nudged up so a long fall stays in frame without pushing a short cut out of the top. */}
        <group position={[0, 0.08, 0]}>
          <PreviewHead spec={spec} spin={spin} />
        </group>
      </Canvas>

      <button
        type="button"
        onClick={turn}
        aria-label="旋轉檢視髮型"
        className="absolute bottom-2 right-2 h-9 px-3 gap-1.5 rounded-xl bg-white/95 border border-island-line hover:border-island-teal hover:text-island-teal text-island-navy-soft flex items-center justify-center transition-all active:scale-90 shadow-sm"
      >
        <RotateCw size={15} strokeWidth={2.8} />
        <span className="text-[10px] font-black tracking-widest">360°</span>
      </button>

      <span className="absolute bottom-3 left-3 text-[9px] font-bold tracking-wide text-island-navy-soft/50 pointer-events-none">
        可拖曳
      </span>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import React, { useMemo, useState } from 'react';
import { motion } from 'motion/react';
import {
  ArrowLeft, Compass, Home, Move, Package, Paintbrush, Palette, ShoppingBag,
} from 'lucide-react';
import { UserProfile } from '../../types';
import { HOUSE_STYLES, HouseStyleDefinition } from '../../constants/houseStyles';
import { ItemDefinition, getItemById } from '../../constants/items';
import { ResolvedHome } from '../../hooks/usePlayerHome';
import { ANGEL_AVOID } from '../../constants/angelAvoid';
import { QVersionIcon } from '../QVersionIcon';
import { useEscapeToClose } from '../../hooks/useEscapeToClose';
import { IconTile, KeyCap, PanelHeader } from './DesignKit';
import { DrawerSectionDivider, OWNED_DIVIDER, PlacementItemRow, UNOWNED_DIVIDER } from './PlacementCatalog';
import { worldYawToFacingDeg } from './minimap/miniMapCore';

/**
 * 我的家 — the Home's own management surface.
 *
 * ## The problem this exists to fix
 *
 * The Home used to have no SELECTED state, only an EDITING one. `selectHome()` wrote an island
 * draft on the spot, so the single entry point 「我的家」 (a row inside 島上物件, a tool whose own
 * subtitle promises 移動或收回) did four things at once: it hid the house behind its own ghost,
 * closed the list the player was reading, put up the placement dock, and left them owing a
 * 確認/取消 for a change they had not asked to make. A player who wanted to *look* at their house,
 * or repaint it, or turn it a notch, was moving it before they had said anything.
 *
 * Appearance was the sharpest edge of that: 更換外觀 lived on the placement dock as an extra key,
 * i.e. it was reachable only from inside a move — and because `applyHouseStyle` writes
 * immediately while the transform is still a draft, 取消 cancelled the move but kept the new
 * paint. One panel, two different meanings of "confirm".
 *
 * ## What it is instead
 *
 * Selecting the Home now opens *this*, and nothing else happens: the house stays standing, the
 * world is untouched, and the player picks the verb. That is the whole point — this panel is a
 * **state, not an action**.
 *
 *   我的家 (dock tool · 島上物件 row · clicking the house)
 *     └─ 房屋總覽 — what it looks like now, which way the door faces, how many styles are open
 *          ├─ 更換外觀 → the style list, applied in place, never touches position
 *          └─ 移動與轉向 → hands over to the ONE island editing session (drag + R)
 *
 * ## Why 旋轉 is not a third destination
 *
 * The brief asked for 更換外觀 / 移動位置 / 旋轉 as three peers. Position and rotation are one
 * continuous manipulation here, and — more decisively — they are one *validation*: a turned house
 * covers different ground, so a rotate that skipped the draft would skip `isDraftBlocked` and
 * could quietly park a corner of the building on a fence or off the terrain. So they stay one
 * session, the row is named 移動與轉向 rather than 移動位置, and rotation earns its legibility
 * where it was actually missing — the facing is now a readable fact (the dial below, and the same
 * reading on the placement dock) instead of something only discoverable by pressing R.
 *
 * ## Shape
 *
 * Deliberately the same shell as `CatalogDrawer` — right-hand drawer, `max-w-md`, `PanelHeader`,
 * a two-layer body with a back arrow — because it is the third drawer of the same build mode.
 * The overview's action rows are the build dock's tool card, restated: icon tile, label, hint.
 * Nothing here is a new visual language, which is the point of putting it here rather than
 * inventing a house screen.
 */

/** The eight bearings a 45° rotation step can land on, from north, clockwise. */
const COMPASS_POINTS = ['北', '東北', '東', '東南', '南', '西南', '西', '西北'];

/**
 * Which way the front door points, in the minimap's own north-up frame.
 *
 * Goes through `worldYawToFacingDeg` rather than doing its own trigonometry so the house's stated
 * facing and every marker on the map are the same conversion — a second copy of "which way is
 * north" is exactly the kind of thing that ends up half a turn out.
 */
function facingDegrees(rotation: number): number {
  return ((worldYawToFacingDeg(rotation) % 360) + 360) % 360;
}

/**
 * The door's bearing as a word. Exported because the placement dock says the same thing live
 * while the house is being turned — one reading, so the panel and the dock can never disagree.
 */
export function facingLabel(rotation: number): string {
  return COMPASS_POINTS[Math.round(facingDegrees(rotation) / 45) % 8];
}

/**
 * A dial showing where the front door points. The needle is the DOOR, not the building: a house
 * is symmetric enough from the outside that "which way is it turned" only means anything if you
 * say which end you are talking about.
 */
function HouseCompass({ rotation, size = 68 }: { rotation: number; size?: number }) {
  return (
    <div
      className="relative flex flex-shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-full border border-island-line bg-island-cream-2"
      style={{ width: size, height: size }}
    >
      <span className="absolute top-1 text-[8px] font-black leading-none text-island-navy-soft/55">N</span>
      <svg
        viewBox="0 0 40 40"
        aria-hidden="true"
        className="text-island-teal transition-transform duration-300"
        style={{ width: size * 0.72, height: size * 0.72, transform: `rotate(${facingDegrees(rotation)}deg)` }}
      >
        <path d="M20 7 L26.5 21.5 L20 18.5 L13.5 21.5 Z" fill="currentColor" />
        <circle cx="20" cy="26" r="2.4" fill="currentColor" opacity="0.35" />
      </svg>
    </div>
  );
}

/** Whether a style is available to wear — the starter coat is granted, everything else is bought. */
function ownsStyle(profile: UserProfile | null, style: HouseStyleDefinition): boolean {
  return !style.purchasable || !!profile?.inventory?.includes(style.itemId);
}

interface StyleEntry {
  style: HouseStyleDefinition;
  item: ItemDefinition;
  owned: boolean;
}

export function HomePanel({
  home,
  profile,
  onStartTransform,
  onApplyStyle,
  onBuy,
  onClose,
}: {
  home: ResolvedHome;
  profile: UserProfile | null;
  /** 移動與轉向 — hands the Home to the island editing session (useIslandEditor). */
  onStartTransform: () => void;
  onApplyStyle: (styleItemId: string) => void;
  onBuy: (item: ItemDefinition) => void;
  onClose: () => void;
}) {
  const [view, setView] = useState<'overview' | 'styles'>('overview');
  // Esc unwinds one layer at a time rather than closing outright, the same way the back arrow
  // does — a player deep in the style list has not asked to leave 我的家.
  useEscapeToClose(() => (view === 'styles' ? setView('overview') : onClose()));

  const styles = useMemo(() => {
    const decorated = HOUSE_STYLES
      .map(style => ({ style, item: getItemById(style.itemId), owned: ownsStyle(profile, style) }))
      .filter((entry): entry is StyleEntry => !!entry.item);
    return {
      owned: decorated.filter(e => e.owned),
      unowned: decorated.filter(e => !e.owned),
    };
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [profile?.inventory]);

  return (
    <motion.div
      initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
      animate={{ opacity: 1 }}
      exit={{ opacity: 0 }}
      onClick={onClose}
      onWheel={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
      onTouchMove={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
      className="absolute inset-0 z-floating-panel flex items-center justify-end bg-island-navy/45 p-4 md:p-8"
    >
      <motion.div
        // Marked as an obstacle so the 小天使 narrates it from beside rather than on top of it,
        // exactly as she does for the catalog drawer. See constants/angelAvoid.ts.
        {...ANGEL_AVOID}
        initial={{ x: 100 }}
        animate={{ x: 0 }}
        onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
        onWheel={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
        onTouchMove={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
        className="pointer-events-auto flex h-full w-full max-w-md flex-col overflow-hidden rounded-[2rem] border border-island-line bg-island-cream shadow-[0_24px_60px_rgba(38,70,83,0.3)]"
      >
        <PanelHeader
          icon={
            view === 'styles' ? (
              <button
                onClick={() => setView('overview')}
                className="flex h-full w-full items-center justify-center"
                title="返回房屋總覽"
              >
                <ArrowLeft size={20} strokeWidth={2.5} />
              </button>
            ) : (
              <Home size={20} strokeWidth={2.5} />
            )
          }
          title={view === 'styles' ? '更換房屋外觀' : '我的家'}
          subtitle={
            view === 'styles'
              ? '套用後位置、室內格局與家具都會完整保留'
              : '先看看目前的房子，再決定要做什麼'
          }
          onClose={onClose}
        />

        <div
          onTouchMove={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
          className="no-scrollbar flex-1 space-y-4 overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain bg-island-cream-2/40 p-5 sm:p-6"
          style={{ overflowY: 'auto', scrollbarWidth: 'none' }}
        >
          {view === 'overview' ? (
            <>
              {/* --- What is standing out there right now --------------------------------
                  The panel answers 「我現在的家長什麼樣子」 before it offers a single verb. Teal,
                  the same treatment PlacementItemRow gives an applied style, because that is
                  exactly what this is: the style currently in effect. */}
              <section className="rounded-[1.75rem] border border-island-teal bg-island-teal/6 p-4 sm:p-5">
                <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
                  <IconTile size={84} className="flex-shrink-0 bg-white">
                    <QVersionIcon itemId={home.style.itemId} size={72} />
                  </IconTile>
                  <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
                    <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-1 rounded-md border border-island-teal/20 bg-island-teal/10 px-2 py-0.5 text-[9px] font-black text-island-teal-dark">
                      使用中
                    </span>
                    <p className="mt-1.5 truncate text-lg font-black text-island-navy">{home.style.name}</p>
                    <p className="mt-0.5 line-clamp-2 text-xs font-black leading-relaxed text-island-navy-soft/70">
                      {home.style.description}
                    </p>
                  </div>
                </div>

                {/* Facing, stated. Rotation used to be invisible until the player was already
                    inside a transform session pressing R to find out what it did. */}
                <div className="mt-4 flex items-center gap-4 rounded-[1.25rem] border border-island-line bg-white p-3">
                  <HouseCompass rotation={home.rotation} />
                  <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
                    <p className="text-[10px] font-black uppercase tracking-widest text-island-navy-soft/70">
                      大門朝向
                    </p>
                    <p className="text-xl font-black text-island-navy">{facingLabel(home.rotation)}</p>
                    <p className="mt-0.5 text-[11px] font-bold leading-relaxed text-island-navy-soft/70">
                      到「移動與轉向」調整，每次轉 45°
                    </p>
                  </div>
                </div>
              </section>

              {/* --- The verbs ----------------------------------------------------------
                  Two, not three, and each says out loud what it will NOT do — because the whole
                  complaint this panel answers is a player being moved when they meant to browse. */}
              <section className="space-y-3">
                <DrawerSectionDivider
                  icon={<Palette size={13} strokeWidth={3} />}
                  label="房屋管理"
                  count={2}
                  owned
                />

                <HomeActionRow
                  icon={<Paintbrush size={24} strokeWidth={2.5} />}
                  label="更換外觀"
                  hint={`${styles.owned.length} 款可以使用 · 不會移動房子`}
                  onClick={() => setView('styles')}
                />

                <HomeActionRow
                  icon={<Move size={24} strokeWidth={2.5} />}
                  label="移動與轉向"
                  hint={
                    <>
                      拖曳搬移，按 <KeyCap size="sm">R</KeyCap> 或旋轉鍵轉 45°
                    </>
                  }
                  onClick={onStartTransform}
                />
              </section>

              <p className="px-2 pb-1 text-center text-[10px] font-bold leading-relaxed text-island-navy-soft/70">
                想佈置屋子裡面的家具，走到門口按「進入我的家」就可以了。
              </p>
            </>
          ) : (
            <>
              {/* --- Layer 2: the wardrobe ---------------------------------------------
                  The same rows, dividers and 購買 path as every other catalog in the game, so
                  「我在哪裡看過這個」 still has one answer. It replaces a modal that listed only
                  what the player already owned — from which the other six houses were invisible. */}
              {styles.owned.length > 0 && (
                <section className="space-y-3">
                  <DrawerSectionDivider {...OWNED_DIVIDER} count={styles.owned.length} owned />
                  {styles.owned.map(entry => (
                    <PlacementItemRow
                      key={entry.style.id}
                      item={entry.item}
                      owned
                      // Own-once, and never standing anywhere: a style is worn, not placed, so
                      // there is no stock to run out of (see PlacementItemRow's `outOfStock`).
                      available={1}
                      applied={home.style.id === entry.style.id}
                      // 毛胚屋 is granted with the Home and its inventory token is spent placing
                      // it, so `getOwnedCount` is 0 forever and StockBadge (which is what draws
                      // 已解鎖 on every other row) renders nothing. Without this the one style
                      // every player has is the one row with no chip at all.
                      tags={entry.style.purchasable ? undefined : (
                        <span className="rounded-md border border-island-line bg-island-cream-2 px-2 py-0.5 text-[9px] font-black text-island-navy-soft/80">
                          初始外觀
                        </span>
                      )}
                      placeLabel="套用"
                      placeIcon={<Paintbrush size={13} strokeWidth={2.5} />}
                      onPlace={() => onApplyStyle(entry.style.itemId)}
                      onBuy={() => onBuy(entry.item)}
                    />
                  ))}
                </section>
              )}

              {styles.unowned.length > 0 && (
                <section className="space-y-3 pt-1">
                  <DrawerSectionDivider {...UNOWNED_DIVIDER} count={styles.unowned.length} />
                  {styles.unowned.map(entry => (
                    <PlacementItemRow
                      key={entry.style.id}
                      item={entry.item}
                      owned={false}
                      available={0}
                      placeLabel="套用"
                      placeIcon={<Paintbrush size={13} strokeWidth={2.5} />}
                      onPlace={() => onApplyStyle(entry.style.itemId)}
                      onBuy={() => onBuy(entry.item)}
                    />
                  ))}
                </section>
              )}

              <p className="flex items-center justify-center gap-1.5 px-4 pb-1 pt-2 text-center text-[10px] font-bold text-island-navy-soft/70">
                <ShoppingBag size={11} strokeWidth={3} />
                商店的「室外 · 房屋外觀」賣的是同一批款式
              </p>
            </>
          )}
        </div>

        {/* 「我現在在編輯什麼」, permanently on screen while this panel is up. A footer strip rather
            than another button: it names the subject, it is not a verb. */}
        <div className="flex items-center gap-2.5 border-t border-island-line bg-island-cream px-5 py-3">
          <Compass size={14} strokeWidth={3} className="flex-shrink-0 text-island-teal" />
          <p className="min-w-0 flex-1 truncate text-[11px] font-black text-island-navy-soft">
            編輯中：我的家 · {home.style.name}
          </p>
          <span className="inline-flex flex-shrink-0 items-center gap-1 rounded-lg border border-island-line bg-island-cream-2 px-2 py-0.5 text-[10px] font-black text-island-navy-soft">
            <Package size={11} strokeWidth={3} />
            {styles.owned.length}/{HOUSE_STYLES.length}
          </span>
        </div>
      </motion.div>
    </motion.div>
  );
}

/**
 * One verb on the overview.
 *
 * Same anatomy as a build-dock tool card (solid tile, label, hint) so the two read as one family —
 * a player who has already learned the dock has learned this.
 */
function HomeActionRow({
  icon,
  label,
  hint,
  onClick,
}: {
  icon: React.ReactNode;
  label: string;
  hint: React.ReactNode;
  onClick: () => void;
}) {
  return (
    <button
      onClick={onClick}
      className="group flex w-full items-center gap-4 rounded-[1.5rem] border border-island-line bg-white p-4 text-left transition-all duration-300 hover:-translate-y-0.5 hover:border-island-teal hover:shadow-[0_14px_28px_-12px_rgba(42,157,143,0.45)] active:scale-[0.99]"
    >
      <IconTile size={56} solid className="flex-shrink-0 transition-transform duration-300 group-hover:scale-105">
        {icon}
      </IconTile>
      <span className="min-w-0 flex-1">
        <span className="block text-base font-black text-island-navy transition-colors group-hover:text-island-teal-dark">
          {label}
        </span>
        <span className="mt-0.5 block text-xs font-bold leading-relaxed text-island-navy-soft/80">
          {hint}
        </span>
      </span>
    </button>
  );
}
```

## src/components/UI/HomeSetupGuide.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { AnimatePresence } from 'motion/react';
import { Home, MapPin, Sparkles } from 'lucide-react';
import { useApp } from '../../context/AppContext';
import { CameraMode, View } from '../../types';
import { FIRST_PERSON_ZOOM, THIRD_PERSON_ZOOM } from '../../constants/cameraZoom';
import { hasPlacedHome } from '../../hooks/usePlayerHome';
import { STARTER_HOUSE_ITEM_ID, getHouseStyle } from '../../constants/houseStyles';
import { playSound, SoundEffect, triggerHaptic } from '../../lib/soundUtils';
import { ModalOverlay, ModalShell, PanelHeader, Button, IconTile, MODAL_ABOVE_DOCK } from './DesignKit';
import { ONBOARDING_MODAL_CLASS, useOnboardingSlot } from '../../lib/onboardingQueue';

/**
 * First-time guidance for establishing the player's Home.
 *
 * Shows exactly when the player holds the Starter House but hasn't placed it — i.e. the
 * condition *is* the game state, so there's no "have they seen it?" flag to persist and no way
 * for it to reappear once the Home exists. Dismissing it only hides it for the session; the
 * player is nudged again next login until they actually place their home.
 *
 * That "no flag, ask the world" design is deliberate and stays — but it does mean this guide
 * cannot end until `placeHome` actually lands, so a save the server refuses reads from here as a
 * tutorial that will not stop asking. It looked like a tutorial loop; it was a rejected write
 * with nothing reporting it. The fix belongs at the two ends, not here: the write layer now
 * returns its failure instead of throwing it away (lib/firebase.ts) and the placement session
 * says so out loud (IslandEditorOverlay / PlacementGhost). Do NOT "fix" a recurrence of this by
 * adding a seen-flag here — that would hide a broken save behind a tutorial that quietly gave up.
 */
export function HomeSetupGuide() {
  const {
    profile, currentView, setCurrentView, setActivePlacementItem, activePlacementItem,
    setCameraMode, setUiScale,
  } = useApp();
  const [dismissed, setDismissed] = useState(false);

  const holdsStarterHouse = !!profile?.inventory?.includes(STARTER_HOUSE_ITEM_ID);
  const needsHome = !!profile && !hasPlacedHome(profile) && holdsStarterHouse;

  // Once the Home exists, reset local dismissal so a later Home-less state (only reachable via
  // a data reset) would guide again rather than staying silently suppressed.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!needsHome) setDismissed(false);
  }, [needsHome]);

  // Last in the first-run queue (lib/onboardingQueue.ts): the login bonus is
  // cleared and the 新手引導 has walked the HUD before this asks for a decision
  // about the island. Nothing is lost by waiting — the condition above IS the
  // game state, so the moment the step ahead finishes this appears on its own.
  //
  // `activePlacementItem` is part of the claim, not just of `isVisible`: once
  // the player has armed the house the guide has handed over to the placement
  // system, and while a session is running it must not still be holding the
  // onboarding slot against whatever comes next.
  const isVisible = useOnboardingSlot(
    'homeSetup',
    needsHome && !dismissed && currentView === View.HOME && activePlacementItem === null,
  );
  const starterStyle = getHouseStyle('starter');

  const handleStart = () => {
    playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
    triggerHaptic('medium');
    // Arms the placement ghost and stays on the island view. The editing panel
    // (IslandEditorOverlay) with its "drag / R to rotate / double-click to confirm" copy follows
    // the session rather than the view, so the house is sited with instructions on screen here
    // exactly as it would be in build mode. If they cancel, build mode still offers the Starter
    // House as its only placeable item until the Home exists.
    // Third person for the siting itself. AppContext already puts a Home-less player's camera here
    // when their profile loads, so this is the second half of that guarantee rather than a repeat
    // of it: the player may have gone first-person in between, and this button is the exact moment
    // the game asks them to look at a plot of ground and a house they cannot see from inside their
    // own head. Only a zoom that is genuinely in the first-person band is touched.
    setCameraMode(CameraMode.THIRD_PERSON);
    setUiScale(prev => (prev >= FIRST_PERSON_ZOOM ? THIRD_PERSON_ZOOM : prev));
    setActivePlacementItem(STARTER_HOUSE_ITEM_ID);
    setCurrentView(View.HOME);
    setDismissed(true);
  };

  const handleLater = () => {
    playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
    setDismissed(true);
  };

  return (
    <AnimatePresence>
      {/* ONBOARDING_MODAL_CLASS marks this as a first-run scrim, so the 新手引導's
          "is a blocking dialog up?" probe doesn't mistake the guide queued behind
          it for a reason to stand down — the two are sequenced by the queue, not
          by the DOM. */}
      {isVisible && (
        <ModalOverlay className={`${ONBOARDING_MODAL_CLASS} ${MODAL_ABOVE_DOCK}`} onClick={handleLater}>
          <ModalShell maxWidthClassName="max-w-md">
            <PanelHeader
              icon={<Home size={20} strokeWidth={2.5} />}
              title="你的第一棟房屋"
              subtitle="歡迎來到你的島嶼"
              onClose={handleLater}
            />

            <div className="p-6 md:p-8 flex flex-col gap-5 text-left">
              <div className="flex items-start gap-4">
                <IconTile size={56} active className="text-island-teal-dark shrink-0">
                  <MapPin size={24} strokeWidth={2.5} />
                </IconTile>
                <p className="text-sm font-bold text-island-navy leading-relaxed pt-1">
                  這是你的第一棟房屋「{starterStyle.name}」，
                  請找一個喜歡的位置放置它，那裡就會成為你的家。
                </p>
              </div>

              <div className="bg-island-cream-2 border border-island-line rounded-2xl p-4 flex items-start gap-3">
                <Sparkles size={16} className="text-island-gold shrink-0 mt-0.5" strokeWidth={2.5} />
                <p className="text-xs font-bold text-island-navy-soft leading-relaxed">
                  之後在商店購買的房屋外觀，都會直接套用到這個家上，
                  你的家具、室內與收納都會完整保留。
                </p>
              </div>

              <div className="flex gap-3 pt-1">
                <Button variant="secondary" onClick={handleLater} className="flex-1 py-3 text-sm">
                  稍後再說
                </Button>
                <Button variant="primary" onClick={handleStart} className="flex-1 py-3 text-sm">
                  <MapPin size={16} strokeWidth={2.5} />
                  <span>開始放置我的家</span>
                </Button>
              </div>
            </div>
          </ModalShell>
        </ModalOverlay>
      )}
    </AnimatePresence>
  );
}
```

## src/components/UI/HudFrame.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import React from 'react';
import { motion } from 'motion/react';

/**
 * Shared CSS-Grid layout frame for the persistent HUD chrome.
 *
 * WHY THIS EXISTS: every floating HUD element used to be independently
 * `position: fixed` with hand-tuned pixel offsets that encoded other
 * elements' sizes (SideButtons' `top-[360px]` tuned to TopBar's height,
 * AccountPanel's `top-[128px] left-[104px]`, PettingMiniGame's `left-[88px]`,
 * ...). Those couplings drifted out of sync across resolutions/aspect ratios
 * and caused the overlap / off-screen / clipping RWD bugs. This frame places
 * each element into a grid region instead, so no element needs to know any
 * other's size — the grid keeps clusters structurally separated and the
 * `--hud-inset`/`--hud-gap` tokens (src/index.css) drive all spacing.
 *
 * LAYOUT: a `fixed inset-0` 3x3 grid (`auto | 1fr | auto` both axes). The
 * centre cell is intentionally left empty and everything is
 * `pointer-events-none` except the real cards, so pointer events fall
 * through the middle to the 3D canvas underneath (camera drag/orbit must
 * keep working). Padding is `max(--hud-inset, env(safe-area-inset-*))` so
 * corner chrome never clips on notched / rounded-corner devices.
 *
 * Z-INDEX: the frame is one stacking context on the `.z-hud-frame` tier (see
 * the z-index layer doc in index.css). The `.z-hud-*` tiers used by children
 * now order pieces *within* the frame as a local sub-scale. Anything that
 * must out-rank the whole HUD (floating panels, toasts, modals, loading,
 * MobileControls' touch layers) stays OUTSIDE the frame as an App-level
 * sibling on its own global tier.
 */

export type HudArea =
  | 'left-rail'
  | 'top-center'
  | 'top-right'
  | 'mid-right'
  | 'bottom-center'
  | 'bottom-right'
  | 'bottom-left';

// Grid placement per region. Centre-anchored bands span all columns
// (`1 / -1`) and centre on the viewport, deliberately overlapping the side
// columns — CSS Grid allows items to share cells, so a wide element in one
// row (e.g. a wide mobile TopBar in the left rail) can never steal width
// from a centred element in another row (e.g. the bottom NavBar).
const areaStyle: Record<HudArea, React.CSSProperties> = {
  // `maxHeight` adds the scroll gutter back on purpose. `.hud-scroll-gutter`
  // (index.css) pads this element by `--hud-gutter` on all four sides and
  // cancels it with an equal negative margin — but the padding is INSIDE the
  // border box, so a plain `maxHeight: 100%` handed the rail's contents
  // `100% - 2 * --hud-gutter` (~88px less) of usable height and made it start
  // scrolling ~88px too early. Because the rail also hides its scrollbar
  // (`no-scrollbar`), that overflow showed up as the bottom signpost tag
  // (角色動作) sliced in half with nothing on screen saying it could scroll.
  // Growing the cap by the same gutter it reserves lets the content use the
  // whole grid area; the extra 2 * --hud-gutter is transparent padding, so
  // nothing moves and card shadows still have room to paint.
  'left-rail':     { gridColumn: '1', gridRow: '1 / -1', justifySelf: 'start', alignSelf: 'start', maxHeight: 'calc(100% + var(--hud-gutter, 0px) * 2)' },
  'top-center':    { gridColumn: '1 / -1', gridRow: '1', justifySelf: 'center', alignSelf: 'start' },
  'top-right':     { gridColumn: '3', gridRow: '1', justifySelf: 'end', alignSelf: 'start' },
  // The right rail's lower dock: the zoom dial, then 幸運轉盤, stacked and parked at the FOOT of
  // the middle row.
  //
  // `alignSelf: 'end'` rather than `'center'`, and one region rather than two. 幸運轉盤 first went
  // in as a second right-edge region aligned to the row's end while this one stayed centred, which
  // is precisely the failure this frame exists to remove: two boxes in the SAME grid cell with
  // different alignments overlap as soon as their combined height exceeds the row, and on a
  // 1440x900 window the dial's lower button landed on top of the wheel's ticket chip. Members of
  // one flex column cannot do that to each other at any height.
  'mid-right':     { gridColumn: '3', gridRow: '2', justifySelf: 'end', alignSelf: 'end' },
  'bottom-center': { gridColumn: '1 / -1', gridRow: '3', justifySelf: 'center', alignSelf: 'end' },
  'bottom-right':  { gridColumn: '3', gridRow: '3', justifySelf: 'end', alignSelf: 'end' },
  'bottom-left':   { gridColumn: '1', gridRow: '3', justifySelf: 'start', alignSelf: 'end' },
};

const areaAlignClass: Record<HudArea, string> = {
  'left-rail':     'items-start',
  'top-center':    'items-center',
  'top-right':     'items-end',
  'mid-right':     'items-end',
  'bottom-center': 'items-center',
  'bottom-right':  'items-end',
  'bottom-left':   'items-start',
};

export function HudFrame({
  children,
  className = '',
}: {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  className?: string;
}) {
  return (
    <motion.div
      initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
      animate={{ opacity: 1 }}
      exit={{ opacity: 0 }}
      className={`fixed inset-0 z-hud-frame grid pointer-events-none ${className}`}
      style={{
        gridTemplateColumns: 'auto minmax(0, 1fr) auto',
        gridTemplateRows: 'auto minmax(0, 1fr) auto',
        // top / right / bottom / left, each never smaller than the device
        // safe-area inset (index.html opts in via viewport-fit=cover).
        paddingTop: 'max(var(--hud-inset), env(safe-area-inset-top))',
        paddingRight: 'max(var(--hud-inset), env(safe-area-inset-right))',
        paddingBottom: 'max(var(--hud-inset), env(safe-area-inset-bottom))',
        paddingLeft: 'max(var(--hud-inset), env(safe-area-inset-left))',
      }}
    >
      {children}
    </motion.div>
  );
}

/**
 * A single HUD region (grid cell) that aligns its content toward the correct
 * viewport edge and spaces stacked cards by `--hud-gap`. Stays
 * `pointer-events-none`; the cards inside re-enable `pointer-events-auto`
 * themselves, exactly as before.
 *
 * CLIPPING BOUNDARY — read before adding a pop-out to a rail: `left-rail` is a
 * scroll container (see the safety valve below), and per the CSS overflow spec
 * a box with `overflow-y: auto` computes `overflow-x` to `auto` too. So this
 * region clips its content on BOTH axes, at the width of its widest card —
 * roughly the profile card's ~220px. That silently cropped SideButtons' emote
 * tray, which flew out to ~550px. A clip is not a stacking problem: no z-index,
 * no taller rail and no hardcoded offset can escape it. Anything that must
 * extend past a region's own box (a tool panel, a hover label, a dropdown) is
 * portaled out with `AnchoredPopover` (AnchoredPopover.tsx) and positioned from
 * its trigger's measured rect.
 *
 * The same clip also caught things that were never trying to leave the rail:
 * a card's own SHADOW is painted outside its border box, so the region was
 * slicing it off at its edge — the MiniMap's bottom shadow became a hard
 * horizontal line, which reads as the map itself being cropped, and the left
 * edge it deliberately tucks into the corner with `-ml-*` was shaved off.
 * `.hud-scroll-gutter` (index.css) reserves transparent room inside the scroll
 * box and cancels it with an equal negative margin, so cards can paint outside
 * themselves while the region stays exactly where it was. That is a property of
 * the region, not of any one card: nothing here special-cases the MiniMap.
 */
export function HudRegion({
  area,
  children,
  className = '',
}: {
  area: HudArea;
  children: React.ReactNode;
  className?: string;
}) {
  return (
    <div
      className={`pointer-events-none flex flex-col ${areaAlignClass[area]} ${
        // Safety valve: on extremely short viewports the top-anchored left
        // rail could exceed the frame height — let it scroll rather than
        // overflow onto the bottom chrome. Responsive sizing keeps this from
        // triggering in normal use.
        //
        // `.hud-scroll-gutter` is not optional decoration next to it: making a
        // region scrollable also makes it CLIP (see the note below), which cut
        // every rail card's shadow off at the region's edge. The gutter gives
        // that painting room back without moving the region. The two classes
        // belong together — never add the overflow without it.
        area === 'left-rail' ? 'overflow-y-auto no-scrollbar hud-scroll-gutter' : ''
      } ${className}`}
      style={{ ...areaStyle[area], gap: 'var(--hud-gap)' }}
    >
      {children}
    </div>
  );
}

```

## src/components/UI/InteractionPrompt.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { motion, AnimatePresence } from 'motion/react';
import {
  Armchair, Bath, BedDouble, BookOpen, Brush, DoorOpen, Droplets, Eye, Flame, Hand, MessageCircle,
  Power, ShoppingBag, Sparkles, Sprout, Utensils, Wind,
} from 'lucide-react';
import { getItemById } from '../../constants/items';
import { useApp } from '../../context/AppContext';
import { View } from '../../types';
import { useIsTouchDevice } from '../../hooks/useIsTouchDevice';
import { playerBus } from '../../lib/playerBus';
import { getPetSpec, petCompanionNoun } from '../../constants/pets';
import { playSound, SoundEffect, triggerHaptic } from '../../lib/soundUtils';
import { HintBubble } from './DesignKit';
import { PROMPT_SAFE_MARGIN } from '../../constants/hudLayout';

interface InteractionPromptProps {
  onEnterBuilding: () => void;
}

/**
 * The touch button's icon for a furniture interaction, keyed by the small closed set the catalog
 * speaks (constants/furnitureInteractions.ts's InteractionIcon).
 *
 * The catalog names an idea — 'sit', 'lie', 'book' — and this file turns it into a component, so
 * the item data never has to know which icon library the HUD is drawn with. Same separation the
 * shop's category icons already use (CategoryIcon.tsx).
 */
const INTERACTION_ICONS: Record<string, typeof Hand> = {
  sit: Armchair,
  lie: BedDouble,
  bath: Bath,
  hand: Hand,
  door: DoorOpen,
  panel: Power,
  cook: Utensils,
  droplet: Droplets,
  eye: Eye,
  book: BookOpen,
  sparkle: Sparkles,
  flame: Flame,
  brush: Brush,
  push: Wind,
};

// Keeps the floating badge clear of the persistent HUD chrome around the
// edges (left rail, ZoomControl, top banners, bottom NavBar). The keep-out
// margins live in constants/hudLayout.ts so they stay tied to the HUD layout
// instead of being magic numbers here — a plain screen-space clamp is enough
// since the interactable is always within a few metres of the player (see
// InteractionPromptTracker's trigger radii), so the projected point is
// normally well inside this safe zone; this only guards rare edge cases.

/**
 * Floating "above the object" interaction badge - anchored to whichever single nearest
 * interactable (building door / hammock / dog / a patch of 離線環境變化 to tidy)
 * InteractionPromptTracker.tsx (living inside the
 * Canvas, see Scene.tsx) projects into screen space each frame. This component itself never
 * touches THREE.Camera/scene: it only polls playerBus.interactionPrompt via requestAnimationFrame
 * and applies the result as a direct transform, then renders the small card/icon on top.
 *
 * Desktop shows a "[E]" key badge; touch devices show a tappable icon instead (no keyboard hint
 * makes sense on a screen with no keyboard) - the same card doubles as the actual button either
 * way, so tapping it on mobile activates the interaction directly.
 */
export function InteractionPrompt({ onEnterBuilding }: InteractionPromptProps) {
  const isTouch = useIsTouchDevice();
  const {
    currentView, nearbyBuilding, nearbyInteractable, triggerExternalAction, isWorkoutActive, profile,
    pendingPetFood,
  } = useApp();
  const wrapperRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  // `label` and `icon` ride along with the polled prompt rather than being derived here: what a
  // piece of furniture offers is decided once, by the scan that found it (Three/Avatar.tsx via
  // playerBus.nearbyInteraction), so the badge and the key can never end up offering different
  // things. See constants/furnitureInteractions.ts.
  const [prompt, setPrompt] = useState<{ key: string; visible: boolean; label: string; icon: string } | null>(null);

  // Polls playerBus.interactionPrompt (written every Canvas frame by InteractionPromptTracker)
  // and applies its x/y as a direct style.transform - bypassing React state for the
  // high-frequency position updates so this doesn't re-render 60x/sec. React state is only used
  // for the low-frequency fields (which target, whether it's currently visible), which is what
  // actually needs to trigger a re-render (swapping label/icon, playing the enter/exit fade).
  useEffect(() => {
    let raf: number;
    const tick = () => {
      const p = playerBus.interactionPrompt;
      if (wrapperRef.current && p) {
        const clampedX = Math.min(Math.max(p.x, PROMPT_SAFE_MARGIN.left), window.innerWidth - PROMPT_SAFE_MARGIN.right);
        const clampedY = Math.min(Math.max(p.y, PROMPT_SAFE_MARGIN.top), window.innerHeight - PROMPT_SAFE_MARGIN.bottom);
        wrapperRef.current.style.transform = `translate3d(${clampedX}px, ${clampedY}px, 0)`;
      }
      setPrompt((prev) => {
        if (!p) return prev === null ? prev : null;
        const furniture = playerBus.nearbyInteraction;
        // A resident's label changes mid-conversation (聊天 → 繼續聊天), so it rides the same
        // low-frequency comparison as a piece of furniture's verb rather than being read at render.
        const label = p.key === 'npc' ? playerBus.npcTarget?.label ?? '' : furniture?.verb ?? '';
        const icon = furniture?.icon ?? 'hand';
        if (prev && prev.key === p.key && prev.visible === p.visible
          && prev.label === label && prev.icon === icon) return prev;
        return { key: p.key, visible: p.visible, label, icon };
      });
      raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
    };
    raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
    return () => cancelAnimationFrame(raf);
  }, []);

  // Both worlds. Furniture is the only thing that prompts indoors, and the badge is identical
  // there — same anchoring, same card, same key — because it is the same component driven by a
  // second tracker inside the house's Canvas (see Three/InteractionPromptTracker.tsx).
  const inPromptableView = currentView === View.HOME || currentView === View.BUILDING_INTERIOR;
  if (!inPromptableView || isWorkoutActive || !prompt) return null;

  let label = '';
  let onActivate = () => {};
  // The touch button carries the verb the badge is offering. 摸摸 and 進入 are both a hand;
  // 整理 is not, and a hand icon over 「整理這裡」 reads as petting the weeds.
  let ActionIcon = Hand;

  if (prompt.key === 'interactable') {
    // The VERB, not 「使用 <名稱>」. A badge reading 「使用 五星級雙人床」 says nothing about what
    // pressing the key will do; 「躺下」 does. The piece decides its own verb in the catalog, so
    // 沙發 offers 坐下, 許願井 offers 許願, and nothing here branches per item.
    label = prompt.label || `使用 ${nearbyInteractable ?? ''}`.trim();
    ActionIcon = INTERACTION_ICONS[prompt.icon] ?? Hand;
    // No sound here, unlike the branches below: the furniture path plays its own, in the one
    // place that knows what was activated (Three/Avatar.tsx's handleAction), so tapping the badge
    // and pressing E sound identical instead of the tap getting an extra UI click.
    onActivate = () => {
      triggerHaptic('light');
      triggerExternalAction();
    };
  } else if (prompt.key === 'dog') {
    // The 'dog' slot is whichever animal is actually standing there — read off the bus, so with
    // more than one companion out the badge names the one the player walked up to rather than
    // 「the pet」 resolved from the profile. Naming it 小狗 unconditionally called a 橘貓 a dog, so
    // the label follows that animal's own species.
    const petId = playerBus.petTargetId ?? profile?.equippedItems?.find(id => getPetSpec(id));
    // 小狗 / 小貓 / 小鳥, from the species table (constants/pets.ts) rather than from a
    // `Record<PetSpecies, string>` kept in this file — which is what it used to be. A fourth
    // species would have been called 「寵物」 on this badge until somebody remembered to add a
    // fourth row here, and this badge is the one place the animal is spoken to by name.
    const noun = petCompanionNoun(petId);
    if (pendingPetFood) {
      // 餵食模式 — the 「先選好飼料再走過去」 fast path (see UI/PetCarePanel.tsx). The SAME badge and
      // the SAME key: a companion the player is standing next to offers exactly one thing, and
      // which one is decided by whether they have already chosen a food. A second prompt competing
      // for the same corner of the screen is how 互動 and 餵食 would start covering each other and
      // the front door.
      label = `餵${noun}吃${getItemById(pendingPetFood)?.name ?? '飼料'}`;
      ActionIcon = Utensils;
      onActivate = () => {
        playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
        triggerHaptic('light');
        // Dispatched rather than written here, for the reason 整理 is: the write, the sound and the
        // toast belong with the component that owns the feature (UI/PetFeeding.tsx), not the badge.
        window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('pet-feed'));
      };
    } else {
      // 與寵物互動 — the ordinary case, and the brief's §16. The badge offers ONE thing and it is
      // small; the choice between 餵食 and 摸摸 is inside the panel that opens
      // (UI/PetInteractionPanel.tsx), where there is room to also show the animal's name and how it
      // is doing. It used to offer 摸摸 directly, which made petting one press and feeding five —
      // and left a player who wanted to feed their pet with no way to find that out from the world.
      label = `與${noun}互動`;
      onActivate = () => {
        playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
        triggerHaptic('light');
        window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('pet-interact'));
      };
    }
  } else if (prompt.key === 'npc') {
    // 居民（constants/npcSocial.ts）. The label comes off the bus with the target — 「與餅乾兔園丁
    // 聊天」 before the conversation, 「繼續聊天」 during it — so this file does not learn who lives
    // where. The press is an event naming WHICH resident, the same shape as the merchant's, and
    // the E key (Three/Avatar.tsx) sends the identical one: the walker that draws her decides what
    // it means, and the avatar turns to her and gestures.
    label = prompt.label || '聊天';
    ActionIcon = MessageCircle;
    onActivate = () => {
      playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
      triggerHaptic('light');
      const npcId = playerBus.npcTarget?.npcId;
      if (npcId) window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('npc-interact', { detail: { npcId } }));
    };
  } else if (prompt.key === 'merchant') {
    // 旅行商人. The label is the MERCHANT's own (constants/merchants.ts's `prompt`), read off the
    // bus rather than written here — so a second visitor says 「與家具商人交談」 without this file
    // learning that a second visitor exists.
    //
    // MOBILE IS THIS SAME BUTTON. There is no separate touch entry point for the merchant and
    // there must not be: on a touch device the badge already IS the button (see `isTouch` below),
    // so tapping the 🛍 icon floating over his head does exactly what E does on a keyboard. That
    // is the whole of §16's mobile requirement, and it costs nothing because the merchant joined
    // the existing prompt instead of bringing its own UI.
    label = playerBus.merchantTarget?.label ?? '與旅行商人交易';
    ActionIcon = ShoppingBag;
    onActivate = () => {
      playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
      triggerHaptic('light');
      const merchantId = playerBus.merchantTarget?.merchantId;
      if (merchantId) {
        window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('merchant-interact', { detail: { merchantId } }));
      }
    };
  } else if (prompt.key === 'tidy') {
    // 離線環境變化. The count comes off the bus rather than out of a second scan here, so the
    // number on the badge is exactly what the press will clear (see findTidyTarget). Dispatched
    // as an event for the same reason 摸摸 is: the work — the write, the sound, the toast — belongs
    // with the component that owns that feature (UI/IslandTidy.tsx), not in the badge.
    label = `整理這裡 ×${playerBus.tidyTarget?.count ?? 1}`;
    onActivate = () => {
      playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
      triggerHaptic('light');
      window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('island-tidy'));
    };
    ActionIcon = Sprout;
  } else if (prompt.key === 'building' && nearbyBuilding) {
    label = `進入 ${nearbyBuilding.name}`;
    onActivate = onEnterBuilding;
  } else {
    return null;
  }

  return (
    <div
      ref={wrapperRef}
      className="fixed top-0 left-0 z-hud-toolbar pointer-events-none will-change-transform"
    >
      <div className="-translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-full flex flex-col items-center">
        <AnimatePresence mode="wait">
          {prompt.visible && (
            <motion.button
              key={prompt.key}
              initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 8, scale: 0.85 }}
              animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0, scale: 1 }}
              exit={{ opacity: 0, y: 8, scale: 0.85 }}
              transition={{ duration: 0.18, ease: 'easeOut' }}
              whileHover={{ y: -2 }}
              whileTap={{ scale: 0.94 }}
              onClick={onActivate}
              className="pointer-events-auto flex flex-col items-center gap-1.5 cursor-pointer group"
            >
              <HintBubble
                nub="arrow"
                className="px-4 py-2.5 flex items-center gap-2.5 group-hover:shadow-[0_8px_26px_rgba(38,70,83,0.24)] transition-shadow"
              >
                {isTouch ? (
                  <span className="w-8 h-8 rounded-full bg-island-teal flex items-center justify-center shadow-[0_2px_6px_rgba(38,70,83,0.2)] flex-shrink-0">
                    <ActionIcon size={16} strokeWidth={2.5} className="text-white" />
                  </span>
                ) : (
                  <span className="w-7 h-7 bg-island-cream-2 rounded-lg flex items-center justify-center font-mono border border-island-line shadow-[0_2px_6px_rgba(38,70,83,0.12)] text-sm text-island-navy flex-shrink-0">
                    E
                  </span>
                )}
                <span className="text-island-navy text-sm whitespace-nowrap">{label}</span>
              </HintBubble>
            </motion.button>
          )}
        </AnimatePresence>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```
