## src/components/UI/PurchaseDialog.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { useState } from 'react';
import { getBalance } from '../../constants/currency';
import { motion } from 'motion/react';
import { Check, Coins, Sparkles, Zap } from 'lucide-react';
import confetti from 'canvas-confetti';
import { useApp } from '../../context/AppContext';
import { ItemDefinition } from '../../constants/items';
import { getItemCategoryLabel } from '../../utils/categoryUtils';
import { getAvailableStock, getOwnedCount, isStackableItem } from '../../utils/inventory';
import { getPlayerXp, getXpRemaining, getXpRequirement, isXpLocked } from '../../utils/unlock';
import {
  FRAGMENTS_TO_UNLOCK,
  canUnlockWithFragments,
  collectsFragments,
  getFragmentCount,
  getRaffleTickets,
  isRepeatableFragmentItem,
} from '../../constants/fragments';
import { playSound, triggerHaptic } from '../../lib/soundUtils';
import { playerBus } from '../../lib/playerBus';
import { getHairSpec } from '../../constants/hair';
import { getPurchaseFx, RarityFxSpec } from '../../constants/rarityFx';
import { getItemRarity } from '../../utils/debugOverrides';
import { isNpcPortrait, NpcPortrait, QVersionIcon } from '../QVersionIcon';
import { HairSpinPreview } from './HairSpinPreview';
import { FragmentMeter, FragmentShard, RaffleTicket } from './FragmentProgress';
import { RarityReveal } from './RarityReveal';
import { Button, IconTile, ModalOverlay, ModalShell, PanelHeader, SCRIM_NEUTRAL } from './DesignKit';

/**
 * The one purchase confirmation in the game.
 *
 * Every buy button — the shop catalog, the outdoor build rail's 購買/再購買, the indoor
 * furniture drawer's not-yet-owned section — opens this same dialog, so the price shown, the
 * balance check, the confirmation copy and the celebration are identical wherever a player
 * spends gold. Buying from where you are standing is then genuinely the same act as buying from
 * the shop, rather than a second, quieter purchase flow that happens to charge the same amount.
 *
 * The write itself belongs to the Shop System (context/useShopActions.ts); this is only its UI.
 *
 * ## The second route
 *
 * An item can also be owned by collecting {@link FRAGMENTS_TO_UNLOCK} of its own 商品碎片
 * (constants/fragments.ts). That is not a second dialog: it is this one, with a different thing being
 * spent — the same preview, the same confirmation, the same celebration. When a stack is full the
 * fragment route is what the dialog offers first, because it costs nothing, and the gold route stays
 * one tap away underneath for a player who would rather keep the fragments for the 抽獎券 that a
 * gold purchase would turn them into.
 */
export function PurchaseDialog({
  item,
  onClose,
  zIndexClassName = 'z-modal',
}: {
  /** The item being bought — `null` closes the dialog. */
  item: ItemDefinition | null;
  onClose: () => void;
  /** Override only when the caller lives in its own local z sub-scale (e.g. ShopView). */
  zIndexClassName?: string;
}) {
  const { profile, purchaseItem, unlockWithFragments } = useApp();
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const [purchased, setPurchased] = useState(false);
  /**
   * The player has chosen to pay gold even though the fragment route is open.
   *
   * Opt-IN rather than opt-out: with a full stack, fragments are free and gold is not, so defaulting
   * to gold would be the shop charging for something already earned. The escape hatch exists because
   * keeping the fragments is a real choice — buying with gold converts them to 抽獎券 (see
   * `fragmentPatchForPurchase`), which a player saving for the 轉盤 may well prefer.
   */
  const [payWithGold, setPayWithGold] = useState(false);
  // Set for 史詩/神話 only. While it is on, the reveal owns when this dialog closes — see
  // handleConfirm.
  const [revealing, setRevealing] = useState(false);

  if (!item) return null;

  const balance = getBalance(profile, 'coins');
  const cannotAfford = balance < item.price;
  // 經驗值-unlocked items (utils/unlock.ts) come through this same dialog: it is still the one
  // place ownership is confirmed, only the thing being spent is training rather than gold — so
  // the readout below swaps currency for XP rather than the flow forking into a second dialog.
  const xpRequired = getXpRequirement(item);
  const xpLocked = isXpLocked(profile, item);
  const ownedCount = getOwnedCount(profile, item.id);
  const stackable = isStackableItem(item.id);
  const hairSpec = getHairSpec(item.id);

  // The tier this purchase celebrates as. ALWAYS a tier — every catalog item is graded
  // (constants/rarity.ts) — which is why the reveal below is gated on `revealing` alone rather
  // than on the item having one. Read through getItemRarity rather than off the item so the
  // ?rarity= debug override reaches the celebration too: 史詩 is sixteen items and 神話 is one, so
  // that URL is still the only practical way to look at either of their reveals.
  const rarity = getItemRarity(item);
  const fx = getPurchaseFx(rarity);

  // The fragment route, and whether this confirmation is currently spending fragments or gold.
  const fragmentsHeld = getFragmentCount(profile, item.id);
  // 「還在收集嗎」, not 「已擁有嗎」. A stackable item keeps collecting after the first copy — see
  // constants/fragments.ts. This is what decides whether the meter below is drawn at all, and it has
  // to be the same predicate the write path uses, or the dialog will offer a route the write refuses
  // (or hide one it would have allowed).
  const stillCollecting = collectsFragments(item.id, ownedCount > 0);
  const fragmentReady = canUnlockWithFragments(profile, item.id, ownedCount > 0);
  const usingFragments = fragmentReady && !payWithGold;

  const close = () => {
    setPurchased(false);
    setBusy(false);
    setRevealing(false);
    setPayWithGold(false);
    onClose();
  };

  // Fires a tier's bursts on canvas-confetti's global canvas. Only the tiers without a reveal
  // come through here; 史詩/神話 hand their bursts to RarityReveal, which owns a canvas that can
  // actually be seen above the reveal's own dim.
  const celebrate = (fx: RarityFxSpec) => {
    for (const burst of fx.confetti) {
      const fire = () => confetti({
        particleCount: burst.particleCount,
        spread: burst.spread,
        colors: burst.colors,
        ticks: burst.ticks,
        startVelocity: burst.startVelocity,
        angle: burst.angle,
        origin: burst.origin ?? { x: 0.5, y: 0.6 },
        shapes: ['circle', 'square'],
        disableForReducedMotion: true,
      });
      if (burst.delay) setTimeout(fire, burst.delay); else fire();
    }
  };

  const handleConfirm = async () => {
    if (busy || purchased) return;
    // The tap's own acknowledgement, deliberately the lightest one available: how hard the phone
    // buzzes for the PURCHASE is graded by tier below, and a heavy thud on the press would land
    // harder than 普通's own celebration and invert the ladder before it started.
    triggerHaptic('light');
    setBusy(true);
    // The two routes differ in exactly one line — what is spent. Everything after it (the tier's
    // haptics, its sounds, its confetti or its reveal) is the same table played back, because owning
    // the item is the same event however it was earned.
    const result = usingFragments
      ? await unlockWithFragments(item.id)
      : await purchaseItem(item.id);
    setBusy(false);
    if (result !== 'ok') return;

    // Everything from here is one row of constants/rarityFx.ts (`fx`) played back. No branch in
    // this function knows a tier name — adding a tier is a row in that table, not an `if` here.
    // `hapticDelayMs` is what lets the reveal tiers thump when the item LANDS rather than when the
    // button was pressed — see constants/rarityFx.ts. It defaults to 0, so every other tier still
    // buzzes on the frame it always did.
    fx.haptic.forEach((strength, i) => {
      const at = (fx.hapticDelayMs ?? 0) + i * fx.hapticGapMs;
      if (at === 0) triggerHaptic(strength);
      else setTimeout(() => triggerHaptic(strength), at);
    });
    for (const sound of fx.sounds) {
      if (sound.delayMs) setTimeout(() => playSound(sound.effect, sound.volume), sound.delayMs);
      else playSound(sound.effect, sound.volume);
    }

    setPurchased(true);
    playerBus.happyReactionCount = (playerBus.happyReactionCount || 0) + 1;

    if (fx.reveal) {
      // No close timer at all: the reveal calls back when it has finished playing. This used to
      // be a flat 1200ms for every purchase, which is most of a second SHORTER than the reveal —
      // the dialog would vanish mid-flash. Swapping in a larger constant would have been the same
      // bug with a better number.
      setRevealing(true);
    } else {
      celebrate(fx);
      if (fx.closeDelayMs !== null) setTimeout(close, fx.closeDelayMs);
    }
  };

  return (
    <>
    {/* Neutral scrim, not the ink one every other modal uses. Two reasons, and the second is the
        one that decided it.
        A purchase is the only modal in the game that can hand straight over to a full-screen
        celebration, and the reveal's ground is neutral black — on the ink scrim the handover was
        a blue screen turning into a dark one, which is a colour change happening at the exact
        moment the player is supposed to be looking at what they bought.
        And it is what the player is looking at for the whole confirmation before that: navy at 45%
        over the cream shop is roughly #9AA5A4, which is a blue-grey wash. It suits a settings panel;
        it does not suit the moment a warm shop is about to give someone a pet. */}
    <ModalOverlay zIndexClassName={zIndexClassName} scrimClassName={SCRIM_NEUTRAL} onClick={close}>
      <ModalShell maxWidthClassName="max-w-sm">
        <PanelHeader
          icon={
            usingFragments
              ? <FragmentShard size={20} />
              : xpRequired > 0
                ? <Zap size={20} strokeWidth={2.5} />
                : <Coins size={20} strokeWidth={2.5} />
          }
          title={usingFragments ? '請確認碎片解鎖' : xpRequired > 0 ? '請確認解鎖獎勵' : '請確認購買商品'}
          subtitle={usingFragments ? 'FRAGMENT UNLOCK' : xpRequired > 0 ? 'XP UNLOCK' : 'STORE PURCHASE'}
          onClose={close}
        />

        <div className="p-6 flex flex-col items-center text-center">
          {/* Hairstyles get the turntable instead of the flat icon. They are the one category
              whose back is as much of the purchase as its front, and the thumbnail only ever
              shows the front. Everything else stays on the icon: a turntable of a hat or a pair
              of trousers would be motion for its own sake. */}
          {hairSpec ? (
            <div className="my-1">
              <HairSpinPreview spec={hairSpec} size={160} />
            </div>
          ) : isNpcPortrait(item.id) ? (
            // 居民填滿整格，跟商店卡上同一張半身照 —— 這裡是玩家決定要不要把這個人請上島的
            // 地方，一顆浮在格子中央的小頭給不了那個決定任何東西。
            <IconTile size={160} className="my-1">
              {/* IconTile 是 flex 置中的定高方格，所以 NpcPortrait 自己的 w-full h-full 就填得滿；
                  不從外面丟 absolute 進去 —— 兩個 position 打架時贏的是樣式表順序（DESIGN_SYSTEM.md）。 */}
              <NpcPortrait itemId={item.id} />
            </IconTile>
          ) : (
            <IconTile size={160} className="my-1">
              <div className="scale-[1.08] flex items-center justify-center">
                <QVersionIcon itemId={item.id} size={110} />
              </div>
            </IconTile>
          )}

          <div className="space-y-3.5 w-full mt-3">
            <div>
              <h4 className="text-lg font-black text-island-navy leading-tight mb-1">{item.name}</h4>
              <span className="text-xs text-island-navy-soft/70 font-bold">
                分類：{getItemCategoryLabel(item.id)}
              </span>
              <p className="text-xs text-island-navy-soft/70 font-medium leading-relaxed mt-1.5 px-2 line-clamp-2">
                {item.description}
              </p>
            </div>

            <div className="bg-island-cream-2 p-4 rounded-2xl border border-island-line space-y-2">
              <div className="flex items-center justify-between text-xs font-bold text-island-navy-soft/70">
                <span>{usingFragments ? '目前碎片：' : xpRequired > 0 ? '目前經驗值：' : '目前持有：'}</span>
                <span className="flex items-center gap-1 text-island-navy font-black">
                  {usingFragments ? (
                    <>
                      <FragmentShard size={14} />
                      {fragmentsHeld.toLocaleString()}
                    </>
                  ) : xpRequired > 0 ? (
                    <>
                      <Zap size={14} className="text-island-teal" strokeWidth={2.75} />
                      {getPlayerXp(profile).toLocaleString()}
                    </>
                  ) : (
                    <>
                      <Coins size={14} className="text-island-gold" />
                      {balance.toLocaleString()}
                    </>
                  )}
                </span>
              </div>
              <div className="flex items-center justify-between border-t border-island-line pt-2">
                <span className="text-sm font-bold text-island-navy">
                  {usingFragments ? '解鎖需要：' : xpRequired > 0 ? '解鎖條件：' : '購買價格：'}
                </span>
                <div className="flex items-center gap-1 text-base font-black text-island-navy">
                  {usingFragments ? (
                    <>
                      <FragmentShard size={15} />
                      <span>{FRAGMENTS_TO_UNLOCK}</span>
                      <span className="text-xs font-bold text-island-navy-soft/70">碎片 · 不扣金幣</span>
                    </>
                  ) : xpRequired > 0 ? (
                    <>
                      <Zap size={15} className="text-island-teal" strokeWidth={2.75} />
                      <span>{xpRequired}</span>
                      <span className="text-xs font-bold text-island-navy-soft/70">經驗值</span>
                    </>
                  ) : (
                    <>
                      <Coins size={15} className="text-island-gold" />
                      <span>{item.price}</span>
                    </>
                  )}
                </div>
              </div>
              {/* Said outright, because an unlock that costs nothing looks like a missing price. */}
              {xpRequired > 0 && !xpLocked && (
                <div className="flex items-center justify-between border-t border-island-line pt-2 text-xs font-bold text-island-navy-soft/70">
                  <span>已達成解鎖條件</span>
                  <span className="text-island-teal-dark font-black">免費領取，不扣金幣</span>
                </div>
              )}
              {/* 抽獎券 says what the purchase does to the balance it actually pays into. Without
                  this the dialog is silent about where the goods go: the two lines above talk about
                  金幣, the 已擁有 line below cannot fire (a ticket never enters the inventory), and
                  the player is left to trust that a card called 抽獎券 becomes a 抽獎券. */}
              {item.grantsTickets && (
                <div className="flex items-center justify-between border-t border-island-line pt-2 text-xs font-bold text-island-navy-soft/70">
                  <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-1">
                    <RaffleTicket size={13} />
                    目前持有 {getRaffleTickets(profile).toLocaleString()} 張
                  </span>
                  <span className="text-island-navy font-black">
                    購買後 {(getRaffleTickets(profile) + item.grantsTickets).toLocaleString()} 張
                  </span>
                </div>
              )}

              {/* Stackable items say what a second copy buys you, so 再購買 never looks like a
                  mis-tap on something already owned. */}
              {stackable && ownedCount > 0 && (
                <div className="flex items-center justify-between border-t border-island-line pt-2 text-xs font-bold text-island-navy-soft/70">
                  <span>已擁有 {ownedCount} 件</span>
                  <span>可擺放庫存 {getAvailableStock(profile, item.id)} 件</span>
                </div>
              )}

              {/* 商品碎片. Shown whenever this item is still collecting — including at 0 — because
                  this dialog is where a player decides how to get the thing, and 「還有另一條路，你
                  走了多遠」 is part of that decision. On the shelf it would be noise under every
                  card; here it is the answer to the question being asked.

                  The gate used to be `ownedCount === 0`, which hid the meter the moment one copy was
                  owned — on a stackable item that is precisely when the dialog is open to buy the
                  SECOND one, and the fragments being collected are for it. */}
              {stillCollecting && (
                <div className="border-t border-island-line pt-2.5">
                  <FragmentMeter itemId={item.id} />
                </div>
              )}

              {/* What the gold route COSTS beyond the gold, said out loud. Buying now converts the
                  stack (context/useShopActions.ts), and a player who has been collecting deserves to
                  learn that before the write, not from a number that quietly changed afterwards.

                  Not shown for a repeat-buyable item, because there it is no longer TRUE: buying one
                  with gold leaves the stack alone, since it is still valid for the next copy — see
                  `fragmentPatchForPurchase`. The warning and the write are the same rule read twice,
                  so they move together. */}
              {!usingFragments && !fragmentReady && fragmentsHeld > 0 && !isRepeatableFragmentItem(item) && ownedCount === 0 && (
                <div className="flex items-start gap-1.5 border-t border-island-line pt-2 text-[11px] font-bold text-island-navy-soft/70">
                  <FragmentShard size={12} className="mt-0.5 flex-shrink-0" />
                  <span>用金幣購買後，已收集的 {fragmentsHeld} 個碎片會轉換成抽獎券。</span>
                </div>
              )}
            </div>

            {xpLocked ? (
              <div className="bg-island-coral/10 border border-island-coral/25 rounded-xl p-2.5 text-island-coral text-center text-xs font-bold">
                經驗值不足！還差 {getXpRemaining(profile, item)} 經驗值才能解鎖。
              </div>
            ) : cannotAfford && !usingFragments && (
              <div className="bg-island-coral/10 border border-island-coral/25 rounded-xl p-2.5 text-island-coral text-center text-xs font-bold">
                餘額不足！您的金幣數量不足以購買此商品。
              </div>
            )}

            {/* Switching routes. Only ever offered when BOTH are open, and always phrased as what it
                costs rather than as a mode toggle — a player should never have to work out which of
                two states a switch is currently in to know what pressing 確認 will spend. */}
            {fragmentReady && !purchased && (
              <button
                onClick={() => { triggerHaptic('light'); setPayWithGold(v => !v); }}
                className="w-full text-[11px] font-bold text-island-navy-soft/70 hover:text-island-teal-dark underline underline-offset-4 decoration-island-line transition-colors cursor-pointer"
              >
                {usingFragments
                  ? `保留碎片，改用 ${item.price.toLocaleString()} 金幣購買`
                  : `改用 ${FRAGMENTS_TO_UNLOCK} 個碎片免費解鎖`}
              </button>
            )}

            <div className="pt-2 flex gap-3">
              <Button variant="secondary" onClick={close} className="flex-1 py-3 text-sm">
                取消
              </Button>
              <motion.button
                disabled={!purchased && (busy || (cannotAfford && !usingFragments) || xpLocked)}
                animate={purchased ? { scale: [1, 1.15, 1.05, 1.12, 1], transition: { duration: 0.9, ease: 'easeInOut' } } : { scale: 1 }}
                whileHover={{ scale: 1.02 }}
                whileTap={{ scale: 0.98 }}
                onClick={handleConfirm}
                className={`flex-1 py-3.5 rounded-xl text-white font-black text-base flex items-center justify-center gap-1.5 transition-all disabled:opacity-40 disabled:pointer-events-none duration-150 cursor-pointer ${
                  purchased ? 'bg-island-gold shadow-[0_10px_24px_rgba(232,170,62,0.35)]' : 'confirm-buy-btn'
                }`}
              >
                {busy && !purchased ? (
                  <div className="w-5 h-5 border-2 border-white/30 border-t-white rounded-full animate-spin" />
                ) : purchased ? (
                  <>
                    <Sparkles size={16} className="text-white animate-bounce" strokeWidth={3} />
                    <span className="uppercase tracking-wide">{xpRequired > 0 || usingFragments ? '解鎖成功！' : '購入成功！'}</span>
                  </>
                ) : usingFragments ? (
                  <>
                    <FragmentShard size={16} />
                    <span>用碎片解鎖</span>
                  </>
                ) : (
                  <>
                    <Check size={16} strokeWidth={3} />
                    <span>{xpRequired > 0 ? '確認解鎖' : '確認購買'}</span>
                  </>
                )}
              </motion.button>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </ModalShell>
    </ModalOverlay>

    {/* Rendered as a SIBLING of the dialog, not inside it: the reveal has to cover the dialog it
        was launched from, and a child of `.z-modal`'s stacking context can never out-rank its own
        ancestor no matter what z-index it is given. `.z-reveal` (1500) is the tier that says so —
        see index.css's layer table. */}
    {revealing && (
      <RarityReveal
        item={item}
        rarity={rarity}
        bursts={fx.confetti}
        turns={fx.revealTurns}
        shake={fx.shake}
        onDone={close}
      />
    )}
    </>
  );
}
```

## src/components/UI/RarityAura.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { Rarity, RARITY_SPECS } from '../../constants/rarity';

/**
 * Where the sparkles sit in the well, as percentages, with each one's stagger into the twinkle.
 *
 * Six positions, of which a tier lights the first `layers.sparks` — so this is the ladder's
 * loudest dial and 稀有 (2) genuinely looks calmer than 神話 (6). All of them stay small: these
 * are the one element that can tip the whole treatment from "jewelled" to "free-to-play", since a
 * scatter of big popping stars is the visual signature of a gacha pull screen. Kept sparse, kept
 * off the middle where the animal stands, and staggered across the 6.8s cycle so that even at six
 * stars roughly two are alight at once — the phases, not the count, are what keep it quiet.
 *
 * Order matters: the first four are the original scatter (the two upper corners, then the two
 * lower ones), so 史詩 renders exactly the arrangement it shipped with. Positions 5 and 6 are top
 * centre and bottom right, added last because they are the two that come nearest the animal.
 */
const SPARKS = [
  { left: '11%', top: '20%', size: 13, delay: '0s' },
  { left: '85%', top: '15%', size: 16, delay: '1.7s' },
  { left: '91%', top: '62%', size: 10, delay: '3.4s' },
  { left: '7%',  top: '68%', size: 11, delay: '5.1s' },
  { left: '49%', top: '7%',  size: 12, delay: '2.6s' },
  { left: '71%', top: '87%', size: 11, delay: '4.3s' },
] as const;

/**
 * The 稀有度 treatment painted behind a shop item.
 *
 * Built as an *object* rather than as a set of effects: an enamel plate, recessed into a turned
 * metal bezel, with a sunray grain under the glaze and a slow specular pass over it. That framing
 * is the point — see DESIGN_SYSTEM.md's "change the construction, not the colour", whose worked
 * example is the build-mode toolbar and whose two recorded failures were making a thing heavier and
 * re-tinting the same shape. A tinted panel with rays and sparkles thrown on top is the second of
 * those failures; a plate set into a bezel is a different object.
 *
 * Layer order, back to front — each one is doing a job the one before it cannot:
 *  1. `.rarity-bezel`  the metal ring. Fills the well; the plate covers all but its outer 1.5px.
 *  2. `.rarity-field`  the plate itself: inset, recessed by its own shadow, vignetted at the corners.
 *  3. `.rarity-rays`   sunray grain in the glaze — fine enough to read as brushed metal, not a burst.
 *  4. `.rarity-spark`  the twinkles.
 *  5. `.rarity-metal`  史詩 and above: a very slow highlight travelling along the bezel.
 *  6. `.rarity-shine`  one slow specular sweep across the glaze.
 *
 * **Which of those get drawn is the tier's `layers` budget, not a constant.** Only the first two
 * are unconditional; everything after them is spent one rung at a time (constants/rarity.ts's
 * {@link RarityLayers}), because four tiers each drawing every layer would be four colours rather
 * than four grades. The tier's own class (`.rarity-common` … `.rarity-mythic`) rides on the root so
 * the stylesheet can hang the two per-tier behaviours — 普通's flat plate and 神話's drifting hue
 * — off it without either becoming a prop.
 *
 * Drops into any icon well as a plain `absolute inset-0` layer: it draws only behind the item (the
 * item's own wrapper sits above it) and takes no pointer events, so a card keeps behaving exactly
 * as it did before it had a rarity. The container must already clip and round its corners — the
 * rays and the sweep both deliberately overflow the well so they have somewhere to come from.
 *
 * Colours come in as the custom properties `rarityStyleVars()` writes on the card; the shapes and
 * timing live in `index.css` (`.rarity-*`). Nothing here is per-item — a new tier is a palette
 * entry in constants/rarity.ts and nothing else.
 */
export function RarityAura({ rarity }: { rarity: Rarity }) {
  const { label, layers } = RARITY_SPECS[rarity];
  return (
    // The tier is spelled out for assistive tech only. It is the single place the label exists,
    // because a rarity said purely in hue is a rarity a colour-blind or screen-reader player
    // cannot read at all — see constants/rarity.ts.
    <div
      className={`absolute inset-0 pointer-events-none rarity-${rarity}`}
      role="img"
      aria-label={`${label}稀有度`}
    >
      <div className="rarity-bezel" />
      <div className="rarity-field" />
      {layers.rays > 0 && (
        // The half-strength pass is unspent since the ladder came down to four (it was 優秀's),
        // but the branch stays: a rung between 普通 and 稀有 gets the same grain at half strength
        // rather than a coarser one of its own — the
        // rung below the full finish should look like less of the same object, not like a
        // different object. See DESIGN_SYSTEM.md on density.
        <div className={`rarity-rays${layers.rays < 1 ? ' rarity-rays-half' : ''}`} />
      )}
      {SPARKS.slice(0, layers.sparks).map((spark, i) => (
        <span
          key={i}
          className="rarity-spark"
          style={{
            left: spark.left,
            top: spark.top,
            width: spark.size,
            height: spark.size,
            animationDelay: spark.delay,
          }}
        />
      ))}
      {layers.metal && <div className="rarity-metal" />}
      {layers.shine && <div className="rarity-shine" />}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## src/components/UI/RarityReveal.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { useCallback, useEffect, useLayoutEffect, useRef, useState, type CSSProperties } from 'react';
import confetti from 'canvas-confetti';
import { ItemDefinition } from '../../constants/items';
import { Rarity, rarityStyleVars } from '../../constants/rarity';
import { ConfettiBurst, REVEAL_COLOUR_RISE_MS, REVEAL_SETTLE_MS } from '../../constants/rarityFx';
import { playRevealSpin } from '../../lib/soundUtils';
import { getRevealCopy } from '../../constants/revealCopy';
import { QVersionIcon } from '../QVersionIcon';
import { RarityAura } from './RarityAura';
import { ModalOverlay } from './DesignKit';

/**
 * How long the choreography runs. Matches the timeline documented over
 * `.rarity-reveal-*` in index.css — change one and change the other.
 */
const REVEAL_MS = 9000;
/** A beat after the item has faded before the dialog behind it is allowed to close. */
const TAIL_MS = 400;
// Their sum (9400ms) is also `.rarity-reveal-layer`'s duration — that animation fades this whole
// overlay out just as the callback fires, so the unmount lands on an already-invisible layer.
//
// 9000, having been 5000, 6500, 8000 and then 11000. Every move is exactly what the ARRIVAL grew or
// shrank by (see REVEAL_SETTLE_MS); the reading time after the settle has never changed. The copy
// still lands on the same beats measured from the stop and the player still gets the same ~3.5s
// with it up — this last move is the first that took time OFF the front rather than adding it.

/**
 * When the copy starts arriving, and how far apart the lines are.
 *
 * Here rather than in the stylesheet because the stagger is DATA — line three is 300ms after line
 * one because it is line three — and expressing it in CSS means one near-identical rule per line
 * plus a new one every time a line is added. The animation itself is a single class
 * (`.rarity-reveal-line`); this is only when each copy of it starts.
 */
const COPY_START_MS = REVEAL_SETTLE_MS + 250;
const COPY_GAP_MS = 150;
/** The tags land tighter than the sentences above them — they are one row, read as a group. */
const TAG_GAP_MS = 90;

/** When the overlay starts accepting a tap. Matches `.rarity-reveal-hint`'s delay in index.css. */
const SKIPPABLE_AT_MS = 6800;

/**
 * How loud the 轉動音 sits under everything else.
 *
 * 0.55, up from 0.38. Under the 神話 brass (0.5) a 0.38 noise bed is not quiet, it is gone — and
 * 「旋轉要有種持續的音效」 was reporting exactly that. See {@link playRevealSpin}.
 */
const SPIN_VOLUME = 0.55;

/**
 * The full-screen 揭曉 played when a 史詩 item or better is bought.
 *
 * The one moment in the game that is allowed to be loud, and it is only reachable from the top
 * two of the four rarity tiers — see constants/rarityFx.ts on why the quiet of the other two is
 * what pays for it.
 *
 * ## The shape of it
 *
 * The screen collapses to dark, and the item turns in from far away as a SILHOUETTE — a black
 * speck with a rim of the tier's own light, under a whoosh that slows with it ({@link playRevealSpin}).
 * It comes round many times, quickly at first and then slowing, SWELLING from a twelfth of its
 * size to its full size as it comes, with its colour rising into it as it decelerates, and it
 * stops facing front with a small bounce. Everything blooms on that stop: a flash, a ring pushed
 * out across the screen, a pool of light under its feet, the tier's gradient welling up behind
 * it, and the confetti. Then it breathes, and its name, its kind, a one-sentence greeting and
 * its tags arrive underneath, one every 150ms. About nine and a half seconds end to end, five and
 * a half of which are the arrival.
 *
 * The silhouette is the load-bearing idea and everything else is dressing. A reveal that simply
 * shows you the thing has no moment in it; a reveal that shows you a shape first has one, and it
 * is the instant you recognise what you got — which is a fraction of a second BEFORE the animation
 * tells you, and is therefore yours rather than the animation's.
 *
 * ## Everything is aimed at the item, not at the middle of the screen
 *
 * The stage is a COLUMN — the item, then its name, kind, greeting and tags — and the whole column
 * is what gets centred in the viewport. So the item itself sits well ABOVE centre, by half the
 * height of the copy underneath it (~110px on a phone, and it moves whenever a line wraps).
 * Every radial layer here used to be pinned to a hand-picked percentage of the SCREEN instead —
 * the rays at 50%, the rings and the settle flash at 44%, the gradient at 46% — which put the
 * point all that light converges on somewhere below the thing it is supposed to be coming off,
 * and read as 「商品有點偏光芒中間的上方」.
 *
 * {@link useLayoutEffect} below measures where the item actually lands and publishes it as
 * `--reveal-focus`, a pixel offset from the middle of the screen; the four layers in index.css
 * are anchored to `calc(50% + var(--reveal-focus))` and there is no per-layer percentage left to
 * drift. Do not re-introduce one — if a layer looks low, it is because the focus is wrong for
 * every layer, and it is measured in one place.
 *
 * ## What it deliberately does NOT do
 *
 * **It never names the tier.** The copy block shows the item's name and its KIND (「神鳥」, 「立耳
 * 犬」) — there is no 「神話」 caption, exactly as there is none on the card (constants/rarity.ts).
 * A reveal is the one place a label would be easy to justify and it would still be the same
 * mistake: the player is being shown what they now own, not being read their receipt. The tier is
 * said at full volume anyway, by the colour of every layer around that text.
 *
 * **It does not re-draw the item.** The plinth is the shop card's icon well at presentation size,
 * carrying the same `RarityAura` layers off the same palette, so this reads as the card the player
 * was just looking at rather than as a second illustration that happens to match.
 *
 * **It does not offer an exit until the copy has landed.** Five seconds is long enough that it has
 * to be skippable, but a skip offered at second one is an invitation to dismiss the thing the
 * player just paid for. The hint appears at {@link SKIPPABLE_AT_MS}, after the last tag.
 *
 * Confetti runs on a canvas owned by this overlay, the way AngelGuide does it: the library's
 * global canvas is appended to `<body>` at z-index 100, which is far below `.z-reveal` (1500), so
 * a global burst would fire *behind* the dim and be invisible. The quieter tiers keep using the
 * global canvas — they have no overlay to get stuck behind.
 */
export function RarityReveal({
  item,
  rarity,
  bursts,
  turns,
  shake,
  onDone,
}: {
  item: ItemDefinition;
  rarity: Rarity;
  bursts: ConfettiBurst[];
  /** Full rotations on the way in — the tier's `revealTurns` (constants/rarityFx.ts). */
  turns: number;
  /** 神話 only — see index.css's `.rarity-shake`. */
  shake: boolean;
  /** Fired once the reveal has finished playing. This is what closes the purchase dialog. */
  onDone: () => void;
}) {
  const canvasRef = useRef<HTMLCanvasElement | null>(null);
  const stageRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);
  const pivotRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);
  const timersRef = useRef<number[]>([]);
  const [skippable, setSkippable] = useState(false);
  /**
   * How far the item's centre sits from the centre of the screen, in px — negative, because the
   * copy underneath it pushes it up. Every radial layer is aimed at this. See the component doc.
   */
  const [focus, setFocus] = useState(0);
  // Held in a ref so the effect below can call the latest one without listing it as a dependency
  // and re-running the whole choreography every render.
  const onDoneRef = useRef(onDone);
  onDoneRef.current = onDone;

  const copy = getRevealCopy(item);

  const later = useCallback((fn: () => void, ms: number) => {
    timersRef.current.push(window.setTimeout(fn, ms));
  }, []);

  // Layout, not paint: `offsetTop`/`offsetHeight` ignore transforms, and on this subtree that is
  // the only way to get a straight answer — the stage is mid push-in, the pivot's child is mid
  // spin and mid swell, so on the first frame `getBoundingClientRect()` would be measuring the
  // item at 22% of its size, turned edge-on. The pivot's own box is the plinth's un-transformed
  // one (its ground light is absolute and its spinning child is scaled), so the pivot's middle IS
  // the item's middle; the stage's middle is the middle of the screen, because the overlay centres
  // it with symmetric padding.
  //
  // A ResizeObserver rather than a one-shot measure: the copy is what decides the offset, and it
  // reflows when a webfont lands or when a long item name wraps to a second line at a narrow
  // width. It watches the layout box, which a transform does not change — so the push-in does not
  // wake it once, let alone every frame.
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const stage = stageRef.current;
    const pivot = pivotRef.current;
    if (!stage || !pivot) return;
    // Un-rounded on purpose. `offsetTop`/`offsetHeight` are already integers, so the two halves
    // carry up to a quarter-pixel of rounding each; rounding their difference as well is a third
    // helping of the same error, and a half-pixel here costs nothing — the value only changes on
    // a reflow, so there is no subpixel churn to avoid.
    const measure = () =>
      setFocus(pivot.offsetTop + pivot.offsetHeight / 2 - stage.offsetHeight / 2);
    measure();
    const observer = new ResizeObserver(measure);
    observer.observe(stage);
    return () => observer.disconnect();
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    const canvas = canvasRef.current;
    const timers = timersRef.current;
    // `resize: true` keeps the canvas matched to the overlay; `useWorker` is left off for the
    // same reason AngelGuide leaves it off — it transfers the canvas permanently and this
    // component unmounts as soon as the reveal ends.
    const fire = canvas ? confetti.create(canvas, { resize: true }) : null;
    // 轉動音, for the silhouette phase only — the full turn drives its deceleration, but it is
    // faded out at REVEAL_COLOUR_RISE_MS, the instant the item stops being a black shape. Once the
    // player can see what they have, the sound has nothing left to describe. Started here rather
    // than from a row of
    // constants/rarityFx.ts because it belongs to the SPIN and not to a tier — every reveal tier
    // turns for the same REVEAL_SETTLE_MS, so there is nothing per-tier to grade — and because the
    // table's sounds are fire-and-forget while this one has to be STOPPABLE: the overlay can be
    // tapped away from SKIPPABLE_AT_MS, and a whoosh outliving the reveal is a whoosh over the shop.
    // Silenced under prefers-reduced-motion for the same reason the CSS cancels the spin there: the
    // sound of a thing turning, over a thing that is not turning, is noise.
    const stopSpin = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches
      ? null
      : playRevealSpin(SPIN_VOLUME, REVEAL_SETTLE_MS, REVEAL_COLOUR_RISE_MS);

    // Tall thin rectangle = a paper streamer. canvas-confetti tumbles and foreshortens each
    // particle in flight, so this reads as 彩帶 rather than as the default dots.
    const ribbon = confetti.shapeFromPath({ path: 'M0 0 H5 V17 H0 Z' });

    for (const burst of bursts) {
      later(() => {
        fire?.({
          particleCount: burst.particleCount,
          spread: burst.spread,
          colors: burst.colors,
          ticks: burst.ticks,
          startVelocity: burst.startVelocity,
          angle: burst.angle,
          origin: burst.origin ?? { x: 0.5, y: 0.62 },
          shapes: burst.ribbon ? [ribbon] : ['circle', 'square'],
          scalar: burst.ribbon ? 1.05 : 1,
          // Every burst in this file carries it: the reveal still plays for a player who has
          // asked for less motion (silently skipping it would read as the purchase failing), but
          // nothing may be thrown across their screen.
          disableForReducedMotion: true,
        });
      }, burst.delay);
    }

    // 神話's screen shake, on the settle rather than on the purchase — the room moves when the
    // thing lands, not when the button is pressed. Applied to the app root rather than to this
    // overlay, because a shake that moves only the celebration is the celebration wobbling. The
    // CSS cancels itself under prefers-reduced-motion, so no media query is needed here — but the
    // class is still removed on the way out so a re-mount can re-trigger it.
    const root = shake ? document.getElementById('root') : null;
    if (root) {
      later(() => root.classList.add('rarity-shake'), REVEAL_SETTLE_MS);
      later(() => root.classList.remove('rarity-shake'), REVEAL_SETTLE_MS + 700);
    }

    later(() => setSkippable(true), SKIPPABLE_AT_MS);
    later(() => onDoneRef.current(), REVEAL_MS + TAIL_MS);

    return () => {
      timers.forEach(window.clearTimeout);
      timers.length = 0;
      root?.classList.remove('rarity-shake');
      fire?.reset();
      // Covers both endings: the reveal running out, and the player tapping it away mid-spin.
      stopSpin?.();
    };
  }, [bursts, shake, later]);

  return (
    // ModalOverlay, not a bespoke fixed div: the scrim, the fade preset and the z-token plumbing
    // are the ones every other modal uses, so this is the same vocabulary played louder rather
    // than a second animation system. Clicks are ignored until the copy has landed — until then
    // there is nothing to dismiss, and the reveal must never be mistaken for a dialog that needs
    // dismissing.
    <ModalOverlay
      zIndexClassName="z-reveal"
      // NO scrim of its own. `.rarity-reveal-dim` is this layer's darkness and it goes almost the
      // whole way to opaque; the inherited ink scrim on top of that was 45% of a dark BLUE laid
      // over the black, which is where the blue cast in the first half-second came from. There
      // must be exactly one thing darkening this screen.
      scrimClassName="bg-transparent"
      className={`rarity-reveal-layer overflow-hidden ${skippable ? 'cursor-pointer' : 'pointer-events-none'}`}
      // The overlay is the nearest element the light layers and the stage have in common, so this
      // is where the measured focus has to be published for all of them to inherit it.
      style={{ '--reveal-focus': `${focus}px` } as CSSProperties}
      onClick={skippable ? () => onDoneRef.current() : undefined}
    >
      <div className="rarity-reveal-dim" />
      <div className="rarity-reveal-backdrop" style={rarityStyleVars(rarity)} />
      <div className="rarity-reveal-flash" />
      <div className="rarity-reveal-rays" />
      <div className="rarity-reveal-burst" style={rarityStyleVars(rarity)} />
      <div className="rarity-reveal-ring" style={rarityStyleVars(rarity)} />
      <div className="rarity-reveal-ring rarity-reveal-ring-2" style={rarityStyleVars(rarity)} />

      <div ref={stageRef} className="rarity-reveal-stage" style={rarityStyleVars(rarity)}>
        {/* Not `relative` any more but `.rarity-reveal-pivot`, which is that plus the
            `perspective` the turn below actually renders through. It has to be THIS element —
            perspective only reaches an element's direct children, and this is the spin's parent.
            The stage's own perspective never applied to the rotation; see index.css. */}
        <div ref={pivotRef} className="rarity-reveal-pivot">
          {/* 腳下的光環, behind the item and anchored to the bottom of its well. */}
          <div className="rarity-reveal-ground">
            <div className="rarity-reveal-pool" />
            <div className="rarity-reveal-halo" />
          </div>

          {/* The turn count reaches `.rarity-reveal-spin`'s keyframes as a custom property — the
              rotation is one `calc()` off it, so grading a tier is a number in the FX table and
              never a second copy of the keyframes. */}
          <div className="rarity-reveal-spin" style={{ '--reveal-turns': turns } as CSSProperties}>
            {/* TWO elements for one move, and the nesting is what makes 由小變大 legible: the turn
                is on the parent and the swell is on this child, so each gets its own timing
                function instead of the growth inheriting the rotation's front-loaded decay. See
                `.rarity-reveal-grow` in index.css. */}
            <div className="rarity-reveal-grow">
              <div className="rarity-reveal-plinth w-[248px] aspect-[4/3] flex items-center justify-center">
                {/* The aura is wrapped so the plate can be held back during the silhouette phase
                    without the icon in front of it fading too — see `.rarity-reveal-plate`. */}
                <div className="rarity-reveal-plate">
                  <RarityAura rarity={rarity} />
                </div>
                <div className="rarity-reveal-silhouette">
                  <QVersionIcon itemId={item.id} size={132} />
                </div>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>

        {/* The copy. Each line is the same `.rarity-reveal-line` animation started at a different
            time; the delays are the stagger and nothing else differs. */}
        <div className="flex flex-col items-center text-center gap-2 px-2">
          {/* The item's name, never the tier's. See the component doc. */}
          <span
            className="rarity-reveal-line text-white font-black text-2xl tracking-wide drop-shadow-[0_2px_14px_rgba(0,0,0,0.6)]"
            style={{ animationDelay: `${COPY_START_MS}ms` }}
          >
            {item.name}
          </span>

          <span
            className="rarity-reveal-line px-3 py-0.5 rounded-full text-xs font-black tracking-widest text-white/95 border border-white/30 bg-white/10 backdrop-blur-sm"
            style={{ animationDelay: `${COPY_START_MS + COPY_GAP_MS}ms` }}
          >
            {copy.kind}
          </span>

          <p
            className="rarity-reveal-line text-white/85 text-sm font-medium leading-relaxed max-w-[300px] drop-shadow-[0_2px_10px_rgba(0,0,0,0.65)]"
            style={{ animationDelay: `${COPY_START_MS + COPY_GAP_MS * 2}ms` }}
          >
            {copy.intro}
          </p>

          {/* Absent entirely for an item with no written copy — getRevealCopy returns no tags
              rather than inventing three, and an empty row is better than three guesses. */}
          {copy.tags.length > 0 && (
            <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-1.5 mt-0.5">
              {copy.tags.map((tag, i) => (
                <span
                  key={tag}
                  className="rarity-reveal-line px-2.5 py-1 rounded-lg text-[11px] font-black text-island-navy bg-white/85 shadow-[0_2px_8px_rgba(0,0,0,0.25)]"
                  style={{ animationDelay: `${COPY_START_MS + COPY_GAP_MS * 3 + i * TAG_GAP_MS}ms` }}
                >
                  {tag}
                </span>
              ))}
            </div>
          )}

          <span className="rarity-reveal-hint text-white text-[11px] font-bold tracking-widest mt-1">
            輕觸繼續
          </span>
        </div>
      </div>

      <canvas ref={canvasRef} className="absolute inset-0 w-full h-full pointer-events-none" />
    </ModalOverlay>
  );
}
```

## src/components/UI/SideButtons.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { ShoppingBag, Backpack, Hammer, Smile } from 'lucide-react';
import { View } from '../../types';
import { useApp } from '../../context/AppContext';
import { useEffect, useRef, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import { motion, AnimatePresence } from 'motion/react';
import { playSound, SoundEffect, triggerHaptic } from '../../lib/soundUtils';
import { useIsTouchDevice } from '../../hooks/useIsTouchDevice';
import { EMOTE_ITEMS } from './EmoteGrid';
import { SignpostTag, HintBubble } from './DesignKit';
import { AnchoredPopover } from './AnchoredPopover';
// Station 2 of the 新手引導 (NewbieTour.tsx). It lights the whole signpost
// column, not one tag — the lesson is "these four are your tools".
import { TOUR_TARGET, tourTag } from '../../constants/tourTargets';

/**
 * One tag on the signpost rail, plus everything that pops *out* of it: the
 * desktop hover label and, optionally, that tool's own panel.
 *
 * Both pop-outs go through `AnchoredPopover`, which portals them out of the
 * rail and positions them from this button's measured rect. That is not a
 * stylistic choice — a pop-out laid out inside the rail is clipped twice over
 * and no z-index can rescue it: `SignpostTag`'s arrow silhouette is a
 * `clip-path` (which clips its whole painted subtree, so an in-button tooltip
 * is invisible), and the `left-rail` HUD region is a scroll container (which
 * clips horizontally as well as vertically, which is what cropped the emote
 * tray to the rail's width). See AnchoredPopover.tsx for the full write-up.
 *
 * Any future rail tool — backpack, settings, house appearance — gets its panel
 * by passing `panel` here, and inherits the same escape hatch, viewport
 * flipping and open/close animation for free.
 */
function RailButton({
  id,
  icon,
  tooltip,
  caption,
  active = false,
  onClick,
  title,
  isMobile,
  sizeClass,
  panel,
}: {
  id?: string;
  icon: ReactNode;
  /** Hover label, desktop only — the long form, when there is room to hover for it. */
  tooltip: string;
  /** Always-visible label under the tag. */
  caption: string;
  active?: boolean;
  onClick: () => void;
  title?: string;
  isMobile: boolean;
  sizeClass: string;
  panel?: {
    open: boolean;
    onClose: () => void;
    /** Surface classes for the popover card itself (radius, padding, layout). */
    className?: string;
    children: ReactNode;
  };
}) {
  const anchorRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const [hovered, setHovered] = useState(false);

  return (
    <div className="relative z-10 flex flex-col items-center gap-1">
      {/* The measured anchor for both pop-outs below. Kept as its own wrapper
          rather than the column item, so a panel lines up with the tag itself
          and not with the tag-plus-mobile-caption stack. */}
      <div
        ref={anchorRef}
        className="flex"
        onPointerEnter={() => setHovered(true)}
        onPointerLeave={() => setHovered(false)}
      >
        <SignpostTag
          id={id}
          shape="arrow"
          active={active}
          onClick={onClick}
          title={title}
          // No `shadow-*` here: SignpostTag clips itself to the arrow
          // silhouette, so a shadow on the tag is clipped away and renders
          // nothing (this used to be a `shadow-md`, which was both invisible
          // and a raw-black Tailwind shadow the design system rules out for
          // chrome). SignpostTag puts the real shadow on its own wrapper.
          className={`items-center justify-center group hover:translate-x-1 ${sizeClass}`}
        >
          {icon}
        </SignpostTag>
      </div>

      {/* 標籤，每一種尺寸都畫。
          ────────────────────
          以前這一行是 `isMobile ? 'block' : 'hidden'`：手機看得到「建造／商店／更衣室／動作」，
          桌面只剩四個沒有字的圖示，要把滑鼠停在上面才知道那是什麼。那是反過來的 —— 觸控裝置至少
          還會因為誤觸而發現，而桌面玩家沒有理由去 hover 一個看不出是什麼的東西。新手引導第二站
          之所以得逐字念出「由上到下是…」，正是因為畫面自己沒說。

          hover 標籤留著，而且沒有重複：它給的是長一點的說法（「建造模式」「角色動作」），這裡是
          四個字以內的短名。尺寸跟著路牌一起用 clamp() 縮，理由跟 `btnSizeClass` 一樣。 */}
      <HintBubble
        variant="floating"
        className={`block rounded-md leading-none tracking-tight whitespace-nowrap pointer-events-none ${
          isMobile
            ? 'text-[8px] px-1.5 py-0.5'
            : 'text-[clamp(0.5rem,1.15vh,0.7rem)] px-[clamp(0.3rem,0.7vh,0.5rem)] py-[clamp(0.1rem,0.3vh,0.2rem)]'
        }`}
      >
        {caption}
      </HintBubble>

      {/* Hover label. Suppressed while this button's own panel is open — they
          share an anchor and a side, so both at once would collide. */}
      <AnchoredPopover
        open={!isMobile && hovered && !panel?.open}
        anchorRef={anchorRef}
        side="right"
        align="center"
        role="tooltip"
        interactive={false}
        closeOnOutsideClick={false}
        closeOnEscape={false}
      >
        <HintBubble variant="solid" className="rounded-xl text-sm px-5 py-2.5 whitespace-nowrap">
          {tooltip}
        </HintBubble>
      </AnchoredPopover>

      {panel && (
        <AnchoredPopover
          open={panel.open}
          anchorRef={anchorRef}
          onClose={panel.onClose}
          side="right"
          align="center"
          gap={isMobile ? 8 : 12}
          // The trigger toggles, and the panel sits over a walkable 3D world —
          // a tap on the island (or on the mobile joystick under it) is a move
          // command, not a dismiss. Esc still closes.
          closeOnOutsideClick={false}
          className={panel.className}
        >
          {panel.children}
        </AnchoredPopover>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

export function SideButtons() {
  const { currentView, setCurrentView } = useApp();
  const [isEmoteTrayOpen, setIsEmoteTrayOpen] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    setIsEmoteTrayOpen(false);
  }, [currentView]);

  const handleAction = (action: () => void) => {
    playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
    triggerHaptic('light');
    action();
  };

  const isMobile = useIsTouchDevice();

  const isInterior = currentView === View.BUILDING_INTERIOR;

  // Placement (which viewport edge, how far from it, and clear of TopBar) is
  // now owned by the shared HUD grid frame — this column just renders into
  // the `left-rail` region below TopBar/MiniMap (see HudFrame.tsx and
  // App.tsx), so it no longer carries any `fixed`/`top-[Npx]` offset tuned to
  // TopBar's height. That hand-tuned coupling (`top-[360px]`, re-tuned from
  // 285px whenever TopBar grew) was the exact thing that overlapped on
  // shorter/guest layouts; the flex rail keeps them apart automatically.
  //
  // Desktop button size is height-responsive via clamp() so the four-tag
  // column always fits under TopBar even on a short (laptop / resized)
  // window — it lands on today's ~88px at normal desktop heights and only
  // shrinks when vertical space is genuinely tight. `isMobile`
  // (pointer-type) still picks mobile-vs-desktop so a touch tablet keeps its
  // compact fixed sizing at every width.
  // The vh floor matters as much as the ceiling: the rail above this column
  // (TopBar, and ~140px more of it once its detail panel is expanded) shares
  // one scrollable region with it, so a size that stops shrinking too early
  // pushes the bottom tag (角色動作) past the region's clip. 9vh with a 3.25rem
  // floor keeps all four tags whole down to a ~600px-tall window; the gap
  // shrinks with it so the column scales as one piece rather than staying
  // spaced for a full-height screen.
  const btnSizeClass = isMobile
    ? 'w-13 h-13'
    : 'w-[clamp(3.25rem,9vh,6rem)] h-[clamp(3.25rem,9vh,6rem)]';
  // Sized in CSS, not by lucide's `size` alone: the tag is vh-responsive now,
  // so a fixed 40px glyph would crowd the arrow silhouette at the small end.
  // CSS width/height beat the SVG presentation attributes, so `size` stays as
  // the pre-CSS fallback only.
  const iconSize = isMobile ? 22 : 40;
  const iconSizeClass = isMobile ? '' : 'w-[clamp(1.4rem,4.6vh,2.5rem)] h-[clamp(1.4rem,4.6vh,2.5rem)]';
  const columnGapClass = isMobile ? 'gap-3' : 'gap-[clamp(0.5rem,1.6vh,1.25rem)]';

  return (
    <>
      {/* Left-side Category / Camera Mode Navigation Buttons — mounted on a
          signpost pole so the four tags read as one object, not four
          separately floating tiles. Positioned by the `left-rail` HUD region
          (HudFrame.tsx); `relative` keeps the z-hud-toolbar tier working for
          local stacking within the frame.

          Note that this column is INSIDE a clipping ancestor (the left rail is
          a scroll container) — anything that has to extend past the rail's own
          width is a popover on `RailButton`, never an `absolute` child here. */}
      <div
        id="game-toolbar-group"
        {...tourTag(TOUR_TARGET.toolbar)}
        className={`relative z-hud-toolbar flex flex-col ${columnGapClass} pointer-events-auto`}
      >
        <AnimatePresence mode="wait">
          {!isInterior ? (
            <motion.div
              key="island-controls"
              initial={{ opacity: 0, x: -20 }}
              animate={{ opacity: 1, x: 0 }}
              exit={{ opacity: 0, x: -20 }}
              className={`relative flex flex-col ${columnGapClass}`}
            >
              <div className="signpost-post" />

              <RailButton
                isMobile={isMobile}
                sizeClass={btnSizeClass}
                active={currentView === View.BUILD_MODE}
                onClick={() => handleAction(() => setCurrentView(View.BUILD_MODE))}
                icon={<Hammer size={iconSize} className={`group-hover:scale-110 group-hover:rotate-6 transition-transform ${iconSizeClass}`} />}
                tooltip="建造模式"
                caption="建造"
              />

              <RailButton
                id="shopBtn"
                isMobile={isMobile}
                sizeClass={btnSizeClass}
                active={currentView === View.SHOP}
                onClick={() => handleAction(() => setCurrentView(View.SHOP))}
                icon={<ShoppingBag size={iconSize} className={`group-hover:scale-110 group-hover:-rotate-6 transition-transform ${iconSizeClass}`} />}
                tooltip="商店"
                caption="商店"
              />

              {/* 限時小攤 沒有路牌。
                  ────────────────
                  這裡以前有第三格（`limitedShopBtn`），按下去直接開限時商店。它被拿掉了，而
                  且**不是**藏起來：整個按鈕、它的 View 切換與它的 tour id 都不在了，因為那家
                  店現在的入口是島上那位旅行商人本人（constants/merchants.ts）。玩家走到海邊、
                  對著他按動作鍵，UI/MerchantSession.tsx 才會開那個畫面。

                  路牌是「隨時可以做的事」——建造、買常駐商品、換衣服、做動作。一位會走的商人
                  不是隨時可以做的事，把他放在這裡就等於承諾他永遠在，而那正好是這次要拆掉的
                  那個承諾。 */}

              <RailButton
                isMobile={isMobile}
                sizeClass={btnSizeClass}
                active={currentView === View.DRESSING_ROOM}
                onClick={() => handleAction(() => setCurrentView(View.DRESSING_ROOM))}
                icon={<Backpack size={iconSize} className={`group-hover:scale-110 group-hover:rotate-12 transition-transform ${iconSizeClass}`} />}
                // 「背包」 —— 這一格通往的畫面沒有變得更遠：它預設就開在「穿戴」，也就是以前的
                // 更衣室。變的是另外三種「我擁有的東西」（可擺放的、消耗品、已套用的外觀）從三到
                // 四次點擊變成兩次 —— 它們以前散在商店的 banner、商店 header 的兩個背包、以及兩個
                // 建造抽屜的已擁有區裡。見 components/UI/BackpackTabs.tsx。
                tooltip="背包・更衣室"
                caption="背包"
              />

              {/* Emotes trigger + its tray. The tray still flips out to the
                  right of the pole exactly as before — it is just no longer
                  laid out inside the rail, so nothing can crop it. */}
              <RailButton
                isMobile={isMobile}
                sizeClass={btnSizeClass}
                active={isEmoteTrayOpen}
                onClick={() => handleAction(() => {
                  if (currentView === View.HOME) {
                    setIsEmoteTrayOpen(!isEmoteTrayOpen);
                  }
                })}
                icon={<Smile size={iconSize} className={`group-hover:scale-110 group-hover:rotate-12 transition-transform ${iconSizeClass}`} />}
                tooltip="角色動作"
                caption="動作"
                title="動作與表情"
                panel={{
                  open: isEmoteTrayOpen,
                  onClose: () => setIsEmoteTrayOpen(false),
                  // `flex-wrap` only ever engages on a viewport too narrow to
                  // lay the row out beside the rail; it keeps the tray inside
                  // the popover's viewport clamp instead of overflowing it.
                  //
                  // WIDTH IS BOUNDED, NOT FIXED. This row flies out to the
                  // right of the pole, so its width decides how far across the
                  // screen it reaches — at the old fixed 4.5rem-per-key it was
                  // ~450px whatever the window size, which on anything but a
                  // wide desktop ran into the right-hand HUD. `max-w` caps it
                  // at the smaller of "as wide as it wants" and 44vw, so the
                  // tray can never cross the middle of the screen and reach the
                  // right-edge chrome; the keys themselves scale with the
                  // viewport (below) so all five still sit on one row inside
                  // that cap rather than wrapping into a second, taller one.
                  className: `flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center bg-island-cream border border-island-line shadow-[0_12px_32px_rgba(38,70,83,0.15)] ${
                    isMobile
                      ? 'gap-3 rounded-[1.2rem] px-3 py-1.5'
                      : 'gap-[clamp(0.4rem,0.8vw,0.75rem)] rounded-[2rem] px-[clamp(0.75rem,1.2vw,1.25rem)] py-2 max-w-[min(28rem,44vw)]'
                  }`,
                  children: EMOTE_ITEMS.filter((em) => em.id !== 'NONE').map((em) => {
                    const IconComponent = em.icon;
                    return (
                      <button
                        key={em.id}
                        onClick={() => {
                          handleAction(() => {
                            window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('trigger-avatar-emote', { detail: { emote: em.id } }));
                          });
                        }}
                        // Desktop keys are vw-responsive for the same reason
                        // the rail's own tags are vh-responsive: five fixed
                        // 4.5rem keys make a row that is as wide on a 1280px
                        // laptop as on a 4K display, and it was the laptop that
                        // had no room for it. Ceiling keeps today's size where
                        // there is space; the 3rem floor keeps the 2-character
                        // label readable at the small end.
                        className={`flex flex-col items-center justify-center gap-1 ${
                          isMobile
                            ? 'w-11 h-11 rounded-xl'
                            : 'w-[clamp(3rem,3.6vw,4.5rem)] h-[clamp(3rem,3.6vw,4.5rem)] rounded-[1.3rem]'
                        } bg-island-cream-2 hover:bg-island-teal/10 active:scale-95 text-island-navy hover:text-island-teal transition-all border border-island-line hover:border-island-teal cursor-pointer`}
                        title={em.shortName}
                      >
                        {/* CSS wins over lucide's `size` attribute, so `size`
                            is only the pre-CSS fallback here — same pattern as
                            the rail icons above. */}
                        <IconComponent
                          size={isMobile ? 16 : 26}
                          className={isMobile ? '' : 'w-[clamp(1.05rem,1.5vw,1.6rem)] h-[clamp(1.05rem,1.5vw,1.6rem)]'}
                        />
                        <span className={`${isMobile ? 'text-[7.5px]' : 'text-[clamp(0.6rem,0.75vw,0.75rem)]'} font-black tracking-wider leading-none mt-0.5 whitespace-nowrap`}>{em.shortName}</span>
                      </button>
                    );
                  }),
                }}
              />
            </motion.div>
          ) : null}
        </AnimatePresence>
      </div>
    </>
  );
}
```

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { useState } from 'react';
import { Coins, Gem, ChevronDown } from 'lucide-react';
import { motion, AnimatePresence } from 'motion/react';
import { useApp } from '../../context/AppContext';
import { getBalance } from '../../constants/currency';
import { playSound, SoundEffect } from '../../lib/soundUtils';
import { AccountPanel } from './AccountPanel';
import { AvatarIcon } from './AvatarIcon';
import { PortholeFrame } from './DesignKit';
import { View } from '../../types';
import { useHudTier, useIsShortViewport } from '../../hooks/useHudTier';
// 管理員數值調整 — the quick +10K 金幣 / +1K XP row, and the exact-figure editor it belongs with.
// Shared with AccountPanel so the two can never drift apart; they used to each hand-roll a copy.
import { profileLevel, xpIntoLevel } from '../../utils/level';
// Station 1 of the 新手引導 (NewbieTour.tsx) — the marker goes on the outermost card.
import { TOUR_TARGET, tourTag } from '../../constants/tourTargets';

/**
 * 個人資訊卡 — the top-left profile card, and the reference implementation of
 * the responsive HUD size system (index.css, hooks/useHudTier.ts).
 *
 * WHAT CHANGED AND WHY. This used to be two entirely separate JSX trees picked
 * by POINTER TYPE: a compact strip for `pointer: coarse`, a ~255x269px ticket
 * for everything else. Two things were wrong with that.
 *
 *   1. Pointer type is not screen size. A touchscreen laptop got the phone
 *      card; a narrow non-touch window got the full-size one, at which point
 *      the card covered ~18% of the viewport. Layout now follows the WIDTH
 *      TIER (useHudTier) and touch only decides hit-target size (`.hud-hit`),
 *      which is the split those two signals actually describe.
 *   2. Every size was written twice, so "make it smaller" meant editing two
 *      trees and six copies of the same progress bar. There is now ONE tree;
 *      what varies with the tier is the ARRANGEMENT (below), and every
 *      dimension in it comes from the --hud-* token scale rather than from a
 *      literal in this file. Resizing the whole HUD is an edit to index.css.
 *
 * INFORMATION HIERARCHY — three rungs, and no tier drops a rung entirely:
 *
 *   Primary   頭像, 名稱, 等級, 金幣, 碎片 — visible at every tier, in every
 *             state. 金幣 AND 碎片 both: a HUD that shows one resource and
 *             hides the other is how a player concludes there is only one
 *             (DESIGN_SYSTEM.md, 貨幣).
 *   Secondary the three progress bars — how far into the level, how each
 *             balance sits against its own scale, and which activity pays it.
 *             Present at every tier, but foldable, and folded by default where
 *             the screen cannot spare the height.
 *   Tertiary  管理員數值調整 — inside the fold, admins only.
 *
 * ARRANGEMENT PER TIER:
 *
 *   mobile / tablet ("compact")  one line: avatar · name/LV · 金幣 · 碎片 · ⌄.
 *                                The fold opens underneath.
 *   laptop / desktop ("full")    avatar · name/LV · ⌄ over a fixed-width
 *                                column; the fold swaps the currency chip row
 *                                for the three bars.
 *
 * The fold's DEFAULT is open on the two big tiers and closed on the two small
 * ones — except on a short viewport (<=800px tall, `useIsShortViewport`), where
 * a 1366x768 laptop is wide enough for the full layout and has no vertical room
 * to spare: the rail below this card (SideButtons) shares one scroll region
 * with it. Whatever the player then chooses wins for the rest of the session at
 * every size — hence `detailOverride`'s three states rather than a boolean.
 */

/**
 * Primary numbers never wrap and never truncate — a balance read as "12,3…" is
 * worse than no balance at all. Five characters at most, so the compact row's
 * width is bounded however rich the player gets.
 */
function shortNumber(n: number): string {
  if (n >= 1_000_000) return `${(n / 1_000_000).toFixed(1)}M`;
  if (n >= 10_000) return `${(n / 1_000).toFixed(1)}K`;
  return n.toLocaleString();
}

/** 金幣 + 碎片, side by side. The primary rung, so it is never behind the fold. */
function CurrencyChips({ coins, fragments }: { coins: number; fragments: number }) {
  return (
    <span className="flex items-center" style={{ gap: 'var(--hud-chip-gap)' }}>
      <span className="flex items-center gap-1" aria-label={`金幣 ${coins}`}>
        <Coins size={13} className="hud-icon text-island-gold" aria-hidden="true" />
        <span className="hud-text-title font-mono font-black text-island-gold whitespace-nowrap">
          {shortNumber(coins)}
        </span>
      </span>
      <span className="flex items-center gap-1" aria-label={`碎片 ${fragments}`}>
        <Gem size={13} className="hud-icon text-island-teal-dark" aria-hidden="true" />
        <span className="hud-text-title font-mono font-black text-island-teal-dark whitespace-nowrap">
          {shortNumber(fragments)}
        </span>
      </span>
    </span>
  );
}

/**
 * One labelled progress bar. Six hand-written copies of this markup (three per
 * layout) is what made the card expensive to resize. The label row truncates
 * and the value never does, so the same component serves a 148px laptop column
 * and a phone card's full width.
 */
function StatBar({
  icon,
  label,
  value,
  valueClass,
  percent,
  barClass,
}: {
  icon?: React.ReactNode;
  label: string;
  value: string;
  valueClass: string;
  percent: number;
  barClass: string;
}) {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col text-left" style={{ gap: 'var(--hud-row-gap)' }}>
      <div className="flex justify-between items-center gap-1.5 hud-text-meta font-black text-island-navy-soft tracking-wide">
        <span className="flex items-center gap-1 min-w-0 truncate">
          {icon}
          {label}
        </span>
        <span className={`font-mono font-black shrink-0 ${valueClass}`}>{value}</span>
      </div>
      <div
        className="w-full bg-white rounded-full overflow-hidden border border-island-line relative"
        style={{ height: 'var(--hud-bar-h)' }}
      >
        <div
          className={`h-full rounded-full transition-all duration-500 relative ${barClass}`}
          style={{ width: `${percent}%` }}
        >
          <span className="absolute inset-x-0 top-0 h-[40%] bg-white/25 rounded-t-full pointer-events-none" />
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

export function TopBar() {
  const { profile, activePlacementItem, currentView } = useApp();
  const [showAccountPanel, setShowAccountPanel] = useState(false);
  const tier = useHudTier();
  const isShortViewport = useIsShortViewport();
  // Three states, not two: `null` means "whatever this tier defaults to", so a
  // player who resizes their window (or rotates a tablet) gets the arrangement
  // that fits — while an explicit tap is remembered across every later resize.
  const [detailOverride, setDetailOverride] = useState<boolean | null>(null);

  if (!profile || currentView !== View.HOME || activePlacementItem !== null) return null;

  const isCompact = tier === 'mobile' || tier === 'tablet';
  const showDetail = detailOverride ?? (!isCompact && !isShortViewport);

  // Calculate XP progress ratio.
  //
  // Both numbers come from utils/level.ts, which derives 等級 from cumulative XP — `profile.level`
  // is seeded as 1 and never written again, so the badge could not move however much XP was
  // earned. See that file for why the 測試補給 button in particular looked completely dead: +1000 XP
  // is a whole number of levels, so the bar below comes back to the very same width.
  const xpProgress = xpIntoLevel(profile.currentXp);
  const level = profileLevel(profile);
  // Both balances come from the currency table rather than off the profile, so where each one is
  // stored stays a detail of constants/currency.ts. See §22 on why they are shown together.
  const coins = getBalance(profile, 'coins');
  const fragments = getBalance(profile, 'fragments');
  // Calculate Gold tracking budget (target goal of 50,000 for visuals)
  const goldLimit = 50000;
  const goldProgress = Math.min(100, (coins / goldLimit) * 105);
  /**
   * 碎片's own bar, on its own scale.
   *
   * 1,000 rather than 50,000, and that ratio IS the point: a shared axis would draw the fragment
   * bar as a permanently empty sliver next to a full gold one, which reads as 「你幾乎沒有碎片」
   * rather than as 「這是另一種資源」. Roughly six full daily-login rounds (156 碎片 each), so the
   * bar moves visibly for a player who actually collects them.
   */
  const fragmentLimit = 1000;
  const fragmentProgress = Math.min(100, (fragments / fragmentLimit) * 105);

  const toggleDetail = () => {
    playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
    setDetailOverride(!showDetail);
  };

  const avatarButton = (
    <button
      type="button"
      onClick={() => {
        playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
        setShowAccountPanel(true);
      }}
      // `.hud-hit` grows the finger target to 44px on touch without changing
      // the drawn size — a 32px avatar is a legible picture and an unreliable
      // button, and shrinking the card must not shrink the target with it.
      className="hud-hit shrink-0 cursor-pointer hover:scale-105 active:scale-95 transition-transform"
      title="查看帳號中心"
      aria-label="查看帳號中心"
    >
      {/* Bolts only on the big tiers: four dots around a 32px porthole is
          noise, not detail. Both sizes are the one --hud-avatar token. */}
      <PortholeFrame
        size="var(--hud-avatar)"
        bolts={!isCompact}
        className="shadow-[0_3px_10px_rgba(42,157,143,0.15)]"
      >
        <AvatarIcon id={profile.avatar} size="calc(var(--hud-avatar) * 0.82)" />
      </PortholeFrame>
    </button>
  );

  const nameBlock = (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-0.5 min-w-0 text-left">
      <span
        className="hud-text-title font-black text-island-navy select-none truncate"
        style={{ maxWidth: 'var(--hud-name-max-w)' }}
        title={profile.displayName}
      >
        {profile.displayName}
      </span>
      {/* 「LV n」 at every tier rather than 「等級 n」 on the big ones: two glyphs
          instead of four buys the name that much more room, and the badge is
          then the same object on every screen. */}
      <span className="hud-text-meta self-start font-black font-mono tracking-wider text-island-teal bg-island-teal/10 px-1.5 py-px rounded-full border border-island-teal/30">
        LV {level}
      </span>
    </div>
  );

  const chevron = (
    <ChevronDown
      size={14}
      className={`hud-icon text-island-navy-soft transition-transform duration-200 ${showDetail ? 'rotate-180' : ''}`}
      aria-hidden="true"
    />
  );

  const detailPanel = (
    <div
      className="flex flex-col bg-island-cream-2 rounded-2xl border border-island-line"
      style={{ gap: 'var(--hud-card-gap)', padding: 'var(--hud-stat-pad)' }}
    >
      <StatBar
        label="經驗 XP"
        value={`${xpProgress} / 100`}
        valueClass="text-island-navy-soft"
        percent={xpProgress}
        barClass="bg-island-teal"
      />
      <StatBar
        icon={<Coins size={11} strokeWidth={2.5} className="hud-icon text-island-gold" aria-hidden="true" />}
        label="金幣・健身取得"
        value={coins.toLocaleString()}
        valueClass="text-island-gold"
        percent={goldProgress}
        barClass="bg-island-gold"
      />
      {/* 碎片 gets a bar of its own rather than a number tucked elsewhere: the
          subtitle on each bar is where the two resources are actually told
          apart — a colour says 「不同」, a source says 「為什麼不同」. */}
      <StatBar
        icon={<Gem size={11} strokeWidth={2.5} className="hud-icon text-island-teal-dark" aria-hidden="true" />}
        label="碎片・非健身取得"
        value={fragments.toLocaleString()}
        valueClass="text-island-teal-dark"
        percent={fragmentProgress}
        barClass="bg-island-teal"
      />
      {/* 管理員數值調整 used to hang here, inside the player's own profile card. It moved to the
          管理員測試 console (UI/admin/, 玩家數值), which is also where it stopped having to fold
          into a ~170px column — see AdminSupplyButtons' own note about wrapping to 2x2. */}
    </div>
  );

  return (
    <>
      {/* Placed by the `left-rail` HUD region (HudFrame.tsx); `relative` keeps
          the z-hud-topbar tier for local stacking within the frame.

          The card's shadow is `.notch-shadow-hoverable` on this WRAPPER, not a
          `shadow-[...]` on the `dock-notch` element — a clip-path clips the
          element's own box-shadow away (see index.css). */}
      <div
        {...tourTag(TOUR_TARGET.account)}
        className={`relative z-hud-topbar notch-shadow-hoverable pointer-events-auto transition-all duration-300 ease-out ${
          showAccountPanel ? 'opacity-0 scale-95 pointer-events-none' : ''
        }`}
      >
        {/* Width comes from --hud-card-w: `max-content` on the compact tiers
            (the card is exactly as wide as its one row) and a fixed column on
            the big ones. --hud-card-max-w is the guarantee that it can never
            run off a narrow viewport or swallow the view, however long a
            player's display name is. */}
        <div
          className="flex flex-col bg-white dock-notch rounded-2xl border border-island-line"
          style={{
            width: 'var(--hud-card-w)',
            maxWidth: 'var(--hud-card-max-w)',
            padding: 'var(--hud-card-pad)',
            gap: 'var(--hud-card-gap)',
          }}
        >
          <div className="flex items-center" style={{ gap: 'var(--hud-chip-gap)' }}>
            {avatarButton}
            {nameBlock}

            {isCompact ? (
              /* Compact: the currencies and the fold control are ONE button,
                 which is also what keeps ONE target instead of two adjacent
                 small ones. `self-stretch` gives it the row's full height and
                 `.hud-hit` takes it the rest of the way to 44px on touch — the
                 row is only ~32px tall once the card is this small. */
              <button
                type="button"
                onClick={toggleDetail}
                aria-expanded={showDetail}
                className="hud-hit flex items-center gap-1.5 ml-auto self-stretch shrink-0 pl-2 border-l border-island-line cursor-pointer"
                title={showDetail ? '收合詳細數值' : '展開詳細數值'}
              >
                <CurrencyChips coins={coins} fragments={fragments} />
                {chevron}
              </button>
            ) : (
              <button
                type="button"
                onClick={toggleDetail}
                aria-expanded={showDetail}
                className="hud-hit ml-auto shrink-0 p-1 -mr-0.5 rounded-lg hover:bg-island-sand cursor-pointer"
                title={showDetail ? '收合詳細數值' : '展開詳細數值'}
                aria-label={showDetail ? '收合詳細數值' : '展開詳細數值'}
              >
                {chevron}
              </button>
            )}
          </div>

          {(showDetail || !isCompact) && <div className="rope-stitch" />}

          {/* Full layout, folded: the primary numbers move out of the fold and
              onto their own line, so collapsing the card hides the SECONDARY
              rung only. Nothing a player needs at a glance is ever behind a
              tap. */}
          {!isCompact && !showDetail && (
            <div className="flex justify-center py-0.5">
              <CurrencyChips coins={coins} fragments={fragments} />
            </div>
          )}

          <AnimatePresence initial={false}>
            {showDetail && (
              <motion.div
                initial={{ height: 0, opacity: 0 }}
                animate={{ height: 'auto', opacity: 1 }}
                exit={{ height: 0, opacity: 0 }}
                transition={{ duration: 0.2, ease: 'easeInOut' }}
                className="overflow-hidden"
              >
                {detailPanel}
              </motion.div>
            )}
          </AnimatePresence>
        </div>
      </div>

      <AnimatePresence>
        {showAccountPanel && <AccountPanel onClose={() => setShowAccountPanel(false)} />}
      </AnimatePresence>
    </>
  );
}
```
