```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * The four shapes every 管理員測試 category is built from.
 *
 * These exist so the console reads as ONE screen rather than as five panels that happened to be
 * moved into the same drawer. Each control that came in from the game UI kept its own body — the
 * offline simulator, the value editor and the workout panel are the same components they always
 * were — but the frame around them, the heading, the one-line explanation of what the control
 * WRITES, and the way an on/off state is shown are all from here.
 *
 * {@link AdminStatePill} deserves a note. 「Toggle 不應只有視覺差異極小的顏色變化」 — so a state in
 * this console is never carried by colour alone: every pill has a WORD (啟用中 / 已關閉 / 生效中),
 * a filled-or-hollow dot, and a border weight that differ together. That triple survives a
 * colour-blind reader, a washed-out projector, and a screenshot in a bug report.
 */

import type { ReactNode } from 'react';

export type AdminStateTone = 'on' | 'off' | 'info' | 'warn';

const pillToneClass: Record<AdminStateTone, string> = {
  on: 'bg-island-teal/12 border-island-teal/45 text-island-teal-dark',
  off: 'bg-white border-island-line text-island-navy-soft/80',
  info: 'bg-island-navy/8 border-island-navy/25 text-island-navy',
  warn: 'bg-island-gold/14 border-island-gold/50 text-island-navy',
};

const dotToneClass: Record<AdminStateTone, string> = {
  on: 'bg-island-teal',
  off: 'bg-island-navy-soft/35',
  info: 'bg-island-navy/60',
  warn: 'bg-island-gold',
};

/** A state, said in a word. The dot is the redundancy, never the message. */
export function AdminStatePill({ tone, children }: { tone: AdminStateTone; children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <span
      className={`inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 px-2 py-1 rounded-full border text-[10px] font-black leading-none whitespace-nowrap ${pillToneClass[tone]}`}
    >
      <span className={`w-1.5 h-1.5 rounded-full flex-shrink-0 ${dotToneClass[tone]}`} />
      {children}
    </span>
  );
}

/**
 * One labelled block inside a category: what the control is, what it costs the save, then the
 * control.
 *
 * `note` is not decoration. Half of these controls write to the account and half do not, and which
 * is which is the single most useful thing to know before pressing one — so every group says it in
 * its own line rather than leaving it to be inferred from the button's colour.
 */
export function AdminGroup({
  icon,
  title,
  note,
  state,
  children,
}: {
  icon?: ReactNode;
  title: string;
  note?: string;
  state?: ReactNode;
  children: ReactNode;
}) {
  return (
    <section className="rounded-[1.5rem] border border-island-line bg-white/70 overflow-hidden">
      <header className="flex items-start justify-between gap-2 px-3.5 pt-3 pb-2">
        <div className="flex items-start gap-2 min-w-0">
          {icon && <span className="text-island-teal-dark mt-[1px] flex-shrink-0">{icon}</span>}
          <div className="min-w-0">
            <h4 className="text-[12px] font-black text-island-navy leading-tight">{title}</h4>
            {note && (
              <p className="text-[10px] font-bold text-island-navy-soft/85 leading-snug mt-0.5">{note}</p>
            )}
          </div>
        </div>
        {state && <div className="flex-shrink-0">{state}</div>}
      </header>
      <div className="px-3 pb-3">{children}</div>
    </section>
  );
}

/**
 * A read-only fact about the current state — 「這個開關現在是開的」, 「這個覆寫正在生效」.
 *
 * Rows like these are why the console can answer 「是否正在生效」 without the tester having to go
 * and look at the game: several Admin behaviours (教學重播, the URL overrides) have no button at
 * all, and before this there was nowhere at all that said they were on.
 */
export function AdminStatusRow({
  label,
  detail,
  state,
}: {
  label: string;
  detail?: string;
  state: ReactNode;
}) {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-start justify-between gap-2 py-2 border-b border-dashed border-island-line last:border-b-0">
      <div className="min-w-0">
        <span className="block text-[11px] font-black text-island-navy leading-tight">{label}</span>
        {detail && (
          <span className="block text-[10px] font-bold text-island-navy-soft/80 leading-snug mt-0.5">
            {detail}
          </span>
        )}
      </div>
      <div className="flex-shrink-0 pt-0.5">{state}</div>
    </div>
  );
}

const actionToneClass = {
  neutral: 'bg-white hover:bg-island-cream-2 border-island-line text-island-navy',
  teal: 'bg-island-teal/10 hover:bg-island-teal/20 border-island-teal/30 text-island-navy',
  danger: 'bg-island-coral/10 hover:bg-island-coral/20 border-island-coral/30 text-island-coral',
} as const;

/**
 * The console's own button. Same size and shape everywhere so a destructive one and a harmless one
 * are told apart by their WORDS and their tone, never by being differently built.
 */
export function AdminActionButton({
  tone = 'neutral',
  icon,
  label,
  onClick,
  disabled,
  title,
  full = false,
}: {
  tone?: keyof typeof actionToneClass;
  icon?: ReactNode;
  label: ReactNode;
  onClick: () => void;
  disabled?: boolean;
  title?: string;
  /** Occupy the row on its own — for the one-of-a-kind actions (a wipe, a grant). */
  full?: boolean;
}) {
  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      onClick={onClick}
      disabled={disabled}
      title={title}
      className={`${full ? 'w-full' : ''} flex items-center justify-center gap-1.5 px-3 py-2 rounded-xl border text-[11px] font-black leading-none transition-all active:scale-95 disabled:opacity-45 disabled:pointer-events-none ${actionToneClass[tone]}`}
    >
      {icon}
      <span>{label}</span>
    </button>
  );
}
```

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * The 【管理員測試】 handle — the ONE thing 管理員測試模式 adds to the game screen.
 *
 * ## Where it sits, and why that took two mounts
 *
 * Right edge, as a drawer handle: it is where the panel comes from, and every other edge is
 * already spoken for — 個人資訊卡 and 小地圖 and the signpost column on the left, NavBar and the
 * placement dock along the bottom, ControlsHint and 幸運轉盤 in the bottom-right corner, and the
 * character in the middle, which is non-negotiable.
 *
 * The first version of this was `fixed right-0 top-1/2`, and it was WRONG in a way that only
 * showed up on screen: the 鏡頭遠近轉盤 is a 260px column anchored ~225px above the bottom edge, so
 * on a 1440x900 window its top lands at y=409 and a vertically-centred tab (y=431..469) sat
 * squarely on its ＋ button. A hand-tuned offset would have fixed that one window size and drifted
 * on every other — which is the exact class of bug HudFrame was built to end.
 *
 * So in the island and interior views this is a CHILD of the `mid-right` HUD region, stacked
 * directly above the dial in the same flex column. The grid keeps them apart at every viewport
 * size without either one knowing the other's height. That region is also Admin-only in practice —
 * the dial is its only other occupant — so the two pieces of Admin chrome share one column and
 * take nothing from a normal player, for whom the region is empty.
 *
 * `floating` covers the views where HudFrame is not mounted at all (商店, 設定, 更衣室, 健康,
 * 限時小攤, 健身): those are full-page cards with a 24px page gutter, and the right edge at mid
 * height is bare background there — checked with `elementFromPoint`, not assumed. There is no dial
 * in those views either, so the centred position is free.
 *
 * Both mounts sit the same distance from the right edge — the HUD's own `--hud-inset` token, which
 * the frame supplies as padding in one case and `.admin-console-handle-floating` (index.css)
 * repeats in the other. So the handle is one shape at one distance wherever it appears, lined up
 * with the dial and the 幸運轉盤 rather than reading as two similar buttons.
 *
 * ## Two states, two shapes
 *
 * `closed` is the tab: icon plus the label, set vertically because 管理員測試 is four characters
 * and vertical CJK keeps the handle a sliver of the edge instead of a corner of the game.
 * `minimized` keeps the same silhouette but names the category it will come back to, and carries
 * its own X — the difference between 「put this away for a moment」 and 「I'm done」 is the whole
 * reason both states exist (see AdminTestContext).
 */

import { motion } from 'motion/react';
import { ChevronLeft, FlaskConical, X } from 'lucide-react';
import { playSound, SoundEffect } from '../../../lib/soundUtils';
import { ADMIN_SECTIONS } from './adminTestSections';
import { useAdminTest } from './AdminTestContext';

const shell =
  'flex flex-col items-center rounded-2xl bg-island-navy/92 backdrop-blur-md border ' +
  'border-island-navy-dark/40 text-white shadow-[0_10px_28px_rgba(38,70,83,0.32)] pointer-events-auto';

export function AdminTestLauncher({ floating = false }: { floating?: boolean }) {
  const { mode, section, open, restore, close } = useAdminTest();

  if (mode === 'open') return null;

  const active = ADMIN_SECTIONS.find((s) => s.id === section) ?? null;
  const position = floating
    ? 'admin-console-handle-floating z-admin-console'
    : 'relative z-hud-toolbar';

  if (mode === 'minimized') {
    return (
      <motion.div
        initial={{ opacity: 0, x: 12 }}
        animate={{ opacity: 1, x: 0 }}
        transition={{ duration: 0.18, ease: 'easeOut' }}
        className={`${position} ${shell} gap-1 px-1.5 py-2`}
      >
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={() => {
            playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
            restore();
          }}
          title={active ? `展開管理員測試面板（${active.label}）` : '展開管理員測試面板'}
          aria-label="展開管理員測試面板"
          className="flex flex-col items-center gap-1.5 transition-opacity hover:opacity-80 active:scale-95"
        >
          <ChevronLeft size={13} strokeWidth={2.75} className="flex-shrink-0 opacity-75" />
          <FlaskConical size={13} strokeWidth={2.5} className="flex-shrink-0" />
          <span className="text-[10px] font-black tracking-[0.14em] [writing-mode:vertical-rl] leading-none">
            {active?.label ?? '管理員測試'}
          </span>
        </button>
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={() => {
            playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
            close();
          }}
          title="關閉管理員測試面板"
          aria-label="關閉管理員測試面板"
          className="w-5 h-5 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center bg-white/12 hover:bg-white/25 transition-colors active:scale-90"
        >
          <X size={11} strokeWidth={3} />
        </button>
      </motion.div>
    );
  }

  return (
    <motion.button
      type="button"
      initial={{ opacity: 0, x: 12 }}
      animate={{ opacity: 1, x: 0 }}
      transition={{ duration: 0.18, ease: 'easeOut' }}
      onClick={() => {
        playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
        open();
      }}
      title="開啟管理員測試面板"
      aria-label="開啟管理員測試面板"
      className={`${position} ${shell} gap-1.5 px-1.5 py-3 transition-all active:scale-95 hover:bg-island-navy`}
    >
      <FlaskConical size={14} strokeWidth={2.5} className="flex-shrink-0" />
      <span className="text-[10px] font-black tracking-[0.2em] [writing-mode:vertical-rl] leading-none">
        管理員測試
      </span>
    </motion.button>
  );
}
```

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { ZoomControl } from '../ZoomControl';
import { AdminOnly } from '../AdminOnly';
import { useAdminTest } from './AdminTestContext';

/**
 * The 鏡頭遠近轉盤's mount, which is now the one piece of Admin chrome still allowed onto the game
 * screen — and the only one with an off switch (管理員測試 → 場景與環境).
 *
 * Two gates, and they mean different things. `<AdminOnly>` is the account-level rule: a normal
 * player never has this dial, full stop. `showZoomDial` is the session-level preference: a tester
 * who wants a clean screenshot of the island can put it away without leaving 管理員測試模式 and
 * losing every other test control at the same time.
 *
 * Zoom itself is untouched by either gate. The mouse wheel, pinch, and the crossover into first
 * person all run through constants/cameraZoom.ts, which this component does not sit in front of —
 * hiding the dial hides a dial.
 *
 * Kept as its own component rather than as a condition inlined into App.tsx so ZoomControl stays a
 * pure view with no idea that an admin console exists, which is what let it keep working unchanged
 * through this whole rearrangement.
 */
export function AdminZoomDial() {
  return (
    <AdminOnly>
      <AdminZoomDialInner />
    </AdminOnly>
  );
}

function AdminZoomDialInner() {
  const { showZoomDial } = useAdminTest();
  if (!showZoomDial) return null;
  return <ZoomControl />;
}
```

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 管理員測試面板的資訊架構 — the six categories, and what is inside each one.
 *
 * ## Why this file is a list and not a pile of JSX
 *
 * The problem this console was opened to fix is not that the Admin controls looked bad; it is that
 * there was no ANSWER to 「有哪些類型的測試功能」. They were scattered across seven screens
 * (TopBar, AccountPanel, ShopView twice, PetCarePanel, UtilityCard, SettingsView) and the only way
 * to learn what existed was to turn the mode on and go hunting for what had changed.
 *
 * So the categories are data. The panel renders the LIST first and a category second, which means
 * the front page of the console is a table of contents rather than a wall of buttons, and adding a
 * test control later means adding it to a category here rather than finding a corner of the game
 * UI to hang it on.
 *
 * ## The categories are the ones that exist, not the ones that sound complete
 *
 * There is no 房屋與建造 category, because 建造模式 has no Admin-only control — the only thing
 * 管理員測試模式 changes in there is that the four 小天使 guides replay, which is a TUTORIAL
 * behaviour and is reported under 新手與登入流程 with the rest of them. An empty category with a
 * promising name is worse than no category: it sends a tester looking for a switch that was never
 * built. Same reason there is no 天氣 / 時間 / NPC category — those are ordinary game systems with
 * no test-only surface today. See constants/adminFeatures.ts, which remains the registry of record.
 *
 * `entries` is written down rather than derived because a category's controls are not a uniform
 * list — 場景 is one imported panel plus one switch, 玩家數值 is one quick row plus four editors —
 * and a count taken off the DOM would say something different from what a reader would count.
 */

import { useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import {
  Coins,
  Dices,
  Dumbbell,
  Eye,
  Gift,
  GraduationCap,
  PawPrint,
  RotateCcw,
  Sailboat,
  Sprout,
  Store,
  Ticket,
  Trash2,
  Trophy,
  Wrench,
} from 'lucide-react';
import { useApp } from '../../../context/AppContext';
import { playSound, SoundEffect } from '../../../lib/soundUtils';
import { describeRecentFailure } from '../../../lib/saveStatus';
import { resetOwnedContent } from '../../../lib/adminSaveReset';
import { RARITY_OVERRIDE, UNOWNED_OVERRIDE } from '../../../utils/debugOverrides';
import { PET_CONDITION_BANDS } from '../../../constants/petCare';
import { MERCHANTS, getMerchantShop } from '../../../constants/merchants';
import { merchantAlwaysDocked } from '../../../constants/merchantVisit';
import { useMerchantVisits } from '../../../hooks/useMerchantVisit';
import { AdminIslandControls } from '../AdminIslandControls';
import { AdminWorkoutRewardControls } from '../AdminWorkoutRewardControls';
import { AdminSupplyButtons, AdminValuePanel, GrantAllItemsButton } from '../AdminValueControls';
import { AdminOwnAllItemsRow } from '../settings/AdminOwnAllItemsRow';
import { Button, Toggle } from '../DesignKit';
import { useAdminTest } from './AdminTestContext';
import { AdminActionButton, AdminGroup, AdminStatePill, AdminStatusRow } from './AdminTestKit';

export interface AdminSection {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  /** One line on the category card — what a tester comes to this category FOR. */
  tagline: string;
  icon: ReactNode;
  /** Named controls, listed on the card so the front page says what is inside without opening it. */
  entries: string[];
  Body: () => ReactNode;
}

// --- 場景與環境 -------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * The 鏡頭遠近轉盤's visibility switch.
 *
 * The dial is Admin-only and always has been (constants/adminFeatures.ts), but until now 「admin
 * mode is on」 and 「the dial is on screen」 were the same fact, so the one piece of Admin chrome
 * that actually sits over the game had no off switch. It has one now, and the switch reports which
 * state it is in rather than leaving it to be read off the corner of the screen.
 *
 * Zoom itself is untouched either way — the wheel, pinch, and the first-person crossover all run
 * through constants/cameraZoom.ts and never through this dial.
 */
function ZoomDialSwitch() {
  const { showZoomDial, setShowZoomDial } = useAdminTest();
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-3 p-3 rounded-2xl bg-island-cream-2 border border-island-line">
      <div className="min-w-0">
        <span className="block text-[11px] font-black text-island-navy leading-tight">
          在畫面右側顯示轉盤
        </span>
        <span className="block text-[10px] font-bold text-island-navy-soft/80 leading-snug mt-0.5">
          {showZoomDial
            ? '目前顯示中：轉盤在畫面右緣，新手引導第四站也會講到它。'
            : '目前已隱藏：滑鼠滾輪、雙指捏合與第一人稱切換全部照常，只是畫面上沒有轉盤。'}
        </span>
      </div>
      <Toggle
        checked={showZoomDial}
        onChange={(next) => {
          playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
          setShowZoomDial(next);
        }}
      />
    </div>
  );
}

function SceneSection() {
  const { showZoomDial } = useAdminTest();
  return (
    <>
      <AdminGroup
        icon={<Sprout size={14} />}
        title="離線回歸測試"
        note="會寫入存檔的 islandState（只有這一個欄位）；「畫面飽和」那一排完全不寫入。"
      >
        <AdminIslandControls />
      </AdminGroup>

      <AdminGroup
        icon={<Eye size={14} />}
        title="鏡頭遠近轉盤"
        note="只影響畫面上的轉盤，不影響縮放功能本身。不寫入存檔。"
        state={
          <AdminStatePill tone={showZoomDial ? 'on' : 'off'}>
            {showZoomDial ? '顯示中' : '已隱藏'}
          </AdminStatePill>
        }
      >
        <ZoomDialSwitch />
      </AdminGroup>
    </>
  );
}

// --- 玩家數值 ---------------------------------------------------------------

function PlayerSection() {
  return (
    <>
      <AdminGroup
        icon={<Wrench size={14} />}
        title="快捷加值"
        note="一鍵加值，走的是正式的發放路徑（source 標記為 admin-test）。會寫入存檔。"
      >
        <div className="p-3 rounded-2xl bg-island-cream-2 border border-island-line">
          <AdminSupplyButtons goldLabel="+10K 金幣" />
        </div>
      </AdminGroup>

      <AdminGroup
        icon={<Coins size={14} />}
        title="精準數值調整"
        note="金幣、碎片、經驗值、抽獎券各自可加值、歸零或直接寫成指定數字。會寫入存檔。等級沒有獨立欄位，由累計 XP 換算。"
      >
        <AdminValuePanel showGrantAll={false} />
      </AdminGroup>
    </>
  );
}

// --- 商店與經濟 -------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * 模擬輪盤抽獎 / 重置功能卡 — moved out of the 功能卡背包.
 *
 * They were at the bottom of a bag that is itself only reachable through the 限時小攤, which is
 * only reachable while the travelling merchant is moored on the beach. That gate is deliberate for
 * the SHOP (see docs/traveling-merchant.md), but it was never meant to gate the test buttons: it
 * made 「重置功能卡」 unreachable for roughly twenty hours of every fourteen-day rotation. Here they
 * are always reachable, and they still run the real wheel table and the real grant path.
 */
function UtilityCardControls() {
  const { spinWheel, resetUtilityCards, showIslandAlert } = useApp();
  const [message, setMessage] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 p-3 rounded-2xl bg-island-cream-2 border border-island-line">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <AdminActionButton
          tone="teal"
          icon={<Dices size={12} strokeWidth={2.75} />}
          label="模擬輪盤抽獎"
          disabled={busy}
          title="管理員：跑一次真正的輪盤加權抽選與發放，不是直接塞一張卡"
          onClick={() => {
            void (async () => {
              playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
              setBusy(true);
              const result = await spinWheel();
              setBusy(false);
              setMessage(
                result.ok ? `輪盤：${result.prize.label}` : `輪盤沒有發出獎勵（${result.reason}）`,
              );
            })();
          }}
        />
        <AdminActionButton
          tone="danger"
          icon={<RotateCcw size={12} strokeWidth={2.75} />}
          label="重置功能卡"
          disabled={busy}
          title="管理員：清空持有數量、進行中的效果與使用次數統計（不退錢、不補卡）"
          onClick={() => {
            void (async () => {
              playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
              setBusy(true);
              const ok = await resetUtilityCards();
              setBusy(false);
              if (!ok) {
                showIslandAlert(describeRecentFailure());
                return;
              }
              setMessage('功能卡狀態已重置');
            })();
          }}
        />
      </div>
      {message && (
        <span className="text-[10px] font-black text-island-teal-dark leading-snug">{message}</span>
      )}
      <span className="text-[9px] text-island-navy-soft/80 leading-tight">
        這裡刻意沒有「發一張卡」的按鈕：要測效果就抽或買，因為那才是玩家會走的路。
      </span>
    </div>
  );
}

/** 清空裝備 — the console's one destructive control, and the only one that asks first. */
function ResetOwnedContentControl() {
  const { profile, showIslandAlert } = useApp();
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);

  const run = () => {
    if (!profile || busy) return;
    if (
      !window.confirm(
        '警告：確定要清空裝備嗎？這會刪除背包內所有物品、清空室內家具與島上擺設，並重設角色裝扮與地板／牆面樣式。金幣、碎片、經驗值與抽獎券不受影響。此操作無法復原。',
      )
    ) {
      return;
    }
    void (async () => {
      playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
      setBusy(true);
      const result = await resetOwnedContent(profile.userId);
      setBusy(false);
      if (!result.ok) {
        showIslandAlert(result.error ?? describeRecentFailure());
        return;
      }
      playSound(SoundEffect.REWARD, 0.4);
      showIslandAlert('已清空背包、裝扮、室內家具與島上擺設。');
    })();
  };

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 p-3 rounded-2xl bg-island-cream-2 border border-island-line">
      <AdminActionButton
        full
        tone="danger"
        icon={<Trash2 size={12} strokeWidth={2.75} />}
        label={busy ? '清空中…' : '清空裝備（重置存檔內容）'}
        disabled={busy || !profile}
        title="管理員：清空背包、裝扮、室內家具與島上擺設"
        onClick={run}
      />
      <span className="text-[9px] text-island-navy-soft/80 leading-tight">
        清掉的是「東西」不是「錢」：背包、已穿戴、室內家具、地板與牆面樣式、島上擺設（含房屋）。
        金幣、碎片、經驗值、抽獎券、寵物照護、登入與健身紀錄都不會動到。這是面板上唯一會二次確認的按鈕。
      </span>
    </div>
  );
}

/** What `?unown=` / `?rarity=` are doing to this session, if anything. */
function UrlOverrideStatus() {
  const unowned = [...UNOWNED_OVERRIDE];
  const rarities = [...RARITY_OVERRIDE.entries()];

  return (
    <div className="p-3 rounded-2xl bg-island-cream-2 border border-island-line">
      <AdminStatusRow
        label="?unown= 未擁有覆寫"
        detail={unowned.length > 0 ? unowned.join('、') : '把指定商品當成還沒買，用來看購買按鈕與上鎖狀態'}
        state={
          <AdminStatePill tone={unowned.length > 0 ? 'warn' : 'off'}>
            {unowned.length > 0 ? `生效中 ${unowned.length}` : '未使用'}
          </AdminStatePill>
        }
      />
      <AdminStatusRow
        label="?rarity= 稀有度覆寫"
        detail={
          rarities.length > 0
            ? rarities.map(([id, tier]) => `${id}:${tier}`).join('、')
            : '只改卡片的塗裝，不動價格、庫存、擁有狀態或獎勵池'
        }
        state={
          <AdminStatePill tone={rarities.length > 0 ? 'warn' : 'off'}>
            {rarities.length > 0 ? `生效中 ${rarities.length}` : '未使用'}
          </AdminStatePill>
        }
      />
      <p className="text-[9px] text-island-navy-soft/80 leading-tight pt-2">
        這兩個是網址參數，不受管理員測試模式控制（它們必須在純函式裡就能回答，讀不到帳號設定）。
        兩者都只會「拿掉」擁有權或改變塗裝，永遠不會發出物品，重新整理即失效。
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}

/**
 * 問船的行程 —— 唯讀。
 *
 * 這一區沒有按鈕，因為「商船一直停靠」不是一個可以單獨按的開關 —— 它就是管理員測
 * 試模式本身（見 components/UI/admin/AdminMerchantDock.tsx）。所以這裡要回答的是另一件事：
 * 現在看到的那艘船，到底是被釘住的還是正式行程列的，以及關掉之後玩家會看到什麼。
 *
 * 天數是算出來的（一檔長度 × 行程比例）而不是寫在這裡的「3」與「4」：面板講的必須是
 * 設定檔現在真正的值，否則有人把檔期改回 14 天之後，這裡會是全遊戲唯一一個還在說謊的地方。
 */
function MerchantScheduleStatus() {
  const visits = useMerchantVisits();
  const pinned = merchantAlwaysDocked();

  const spec = MERCHANTS[0];
  const periodDays = getMerchantShop(spec).periodLengthMs() / 86_400_000;
  const awayRatio = spec.schedule.arrivesAfter + spec.schedule.departsBefore;
  const dockedDays = periodDays * (1 - awayRatio);
  const awayDays = periodDays * awayRatio;
  const days = (value: number) =>
    Number.isInteger(Number(value.toFixed(2))) ? value.toFixed(0) : value.toFixed(1);

  const visit = visits.find((entry) => entry.merchantId === spec.id) ?? null;
  const phaseLabel =
    visit?.phase === 'visiting' ? '停靠中' : visit?.phase === 'awaited' ? '尚未抵達' : '已離開';

  return (
    <div className="p-3 rounded-2xl bg-island-cream-2 border border-island-line">
      <AdminStatusRow
        label="商船一直停靠岸邊"
        detail="行程被拿掉，不用等四天就能再跟商人講話。關掉管理員測試模式即恢復正式行程。"
        state={
          <AdminStatePill tone={pinned ? 'on' : 'off'}>{pinned ? '生效中' : '未生效'}</AdminStatePill>
        }
      />
      <AdminStatusRow
        label="正式行程"
        detail={`停 ${days(dockedDays)} 天 → 離開 ${days(awayDays)} 天 → 再停 ${days(dockedDays)} 天（一檔 ${days(periodDays)} 天）`}
        state={<AdminStatePill tone="off">{`${days(dockedDays)} / ${days(awayDays)}`}</AdminStatePill>}
      />
      <AdminStatusRow
        label="這一趟造訪"
        detail={visit ? `${visit.visitId}（貨架跟著這一檔換）` : '名單上沒有商人'}
        state={<AdminStatePill tone={visit?.open ? 'on' : 'off'}>{phaseLabel}</AdminStatePill>}
      />
      <p className="text-[9px] text-island-navy-soft/80 leading-tight pt-2">
        釘住的是「他在不在」，不是時間。貨架照樣每一檔換一批、造訪 id 照樣會換，
        所以換檔那一刻（這家店最容易出錯的地方）在這個模式下依然測得到。
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}

function EconomySection() {
  const { settings } = useApp();
  const ownAll = !!settings?.adminOwnAllItems;

  return (
    <>
      <AdminGroup

            border and the radius), so it is dropped in bare — a wrapper here would draw a second
            border around the first. */}
        <AdminOwnAllItemsRow />
        <div className="pt-2">
          <GrantAllItemsButton />
        </div>
      </AdminGroup>

      <AdminGroup
        icon={<Ticket size={14} />}
        title="輪盤與功能卡"

      >

// --- 健身與獎勵 -------------------------------------------------------------

function WorkoutSection() {
  return (
    <AdminGroup
      icon={<Dumbbell size={14} />}
      title="健身獎勵測試"
      note="「模擬完成健身」發出的是真正的完成事件，走完整的獎勵流程；「抽獎預覽」不寫入任何東西。"
    >
      <AdminWorkoutRewardControls />

// --- 寵物 -------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * 直接設定寵物狀態 — moved out of 寵物照護面板, which is itself only reachable while a companion
 * is out. The write path is unchanged (context/usePetCare.ts), so what a tester sees is what a
 * player in that condition sees.
 */
function PetSection() {
  const { profile, setPetCare, showIslandAlert } = useApp();
  const care = profile?.islandState?.pet?.care;
  const [applied, setApplied] = useState<string | null>(null);

  const pct = (value: number | undefined) =>
    typeof value === 'number' ? `${Math.round(value * 100)}%` : '—';

  return (
    <AdminGroup
      icon={<PawPrint size={14} />}
      title="寵物照護狀態"
      note="直接把飽足與活動力設定到指定區間，走的是正式的照護寫入路徑。會寫入存檔。"
      state={
        <AdminStatePill tone={care ? 'info' : 'off'}>{care ? '已有紀錄' : '尚未建立'}</AdminStatePill>
      }
    >
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 p-3 rounded-2xl bg-island-cream-2 border border-island-line">
        <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-1.5 text-[10px] font-bold text-island-navy-soft">
          <span>
            飽足：<span className="font-mono text-island-navy">{pct(care?.nutrition)}</span>
          </span>
          <span>
            活動力：<span className="font-mono text-island-navy">{pct(care?.energy)}</span>
          </span>
        </div>
        <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2 pt-1.5 border-t border-dashed border-island-line">
          {PET_CONDITION_BANDS.map((band) => (
            <Button
              key={band.id}
              variant="secondary"
              className="px-3 py-1.5 text-[11px]"
              title={band.note}
              onClick={() => {
                void (async () => {
                  playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
                  // Just above the band's own floor, so the state lands INSIDE the band being
                  // tested rather than on the boundary between it and the one below.
                  const level = Math.min(1, band.fromActivity + 0.05);
                  const ok = await setPetCare(level, level);
                  if (!ok) {
                    showIslandAlert(describeRecentFailure());
                    return;
                  }
                  setApplied(band.id);
                  window.setTimeout(() => setApplied((k) => (k === band.id ? null : k)), 1400);
                })();
              }}
            >
              {applied === band.id ? '已套用' : band.label}
            </Button>
          ))}
        </div>
        <span className="text-[9px] text-island-navy-soft/80 leading-tight">
          沒有「殺死寵物」的按鈕，因為沒有那個狀態。設定後回島上看牠怎麼動，就是玩家會看到的樣子。
        </span>
      </div>
    </AdminGroup>
  );
}

// --- 新手與登入流程 ---------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * The category with the most STATUS and the fewest buttons, on purpose.
 *
 * 新手引導 and the seven 小天使 guides have no Admin control — what 管理員測試模式 does to them is
 * change a rule (replay every session instead of once ever, see lib/tutorialReplay.ts). Before
 * this console there was nowhere in the game that said so, which is exactly the 「是否正在生效」
 * question the brief's §7 is about. They are reported here rather than given a fake button,
 * because inventing a 「重播教學」 control would be inventing a feature that does not exist.
 */
function OnboardingSection() {
  const { profile, forceShowLoginBonus } = useApp();
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);

  return (
    <>
      <AdminGroup
        icon={<Trophy size={14} />}
        title="每日補給與連續登入"
        note="這顆不是「顯示」而是「再發一次」：每按一次 loginStreak +1 並再度發放，沒有每日上限。會寫入存檔。"
      >
        <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 p-3 rounded-2xl bg-island-cream-2 border border-island-line">
          <div className="text-[10px] font-bold text-island-navy-soft">
            目前連續登入：
            <span className="font-mono text-island-navy">{profile?.loginStreak || 0}</span> 天
          </div>
          <AdminActionButton
            full
            tone="teal"
            icon={<Trophy size={12} strokeWidth={2.75} />}
            label={busy ? '發放中…' : '再觸發一次每日補給'}
            disabled={busy || !profile}
            title="管理員：再跑一次連續登入的發放"
            onClick={() => {
              void (async () => {
                playSound(SoundEffect.CLICK);
                setBusy(true);
                await forceShowLoginBonus();
                setBusy(false);
              })();
            }}
          />
        </div>
      </AdminGroup>

      <AdminGroup
        icon={<GraduationCap size={14} />}
        title="教學重播規則"
        note="唯讀。這些是管理員測試模式改變的「規則」，不是按鈕 —— 關掉模式就恢復成玩家的規則。"
      >
        <div className="p-3 rounded-2xl bg-island-cream-2 border border-island-line">
          <AdminStatusRow
            label="新手引導（教練阿肌）"
            detail="正式玩家每個裝置只看一次；現在每次登入都會重播，且不會覆寫玩家的「已完成」紀錄"
            state={<AdminStatePill tone="on">重播中</AdminStatePill>}
          />
          <AdminStatusRow
            label="小天使導覽 ×7"
            detail="建造模式總覽、我的家、建築與裝飾、島上物件、領土規劃、家具、房間擴建 —— 建造模式與室內的七個導覽同樣每次重播"
            state={<AdminStatePill tone="on">重播中</AdminStatePill>}
          />
          <AdminStatusRow
            label="每日登入面板"
            detail="正式規則是每個台北曆日第一次進遊戲才自動打開；現在每次重新整理都會自動打開"
            state={<AdminStatePill tone="on">每次開啟</AdminStatePill>}
          />
          <AdminStatusRow
            label="新手引導・第四站"
            detail="這一站講的就是鏡頭遠近轉盤，所以它跟著轉盤走（見「場景與環境」）"
            state={<AdminStatePill tone="info">跟隨轉盤</AdminStatePill>}
          />
        </div>
      </AdminGroup>
    </>
  );
}

// --- 目錄 -------------------------------------------------------------------
```

```tsx
/**
 * @license

 */

import { useMemo, useSyncExternalStore, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import {
  ROOM_DEFS,
  ROOM_GRID_SIZE,
  ROOM_HALF_SIZE,
  parseUnlockedRooms,
  type RoomInstance,
  type RoomKey,
} from '../../../constants/rooms';
import { getPlacementLayer } from '../../../constants/placement';
import {
  getFootprint,
  getFootprintVersion,
  footprintOutline,
  subscribeFootprints,
} from '../../../lib/furniturePlacement';
import type { PlacedItem } from '../../../types';
import { mmPx } from './miniMapCore';
import type { MiniMapBounds } from './MiniMapViewport';

/**
 * The house floor plan, as world-space SVG for MiniMapViewport.
 *
 * This file owns *what the interior looks like on a map* and nothing else —
 * no tracking, no rotation, no framing, no placement on screen. A second scene
 * (the island, another floor) is a sibling of this file and inherits all of
 * those from the shared pieces; see miniMapCore.ts.
 *
 * Rooms are laid out on the fixed ROOM_GRID_SIZE world grid
 * (src/constants/rooms.ts), so nothing here hardcodes a room count or layout —
 * it draws whatever parseUnlockedRooms() currently returns, and an expansion
 * shows up without extra wiring.
 */

const HALF = ROOM_HALF_SIZE;

// Doorway openings: every wall shared by two unlocked rooms has a centred
// 3-world-unit doorway in 3D (BuildingInteriorView's DoorwayWall), so the plan
// draws the same gap and shows exactly where the player can walk.
const DOOR_WORLD_WIDTH = 3;
// Thickness of the drawn gap across the shared edge, in px — just wide enough
// to erase both rooms' strokes on either side of the edge.
const WALL_GAP_PX = 8;

// Now that the map holds a fixed zoom (MINIMAP_PX_PER_WORLD), a room is always
// the same size on screen and these can be plain constants instead of the
// former "shrink the type until the whole house fits" arithmetic.
const WALL_PX = 2.4;
const LABEL_PX = 12;
const GLYPH_PX = 22;
// The player is pinned to the middle of the window, so anything drawn at the
// centre of the room they are standing in lands under the player marker — and
// that is precisely the room whose label matters most. The room you are IN
// therefore keeps only its glyph, lifted clear of the marker; its *name* is
// already on the frame's nameplate, at full size, every frame. Rooms you are
// not in are unobstructed and keep both.
const CURRENT_GLYPH_LIFT_PX = 20;

// Mirrors --color-island-navy / --color-island-teal (index.css). Local consts
// because each is repeated across every glyph below.
const INK = '#264653';
const INK_ACCENT = '#2A9D8F';

// Map glyph per room type. Names/colors come from ROOM_DEFS so new room types
// added there pick up their fill/label here automatically; the icon merely
// falls back to a generic house until one is added to this table.
//
// These are hand-drawn rather than emoji. Emoji (🛋️🍳🛁…) are rendered by the
// OS emoji font, so they arrived glossy, multi-coloured and in Apple/Segoe's
// house style - the one thing on screen that ignored the island palette
// entirely, and visibly a different product from the flat cream/teal/navy HUD
// around them (they also differ per platform, so the plan never looked the same
// on two machines). Drawn as plain SVG they follow the same language as the
// rest of the game's art: chunky flat silhouettes, generous corner radii, two
// tones only - the navy ink the plan's walls and labels already use, plus the
// teal accent - which is exactly how QVersionIcon builds the shop's item icons.
const GLYPH_BOX = 24;

// Authored on a 24x24 box, content inset ~1.5 units so every glyph carries the
// same optical margin. Kept to 2-4 shapes each: at the size these actually
// render anything finer turns to mush. Partial on purpose: a room type added to
// ROOM_DEFS without a glyph here still draws - it gets `fallback` - rather than
// failing the build. Only `fallback` itself is mandatory.
const ROOM_GLYPHS: Partial<Record<RoomKey, ReactNode>> & { fallback: ReactNode } = {
  // Sofa, side-on: backrest, seat cushion, two feet.
  living: (
    <>
      <rect x="2.5" y="8" width="19" height="6.5" rx="3" fill={INK} />
      <rect x="1.5" y="12.5" width="21" height="5.5" rx="2.5" fill={INK_ACCENT} />
      <rect x="3.5" y="18" width="2.5" height="2.5" rx="1.25" fill={INK} />
      <rect x="18" y="18" width="2.5" height="2.5" rx="1.25" fill={INK} />
    </>
  ),
  // Cooking pot: lid (overhanging, with a knob) over a body with two ears. The
  // overhang and knob are what keep it from reading as the warehouse crate -
  // both would otherwise be "navy box, teal band on top".
  kitchen: (
    <>
      <rect x="10.4" y="4.2" width="3.2" height="2.6" rx="1.3" fill={INK_ACCENT} />
      <rect x="1.5" y="6.5" width="21" height="3.2" rx="1.6" fill={INK_ACCENT} />
      <rect x="1.5" y="11.5" width="3.2" height="3" rx="1.5" fill={INK} />
      <rect x="19.3" y="11.5" width="3.2" height="3" rx="1.5" fill={INK} />
      <rect x="4" y="9.5" width="16" height="10" rx="2.4" fill={INK} />
    </>
  ),
  // Bathtub with a riser tap.
  bathroom: (
    <>
      <rect x="4" y="5.5" width="2.5" height="6.5" rx="1.25" fill={INK_ACCENT} />
      <path d="M1.5 11 h21 v2.5 a6 6 0 0 1 -6 6 h-9 a6 6 0 0 1 -6 -6 z" fill={INK} />
      <rect x="5" y="18.5" width="2.5" height="2.5" rx="1.25" fill={INK} />
      <rect x="16.5" y="18.5" width="2.5" height="2.5" rx="1.25" fill={INK} />
    </>
  ),
  // Three book spines of uneven height on a shelf.
  study: (
    <>
      <rect x="3.5" y="6.5" width="4.5" height="12.5" rx="1.2" fill={INK} />
      <rect x="9.5" y="4.5" width="4.5" height="14.5" rx="1.2" fill={INK_ACCENT} />
      <rect x="15.5" y="8" width="4.5" height="11" rx="1.2" fill={INK} />
      <rect x="2" y="19" width="20" height="2.5" rx="1.25" fill={INK} />
    </>
  ),
  // Dumbbell: bar plus a plate at each end.
  fitness: (
    <>
      <rect x="7" y="10.5" width="10" height="3" rx="1.5" fill={INK_ACCENT} />
      <rect x="2.5" y="6.5" width="4.5" height="11" rx="1.8" fill={INK} />
      <rect x="17" y="6.5" width="4.5" height="11" rx="1.8" fill={INK} />
    </>
  ),
  // Bed, side-on: tall headboard, pillow, mattress, feet. The headboard is
  // deliberately tall - it is the one feature that separates this from the
  // sofa above, which is otherwise the same wide low navy-and-teal bar.
  bedroom: (
    <>
      <rect x="1.5" y="4.5" width="4" height="14" rx="2" fill={INK} />
      <rect x="6" y="8.5" width="7" height="4.2" rx="2.1" fill={INK_ACCENT} />
      <rect x="1.5" y="12.5" width="21" height="5.5" rx="2.5" fill={INK} />
      <rect x="2" y="18" width="2.5" height="2.5" rx="1.25" fill={INK} />
      <rect x="19.5" y="18" width="2.5" height="2.5" rx="1.25" fill={INK} />
    </>
  ),
  // Taped parcel: the full-height tape stripe survives at small sizes, where a
  // lid band alone just read as a stray tab floating on a square.
  warehouse: (
    <>
      <rect x="3" y="5.5" width="18" height="15" rx="2.2" fill={INK} />
      <rect x="10.4" y="5.5" width="3.2" height="15" fill={INK_ACCENT} />
    </>
  ),
  // Hammer, canted so the head and handle both read at a glance. Handle kept
  // long and narrow against the head: at this size a stubby one reads as a
  // mushroom rather than a tool.
  workshop: (
    <g transform="rotate(-20 12 12)">
      <rect x="4" y="3.5" width="16" height="5.6" rx="1.6" fill={INK} />
      <rect x="10.6" y="8.8" width="2.8" height="11.7" rx="1.4" fill={INK_ACCENT} />
    </g>
  ),
  // Generic house, matching the gable silhouette QVersionIcon draws for the
  // shop's House Styles.
  fallback: (
    <>
      <path d="M12 3.5 L22.5 12.5 H1.5 Z" fill={INK} strokeLinejoin="round" />
      <rect x="4.5" y="11.5" width="15" height="9" rx="1.8" fill={INK} />
      <rect x="9.5" y="14.5" width="5" height="6" rx="1.2" fill={INK_ACCENT} />
    </>
  ),
};

/** One room glyph, centred on the current local origin. */
function RoomGlyph({ type, cy, dim }: { type: RoomKey; cy: number; dim: boolean }) {
  const s = GLYPH_PX / GLYPH_BOX;
  return (
    <g
      transform={`translate(${-GLYPH_PX / 2} ${cy - GLYPH_PX / 2}) scale(${s})`}
      opacity={dim ? 0.72 : 1}
    >
      {ROOM_GLYPHS[type] ?? ROOM_GLYPHS.fallback}
    </g>
  );
}

export interface InteriorPlan {
  rooms: RoomInstance[];
  bounds: MiniMapBounds;
}

/**
 * The unlocked-room list as a drawable plan. Pure function of the profile's
 * room strings, memoised because the pose loop above it runs at display rate
 * and re-parsing room strings there would be pure waste.
 */
export function useInteriorPlan(unlockedRooms: string[] | undefined): InteriorPlan {
  return useMemo(() => {
    const rooms = parseUnlockedRooms(unlockedRooms);
    const xs = rooms.map(r => r.cx);
    const zs = rooms.map(r => r.cz);
    return {
      rooms,
      bounds: {
        minX: (xs.length ? Math.min(...xs) : 0) - HALF,
        maxX: (xs.length ? Math.max(...xs) : 0) + HALF,
        minZ: (zs.length ? Math.min(...zs) : 0) - HALF,
        maxZ: (zs.length ? Math.max(...zs) : 0) + HALF,
      },
    };
  }, [unlockedRooms]);
}

export function InteriorMiniMapScene({
  rooms,
  placements,
  currentRoomId,
}: {
  rooms: RoomInstance[];
  placements: PlacedItem[] | undefined;
  currentRoomId: string | null;
}) {
  // One entry per shared edge: scanning only each room's east/south neighbour
  // visits every adjacent pair exactly once.
  const doors = useMemo(
    () =>
      rooms.flatMap(a =>
        rooms
          .filter(
            b =>
              (b.cx - a.cx === ROOM_GRID_SIZE && b.cz === a.cz) ||
              (b.cz - a.cz === ROOM_GRID_SIZE && b.cx === a.cx)
          )
          .map(b => ({
            x: mmPx((a.cx + b.cx) / 2),
            y: mmPx((a.cz + b.cz) / 2),
            // true = neighbours stack vertically on the plan, so the shared
            // wall (and its doorway) runs horizontally.
            alongX: b.cz !== a.cz,
          }))
      ),
    [rooms]
  );

  // Furniture footprints are MEASURED off the real models rather than typed by
  // hand (lib/furniturePlacement.ts) — the same boxes the placement rules and
  // the ghost outline use, so what the map shows can't disagree with what the
  // player can actually walk around. They arrive as each model mounts, hence
  // the subscription: pieces appear on the plan the moment they're measurable
  // instead of waiting for an unrelated re-render.
  const footprintVersion = useSyncExternalStore(
    subscribeFootprints,
    getFootprintVersion,
    getFootprintVersion
  );

  // `footprintVersion` is a dependency rather than an unused read: a new
  // measurement is exactly when this has to be recomputed.
  const furniture = useMemo(() => {
    if (!placements?.length) return [];
    return placements.flatMap(p => {
      const fp = getFootprint(p.itemId);
      if (!fp) return [];
      // The collider's own outline, not a box around it — the map is a picture of what the
      // placement rules think is there, so it has to be drawn from the same polygon they test.
      return [
        {
          id: p.instanceId,
          points: footprintOutline(fp, p.position[0], p.position[2], p.rotation || 0)
            .map(([x, z]) => `${mmPx(x).toFixed(1)},${mmPx(z).toFixed(1)}`)
            .join(' '),
          layer: getPlacementLayer(p.itemId),
        },
      ];
    });
  }, [placements, footprintVersion]);

  return (
    <>
      {rooms.map(room => (
        <rect
          key={room.id}
          x={mmPx(room.cx - HALF)}
          y={mmPx(room.cz - HALF)}
          width={mmPx(ROOM_GRID_SIZE)}
          height={mmPx(ROOM_GRID_SIZE)}
          rx={5}
          fill={ROOM_DEFS[room.type].styleColor}
          stroke={INK}
          strokeOpacity={0.45}
          strokeWidth={WALL_PX}
        />
      ))}

      {/* Furniture. The plan used to draw empty boxes with a label in them,
          which told the player nothing they didn't already know; the shapes
          are what make a room recognisable as *their* room from the map
          alone. Rugs sit lower in the stack and lighter, since you walk over
          them rather than around them. */}
      {furniture.map(f => (
        <polygon
          key={f.id}
          points={f.points}
          fill={INK}
          fillOpacity={f.layer === 'rug' ? 0.1 : 0.2}
          stroke={INK}
          strokeOpacity={f.layer === 'rug' ? 0.14 : 0.3}
          strokeWidth={1}
          strokeLinejoin="round"
        />
      ))}

      {/* Doorways: erase the shared wall over the opening, then mark both ends
          with a jamb tick. The ticks are what make an opening read as a *door*
          on a floor plan rather than a wall that just happens to stop. */}
      {doors.map((door, i) => {
        const doorLen = mmPx(DOOR_WORLD_WIDTH);
        return (
          <g key={`door-${i}`}>
            <rect
              x={door.x - (door.alongX ? doorLen : WALL_GAP_PX) / 2}
              y={door.y - (door.alongX ? WALL_GAP_PX : doorLen) / 2}
              width={door.alongX ? doorLen : WALL_GAP_PX}
              height={door.alongX ? WALL_GAP_PX : doorLen}
              rx={1.5}
              fill="#FFFDF6"
            />
            {[-1, 1].map(side => (
              <rect
                key={side}
                x={door.alongX ? door.x + (side * doorLen) / 2 - 1 : door.x - WALL_GAP_PX / 2}
                y={door.alongX ? door.y - WALL_GAP_PX / 2 : door.y + (side * doorLen) / 2 - 1}
                width={door.alongX ? 2 : WALL_GAP_PX}
                height={door.alongX ? WALL_GAP_PX : 2}
                rx={1}
                fill={INK}
                opacity={0.4}
              />
            ))}
          </g>
        );
      })}

      {rooms
        .filter(room => room.id === currentRoomId)
        .map(room => (
          <g key={`here-${room.id}`}>
            <rect
              x={mmPx(room.cx - HALF)}
              y={mmPx(room.cz - HALF)}
              width={mmPx(ROOM_GRID_SIZE)}
              height={mmPx(ROOM_GRID_SIZE)}
              rx={6}
              fill={INK_ACCENT}
              opacity={0.13}
            />
            {/* Breathing highlight ring — the one moving element on the plan
                besides the player, so "you are here" is legible at a glance
                without reading any label. */}
            <rect
              x={mmPx(room.cx - HALF) + 2}
              y={mmPx(room.cz - HALF) + 2}
              width={mmPx(ROOM_GRID_SIZE) - 4}
              height={mmPx(ROOM_GRID_SIZE) - 4}
              rx={5}
              fill="none"
              stroke={INK_ACCENT}
              strokeWidth={3}
            >
              <animate
                attributeName="stroke-opacity"
                values="1;0.45;1"
                dur="2.4s"
                repeatCount="indefinite"
              />
            </rect>
          </g>
        ))}

      {rooms.map(room => {
        const isCurrent = room.id === currentRoomId;
        return (
          // Rooms turn with the map; what's written ON them must not. Each
          // piece of type is wrapped in `.minimap-upright`, which cancels the
          // map's rotation about that piece's own centre (index.css) — so the
          // glyph and the name stay pinned to their room while staying the
          // right way up, rather than reading sideways whenever the player
          // looks south.
          <g key={`label-${room.id}`} transform={`translate(${mmPx(room.cx)} ${mmPx(room.cz)})`}>
            <g textAnchor="middle" pointerEvents="none">
              <g className="minimap-upright">
                <RoomGlyph
                  type={room.type}
                  cy={isCurrent ? -CURRENT_GLYPH_LIFT_PX : -LABEL_PX * 0.55}
                  dim={!isCurrent}
                />
              </g>
              {!isCurrent && (
                <g className="minimap-upright">
                  <text
                    y={GLYPH_PX * 0.62}
                    fontSize={LABEL_PX}
                    fontWeight={900}
                    dominantBaseline="central"
                    fill={INK}
                    opacity={0.72}
                    // Cream halo behind the ink: room fills, furniture blocks and
                    // the sand paper outside the house are all different values,
                    // and a plain navy label lands on all three as the map turns.
                    stroke="#FFFDF6"
                    strokeWidth={2.6}
                    strokeOpacity={0.55}
                    paintOrder="stroke"
                  >
                    {room.name}
                  </text>
                </g>
              )}
            </g>
          </g>
        );
      })}
    </>
  );
}
```

## src/components/UI/minimap/MiniMapFrame.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import type { ReactNode } from 'react';

/**
 * The minimap bezel: a low-poly wooden ship's wheel with a brass-riveted rim,
 * and a hanging plank under it for the room you're standing in.
 *
 * WHY IT LOOKS LIKE AN OBJECT. The old map was a rounded cream rectangle with
 * a title row — correct tokens, no personality, and the one piece of HUD that
 * didn't read as something you'd find on the island. This follows
 * DESIGN_SYSTEM.md's "change the construction, not the colour": the shape
 * carries it. Sixteen flat facets rather than a smooth ring (so it reads
 * carved, and matches the game's low-poly models), eight turned handles, eight
 * rivets, a shadowed inner lip the map sinks behind, and a lit top edge —
 * light comes from above, as it does everywhere else in this HUD.
 *
 * PALETTE — a documented art exception, like QVersionIcon's wood grain and the
 * floor/wall material swatches (see DESIGN_SYSTEM.md § Documented exceptions).
 * These four tones depict weathered driftwood; they are not chrome, and no
 * other component may reach for them. Everything *functional* about this
 * component — the map inside, the nameplate's ink and live dot, the shadow
 * family, the radius scale — stays on the island tokens. The tones are
 * deliberately desaturated: a saturated oak would fight the muted teal/cream
 * HUD it sits in, which is the same mistake the pre-2026-07 amber chrome made.
 */
const WOOD = ['#E3CDA9', '#D2B68C', '#BE9E72', '#A2825A'] as const;
const WOOD_EDGE = '#8A6B47';
const RIVET = '#F3EFE6';

// --- Wheel geometry, in the bezel's own 0-100 viewBox -----------------------
const C = 50;
const R_HANDLE = 50.5; // outer tip of the turned handles
const R_OUT = 47;      // outer edge of the rim
const R_IN = 38.6;     // inner lip — the map's own edge sits here
const FACETS = 16;
const HANDLES = 8;

/**
 * Fraction of the bezel's width taken by the map window. Derived from R_IN, so
 * the hole and the drawing can't drift apart: change R_IN and the map follows.
 */
const MAP_INSET_PCT = 50 - R_IN;

const pt = (r: number, a: number) => `${(C + r * Math.cos(a)).toFixed(2)},${(C + r * Math.sin(a)).toFixed(2)}`;

// Angles run clockwise from straight up, matching the map's own heading
// convention, so a facet's shading and a marker's bearing are described the
// same way.
const angleAt = (turns: number) => turns * Math.PI * 2 - Math.PI / 2;

// One flat quad per facet. Precomputed at module load: this is a fixed
// silhouette, not something that depends on props or state.
const RIM_FACETS = Array.from({ length: FACETS }, (_, i) => {
  const a0 = angleAt(i / FACETS);
  const a1 = angleAt((i + 1) / FACETS);
  // 1 at the top of the wheel, -1 at the bottom: the wood is lit from above.
  const lit = -Math.sin((a0 + a1) / 2);
  // The parity term is what keeps it reading as *facets* rather than a smooth
  // gradient — adjacent panels of carved wood never catch the light equally.
  const tone = Math.min(3, Math.max(0, Math.round((1 - lit) * 1.4) + (i % 2)));
  return {
    points: `${pt(R_OUT, a0)} ${pt(R_OUT, a1)} ${pt(R_IN, a1)} ${pt(R_IN, a0)}`,
    fill: WOOD[tone],
  };
});

const RIM_OUTLINE = Array.from({ length: FACETS }, (_, i) => pt(R_OUT, angleAt(i / FACETS))).join(' ');

// The turned handles a helmsman grips. Drawn under the rim so they emerge from
// beneath it rather than sitting on top like stickers.
const WHEEL_HANDLES = Array.from({ length: HANDLES }, (_, i) => {
  const a = angleAt(i / HANDLES);
  // Perpendicular to the spoke, for the handle's half-width.
  const px = -Math.sin(a);
  const py = Math.cos(a);
  const at = (r: number, half: number, sign: number) =>
    `${(C + r * Math.cos(a) + px * half * sign).toFixed(2)},${(C + r * Math.sin(a) + py * half * sign).toFixed(2)}`;
  return {
    // Slightly tapered toward the tip — a lathe-turned peg, not a matchstick.
    points: `${at(R_OUT - 5, 3.1, 1)} ${at(R_HANDLE - 2.2, 2.3, 1)} ${at(R_HANDLE - 2.2, 2.3, -1)} ${at(R_OUT - 5, 3.1, -1)}`,
    capX: C + (R_HANDLE - 2.2) * Math.cos(a),
    capY: C + (R_HANDLE - 2.2) * Math.sin(a),
    lit: -Math.sin(a),
  };
});

// Brass rivets, set between the handles so the rim never looks crowded.
const RIVETS = Array.from({ length: HANDLES }, (_, i) => {
  const a = angleAt((i + 0.5) / HANDLES);
  const r = (R_OUT + R_IN) / 2;
  return { x: C + r * Math.cos(a), y: C + r * Math.sin(a) };
});

export function MiniMapFrame({
  label,
  children,
}: {
  /** Contents of the nameplate hanging under the wheel. */
  label: ReactNode;
  /** The map window itself — sized and positioned by this component. */
  children: ReactNode;
}) {
  return (
    <div
      className="relative"
      style={{ width: 'var(--minimap-w)', height: 'var(--minimap-h)' }}
    >
      <div className="relative" style={{ width: 'var(--minimap-w)', height: 'var(--minimap-w)' }}>
        {/* The bezel's shadow is a drop-shadow FILTER, not a box-shadow: this
            silhouette has eight handles poking out of a sixteen-sided ring,
            and a box-shadow would trace the square bounding box instead of
            the wheel. Same rule as .notch-shadow* for clipped chrome — see
            DESIGN_SYSTEM.md. */}
        <svg
          viewBox="0 0 100 100"
          className="absolute inset-0 h-full w-full"
          style={{ filter: 'drop-shadow(0 10px 18px rgba(38,70,83,0.30))' }}
        >
          {WHEEL_HANDLES.map((h, i) => (
            <g key={`handle-${i}`}>
              <polygon points={h.points} fill={h.lit > 0 ? WOOD[1] : WOOD[2]} />
              <circle cx={h.capX} cy={h.capY} r={2.3} fill={h.lit > 0 ? WOOD[0] : WOOD[1]} />
            </g>
          ))}

          {RIM_FACETS.map((f, i) => (
            <polygon key={`facet-${i}`} points={f.points} fill={f.fill} />
          ))}
          <polygon
            points={RIM_OUTLINE}
            fill="none"
            stroke={WOOD_EDGE}
            strokeWidth={0.8}
            strokeLinejoin="round"
            opacity={0.45}
          />

          {RIVETS.map((r, i) => (
            <g key={`rivet-${i}`}>
              <circle cx={r.x} cy={r.y} r={1.7} fill={RIVET} />
              <circle cx={r.x} cy={r.y} r={1.7} fill="none" stroke={WOOD_EDGE} strokeWidth={0.5} opacity={0.55} />
            </g>
          ))}

          {/* Inner lip: a shadowed groove the map sinks into, with a lit
              hairline just inside it. Two tiers of edge, never one flat
              stroke — the same reason the Toolbar's track has both. */}
          <circle cx={C} cy={C} r={R_IN + 0.9} fill="none" stroke={WOOD_EDGE} strokeWidth={2} opacity={0.5} />
          <circle cx={C} cy={C} r={R_IN - 0.5} fill="none" stroke="#FFFDF6" strokeWidth={0.9} opacity={0.8} />
        </svg>

        <div className="absolute" style={{ inset: `${MAP_INSET_PCT}%` }}>
          {children}
        </div>
      </div>

      {/* Nameplate — a small plank hung off the bottom of the wheel, carrying
          the one piece of live text the map needs. It overlaps the rim rather
          than floating below it, so the whole thing stays one object. */}
      <div className="absolute bottom-0 left-1/2 flex max-w-[86%] -translate-x-1/2 justify-center">
        <div
          className="flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-full border px-3 py-1 shadow-[0_4px_10px_rgba(38,70,83,0.22)]"
          style={{ background: WOOD[0], borderColor: WOOD_EDGE }}
        >
          {label}
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { mmPx } from './miniMapCore';

/**
 * MiniMap indicator system — anything that says "someone is here, facing that
 * way", drawn on top of a scene.
 *
 * Split out from both the map and the scenes on purpose: an indicator's angle
 * is a fact about the *subject* (the player's model yaw, an NPC's yaw, a quest
 * arrow's bearing) stated as a plain world bearing, never as a screen angle.
 * The window is what knows about the camera. That makes every indicator the
 * same two questions — where is it, which way is it pointing — which is what
 * this file answers once.
 *
 *   MiniMapMarker       — world-anchored: an NPC, a quest target, a pet.
 *                         Lives inside a scene's SVG, so it pans AND turns with
 *                         the map; its world bearing therefore becomes the
 *                         right screen angle with no work on its part.
 *   MiniMapPlayerMarker — the player: pinned to the centre of the window,
 *                         OUTSIDE the map, with its angle driven live by CSS
 *                         (below).
 *
 * The artwork pieces (`MarkerCone`, `MarkerPip`) are shared so a second
 * indicator reads as the same family rather than a new invention, and every
 * marker is authored pointing STRAIGHT UP in its own local space — one
 * convention, so a rotation is always just the subject's facing angle.
 */

/** Screen-clockwise degrees, i.e. what {@link worldYawToFacingDeg} returns. */
export type FacingDeg = number;

/**
 * A world-anchored indicator. `facingDeg` omitted means the thing has no
 * meaningful facing (a chest, a marker pin) and the artwork is drawn upright.
 */
export function MiniMapMarker({
  x,
  z,
  facingDeg,
  children,
}: {
  /** World XZ. */
  x: number;
  z: number;
  facingDeg?: FacingDeg;
  children: ReactNode;
}) {
  return (
    <g
      transform={`translate(${mmPx(x).toFixed(1)} ${mmPx(z).toFixed(1)})${
        facingDeg === undefined ? '' : ` rotate(${facingDeg.toFixed(1)})`
      }`}
      pointerEvents="none"
    >
      {children}
    </g>
  );
}

/**
 * The player's own indicator: fixed at the centre of the window, pointing
 * wherever the CHARACTER MODEL is facing — never where the camera is looking.
 *
 * Rendered as a sibling of the map, not a child of it, so the map's own
 * rotation cannot reach this artwork. Its angle comes from `--mm-facing`, which
 * MiniMapViewport rewrites once per frame with the character's bearing already
 * expressed in the turned map's frame — so the arrow tracks the character at
 * display rate, stays welded to the map through a camera turn, and React
 * re-renders nothing.
 *
 * Rotation pivots on the marker's own local origin (`.minimap-facing`), which
 * is where this artwork is centred and also the window's centre — and
 * therefore the player's world position, so the arrow spins on the spot rather
 * than orbiting. That class pins `transform-origin: 0 0` for a reason worth
 * knowing before authoring another marker; see index.css.
 */
export function MiniMapPlayerMarker() {
  return (
    <svg
      className="pointer-events-none absolute left-1/2 top-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2"
      width="72"
      height="72"
      viewBox="-36 -36 72 72"
    >
      <defs>
        <linearGradient id="mm-player-cone" x1="0" y1="1" x2="0" y2="0">
          <stop offset="0" stopColor="#2A9D8F" stopOpacity="0.55" />
          <stop offset="1" stopColor="#2A9D8F" stopOpacity="0" />
        </linearGradient>
      </defs>

      {/* Everything directional is inside the one rotating group. The ping is
          in here too — it's a circle, so it reads identically at any angle,
          and keeping it in the same group means there is exactly one thing
          that can be out of date. */}
      <g className="minimap-facing">
        <MarkerCone fill="url(#mm-player-cone)" stroke="#1F7A70" />
        <circle r="7" fill="#2A9D8F" opacity="0.35">
          <animate attributeName="r" from="7" to="17" dur="2s" repeatCount="indefinite" />
          <animate attributeName="opacity" from="0.35" to="0" dur="2s" repeatCount="indefinite" />
        </circle>
        {/* An arrowhead rather than the old plain dot: with the map held still,
            the marker is the ONLY thing carrying heading, so the silhouette
            itself has to state it. A circle with a soft cone behind it reads as
            "you are here" but not as "you are facing there". */}
        <path
          d="M 0 -8.6 L 6.4 6.2 A 1.6 1.6 0 0 1 4.3 8.2 L 0 6.2 L -4.3 8.2 A 1.6 1.6 0 0 1 -6.4 6.2 Z"
          fill="#2A9D8F"
          stroke="#FFFFFF"
          strokeWidth="2.2"
          strokeLinejoin="round"
          paintOrder="stroke"
        />
      </g>
    </svg>
  );
}

/**
 * The soft "what I can see" wedge, authored pointing up. Shared so the player
 * and any facing NPC use the same visual language for the same idea.
 *
 * The outlined edges are not decoration: the room the player stands in is
 * itself washed teal, and a soft teal-on-teal gradient disappears into it. A
 * line survives where a wash doesn't.
 */
export function MarkerCone({ fill, stroke }: { fill: string; stroke: string }) {
  return (
    <path
      d="M 0 0 L -15 -26 A 30 30 0 0 1 15 -26 Z"
      fill={fill}
      stroke={stroke}
      strokeOpacity="0.35"
      strokeWidth="1.4"
      strokeLinejoin="round"
    />
  );
}

/** A small filled dot with a white keyline — the base body of any marker. */
export function MarkerPip({ color, r = 5 }: { color: string; r?: number }) {
  return <circle r={r} fill={color} stroke="#FFFFFF" strokeWidth={2} />;
}
```

## src/components/UI/minimap/MiniMapViewport.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { useEffect, useId, useRef, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import {
  MINIMAP_MAX_DT,
  MINIMAP_WORLD_PAD,
  mmPx,
  readMiniMapPose,
  smoothFacingDeg,
  smoothViewDeg,
  wrapDeg,
  type MiniMapPose,
} from './miniMapCore';
import { MiniMapPlayerMarker } from './MiniMapMarker';

export interface MiniMapBounds {
  minX: number;
  minZ: number;
  maxX: number;
  maxZ: number;
}

/**
 * The round map window: a heading-up view of one scene, panned so the player is
 * always at its centre and turned so the camera's direction is always at its
 * top.
 *
 * HOW IT WORKS. The scene is drawn once, flat, in world space (`children`,
 * positioned through mmPx). Nothing in it is ever re-laid-out. Every frame
 * this component only rewrites four custom properties on its own root:
 *
 *   --mm-tx / --mm-ty   how far the plan is slid so the player lands on the
 *                       window's centre
 *   --mm-map            how far the plan is turned, from the CAMERA
 *   --mm-facing         how far the player's arrow is turned, from the
 *                       CHARACTER MODEL
 *
 * The first three drive `.minimap-plan`; the last drives `.minimap-facing`,
 * which lives in a separate element entirely (MiniMapMarker.tsx) — the arrow is
 * NOT a child of the plan, so the map's rotation cannot reach it.
 *
 * THE ONE CONVERSION FROM WORLD TO SCREEN. A pose states two bearings in the
 * map's north-up frame (miniMapCore). Turning the plan by `-viewDeg` is what
 * makes the window heading-up, and it drags everything drawn *inside* the plan
 * around with it — so a world-anchored marker at bearing B lands at `B - view`
 * on screen for free, with no per-marker arithmetic (see MiniMapMarker). The
 * player's arrow is outside the plan and therefore has to be handed that same
 * subtraction explicitly: `facing - view`. Both use the SAME smoothed view
 * angle, which is what keeps the arrow welded to the map through a camera turn
 * instead of drifting against it for as long as the two eases disagree.
 *
 * The upshot, and the reason the two are split: orbiting the camera around a
 * standing character turns the map under a stationary arrow (the character
 * still faces the same door), while turning the character under a still camera
 * turns the arrow on a stationary map. Both at once compose without either
 * system knowing about the other.
 *
 * WHY CUSTOM PROPERTIES rather than React state: this runs at display rate.
 * The original map called setState on every animation frame the player walked,
 * re-rendering the entire plan (every room, label, glyph and doorway) 60 times
 * a second to move one dot. Here React re-renders only when the *scene*
 * changes — a room unlocked, a piece of furniture placed.
 *
 * `onPose` is called every frame with the raw pose for consumers that need
 * position-derived state (which room am I in?). It MUST compare before
 * setting React state — see MiniMap.tsx's handler for the pattern.
 */
export function MiniMapViewport({
  bounds,
  active,
  onPose,
  children,
}: {
  /** World-unit extent of the scene being drawn (before paper padding). */
  bounds: MiniMapBounds;
  /** Drive the frame loop only while the map is actually on screen. */
  active: boolean;
  onPose?: (pose: MiniMapPose) => void;
  /** World-space SVG content, drawn in mmPx() units. */
  children: ReactNode;
}) {
  const rootRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  // Read through a ref so a caller's inline arrow doesn't restart the loop on
  // every render.
  const onPoseRef = useRef(onPose);
  onPoseRef.current = onPose;

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!active) return;
    const root = rootRef.current;
    if (!root) return;

    let raf = 0;
    let last = performance.now();
    // Null until the first pose arrives, so the map opens already oriented and
    // the arrow already pointing the right way, instead of both visibly
    // unwinding from 0° on mount.
    let facing: number | null = null;
    let view: number | null = null;

    const tick = (now: number) => {
      raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
      const dt = Math.min((now - last) / 1000, MINIMAP_MAX_DT);
      last = now;

      const pose = readMiniMapPose();
      if (!pose) return;

      // Two eases over two independent sources. Neither reads the other.
      facing = facing === null ? pose.facingDeg : smoothFacingDeg(facing, pose.facingDeg, dt);
      view = view === null ? pose.viewDeg : smoothViewDeg(view, pose.viewDeg, dt);

      // Wrapped so the values can't grow without bound over a long session.
      // Safe to do abruptly *because* nothing here is CSS-transitioned — the
      // smoothing above is the only thing animating, so a 180°/-180° flip is
      // the same rendered angle rather than a spin.
      root.style.setProperty('--mm-map', `${wrapDeg(-view).toFixed(2)}deg`);
      root.style.setProperty('--mm-facing', `${wrapDeg(facing - view).toFixed(2)}deg`);
      root.style.setProperty('--mm-tx', `${(-mmPx(pose.x)).toFixed(2)}px`);
      root.style.setProperty('--mm-ty', `${(-mmPx(pose.z)).toFixed(2)}px`);

      onPoseRef.current?.(pose);
    };

    raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
    return () => cancelAnimationFrame(raf);
  }, [active]);

  // Ids must be unique per instance: a duplicate anywhere in the document
  // silently repoints every url(#…) at the first match (two minimaps could
  // legitimately co-exist during a view cross-fade).
  const uid = useId().replace(/:/g, '');
  const dots = `${uid}-paper`;

  const paperX = mmPx(bounds.minX - MINIMAP_WORLD_PAD);
  const paperY = mmPx(bounds.minZ - MINIMAP_WORLD_PAD);
  const paperW = mmPx(bounds.maxX - bounds.minX + MINIMAP_WORLD_PAD * 2);
  const paperH = mmPx(bounds.maxZ - bounds.minZ + MINIMAP_WORLD_PAD * 2);

  return (
    <div
      ref={rootRef}
      className="relative h-full w-full overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-island-sand"
    >
      <div className="minimap-plan">
        <svg
          className="absolute block"
          style={{ left: paperX, top: paperY, width: paperW, height: paperH }}
          viewBox={`${paperX} ${paperY} ${paperW} ${paperH}`}
        >
          <defs>
            <pattern id={dots} width="10" height="10" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
              <circle cx="5" cy="5" r="1" fill="#264653" opacity="0.07" />
            </pattern>
          </defs>
          {/* Paper extends well past the scene so the window never runs off
              the edge of the drawing at any heading. */}
          <rect x={paperX} y={paperY} width={paperW} height={paperH} fill="#EFE9DC" />
          <rect x={paperX} y={paperY} width={paperW} height={paperH} fill={`url(#${dots})`} />
          {children}
        </svg>
      </div>

      {/* Corner falloff, so the plan reads as sunk into the bezel rather than
          printed flat on it. Outside the rotating layer — the light doesn't
          turn with the map. */}
      <div
        className="pointer-events-none absolute inset-0 rounded-full"
        style={{
          background:
            'radial-gradient(circle at 50% 50%, rgba(38,70,83,0) 52%, rgba(38,70,83,0.16) 100%)',
        }}
      />

      {/* THE PLAYER — pinned dead centre, a sibling of the plan rather than a
          child of it, so nothing the map does can rotate it. See
          MiniMapMarker.tsx. */}
      <MiniMapPlayerMarker />

      {/* North mark. The window is heading-up, so north is a live bearing: the
          badge rides around the rim on the map's own rotation (its ring is
          concentric with the window, so `rotate` alone walks it round the
          circle) while `.minimap-upright` keeps the letter itself readable. */}
      <div
        className="pointer-events-none absolute inset-0"
        style={{ transform: 'rotate(var(--mm-map, 0deg))' }}
      >
        <div className="absolute left-1/2 top-[3%] -translate-x-1/2">
          <div className="minimap-upright flex h-[17px] w-[17px] items-center justify-center rounded-full border border-island-line bg-island-cream/95 text-[8px] font-black leading-none text-island-navy-soft shadow-[0_1px_3px_rgba(38,70,83,0.18)]">
            N
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```
