```ts
  /**
   * 音樂盒吊飾 — plays only while you walk, and leaves the notes behind you.
   *
   * A music box is wound by movement, so the emitter is gated on it: standing still this item is
   * completely silent, which is both the truthful behaviour and the reason it can afford a much
   * shorter interval than anything ambient. The notes SETTLE, so a walk leaves a line of them
   * hanging in the air along the path — the same mechanism as the wings' feathers, and the
   * clearest evidence that these capabilities are general rather than one-item features.
   */
  {
    itemId: 'fx-musicbox-charm',
    series: 'music',
    socket: 'pendant',
    model: 'musicBox',
    effect: {
      motion: {
        // THE BOX ITSELF NO LONGER SPINS, and that is the correction this pass is proudest of.
        // The old row turned the whole ornament about Y at 0.5 rad/s to suggest a crank turning.
        // What that actually draws is a pendant rotating on its cord — a bauble. A music box is a
        // MECHANISM: the case hangs still and the works move inside it, which is only expressible
        // now that sub-parts can be driven (see PartMotionSpec).
        sway: { axis: 'x', amplitude: 0.04, speed: 1.1 },
        parts: [
          // The pinned barrel. Its axis is X (the cylinder is laid across the box), and the four
          // pins on its surface are what make the rotation visible — a smooth cylinder turning
          // about its own axis is invariant, the same trap the halo's flat ring records.
          { tag: 'barrel', spin: { axis: 'x', speed: 1.15 } },
          // The two gears on the face, turning the other way and slower, half a cycle apart.
          { tag: 'gear', spin: { axis: 'z', speed: -0.85 }, stagger: 0.5 },
          { tag: 'ribbon', sway: { axis: 'z', amplitude: 0.24, speed: 0.75 } },
        ],
      },
      emit: [
        {
          shape: 'note',
          colors: [COSMETIC_PALETTE.music.body, COSMETIC_PALETTE.music.glow, COSMETIC_PALETTE.music.deep],
          interval: 0.91,
          intervalJitter: 0.5,
          count: [1, 2],
          lifetime: [2.75, 3.75],
          size: [0.042, 0.066],
          offset: [0, 0.06, 0],
          spread: 0.12,
          rise: 0.5,
          drift: 0.24,
          // 「向上漂浮 → 左右輕微擺動 → 淡出」, and the middle clause is this line. Before it the
          // notes went up a straight ramp; a note that does not waver is a note on a rail.
          wobble: { amplitude: 0.09, speed: 0.5 },
          // Very low: a note has an up and a down, and a fast tumble turns it into a smudge.
          // It is not SHAPE_FLAT because a note frozen square to the camera looks printed.
          tumble: 0.35,
          settle: 0.55,
          opacity: 0.85,
          maxAlive: 10,
          trigger: 'moving',
          // A whole note among the quavers, now and then. 1.35 rather than 1.7 for the size-budget
          // reason recorded on the star hairpin — a note is a tall thin glyph and 0.112 world was
          // a 22 cm quaver hanging at chest height. `npm run audit:cosmetics` is what pinned the
          // final value: at 1.45 it came out at 0.096 against the 0.09 solid ceiling, which is the
          // kind of two-thousandths overshoot nobody catches by looking at a render.
          rare: { chance: 0.12, size: 1.35, lifetime: 1.25, opacity: 0.95 },
        },
        {
          // 「小星星」. Sparse, always on, and the reason this item is no longer completely dead
          // standing still — which mattered because the whole point of it is that it plays only
          // when you walk, and an item that is nothing at all on the shop stand does not get
          // bought for what it does when you leave.
          shape: 'star',
          colors: [COSMETIC_PALETTE.music.glow, COSMETIC_PALETTE.starlight.body],
          interval: 2.5,
          intervalJitter: 0.45,
          count: [1, 1],
          lifetime: [2.4, 3.4],
          size: [0.024, 0.04],
          offset: [0, 0.05, 0.01],
          spread: 0.12,
          rise: 0.28,
          drift: 0.12,
          wobble: { amplitude: 0.04, speed: 0.45 },
          tumble: 0.4,
          opacity: 0.7,
          maxAlive: 3,
          trigger: 'always',
        },
        {
          // 「小光點」 riding with the notes and settling with them, so the trail left along a walk

          shape: 'mote',
          colors: [COSMETIC_PALETTE.music.glow, COSMETIC_PALETTE.music.body],
          interval: 0.85,
          intervalJitter: 0.5,
          count: [1, 2],
          lifetime: [1.8, 2.6],

          offset: [0, 0.05, 0],
          spread: 0.18,
          rise: 0.32,
          drift: 0.16,

          settle: 0.5,
          opacity: 0.6,

  /**
   * 海洋腳環 — the first cosmetic on the legs, and the cheapest kind of pair there is.
   *
   * One catalog row, two anklets: the ankle slot is rendered by the LEG, so both legs mount it
   * and each swings with the joint it is on. Nothing here says "pair" and nothing had to — the
   * walk cycle already moves the two legs separately, so they are out of step for free. Compare
   * the wings, where a pair had to be built and driven by hand because both halves hang off one
   * socket on the back.
   *
   * Its bubbles are gated on movement and rise from ankle height, so they read as coming off the
   * feet of someone walking through shallow water.
   */
  {
    itemId: 'fx-ocean-anklet',
    series: 'ocean',
    socket: 'ankle',
    model: 'oceanAnklet',
    effect: {

        {
          // Now ALWAYS on, at a long interval, with `movingScale` cutting it by more than half

          shape: 'bubble',

          trigger: 'always',
          movingScale: 0.42,

  /**
   * 花環足跡 — a ring of moss and blooms lying on the GROUND, and the item the aura socket was
   * built for.
   *
   * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   * WHY THIS ONE EXISTS
   * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   *
   * Two jobs, and it is worth being explicit that they are two:
   *
   *   IT PROVES THE GROUND SOCKET. Everything else in this file is worn on a body and inherits
   *   the body's transform. This is the first cosmetic that belongs to the floor, so it is the
   *   first that has to REFUSE the body's transform and follow the terrain instead — see
   *   {@link GroundSpec}. A ring is also the shape that makes the conforming visible: a ring
   *   cutting into a hillside is unmistakable, which is exactly why it is the right thing to
   *   ship the capability with rather than something forgiving.
   *
   *   IT REVIVES THE FLOWER BOND. flower had two pet items and no player item, so its bond could
   *   never fire (see the note in SERIES_BONDS). This is the player half it was missing, and
   *   with it the table goes from five producible pairs to six.
   *
   * Petals only while moving, so standing still this is a quiet circle of flowers and walking
   * scatters them — the same `moving` gate the mushroom cap and the flower collar use, which is
   * what makes the three read as one series doing one thing.
   */
  {
    itemId: 'fx-bloom-circle',
    series: 'flower',
    socket: 'aura',
    model: 'bloomCircle',
    effect: {
      ground: {
        // The model's local radius 0.32 at the character root's 2.25x — see the world-units
        // note on GroundSpec.radius, which this got wrong once.
        radius: 0.72,
        // 3 cm. Enough to clear z-fighting against the terrain on a slope, small enough that the
        // ring never reads as hovering.
        lift: 0.03,
        // ~23 degrees. Past that the island is a cliff rather than a hill, and a ring standing
        // up at 40 degrees looks like a wheel — floating flat is the better failure.
        maxTilt: 0.4,
      },
      motion: {
        // Slow enough to be a drift rather than a spin, and it is the only WHOLE-RING motion
        // here: a `bob` would fight the ground for position.y, and the ground wins by
        // construction.
        spin: { axis: 'y', speed: 0.09 },
        parts: [
          // The three mushrooms, breathing. `bob` on a sub-part is safe where it is not on the
          // group: the ground spec owns the GROUP's y and overwrites it every frame, but a child
          // of that group is measured from wherever the group ended up, so the two cannot fight.
          { tag: 'shroom', bob: { amplitude: 0.004, speed: 0.55 }, stagger: 0.33 },
        ],
      },
      emit: [
        {
          shape: 'petal',
          colors: [COSMETIC_PALETTE.flower.body, COSMETIC_PALETTE.flower.glow, COSMETIC_PALETTE.flower.deep],
          interval: 0.77,
          intervalJitter: 0.5,
          count: [1, 2],
          lifetime: [2, 3],
          size: [0.03, 0.054],
          // Spawned at the ring's own height, out at its edge, so petals leave the CIRCLE rather
          // than the wearer's feet.
          offset: [0, 0.05, 0],
          // Roughly the ring's world diameter: petals appear ANYWHERE on the circle rather than
          // at its centre, which is what makes them look shed by the ring and not by the wearer.
          spread: 1.4,
          rise: 0.2,
          drift: 0.22,
          wobble: { amplitude: 0.06, speed: 0.5 },
          tumble: 1.6,
          settle: 0.5,
          opacity: 0.8,
          maxAlive: 9,
          trigger: 'moving',
        },
        {
          // THE FOOTPRINTS — 「玩家走過的地方留下短暫的花朵痕跡」, and the thing this item is
          // named after but did not previously do.
          //
          // Four fields together are the whole trick, and none of them is new machinery:
          //
          //   `spread` 0.24    — at the FEET, not out on the ring. The petals above are shed by
          //                      the circle; these are left by the walker.
          //   `settle` 0.05    — it stops travelling almost immediately, so it is a mark lying on
          //                      the ground rather than a petal drifting past it.
          //   `grow` 0.4       — 「縮小 → 淡出」. It ends at two fifths of the size it started, so
          //                      the bloom closes as it goes instead of only getting fainter. This
          //                      is the first use of a grow BELOW one, and it is the reason the
          //                      field is a multiplier rather than an "expand" flag.
          //   `interval` 0.78  — one flower roughly every three quarters of a second at a walk,
          //                      which at this character's pace is a mark every stride or so.
          //                      Written at 0.62 first, which is under the 0.75 s floor the
          //                      visibility pass fixed and `npm run audit:cosmetics` enforces —
          //                      and the floor is right: faster than this a trail stops being a
          //                      trail and becomes a carpet.
          shape: 'petal',
          colors: [COSMETIC_PALETTE.flower.glow, COSMETIC_PALETTE.flower.body, COSMETIC_PALETTE.forest.glow],
          interval: 0.78,
          intervalJitter: 0.35,
          count: [1, 1],
          lifetime: [2.4, 3.2],
          size: [0.05, 0.075],
          grow: 0.4,
          offset: [0, 0.015, 0],
          spread: 0.24,
          rise: 0.015,
          drift: 0.03,
          tumble: 0.25,
          settle: 0.05,
          opacity: 0.85,
          maxAlive: 7,
          trigger: 'moving',
        },
        {
          // Pollen over the ring, always. Standing still this item used to emit nothing at all —
          // correct for a trail, wrong for a circle of flowers you are standing in.
          shape: 'spore',
          colors: [COSMETIC_PALETTE.flower.heart, COSMETIC_PALETTE.forest.glow],
          interval: 1.9,
          intervalJitter: 0.5,
          count: [1, 2],
          lifetime: [2.4, 3.4],
          size: [0.024, 0.036],
          offset: [0, 0.08, 0],
          spread: 1.2,
          rise: 0.22,
          drift: 0.1,
          wobble: { amplitude: 0.06, speed: 0.4 },
          tumble: 0,
          opacity: 0.5,
          maxAlive: 5,
          trigger: 'always',
        },
      ],
    },
  },

  /**
   * 結霜光環 — the first cosmetic on this shelf that is not in any of the existing families.
   *
   * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   * WHY A NEW SERIES RATHER THAN A COLD STARLIGHT ITEM
   * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   *
   * It shares a socket with 精靈光環 and half a silhouette, so the temptation is to file it under
   * starlight as "the blue one". That would be wrong for a reason the bond table makes concrete:
   * a series is the KEY two cosmetics match on, so putting frost under starlight would mean a
   * player wearing this and a pet in a 星星項圈 fire a starlight bond — a burst of warm gold
   * between an ice halo and a star collar. A series that a player cannot predict from looking is
   * worse than an extra series.
   *
   * `frost` is therefore declared with no pet half, which is a legal state the SERIES_BONDS
   * assertion at the bottom of this file deliberately permits in one direction only: registering
   * a bond for a one-sided series throws; HAVING a one-sided series does not.
   *
   * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   * THE THREE LAYERS, AND WHICH REQUIREMENT EACH ONE ANSWERS
   * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   *
   *   SNOW falls, flutters, and is the one thing here anyone recognises instantly.
   *   CRYSTALS orbit rather than drift, so the halo has substance going round it and not just
   *     weather coming off it — and one in eight is 「較大的冰晶」 that SHRINKS as it fades
   *     (`rare.grow` below 1), which is how a crystal breaks apart without any shatter geometry.
   *   MIST is the wisp layer, and it is what stops the other two reading as two emitters in the
   *     same place. Fog between things is what makes them look like they are in the same air.
   */
  {
    itemId: 'fx-frost-halo',
    series: 'frost',
    socket: 'halo',
    model: 'frostHalo',
    effect: {
      motion: {
        // SLOWER than the spirit halo's 0.28, and unlike that one this rotation is VISIBLE on the
        // ring itself — the hoop carries six spikes, so it is not invariant under its own spin.
        // That is the whole structural difference between the two halos: one is a still ring that
        // things travel around, this one is a body that turns.
        spin: { axis: 'y', speed: 0.2 },
        bob: { amplitude: 0.015, speed: 0.45 },
        pulse: { amplitude: 0.035, speed: 0.7 },
        parts: [
          { tag: 'orbit', spin: { axis: 'y', speed: 0.38 }, stagger: 0.333 },
          // The spikes breathe very slightly, staggered round the ring so the pulse travels
          // rather than happening everywhere at once. 8% is under the threshold where it reads as
          // an animation at all; what it stops is ice looking like moulded plastic.
          { tag: 'spike', pulse: { amplitude: 0.08, speed: 0.9 }, stagger: 0.16 },
        ],
      },
      emit: [
        {
          shape: 'snow',
          colors: [COSMETIC_PALETTE.frost.glow, COSMETIC_PALETTE.frost.body],
          // 1.4 s, giving ~4 flakes alive. Measured rather than chosen: at 1.25 the three emitters
          // on this item summed to ~8.7 particles, which is the highest ambient total in the
          // catalog and a clear step above 精靈光環's 6.2 by day. Two legendaries on one shelf
          // should be comparably loud, and this one already has the busiest MODEL of the two.
          interval: 1.4,
          intervalJitter: 0.45,
          count: [1, 2],
          lifetime: [3, 4.4],
          size: [0.03, 0.05],
          offset: [0, -0.02, 0],
          spread: 0.28,
          rise: -0.55,
          drift: 0.16,
          // The largest wobble in the catalog, and the only one where the flutter IS the subject
          // rather than a correction to a straight line. A flake that falls plumb is a pixel.
          wobble: { amplitude: 0.1, speed: 0.38 },
          tumble: 0.4,
          opacity: 0.85,
          maxAlive: 7,
          trigger: 'always',
        },
        {
          shape: 'crystal',
          colors: [COSMETIC_PALETTE.frost.ice, COSMETIC_PALETTE.frost.glow],
          interval: 1.9,
          intervalJitter: 0.45,
          count: [1, 2],
          lifetime: [2.6, 3.8],
          size: [0.026, 0.042],
          offset: [0, 0, 0],
          spread: 0.14,
          rise: 0.1,
          drift: 0.22,
          orbit: 0.6,
          tumble: 0.6,
          opacity: 0.9,
          maxAlive: 5,
          trigger: 'always',
          // 「偶爾產生一個較大的冰晶，然後慢慢碎裂消失」. `grow: 0.25` is the shrink — it ends at a
          // quarter of the size it was drawn at, so the crystal dwindles while it fades instead of
          // simply going transparent at full size. A slower tumble too, because a big shard that
          // spins at the same rate as a chip has no weight.
          rare: { chance: 0.13, size: 2.4, lifetime: 1.45, grow: 0.25, tumble: 0.45, opacity: 0.95 },
        },
        {
          shape: 'wisp',
          colors: [COSMETIC_PALETTE.frost.glow, COSMETIC_PALETTE.frost.body],
          interval: 2.1,
          intervalJitter: 0.45,
          count: [1, 1],
          lifetime: [2.6, 3.6],
          size: [0.05, 0.08],
          grow: 2,
          offset: [0, -0.06, 0],
          spread: 0.22,
          rise: -0.12,
          drift: 0.12,
          tumble: 0,
          opacity: 0.5,
          maxAlive: 3,
          trigger: 'always',
        },
      ],
      glow: {
        color: COSMETIC_PALETTE.frost.body,
        // 14, and the two revisions this number went through are the whole of what "measured, not
        // reasoned" means for a light in this scene.
        //
        // It was written at 11 on the reasoning that frost should be a cold TINT rather than a
        // lamp, one clear step under the spirit halo's 16. Rendered side by side at the island's
        // midnight ambient, 16 puts a visible pool of light on the ground the wearer is standing
        // in and 11 puts nothing there at all — the character picked up a blue rim and the floor
        // was unchanged. That is not "quieter", it is the item's headline effect not happening,
        // and it is the same cliff the spirit halo's own note describes finding below ~6: the
        // response is not linear anywhere near the bottom of it.
        //
        // 14 is a real pool that is still visibly dimmer than the spirit halo's. The step between
        // two lights has to be measured in what lands on the FLOOR, not in the numbers.
        intensity: 14,
        distance: 5,
        pulse: { amplitude: 0.14, speed: 0.45 },
        // Same hard constraint as the spirit halo's: a point light must stay OUTSIDE the 0.585
        // skull sphere, or it lights the inside of the head and nothing else.
        offset: [0, -0.2, 0],
        trigger: 'night',
      },
    },
  },

  /**
   * 昆蟲之翼 — the second pair of wings, and deliberately the opposite build to the first.
   *
   * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   * TWO BACK ITEMS ON ONE SHELF ONLY WORKS IF THEY ARE DIFFERENT KINDS OF THING
   * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   *
   * 星軌之翼 is a FAN of opaque quills that opens when you walk, leaves feathers where you have
   * been, and bursts when you jump. Every one of those is about the player's MOVEMENT.
   *
   * This one is about the object. Four translucent membranes, a fine fast flutter that barely
   * changes between standing and walking, and a haze of luminous motes that is there whatever the
   * player is doing. Where the star wings are loudest at the moment of a jump, these are at their
   * best when the player is standing still and being looked at — which is the other half of what
   * a premium cosmetic is for, and the half the shelf did not have.
   *
   * Three specific differences, all in the numbers rather than in new machinery:
   *
   *   THE BEAT IS FAST AND SMALL.  3.4 Hz against the star wings' 1.6, at 0.3 rad against 0.2 —
   *     an insect's flutter, not a bird's stroke. And the resting speed is 0.9 rather than 0.32:
   *     these never really stop.
   *   FOUR WINGS, LAGGED.  `secondaryLag` puts the hind pair a quarter beat behind the fore pair.
   *     Two pairs beating together are one thick wing; the lag is the whole read.
   *   THE BURST IS SOFT.  The star wings throw sixteen hard stars that arc and fall. This throws
   *     fourteen motes that barely travel and hang — 「螢光」 rather than 「星屑」. Both are the
   *     one loud moment each item is allowed; they should not sound alike.
   */
  {
    itemId: 'fx-insect-wings',
    // Not a new series: 蝴蝶髮夾 is already butterfly, and the two make a matched pair a player can
    // wear a step apart in price. butterfly has no pet half and is therefore not in SERIES_BONDS,
    // which is legal — see the note on 結霜光環 above.
    series: 'butterfly',
    socket: 'back',
    model: 'insectWings',
    effect: {
      motion: {
        flap: {
          // Note how little the resting and moving poses differ compared with the star wings
          // (0.06→0.2 amplitude, 0.32→1.6 speed there). An insect's wings do not open BECAUSE it
          // started walking; they are already going. The crossfade still runs, it just has much
          // less to travel, which is what makes this pair read as alive rather than as responsive.
          amplitude: 0.12, speed: 0.95, spread: 0.08, sweep: 0.06,
          movingAmplitude: 0.3, movingSpeed: 3.4, movingSpread: 0.16, movingSweep: 0.22,
          secondaryLag: 1.55,
          secondaryScale: 0.7,
        },
        bob: { amplitude: 0.006, speed: 0.5 },
      },
      emit: [
        {
          // 「螢光粒子」. Always on, filling the span of the wings rather than trailing off them —
          // `spread` 0.55 is about the full wingspan, and `rise` is small, so these hang in the
          // wings instead of leaving.
          shape: 'mote',
          colors: [COSMETIC_PALETTE.butterfly.glow, COSMETIC_PALETTE.flower.glow, COSMETIC_PALETTE.butterfly.body],
          interval: 1.45,
          intervalJitter: 0.5,
          count: [1, 2],
          lifetime: [2.4, 3.6],
          size: [0.024, 0.038],
          offset: [0, 0.02, -0.04],
          spread: 0.55,
          rise: 0.16,
          drift: 0.12,
          wobble: { amplitude: 0.05, speed: 0.4 },
          tumble: 0,
          opacity: 0.72,
          maxAlive: 7,
          trigger: 'always',
          rare: { chance: 0.1, size: 1.8, lifetime: 1.3, opacity: 0.92 },
        },
        {
          // The moving trail. `spore` rather than `feather`: the star wings own the falling-quill
          // read and two items shedding the same shape from the same socket would be one item with
          // two skins. These are soft points of light that stop where they were dropped.
          shape: 'spore',

const BY_ITEM_ID = new Map(SPECIAL_COSMETICS.map(def => [def.itemId, def]));

/**
 * The catalog and the shop must agree, and neither can enforce it alone.
 *
 * Two ways for them to drift, both silent at runtime and both caught here at module load:
 * a row whose item does not exist can never be equipped (so the cosmetic is unreachable),
 * and an item in one of the special categories with no row equips to nothing at all (so the
 * player buys an ornament and sees no ornament). The second is the one that would actually
 * ship — it looks like a rendering bug rather than a missing table entry.
 */
const SPECIAL_SHOP_CATEGORIES = ['SpecialFx', 'PetGear'];

const catalogProblems: string[] = [];
for (const def of SPECIAL_COSMETICS) {
  const item = ALL_ITEMS.find(i => i.id === def.itemId);
  if (!item) {
    catalogProblems.push(`${def.itemId} has no item in constants/items.ts, so it can never be equipped.`);
  } else if (!SPECIAL_SHOP_CATEGORIES.includes(item.shopCategory)) {
    catalogProblems.push(
      `${def.itemId} sits in shopCategory '${item.shopCategory}', which is not one of ` +
      `${SPECIAL_SHOP_CATEGORIES.join('/')} — it would share its single-select slot with ordinary wearables.`,
    );
  }
}
for (const item of ALL_ITEMS) {
  if (SPECIAL_SHOP_CATEGORIES.includes(item.shopCategory) && !BY_ITEM_ID.has(item.id)) {
    catalogProblems.push(`item ${item.id} (${item.name}) is sold as a special cosmetic but has no row here, so equipping it draws nothing.`);
  }
}
if (catalogProblems.length > 0) {
  throw new Error(`[cosmeticEffects] catalog is out of step with the shop:\n  - ${catalogProblems.join('\n  - ')}`);
}

/** The special-cosmetic row for an item id, or null for an ordinary item. */
export function getSpecialCosmetic(itemId: string): SpecialCosmeticDef | null {
  return BY_ITEM_ID.get(itemId) ?? null;
}

/**
 * Every special cosmetic in an equipped list, for one wearer.
 *
 * ID lookup, not name matching. The wardrobe resolver next door (Three/character/outfit.ts)
 * matches on substrings of Chinese item names because it predates item ids being stable;
 * that is a pattern to contain, not to copy — a cosmetic named 星星髮飾 and one named
 * 小星星髮飾 would both match `wearing('星星髮飾')`, and the wrong one would win.
 */
export function resolveSpecialCosmetics(
  equippedIds: readonly string[],
  wearer: CosmeticWearer,
): SpecialCosmeticDef[] {
  const out: SpecialCosmeticDef[] = [];
  for (const id of equippedIds) {
    const def = BY_ITEM_ID.get(id);
    if (def && SOCKET_WEARER[def.socket] === wearer) out.push(def);
  }
  return out;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// PLAYER ↔ PET BOND (section 四)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * What happens when the player and the pet wear the SAME SERIES and stand close.
 *
 * The constraints in the brief are all about restraint, so they are all encoded as numbers
 * rather than left to the implementation:
 *
 *   - it is not permanent — `cooldown` seconds must pass between firings, and the burst
 *     itself lives for `lifetime` and is gone;
 *   - it is not a lot — one larger particle in the gap between the two, plus `sideCount`
 *     small ones near each of them;
 *   - it needs them genuinely together — `radius` is 2.2 world units, roughly one dog's
 *     length past arm's reach, so walking past does not set it off.
 */
export interface SeriesBondSpec {
  shape: ParticleShape;
  colors: string[];
  /** Radius of the larger particle that appears BETWEEN the two. */
  centreSize: number;
  /** Radius of the small ones that appear beside each of them. */
  sideSize: number;
  sideCount: number;
  lifetime: number;
  rise: number;
  opacity: number;
}

/** How close the two must be for a bond to fire, world units. */
export const BOND_RADIUS = 2.2;
/** Minimum seconds between bond firings. Long on purpose — this is a moment, not an aura. */
export const BOND_COOLDOWN = 9;

/**
 * Only series that BOTH a player item and a pet item exist for can ever bond, so this table is
 * the shorter of the two lists by construction. It was three for as long as the catalog had only
 * three such families; cloud, ocean and music were declared in {@link CosmeticSeries} and given
 * palettes from the start and sat empty, so they could never fire. Filling in one player item
 * and one pet item each is what promoted them, and NOTHING in the runtime changed to allow it.
 *
 * A series with no entry here simply does not bond — that is a state, not a bug. bubble,
 * campfire, honey and butterfly are each still one-sided.
 */
export const SERIES_BONDS: Partial<Record<CosmeticSeries, SeriesBondSpec>> = {
  starlight: {
    shape: 'star',
    colors: [COSMETIC_PALETTE.starlight.glow, COSMETIC_PALETTE.starlight.body],
    centreSize: 0.1,
    sideSize: 0.04,
    sideCount: 2,
    lifetime: 2.6,
    rise: 0.3,
    opacity: 0.85,
  },
  forest: {
    shape: 'leaf',
    colors: [COSMETIC_PALETTE.forest.glow, COSMETIC_PALETTE.forest.body],
    centreSize: 0.08,
    sideSize: 0.04,
    sideCount: 2,
    lifetime: 2.8,
    rise: 0.22,
    opacity: 0.8,
  },
  // flower CAME BACK. It could never fire while its only products were 蝴蝶結 and 花朵項圈 —
  // both PET items — because a bond needs one visible PLAYER cosmetic and one visible PET
  // cosmetic of the same series (CosmeticRuntime.sharedSeries). 花環足跡 is the player half it
  // was missing, so the pair is now 花環足跡 ↔ 花朵項圈 (or 蝴蝶結), and this entry is producible.
  //
  // The assertion at the bottom of this file is what lets it be re-added safely: if the player
  // item is ever removed, the catalog throws at module load instead of quietly going back to
  // "the bond that looks implemented and never fires".
  flower: {
    shape: 'heart',
    colors: [COSMETIC_PALETTE.flower.glow, COSMETIC_PALETTE.flower.body],
    centreSize: 0.075,
    sideSize: 0.035,
    sideCount: 2,
    lifetime: 2.4,
    rise: 0.28,
    opacity: 0.8,
  },
  // The history, kept because it is the reason the assertion exists:
  //
  // The entry named its pair as 蝴蝶結 ↔ 花朵項圈 — and both of those are PET items. A bond needs
  // one visible PLAYER cosmetic and one visible PET cosmetic of the same series (see
  // CosmeticRuntime.sharedSeries), so a series whose only products are both on the pet has no
  // way to produce one. It sat in this table looking implemented for as long as the table
  // existed, and nothing failed: the check simply never found a match, which is indistinguishable
  // from two characters never standing close enough.
  //
  // That is why the assertion at the bottom of this file exists — it turns exactly this mistake
  // into a module-load Error instead of a bond nobody ever sees.
  cloud: {
    shape: 'spore',
    colors: [COSMETIC_PALETTE.cloud.glow, COSMETIC_PALETTE.cloud.body],
    // The largest centre particle of the six, because a spore is the softest shape in the set
    // and at the sizes the others use it simply is not seen.
    centreSize: 0.11,
    sideSize: 0.05,
    sideCount: 2,
    lifetime: 2.6,
    rise: 0.2,
    opacity: 0.7,
  },
  ocean: {
    // The one bond that is a RING, so the moment between an ocean player and an ocean pet is a
    // ripple passing between them rather than a third thing appearing there.
    shape: 'ring',
    colors: [COSMETIC_PALETTE.ocean.glow],
    centreSize: 0.14,
    sideSize: 0.06,
    sideCount: 1,
    lifetime: 1.8,
    rise: 0.12,
    opacity: 0.85,
  },
  music: {
    shape: 'note',
    colors: [COSMETIC_PALETTE.music.glow, COSMETIC_PALETTE.music.body],
    centreSize: 0.085,
    sideSize: 0.042,
    sideCount: 2,
    lifetime: 2.4,
    rise: 0.34,
    opacity: 0.85,
  },
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// BOND INVARIANT
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * A registered bond must be PRODUCIBLE: the series needs at least one player cosmetic and at
 * least one pet cosmetic, because that is exactly what CosmeticRuntime.sharedSeries looks for.
 *
 * This exists because the failure it catches is invisible. `flower` sat in SERIES_BONDS with a
 * comment naming its pair as 蝴蝶結 ↔ 花朵項圈 — both of which are PET items — so the check ran
 * forever and never matched. Nothing threw, nothing logged, and the symptom ("this series never
 * bonds") is the same thing you would see if the two characters simply never stood together.
 * It was only found by driving all six series through the bond and counting particles.
 *
 * The reverse is deliberately NOT asserted: a series with both halves and no bond entry is a
 * legitimate state (it means "no bond designed for this pair yet"), and turning that into an
 * error would make adding a pet item to an existing series a breaking change.
 */
const bondProblems: string[] = [];
for (const series of Object.keys(SERIES_BONDS) as CosmeticSeries[]) {
  const rows = SPECIAL_COSMETICS.filter(def => def.series === series);
  const hasPlayer = rows.some(def => SOCKET_WEARER[def.socket] === 'player');
  const hasPet = rows.some(def => SOCKET_WEARER[def.socket] === 'pet');
  if (!hasPlayer || !hasPet) {
    bondProblems.push(
      `${series} has a bond registered but no ${!hasPlayer ? 'PLAYER' : 'PET'} cosmetic, so it ` +
      `can never fire — the bond needs one of each and silently matches nothing without it.`,
    );
  }
}
if (bondProblems.length > 0) {
  throw new Error(`[cosmeticEffects] unproducible bond:\n  - ${bondProblems.join('\n  - ')}`);
}
```

```ts
/**
 * 貨幣 — what the player can hold, where each kind is stored, and how it is named on screen.
 *
 * This is the single declaration of the game's wallet. Nothing else in the app may decide that a
 * number "is gold", read `profile.balanceGold` to answer 「玩家有多少錢」, or invent a second place
 * to keep a balance. A screen asks {@link getBalance}; a grant or a charge goes through the economy
 * service (context/useEconomyActions.ts), which is the only writer.
 *
 * ## Two currencies, and they are NOT two flavours of the same thing
 *
 *   金幣 (coins)      earned by TRAINING, and by nothing else. Spent on the ordinary catalog.
 *   碎片 (fragments)  earned by everything that is NOT training — 每日登入, 輪盤, 活動, 任務,
 *                     摸摸寵物, 島嶼秘寶. A long-horizon collectible resource.
 *
 * The separation is the point, and it is enforced structurally rather than by convention: see
 * {@link constants/rewards.ts}'s source→currency policy, which refuses a coin grant from any source
 * that is not a workout. Making 碎片 「another kind of gold」 — spendable on the same shelf, granted
 * by the same rewards — would collapse the two back into one currency with two names, and the whole
 * reason 金幣 means anything is that the only way to get more is to exercise.
 *
 * ## Where a balance lives, and why the two are not stored the same way
 *
 * `coins` stays on the top-level `balanceGold` field it has always used. That field is load-bearing:
 * `firestore.rules`' `isValidUser` requires it UNCONDITIONALLY on every write, the daily-login server
 * transaction reads and increments it directly, and every existing save in the wild carries it.
 * Moving it into a map would be a migration of the one number a player would notice going missing,
 * bought for no player-visible gain — see docs/FIRESTORE_RULES.md on what a rules/shape mismatch
 * costs.
 *
 * Everything after coins lives in ONE nested map, `profile.wallet`. That is the same shape (and the
 * same reasoning) as `islandState` and `workoutRewards`: one key in `firestore.rules`, one entry in
 * the update whitelist, and a third currency later is a row in {@link CURRENCY_SPECS} rather than a
 * schema change plus a rules deploy. A bare `balanceFragments` field was the obvious shape and is
 * the one that needs a rules deploy per currency.
 *
 * The asymmetry is hidden here and nowhere else: every caller says `getBalance(profile, 'coins')`.
 */

import type { UserProfile } from '../types';

/**
 * The currencies that exist. Adding one is a member here plus a row in {@link CURRENCY_SPECS};
 * `Tickets`/`EventCurrency`/`PremiumCurrency` are named in the brief as possible futures and are
 * deliberately NOT pre-declared — a currency with no source and no sink is a promise the save
 * format has to keep.
 */
export type CurrencyId = 'coins' | 'fragments';

/** The ladder as an ORDER, for anything that iterates the wallet (the HUD, the admin panel). */
export const CURRENCY_IDS: readonly CurrencyId[] = ['coins', 'fragments'];

/** Where one currency's balance is kept in the profile. See the file doc for why there are two. */
export type CurrencyStorage =
  /** A top-level `UserProfile` field, e.g. `balanceGold`. */
  | { kind: 'profile-field'; field: 'balanceGold' }
  /** A key inside the `wallet` map, e.g. `wallet.fragments`. */
  | { kind: 'wallet-key'; key: keyof PlayerWallet };

export interface CurrencySpec {
  id: CurrencyId;
  /** What the player is shown. Never derived from the id. */
  label: string;
  /**
   * How this currency is EARNED, in one line, for the admin panel and for whoever reads this file
   * next. Not player-facing copy — the rule it describes is enforced in constants/rewards.ts.
   */
  sourceRule: string;
  storage: CurrencyStorage;
}

export const CURRENCY_SPECS: Record<CurrencyId, CurrencySpec> = {
  coins: {
    id: 'coins',
    label: '金幣',
    sourceRule: '主要來源是健身（workout）。唯一的例外是每日登入，見 constants/rewards.ts 的政策表。',
    storage: { kind: 'profile-field', field: 'balanceGold' },
  },
  fragments: {
    id: 'fragments',
    label: '碎片',
    sourceRule: '非健身型獎勵：輪盤、活動、任務、島上互動。每日登入已改發金幣與商品碎片。',
    storage: { kind: 'wallet-key', key: 'fragments' },
  },
};

/**
 * The non-coin half of the wallet.
 *
 * Every field optional and every absence meaning zero, which is what makes this safe to add to a
 * save that predates it: a player who has never been paid a 碎片 and a save written before 碎片
 * existed are the same state, and neither needs a migration.
 */
export interface PlayerWallet {
  fragments?: number;
}

/** A whole, non-negative number. A balance that is `NaN`, negative or fractional is read as 0. */
function sane(value: unknown): number {
  return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0 ? Math.floor(value) : 0;
}

/**
 * What the player holds of one currency. The ONE reader — a screen never touches `balanceGold`.
 *
 * Tolerant by construction: a missing profile, a missing field and a missing `wallet` map all read
 * as 0, because every one of them is a real state (loading, a pre-wallet save, a brand-new player)
 * and none of them is an error worth showing a player.
 */
export function getBalance(profile: UserProfile | null | undefined, currency: CurrencyId): number {
  if (!profile) return 0;
  const storage = CURRENCY_SPECS[currency].storage;
  if (storage.kind === 'profile-field') return sane(profile[storage.field]);
  return sane(profile.wallet?.[storage.key]);
}

/**
 * The Firestore update key a write to this currency has to use — `balanceGold` or `wallet.fragments`.
 *
 * A dot path, which both the real SDK and the local save shim (save/LocalSaveStore.ts) apply as a
 * nested write. Exported so the economy service can build an `increment()` update without
 * re-deriving the layout, and so nothing else has to know there are two layouts at all.
 */
export function currencyFieldPath(currency: CurrencyId): string {
  const storage = CURRENCY_SPECS[currency].storage;
  return storage.kind === 'profile-field' ? storage.field : `wallet.${storage.key}`;
}

/**
 * The profile patch that reflects an already-accepted currency write in local state.
 *
 * Separate from {@link currencyFieldPath} because the two shapes genuinely differ: Firestore takes
 * a dot path, while React state takes a `Partial<UserProfile>` with the whole `wallet` map rebuilt
 * (a patch of `{'wallet.fragments': n}` would land as a literal key). `next` is the new BALANCE, not
 * a delta — the caller has already decided what the number is.
 */
export function currencyPatch(
  profile: UserProfile | null | undefined,
  currency: CurrencyId,
  next: number,
): Partial<UserProfile> {
  const storage = CURRENCY_SPECS[currency].storage;
  if (storage.kind === 'profile-field') return { [storage.field]: next } as Partial<UserProfile>;
  return { wallet: { ...(profile?.wallet ?? {}), [storage.key]: next } };
}

/** `金幣` / `碎片`. The one place a currency is named for a player. */
export const currencyLabel = (currency: CurrencyId): string => CURRENCY_SPECS[currency].label;

```

## src/constants/dailyLogin.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 每日登入獎勵 — the seven-day round, its calendar, and the state machine the panel draws.
 *
 * This is the data-and-rules half of the feature; components/UI/DailyLoginPanel.tsx is the other
 * half and holds no rules of its own. Same split as constants/rarityFx.ts ↔ PurchaseDialog: a
 * designer changing what a day is worth, when a round turns over, or what a make-up costs should
 * never have to open a component, and a component should never be where a game rule is discovered.
 *
 * The API here is pinned by scripts/test-daily-login.ts (`npm run test:daily-login`) — that file is
 * the specification, this one is the implementation, and the names/semantics below exist to satisfy
 * it exactly. If you change a signature here, that test is where you find out what depended on it.
 *
 * ## What replaced what
 *
 * The old daily bonus paid `50 + streak * 10` gold and `20 + streak * 5` XP the instant the app
 * noticed a new calendar day, and told the player afterwards. It could not be looked forward to
 * (nothing showed what tomorrow was worth), it could not be missed (there was nothing to miss) and
 * it never ended (an unbounded streak means the number is either meaningless early or absurd
 * later). A seven-day round fixes all three: every reward is visible from day one, the round has a
 * top worth walking to, and the ladder resets so that top stays reachable.
 *
 * The XP that grant used to include is deliberately not carried over: XP stays where it is earned,
 * in 運動. No day of the round pays any.
 *
 * ## The round stopped being a ladder (2026-09-17)
 *
 * It was a straight line of 碎片 — 4, 6, 10, 16, 24, 36, 60 — and every card said the same thing
 * seven times at increasing volume. A ladder is the right shape when the reward is a NUMBER, and
 * the wrong one when what a week should feel like is 「今天會是什麼」. So the seven days are now
 * seven different KINDS of thing, and four of them are a coin flip (see {@link DAILY_PRIZE_PLAN}):
 *
 *   1, 3, 4, 6   商品碎片 ×10, or 金幣 ×15 — 50／50
 *   2            功能卡 ／ 抽獎券 ／ 金幣＋碎片 — 33 each
 *   5            a whole product, 普通／稀有／史詩 — 33 each
 *   7            one free turn of the 幸運轉盤
 *
 * What survived the rewrite, deliberately: every prize is still decided BEFORE the day arrives, so
 * a board can still show seven cards and mean it (see {@link dailyPrizeFor} on why the roll is
 * seeded rather than live), and the round is still a calendar tiling rather than a punch card.
 *
 * ## The round pays 金幣 again, and that IS a rule being spent
 *
 * From 2026-08-25 to 2026-09-17 this round paid the wallet's 碎片, because 金幣 had exactly one
 * source — 健身 — and constants/rewards.ts refused a coin grant from anything else. This round
 * gives that up: four of its seven days can pay 15 金幣, and `SOURCE_CURRENCY_POLICY` was widened
 * to let them. The reasoning that rule was built on has not stopped being true — see the note over
 * the policy table for what 15 a day is measured against, and why it is small enough that showing
 * up is still not a substitute for training.
 *
 * The 碎片 this round talks about are 商品碎片 (constants/fragments.ts): a stack that belongs to one
 * product and unlocks that product at 200. They are not the wallet's 碎片 and are not a currency.
 * No day of the round pays the wallet's 碎片 any more.
 *
 * The 補簽 fee is 金幣, as it always was — which now makes it the same currency the round can pay,
 * so a make-up is an ordinary purchase rather than the exchange rate between two resources that it
 * used to be. At {@link MAKEUP_SURCHARGE} against a 15 金幣 day it is still strictly worse than
 * showing up, which is the property that matters: it exists so that missing one day does not put
 * 第 7 天 out of reach (the grand prize requires the first six), not as a way to buy a week.
 */

import type { CurrencyId } from './currency';
import type { Rarity } from './rarity';
import { seedFrom, seedPick } from './seed';
import {
  CIVIL_TZ,
  addCivilDays,
  civilDateAt,
  civilDaysBetween,
  formatCountdown,
  msUntilNextCivilDay,
  type CivilDate,
} from './civilTime';

/**
 * 行事曆已經搬到 constants/civilTime.ts。
 *
 * 這一段原本是這個檔案自己的實作，現在只是轉出口 —— 每週任務（constants/weeklyTasks.ts）需要
 * 同一套日期運算，而讓它 import「每日登入」等於把兩個互不相干的功能綁在一起。既有的
 * `from './dailyLogin'` 一行都不用改，這正是保留這些 re-export 的理由。
 */
export {
  addCivilDays,
  civilDateAt,
  civilDaysBetween,
  formatCountdown,
  msUntilNextCivilDay,
  type CivilDate,
};

/**
 * 沿用舊名字：這個常數是每日登入 API 回應裡的一個欄位名（src/server/dailyLoginApi.ts），改名
 * 會動到那份合約，而它真正的值現在由 {@link CIVIL_TZ} 持有。
 */
export const DAILY_LOGIN_TZ = CIVIL_TZ;

/**
 * What one day of the round can hand over.
 *
 *   item-fragments       商品碎片 for one 普通／稀有 product. Which product is decided by
 *                        constants/dailyLoginPrizes.ts, which is the half of this feature that is
 *                        allowed to know the catalog exists.
 *   coins                金幣. The one kind that is paid by the SERVER — see the note below.
 *   coins-and-fragments  both of the above at once, which is what makes 第 2 天's third option the
 *                        good one rather than a third flavour of the same shrug.
 *   utility-card         一張功能卡 (constants/utilityCards.ts).
 *   raffle-ticket        抽獎券, for the 幸運轉盤.
 *   item                 a whole product, at a tier the roll picks. 第 5 天 only.
 *   free-spin            one turn of the 幸運轉盤, charged to nobody. 第 7 天 only.
 */
export type DailyPrizeKind =
  | 'item-fragments'
  | 'coins'
  | 'coins-and-fragments'
  | 'utility-card'
  | 'raffle-ticket'
  | 'item'
  | 'free-spin';

/**
 * One day's prize — AMOUNTS only, never a catalog id.
 *
 * That split is the whole reason this file can still be imported by the Express server
 * (src/server/dailyLoginApi.ts): the server has to know that 第 3 天 is worth 15 金幣, and it must
 * not have to load a few hundred item definitions, three rarity tables and a category taxonomy to
 * find that out. Which ITEM a fragment day lands on, and which card 第 2 天 hands over, are decided
 * in constants/dailyLoginPrizes.ts from the same seed — so the two halves agree without either one
 * importing the other's dependencies.
 *
 * Every field is present on every prize and most of them are 0. A discriminated union would be the
 * tidier type and the worse one to read: the card, the reveal and the write path would each have to
 * switch on `kind` before they could ask 「這一天有幾個金幣」, and the answer for six of the seven
 * kinds is simply zero.
 */
export interface DailyPrize {
  kind: DailyPrizeKind;
  /** 金幣. */
  coins: number;
  /** 商品碎片 — of ONE product, named by constants/dailyLoginPrizes.ts. */
  itemFragments: number;
  /** 抽獎券. */
  tickets: number;
  /** 功能卡, in copies. */
  cards: number;
  /** Free turns of the 幸運轉盤. */
  spins: number;
  /** Which tier an `item` day promises. Null on every other kind. */
  itemRarity: Rarity | null;
}

/**
 * The currency the round MINTS.
 *
 * It was 碎片 (the wallet currency) until 2026-09-17 and is 金幣 now, because the new round pays
 * 金幣 on four of its seven days and pays the wallet's 碎片 on none of them. The 碎片 this round
 * talks about are 商品碎片 — a stack that belongs to one product (constants/fragments.ts) — which
 * is a different thing with a different store and is NOT a currency.
 *
 * Named once, here, because three places have to agree on it: the server's transaction, the offline
 * claim path, and the chip the panel counts up. It is also the currency a 補簽 is charged in, which
 * is new — the two used to be deliberately different and the reason for that is gone.
 *
 * See constants/rewards.ts on why 每日登入 is now allowed to pay it at all. That was a real rule
 * with real teeth and this round is the decision to spend it.
 */
export const DAILY_LOGIN_CURRENCY: CurrencyId = 'coins';

/** 商品碎片 a fragment day pays, of one product. 200 unlock it, so this is a twentieth of one. */
export const DAILY_PRIZE_FRAGMENTS = 10;

/** 金幣 a coin day pays. */
export const DAILY_PRIZE_COINS = 15;

/**
 * 抽獎券 第 2 天 hands over when it rolls that way.
 *
 * NOT enough for a spin on its own, which is the point: 第 7 天 is where the round gives a turn of
 * the wheel away, and a 第 2 天 that could be spun immediately would take that away from it.
 *
 * ⚠ That only holds while a spin costs more than this. It costs {@link WHEEL_SPIN_COST} = 1 today
 * (constants/luckyWheel.ts), so as things stand two tickets are two spins and 第 2 天 IS
 * immediately spinnable. Raising the spin price to 5 is the one-line change that makes this
 * constant mean what it says; it is deliberately not made here, because it re-prices every other
 * ticket source in the game (the overflow conversion, the duplicate-outfit consolation, the
 * 限時商店's ticket bundles) and that is a balance decision, not a daily-login one.
 */
export const DAILY_PRIZE_TICKETS = 2;

/** 功能卡 第 2 天 hands over. One — a card is a real thing to be given, not a stack. */
export const DAILY_PRIZE_CARDS = 1;

/** Free turns 第 7 天 hands over. */
export const DAILY_PRIZE_SPINS = 1;

/** The tiers 第 5 天's product can come out at, each equally likely. */
export const DAILY_PRIZE_ITEM_RARITIES: readonly Rarity[] = ['common', 'rare', 'epic'];

/**
 * What each day of the round can roll, day 1 first — and this table IS the seven-day design.
 *
 * ## Why a day is a LIST of kinds rather than one kind
 *
 * Because the brief is 「隨機」, and the honest way to write 「50／50 碎片或金幣」 is two entries
 * with no weights on them. A weight table of `{ weight: 1 }` rows says a designer balanced these
 * against each other and landed on equal; a bare list says they are equal because nobody has
 * decided otherwise yet. The draw ({@link dailyPrizeFor}) picks uniformly, so 第 2 天 and 第 5 天
 * are 33／33／33 by construction rather than by three numbers that have to keep summing to 100.
 *
 * ## The shape of the week
 *
 *   1, 3, 4, 6   the everyday days: 商品碎片 or 金幣, a coin flip.
 *   2            the small surprise: 功能卡, 抽獎券, or both currencies at once.
 *   5            a whole product — the mid-week peak, and the only day that can pay 史詩.
 *   7            a free turn of the 幸運轉盤 — the round's own ending, and the one prize the
 *                player cannot buy their way to with a single day's luck.
 *
 * Day 5 and day 7 are single-entry lists rather than special cases in the draw. A day is always
 * 「pick one of these」, and a day with one option is simply a day that always gives the same thing.
 */
export const DAILY_PRIZE_PLAN: readonly (readonly DailyPrizeKind[])[] = [
  ['item-fragments', 'coins'],
  ['utility-card', 'raffle-ticket', 'coins-and-fragments'],
  ['item-fragments', 'coins'],
  ['item-fragments', 'coins'],
  ['item'],
  ['item-fragments', 'coins'],
  ['free-spin'],
];

/** Days in one round. Derived from the plan's length rather than a literal 7. */
export const CYCLE_LENGTH = DAILY_PRIZE_PLAN.length;

/**
 * What this day of this round pays — the whole draw, as a pure function of (round, day).
 *
 * ## Seeded, and therefore visible in advance
 *
 * `Math.random()` at claim time would be the obvious reading of 「隨機」 and it breaks two things
 * this feature is built on. The board shows seven cards precisely so the player can see what is
 * coming — a card that cannot say what 第 5 天 is worth until 第 5 天 is a locked door with a
 * number missing — and the claim has to survive being retried, which a re-rolled prize does not:
 * a write whose confirmation was lost would be replayed as a DIFFERENT reward.
 *
 * Seeding on the cycle id makes the week a fixed, unknown-until-you-look thing rather than a
 * re-rollable one: it is the same answer on day 1 as on day 7, it changes on its own when the
 * round turns over, and the server and the browser reach it independently without talking.
 *
 * ## And therefore the same for everybody
 *
 * The seed has no player in it, so every account in the same round sees the same week. That is the
 * deliberate trade and it is the one the rest of the game already makes — the 限時商店's rotation
 * (constants/limitedShopRotation.ts) is seeded the same way for the same reason. Adding the uid
 * would personalise it and would stop the board being previewable from anything that does not have
 * a profile in hand, which is how it is drawn in tmp-daily-login.tsx and in every test.
 */
export function dailyPrizeFor(cycleId: string, day: number): DailyPrize {
  const options = DAILY_PRIZE_PLAN[day - 1] ?? [];
  const kind = seedPick(options, seedFrom(`daily-prize:${cycleId}:${day}`)) ?? 'coins';

  const prize: DailyPrize = {
    kind,
    coins: 0,
    itemFragments: 0,
    tickets: 0,
    cards: 0,
    spins: 0,
    itemRarity: null,
  };

  switch (kind) {
    case 'item-fragments':
      prize.itemFragments = DAILY_PRIZE_FRAGMENTS;
      break;
    case 'coins':
      prize.coins = DAILY_PRIZE_COINS;
      break;
    case 'coins-and-fragments':
      prize.coins = DAILY_PRIZE_COINS;
      prize.itemFragments = DAILY_PRIZE_FRAGMENTS;
      break;
    case 'utility-card':
      prize.cards = DAILY_PRIZE_CARDS;
      break;
    case 'raffle-ticket':
      prize.tickets = DAILY_PRIZE_TICKETS;
      break;
    case 'item':
      // A second seed rather than a second use of the first: reusing one seed for two independent
      // draws correlates them, and here it would mean the tier a day pays was a function of the
      // fact that it pays an item at all — which for a single-option day is a constant.
      prize.itemRarity =
        seedPick(DAILY_PRIZE_ITEM_RARITIES, seedFrom(`daily-rarity:${cycleId}:${day}`)) ?? 'common';
      break;
    case 'free-spin':
      prize.spins = DAILY_PRIZE_SPINS;
      break;
  }

  return prize;
}

/**
 * The one number a card, a claim record and the API's `quantity` field put on a prize.
 *
 * Not every prize HAS one number — 第 2 天's 「金幣＋碎片」 has two — so this reports the headline
 * and the card prints the rest itself. The order below is the order the prize is read in: money
 * first, then the thing that is not money.
 */
export function dailyPrizeHeadline(prize: DailyPrize): number {
  if (prize.coins > 0) return prize.coins;
  if (prize.itemFragments > 0) return prize.itemFragments;
  if (prize.tickets > 0) return prize.tickets;
  if (prize.cards > 0) return prize.cards;
  return prize.spins;
}

/**
 * The 補簽 price, in 金幣.
 *
 * ## It is a PRICE now, not a surcharge — the round stopped paying the currency it charges
 *
 * While a day paid 金幣, a make-up cost `reward + 500` and paid `reward` back, so the player was out
 * exactly the fee: charging more than the day was worth would have been a trap, and charging less
 * than it paid would have made skipping days profitable. A flat fee on top of a wash was the only
 * shape that was neither.
 *
 * A day does not pay a fixed amount any more — four of the seven are a coin flip and three of them
 * pay no currency at all (see {@link DAILY_PRIZE_PLAN}) — so there is no 「reward」 for a fee to sit
 * on top of and nothing to add it to. That makes this a flat PRICE, identical on every day of the
 * round, and {@link makeupCostForDay} does not vary with the day.
 *
 * 500 金幣 against a day worth at most 15 金幣 is deliberately steep, and it has to be: a 補簽 must
 * never be a better deal than turning up, and the day it becomes one is the day the round stops
 * being about turning up. What it buys is not the day's prize — it is 第 7 天, which requires the
 * first six ({@link isGrandPrizeUnlocked}). A player who simply shows up pays nothing at all.
 */
export const MAKEUP_SURCHARGE = 500;

/**
 * 金幣 minted by a day of the round. `day` is 1-based, as it is everywhere the player can see it.
 *
 * This is the ONLY part of a day's prize that moves a wallet, and therefore the only part the
 * server pays. Everything else a day can hand over — 商品碎片, 抽獎券, 功能卡, a product, a free
 * spin — lives in the player's own document and is written by the client after the server has
 * accepted the claim as new (context/useDailyLoginPrize.ts). See src/server/dailyLoginApi.ts.
 */
export function coinsForDay(cycleId: string, day: number): number {
  return dailyPrizeFor(cycleId, day).coins;
}

/**
 * What a 補簽 on that day costs, in 金幣.
 *
 * Flat, and no longer a function of the day — see {@link MAKEUP_SURCHARGE} for why the old
 * `reward + fee` shape stopped making sense once the payout changed currency. The parameter is kept
 * so every call site reads as it did, and so a future ladder-priced make-up is a change here rather
 * than at seven call sites.
 */
export function makeupCostForDay(day: number): number {
  void day;
  return MAKEUP_SURCHARGE;
}

/** Where a player is in the seven-day tiling, and which tile that is. */
export interface CycleWindow {
  /** Stable per round, and what a claim record is filed under: `cycle-YYYY-MM-DD`. */
  cycleId: string;
  /** How many complete rounds have elapsed since the player's anchor. The first round is 0. */
  cycleNumber: number;
  startDate: CivilDate;
  endDate: CivilDate;
  /** Which day of THIS round today is, 1…7. */
  currentDayIndex: number;
}

/**
 * Tiles the calendar into seven-day rounds from the player's anchor and reports the tile they are
 * standing in.
 *
 * Rounds are CALENDAR-driven, not claim-driven: a player who vanishes for five weeks comes back to
 * a fresh round rather than to where they left off, and a player who skips Wednesday finds Thursday
 * is still day 4. That is the honest reading of 「每日」 — counting logins instead would make the
 * round a punch card and would make the countdown in the header a lie, because the header would be
 * promising a day that only arrives when the player next opens the game.
 *
 * A clock rolled back before the anchor cannot produce a negative round: it reports the anchor's own
 * round, day 1, so the worst a wound-back device can do is show the player a day they have already
 * claimed rather than open one they have not earned.
 */
export function resolveCycle(anchor: CivilDate, now: Date = new Date()): CycleWindow {
  const offset = civilDaysBetween(anchor, civilDateAt(now));
  const cycleNumber = offset < 0 ? 0 : Math.floor(offset / CYCLE_LENGTH);
  const startDate = addCivilDays(anchor, cycleNumber * CYCLE_LENGTH);
  return {
    cycleId: `cycle-${startDate}`,
    cycleNumber,
    startDate,
    endDate: addCivilDays(startDate, CYCLE_LENGTH - 1),
    currentDayIndex: offset < 0 ? 1 : (offset % CYCLE_LENGTH) + 1,
  };
}

/**
 * What one card can be:
 *
 *   claimed           已領取 — collected. Terminal: never re-claimable, never buyable.
 *   available         今日可領 — the one card with a primary action. There is never more than one.
 *   makeup_available  已錯過 — passed unclaimed, inside the round the player is still in, so it can
 *                     still be bought back for {@link makeupCostForDay}.
 *   missed            已錯過 — the same day once the round it belongs to is over. Nothing can be
 *                     done with it; it is shown so the round reads as a record rather than a blank.
 *   future            未開放 — not here yet. Previewable, never actionable.
 */
export type SquareState = 'claimed' | 'available' | 'makeup_available' | 'missed' | 'future';

export interface DaySquare {
  /** 1-based, as shown. */
  day: number;
  state: SquareState;
  /** Everything this day is worth. The card, the claim and the API all read it from here. */
  prize: DailyPrize;
  /**
   * The prize's kind, repeated flat.
   *
   * It is what the server's claim document is named after
   * (`{cycleId}__{dayIndex}__{rewardType}`, src/server/dailyLoginApi.ts) and what the wire's
   * `reward_type` carries, so it stays a bare string on the square rather than something a reader
   * has to reach into `prize` for. That path is a uniqueness constraint, which is why it matters
   * that {@link dailyPrizeFor} is deterministic: a kind that changed between two attempts would be
   * a second document, and a second document is a second payout.
   */
  rewardType: DailyPrizeKind;
  /** The tier an `item` day promises, or the kind's own name. Never a catalog id — see DailyPrize. */
  rewardId: string;
  /** {@link dailyPrizeHeadline} — the one number the card leads with. */
  quantity: number;
  /** The all-in 補簽 price, and ONLY on a square that can actually be bought. Null everywhere else. */
  makeupCost: number | null;
}

/**
 * The seven cards, from a round, the days already collected in it, and whether it is the round the
 * player is currently living in.
 *
 * `isCurrentCycle` is what separates 「已錯過（可補簽）」 from 「已錯過」: a past round is a record,
 * and selling a day back inside it would let a player buy a week they never played. Everything a
 * card needs to draw itself is on the square — most importantly `quantity`, which is present in
 * every state including `future`, because the whole point of showing seven cards is that the player
 * can see what is coming.
 */
/**
 * Whether 第 7 天 has been earned: every day under it collected, a 補簽 counting the same as a
 * free claim.
 *
 * This is the rule that makes a 補簽 worth buying, and it was missing for one revision — with day 7
 * opening on its own date regardless, paying for a missed day bought the player nothing at all but
 * a card that said 已領取. A make-up is a real decision: 500 金幣 to keep the round's free 輪盤 turn
 * in reach, which is the player's call rather than a toll.
 *
 * It also gives the grand square something honest to say while it is shut: 「集滿前六天」 is a
 * condition the player can act on, where a bare lock icon on the last day of the round is just a
 * closed door.
 */
export function isGrandPrizeUnlocked(claimedDays: ReadonlySet<number>): boolean {
  for (let day = 1; day < CYCLE_LENGTH; day++) {
    if (!claimedDays.has(day)) return false;
  }
  return true;
}

export function buildSquares(
  cycle: CycleWindow,
  claimedDays: ReadonlySet<number>,
  isCurrentCycle: boolean,
): DaySquare[] {
  return DAILY_PRIZE_PLAN.map((_options, i) => {
    const day = i + 1;
    const prize = dailyPrizeFor(cycle.cycleId, day);
    let state: SquareState;
    if (claimedDays.has(day)) state = 'claimed';
    else if (!isCurrentCycle) state = 'missed';
    else if (day === CYCLE_LENGTH && !isGrandPrizeUnlocked(claimedDays)) state = 'future';
    else if (day === cycle.currentDayIndex) state = 'available';
    else if (day < cycle.currentDayIndex) state = 'makeup_available';
    else state = 'future';

    return {
      day,
      state,
      prize,
      rewardType: prize.kind,
      rewardId: prize.itemRarity ?? prize.kind,
      quantity: dailyPrizeHeadline(prize),
      makeupCost: state === 'makeup_available' ? makeupCostForDay(day) : null,
    };
  });
}

/**
 * Whether a square can be taken by that route — the single gate both the button's disabled state and
 * the write path ask, so a card can never offer something the write would refuse.
 */
export function canClaim(square: DaySquare, mode: 'free' | 'makeup'): boolean {
  return mode === 'free' ? square.state === 'available' : square.state === 'makeup_available';
}
```

## src/constants/dailyLoginPrizes.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 每日登入獎勵 — the half that knows the catalog.
 *
 * constants/dailyLogin.ts decides what each day is WORTH ({@link DailyPrize}: 10 商品碎片, 15 金幣,
 * one 功能卡, a 史詩 product…) and deliberately cannot say WHICH product or WHICH card, because it
 * is imported by the Express server and must not drag a few hundred item definitions across with
 * it. This file answers the second question, from the SAME seed, so the two halves agree without
 * either one importing the other's dependencies.
 *
 * Everything here is a pure function of `(cycleId, day)` and the player's own inventory. Nothing
 * writes; the write is context/useDailyLoginPrize.ts.
 *
 * ## Why the pools are rules and not lists
 *
 * Same reason as everywhere else in this game (constants/rewardPools.ts): adding a 稀有 lamp to the
 * shop should put it on 第 5 天 with no edit here, and grading something 神話 should take it off.
 * There is not one item id in this file.
 */

import { getItemById, type ItemDefinition } from './items';
import { FRAGMENT_ITEMS } from './fragments';
import { RARITY_SPECS, type Rarity } from './rarity';
import { drawReward, type RewardPool } from './rewardPools';
import { seedFrom, seedPick } from './seed';
import { ALL_UTILITY_CARDS, type UtilityCardId } from './utilityCards';
import { dailyPrizeFor, type DailyPrize, type DailyPrizeKind } from './dailyLogin';

/**
 * The tiers a 碎片 day may collect toward.
 *
 * 普通 and 稀有 only, as briefed, and the restriction is doing real work rather than decorating the
 * table: 10 碎片 is a twentieth of an unlock, so a 史詩 or 神話 piece would take twenty fragment
 * days — most of three rounds — to reach through this route alone. A bar that cannot move is worse
 * than no bar, and 第 5 天 is where the round hands the expensive tiers over outright instead.
 */
export const DAILY_FRAGMENT_RARITIES: readonly Rarity[] = ['common', 'rare'];

/**
 * Every product a 碎片 day can land on: has a fragment of its own, and is 普通 or 稀有.
 *
 * Derived from {@link FRAGMENT_ITEMS}, which is already 「everything the ordinary shop sells that
 * has a fragment」 — so the 經驗值 unlocks, the 0-price 毛胚屋, the 抽獎券 bundles and the 限時商店
 * exclusives are all excluded before this filter ever runs. Computed once: the catalog is a
 * module-level constant and re-filtering it per render would be re-deriving the same list all day.
 */
export const DAILY_FRAGMENT_POOL: readonly ItemDefinition[] = FRAGMENT_ITEMS.filter((item) =>
  DAILY_FRAGMENT_RARITIES.includes(item.rarity),
);

/**
 * Which product THIS day's 商品碎片 are for.
 *
 * One item per DAY now, not one per round. The old round picked a single 主打商品 and paid a ladder
 * of fragments toward it, on the argument that seven scattered stacks are each a tenth of the way
 * to nothing. That argument was right about the old round and does not survive this one: at most
 * four days of a round pay fragments at all, and they pay 10 each — so 「本輪主打」 would have meant
 * 40 fragments toward one item, a fifth of an unlock, which is not a week's worth of anything
 * either. What a per-day roll buys instead is variety, and the stack a player actually wants to
 * finish is the one 運動 tops up (constants/fragments.ts's `rollWorkoutFragmentItem`, which is
 * deliberately weighted toward a stack already started).
 *
 * Seeded on the round AND the day, so a card can show the item before the day arrives and the
 * payout lands on the one that was shown.
 */
export function dailyFragmentItem(cycleId: string, day: number): ItemDefinition | null {
  return seedPick(DAILY_FRAGMENT_POOL, seedFrom(`daily-fragment-item:${cycleId}:${day}`));
}

/**
 * 第 5 天的商品池, pinned to exactly one tier.
 *
 * Floor and ceiling on the same rung for the reason the wheel's outfit pools are
 * (constants/luckyWheel.ts): the card says 史詩商品, so it must not be able to pay 普通 — a promise
 * broken downward — or 神話, which would quietly make 神話 something a login can hand out.
 *
 * No category restriction and no price bounds. 「商品」 in the brief means a product, not a
 * wearable: a sofa, a pet accessory and a hat are all things the shop sells and all things this day
 * may give. Price is deliberately not bounded either — this game grades by rarity and the catalog is
 * laid out to disprove 「貴的就是稀有的」, so a price ceiling here would quietly re-introduce it.
 */
export function dailyItemPool(rarity: Rarity): RewardPool {
  return {
    id: `daily-login-item-${rarity}`,
    label: `每日登入：${RARITY_SPECS[rarity].label}商品`,
    categories: [],
    maxPrice: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER,
    minPrice: 1,
    maxRarity: rarity,
    minRarity: rarity,
    allowXpUnlock: false,
    // A duplicate own-once wearable is a no-op in the inventory (utils/inventory.ts), so a repeat
    // pick would read to the player as having been handed nothing at all on the one day of the
    // round that gives a whole product.
    preferUnowned: true,
  };
}

/**
 * The product 第 5 天 actually hands over.
 *
 * Takes the owned ids rather than a profile so it stays pure, and because `preferUnowned` is the
 * one part of this that is not a function of the seed alone — the same round shows a different item
 * to a player who has bought half the shop, which is correct and is why the CARD shows the tier
 * rather than the item (see DailyLoginPanel). A board that named the item would be promising
 * something that changes when the player goes shopping.
 */
export function dailyPrizeItem(
  cycleId: string,
  day: number,
  rarity: Rarity,
  ownedItemIds: readonly string[],
): ItemDefinition | null {
  const draw = drawReward(dailyItemPool(rarity), ownedItemIds, seedFrom(`daily-item:${cycleId}:${day}`));
  return draw.ok ? draw.item : null;
}

/**
 * Which 功能卡 第 2 天 hands over.
 *
 * Drawn from the cards that declare 每日登入 as a channel, so a second card ships by adding
 * `'daily-login'` to its own `channels` rather than by editing this file. There is one card today
 * (雙倍金幣券) and the draw is therefore a formality — which is exactly the state in which it is
 * cheap to write it correctly.
 */
export function dailyPrizeCard(cycleId: string, day: number): UtilityCardId | null {
  const pool = ALL_UTILITY_CARDS.filter((card) => card.channels.includes('daily-login'));
  return seedPick(pool, seedFrom(`daily-card:${cycleId}:${day}`))?.id ?? null;
}

/**
 * One day's prize with every blank filled in — the shape the card draws and the write path pays.
 *
 * `prize` is the amounts (from constants/dailyLogin.ts) and the three ids are this file's answer to
 * 「哪一個」. An id is null when that kind of thing is not part of this day, and ALSO when the pool
 * that should have supplied it came back empty — a catalog with no 史詩 product, say. The write
 * path treats those the same way and simply pays what it can: a prize that cannot be granted must
 * never fail a claim, because the claim is the thing that marks the day off.
 */
export interface ResolvedDailyPrize {
  prize: DailyPrize;
  /** The product this day's 商品碎片 belong to. */
  fragmentItemId: string | null;
  /** The product this day hands over outright. */
  itemId: string | null;
  /** The 功能卡 this day hands over. */
  cardId: UtilityCardId | null;
}

export function resolveDailyPrize(
  cycleId: string,
  day: number,
  ownedItemIds: readonly string[],
): ResolvedDailyPrize {
  const prize = dailyPrizeFor(cycleId, day);
  return {
    prize,
    fragmentItemId: prize.itemFragments > 0 ? dailyFragmentItem(cycleId, day)?.id ?? null : null,
    itemId:
      prize.itemRarity !== null
        ? dailyPrizeItem(cycleId, day, prize.itemRarity, ownedItemIds)?.id ?? null
        : null,
    cardId: prize.cards > 0 ? dailyPrizeCard(cycleId, day) : null,
  };
}

/**
 * What a claim ACTUALLY banked, as opposed to what the day promised.
 *
 * The two differ often enough that reporting the promise would be a lie in the ordinary case, not
 * just the edge one: a 碎片 stack already at 200 keeps none of its 10 and pays 抽獎券 instead, and
 * a 功能卡 the player is already carrying the maximum of cannot be added at all. The reveal
 * announces THIS, never the prize, for the same reason the old one read its number off the write
 * rather than off the ladder.
 */
export interface DailyPrizeAward {
  kind: DailyPrizeKind;
  /**
   * Whether the write that hands all of this over actually landed.
   *
   * False is a REAL state and not a defensive nicety: the prize write touches keys that
   * firestore.rules has to name (`freeWheelSpins` is the newest of them), and a rules file that has
   * not been deployed yet refuses the whole update — see docs/FIRESTORE_RULES.md. The claim itself
   * still stands in that case, because it is a different write, so the day is marked off and the
   * player is owed something they did not get.
   *
   * Everything below describes what the day WAS worth either way. The reveal reads this flag to
   * decide whether it may say 「已入袋」, because announcing a grant that was refused is the one
   * thing a celebration must never do.
   */
  saved: boolean;
  /** 金幣 banked. Paid by the server, or by the offline claim path — never by the prize write. */
  coins: number;
  /** The product the 商品碎片 went to, if any. */
  fragmentItemId: string | null;
  /** How many of them stayed on the item. */
  fragmentsKept: number;
  /** How many had nowhere to go, because the stack was full. */
  fragmentsOverflow: number;
  /** 抽獎券 minted by that overflow, on top of {@link tickets}. */
  ticketsFromOverflow: number;
  /** 抽獎券 the day itself paid. */
  tickets: number;
  cardId: UtilityCardId | null;
  /** Copies that fit under the card's own cap. 0 means the bag was already full. */
  cardsGranted: number;
  /** The product handed over, or null when the pool had nothing to give. */
  itemId: string | null;
  /** Free 輪盤 turns banked. */
  spins: number;
}

/** An award that granted nothing — what a claim reports before the prize write has run. */
export function emptyAward(kind: DailyPrizeKind): DailyPrizeAward {
  return {
    kind,
    saved: true,
    coins: 0,
    fragmentItemId: null,
    fragmentsKept: 0,
    fragmentsOverflow: 0,
    ticketsFromOverflow: 0,
    tickets: 0,
    cardId: null,
    cardsGranted: 0,
    itemId: null,
    spins: 0,
  };
}

/** The product behind an award, for whatever wants to draw its artwork. Null once retired. */
export function awardItem(itemId: string | null): ItemDefinition | null {
  return itemId ? getItemById(itemId) ?? null : null;
}
```

## src/constants/distribution.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * Distribution Channel — 「這件東西是什麼」 and 「這件東西從哪裡拿到」 are two different questions.
 *
 * The catalog (constants/items.ts) answers the first one: a name, a category, a price, a tier, a
 * placement rule. It used to answer the second one too, by accident — an item existed, therefore
 * the 商店 sold it, because the shop was `ALL_ITEMS.filter(byCategory)`. That is the coupling this
 * file removes.
 *
 * An item now declares the channels it is DISTRIBUTED through ({@link ItemDefinition.availableIn}),
 * and each storefront builds its shelf from the channel it owns rather than from the whole catalog:
 *
 *   ALL_ITEMS            every item that exists — the definitions. Ownership, the wardrobe, the
 *                        avatar and every save-repair path read this, because 「我擁有的東西」 has
 *                        nothing to do with where it was bought.
 *   MAIN_SHOP_CATALOG    what the ordinary 商店 sells.
 *   LIMITED_SHOP_ITEMS   what the 限時商店 may put on its shelf.
 *
 * ## Why this is a channel list and not a boolean
 *
 * Because an item can legitimately have more than one source, and already does: a 特殊飾品 is sold
 * in the 限時商店 for 碎片, can drop from the 輪盤, and can be unlocked by collecting its own
 * 商品碎片. Those are three channels for one definition, and 「限時商店限定」 is a statement about
 * one of them rather than about the item. A boolean (`limitedOnly`) would have to be re-interpreted
 * by every system that hands anything out; a list can simply be asked.
 *
 * ## Adding a channel
 *
 * A member of {@link DistributionChannel}, a label, and ONE reader — the surface that owns it. What
 * must not happen is a channel nothing reads: an item tagged `event-shop` with no 活動商店 to sell
 * it is an item that has quietly left the game. That is why the union below is exactly the channels
 * that exist today, and why 活動商店 / 任務獎勵 are named here in prose rather than pre-declared.
 */

import type { ItemDefinition } from './items';
import { ALL_ITEMS } from './items';

/**
 * Where an item can be obtained.
 *
 *   `main-shop`     the permanent 商店 (components/ShopView.tsx). Bought with 金幣, always there.
 *   `limited-shop`  the rotating 限時商店 (components/LimitedShopView.tsx). Only on the shelf while
 *                   a rotation lists it, and never sold by the ordinary shop.
 *   `reward`        handed out rather than sold — 輪盤 prizes, 商品碎片 unlocks, 每日登入, 新手禮.
 *                   Those systems each own an eligibility spec (constants/rewardPools.ts) and this
 *                   is the item's half of that contract: 「我可以被當成獎勵發出去」.
 */
export type DistributionChannel = 'main-shop' | 'limited-shop' | 'reward';

export const DISTRIBUTION_CHANNELS: readonly DistributionChannel[] = [
  'main-shop',
  'limited-shop',
  'reward',
];

/** What a channel is called, for admin readouts and for the 「哪裡買得到」 line on a card. */
export const CHANNEL_LABELS: Record<DistributionChannel, string> = {
  'main-shop': '商店',
  'limited-shop': '限時商店',
  reward: '獎勵',
};

/**
 * What an item declaring nothing is distributed through.
 *
 * `main-shop` plus `reward`, which is what the catalog meant for its entire life before this file
 * existed: an ordinary item is on the ordinary shelf and may also be given away. Making the default
 * explicit is what keeps ~180 catalog rows from having to grow a field to stay where they are —
 * only an item that is NOT ordinary says so.
 */
export const DEFAULT_CHANNELS: readonly DistributionChannel[] = ['main-shop', 'reward'];

/** The channels this item is distributed through. Never reads a category, a price or an id. */
export function itemChannels(
  item: ItemDefinition | null | undefined,
): readonly DistributionChannel[] {
  if (!item) return [];
  return item.availableIn ?? DEFAULT_CHANNELS;
}

/** Whether this item may be obtained through `channel`. The one question every storefront asks. */
export function isInChannel(
  item: ItemDefinition | null | undefined,
  channel: DistributionChannel,
): boolean {
  return itemChannels(item).includes(channel);
}

/** Every item in a channel, in catalog order. */
export function itemsInChannel(channel: DistributionChannel): ItemDefinition[] {
  return ALL_ITEMS.filter((item) => isInChannel(item, channel));
}

/**
 * What the ordinary 商店 sells.
 *
 * Computed once, at module load, for the same reason `FRAGMENT_ITEMS` is: `ALL_ITEMS` is a
 * module-level constant, and re-filtering ~180 rows on every shelf change is re-deriving a list
 * that cannot have changed. Every main-shop surface — the catalog grid, the collection drawer's
 * category counts, the build rail, the furniture drawer — reads THIS, so 「普通商店賣什麼」 has
 * exactly one answer and a limited-shop exclusive cannot leak into one of them by being forgotten.
 */
export const MAIN_SHOP_CATALOG: readonly ItemDefinition[] = ALL_ITEMS.filter((item) =>
  isInChannel(item, 'main-shop'),
);

/**
 * The items the 限時商店 is allowed to put on its shelf.
 *
 * Being in this list does NOT mean an item is on sale — that is a rotation (constants/
 * limitedShopRotation.ts), and it is also not enough on its own: an item still needs a row in the
 * shop's own pool (constants/limitedShop.ts) to say what it costs there. This is the eligibility
 * half, and it is what `npm run test:limited-shop` checks the pool against, so a pool row for an
 * item the catalog does not consider limited is a failing test rather than a silent inconsistency.
 */
export const LIMITED_SHOP_ITEMS: readonly ItemDefinition[] = ALL_ITEMS.filter((item) =>
  isInChannel(item, 'limited-shop'),
);

/** Ids of everything the ordinary shop sells. For O(1) guards on a purchase write. */
const MAIN_SHOP_IDS = new Set(MAIN_SHOP_CATALOG.map((item) => item.id));

/**
 * Whether the ordinary shop may sell this id. Asked at the WRITE (context/useShopActions.ts) as
 * well as in the UI, so no surface can buy a limited exclusive by holding a stale card.
 */
export function isMainShopItem(itemId: string | null | undefined): boolean {
  return !!itemId && MAIN_SHOP_IDS.has(itemId);
}
```
