## src/constants/rarity.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import type { CSSProperties } from 'react';

/**
 * 稀有度 — how special an item is, said in colour instead of in words.
 *
 * Deliberately wordless. Every card already carries a name, a category chip, a stock badge and a
 * price, and a 「神話」 tag would be a fifth line of text competing with those for the same glance.
 * What games actually train players to read is the *frame*: a card lit a different colour is
 * understood as rarer before a single word is parsed, and it keeps working at thumbnail size and
 * in a language the player doesn't read. So the whole ladder below is a palette, and no surface
 * renders {@link RaritySpec.label} — it exists for code, comments and the aura's `aria-label`,
 * which is the one place the tier has to be spelled out (hue alone tells a colour-blind or
 * screen-reader player nothing).
 *
 * ## Four rungs, down from six (2026-08-28)
 *
 * The ladder shipped as six — 普通／優秀／稀有／史詩／傳說／神話 — and has been cut to the four a
 * player can actually name at a glance:
 *
 *   普通 白 · 稀有 綠 · 史詩 紫 · 神話 紅
 *
 * The two rungs that went were the two that were only ever legible NEXT TO their neighbour.
 * 優秀's leaf green and 稀有's sea blue were two different 「比普通好一點」 signals, and 傳說's
 * amber and 神話's magenta were two different 「店裡最好的東西」 signals; asked to rank a shelf, a
 * player tells white from green from purple from red instantly, and cannot tell green from blue
 * without putting the two cards side by side. A rung that only reads in a comparison is not a
 * rung, it is a shade.
 *
 * Both merges went DOWNWARDS, which is the only direction that keeps the two rules below true:
 *
 *  - **優秀 → 普通.** Merging it upwards into 稀有 would have made 稀有 the biggest tier in the
 *    game (95 items against 普通's 84) — the ladder inverted, and 「稀有」 turned into the word for
 *    the commonest thing on the shelf.
 *  - **傳說 → 史詩.** Merging it upwards would have put four items in 神話, and 神話 is capped at
 *    one. 傳說's own layer — the slow highlight crawling along the bezel — moved down with its
 *    items, so 史詩 inherited the treatment as well as the stock.
 *
 * The colours are inherited rather than reinvented: 稀有 wears the green that was tuned for 優秀
 * (and keeps its 「never a green that leans cyan」 rule — see below), 史詩 keeps its violet
 * untouched, and only two swatches are new — 普通's near-white and 神話's red.
 *
 * ## EVERY item has a tier. There is no untagged item (2026-08-25)
 *
 * `rarity` is REQUIRED on {@link ItemDefinition}. Two things follow, and both are the point:
 *
 *  - **The ladder is complete.** Every shelf is graded, so every shelf shows adjacent rungs, so
 *    the colour ladder can be READ rather than merely asserted.
 *  - **A missing tier is a compile error**, not a card that quietly renders plain. That is the
 *    whole reason the field is required rather than defaulted: a default would let an item ship
 *    ungraded and look deliberate.
 *
 * ## What has NOT changed: a high tier is still rare, and it is still rare BY COUNT
 *
 * Universal grading is not universal decoration. What keeps 神話 worth anything is the same thing
 * that always did — the SHAPE of the distribution and the {@link RarityLayers} budget:
 *
 *   普通 ~73%   稀有 ~19%   史詩 ~8%   神話 1 item
 *
 * 普通 draws a plate in a ring and nothing else — no rays, no sparkles, no sweep — so a shelf of
 * 普通 cards looks almost exactly like the plain card it replaced. Absorbing 優秀 made it the great
 * majority of the catalog, and that is the correct shape for a floor: it is the thing the three
 * rungs above it are measured against. The hard rules on the top of the ladder survive verbatim:
 *
 *  - **`mythic` is ≤ 1 item in the entire game.** It is 鳳凰 (`pet-bird-phoenix`). Tagging a
 *    second thing 神話 does not make two special items, it makes the tier meaningless — one of the
 *    two has to come down to 史詩 instead.
 *  - **`epic` stays scarce** — under ~12% of the catalog — and is spent on items that change what
 *    the player can DO or how the world looks, never on "the expensive one".
 *  - **Never derive a tier** from a price threshold, an id prefix or a category. Price and rarity
 *    are separate properties of an item: a 1,050g torch is 普通 and a 400g 部落面具 is 史詩, and
 *    the catalog is laid out so that rule can be read off it rather than only asserted here.
 *
 * `npm run audit:catalog` is the guard. It fails the build if any item is missing a tier, if
 * `mythic` is used more than once, if `epic` outgrows its share, or if the distribution inverts
 * (a rarer tier outnumbering the one below it).
 *
 * Adding a tier to an item is one `rarity:` field in constants/items.ts. Nothing else in the app
 * may re-derive rarity from a price threshold, an id prefix or a category.
 */

/**
 * The ladder, rarest last.
 *
 * Four rungs, and the ladder is legible on two axes at once: the hue changes (white → green →
 * violet → red) AND the *amount of treatment* climbs with it — see {@link RaritySpec.layers}.
 * Four tiers all painted with five layers would be four colours, not four grades.
 */
export type Rarity = 'common' | 'rare' | 'epic' | 'mythic';

/**
 * The same four rungs as an ORDER, so 「這個比那個稀有嗎」 is a comparison rather than a
 * hand-written chain of `||`s.
 *
 * The union above already spells the ladder out, but a type cannot be read at runtime, and
 * `Object.keys(RARITY_SPECS)` is insertion order — true today and silently wrong the first time
 * somebody re-sorts that literal. Anything that needs to RANK tiers (a reward pool's ceiling, a
 * sort, a filter) reads this instead.
 */
export const RARITY_LADDER: readonly Rarity[] = ['common', 'rare', 'epic', 'mythic'];

/**
 * Where a tier sits on the ladder, 0-based. Higher is rarer, so 「這個比那個稀有嗎」 is `>`.
 *
 * Still tolerant of `null`/`undefined`, which now answers -1 — BELOW 普通 rather than equal to it.
 * No catalog item can be in that state any more (the field is required), but a REWARD POOL can:
 * a pool whose floor is 「不設下限」 passes `null`, and a pool whose ceiling is 「不設上限」 does
 * too. Answering -1 keeps `rank(item) >= rank(null)` true for every real item, which is what makes
 * an unset bound mean "no bound" rather than "exclude everything".
 */
export function rarityRank(rarity: Rarity | null | undefined): number {
  return rarity ? RARITY_LADDER.indexOf(rarity) : -1;
}

/**
 * The floor of the ladder, and the tier a catalog entry gets when nobody has thought about it yet.
 *
 * Exported so a generated catalog (constants/artwork.ts, constants/houseStyles.ts) can be explicit
 * about grading a piece as ordinary rather than silently omitting the field — the field is required
 * now, so "I have not decided" has to be SAID.
 */
export const DEFAULT_RARITY: Rarity = 'common';

/**
 * One tier's palette.
 *
 * Note which way round the contrast runs. Most games light their rarity frames the other way —
 * pale rays and white sparkles over a deep, saturated card — because their catalogs are dark. This
 * shop's cards are cream (`island-cream-2`), so a pale sparkle over pale cream would be invisible.
 * The fix is to tint the *field* the item sits on until it is saturated enough to carry light marks,
 * and then draw the rays and sparkles in white. Hence a pair of field tones rather than one accent:
 * the well is the light source, and everything else reads against it.
 *
 * ## Why these are only four values
 *
 * A tier is a *material*, not a colour scheme — see DESIGN_SYSTEM.md's 稀有度 section and the
 * "change the construction, not the colour" section it follows. The bezel's metal ramp, the plate's
 * recess, the sunray grain and the corner vignette are all built from white and navy alphas laid
 * over these four values, so they are identical for every tier and a new tier never has to hand-tune
 * eight more hexes to look like the same object in a different stone.
 */
export interface RaritySpec {
  /** Tier name. Never rendered as visible text — see the file doc. */
  label: string;
  /**
   * The metal the bezel is made of, and the card's border.
   *
   * Deliberately deeper than the field it surrounds: the bezel's light-to-dark ramp is white and
   * black alphas laid over this one value, and a pale base leaves the "lit" and "shadowed" halves
   * of the ring too close together to read as a turned edge at all. 普通 is the one tier that
   * breaks this on purpose — see its entry.
   */
  edge: string;
  /** Translucent outer glow around the whole card, so the tier reads before the card is looked at. */
  halo: string;
  /** The plate at its top corners — barely off cream, so the card still sits in the palette. */
  fieldTop: string;
  /**
   * The plate under the item, where the light pools and the pet appears to stand.
   *
   * Kept a jewel tone rather than a pastel. The distance between this and {@link fieldTop} is the
   * plate's whole sense of depth: a candy-light core makes a flat sticker, and flatness is the
   * thing that reads as cheap.
   */
  fieldCore: string;
  /** Rays and sparkles. White, because {@link fieldCore} is what carries them — see above. */
  shine: string;
  /** How much of the treatment this tier is allowed to draw — see {@link RarityLayers}. */
  layers: RarityLayers;
}

/**
 * The layer budget: which of the aura's layers a tier may draw at all.
 *
 * This table *is* the ladder. Colour alone cannot carry it — asked to rank four equally busy cards
 * by hue, a player ranks nothing and just picks a favourite colour. What reads as a grade is how
 * much is happening: 普通 is a plate in a ring and nothing else, and each rung afterwards earns
 * more. It is also why the top of the ladder is worth anything — if every card sparkles, sparkling
 * is the baseline.
 *
 * Note what does NOT change with tier: the rays keep their 60-line density and the sparkles keep
 * their size at every rung. Making a high tier louder by thickening the same layer is the gacha
 * failure DESIGN_SYSTEM.md records; a high tier is louder by having *more layers*, not fatter ones.
 */
export interface RarityLayers {
  /**
   * Sunray grain opacity multiplier: 0 draws no rays at all, 1 is the standard grain.
   *
   * 0.5 is the half-strength pass (`.rarity-rays-half` in index.css). No tier spends it since the
   * ladder came down to four — it belonged to 優秀, the rung that used to sit between 普通 and
   * 稀有 — and both the value and the stylesheet rule are kept because it is the correct treatment
   * for a rung inserted there later: half of the same grain, never a coarser grain of its own.
   */
  rays: 0 | 0.5 | 1;
  /** How many of RarityAura's six sparkle positions to light, in order. */
  sparks: number;
  /** The slow specular pass across the glaze. */
  shine: boolean;
  /** 史詩 and above: a second, much slower highlight travelling along the bezel. */
  metal: boolean;
  /** 神話 only: the slow hue drift on the bezel. The one animated hue in the game. */
  iris: boolean;
}

export const RARITY_SPECS: Record<Rarity, RaritySpec> = {
  // 普通 — white, and the floor the whole ladder is measured from. Roughly 73% of the catalog now
  // that it has absorbed 優秀.
  //
  // Near-white rather than the old limestone grey (#9AA5B1): with three saturated rungs above it,
  // the floor's job is to be the ABSENCE of a colour rather than a colour of its own, and a grey
  // frame on a white card still reads as a decision somebody made. This is the one entry that
  // breaks the "edge deeper than the field" rule in {@link RaritySpec.edge}, and it can, because
  // the layer budget below is empty: there is no lit-and-shadowed bezel ramp to read here, no
  // rays, no sparkles, no sweep. What is left is a hairline a shade cooler than `island-line`
  // (#E1DED4) — exactly as much as this tier should say.
  common: {
    label: '普通',
    edge: '#C6CCD3',
    halo: 'rgba(120, 132, 146, 0.12)',
    fieldTop: '#FCFCFD',
    fieldCore: '#EAEEF2',
    shine: '#FFFFFF',
    layers: { rays: 0, sparks: 0, shine: false, metal: false, iris: false },
  },
  // 稀有 — leaf green at hue ~95°, inherited whole from 優秀 when the ladder came down to four.
  //
  // Deliberately NOT any green that leans cyan. `island-teal` (#2A9D8F, ~173°) means "selected"
  // everywhere else in the app, so a teal-ish green frame would be read as "the card I just
  // tapped" rather than as a grade. 78° of separation is what buys that distinction; verify it by
  // putting this card next to a selected one, not on its own.
  //
  // This rung, and not the sea blue it replaced, is why the merge went the way it did: green is a
  // colour a player reads as 「一階之上」 with no neighbour to compare it to, and blue on a cream
  // card was never much more than a slightly cooler white.
  rare: {
    label: '稀有',
    edge: '#6FA24B',
    halo: 'rgba(74, 124, 15, 0.22)',
    fieldTop: '#EDF6E4',
    fieldCore: '#BCDCA0',
    shine: '#FFFFFF',
    layers: { rays: 1, sparks: 2, shine: true, metal: false, iris: false },
  },
  // 史詩 — violet. The one hue in the ladder that appears nowhere else in the game's chrome, so it
  // can never be mistaken for a selected state (teal), a warning (coral) or a price (gold).
  //
  // Unchanged in colour, promoted in treatment: it took 傳說's `metal` layer along with 傳說's
  // items when the two merged. That matters more than it sounds — 史詩 is now the rung directly
  // below 神話, and a second-from-top drawing exactly what the middle draws leaves the ladder with
  // one big step at the top and none in the middle.
  epic: {
    label: '史詩',
    edge: '#8B62C4',
    halo: 'rgba(107, 63, 160, 0.28)',
    fieldTop: '#EFE7FA',
    fieldCore: '#BFA0E4',
    shine: '#FFFFFF',
    layers: { rays: 1, sparks: 4, shine: true, metal: true, iris: false },
  },
  // 神話 — red, and cut deliberately as a CRIMSON red (~357°) rather than a warm one.
  //
  // The tier used to be magenta at ~332°, and the note here used to explain at length why it was
  // not red: `island-coral` (#E8836A, ~13°) means 危險/刪除, and the top of a rarity ladder must
  // never be readable as a warning. That constraint has not gone away — the answer to it moved
  // from the hue to the VALUE. Coral is a pale, desaturated salmon on a white surface (66%
  // lightness); this is a deep saturated crimson (45%), so the two never read as the same material
  // even though they sit 16° apart on the wheel.
  //
  // The other half of the answer is that this tier's real identity is a colour that MOVES
  // (`layers.iris`), and that drift now runs the other way: `@keyframes rarity-iris` in index.css
  // rotates NEGATIVE, so the bezel travels red → crimson → magenta, back toward the swatch this
  // tier used to be. Rotating positive from here would walk it through coral and land it on
  // `island-gold` (~40°), the 金幣 colour — the one thing worse than a top tier that reads as
  // danger is a top tier that reads as a price.
  //
  // Verify it beside a delete-confirmation, not beside the other tiers.
  mythic: {
    label: '神話',
    edge: '#C2262E',
    halo: 'rgba(170, 28, 34, 0.32)',
    fieldTop: '#FCE8E7',
    fieldCore: '#E9868A',
    shine: '#FFFFFF',
    layers: { rays: 1, sparks: 6, shine: true, metal: false, iris: true },
  },
};

/**
 * The tier's palette as the custom properties `index.css`'s `.rarity-*` rules read.
 *
 * The colours live here and the shapes/animations live in the stylesheet, so re-tuning a tier is
 * a hex edit in this file and never a second copy of the gradient maths.
 */
export function rarityStyleVars(rarity: Rarity): CSSProperties {
  const spec = RARITY_SPECS[rarity];
  return {
    '--rarity-edge': spec.edge,
    '--rarity-halo': spec.halo,
    '--rarity-field-top': spec.fieldTop,
    '--rarity-field-core': spec.fieldCore,
    '--rarity-shine': spec.shine,
  } as CSSProperties;
}
```

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { Rarity, RARITY_SPECS } from './rarity';
import { SoundEffect } from '../lib/soundUtils';

/**
 * 購買回饋 — what a purchase feels like, per 稀有度.
 *
 * The companion table to constants/rarity.ts: that one grades how a card LOOKS on the shelf, this
 * one grades what happens when it is bought. Same principle behind both — the tier is expressed by
 * how much is spent, not by a different colour of the same amount — and the same shape of file:
 * data here, behaviour in the component (components/UI/PurchaseDialog.tsx reads a row and plays
 * it; nothing in it branches on a tier name). Adding a tier is a row.
 *
 * ## Why the bottom of this table has to stay boring
 *
 * Before this, every purchase in the game fired the same two confetti bursts, so buying the 史詩
 * 柴犬 you trained 100 XP for celebrated exactly as hard as buying a 200g floor tile. Grading it
 * only works if the low rungs are genuinely quiet: 普通 keeps ONE burst and the plainest sound in
 * the set, and it is that restraint the 神話 fanfare is spending. A game that throws fireworks at
 * every transaction has no fireworks left.
 *
 * That is a deliberate reversal of DESIGN_SYSTEM.md's "nothing pops and nothing hurries", which
 * still governs everything on the shelf — the reveal is the one sanctioned exception.
 *
 * The reveal's threshold is 史詩, which on a four-rung ladder means 「the top two tiers」. It used
 * to sit one rung higher, back when nothing in the game was tagged above 史詩 and so the loudest
 * thing a player could actually reach was the middle of the ladder. Moving it down is what put the
 * game's only earned companion (柴犬, 100 XP) on the same footing as its most expensive one.
 *
 * ## What the four-rung ladder did to this table (2026-08-28)
 *
 * Two rows went with the two tiers that went (constants/rarity.ts): 優秀's — which was the exact
 * celebration EVERY purchase in the game used to fire, before any of this was graded — and 傳說's
 * ribbons-and-fanfare. Their items landed on the rows below them, so what changed is the
 * denominator and not the shape: 史詩 and above is 17 items out of 196, so **~8.7% of purchases
 * get a reveal, and ~91% do not.**
 *
 * That is still the right shape, and it is the number to watch. The restraint at the bottom is
 * what the celebration at the top is spending, and 普通 — three quarters of the catalog now — is
 * by a long way the commonest purchase in the game. If its row ever grows a second burst
 * 「because most purchases feel flat」, the fireworks stop meaning anything the same week; the fix
 * for a flat 普通 purchase is never a louder 普通, it is checking that the item was graded
 * honestly.
 *
 * The one row that could have been re-cut and was not is 史詩. It absorbed 傳說's items and 傳說's
 * *visual* layer (the bezel highlight — see rarity.ts), and it deliberately did NOT absorb 傳說's
 * fanfare or its ribbons: with four rungs there are exactly two reveal tiers left, and the whole
 * job of the lower one is to make the upper one feel like more. 史詩 is a reveal; 神話 is a reveal
 * that the room joins in with.
 */

/** One confetti call: a subset of canvas-confetti's options plus when to fire it. */
export interface ConfettiBurst {
  /** Milliseconds after the celebration starts. Staggering is what makes it unfurl, not pop. */
  delay: number;
  particleCount: number;
  spread: number;
  colors: string[];
  /** canvas-confetti measures a particle's life in ticks, NOT in CSS duration. 110 is standard. */
  ticks: number;
  startVelocity?: number;
  origin?: { x: number; y: number };
  angle?: number;
  /**
   * Draw the particles as tall thin streamers (紙彩帶) instead of the default dots and squares.
   * The shape itself is built in the component with `confetti.shapeFromPath`, because a Path2D
   * cannot be a module constant — it needs a canvas context that exists at call time.
   */
  ribbon?: boolean;
}

/** One sound in a tier's cue, scheduled relative to the celebration's start. */
export interface FxSound {
  effect: SoundEffect;
  delayMs: number;
  volume: number;
}

export interface RarityFxSpec {
  /**
   * Haptic pulses, played in order `hapticGapMs` apart. A list rather than a single strength
   * because the top two tiers are recognisable by their RHYTHM through a pocket — one thud is a
   * confirmation, three is an event, and neither needs the phone to buzz harder.
   */
  haptic: Array<'light' | 'medium' | 'heavy' | 'double'>;
  hapticGapMs: number;
  /**
   * When the first pulse fires, in ms after the celebration starts. Defaults to 0.
   *
   * Non-zero only on the reveal tiers, and it is the same argument as their confetti delays: the
   * item does not arrive until ~1.5s in, so a thud on the button press would be acknowledging the
   * tap rather than the thing appearing. PurchaseDialog already fires its own `light` haptic on the
   * press, so the phone is not silent in between.
   */
  hapticDelayMs?: number;
  sounds: FxSound[];
  confetti: ConfettiBurst[];
  /** 史詩 and above: the full-screen reveal (components/UI/RarityReveal.tsx). */
  reveal: boolean;
  /**
   * How many full turns the item makes on its way in. Reveal tiers only.
   *
   * The one part of the choreography that grades. Every reveal tier settles at the same instant
   * ({@link REVEAL_SETTLE_MS}), so a rarer item does not keep the player waiting longer — it spins
   * FASTER through the same window, which is the difference between "this is worth more" and "this
   * takes more of your time". Grading the duration instead was the obvious first idea and it makes
   * the best item in the game the most tedious one to buy.
   */
  revealTurns: number;
  /** 神話 only: ±4px screen shake under the reveal. */
  shake: boolean;
  /**
   * How long the dialog stays open after a successful purchase, in ms.
   *
   * `null` means "do not use a timer at all" — the reveal tiers close when the reveal reports
   * that it has finished. The old code closed on a flat 1200ms, which for a 2.2-second reveal
   * meant the dialog vanished mid-animation; replacing that with a bigger magic number would
   * just be the same bug tuned to one machine.
   */
  closeDelayMs: number | null;
}

/** Currency-adjacent moment, so gold is the documented exception to the palette. See index.css. */
const GOLD = ['#E8AA3E', '#FFFFFF'];

/** A tier's own two tones plus white — the confetti is literally the card coming apart. */
const tierColors = (rarity: Rarity) => [
  RARITY_SPECS[rarity].edge,
  RARITY_SPECS[rarity].fieldCore,
  '#FFFFFF',
];

/** The opening burst every tier shares, so a purchase always starts the same way. */
const OPENING: ConfettiBurst = { delay: 0, particleCount: 80, spread: 60, colors: GOLD, ticks: 110 };

/**
 * When the item stops turning and faces front, in ms after a reveal starts.
 *
 * The reveal's choreography lives in index.css (`.rarity-reveal-spin`); this is the one instant out
 * of it that the rest of the celebration has to agree with. Confetti, haptics and the screen shake
 * all hang off this number, because the whole point of the stop is that everything blooms ON it —
 * a burst 200ms early reads as the item arriving into confetti that was already there.
 *
 * Change it here, in `.rarity-reveal-spin`'s duration, and in RarityReveal's timeline comment, or
 * the celebration comes apart from the animation it is celebrating.
 *
 * 5500, having been 1500, then 3000, then 4500, then 7500. The arrival — a black silhouette
 * spinning in from far away and growing to full size — is the part of this players actually watch,
 * and every extension came from being told it was still too quick to enjoy. 5500 is the first time
 * it has come back DOWN:「音效可以短個兩秒」— the whoosh runs for the whole arrival, so a spin that
 * is two seconds too long is heard before it is seen. 7.5s had gone past the point where more time
 * is more to enjoy and become a wait between paying and being shown what you bought.
 *
 * Nothing has been re-choreographed on any of those passes, this one included: every beat that
 * hangs off this constant kept its gap from the settle, so the copy still lands on the same rhythm
 * and the reading time after the stop is unchanged. The only thing shortening the track took time
 * out of is the APPROACH — the bounce at the end is still ~1.5s, which is why `.rarity-reveal-spin`
 * and `.rarity-reveal-grow` moved their overshoot stop from 80% back to 73%.
 *
 * Note this is the DURATION, not the speed. How fast the item turns is {@link RarityFxSpec.revealTurns}
 * per tier — the same turn count on a shorter track is a FASTER spin, so the two move together:
 * every change to this number has carried the same proportional change to all three turn counts,
 * which is what keeps「轉得更久」from quietly meaning「轉得更慢」and「短個兩秒」from meaning「轉快一點」.
 */
export const REVEAL_SETTLE_MS = 5500;

/**
 * When the item stops being a black shape and its own colour starts rising into it.
 *
 * 62% of the arrival, which is `.rarity-reveal-silhouette`'s middle keyframe in index.css — that
 * stop is the source of truth and this is it in milliseconds. Move one, move the other.
 *
 * It exists because the 轉動音 starts BACKING OFF here: 「當已經可以看到鳳凰 icon 的顏色的時候就
 * 可以不用有旋轉的聲音」. The reasoning holds up beyond the ask — the whoosh belongs to the
 * SILHOUETTE phase, the part where the player is being asked to guess at a turning shape. Once the
 * thing has colour it is not a spinning object any more, it is the pet they just bought.
 *
 * Backing off, though, and not stopping. This used to be a hard cut, and measured that left the
 * last 2.85s of the spin at exactly zero while the item was still visibly turning — 「旋轉音效不
 * 要不見」. It is now where a ramp to silence BEGINS, landing on {@link REVEAL_SETTLE_MS}. See
 * playRevealSpin in lib/soundUtils.ts.
 */
export const REVEAL_COLOUR_RISE_MS = Math.round(REVEAL_SETTLE_MS * 0.62);

export const RARITY_FX: Record<Rarity, RarityFxSpec> = {
  // 普通 — roughly 43% of the shop, and the floor everything above is measured against. One burst,
  // one chime, and it has to STAY that quiet now that it is the commonest purchase in the game. This is
  // the floor the whole table is measured against.
  common: {
    haptic: ['light'],
    hapticGapMs: 0,
    sounds: [{ effect: SoundEffect.SUCCESS, delayMs: 0, volume: 0.6 }],
    confetti: [OPENING],
    reveal: false,
    revealTurns: 0,
    shake: false,
    closeDelayMs: 1200,
  },
  // 稀有 — the first tier whose celebration is in the ITEM's colour rather than the game's. The
  // second burst swaps teal for the tier, which is the moment the confetti starts belonging to
  // the thing bought instead of to the shop.
  rare: {
    haptic: ['medium'],
    hapticGapMs: 0,
    sounds: [
      { effect: SoundEffect.SUCCESS, delayMs: 0, volume: 0.6 },
      { effect: SoundEffect.RARE_REVEAL, delayMs: 150, volume: 0.5 },
    ],
    confetti: [OPENING, { delay: 200, particleCount: 150, spread: 100, colors: tierColors('rare'), ticks: 110 }],
    reveal: false,
    revealTurns: 0,
    shake: false,
    closeDelayMs: 1400,
  },
  // 史詩 — the first tier that gets the full-screen reveal, and the reason the threshold moved down
  // to here.
  //
  // It used to be three confetti bursts over the dialog. That was the right shape when nothing in
  // the shop was tagged above 史詩, but the graded pet shelf put 柴犬 at this tier — the one
  // companion in the game that is EARNED (100 XP, no gold price) rather than bought — and finishing
  // a hundred training sessions was being celebrated with confetti over a dialog box while a 4800g
  // purchase got the screen. The reveal is what a milestone looks like; 史詩 is where milestones
  // start.
  //
  // It is the quieter of the two reveals left, and by the same means the whole table uses: no
  // ribbons thrown in from the edges, no fanfare, no shake, one burst fewer. That gap is the only
  // thing separating the second rung from the top one now, so nothing here may grow into it.
  epic: {
    haptic: ['heavy'],
    hapticGapMs: 0,
    hapticDelayMs: REVEAL_SETTLE_MS,
    sounds: [
      { effect: SoundEffect.SUCCESS, delayMs: 0, volume: 0.45 },
      { effect: SoundEffect.EPIC_REVEAL, delayMs: REVEAL_SETTLE_MS - 60, volume: 0.55 },
    ],
    confetti: [
      { delay: REVEAL_SETTLE_MS, particleCount: 120, spread: 110, startVelocity: 34, colors: tierColors('epic'), ticks: 160 },
      { delay: REVEAL_SETTLE_MS + 140, particleCount: 80, spread: 150, startVelocity: 28, colors: [RARITY_SPECS.epic.edge, '#FFFFFF'], ticks: 170 },
    ],
    reveal: true,
    // 6, from 8 when the track came down to 5.5s — the same ~65rpm, six passes instead of eight.
    // Before that it was 8 from 10, the first time this column ever went DOWN: every raise until
    // then was compensating for a spin that did not look like one, and the cause turned out to be a
    // missing perspective (see `.rarity-reveal-pivot` in index.css), not a rate. With the turn
    // actually rendering in 3D the rate has been right ever since; what moves it now is the length
    // of the track, and only so that the rate does NOT move with it.
    revealTurns: 6,
    shake: false,
    closeDelayMs: null,
  },
  // 神話 — 史詩's reveal plus the four things nothing else in the game does: a brass fanfare,
  // streamers thrown in from both sides of the screen instead of up from the middle, a hue that
  // moves and a screen that moves. The celebration stops coming from the dialog and starts coming
  // from the room. Its confetti is the only place the whole ladder's palette appears at once,
  // which is the point — this tier is the top of a ladder, so it wears all of it.
  //
  // The fanfare is SoundEffect.MYTHIC_FANFARE, which lib/soundUtils.ts builds as 「the 傳說
  // fanfare plus a run」. That composition outlived the tier it names, and the argument for it is
  // unchanged now that the brass underneath is nobody's own sound: the top of a ladder is
  // recognisable because it contains the rung below it.
  mythic: {
    haptic: ['heavy', 'heavy', 'heavy'],
    hapticGapMs: 90,
    hapticDelayMs: REVEAL_SETTLE_MS,
    sounds: [
      { effect: SoundEffect.MYTHIC_FANFARE, delayMs: 0, volume: 0.5 },
      { effect: SoundEffect.REWARD, delayMs: REVEAL_SETTLE_MS + 40, volume: 0.45 },
    ],
    confetti: [
      { delay: REVEAL_SETTLE_MS - 20, particleCount: 80, spread: 60, startVelocity: 46, angle: 66, origin: { x: 0.16, y: 0.62 }, colors: tierColors('mythic'), ticks: 200, ribbon: true },
      { delay: REVEAL_SETTLE_MS + 60, particleCount: 80, spread: 60, startVelocity: 46, angle: 114, origin: { x: 0.84, y: 0.62 }, colors: tierColors('mythic'), ticks: 200, ribbon: true },
      {
        delay: REVEAL_SETTLE_MS + 240,
        particleCount: 170,
        spread: 150,
        startVelocity: 40,
        // The whole ladder, rarest first, then gold and white. `#FFFFFF` is doing double duty as
        // 普通's rung and as the neutral every tier's own confetti carries — which is exactly what
        // that tier's near-white swatch is, so reading `RARITY_SPECS.common.edge` here would add a
        // second almost-white to the same handful and change nothing a player can see.
        colors: [
          RARITY_SPECS.mythic.edge,
          RARITY_SPECS.mythic.fieldCore,
          RARITY_SPECS.epic.edge,
          RARITY_SPECS.rare.edge,
          '#E8AA3E',
          '#FFFFFF',
        ],
        ticks: 200,
      },
    ],
    reveal: true,
    // The most-revised number in this file. The history IS the reasoning, so all of it is kept:
    //
    //   5  the original — top of the ladder, the request the field was added for.
    //   0  after seeing it on the 鳳凰: "神話 does not spin at all". Five turns inside what was
    //      then a 1.5s entrance is 200rpm, and the thing the player is meant to be recognising was
    //      a blur for most of its arrival.
    //   2  the entrance had been slowed to 3s, and zero turns across it was not a calm arrival but
    //      an item that grows and does nothing else — 「沒有旋轉的感覺」.
    //  10  with the track at 4.5s and the ask 「轉速幫我提高，轉的時間幫我再拉長」.
    //  17  with the track at 7.5s and the ask 「轉的時間幫我再增加3秒」, holding the ~136rpm that
    //      10-across-4.5s had so that lengthening the track did not quietly slow the spin.
    //  12  with the track still at 7.5s, and the first DECREASE this field ever took. Every raise
    //      above it was chasing
    //      「看不出來在轉」, and the cause was never the rate: the perspective was not reaching the
    //      rotation at all (see `.rarity-reveal-pivot` in index.css), so what the player was
    //      watching was a card squashing horizontally, which reads as flickering however fast it
    //      goes. With that fixed, each pass has a near edge that swings toward the viewer, and
    //      ~96rpm shows twelve of them. More would go back to being a blur — this time a
    //      three-dimensional one.
    //
    //   9  now, with the track at 5.5s and the ask 「音效可以短個兩秒」. Twelve turns on the shorter
    //      track would be ~131rpm — the blur 12 was chosen to avoid — so the count comes down with
    //      the duration and the item keeps turning at the ~96rpm that was found to read.
    //
    // The ladder stays monotonic (6 / 9 — it was 6 / 7 / 9 while 傳說 sat between them), the
    // curve still front-loads the rotation, and the
    // spin still ends in a long decay into the stop. What changed is that the turns are now
    // visible, so fewer of them say more.
    revealTurns: 9,
    shake: true,
    closeDelayMs: null,
  },
};

/**
 * The celebration for an item.
 *
 * The optional parameter is a leftover from when most of the catalog declared no tier at all, and
 * it is deliberately kept: every catalog item is graded now (constants/rarity.ts), but a caller
 * holding a partially-built item — a test fixture, a preview — should get the quietest row rather
 * than a crash. Nothing in the app passes `undefined` any more.
 */
export const getPurchaseFx = (rarity?: Rarity): RarityFxSpec => RARITY_FX[rarity ?? 'common'];
```

## src/constants/retiredItems.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { UserProfile } from '../types';

/**
 * Catalog ids that have been withdrawn from the game.
 *
 * Every screen already reads the catalog rather than the save file — the shop and the dressing
 * room list `ALL_ITEMS` filtered by ownership, and the avatar resolves each equipped id through
 * `getItemById` and drops what it cannot find. So deleting an item from constants/items.ts is
 * enough to make it disappear from the UI, and a retired id left in a save is inert rather than
 * broken.
 *
 * This list exists for the save file itself: without it a player who bought one keeps carrying a
 * dead id in `inventory`/`equippedItems` forever. Sweeping it once on load keeps the persisted
 * profile honest about what the game contains.
 */
export const RETIRED_ITEM_IDS: readonly string[] = [
  // Tattoos, removed from the catalog entirely (shop + dressing room + avatar).
  'tattoo-trad',
  'tattoo-jp',
  'tattoo-real',
  'tattoo-mini',
  'tattoo-ink',
];

const RETIRED = new Set(RETIRED_ITEM_IDS);

/**
 * Strips retired ids from a profile's owned and worn lists.
 *
 * Returns `null` when there is nothing to remove, so a healthy profile — which is every profile
 * after the first sweep — costs one `some()` and no Firestore write.
 */
export function stripRetiredItems(
  profile: UserProfile
): { inventory: string[]; equippedItems: string[] } | null {
  const inventory = profile.inventory || [];
  const equippedItems = profile.equippedItems || [];

  const affected =
    inventory.some(id => RETIRED.has(id)) || equippedItems.some(id => RETIRED.has(id));
  if (!affected) return null;

  return {
    inventory: inventory.filter(id => !RETIRED.has(id)),
    equippedItems: equippedItems.filter(id => !RETIRED.has(id)),
  };
}

```

```ts
/**

import { ItemDefinition } from './items';
import { getItemCategoryLabel } from '../utils/categoryUtils';

/**
 * 揭曉文案 — the three lines that land under an item during its 稀有度揭曉.
 *
 * Separate from `ItemDefinition.description` on purpose, and the difference is who is being
 * addressed. A card's `description` is a *catalogue entry*: it describes an object to someone
 * deciding whether to buy it, in the third person, at whatever length the object needs (鳳凰's runs
 * to four clauses about 梧桐 and 醴泉). What plays after the purchase is a *greeting*: the thing is
 * already yours, so the copy's job is to introduce a new companion rather than to sell one, and it
 * has about two seconds of screen time to do it in.
 *
 * Reusing the catalogue line for the greeting was the obvious first idea and it reads wrong twice
 * over — it is too long to take in against a moving background, and having just spent 4800 gold the
 * player is re-read the sales pitch they already agreed to.
 *
 * ## The template
 *
 *   認識【名稱】！這是一隻／一個【類型與特徵】的【寵物／物品】，最喜歡【喜好或用途】，
 *   將為你的【日常／旅程】帶來【溫暖、陪伴或實用價值】。
 *
 * Every `intro` below is that sentence. Keeping the shape identical is what makes nine different
 * animals read as nine members of one shelf; a table where each entry found its own phrasing would
 * read as nine unrelated pieces of marketing copy.
 *
 * ## Why only the pets are written out
 *
 * The reveal is reachable by 史詩 and above (constants/rarityFx.ts), whose pets are 柴犬 and 鳳凰
 * — both pets — and, through the `?rarity=` debug override, anything at all. So the pet shelf is
 * hand-written and everything else falls back (see {@link getRevealCopy}). Writing greeting copy for
 * 121 items that can never show it would be 121 strings to keep in step with their descriptions for
 * no visible gain.
 *
 * The whole shelf is written rather than just the two that can reach the reveal, because the tier on
 * a pet is a balance value that has already moved once; copy that exists only for the tiers that
 * happen to be high today would silently fall back to the generic line the first time 賓士貓 is
 * promoted.
 */
export interface RevealCopy {
  /**
   * 類型 — what kind of thing this is, in two to four characters.
   *
   * Note this is NOT the 稀有度. The tier is deliberately wordless everywhere in the game
   * (constants/rarity.ts) and the reveal is the one place a 「神話」 caption would be easiest to
   * justify and still be the same mistake: the player is being shown what they now own, not read
   * their receipt. What they are told instead is what it IS — 「短毛犬」, 「神鳥」 — which is the
   * useful half of that line and stays true whatever the tier is tuned to later. The tier is still
   * said, at full volume, by the colour of everything around this text.
   */
  kind: string;
  /** One warm sentence in the template above. Two or three lines at reveal width; never four. */
  intro: string;
  /**
   * Two or three short badges.
   *
   * Two to three because one badge is an afterthought and four wrap onto a second row, which turns
   * the calmest part of the reveal into a paragraph. Four characters each, at most — these are read
   * at a glance while the item is still bobbing, not studied.
   */
  tags: string[];
}

/** Keyed by item id, matching constants/items.ts. */
export const REVEAL_COPY: Record<string, RevealCopy> = {
  // --- 狗 ---
  'pet-dog-dachshund': {
    kind: '短腿犬',
    intro: '認識臘腸犬！牠是一隻長腰短腿、走起路來整條背都在晃的小獵犬，最喜歡貼著地板到處嗅聞，將為你的日常帶來慢悠悠的好心情。',
    tags: ['忠心', '愛嗅聞', '長腰短腿'],
  },
  'pet-dog-poodle': {
    kind: '捲毛犬',
    intro: '認識紅貴賓犬！牠是一隻杏紅色、從頭蓬到腳踝的捲毛小狗，最喜歡被抱在懷裡撒嬌，將為你的日常帶來柔軟而療癒的時光。',
    tags: ['愛撒嬌', '蓬鬆', '好抱'],
  },
  // 柴犬 is the shelf's earned companion — unlocked at 100 XP, not bought — so its greeting is the
  // one that mentions how it arrived. 「陪你走過的每一次訓練」 is literally true of this pet and of
  // no other on the shelf.
  'pet-dog-shiba': {
    kind: '立耳犬',
    intro: '認識柴犬！牠是一隻結實挺拔、尾巴驕傲捲在背上的赤色夥伴，最喜歡陪你走過每一次訓練，將為你的旅程帶來穩穩的信賴與陪伴。',
    tags: ['訓練夥伴', '驕傲', '結實'],
  },

  // --- 貓 ---
  'pet-cat-orange': {
    kind: '虎斑貓',
    intro: '認識橘貓！牠是一隻暖橘毛色、額頭帶著 M 字紋的圓潤家貓，最喜歡趴在有陽光的地方打盹，將為你的日常帶來慵懶又安心的午後。',
    tags: ['愛睡覺', '溫暖', '圓潤'],
  },
  'pet-cat-tabby': {
    kind: '虎斑貓',
    intro: '認識虎斑貓！牠是一隻身側排著細直紋、眼角向後拉長的褐灰色貓咪，最喜歡從高處靜靜觀察你，將為你的日常帶來安靜的默契。',
    tags: ['優雅', '愛觀察', '安靜'],
  },
  'pet-cat-tuxedo': {
    kind: '賓士貓',
    intro: '認識賓士貓！牠是一隻黑毛配雪白胸兜與四隻白襪的紳士貓，最喜歡端正地坐在你身旁，將為你的日常帶來體面又親近的陪伴。',
    tags: ['紳士', '親人', '天生正裝'],
  },

  // --- 鳥 ---
  'pet-bird-budgie': {
    kind: '小鸚鵡',
    intro: '認識虎皮鸚鵡！牠是一隻草綠帶黃、後頸鋪著整片虎斑的小鸚鵡，最喜歡歪著頭學你說話，將為你的日常帶來熱鬧又逗趣的聲音。',
    tags: ['愛說話', '好奇', '活潑'],
  },
  'pet-bird-javasparrow': {
    kind: '小文鳥',
    intro: '認識文鳥！牠是一隻灰背粉肚、頂著黑頭罩與雪白臉頰的圓潤小鳥，最喜歡停在你的指尖上打盹，將為你的日常帶來小小的溫熱重量。',
    tags: ['圓潤', '親人', '愛停手'],
  },
  'pet-bird-canary': {
    kind: '鳴禽',
    intro: '認識金絲雀！牠是一隻通身金黃、臉頰暈著暖橘的歌唱家，最喜歡在清晨對著光唱上一段，將為你的日常帶來明亮而清脆的開場。',
    tags: ['歌聲動人', '明亮', '晨型'],
  },
  // 鳳凰 is the game's only 神話 item and the greeting is allowed to be the grandest on the shelf —
  // but still warm, and still about companionship. 「浴火重生」 belongs to the catalogue line; what
  // this one promises is that it stays with you, which is what a reveal is for.
  'pet-bird-phoenix': {
    kind: '神鳥',
    intro: '認識鳳凰！牠是一隻朱紅羽衣鑲著流金翎邊、頂著火冠的傳說神鳥，最喜歡在你身邊靜靜盤旋，將為你的旅程帶來溫暖而長久的守護。',
    tags: ['傳說', '守護', '火羽'],
  },
};

/** The first sentence of a catalogue line — up to and including its first 。, ！ or ，. */
function firstClause(description: string): string {
  const end = description.search(/[。！]/);
  if (end >= 0) return description.slice(0, end);
  const comma = description.indexOf('，');
  return comma >= 0 ? description.slice(0, comma) : description;
}

/**
 * The greeting for an item, including everything the table above does not name.
 *
 * The fallback builds the template's opening from what every item already has — its name and its
 * category — and borrows the first clause of its catalogue line for the middle. That is a weaker
 * sentence than a written one and it is meant to be: it exists so a debug override
 * (`?rarity=mythic` on a floor tile) still renders a complete reveal instead of a hole where the
 * copy should be, not so that the table can be left unfilled.
 *
 * It returns NO tags rather than inventing them. Tags are the one part of the block that cannot be
 * derived — 「愛撒嬌」 is a judgement about an animal, not a fact about a record — and three plausible
 * guesses would be worse than an empty row the layout already handles.
 */
export function getRevealCopy(item: ItemDefinition): RevealCopy {
  const written = REVEAL_COPY[item.id];
  if (written) return written;

  const kind = getItemCategoryLabel(item.id);
  return {
    kind,
    intro: `認識${item.name}！這是一件${firstClause(item.description)}的${kind}，將為你的島嶼帶來一點新的樂趣。`,
    tags: [],
  };
}
```

## src/constants/rewardEffects.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 獎勵計算層 — the one place a reward is changed by anything the player has activated.
 *
 *   Base Reward  →  Active Effects  →  Final Reward
 *
 * Every reward in the game passes through {@link settleReward} on its way to the wallet, and it is
 * the ONLY place a multiplier is ever applied. That is the whole point of the file, and it is what
 * §3 and §16 of the brief are asking for: a new card that doubles 碎片, or triples 經驗值 on a
 * weekend, is a row in constants/utilityCards.ts — not an edit to 健身, not an edit to 每日登入,
 * not an edit to whatever pays out next year.
 *
 * ## Where it is actually wired in, and why there is exactly one seam
 *
 * `buildCurrencyUpdate` in context/useEconomyActions.ts is the single function in the game that
 * turns a currency grant into a database write, and it calls this file. Everything that pays a
 * currency goes through it — the standalone grant path, 摸摸寵物, the offline 每日登入 claim and
 * the 健身 payout — so 「×2 在哪一層計算」 has one answer and cannot grow a second.
 *
 * The alternative was to multiply at each source, which is the arrangement the brief specifically
 * forbids: `coinReward * 2` inside a fitness screen is invisible to the next reward source that is
 * written, and two sources that each remember to multiply are one refactor away from a reward that
 * is multiplied twice.
 *
 * ## Base is preserved, never overwritten
 *
 * A settlement returns BOTH numbers ({@link SettledReward.base} and {@link SettledReward.reward}).
 * The base is what the rule tables decided (constants/workoutRewards.ts et al.) and it stays
 * readable, so a receipt can say 「基礎 40 ＋ 雙倍 40」 and a log can show what a workout was worth
 * before the card. Nothing here ever rewrites the payout tables.
 *
 * ## Consuming a use is part of the SAME write
 *
 * A `uses`-based effect must be decremented exactly when the reward it boosted is banked. So this
 * function does not write anything: it returns {@link SettledReward.cardsAfter}, the card state as
 * it should be saved, and the caller folds that into the one `updateDoc` that also moves the
 * balance. A failed save then costs the player nothing — no coins, and no spent use.
 */

import type { Reward } from './rewards';
import {
  activeEffects,
  getUtilityCard,
  type ActiveUtilityEffect,
  type UtilityCardId,
  type UtilityCardState,
  type UtilityEffect,
  type UtilityEffectKind,
} from './utilityCards';

/**
 * What the player has running, and when 「now」 is.
 *
 * `nowMs` is passed in rather than read here for the same reason it is passed into every function
 * in constants/utilityCards.ts: a pure calculation layer that reads the clock cannot be tested, and
 * the day a server owns the clock this is the only argument that changes.
 */
export interface RewardEffectContext {
  cards?: UtilityCardState | null;
  nowMs: number;
}

/** No effects at all — for a caller that has no profile yet, and for tests of the base case. */
export const NO_EFFECTS: RewardEffectContext = { cards: null, nowMs: 0 };

/** One effect's contribution to a settlement. Carried for the receipt and for the log line. */
export interface AppliedEffectNote {
  activationId: string;
  cardId: UtilityCardId;
  kind: UtilityEffectKind;
  /** What this one effect multiplied by. */
  factor: number;
}

export interface SettledReward {
  /** What the reward tables decided, untouched. */
  base: Reward;
  /** What is actually paid. Identical to `base` when nothing is running. */
  reward: Reward;
  /** The combined factor, after the cap. 1 when nothing applied. */
  multiplier: number;
  applied: AppliedEffectNote[];
  /**
   * The card state to persist alongside the reward, or null when no effect was consumed.
   *
   * Null in the overwhelmingly common case (nothing running, or a timed effect that is not spent by
   * being used), which is what keeps the ordinary write byte-for-byte what it always was.
   */
  cardsAfter: UtilityCardState | null;
}

/**
 * The ceiling on the combined multiplier.
 *
 * A guard, not a balance dial — the same role `maxCoinsPerWorkout` plays in constants/
 * workoutRewards.ts. Effects multiply together, so three ×2 cards would be ×8 and a fourth would be
 * ×16; with 金幣 the only currency that buys anything, a stack like that is not a good day, it is a
 * broken economy. Today only one card exists and the cap is unreachable, which is exactly when it
 * should be written down.
 */
export const MAX_REWARD_MULTIPLIER = 4;

/** Whether one effect applies to this reward. The only place that question is answered. */
function matches(effect: UtilityEffect, reward: Reward): boolean {
  if (effect.kind === 'currency-multiplier') {
    return reward.kind === 'currency' && reward.currency === effect.currency;
  }
  return reward.kind === 'xp';
}

/** A sane, positive factor. A card configured with 0, NaN or a negative reads as 「no effect」. */
function factorOf(effect: UtilityEffect): number {
  const raw = effect.multiplier;
  return Number.isFinite(raw) && raw > 0 ? raw : 1;
}

/**
 * Applies everything the player has running to one reward.
 *
 * Order is: find live effects → keep the ones that match THIS reward → multiply (capped) → floor →
 * consume any uses that were actually spent. An effect that does not match is never consumed, which
 * is what stops a 「接下來一次獎勵」 card from being eaten by a 經驗值 grant it did nothing to.
 *
 * Item and 功能卡 rewards pass through untouched. There is no such thing as ×2 of one hat, and a
 * card that doubled card drops would need a rule about caps and duplicates that nothing has asked
 * for — so the shape simply does not offer it.
 */
export function settleReward(base: Reward, ctx: RewardEffectContext): SettledReward {
  const unchanged: SettledReward = {
    base,
    reward: base,
    multiplier: 1,
    applied: [],
    cardsAfter: null,
  };

  if (base.kind !== 'currency' && base.kind !== 'xp') return unchanged;

  const live = activeEffects(ctx.cards, ctx.nowMs);
  if (live.length === 0) return unchanged;

  const applied: AppliedEffectNote[] = [];
  let multiplier = 1;

  for (const active of live) {
    const card = getUtilityCard(active.cardId);
    if (!card || !matches(card.effect, base)) continue;
    const factor = factorOf(card.effect);
    if (factor === 1) continue;
    multiplier *= factor;
    applied.push({
      activationId: active.activationId,
      cardId: active.cardId,
      kind: card.effect.kind,
      factor,
    });
  }

  if (applied.length === 0) return unchanged;

  multiplier = Math.min(MAX_REWARD_MULTIPLIER, multiplier);

  // Floored, because both currencies and 經驗值 are integers everywhere else (the wallet, the HUD,
  // firestore.rules), and never below the base — a multiplier is a bonus, so a rounding path that
  // could pay less than the base reward would be a card that punishes the player for using it.
  const amount = Math.max(base.amount, Math.floor(base.amount * multiplier));
  const reward: Reward =
    base.kind === 'currency' ? { ...base, amount } : { kind: 'xp', amount };

  return { base, reward, multiplier, applied, cardsAfter: consume(ctx.cards, applied) };
}

/**
 * The card state after the applied `uses`-based effects have spent one use each.
 *
 * Returns null when nothing changed — a timed effect is not consumed by being applied, and that is
 * the only kind of card the game ships with today, so the common path writes nothing extra.
 */
function consume(
  cards: UtilityCardState | null | undefined,
  applied: readonly AppliedEffectNote[],
): UtilityCardState | null {
  if (!cards?.active || applied.length === 0) return null;

  const spent = new Set(applied.map((note) => note.activationId));
  let changed = false;

  const next: ActiveUtilityEffect[] = [];
  for (const effect of cards.active) {
    if (!spent.has(effect.activationId) || typeof effect.usesLeft !== 'number') {
      next.push(effect);
      continue;
    }
    changed = true;
    const usesLeft = effect.usesLeft - 1;
    // Dropped rather than kept at zero: `activeEffects` would filter it out anyway, and a record
    // that is never live again is noise in a save that has to stay small.
    if (usesLeft > 0) next.push({ ...effect, usesLeft });
  }

  return changed ? { ...cards, active: next } : null;
}

/** One line for the console, when a grant was boosted. Never player-facing copy. */
export function describeSettlement(settled: SettledReward): string {
  if (settled.applied.length === 0) return '';
  const names = settled.applied.map((note) => getUtilityCard(note.cardId)?.name ?? note.cardId);
  const before = settled.base.kind === 'item' ? settled.base.quantity : 'amount' in settled.base ? settled.base.amount : 0;
  const after = settled.reward.kind === 'item' ? settled.reward.quantity : 'amount' in settled.reward ? settled.reward.amount : 0;
  return `[effects] ${names.join('、')} → ×${settled.multiplier}（${before} → ${after}）`;
}

```

## src/constants/rewardPools.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 獎勵池 — 「這個獎勵可以發出哪些東西」, declared as RULES about items and never as a list of ids.
 *
 * This is §6 of the brief and the reason it is its own file: 每日簽到, 輪盤, 新手獎勵, 活動獎勵 and
 * 任務獎勵 all need to answer the same question, and each of them answering it separately is how a
 * game ends up with five slightly different definitions of 「稀有商品」. There is one definition
 * here, and every reward system reads it.
 *
 * It was extracted from constants/workoutRewards.ts, which owned this shape while 健身 was the only
 * system that drew items. Nothing about the semantics changed in the move — isEligibleForPool
 * applies the same checks in the same order — but the file it lives in no longer implies that
 * drawing an item is a fitness feature.
 *
 * ## Filter → Select, never Select → Check
 *
 * A pool is RESOLVED to a list before anything is drawn from it ({@link buildRewardPool}), so there
 * is no path on which a draw can produce an item the rules forbid and then have to reject it. The
 * other order is the shape that eventually hands out the thing it was supposed to exclude, because
 * the "check" is one `if` somebody forgets on the third code path.
 *
 * ## Everything here is derived from the live catalog
 *
 * Adding 「休閒帽 T」 to the shop at 180 金幣 puts it in the newbie pool automatically; re-pricing an
 * existing hat at 2,000 takes it out; grading a piece 史詩 takes it out of every pool whose ceiling
 * is below that. No edit here, and nothing in any reward system may ever say `if (itemId === ...)`.
 */

import { ALL_ITEMS, getItemById, type ItemDefinition } from './items';
import { RETIRED_ITEM_IDS } from './retiredItems';
import { RARITY_LADDER, rarityRank, type Rarity } from './rarity';
import { seedFrom, seedPick, seedUnit } from './seed';
import { getDisplayCategory } from '../utils/categoryUtils';

/**
 * An eligibility spec.
 *
 * Every field is a rule about items rather than a set of them. The four dimensions the brief names
 * — Allowed Rarity, Excluded Rarity, Category, Price Range — are all here, and a reward system
 * combines them rather than inventing a fifth.
 */
export interface RewardPool {
  id: string;
  /** Shown in 管理員測試 only. Never on a player's screen. */
  label: string;
  /**
   * Shop/display category ids (utils/categoryUtils.ts) the reward may come from — the SAME
   * taxonomy the shop, the wardrobe and the build rail read, so 「這是人物裝飾嗎」 has exactly one
   * answer in the whole app. An empty list means 「不限分類」.
   */
  categories: readonly string[];
  /** Inclusive gold ceiling. */
  maxPrice: number;
  /** Inclusive floor. A floor of 1 excludes 0-price items, which are unlocks rather than goods. */
  minPrice: number;
  /**
   * The rarest tier allowed, inclusive. `null` means 「不設上限」.
   *
   * Note what this no longer means. While rarity was opt-in, `null` was the STRICTEST setting —
   * 「只收沒有稀有度標記的普通商品」 — because an untagged card was an ordinary item and
   * `rarity: 'common'` marked the bottom rung of a specially graded shelf. Every item is graded
   * now (constants/rarity.ts), so there is no untagged state to single out, and `null` reads the
   * ordinary way round: no ceiling at all. A pool that wants only ordinary goods now says
   * `maxRarity: 'common'`.
   */
  maxRarity: Rarity | null;
  /** The least rare tier allowed, inclusive. `null` or absent means 「不設下限」. */
  minRarity?: Rarity | null;
  /**
   * Tiers refused outright, whatever the range above says.
   *
   * Not redundant with the range: a pool can legitimately want 「普通到神話，但跳過史詩」 for an
   * event, and expressing that as two pools would duplicate every other field. Absent on every
   * pool that does not need it, which is most of them.
   */
  excludeRarities?: readonly Rarity[];
  /** 經驗值解鎖 items are earned by training, never handed out. See utils/unlock.ts. */
  allowXpUnlock: boolean;
  /**
   * Skip items the player already owns, when doing so still leaves something to give.
   *
   * A duplicate wearable is a no-op in the inventory (own-once, see utils/inventory.ts), so a
   * repeat pick would read to the player as having been given nothing. It falls BACK to the full
   * pool rather than failing when everything is owned — a reward that cannot be granted is worse
   * than one the player already has.
   */
  preferUnowned: boolean;
}

const RETIRED = new Set(RETIRED_ITEM_IDS);

/**
 * Whether one catalog item satisfies a pool's rules. The single eligibility gate — the pool
 * builder, every admin preview and every test ask this one question.
 */
export function isEligibleForPool(item: ItemDefinition, pool: RewardPool): boolean {
  if (RETIRED.has(item.id)) return false;
  if (pool.categories.length > 0 && !pool.categories.includes(item.shopCategory)) return false;
  // A category that no longer exists in the taxonomy cannot be reasoned about, so it is refused
  // rather than assumed harmless — the failure mode of guessing here is handing out a sofa.
  if (!getDisplayCategory(item.shopCategory)) return false;
  if (item.price < pool.minPrice || item.price > pool.maxPrice) return false;
  if (!pool.allowXpUnlock && (item.xpUnlock ?? 0) > 0) return false;
  if (pool.maxRarity != null && rarityRank(item.rarity) > rarityRank(pool.maxRarity)) return false;
  if (pool.minRarity != null && rarityRank(item.rarity) < rarityRank(pool.minRarity)) return false;
  if (pool.excludeRarities?.includes(item.rarity)) return false;
  return true;
}

/**
 * The pool, resolved against the live catalog. Catalog order, which is stable, so a seeded pick is
 * reproducible — see {@link pickRewardFrom}.
 */
export function buildRewardPool(pool: RewardPool): ItemDefinition[] {
  return ALL_ITEMS.filter((item) => isEligibleForPool(item, pool));
}

/** What a pool currently contains, per tier. For the admin readout and for balance checks. */
export function poolRarityBreakdown(pool: RewardPool): Record<Rarity, number> {
  const counts = Object.fromEntries(RARITY_LADDER.map((r) => [r, 0])) as Record<Rarity, number>;
  for (const item of buildRewardPool(pool)) counts[item.rarity] += 1;
  return counts;
}

// --- Choosing one ------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * A small deterministic hash, so a pick can be reproduced from the event that caused it.
 *
 * `Math.random()` would work exactly once: on a retry it would choose a DIFFERENT item, so a grant
 * that was written but whose confirmation was lost could not be recognised as the same grant.
 * Seeding on the event id makes the choice a function of the event, which is what lets the write
 * path be replayed safely.
 *
 * Moved to constants/seed.ts and re-exported here, unchanged. It had been copied a second time into
 * constants/fragments.ts and was about to be copied a third time into the daily-login prize roll;
 * two hashes that are supposed to agree and do not is a board that previews one prize and a claim
 * that pays another. Re-exported rather than relocated at the call sites because every existing
 * importer says `from './rewardPools'` and none of them is wrong to.
 */
export { seedFrom, seedUnit, seedPick };

/**
 * Picks one item from an already-filtered list.
 *
 * The order is Filter → Select, never Select → Check: by the time anything reaches here the list
 * contains only items the rules allow.
 */
export function pickRewardFrom(items: readonly ItemDefinition[], seed: number): ItemDefinition | null {
  if (items.length === 0) return null;
  return items[seed % items.length];
}

// --- Weighted choice ---------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * 加權隨機 — one implementation, for every table in the game that has to pick 「常見的東西比較常
 * 出現」.
 *
 * The 輪盤 (constants/wheelRewards.ts) draws its prize with this, and the 限時商店
 * (constants/limitedShop.ts) picks which products go on sale with it. Both used to be described in
 * the brief as 「不要散落的 if / else 或 Math.random() > 0.9」, and this is what replaces that: a
 * table of `{ value, weight }` and one function that reads it. A rarer outcome is a smaller number
 * in a data row — never a nested condition, and never a threshold typed into a component.
 *
 * Seeded, exactly like {@link pickRewardFrom} and for the same reason: a draw has to be a function
 * of the EVENT that caused it. `Math.random()` inside a React tree re-rolls on every re-render, so
 * a spinning wheel would land on a different prize each time its parent re-rendered — the failure
 * §19 of the brief asks to be tested for. Seed on the spin id and the answer is fixed the moment
 * the spin exists.
 */
export interface Weighted<T> {
  value: T;
  /** Relative likelihood. Zero or negative means 「never」, and is skipped rather than clamped. */
  weight: number;
}

/** Total of the positive weights. Zero when nothing in the table can be drawn. */
export function totalWeight<T>(entries: readonly Weighted<T>[]): number {
  return entries.reduce((sum, entry) => sum + (entry.weight > 0 ? entry.weight : 0), 0);
}

/** One entry's probability, 0…1. What an odds readout and the tests both ask. */
export function weightedChance<T>(entries: readonly Weighted<T>[], value: T): number {
  const total = totalWeight(entries);
  if (total <= 0) return 0;
  const weight = entries.find((entry) => entry.value === value)?.weight ?? 0;
  return weight > 0 ? weight / total : 0;
}

/**
 * `seedUnit` — a deterministic 0…1 from a seed, for the callers that need a NUMBER rather than a
 * table entry. It lives in constants/seed.ts with the hash and is re-exported above.
 *
 * The 限時商店 rolls a bundle's size and its price this way (constants/limitedShopRotation.ts).
 * Those are the same kind of decision a prize draw is and must obey the same rule: seeded on the
 * event, never on `Math.random()`, so re-opening the shop, reloading the page or re-rendering the
 * component cannot produce a second answer. A shop whose price changed on refresh is the exact
 * failure that function exists to make unrepresentable.
 */

/**
 * A deterministic whole number in `[min, max]`, inclusive at both ends.
 *
 * Inclusive of `max` because every caller so far is a COUNT the designer wrote down — 「2 到 4
 * 張」 means four is possible — and an exclusive ceiling is the off-by-one that quietly makes the
 * top of a stated range unreachable.
 */
export function seedIntInRange(seed: number, min: number, max: number): number {
  const lo = Math.min(Math.round(min), Math.round(max));
  const hi = Math.max(Math.round(min), Math.round(max));
  if (hi <= lo) return lo;
  return lo + Math.min(hi - lo, Math.floor(seedUnit(seed) * (hi - lo + 1)));
}

/** Picks one entry, in table order, by weight. Null only when nothing has a positive weight. */
export function pickWeighted<T>(entries: readonly Weighted<T>[], seed: number): T | null {
  const total = totalWeight(entries);
  if (total <= 0) return null;

  let target = seedUnit(seed) * total;
  for (const entry of entries) {
    if (entry.weight <= 0) continue;
    target -= entry.weight;
    if (target < 0) return entry.value;
  }
  // Floating-point drift only — the last positive entry is the correct answer here.
  for (let i = entries.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (entries[i].weight > 0) return entries[i].value;
  return null;
}

/**
 * Picks up to `count` DISTINCT entries, by weight, without replacement.
 *
 * What a shop rotation needs and a single pick cannot express: 「這一檔挑三樣，不要重複」. Each
 * round re-seeds off the caller's seed and the round index, so the whole draw stays a pure function
 * of one seed — the same seed always produces the same shelf, which is what makes every player see
 * the same limited shop without a server telling them what it is.
 */
export function pickWeightedMany<T>(
  entries: readonly Weighted<T>[],
  count: number,
  seed: number,
): T[] {
  const pool = entries.filter((entry) => entry.weight > 0);
  const picked: T[] = [];
  for (let round = 0; round < count && pool.length > 0; round++) {
    const choice = pickWeighted(pool, seedFrom(`${seed}:${round}`));
    if (choice === null) break;
    picked.push(choice);
    const index = pool.findIndex((entry) => entry.value === choice);
    if (index >= 0) pool.splice(index, 1);
  }
  return picked;
}

/** What a resolution produced, or why it produced nothing. */
export type RewardDraw =
  | { ok: true; item: ItemDefinition; poolSize: number; fromOwnedFallback: boolean }
  | { ok: false; reason: 'empty-pool' };

/**
 * The whole selection flow for one grant: build the pool, drop what the player already owns, draw.
 *
 * Takes the owned ids rather than a profile so it stays pure and testable — the service passes
 * `profile.inventory`, a test passes whatever case it is pinning.
 */
export function drawReward(
  pool: RewardPool,
  ownedItemIds: readonly string[],
  seed: number,
): RewardDraw {
  const all = buildRewardPool(pool);
  if (all.length === 0) return { ok: false, reason: 'empty-pool' };

  const owned = new Set(ownedItemIds);
  const fresh = pool.preferUnowned ? all.filter((item) => !owned.has(item.id)) : all;
  const candidates = fresh.length > 0 ? fresh : all;

  const item = pickRewardFrom(candidates, seed);
  if (!item) return { ok: false, reason: 'empty-pool' };
  return { ok: true, item, poolSize: candidates.length, fromOwnedFallback: fresh.length === 0 };
}

// --- The pools themselves ----------------------------------------------------

/**
 * The newbie ceiling, in 金幣.
 *
 * Anchored to the economy rather than picked: a short prototype workout pays roughly 8–16 金幣
 * (constants/workoutRewards.ts), so 300 is a couple of dozen sessions' worth of the game's only
 * income. That is the right size for 「第一次健身」 — enough to be a real item the player can put on
 * immediately, small enough that it cannot short-circuit anything they were saving for. It also
 * lands the pool squarely on the cheap end of the wardrobe: 上衣 100–250, 帽子 120–300,
 * 髮型 150–300, 草裙 50, 涼鞋 250, 復古墨鏡 120.
 *
 * Raising it is a one-line change AND a real design decision: at 500 the pool swallows most of the
 * mid-priced wardrobe, and 「新手小禮物」 stops being small.
 */
export const NEWBIE_PRICE_CEILING = 300;

/**
 * 新手小禮物 — low-price, ordinary wearables and nothing else.
 *
 * The categories are the ones the brief names (上衣 / 下裝 / 配件 / 帽子 / 鞋子) plus 髮型, which is
 * the same kind of thing at the same prices. Everything else in the catalog is excluded BY
 * CONSTRUCTION rather than by a list of exceptions:
 *
 *  - 特殊飾品 (`SpecialFx`) — the game's premium cosmetics, none under 600. Not in `categories`.
 *  - 寵物 and 寵物飾品 — companions, not decorations, and 480+.
 *  - Furniture, 藝術品, 房屋外觀, 地板/牆面 — not worn, and several are four figures.
 *  - Anything above 普通 or earned — caught by `maxRarity` and `allowXpUnlock: false` even if it
 *    were somehow cheap enough and in one of these categories.
 *
 * `maxRarity: 'common'` is what the old `maxRarity: null` used to mean, back when 「no rarity
 * field」 was how an ordinary item was spelled. Every item is graded now, so the intent —
 * 「只發普通商品」 — has to be said with the tier's own name. See {@link RewardPool.maxRarity}.
 */
export const NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL: RewardPool = {
  id: 'newbie-basics',
  label: '新手小物（低價人物裝飾）',
  categories: ['Tops', 'Bottoms', 'Hats', 'Shoes', 'Accessories', 'Hair'],
  maxPrice: NEWBIE_PRICE_CEILING,
  minPrice: 1,
  maxRarity: 'common',
  allowXpUnlock: false,
  preferUnowned: true,
};

/**
 * Every pool in the game, so an admin panel can list them and a rule can name one.
 *
 * One entry today. 輪盤 and 活動獎勵 add rows here when they are built — a pool is data, and a new
 * reward system that needs 「稀有以上的家具」 writes a row rather than a filter of its own.
 */
export const REWARD_POOLS: readonly RewardPool[] = [NEWBIE_REWARD_POOL];

export function getRewardPool(poolId: string): RewardPool | undefined {
  return REWARD_POOLS.find((pool) => pool.id === poolId);
}

/** The item behind a recorded grant, for an admin readout. Null once that item has been retired. */
export function getPoolItem(itemId: string | null | undefined): ItemDefinition | null {
  return itemId ? getItemById(itemId) ?? null : null;
}
```

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 獎勵 — what the game can hand a player, where it may come from, and the one rule that keeps the
 * two currencies from collapsing into one.
 *
 * This file is a vocabulary and a policy. It has no React, no Firestore and no item ids: it says
 * what a reward IS ({@link Reward}), what may have caused one ({@link RewardSource}) and which
 * sources are allowed to pay which currency ({@link SOURCE_CURRENCY_POLICY}). The service that
 * actually writes them is context/useEconomyActions.ts, and it is the only writer in the game.
 *
 * ## The rule this file exists to make unbreakable
 *
 *   金幣 is minted by 健身, and by nothing that was not deliberately let through this table.
 *
 * That is a game-design decision with real teeth — it is the reason the shop means anything — and
 * a rule of that kind cannot survive as a comment. Every reward carries its {@link RewardSource},
 * and {@link checkGrant} refuses a coin grant from any source whose row does not name `coins`. So
 * 「輪盤不小心發了金幣」 is not a bug that ships and is noticed in a month; it is a grant that does
 * not happen and a console error naming the source that tried.
 *
 * The table has exactly one exception to 「只有健身」 and it was added on purpose rather than by
 * accident, which is the whole point of a list that has to be edited: see 每日登入's row.
 *
 *   Workout      → Reward Service → 金幣 ✔
 *   Daily Login  → Reward Service → 金幣 ✔ (capped by design, see the policy table) / 碎片 ✔
 *   Wheel        → Reward Service → 金幣 ✘ (refused here) / 碎片 ✔
 *
 * ## Why a grant carries its source at all
 *
 * §17 of the brief, and it costs one field: a resource that appears in a wallet with no record of
 * why is un-debuggable, un-balanceable and impossible to audit for double payment. The source
 * travels with the reward from the thing that caused it all the way to the write, so a log line
 * can always answer 「玩家為什麼得到這些資源」.
 */

import type { CurrencyId } from './currency';
import type { UtilityCardId } from './utilityCards';

/**
 * What caused a reward. Recorded on every grant, and the input the policy below reads.
 *
 * These are CAUSES, not features — `wheel` and `quest` have no code behind them yet and are
 * declared anyway, because the policy has to be able to say 「輪盤不得發金幣」 before a 輪盤
 * exists. A source with no rule behind it grants nothing; it simply cannot be used to mint coins
 * the day somebody builds it.
 */
export type RewardSource =
  /** 健身完成 — the prototype screen today, a fitness API tomorrow. The ONLY coin source. */
  | 'workout'
  /** 每日登入獎勵 (constants/dailyLogin.ts). */
  | 'daily-login'
  /** 輪盤抽獎. Not built yet — see the file doc on why it is named here anyway. */
  | 'wheel'
  /** 新手獎勵 — anything granted for reaching a first milestone that is not a workout. */
  | 'newbie'
  /** 活動獎勵. */
  | 'event'
  /** 任務獎勵. */
  | 'quest'
  /** 島上互動 — 摸摸寵物, 島嶼秘寶, and anything else the world hands over for touching it. */
  | 'island-interaction'
  /** 管理員測試 (constants/adminFeatures.ts). Never reachable by a player. */
  | 'admin-test';

/** Human-readable cause, for the admin readout and for log lines. Never player-facing copy. */
export const REWARD_SOURCE_LABELS: Record<RewardSource, string> = {
  workout: '健身',
  'daily-login': '每日登入',
  wheel: '輪盤',
  newbie: '新手獎勵',
  event: '活動獎勵',
  quest: '任務獎勵',
  'island-interaction': '島上互動',
  'admin-test': '管理員測試',
};

/**
 * Which currencies each source may pay.
 *
 * The whole of §8/§9/§10/§12 in one table. Read it as: 健身 and 每日登入 are the only rows containing
 * `coins`, and every other row pays 碎片. `admin-test` may pay both because putting the save into an
 * arbitrary state is what 管理員測試模式 is FOR — and it is unreachable for a player (see AdminOnly).
 *
 * Adding a source without adding a row here means it can grant no currency at all, which is the
 * safe direction to fail in: a new reward that pays nothing is noticed immediately, a new reward
 * that quietly mints gold is not.
 *
 * ## 每日登入 was given `coins` on 2026-09-17, and that is a real concession
 *
 * 「金幣只有一個來源」 was the rule this table was written to enforce, and the file doc above still
 * says so in three places because it is still very nearly true. What changed is the seven-day round
 * (constants/dailyLogin.ts): four of its days can now pay 15 金幣, because a round where every
 * outcome is a resource the player cannot spend in the ordinary shop reads as a consolation prize
 * seven days running.
 *
 * What makes it survivable is the SIZE, and the size is the thing to defend rather than the rule:
 * at most 60 金幣 a week, against a short workout's 8–16 for one session
 * (constants/workoutRewards.ts). A player who opens the app every day for a week and never trains
 * has earned roughly four minutes of exercise. That is a greeting, not an income — the failure this
 * rule exists to prevent is 「開 app 比運動好賺」, and 60 a week is two orders of magnitude away
 * from it.
 *
 * The number is therefore load-bearing in a way the permission is not. Raising DAILY_PRIZE_COINS
 * is not a tuning change: it is a re-decision of this paragraph, and the rule it is spending was
 * built to have teeth.
 */
export const SOURCE_CURRENCY_POLICY: Record<RewardSource, readonly CurrencyId[]> = {
  workout: ['coins'],
  'daily-login': ['coins', 'fragments'],
  wheel: ['fragments'],
  newbie: ['fragments'],
  event: ['fragments'],
  quest: ['fragments'],
  'island-interaction': ['fragments'],
  'admin-test': ['coins', 'fragments'],
};

/** One thing granted. A discriminated union so an item grant can never be read as an amount. */
export type Reward =
  | { kind: 'currency'; currency: CurrencyId; amount: number }
  /** A catalog id (constants/items.ts). Quantity is 1 for everything own-once. */
  | { kind: 'item'; itemId: string; quantity: number }
  /**
   * 功能卡 (constants/utilityCards.ts) — a card that goes into the bag, to be used later.
   *
   * Its own member rather than a flavour of `item` because the two are stored in different places
   * and obey different rules: an item lands in `inventory` and is own-once or stock-counted, while
   * a card lands in `utilityCards.owned` as a count with a cap. Collapsing them would mean every
   * reader of a grant having to ask which kind of id it is holding.
   */
  | { kind: 'utility-card'; cardId: UtilityCardId; quantity: number }
  /** 經驗值. Not a currency — it is never spent, so it has no wallet and no policy row. */
  | { kind: 'xp'; amount: number };

/**
 * A reward plus the story of why it is being paid. This is what the economy service takes.
 *
 * `idempotencyKey` is optional because not every grant needs one — an admin button pressed twice
 * meaning twice is correct. Where a grant MUST be paid at most once (a workout, a login day), the
 * caller supplies a key derived from the event, and the guard lives with whoever owns that event's
 * record: this file does not keep a ledger.
 */
export interface RewardGrant {
  reward: Reward;
  source: RewardSource;
  /** Free-form detail for the log line — a workout id, a day index, a pool id. */
  reason?: string;
  idempotencyKey?: string;
}

/** Why a grant was refused, when it was refused before anything was written. */
export type RewardPolicyError =
  /** The source is not allowed to pay this currency. See {@link SOURCE_CURRENCY_POLICY}. */
  | 'currency-not-allowed-for-source'
  /** Zero, negative, fractional or non-finite. A grant of nothing is a bug, not a no-op. */
  | 'invalid-amount';

export type RewardPolicyResult = { ok: true } | { ok: false; error: RewardPolicyError; message: string };

/**
 * Whether this grant is allowed to happen at all — the gate every write goes through.
 *
 * Called by the economy service BEFORE it touches the save, so a refused grant leaves nothing
 * behind: no balance moved, no record written, nothing announced. It is deliberately a pure
 * function so the admin panel and the tests can ask the same question without a profile.
 */
export function checkGrant(grant: RewardGrant): RewardPolicyResult {
  const { reward, source } = grant;

  if (reward.kind === 'currency') {
    const allowed = SOURCE_CURRENCY_POLICY[source] ?? [];
    if (!allowed.includes(reward.currency)) {
      return {
        ok: false,
        error: 'currency-not-allowed-for-source',
        message:
          `${REWARD_SOURCE_LABELS[source] ?? source} 不得發放 ${reward.currency}` +
          `（允許：${allowed.join('、') || '無'}）— 見 constants/rewards.ts 的 SOURCE_CURRENCY_POLICY`,
      };
    }
  }

  const amount =
    reward.kind === 'item' || reward.kind === 'utility-card' ? reward.quantity : reward.amount;
  if (!Number.isFinite(amount) || amount <= 0 || !Number.isInteger(amount)) {
    return { ok: false, error: 'invalid-amount', message: `獎勵數量不合法：${amount}` };
  }

  return { ok: true };
}

/** One line describing a grant, for `console` and the admin readout. Never shown to a player. */
export function describeGrant(grant: RewardGrant): string {
  const who = REWARD_SOURCE_LABELS[grant.source] ?? grant.source;
  const what =
    grant.reward.kind === 'currency'
      ? `${grant.reward.amount} ${grant.reward.currency}`
      : grant.reward.kind === 'xp'
        ? `${grant.reward.amount} XP`
        : grant.reward.kind === 'utility-card'
          ? `功能卡 ${grant.reward.cardId} ×${grant.reward.quantity}`
          : `${grant.reward.itemId} ×${grant.reward.quantity}`;
  return `[reward] ${who} → ${what}${grant.reason ? ` (${grant.reason})` : ''}`;
}
```

```ts
export function parseUnlockedRooms(unlockedRoomsRaw: string[] | undefined): RoomInstance[] {
  const rooms: RoomInstance[] = [];
```
