## src/context/useIslandLife.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { useCallback, useRef } from 'react';
import { db, doc, updateDoc, handleFirestoreError, OperationType } from '../lib/firebase';
import type { AuthUser } from '../auth/types';
import type { UserProfile } from '../types';
import { getPlayerHome } from '../hooks/usePlayerHome';
import { getPetSpec } from '../constants/pets';
import {
  IslandEnvironmentState,
  OfflineStageId,
  PET_HOME_STATE,
  PET_MOODS,
  SEEN_HEARTBEAT_MS,
  makePetState,
  pickReturnLine,
  resolveOfflineReturn,
  resolvePetMood,
  stageForHours,
  vitalityForHours,
} from '../constants/islandReturn';
import {
  newPetCareState,
  petCondition,
  readPetCareState,
  readPetCareStates,
  settlePetCare,
  type PetCareState,
} from '../constants/petCare';
import { equippedPetId, equippedPetIds } from './usePetCare';
import {
  growOvergrowth,
  summariseOvergrowth,
  tidyOvergrowthAt,
} from '../lib/islandOvergrowth';

/**
 * 離線回歸 — the writes, and the one calculation that runs when a player arrives.
 *
 * Split out of AppContext for the same reason useEconomyActions and useHomeActions were: the
 * provider should not be one block in which the wallet, the house and the weather all live
 * together. Everything here goes through the same `updateDoc` path as every other save, touches
 * exactly one profile field (`islandState`), and can be refused without costing the player
 * anything — which is the point of a feature whose entire output is decoration.
 *
 * ## What is deliberately NOT here
 *
 * No currency, no XP, no inventory, no placement writes. Tidying pays nothing and losing an
 * absence costs nothing; the reward for coming back is that the island is yours to put right. If
 * a future pass wants to pay for tidying, it belongs in useEconomyActions with every other grant,
 * not smuggled into the environment layer.
 */

/**
 * The greeting a returning player is shown, assembled once at arrival.
 *
 * A resolved value rather than a pointer at the state, because the panel must keep saying the
 * same thing while the player is reading it: the moment they walk out and tidy the first patch,
 * the island's state no longer describes the absence they just came back from.
 */
export interface IslandReturnEvent {
  hours: number;
  days: number;
  stageId: OfflineStageId;
  /** One of the stage's lines, picked by seed — see constants/islandReturn.ts. */
  line: string;
  /** 「落葉 x5・雜草 x3」, or empty when the island grew nothing new this time. */
  summary: string;
  /** What to say about the companion, or null when there is none or nothing to say. */
  petLine: string | null;
}

/**
 * 離線褪色的恢復 — the transient half of the environment state, held in memory for one session.
 *
 * Deliberately NOT part of {@link IslandEnvironmentState} and deliberately never written to the
 * save. The brief's §12 is explicit that there must be no persisted 「正在播放恢復動畫」 flag, and
 * this shape is what that rule looks like: two numbers, created at arrival, thrown away when the
 * tab closes. A player who leaves halfway through simply measures a shorter absence next time and
 * gets a shallower drain — the correct answer, arrived at by having nothing to reconcile.
 */
export interface IslandRecovery {
  /** Whole hours this arrival measured. The only input to the colour curve. */
  hours: number;
  /** Whether to play the recovery, or hold the arrival state for an admin to look at. */
  play: boolean;
  /** Distinguishes one arrival (or one admin press) from the next, so the veil restarts cleanly. */
  token: number;
}

/** What an arrival produced: the state to persist, and the greeting to show (if any). */
export interface IslandArrival {
  state: IslandEnvironmentState;
  event: IslandReturnEvent | null;
  /**
   * How long the absence was, in whole hours — the input the colour drain reads.
   *
   * Returned rather than re-derived by the caller so that 「島上長出了多少」 and 「畫面褪了多少色」
   * are answers to the same measurement of the same absence, taken once. Zero for a first sighting.
   */
  offlineHours: number;
}

/** The island's XZ scale at a given territory level — the same derivation the scene uses. */
function islandScaleFor(profile: UserProfile): number {
  return 1 + ((profile.territoryLevel ?? 1) - 1) * 0.4;
}

/**
 * Whether this player has a companion out on the island.
 *
 * Asks the shared definition (context/usePetCare.ts) rather than re-testing `equippedItems` here,
 * which is what it used to do. Two copies of 「什麼算是一隻寵物」 is how a screen that stops offering
 * to feed an animal and a panel that still greets one end up disagreeing about the same save.
 */
function hasCompanion(profile: UserProfile): boolean {
  return equippedPetIds(profile).length > 0;
}

/**
 * Every companion's 照護狀態, brought up to `nowMs`.
 *
 * Two things get folded together here, and only one of them is arithmetic:
 *
 *  - the stored map is settled entry by entry, which is what makes the save reflect what the player
 *    is about to see rather than what they left behind;
 *  - the PRIMARY companion, if it has no entry yet, inherits the pre-multi-pet single `care`. That
 *    is the migration, and running it at arrival means it happens once, at login, on the path that
 *    was going to write `islandState.pet` anyway — rather than lazily inside a render.
 *
 * An animal the player owns but has never had out gets nothing here: it acquires an entry the first
 * time it is fed. An absent entry already reads as 「還沒餓過」 everywhere (context/usePetCare.ts's
 * `rawPetCare`), so writing full states for pets sitting in a wardrobe would only make the save
 * bigger.
 */
function settleAllPetCare(profile: UserProfile, nowMs: number): Record<string, PetCareState> {
  const pet = profile.islandState?.pet;
  const cares = readPetCareStates(pet?.cares, nowMs);
  const primary = equippedPetId(profile);
  if (primary && !cares[primary] && pet?.care) cares[primary] = readPetCareState(pet.care, nowMs);
  const settled: Record<string, PetCareState> = {};
  for (const [id, state] of Object.entries(cares)) settled[id] = settlePetCare(state, nowMs);
  return settled;
}

/**
 * Works out what the island did while this player was away, from their saved profile.
 *
 * A pure function taking the profile, NOT a hook, because the two places that need it cannot both
 * be a hook: it runs inside AppContext's profile load (before the profile is state at all) and
 * again from the admin's offline simulator. Given the same profile and the same instant it always
 * produces the same answer, which is what makes the simulator a real test of the live path rather
 * than a second implementation of it.
 *
 * A first sighting — no `lastSeenAt`, which is every brand-new player and every save written
 * before this feature existed — stamps the clock and does nothing else. That is the brief's §15,
 * and it is why the check is for a missing timestamp rather than for a missing profile: a save
 * from last year has never been *away*, it has only never been *seen*.
 */
export function resolveIslandArrival(profile: UserProfile, now: Date = new Date()): IslandArrival {
  const previous = profile.islandState ?? {};
  const stamp = now.toISOString();
  const ret = resolveOfflineReturn(previous.lastSeenAt, now);

  if (ret.isFirstSighting) {
    // A first sighting stamps the clock and does nothing else — including to the pet. Its care
    // state is created full (a brand-new companion is not hungry) and, crucially, is stamped as of
    // NOW: a save that predates the care system has no `updatedAt` to measure from, and giving one
    // an anchor in the past would charge a player for every day the feature did not exist.
    //
    // The per-pet map is RE-STAMPED rather than carried through, for that same reason: a save from
    // before the care system has no `lastSeenAt`, so every state in it — however it got there — is
    // anchored to a moment this feature was not measuring, and the honest answer to 「牠餓了多久」
    // is 「還沒開始算」. Re-stamping keeps the entries (so a household of three stays a household of
    // three) and moves each of their clocks to now.
    const stamped = Object.fromEntries(
      Object.keys(readPetCareStates(previous.pet?.cares, now.getTime())).map((id) => [
        id,
        newPetCareState(now.getTime()),
      ]),
    );
    const pet = previous.pet
      ? makePetState(
          previous.pet.mood,
          previous.pet.vitality,
          previous.pet.lastGreetedAt,
          previous.pet.care ?? newPetCareState(now.getTime()),
          stamped,
        )
      : makePetState(
          PET_HOME_STATE.mood,
          PET_HOME_STATE.vitality,
          undefined,
          newPetCareState(now.getTime()),
          {},
        );
    return {
      state: { ...previous, lastSeenAt: stamp, pet },
      event: null,
      offlineHours: 0,
    };
  }

  const before = previous.sprouts ?? [];
  const sprouts = growOvergrowth({
    existing: before,
    hours: ret.hours,
    // ResolvedHome is structurally a HomeObstacle — see utils/placementRules.ts, which declares
    // the shape locally so the solver stays free of React.
    home: getPlayerHome(profile),
    islandScale: islandScaleFor(profile),
    placements: profile.islandPlacements ?? [],
  });

  const mood = resolvePetMood(ret.hours, { justReturned: ret.shouldGreet });
  /**
   * 寵物照護, brought up to date — the whole of 「離線期間寵物狀態怎麼變」 (brief §16).
   *
   * There is no offline code path, and that is the design: the care state carries the moment it was
   * last true, so settling it against `now` gives what an absence did to it in exactly the same
   * arithmetic that covers a tab left open over lunch. Nothing counted down while the player was
   * gone, and nothing had to.
   *
   * It is settled HERE, on arrival, rather than only being read lazily, so the save reflects what
   * the player is about to see. Every other reader settles again for itself and lands on the same
   * answer — see `settlePetCare` on why calling it twice is free.
   *
   * Every animal in the household, not just the one out front (§6): the state is a map keyed by
   * companion id, and each entry is settled against the same instant. Settling them all costs a
   * couple of arithmetic operations per pet and keeps 「牠餓了嗎」 an answer about THAT animal.
   */
  const cares = settleAllPetCare(profile, now.getTime());
  /** The animal the arrival panel is talking about — the one that will be standing there. */
  const care = cares[equippedPetId(profile) ?? ''] ?? newPetCareState(now.getTime());
  const state: IslandEnvironmentState = {
    ...previous,
    lastSeenAt: stamp,
    sprouts,
    // Through the builder, never as an object literal: `lastGreetedAt` is absent for a pet that
    // has never been greeted, and an explicit `undefined` is what Firestore refuses. See
    // makePetState — that one field is enough to make this entire feature silently not exist.
    pet: makePetState(
      mood,
      vitalityForHours(ret.hours),
      previous.pet?.lastGreetedAt,
      previous.pet?.care,
      cares,
    ),
  };

  if (!ret.shouldGreet) return { state, event: null, offlineHours: ret.hours };

  state.lastReturnAt = stamp;
  state.lastReturnStage = ret.stage.id;
  state.lastReturnHours = ret.hours;

  // What grew THIS time. growOvergrowth appends, so the tail is the new growth — and when an
  // absence adds nothing (the ceiling was already reached, or the island had nowhere left to put
  // anything) the panel falls back to describing what is standing there, so a returning player is
  // never told about an island that grew nothing while looking at one covered in weeds.
  const fresh = sprouts.slice(before.length);
  const summary = summariseOvergrowth(fresh.length > 0 ? fresh : sprouts);

  return {
    state,
    offlineHours: ret.hours,
    event: {
      hours: ret.hours,
      days: ret.days,
      stageId: ret.stage.id,
      line: pickReturnLine(ret.stage, now.getTime() / 60000),
      summary,
      // The mood's line first, and the care band's only when the animal is at the bottom of the
      // ladder. Two sentences about the same pet on every return would read as a status report;
      // 「餓了」 is worth saying exactly when it is the thing the player can do something about.
      petLine: hasCompanion(profile)
        ? [PET_MOODS[mood].greeting, petCondition(care).band.id === 'drowsy' ? '牠的碗空了，餵一點東西吧。' : null]
            .filter(Boolean)
            .join('') || null
        : null,
    },
  };
}

export function useIslandLife(
  user: AuthUser | null,
  profile: UserProfile | null,
  /** Writes a value the database has already accepted into local state — see AppContext. */
  applyProfilePatch: (updates: Partial<UserProfile>) => void,
  /** Hands the arrival greeting to whoever is showing it (AppContext holds it as state). */
  publishReturn: (event: IslandReturnEvent | null) => void,
  /**
   * Hands the colour recovery to whoever is drawing it. In-memory only — see {@link IslandRecovery}
   * for why this one deliberately does not travel with the rest of the island state.
   */
  publishRecovery: (recovery: IslandRecovery | null) => void,
) {
  /**
   * When `lastSeenAt` was last pushed to the save, so the heartbeat can stay off the wire.
   *
   * Seeded to NOW rather than to zero, because the arrival write that runs moments after this hook
   * mounts has already stamped it. Starting at zero makes the very first beat — which a single tab
   * switch is enough to trigger — a duplicate of a write that just happened.
   */
  const lastStampRef = useRef(Date.now());
  const uid = user?.uid ?? null;

  /**
   * Persists a change to `islandState`, keeping local state and the save in step.
   *
   * Optimistic, and rolled back on refusal, exactly like AppContext's updateProfile: everything
   * this feature writes is something the player can already SEE on the island, so waiting for a
   * round trip before the weeds disappear would make tidying feel broken on a slow connection.
   *
   * `fields` is what actually goes to Firestore and `next` is what the screen should show. They
   * are separate arguments because the two callers want different granularity, and the difference
   * matters: the heartbeat is re-stamping `lastSeenAt` every few minutes WHILE the player is out
   * tidying, so a tidy that wrote the whole map would carry a stale timestamp back over a fresher
   * one. The per-field callers below therefore write `islandState.sprouts` / `islandState.pet`
   * alone, and only the arrival — which genuinely replaces all of it in one go — writes the map.
   */
  const writeIslandState = useCallback(
    async (fields: Record<string, unknown>, next: IslandEnvironmentState, label: string): Promise<boolean> => {
      if (!uid || !profile) return false;
      const rollback = profile.islandState;
      applyProfilePatch({ islandState: next });
      try {
        await updateDoc(doc(db, 'users', uid), fields);
        return true;
      } catch (error) {
        applyProfilePatch({ islandState: rollback });
        console.warn(`[island] ${label} 沒有存檔成功：`, error);
        handleFirestoreError(error, OperationType.UPDATE, `users/${uid}`);
        return false;
      }
    },
    [uid, profile, applyProfilePatch],
  );

  /**
   * Re-stamps "I am here", at most once per {@link SEEN_HEARTBEAT_MS}.
   *
   * A dotted-path write, so it cannot disturb the sprouts or the pet sitting beside it in the same
   * map. It also deliberately does NOT touch local state: the value is only ever read at the next
   * login, so pushing it into the profile would re-render the world every few minutes to carry a
   * string nothing on screen is looking at.
   *
   * The throttle is a ref rather than a timer, so every caller — the interval, the tab coming
   * back — funnels through one rate limit instead of each having its own.
   */
  const markSeen = useCallback(async (): Promise<void> => {
    if (!uid) return;
    const nowMs = Date.now();
    if (nowMs - lastStampRef.current < SEEN_HEARTBEAT_MS) return;
    lastStampRef.current = nowMs;
    try {
      await updateDoc(doc(db, 'users', uid), {
        'islandState.lastSeenAt': new Date(nowMs).toISOString(),
      });
    } catch (error) {
      // Deliberately quiet. A missed beat costs at most a slightly longer measured absence next
      // time, which is invisible against a ladder whose first threshold is twelve hours — not
      // worth a red banner over the player's island.
      console.warn('[island] 上線時間戳記沒有寫入：', error);
    }
  }, [uid]);

  /**
   * Clears the overgrowth the player is standing in. Returns how many pieces went.
   *
   * The reach test is `lib/islandOvergrowth.ts`'s, the same one the floating prompt asks before it
   * offers the action, so a badge can never promise a tidy that finds nothing to do.
   */
  const tidyIslandAt = useCallback(
    async (x: number, z: number): Promise<number> => {
      if (!profile) return 0;
      const sprouts = profile.islandState?.sprouts ?? [];
      if (sprouts.length === 0) return 0;

      const { sprouts: kept, removed } = tidyOvergrowthAt(sprouts, x, z, getPlayerHome(profile));
      if (removed.length === 0) return 0;

      const ok = await writeIslandState(
        { 'islandState.sprouts': kept },
        { ...profile.islandState, sprouts: kept },
        '整理環境',
      );
      // Zero on a refused write, not the count that was rolled back: the caller uses this to
      // decide whether to congratulate the player, and the weeds are back on their screen.
      return ok ? removed.length : 0;
    },
    [profile, writeIslandState],
  );

  /**
   * The companion has seen its owner again — back to normal.
   *
   * Called by Three/IslandPet.tsx once the animal has actually reached the player, not when the
   * greeting panel is dismissed: the reunion is a thing that happens in the world, and clearing it
   * from a button press would end the moment before it had been seen.
   */
  const greetPet = useCallback(async (): Promise<void> => {
    if (!profile) return;
    if (profile.islandState?.pet?.mood === 'lively') return;
    // The care state rides through untouched. A reunion says 「你回來了」, not 「你餵過牠了」 — an
    // animal that arrives at its owner's feet with a full bowl is the free meal this whole feature
    // is careful not to hand out, and dropping the field here would have done exactly that by
    // making the next read treat it as a never-fed pet.
    const pet = makePetState(
      PET_HOME_STATE.mood,
      PET_HOME_STATE.vitality,
      new Date().toISOString(),
      profile.islandState?.pet?.care,
      profile.islandState?.pet?.cares,
    );
    await writeIslandState({ 'islandState.pet': pet }, { ...profile.islandState, pet }, '寵物狀態');
  }, [profile, writeIslandState]);

  /**
   * 管理員測試 — rewinds the last sighting by `days` and replays the arrival for real.
   *
   * It does not fabricate a result: it moves the one timestamp the feature measures from and then
   * runs {@link resolveIslandArrival}, the same function the login path runs, so what the tester
   * sees is what a player who was genuinely away that long would see. That is why the simulator is
   * worth having at all — a shortcut that painted the outcome directly would be a second
   * implementation, and would pass while the real one was broken.
   */
  const simulateOfflineDays = useCallback(
    async (days: number): Promise<boolean> => {
      if (!profile) return false;
      const rewound = new Date(Date.now() - days * 86_400_000).toISOString();
      const arrival = resolveIslandArrival(
        { ...profile, islandState: { ...profile.islandState, lastSeenAt: rewound } },
        new Date(),
      );
      const ok = await writeIslandState({ islandState: arrival.state }, arrival.state, '離線模擬');
      if (ok) {
        publishReturn(arrival.event);
        // The same hour count the growth was sited from, so the tester sees one absence expressed
        // two ways rather than two features that happen to have been pressed at the same time.
        publishRecovery({ hours: arrival.offlineHours, play: true, token: performance.now() });
      }
      return ok;
    },
    [profile, writeIslandState, publishReturn, publishRecovery],
  );

  /** 管理員測試 — back to a clean island and a lively pet, without touching anything else. */
  const resetIslandEnvironment = useCallback(async (): Promise<boolean> => {
    if (!profile) return false;
    publishReturn(null);
    publishRecovery(null);
    const next: IslandEnvironmentState = {
      ...profile.islandState,
      lastSeenAt: new Date().toISOString(),
      sprouts: [],
      // A fed, rested animal — not a pet with the care field stripped off. An absent state reads
      // as 「從沒餓過」 which is the same outcome, but the tester pressing 重置 needs to be able to
      // see the numbers they just reset rather than an empty map.
      //
      // EVERY companion, not just the one out front: 重置環境 means 「回到乾淨的島和一隻精神很好的
      // 寵物」, and a reset that left the cat listless because it happened not to be equipped would
      // be a reset the tester has to do twice and cannot tell has only half happened.
      pet: makePetState(
        PET_HOME_STATE.mood,
        PET_HOME_STATE.vitality,
        undefined,
        newPetCareState(Date.now()),
        Object.fromEntries(
          Object.keys(readPetCareStates(profile.islandState?.pet?.cares, Date.now())).map((id) => [
            id,
            newPetCareState(Date.now()),
          ]),
        ),
      ),
    };
    return writeIslandState({ islandState: next }, next, '重置環境');
  }, [profile, writeIslandState, publishReturn, publishRecovery]);

  /**
   * 管理員測試 — puts the screen at the colour a given absence drains to, without touching the save.
   *
   * The only thing in this file that writes nothing at all, and the only admin control that is
   * allowed to skip {@link resolveIslandArrival}: the colour drain is a pure function of hours and
   * is not persisted, so there is no state here for a shortcut to get out of step with. Everything
   * it can express, a real absence of `hours` would express identically — the panel obtains its
   * hour counts from the production curve's own inverse rather than inventing levels.
   *
   * `hours: null` ends the preview (「恢復完成」); `play: false` holds the arrival state on screen
   * so a level can actually be looked at instead of flashing past.
   */
  const previewIslandColour = useCallback(
    (hours: number | null, play = false) => {
      publishRecovery(hours === null ? null : { hours, play, token: performance.now() });
    },
    [publishRecovery],
  );

  return {
    markSeen,
    tidyIslandAt,
    greetPet,
    simulateOfflineDays,
    resetIslandEnvironment,
    previewIslandColour,
  };
}

/** Admin readout: what the current absence would be called. Never shown to an ordinary player. */
export function describeOfflineStage(hours: number): string {
  return stageForHours(hours).label;
}
```

## src/context/useLimitedShop.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { db, doc, updateDoc, handleFirestoreError, OperationType } from '../lib/firebase';
import { publishMerchantPurchase } from '../lib/playerBus';
import type { AuthUser } from '../auth/types';
import type { AppSettings, UserProfile } from '../types';
import { currencyPatch, getBalance } from '../constants/currency';
import { buildSpendUpdate } from './useEconomyActions';
import { fragmentPatchForPurchase } from './useFragmentActions';
import { isStackableItem, ownsItem } from '../utils/inventory';
import { getRaffleTickets } from '../constants/fragments';
import { getOwnedCardCount, getUtilityCard, grantCards } from '../constants/utilityCards';
import {
  checkPurchase,
  currentRotation,
  findOffer,
  getOfferPrice,
  recordPurchase,
  type LimitedOffer,
  type LimitedRotation,
} from '../constants/limitedShopRotation';
import { getPurchasedCount } from '../constants/limitedShop';

/**
 * 限時商店的購買寫入 —— 這家店唯一一條買東西的路。
 *
 * 刻意是 context/useShopActions.ts 的**兄弟**而不是它裡面的一個分支。兩家店收不同的貨幣、遵守
 * 不同的限制、交付不同**種類**的東西，而且限時商店賣的是一個「這一檔算出來的組合包」而不是一件
 * 目錄商品；把輪替、購買額度與整包卡牌的發放塞進普通商店最單純的那條路，等於讓每一次買帽子都
 * 帶著這些東西跑。兩者**共用**的是真正重要的部分 —— 扣款走經濟服務的 {@link buildSpendUpdate}、
 * 背包寫入遵守同一條堆疊/去重規則（utils/inventory.ts）、碎片清算是同一個 helper —— 所以「購買
 * 的行為」不可能在兩家店之間走鐘。
 *
 * ## 一條路，所有商品類型（§20/§22）
 *
 * 下面只有一個函數，而且它**不**去分辨在買哪一個商品，只看 Offer 的 `grant` 說要交付什麼
 * （constants/limitedShopRotation.ts）。之後要加「活動限定家具」或「碎片包」是 `LimitedGrant`
 * 多一個成員加這裡多一個 arm，不是第二套購買流程。
 *
 * ## 整包，不能拆（§4/§7/§17）
 *
 * 買的單位是一個 Offer，不是「幾份」。畫面上沒有數量選擇器，這裡也沒有 quantity 參數 —— 一包
 * 三張就是三張，扣一次整包價、發三張。要拆包唯一的方法是改資料讓它變成一包一張，這也正是應該
 * 的方式。
 *
 * ## 全部落在同一次寫入
 *
 * 扣款、商品、購買紀錄在同一個 `updateDoc` 裡。扣了錢沒拿到東西、拿到東西沒扣錢都是修不回來
 * 的，而「算進限購但沒付錢」是同一個 bug 的第三種樣子。
 */

/** 沒買成的理由，讓對話框可以講一句具體的話。 */
export type LimitedPurchaseResult =
  | 'ok'
  | 'unknown-offer'
  /** 不在**這一檔**架上 —— 從打開商店到按下購買之間換檔了。 */
  | 'not-on-sale'
  | 'limit-reached'
  | 'insufficient-funds'
  /** 一件「擁有一次」的目錄商品，玩家已經有了。 */
  | 'already-owned'
  /** 卡牌上限（constants/utilityCards.ts）裝不下**整包**。 */
  | 'card-limit-reached'
  | 'error';

/** 每一種結果對玩家講什麼。這段文案只住在這裡。 */
export const LIMITED_PURCHASE_MESSAGES: Record<LimitedPurchaseResult, string> = {
  ok: '購買成功',
  'unknown-offer': '這個商品已經不存在了',
  'not-on-sale': '這個商品已經下架，等待下次返場',
  'limit-reached': '本檔期已達購買上限',
  'insufficient-funds': '餘額不足',
  'already-owned': '你已經擁有這個商品',
  'card-limit-reached': '卡牌數量已達上限，這一包放不下',
  error: '購買失敗，請稍後再試',
};

export function useLimitedShop(
  user: AuthUser | null,
  profile: UserProfile | null,
  /** 只給碎片清算用 —— 見 `fragmentPatchForPurchase`。 */
  settings: AppSettings | null,
  /** 把已被接受的值直接寫進本地狀態 —— 見 AppContext 的 applyProfilePatch。 */
  applyProfilePatch: (updates: Partial<UserProfile>) => void,
) {
  /**
   * 買下這一檔的一個 Offer，用它其中一條付款路線。
   *
   * 每一道檢查都在**寫入這裡**做，站在按鈕已經顯示過的狀態後面：貨架是從時鐘重新推導出來的，
   * 而不是相信呼叫端傳來的，所以換檔之後才送到的購買會被拒絕，而不是安靜地買下一個已經不在架
   * 上的東西 —— 更重要的是，價格與張數也是重新算出來的，畫面上顯示的那一份永遠不會是權威。
   */
  const buyLimitedOffer = async (
    offerId: string,
    priceId: string,
  ): Promise<LimitedPurchaseResult> => {
    if (!user || !profile) return 'error';

    const rotation: LimitedRotation = currentRotation(Date.now());
    const offer = findOffer(rotation, offerId);
    if (!offer) return 'not-on-sale';
    const price = getOfferPrice(offer, priceId);
    if (!price) return 'unknown-offer';

    // Every rule about whether this purchase may happen lives in ONE pure function
    // (constants/limitedShopRotation.ts), so it can be tested without a Firestore and so this file
    // is only ever about the WRITE. All this half does is read the numbers off the profile.
    const card = offer.grant.kind === 'utility-card' ? getUtilityCard(offer.grant.cardId) : null;
    const itemId = offer.grant.kind === 'item' ? offer.grant.itemId : null;
    const verdict = checkPurchase({
      rotation,
      offerId,
      priceId,
      purchased: getPurchasedCount(profile.limitedShop, rotation.id, offer.id),
      balance: getBalance(profile, price.currency),
      alreadyOwned: !!itemId && !isStackableItem(itemId) && ownsItem(profile, itemId),
      heldCards: card ? getOwnedCardCount(profile.utilityCards, card.id) : 0,
      maxCards: card?.maxOwned,
    });
    if (verdict !== 'ok') return verdict;

    const goods = buildGoodsUpdate(profile, settings, offer);
    if (typeof goods === 'string') return goods;

    const purchases = recordPurchase(profile.limitedShop, rotation, offer.id, 1);

    try {
      await updateDoc(doc(db, 'users', user.uid), {
        // 扣款走經濟服務，所以「一種貨幣住在哪個欄位」只有一個地方決定
        // （constants/currency.ts）—— 而且它跟商品在同一次寫入裡。
        ...(buildSpendUpdate(price.currency, price.amount) ?? {}),
        ...goods.fields,
        limitedShop: { ...(profile.limitedShop ?? {}), purchases },
      });
    } catch (error) {
      handleFirestoreError(error, OperationType.UPDATE, `users/${user.uid}`);
      return 'error';
    }

    // 寫入被接受之後才反映到本地，所以貨架、錢包與背包在同一幀一起動 —— 而且絕不會在存檔同意
    // 之前先動。
    applyProfilePatch({
      ...currencyPatch(profile, price.currency, getBalance(profile, price.currency) - price.amount),
      ...goods.patch,
      limitedShop: { ...(profile.limitedShop ?? {}), purchases },
    });

    // 交易成功 → 存檔接受 → 錢包與背包更新 → **然後**才告訴世界那一頭（§11）。
    //
    // 這一行放在這裡而不是放在對話框的 `result === 'ok'` 分支裡，理由是這裡才是唯一一條買得
    // 到東西的路：任何未來的呼叫端（活動、批次購買、機器人測試）都會經過這一行，而**沒有任何
    // 一條路徑**能在上面每一道檢查失敗時走到它。所以「購買失敗商人卻在慶祝」不是靠記得不要那
    // 樣寫，是根本沒有那條路。
    publishMerchantPurchase('limited-shop', price.currency, price.amount);
    return 'ok';
  };

  /**
   * 記下「這一趟商人到訪的招呼，跟這位玩家講過了」。
   *
   * 為什麼在**這個檔案**：它是限時商店唯一的寫入點，而這一格就住在限時商店自己的存檔 map
   * 裡（`limitedShop.greetedVisitId`）。放到別處會變成第二個知道這個 map 該長什麼樣的地方。
   *
   * 為什麼要存：不存的話，那句「一位旅行商人抵達了島嶼」會在**每一次**登入都再講一次，而
   * 一檔有兩個星期。一句每天都出現的到訪通知不是通知，是雜訊。
   *
   * 失敗就算了，不重試、不報錯：沒存到的代價是這句話多講一次，而為了一句招呼把一個錯誤訊
   * 息推到玩家臉上，比那句話本身更吵。回傳成功與否，讓呼叫端決定要不要記在本地。
   */
  const markMerchantGreeted = async (visitId: string): Promise<boolean> => {
    if (!user || !profile) return false;
    if (profile.limitedShop?.greetedVisitId === visitId) return true;

    const limitedShop = { ...(profile.limitedShop ?? {}), greetedVisitId: visitId };
    try {
      await updateDoc(doc(db, 'users', user.uid), { limitedShop });
    } catch (error) {
      handleFirestoreError(error, OperationType.UPDATE, `users/${user.uid}`);
      return false;
    }
    applyProfilePatch({ limitedShop });
    return true;
  };

  return { buyLimitedOffer, markMerchantGreeted };
}

/**
 * 交付商品的那幾個欄位，加上鏡射它們的本地 patch。
 *
 * 「可不可以買」的權威判斷是上面的 `checkPurchase`（constants/limitedShopRotation.ts，純函數、有
 * 測試）。這裡的兩道守衛是同樣兩件事在**真正組出寫入內容的那一刻**再讀一次 —— 那是它們確定還
 * 成立的唯一時刻。守不住時回傳一個 {@link LimitedPurchaseResult} 而不是丟例外，所以檢查與寫入
 * 之間萬一有落差，玩家看到的是一句誠實的訊息，而不是一筆扣款。
 */
function buildGoodsUpdate(
  profile: UserProfile,
  settings: AppSettings | null,
  offer: LimitedOffer,
): { fields: Record<string, unknown>; patch: Partial<UserProfile> } | LimitedPurchaseResult {
  if (offer.grant.kind === 'utility-card') {
    const { cardId, quantity } = offer.grant;
    const card = getUtilityCard(cardId);
    if (!card) return 'unknown-offer';

    // 整包放不下就整包不賣。`grantCards` 會樂意只發得下的那幾張，但在這裡那等於收整包的錢卻只
    // 給一部分 —— 組合包不能拆，退不了的那一半也一樣不能拆。
    if (getOwnedCardCount(profile.utilityCards, cardId) + quantity > card.maxOwned) {
      return 'card-limit-reached';
    }

    const result = grantCards(profile.utilityCards, cardId, quantity);
    if (result.granted < quantity) return 'card-limit-reached';
    return { fields: { utilityCards: result.state }, patch: { utilityCards: result.state } };
  }

  // 抽獎券 —— 這家店唯一一種「買到的不是東西，是餘額」的商品。
  //
  // 加的是 `raffleTickets`，也就是幸運轉盤直接讀的那個數字（constants/fragments.ts），不進
  // `inventory`：背包裡的一筆券是一筆什麼都不做的資料，轉盤永遠看不到它，而商店還會因此報
  // 「已擁有」一個玩家早就花掉的東西。
  //
  // 寫成絕對值而不是 `increment()`，跟普通商店賣券時同一個理由：它讀的是上面那一次餘額檢查用
  // 的同一份快照，所以兩者不可能對「這一次購買是什麼」有不同意見。
  if (offer.grant.kind === 'raffle-ticket') {
    const next = getRaffleTickets(profile) + offer.grant.quantity;
    return { fields: { raffleTickets: next }, patch: { raffleTickets: next } };
  }

  const itemId = offer.grant.itemId;
  const stackable = isStackableItem(itemId);
  if (!stackable && ownsItem(profile, itemId)) return 'already-owned';

  // 寫成明確的陣列而不是 `arrayUnion`，因為本地 patch 本來就需要同一個陣列，兩者必須一致。
  // 「擁有一次」的情況才去重，理由跟 context/useFragmentActions.ts 一樣：`inventory` 對可擺放的
  // 商品是**一份一筆**，整份去重會刪掉某個人的第二張沙發。
  const inventory = [...(profile.inventory ?? [])];
  if (stackable || !inventory.includes(itemId)) inventory.push(itemId);

  // 跟普通商店一樣的碎片清算，理由也一樣：東西一旦擁有了，為它收集的商品碎片再也解鎖不了任何
  // 東西。用哪一種貨幣付的不影響這件事 —— 殺掉那疊碎片的是「已經擁有了」，不是收銀台。
  const fragments = fragmentPatchForPurchase(profile, settings, itemId);

  return {
    fields: { inventory, ...fragments },
    patch: { inventory, ...fragments },
  };
}
```

## src/context/usePetCare.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { useCallback, useState } from 'react';
import { db, doc, updateDoc, handleFirestoreError, OperationType } from '../lib/firebase';
import type { AuthUser } from '../auth/types';
import type { UserProfile } from '../types';
import { consumableAcceptsSpecies, getConsumableSpec, petEffectsFrom } from '../constants/consumables';
import {
  applyPetCareEffects,
  newPetCareState,
  petCondition,
  readPetCareState,
  readPetCareStates,
  settlePetCare,
  withPetCare,
  type PetCareDelta,
  type PetCareState,
  type PetCondition,
} from '../constants/petCare';
import { PET_HOME_STATE, makePetState } from '../constants/islandReturn';
import { getPetSpec, getPetSpecies } from '../constants/pets';
import { getAvailableStock } from '../utils/inventory';
import { playSound, SoundEffect, triggerHaptic } from '../lib/soundUtils';

/**
 * 寵物照護 Service — the one place food leaves the backpack and a pet's state changes.
 *
 * The same shape as every other write service in this codebase (context/useUtilityCards.ts,
 * context/useFragmentActions.ts, context/useWorkoutRewards.ts) and here for the same reason: more
 * than one surface will eventually want to feed an animal (the panel, the in-world prompt, a future
 * NPC who hands you a treat), and every one of them has to spend the same copy, apply the same
 * clamps and write the same map. A second call site that touches `inventory` and `islandState.pet`
 * itself is a second set of those rules, and the first to drift wins silently.
 *
 * The RULES are pure functions in constants/petCare.ts; this file is only the write.
 *
 * ## One write, and why it has to be one
 *
 * A feed spends a bag AND restores the animal. Those cannot be two updates: a failure between them
 * either takes the food without feeding the pet or feeds it for free, and there is no way for the
 * player to tell which happened. So `inventory` and `islandState.pet` go in a single `updateDoc` —
 * the same reasoning that puts a 功能卡's spend in the same write as the reward it boosted.
 *
 * `islandState.pet` is written as a DOTTED path rather than as the whole `islandState` map, and that
 * is not tidiness either: the 「我還在」 heartbeat is re-stamping `islandState.lastSeenAt` every few
 * minutes while the player is out feeding, and a feed that wrote the whole map would carry a stale
 * timestamp back over a fresher one. Same rule context/useIslandLife.ts's partial writers follow.
 *
 * ## Nothing here is optimistic
 *
 * The bag empties only after the save is accepted — the rule stated in context/useUtilityCards.ts,
 * and it matters more here: a player who watches a bag disappear and then reappear has no way to
 * know whether their pet was actually fed.
 *
 * ## What this service deliberately does NOT do
 *
 * It never writes on a timer. Nutrition and energy decay are a function of `updatedAt` and the
 * clock (constants/petCare.ts), so the only things that ever write a care state are a feed and an
 * arrival. There is no heartbeat for the pet and there must not be one — see the brief's §16.
 */

/** What a feed did. Every `reason` except the last two is an ordinary state the UI explains. */
export type FeedPetOutcome =
  | {
      ok: true;
      itemId: string;
      /** WHICH animal was fed — so a toast can name it rather than saying 「牠」 in a three-pet house. */
      petItemId: string;
      delta: PetCareDelta;
      condition: PetCondition;
    }
  | {
      ok: false;
      reason:
        | 'no-profile'
        | 'not-consumable'
        | 'wrong-target'
        | 'wrong-species'
        | 'none-owned'
        | 'no-companion'
        | 'already-full'
        | 'save-failed';
    };

export type FeedPetError = Extract<FeedPetOutcome, { ok: false }>['reason'];

/** Why a feed was refused, in the player's words. The one place this copy is written. */
export const FEED_PET_MESSAGES: Record<FeedPetError, string> = {
  'no-profile': '尚未登入，沒辦法餵食',
  'not-consumable': '這個東西不能拿來餵寵物',
  'wrong-target': '這個東西不是給寵物用的',
  // A message the player should never actually read: every feeding surface lists only what the
  // animal in front of them can eat (§17), so reaching this means something offered a food it
  // should not have. It exists because the WRITE has to be safe on its own — a UI filter is a
  // convenience, not a rule.
  'wrong-species': '這種食物不適合這隻寵物',
  'none-owned': '你手上沒有這個了，先到商店補貨吧',
  'no-companion': '先在更衣室帶一隻寵物出場，才能餵牠',
  'already-full': '牠現在很飽，等牠餓一點再餵吧',
  'save-failed': '存檔失敗，飼料沒有被用掉',
};

/**
 * Every companion the player currently has out, in equipped order.
 *
 * The one definition of 「島上有哪些寵物」, and a LIST rather than a single id because §6 says the
 * species a player owns is not one global value. Today the dressing room equips one animal at a
 * time so this returns zero or one entry — but every caller downstream is already written against
 * a list, so the day a second slot opens, nothing here or above it has to be rewritten.
 */
export function equippedPetIds(profile: UserProfile | null | undefined): string[] {
  return (profile?.equippedItems ?? []).filter((id) => !!getPetSpec(id));
}

/**
 * The primary companion — the first one equipped, and the one a surface means when it does not say
 * which animal it is talking about.
 *
 * Kept as its own function rather than being spelled `equippedPetIds(profile)[0]` at eight call
 * sites, because 「沒有指定的時候是哪一隻」 is a rule and rules belong in one place.
 */
export function equippedPetId(profile: UserProfile | null | undefined): string | undefined {
  return equippedPetIds(profile)[0];
}

/**
 * The pet's care state as of `nowMs`, settled — what every reader should ask for.
 *
 * A read helper rather than a piece of state, for the reason `readLiveEffects` is one
 * (context/useUtilityCards.ts): the profile is the only copy, and a component that cached this would
 * be a second one that goes stale by the minute. Settling is a couple of arithmetic operations, so
 * this is cheap enough to call from a render or from a behaviour decision.
 */
export function readPetCare(
  profile: UserProfile | null | undefined,
  /** Which animal. Omitted means the primary companion — see {@link equippedPetId}. */
  petItemId: string | null | undefined,
  nowMs: number,
): PetCareState {
  return settlePetCare(rawPetCare(profile, petItemId, nowMs), nowMs);
}

/**
 * The stored state for one animal, unsettled, with the pre-multi-pet save folded in.
 *
 * The migration is this one branch and nothing else: a profile written before `cares` existed has a
 * single `care`, and it belonged to whichever animal was out at the time — which is the primary
 * companion. So the primary inherits it once, the first write puts the result in `cares`, and the
 * old field is never consulted for that animal again. Any OTHER animal starts fresh, which is what
 * a pet that has never been out is: 「還沒餓過」, exactly like one just bought.
 */
function rawPetCare(
  profile: UserProfile | null | undefined,
  petItemId: string | null | undefined,
  nowMs: number,
): PetCareState {
  const pet = profile?.islandState?.pet;
  const id = petItemId ?? equippedPetId(profile);
  const stored = id ? readPetCareStates(pet?.cares, nowMs)[id] : undefined;
  if (stored) return stored;
  if (id && id === equippedPetId(profile)) return readPetCareState(pet?.care, nowMs);
  return newPetCareState(nowMs);
}

/** The same thing, read as bands and multipliers. What every screen actually shows. */
export function readPetCondition(
  profile: UserProfile | null | undefined,
  petItemId: string | null | undefined,
  nowMs: number,
): PetCondition {
  return petCondition(readPetCare(profile, petItemId, nowMs));
}

/**
 * How full is 「too full to bother」.
 *
 * A feed that moves nothing has still spent a bag, and a player who watches that happen has been
 * charged for nothing. Refusing just under the ceiling is kinder than clamping silently, and it is
 * the one and only thing standing between a player and wasting food.
 */
const FULL_ENOUGH = 0.97;

export function usePetCare(
  user: AuthUser | null,
  profile: UserProfile | null,
  /** Writes an accepted value straight into local state — see AppContext's applyProfilePatch. */
  applyProfilePatch: (updates: Partial<UserProfile>) => void,
) {
  /**
   * 餵食模式 — the food the player has chosen but not yet given to the animal.
   *
   * Held in React state rather than on playerBus, unlike almost everything else the pet touches:
   * this changes when a button is pressed, not every frame, and the two things that read it (the
   * floating prompt and the HUD chip) are both ordinary components that re-render anyway. The bus is
   * for per-frame data that a `useFrame` loop is already sampling; putting a once-a-minute value
   * there would mean polling for it.
   *
   * It is also deliberately NOT persisted. Arming a feed is a thing you are in the middle of doing,
   * not a fact about your save — and a mode that survived a reload would leave a player wondering
   * why their pet prompt says something strange three days later.
   */
  const [pendingPetFood, setPendingPetFood] = useState<string | null>(null);

  const armPetFeeding = useCallback((itemId: string | null) => {
    setPendingPetFood(itemId);
  }, []);

  const cancelPetFeeding = useCallback(() => setPendingPetFood(null), []);

  /**
   * Feeds one serving to the companion. The single write path for every surface.
   *
   * Everything about WHAT the food does is the item's own definition — this function does not know
   * that 基礎飼料 restores 營養. It resolves the item's declared effects, hands them to the one
   * function that may change a care state, and writes the result.
   */
  const feedPet = useCallback(
    async (
      itemId: string,
      /**
       * WHICH animal is being fed. Omitted means the primary companion, which is what the pre-
       * multi-pet callers meant when they did not say.
       *
       * The whole of §21 is that this argument exists and is threaded from the thing the player is
       * standing next to (UI/PetInteractionPanel.tsx reads it off the prompt target), rather than
       * the feed resolving 「the pet」 for itself down here. A write that picked the animal on its
       * own could only ever pick one, and it would be the same one every time.
       */
      petItemId?: string,
    ): Promise<FeedPetOutcome> => {
      if (!user || !profile) return { ok: false, reason: 'no-profile' };

      const spec = getConsumableSpec(itemId);
      if (!spec) return { ok: false, reason: 'not-consumable' };
      if (spec.target !== 'pet') return { ok: false, reason: 'wrong-target' };
      const petId = petItemId ?? equippedPetId(profile);
      // Not merely 「有沒有寵物」: the named animal has to be one the player actually has out, or a
      // stale panel left open across an unequip would feed a companion that is not there.
      if (!petId || !equippedPetIds(profile).includes(petId)) {
        return { ok: false, reason: 'no-companion' };
      }
      const species = getPetSpecies(petId);
      // Compatibility enforced at the WRITE, not only in the list that offered it. The filter above
      // this is what the player experiences (§5, §17); this is what makes it true.
      if (species && !consumableAcceptsSpecies(spec, species)) {
        return { ok: false, reason: 'wrong-species' };
      }
      // The same derived stock every other screen reads (utils/inventory.ts), not a count of its
      // own: 「我還有幾包」 must have one answer, and the shop's badge is already showing it.
      if (getAvailableStock(profile, itemId) <= 0) return { ok: false, reason: 'none-owned' };

      const nowMs = Date.now();
      const current = readPetCare(profile, petId, nowMs);
      if (current.nutrition >= FULL_ENOUGH && current.energy >= FULL_ENOUGH) {
        return { ok: false, reason: 'already-full' };
      }

      const { state: care, delta } = applyPetCareEffects(current, petEffectsFrom(spec.effects), nowMs);

      // One copy leaves the flat inventory list. `indexOf`/`splice` rather than a filter, because a
      // filter would remove EVERY bag the player owns — the list holds one entry per copy (see
      // utils/inventory.ts), so removing a stack means removing exactly one element of it.
      const inventory = [...(profile.inventory ?? [])];
      const at = inventory.indexOf(itemId);
      if (at < 0) return { ok: false, reason: 'none-owned' };
      inventory.splice(at, 1);

      const previous = profile.islandState?.pet;
      const pet = makePetState(
        previous?.mood ?? PET_HOME_STATE.mood,
        previous?.vitality ?? PET_HOME_STATE.vitality,
        previous?.lastGreetedAt,
        // The legacy field rides through unchanged — see PetLifeState.care. It is not updated,
        // because the animal this feed belongs to is named and its state goes in the map below.
        previous?.care,
        // Only THIS animal's entry changes — §21 in one call. See withPetCare on why that is a
        // named function rather than a spread written out here.
        withPetCare(previous?.cares, petId, care, nowMs),
      );

      try {
        await updateDoc(doc(db, 'users', user.uid), {
          inventory,
          // Dotted, so the heartbeat's `islandState.lastSeenAt` and the sprouts beside it are not
          // carried back to whatever they were when this profile was loaded. See the file doc.
          'islandState.pet': pet,
          lastUpdated: new Date(nowMs).toISOString(),
        });
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('[pet] 餵食沒有存檔成功：', error);
        handleFirestoreError(error, OperationType.UPDATE, `users/${user.uid}`);
        return { ok: false, reason: 'save-failed' };
      }

      applyProfilePatch({
        inventory,
        islandState: { ...profile.islandState, pet },
      });
      setPendingPetFood(null);
      playSound(SoundEffect.SUCCESS, 0.32);
      triggerHaptic('light');
      return { ok: true, itemId, petItemId: petId, delta, condition: petCondition(care) };
    },
    [user, profile, applyProfilePatch],
  );

  /**
   * 管理員測試 — puts the animal at a given 營養/活動力 without waiting for real time to pass.
   *
   * Writes a real care state down the real path, so what the tester sees is what a player in that
   * condition would see. It is the counterpart to `simulateOfflineDays` (context/useIslandLife.ts)
   * and exists for the same reason: a shortcut that painted the outcome would be a second
   * implementation, and would pass while the real one was broken.
   */
  const setPetCare = useCallback(
    async (nutrition: number, energy: number, petItemId?: string): Promise<boolean> => {
      if (!user || !profile) return false;
      const petId = petItemId ?? equippedPetId(profile);
      if (!petId) return false;
      const nowMs = Date.now();
      const previous = profile.islandState?.pet;
      const base = newPetCareState(nowMs);
      const care: PetCareState = {
        ...base,
        nutrition: Math.min(1, Math.max(0, nutrition)),
        energy: Math.min(1, Math.max(0, energy)),
      };
      const pet = makePetState(
        previous?.mood ?? PET_HOME_STATE.mood,
        previous?.vitality ?? PET_HOME_STATE.vitality,
        previous?.lastGreetedAt,
        previous?.care,
        // One animal, the same as a feed: a tester who sets 「懶洋洋」 on the dog must not find the
        // cat listless too, or what they are testing is not what a player would experience.
        withPetCare(previous?.cares, petId, care, nowMs),
      );
      try {
        await updateDoc(doc(db, 'users', user.uid), { 'islandState.pet': pet });
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('[pet] 寵物狀態調整沒有存檔成功：', error);
        handleFirestoreError(error, OperationType.UPDATE, `users/${user.uid}`);
        return false;
      }
      applyProfilePatch({ islandState: { ...profile.islandState, pet } });
      return true;
    },
    [user, profile, applyProfilePatch],
  );

  return { feedPet, pendingPetFood, armPetFeeding, cancelPetFeeding, setPetCare };
}
```

## src/context/usePlacementActions.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { db, doc, updateDoc, handleFirestoreError, OperationType } from '../lib/firebase';
import type { AuthUser } from '../auth/types';
import { PlacedItem, UserProfile } from '../types';
import { canPlaceItem } from '../utils/inventory';

/**
 * Island placement store — every write to `profile.islandPlacements` goes through here.
 *
 * These used to branch on the current view to decide whether they were writing island or
 * interior placements. They never were: the house interior has always written
 * `interiorData.placements` through its own handlers, so the interior branch was dead code that
 * made the island's own rules read as conditional. They are island-only now, and the interior
 * enforces the same stock rule (utils/inventory.ts) at its own write.
 *
 * Adding a placement consumes one copy from the inventory implicitly — stock is
 * `owned − placed`, so appending here is what spends it, and removing below is what refunds it.
 * That is why `placeIslandItem` refuses when nothing is in stock: it is the last line of
 * defence behind a disabled button, so no keyboard path or stale click can put down a copy the
 * player never bought.
 */
export function usePlacementActions(user: AuthUser | null, profile: UserProfile | null) {
  const placeIslandItem = async (
    itemId: string,
    position: [number, number, number],
    rotation: number
  ): Promise<boolean> => {
    if (!user || !profile) return false;
    if (!canPlaceItem(profile, itemId)) return false;

    const newPlacement: PlacedItem = {
      instanceId: `inst-${Date.now()}-${Math.floor(Math.random() * 1000000)}`,
      itemId,
      position,
      rotation,
    };

    try {
      await updateDoc(doc(db, 'users', user.uid), {
        islandPlacements: [...(profile.islandPlacements || []), newPlacement],
      });
      return true;
    } catch (error) {
      handleFirestoreError(error, OperationType.UPDATE, `users/${user.uid}`);
      return false;
    }
  };

  /** Moves/rotates an existing placement in place. Never touches stock — it's the same copy. */
  const updateIslandPlacement = async (
    instanceId: string,
    position: [number, number, number],
    rotation: number
  ): Promise<boolean> => {
    if (!user || !profile) return false;
    const placements = profile.islandPlacements || [];
    if (!placements.some(p => p.instanceId === instanceId)) return false;

    try {
      await updateDoc(doc(db, 'users', user.uid), {
        islandPlacements: placements.map(p =>
          p.instanceId === instanceId ? { ...p, position, rotation } : p
        ),
      });
      return true;
    } catch (error) {
      handleFirestoreError(error, OperationType.UPDATE, `users/${user.uid}`);
      return false;
    }
  };

  /** Picks a placed object back up. The copy returns to stock because it is no longer placed. */
  const removeIslandPlacement = async (instanceId: string): Promise<boolean> => {
    if (!user || !profile) return false;

    try {
      await updateDoc(doc(db, 'users', user.uid), {
        islandPlacements: (profile.islandPlacements || []).filter(p => p.instanceId !== instanceId),
      });
      return true;
    } catch (error) {
      handleFirestoreError(error, OperationType.UPDATE, `users/${user.uid}`);
      return false;
    }
  };

  return { placeIslandItem, updateIslandPlacement, removeIslandPlacement };
}
```

## src/context/useShopActions.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { db, doc, updateDoc, arrayUnion, handleFirestoreError, OperationType } from '../lib/firebase';
import { getBalance, type CurrencyId } from '../constants/currency';
import { buildSpendUpdate } from './useEconomyActions';
import type { AuthUser } from '../auth/types';
import { AppSettings, UserProfile } from '../types';
import { ALL_ITEMS, getItemById } from '../constants/items';
import { isMainShopItem } from '../constants/distribution';
import { STARTER_HOUSE_ITEM_ID, getHouseStyle } from '../constants/houseStyles';
import { isStackableItem, ownsItem } from '../utils/inventory';
import { getRaffleTickets } from '../constants/fragments';
import { isXpLocked } from '../utils/unlock';
import { fragmentPatchForPurchase } from './useFragmentActions';

/**
 * What the ordinary catalog is priced in.
 *
 * 金幣, and named rather than assumed: 碎片 exists now (constants/currency.ts) and the brief is
 * explicit that it is NOT a second kind of gold — the shop's shelves stay 金幣-only, and a future
 * 碎片 exchange is a separate surface with its own rules (§11/§18), not a second price on these
 * cards. Naming it here is what makes that a decision somebody has to change rather than one
 * `increment(-item.price)` happens to encode.
 */
const SHOP_CURRENCY: CurrencyId = 'coins';

/** Why a purchase didn't go through, so callers can say something specific. */
export type PurchaseResult =
  | 'ok'
  | 'unknown-item'
  /** A real item, but not one this shop sells — see {@link isMainShopItem}. */
  | 'not-sold-here'
  | 'insufficient-gold'
  /** Gated on 經驗值 and the player hasn't reached it — see utils/unlock.ts. */
  | 'insufficient-xp'
  | 'already-owned'
  | 'error';

/**
 * What 一鍵擁有全部商品 did: how many ids it added, WHICH ids those were, or that the save
 * refused the write.
 *
 * `grantedIds` is what makes the 全部商品 switch (UI/settings/AdminOwnAllItemsRow.tsx) able to
 * turn back off: it is the receipt of what this call put in, so switching off can take back
 * exactly that and nothing the player bought themselves.
 */
export type GrantAllResult =
  | { ok: true; granted: number; grantedIds: string[] }
  | { ok: false };

/**
 * What 關掉 the 全部商品 switch did: how many granted ids were taken back, and how many were
 * kept because they are currently in use (worn, placed, painted on a wall, or the style the
 * Home is wearing — see {@link idsInUse}).
 */
export type RevokeGrantedResult =
  | { ok: true; revoked: number; kept: number }
  | { ok: false };

/**
 * Every catalog id the save is currently USING rather than merely holding.
 *
 * Only 撤回 reads this, and it reads it to refuse: an id in here is never taken out of the
 * inventory, because every one of these fields points AT an inventory entry — the shirt on the
 * avatar, the sofa standing in the living room, the floor painted in the study, the style the
 * Home is wearing. Removing the entry under any of them leaves a save referring to something it
 * does not own, which is a worse state than 「多了一件沒買過的衣服」.
 *
 * Over-inclusive on purpose. A false positive keeps one granted item owned (harmless — the
 * switch says so); a false negative is a dangling reference.
 */
function idsInUse(profile: UserProfile): Set<string> {
  const used = new Set<string>(profile.equippedItems || []);
  for (const placed of profile.islandPlacements || []) used.add(placed.itemId);

  const interior = profile.interiorData;
  for (const placed of interior?.placements || []) used.add(placed.itemId);
  // Floors and walls are stored as the catalog id of the paint/tile that was applied — see the
  // `interiorData.roomStyles` write in BuildingInteriorView.tsx.
  for (const style of Object.values(interior?.roomStyles || {})) {
    if (style?.floor) used.add(style.floor);
    if (style?.wall) used.add(style.wall);
  }
  if (interior?.selectedFloorStyle) used.add(interior.selectedFloorStyle);
  if (interior?.selectedWallStyle) used.add(interior.selectedWallStyle);

  // `home.currentStyle` is a HouseStyleId ('grass'), not the item id that grants it
  // ('house-grass'); ownership is checked against the latter (useHomeActions.applyHouseStyle).
  if (profile.home?.currentStyle) used.add(getHouseStyle(profile.home.currentStyle).itemId);

  return used;
}

/**
 * The Shop System — the one place an item is ever bought.
 *
 * Every buy button in the game (the shop catalog, the outdoor build rail's 購買/再購買, the
 * indoor furniture drawer's not-yet-owned section) calls this, so the price charged, the
 * ownership rule and the way a copy lands in the inventory can't diverge per screen.
 *
 * Stacking is decided by the item's category kind (utils/inventory.ts): a placeable object
 * appends another copy — buying a second sofa means you can stand two sofas up — while
 * wearables, floors/walls and house styles are `arrayUnion`'d, so buying them twice is
 * impossible rather than merely discouraged.
 *
 * `settings` is here for one reason: 商品碎片. Buying an item with gold strands whatever fragments
 * were collected toward it, and whether those become 抽獎券 is a per-save setting — see
 * `fragmentPatchForPurchase` in context/useFragmentActions.ts. Nothing else in this file reads it.
 */
export function useShopActions(
  user: AuthUser | null,
  profile: UserProfile | null,
  settings: AppSettings | null,
) {
  const purchaseItem = async (itemId: string): Promise<PurchaseResult> => {
    if (!user || !profile) return 'error';

    const item = getItemById(itemId);
    if (!item) return 'unknown-item';
    // The Distribution Channel gate (constants/distribution.ts), applied at the WRITE and not only
    // in the grid. Every main-shop surface already builds its list from `MAIN_SHOP_CATALOG`, so
    // nothing should ever reach here with a 限時商店 exclusive — which is exactly why the check
    // belongs here: a deep link, a stale card or a surface added next year cannot buy an item at
    // its gold price behind a shop that no longer stocks it.
    if (!isMainShopItem(itemId)) return 'not-sold-here';

    const stackable = isStackableItem(itemId);
    if (!stackable && ownsItem(profile, itemId)) return 'already-owned';
    // The XP gate is checked here rather than only in the UI, so an item that has to be earned
    // cannot be acquired by whichever surface forgets to grey its button out.
    if (isXpLocked(profile, item)) return 'insufficient-xp';
    if (getBalance(profile, SHOP_CURRENCY) < item.price) return 'insufficient-gold';

    try {
      // 抽獎券 — the one product whose goods are a BALANCE rather than an object.
      //
      // NO main-shop item declares `grantsTickets` today: 抽獎券 moved to the 限時小攤 with the
      // rest of 特殊卡牌 (constants/items.ts, constants/limitedShop.ts), and the channel guard
      // above refuses it here. This branch stays because it belongs to the FIELD rather than to
      // that one row — a 五張裝 ticket pack sold on the ordinary shelf later is a catalog row, and
      // deleting this would silently file it into the inventory as a row that does nothing.
      //
      // It leaves by the same door it would if it were an ordinary item (same dialog, same
      // affordability check, same single write that charges and delivers together); what differs is
      // where the goods land: `raffleTickets`, which is the number the 轉盤 spends
      // (constants/fragments.ts), instead of an entry in `inventory`. An inventory entry would be a
      // second, unspendable copy of the same thing — the wheel would never see it, and the shop
      // would report 已擁有 for something the player had already spent.
      //
      // Written as an absolute value rather than `increment()` because the ceiling has to be
      // applied to the RESULT; the read it is based on is the same snapshot the affordability check
      // above used, so the two cannot disagree about what this purchase is.
      if (item.grantsTickets) {
        await updateDoc(doc(db, 'users', user.uid), {
          ...(buildSpendUpdate(SHOP_CURRENCY, item.price) ?? {}),
          raffleTickets: getRaffleTickets(profile) + item.grantsTickets,
        });
        return 'ok';
      }

      // The fragment settlement rides along in the SAME write rather than following it. A player
      // who was 180/200 of the way to this item is holding 180 fragments that can never unlock
      // anything again once it is owned; folding their conversion into the purchase means the gold
      // leaving, the item arriving and the fragments settling all land together or not at all.
      // Empty for the overwhelmingly common case of an item with no fragments collected, in which
      // case this write is byte-for-byte what it always was.
      await updateDoc(doc(db, 'users', user.uid), {
        // The charge comes from the Economy Service so that which field 金幣 lives in is decided in
        // exactly one place (constants/currency.ts) — and it stays in the SAME write as the
        // inventory entry, because a charge without the goods and goods without the charge are both
        // unrepairable. See buildSpendUpdate.
        ...(buildSpendUpdate(SHOP_CURRENCY, item.price) ?? {}),
        inventory: stackable ? [...(profile.inventory || []), itemId] : arrayUnion(itemId),
        ...fragmentPatchForPurchase(profile, settings, itemId),
      });
      return 'ok';
    } catch (error) {
      handleFirestoreError(error, OperationType.UPDATE, `users/${user.uid}`);
      return 'error';
    }
  };

  /**
   * 一鍵擁有全部商品 — 管理員測試模式 only (constants/adminFeatures.ts).
   *
   * The point of Admin Test Mode is putting the save into whatever state a test needs without
   * grinding for it, and 「每一件都買得起」 is the state most shop/dressing-room/furniture work
   * needs: every card in its owned form, every wearable in the wardrobe, every piece of furniture
   * in the drawer. Doing that by hand is ~100 purchases plus enough gold to cover them.
   *
   * It GRANTS, it never charges and never takes anything away — gold, worn items and placements
   * are untouched, so pressing it can't cost a tester the state they were setting up. One copy of
   * each catalog id, which is what the shop calls 已擁有; a placeable item can be bought again
   * afterwards for a second copy through the ordinary path above.
   *
   * Two ids are deliberately NOT granted:
   *  - {@link STARTER_HOUSE_ITEM_ID} (毛胚屋), because holding it in the inventory *means* 「家還沒
   *    蓋」 — useHomeActions.placeHome spends it. Handing it back to a player who already has a
   *    Home would re-arm the 放置我的家 flow for a house they already live in. It is also not for
   *    sale (houseStyles.ts marks it `purchasable: false`), so it is not one of 商店裡的商品.
   *  - anything already in the inventory, read from the raw array rather than through
   *    `ownsItem`, so the `?unown=` display override (utils/debugOverrides.ts) can't make this
   *    append a duplicate of something the save already holds. Pressing it twice is a no-op.
   *  - 抽獎券 (`grantsTickets`, constants/items.ts), because it is not an object: what it grants is
   *    a balance, and an inventory entry for it would be a row that does nothing. 管理員 gets
   *    tickets from its own control instead — the 抽獎券 row in UI/AdminValueControls.tsx.
   */
  const grantAllItems = async (): Promise<GrantAllResult> => {
    if (!user || !profile) return { ok: false };

    const inventory = profile.inventory || [];
    const owned = new Set(inventory);
    const missing = ALL_ITEMS
      .filter(item => item.id !== STARTER_HOUSE_ITEM_ID && !item.grantsTickets && !owned.has(item.id))
      .map(item => item.id);

    // Nothing to add is a success with nothing written — the caller says 「已經全部擁有」 rather
    // than reporting a failed save.
    if (missing.length === 0) return { ok: true, granted: 0, grantedIds: [] };

    try {
      await updateDoc(doc(db, 'users', user.uid), { inventory: [...inventory, ...missing] });
      return { ok: true, granted: missing.length, grantedIds: missing };
    } catch (error) {
      handleFirestoreError(error, OperationType.UPDATE, `users/${user.uid}`);
      return { ok: false };
    }
  };

  /**
   * 撤回 what {@link grantAllItems} handed over — the OFF half of the 全部商品 switch
   * (UI/settings/AdminOwnAllItemsRow.tsx), and the reason that control can be a 開關 at all
   * rather than a button pretending to be one.
   *
   * `ids` is the receipt the switch kept when it was turned on, not 「everything in the catalog」.
   * That distinction is the whole design: an item the player bought with their own gold was never
   * on the receipt, so it cannot be swept up here — which is what separates this from 清空裝備
   * (ShopView's full wipe) and is why, like the grant, it needs no confirm().
   *
   * Two further refusals, both about not leaving the save worse than it found it:
   *  - anything currently in use is KEPT and reported as `kept` ({@link idsInUse}). Worn, placed,
   *    painted or lived-in things point at their inventory entry; pulling it out from under them
   *    is the one way this could break a save.
   *  - exactly ONE copy per id, not every copy. A stackable item granted here and then bought
   *    again through the ordinary path leaves two in the inventory; the receipt only covers the
   *    one this granted, so `filter(id => !toRemove.has(id))` would silently eat a purchase.
   */
  const revokeGrantedItems = async (ids: string[]): Promise<RevokeGrantedResult> => {
    if (!user || !profile) return { ok: false };

    const inUse = idsInUse(profile);
    const removable = new Set(ids.filter(id => !inUse.has(id)));
    const kept = new Set(ids.filter(id => inUse.has(id))).size;
    if (removable.size === 0) return { ok: true, revoked: 0, kept };

    const inventory = profile.inventory || [];
    const budget = new Map<string, number>();
    for (const id of removable) budget.set(id, 1);
    const next = inventory.filter(id => {
      const left = budget.get(id) ?? 0;
      if (left <= 0) return true;
      budget.set(id, left - 1);
      return false;
    });

    const revoked = inventory.length - next.length;
    // The receipt can name ids the inventory no longer holds (a 清空裝備 in between, say). That
    // is not a failure and not a write.
    if (revoked === 0) return { ok: true, revoked: 0, kept };

    try {
      await updateDoc(doc(db, 'users', user.uid), { inventory: next });
      return { ok: true, revoked, kept };
    } catch (error) {
      handleFirestoreError(error, OperationType.UPDATE, `users/${user.uid}`);
      return { ok: false };
    }
  };

  return { purchaseItem, grantAllItems, revokeGrantedItems };
}
```

## src/context/useUtilityCards.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { db, doc, updateDoc, handleFirestoreError, OperationType } from '../lib/firebase';
import type { AuthUser } from '../auth/types';
import type { UserProfile } from '../types';
import {
  activeEffects,
  getOwnedCardCount,
  getUtilityCard,
  grantCards,
  useCard,
  type ActiveUtilityEffect,
  type CardUseError,
  type UtilityCardId,
  type UtilityCardState,
} from '../constants/utilityCards';
import { playSound, SoundEffect, triggerHaptic } from '../lib/soundUtils';

/**
 * 功能卡 Service — the one place a card enters the bag, leaves it, or starts running.
 *
 * Same shape as the Shop System (context/useShopActions.ts) and the 商品碎片 service
 * (context/useFragmentActions.ts), and here for the same reason: three different things hand out
 * cards (a 限時商店 purchase, a 輪盤 drop, 管理員測試) and every one of them has to apply the same
 * cap, write the same map and reflect the same local state. A second call site that writes
 * `utilityCards` itself is a second set of those rules, and the first one to drift wins silently.
 *
 * The RULES are pure functions in constants/utilityCards.ts; this file is only the write.
 *
 * ## Why the whole map is written
 *
 * `utilityCards` is a nested map whose keys are card ids (`double-coin`), and ids contain hyphens.
 * Firestore's dotted field paths cannot address those without backtick quoting, and the offline save
 * (save/LocalSaveStore.ts) splits dotted keys on `.` with no quoting at all — so
 * `utilityCards.owned.double-coin` would mean two different things in the two back-ends this app
 * runs on. Writing the map whole means one behaviour in both. It is a handful of numbers.
 *
 * ## Use is not optimistic
 *
 * A card leaves the bag only after the save accepts it, like every other grant in this codebase
 * (see the 「grant first, celebrate second」 note in context/useWorkoutRewards.ts). Showing a
 * consumed card and then rolling back is the one lie this UI must never tell — the player would
 * have no way to know whether their card is gone.
 */

/** What a grant did. `dropped` is what the per-card cap refused, not an error. */
export type CardGrantOutcome =
  | { ok: true; granted: number; dropped: number }
  | { ok: false; reason: 'no-profile' | 'unknown-card' | 'save-failed' };

/** What a use did. Every `reason` except the last two is an ordinary state the UI explains. */
export type CardUseOutcome =
  | { ok: true; effect: ActiveUtilityEffect }
  | { ok: false; reason: CardUseError | 'no-profile' | 'save-failed' };

/** Why a use was refused, in the player's words. The one place this copy is written. */
export const CARD_USE_MESSAGES: Record<CardUseError | 'no-profile' | 'save-failed', string> = {
  'unknown-card': '這張卡片已經不存在了',
  'none-owned': '你目前沒有這張卡片',
  'already-active': '效果正在進行中，等結束後再使用一張',
  'no-profile': '尚未登入，無法使用卡片',
  'save-failed': '存檔失敗，卡片沒有被使用',
};

export function useUtilityCards(
  user: AuthUser | null,
  profile: UserProfile | null,
  /** Writes an accepted value straight into local state — see AppContext's applyProfilePatch. */
  applyProfilePatch: (updates: Partial<UserProfile>) => void,
) {
  /**
   * Hands the player cards. The single grant path for every source.
   *
   * Takes a quantity because a drop table is allowed to pay more than one, and reports what the cap
   * refused rather than throwing it away silently — a 輪盤 that keeps paying a card the player
   * cannot hold is a balance problem somebody has to be able to see.
   */
  const grantUtilityCards = async (
    cardId: UtilityCardId,
    quantity = 1,
  ): Promise<CardGrantOutcome> => {
    if (!user || !profile) return { ok: false, reason: 'no-profile' };
    if (!getUtilityCard(cardId)) return { ok: false, reason: 'unknown-card' };

    const result = grantCards(profile.utilityCards, cardId, quantity);
    // Nothing to add — the bag is full — is a success with nothing written, so the caller can say
    // 「已達上限」 rather than reporting a failed save.
    if (result.granted === 0) return { ok: true, granted: 0, dropped: result.dropped };

    try {
      await updateDoc(doc(db, 'users', user.uid), { utilityCards: result.state });
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('[cards] 功能卡發放沒有存檔成功：', error);
      handleFirestoreError(error, OperationType.UPDATE, `users/${user.uid}`);
      return { ok: false, reason: 'save-failed' };
    }

    applyProfilePatch({ utilityCards: result.state });
    return { ok: true, granted: result.granted, dropped: result.dropped };
  };

  /**
   * Uses one card: spends a copy and starts its effect.
   *
   * Everything about WHAT happens next is the card's own definition — this function does not know
   * that 雙倍金幣券 doubles anything. It writes the state that `useCard` computed, and the next
   * reward that is paid finds the effect through the 獎勵計算層 (constants/rewardEffects.ts).
   *
   * The activation id is minted here, once per attempt, so a retry of the same tap cannot become a
   * second activation.
   */
  const useUtilityCard = async (cardId: UtilityCardId): Promise<CardUseOutcome> => {
    if (!user || !profile) return { ok: false, reason: 'no-profile' };

    const result = useCard(profile.utilityCards, cardId, {
      nowMs: Date.now(),
      activationId: newActivationId(),
    });
    if (!result.ok) return { ok: false, reason: result.error };

    try {
      await updateDoc(doc(db, 'users', user.uid), { utilityCards: result.state });
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('[cards] 使用功能卡沒有存檔成功：', error);
      handleFirestoreError(error, OperationType.UPDATE, `users/${user.uid}`);
      return { ok: false, reason: 'save-failed' };
    }

    applyProfilePatch({ utilityCards: result.state });
    playSound(SoundEffect.REWARD, 0.35);
    triggerHaptic('medium');
    return { ok: true, effect: result.effect };
  };

  /**
   * 管理員測試 — empties the bag and stops every effect.
   *
   * Written as an empty map rather than deleted, for the same reason `resetWorkoutRewards` is:
   * `deleteField()` is not part of the storage facade's exports (lib/firebase.ts), and an absent map
   * and an empty one read identically everywhere in this feature.
   */
  const resetUtilityCards = async (): Promise<boolean> => {
    if (!user || !profile) return false;
    const cleared: UtilityCardState = {};
    try {
      await updateDoc(doc(db, 'users', user.uid), { utilityCards: cleared });
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('[cards] 重置功能卡狀態失敗：', error);
      handleFirestoreError(error, OperationType.UPDATE, `users/${user.uid}`);
      return false;
    }
    applyProfilePatch({ utilityCards: cleared });
    return true;
  };

  return { grantUtilityCards, useUtilityCard, resetUtilityCards };
}

/**
 * A fresh activation id.
 *
 * `crypto.randomUUID` where it exists, with the same fallback shape as `newWorkoutId`
 * (lib/workoutCompletion.ts) — this runs in the same browsers.
 */
function newActivationId(): string {
  if (typeof crypto !== 'undefined' && 'randomUUID' in crypto) return `act-${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
  return `act-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10)}`;
}

/**
 * What the player has running, as a screen wants to read it: the effect, its card, and whether it
 * is a countdown or a use counter.
 *
 * A read helper rather than another piece of state — the profile is the only copy, and a component
 * that cached this would be a second one that goes stale the moment an effect expires.
 */
export interface LiveEffectView {
  effect: ActiveUtilityEffect;
  name: string;
  summary: string;
  expiresAt?: string;
  usesLeft?: number;
}

export function readLiveEffects(
  profile: UserProfile | null | undefined,
  nowMs: number,
): LiveEffectView[] {
  return activeEffects(profile?.utilityCards, nowMs).flatMap((effect) => {
    const card = getUtilityCard(effect.cardId);
    if (!card) return [];
    return [
      {
        effect,
        name: card.name,
        summary: card.effectSummary,
        ...(effect.expiresAt ? { expiresAt: effect.expiresAt } : {}),
        ...(typeof effect.usesLeft === 'number' ? { usesLeft: effect.usesLeft } : {}),
      },
    ];
  });
}

/** How many of one card the profile holds. The read every 使用 button asks. */
export function readOwnedCardCount(
  profile: UserProfile | null | undefined,
  cardId: UtilityCardId,
): number {
  return getOwnedCardCount(profile?.utilityCards, cardId);
}

```
