```css
     different jobs: the first is a shutter closing on the shop, this one is
     light coming OFF the thing that just stopped. A second full-strength white
     flash here reads as the animation restarting. */
  .rarity-reveal-burst {
    position: absolute;
    inset: 0;
    background: radial-gradient(closest-side at 50% calc(50% + var(--reveal-focus, 0px)), #FFFFFF 0%, var(--rarity-field-core) 45%, transparent 78%);
    opacity: 0;
    animation: rarity-reveal-burst 0.55s ease-out 5.46s forwards;
  }

  @keyframes rarity-reveal-burst {
    0%   { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.6); }
    18%  { opacity: 0.55; }
    100% { opacity: 0; transform: scale(1.25); }
  }

  /* 能量環 — two rings pushed out of the item as it stops, the second a beat
     behind the first so it reads as a pulse travelling outwards rather than as
     one ring that got thicker. Sized in vmin so they clear the plinth on a
     phone and still stay on screen on a desktop. */
  .rarity-reveal-ring {
    position: absolute;
    left: 50%;
    top: calc(50% + var(--reveal-focus, 0px));
    width: 34vmin;
    aspect-ratio: 1;
    translate: -50% -50%;
    border-radius: 50%;
    border: 2px solid var(--rarity-edge);
    box-shadow: 0 0 24px var(--rarity-halo), inset 0 0 24px var(--rarity-halo);
    opacity: 0;
    animation: rarity-reveal-ring 0.95s cubic-bezier(0.1, 0.7, 0.2, 1) 5.48s forwards;
  }

  /* The second ring, 160ms behind the first — a settle-anchored delay like every
     other one in this block, and it has to be re-derived with them. It was left
     at 4.64s across the move to a 7.5s arrival, which fired it 2.8s BEFORE the
     stop it is meant to be part of. */
  .rarity-reveal-ring-2 {
    animation-delay: 5.64s;
    border-width: 1px;
  }

  @keyframes rarity-reveal-ring {
    0%   { opacity: 0; scale: 0.25; }
    20%  { opacity: 0.85; }
    100% { opacity: 0; scale: 2.1; }
  }

  /* Light thrown off the item. Same repeating-conic construction as the card's
     grain but coarser and much larger, because this one IS meant to read as a
     burst rather than as a machined surface — the card is an object, this is
     an event.

     The mask stops the rays well inside the viewport (opaque at 15%, gone by
     42%). Rays that reach the corners stop reading as light coming off the
     item and start reading as fog over the whole page.

     `rotate`/`scale` as individual properties, not `transform`: `translate`
     is already carrying the centring, and the individual properties compose
     with it instead of overwriting it. */
  .rarity-reveal-rays {
    position: absolute;
    left: 50%;
    top: calc(50% + var(--reveal-focus, 0px));
    width: 190vmax;
    aspect-ratio: 1;
    translate: -50% -50%;
    background: repeating-conic-gradient(
      from 0deg,
      rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.85) 0deg 1.4deg,
      transparent 1.4deg 7deg
    );
    -webkit-mask-image: radial-gradient(closest-side, transparent 3%, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9) 15%, transparent 42%);
    mask-image: radial-gradient(closest-side, transparent 3%, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9) 15%, transparent 42%);
    opacity: 0;
    animation: rarity-reveal-rays 7.6s ease-out 0.25s forwards;
  }

  /* Two-stage, because the reveal has two moments instead of one. The rays
     bleed in at a low 0.2 while the item is still turning — that is the 「柔和
     放射光」 the spin happens inside, and it must stay under the silhouette
     rather than competing with it — then flare to 0.42 exactly on the settle
     and fall away over the rest. They keep turning throughout at a constant
     rate, so the flare reads as the light getting brighter, not as it starting
     over.

     The flare's stop is (SETTLE − this animation's 250ms offset) / 7.6s =
     69%, and it has to be RE-DERIVED every time the arrival changes length.
     It was left at 35% across two of those and had drifted almost two seconds
     early — the light was peaking over an item that was still turning, and was
     already dimming by the time it landed. If you move the settle, do this
     division again — and the two stops before it as well: they hold their own
     ABSOLUTE lead on the flare (the rise is over ~1.1s in, the low plateau ends
     ~0.5s before it), because they describe the light, not a fraction of a track. */
  @keyframes rarity-reveal-rays {
    0%    { opacity: 0; rotate: 0deg; scale: 0.4; }
    11.4% { opacity: 0.2; }
    62%   { opacity: 0.2; }
    69%   { opacity: 0.42; scale: 0.86; }
    100%  { opacity: 0; rotate: 30deg; scale: 1.1; }
  }

  /* The stage: everything that belongs to the item, and the 鏡頭推近.

     The push-in is a scale on this wrapper rather than on the item itself, so
     the copy underneath is carried in by the same move — a camera that pushes
     in on the pet while its name sits at a fixed size is not a camera, it is
     the pet getting bigger. It settles at 1 and stays: the shot arrives and
     then holds, because everything after the settle is meant to be READ.

     It carries a `perspective` too, but that one is NOT what the turn uses —
     see `.rarity-reveal-pivot` below, which is the fix for why the turn spent
     so long not looking like one. This value is kept because the push-in and
     anything else 3D on this element's own children should share the depth. */
  .rarity-reveal-stage {
    position: relative;
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 18px;
    max-width: min(340px, 86vw);
    perspective: 900px;
    opacity: 0;
    animation:
      rarity-reveal-appear 0.3s ease-out forwards,
      rarity-reveal-push 5.9s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) forwards;
  }

  @keyframes rarity-reveal-appear {
    to { opacity: 1; }
  }

  @keyframes rarity-reveal-push {
    0%   { transform: scale(0.9); }
    100% { transform: scale(1); }
  }

  /* The wrapper the turn actually hangs from, and the reason it now reads as a
     turn at all.

     `perspective` only applies to an element's DIRECT children. The stage has
     carried `perspective: 900px` since the beginning, but the spinning element
     is its GRANDCHILD — the item and its ground share a positioned wrapper —
     and that wrapper, having no `transform-style: preserve-3d`, flattens
     everything under it. So the perspective never reached the rotation: what
     was on screen for every version of this reveal was a rotateY rendered
     orthographically, which is not a spin, it is a horizontal SQUASH. Hence
     「看不出來在轉」, and hence a turn count raised three times trying to fix a
     problem that was never about speed.

     760px rather than the stage's 900px: closer is more foreshortening, and
     against a 248px plinth this is where the near edge visibly swings toward
     the viewer — the frame stops being a rectangle that narrows and becomes a
     trapezoid that turns — without going fish-eye. */
  .rarity-reveal-pivot {
    position: relative;
    perspective: 760px;
  }

  /* The turn. 「輕快啟動 → 平順減速 → 正面停住」, with the bounce at the end.

     ABOUT Y — 陀螺: the item stands upright and spins about its own vertical
     axis, like a figurine on a turntable. Not `rotate`, which spins it in the
     picture plane like a pinwheel; that was tried and rejected as 「像逆時針
     或順時針」, the wrong motion entirely.

     The known cost of Y on flat art is the edge-on frame: twice per revolution
     a flat plane is one pixel wide and effectively gone. **Speed is what pays
     for it.** At the slow end those blank moments read as the item blinking
     out and returning bigger — which is what 「不是直接出現」 was complaining
     about — but spun fast the same frames read as exactly what they are, a
     solid thing turning edge-on. That is why the turn counts below are what
     they are, and why lowering them without also shortening the track brings
     the flicker back.

     Two things beyond the axis make it read as a top rather than a squash:
     the stage's `perspective: 900px` (a Y rotation with no vanishing point is
     just a horizontal scale) and `transform-style: preserve-3d` here.

     **How many turns is per-tier**, read from `--reveal-turns` (set inline by
     RarityReveal off constants/rarityFx.ts): 史詩 turns six times and 神話
     nine. (It was 6 / 7 / 9 while 傳說 sat between them.) It is the one part of
     the choreography that grades, and it grades on the same principle as
     everything else in that table — the tier is expressed by how much is
     spent, not by a different colour of the same amount. Both settle at the
     same instant, so a rarer item is not a longer wait; it is a faster whirl
     slowing into the same stop.

     More than one turn whatever the tier, because a single rotation at this
     duration is slow enough to be watched all the way round, and what should
     be a flourish becomes a lazy susan. That is doubly true now the track is
     3s rather than 1.5s: at one turn it would be a full half-minute-per-
     revolution crawl. The turn COUNTS were deliberately left alone when the
     duration doubled — halving the angular speed is exactly what "let me see
     it arrive" asks for, and it keeps the tier grading (3/4/5) intact.

     Starting at 0.12 scale puts it far enough away that the turn is nearly
     over before there is anything to see, so the detail arrives only once it
     is almost still — which is the whole trick of the 「由小至大旋轉登場」. It
     started at 0.26 and that was not small enough to read as arriving from a
     distance; it read as a card that was already there and grew a bit.

     The `var()` carries a fallback (3) because the whole `transform` is
     dropped if the custom property fails to resolve — and a dropped transform
     here means no scale either, so the item would simply be sitting at full
     size from frame one rather than merely not spinning.

     Per-keyframe timing functions, because the brief asks for three different
     motions in one gesture and a single curve cannot express them:

       0 → 73%   cubic-bezier(0.06, 0.72, 0.24, 1) — the quick launch and the
                 long smooth decay out of it. Nearly all the turn is spent here.
       73 → 88%  the overshoot swinging back past front, easing IN so it reads
                 as weight carrying it through rather than as a second push.
       88 → 100% the settle onto front, easing out to nothing.

     The overshoot is deliberately asymmetric — +26deg past front, then -8deg
     back — because a symmetric bounce reads as a spring, and this is a thing
     with mass coming to rest. About Y these angles cost only a little
     foreshortening; the in-plane experiment had to run at half of them,
     because the same numbers there leave the item visibly crooked rather than
     carrying momentum. Opacity is a SEPARATE animation on the stage
     above rather than a keyframe here: mixing a 0.3s fade into a 4.5s
     transform track means the fade inherits the transform's easing and the
     item ghosts in over half a second.

     The keyframe stops are PERCENTAGES, so lengthening the track stretched the
     whole gesture — launch, decay, overshoot and settle — in proportion. That
     is the intent: the ask was for the arrival to take longer, not for a fast
     spin followed by a pause. */
  .rarity-reveal-spin {
    transform-style: preserve-3d;
    animation: rarity-reveal-spin 5.5s forwards;
  }

  /* ROTATION ONLY. The scale that used to share these keyframes now lives on
     `.rarity-reveal-grow`, a wrapper inside this element, and the split is the
     whole reason the growth reads: the two moves want OPPOSITE curves. The turn
     is front-loaded (a hard launch, then a long decay into the stop); the swell
     has to be back-loaded (small and far away for most of the track, then a
     rush toward the viewer). One keyframe list means one timing function, and
     the turn's curve won — which is why the item used to reach nearly full size
     in the first fifth of the arrival and then simply sit there rotating. Two
     elements, two curves, one composed transform. */
  @keyframes rarity-reveal-spin {
    0% {
      transform: rotateY(calc(var(--reveal-turns, 5) * -360deg));
      animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.06, 0.72, 0.24, 1);
    }
    /* 73%: it was 74% originally, 80% while the track was 7.5s, and is back to
       about 74% now the track is 5.5s. These stops are percentages, so the tail
       after the overshoot moves with the track — which is exactly what must NOT
       happen here. The bounce wants to stay about a second and a half whatever
       the track is (73% of 5.5s leaves 1.49s, as 80% of 7.5s left 1.5s); every
       second added to or taken from the arrival belongs to the approach, not to
       an item that has already got here rocking into place for longer. */
    73% {
      transform: rotateY(26deg);
      animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.3, 1);
    }
    88% {
      transform: rotateY(-8deg);
      animation-timing-function: ease-out;
    }
    100% {
      transform: rotateY(0deg);
    }
  }

  /* 由小變大 — the approach, on its own element so it can have its own curve.

     0.22 → 1.16, a five-fold swell, and WHERE it is spent matters more than how
     big the ratio is. At the halfway mark the item is still only about half its
     final size, so the growth is something the player watches HAPPEN rather
     than something that is over before they have focused on it. That is what
     「由小變大更明顯」 asks for: not a smaller start, but a change that is still
     visibly changing all the way to the stop.

     The opening value has been up and down and this is the settled reasoning:

       0.12  the original, on a track where growth finished in the first fifth.
       0.08  chasing a bigger ratio. 「不要小到使用者分不出來」 — at 0.08 the
             132px icon is an 11px smudge, and a smudge has no shape to
             recognise, no rotation you can see and nothing to grow FROM. The
             ratio looked better in the keyframes and the animation looked worse.
       0.22  now. ~29px: small enough to read as far away, big enough that the
             silhouette is a bird and its turn is legible from the first second.

     The lesson is that the opening frame is not the drama, it is the PREMISE —
     it has to establish what is arriving. Distance is sold by the rim-light and
     the dark around it, not by making the thing too small to identify. */

     The peak (1.16) and the two frames after it are the same bounce the turn
     makes, at the same stops: 73% / 88% / 100% here and there. They must stay
     in step. The overshoot toward the viewer and the overshoot past front are
     one gesture, and drift between them reads as a wobble. */
  .rarity-reveal-grow {
    animation: rarity-reveal-grow 5.5s forwards;
  }

  @keyframes rarity-reveal-grow {
    0% {
      transform: scale(0.22);
      /* Slow to leave on purpose: a distant thing gets closer slowly, and then
         all at once. */
      animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.5, 0, 0.85, 0.45);
    }
    50% {
      transform: scale(0.62);
      animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.55, 0, 0.3, 1);
    }
    73% {
      transform: scale(1.16);
      animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.3, 1);
    }
    88% {
      transform: scale(0.97);
      animation-timing-function: ease-out;
    }
    100% {
      transform: scale(1);
    }
  }

  /* The plinth is the shop card's own well at presentation size, carrying the
     same `.rarity-*` layers — so what the player is shown is literally the
     card they were looking at, enlarged, and not a second piece of art that
     happens to be the same colour.

     The border starts transparent and arrives with the colour: during the
     silhouette phase a lit tier-coloured frame around a black shape gives the
     shape away before it is meant to be given away. */
  .rarity-reveal-plinth {
    position: relative;
    overflow: hidden;
    border-radius: 22px;
    border: 2px solid transparent;
    animation:
      rarity-reveal-edge 5.5s ease-out forwards,
      rarity-reveal-idle 3.4s ease-in-out 5.62s infinite;
  }

  @keyframes rarity-reveal-edge {
    0%, 62% { border-color: transparent; }
    100%    { border-color: var(--rarity-edge); }
  }

  /* 待機動作 — the breathing, once it has arrived. ±5px and a 1.5% swell over
     3.4s, which is under the threshold at which motion pulls the eye: the
     player is reading the copy by now and this is meant to keep the thing
     alive in the corner of their vision, not to take their attention back.
     Species-specific idles (a wag, a blink) belong to the 3D companion in
     Three/Pets.tsx — this plinth holds a flat SVG icon and cannot pose it, so
     what it does is breathe. */
  @keyframes rarity-reveal-idle {
    0%, 100% { transform: translateY(0) scale(1); }
    50%      { transform: translateY(-5px) scale(1.015); }
  }

  /* The tier's plate, held back while the silhouette reads.

     This is the aura wrapper and not the plinth itself, which matters: the
     icon inside must NOT be faded with it (a translucent silhouette is a
     smudge), so the darkening is applied to the layer behind the icon rather
     than to their common parent. */
  .rarity-reveal-plate {
    position: absolute;
    inset: 0;
    animation: rarity-reveal-plate 5.5s ease-out forwards;
  }

  /* Fully OFF for the first 58%, not the 0.07 it used to hold. A plate at 7%
     is still a faint rectangle on screen, and a faint rectangle behind a black
     shape is a card with something on it — which is precisely what these
     opening frames must not be. Nothing is on screen but the shape. */
  @keyframes rarity-reveal-plate {
    0%, 58% { opacity: 0; }
    100%    { opacity: 1; }
  }

  /* 剪影與輪廓光 → the item itself.

     `brightness(0)` crushes the icon to a flat black shape whatever its own
     colours are, and the `drop-shadow` after it in the filter chain is the rim
     light — filters apply in order, so the glow is drawn from the already-black
     shape and comes out in the tier's colour rather than in the pet's.

     It stays black for the first 62% — the whole of the fast part of the turn —
     and resolves over the next 31%, landing at 5115ms against a settle at
     5500ms. Both ends of that are deliberate. It holds because the black
     spinning shape IS the beat, and an item that starts colouring up at a
     third of the way through is a coloured item for most of its entrance. And
     it finishes BEFORE the bounce, because the point of the bounce is that you
     are watching the thing you now own come to rest — a silhouette still
     resolving at the settle puts the reveal's two biggest moments in the same
     instant, fighting. */
  .rarity-reveal-silhouette {
    position: relative;
    animation: rarity-reveal-silhouette 5.5s ease-out forwards;
  }

  @keyframes rarity-reveal-silhouette {
    0% {
      filter: brightness(0) drop-shadow(0 0 8px var(--rarity-edge));
    }
    62% {
      filter: brightness(0) drop-shadow(0 0 26px var(--rarity-shine));
    }
    93%, 100% {
      filter: brightness(1) drop-shadow(0 4px 10px rgba(38, 70, 83, 0.25));
    }
  }

  /* 腳下的光環. Two layers doing two jobs: `pool` is the soft pad of light the
     item comes to rest ON and it stays for the rest of the reveal, `halo` is
     the single ring that spreads out of the impact and is gone in a second.
     Flattened hard (aspect 4.5:1) so both read as light lying on a floor
     rather than as a circle floating behind the item. */
  .rarity-reveal-ground {
    position: absolute;
    left: 50%;
    bottom: -14px;
    width: 240px;
    aspect-ratio: 4.5;
    translate: -50% 0;
    pointer-events: none;
  }

  .rarity-reveal-pool {
    position: absolute;
    inset: 0;
    border-radius: 50%;
    background: radial-gradient(closest-side, var(--rarity-field-core) 0%, var(--rarity-halo) 45%, transparent 75%);
    opacity: 0;
    animation: rarity-reveal-pool 0.7s ease-out 5.42s forwards;
  }

  @keyframes rarity-reveal-pool {
    from { opacity: 0; scale: 0.5 1; }
    to   { opacity: 0.7; scale: 1 1; }
  }

  /* Drawn as a soft band in a gradient rather than as a `border`, which is what
     it was first. A 2px solid ring flattened to this aspect is a crisp white
     ellipse with a hard edge on both sides, and a hard edge is a physical rim —
     it read as a plastic hoop the pet was standing inside rather than as light
     spreading across a floor. A gradient band has no edge to give it away, and
     the blur takes the last of it. */
  .rarity-reveal-halo {
    position: absolute;
    inset: 0;
    border-radius: 50%;
    background: radial-gradient(closest-side,
      transparent 52%,
      var(--rarity-shine) 72%,
      var(--rarity-field-core) 84%,
      transparent 96%);
    filter: blur(3px);
    opacity: 0;
    animation: rarity-reveal-halo 1.2s cubic-bezier(0.1, 0.7, 0.2, 1) 5.46s forwards;
  }

  @keyframes rarity-reveal-halo {
    0%   { opacity: 0; scale: 0.2 1; }
    18%  { opacity: 0.8; }
    100% { opacity: 0; scale: 1.9 1.4; }
  }

  /* The copy, one line at a time.

     Each line carries the same 0.52s bounce and differs only in its delay,
     which RarityReveal sets inline — the stagger is data (which line is third)
     and not four near-identical rules. `backwards` is what holds a line
     invisible during its delay; without it every line is fully drawn at frame
     one and then jumps.

     The overshoot in the curve is small (1.12) and the travel is 12px. This is
     the calm end of the reveal: the fireworks have gone off and what is left
     is meant to be readable. */
  .rarity-reveal-line {
    animation: rarity-reveal-line 0.52s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1.12) backwards;
  }

  @keyframes rarity-reveal-line {
    0%   { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(12px) scale(0.94); }
    100% { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0) scale(1); }
  }

  /* 「輕觸繼續」. Fades in only after the last tag has landed — offered earlier
     it would be an invitation to skip the thing the player just paid for, and
     a reveal nobody watches once is a reveal that should not have been built.
     From here the overlay accepts a tap; see RarityReveal.tsx. */
  .rarity-reveal-hint {
    /* `both`, not `backwards`: the end value (0.55) is not the element's own
       opacity, so it has to be held after the animation finishes as well as
       before it starts. */
    animation: rarity-reveal-hint 0.6s ease-out 6.8s both;
  }

  @keyframes rarity-reveal-hint {
    from { opacity: 0; }
    to   { opacity: 0.55; }
  }

  /* 神話 only: ±4px for two cycles. Small on purpose — a shake big enough to
     be described as a shake is a bug report about the page jumping. */
  .rarity-shake {
    animation: rarity-shake 0.28s cubic-bezier(0.36, 0.07, 0.19, 0.97) 2;
  }

  /* Every frame carries `scale(1.015)` alongside its offset, and that is not
     part of the motion — it is what keeps the shake from showing the wall
     behind the app. The room is a full-viewport layer over a body painted
     `bg-sky-500`, so sliding it 4px left uncovers a 4px strip of hard blue
     down the edge for the length of the shake. Overscaling by 1.5% (≈12px on a
     phone, more on a desktop) means the layer always overfills the viewport by
     more than the largest offset, so there is nothing to uncover. The scale is
     held CONSTANT across the keyframes so it reads as nothing at all — a pulse
     in it would be a zoom, and this is a knock. */
  @keyframes rarity-shake {
    0%, 100% { transform: translate(0, 0) scale(1.015); }
    20%      { transform: translate(-4px, 2px) scale(1.015); }
    40%      { transform: translate(4px, -2px) scale(1.015); }
    60%      { transform: translate(-3px, -2px) scale(1.015); }
    80%      { transform: translate(3px, 2px) scale(1.015); }
  }

  /* Reduced motion: the reveal still HAPPENS — it is the feedback for a
     purchase and silently skipping it would read as the buy having failed —
     but nothing travels, nothing spins and nothing flashes.

     What survives is the STRUCTURE: the screen still dims, the item still
     arrives in the middle, the copy still appears in order, and the tier's
     gradient is still there (held still). A player who has asked for less
     motion gets the same information in the same order, which is the whole
     point — the reveal's job is to introduce a companion, and only the
     flourish around that job is motion.

     The spin is the one that MUST be cancelled rather than softened: three
     full rotations is exactly the vestibular trigger this media query exists
     for. It is replaced by a plain fade, and the silhouette resolves in place
     without the rim-light pulse.

     Every duration and delay below is unchanged, so the copy still lands on
     the same beats and RarityReveal's completion callback still fires when it
     always did. */
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    .rarity-reveal-flash,
    .rarity-reveal-burst,
    .rarity-reveal-rays { animation: none; opacity: 0.22; }
    .rarity-reveal-ring { animation: none; opacity: 0; }
    .rarity-reveal-backdrop { animation: rarity-reveal-backdrop 1s ease-out 5.35s forwards; }
    .rarity-reveal-stage { animation: rarity-reveal-appear 0.3s ease-out forwards; }
    /* Both halves of the arrival go: no turn, and no rush toward the viewer
       either — a five-fold swell is as vestibular as the rotation is. */
    .rarity-reveal-spin { animation: none; }
    .rarity-reveal-grow { animation: none; }
    .rarity-reveal-plinth { animation: rarity-reveal-edge 5.05s ease-out forwards; }
    .rarity-reveal-silhouette { animation: rarity-reveal-unveil 5.25s ease-out forwards; }
    .rarity-reveal-halo { animation: none; opacity: 0; }
    .rarity-reveal-line { animation-name: rarity-reveal-unveil; }
    .rarity-shake { animation: none; }
  }

  /* The stand-in for anything that would otherwise travel. Also the
     reduced-motion form of a copy line, which is why it ends at opacity 1
     rather than at a held value. */
  @keyframes rarity-reveal-unveil {
    from { opacity: 0; }
    to   { opacity: 1; }
  }

  .confirm-buy-btn {
    @apply w-full py-4 rounded-2xl font-black text-white transition-all text-base shadow-[0_10px_24px_rgba(42,157,143,0.35)] flex items-center justify-center gap-2 active:scale-[0.98];
    background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--color-island-teal) 0%, var(--color-island-teal-dark) 100%);
  }

  /* Floor Previews */
  .floor-oak-preview {
    background:
      linear-gradient(90deg, #78350f 1px, transparent 1px) 0 0 / 40px 100%,
      linear-gradient(#451a03 1px, transparent 1px) 0 0 / 100% 10px,
      #78350f;
    background-blend-mode: overlay;
  }

  .floor-tile-preview {
    background-image:
      linear-gradient(90deg, #cbd5e1 1px, transparent 1px),
      linear-gradient(#cbd5e1 1px, transparent 1px);
    background-size: 24px 24px;
    background-color: #f8fafc;
  }

  .floor-concrete-preview {
    background-color: #475569;
    background-image:
      radial-gradient(circle at 20% 30%, rgba(0,0,0,0.1) 1%, transparent 0),
      radial-gradient(circle at 70% 80%, rgba(255,255,255,0.05) 1%, transparent 0);
    background-size: 40px 40px;
  }

  .floor-pattern-preview {
    background-color: #334155;
    background-image:
      linear-gradient(45deg, #475569 25%, transparent 25%),
      linear-gradient(-45deg, #475569 25%, transparent 25%),
      linear-gradient(45deg, transparent 75%, #475569 75%),
      linear-gradient(-45deg, transparent 75%, #475569 75%);
    background-size: 20px 20px;
    background-position: 0 0, 0 10px, 10px -10px, -10px 0px;
  }

  .floor-marble-preview {
    background:
      linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(0,0,0,0.02) 25%, transparent 25%) -50px 0,
      linear-gradient(225deg, rgba(0,0,0,0.02) 25%, transparent 25%) -50px 0,
      linear-gradient(315deg, rgba(0,0,0,0.02) 25%, transparent 25%),
      linear-gradient(45deg, rgba(0,0,0,0.02) 25%, transparent 25%);
    background-size: 100px 100px;
    background-color: #f1f5f9;
  }
}


@layer components {
  /* =======================================================================
     每日登入獎勵 — the claim celebration (components/UI/DailyLoginPanel.tsx)
     =======================================================================
     One second, entirely inside the card that was just claimed, and quiet on
     purpose: the loud moment in this game is a 神話 purchase reveal, and a
     reward the player collects every day must not spend anything like the
     same amount. Nothing flashes, nothing shakes, nothing leaves the card.

     Four parts on one clock — the card lifts and settles, a few coins drift
     out, the amount floats up, and the tick drops into place. */

  /* The lift. Up 6px, then a soft settle — a card acknowledging a tap, not a
     card jumping. */
  .daily-claim-pop {
    animation: daily-claim-pop 0.62s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.28, 1);
  }

  @keyframes daily-claim-pop {
    0%   { transform: translateY(0) scale(1); }
    32%  { transform: translateY(-6px) scale(1.035); }
    100% { transform: translateY(0) scale(1); }
  }

  /* The coins. Six of them, fanned by index (`--i` is set per element) so they
     leave along different paths without six sets of keyframes — the same trick
     the reveal's rings use for their offset. They start behind the numbers and
     never travel outside the card's own footprint. */
  .daily-claim-coin {
    position: absolute;
    left: 50%;
    top: 40%;
    pointer-events: none;
    opacity: 0;
    /* -35deg to +35deg across the six, so the fan opens upward. */
    --angle: calc((var(--i) - 2.5) * 14deg);
    animation: daily-claim-coin 0.9s ease-out forwards;
    animation-delay: calc(var(--i) * 28ms);
  }

  @keyframes daily-claim-coin {
    0%   { opacity: 0; transform: translate(-50%, -50%) rotate(var(--angle)) translateY(0) scale(0.6); }
    18%  { opacity: 1; }
    100% { opacity: 0; transform: translate(-50%, -50%) rotate(var(--angle)) translateY(-46px) scale(1); }
  }

  /* The amount, floating off the card. Gold, heavy, and gone before the player
     has to decide whether to read it twice. */
  .daily-claim-float {
    position: absolute;
    left: 50%;
    top: 8%;
    translate: -50% 0;
    pointer-events: none;
    font-weight: 900;
    font-size: 1.05rem;
    color: #C98A24;
    text-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.9);
    opacity: 0;
    animation: daily-claim-float 1s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1) forwards;
  }

  @keyframes daily-claim-float {
    0%   { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(4px) scale(0.9); }
    22%  { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(-8px) scale(1); }
    72%  { opacity: 1; }
    100% { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-34px) scale(1); }
  }

  /* The tick, dropping in. Overshoots by a hair on the way down so it lands
     rather than appears. */
  .daily-claim-check {
    animation: daily-claim-check 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.2, 1.5, 0.4, 1) 0.28s backwards;
  }

  @keyframes daily-claim-check {
    0%   { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-9px) scale(0.5); }
    100% { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0) scale(1); }
  }

  /* 金幣入袋 — the coins travelling from the claimed card to the wallet chip.
     Positions come from the component, which measures both ends at claim time
     (see useCoinFlight); everything here is the motion between them.

     `--x`/`--y` are where the coin starts in the board's own coordinates and
     `--dx`/`--dy` the vector to the wallet. Keeping the delta separate from the
     origin is what lets one keyframe serve a coin flying up-right on a desktop
     and one flying almost straight up on a phone.

     The 34% waypoint is a LIFT, not a curve for its own sake: coins that travel
     in a straight line read as sliding, and this is meant to read as thrown. It
     is applied as a fraction of the trip rather than a fixed offset so a short
     hop on a narrow screen arcs proportionally instead of looping. */
  .daily-coin-fly {
    position: absolute;
    left: 0;
    top: 0;
    pointer-events: none;
    z-index: 2;
    opacity: 0;
    animation: daily-coin-fly 0.64s cubic-bezier(0.36, 0.02, 0.2, 1) forwards;
    animation-delay: calc(var(--i) * 55ms);
  }

  @keyframes daily-coin-fly {
    0% {
      opacity: 0;
      transform: translate(var(--x), var(--y)) scale(0.45);
    }
    14% {
      opacity: 1;
      transform: translate(var(--x), calc(var(--y) - 10px)) scale(1.08);
    }
    34% {
      transform:
        translate(calc(var(--x) + var(--dx) * 0.34), calc(var(--y) + var(--dy) * 0.34 - 22px))
        scale(1);
    }
    88% { opacity: 1; }
    /* Lands SMALL. A coin that arrives full size sits on top of the wallet as a
       coin; shrinking into it is what reads as going in. */
    100% {
      opacity: 0;
      transform: translate(calc(var(--x) + var(--dx)), calc(var(--y) + var(--dy))) scale(0.3);
    }
  }

  /* The wallet taking the money. One short swell with the gold ring flashing
     around it — the counter is already ticking up on its own (useCountUp), and
     this is only what tells the eye WHERE to look while it does. */
  .daily-wallet-hit {
    animation: daily-wallet-hit 0.42s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1.4, 0.36, 1);
  }

  @keyframes daily-wallet-hit {
    0%   { transform: scale(1); filter: drop-shadow(0 0 0 rgba(232, 170, 62, 0)); }
    38%  { transform: scale(1.14); filter: drop-shadow(0 0 12px rgba(232, 170, 62, 0.75)); }
    100% { transform: scale(1); filter: drop-shadow(0 0 0 rgba(232, 170, 62, 0)); }
  }

  /* 本輪大獎's halo. A single soft radial behind the card's content, sized to
     stay inside the card — light coming off the prize, not a second card. */
  .daily-grand-glow {
    position: absolute;
    inset: -14%;
    border-radius: inherit;
    pointer-events: none;
    background: radial-gradient(closest-side, rgba(243, 197, 102, 0.42), transparent 72%);
  }

  /* Reduced motion: the claim still REPORTS itself — the tick appears, the
     amount is readable, the balance still updates — but nothing travels. A
     silent claim would read as the button having failed. */
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    .daily-claim-pop,
    .daily-claim-check {
      animation: none;
    }

    .daily-claim-coin {
      display: none;
    }

    /* The flight is travel by definition, so it does not happen. The wallet
       still flashes: with the coins gone it is the only thing left that says
       the money went THERE, and a flash is not motion. */
    .daily-coin-fly {
      display: none;
    }

    .daily-wallet-hit {
      animation: daily-wallet-hit-still 0.42s linear;
    }

    @keyframes daily-wallet-hit-still {
      0%, 100% { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 0 rgba(232, 170, 62, 0)); }
      38%      { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 12px rgba(232, 170, 62, 0.75)); }
    }

    .daily-claim-float {
      animation: daily-claim-float-still 1s linear forwards;
    }

    @keyframes daily-claim-float-still {
      0%, 80% { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(-10px); }
      100%    { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-10px); }
    }
  }
}


@layer components {
  /* =======================================================================
     每日登入 領取揭曉 — the full-screen claim moment
     (components/UI/DailyClaimReveal.tsx)
     =======================================================================
     The purchase reveal's vocabulary played on gold, at a third of its
     length. `.rarity-reveal-*` above is the model for every layer here and
     the reasoning written over each of those rules applies to its twin — the
     near-opaque dim, the flash that fades OUT rather than in, the rings as a
     pulse rather than a thicker ring, the rays masked well inside the
     viewport. What differs is the clock: everything blooms at 900ms rather
     than 4500ms, and the arrival is over in well under two seconds.

     Not shared with those rules, deliberately. They are graded by 稀有度 and
     read their colours from `--rarity-*` custom properties set per tier; this
     one is always gold and always the same, and folding it in would mean a
     tier variable for "the currency" plus a second timeline inside keyframes
     that already carry one. Two short timelines beat one that branches.

     THE TIMELINE (ms from the start; REVEAL_SETTLE_MS is 900):
       0     the screen drops to dark, rays bleed in
       0-900 the coin turns in from far away, decelerating
       900   THE STOP — flash, bloom, three rings, sparks, confetti, sound,
             haptic, 大獎's screen shake, and the label
       1010  the amount slams in
       1120  金幣已入袋
       1300  a tap is accepted and 結束 appears
       ...   the stage HOLDS here — the coin breathes, the amount stays up —
             until the player presses 結束 or taps the backdrop
       +280  faded out; the board takes over, pays into the wallet, and the
             每日登入獎勵 panel closes itself behind it */

  /* The whole layer's fade, overriding ModalOverlay's motion-driven opacity —
     legal, and for the same reason `.rarity-reveal-layer` does it: a CSS
     animation wins over an inline style.

     Fades IN and then holds. It used to be one 3.15s animation that faded the
     layer back out at the end, which is what made the reveal dismiss itself;
     the moment now ends when the player presses 結束 (DailyClaimReveal.tsx),
     and `.is-exiting` is that press. Two animations rather than one so the
     hold has no duration to run out of. */
  .daily-reveal-layer {
    animation: daily-reveal-layer-in 0.22s linear both;
  }

  .daily-reveal-layer.is-exiting {
    animation: daily-reveal-layer-out 0.28s linear forwards;
  }

  @keyframes daily-reveal-layer-in {
    from { opacity: 0; }
    to   { opacity: 1; }
  }

  @keyframes daily-reveal-layer-out {
    from { opacity: 1; }
    to   { opacity: 0; }
  }

  /* The dark. background-COLOR and never the `background` shorthand — a
     shorthand is not interpolatable and animating it in a keyframe silently
     does nothing (see `.rarity-reveal-dim`, where that cost an hour).

     Warmer and one notch lighter than the purchase reveal's near-black: there
     is no silhouette to resolve here, the coin is legible from the first
     frame, and 0.9 of a brown-black keeps the moment reading as lamplight on
     metal rather than as the lights going out. */
  .daily-reveal-dim {
    position: absolute;
    inset: 0;
    background-color: rgba(14, 10, 8, 0);
    animation: daily-reveal-dim 0.28s ease-out forwards;
  }

  @keyframes daily-reveal-dim {
    from { background-color: rgba(14, 10, 8, 0); }
    to   { background-color: rgba(14, 10, 8, 0.9); }
  }

  /* Light thrown off the shard. Same repeating-conic construction as the
     purchase reveal's rays, and masked so they die well inside
     the viewport — rays that reach the corners stop reading as light off the
     coin and start reading as fog over the page.

     Two-stage on purpose: a low bleed while the coin is still turning (this
     is the space it turns INSIDE, and it must stay under the coin rather than
     compete with it), then a flare exactly on the stop at 31% of the span. */
  .daily-reveal-rays {
    position: absolute;
    left: 50%;
    top: 42%;
    width: 190vmax;
    aspect-ratio: 1;
    translate: -50% -50%;
    background: repeating-conic-gradient(
      from 0deg,
      rgba(198, 237, 229, 0.9) 0deg 1.6deg,
      transparent 1.6deg 8deg
    );
    -webkit-mask-image: radial-gradient(closest-side, transparent 3%, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9) 14%, transparent 40%);
    mask-image: radial-gradient(closest-side, transparent 3%, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9) 14%, transparent 40%);
    opacity: 0;
    animation: daily-reveal-rays 2.6s ease-out 0.1s forwards;
  }

  @keyframes daily-reveal-rays {
    0%   { opacity: 0; rotate: 0deg; scale: 0.4; }
    16%  { opacity: 0.16; }
    28%  { opacity: 0.18; scale: 0.82; }
    31%  { opacity: 0.46; scale: 0.94; }
    100% { opacity: 0; rotate: 26deg; scale: 1.16; }
  }

  /* The flash, on the stop. Up in a tenth of its life and down over the rest,
     because a flash that fades IN is a lightbulb. */
  .daily-reveal-flash {
    position: absolute;
    inset: 0;
    background: #FFFFFF;
    opacity: 0;
    animation: daily-reveal-flash 0.45s ease-out 0.9s both;
  }

  @keyframes daily-reveal-flash {
    0%   { opacity: 0; }
    10%  { opacity: 0.85; }
    100% { opacity: 0; }
  }

  /* The bloom under it: tinted rather than white, because the two are doing
     different jobs — the flash is the shutter, this is light coming OFF the
     shard that just landed.

     Teal, not gold. Every colour in this reveal follows the CURRENCY it is
     celebrating, and the daily round pays 碎片 (see DailyClaimReveal.tsx and
     constants/dailyLogin.ts). island-gold stays reserved for 金幣. */
  .daily-reveal-burst {
    position: absolute;
    inset: 0;
    background: radial-gradient(closest-side at 50% 42%, #FFFFFF 0%, #7FCFC3 42%, rgba(42, 157, 143, 0) 76%);
    opacity: 0;
    animation: daily-reveal-burst 0.6s ease-out 0.9s both;
  }

  @keyframes daily-reveal-burst {
    0%   { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.55); }
    18%  { opacity: 0.6; }
    100% { opacity: 0; transform: scale(1.35); }
  }

  /* 能量環 — three, each a beat behind the last, so it reads as a pulse
     travelling outwards rather than as one ring that got thicker. Three
     rather than the purchase reveal's two: this is the one place the daily
     claim is allowed to be the louder of the pair, and rings are cheap.
     Sized in vmin so they clear the coin on a phone and stay on screen on a
     desktop. */
  .daily-reveal-ring {
    position: absolute;
    left: 50%;
    top: 42%;
    width: 30vmin;
    aspect-ratio: 1;
    translate: -50% -50%;
    border-radius: 50%;
    border: 2px solid #7FCFC3;
    box-shadow: 0 0 26px rgba(127, 207, 195, 0.55), inset 0 0 26px rgba(127, 207, 195, 0.45);
    opacity: 0;
    animation: daily-reveal-ring 0.9s cubic-bezier(0.1, 0.7, 0.2, 1) 0.92s forwards;
  }

  .daily-reveal-ring-2 {
    animation-delay: 1.06s;
    border-width: 1px;
  }

  .daily-reveal-ring-3 {
    animation-delay: 1.2s;
    border-width: 1px;
    border-color: rgba(234, 251, 247, 0.75);
  }

  @keyframes daily-reveal-ring {
    0%   { opacity: 0; scale: 0.22; }
    20%  { opacity: 0.9; }
    100% { opacity: 0; scale: 2.3; }
  }

  /* The stage: everything that belongs to the coin and its copy.

     `perspective` is what makes the turn below a turn — the coin rotates
     about its own vertical axis, and without a vanishing point a Y rotation
     on a flat element is not a rotation at all, it is a horizontal squash.
     900px matches the purchase reveal's, and against a 180px coin it is close
     enough that the near edge visibly swings toward the viewer. */
  .daily-reveal-stage {
    position: relative;
    z-index: 1;
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 1.4rem;
    perspective: 900px;
  }

  /* The pool of light the coin lands in, behind everything it lights. */
  .daily-reveal-glow {
    position: absolute;
    width: 460px;
    max-width: 92vw;
    aspect-ratio: 1;
    border-radius: 50%;
    pointer-events: none;
    background: radial-gradient(closest-side, rgba(127, 207, 195, 0.5), rgba(42, 157, 143, 0.14) 45%, transparent 72%);
    opacity: 0;
    animation: daily-reveal-glow 1.1s ease-out 0.86s forwards;
  }

  @keyframes daily-reveal-glow {
    0%   { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.5); }
    30%  { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1.06); }
    100% { opacity: 0.72; transform: scale(1); }
  }

  /* 硬幣進場 — from far away, turning, and decelerating into a bounce.

     The turn count is a custom property (`--reveal-turns`, set per day by the
     component) so 大獎 spinning harder is a number at the call site and not a
     second copy of these keyframes. It is spent on the way IN: by 72% the
     coin is nearly face-on and only the last few degrees are left, which is
     what makes the stop feel like something arriving rather than like an
     animation running out.

     The overshoot at 72% and the dip at 86% are the whole trick. A coin that
     eases to exactly 1.0 lands like a value being set; one that goes past its
     size and comes back has weight. */
  .daily-reveal-spin {
    transform-origin: center;
    animation: daily-reveal-spin 0.9s cubic-bezier(0.16, 0.84, 0.24, 1) both;
  }

  @keyframes daily-reveal-spin {
    0% {
      opacity: 0;
      transform: translateY(-16vh) scale(0.1) rotateY(calc(var(--reveal-turns, 3) * -360deg));
    }
    14%  { opacity: 1; }
    72%  { transform: translateY(0) scale(1.2) rotateY(-26deg); }
    86%  { transform: translateY(0) scale(0.93) rotateY(7deg); }
    100% { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0) scale(1) rotateY(0deg); }
  }

  /* Once it has landed it breathes, so the two seconds the copy is being read
     are not two seconds of a still image. Clipped to its own circle because
     the shine below sweeps across it and must not leave the coin. */
  .daily-reveal-coin {
    position: relative;
    display: block;
    border-radius: 50%;
    overflow: hidden;
    animation: daily-reveal-breathe 2.4s ease-in-out 1s infinite;
  }

  @keyframes daily-reveal-breathe {
    0%, 100% { transform: translateY(0) scale(1); }
    50%      { transform: translateY(-7px) scale(1.03); }
  }

  /* The shine crossing the face on the stop — the one mark that says this is
     metal and not a gold-coloured disc. */
  .daily-reveal-shine {
    position: absolute;
    inset: 0;
    pointer-events: none;
    background: linear-gradient(100deg, transparent 38%, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.85) 50%, transparent 62%);
    opacity: 0;
    animation: daily-reveal-shine 0.75s ease-out 0.92s forwards;
  }

  @keyframes daily-reveal-shine {
    0%   { opacity: 0; transform: translateX(-130%); }
    25%  { opacity: 1; }
    100% { opacity: 0; transform: translateX(130%); }
  }

  /* 火花 — eight, thrown outward as the coin lands. Fanned by index (`--i` is
     set per element) so eight paths cost one set of keyframes, the same trick
     the card's little coins use. */
  .daily-reveal-spark {
    position: absolute;
    left: 50%;
    top: 50%;
    width: 11px;
    height: 11px;
    border-radius: 50%;
    pointer-events: none;
    background: radial-gradient(circle, #EAFBF7 0%, #7FCFC3 52%, rgba(127, 207, 195, 0) 72%);
    --angle: calc(var(--i) * 45deg);
    opacity: 0;
    animation: daily-reveal-spark 0.85s cubic-bezier(0.15, 0.7, 0.3, 1) calc(900ms + var(--i) * 18ms) forwards;
  }

  @keyframes daily-reveal-spark {
    0%   { opacity: 0; transform: translate(-50%, -50%) rotate(var(--angle)) translateY(-40px) scale(0.4); }
    22%  { opacity: 1; }
    100% { opacity: 0; transform: translate(-50%, -50%) rotate(var(--angle)) translateY(-200px) scale(1.15); }
  }

  /* The amount. The headline, and the reason the screen went dark — so it is
     the biggest thing on it, struck with a hard lower edge rather than a
     flat fill, and it arrives out of focus and slams into place.

     `filter` carries the blur alone; the glow is text-shadow rather than a
     drop-shadow so the two are not fighting over the same property mid
     animation. */
  .daily-reveal-amount {
    font-size: clamp(3.2rem, 13vw, 5.4rem);
    font-weight: 900;
    line-height: 1;
    font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
    color: #EAFBF7;
    text-shadow:
      0 3px 0 #1F7A6E,
      0 5px 0 #155F56,
      0 0 26px rgba(127, 207, 195, 0.85),
      0 10px 34px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55);
    opacity: 0;
    animation: daily-reveal-amount 0.62s cubic-bezier(0.2, 1.5, 0.35, 1) both;
  }

  /* The gold cut of it. The round pays several different KINDS of thing now
     (constants/dailyLogin.ts) and the number has to be lit by the same light
     as the mark above it — a teal-shadowed +15 under a gold coin is the
     currency confusion §22 is about, written in the largest type on screen.
     Only the colours differ; the animation and the geometry are shared. */
  .daily-reveal-amount-gold {
    color: #FFF7E2;
    text-shadow:
      0 3px 0 #B87C1C,
      0 5px 0 #8A5C12,
      0 0 26px rgba(242, 194, 96, 0.85),
      0 10px 34px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55);
  }

  @keyframes daily-reveal-amount {
    0%   { opacity: 0; transform: scale(2.6); filter: blur(12px); }
    40%  { opacity: 1; }
    72%  { transform: scale(0.94); filter: blur(0); }
    100% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); filter: blur(0); }
  }

  /* The copy either side of it. One animation, started at a different time per
     line — the stagger is data and lives in the component. */
  .daily-reveal-line {
    opacity: 0;
    animation: daily-reveal-line 0.5s ease-out both;
  }

  @keyframes daily-reveal-line {
    from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(12px); }
    to   { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
  }

  /* The way out, offered only once there is something to leave — before the
     amount has landed there is nothing to dismiss, and a skip offered at the
     first frame is an invitation to dismiss the thing the player came back
     for. Two animations: it fades in once, then breathes. */
  .daily-reveal-hint {
    opacity: 0;
    animation:
      daily-reveal-line 0.5s ease-out 1.8s both,
      daily-reveal-hint 2s ease-in-out 2.3s infinite;
  }

  @keyframes daily-reveal-hint {
    0%, 100% { opacity: 0.85; }
    50%      { opacity: 0.35; }
  }

  /* Reduced motion: the claim still REPORTS itself at full size — the coin,
     the amount and the copy all appear and hold, so the moment is still a
     moment — but nothing travels, spins, flares or sweeps. The confetti opts
     itself out in the component (`disableForReducedMotion`). */
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    .daily-reveal-rays,
    .daily-reveal-flash,
    .daily-reveal-burst { animation: none; opacity: 0.18; }

    .daily-reveal-ring,
    .daily-reveal-spark,
    .daily-reveal-shine { animation: none; opacity: 0; }

    .daily-reveal-glow { animation: daily-reveal-line 0.4s ease-out both; }

    .daily-reveal-spin,
    .daily-reveal-coin { animation: none; }

    /* The number still arrives — it just arrives by appearing. */
    .daily-reveal-amount { animation: daily-reveal-line 0.4s ease-out both; }
  }
}


@layer components {
  /* =======================================================================
     商品碎片 — 稜鏡 (components/UI/FragmentProgress.tsx)
     =======================================================================
     The fragment track used to be one flat teal bar. Teal was the right
     FAMILY — a fragment is earned, not spent, so it must never wear the gold
     that means currency — but one flat colour said nothing except "a bar",
     and the one thing a fragment stack has to say is 「我走了多遠」.

     So the bar is a PRISM: a shard of glass splits light, and this one splits
     it further the more of it there is. The ramp below runs teal → 水藍 →
     violet → 珊瑚, anchored on --color-island-teal at 0% and landing on the
     existing --color-island-coral at 100%, so it is a new gradient inside the
     island palette rather than a seventh colour scheme.

     THE MECHANIC — the ramp is painted across the whole TRACK and then
     clipped to the fill, not stretched to fit it. A stack at 30% shows the
     teal-to-sky third of the ramp and nothing else; only a full 200/200 has
     the violet and the coral in it. The colour is therefore a second reading
     of the same number: 「越接近集滿，越繽紛」. Stretching the ramp to the
     fill would make every stack look identical and cost the feature the only
     thing the colour was bought for. `.fragment-ink` is sized by the
     component (see FragmentBar) for exactly this reason. */
  :root {
    --fragment-1: #2A9D8F; /* = --color-island-teal, the anchor */
    --fragment-2: #35C6B4;
    --fragment-3: #4FB9E8;
    --fragment-4: #8E8CEB;
    --fragment-5: #CE84D8;
    --fragment-6: #E8836A; /* = --color-island-coral */
    --fragment-ramp: linear-gradient(
      90deg,
      var(--fragment-1) 0%,
      var(--fragment-2) 22%,
      var(--fragment-3) 44%,
      var(--fragment-4) 64%,
      var(--fragment-5) 82%,
      var(--fragment-6) 100%
    );
  }

  /* The empty track. Carries a whisper of the same ramp (4%) so an untouched
     bar still belongs to the coloured one it will become, plus an inset
     hairline so the fill reads as sitting INSIDE a channel rather than as a
     stripe painted on the card. */
  .fragment-track {
    position: relative;
    overflow: hidden;
    border-radius: 999px;
    background-color: #E7E3DA;
    background-image: linear-gradient(
      90deg,
      rgba(42, 157, 143, 0.10),
      rgba(79, 185, 232, 0.08) 45%,
      rgba(206, 132, 216, 0.08) 78%,
      rgba(232, 131, 106, 0.10)
    );
    box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px rgba(38, 70, 83, 0.10);
  }

  /* The clip. Width is the progress, and it is the ONLY thing that animates
     when a workout pays out — the ink underneath does not move, so the hues
     already earned stay exactly where they were and the bar grows into new
     colour instead of resliding through it. */
  .fragment-fill {
    position: absolute;
    inset: 0 auto 0 0;
    overflow: hidden;
    border-radius: 999px;
    transition: width 600ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.28, 1);
  }

  /* The ramp itself, stretched to the TRACK by an inline width (100/pct×100%)
     and then clipped by the fill above. */
  .fragment-ink {
    position: absolute;
    inset: 0 auto 0 0;
    background-image: var(--fragment-ramp);
    background-size: 100% 100%;
  }

  /* 折光 — one gloss travelling the bar, the thing that makes it read as
     glass rather than as paint. Slow (3.4s) and low-contrast on purpose: this
     sits under every card on the shelf, and a shelf of racing bars is a
     shelf nobody can read a price off. */
  .fragment-sheen {
    position: absolute;
    inset: 0;
    background-image: linear-gradient(
      104deg,
      rgba(255, 255, 255, 0) 38%,
      rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.85) 50%,
      rgba(255, 255, 255, 0) 62%
    );
    background-size: 260% 100%;
    background-repeat: no-repeat;
    opacity: 0.55;
    animation: fragment-sheen 3.4s ease-in-out infinite;
  }

  @keyframes fragment-sheen {
    0%   { background-position: -60% 0; }
    55%  { background-position: 160% 0; }
    100% { background-position: 160% 0; }
  }

  /* Quarter marks. They turn 「74 / 200」 into a shape the eye can judge
     without reading the number, and they are the reason the bar can afford to
     be short. Dark rather than white so they are legible on the pale empty
     half as well as on the lit one. */
  .fragment-notch {
    position: absolute;
    top: 0;
    bottom: 0;
    width: 1px;
    background: rgba(38, 70, 83, 0.16);
  }

  /* 集滿. The stack is full, the whole ramp is showing, and the bar says so
     by lighting the card around it — the halo is violet-to-coral (the END of
     the ramp) rather than teal, so 「可解鎖」 is the far end of the same
     journey and not a different state colour. */
  .fragment-ready {
    box-shadow:
      inset 0 1px 2px rgba(38, 70, 83, 0.10),
      0 0 0 1px rgba(142, 140, 235, 0.35),
      0 4px 14px -4px rgba(206, 132, 216, 0.65);
    animation: fragment-ready-pulse 2.6s ease-in-out infinite;
  }

  @keyframes fragment-ready-pulse {
    0%, 100% {
      box-shadow:
        inset 0 1px 2px rgba(38, 70, 83, 0.10),
        0 0 0 1px rgba(142, 140, 235, 0.30),
        0 4px 12px -5px rgba(206, 132, 216, 0.45);
    }
    50% {
      box-shadow:
        inset 0 1px 2px rgba(38, 70, 83, 0.10),
        0 0 0 1px rgba(206, 132, 216, 0.55),
        0 6px 18px -4px rgba(232, 131, 106, 0.70);
    }
  }

  /* The block the meter sits in on a shop card — a tinted well so 「另一條
     路」 reads as its own offer next to the gold price, instead of as two
     more lines of card copy. Kept at 7% because it is behind text. */
  .fragment-well {
    border-radius: 0.9rem;
    border: 1px solid rgba(142, 140, 235, 0.20);
    background-image: linear-gradient(
      135deg,
      rgba(42, 157, 143, 0.09) 0%,
      rgba(79, 185, 232, 0.07) 45%,
      rgba(206, 132, 216, 0.07) 72%,
      rgba(232, 131, 106, 0.09) 100%
    );
  }

  .fragment-well-ready {
    border-color: rgba(206, 132, 216, 0.42);
    background-image: linear-gradient(
      135deg,
      rgba(42, 157, 143, 0.14) 0%,
      rgba(79, 185, 232, 0.12) 45%,
      rgba(206, 132, 216, 0.14) 72%,
      rgba(232, 131, 106, 0.16) 100%
    );
  }

  /* The count, written in the ramp itself. Only ever used on 集滿 and on the
     +N of a fresh grant: gradient text is thinner to read than solid navy, so
     it is spent on the two numbers that are an announcement rather than on
     every number on the shelf. */
  .fragment-ramp-text {
    background-image: var(--fragment-ramp);
    background-size: 140% 100%;
    -webkit-background-clip: text;
    background-clip: text;
    color: transparent;
  }

  /* The shard mark when its stack is full. */
  .fragment-shard-lit {
    filter: drop-shadow(0 0 3px rgba(142, 140, 235, 0.65));
  }

  /* Reduced motion: the bar keeps every colour — the ramp IS the readout and
     removing it would remove information — and only the two things that move
     stop. */
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    .fragment-fill { transition: none; }
    .fragment-sheen { animation: none; opacity: 0.25; background-position: 40% 0; }
    .fragment-ready { animation: none; }
  }
}

@layer components {
  /* ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     幸運轉盤 —— 讓機台活起來的那幾件事
     (components/UI/LuckyWheel.tsx)

     The face was never the problem: ten wedges, ten prizes, honest odds. What
     it lacked was the CABINET. A prize wheel in the world is a lit object —
     bulbs round the rim, a ticker being hit, a turned knob in the middle, and
     light thrown on the wall behind it — and none of that is on the wedges.
     Everything in this block is the machine around the drawing, and every rule
     obeys the same two constraints:

       1. **Nothing here is information.** A player who never notices one pixel
          of it still reads the same ten prizes and the same odds. So it may be
          cut entirely by prefers-reduced-motion, at the bottom, without taking
          anything with it.
       2. **Nothing here is gold.** island-gold is 金幣 (see the token), and ten
          glowing discs round the rim of a PRIZE wheel would read as a payout
          before they read as decoration. The bulbs are lamplight — a filament
          warm, sat in a white socket, and visibly going out again.
     ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */

  /* The pool of light the cabinet stands in. Sized off the wheel's own box and
     pushed out past it, so the panel has a centre even before anything moves. */
  .wheel-stage::before {
    content: '';
    position: absolute;
    inset: -16%;
    border-radius: 9999px;
    background: radial-gradient(
      circle,
      rgba(42, 157, 143, 0.15) 0%,
      rgba(42, 157, 143, 0.06) 44%,
      rgba(42, 157, 143, 0) 70%
    );
    pointer-events: none;
  }

  /* The ray fan behind the wheel.

     Masked to a RING that starts outside the bezel (the wheel's outer lip lands
     at ~38% of this element's radius; the mask opens at 44%), because rays that
     reach under the face would be a pattern showing through the prizes instead
     of light coming off the machine. 78s is deliberately at the edge of
     noticing: this runs the whole time the panel is open, and anything faster
     turns a prize table into a screensaver. The spin state is the exception —
     see .wheel-rays-fast. */
  .wheel-rays {
    position: absolute;
    inset: -15%;
    border-radius: 9999px;
    pointer-events: none;
    background: repeating-conic-gradient(
      from 0deg,
      rgba(42, 157, 143, 0.17) 0deg 7deg,
      rgba(42, 157, 143, 0) 7deg 18deg
    );
    -webkit-mask-image: radial-gradient(circle, transparent 44%, #000 58%, transparent 92%);
    mask-image: radial-gradient(circle, transparent 44%, #000 58%, transparent 92%);
    animation: wheel-rays-turn 78s linear infinite;
  }

  /* While a spin is running. It is the one thing in the panel that says 「正在
     轉」 without being the wheel — which matters, because the wheel is the thing
     the player is trying to read, and a result you are watching for should not
     be the only place the state is written. */
  .wheel-rays-fast {
    animation-duration: 9s;
  }

  @keyframes wheel-rays-turn {
    to { transform: rotate(360deg); }
  }

  /* One bulb's lit layer — the halo and the hot filament, both under the same
     class so they light and die together. The chase is ONE animation given a
     NEGATIVE delay per index (LuckyWheel.tsx computes it): ten bulbs each
     starting a tenth of a cycle into the same loop is a light running around
     the rim, where ten separate timings would be ten things blinking. */
  .wheel-bulb {
    animation: wheel-bulb-chase 2.6s ease-in-out infinite;
  }

  /* A spin quadruples the marquee. Same chase, same order — a fairground turns
     its lights up when the wheel is moving, not on a different pattern. */
  .wheel-lit .wheel-bulb {
    animation-duration: 0.62s;
  }

  /* Long dark, short bright: a bulb that is on half the time reads as ten bulbs
     flickering. The 38% step is the filament cooling rather than snapping off. */
  @keyframes wheel-bulb-chase {
    0%, 100% { opacity: 0.12; }
    12%      { opacity: 1; }
    38%      { opacity: 0.22; }
  }

  /* The winning wedge, outlined in light. Flares, then keeps two thirds of it —
     the wedge stays marked while the prize card is being read, and the mark is
     an OUTLINE so the prize itself is never covered by its own announcement. */
  .wheel-wedge-win {
    animation: wheel-wedge-win 1.5s cubic-bezier(0.16, 0.9, 0.3, 1) forwards;
    filter: drop-shadow(0 0 3px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.9));
  }

  @keyframes wheel-wedge-win {
    0%   { opacity: 0; }
    14%  { opacity: 1; }
    100% { opacity: 0.62; }
  }

  /* ── The hub, as a turned knob ─────────────────────────────────────────────
     It was a flat teal disc with a cream border: the correct token, and no
     object. This is the Toolbar lesson from DESIGN_SYSTEM.md applied to a round
     control — 「change the construction, not the colour」. It is the same teal.

       · the conic gradient is the knurl catching light on four sides, which is
         what a metal knob does and a painted one does not;
       · inset 0 2px 0 white is the crown, inset 0 -5px 10px navy the undercut;
       · the two 0-blur rings are the collar it is seated in, so the knob has a
         white lip against whatever wedge happens to be behind it. */
  .wheel-hub {
    background:
      radial-gradient(circle at 34% 26%, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.55) 0%, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0) 56%),
      conic-gradient(
        from 210deg,
        #2A9D8F 0deg,
        #45BCAC 34deg,
        #2A9D8F 72deg,
        #1F7A70 110deg,
        #2A9D8F 150deg,
        #45BCAC 190deg,
        #2A9D8F 228deg,
        #1F7A70 268deg,
        #2A9D8F 306deg,
        #45BCAC 340deg,
        #2A9D8F 360deg
      );
    box-shadow:
      0 0 0 3px var(--color-island-cream),
      0 0 0 4.5px var(--color-island-line),
      inset 0 2px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.45),
      inset 0 -5px 10px rgba(26, 46, 53, 0.30),
      0 8px 20px rgba(38, 70, 83, 0.34);
  }

  .wheel-hub:hover {
    filter: brightness(1.07);
  }

  /* 抽獎券不足. Same knob, unplated — sand instead of teal, and the drop shadow
     pulled in so it sits DOWN in its collar rather than standing proud of it.
     Still a knob, so the control has not changed shape under the player; it has
     just gone cold. */
  .wheel-hub-off {
    background:
      radial-gradient(circle at 34% 26%, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.75) 0%, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0) 58%),
      conic-gradient(
        from 210deg,
        #EFE9DC 0deg,
        #F8F6F1 60deg,
        #E3DCCA 140deg,
        #F8F6F1 220deg,
        #E3DCCA 300deg,
        #EFE9DC 360deg
      );
    box-shadow:
      0 0 0 3px var(--color-island-cream),
      0 0 0 4.5px var(--color-island-line),
      inset 0 2px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7),
      inset 0 -4px 9px rgba(38, 70, 83, 0.14),
      0 3px 10px rgba(38, 70, 83, 0.16);
  }

  /* A ring breathing off the knob whenever a spin is affordable. The launcher
     out on the island already does this at 2.4s (its animate-ping halo), and
     this is the same promise repeated where the player's hand actually is. */
  .wheel-hub-ready::after {
    content: '';
    position: absolute;
    inset: -11%;
    border-radius: 9999px;
    border: 2px solid rgba(42, 157, 143, 0.45);
    animation: wheel-hub-breathe 2.9s ease-in-out infinite;
    pointer-events: none;
  }

  @keyframes wheel-hub-breathe {
    0%, 100% { opacity: 0.14; transform: scale(0.97); }
    50%      { opacity: 0.85; transform: scale(1.06); }
  }

  /* Every one of these is decoration by construction, so reduced motion simply
     stops them where they look settled rather than hiding them: the marquee is
     left ON (a dark bulb reads as a broken one), the fan is left parked, and the
     winning wedge keeps the outline it would have ended on. Nothing a player
     needs in order to read the wheel lives in this block. */
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    .wheel-rays { animation: none; }
    .wheel-bulb { animation: none; opacity: 0.7; }
    .wheel-hub-ready::after { animation: none; opacity: 0.45; }
    .wheel-wedge-win { animation: none; opacity: 0.62; }
  }
}
```

## src/lib/adminSaveReset.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 清空裝備 — the one genuinely destructive 管理員測試 action, in one place.
 *
 * It used to live inline in ShopView, wired to two buttons in that screen's chrome (the header and
 * the collection drawer). Both were Admin-only, and both sat inside a screen a normal player uses
 * constantly, which is a bad home for the only control in the game that can delete an afternoon's
 * decorating. It moved into the 管理員測試 console with everything else; the write is unchanged and
 * lives here so exactly one copy of it exists.
 *
 * WHAT IT WRITES, precisely — this is a reset of the save's CONTENTS and nothing else:
 *
 *   inventory                        emptied
 *   equippedItems                    emptied (the avatar goes back to its default look)
 *   interiorData.placements          emptied (every piece of furniture in the house)
 *   interiorData.selectedFloorStyle  back to 'default'
 *   interiorData.selectedWallStyle   back to 'default'
 *   islandPlacements                 emptied (everything sited outdoors, the Home included)
 *
 * It does NOT touch 金幣, 碎片, 抽獎券, XP, 寵物照護, 每日登入 or 健身獎勵 records. Those have
 * their own controls in the console, and a button that quietly reset a balance while claiming to
 * clear 裝備 would be the kind of surprise this console exists to remove.
 *
 * The caller confirms. This module deliberately does not own the `confirm()` so the copy can name
 * the console it was pressed in — and because a function that cannot be called without a browser
 * dialog is one no test can ever exercise.
 */

import { db, doc, updateDoc } from './firebase';

export interface AdminResetResult {
  ok: boolean;
  /** Present when `ok` is false — already human-readable, safe to show. */
  error?: string;
}

export async function resetOwnedContent(userId: string): Promise<AdminResetResult> {
  try {
    await updateDoc(doc(db, 'users', userId), {
      inventory: [],
      equippedItems: [],
      'interiorData.placements': [],
      'interiorData.selectedFloorStyle': 'default',
      'interiorData.selectedWallStyle': 'default',
      islandPlacements: [],
    });
    return { ok: true };
  } catch (e) {
    console.error('[admin] resetOwnedContent failed', e);
    return { ok: false, error: '重製失敗，存檔沒有被修改。請稍後再試。' };
  }
}
```
