```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * THE MOTION MATHS BEHIND EVERY MOVING OUTDOOR OBJECT — one wind field, one pendulum, and
 * nothing else. No React, no three.js, no scene graph: only pure functions of time.
 *
 * ## Why this is a separate file from the runtime that calls it
 *
 * Two things have to agree on where a swinging piece of furniture IS at a given moment, and they
 * live at opposite ends of the codebase:
 *
 *   Three/FurnitureItem.tsx   draws the seat, the ropes, the hammock's cloth.
 *   Three/Avatar.tsx          drives the body that is sitting on it.
 *
 * Before this file, they did not agree. The hammock's model was static and the AVATAR alone was
 * nudged 2 cm on a `sin(t * 1.5)` — in WORLD space, so a hammock rotated in build mode rocked its
 * occupant sideways across the cloth. The swing was the mirror image: the SEAT swung on its own
 * timer and the player stood beside it playing a push animation. In both cases the piece and the
 * person were two animations that happened to be near each other.
 *
 * They are now one number. Both callers evaluate {@link suspendedAngle} with the same spec and
 * the same two timestamps, so they cannot drift — not because they are carefully kept in step,
 * but because there is only one thing to be in step with.
 *
 * ## Everything here is a pure function of time, and that is a performance decision
 *
 * Nothing integrates. An object's pose at time *t* depends only on *t* (and, for a piece someone
 * is sitting on, on when they sat down) — never on its pose last frame. That is what makes
 * distance and frustum culling FREE: a palm tree that is skipped for two hundred frames because
 * it is behind the camera does not drift out of phase, and does not have to be caught up when it
 * comes back. It simply evaluates the current time and is instantly correct.
 *
 * An integrator would have made culling a trade — smoothness for frames — and every "why did that
 * object pop" bug after it. See Three/outdoorAnimation.tsx for the culling that this buys.
 */

import { WeatherType } from '../types';
import { getWeatherSwayFactors } from '../utils/weatherSway';

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ the wind field */

/**
 * The prevailing wind, radians about +Y. Gusts travel ALONG this direction across the island,
 * which is the cheapest possible way to stop a grove of palms moving as one object: two trees
 * ten metres apart are sampling the same wave at different points on it, so they are out of
 * phase by construction rather than by a per-tree random number.
 */
const WIND_HEADING = 0.72;
const WIND_DX = Math.sin(WIND_HEADING);
const WIND_DZ = Math.cos(WIND_HEADING);

/**
 * How much of a gust cycle one world unit downwind is worth.
 *
 * Small on purpose. At 0.055 a gust front takes about 18 world units to shift a full radian of
 * phase, so neighbouring plants lean together (they are in the same gust) while opposite ends of
 * the island do not (they are not). Crank it up and the island reads as rippling; zero it and
 * every plant is a metronome copy of every other.
 */
const WIND_SPATIAL = 0.055;

/**
 * The three sway harmonics, in cycles per second of wind clock.
 *
 * Deliberately NOT harmonically related: 0.19, 0.47 and 1.13 have no common period inside any
 * time a player will stand and watch, so the sway never visibly repeats. One sine alone is a
 * windscreen wiper; three at these ratios read as air.
 */
const SWAY_HZ = [0.19, 0.47, 1.13] as const;
const SWAY_GAIN = [0.60, 0.28, 0.12] as const;
const SWAY_PHASE = [0, 1.7, 4.1] as const;

/** The gust envelope: slower still, and always positive — the wind drops but never reverses. */
const GUST_HZ = [0.083, 0.21] as const;
const GUST_GAIN = [0.34, 0.16] as const;
const GUST_PHASE = [2.3, 5.0] as const;
const GUST_BASE = 0.5;

const TAU = Math.PI * 2;

/**
 * How hard the wind is blowing, as a function of the weather.
 *
 * A module-level value rather than a React context because the things that read it are the
 * FURNITURE MODELS, which are also rendered by the build-time audits (scripts/lib/
 * measureFurnitureModel.ts) with a stub hook dispatcher that has no provider above it. A model
 * that called `useApp()` to find out how windy it is would throw there, and the audit would file
 * it under "unmeasurable" — which is exactly the hole that harness was written to close.
 *
 * Published by Three/Scene.tsx, which already has the weather.
 */
let windSpeedMult = 1;
let windAmountMult = 1;

export function setWindWeather(weather: WeatherType): void {
  const { speedMult, swayAmt } = getWeatherSwayFactors(weather);
  windSpeedMult = speedMult;
  windAmountMult = swayAmt;
}

/** How far the wind's own amplitude is scaled by the current weather, 0.2 (snow) .. 2.5 (storm). */
export function windAmount(): number {
  return windAmountMult;
}

/**
 * THE WIND CLOCK — accumulated rather than read off `state.clock`, and the reason is a one-line
 * bug that would otherwise ship every time the weather changed.
 *
 * The obvious implementation is `sin(elapsed * speedMult)`: multiply the clock by how windy it
 * is. But `speedMult` jumps from 1.0 to 2.8 the moment a storm rolls in, and multiplying an
 * already-large elapsed time by a different constant TELEPORTS the phase — every plant on the
 * island snaps to a new angle on that one frame. Integrating the multiplier instead means a
 * storm makes the wind speed UP from wherever it currently is, which is what weather does.
 *
 * One accumulator for the whole island, advanced once per frame by the animation driver.
 */
let windClockSeconds = 0;

export function advanceWindClock(delta: number): number {
  // Clamped: a tab that has been in the background hands back a delta of several seconds, and
  // letting that through would fast-forward every plant by half a minute on the frame the player
  // comes back to it.
  windClockSeconds += Math.min(delta, 0.1) * windSpeedMult;
  return windClockSeconds;
}

export function windClock(): number {
  return windClockSeconds;
}

/** What the wind is doing at one point on the island. Reused in place — never held across calls. */
export interface WindSample {
  /** Signed sway along the prevailing wind, roughly -1..1 before weather scaling. */
  sway: number;
  /**
   * A second, decorrelated sway for the perpendicular axis. Applying only `sway` makes every
   * leaf trace a straight line back and forth; a small amount of this turns it into a figure,
   * which is the difference between a hinge and a leaf.
   */
  cross: number;
  /** 0..1, how hard it is blowing right now. Never negative — the wind drops, it does not flip. */
  gust: number;
}

/**
 * Samples the wind at a world position.
 *
 * `lag` shifts the sample BACK in time, which is how follow-through is done here: a frond that
 * reads the field 0.2 s in the past is a frond that trails what the trunk is doing, with no
 * spring, no state and no extra cost. Every node of a wind rig is the same field at a different
 * moment.
 *
 * Writes into `out` and returns it. Called once per animated object per frame, so it allocates
 * nothing.
 */
export function sampleWind(x: number, z: number, lag: number, out: WindSample): WindSample {
  // The gust front travels downwind: a point further along the wind direction sees the same wave
  // later, so `u` runs backwards with distance.
  const u = windClockSeconds - lag - (x * WIND_DX + z * WIND_DZ) * WIND_SPATIAL;

  let sway = 0;
  let cross = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    const w = TAU * SWAY_HZ[i] * u + SWAY_PHASE[i];
    sway += SWAY_GAIN[i] * Math.sin(w);
    // The perpendicular component is the SAME harmonics read a quarter turn round, which is what
    // makes it decorrelated from `sway` without a second set of constants to keep in step.
    cross += SWAY_GAIN[i] * Math.sin(w * 0.83 + 2.1);
  }

  let gust = GUST_BASE;
  for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) gust += GUST_GAIN[i] * Math.sin(TAU * GUST_HZ[i] * u + GUST_PHASE[i]);

  // The gust modulates the sway rather than sitting beside it: a lull genuinely stills the
  // leaves instead of just making a constant wiggle quieter.
  const drive = 0.45 + gust * 0.55;
  out.sway = sway * drive * windAmountMult;
  out.cross = cross * drive * windAmountMult * 0.6;
  out.gust = gust * windAmountMult;
  return out;
}

/**
 * The ANGLE a wind-driven rotor has turned to — the antiderivative of the gust, in closed form.
 *
 * A spinning ornament cannot use {@link sampleWind} directly: an angle is the integral of a
 * speed, and integrating per frame would be the one piece of state that breaks the "pure function
 * of time" rule the whole system rests on (a mobile culled behind the camera for ten seconds
 * would come back ten seconds behind everything else). Because the gust is a sum of sines, its
 * integral is a sum of cosines, so the angle can be evaluated directly at any *t*.
 *
 * The result is a rotor that never turns at a constant rate and never stops — it winds up in a
 * gust and coasts nearly to a stall in a lull, which is what the brief asks for and what a fixed
 * `rotation.y += speed` cannot do.
 */
export function windRotorAngle(x: number, z: number, turnsPerSecond: number): number {
  const s = (x * WIND_DX + z * WIND_DZ) * WIND_SPATIAL;
  const u = windClockSeconds - s;
  // d/dt of `u` is 1 (the spatial term is constant per object), so each sine integrates to
  // -cos/(2*pi*f) with no chain-rule factor to carry.
  let integral = GUST_BASE * u;
  for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
    const w = TAU * GUST_HZ[i];
    integral -= (GUST_GAIN[i] / w) * Math.cos(w * u + GUST_PHASE[i]);
  }
  return integral * turnsPerSecond * TAU * windAmountMult;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------- pieces that hang and swing */

/**
 * A piece of furniture that hangs from something and swings under its occupant.
 *
 * Stated as data (constants/outdoorAnimation.ts) rather than as code inside the two models that
 * currently need it, because the interesting property of the swing rework is that the hammock
 * got it for free: the same spec, the same solver, two different pivot heights.
 */
export interface SuspendedSpec {
  /**
   * Pivot to seat, world units. Sets the NATURAL PERIOD via the pendulum law, which is why a
   * long-roped swing and a short-slung hammock have different rhythms without either being
   * hand-timed. Nothing else in this file has a number that came from taste.
   */
  length: number;
  /** Where the pivot is, measured up from the piece's own base in the world units it is drawn at. */
  pivotY: number;
  /** Which of the piece's own local axes it rocks about. */
  axis: 'x' | 'z';
  /** The kick the moment weight lands on it, radians. */
  impulse: number;
  /** Seconds for that kick to die away. */
  impulseDecay: number;
  /** The amplitude a settled rider sustains, radians. */
  ride: number;
  /** Seconds from sitting down to reaching `ride` — the "slowly increase" half of the brief. */
  buildUp: number;
  /** Seconds for an empty piece to come back to rest after a rider leaves. */
  release: number;
  /** Amplitude with nobody on it: wind only, radians. Never zero — a hung thing is never still. */
  idle: number;
  /** A one-off vertical dip as weight lands, world units. A hammock's cloth sags; a swing does not. */
  sag: number;
  /**
   * How much of the piece's tilt the RIDER'S BODY carries, 0..1.
   *
   * 1 is rigid with the piece. A swing is near-rigid (you and the seat go over together); a
   * hammock is 0, because its rock is about the rope line, which for a body lying ALONG that
   * line is a roll rather than a pitch — and the controller only offers a pitch. The body still
   * translates with the cloth either way, which is the part that reads as "in the hammock".
   */
  bodyFollow: number;
}

/** Where a suspended piece is in its life, as two timestamps and the wind. */
export interface SuspendedPhase {
  /** Seconds since the current occupant got on, or null when nobody is on it. */
  since: number | null;
  /** How long the last occupant rode it, seconds. 0 if it has never been used. */
  rode: number;
  /** Seconds since the last occupant got off. `Infinity` if it has never been used. */
  free: number;
  /** The wind's sway at the piece, from {@link sampleWind}. */
  wind: number;
}

const GRAVITY = 9.81;

/**
 * How far the wind's own rhythm bends the pendulum's, in radians of phase.
 *
 * The whole point of the note "不要像鐘擺一樣完全固定速度". A real swing in a garden is not a
 * laboratory pendulum: the air pushes it about, so successive arcs are not quite the same length
 * and the beat wanders. This is that, as one term.
 */
const RHYTHM_WOBBLE = 0.14;
const RHYTHM_WOBBLE_HZ = 0.11;

/** The swing's own natural frequency, plus the wobble that stops it being a metronome. */
function pendulumPhase(spec: SuspendedSpec, elapsed: number): number {
  const omega = Math.sqrt(GRAVITY / Math.max(0.05, spec.length));
  return omega * elapsed + RHYTHM_WOBBLE * Math.sin(TAU * RHYTHM_WOBBLE_HZ * elapsed);
}

/** The amplitude a rider has worked up to, `elapsed` seconds after getting on. */
function ridingAmplitude(spec: SuspendedSpec, elapsed: number): number {
  return spec.impulse * Math.exp(-elapsed / spec.impulseDecay)
    + spec.ride * (1 - Math.exp(-elapsed / Math.max(0.05, spec.buildUp)));
}

/**
 * THE ANGLE, radians about {@link SuspendedSpec.axis}. Called by the model AND by the character
 * controller, with the same arguments, which is the entire synchronisation mechanism.
 *
 * Three regimes, and the seams between them are continuous by construction rather than by
 * blending — the released case simply keeps evaluating the same oscillator the ridden case
 * left off, with a decaying envelope over the top.
 */
export function suspendedAngle(spec: SuspendedSpec, p: SuspendedPhase): number {
  const windRest = spec.idle * p.wind;

  if (p.since != null) {
    // OCCUPIED. Starts at zero and grows: the impulse is the body landing, the build-up is the
    // rider working it up. Nothing is instant, which is the "從靜止開始，緩慢增加擺動幅度" note.
    const amp = ridingAmplitude(spec, p.since);
    return amp * Math.sin(pendulumPhase(spec, p.since)) + windRest * 0.35;
  }

  if (!Number.isFinite(p.free)) return windRest;

  // JUST RELEASED. The phase carries straight on through the moment they got off (hence
  // `rode + free`), so the piece does not jump; the envelope decays toward the wind idle it
  // would have had all along.
  const decay = Math.exp(-p.free / Math.max(0.05, spec.release));
  const amp = ridingAmplitude(spec, p.rode) * decay;
  return amp * Math.sin(pendulumPhase(spec, p.rode + p.free)) + windRest * (1 - decay * 0.65);
}

/**
 * The extra dip under a body's weight, world units (negative is down).
 *
 * Separate from the angle because it is a different physical thing: the cloth stretching, not the
 * whole piece swinging. It is over in about a second and a half and never comes back, which is
 * why it reads as "someone just got in" rather than as part of the idle.
 */
export function suspendedSag(spec: SuspendedSpec, p: SuspendedPhase): number {
  if (spec.sag === 0 || p.since == null) return 0;
  return -spec.sag * Math.exp(-p.since * 2.4) * Math.cos(p.since * 7.5);
}

/**
 * THE TWO TIMESTAMPS both halves of a swinging piece keep, and the only state in this file.
 *
 * Held by the MODEL (Three/outdoorAnimation.tsx's `useFurnitureOccupancy`, fed by events) and by
 * the CHARACTER CONTROLLER (Three/Avatar.tsx, which is where the events come from), so that both
 * can build the same {@link SuspendedPhase} for the same frame. The timestamps travel on the
 * event itself rather than being sampled independently at each end — two `performance.now()`
 * calls a few microseconds apart would be close enough to look right and wrong enough to drift
 * over a minute of sitting there.
 */
export interface SuspendedTimeline {
  /** `performance.now()` when the current occupant got on, or null when nobody is on it. */
  mountedAt: number | null;
  /** `performance.now()` when the last occupant got off, or null if it has never been used. */
  releasedAt: number | null;
  /** How long that last occupant rode it, seconds. */
  rode: number;
}

/** Turns the timeline plus the wind into the argument {@link suspendedAngle} wants. */
export function suspendedPhase(tl: SuspendedTimeline, now: number, wind: number): SuspendedPhase {
  return {
    since: tl.mountedAt == null ? null : Math.max(0, (now - tl.mountedAt) / 1000),
    rode: tl.rode,
    free: tl.releasedAt == null ? Infinity : Math.max(0, (now - tl.releasedAt) / 1000),
    wind,
  };
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ per-instance variation */

/**
 * A stable 0..1 from a placement's instance id.
 *
 * Every planted thing needs its own small offsets — a different phase, a slightly different
 * rate, a slightly different reach — or a row of three palms reads as one palm drawn three times.
 * Seeding off the INSTANCE ID rather than `Math.random()` means the same tree wobbles the same
 * way across a reload, and means the drag-preview ghost of a tree matches the tree it becomes.
 */
export function seedFraction(seed: string | number | undefined, salt = 0): number {
  if (seed == null) return 0.5;
  let h = 0x811c9dc5 ^ (salt * 0x9e3779b9);
  const s = String(seed);
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
    h ^= s.charCodeAt(i);
    h = Math.imul(h, 0x01000193);
  }
  return ((h >>> 0) % 100000) / 100000;
}

/** `seedFraction` mapped onto a range — the one-liner every caller was about to write. */
export function seedRange(seed: string | number | undefined, salt: number, lo: number, hi: number): number {
  return lo + seedFraction(seed, salt) * (hi - lo);
}
```

## src/lib/petActivity.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import type { PetPlayStyle, PetReactionId } from '../constants/petInteractions';
import { PET_FEED, PET_PETTING, PET_PLAY } from '../constants/petInteractions';

/**
 * 寵物此刻正在跟主人做什麼 —— 摸摸、吃飯、玩耍 —— 以及牠剛剛做了什麼反應。
 *
 * ## 它取代了什麼
 *
 * 兩個散在 playerBus 上的欄位，各自只說了一半：
 *
 *   `dogIsHappy`   一個布林。迷你遊戲點滿時設 true、`setTimeout` 三秒後設 false。它不知道是哪一隻
 *                  （三隻寵物會一起轉圈）、進行中的「正在被摸」根本沒有表示法，而且一個還沒跑完的
 *                  timer 在玩家離開島嶼時照樣會去改它。
 *   `petEating`    一個時間戳。能說「牠在吃」，說不出碗在哪、牠走到了沒、吃完了沒。
 *
 * 這裡是一張「每一隻寵物一格」的表：UI 那一頭（PettingMiniGame、PetFeeding、PetInteractionPanel）
 * 開始一個活動，3D 那一頭（Three/IslandPet.tsx）推進它的階段、畫出碗和玩具，並在它結束時收掉。
 * 沒有任何 timer：每一個活動的「過期」都是一個時鐘判斷（{@link petActivityExpired}），所以玩家切
 * 走分頁、進了屋子、換了場景，回來時它要嘛還在、要嘛已經自己過期了 —— 不會有一個燒在 timer 裡
 * 的未來事件在沒人看的時候改掉什麼。
 *
 * ## 為什麼不在存檔裡
 *
 * 跟 lib/objectRuntimeState.ts 同一個判斷：這是「此刻」的東西。餵食真正改變的營養值已經由
 * context/usePetCare.ts 寫進存檔；碗在哪、球滾到哪，重新載入之後不存在是對的。
 */

export interface PetPoint {
  x: number;
  y: number;
  z: number;
}

/** 正在被摸。主人每點一下 `lastPatAt` 更新一次。 */
export interface PetPettingActivity {
  kind: 'petting';
  petItemId: string;
  startedAt: number;
  lastPatAt: number;
}

/** 吃飯。碗的位置由 3D 那一頭第一次看到這個活動時解出來（它才知道陸地與家具在哪）。 */
export interface PetEatActivity {
  kind: 'eat';
  petItemId: string;
  startedAt: number;
  /** 碗在地上的哪裡。null = 還沒解出來。 */
  bowl: PetPoint | null;
  /** 開始低頭吃的時刻。null = 還在走過去。 */
  eatingSince: number | null;
  /** 吃完的時刻；之後碗淡出，淡完活動結束。 */
  doneAt: number | null;
}

export type PetPlayPhase = 'flight' | 'chase' | 'carry' | 'return' | 'done';

/** 玩耍。落點由 3D 那一頭解（它知道主人面向哪、哪裡是陸地）。 */
export interface PetPlayActivity {
  kind: 'play';
  petItemId: string;
  startedAt: number;
  style: PetPlayStyle;
  /** 玩具從哪裡丟出、第一次落在哪裡。null = 還沒解出來。 */
  from: PetPoint | null;
  to: PetPoint | null;
  phase: PetPlayPhase;
  phaseSince: number;
  /** 被叼起來的那一刻之後，玩具跟著寵物的嘴。 */
  carried: boolean;
  /** 玩具最後放下的位置（叼回來之後），淡出時留在這裡。 */
  restAt: PetPoint | null;
  doneAt: number | null;
}

export type PetActivity = PetPettingActivity | PetEatActivity | PetPlayActivity;

const activities = new Map<string, PetActivity>();
const reactions = new Map<string, { id: PetReactionId; startedAt: number }>();
const listeners = new Set<() => void>();

function notify(): void {
  listeners.forEach((fn) => fn());
}

/** React 那一頭（碗、玩具要不要掛上）訂閱這個。 */
export function subscribePetActivity(fn: () => void): () => void {
  listeners.add(fn);
  return () => { listeners.delete(fn); };
}

/** 這一隻現在在做什麼。每幀讀，不複製。 */
export function currentPetActivity(petItemId: string | undefined | null): PetActivity | null {
  if (!petItemId) return null;
  return activities.get(petItemId) ?? null;
}

/**
 * 開始摸摸。已經在做別的事（正在吃、正在追球）的話不開始 —— 一隻嘴裡叼著球的狗不會停下來給你摸，
 * 而「摸到一半球不見了」比「摸不到」更糟。回傳是否真的開始了。
 */
export function startPetting(petItemId: string, now = performance.now()): boolean {
  const current = activities.get(petItemId);
  if (current && current.kind !== 'petting' && !petActivityFinishing(current)) return false;
  activities.set(petItemId, { kind: 'petting', petItemId, startedAt: now, lastPatAt: now });
  notify();
  return true;
}

/** 摸了一下。沒有在摸的話什麼都不做。 */
export function patPet(petItemId: string, now = performance.now()): void {
  const current = activities.get(petItemId);
  if (current?.kind !== 'petting') return;
  current.lastPatAt = now;
  playPetReaction(petItemId, 'pat', now);
}

/**
 * 開始吃飯。吃飯**會蓋過**正在進行的摸摸與玩耍 —— 餵食是一次已經寫進存檔的行為（見 PetFeeding：
 * 只有寫入被接受之後才會叫這個），動畫不可以因為牠正在追球就不演。
 */
export function startEating(petItemId: string, now = performance.now()): void {
  activities.set(petItemId, {
    kind: 'eat', petItemId, startedAt: now, bowl: null, eatingSince: null, doneAt: null,
  });
  notify();
}

/** 開始玩耍。正在吃飯的時候不開始（吃飯是確定發生的事，玩耍可以等）。回傳是否真的開始了。 */
export function startPlay(petItemId: string, style: PetPlayStyle, now = performance.now()): boolean {
  const current = activities.get(petItemId);
  if (current?.kind === 'eat' && !petActivityFinishing(current)) return false;
  activities.set(petItemId, {
    kind: 'play', petItemId, startedAt: now, style, from: null, to: null,
    phase: 'flight', phaseSince: now, carried: false, restAt: null, doneAt: null,
  });
  notify();
  return true;
}

/** 活動進入收尾（碗、玩具淡出中）。重複呼叫不會重設淡出的起點。 */
export function finishPetActivity(petItemId: string, now = performance.now()): void {
  const current = activities.get(petItemId);
  if (!current) return;
  if (current.kind === 'petting') {
    activities.delete(petItemId);
    notify();
    return;
  }
  if (current.doneAt == null) {
    current.doneAt = now;
    if (current.kind === 'play') current.phase = 'done';
    notify();
  }
}

/** 立刻結束，不淡出。卸載、換寵物、離開島嶼時用。 */
export function endPetActivity(petItemId: string): void {
  const had = activities.delete(petItemId);
  const hadReaction = reactions.delete(petItemId);
  if (had || hadReaction) notify();
}

/** 已經在收尾了嗎（吃完了、玩完了，只剩碗或玩具在淡出）。 */
export function petActivityFinishing(a: PetActivity): boolean {
  return a.kind !== 'petting' && a.doneAt != null;
}

/**
 * 這個活動該不該被收掉了 —— 一個純粹的時鐘判斷，所以誰來問、什麼時候問都是同一個答案。
 *
 * 每一種都有一個「就算什麼都沒發生也會結束」的上限。這是「寵物卡在互動狀態」寫不出來的原因：
 * 迷你遊戲被晾著、碗放在一個走不到的地方、球滾進了一個永遠到不了的角落 —— 最後都會過期。
 */
export function petActivityExpired(a: PetActivity, now: number): boolean {
  switch (a.kind) {
    case 'petting':
      return now - a.lastPatAt > PET_PETTING.idleTimeout * 1000
        || now - a.startedAt > PET_PETTING.maxSeconds * 1000;
    case 'eat': {
      if (a.doneAt != null) return now - a.doneAt > PET_FEED.fadeSeconds * 1000;
      const ceiling = PET_FEED.approachTimeout + PET_FEED.eatSeconds + 2;
      return now - a.startedAt > ceiling * 1000;
    }
    case 'play':
      if (a.doneAt != null) return now - a.doneAt > PET_PLAY.fadeSeconds * 1000;
      return now - a.startedAt > (PET_PLAY.maxSeconds + PET_PLAY.fadeSeconds) * 1000;
  }
}

/** 收掉所有過期的活動與反應。3D 那一頭每幀呼叫一次；空表時是一次 size 比較。 */
export function sweepPetActivities(now = performance.now()): void {
  if (activities.size === 0 && reactions.size === 0) return;
  let changed = false;
  activities.forEach((a, key) => {
    if (petActivityExpired(a, now)) {
      activities.delete(key);
      changed = true;
    }
  });
  reactions.forEach((r, key) => {
    // 最長的反應不到兩秒；五秒是「一定播完了」的保險，不是一個調過的數字。
    if (now - r.startedAt > 5000) {
      reactions.delete(key);
      changed = true;
    }
  });
  if (changed) notify();
}

/** 播一個一次性的反應（看到你、開心、伸懶腰…）。同一隻同時只有一個，新的蓋過舊的。 */
export function playPetReaction(petItemId: string, id: PetReactionId, now = performance.now()): void {
  reactions.set(petItemId, { id, startedAt: now });
}

export function currentPetReaction(petItemId: string): { id: PetReactionId; startedAt: number } | null {
  return reactions.get(petItemId) ?? null;
}

/** 全部清掉 —— 換帳號、重新載入存檔。 */
export function resetPetActivities(): void {
  if (activities.size === 0 && reactions.size === 0) return;
  activities.clear();
  reactions.clear();
  notify();
}

/** 測試用。 */
export function petActivityCount(): number {
  return activities.size;
}
```

## src/lib/petCompatibility.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 「這件商品是給哪一種寵物的」 — one question, asked of any catalog row.
 *
 * Two unrelated capabilities answer it. A resting place declares `petRest.species`
 * (constants/petHabitats.ts) and a food declares `consumable.species`
 * (constants/consumables.ts), and each of those is read directly by the system that owns it: the
 * resting-spot resolver never asks about food, and the feeding list never asks about beds.
 *
 * This file exists for the one caller that has to span both — the SHOP. A player standing in front
 * of 寵物用品 and 寵物窩 is looking at two shelves that are filtered by the same question, and the
 * chip row doing the filtering should not have to know that one shelf's answer lives on a
 * `petRest` and the other's on a `consumable`. So the union is written down once, here, in the
 * `lib/` layer where the other cross-catalog queries live (lib/petRestingSpots.ts), rather than as
 * an `item.petRest?.species ?? item.consumable?.species` expression repeated at each use.
 *
 * A row that declares NEITHER capability is not a pet item and is suitable for nobody — which is
 * what keeps this safe to call over the whole catalog. A pet-targeted consumable with no `species`
 * is the universal treat and suits everybody; see `consumableAcceptsSpecies`.
 */

import type { ItemDefinition } from '../constants/items';
import { consumableAcceptsSpecies } from '../constants/consumables';
import { habitatAcceptsSpecies } from '../constants/petHabitats';
import { PET_SPECIES, type PetSpecies } from '../constants/pets';

/** Whether this row is for pets at all — a bed, a food, or anything later that declares either. */
export function isPetSupplyItem(item: ItemDefinition): boolean {
  return !!item.petRest || item.consumable?.target === 'pet';
}

/**
 * Whether a catalog row suits a given species.
 *
 * True when EITHER capability accepts it, rather than when both do: no item today declares both,
 * and one that did (a perch with a seed tray built in?) would be for whoever either half is for.
 */
export function itemSuitsSpecies(item: ItemDefinition, species: PetSpecies): boolean {
  if (item.petRest && habitatAcceptsSpecies(item.petRest, species)) return true;
  if (item.consumable?.target === 'pet' && consumableAcceptsSpecies(item.consumable, species)) {
    return true;
  }
  return false;
}

/**
 * Which species a set of rows serves, in the canonical species order.
 *
 * What the shop's chip row is built from, so a chip only ever appears for a species the shelf in
 * front of the player actually has something for — a filter that can only empty the screen is a
 * filter that should not be offered. It also means the row appears on any FUTURE pet shelf (玩具,
 * 清潔用品) the moment its items declare a species, with no edit to the shop.
 */
export function speciesServedBy(items: readonly ItemDefinition[]): PetSpecies[] {
  const served = new Set<PetSpecies>();
  for (const item of items) {
    for (const species of PET_SPECIES) {
      if (itemSuitsSpecies(item, species)) served.add(species);
    }
  }
  return PET_SPECIES.filter((id) => served.has(id));
}
```

## src/lib/petReaction.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import {
  PET_FEED,
  PET_PLAY,
  PET_REACTIONS,
  type PetReactionId,
  type PetReactionSpec,
} from '../constants/petInteractions';
import type { PetPoint } from './petActivity';

/**
 * 寵物互動的數學 —— 反應的形狀、碗放哪、球飛到哪。沒有 React、沒有 three.js。
 *
 * 跟 lib/objectAnimation.ts 同一個原則：能寫成「時間 → 數字」的全部寫成純函式，所以
 * `scripts/test-pet-interactions.ts` 可以不開瀏覽器就驗「反應兩端都回到 0」「球永遠落在地上方」
 * 「碗不會放在主人腳底下」這些畫面上才看得出來、但一改數字就會壞的事。
 *
 * 需要世界資訊的部分（陸地在哪、家具在哪）刻意不在這裡：那些由 Three/IslandPet.tsx 在拿到這裡的
 * 答案之後再夾一次，跟寵物自己的跟隨點一樣。
 */

/** 一個反應在某一刻的樣子。全部是寫在寵物整個 group 上的偏移。 */
export interface PetReactionFrame {
  /** 往上跳多少，身高的比例。 */
  hop: number;
  /** 前傾，弧度，正 = 鼻子朝下。 */
  pitch: number;
  /** 壓低多少，身高的比例。 */
  drop: number;
  /** 左右晃，弧度。 */
  roll: number;
  /** 額外轉了多少，弧度。 */
  spin: number;
  /** 尾巴至少搖多用力。 */
  wag: number;
}

export function emptyReactionFrame(): PetReactionFrame {
  return { hop: 0, pitch: 0, drop: 0, roll: 0, spin: 0, wag: 0 };
}

function clamp01(v: number): number {
  return v < 0 ? 0 : v > 1 ? 1 : v;
}

function smooth(v: number): number {
  const t = clamp01(v);
  return t * t * (3 - 2 * t);
}

/** 陸上或空中的那一份數字。 */
export function reactionSpecFor(id: PetReactionId, airborne: boolean): PetReactionSpec {
  const base = PET_REACTIONS[id];
  return airborne && base.air ? { ...base, ...base.air } : base;
}

/**
 * 一個反應在 `elapsed` 秒時的偏移，乘上 `weight` 加進 `into`。
 *
 * 信封是 smoothstep 進、smoothstep 出，所以任何一個反應的第一幀與最後一幀都是 0 —— 反應之間、
 * 反應與走路之間的交接不會跳。跳躍用 |sin| 的拱形，永遠不會低於地面（見 objectAnimations.ts 裡
 * 沙灘球那一段：用 sin 寫彈跳，一半的時間會在地底下）。
 */
export function addPetReaction(
  into: PetReactionFrame,
  id: PetReactionId,
  elapsed: number,
  airborne: boolean,
  weight = 1,
): void {
  const spec = reactionSpecFor(id, airborne);
  const u = clamp01(elapsed / spec.seconds);
  if (elapsed < 0 || elapsed > spec.seconds) return;
  const raise = spec.raise ?? 0.2;
  const fall = spec.fall ?? 0.3;
  const env = Math.min(smooth(u / raise), 1 - smooth((u - (1 - fall)) / fall)) * weight;

  if (spec.hops) {
    // 每一下是一個完整的拱，而且在整段裡平均分配；不乘信封，否則第一下永遠跳不起來。
    into.hop += Math.abs(Math.sin(u * Math.PI * spec.hops.count)) * spec.hops.height * weight;
  }
  if (spec.pitch) into.pitch += spec.pitch * env;
  if (spec.drop) into.drop += spec.drop * env;
  if (spec.roll) into.roll += Math.sin(elapsed * spec.roll.hz * Math.PI * 2) * spec.roll.amplitude * env;
  // 轉圈用 smoothstep 走完整段，所以起步和停下都是慢的 —— 轉到一半突然停住會像被卡住。
  if (spec.spin) into.spin += smooth(u) * spec.spin * Math.PI * 2 * weight;
  if (spec.wag) into.wag = Math.max(into.wag, spec.wag * Math.max(env, u < 1 ? weight * 0.6 : 0));
}

/**
 * 碗放在哪 —— 主人面前、朝著寵物的那一邊。
 *
 * 寵物就站在主人腳邊（或正好跟主人疊在一起）時，「朝著寵物」沒有方向，就改用主人面向的方向：
 * 碗永遠放在主人看得到、而且不在自己腳底下的地方。
 */
export function bowlSpot(
  owner: { x: number; z: number; yaw: number },
  pet: { x: number; z: number },
  ahead = PET_FEED.bowlAhead,
): { x: number; z: number } {
  let dx = pet.x - owner.x;
  let dz = pet.z - owner.z;
  const d = Math.hypot(dx, dz);
  if (d < 0.3) {
    dx = Math.sin(owner.yaw);
    dz = Math.cos(owner.yaw);
  } else {
    dx /= d;
    dz /= d;
  }
  return { x: owner.x + dx * ahead, z: owner.z + dz * ahead };
}

/**
 * 寵物吃飯時站在哪 —— 碗後面，離主人較遠的那一側，嘴巴剛好在碗上。
 *
 * 「後面」是從主人看過去的後面：寵物面對主人低頭吃，主人看得到牠的臉，而不是一條屁股。
 */
export function eatStandSpot(
  bowl: { x: number; z: number },
  owner: { x: number; z: number },
  petHeight: number,
): { x: number; z: number; yaw: number } {
  let dx = bowl.x - owner.x;
  let dz = bowl.z - owner.z;
  const d = Math.hypot(dx, dz);
  if (d < 1e-4) { dx = 0; dz = 1; } else { dx /= d; dz /= d; }
  const back = PET_FEED.standoff + PET_FEED.standoffPerHeight * petHeight;
  const x = bowl.x + dx * back;
  const z = bowl.z + dz * back;
  // 面向碗（也就是面向主人）。
  return { x, z, yaw: Math.atan2(bowl.x - x, bowl.z - z) };
}

/** 玩具丟出去的第一個落點：主人面向的方向上 `distance` 遠。 */
export function throwLanding(
  owner: { x: number; z: number; yaw: number },
  distance: number,
): { x: number; z: number } {
  return { x: owner.x + Math.sin(owner.yaw) * distance, z: owner.z + Math.cos(owner.yaw) * distance };
}

/**
 * 玩具在丟出去 `elapsed` 秒之後在哪裡，以及它是不是已經停下來了。
 *
 * 三段，全部是時間的函式：一段拋物線飛到 `to`、幾下越來越低的彈跳、然後停在往前滾了一點的地方。
 * 地面高度就是 `to.y` —— 呼叫端解落點的時候已經問過地面了。高度永遠 >= `to.y`：每一段都是 |sin|
 * 或拋物線的正半邊，所以球不會有任何一幀在地底下。
 */
export function toyFlightPosition(
  from: PetPoint,
  to: PetPoint,
  elapsed: number,
  out: PetPoint = { x: 0, y: 0, z: 0 },
): { point: PetPoint; landed: boolean; bounceIndex: number } {
  const dirX = to.x - from.x;
  const dirZ = to.z - from.z;
  const len = Math.hypot(dirX, dirZ) || 1;
  const ux = dirX / len;
  const uz = dirZ / len;

  const flight = PET_PLAY.flightSeconds;
  if (elapsed <= flight) {
    const p = clamp01(elapsed / flight);
    out.x = from.x + dirX * p;
    out.z = from.z + dirZ * p;
    // 從手的高度到地面的直線，加上一個頂點在中間的拋物線。
    const line = from.y + (to.y - from.y) * p;
    out.y = Math.max(to.y, line + 4 * PET_PLAY.arcHeight * p * (1 - p));
    return { point: out, landed: false, bounceIndex: -1 };
  }

  const after = elapsed - flight;
  const bounceTotal = PET_PLAY.bounces * PET_PLAY.bounceSeconds;
  // 彈跳期間順著方向往前滾，速度跟著衰減。
  const rollP = clamp01(after / bounceTotal);
  const rolled = PET_PLAY.rollOn * (1 - (1 - rollP) * (1 - rollP));
  out.x = to.x + ux * rolled;
  out.z = to.z + uz * rolled;
  if (after >= bounceTotal) {
    out.y = to.y;
    return { point: out, landed: true, bounceIndex: PET_PLAY.bounces };
  }
  const index = Math.floor(after / PET_PLAY.bounceSeconds);
  const local = (after - index * PET_PLAY.bounceSeconds) / PET_PLAY.bounceSeconds;
  const height = PET_PLAY.bounceHeight * Math.pow(PET_PLAY.bounceDecay, index);
  out.y = to.y + Math.abs(Math.sin(local * Math.PI)) * height;
  return { point: out, landed: false, bounceIndex: index };
}

/** 玩具最後停下來的地方（落點再往前滾 `rollOn`）。 */
export function toyRestPoint(from: PetPoint, to: PetPoint): PetPoint {
  const dirX = to.x - from.x;
  const dirZ = to.z - from.z;
  const len = Math.hypot(dirX, dirZ) || 1;
  return { x: to.x + (dirX / len) * PET_PLAY.rollOn, y: to.y, z: to.z + (dirZ / len) * PET_PLAY.rollOn };
}

/** 叼回來時停在哪 —— 主人正前方。 */
export function returnSpot(owner: { x: number; z: number; yaw: number }): { x: number; z: number } {
  return {
    x: owner.x + Math.sin(owner.yaw) * PET_PLAY.returnAhead,
    z: owner.z + Math.cos(owner.yaw) * PET_PLAY.returnAhead,
  };
}
```

## src/lib/petRestingSpots.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 寵物的休息位置 — where the animal goes when it wants to lie down, resolved from what is actually
 * standing on the island.
 *
 * The brief's §9 is a list of things this must NOT be, and every one of them is a shape somebody
 * reaches for first:
 *
 *   ❌ a fixed world coordinate            — a bed the player moves would be a bed the pet ignores
 *   ❌ `find(item.id === 'pet-bed-01')`    — a second bed style would need a second branch
 *   ❌ `find(item.name.includes('窩'))`     — the name-keyword guess this codebase already retired
 *                                             once (see constants/furnitureInteractions.ts)
 *
 * What it is instead: a search over the player's own placements for anything whose CATALOG ENTRY
 * declares `petRest` (constants/petHabitats.ts's `PetRestSpec`). A resting spot is a capability a
 * piece has, in the same way a table declares `tabletop` and a hammock declares `interactions`. So
 * an indoor basket, a shaded platform, a bigger kennel or a bird's perch all become resting spots by
 * being added to the catalog with that field, and nothing in this file changes.
 *
 * ## Species is a FILTER here, not a branch anywhere else
 *
 * A cage is not a resting place for a dog, and the way that is expressed is that a dog's scan never
 * returns one — `habitatAcceptsSpecies`, one `includes` over the item's own declaration. There is no
 * 「這隻是鳥嗎」 in this file and none in its callers: a bird with only a kennel placed simply has no
 * owned spot and falls through to the improvised nest, exactly as a bird with nothing placed does.
 * That is the brief's §5 (「不讓玩家看到不適用的選項」) applied to the world rather than to a menu.
 *
 * ## The improvised nest is the FALLBACK, not the rule
 *
 * A player who has never bought a bed still has a pet that needs somewhere to be, so the last resort
 * is 離線回歸's improvised spot beside the Home (`getPetRestSpot`) — the mat, the bowl and the toys
 * that Three/IslandOvergrowth.tsx draws. That is the one place the two systems meet, and they meet
 * through the same function rather than through two copies of the same offset: a pet waiting three
 * metres from its own visible bed is the exact kind of small wrongness that reads as a bug.
 */

import type { PlacedItem } from '../types';
import { getItemById } from '../constants/items';
import { getPetRestSpot } from '../constants/islandReturn';
import { getPetSpecies, type PetSpecies } from '../constants/pets';
import {
  PET_HABITAT_KINDS,
  habitatAcceptsSpecies,
  type PetHabitatKind,
  type PetRestPosture,
  type PetRestSpec,
} from '../constants/petHabitats';

/**
 * A place the animal can settle, in world units.
 *
 * `source` is what the renderer branches on, and it is the whole reason this is a record rather than
 * a bare point: the improvised nest art (mat, empty bowl, scattered toys) is a picture of 「沒人收拾」
 * and must NOT be drawn on top of a bed the player actually bought and placed. See
 * Three/IslandOvergrowth.tsx.
 */
export interface PetRestingSpot {
  x: number;
  z: number;
  /** How close the animal has to get before it counts as having arrived. */
  radius: number;
  /**
   * How high above the ground the animal comes to rest here, in world units. 0 for anything a
   * mammal lies on; a perch, a cage floor or a nest rim is where a bird actually lands.
   */
  height: number;
  /**
   * How the animal is off its feet here — `lie` for a bed, `perch` for anything a bird grips.
   *
   * Carried on the RESOLVED spot rather than looked up again by each mover, for the same reason
   * `nearbyInteraction` carries its verb (lib/playerBus.ts): the thing that found the spot already
   * knows, and two lookups are two chances to disagree.
   */
  posture: PetRestPosture;
  /** `item` — a piece the player owns and placed. `default` — the improvised spot by the Home. */
  source: 'item' | 'default';
  /** What to call it in the care panel. The piece's own name; never a second copy of it. */
  label: string;
  /** Which shape of home it is, for the panel's one-line explanation. */
  kind?: PetHabitatKind;
  /** The catalog id of the piece, when there is one. Diagnostics and copy only. */
  itemId?: string;
  /** Which placement it is, so a second bed of the same kind is still a distinct spot. */
  instanceId?: string;
}

/** The improvised spot's reach — about the size of the mat drawn there. */
const DEFAULT_SPOT_RADIUS = 0.8;

/**
 * Every resting spot currently available to a given species, nearest-to-the-Home first.
 *
 * Exported alongside {@link resolveRestingSpot} because the care panel wants to say 「你有 2 個窩」
 * without re-implementing the scan, and because a future feature that lets the player CHOOSE which
 * bed their pet uses needs the list rather than the winner.
 */
export function collectRestingSpots(opts: {
  placements: readonly PlacedItem[];
  home: { position: [number, number, number]; rotation: number } | null;
  species?: PetSpecies;
}): PetRestingSpot[] {
  const { placements, home, species } = opts;
  const spots: PetRestingSpot[] = [];

  for (const placement of placements) {
    const item = getItemById(placement.itemId);
    const spec = item?.petRest;
    if (!spec) continue;
    // A spot that does not accept this animal is not a spot — the whole of the compatibility
    // system, right here. An absent `species` argument is a caller that has no particular animal in
    // mind (a preview harness, a 「島上有幾個窩」 count) and sees them all.
    if (species && !habitatAcceptsSpecies(spec, species)) continue;
    spots.push(toWorldSpot(placement, spec, item.name));
  }

  // Nearest the Home first, then by instance id. Two beds side by side must resolve to the SAME one
  // on every device and every reload — an order that depends on where the pet happens to be standing
  // would have it change its mind halfway across the garden.
  const anchor = home?.position ?? [0, 0, 0];
  spots.sort((a, b) => {
    const da = Math.hypot(a.x - anchor[0], a.z - anchor[2]);
    const db = Math.hypot(b.x - anchor[0], b.z - anchor[2]);
    if (Math.abs(da - db) > 1e-6) return da - db;
    return (a.instanceId ?? '').localeCompare(b.instanceId ?? '');
  });

  return spots;
}

/**
 * The one spot the animal will actually use. Total — there is always an answer.
 *
 * A placed bed wins over the improvised nest, because buying and putting one down is the player
 * saying where they want the animal to sleep. With none placed, the fallback is 離線回歸's spot beside
 * the Home; with no Home either (a brand-new player, who has never been away and has no pet to worry
 * about) that function still returns a point out on the grass, which is what keeps this total and
 * every caller free of a null branch.
 */
export function resolveRestingSpot(opts: {
  placements: readonly PlacedItem[];
  home: { position: [number, number, number]; rotation: number } | null;
  islandScale: number;
  /** The equipped companion's item id, so a species-specific bed can be honoured. */
  petItemId?: string | null;
}): PetRestingSpot {
  const species = getPetSpecies(opts.petItemId);
  const owned = collectRestingSpots({
    placements: opts.placements,
    home: opts.home,
    ...(species ? { species } : {}),
  });
  if (owned.length > 0) return owned[0];

  const fallback = getPetRestSpot(opts.home, opts.islandScale);
  return {
    x: fallback.x,
    z: fallback.z,
    radius: DEFAULT_SPOT_RADIUS,
    // On the ground and lain in, whatever species is using it: the improvised nest is a mat with a
    // bowl beside it, and a bird with no perch of its own comes down to it rather than hovering over
    // a spot in mid-air. It is the fallback precisely because it suits nobody in particular.
    height: 0,
    posture: 'lie',
    source: 'default',
    label: '屋旁的小窩',
  };
}

/**
 * A placement plus its spec, in world units.
 *
 * The rotation convention is three's own — `x' = x·cos + z·sin`, `z' = -x·sin + z·cos` — stated the
 * same way lib/furniturePlacement.ts and constants/islandReturn.ts state it for their own boxes. A
 * spec with no offset lies at the piece's centre, so the rotation is a no-op for every bed sold
 * today and the maths only starts to matter for the first kennel with a door on one side.
 */
function toWorldSpot(placement: PlacedItem, spec: PetRestSpec, name: string): PetRestingSpot {
  const localX = spec.offset?.x ?? 0;
  const localZ = spec.offset?.z ?? 0;
  const cos = Math.cos(placement.rotation || 0);
  const sin = Math.sin(placement.rotation || 0);
  return {
    x: placement.position[0] + localX * cos + localZ * sin,
    z: placement.position[2] - localX * sin + localZ * cos,
    radius: spec.radius,
    height: spec.height ?? 0,
    posture: PET_HABITAT_KINDS[spec.kind].posture,
    source: 'item',
    // The item's own name, so the panel and the shop card cannot end up calling one basket two
    // different things. This used to be a `label` written on the spec beside it, which was a second
    // copy of a string that was always identical to the first.
    label: name,
    kind: spec.kind,
    itemId: placement.itemId,
    instanceId: placement.instanceId,
  };
}
```

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * THE OBJECT MANIPULATION STATE — one selection/editing session, shared by both placement modes.
 *
 * ## Why this exists
 *
 * Indoors (【佈置模式】) and outdoors (【建造模式】) each grew their own answer to "which object am
 * I moving", and neither of them had one. What existed instead was a single question asked over
 * and over on every pointer event — *what is under the cursor right now* — with the answer written
 * straight back into the selection:
 *
 *   - Indoors, every placed piece carried `onClick={() => onItemClick(p.instanceId)}` with no
 *     guard at all. So while a book was being dragged onto a table, the moment the pointer crossed
 *     the table the release selected the TABLE, and the player was suddenly dragging the furniture
 *     they had been aiming at. Stacking was impossible — not because of the colliders, but because
 *     the target of the gesture changed halfway through it.
 *   - Outdoors the same handler was simply switched off for the whole session
 *     (`isEditable = BUILD_MODE && !islandDraft`). Nothing could steal the selection because
 *     nothing could be selected — the opposite over-correction, and it meant the player could not
 *     deliberately switch subjects either.
 *
 * Both are the same missing distinction, so it is drawn once, here:
 *
 *   - **Hovered** — what the pointer happens to be over this frame. Cursor feedback, nothing else.
 *     Never stored, because it is never a decision.
 *   - **Selected** — what the player chose by clicking. Survives the pointer moving away.
 *   - **Active** — what a gesture currently owns. While a gesture is running, NOTHING may take it.
 *
 * ## The state machine
 *
 *   idle ──select──▶ selected ──pointerdown──▶ moving ──pointerup──▶ selected ──commit──▶ idle
 *                                                                        │
 *                                                          cancel / retrieve ──▶ idle
 *
 * `moving` is the LOCKED phase: {@link canSelect} refuses every subject but the active one, so a
 * raycast that lands on another model during a drag is a hover and no more.
 *
 * There is deliberately no `rotating` phase. Rotation in this game is a discrete 45° step — the R
 * key, or the dock's 旋轉 button (`ROTATION_STEP`) — applied to the piece already held, not a
 * gesture with a beginning and an end. A phase nothing can stay in would be a lock nothing can
 * hold; the piece is `selected` throughout, and its rotation is one more thing about it that
 * changes. If rotation ever becomes a drag, it enters here as its own locked phase and
 * {@link isManipulating} covers it without another call site changing.
 *
 * ## What is deliberately NOT here
 *
 * No geometry, no three.js, no React. This module answers "who owns the gesture" and "how fine is
 * one step"; where an object may go is lib/placementSurfaces.ts (outdoors) and
 * lib/interiorPlacement.ts (indoors), and both call in here for the same two answers.
 */

// --- Precision ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * The step a dragged object moves in, in world units — 2 cm.
 *
 * ### What this replaced
 *
 * Indoor floor placement quantised to `FLOOR_GRID = 0.5`, and had since the mode was written. A
 * room is ROOM_GRID_SIZE (12) across, so the entire floor of a room was a 24 × 24 board and a
 * piece could only ever stand on one of its intersections. That is the reported symptom exactly:
 * a table nudged left does not move, does not move, does not move, and then jumps half a metre —
 * a quarter of its own width. Nothing could be aligned, nothing could be pushed up against a
 * wall, and two chairs could not be set a comfortable distance apart because the only distances
 * that existed were multiples of 0.5.
 *
 * ### Why quantise at all, then
 *
 * Because a drag is an accumulation. The position is recomputed from the ray on every event, not
 * integrated from deltas, so error does not compound within one drag — but the value is written
 * to Firestore, read back, and re-entered as the seed of the NEXT drag, and a float that has been
 * through that loop a dozen times is a number with fifteen digits in it. Quantising is what keeps
 * "the same spot" bit-identical across a save/load round trip, which is in turn what lets
 * BuildingInteriorView's "unchanged transforms are dropped rather than written" short-circuit
 * work at all. See {@link quantize} for the rounding that makes the result exact.
 *
 * 2 cm against furniture roughly a metre across is 1/50th of a piece — below the size of one
 * screen pixel at normal camera distances, so it reads as continuous while still being a grid.
 */
export const PRECISION_STEP = 0.02;

/**
 * The step while the align modifier is held — 25 cm.
 *
 * Grid snap is kept, but demoted from "the only way to move" to "a tool for lining things up",
 * and halved on the way: 0.25 is a quarter of a floor tile rather than half a metre, so a row of
 * cabinets can be made flush without the grid deciding where the row goes.
 */
export const ALIGN_STEP = 0.25;

// --- The click / drag boundary --------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * THE DRAG THRESHOLD: how far the pointer must travel, in CSS pixels, before a press on an object
 * stops being a click and becomes a move.
 *
 * ## Why the distinction has to exist at all
 *
 * Both modes used to treat `pointerdown` as the start of the move, so the first pixel of pointer
 * travel after a press dragged the object. That makes two intents impossible to tell apart:
 * 「我想選這個東西」 and 「我想搬這個東西」. A player reaching for a lamp to see what it is, or
 * simply pressing on a trackpad, moved it — and the only evidence was a piece that no longer sat
 * where it had. Outdoors this compounded with a follow-the-cursor mode where the object tracked
 * the bare mouse, so 「誤移動」 was not an edge case, it was the default experience.
 *
 * So: press → **armed**, and a release from there is a CLICK (select). Travel past the threshold →
 * **dragging**, and the object follows. That is the whole of 「單純點擊 → 選取；按住並移動超過一定
 * 距離 → 進入 Dragging」.
 *
 * ## Why it costs nothing in a real drag
 *
 * The grab offset (see {@link translateRayXZ}) is measured at the PRESS, not at the moment the
 * threshold is crossed. So when the drag does start, the object is placed exactly where the
 * pointer's own travel says it should be — there is no catch-up jump and no dead zone to pull
 * through. The threshold is invisible to anyone who meant to drag, and decisive for anyone who
 * did not.
 *
 * Measured in SCREEN space rather than world units on purpose: the question is "did this hand mean
 * to move something", which has nothing to do with how far away the camera happens to be. Four
 * pixels is about a millimetre on a desktop display — enough to absorb the pixel or two a mouse
 * reports between the button going down and coming back up.
 */
export const DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX = 4;

/**
 * The same threshold for a finger — larger, and it has to be.
 *
 * A fingertip covers ~40px of glass and never lands still: a tap the player experiences as
 * perfectly stationary routinely reports 5–8px of travel between `pointerdown` and `pointerup`.
 * At the mouse's threshold every tap on a piece of furniture would be a small drag, which is the
 * fault this mechanism exists to prevent — and worse on touch than on a mouse, because a
 * touchscreen has no hover, so a tap is the ONLY way to look at something.
 */
export const TOUCH_DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX = 10;

/** The threshold for a given `PointerEvent.pointerType`. Pen is held to the mouse's precision. */
export function dragThresholdFor(pointerType: string | undefined): number {
  return pointerType === 'touch' ? TOUCH_DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX : DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX;
}

/** Has this much screen travel earned the press the right to become a drag? */
export function exceedsDragThreshold(dx: number, dy: number, pointerType?: string): boolean {
  return Math.hypot(dx, dy) >= dragThresholdFor(pointerType);
}

/**
 * Round `v` onto a grid of `step`, exactly.
 *
 * The naive `Math.round(v / step) * step` is not exact: 0.02 is not representable in binary, so
 * `3 * 0.02` is 0.060000000000000005 and the SAME logical position reached from two directions
 * can differ in the last bits. That difference is invisible on screen and fatal to every
 * `a === b` short-circuit downstream. Rounding the product back to six decimals collapses the
 * representable neighbourhood of each grid point to one value, so a position is a function of the
 * grid index and nothing else — which is what "avoid floating point accumulation" actually
 * requires here.
 */
export function quantize(v: number, step: number): number {
  if (!(step > 0)) return v;
  // The trailing `+ 0` collapses -0 to 0. `-0 === 0` is true, so nothing downstream misbehaves,
  // but the output of a canonicaliser should be canonical: two spellings of the origin is exactly
  // the class of thing this function exists to remove.
  return Math.round((Math.round(v / step) * step) * 1e6) / 1e6 + 0;
}

// --- Session state ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Where a manipulation gesture is in its life. See the diagram at the top of this file. */
export type ManipulationPhase = 'idle' | 'selected' | 'moving';

export interface PlacementSessionState {
  phase: ManipulationPhase;
  /**
   * The Active Object: the instance id being manipulated, or a synthetic key for a copy that is
   * not placed yet (`create:<itemId>`). Null exactly when `phase` is `idle`.
   */
  activeId: string | null;
  /** True while the align modifier (Shift) is held — see {@link ALIGN_STEP}. */
  align: boolean;
}

const IDLE: PlacementSessionState = { phase: 'idle', activeId: null, align: false };

let state: PlacementSessionState = IDLE;

const listeners = new Set<() => void>();

function write(next: PlacementSessionState) {
  if (
    next.phase === state.phase &&
    next.activeId === state.activeId &&
    next.align === state.align
  ) {
    return;
  }
  state = next;
  listeners.forEach((fn) => fn());
}

/** `useSyncExternalStore` subscribe. */
export function subscribePlacementSession(fn: () => void): () => void {
  listeners.add(fn);
  return () => {
    listeners.delete(fn);
  };
}

/**
 * The current session. Referentially stable between changes, so it is safe as a
 * `useSyncExternalStore` snapshot.
 */
export function getPlacementSession(): PlacementSessionState {
  return state;
}

/** The player chose a subject: it becomes the Selected Object, and the Active Object. */
export function selectSubject(activeId: string): void {
  write({ phase: 'selected', activeId, align: state.align });
}

/** A drag started on the active subject. This is the phase that locks selection. */
export function beginMove(activeId: string): void {
  write({ phase: 'moving', activeId, align: state.align });
}

/**
 * The gesture ended, but the subject is still held — back to `selected`.
 *
 * Idempotent, and deliberately so: the same release arrives from up to three places (the object's
 * own `pointerup`, the window capture in lib/inputManager.ts, and `lostpointercapture`).
 */
export function endGesture(): void {
  if (state.phase === 'idle') return;
  write({ phase: 'selected', activeId: state.activeId, align: state.align });
}

/** The session is over: confirmed, cancelled, or the mode was left. */
export function endSession(): void {
  clickGuard = false;
  write(IDLE);
}

/** Whether a gesture currently owns the Active Object. */
export function isManipulating(): boolean {
  return state.phase === 'moving';
}

/**
 * May a click on `candidateId` change the selection?
 *
 * The one rule the whole "moving A must not become moving B" problem reduces to. Three cases:
 *
 *  - Nothing is held (`idle`) — yes, this is ordinary selection.
 *  - The candidate IS the active object — yes, and it is a no-op, but saying no would make the
 *    piece the player is holding the one thing they cannot click.
 *  - A gesture is running — **no**. Not "select it later", not "queue it": the click is a hover
 *    and the drag continues. This is the Editing Lock.
 *
 * The remaining case, `selected` with a different candidate, is a deliberate switch and is left to
 * the caller: outdoors a `create` draft holds an unplaced copy, so switching away from it would
 * silently drop the player's armed item, while switching away from a `move` draft costs nothing.
 * The callers state which of the two they are.
 */
export function canSelect(candidateId: string): boolean {
  if (clickGuard) return false;
  if (state.phase === 'idle') return true;
  if (state.activeId === candidateId) return true;
  return !isManipulating();
}

/**
 * A release that ENDED A DRAG is not a click, however the browser labels it.
 *
 * The lock above is not enough on its own, and the reason is event ordering. A click is delivered
 * after the pointerup that produced it, and the pointerup is what ends the gesture — so by the
 * time R3F raycasts the release and offers it to whatever model is underneath, the phase is
 * already back to `selected` and the lock has lifted. Dragging a book across a table and letting
 * go would therefore still have selected the table, on the very last event of the gesture.
 *
 * So a drag that actually moved claims its own release. One flag, consumed by the first selection
 * attempt after it (there is at most one), and cleared on the next press so it can never outlive
 * the gesture that set it.
 */
let clickGuard = false;

/** The gesture that just ended moved the object: the release it produced is not a selection. */
export function guardNextClick(): void {
  clickGuard = true;
}

/** A fresh press. Whatever the previous gesture claimed, it is over. */
export function clearClickGuard(): void {
  clickGuard = false;
}

/**
 * ESC has two meanings, and this is how the inner one tells the outer one it already ran.
 *
 * Mid-drag, Escape means 「取消這次搬動」 (the drag hook puts the object back where the press found
 * it and the piece stays held). At rest it means 「放下這個東西」 (the mode drops the whole
 * session). Both modes bind Escape on the window, so exactly one of the two has to win.
 *
 * The drag hook takes the key in the CAPTURE phase and calls `stopPropagation`, which is enough
 * for a real keypress — its target is the focused element, so stopping at window-capture keeps the
 * event from ever descending, let alone bubbling back. It is NOT enough in general: an event
 * dispatched AT the window (a synthetic one, or a future listener that re-dispatches) has a path
 * of one node, and every listener on that node runs whatever `stopPropagation` says. That case
 * cost a session in testing — the drag cancelled correctly AND the mode then closed the editor.
 *
 * So the drag also raises this flag, and the mode-level handlers consume it. Order-independent by
 * construction: it does not matter which of the two listeners runs first, only that the drag's ran
 * at all.
 *
 * Self-clearing on the next macrotask, for the same reason the click guard is cleared on the next
 * press: a flag that is set and never read (the ordinary case, where `stopPropagation` did its job)
 * must not survive to swallow the NEXT Escape, which the player will mean as "put it down".
 */
let cancelKeyGuard = false;

/** A drag consumed this Escape. Mode-level Escape handlers should ignore it. */
export function guardCancelKey(): void {
  cancelKeyGuard = true;
  // The whole of an event dispatch is synchronous, so a macrotask scheduled here runs after every
  // listener that could have consumed it.
  setTimeout(() => { cancelKeyGuard = false; }, 0);
}

/** Was this Escape already spent cancelling a drag? Reading it consumes it. */
export function consumeCancelKeyGuard(): boolean {
  const consumed = cancelKeyGuard;
  cancelKeyGuard = false;
  return consumed;
}

/**
 * Is the click currently being dispatched the tail of a drag?
 *
 * Selection is not the only thing a stray release can trigger. Both modes also treat a click on
 * the ground as "put it here" — indoors it re-resolves the piece from the raw pointer (throwing
 * away the grab offset, so the piece would snap its origin under the cursor the instant the button
 * came up), outdoors it commits the placement outright. Neither is what letting go of a drag
 * means, and neither was previously distinguishable from a real click.
 */
export function isClickGuarded(): boolean {
  return clickGuard;
}

/** Record whether the align modifier is held. Read off the pointer/key event that carried it. */
export function setAlignModifier(align: boolean): void {
  if (align === state.align) return;
  write({ phase: state.phase, activeId: state.activeId, align });
}

/** The step a drag should quantise to right now. */
export function getPlacementStep(): number {
  return state.align ? ALIGN_STEP : PRECISION_STEP;
}

// --- Rays ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** The minimal shape both placement resolvers accept — three.js `Ray` satisfies it structurally. */
export interface PointerRayLike {
  origin: { x: number; y: number; z: number };
  direction: { x: number; y: number; z: number };
}

/**
 * THE GRAB OFFSET: where the player took hold of the object, relative to its origin.
 *
 * Without one, both modes moved the object's ORIGIN to the pointer. Grab a two-metre table by its
 * near corner and the table teleports a metre the instant the button goes down — which is the
 * other half of "it jumps a long way": not the grid, but the fact that every drag STARTED with a
 * jump the size of whatever was grabbed.
 *
 * Applied by translating the ray horizontally rather than by moving the result, because that is
 * the form that survives every mount. For any horizontal plane the hit is
 * `origin + t·direction` with `t = (planeY − origin.y) / direction.y`, so moving the origin in XZ
 * leaves `t` untouched and moves the hit by exactly the same vector — the object therefore keeps
 * the point the player grabbed under the cursor on the floor, on a tabletop and on a deck alike,
 * with one line and no per-mount case.
 */
export function translateRayXZ(ray: PointerRayLike, dx: number, dz: number): PointerRayLike {
  if (dx === 0 && dz === 0) return ray;
  return {
    origin: { x: ray.origin.x + dx, y: ray.origin.y, z: ray.origin.z + dz },
    direction: { x: ray.direction.x, y: ray.direction.y, z: ray.direction.z },
  };
}

/** Where `ray` meets the horizontal plane at `y`, or null when it runs parallel to or away from it. */
export function rayHitHorizontal(
  ray: PointerRayLike,
  y: number
): { x: number; z: number } | null {
  const dy = ray.direction.y;
  if (Math.abs(dy) < 1e-6) return null;
  const t = (y - ray.origin.y) / dy;
  if (t <= 0) return null;
  return { x: ray.origin.x + t * ray.direction.x, z: ray.origin.z + t * ray.direction.z };
}
```
