## src/lib/placementSurfaces.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { PlacedItem } from '../types';
import {
  getStandableSurface,
  isDisplaySurfaceItem,
  isStandableItem,
  StandableSurface,
} from '../constants/items';
import { WATER_SURFACE_Y } from '../constants/world';
import { getTerrainInfo, isLandTerrain } from '../constants/terrain';
import { HOUSE_FOOTPRINT, STARTER_HOUSE_ITEM_ID } from '../constants/houseStyles';
import { ResolvedHome } from '../hooks/usePlayerHome';
import {
  boxFootprint,
  clampOntoSupport,
  findPlacementConflict,
  footprintContainsPoint,
  footprintOutline,
  getFootprint,
  makeObb,
  registerFootprint,
} from './furniturePlacement';
import { getPlacementStep, quantize } from './placementSession';

/**
 * The island's Placement System: one answer to "how high is the surface here, may this object
 * stand on it, and what does it rest on".
 *
 * ## What this replaced
 *
 * Outdoor placement was four disagreeing rules that each described the same objects differently:
 *
 *   1. `PlacementGhost` tested a candidate against a hand-typed `footprintRadius` circle for the
 *      Home and a measured box for everything else, and wrote every placement at a hard-coded
 *      `y = 0.35` regardless of what was underneath it.
 *   2. `characterMovement.getPlacedItemCollisionRadius` pushed the player out with a *third* set
 *      of numbers, looked up by substring-matching the item's Chinese name.
 *   3. `placementRules.getCollisionBounds` kept a fourth name-keyed table (now deleted — nothing
 *      called it).
 *   4. The 木製平台 got past all of them with three copies of `if (dx < 2.15 && dz < 2.15)
 *      terrainY = 0.6` pasted into Avatar and characterMovement — a square that was neither the
 *      platform's real size (2.64 half-extent) nor its real deck height (0.445 above ground), did
 *      not turn when the platform was rotated, and existed nowhere the placement check could see
 *      it, which is why nothing could be put *on* a platform and why standing on one sank the
 *      player 15cm into the boards.
 *
 * ## The rule that replaced them
 *
 * A placed object's local y = 0 is the surface it stands on. Every model in the catalog is
 * authored that way already — a torch's base, a palm's trunk, a campfire's stones and a deck's
 * boards all start at their own origin — so "where does this go" reduces to "how high is the
 * surface at this XZ", and the answer is the same one for the player's feet, for a prop, and for
 * the ghost's outline. {@link getSurfaceAt} is that answer. A deck is ground because it *declares*
 * it is ({@link StandableSurface}); how big it is and how high its top sits are measured off the
 * model, never typed in.
 *
 * Adding a decoration therefore needs no entry anywhere in this file. Adding a second kind of deck
 * needs one field in the catalog.
 */

/**
 * The Home, expressed as an ordinary placeable box so it goes through the same OBB test as
 * everything else.
 *
 * It is the one obstacle with no measurable model here — it renders through HouseModel and is
 * sized by its House Style — so its box is registered from the footprint that already drives the
 * mesh, the walk collider and the entry trigger. Before this, the ghost carried a separate
 * circle-vs-circle rule for the house: a circle *circumscribing* the 1.9 x 1.7 box, i.e. 2.55
 * where the wall is at 1.9, plus a second circle around the candidate. Those two conservative
 * approximations stacked into roughly a metre of phantom no-build space around the house, which is
 * a large part of "there is obviously room and it still refuses".
 *
 * THE RAW FOOTPRINT, NOT THE SOLID ONE. This used to register `getHomeSolidHalfExtents` — the
 * walls plus the player's own 0.35 radius — which is the right box for stopping a BODY and the
 * wrong one for refusing an OBJECT. Nothing is placed at body height by walking there, so the
 * inflation was 35cm of no-build ring the player could see straight through: a lantern could not
 * be stood against the wall of their own house. The margin belongs to `resolveHomeCollision`,
 * where it started, and this states the building. A prop tucked under the eaves is a feature.
 *
 * `walk` is null because the player's collision against the Home is resolved separately and
 * exactly (`resolveHomeCollision`), against the inflated half-extents.
 */
const HOME_FOOTPRINT = boxFootprint({
  cx: 0,
  cz: 0,
  halfW: HOUSE_FOOTPRINT.halfWidth,
  halfD: HOUSE_FOOTPRINT.halfDepth,
  minY: 0,
  maxY: HOUSE_FOOTPRINT.height,
  walk: null,
});
registerFootprint(STARTER_HOUSE_ITEM_ID, HOME_FOOTPRINT);

/** The Home as a placement, so the shared conflict test can take it as an obstacle. */
function homeAsPlacement(home: ResolvedHome): PlacedItem {
  return {
    instanceId: HOME_INSTANCE_ID,
    itemId: STARTER_HOUSE_ITEM_ID,
    position: [home.position[0], home.position[1], home.position[2]],
    rotation: home.rotation,
  };
}

/** Reserved instance id for the Home, which is not a real placement in `islandPlacements`. */
export const HOME_INSTANCE_ID = '__home__';

/** What is under a given point, and how high its top is. */
export interface SurfaceHit {
  /** World Y of the top of that surface — where an object's origin, or the player's feet, go. */
  y: number;
  /** The placement providing it, or `null` when it is the island itself. */
  supportId: string | null;
  /** The support's material, for footsteps. `null` on natural ground. */
  surface: StandableSurface | null;
  /** True when this is somewhere an ordinary object can stand: dry land, or a deck. */
  isSolid: boolean;
}

/**
 * The topmost surface at `(x, z)` — a placed deck if one covers the point, otherwise the island.
 *
 * Decks stack: the answer is simply the highest one whose box contains the point, so a deck laid
 * on a deck works with no extra rule. `ignoreInstanceId` drops the object currently being dragged,
 * which must not be allowed to stand on itself.
 */
export function getSurfaceAt(
  x: number,
  z: number,
  placements: PlacedItem[],
  islandScale: number,
  ignoreInstanceId?: string | null,
): SurfaceHit {
  return topSurfaceAt(x, z, placements, islandScale, ignoreInstanceId, false);
}

/**
 * The topmost surface an OBJECT may be set down on — the walkable answer above, plus tabletops.
 *
 * Split from {@link getSurfaceAt} rather than folded into it, because the two questions genuinely
 * differ and conflating them would be a bug in both directions:
 *
 *  - **Walking** asks what the player's feet may rest on. A table must not be an answer; making it
 *    one would let the character walk up onto the furniture (and would put the pet, the NPCs and
 *    the footstep sounds up there too, since they all read `getSurfaceAt`).
 *  - **Placement** asks what an object may stand on, and a table is the obvious answer — it is
 *    what `tabletop` means, and the interior has resolved it that way since wall art was added
 *    (`isDisplaySurfaceItem`, lib/interiorPlacement.ts).
 *
 * Before this split the island had no notion of standing anything on anything: only `standable`
 * decks were support, so a lantern dragged over an outdoor table was not "on the table", it was an
 * overlap — the placement was refused and the object could only ever go on the ground beside it.
 * Indoors the same lantern went straight onto the same table. That was the largest remaining
 * inconsistency between the two modes, and it was in the surface lookup rather than in either
 * mode's UI.
 */
export function getSupportAt(
  x: number,
  z: number,
  placements: PlacedItem[],
  islandScale: number,
  ignoreInstanceId?: string | null,
): SurfaceHit {
  return topSurfaceAt(x, z, placements, islandScale, ignoreInstanceId, true);
}

function topSurfaceAt(
  x: number,
  z: number,
  placements: PlacedItem[],
  islandScale: number,
  ignoreInstanceId: string | null | undefined,
  includeDisplaySurfaces: boolean,
): SurfaceHit {
  const info = getTerrainInfo(x, z, islandScale);
  let best: SurfaceHit = {
    y: info.targetY,
    supportId: null,
    surface: null,
    isSolid: isLandTerrain(info.terrain),
  };

  for (const p of placements) {
    if (ignoreInstanceId && p.instanceId === ignoreInstanceId) continue;
    const surface = getStandableSurface(p.itemId);
    // `surface` stays null for a tabletop: it is the footstep material, and nothing walks on a
    // table. A top that only objects may use therefore reports no material, correctly.
    if (!surface && !(includeDisplaySurfaces && isDisplaySurfaceItem(p.itemId))) continue;

    const fp = getFootprint(p.itemId);
    if (!fp) continue;

    if (!footprintContainsPoint(fp, p.position[0], p.position[2], p.rotation || 0, x, z)) continue;

    // THE WALKING SURFACE, NOT THE TOP OF THE MODEL. For a bare platform they are the same
    // number; for anything with a railing they are not, and reading `maxY` put the player on
    // top of 小型觀景平台’s handrails — 0.84 world units above its boards. `standY` is measured
    // off the model exactly the way every other collider dimension is
    // (lib/furniturePlacement.ts’ measureStandTop); it falls back to `maxY` only for a piece
    // whose surface could not be measured, which is the old behaviour and errs high rather
    // than dropping a body through the deck.
    //
    // A tabletop keeps `maxY`: what an OBJECT rests on is the top of the model, and no
    // display surface in the catalog has anything standing up out of it.
    const top = p.position[1] + (surface ? (fp.standY ?? fp.maxY) : fp.maxY);
    if (top <= best.y) continue;
    best = { y: top, supportId: p.instanceId, surface, isSolid: true };
  }

  return best;
}

/**
 * Is there solid footing above the waterline at `(x, z)`?
 *
 * The swim-state machine's override: a player standing on a pier is not swimming, whatever the
 * distance from the island says. Stated as a property of the ground rather than as a check for
 * any particular object, so a second kind of deck needs no change here.
 */
export function isGroundedAt(
  x: number,
  z: number,
  placements: PlacedItem[],
  islandScale: number,
): boolean {
  const hit = getSurfaceAt(x, z, placements, islandScale);
  return hit.isSolid && hit.y > WATER_SURFACE_Y;
}

/**
 * The Y an object of `itemId` should be placed at, at `(x, z)`.
 *
 * A deck sited over open water rests on the sea surface rather than sinking to the seabed — which
 * is what makes it a pier and is the whole reason a deck may be placed there at all. Everything
 * else can only be placed where {@link getSupportAt} already reports solid footing, so this branch
 * never applies to it.
 */
export function resolvePlacementY(
  itemId: string,
  x: number,
  z: number,
  placements: PlacedItem[],
  islandScale: number,
  ignoreInstanceId?: string | null,
): number {
  const hit = getSupportAt(x, z, placements, islandScale, ignoreInstanceId);
  if (hit.isSolid) return hit.y;
  return isStandableItem(itemId) ? Math.max(hit.y, WATER_SURFACE_Y) : hit.y;
}

/** Why a spot was refused, in the order the checks run. */
export type PlacementBlockReason = 'noGround' | 'offEdge' | 'overlap';

export interface PlacementVerdict {
  ok: boolean;
  reason: PlacementBlockReason | null;
  /**
   * Where the object actually ends up.
   *
   * Not simply the `(x, z)` that was asked about: the rule quantises it, and slides it back on
   * when it is hanging off the support it landed on — so the caller must draw the ghost at THIS
   * position rather than at the pointer's. Returning the corrected spot rather than only a verdict
   * is what stops the ghost and the rule from having two different ideas of where the object is,
   * which was the shape of every "it says blocked but it looks fine" report.
   */
  x: number;
  z: number;
  /** Where the object would sit — valid whether or not the spot is legal, so the ghost can draw it. */
  y: number;
  /** The deck or tabletop it would rest on, if any. */
  supportId: string | null;
}

export interface EvaluatePlacementArgs {
  itemId: string;
  x: number;
  z: number;
  rotation: number;
  placements: PlacedItem[];
  home: ResolvedHome | null;
  islandScale: number;
  /** The placement being moved, or the Home when the Home is what's being moved. */
  excludeInstanceId?: string | null;
}

/**
 * The single validity rule for putting something on the island. Used by the drag ghost, by the
 * solver that picks a new object's opening position, and by nothing else — there is no second
 * opinion to drift out of sync with.
 */
export function evaluateIslandPlacement({
  itemId, x: rawX, z: rawZ, rotation, placements, home, islandScale, excludeInstanceId,
}: EvaluatePlacementArgs): PlacementVerdict {
  // PRECISION. The island never had a grid of its own — its problem was the opposite, a raw float
  // straight off a plane intersection, saved and reloaded and re-dragged until the same spot had a
  // dozen spellings. Quantising here gives the island the identical step the interior now uses
  // (2 cm, or the coarse align grid while Shift is held), so "one nudge" means the same distance
  // in both modes and a position survives a save/load round trip unchanged.
  const step = getPlacementStep();
  let x = quantize(rawX, step);
  let z = quantize(rawZ, step);

  let hit = getSupportAt(x, z, placements, islandScale, excludeInstanceId);

  // STACKING. When the spot has landed on another placed object — a deck, an outdoor table — slide
  // the whole footprint back onto that top face rather than letting it hang over the edge. This is
  // the same `clampOntoSupport` the interior uses for tabletops, which is what makes putting a
  // lantern on an outdoor table behave exactly like putting a vase on an indoor one.
  //
  // Only for an object SMALLER than its support: clamping a deck onto a table would drag the deck
  // somewhere the player never pointed. `clampOntoSupport` returns null in that case and the spot
  // is left where it is, to be judged on the corner test below like any other.
  const clampFp = hit.supportId ? getFootprint(itemId) : undefined;
  const support = clampFp
    ? placements.find((p) => p.instanceId === hit.supportId)
    : undefined;
  const supportFp = support ? getFootprint(support.itemId) : undefined;

  if (clampFp && support && supportFp) {
    const slide = clampOntoSupport(
      makeObb(clampFp, x, z, rotation),
      makeObb(supportFp, support.position[0], support.position[2], support.rotation || 0),
    );
    if (slide && (slide.dx !== 0 || slide.dz !== 0)) {
      x += slide.dx;
      z += slide.dz;
      hit = getSupportAt(x, z, placements, islandScale, excludeInstanceId);
    }
  }

  const y = resolvePlacementY(itemId, x, z, placements, islandScale, excludeInstanceId);
  const base: Omit<PlacementVerdict, 'ok' | 'reason'> = { x, z, y, supportId: hit.supportId };

  // 1. There has to be something to stand on. A deck is its own exception, and the only one:
  //    extending buildable ground out over the water is what a deck is for.
  if (!hit.isSolid && !isStandableItem(itemId)) {
    return { ...base, ok: false, reason: 'noGround' };
  }

  const fp = getFootprint(itemId);

  // An unmeasured item is one whose model has never mounted. Refusing on the strength of a box we
  // do not have would block the player for a reason we cannot show them; the first mount measures
  // it and the caller re-runs this (see subscribeFootprints).
  if (!fp) return { ...base, ok: true, reason: null };

  // 2. Whatever holds the centre must hold the whole object. Without this an object dropped near a
  //    deck's edge is half on the boards and half in mid-air — the placement height is resolved
  //    from one point, so it can only ever be right for one point. Checking the corners against
  //    the same surface lookup states the requirement directly, and costs nothing on open ground
  //    where every corner reports the island. It is the same rule at the shoreline, where the
  //    thing hanging off the edge is the beach.
  for (const [cornerX, cornerZ] of footprintOutline(fp, x, z, rotation)) {
    const corner = getSupportAt(cornerX, cornerZ, placements, islandScale, excludeInstanceId);
    // Only when the object is STANDING ON something. "Half on the platform" is a real thing to
    // say to a player who put a fountain on the edge of a deck; it is nonsense said to one who set
    // a chair beside a table and caught its corner — nothing is hanging off anything there, there
    // is simply a table in the way, and rule 3 below says so in words that help.
    if (hit.supportId && corner.supportId !== hit.supportId) {
      return { ...base, ok: false, reason: 'offEdge' };
    }
    if (!corner.isSolid && !isStandableItem(itemId)) {
      return { ...base, ok: false, reason: 'noGround' };
    }
  }

  // 3. Nothing may be put inside anything else. The deck underneath is the exception, because
  //    resting on a surface is the whole point of having placed it there.
  const ignore = new Set<string>();
  if (excludeInstanceId) ignore.add(excludeInstanceId);
  if (hit.supportId) ignore.add(hit.supportId);

  const obstacles = home && excludeInstanceId !== HOME_INSTANCE_ID
    ? [...placements, homeAsPlacement(home)]
    : placements;

  const candidate: PlacedItem = { instanceId: '__draft__', itemId, position: [x, y, z], rotation };
  if (findPlacementConflict(candidate, obstacles, ignore)) {
    return { ...base, ok: false, reason: 'overlap' };
  }

  return { ...base, ok: true, reason: null };
}

/** Player-facing explanation for each refusal, shown by the editor panel and the error toast. */
export const PLACEMENT_BLOCK_MESSAGE: Record<PlacementBlockReason, string> = {
  noGround: '這裡是海面，請放在陸地或木製平台上',
  offEdge: '有一半懸在平台外，請整個放上平台',
  overlap: '此處已有其他擺設',
};
```

```ts
import * as THREE from 'three';

/**
 * Cross-component per-frame state shared outside React between the 3D layer
 * (Avatar, CameraController, IslandPet, PlacementGhost) and a few UI overlays
 * (PettingMiniGame, LoginBonusPopup) that need to read/write it every frame
 * without paying for a React re-render. Previously this lived as untyped
 * `(window as any).playerPos` etc. properties — same runtime mechanism
 * (still a plain mutable object read/written imperatively, still no
 * ordering guarantees beyond whatever useFrame priority each caller runs
 * at), just typed and discoverable instead of a magic string on `window`
 * that silently does nothing if a caller mistypes the key.
 */
export interface PlayerBusState {
  playerPos?: THREE.Vector3;
  playerRotation?: number;
  playerIsMoving?: boolean;
  /**
   * Whether the player is off the ground right now — a jump or a somersault, both of which
   * Avatar.tsx already tracks to drive the height arc.
   *
   * Published for the special-cosmetic runtime's `jump` burst (constants/cosmeticEffects.ts),
   * which watches this flag's RISING EDGE to catch the moment of take-off. A boolean polled
   * once a frame by the one loop that cares beats an event bus here: a subscription would
   * need tearing down per Canvas and would still fire while the island is unmounted.
   */
  playerIsAirborne?: boolean;
  pendingPlayerTeleport?: { x: number; z: number; rotation?: number };
  isDraggingPlacement: boolean;
  cameraYaw?: number;
  /**
   * How far the camera is currently rendering from the point it orbits — the character's head —
   * in world units, or Infinity in the branches where the number would be meaningless.
   *
   * Written every frame by whichever CameraController owns the view, and read by Avatar.tsx,
   * which fades the body out as the camera comes inside the skull. The avatar cannot work this
   * out for itself: it knows the zoom, but the zoom is only ONE of the two ways the camera ends
   * up in the character's head. The other is geometry — walk into a wall and the arm has nowhere
   * left to go — and that one has no signal in React state at all, which is why the camera has to
   * say so out loud. See CameraController's surfaceLimit.
   */
  cameraPivotDistance?: number;
  dogPos?: THREE.Vector3;
  /**
   * WHICH companion {@link PlayerBusState.dogPos} belongs to — its catalog id, or undefined when
   * no animal is in reach.
   *
   * Written by the mover in the same call that publishes the position (Three/IslandPet.tsx's
   * `publishPromptTarget`), so the prompt, the interaction panel and the feed all act on the animal
   * the player is actually standing next to rather than on 「the pet」 resolved separately by each
   * of them. That is the brief's §21: with three companions out, the one being fed has to be the
   * one in front of you, and the only component that knows which that is, is the one drawing it.
   *
   * The field is named for the pet, not for the slot: the bus's other `dog*` fields predate the
   * shop selling cats and birds, and this one is new enough not to inherit the misnomer.
   */
  petTargetId?: string;
  /**
   * Whether the pet is trotting somewhere right now, published by whichever component is
   * moving it — the equipped companion (Three/IslandPet.tsx).
   * Read by the special-cosmetic runtime for `moving`-triggered pet effects (the mushroom
   * cap's spores, the flower collar's petals) — the same role
   * {@link PlayerBusState.playerIsMoving} plays for the player, and published for the same
   * reason: the answer already exists inside the component that animates the walk, and
   * re-deriving it from successive positions outside would be both slower and wrong on the
   * frames where the pet is being pushed out of furniture rather than walking.
   */
  dogIsMoving?: boolean;
  /**
   * Added to the pet's distance when InteractionPromptTracker ranks what to prompt for — a
   * priority handicap, not a real distance (the trigger radius still uses the true one).
   *
   * Anything that wanders on its own leaves 0 here, so being the nearest thing genuinely means
   * the player walked over to it. The EQUIPPED companion
   * (Three/IslandPet.tsx) is at the owner's heel by construction and would otherwise win every
   * ranking it entered — including standing in front of the "進入我的家" prompt at the player's own
   * front door. It sets {@link COMPANION_PROMPT_BIAS}, which puts it behind anything else in range.
   */
  dogPromptBias?: number;
  // `dogIsHappy` and `petEating` used to live here: a boolean flipped by a timer and a bare
  // timestamp, each saying half of what an animal was doing with its owner. Both are
  // lib/petActivity.ts now — one record per animal, with a lifecycle that ends on its own clock.
  /**
   * World position of the currently-nearby interactable (e.g. a hammock), written by
   * Avatar.tsx whenever its own nearbyHammock detection changes - see nearbyInteractable in
   * AppContext, which only carries a display string, not a position. InteractionPromptTracker.tsx
   * reads this to anchor the floating prompt above the object instead of at screen center.
   */
  nearbyInteractablePos?: THREE.Vector3;
  /**
   * 關燈之後角色手上那根蠟燭，火焰的世界座標 —— 由 Three/CandleInHand.tsx 每幀就地改寫。
   *
   * 蠟燭的「形」和它的「光」是分開的兩件事，而且非分開不可：火焰掛在右手的關節底下（所以它跟著
   * 手臂擺動），但打出去的那盞 pointLight 不能掛在那裡 —— 第一人稱視角下整個身體是隱藏的
   * （見 Avatar 的 isHiddenByMode），連帶會把掛在身上的燈一起關掉，於是玩家會發現自己手上
   * 拿著一根照不亮任何東西的蠟燭，站在一片全黑裡。
   *
   * 所以光留在場景那一層（BuildingInteriorView 的 CandleGlow），每幀來這裡拿火焰在哪裡。這
   * 跟 PlayerFollowLight 讀 `playerPos` 是同一個做法，只是跟得更緊一點。
   *
   * undefined 表示現在沒有人拿著蠟燭（燈是亮的，或人在屋外）。
   */
  candlePos?: THREE.Vector3;
  /**

   * re-derived by the badge: the key and the label must never be able to disagree about what
   * they are pointing at, which is the same rule `tidyTarget` below exists to enforce.
   *
   * On this bus rather than in AppContext because it changes at walking speed and exactly one
   * component reads it — one that is already polling this object every animation frame.
   */
  nearbyInteraction?: {
    instanceId: string;
    itemName: string;
    /** 坐下 / 躺下 / 使用 / 起身 — see constants/furnitureInteractions.ts. */
    verb: string;
    /** Which icon the touch button shows: 'sit' | 'lie' | 'hand' | 'book' | 'sparkle'. */
    icon: string;
    occupied: boolean;
  } | null;
  /**
   * Screen-space result of InteractionPromptTracker.tsx's per-frame projection of the single
   * nearest interactable (building door / nearbyInteractablePos / dog) onto the camera's view -
   * x/y are already smoothed and in CSS pixels. `visible` is false when the target is occluded,
   * off-screen, or out of its own trigger radius (in which case there simply is no candidate and
   * this whole field is null). InteractionPrompt.tsx (the HTML overlay, outside the Canvas) polls
   * this every animation frame instead of re-deriving it, since only code inside the Canvas has
   * the camera/scene needed to project and raycast.
   */
  interactionPrompt?: { key: string; x: number; y: number; visible: boolean } | null;
  /**

   *
   * 為什麼不跟其他人排在同一個名次裡（它一開始是的）：開關按的是 Q，不是 E。同一格只能放一個
   * 的理由是「玩家只有一個動作鍵，兩個徽章搶同一個位置就是一次他看不見的擲硬幣」—— 而那個理由
   * 在這裡不成立。站在沙發旁邊的牆邊，E 坐下和 Q 關燈是兩件不衝突的事，兩個徽章都該在。

  lightSwitchPrompt?: { x: number; y: number; visible: boolean } | null;
  /**

   *
   * On this bus rather than in AppContext for the usual reason: it is recomputed every frame from

  tidyTarget?: { x: number; z: number; count: number; wall: boolean } | null;

  merchantTarget?: {

    anchor: THREE.Vector3;

   *

   * （constants/merchants.ts），所以「哪一位商人該高興」是由他自己開的是哪一家店決定的。
   */
  merchantPurchase?: {
    count: number;
    shop: string;
    currency: string;
    amount: number;
  };
  /**
   * 島上或屋裡那位居民，如果玩家此刻**聊得到**她的話（constants/npcSocial.ts）。
   *
   * 跟 {@link merchantTarget} 同一個形狀、同一個理由：由畫她的那個元件（Three/NpcWalker.tsx）每幀
   * 寫入，因為只有它知道她這一幀走到哪裡；它同時是提示與動作鍵的閘門。
   *
   * `scope` 是它跟商人不一樣的地方，而且非有不可：島嶼和室內是兩個 Canvas，**座標是同一個數字
   * 空間**（島心與客廳中心都是 0,0），而室內那條 Canvas 在玩家站在屋外時仍然會稀疏地跑幀。少了
   * 這一格，一位站在客廳原點的管家會讓島上的提示亮起來。每一個讀它的地方都先比對自己的 scope。
   */
  npcTarget?: {
    npcId: string;
    scope: 'island' | 'interior';
    anchor: THREE.Vector3;
    reach: number;
    label: string;
    /** 聊天已經在進行 —— 按下去是「下一句」，玩家的身體語言也跟著換（見 Avatar 的 `chat`）。 */
    talking: boolean;
  } | null;
  /**
   * 居民此刻說的那一句話（泡泡裡的字），或 null。
   *
   * 由說話的那位居民在一句開始時寫入、在聊天結束時清掉（只清自己的）。`anchor` 是每幀就地改寫
   * 的同一顆向量，所以泡泡跟著她走。泡泡本身是 HTML（UI/NpcSpeechBubble.tsx），投影由對應
   * scope 的 InteractionPromptTracker 做，結果寫在 {@link npcSpeechPrompt}。
   */
  npcSpeech?: {
    npcId: string;
    scope: 'island' | 'interior';
    name: string;
    text: string;
    anchor: THREE.Vector3;
    /** `performance.now()` ms。泡泡自己的淡入從這裡算，而且同一句不會因為重繪而重播。 */
    startedAt: number;
    /** 這一句最多停多久。說話的人通常會先清掉它；這個上限是保險。 */
    seconds: number;
  } | null;
  /** {@link npcSpeech} 投影到螢幕上的位置，由 InteractionPromptTracker 寫。 */
  npcSpeechPrompt?: { x: number; y: number; visible: boolean } | null;
  /**
   * The daily-login reward waiting to be shown, or null once claimed.
   *
   * Written through {@link publishLoginBonus}, not assigned directly — see that
   * function for why the difference matters to the first-run sequence.
   */
  showLoginBonus?: LoginBonus | null;
  /**
   * Whether the interior free-edit ("佈置模式") camera is currently active.
   * While true, `playerPos`/`playerRotation` are frozen (the avatar itself
   * doesn't move during build mode - see Avatar.tsx's isControlActive), so
   * consumers that need a live position during build mode (e.g. MiniMap)
   * should read `buildModeCamPos`/`buildModeCamDir` instead. Written by
   * CameraController; nothing else writes or depends on these three fields,
   * so they're safe to read without affecting the existing avatar/camera/
   * build-mode/room-expansion systems.
   */
  isBuildMode?: boolean;
  buildModeCamPos?: THREE.Vector3;
  buildModeCamDir?: { x: number; z: number };
  /**
   * Whether the player is actually INSIDE the house right now, i.e. whether the interior view is
   * the one being looked at. Written by BuildingInteriorView from its own `active` prop.
   *
   * Needed because the interior is not unmounted when the player walks out - it stays alive on
   * `frameloop="demand"` so the room is already compiled on the doorstep - and a demand canvas
   * still draws a frame on every React re-render. Its `useFrame` bodies therefore keep ticking,
   * sparsely, while the player is standing outside on the island. That is harmless for anything
   * purely visual (nobody is looking at it), but NOT for anything audible: the sliding doors
   * (BuildingInteriorView's AutoDoor) went on opening and closing for the butler, and their
   * chimes played out over the island. 「即使在屋外，依然可聽見管家開關門的聲音」.
   *
   * It cannot be inferred from `playerPos`, which is the trap that kept this quiet: the outdoor
   * avatar's coordinates and the room grid's are the same numeric space, so a player standing
   * outside can measure as "right next to" an interior door and pass every proximity test in
   * the house.
   */
  isInsideHouse?: boolean;
  /**
   * Incremented (never reset) by any UI-layer event the avatar should react to with a happy
   * pulse - a successful shop purchase, expanding territory, etc. Avatar.tsx compares this
   * against the last value it saw each frame rather than consuming/clearing it, so it can't
   * miss a trigger that fires between frames or double-fire on the same one.
   */
  happyReactionCount?: number;
  isSwimming?: boolean;
  /**
   * Where the body actually IS, as opposed to where the character logically is.
   *
   * `playerPos` never leaves the walking plane (its Y is the character's logical ground, not the
   * rendered one), so on its own it cannot say that the body has sunk into the sea or that it is
   * lying flat in it. These two say both, and they are published as raw facts about the RENDERED
   * body rather than as a camera height: the body knows where it is, the camera decides what to
   * look at (constants/cameraFocus.ts).
   *
   * `bodyRootY` is the support height the character is being drawn at - terrain, floor, or the
   * blended swim depth - deliberately WITHOUT the jump arc, the somersault's pivot offset or the
   * crawl lift on top of it. Those are transient gestures the shot is meant to SHOW happening,
   * not framing for the camera to cancel out by following them.
   *
   * `swimPose` is Avatar.tsx's own water-pose weight (0 = the land pose, 1 = flat in the water),
   * the same number the pitch, the limbs and the head are blended by - so anything framed from it
   * moves exactly when the body moves, with no rate of its own to fall behind on.
   */
  bodyRootY?: number;
  swimPose?: number;
  /**
   * True while the 匍匐 (CRAWL) emote is held. Read by CameraController, which
   * drops its orbit focus to floor level so the player sees the island from
   * where the prone body actually is, not from standing eye height.
   */
  isCrawling?: boolean;
}

export interface LoginBonus {
  streak: number;
  gold: number;
  xp: number;
  isManual?: boolean;
}

export const playerBus: PlayerBusState = {
  isDraggingPlacement: false,
};

/**
 * The handicap an always-at-your-heel companion carries in the prompt ranking - see
 * {@link PlayerBusState.dogPromptBias}. Larger than any trigger radius in the tracker, so it is
 * simply "last", with no tuning against the individual radii to keep in sync.
 */
export const COMPANION_PROMPT_BIAS = 1000;

/**
 * 記下一筆剛剛**成交**的買賣，讓島上那位商人下次有機會做出反應。
 *
 * 寫成一個函數而不是讓呼叫端直接指定欄位，唯一的理由就是那個計數器：它必須是「上一個值加
 * 一」，而不是任何呼叫端自己記得要遞增的東西。
 */
export function publishMerchantPurchase(shop: string, currency: string, amount: number): void {
  playerBus.merchantPurchase = {
    count: (playerBus.merchantPurchase?.count ?? 0) + 1,
    shop,
    currency,
    amount,
  };
}

// --- Login bonus handoff -----------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Announces a daily-login reward to whoever is showing it.
 *
 * Everything else on this bus is per-frame data that a `useFrame` loop is
 * already sampling, so "write a field and let the reader notice" costs nothing.
 * This one is not: it fires once, at profile load, and LoginBonusPopup used to
 * discover it with its own `setInterval(…, 500)`.
 *
 * That poll is what let the popup lose its place in the first-run sequence. The
 * flag is set immediately *before* the profile is published, so by the time the
 * popup's next tick came round the profile had been live for up to half a second
 * — long enough for HomeSetupGuide (whose condition is satisfied the instant a
 * profile exists) to take the onboarding slot, open, and then be displaced when
 * the bonus finally noticed itself. Publishing synchronously means the reward
 * claims its place in the same tick it is granted, and the queue's declared
 * order (lib/onboardingQueue.ts) holds with no dialog appearing and retracting.
 */
const loginBonusListeners = new Set<(bonus: LoginBonus | null) => void>();

export function publishLoginBonus(bonus: LoginBonus | null): void {
  playerBus.showLoginBonus = bonus;
  loginBonusListeners.forEach((listener) => listener(bonus));
}

/**
 * Subscribes to login-bonus announcements. Fires immediately with anything
 * already pending, so a subscriber that mounts *after* the grant still sees it —
 * which a plain event would miss, and which is the whole reason the old code
 * polled instead of listening.
 */
export function subscribeLoginBonus(listener: (bonus: LoginBonus | null) => void): () => void {
  loginBonusListeners.add(listener);
  if (playerBus.showLoginBonus) listener(playerBus.showLoginBonus);
  return () => {
    loginBonusListeners.delete(listener);
  };
}

// --- Daily-login board, opened on purpose ------------------------------------

/**
 * 「把每日簽到的板子打開」—— 一個**動作**，不是一則獎勵通知。
 *
 * 刻意跟上面那條 {@link publishLoginBonus} 分開，雖然兩者最後都會讓同一個面板出現。它們是兩件
 * 不同的事：登入獎勵是「你今天賺到了東西，這裡是通知」，而這一條是「玩家按了按鈕，帶他過去」。
 * 硬塞進同一條通道要付兩筆代價 —— 呼叫端得偽造一個沒有人會讀的 `{ streak, gold, xp }`，而收
 * 聽端得靠 `isManual` 去猜自己該不該播獎勵音效。那個猜測本來就是這個 flag 存在的唯一理由。
 *
 * 也**沒有**補送（replay）：`subscribeLoginBonus` 會把還沒被消費的通知補給晚掛載的訂閱者，因為
 * 獎勵是在 profile 載入那一瞬間就宣告的，錯過了就永遠錯過。按鈕不是那種東西 —— 按下去的當下
 * 面板早就掛在 App 上聽著了，補送一個「打開」只會讓面板在下一次重新掛載時自己彈出來。
 */
const dailyLoginBoardListeners = new Set<() => void>();

export function openDailyLoginBoard(): void {
  dailyLoginBoardListeners.forEach((listener) => listener());
}

export function subscribeDailyLoginBoard(listener: () => void): () => void {
  dailyLoginBoardListeners.add(listener);
  return () => {
    dailyLoginBoardListeners.delete(listener);
  };
}

/**
 * Where the user effectively *is* right now, for anything that should react to
 * them being somewhere - proximity triggers, doors, ambience.
 *
 * `playerPos` is not that answer on its own. Entering the interior's 佈置模式
 * freezes the avatar and hands control to a free-flying edit camera, so
 * `playerPos` stops at wherever the avatar was standing while the user drives
 * around the house. Anything keyed off `playerPos` therefore goes dead the
 * moment build mode opens - which is exactly how the sliding doors stopped
 * opening and closing (and stopped making any sound) while decorating.
 *
 * Consumers that want "is the user near this thing" should call this rather
 * than reading `playerPos`. Consumers that genuinely mean the AVATAR - its own
 * animation, its collision, its shadow - must keep reading `playerPos`, because
 * during build mode the avatar really is standing still.
 */
export function getActiveViewerPos(): THREE.Vector3 | undefined {
  return playerBus.isBuildMode ? playerBus.buildModeCamPos ?? playerBus.playerPos : playerBus.playerPos;
}

/**
 * Browsers stop (or heavily throttle) requestAnimationFrame while a tab is
 * hidden/unfocused, so the very next frame after it resumes can report a
 * `delta` of several seconds instead of ~1/60s. Any per-frame rotation rate
 * (camera orbit joystick, build-mode look, etc.) that multiplies straight
 * into an angle by that delta would then apply the whole backlog as one
 * instant multi-turn spin - this is what turned "switched tabs and came
 * back" into the camera/character spinning several full rotations. Every
 * such useFrame should route its delta through clampFrameDelta() instead of
 * using the raw value.
 */
export const MAX_FRAME_DELTA = 0.1;
// Wall-clock deadline (not a frame counter) so every caller in the same
// render tick - and the next few real ticks - independently sees the same
// "just resumed" window, regardless of how many components call
// clampFrameDelta() per frame.
let resumeGuardUntil = 0;
const RESUME_GUARD_MS = 150;

/** Call from a visibilitychange/focus handler once the tab/window is active again. */
export function markVisibilityResumed() {
  resumeGuardUntil = performance.now() + RESUME_GUARD_MS;
}

/** Clamp (or, immediately after a resume, zero out) a useFrame delta before using it for rotation/movement. */
export function clampFrameDelta(delta: number): number {
  if (performance.now() < resumeGuardUntil) return 0;
  return Math.min(delta, MAX_FRAME_DELTA);
}
```

## src/lib/rendererTuning.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import type { WebGLRenderer } from 'three';

/**
 * The URL flag that puts shader validation back. `?shaderdebug` on any page.
 *
 * It exists because {@link tuneRenderer} turns off the only thing that reports a broken shader.
 * Anyone editing `onBeforeCompile` (floorMaterial.ts, Island.tsx, Fish.tsx, EffectField.tsx) or
 * the ShaderMaterial in Fireflies.tsx needs that report, and a silently black material is a much
 * worse afternoon than a 2-second hitch.
 */
const SHADER_DEBUG_FLAG = 'shaderdebug';

/**
 * Applied to every `<Canvas>` in the game, and the reason crossing the front door no longer
 * freezes on a black screen for two or three seconds.
 *
 * ## What was actually happening
 *
 * Entering the house mounts a SECOND `<Canvas>` (App.tsx's view overlays; the island's own Canvas
 * stays mounted and is only stopped with `frameloop='never'`). A new Canvas is a new WebGL
 * context, and a new context has no compiled programs — so on its first frame it compiles and
 * links every shader the interior needs, from scratch, every single time the player walks in.
 *
 * A CPU profile of the entry (headless, software renderer, so the absolute numbers are inflated
 * but the shape is honest) attributed a ~4s stall like this:
 *
 *   1472ms  getShaderInfoLog
 *   1333ms  (program)          — the driver's own compile/link work
 *    542ms  getProgramInfoLog
 *    529ms  getContext         — creating the second context
 *    169ms  new WebGLRenderer
 *
 * The two info-log calls are the interesting half, because they are not the compile: they are
 * three.js CHECKING the compile. `renderer.debug.checkShaderErrors` defaults to true, and reading
 * a program's info log forces the driver to finish compiling and linking before it can answer —
 * a synchronous flush, on the main thread, once per program. With the check off, three.js stops
 * asking, the driver is free to compile programs in parallel on its own threads, and the main
 * thread stops blocking on it.
 *
 * ## What this does NOT fix
 *
 * The context creation and the driver's compile work are still there; this removes the part that
 * was serialising them onto the main thread. If the remaining hitch is still visible, the next
 * step is to stop destroying the interior context on exit (keep the Canvas mounted and hidden),
 * which is a bigger change and is why it is not in here.
 */
export function tuneRenderer(gl: WebGLRenderer): void {
  const debugShaders =
    typeof window !== 'undefined' &&
    new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).has(SHADER_DEBUG_FLAG);

  gl.debug.checkShaderErrors = debugShaders;
}
```

## src/lib/saveStatus.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * The last save that did NOT land, in words the player can act on.
 *
 * ## Why this exists
 *
 * Every write in the game is a `try { await updateDoc(...) } catch { ... return
 * false }`, and the whole UI is built on that boolean: the island editor keeps
 * the draft alive when a commit returns false, the shop refuses to close, the
 * first-run Home guide keeps asking until `profile.home` actually exists. That
 * contract is sound — but a boolean cannot say *why*, so every failure looked
 * identical to the player, and the one message we did have ("請稍後再試")
 * described a network blip, which is the one cause it usually was not.
 *
 * The concrete case this was written for: the deployed Firestore ruleset did not
 * permit the `home` field, so establishing a Home was rejected server-side on
 * every single attempt. Nothing on screen said so. The write failed, the guide's
 * condition (`no home yet`) stayed true, and the tutorial asked again — forever.
 *
 * So the error code is captured here at the one place every write already funnels
 * through (`handleFirestoreError`), translated once, and read back by whichever
 * surface is closest to what the player just tried to do.
 *
 * Deliberately NOT React state and NOT part of AppContext: a save failure is not
 * game state, it must be writable from plain async functions with no hooks in
 * scope, and putting it on the context would re-render the entire world every
 * time a write hiccuped.
 */

export interface SaveFailure {
  /** Firestore's error code, e.g. `permission-denied`. `unknown` when it had none. */
  code: string;
  /** What to actually show a player. Complete sentence, zh-TW, no error jargon. */
  message: string;
  /** Document path the write was aimed at, for the console/report only. */
  path: string | null;
  /** `Date.now()` of the failure — lets a reader ignore a stale one. */
  at: number;
}

/**
 * Player-facing text per Firestore error code.
 *
 * Only codes with a *different course of action* get their own line. "Retry in a
 * moment" and "your account is not allowed to do this" are genuinely different
 * situations; `aborted` vs `cancelled` are not, and a wall of near-identical
 * strings is how error copy stops being read.
 */
const MESSAGE_BY_CODE: Record<string, string> = {
  'permission-denied': '伺服器拒絕了這次存檔，資料沒有保存。這通常是帳號權限或伺服器設定的問題，請聯絡管理員。',
  unauthenticated: '登入狀態已失效，請重新登入後再試一次。',
  unavailable: '目前連不上伺服器，資料沒有保存。請檢查網路連線後再試一次。',
  'deadline-exceeded': '連線逾時，資料沒有保存。請檢查網路連線後再試一次。',
  'not-found': '找不到你的存檔資料，請重新整理頁面後再試一次。',
  'resource-exhausted': '伺服器目前忙碌中，請稍後再試一次。',
  /**
   * The client built a value Firestore cannot store — an `undefined` field being by far the most
   * common cause, since the SDK rejects those SYNCHRONOUSLY, before anything is sent.
   *
   * It earns its own line because the course of action is the opposite of the fallback's. Nothing
   * about the server, the network or the security rules is involved, so retrying is the one thing
   * guaranteed not to help — and 「請稍後再試」 is exactly what sends someone off to do it. This was
   * added after an optional field written as `{ x: undefined }` made a whole feature fail on every
   * single write while showing the generic "try again later" line (see constants/islandReturn.ts's
   * makePetState).
   */
  'invalid-argument': '這次存檔的內容有格式問題，資料沒有保存。重試不會有幫助，請回報給開發者。',
  // Offline saves (save/LocalSaveStore.ts). A different course of action from every code above it:
  // no amount of retrying frees space in localStorage, and signing in moves the save to the cloud.
  'local-storage-full': '這個裝置的本機儲存空間已滿，資料沒有保存。請登入帳號改用雲端存檔，或清理瀏覽器資料後再試一次。',
};

const FALLBACK_MESSAGE = '存檔失敗，資料沒有保存，請稍後再試一次。';

/**
 * Pulls the code out of whatever the SDK threw.
 *
 * `FirebaseError` carries a `code`; the local save store and a plain network
 * failure throw ordinary `Error`s. Both arrive here, so this never assumes a
 * shape it hasn't checked.
 */
export function describeSaveError(error: unknown): { code: string; message: string } {
  const raw =
    typeof error === 'object' && error !== null && 'code' in error
      ? String((error as { code: unknown }).code)
      : '';
  // Firestore prefixes some codes with the service name ("firestore/unavailable").
  const code = (raw.includes('/') ? raw.slice(raw.indexOf('/') + 1) : raw) || 'unknown';
  return { code, message: MESSAGE_BY_CODE[code] ?? FALLBACK_MESSAGE };
}

let last: SaveFailure | null = null;
const listeners = new Set<() => void>();

export function recordSaveFailure(error: unknown, path: string | null): SaveFailure {
  const { code, message } = describeSaveError(error);
  last = { code, message, path, at: Date.now() };
  listeners.forEach((listener) => listener());
  return last;
}

/** The most recent failure, or null if every write so far has landed. */
export function getLastSaveFailure(): SaveFailure | null {
  return last;
}

/**
 * The message to show for an action that just reported failure.
 *
 * Takes the *specific* reason when one was recorded in the last few seconds, and
 * falls back to the generic line otherwise — a failure recorded ten minutes ago
 * by an unrelated write must not be used to explain this one.
 */
export function describeRecentFailure(withinMs = 5000): string {
  if (!last || Date.now() - last.at > withinMs) return FALLBACK_MESSAGE;
  return last.message;
}

export function subscribeSaveFailures(listener: () => void): () => void {
  listeners.add(listener);
  return () => {
    listeners.delete(listener);
  };
}

```

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

// These used to point at cdn.pixabay.com, which returns 403 on this network
// (verified directly, including pixabay.com's own homepage) - so every
// playSound(SoundEffect.X) call was silently failing the same way
// FOOTSTEP_*/SWIM used to. Now backed by the local Web Audio synthesis below
// (see playUiClick/playUiTick/playUiSuccess/playUiReward/playPetBark), same
// fix already applied to footsteps/swim - no network dependency at all.
export enum SoundEffect {
  CLICK = 'synth:click',
  SUCCESS = 'synth:success',
  REWARD = 'synth:reward',
  /** 每日登入 領取 — coins landing in the balance. See {@link playUiCoin}. */
  COIN = 'synth:coin',
  BARK = 'synth:bark',
  TICK = 'synth:tick',
  // The 稀有度 purchase ladder (constants/rarityFx.ts). Four sounds rather than one played
  // louder: a rarer item should sound like MORE MUSIC, not like the same chime turned up.
  RARE_REVEAL = 'synth:rare-reveal',
  EPIC_REVEAL = 'synth:epic-reveal',
  LEGENDARY_FANFARE = 'synth:legendary-fanfare',
  MYTHIC_FANFARE = 'synth:mythic-fanfare',
}

/**
 * Whether the player has muted the game, pushed here from the one place that already owns
 * "settings → audio" (components/UI/MusicPlayer.tsx).
 *
 * Necessary because {@link playSound} has never read `settings.isMuted` at all — the flag only
 * ever reached the background-music manager, so every UI blip has always played through a mute.
 * That is survivable for a 45ms click and not survivable for the 2.5-second brass fanfare below,
 * which is by a wide margin the loudest and longest sound in the game: a player who has muted
 * the game and then buys a 神話 item would get exactly the thing they turned off.
 *
 * It WAS scoped to the fanfares, on the reasoning that silencing every blip was a behaviour
 * change owed its own pass. This is that pass, and the reason is the one the scoping note did
 * not anticipate: the sounds it left through are not all 45ms blips. Footsteps fire continuously
 * for as long as the player walks, and the doors, the pet and the garden props all answer to
 * things a player does constantly. A muted game that still taps, barks and slides doors is a
 * mute button that did not work, which is exactly what players reported — and the button's own
 * label promises 全部靜音. Everything one-shot now goes through {@link sfxContext}; the
 * continuous ambiences answer to their own gate (see THE AMBIENCE GATE below), which the same
 * setting drives via setAmbienceMuted.
 */
let sfxMuted = false;

export const setSfxMuted = (muted: boolean) => {
  sfxMuted = muted;
};

/**
 * 讀回靜音狀態。給「不是一次性、而是自己排程的聲音」用 —— 河馬管家的哼唱（lib/npcHum.ts）
 * 每幀都要問一次，而它不能走 sfxContext()，因為它要的是「靜音時把整條聲音拆掉」而不只是
 * 「這一聲不出」。
 */
export const isSfxMuted = () => sfxMuted;

/**
 * The AudioContext a ONE-SHOT sound effect may use — null while the game is muted.
 *
 * The single choke point for "may this effect make a sound at all". Every synthesized one-shot
 * already began with `const ctx = getSynthAudioContext(); if (!ctx) return;`, so routing them
 * through this adds the mute to all of them without a second early-return per function that
 * someone has to remember to copy into the next sound they write.
 *
 * NOT for the continuous ambiences (surf, swim wash) or for the splashes that belong to them:
 * those are scaled by 海浪環境音 as well as by the mute, and `ambienceScale()` is where both of
 * those questions are already answered together.
 */
function sfxContext(): AudioContext | null {
  return sfxMuted ? null : getSynthAudioContext();
}

const audioPool: { [key: string]: HTMLAudioElement } = {};

/**
 * Plays a sound effect. SoundEffect enum values are routed to the local Web
 * Audio synthesizers below; any other string is treated as a playable URL
 * (kept for one-off custom sounds outside the enum).
 * @param effect The URL or SoundEffect enum value to play
 * @param volume Volume from 0 to 1
 */
export const playSound = (effect: SoundEffect | string, volume = 0.4) => {
  switch (effect) {
    case SoundEffect.CLICK: playUiClick(volume); return;
    case SoundEffect.TICK: playUiTick(volume); return;
    case SoundEffect.SUCCESS: playUiSuccess(volume); return;
    case SoundEffect.REWARD: playUiReward(volume); return;
    case SoundEffect.COIN: playUiCoin(volume); return;
    case SoundEffect.BARK: playPetBark(volume); return;
    case SoundEffect.RARE_REVEAL: playRareReveal(volume); return;
    case SoundEffect.EPIC_REVEAL: playEpicReveal(volume); return;
    case SoundEffect.LEGENDARY_FANFARE: playLegendaryFanfare(volume); return;
    case SoundEffect.MYTHIC_FANFARE: playMythicFanfare(volume); return;
  }

  // The URL branch answers to the mute too. The enum branch above is already covered - every
  // synthesizer it reaches goes through sfxContext() - but this one bypasses Web Audio entirely,
  // so it needs the question asked here or a custom sound would be the one thing left audible.
  if (sfxMuted) return;

  try {
    let audio: HTMLAudioElement;
    if (audioPool[effect]) {
      audio = audioPool[effect];
      audio.currentTime = 0;
    } else {
      audio = new Audio(effect);
      audioPool[effect] = audio;
    }
    audio.volume = volume;
    audio.play().catch(e => {
      // Ignore "user must interact" errors
      if (e.name !== 'NotAllowedError') {
        console.log('Audio play failed', e);
      }
    });
  } catch (e) {
    console.error('Sound error', e);
  }
};

// --- Synthesized movement audio (Web Audio, no network dependency) ---
// The free CDN clips SoundEffect.FOOTSTEP_*/SWIM point at (cdn.pixabay.com) return
// 403 on a lot of networks/firewalls, which silently kills the sound since
// HTMLAudioElement.play() just rejects and gets swallowed. These fire constantly
// during normal play, so instead of depending on those remote files, synthesize
// them locally with a single shared AudioContext.
let synthAudioCtx: AudioContext | null = null;

export function getSynthAudioContext(): AudioContext | null {
  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return null;
  const AudioContextClass = window.AudioContext || (window as any).webkitAudioContext;
  if (!AudioContextClass) return null;
  if (!synthAudioCtx) {
    synthAudioCtx = new AudioContextClass();
  }
  if (synthAudioCtx.state === 'suspended') {
    synthAudioCtx.resume().catch(() => {});
  }
  return synthAudioCtx;
}

/**
 * 已經存在的共用 AudioContext，**不會**替你建一個，也不會去 resume。
 *
 * 給「沒有使用者手勢也會一直被呼叫」的聲音用（NPC 的哼唱與挖土聲）：它們每幀都在問，而在
 * 玩家第一次點擊之前就 new 一個 AudioContext，只會換到瀏覽器一句 autoplay 警告和一個永遠
 * suspended 的 context。等玩家自己點過（MusicPlayer / Avatar 的 primeSynthAudio）之後，這裡就
 * 會拿到那個已經解鎖的 context。
 */
export function peekSynthAudioContext(): AudioContext | null {
  return synthAudioCtx;
}

/** Call from a real user-gesture handler (click/keydown) so the AudioContext isn't blocked by autoplay policy. */
export const primeSynthAudio = () => {
  getSynthAudioContext();
};

// --- 兔子園丁的挖土聲 ---------------------------------------------------------------
//
// 兩個聲音，都刻意很輕：一聲「鏟子吃進土裡」和一串「土塊落地」。它們是場景的質地，不是事件
// 提示 —— 蓋過背景音樂就錯了，所以音量由呼叫端再乘上距離衰減（Three/RabbitGardener.tsx）。
// 只在 AudioContext 已經被玩家解鎖時才出聲（peekSynthAudioContext），靜音時一律不出聲。

let digNoiseBuffer: AudioBuffer | null = null;

function digNoise(ctx: AudioContext): AudioBuffer {
  if (!digNoiseBuffer || digNoiseBuffer.sampleRate !== ctx.sampleRate) {
    const length = Math.floor(ctx.sampleRate * 0.3);
    digNoiseBuffer = ctx.createBuffer(1, length, ctx.sampleRate);
    const data = digNoiseBuffer.getChannelData(0);
    for (let i = 0; i < length; i++) data[i] = Math.random() * 2 - 1;
  }
  return digNoiseBuffer;
}

/** 可以出聲的 context：已解鎖、正在跑、沒有靜音。三者缺一就是 null。 */
function unlockedSfxContext(): AudioContext | null {
  if (sfxMuted) return null;
  const ctx = synthAudioCtx;
  return ctx && ctx.state === 'running' ? ctx : null;
}

function noiseGrain(
  ctx: AudioContext, at: number, duration: number, freq: number, q: number, level: number,
) {
  const src = ctx.createBufferSource();
  src.buffer = digNoise(ctx);
  const bp = ctx.createBiquadFilter();
  bp.type = 'bandpass';
  bp.frequency.value = freq;
  bp.Q.value = q;
  const lp = ctx.createBiquadFilter();
  lp.type = 'lowpass';
  lp.frequency.value = 2600;
  const g = ctx.createGain();
  g.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, at);
  g.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(level, at + 0.006);
  g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, at + duration);
  src.connect(bp);
  bp.connect(lp);
  lp.connect(g);
  g.connect(ctx.destination);
  src.start(at, Math.random() * 0.05, duration + 0.02);
}

/** 鏟子插進土裡：一記悶悶的低頻加一小段沙沙的碎土聲。 */
export const playSpadeDig = (volume = 0.12) => {
  const ctx = unlockedSfxContext();
  if (!ctx || volume <= 0.0005) return;
  try {
    const now = ctx.currentTime + 0.005;
    const thud = ctx.createOscillator();
    thud.type = 'sine';
    thud.frequency.setValueAtTime(105, now);
    thud.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(58, now + 0.1);
    const tg = ctx.createGain();
    tg.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, now);
    tg.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(volume * 0.8, now + 0.008);
    tg.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, now + 0.13);
    thud.connect(tg);
    tg.connect(ctx.destination);
    thud.start(now);
    thud.stop(now + 0.15);
    noiseGrain(ctx, now, 0.16, 620, 0.8, volume * 0.9);
    noiseGrain(ctx, now + 0.05, 0.14, 360, 0.9, volume * 0.55);
  } catch (_) { /* Web Audio error — swallow */ }
};

/** 被拋出去的土塊落地：三四顆很小的沙沙聲，間隔不規則。 */
export const playSoilPatter = (volume = 0.08) => {
  const ctx = unlockedSfxContext();
  if (!ctx || volume <= 0.0005) return;
  try {
    const now = ctx.currentTime + 0.005;
    const grains = 3 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 2);
    for (let i = 0; i < grains; i++) {
      noiseGrain(
        ctx,
        now + Math.random() * 0.22,
        0.025 + Math.random() * 0.03,
        850 + Math.random() * 800,
        1.1,
        volume * (0.35 + Math.random() * 0.35),
      );
    }
  } catch (_) { /* Web Audio error — swallow */ }
};

// --- Synthesized UI/reward/pet one-shots (Web Audio, no network dependency) ---
// Warm sine/triangle tones rather than bright square/8-bit blips, matching the
// game's soft, healing tone instead of a sharp arcade "beep".

interface BlipNote {
  freq: number;
  delay: number; // seconds after the blip starts
  duration: number;
  /** Gain (relative to volume) of a soft harmonic layered on top for a bell-like warmth. */
  harmonicGain?: number;
  /** The harmonic's frequency as a multiple of freq (2 = one octave up, 3 = an octave + a fifth). */
  harmonicRatio?: number;
  /**
   * Oscillator shape, defaulting to the warm sine every UI sound uses.
   *
   * Only the rarity fanfares set this, and only to `triangle`, for the sustained root underneath
   * the arpeggio: a sine that low reads as a hum with no instrument attached, while a triangle's
   * odd harmonics give it enough edge to read as brass holding a note.
   */
  type?: OscillatorType;
  /** This note's share of the blip's volume (1 = full). For balancing a chord's inner voices. */
  gain?: number;
}

function playBlip(notes: BlipNote[], volume: number) {
  const ctx = sfxContext();
  if (!ctx) return;
  try {
    const now = ctx.currentTime;
    for (const note of notes) {
      const t0 = now + note.delay;
      const stopAt = t0 + note.duration + 0.02;
      const level = volume * (note.gain ?? 1);

      const osc = ctx.createOscillator();
      osc.type = note.type ?? 'sine';
      osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(note.freq, t0);
      const gain = ctx.createGain();
      gain.gain.setValueAtTime(0, t0);
      gain.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(level, t0 + 0.008);
      gain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.001, t0 + note.duration);
      osc.connect(gain);
      gain.connect(ctx.destination);
      osc.start(t0);
      osc.stop(stopAt);

      if (note.harmonicGain) {
        const hOsc = ctx.createOscillator();
        hOsc.type = 'sine';
        hOsc.frequency.setValueAtTime(note.freq * (note.harmonicRatio ?? 2), t0);
        const hGain = ctx.createGain();
        hGain.gain.setValueAtTime(0, t0);
        hGain.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(level * note.harmonicGain, t0 + 0.008);
        hGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.001, t0 + note.duration * 0.7);
        hOsc.connect(hGain);
        hGain.connect(ctx.destination);
        hOsc.start(t0);
        hOsc.stop(stopAt);
      }
    }
  } catch (e) {
    // Web Audio unavailable/blocked - fail silently like the rest of the audio layer
  }
}

/** Generic button/toggle/select tap - the game's single most frequent sound. */
export const playUiClick = (volume = 0.4) => {
  playBlip([{ freq: 780, delay: 0, duration: 0.045 }], volume * 0.55);
};

/** Quieter, shorter neutral tick for rapid repeated events (e.g. a rep counter). */
export const playUiTick = (volume = 0.4) => {
  playBlip([{ freq: 1500, delay: 0, duration: 0.02 }], volume * 0.35);
};

/** Two-note gentle rising chime for "done" / confirmation moments. */
export const playUiSuccess = (volume = 0.4) => {
  playBlip([
    { freq: 784, delay: 0, duration: 0.18, harmonicGain: 0.3, harmonicRatio: 2 },
    { freq: 988, delay: 0.1, duration: 0.22, harmonicGain: 0.3, harmonicRatio: 2 },
  ], volume);
};

/** Three-note ascending sparkle arpeggio for purchases/rewards/level-ups. */
export const playUiReward = (volume = 0.4) => {
  playBlip([
    { freq: 659, delay: 0, duration: 0.22, harmonicGain: 0.35, harmonicRatio: 3 },
    { freq: 784, delay: 0.09, duration: 0.24, harmonicGain: 0.35, harmonicRatio: 3 },
    { freq: 988, delay: 0.18, duration: 0.3, harmonicGain: 0.35, harmonicRatio: 3 },
  ], volume);
};

/**
 * 金幣入袋 — the 每日登入 claim, and anything else that pays coins straight into the balance.
 *
 * Deliberately not {@link playUiReward}. That arpeggio is this game's generic "something good
 * happened" and it is already what the shop's cheapest purchase plays; a daily reward borrowing it
 * sounds like a confirmation rather than like being paid. This is the same synth saying a different
 * thing — two bright notes struck 40ms apart with a strong third harmonic, which is what reads as
 * metal rather than as a bell, and then one quieter shimmer above them as the pile settles.
 *
 * About 0.4s in total, so it sits inside the claim animation rather than trailing after it, and
 * mixed lower than the reveal fanfares on purpose: this is a sound the player hears every single
 * day, and the loudest thing in the game has to stay the rarest thing in the game.
 */
export const playUiCoin = (volume = 0.4) => {
  playBlip([
    { freq: 1175, delay: 0, duration: 0.14, harmonicGain: 0.5, harmonicRatio: 3 },
    { freq: 1760, delay: 0.04, duration: 0.16, harmonicGain: 0.45, harmonicRatio: 3 },
    { freq: 2349, delay: 0.13, duration: 0.26, harmonicGain: 0.22, gain: 0.45 },
  ], volume * 0.85);
};

// --- 稀有度 purchase ladder ------------------------------------------------
// Four sounds built by ADDING to playUiReward's three-note arpeggio rather than by writing four
// unrelated cues. A player should hear the same instrument getting more to play as the tier
// climbs, which is what makes the ladder audible as a ladder; four different signature sounds
// would just be four sounds. Everything is synthesized (no audio files anywhere in this repo,
// and the CDN that used to host them is 403 on this network - see the file header).

/** 稀有: the reward arpeggio, plus one bright octave landing on top of it. */
export const playRareReveal = (volume = 0.4) => {
  playUiReward(volume);
  playBlip([{ freq: 1319, delay: 0.3, duration: 0.42, harmonicGain: 0.28, gain: 0.6 }], volume);
};

/** 史詩: the arpeggio, then a rising major triad above it — the first tier that gets a chord. */
export const playEpicReveal = (volume = 0.4) => {
  playUiReward(volume);
  playBlip([
    { freq: 1047, delay: 0.3, duration: 0.5, harmonicGain: 0.3 },
    { freq: 1319, delay: 0.38, duration: 0.5, harmonicGain: 0.3 },
    { freq: 1568, delay: 0.46, duration: 0.62, harmonicGain: 0.3 },
  ], volume * 0.9);
};

/**
 * The fanfare — a sustained triangle-wave root and fifth underneath a rising major arpeggio that
 * lands on a held two-note chord. ~1.5s, and the longest sound in the game.
 *
 * Named for 傳說, which was a tier until the ladder came down to four (constants/rarity.ts).
 * Nothing plays it as its OWN cue any more; it survives as the bed {@link playMythicFanfare} is
 * built on, which is the role it was always doing the most work in.
 *
 * Muted players are checked here rather than in playSound: see {@link setSfxMuted}.
 */
export const playLegendaryFanfare = (volume = 0.4) => {
  if (sfxMuted) return;
  // The brass bed. Started at the same instant as the arpeggio so the first note lands ON a
  // chord instead of arriving over silence.
  playBlip([
    { freq: 196, delay: 0, duration: 1.5, type: 'triangle', gain: 0.55 },
    { freq: 392, delay: 0, duration: 1.4, type: 'triangle', gain: 0.32 },
  ], volume);
  playBlip([
    { freq: 392, delay: 0.05, duration: 0.3, harmonicGain: 0.4 },
    { freq: 494, delay: 0.17, duration: 0.3, harmonicGain: 0.4 },
    { freq: 587, delay: 0.29, duration: 0.34, harmonicGain: 0.4 },
    { freq: 784, delay: 0.41, duration: 0.95, harmonicGain: 0.45 },
  ], volume);
  playBlip([
    { freq: 988, delay: 0.6, duration: 0.85, harmonicGain: 0.3, gain: 0.7 },
    { freq: 1175, delay: 0.6, duration: 0.85, harmonicGain: 0.3, gain: 0.55 },
  ], volume);
};

/**
 * 神話: the fanfare above, then a fast eight-note run climbing two octaves over a lower root.
 *
 * Built as "the fanfare plus something" instead of a bigger fanfare of its own — the same
 * argument as the visual layer budget in constants/rarity.ts. The top of a ladder is recognisable
 * because it contains the rung below it.
 */
export const playMythicFanfare = (volume = 0.4) => {
  if (sfxMuted) return;
  playLegendaryFanfare(volume);
  const run = [1047, 1175, 1319, 1397, 1568, 1760, 1976, 2093];
  playBlip(
    run.map((freq, i) => ({ freq, delay: 0.95 + i * 0.055, duration: 0.3, harmonicGain: 0.35, gain: 0.55 })),
    volume,
  );
  playBlip([{ freq: 147, delay: 0.9, duration: 1.6, type: 'triangle', gain: 0.5 }], volume);
};

/**
 * 轉動音 — the sound of the item spinning in, for the whole of the reveal's arrival.
 *
 * The one SUSTAINED sound in the game, and the reason it is not a {@link SoundEffect} played
 * through {@link playSound}: it lasts as long as the spin does (currently 5.5s), so it has to be
 * STOPPABLE — the player can tap the reveal away, and a whoosh still going over the shop after the
 * overlay is gone is a bug that the enum's fire-and-forget signature cannot express. It returns its
 * own stop handle instead, and components/UI/RarityReveal.tsx — which owns the spin — starts it on
 * mount and stops it on unmount.
 *
 * ## What it is made of
 *
 * A CONTINUOUS bed of filtered noise, with an LFO that slows down riding on top of it. Both halves
 * of that matter, and the first one is a correction: 「旋轉要有種持續的音效持續個兩三秒不是一瞬間」.
 * The modulation used to swing the full way to silence (a 0.5 centre with a ±0.5 depth), which at
 * the low end of the sweep is not a spin, it is two or three separate whooshes with holes between
 * them — the sound stopped existing for most of its own duration. The bed now never drops below
 * ~45% of its level: the noise is unbroken for the whole track and the LFO only makes it SURGE.
 *
 * The surge rate is the RPM. One pass of the item past the listener is one swell, so an LFO
 * falling from 18Hz to 1.4Hz across the track is a 陀螺 winding down — the ear hears the
 * deceleration the eye is watching. A fixed-rate whoosh reads as wind, not as rotation.
 *
 * Under it a triangle sweeping 70→190Hz gives the thing mass and, being unmodulated, is the part
 * that guarantees something is audible at every instant. The bandpass rising and then falling is
 * the 都卜勒 of something coming toward you and settling.
 *
 * Level: it sits under the fanfare but not beneath it. The first version was mixed at half the
 * fanfares and the 神話 brass simply ate it — a sound nobody can hear is not a quiet sound, it is
 * an absent one.
 *
 * ## How it leaves
 *
 * It RETREATS across the back half of the turn rather than stopping partway through it. The
 * sweeps — the bandpass, the pitch, the LFO's deceleration — are all scheduled against
 * `durationMs`, because they describe the real turn and have to stay in step with it; the LEVEL
 * is what moves, ramping down from `fadeFromMs` and reaching silence exactly as the item settles.
 *
 * This replaced a hard stop at `fadeFromMs`, which was an attempt at the same idea —「當已經可以
 * 看到鳳凰 icon 的顏色的時候就可以不用有旋轉的聲音」— and overshot it. Measured, that cut left the
 * last 2.85s of a 7.5s spin at exactly zero, and「旋轉音效不要不見」was that silence: a thing
 * visibly turning with no sound on it does not read as restraint, it reads as broken audio. The
 * ramp keeps both halves of the ask — the whoosh is unmistakably backing off once the colour
 * arrives, and it is never absent while the item is still moving.
 *
 * The window it now covers is also the one where it can actually be heard: 史詩 and 神話 fire
 * their fanfares at delayMs 0 (constants/rarityFx.ts), so the brass is over the FRONT of the spin,
 * not the back.
 *
 * Cutting the sweeps short instead — passing the shorter time as `durationMs` — would sound wrong
 * in a way that is hard to name and easy to hear: the sound would finish its whole deceleration
 * early and be crawling while the picture is still turning.
 *
 * Muted players are checked here, as the fanfares do — see {@link setSfxMuted}.
 *
 * @param durationMs How long the item actually turns for. Drives every sweep, and is when the
 *   level reaches silence and the nodes are freed.
 * @param fadeFromMs When the level STARTS ramping down. Defaults to `durationMs`, i.e. no retreat
 *   at all — the reveal passes the moment the item's colour begins to arrive.
 * @param ctxOverride An {@link OfflineAudioContext} to render into instead of the shared live one.
 *   Test-only, and the reason it exists is that this is the one sound in the game whose bug was
 *   inaudibility: rendering it offline and measuring the envelope is the only way to prove it is
 *   still there in second five. Passing it also bypasses the mute check, since an offline render
 *   makes no noise.
 * @returns A function that fades the sound out over ~120ms and frees the nodes. Safe to call twice.
 */
export const playRevealSpin = (
  volume = 0.4,
  durationMs = 4500,
  fadeFromMs = durationMs,
  ctxOverride?: BaseAudioContext,
): (() => void) => {
  const noop = () => {};
  if (sfxMuted && !ctxOverride) return noop;
  const ctx = ctxOverride ?? getSynthAudioContext();
  if (!ctx) return noop;
  try {
    const now = ctx.currentTime;
    const dur = durationMs / 1000;
    // The retreat: full level until `fadeFrom`, then a straight ramp to silence landing on the
    // settle. Linear rather than exponential on purpose — an exponential ramp does nearly all of
    // its travel in the first moments, which is a hard cut wearing a fade's clothing, and a hard
    // cut is the thing being fixed. A minimum length keeps a caller that passes no `fadeFromMs`
    // (or an out-of-range one) from switching the noise bed off, which clicks.
    const MIN_FADE_S = 0.4;
    const end = dur;
    const fadeFrom = Math.max(0, Math.min(fadeFromMs / 1000, end - MIN_FADE_S));

    // Two seconds of white noise on a loop. Long enough that the loop point is not itself a
    // rhythm — a short buffer looped fast is a buzz at the loop frequency.
    const buffer = ctx.createBuffer(1, Math.floor(ctx.sampleRate * 2), ctx.sampleRate);
    const data = buffer.getChannelData(0);
    for (let i = 0; i < data.length; i++) data[i] = Math.random() * 2 - 1;
    const noise = ctx.createBufferSource();
    noise.buffer = buffer;
    noise.loop = true;

    // The 都卜勒: bright as it rushes in, darkening as it comes to rest.
    const band = ctx.createBiquadFilter();
    band.type = 'bandpass';
    band.Q.value = 1.5;
    band.frequency.setValueAtTime(300, now);
    band.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(1700, now + dur * 0.2);
    band.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(360, now + dur);

    // The body under the noise, rising with the approach.
    const tone = ctx.createOscillator();
    tone.type = 'triangle';
    tone.frequency.setValueAtTime(70, now);
    tone.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(190, now + dur * 0.82);
    const toneGain = ctx.createGain();
    toneGain.gain.setValueAtTime(0, now);
    toneGain.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(volume * 0.26, now + 0.4);
    toneGain.gain.setValueAtTime(volume * 0.26, now + fadeFrom);
    toneGain.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, now + end);

    // The RPM. One surge per pass, decelerating with the item.
    const lfo = ctx.createOscillator();
    lfo.type = 'sine';
    lfo.frequency.setValueAtTime(18, now);
    lfo.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(1.4, now + dur * 0.9);
    const lfoDepth = ctx.createGain();
    lfoDepth.gain.value = 0.28;
    // 0.72 ± 0.28, so the quietest instant of a pass is still 45% of the loudest. This is the
    // difference between a continuous sound that pulses and a sound that keeps stopping.
    const chop = ctx.createGain();
    chop.gain.value = 0.72;
    lfo.connect(lfoDepth);
    lfoDepth.connect(chop.gain);

    const bed = ctx.createGain();
    bed.gain.setValueAtTime(0, now);
    bed.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(volume * 0.62, now + 0.3);
    bed.gain.setValueAtTime(volume * 0.62, now + fadeFrom);
    bed.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, now + end);

    noise.connect(band);
    band.connect(chop);
    chop.connect(bed);
    tone.connect(toneGain);
    toneGain.connect(bed);
    bed.connect(ctx.destination);

    const stopAt = now + end + 0.05;
    noise.start(now);
    tone.start(now);
    lfo.start(now);
    noise.stop(stopAt);
    tone.stop(stopAt);
    lfo.stop(stopAt);

    let stopped = false;
    return () => {
      if (stopped) return;
      stopped = true;
      try {
        const t = ctx.currentTime;
        bed.gain.cancelScheduledValues(t);
        bed.gain.setValueAtTime(bed.gain.value, t);
        bed.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + 0.12);
        noise.stop(t + 0.14);
        tone.stop(t + 0.14);
        lfo.stop(t + 0.14);
      } catch (e) {
        // Already stopped by its own schedule - nothing left to do.
      }
    };
  } catch (e) {
    // Web Audio unavailable/blocked - fail silently like the rest of the audio layer
    return noop;
  }
};
/**
 * 幸運轉盤的旋轉音 — the flapper ticking over the wheel's pegs.
 *
 * ## Why a ratchet and not a whoosh
 *
 * {@link playRevealSpin} already owns "something is spinning" as a continuous whoosh, and it is the
 * right sound for what it does: an ITEM flying in past the listener. A prize wheel is a different
 * object. What a wheel sounds like is the flapper clacking over one peg after another, and that
 * carries a thing no whoosh can — the RATE IS THE SPEED. The ear counts the wedges going by and
 * hears the wheel run out of momentum a full second before it stops, which is the entire drama of
 * a wheel and the reason nobody has ever built one that goes 「咻」.
 *
 * The face already has the pegs drawn on its bezel (UI/LuckyWheel.tsx), so this is also the sound
 * of something that is visibly there.
 *
 * ## Why the times are handed in
 *
 * `pegTimesMs` comes from {@link wheelPegTimes} (constants/luckyWheel.ts), which walks the SAME
 * easing curve the visual is animated along. This file therefore knows nothing about wedges, turns
 * or bezier control points — it is handed a list of moments and makes a noise at each of them. Any
 * other split ends with the deceleration written down twice, and the failure mode of that is a
 * wheel that is still clacking after it has stopped.
 *
 * ## The tick
 *
 * Two layers, because one is not a clack: a bright band-passed noise burst (the flapper's edge) and
 * a very short low sine under it (the peg's body). Both decay in under 40ms — this fires up to ~55
 * times in 3.6 seconds and anything with a tail turns the fast section into a buzz.
 *
 * Three things vary across the run, and all three are the same idea — the wheel is losing energy:
 *  * the noise band drops 2600 → 1700Hz, so the last clacks are duller;
 *  * the pitch of each tick wobbles ±6%, so 55 of them do not read as one machine tone;
 *  * the level starts LOW and rises. That is backwards physically, and right dramatically: the
 *    opening burst is ~25 ticks a second, where full-level clacks would be a wall of static, while
 *    the last four are a second apart and are what the player is holding their breath through.
 *
 * Everything is scheduled up front on the audio clock, so the rhythm is sample-accurate and cannot
 * be jittered by a slow frame — which matters here more than usual, since the thing it has to stay
 * in step with is a 3D scene rendering behind it.
 *
 * Muted players are checked here, as the fanfares and {@link playRevealSpin} do — see
 * {@link setSfxMuted}.
 *
 * @param pegTimesMs When each peg passes the pointer, in ms from now. See {@link wheelPegTimes}.
 * @param volume 0–1, scaled per tick well below it — see the level ramp above.
 * @param ctxOverride An {@link OfflineAudioContext} to render into instead of the shared live one.
 *   Test-only, and for the same reason playRevealSpin has one: the only way to prove a rhythm is
 *   actually there — and lands where the picture does — is to render it and measure the peaks.
 * @returns A function that silences any tick that has not fired yet and frees the nodes. Safe to
 *   call twice, and the reason the panel can be closed or unmounted mid-spin without leaving a
 *   ghost ratchet clacking over the island.
 */
export const playWheelSpin = (
  pegTimesMs: readonly number[],
  volume = 0.4,
  ctxOverride?: BaseAudioContext,
): (() => void) => {
  const noop = () => {};
  if (sfxMuted && !ctxOverride) return noop;
  const ctx = ctxOverride ?? getSynthAudioContext();
  if (!ctx || pegTimesMs.length === 0) return noop;

  try {
    const now = ctx.currentTime;
    const total = pegTimesMs.length;

    // One buffer of noise, shared by every tick. Regenerating 55 of these would be 55 allocations
    // for the same 60ms of randomness; a BufferSource per tick is the cheap part.
    const buffer = ctx.createBuffer(1, Math.floor(ctx.sampleRate * 0.06), ctx.sampleRate);
    const data = buffer.getChannelData(0);
    for (let i = 0; i < data.length; i++) data[i] = Math.random() * 2 - 1;

    const live: { stop: (when?: number) => void }[] = [];

    pegTimesMs.forEach((ms, index) => {
      const t0 = now + ms / 1000;
      // 0 at the first peg, 1 at the last. Every ramp below is written against this rather than
      // against the index, so the shape survives a wheel with a different number of wedges.
      const progress = total > 1 ? index / (total - 1) : 1;
      const level = volume * 0.16 * (0.55 + 0.75 * progress);

      const click = ctx.createBufferSource();
      click.buffer = buffer;
      // ±6% playback rate: the same peg struck at a slightly different angle each time.
      click.playbackRate.value = 0.94 + Math.random() * 0.12;

      const band = ctx.createBiquadFilter();
      band.type = 'bandpass';
      band.frequency.setValueAtTime(2600 - 900 * progress, t0);
      band.Q.value = 2.2;

      const clickGain = ctx.createGain();
      clickGain.gain.setValueAtTime(0, t0);
      clickGain.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(level, t0 + 0.001);
      clickGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t0 + 0.035);

      click.connect(band);
      band.connect(clickGain);
      clickGain.connect(ctx.destination);
      click.start(t0);
      click.stop(t0 + 0.05);
      live.push(click);

      // The body under the edge. Without it the tick is a hiss; with it, it is something hitting
      // something. Deliberately even shorter than the noise — a low tone that rings is a drum.
      const body = ctx.createOscillator();
      body.type = 'triangle';
      body.frequency.setValueAtTime(250 - 60 * progress, t0);
      const bodyGain = ctx.createGain();
      bodyGain.gain.setValueAtTime(0, t0);
      bodyGain.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(level * 0.5, t0 + 0.001);
      bodyGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t0 + 0.022);
      body.connect(bodyGain);
      bodyGain.connect(ctx.destination);
      body.start(t0);
      body.stop(t0 + 0.03);
      live.push(body);
    });

    let stopped = false;
    return () => {
      if (stopped) return;
      stopped = true;
      // Stopping a source that has already finished is a no-op; stopping one that has not started
      // yet cancels it. Both are what we want, and neither throws — but a context torn down under
      // us would, so the whole sweep is guarded.
      try {
        const at = ctx.currentTime;
        for (const node of live) node.stop(at);
      } catch (e) {
        // Nodes already gone with their context. Nothing left to silence.
      }
    };
  } catch (e) {
    // Web Audio unavailable/blocked - fail silently like the rest of the audio layer
    return noop;
  }
};

/** Stylized, cartoon-soft "woof" for the pet dog - a noise attack plus a pitch-down sweep. */
export const playPetBark = (volume = 0.4) => {
  const ctx = sfxContext();
  if (!ctx) return;
  try {
    const now = ctx.currentTime;
    const duration = 0.15;

    const bufferSize = Math.floor(ctx.sampleRate * 0.04);
    const buffer = ctx.createBuffer(1, bufferSize, ctx.sampleRate);
    const data = buffer.getChannelData(0);
    for (let i = 0; i < bufferSize; i++) {
      data[i] = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * (1 - i / bufferSize);
    }
    const noise = ctx.createBufferSource();
    noise.buffer = buffer;
    const noiseFilter = ctx.createBiquadFilter();
    noiseFilter.type = 'bandpass';
    noiseFilter.frequency.value = 500;
    noiseFilter.Q.value = 1.2;
    const noiseGain = ctx.createGain();
    noiseGain.gain.setValueAtTime(volume * 0.5, now);
    noiseGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.001, now + 0.04);
    noise.connect(noiseFilter);
    noiseFilter.connect(noiseGain);
    noiseGain.connect(ctx.destination);
    noise.start(now);
    noise.stop(now + 0.04);

    const osc = ctx.createOscillator();
    osc.type = 'sawtooth';
    osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(520, now);
    osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(200, now + duration);
    const oscFilter = ctx.createBiquadFilter();
    oscFilter.type = 'bandpass';
```
