```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * One rule for what the mouse wheel does over this app, and one place to tune how far it goes.
 *
 * ## Why the app scrolls its own panels instead of letting the browser do it
 *
 * Chromium does not jump to the new offset on a wheel notch — it ANIMATES there over roughly a
 * tenth of a second, and no CSS property or browser setting turns that off for one element. On
 * top of a scene that already keeps the main thread busy, that animation is what reads as "the
 * list lags behind the wheel": the panel is still easing toward the previous notch's target when
 * the next one arrives. Writing `scrollTop` directly lands the whole distance on the event
 * itself, so the list is where the wheel left it before the next frame is painted.
 *
 * There is a second, structural reason. The wheel over a panel must NOT also reach
 * CameraController's window-level listener, which would zoom the island behind it. That listener
 * used to decide by walking the event's ancestors through `getComputedStyle` on every notch —
 * a style recalc per ancestor per event, on the same main thread the scroll is waiting for.
 * Claiming the event here, at `document`, settles it before that listener ever sees it.
 *
 * ## Where this runs
 *
 * {@link installDirectWheelScroll} registers ONE listener on `document`, in the bubble phase.
 * That placement is what makes it composable rather than a blunt override:
 *
 *   · Anything that wants different behaviour (the horizontal carousels' vertical-to-horizontal
 *     translation, see useWheelToHorizontalScroll) handles the event on its own node and calls
 *     `stopPropagation`, so the event never reaches us and its rule wins.
 *   · Anything we DO claim gets `stopPropagation` in turn, so it never reaches the window-level
 *     camera zoom. `document` is the last node before `window` in the bubble path, which is
 *     exactly the slot that lets one listener stand between the two.
 *
 * @see useScrollIsolation.ts — the per-node hooks, for panels that need their own multiplier.
 */

/**
 * How far one wheel notch scrolls, as a multiple of what the browser would have done with it.
 * 1 is "same distance, just without the animation"; below 1 the list moves less per notch, above
 * it more. This is THE sensitivity knob for the whole app — the only number to change if panels
 * scroll too far or not far enough per notch.
 *
 * Deliberately BELOW 1. The panels this moves are catalogues people read item by item, not pages
 * they skim: a shop card is most of a grid row, so a notch that covers a whole card leaves no
 * resting position between "this row" and "the next", and a short list reaches its bottom in one
 * flick of the wheel. A fraction of a card per notch is what makes the list stoppable on the item
 * someone is actually aiming for. Landing the distance instantly (see the module comment) is what
 * keeps the smaller step from reading as sluggish — less distance, still no lag behind the wheel.
 */
export const WHEEL_SCROLL_MULTIPLIER = 0.85;

/**
 * The same knob for the horizontal carousels — shop sub-category tabs, build-mode tiles — which
 * translate a vertical wheel into `scrollLeft`. Its own number, and a touch lower: those items
 * are narrow, so one notch at 1:1 sweeps past several of them and the strip overshoots the tab
 * that was being aimed at.
 */
export const WHEEL_HORIZONTAL_SCROLL_MULTIPLIER = 0.8;

/**
 * Deltas at or above this are treated as discrete wheel notches and get the multiplier; anything
 * finer is a trackpad's continuous scroll and is passed through at 1:1.
 *
 * A mouse wheel reports one notch as a whole ~100px (120 on some drivers) step, so amplifying it
 * is a real sensitivity gain. A trackpad reports the pixels your fingers actually moved, and
 * amplifying THOSE means the panel no longer tracks the fingers — the gesture overshoots. One
 * multiplier applied to both is what makes a knob that suits one device feel broken on the other.
 */
const NOTCH_THRESHOLD_PX = 40;

/** Wheel events measured in lines rather than pixels (deltaMode 1) — assume a 16px line. */
const WHEEL_LINE_PX = 16;

/**
 * Converts one wheel event's `deltaY` into a pixel distance, in the units `scrollTop` wants.
 *
 * Shared with the per-node hooks so the app has exactly one answer to "how far is one notch",
 * rather than a constant that panels re-derive and drift apart on.
 */
export function wheelDeltaToPixels(
  e: WheelEvent,
  element: HTMLElement,
  multiplier: number = WHEEL_SCROLL_MULTIPLIER,
  /** Page size for deltaMode 2 ("pages") — the visible extent of the axis being scrolled. */
  pageSizePx: number = element.clientHeight,
): number {
  const unit = e.deltaMode === 1 ? WHEEL_LINE_PX : e.deltaMode === 2 ? pageSizePx : 1;
  const px = e.deltaY * unit;
  return Math.abs(px) >= NOTCH_THRESHOLD_PX ? px * multiplier : px;
}

/** Applies one wheel event to an element's `scrollTop`, clamped to its range. */
export function applyWheelScroll(
  e: WheelEvent,
  element: HTMLElement,
  multiplier: number = WHEEL_SCROLL_MULTIPLIER,
): void {
  const max = element.scrollHeight - element.clientHeight;
  element.scrollTop = Math.max(0, Math.min(max, element.scrollTop + wheelDeltaToPixels(e, element, multiplier)));
}

/**
 * Applies one wheel event's vertical delta to an element's `scrollLeft`, clamped to its range —
 * for the horizontal carousels, where a vertical wheel is the only way through the strip on a
 * mouse. Clamping here, rather than letting a running `scrollLeft +=` saturate on its own, keeps
 * the end of the strip from banking a burst of notches that then have to be unwound.
 */
export function applyHorizontalWheelScroll(
  e: WheelEvent,
  element: HTMLElement,
  multiplier: number = WHEEL_HORIZONTAL_SCROLL_MULTIPLIER,
): void {
  const max = element.scrollWidth - element.clientWidth;
  const px = wheelDeltaToPixels(e, element, multiplier, element.clientWidth);
  element.scrollLeft = Math.max(0, Math.min(max, element.scrollLeft + px));
}

/**
 * True when this element is the one a wheel over it should move: its own overflow makes it a
 * scroll container, and its content actually overflows.
 *
 * Deliberately decided from computed style rather than from class names. The class list is a
 * moving target (`overflow-y-auto`, `custom-scrollbar`, `custom-scrollbar-teal`, `no-scrollbar`,
 * panels that set `overflowY` inline...) and a check written against it silently stops covering
 * a panel the day someone styles one a new way; every one of those spellings resolves to the
 * same computed `overflow-y`, which is what actually decides whether the browser would scroll it.
 */
function isScrollContainer(el: HTMLElement): boolean {
  const overflowY = window.getComputedStyle(el).overflowY;
  if (overflowY !== 'auto' && overflowY !== 'scroll' && overflowY !== 'overlay') return false;
  // +1 for sub-pixel layout: a container whose content is the same height as its box reports a
  // scrollHeight a fraction larger on fractional-DPR displays, and would otherwise be claimed
  // here as scrollable and then never move.
  return el.scrollHeight > el.clientHeight + 1;
}

// The ancestor walk is cached for the length of a scroll burst. One walk costs a
// getComputedStyle per ancestor - each a forced style recalc - and a wheel spin delivers events
// far faster than the pointer moves between panels, so re-walking per event was paying that cost
// dozens of times over for an answer that had not changed.
const RESOLVE_CACHE_MS = 250;
let cachedFrom: Element | null = null;
let cachedScroller: HTMLElement | null = null;
let cachedAt = 0;

/**
 * The scroll container a wheel event over `from` belongs to, or null if the wheel should be left
 * to the browser (and, failing that, to the camera zoom).
 */
export function findWheelScrollTarget(from: EventTarget | null): HTMLElement | null {
  if (!(from instanceof Element)) return null;

  const now = performance.now();
  if (cachedFrom === from && now - cachedAt < RESOLVE_CACHE_MS) {
    cachedAt = now;
    // A cached scroller that has since been unmounted (a panel closed mid-scroll) must not be
    // written to - it would be a silent no-op that also swallows the event.
    if (!cachedScroller || cachedScroller.isConnected) return cachedScroller;
  }

  let node: HTMLElement | null = from instanceof HTMLElement ? from : from.parentElement;
  let found: HTMLElement | null = null;
  while (node && node !== document.body && node !== document.documentElement) {
    if (isScrollContainer(node)) {
      found = node;
      break;
    }
    node = node.parentElement;
  }

  cachedFrom = from;
  cachedScroller = found;
  cachedAt = now;
  return found;
}

/**
 * Registers the app-wide wheel handler. Call once, from the app root.
 *
 * Returns an unsubscribe function, so a caller that mounts and unmounts (React StrictMode runs
 * every effect twice in development) cannot leave two handlers stacked and scroll twice as far.
 */
export function installDirectWheelScroll(): () => void {
  const handleWheel = (e: WheelEvent) => {
    // ctrl+wheel is the browser's own page zoom, and a trackpad pinch on the way in. Never eat it.
    if (e.ctrlKey || e.defaultPrevented || e.deltaY === 0) return;

    const scroller = findWheelScrollTarget(e.target);
    if (!scroller) return;

    // Claimed even when the list is already at an end and the position cannot change: a panel
    // covering the screen must not let a tick from its last row through to the window-level
    // camera zoom, which would spin the island behind it.
    e.preventDefault();
    e.stopPropagation();
    applyWheelScroll(e, scroller);
  };

  // Bubble phase, on `document` — see the module comment for why this exact slot.
  document.addEventListener('wheel', handleWheel, { passive: false });
  return () => document.removeEventListener('wheel', handleWheel);
}
```

## src/lib/workoutCompletion.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 健身完成事件 — the seam between "somebody exercised" and "the game reacts to it".
 *
 * This module is the whole of §7/§8/§10. It knows nothing about rewards, inventories, items,
 * currencies, saves or screens, and it must stay that way: its only exports are a shape
 * ({@link WorkoutCompletion}, declared in constants/workoutRewards.ts), a way to announce one, and
 * a way to listen for one.
 *
 * ## The two sides, and why neither knows the other exists
 *
 *   目前 Prototype:      components/FitnessView.tsx → reportWorkoutCompletion() ─┐
 *                                                                                ├→ Reward Service
 *   未來 Fitness API:    (an adapter, see below)    → reportWorkoutCompletion() ─┘   (context/
 *                                                                                    useWorkoutRewards.ts)
 *
 * The prototype's contribution is ONE call at the moment its 結束 handler finishes — no reward
 * logic, no item ids, no inventory write, no popup. Replacing it with a real fitness service means
 * deleting that call and adding an adapter that makes the same one; the reward system is not
 * touched, and neither is this file.
 *
 * That is also why this is a bus rather than a direct function call into the reward hook. A direct
 * call would make FitnessView import the reward service, which is exactly the coupling the brief
 * forbids — and it would tie the grant to a component that unmounts the moment the player walks
 * back out to the island.
 *
 * ## Adapters (§9)
 *
 * When the external service arrives, its integration layer lives beside this file and does three
 * things: authenticate, translate the vendor's payload into a {@link WorkoutCompletion}, and call
 * {@link reportWorkoutCompletion}. Nothing else in the game learns the vendor's field names, so a
 * change to their response is a change to one adapter. {@link makeWorkoutCompletion} is the
 * translation helper: it fills in the id, the timestamp and the source so an adapter cannot forget
 * them, and it is the only place a workout id is minted.
 *
 * ## Delivery guarantees
 *
 * Fan-out to every subscriber, synchronously, and a listener that throws cannot stop the others —
 * a broken UI subscriber must never be able to prevent a grant. The last event is REPLAYED to a
 * subscriber that arrives late, for the same reason `subscribeLoginBonus` replays: the completion
 * can be published in the same tick the profile loads, and a listener mounted one tick later would
 * otherwise miss the only announcement it will ever get. Replay is safe precisely because the
 * consumer is idempotent on `workoutId` (see constants/workoutRewards.ts) — the bus is allowed to
 * deliver twice because being delivered twice is already survivable.
 */

import type { WorkoutCompletion, WorkoutSource } from '../constants/workoutRewards';

export type { WorkoutCompletion, WorkoutSource };

/** What an adapter provides. Everything the caller cannot be expected to invent is filled in below. */
export interface WorkoutCompletionInput {
  userId: string;
  workoutType: string;
  durationSeconds: number;
  repCount?: number;
  source: WorkoutSource;
  /** The service's own id, when there is one. Generated only when there is not — see below. */
  workoutId?: string;
  /** The service's own timestamp, when there is one. Defaults to now. */
  completedAt?: string;
}

/**
 * A fresh id for a completion that does not already have one.
 *
 * The prototype has no server and therefore no authoritative id, so one is minted here. An adapter
 * for a real service must pass that service's id through instead: the id is what makes a redelivery
 * recognisable as a redelivery, and an id invented on the client is fresh on every retry, which
 * would defeat the guard it exists to feed.
 */
function newWorkoutId(): string {
  if (typeof crypto !== 'undefined' && 'randomUUID' in crypto) return `wk-${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
  return `wk-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10)}`;
}

/** Builds a completion, filling in what the caller did not supply. */
export function makeWorkoutCompletion(input: WorkoutCompletionInput): WorkoutCompletion {
  return {
    workoutId: input.workoutId || newWorkoutId(),
    userId: input.userId,
    completedAt: input.completedAt ?? new Date().toISOString(),
    workoutType: input.workoutType,
    durationSeconds: Math.max(0, Math.round(input.durationSeconds)),
    ...(input.repCount === undefined ? {} : { repCount: Math.max(0, Math.round(input.repCount)) }),
    source: input.source,
  };
}

type Listener = (completion: WorkoutCompletion) => void;

const listeners = new Set<Listener>();

/**
 * The most recent announcement, kept for late subscribers.
 *
 * Never cleared on consumption. Clearing it would make "has this been handled" a property of the
 * bus, and it is not — it is a property of the SAVE (`processedIds`), which is the only copy that
 * survives a reload. A bus that tried to remember would be a second, weaker answer to the same
 * question, and the two would eventually disagree.
 */
let lastCompletion: WorkoutCompletion | null = null;

/**
 * Announces that a workout finished. The one entry point, for every source.
 *
 * Deliberately returns nothing. A publisher does not get to know whether a reward was granted,
 * because the moment it does, somebody writes `if (!granted) …` in a fitness screen and the reward
 * rules are back inside the UI.
 */
export function reportWorkoutCompletion(completion: WorkoutCompletion): void {
  lastCompletion = completion;
  for (const listener of [...listeners]) {
    try {
      listener(completion);
    } catch (error) {
      // One broken listener must not stop the next one — the reward service is a listener.
      console.error('[workout] 完成事件的訂閱者發生錯誤：', error);
    }
  }
}

/**
 * Subscribes to completions. Fires immediately with the last one, if there was one this session.
 *
 * See the module doc for why a replay is safe: the consumer de-duplicates on `workoutId`.
 */
export function subscribeWorkoutCompletion(listener: Listener): () => void {
  listeners.add(listener);
  if (lastCompletion) {
    try {
      listener(lastCompletion);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('[workout] 完成事件的訂閱者發生錯誤：', error);
    }
  }
  return () => {
    listeners.delete(listener);
  };
}

/** The last completion announced this session, or null. For 管理員測試 readouts. */
export function getLastWorkoutCompletion(): WorkoutCompletion | null {
  return lastCompletion;
}

/** Test-only: forgets the replay buffer so one script's events cannot leak into the next. */
export function resetWorkoutCompletionBus(): void {
  lastCompletion = null;
  listeners.clear();
}
```

## src/lib/worldSolids.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import type { SolidBox } from './furniturePlacement';

/**
 * TRANSIENT WORLD SOLIDS —— 世界裡擋得住玩家、但**不在任何人存檔裡**的東西。
 *
 * ## 為什麼需要第三種來源
 *
 * 這個遊戲原本只有兩種實體：玩家自己擺的東西（`islandPlacements` / `interiorData.placements`，
 * 走 lib/furniturePlacement.ts 的量測盒），以及玩家的家（走它自己的 House Style footprint）。
 * 兩者的共通點是**存在存檔裡**，所以碰撞的那一邊只要拿到 profile 就拿得到它們。
 *
 * 旅行商人的船兩者都不是：它因為「現在是這一檔」而存在，位置每一幀都在動，而且沒有任何一
 * 個玩家擁有它。它需要的不是一套新的碰撞邏輯（那正是要避免的），而是一個**把盒子送進既有
 * 碰撞流程的入口**。這個檔案就是那個入口，而且只有那個。
 *
 * \`\`\`
 *   MerchantVisitor（每幀寫自己那組盒子的世界座標）
 *          │ publishWorldSolids(sourceId, boxes)
 *          ▼
 *   worldSolids（這裡）—— 一份攤平的清單
 *          │ getWorldSolids()
 *          ▼
 *   Avatar → resolveCollisions → resolvePlayerAgainstSolids
 *                                （跟家具用的是同一個 pushOutOfBox）
 * \`\`\`
 *
 * ## 為什麼是登記制而不是 playerBus 上的一個欄位
 *
 * 一個欄位只有一個寫入者。同時來兩位商人（`MERCHANTS` 多一列就會發生）時，第二位會蓋掉第
 * 一位的盒子，而那個 bug 的症狀是「其中一艘船可以游過去」—— 沒有錯誤、沒有紅字，只有偶爾
 * 穿模。以來源為鍵登記，兩位商人各自寫自己那組，誰先誰後都不影響。
 *
 * ## 每幀零配置
 *
 * 攤平的那份清單裝的是**登記進來的那些物件本身**，不是複本。所以來源每幀就地改寫自己的盒
 * 子時，這裡看到的就已經是新值 —— `flat` 只有在來源加入或離開時才重建，也就是一檔期兩次。
 */

/** 每個來源自己那組盒子。來源每幀就地改寫它們，這裡只持有參考。 */
const sources = new Map<string, readonly SolidBox[]>();

/** 攤平後的清單。碰撞每幀讀它，所以它必須是穩定的同一顆物件。 */
let flat: readonly SolidBox[] = [];

const EMPTY: readonly SolidBox[] = [];

function rebuild(): void {
  if (sources.size === 0) {
    flat = EMPTY;
    return;
  }
  const next: SolidBox[] = [];
  for (const boxes of sources.values()) next.push(...boxes);
  flat = next;
}

/**
 * 登記（或撤銷）一個來源的碰撞盒。
 *
 * 傳 `null` 撤銷 —— 船開走之後它的盒子必須跟著走，否則海上會留下一塊游不過去的水，而那正
 * 是「Boat Mesh 已經移動，但 Collider 留在原地」那個失敗最惡劣的版本：看不見的牆。
 *
 * 只在**集合改變**時才重建攤平清單。同一組盒子重複登記是無操作，所以呼叫端可以在每幀無腦
 * 呼叫而不必自己記得有沒有登記過。
 */
export function publishWorldSolids(sourceId: string, boxes: readonly SolidBox[] | null): void {
  if (!boxes) {
    if (sources.delete(sourceId)) rebuild();
    return;
  }
  if (sources.get(sourceId) === boxes) return;
  sources.set(sourceId, boxes);
  rebuild();
}

/**
 * 現在世界上所有的暫時性實體。
 *
 * 回傳的是同一顆穩定的陣列（見上），所以每幀呼叫不會配置任何東西。空的時候回傳共用的空陣
 * 列，因此「島上沒有商人」那段期間，碰撞多付的成本是一次 `for` 迴圈的零次迭代。
 */
export function getWorldSolids(): readonly SolidBox[] {
  return flat;
}

/** 測試與場景卸載用。 */
export function clearWorldSolids(): void {
  if (sources.size === 0) return;
  sources.clear();
  rebuild();
}
```

## src/lib/youtubeMusic.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * Real YouTube / YouTube Music playback, via the official IFrame Player API.
 *
 * Why an iframe and not an API client: YouTube Music has NO public API, and
 * `music.youtube.com` sends X-Frame-Options, so it cannot be embedded or read
 * directly. What IS official and free is the IFrame Player API, which plays any
 * public video or playlist without an API key. YouTube Music shares its IDs with
 * YouTube - the `PL...`/`OLAK5uy_...` in a music.youtube.com playlist link is
 * the same list ID youtube.com uses - so pasting a YT Music link and handing the
 * extracted ID to this player genuinely plays that music. The exceptions are
 * Premium-exclusive tracks and personal uploads, which no embed can reach; those
 * surface as an onError below rather than failing silently.
 *
 * This module owns exactly one player instance for the whole app, INCLUDING the
 * DOM element it lives in, so that music keeps playing while the user moves
 * between views. React reads its state through `subscribe`/`getSnapshot`
 * (useSyncExternalStore) and positions the player with `setYtmSlot`, but never
 * creates, re-parents or destroys it - see "The host element" below for why.
 *
 * This is a TRANSPORT, not a policy layer: it knows how to play what it is told
 * to play, and nothing about the built-in synth BGM or about which source the
 * app currently wants. That decision lives in one place, lib/backgroundMusic.ts,
 * which is the only module that should be driving the functions below.
 */

export interface YouTubeMusicRef {
  videoId?: string;
  playlistId?: string;
}

/**
 * `cued` is its own state rather than a flavour of `paused`: it means "loaded on
 * purpose without starting", which is what a restore-after-reload does (there is
 * no user gesture on a fresh page, so starting there would be blocked by the
 * browser). The manager waits for the first gesture and then plays it.
 */
export type YtmStatus = 'idle' | 'loading' | 'cued' | 'playing' | 'paused' | 'ended' | 'error';

export interface YtmSnapshot {
  /** The IFrame API script has loaded and the player object exists. */
  ready: boolean;
  status: YtmStatus;
  /** Video title reported by the player, '' until it starts loading one. */
  title: string;
  author: string;
  videoId: string | null;
  playlistId: string | null;
  /** Human-readable failure, already localised. Null when fine. */
  error: string | null;
  /** True once something has been loaded - drives whether the mini bar shows. */
  hasQueue: boolean;
  /** True when the queue is a playlist, so prev/next are meaningful. */
  isPlaylist: boolean;
  /**
   * The PLAYER's own mute flag, which is independent of both the app's mute
   * setting and of `playerVolume`. Surfaced because a muted player is the one
   * failure that looks like success: the video plays, the picture moves, and
   * nothing anywhere reports an error - there is just no sound.
   */
  playerMuted: boolean;
  /** The player's own 0-100 volume, as read back from YouTube (not what we requested). */
  playerVolume: number;
}

/**
 * A YouTube video ID is exactly 11 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-]. Anchored so that a
 * pasted URL never matches this branch by accident - URLs go through the parser.
 */
const VIDEO_ID_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{11}$/;

/**
 * Playlist IDs YouTube actually issues: user/created lists (PL, FL), album
 * "release" lists that YT Music links use (OLAK5uy_), auto-generated channel
 * lists (UU, LL), and radio/mix lists (RD). RD mixes are accepted because the
 * link is valid, but they very often refuse to embed - the error path below
 * explains that rather than leaving the user staring at a dead player.
 */
const PLAYLIST_ID_RE = /^(PL|FL|UU|LL|RD|OLAK5uy_)[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/;

/**
 * Pull the video and/or playlist ID out of anything a user is likely to paste:
 * a YouTube Music link, a normal YouTube link, a youtu.be share link, a Shorts
 * link, or a bare ID. Returns null when nothing usable is in there.
 */
export function parseYouTubeMusicInput(raw: string): YouTubeMusicRef | null {
  const input = raw.trim();
  if (!input) return null;

  // Bare IDs, before any URL parsing - these are not URLs at all.
  if (VIDEO_ID_RE.test(input)) return { videoId: input };
  if (PLAYLIST_ID_RE.test(input)) return { playlistId: input };

  let url: URL;
  try {
    // Accept links pasted without a scheme ("music.youtube.com/..."), which is
    // what you get from some share sheets and from retyping a link by hand.
    url = new URL(/^https?:\/\//i.test(input) ? input : `https://${input}`);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }

  const host = url.hostname.replace(/^www\./, '').toLowerCase();
  const isYouTubeHost =
    host === 'youtube.com' ||
    host === 'm.youtube.com' ||
    host === 'music.youtube.com' ||
    host === 'youtube-nocookie.com' ||
    host === 'youtu.be';
  if (!isYouTubeHost) return null;

  const ref: YouTubeMusicRef = {};

  const list = url.searchParams.get('list');
  if (list && PLAYLIST_ID_RE.test(list)) ref.playlistId = list;

  if (host === 'youtu.be') {
    // youtu.be/<id>
    const id = url.pathname.slice(1).split('/')[0];
    if (VIDEO_ID_RE.test(id)) ref.videoId = id;
  } else {
    const v = url.searchParams.get('v');
    if (v && VIDEO_ID_RE.test(v)) {
      ref.videoId = v;
    } else {
      // /shorts/<id>, /embed/<id>, /live/<id>
      const m = url.pathname.match(/^\/(?:shorts|embed|live|v)\/([A-Za-z0-9_-]{11})/);
      if (m) ref.videoId = m[1];
    }
  }

  if (!ref.videoId && !ref.playlistId) return null;
  return ref;
}

/**
 * True when the input looks like something `parseYouTubeMusicInput` can resolve
 * - i.e. a link or a bare ID rather than a song name.
 *
 * Used to decide whether pressing 播放 should search or play directly, so one box
 * serves both. Kept as its own predicate (instead of just null-checking the
 * parser) because "this is a link that I could not parse" and "this is a song
 * title" need different handling: the first is a broken link worth an error, the
 * second is a perfectly normal search.
 */
export function looksLikeYouTubeRef(raw: string): boolean {
  const input = raw.trim();
  if (!input) return false;
  if (VIDEO_ID_RE.test(input) || PLAYLIST_ID_RE.test(input)) return true;
  return /^(https?:\/\/)?(www\.|m\.|music\.)?(youtube(-nocookie)?\.com|youtu\.be)\//i.test(input);
}

export interface YouTubeSearchResult {
  videoId: string;
  title: string;
  channel: string;
  thumbnail: string;
}

/**
 * Search YouTube by song name, through this app's own server.
 *
 * The request cannot go straight to the Data API from here: it needs an API key,
 * and a key in the browser bundle is a key anyone can take. See the
 * /api/youtube/search route in server.ts for the rest of the reasoning (and for
 * why the results are pre-filtered to embeddable videos).
 */
export async function searchYouTubeMusic(query: string): Promise<YouTubeSearchResult[]> {
  const res = await fetch(`/api/youtube/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query.trim())}`);
  let payload: any = null;
  try {
    payload = await res.json();
  } catch {
    // A non-JSON body here means the dev server isn't running the API route at
    // all (e.g. the static build opened directly), which needs a clearer message
    // than "Unexpected token <".
    throw new Error('搜尋服務沒有回應,請確認伺服器是否啟動 (npm run dev)。');
  }
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(payload?.error || 'YouTube 搜尋失敗。');
  return (payload?.results ?? []) as YouTubeSearchResult[];
}

/** A stable, human-readable label for a parsed reference (used before the player reports a title). */
export function describeRef(ref: YouTubeMusicRef): string {
  if (ref.playlistId) return `播放清單 ${ref.playlistId.slice(0, 12)}…`;
  return `影片 ${ref.videoId}`;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *
 * IFrame API loading
 * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

declare global {
  interface Window {
    YT?: any;
    onYouTubeIframeAPIReady?: () => void;
  }
}

const IFRAME_API_SRC = 'https://www.youtube.com/iframe_api';
let apiPromise: Promise<any> | null = null;

function loadIframeApi(): Promise<any> {
  if (apiPromise) return apiPromise;

  apiPromise = new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    if (window.YT?.Player) {
      resolve(window.YT);
      return;
    }

    // Network blocks (offline, extension, corporate filter) never fire the hook
    // at all, so without this the UI would sit on "loading" forever. Cleared on
    // both settle paths: a live 15s timer that outlives a successful load keeps
    // the whole promise chain (and this closure) alive for no reason, and on a
    // slow connection it used to fire AFTER the script arrived - harmless to the
    // already-resolved promise, but it left `apiPromise` nulled out in the catch
    // below, so the next caller re-entered the whole load path from scratch.
    // 25s, not 15: a cold cache on a slow connection genuinely takes that long,
    // and a premature reject surfaced "無法載入 YouTube 播放器" over a script that
    // was still on its way. (It recovers - the next reconcile re-enters this
    // function and finds window.YT already there - but the user has seen an
    // error for something that was not broken.) This is a bound on hanging, not
    // a retry: what it protects against is an ad blocker or a firewall, where
    // the hook never fires at all.
    const timeout = window.setTimeout(() => reject(new Error('iframe_api_timeout')), 25000);

    // The API calls exactly one global hook when it finishes. Chain rather than
    // overwrite, so this stays safe if anything else ever loads the same script.
    const prevHook = window.onYouTubeIframeAPIReady;
    window.onYouTubeIframeAPIReady = () => {
      prevHook?.();
      clearTimeout(timeout);
      resolve(window.YT);
    };

    if (!document.querySelector(`script[src="${IFRAME_API_SRC}"]`)) {
      const script = document.createElement('script');
      script.src = IFRAME_API_SRC;
      script.async = true;
      script.onerror = () => {
        clearTimeout(timeout);
        reject(new Error('iframe_api_blocked'));
      };
      document.head.appendChild(script);
    }
  }).catch((err) => {
    apiPromise = null; // allow a later retry
    throw err;
  });

  return apiPromise;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *
 * Controller
 * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

const listeners = new Set<() => void>();

let snapshot: YtmSnapshot = {
  ready: false,
  status: 'idle',
  title: '',
  author: '',
  videoId: null,
  playlistId: null,
  error: null,
  hasQueue: false,
  isPlaylist: false,
  playerMuted: false,
  playerVolume: 0,
};

function emit(patch: Partial<YtmSnapshot>) {
  // Replaced wholesale (never mutated) because useSyncExternalStore compares
  // snapshots by identity.
  snapshot = { ...snapshot, ...patch };
  listeners.forEach((l) => l());
}

export function subscribeYtm(listener: () => void): () => void {
  listeners.add(listener);
  return () => listeners.delete(listener);
}

export function getYtmSnapshot(): YtmSnapshot {
  return snapshot;
}

let player: any = null;
/**
 * Set for the whole of the async creation window (script fetch included), so a
 * second call cannot start building a second player while the first is still in
 * flight. This is not a micro-optimisation: React StrictMode runs every effect
 * twice, and the old `if (player) return` guard tested a variable that is only
 * assigned at the END of that window - so both passes sailed through, appended
 * their own div, and left TWO live iframes fighting over the same music with
 * only the second one reachable from `player`. That is the "it plays, then it
 * breaks" report.
 */
let creating = false;
/** Command to run the moment onReady fires, for anything requested before that. */
let pendingCommand: { ref: YouTubeMusicRef; start: boolean } | null = null;
/**
 * Whether a CUED state should be nudged into playing. False for a deliberate cue
 * (see the `cued` status), true for every ordinary load.
 */
let autoStart = true;
let desiredVolume = 0.5;
let titlePoll: number | null = null;

/**
 * Every call into the YouTube player goes through here.
 *
 * The IFrame API object is a facade over postMessage: its methods only exist
 * once the iframe has handshaked, and they throw (or silently vanish) if the
 * iframe is navigating, blocked, or gone. Calling a method that "obviously"
 * exists is the single most common way this integration used to throw
 * `player.loadVideoById is not a function` up into React and take the screen
 * out with it. One guarded call site means that can no longer happen anywhere.
 */
function call<T = unknown>(method: string, ...args: unknown[]): T | undefined {
  const p = player;
  if (!p || typeof p[method] !== 'function') return undefined;
  try {
    return p[method](...args) as T;
  } catch {
    return undefined;
  }
}

/**
 * Force the player's audio on.
 *
 * `setVolume` alone is NOT enough: the player carries its own mute flag, and a
 * muted player ignores its volume completely. YouTube raises that flag itself
 * when the browser refuses autoplay-with-sound - it falls back to starting
 * MUTED so playback can begin at all. The result looks entirely healthy (the
 * picture moves, no error is reported anywhere) and is silent. Every path that
 * can start playback therefore goes through here.
 *
 * WITH ONE EXCEPTION, and it is the whole point of the exception existing: at `desiredVolume` 0
 * the app has said silence (muted, or the music slider at zero - lib/backgroundMusic.ts's
 * `isSilenced` pushes both here the same way), and lifting the player's mute flag then is how a
 * muted game gets a burst of music out of a player that was about to start anyway. There is
 * exactly one thing to force in that state, which is the volume, downward.
 */
function forceAudioOn(): void {
  if (desiredVolume <= 0) {
    call('setVolume', 0);
    return;
  }
  call('unMute');
  call('setVolume', Math.round(desiredVolume * 100));
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *
 * The host element
 * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

/**
 * THE IFRAME IS NOT REACT'S TO OWN.
 *
 * It used to be: the player was created into a div rendered by the Settings
 * panel and destroyed in that component's unmount cleanup. Both halves of that
 * are wrong for something whose entire job is to outlive the screen you started
 * it from:
 *
 *   - closing Settings destroyed the player, which is why the music stopped;
 *   - re-opening it built a NEW player, so every visit paid the load cost again
 *     and raced the previous teardown;
 *   - and an iframe cannot be re-parented as a fix - moving an iframe in the DOM
 *     reloads its document, which stops the music just as dead.
 *
 * So the host is created once, parented to <body>, and never removed. React
 * tells it WHERE to be (`setYtmSlot`) and never anything about whether to exist.
 */

/**
 * Where the player sits when no UI is showing it. Deliberately off-screen rather
 * than `display:none` / `visibility:hidden` / zero-size: a hidden iframe is
 * throttled by the browser and YouTube's API refuses to begin playback in one,
 * whereas an element that is merely outside the viewport keeps playing normally.
 * A negative left (never a bottom/right overflow) so parking can never produce a
 * stray scrollbar.
 */
const PARKED_LEFT = -10000;

let hostEl: HTMLDivElement | null = null;
let slotEl: HTMLElement | null = null;
let placementRaf: number | null = null;

function ensureHost(): HTMLDivElement {
  if (hostEl) return hostEl;
  const el = document.createElement('div');
  el.id = 'ytm-player-host';
  Object.assign(el.style, {
    position: 'fixed',
    left: `${PARKED_LEFT}px`,
    top: '0px',
    width: '320px',
    height: '180px',
    overflow: 'hidden',
    background: '#000',
    // Sits between the Settings surface (z-40, see index.css's layer table) and
    // its own close button (z-50). It is only ever on-screen while Settings is
    // open, which is the one screen that renders a slot for it.
    zIndex: '45',
    pointerEvents: 'none',
  });
  document.body.appendChild(el);
  hostEl = el;
  return el;
}

function parkHost(): void {
  if (!hostEl) return;
  hostEl.style.left = `${PARKED_LEFT}px`;
  hostEl.style.top = '0px';
  hostEl.style.width = '320px';
  hostEl.style.height = '180px';
  hostEl.style.opacity = '1';
  hostEl.style.pointerEvents = 'none';
}

/**
 * The slot's opacity as actually rendered, ancestors included.
 *
 * The host is a child of <body>, so it inherits none of the fades its slot sits
 * inside - and the screen it sits inside animates in and out. Without this, the
 * video stayed fully opaque over a Settings panel that was fading away, then
 * vanished in one frame when the component finally unmounted.
 */
function effectiveOpacity(el: HTMLElement): number {
  let opacity = 1;
  let node: HTMLElement | null = el;
  while (node && node !== document.body) {
    const own = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(node).opacity);
    if (!Number.isNaN(own)) opacity *= own;
    if (opacity <= 0.01) return 0;
    node = node.parentElement;
  }
  return opacity;
}

function applyPlacement(): void {
  if (!hostEl) return;
  const slot = slotEl;
  if (!slot || !slot.isConnected) {
    parkHost();
    return;
  }
  const rect = slot.getBoundingClientRect();
  if (rect.width < 1 || rect.height < 1) {
    parkHost();
    return;
  }
  hostEl.style.left = `${rect.left}px`;
  hostEl.style.top = `${rect.top}px`;
  hostEl.style.width = `${rect.width}px`;
  hostEl.style.height = `${rect.height}px`;
  hostEl.style.borderRadius = getComputedStyle(slot).borderRadius;
  // Never `visibility`/`display` - see PARKED_LEFT. A fully transparent player
  // still plays; a hidden one is suspended.
  hostEl.style.opacity = `${effectiveOpacity(slot)}`;
  hostEl.style.pointerEvents = 'auto';
}

/**
 * Tracked per frame rather than with a ResizeObserver plus scroll/resize
 * listeners, because the slot is inside a scroll container that also runs an
 * entry animation (motion's scale) - none of those events fire during a
 * transform tween, and the alternative is a video that lags a moving panel. One
 * getBoundingClientRect a frame, only while Settings is open, is not a cost
 * worth optimising against that.
 */
function startPlacementLoop(): void {
  if (placementRaf !== null) return;
  const step = () => {
    applyPlacement();
    placementRaf = requestAnimationFrame(step);
  };
  placementRaf = requestAnimationFrame(step);
}

function stopPlacementLoop(): void {
  if (placementRaf !== null) {
    cancelAnimationFrame(placementRaf);
    placementRaf = null;
  }
}

/**
 * Show the player inside `el` (a plain, empty div rendered wherever the UI wants
 * the video to appear), or park it off-screen when passed null.
 *
 * This is the ONLY thing the UI is allowed to say about the player's existence:
 * unmounting the screen that called this stops showing the video, and does not
 * stop the music.
 */
export function setYtmSlot(el: HTMLElement | null): void {
  slotEl = el;
  ensureHost();
  if (el) {
    applyPlacement();
    startPlacementLoop();
  } else {
    stopPlacementLoop();
    parkHost();
  }
}

function errorMessage(code: number): string {
  switch (code) {
    case 2:
      return '這個連結的 ID 無效,請確認後再貼一次。';
    case 5:
      return '這個項目無法在網頁播放器中播放。';
    case 100:
      return '找不到這個影片/清單,可能已被刪除或設為私人。';
    case 101:
    case 150:
      return '這個項目的擁有者不允許嵌入播放。YouTube Music 的「自動混音」與 Premium 專屬曲目通常屬於此類,請改用一般的播放清單連結。';
    default:
      return '播放失敗,請換一個連結試試。';
  }
}

/**
 * Poll the title, because the API has no "metadata changed" event for playlist
 * advances - and poll the player's own mute/volume alongside it, so a silently
 * muted player is visible in the UI instead of having to be guessed at.
 */
function startTitlePoll() {
  if (titlePoll !== null) return;
  titlePoll = window.setInterval(() => {
    const data = call<any>('getVideoData');
    if (data?.title && data.title !== snapshot.title) {
      emit({ title: data.title, author: data.author || '', videoId: data.video_id || snapshot.videoId });
    }
    const muted = !!call<boolean>('isMuted');
    const vol = call<number>('getVolume') ?? 0;
    if (muted !== snapshot.playerMuted || vol !== snapshot.playerVolume) {
      emit({ playerMuted: muted, playerVolume: vol });
    }
  }, 1000);
}

function stopTitlePoll() {
  if (titlePoll !== null) {
    clearInterval(titlePoll);
    titlePoll = null;
  }
}

/**
 * Bring the one player into existence. Idempotent, re-entrant-safe, and cheap to
 * call from anywhere - including on app start, which is the point: a player that
 * already exists can be handed a video INSIDE the click that asked for it, and
 * browsers only allow sound to start from a real user gesture. Creating it on
 * demand instead meant the click had long finished by the time the async chain
 * (fetch iframe_api -> new YT.Player -> onReady -> load) reached playback, and
 * the browser blocked it.
 */
export function ensureYtmPlayer(): void {
  if (player || creating) return;
  creating = true;

  const host = ensureHost();

  loadIframeApi().then(
    (YT: any) => {
      // A destroy/park can't null this out any more, but keep the check: it also
      // covers a second createPlayer that slipped in while the script loaded.
      if (player) {
        creating = false;
        return;
      }

      // YT.Player REPLACES the element it is given with the generated iframe, so
      // give it a throwaway child of our host rather than the host itself - the
      // host must survive to be re-positioned.
      const target = document.createElement('div');
      host.appendChild(target);

      player = new YT.Player(target, {
        height: '100%',
        width: '100%',
        playerVars: {
          autoplay: 0,
          controls: 1,
          playsinline: 1,
          rel: 0,
          modestbranding: 1,
          // Required for the postMessage handshake to be accepted; without it
          // some browsers drop every command silently.
          enablejsapi: 1,
          origin: window.location.origin,
        },
        events: {
          onReady: () => {
            forceAudioOn();
            emit({ ready: true });
            const queued = pendingCommand;
            pendingCommand = null;
            if (queued) applyQueue(queued.ref, queued.start);
          },
          onStateChange: (e: any) => {
            const S = window.YT?.PlayerState;
            if (!S) return;
            switch (e.data) {
              case S.PLAYING: {
                // Playback beginning is the exact moment YouTube's
                // autoplay-fallback mute would be in force, so lift it here too -
                // onReady fires long before this and cannot know.
                forceAudioOn();
                const data = call<any>('getVideoData');
                emit({
                  status: 'playing',
                  error: null,
                  title: data?.title || snapshot.title,
                  author: data?.author || snapshot.author,
                  videoId: data?.video_id || snapshot.videoId,
                });
                startTitlePoll();
                break;
              }
              case S.PAUSED:
                emit({ status: 'paused' });
                break;
              case S.BUFFERING:
                // NOT reported as 'loading' any more. Buffering is a normal blip
                // in the middle of a track (and fires on every playlist advance),
                // and while the built-in BGM was gated on "is YouTube playing
                // right now", every one of those blips let the synth music start
                // up underneath - which is the reported "both play at once".
                // Source ownership is now declared, not inferred from this event.
                break;
              case S.CUED:
                // stopVideo() also parks the player in CUED, so an empty queue
                // here means "we just stopped", not "something is waiting to
                // play" - reporting it as cued would leave a stopped player
                // claiming to be ready to go.
                if (!snapshot.hasQueue) break;
                // The item is ready but nothing started it. That is correct after
                // a deliberate cue (restore-on-reload), and a dropped play
                // otherwise - the state that looks like "the app is broken, there
                // is no sound". Nudge it only in the second case.
                // ...and not while the app is silenced: a dropped play is only worth nudging
                // if the result is meant to be audible. Reported as `cued` instead, which is the
                // honest answer (loaded, not started) and the state the manager already knows how
                // to resume from once the sound comes back.
                if (autoStart && desiredVolume > 0) {
                  forceAudioOn();
                  call('playVideo');
                } else {
                  emit({ status: 'cued' });
                }
                break;
              case S.ENDED:
                // Background music does not stop after one song. A playlist that
                // reaches its end restarts at the top; a single video repeats.
                // (Leaving it ended was also a second way the synth BGM could
                // come back in over a YouTube session that was merely finished.)
                //
                // Unless the app is silenced, and this is the case that made a muted game start
                // playing music by itself: whatever the manager paused at the mute, a track that
                // was ALREADY running kept running until it ended - and then this restarted it,
                // unprompted, minutes into a mute. Report it as paused instead; the manager
                // resumes it on unmute exactly like the one it paused itself.
                if (desiredVolume <= 0) {
                  call('pauseVideo');
                  emit({ status: 'paused' });
                  break;
                }
                if (snapshot.isPlaylist) {
                  call('playVideoAt', 0);
                } else {
                  call('seekTo', 0, true);
                  call('playVideo');
                }
                break;
              default:
                break;
            }
          },
          onError: (e: any) => {
            emit({ status: 'error', error: errorMessage(e?.data) });
            stopTitlePoll();
          },
        },
      });
      creating = false;
    },
    () => {
      creating = false;
      emit({
        status: 'error',
        error: '無法載入 YouTube 播放器,請確認網路連線或廣告封鎖器設定。',
      });
    },
  );
}

/** The actual API calls behind loadYtm/cueYtm, once the player is known ready. */
function applyQueue(ref: YouTubeMusicRef, start: boolean): void {
  autoStart = start;
  forceAudioOn();

  // LOAD, not cue, for the ordinary path.
  //
  // An earlier version cued and then called playVideo() immediately, on the
  // theory that a self-starting load was being muted by the browser. Driving a
  // real Edge over the DevTools protocol disproved that: a player that starts on
  // its own reports muted=false, volume=100. What the cue path DID produce was a
  // player parked in state 5 (cued, never started), because playVideo() issued in
  // the same tick as the cue is dropped before cueing settles. load* starts by
  // itself and needs no such timing.
  if (ref.playlistId) {
    // Playlist wins when a link carries both (a YT Music "watch?v=X&list=Y").
    // Chaining a video load after the playlist to start on X does NOT work - it
    // tears the queue back down to a single video, losing prev/next - and the API
    // offers no way to look up X's index without the list contents. Starting at
    // the top keeps the whole playlist intact, which is the point of the link.
    const args = { list: ref.playlistId, listType: 'playlist', index: 0 };
    call(start ? 'loadPlaylist' : 'cuePlaylist', args);
  } else if (ref.videoId) {
    call(start ? 'loadVideoById' : 'cueVideoById', ref.videoId);
  }

  // Loading resets the player, so the unmute above does not survive it.
  forceAudioOn();
}

function queue(ref: YouTubeMusicRef, start: boolean): void {
  emit({
    status: start ? 'loading' : 'cued',
    error: null,
    hasQueue: true,
    title: '',
    author: '',
    videoId: ref.videoId ?? null,
    playlistId: ref.playlistId ?? null,
    isPlaylist: !!ref.playlistId,
  });

  // Safe from any state: if the player is still being built, the command waits
  // for onReady instead of being fired at a half-built facade and lost.
  ensureYtmPlayer();
  if (!player || !snapshot.ready) {
    pendingCommand = { ref, start };
    autoStart = start;
    return;
  }
  applyQueue(ref, start);
}

/** Queue a video and/or playlist and start it. */
export function loadYtm(ref: YouTubeMusicRef): void {
  queue(ref, true);
}

/**
 * Queue without starting - for restoring the last-played link on a fresh page,
 * where there is no user gesture yet and a play attempt would be blocked (or,
 * worse, silently demoted to muted playback).
 */
export function cueYtm(ref: YouTubeMusicRef): void {
  queue(ref, false);
}

export function playYtm(): void {
  autoStart = true;
  forceAudioOn();
  call('playVideo');
}

/** Manual escape hatch for the UI's "解除靜音" button. */
export function unmuteYtm(): void {
  forceAudioOn();
}

export function pauseYtm(): void {
  autoStart = false;
  call('pauseVideo');
}

export function nextYtm(): void {
  call('nextVideo');
}

export function prevYtm(): void {
  call('previousVideo');
}

/**
 * Stop and clear the queue. The player itself stays alive and stays where it is:
 * it holds no audio once stopped, and keeping it means the next 播放 press starts
 * inside its own click instead of behind another script load.
 */
export function stopYtm(): void {
  autoStart = false;
  pendingCommand = null;
  call('stopVideo');
  stopTitlePoll();
  emit({ status: 'idle', hasQueue: false, title: '', author: '', videoId: null, playlistId: null, error: null });
}

/** volume is 0..1, matching the app's own `bgmVolume`. */
export function setYtmVolume(volume: number): void {
  desiredVolume = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, volume));
  // Raising the slider off zero has to lift the player's own mute as well, or
  // the slider appears to do nothing on a player YouTube muted behind our back.
  if (desiredVolume > 0) forceAudioOn();
  else call('setVolume', 0);
}
```

## src/main.tsx

```tsx
import {StrictMode, Component, ErrorInfo, ReactNode} from 'react';
import {createRoot} from 'react-dom/client';
import App from './App.tsx';
import './index.css';
import { installGlobalInputGuards } from './lib/inputManager';

// Installed before the first render so EVERY screen is covered from the very first frame - the
// loading screen and auth screen included, not just the game views. See inputManager.ts: this is
// the one and only place the browser's native right-click menu is suppressed, and the one place
// that watches for the browser tearing a pointer gesture down behind our back.
installGlobalInputGuards();

interface ErrorBoundaryProps {
  children: ReactNode;
}

interface ErrorBoundaryState {
  hasError: boolean;
  error: Error | null;
  errorInfo: ErrorInfo | null;
}

class ErrorBoundary extends Component<ErrorBoundaryProps, ErrorBoundaryState> {
  public state: ErrorBoundaryState = {
    hasError: false,
    error: null,
    errorInfo: null
  };

  public static getDerivedStateFromError(error: Error): ErrorBoundaryState {
    return { hasError: true, error, errorInfo: null };
  }

  public componentDidCatch(error: Error, errorInfo: ErrorInfo) {
    console.error("Uncaught error at ErrorBoundary:", error, errorInfo);
    this.setState({ errorInfo });
  }

  public render() {
    if (this.state.hasError) {
      return (
        <div style={{
          padding: '2rem',
          backgroundColor: '#fef2f2',
          color: '#991b1b',
          fontFamily: 'monospace',
          whiteSpace: 'pre-wrap',
          fontSize: '14px',
          border: '4px solid #f87171',
          margin: '1rem',
          borderRadius: '8px',
          overflow: 'auto',
          maxHeight: '90vh'
        }}>
          <h2 style={{ margin: '0 0 1rem 0', fontSize: '18px', fontWeight: 'bold' }}>
            🚨 Application Runtime Error Detected
          </h2>
          <p style={{ fontWeight: 'bold' }}>Error Message:</p>
          <pre style={{ margin: '0 0 1.5rem 0', background: '#fee2e2', padding: '1rem', borderRadius: '4px' }}>
            {this.state.error?.toString()}
          </pre>
          {this.state.error && (
            <>
              <p style={{ fontWeight: 'bold' }}>Stack Trace:</p>
              <pre style={{ margin: '0 0 1.5rem 0', background: '#fee2e2', padding: '1rem', borderRadius: '4px', overflowX: 'auto' }}>
                {this.state.error.stack}
              </pre>
            </>
          )}
          {this.state.errorInfo && (
            <>
              <p style={{ fontWeight: 'bold' }}>Component Stack:</p>
              <pre style={{ margin: 0, background: '#fee2e2', padding: '1rem', borderRadius: '4px', overflowX: 'auto' }}>
                {this.state.errorInfo.componentStack}
              </pre>
            </>
          )}
        </div>
      );
    }

    return this.props.children;
  }
}

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <StrictMode>
    <ErrorBoundary>
      <App />
    </ErrorBoundary>
  </StrictMode>,
);
```

## src/save/LocalSaveStore.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * A tiny document store over localStorage, shaped like Firestore.
 *
 * ## What this replaces
 *
 * The offline/guest save used to be three `if (path === 'users/local-guest-uid')`
 * branches inside `lib/firebase.ts`, writing to three fixed keys:
 * `local_profile`, `local_settings`, `local_logs`. Two consequences, both of
 * which the brief asks about directly:
 *
 *  - **「是否避免不同帳號共用同一份存檔」** — it did not. Every guest on Earth
 *    shared the uid `local-guest-uid` and therefore those same three keys. On a
 *    shared browser, two players overwrote each other's island; and because the
 *    keys had no account in them, data from a previous session leaked into the
 *    next one.
 *  - Any path the three branches did not spell out was silently dropped: the
 *    write resolved successfully and stored nothing.
 *
 * Documents here are namespaced by uid and addressed by their full path, so the
 * store works for any path the game invents later without being taught about it.
 */

/** Write sentinels, mirroring Firestore's `increment`/`arrayUnion`/`arrayRemove`. */
export type LocalFieldValue =
  | { __localFieldValue: 'increment'; value: number }
  | { __localFieldValue: 'arrayUnion'; values: unknown[] }
  | { __localFieldValue: 'arrayRemove'; values: unknown[] };

export function localIncrement(n: number): LocalFieldValue {
  return { __localFieldValue: 'increment', value: n };
}

export function localArrayUnion(...values: unknown[]): LocalFieldValue {
  return { __localFieldValue: 'arrayUnion', values };
}

export function localArrayRemove(...values: unknown[]): LocalFieldValue {
  return { __localFieldValue: 'arrayRemove', values };
}

function isFieldValue(value: unknown): value is LocalFieldValue {
  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && '__localFieldValue' in value;
}

type Doc = Record<string, unknown>;

const KEY_PREFIX = 'island.save';

/** `island.save::<uid>::users/<uid>/settings/current` */
function storageKey(uid: string, path: string): string {
  return `${KEY_PREFIX}::${uid}::${path}`;
}

function namespacePrefix(uid: string): string {
  return `${KEY_PREFIX}::${uid}::`;
}

/** Applies one field write on top of the existing value. */
function resolveValue(current: unknown, incoming: unknown): unknown {
  if (!isFieldValue(incoming)) return incoming;

  switch (incoming.__localFieldValue) {
    case 'increment':
      return (typeof current === 'number' ? current : 0) + incoming.value;
    case 'arrayUnion': {
      const array = Array.isArray(current) ? [...current] : [];
      for (const value of incoming.values) {
        if (!array.some((existing) => deepEquals(existing, value))) array.push(value);
      }
      return array;
    }
    case 'arrayRemove': {
      const array = Array.isArray(current) ? [...current] : [];
      return array.filter((existing) => !incoming.values.some((value) => deepEquals(existing, value)));
    }
  }
}

/**
 * Structural equality, because `arrayUnion`/`arrayRemove` are used with placement
 * objects (`{ instanceId, itemId, position, rotation }`), not just id strings —
 * the old `arr.includes(el)` compared those by reference and so never matched,
 * which made retrieving a placed item a silent no-op offline.
 */
function deepEquals(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean {
  if (a === b) return true;
  if (typeof a !== typeof b || a === null || b === null) return false;
  if (typeof a !== 'object') return false;
  return JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b);
}

/** Writes `a.b.c` style keys into a nested object, matching Firestore's updateDoc. */
function applyUpdate(target: Doc, key: string, value: unknown): void {
  if (!key.includes('.')) {
    target[key] = resolveValue(target[key], value);
    return;
  }

  const segments = key.split('.');
  let cursor: Doc = target;
  for (let i = 0; i < segments.length - 1; i += 1) {
    const segment = segments[i];
    if (typeof cursor[segment] !== 'object' || cursor[segment] === null) {
      cursor[segment] = {};
    }
    cursor = cursor[segment] as Doc;
  }
  const leaf = segments[segments.length - 1];
  cursor[leaf] = resolveValue(cursor[leaf], value);
}

type Listener = (data: Doc | null) => void;

/**
 * A local write that did not land — storage full, or blocked by the browser.
 *
 * Shaped like a `FirebaseError` (a `code` property) on purpose: `describeSaveError`
 * (lib/saveStatus.ts) reads that one field, so an offline save failure is reported through the same
 * path, and in the same red banner, as a cloud one instead of needing its own branch at every call
 * site.
 */
export class LocalSaveError extends Error {
  readonly code = 'local-storage-full';
  constructor(path: string, readonly cause?: unknown) {
    super(`Local save failed for ${path}`);
    this.name = 'LocalSaveError';
  }
}

export class LocalSaveStore {
  /** path → listeners, per uid namespace. */
  private listeners = new Map<string, Set<Listener>>();

  private listenerKey(uid: string, path: string): string {
    return `${uid}::${path}`;
  }

  read(uid: string, path: string): Doc | null {
    try {
      const raw = localStorage.getItem(storageKey(uid, path));
      return raw ? (JSON.parse(raw) as Doc) : null;
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Persists one document, or THROWS.
   *
   * It used to log the failure and `return`, with a comment claiming nothing was silently
   * reported as saved — which is precisely what happened. Every caller is an `await updateDoc(...)`
   * inside a `try/catch` (context/use*Actions.ts): swallowing the error here resolved that promise
   * normally, so the write was reported as a success, no `catch` ran, no message was shown, and the
   * value on screen simply never moved. A full or disabled localStorage looked exactly like a dead
   * button — the 管理員測試補給 +10K 金幣 being the clearest case, since one press writes nothing
   * else that would have revealed the problem.
   *
   * The thrown error carries a Firestore-shaped `code` so it travels the same route as a refused
   * cloud write: handleFirestoreError → lib/saveStatus.ts → the red banner, in the player's words.
   */
  write(uid: string, path: string, data: Doc): void {
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(storageKey(uid, path), JSON.stringify(data));
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(`[save] Could not persist ${path} locally.`, error);
      throw new LocalSaveError(path, error);
    }
    this.emit(uid, path, data);
  }

  set(uid: string, path: string, data: Doc, options?: { merge?: boolean }): void {
    const next = options?.merge ? { ...(this.read(uid, path) ?? {}), ...data } : { ...data };
    next.lastUpdated = new Date().toISOString();
    this.write(uid, path, next);
  }

  update(uid: string, path: string, updates: Doc): void {
    const current = this.read(uid, path);
    // Firestore's updateDoc rejects on a missing document; matching that keeps
    // offline and online behaviour honest instead of inventing a document.
    const next: Doc = current ? structuredClone(current) : {};
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(updates)) applyUpdate(next, key, value);
    next.lastUpdated = new Date().toISOString();
    this.write(uid, path, next);
  }

  delete(uid: string, path: string): void {
    try {
      localStorage.removeItem(storageKey(uid, path));
    } catch {
      /* ignore */
    }
    this.emit(uid, path, null);
  }

  /** Every document directly or transitively under a collection path. */
  list(uid: string, collectionPath: string): Doc[] {
    const prefix = `${namespacePrefix(uid)}${collectionPath}/`;
    const results: Doc[] = [];
    try {
      for (let i = 0; i < localStorage.length; i += 1) {
        const key = localStorage.key(i);
        if (!key || !key.startsWith(prefix)) continue;
        const raw = localStorage.getItem(key);
        if (raw) results.push(JSON.parse(raw) as Doc);
      }
    } catch {
      /* ignore */
    }
    return results;
  }

  /** Every stored path in a uid's namespace — the basis of the guest claim. */
  paths(uid: string): string[] {
    const prefix = namespacePrefix(uid);
    const paths: string[] = [];
    try {
      for (let i = 0; i < localStorage.length; i += 1) {
        const key = localStorage.key(i);
        if (key?.startsWith(prefix)) paths.push(key.slice(prefix.length));
      }
    } catch {
      /* ignore */
    }
    return paths;
  }

  /** Drops an entire account's local save. Used after a successful claim. */
  clearNamespace(uid: string): void {
    for (const path of this.paths(uid)) {
      try {
        localStorage.removeItem(storageKey(uid, path));
      } catch {
        /* ignore */
      }
    }
  }

  /**
   * Watches a document. Fires immediately with the current value, then on every
   * later write, matching `onSnapshot`.
   */
  subscribe(uid: string, path: string, listener: Listener): () => void {
    const key = this.listenerKey(uid, path);
    let set = this.listeners.get(key);
    if (!set) {
      set = new Set();
      this.listeners.set(key, set);
    }
    set.add(listener);

    // Async, so subscribing during render cannot synchronously set state.
    const initial = this.read(uid, path);
    queueMicrotask(() => {
      if (set?.has(listener)) listener(initial);
    });

    return () => {
      set?.delete(listener);
      if (set?.size === 0) this.listeners.delete(key);
    };
  }

  /**
   * Watches a collection. Same contract as {@link subscribe}, but re-lists on
   * any write beneath the collection path.
   */
  subscribeCollection(uid: string, collectionPath: string, listener: (docs: Doc[]) => void): () => void {
    const key = this.listenerKey(uid, `${collectionPath}/*`);
    let set = this.listeners.get(key);
    if (!set) {
      set = new Set();
      this.listeners.set(key, set);
    }
    const wrapped: Listener = () => listener(this.list(uid, collectionPath));
    set.add(wrapped);

    queueMicrotask(() => {
      if (set?.has(wrapped)) listener(this.list(uid, collectionPath));
    });

    return () => {
      set?.delete(wrapped);
      if (set?.size === 0) this.listeners.delete(key);
    };
  }

  private emit(uid: string, path: string, data: Doc | null): void {
    this.listeners.get(this.listenerKey(uid, path))?.forEach((listener) => listener(data));

    // Wake any collection watchers whose path is a prefix of this document.
    const segments = path.split('/');
    for (let i = segments.length - 1; i > 0; i -= 1) {
      const collectionKey = this.listenerKey(uid, `${segments.slice(0, i).join('/')}/*`);
      this.listeners.get(collectionKey)?.forEach((listener) => listener(data));
    }
  }
}

export const localSaveStore = new LocalSaveStore();

/**
 * Moves a pre-existing `local_profile` / `local_settings` / `local_logs` save
 * into this store, under `uid`.
 *
 * This matters more than it looks: because Firebase anonymous sign-in is
 * disabled on this project, the legacy local guest was the ONLY working mode,
 * so every current player's island lives in exactly those three keys. Fixing
 * login must not orphan them.
 *
 * Idempotent, and it leaves the legacy keys in place — reading them again is
 * harmless, whereas deleting them makes a rollback lose real player data.
 */
const LEGACY_UID = 'local-guest-uid';
const LEGACY_CLAIMED_FLAG = 'island.save.legacyAdopted';

export function adoptLegacyLocalSave(uid: string): boolean {
  try {
    if (localStorage.getItem(LEGACY_CLAIMED_FLAG) === '1') return false;

    const profileRaw = localStorage.getItem('local_profile');
    if (!profileRaw) {
      // Nothing to rescue; mark done so we stop looking on every start-up.
      localStorage.setItem(LEGACY_CLAIMED_FLAG, '1');
      return false;
    }

    const profile = JSON.parse(profileRaw) as Doc;
    profile.userId = uid;
    localSaveStore.write(uid, `users/${uid}`, profile);

    const settingsRaw = localStorage.getItem('local_settings');
    if (settingsRaw) {
      const settings = JSON.parse(settingsRaw) as Doc;
      settings.userId = uid;
      localSaveStore.write(uid, `users/${uid}/settings/current`, settings);
    }

    const logsRaw = localStorage.getItem('local_logs');
    if (logsRaw) {
      const logs = JSON.parse(logsRaw) as Doc[];
      for (const log of logs) {
        const logId = String(log.logId ?? crypto.randomUUID());
        localSaveStore.write(uid, `users/${uid}/workout_logs/${logId}`, { ...log, userId: uid });
      }
    }

    localStorage.setItem(LEGACY_CLAIMED_FLAG, '1');
    console.info(`[save] 已將舊版訪客存檔轉移到新的帳號空間 (${uid})。`);
    return true;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('[save] Legacy local save adoption failed.', error);
    return false;
  }
}

export { LEGACY_UID };
```

## src/save/guestClaim.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { doc, getDoc, setDoc, writeBatch } from 'firebase/firestore';
import { db } from '../lib/firebaseCore';
import { localSaveStore } from './LocalSaveStore';

/**
 * Moves a local-only guest's island into a real account after they sign in —
 * 「將 Guest 存檔綁定至正式帳號」.
 *
 * There are two guest→account paths in the system and only this one needs to
 * copy anything:
 *
 *  - A **Firebase anonymous** guest is upgraded in place by
 *    `AuthenticationManager.linkProvider()`. The uid does not change, so
 *    `users/{uid}` is already the right document and there is nothing to move.
 *    That is the good path, and it becomes the default once Anonymous sign-in
 *    is enabled in the console (docs/AUTH_SETUP.md).
 *  - A **local-only** guest has no Firebase account at all, so their save lives
 *    in localStorage under a device-scoped uid. That is what this claims.
 */

export type ClaimOutcome =
  /** Local save copied into the account. */
  | 'claimed'
  /** The account already has cloud progress; the local save was left untouched. */
  | 'target-has-save'
  /** The guest never got as far as creating a save. */
  | 'nothing-to-claim'
  | 'failed';

export interface ClaimResult {
  outcome: ClaimOutcome;
  /** Documents written. Zero unless `outcome === 'claimed'`. */
  documentsWritten: number;
}

/**
 * @param fromUid device-scoped uid the local save is filed under
 * @param toUid   the newly signed-in Firebase uid
 *
 * **Never overwrites an existing cloud save.** A player who already has an
 * island on their account and then signs in on a friend's device — where a
 * local guest save happens to exist — must not have their real island replaced
 * by that stranger's. When the target already has a profile we report
 * `target-has-save` and leave both saves alone; the caller decides what to tell
 * the player.
 */
export async function claimLocalSave(fromUid: string, toUid: string): Promise<ClaimResult> {
  const localPaths = localSaveStore.paths(fromUid);
  if (localPaths.length === 0) {
    return { outcome: 'nothing-to-claim', documentsWritten: 0 };
  }

  const localProfile = localSaveStore.read(fromUid, `users/${fromUid}`);
  if (!localProfile) {
    return { outcome: 'nothing-to-claim', documentsWritten: 0 };
  }

  try {
    const targetProfileRef = doc(db, 'users', toUid);
    const targetSnapshot = await getDoc(targetProfileRef);
    if (targetSnapshot.exists()) {
      return { outcome: 'target-has-save', documentsWritten: 0 };
    }

    // The profile is written first and on its own. Firestore rules validate a
    // *created* user document structurally (`isValidUser`), and sub-collection
    // rules assume the owner document exists, so batching it together with the
    // logs would fail as one unit if any single log were malformed.
    const profileToWrite = { ...localProfile, userId: toUid };
    await setDoc(targetProfileRef, profileToWrite);

    let written = 1;
    const batch = writeBatch(db);
    let batched = 0;

    for (const path of localPaths) {
      if (path === `users/${fromUid}`) continue; // already written
      const data = localSaveStore.read(fromUid, path);
      if (!data) continue;

      // Re-file the document under the new uid: `users/<old>/settings/current`
      // becomes `users/<new>/settings/current`.
      const rebased = path.replace(`users/${fromUid}`, `users/${toUid}`);
      const segments = rebased.split('/');
      if (segments.length < 2 || segments.length % 2 !== 0) continue; // not a document path

      batch.set(doc(db, ...(segments as [string, string, ...string[]])), { ...data, userId: toUid });
      batched += 1;
      written += 1;
    }

    if (batched > 0) await batch.commit();

    // Only drop the local copy once the cloud write has actually succeeded.
    localSaveStore.clearNamespace(fromUid);

    console.info(`[save] 訪客存檔已綁定至帳號 ${toUid}（${written} 份文件）。`);
    return { outcome: 'claimed', documentsWritten: written };
  } catch (error) {
    // The local save is deliberately still intact here, so the player can retry
    // by signing out and back in rather than losing the island.
    console.error('[save] Guest save claim failed; the local copy has been kept.', error);
    return { outcome: 'failed', documentsWritten: 0 };
  }
}
```
