## src/server/dailyLoginApi.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 每日登入 — the server half, and the ONLY thing in this game that is allowed to decide whether a
 * reward is owed.
 *
 * ## Why this file exists at all
 *
 * Everything else in this app writes its own save: the browser holds a Firestore handle and updates
 * `users/{uid}` directly, with `firestore.rules` as the only gate. That is fine for where a sofa is
 * standing. It is not fine for currency that is minted by the passage of time, because the two
 * things the client would have to be trusted with — WHAT DAY IT IS and WHETHER THIS DAY WAS ALREADY
 * PAID — are exactly the two a player can change (system clock) or race (two tabs, two devices, a
 * retried request). So this endpoint owns both:
 *
 *   - The clock is the SERVER's, read once per request and converted to a 台北 calendar day. The
 *     request body cannot carry a date, and nothing in it is consulted for one.
 *   - Eligibility is recomputed from (anchor, server now, claim records) on every call. There is no
 *     cached cycle state to go stale, so a scheduled job that never runs cannot corrupt anything —
 *     there is no scheduled job.
 *
 * ## What guarantees a reward is paid exactly once
 *
 * Firestore has no UNIQUE constraint, but it has something stronger for this shape: a document
 * either exists or it does not, and `create` fails if it does. So the spec's
 * `UNIQUE(user_id, cycle_id, day_index, reward_type)` is expressed as the claim document's own PATH:
 *
 *     users/{uid}/daily_login_claims/{cycleId}__{dayIndex}__{rewardType}
 *
 * The id is DERIVED, never random, so two requests for the same day are two attempts to create the
 * same document — from one tab, from ten tabs, from a phone and a laptop at once, or from a client
 * retrying because it never saw the first response. The write happens inside a Firestore
 * transaction that also reads the wallet, so the balance change and the claim record commit or
 * roll back together; a transaction whose read set changed underneath it is retried by the SDK and
 * then fails the existence check, which is how the concurrent case collapses to exactly one winner.
 *
 * `idempotencyKey` from the client is recorded but is NOT the uniqueness mechanism — it is how a
 * retry is told apart from a genuine double-claim. Same key on an existing claim means "you already
 * did this, here is the result you missed"; a different key means "that day is taken".
 *
 * ## What is deliberately NOT here
 *
 * No currency is invented and no wallet layout is decided. The fields this transaction touches come
 * from `constants/currency.ts` (`currencyFieldPath`), the same module the browser reads, so 「碎片
 * 存在哪裡」 has one answer on both sides of the wire.
 *
 * ## It pays 金幣, and it is no longer the whole prize (2026-09-17)
 *
 * The round pays seven different KINDS of thing now (constants/dailyLogin.ts): 商品碎片, 金幣,
 * 抽獎券, a 功能卡, a whole product, and on 第 7 天 a free turn of the 幸運轉盤. Exactly one of
 * those moves a wallet, and it is the only one this endpoint touches — 15 金幣 on four of the seven
 * days, netted against the 補簽 fee inside the same transaction that creates the claim record.
 *
 * Everything else is granted by the CLIENT, after this endpoint has accepted the claim as new
 * (context/useDailyLoginPrize.ts). That is not a weakening of the guarantee this file exists for:
 * what a browser must not be trusted with is WHAT DAY IT IS and WHETHER THIS DAY WAS ALREADY PAID,
 * and both of those are still decided here. A fragment stack and a card bag have no wallet to
 * protect, and teaching this endpoint to read a catalog of a few hundred items — plus a rarity
 * table, plus the reward pools — to hand one out would buy nothing but a schema migration.
 *
 * Between 2026-08-25 and 2026-09-17 the payout was the wallet's 碎片 and the fee was 金幣, so the
 * transaction moved two fields. It moves one now, which is why the increment below is netted where
 * it used to be deliberately split.
 */

import type { Express, NextFunction, Request, Response } from 'express';
import { cert, getApps, initializeApp, type App } from 'firebase-admin/app';
import { getAuth } from 'firebase-admin/auth';
import { FieldValue, getFirestore, type Firestore, type Transaction } from 'firebase-admin/firestore';

import {
  CYCLE_LENGTH,
  DAILY_LOGIN_CURRENCY,
  DAILY_LOGIN_TZ,
  buildSquares,
  canClaim,
  civilDateAt,
  dailyPrizeFor,
  dailyPrizeHeadline,
  makeupCostForDay,
  resolveCycle,
  type CivilDate,
} from '../constants/dailyLogin';
import { currencyFieldPath } from '../constants/currency';

/**
 * Where the balance this endpoint moves lives, resolved once from the shared currency table.
 *
 * Read through `currencyFieldPath` rather than written as a string literal, so the server cannot
 * drift from the client about which document field a balance is in — a mismatch there would pay a
 * reward into a field nothing reads, with no error anywhere.
 */
const COIN_FIELD = currencyFieldPath(DAILY_LOGIN_CURRENCY);

/**
 * The rules module above is shared VERBATIM with the browser, and that is on purpose: the panel has
 * to be able to grey out a button for the same reason the server refuses the write, and two copies
 * of "which day is this" would drift the first time the ladder is retuned. The client's copy is an
 * optimistic preview; this one is the verdict. They agree because they are the same file.
 */

// --- Firestore admin ---------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * The named database this project actually uses.
 *
 * NOT `(default)`. firebase.json points the rules at a named database, and an Admin SDK handle
 * opened without this id talks to an empty default database instead — silently, with reads simply
 * returning nothing, which reads as "the player has no profile" rather than as a misconfiguration.
 * Overridable so a staging project can point elsewhere.
 */
const DATABASE_ID = process.env.FIREBASE_DATABASE_ID ?? 'ai-studio-07ffb391-da53-4ca6-99c4-9c12d59da230';

let cachedDb: Firestore | null = null;
let initError: string | null = null;

/**
 * Credentials come from the environment, never from the repo.
 *
 * Two accepted shapes, because the two deployment styles in use want different things:
 * `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` as inline JSON (one env var, which is what a container platform wants)
 * or `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` pointing at a file (which is what the gcloud tooling sets up,
 * and what Application Default Credentials picks up on its own).
 */
function initAdmin(): App | null {
  const existing = getApps();
  if (existing.length > 0) return existing[0];

  const inline = process.env.FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT;
  try {
    if (inline) {
      const parsed = JSON.parse(inline);
      return initializeApp({ credential: cert(parsed), projectId: parsed.project_id });
    }
    if (process.env.GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS) {
      // Application Default Credentials: initializeApp() with no argument finds them.
      return initializeApp();
    }
  } catch (error) {
    initError = `daily-login: service account could not be loaded — ${(error as Error).message}`;
    return null;
  }
  initError =
    'daily-login: no server credentials. Set FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT (inline JSON) or ' +
    'GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS (path to the key file). See docs/daily-login.md.';
  return null;
}

function getDb(): Firestore | null {
  if (cachedDb) return cachedDb;
  const app = initAdmin();
  if (!app) return null;
  cachedDb = getFirestore(app, DATABASE_ID);
  return cachedDb;
}

// --- Errors ------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * The error codes the client is allowed to branch on.
 *
 * A closed set with stable names, because the panel has a specific message and a specific recovery
 * for each one (see components/UI/DailyLoginPanel.tsx). Anything unexpected becomes `server_error`
 * rather than leaking a Firestore message to a player.
 */
export type DailyLoginErrorCode =
  | 'unauthenticated'
  | 'not_configured'
  | 'invalid_request'
  | 'no_profile'
  | 'not_available_yet'
  | 'already_claimed'
  | 'makeup_window_closed'
  | 'insufficient_gold'
  | 'server_error';

class ClaimError extends Error {
  constructor(readonly code: DailyLoginErrorCode, readonly status: number, message: string) {
    super(message);
  }
}

// --- Auth --------------------------------------------------------------------

interface AuthedRequest extends Request {
  uid?: string;
}

/**
 * Identity comes from a verified Firebase ID token and nothing else.
 *
 * Explicitly NOT from a `user_id` in the body or a query string, which is the single most important
 * line in this file: with the uid taken from the request, any signed-in player could mint gold into
 * any other account by editing one field.
 */
async function requireAuth(req: AuthedRequest, res: Response, next: NextFunction): Promise<void> {
  const app = initAdmin();
  if (!app) {
    res.status(503).json({ error: { code: 'not_configured', message: initError } });
    return;
  }
  const header = req.headers.authorization ?? '';
  const token = header.startsWith('Bearer ') ? header.slice(7).trim() : '';
  if (!token) {
    res.status(401).json({ error: { code: 'unauthenticated', message: '請先登入' } });
    return;
  }
  try {
    const decoded = await getAuth(app).verifyIdToken(token);
    req.uid = decoded.uid;
    next();
  } catch {
    res.status(401).json({ error: { code: 'unauthenticated', message: '登入憑證已失效，請重新登入' } });
  }
}

// --- Paths -------------------------------------------------------------------

const userDoc = (db: Firestore, uid: string) => db.collection('users').doc(uid);

/**
 * The claim record's id — and therefore the uniqueness constraint. See the file header.
 *
 * `rewardType` is in the key because the day a cycle hands out a pet AND currency on the same
 * square, those are two grants that must be independently recorded and independently idempotent.
 * Leaving it out would make that a schema migration.
 *
 * It is now the PRIZE's kind (`coins`, `item-fragments`, `free-spin`…), which is a pure function of
 * the round and the day, so two attempts at one square always name the same document. Note what
 * that means across a change to the prize table: a claim paid under the old ladder is filed under
 * `…__fragments` and one paid under the new table may be filed under `…__coins`, so the same day of
 * the same cycle could in principle be claimed once under each. That window is a single cycle wide
 * and closes on its own (a cycle is seven days, and `readState` only ever reads the CURRENT cycle's
 * claims); the alternative — reusing an old key for a different reward — would file two different
 * payouts under one id and make the audit trail lie about what was paid.
 */
function claimId(cycleId: string, day: number, rewardType: string): string {
  return `${cycleId}__d${day}__${rewardType}`;
}

const claimDoc = (db: Firestore, uid: string, id: string) =>
  userDoc(db, uid).collection('daily_login_claims').doc(id);

const auditCol = (db: Firestore, uid: string) => userDoc(db, uid).collection('daily_login_audit');

// --- Shared read -------------------------------------------------------------

interface ProfileShape {
  balanceGold?: number;
  /** The non-coin half of the wallet — see constants/currency.ts. */
  wallet?: { fragments?: number };
  dailyLoginAnchor?: CivilDate;
}

/** A balance as a whole non-negative number, whatever the document actually holds. */
const sane = (value: unknown): number =>
  typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0 ? Math.floor(value) : 0;

/**
 * Both balances off a profile document.
 *
 * Every absence reads as 0, which is correct for all three ways it happens: a brand-new player, a
 * save written before 碎片 existed, and a document whose field somehow holds a non-number.
 */
const walletOf = (profile: ProfileShape): { coins: number; fragments: number } => ({
  coins: sane(profile.balanceGold),
  fragments: sane(profile.wallet?.fragments),
});

interface ClaimRecord {
  cycleId: string;
  dayIndex: number;
  rewardType: string;
  rewardId: string | null;
  quantity: number;
  mode: 'free' | 'makeup';
  /** What the player PAID, in 金幣. Named for the currency it is in, because the payout no longer is. */
  costGold: number;
  idempotencyKey: string | null;
}

/**
 * Reads everything a status response needs, inside whatever transaction the caller is running (or
 * outside one, for a plain read).
 *
 * The anchor is READ here and written by the caller if missing — a first-ever visit establishes
 * Day 1 as the server's today, which is what makes "第一次進入以當天為 Day 1" true without the
 * client ever proposing a date.
 */
async function readState(
  db: Firestore,
  uid: string,
  now: Date,
  tx?: Transaction
): Promise<{
  profile: ProfileShape;
  anchor: CivilDate;
  anchorWasMissing: boolean;
  cycle: ReturnType<typeof resolveCycle>;
  claimedDays: Set<number>;
  claims: Record<string, ClaimRecord>;
}> {
  const ref = userDoc(db, uid);
  const snap = tx ? await tx.get(ref) : await ref.get();
  if (!snap.exists) {
    throw new ClaimError('no_profile', 404, '找不到玩家資料');
  }
  const profile = (snap.data() ?? {}) as ProfileShape;

  const today = civilDateAt(now);
  const anchorWasMissing = !profile.dailyLoginAnchor;
  const anchor = profile.dailyLoginAnchor ?? today;
  const cycle = resolveCycle(anchor, now);

  // Only THIS cycle's claims are needed to decide anything; older ones are history and are left
  // where they are. A range query on the id prefix keeps the read one collection scan of at most
  // seven documents rather than the player's whole claim history.
  const col = userDoc(db, uid).collection('daily_login_claims');
  const q = col.where('cycleId', '==', cycle.cycleId);
  const claimSnap = tx ? await tx.get(q) : await q.get();

  const claimedDays = new Set<number>();
  const claims: Record<string, ClaimRecord> = {};
  claimSnap.forEach((d) => {
    const rec = d.data() as ClaimRecord;
    claimedDays.add(rec.dayIndex);
    claims[d.id] = rec;
  });

  return { profile, anchor, anchorWasMissing, cycle, claimedDays, claims };
}

/** The response shape both endpoints return, so the client has one thing to parse. */
function buildStatusPayload(
  now: Date,
  anchor: CivilDate,
  cycle: ReturnType<typeof resolveCycle>,
  claimedDays: Set<number>,
  balances: { coins: number; fragments: number }
) {
  const squares = buildSquares(cycle, claimedDays, true);
  return {
    server_now: now.toISOString(),
    timezone: DAILY_LOGIN_TZ,
    anchor_date: anchor,
    cycle_id: cycle.cycleId,
    cycle_number: cycle.cycleNumber,
    cycle_start_at: cycle.startDate,
    cycle_end_at: cycle.endDate,
    current_day_index: cycle.currentDayIndex,
    /** 金幣 — what a 補簽 is paid out of. Kept under its original name so no client breaks. */
    coin_balance: balances.coins,
    /** 碎片 — the wallet currency. No day of the round pays it any more; reported for reconciliation. */
    fragment_balance: balances.fragments,
    /**
     * Which currency a MONEY square's `quantity` is denominated in. Squares that pay no money
     * (`reward_type` of `item-fragments`, `utility-card`, `raffle-ticket`, `item`, `free-spin`)
     * carry a count of that thing instead — see constants/dailyLogin.ts's `dailyPrizeHeadline`.
     */
    reward_currency: DAILY_LOGIN_CURRENCY,
    rewards: squares.map((s) => ({
      day_index: s.day,
      reward_type: s.rewardType,
      reward_id: s.rewardId,
      quantity: s.quantity,
      state: s.state,
      makeup_cost: s.makeupCost,
    })),
    /**
     * Monotonic version for the client's "never let an older response overwrite a newer one" rule.
     * The server's own clock in milliseconds: every response is stamped when it is built, so two
     * responses that crossed on the wire are ordered by when the SERVER answered, not by when the
     * browser happened to receive them.
     */
    updated_at: now.getTime(),
  };
}

export type DailyLoginStatus = ReturnType<typeof buildStatusPayload>;

// --- Routes ------------------------------------------------------------------

export function registerDailyLoginApi(app: Express): void {
  /**
   * The whole board, recomputed from the server's clock.
   *
   * Also the only place the anchor is created. Doing it on a READ is deliberate: 「玩家第一次進入
   * 每日登入功能時，以當天的伺服器日期作為 Day 1」 — opening the panel is the first entry, and
   * waiting for the first claim would mean a player who looked on Monday and claimed on Tuesday
   * would have their Day 1 be Tuesday.
   */
  app.get('/api/daily-login/status', requireAuth, async (req: AuthedRequest, res: Response) => {
    const db = getDb();
    if (!db) {
      res.status(503).json({ error: { code: 'not_configured', message: initError } });
      return;
    }
    try {
      const now = new Date();
      const state = await readState(db, req.uid!, now);
      if (state.anchorWasMissing) {
        // Not a transaction: the anchor is write-once and the value is the server's today, so two
        // concurrent first visits write the identical date. Nothing is lost by the second write.
        await userDoc(db, req.uid!).update({ dailyLoginAnchor: state.anchor });
      }
      res.json(
        buildStatusPayload(now, state.anchor, state.cycle, state.claimedDays, walletOf(state.profile))
      );
    } catch (error) {
      sendError(res, error);
    }
  });

  /**
   * Take one square, free or bought back.
   *
   * The body carries only WHICH square and HOW, plus a retry key. It carries no amounts, no prices,
   * no dates and no user id — every one of those is derived here, because every one of those is
   * something a client would otherwise be able to choose for itself.
   */
  app.post('/api/daily-login/claim', requireAuth, async (req: AuthedRequest, res: Response) => {
    const db = getDb();
    if (!db) {
      res.status(503).json({ error: { code: 'not_configured', message: initError } });
      return;
    }

    const uid = req.uid!;
    const dayIndex = Number((req.body ?? {}).day_index);
    const mode = (req.body ?? {}).mode === 'makeup' ? 'makeup' : 'free';
    const idempotencyKey =
      typeof (req.body ?? {}).idempotency_key === 'string' ? (req.body.idempotency_key as string).slice(0, 128) : null;

    if (!Number.isInteger(dayIndex) || dayIndex < 1 || dayIndex > CYCLE_LENGTH) {
      res.status(400).json({ error: { code: 'invalid_request', message: '無效的日期' } });
      return;
    }

    try {
      const now = new Date();
      const result = await db.runTransaction(async (tx) => {
        const state = await readState(db, uid, now, tx);
        const { cycle, claimedDays, claims } = state;
        // The prize is a pure function of (round, day) — see constants/dailyLogin.ts on why the
        // roll is seeded rather than live. That is what lets this line name the claim document
        // after the prize's KIND: two attempts at the same day are two attempts to create the same
        // path, which is the uniqueness constraint Firestore does not otherwise have. A prize that
        // re-rolled would be a second path, and a second path is a second payout.
        const prize = dailyPrizeFor(cycle.cycleId, dayIndex);
        const id = claimId(cycle.cycleId, dayIndex, prize.kind);

        // --- Idempotent replay ------------------------------------------------
        // A claim that already exists is not automatically an error: if it carries the same
        // idempotency key, this is the same request arriving twice (the first response was lost,
        // the tab was reloaded mid-flight, the network retried) and the honest answer is the
        // result it already produced. Only a DIFFERENT key means a genuine second attempt.
        const existing = claims[id];
        if (existing) {
          if (idempotencyKey && existing.idempotencyKey === idempotencyKey) {
            return { replayed: true, granted: existing.quantity, spent: existing.costGold, state };
          }
          throw new ClaimError('already_claimed', 409, '這一天已經領過了');
        }

        // --- Eligibility, from the server's own clock -------------------------
        const square = buildSquares(cycle, claimedDays, true)[dayIndex - 1];
        if (!canClaim(square, mode)) {
          if (square.state === 'claimed') throw new ClaimError('already_claimed', 409, '這一天已經領過了');
          if (square.state === 'future') throw new ClaimError('not_available_yet', 409, '這一天還沒開放');
          if (square.state === 'missed') throw new ClaimError('makeup_window_closed', 409, '這一輪已結束，無法補簽');
          if (mode === 'free' && square.state === 'makeup_available') {
            throw new ClaimError('not_available_yet', 409, '這一天需要補簽才能領取');
          }
          throw new ClaimError('not_available_yet', 409, '目前無法領取這一天');
        }

        // --- Price and payout, both in 金幣 now -------------------------------
        //
        // The day pays 金幣 on four of its seven days and pays nothing this endpoint can move on the
        // other three: 商品碎片, 抽獎券, 功能卡, a product and a free 輪盤 turn all live in the
        // player's own document and are granted by the client after this claim is accepted (see
        // context/useDailyLoginPrize.ts). That is deliberate — those have no wallet to protect, and
        // teaching this API about the catalog would buy nothing.
        //
        // Only the PRICE is checked for affordability; a payout cannot fail for lack of funds.
        const costGold = mode === 'makeup' ? makeupCostForDay(dayIndex) : 0;
        const grantCoins = prize.coins;
        const wallet = walletOf(state.profile);
        if (costGold > wallet.coins) {
          throw new ClaimError('insufficient_gold', 402, '金幣不足');
        }

        // --- One transaction: record, pay, audit ------------------------------
        // `create` (not set) is what makes the claim record the uniqueness constraint: it fails if
        // the document exists, and the whole transaction rolls back with it.
        const record: ClaimRecord & { claimedAt: FirebaseFirestore.FieldValue } = {
          cycleId: cycle.cycleId,
          dayIndex,
          rewardType: prize.kind,
          rewardId: prize.itemRarity ?? prize.kind,
          quantity: dailyPrizeHeadline(prize),
          mode,
          costGold,
          idempotencyKey,
          claimedAt: FieldValue.serverTimestamp(),
        };
        tx.create(claimDoc(db, uid, id), record);

        // ONE increment, netted — which is the opposite of what this did while the payout and the
        // price were different currencies. It has to be: they are the same field now, and two
        // `increment`s written under the same key in one update object is not two increments, it is
        // the second one silently replacing the first. Netting is correct here for exactly the
        // reason it was wrong there — there IS a net between 15 金幣 in and 500 金幣 out.
        const netCoins = grantCoins - costGold;
        if (netCoins !== 0) {
          tx.update(userDoc(db, uid), { [COIN_FIELD]: FieldValue.increment(netCoins) });
        }

        const after = { coins: wallet.coins + netCoins, fragments: wallet.fragments };

        // The audit row records BOTH balances before and after. It used to record one number under
        // `balanceBefore`/`balanceAfter`, which cannot describe a transaction that moves two
        // currencies — and an audit trail that silently drops half of what happened is worse than
        // none, because it looks complete.
        tx.create(auditCol(db, uid).doc(), {
          ...record,
          claimRef: id,
          rewardCurrency: DAILY_LOGIN_CURRENCY,
          grantedCoins: grantCoins,
          balanceBefore: wallet.coins,
          balanceAfter: after.coins,
          fragmentsBefore: wallet.fragments,
          fragmentsAfter: after.fragments,
          serverDate: civilDateAt(now),
        });

        return {
          replayed: false,
          granted: grantCoins,
          spent: costGold,
          state: {
            ...state,
            claimedDays: new Set([...claimedDays, dayIndex]),
            profile: {
              ...state.profile,
              balanceGold: after.coins,
              wallet: { ...state.profile.wallet, fragments: after.fragments },
            },
          },
        };
      });

      const after = await readState(db, uid, now);
      res.json({
        ok: true,
        replayed: result.replayed,
        granted_quantity: result.granted,
        spent_gold: result.spent,
        status: buildStatusPayload(now, after.anchor, after.cycle, after.claimedDays, walletOf(after.profile)),
      });
    } catch (error) {
      sendError(res, error);
    }
  });
}

function sendError(res: Response, error: unknown): void {
  if (error instanceof ClaimError) {
    res.status(error.status).json({ error: { code: error.code, message: error.message } });
    return;
  }
  // Firestore's own "document already exists" from tx.create losing the race. Two clients that
  // passed eligibility in parallel both reach the write; exactly one commits and the other lands
  // here, which is the concurrency guarantee actually being observed.
  const message = (error as Error)?.message ?? '';
  if (/ALREADY_EXISTS|already exists/i.test(message)) {
    res.status(409).json({ error: { code: 'already_claimed', message: '這一天已經領過了' } });
    return;
  }
  console.error('daily-login:', error);
  res.status(500).json({ error: { code: 'server_error', message: '伺服器忙碌中，請稍後再試' } });
}

```

## src/types.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import type { PlayerWallet } from './constants/currency';
import type { Rarity } from './constants/rarity';
import type { IslandEnvironmentState } from './constants/islandReturn';
import type { WorkoutRewardState } from './constants/workoutRewards';
import type { UtilityCardState } from './constants/utilityCards';
import type { LimitedShopState } from './constants/limitedShop';
import type { WeeklyTaskState } from './constants/weeklyTasks';

/**
 * ⚠️ 這個 enum 是**舊的分類法**，而且已經名不符實。真正在用的分類是
 * `ItemDefinition.shopCategory` + utils/categoryUtils.ts 的 `DISPLAY_CATEGORIES`（32 個分類、
 * 6 個主分區），那才是商店、收納庫、更衣室與兩個建造抽屜共同讀的那一張表。
 *
 * 這裡剩下的三個實際分支是：outfit.ts 的項鍊判斷、FurnitureItem.tsx 的 `building` 判斷、
 * artwork.ts 的產生器。其餘的 270 多處只是每一列商品都得填一格。
 *
 * 對不上的地方已經很明顯：`building` 同時涵蓋地板、牆面、花草、樹木與寵物窩；`outfit` 涵蓋帽子
 * 與**寵物飾品**；`furniture` 涵蓋大多掛在牆上的藝術品。
 *
 * 不在這一輪動它 —— 它會影響 276 處商品資料與三個渲染分支，那是一次獨立的收斂，不是資訊架構
 * 整理的一部分。但 `EARRING` 已經移除：它有 **0 件商品**，唯一叫這個名字的東西是
 * Three/character/legacy/wardrobe.tsx 裡自己的 `EarringKind`（跟這個 enum 無關）。留著一個沒有
 * 任何商品、也沒有任何程式讀的成員，只會讓下一個人以為耳環是一個還沒接完的功能。
 */
export enum ItemCategory {
  OUTFIT = 'outfit',
  BUILDING = 'building',
  FURNITURE = 'furniture',
  HAT = 'hat',
  NECKLACE = 'necklace',
  SHOES = 'shoes',
  PANTS = 'pants',
  /**
   * An exterior appearance for the player's one Home — NOT a building you place. Buying one
   * grants the style; applying it re-skins the existing Home in place. See
   * constants/houseStyles.ts.
   */
  HOUSE_STYLE = 'house_style',
  /** A companion the player keeps — bought in 商店's 寵物 section, not worn and not placed. */
  PET = 'pet',
  /**
   * 島上的居民 — bought in 商店's NPC section. Owned once, never worn and never placed by the
   * player: where each one stands is declared in constants/npcs.ts. See the `Npcs` category in
   * utils/categoryUtils.ts for why that makes it own-once rather than placeable.
   */
  NPC = 'npc',
  /**
   * 特殊卡牌 — 抽獎券 and 功能卡, bought in 商店's 特殊卡牌 section. The only goods that are
   * used up: they are held in the backpack and spent, never worn, placed or applied. See the
   * `consumable` kind in utils/categoryUtils.ts.
   */
  CARD = 'card',
  /**
   * 消耗品 — goods that are used up. 寵物飼料 is the first, sold in 商店's 寵物 section.
   *
   * Distinct from {@link ItemCategory.CARD}, which is also spent: a 卡牌 is not a thing in the
   * world (it changes how rewards pay out) while a consumable is an object with a price, a stack
   * and something it is used ON. What each one does when it is used is declared per item — see
   * constants/consumables.ts.
   */
  CONSUMABLE = 'consumable',
}

export interface PlacedItem {
  instanceId: string;
  itemId: string;
  position: [number, number, number];
  rotation: number;
}

/**
 * The interior of the player's Home. Stored at the profile top level rather than nested under
 * `home` because there has only ever been one of these — `activeBuildingId` was written but
 * never read, and BuildingInteriorView has always rendered this single shared record. Keeping
 * it in place avoids migrating every existing player's room layout.
 */
/** A single room's applied floor/wall style ids. Absent fields fall through to the defaults. */
export interface RoomStyle {
  floor?: string;
  wall?: string;
}

export interface HouseInteriorData {
  placements: PlacedItem[];
  unlockedRooms: string[]; // ['kitchen', 'bathroom', 'study', 'living']
  /**
   * Per-room style overrides, keyed by RoomInstance.id (so 'living', 'bathroom', or the
   * trailing id of an `ext_*` room string - see parseUnlockedRooms). This is the primary
   * source: applying a paint or floor writes only the room the player is standing in.
   */
  roomStyles?: Record<string, RoomStyle>;
  /**
   * Legacy house-wide styles, kept as a fallback beneath roomStyles so players who applied a
   * style before it became per-room keep the look they had, with no data migration. Nothing
   * writes these any more.
   */
  selectedFloorStyle?: string;
  selectedWallStyle?: string;
}

/**
 * The player's single dwelling. Distinct from a Building (an ordinary placeable object in
 * `islandPlacements`): there is exactly one Home per player for the whole game, it is the only
 * structure that can be entered, and changing its appearance never creates a second one.
 *
 * `undefined`/`null` means the Home has not been placed yet — the player still holds the
 * Starter House in their inventory and the first-time guide is pending.
 */
export interface PlayerHome {
  /** World position of the Home's centre. */
  position: [number, number, number];
  /** Y-axis rotation in radians. */
  rotation: number;
  /**
   * Which exterior appearance is currently worn. A HouseStyleId from
   * constants/houseStyles.ts. Swapping this changes only the model — position, rotation,
   * interior, furniture and storage are untouched.
   */
  currentStyle: string;
  /** ISO timestamp of when the Home was first established. */
  placedAt: string;
}

export interface UserProfile {
  userId: string;
  displayName: string;
  level: number;
  currentXp: number;
  territoryLevel: number;
  /**
   * 金幣. Kept as a top-level field rather than moved into {@link UserProfile.wallet} — see
   * constants/currency.ts for why: `firestore.rules` requires it unconditionally on every write,
   * the daily-login server increments it inside a transaction, and every save in the wild carries
   * it. Nothing outside constants/currency.ts should read it directly; ask `getBalance()`.
   */
  balanceGold: number;
  /**
   * 碎片, and every currency added after it — the non-coin half of the wallet.
   *
   * One nested map for the reason {@link UserProfile.islandState} and
   * {@link UserProfile.workoutRewards} are one: it is ONE key in firestore.rules and ONE entry in
   * the update whitelist, so a third currency later is a row in CURRENCY_SPECS rather than a
   * schema change plus a rules deploy.
   *
   * Absent on every save written before 碎片 existed, which is deliberately indistinguishable from
   * a player who has never been paid one: neither has any. See constants/currency.ts.
   */
  wallet?: PlayerWallet;
  inventory: string[];
  equippedItems: string[];
  lastUpdated: string;
  avatar?: string;
  lastLoginDate?: string;
  loginStreak?: number;
  /**
   * The player's 每日登入 anchor: the civil date (`YYYY-MM-DD`, Asia/Taipei) their very first
   * round began on. Every later round is a seven-day tile counted from here, so this is written
   * once and never again. See constants/dailyLogin.ts.
   */
  loginAnchorDate?: string;
  /** Which round {@link loginClaimedDays} belongs to (`cycle-YYYY-MM-DD`). Claims reset with it. */
  loginCycleId?: string;
  /** Days of that round already collected, 1-based. A 補簽 writes into this list too. */
  loginClaimedDays?: number[];
  lastPetDate?: string;
  petCountToday?: number;
  /**
   * The player's one and only Home. Absent until they place the Starter House.
   */
  home?: PlayerHome | null;
  /** Interior of {@link home} — see HouseInteriorData for why it lives here. */
  interiorData?: HouseInteriorData;
  /** Ordinary Buildings/decorations on the island. Never contains the Home. */
  islandPlacements?: PlacedItem[];
  /**
   * 離線回歸 — what the island did while nobody was here, and how the pet spent that time.
   *
   * One nested map rather than a spread of top-level fields, because every piece of it moves
   * together: the sighting the absence is measured from, the overgrowth that absence grew, and
   * the mood it left the companion in are written in the same breath and read in the same breath.
   * It is also one key in firestore.rules and one entry in every write whitelist, which is the
   * difference between adding a feature and re-teaching the ruleset five field names.
   *
   * Absent on every save that predates the feature, which is deliberately indistinguishable from
   * a brand-new player: neither has ever been away. See constants/islandReturn.ts.
   */
  islandState?: IslandEnvironmentState;
  /**
   * 商品碎片 — how many of each item's OWN fragments the player is holding, keyed by catalog id.
   *
   * A map rather than a list of `{ itemId, count }` records for the reason the feature exists: a
   * fragment is unique to one product and can never be spent on another, and a map makes that a
   * property of the storage instead of a rule some future write has to remember. `itemFragments['item-5']`
   * IS 草帽's fragment count; there is no key it could be confused with and no shared pool to leak into.
   *
   * Absent on every save that predates the feature, which reads as "no fragments yet" — the same
   * thing a brand-new player has. No migration needed. A stack is capped at FRAGMENTS_TO_UNLOCK by
   * the write path (constants/fragments.ts); anything over the cap becomes {@link raffleTickets}.
   */
  itemFragments?: Record<string, number>;
  /**
   * 抽獎券 — what 多出來的碎片 turn into, and what the 轉盤 will spend.
   *
   * Minted in three places: the two settle functions in constants/fragments.ts (fragments granted
   * onto an already-full stack, and the stack left stranded when its item is bought with gold
   * instead), and 第 2 天 of the 每日登入 round when it rolls that way. Nothing else may create one.
   */
  raffleTickets?: number;
  /**
   * 免費轉盤次數 — turns of the 幸運轉盤 that cost no 抽獎券.
   *
   * Its own counter rather than 「just give them the tickets」, because the two are not the same
   * promise. A ticket is a resource: it can be saved, it can be spent alongside others, and how far
   * it goes depends on what a spin costs that week. A free turn is a turn — it is worth exactly one
   * spin no matter what a spin is priced at, which is what 第 7 天 of the round is actually giving
   * away (constants/dailyLogin.ts). Paying it in tickets would have quietly re-priced the prize
   * every time the wheel was re-balanced.
   *
   * Spent by context/useWheelActions.ts, which consumes one of these BEFORE it looks at the ticket
   * balance. Absent on every save that predates the feature, which reads as zero.
   */
  freeWheelSpins?: number;
  /**
   * The fraction of the next 抽獎券 already paid for — 0…FRAGMENTS_PER_TICKET-1.
   *
   * The conversion rate does not divide evenly into every overflow, and this is where the remainder
   * waits instead of being discarded. It is deliberately NOT shown as a currency of its own: the
   * player sees it as the little bar under the ticket count, and it exists so the promise that
   * overflow becomes tickets is true for 5 fragments as well as for 20.
   */
  raffleTicketProgress?: number;
  /**
   * 健身獎勵 — what this account has earned by training, and what it has already been paid.
   *
   * One nested map for the same reason {@link islandState} is one: every part of it is written in
   * the same breath, and it is ONE key in firestore.rules and ONE entry in the write whitelist
   * rather than one per reward. A bare `firstWorkoutRewardClaimed` boolean was the obvious shape
   * and is the one that needs a schema change — and a rules deploy — for every reward added after
   * the first.
   *
   * Absent on every save that predates the feature, which is deliberately indistinguishable from a
   * brand-new player: neither has claimed anything. See constants/workoutRewards.ts.
   */
  workoutRewards?: WorkoutRewardState;
  /**
   * 功能卡 — the cards this account holds and the effects it has running.
   *
   * One nested map, for exactly the reason {@link workoutRewards} and {@link islandState} are one:
   * every part of it moves together (a card leaves the bag in the same breath its effect starts),
   * and it is ONE key in firestore.rules and ONE entry in each update whitelist — so the second
   * card, and the first effect that needs a new field, is a change in constants/utilityCards.ts
   * rather than a schema change plus a rules deploy.
   *
   * Absent on every save that predates the feature, which is deliberately indistinguishable from a
   * player who has never been given a card: neither holds one.
   */
  utilityCards?: UtilityCardState;
  /**
   * 限時商店 — what this account has bought from the current rotations.
   *
   * Only the PURCHASES are saved. The rotation itself is derived from the clock
   * (constants/limitedShop.ts), so there is nothing about the shelf to persist and no stored copy
   * that could go stale against what the shop actually shows.
   */
  limitedShop?: LimitedShopState;
  /**
   * 每週任務 — 玩家自己設的每週健康目標。
   *
   * 一個巢狀 map，理由跟 {@link workoutRewards} 與 {@link islandState} 完全一樣：它在
   * firestore.rules 裡是一個 key、在每一份寫入白名單裡是一個項目，所以多一種目標類型是
   * constants/weeklyTasks.ts 裡的一列，不是一次 schema 變更加一次 rules 部署。
   *
   * 只存**定義**。目前進度永遠是從 `workout_logs` 重新算出來的（constants/weeklyTasks.ts），所
   * 以存檔裡沒有任何一個可能跟實際運動紀錄不同步的進度數字。
   *
   * 在這個功能之前寫下的每一份存檔都沒有這個欄位，而那跟一個還沒建過任務的新玩家是同一件事：兩
   * 者都沒有任務。不需要 migration。
   */
  weeklyTasks?: WeeklyTaskState;
}

export interface ShopItem {
  itemId: string;
  name: string;
  category: ItemCategory;
  price: number;
  /**
   * 稀有度 — mirrors `ItemDefinition.rarity`, and required for the same reason it is required
   * there: every item in the game has a tier, and a shape that lets one be built without a tier is
   * a shape that eventually ships one. See constants/rarity.ts.
   */
  rarity: Rarity;
  modelPath: string;
  previewImage?: string;
  isOwned?: boolean;
}

export interface WorkoutLog {
  logId: string;
  userId: string;
  type: string;
  duration: number;
  counts: number;
  calories: number;
  goldEarned: number;
  timestamp: string;
}

export interface AppSettings {
  userId: string;
  bgmVolume: number;
  /**
   * Volume of the looping outdoor ambience (the surf), 0..1. Separate from `bgmVolume` on
   * purpose: it is not music, and muting the music must not silence the sea.
   * Optional — profiles saved before this existed read as `undefined` and default to 1, which
   * is exactly the level they were already hearing.
   */
  ambienceVolume?: number;
  isMuted: boolean;
  voiceGuideEnabled: boolean;
  warmupEnabled: boolean;
  currentTrackIndex?: number;
  /** YouTube music mode is on: the local synth BGM steps aside and the embedded player drives audio. */
  youtubeMusicEnabled?: boolean;
  /** The last link the user played, verbatim, so it can be restored after a reload. */
  youtubePlaylistId?: string;
  /** Most-recent-first list of previously played links (capped, see SettingsView). */
  youtubeRecentLinks?: string[];
  /**
   * 管理員測試模式 — gates every Admin/QA-only feature in the app (see
   * hooks/useAdminMode.ts and constants/adminFeatures.ts for the registry).
   * Persisted per-account like any other setting; OFF for every player by
   * default and never implied by anything else (env, build mode, etc.).
   */
  adminTestMode?: boolean;
  /**
   * 擁有全部商品 — the 管理員測試模式 switch that hands over the whole shop catalog
   * (UI/settings/AdminOwnAllItemsRow.tsx, context/useShopActions.ts).
   *
   * A stored switch rather than a fired-and-forgotten button because it is one: ON means 「this
   * save is in the everything-owned test state」, and it stays true across reloads so the row can
   * show which state the save is in. It is also what makes turning it OFF meaningful — see
   * {@link adminGrantedItemIds}.
   *
   * Absent/false for every player, and it can only ever be seen while `adminTestMode` is on.
   */
  adminOwnAllItems?: boolean;
  /**
   * The receipt for {@link adminOwnAllItems}: exactly which catalog ids that switch put into the
   * inventory when it was turned on.
   *
   * Stored so that switching OFF can take back what the switch gave and NOTHING else. Without it
   * the only available "off" would be either a lie (leave everything, pretend it's off) or a
   * wipe (remove every catalog id, eating the player's own purchases along with the grant).
   *
   * It lives in settings next to the switch rather than on the profile because it is bookkeeping
   * ABOUT the switch, not part of the save's contents — and keeping it out of the profile leaves
   * the actual grant/revoke write touching `inventory` alone, which firestore.rules already
   * allows without a ruleset change.
   */
  adminGrantedItemIds?: string[];
  /**
   * 多餘碎片自動轉換成抽獎券 — see constants/fragments.ts.
   *
   * ON (and `undefined`, for every save that predates it) means a fragment granted onto a full stack,
   * or a stack stranded by buying its item with gold, is converted into 抽獎券 at the standard rate.
   * OFF means those fragments are simply not kept — which is what the setting's own copy says, because
   * the alternative reading ("they are stored somewhere else") would be a lie about a currency.
   */
  fragmentOverflowToTickets?: boolean;
}

export enum View {
  HOME = 'home',
  FITNESS = 'fitness',
  /**
   * 健康 — 玩家的運動數據、每週任務與活動紀錄。
   *
   * 2026-09-20 之前這個畫面叫「追蹤」，enum 成員叫 `TRACKER`，值是 `'tracker'`。名字連同值一起
   * 改掉而不是只改按鈕文字，是因為這個值沒有離開過記憶體：它不寫進存檔、不出現在網址、也不在任
   * 何 API 合約裡（`currentView` 只是 AppContext 的一個 state）。留著一個跟畫面上四個字都對不
   * 起來的內部名字，只會讓下一個人先去找「追蹤」在哪裡。
   *
   * 沒有跟著改的是資料那一側：Firestore 的 `workout_logs` 集合、`WorkoutLog` 這個型別、以及
   * firestore.rules 裡的對應規則全部原樣保留。那些名字寫在每一份既有存檔裡，改名等於一次資料遷
   * 移，而它們本來就叫「運動紀錄」而不是「追蹤」—— 名字沒有錯，不需要動。
   */
  HEALTH = 'health',
  SETTINGS = 'settings',
  SHOP = 'shop',
  /**
   * 限時商店 — 一家獨立的店，不是 {@link View.SHOP} 裡的一個分頁。
   *
   * 它有自己的商品池（constants/limitedShop.ts）、自己的購買寫入與自己的存檔紀錄，而且它的
   * 商品**不會**出現在普通商店裡（constants/distribution.ts）。做成一個 View 而不是商店裡的一
   * 個 modal，是因為玩家要找的是「那家會換商品的店」，而不是「商店裡那個會換商品的分類」——
   * 藏在另一家店裡面的店，玩家每次都得先想起來它在哪裡。
   *
   * **它沒有路牌入口，而且是刻意的。** 路牌上那一格已經拿掉了：現在的入口是島邊那位搭船來的
   * 旅行商人（constants/merchants.ts），玩家走過去跟他互動才開得了這個畫面。切到這個 view 的
   * 路只有一條 —— UI/MerchantSession.tsx，而它會先確認商人還在。所以「商人不在島上時商店開不
   * 了」不是靠每個入口各自記得檢查，是因為只有一個入口。
   */
  LIMITED_SHOP = 'limited_shop',
  DRESSING_ROOM = 'dressing_room',
  BUILDING_INTERIOR = 'building_interior',
  BUILD_MODE = 'build_mode',
}

export enum FitnessCategory {
  AEROBIC = 'aerobic',
  WARMUP = 'warmup',
}

export enum CameraMode {
  THIRD_PERSON = 'third_person',
  SECOND_PERSON = 'second_person',
}

export enum WeatherType {
  SUNNY = 'sunny',
  RAINY = 'rainy',
  STORM = 'storm',
  SNOW = 'snow',
  TWILIGHT = 'twilight',
  /**
   * 深夜 — the one member that is a time of day rather than a kind of weather,
   * which is why the settings block it lives in is called 島嶼狀態 and not
   * 島嶼天氣. Its moon, stars and shooting stars are Three/NightSky.tsx; every
   * other per-weather table below treats it like any other entry.
   */
  MIDNIGHT = 'midnight',
}
```

## src/utils/categoryUtils.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { ALL_ITEMS, getItemById } from '../constants/items';
import { MAIN_SHOP_CATALOG, type DistributionChannel } from '../constants/distribution';

/**
 * The catalog taxonomy — one table that every surface in the game reads.
 *
 * Two tiers:
 *  - {@link MainSection}: 人物 / 室內 / 室外 / 寵物 / NPC. This is the shelf a player goes to — how
 *    the catalog is *browsed*.
 *  - {@link DisplayCategory.placementScope}: which world a category's goods are put down in. It
 *    DEFAULTS to the main section, which is right for almost everything, and is stated separately
 *    for the shelves where 「我去哪裡找它」 and 「它放在哪裡」 have different answers — see that
 *    field. Indoor furniture and outdoor decorations are still separated by construction; no screen
 *    re-guesses either question from an id prefix or a name keyword.
 *  - {@link DisplayCategory}: the sub-category chips inside a section (客廳 / 臥室 / 花園 …).
 *
 * Each category also declares its {@link CategoryKind}, which is what the shop, the inventory
 * and the placement systems branch on instead of per-item special cases:
 *  - `wearable`  — owned once, equipped on the avatar (dressing room).
 *  - `placeable` — a physical object. Stacks: each copy bought can be placed once, and placing
 *                  one consumes a copy (see utils/inventory.ts).
 *  - `applied`   — owned once, applied to something that already exists (a room's floor/wall,
 *                  the Home's exterior). Never placed, never stacked.
 *  - `consumable`— 特殊卡牌: held in the backpack, stacks like `placeable`, but is SPENT rather
 *                  than put down, so it never reaches a placement flow. Split from `placeable`
 *                  precisely so it cannot: `canPlaceItem` (utils/inventory.ts) asks for that kind
 *                  by name, and a 抽獎券 must never become an object standing on the island.
 *                  Stacking is the half it does share — buying a second ticket has to mean
 *                  holding two.
 *
 * Adding a category here makes it show up in the shop, the outdoor build rail and the indoor
 * furniture drawer at once. Adding an item is one `shopCategory` field in constants/items.ts.
 */

/** The top-level tabs every item rolls up into. Also the item's placement scope. */
export type MainSection = 'PERSON' | 'INDOOR' | 'OUTDOOR' | 'PET' | 'NPC' | 'CARD';

/** How the game treats the items in a category — see the file doc above. */
export type CategoryKind = 'wearable' | 'placeable' | 'applied' | 'consumable';

export interface MainSectionMeta {
  id: MainSection;
  label: string;
  /**
   * Optional. A section with no glyph renders as its label alone — which is the right answer
   * for a section whose art has not been drawn yet, because the alternative is a placeholder
   * icon sitting in the primary navigation looking like a permanent decision. NPC is the one
   * such section today.
   */
  iconName?: string;
}

/** Top-level tab metadata — order here is the order tabs render in. */
export const MAIN_SECTIONS: MainSectionMeta[] = [
  { id: 'PERSON', label: '人物外觀', iconName: 'UserCircle2' },
  { id: 'INDOOR', label: '室內', iconName: 'Sofa' },
  { id: 'OUTDOOR', label: '室外', iconName: 'Palmtree' },
  // 寵物 ships with its 狗/貓/鳥 chips but no items yet — the shop shows its empty state under
  // each until pets are added to constants/items.ts with the matching `shopCategory`.
  { id: 'PET', label: '寵物', iconName: 'PawPrint' },
  // NPC — 島上的居民，跟寵物分開的一層：寵物是玩家帶在身邊的動物，NPC 是住在島上、
  // 各有職務的角色。兩者都是「買一次就擁有」，但把他們塞進寵物頁會讓那一頁同時是
  // 「我的動物」和「島上的人」，玩家就沒地方可以直覺地找 NPC 了。
  //
  // 沒有 iconName：造型還沒定案之前，主分頁上掛一個問號等於把「還沒想好」做成常駐導覽的
  // 一部分。商品卡上的問號是另一回事 —— 那是在講「這件商品長什麼樣還沒公開」，是內容；
  // 分頁圖示講的是「這一類是什麼」，那件事我們早就知道了，寫成 NPC 兩個字就夠。
  { id: 'NPC', label: 'NPC' },
  // 特殊卡牌 — the only section whose goods are not a THING in the world. Everything above is
  // owned and then worn, placed or applied; a card is held and then spent, and that difference
  // is the whole reason it is a section rather than a shelf inside 人物外觀 or 室外: a player
  // looking for 「我手上有什麼可以用」 has nowhere else to look, and filing tickets beside hats
  // would put a consumable in a drawer whose every other row is permanent.
  { id: 'CARD', label: '特殊卡牌', iconName: 'Layers' },
];

export interface DisplayCategory {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  iconName: string;
  mainSection: MainSection;
  kind: CategoryKind;
  /**
   * One line telling the player what belongs on this shelf, shown by the shared `CategoryNote`
   * (UI/CategoryTabs.tsx) wherever a category row is.
   *
   * WHY IT IS DATA AND NOT COPY IN THE SHOP. Two shelves in 人物外觀 sell what a player would
   * describe with the same words — 配件 and 特殊飾品 are both "small things you put on" — and the
   * only thing separating them was that the second one's goods happened to move once you had
   * bought them. A label cannot say that, an icon cannot say that, and a player standing in front
   * of two racks of jewellery should not have to buy one to find out. So each category says what
   * it is, once, here: the shop, the dressing room and anything added later all read the same
   * sentence, and a new category cannot ship without one.
   *
   * Say what is IN the shelf and how it differs from its neighbour. Not a slogan.
   */
  description: string;
  /**
   * Optional QVersionIcon category artwork key, used by the big category tiles in the indoor
   * furniture drawer. Falls back to the lucide `iconName` when absent, so a new category never
   * has to wait for hand-drawn art to exist.
   */
  artKey?: string;
  /**
   * Kept out of the section chip rows {@link getCategoriesFor} builds, so only a screen that
   * names the category outright shows it. Every other lookup here still resolves it, which is
   * what separates this from simply leaving the category out of the table.
   *
   * 更衣室's 寵物 rack is the only one: it is a slot on that screen alone, and the shop sells
   * pets from its own 寵物 section instead — a chip in 人物外觀 would be a second, contradictory
   * answer to where pets live.
   */
  standalone?: boolean;
  /**
   * 哪一家店賣這個貨架上的東西。沒寫的時候是 `main-shop`，也就是幾乎全部。
   *
   * 一個貨架的所有商品必然出自同一家店（一個 `shopCategory` 就是一個貨架），所以販售通道是
   * 貨架的屬性而不是每件商品各自的畫面判斷。這個欄位存在的理由是**分頁列**：特殊飾品 只在
   * 限時商店賣，所以普通商店的人物外觀分頁列裡不該有一個點進去永遠是空的「特殊飾品」chip。
   *
   * 注意它**不是**排除商品的機制 —— 那是 constants/distribution.ts 的
   * `MAIN_SHOP_CATALOG` / `LIMITED_SHOP_ITEMS` 在做的事，而且是以「商品」為單位。這一格只決定
   * 「哪家店的分頁列裡有這個 chip」，所以更衣室的衣架（顯示的是**已擁有**的東西，跟哪裡買的
   * 無關）仍然拿得到完整的分類清單 —— 見 {@link getCategoriesFor} 與
   * {@link getShopCategoriesFor} 的分工。
   */
  channel?: DistributionChannel;
  /**
   * Which world this category's goods are PUT DOWN in, when that is not the section they are
   * browsed in. Absent — which is every category but one — means the two are the same.
   *
   * The two questions are 「我去哪裡找它」 and 「它放在哪裡」, and for almost the whole catalog they
   * have the same answer, which is why they shared one field for so long. 寵物窩 is where they
   * come apart: a player looking for one goes to 寵物, because it is a thing for their pet — but it
   * is an object that stands on the island, and the island's build rail is built from the
   * PLACEABLE categories of the outdoor world. Filed under 寵物 with no scope it would be a piece
   * of furniture the player owns and can never put down; filed under 室外 it is correct and
   * unfindable.
   *
   * So the shelf follows the player and the scope follows the object. Every rail asks
   * {@link getPlacementCategoriesIn}, never the section directly, which is what makes an INDOOR
   * pet bed later a one-line change here rather than a bug report about a basket that cannot be
   * placed.
   */
  placementScope?: MainSection;
  /**
   * What to say under 「目前該分類尚無商品」 when this shelf is empty.
   *
   * A shelf can be empty for two very different reasons and the generic line cannot tell them
   * apart: 寵物 is empty because the animals have not been drawn yet (「來晚了，再等等」), while
   * 抽獎券 is empty because tickets are not bought at all (「你找錯地方了」). A player who reads
   * the same sentence in both places learns nothing from either.
   *
   * Optional, and deliberately a field rather than a branch in ShopView: the shop must not grow
   * an `if (categoryId === '…')`, which is the same rule the reward pools live under
   * (docs/economy.md 三). A category with nothing special to say renders the bare title exactly
   * as before.
   */
  emptyNote?: string;
}

// Adding a new category here automatically shows up under its main tab everywhere (shop
// catalog, owned-items drawer, dressing room, build rail, furniture drawer) — no other file
// needs to change.
export const DISPLAY_CATEGORIES: DisplayCategory[] = [
  // --- 人物外觀 ---

const CATEGORY_BY_ID = new Map(DISPLAY_CATEGORIES.map(c => [c.id, c]));

export function getDisplayCategory(categoryId: string): DisplayCategory | undefined {
  return CATEGORY_BY_ID.get(categoryId);
}

/**
 * Categories belonging to a main section, optionally narrowed to certain kinds. `standalone`
 * categories are excluded — a screen that wants one appends it to this list itself.
 */
export function getCategoriesFor(mainSection: MainSection, kinds?: CategoryKind[]): DisplayCategory[] {
  return DISPLAY_CATEGORIES.filter(
    c => !c.standalone && c.mainSection === mainSection && (!kinds || kinds.includes(c.kind))
  );
}

/**
 * The shop/display category an item belongs to. Declared by the item itself
 * (constants/items.ts), so this is a lookup rather than a chain of id-prefix and name-keyword
 * guesses that every screen used to re-implement slightly differently.
 */
export function getItemDisplayCategory(itemId: string): string | undefined {
  return getItemById(itemId)?.shopCategory;
}

/** The category record for an item, or undefined for an unknown/removed item id. */
export function getItemCategoryMeta(itemId: string): DisplayCategory | undefined {
  const categoryId = getItemDisplayCategory(itemId);
  return categoryId ? CATEGORY_BY_ID.get(categoryId) : undefined;
}

/** How the item behaves — see {@link CategoryKind}. Unknown items are treated as wearables. */
export function getItemKind(itemId: string): CategoryKind {
  return getItemCategoryMeta(itemId)?.kind ?? 'wearable';
}

/** The section an item is BROWSED in — which shop tab it sits under. */
export function getItemSection(itemId: string): MainSection | undefined {
  return getItemCategoryMeta(itemId)?.mainSection;
}

/**
 * Which world a category's goods are put down in — its {@link DisplayCategory.placementScope} when
 * it declares one, and its section otherwise.
 *
 * One function so the default lives in exactly one place. A rail that wrote
 * `c.placementScope ?? c.mainSection` itself would be the second copy of that rule, and the first
 * one to be forgotten is the one that silently drops a shelf out of a build menu.
 */
export function getCategoryPlacementScope(category: DisplayCategory): MainSection {
  return category.placementScope ?? category.mainSection;
}

/**
 * Where an item may be placed: `INDOOR` items only appear in the house's furniture drawer,
 * `OUTDOOR` items only on the island's build rail. This is the single rule that keeps the two
 * catalogs from mixing — and it is deliberately NOT the same question as which tab sells it, which
 * is what {@link getItemSection} answers.
 */
export function getItemPlacementScope(itemId: string): MainSection | undefined {
  const category = getItemCategoryMeta(itemId);
  return category ? getCategoryPlacementScope(category) : undefined;
}

/**
 * The categories a build rail is built from: everything put down in `scope`, whatever tab it is
 * sold under. The island's rail and the house's furniture drawer both ask this rather than
 * filtering on the section, which is what lets a shelf be browsed in one place and placed in
 * another (see {@link DisplayCategory.placementScope}).
 */
export function getPlacementCategoriesIn(scope: MainSection, kinds?: CategoryKind[]): DisplayCategory[] {
  return DISPLAY_CATEGORIES.filter(
    c => !c.standalone && getCategoryPlacementScope(c) === scope && (!kinds || kinds.includes(c.kind))
  );
}

/** First category of a placement scope — what a build rail opens on. */
export function getFirstPlacementCategoryId(
  scope: MainSection,
  kinds?: CategoryKind[],
): string | undefined {
  return getPlacementCategoriesIn(scope, kinds)[0]?.id;
}

/**
 * The chip row ONE STOREFRONT shows for a section — the categories that shop actually sells.
 *
 * Split from {@link getCategoriesFor} rather than replacing it, because the two answer different
 * questions and both are asked. This one is 「這家店的分頁列有哪些」 (the shop catalog); the other
 * is 「這一區總共有哪些分類」 (the dressing room's racks, which list what the player OWNS and must
 * keep showing 特殊飾品 whether or not the ordinary shop sells one).
 *
 * Defaulting to `main-shop` is what makes this a no-op for every category that has never had to
 * think about it — see {@link DisplayCategory.channel}.
 */
export function getShopCategoriesFor(
  mainSection: MainSection,
  channel: DistributionChannel = 'main-shop',
  kinds?: CategoryKind[],
): DisplayCategory[] {
  return getCategoriesFor(mainSection, kinds).filter(c => (c.channel ?? 'main-shop') === channel);
}

/**
 * The SECTIONS one storefront has anything to show — its top-tier tab row.
 *
 * The sibling of {@link getShopCategoriesFor}, one tier up, and needed for the same reason: with
 * every 特殊卡牌 shelf moved to the 限時小攤, the ordinary shop's 特殊卡牌 tab would open onto a
 * section with no chips and no goods. A tab that leads nowhere is worse than an absent one — the
 * player reads it as broken rather than as 「那不在這裡賣」.
 *
 * Order follows {@link MAIN_SECTIONS}, so removing a section never reshuffles the rest.
 */
export function getShopMainSections(
  channel: DistributionChannel = 'main-shop',
): MainSectionMeta[] {
  return MAIN_SECTIONS.filter(section => getShopCategoriesFor(section.id, channel).length > 0);
}

/** First category of a section that `channel` actually sells — what a shop's tab switch selects. */
export function getFirstShopCategoryId(
  mainSection: MainSection,
  channel: DistributionChannel = 'main-shop',
  kinds?: CategoryKind[],
): string | undefined {
  return getShopCategoriesFor(mainSection, channel, kinds)[0]?.id;
}

/**
 * Every item in a display category, in catalog order.
 *
 * The ORDINARY SHOP's catalog (constants/distribution.ts), not `ALL_ITEMS`: this is what the shop
 * grid, the outdoor build rail and the indoor furniture drawer are built from, so a 限時商店
 * exclusive cannot reach any of them. A surface that genuinely wants every definition — the
 * wardrobe, an ownership check, the avatar's resolver — reads `ALL_ITEMS` directly and says so.
 */
export function getItemsInCategory(categoryId: string) {
  return MAIN_SHOP_CATALOG.filter(item => item.shopCategory === categoryId);
}

/** Every item in a category, whatever channel sells it. For ownership-driven screens. */
export function getAllItemsInCategory(categoryId: string) {
  return ALL_ITEMS.filter(item => item.shopCategory === categoryId);
}

/** Human-readable category name for an item, for inventory rows and confirm dialogs. */
export function getItemCategoryLabel(itemId: string): string {
  return getItemCategoryMeta(itemId)?.label ?? '其他';
}

/**
 * Items applied to something the player already owns rather than placed as a new object — the
 * shop renders 已解鎖/使用中 for these instead of a placement flow.
 */
export function isApplyOnOwnCategory(displayCategoryId: string): boolean {
  return CATEGORY_BY_ID.get(displayCategoryId)?.kind === 'applied';
}

/** First category of a section — what a tab switch selects. */
export function getFirstCategoryId(mainSection: MainSection, kinds?: CategoryKind[]): string | undefined {
  return getCategoriesFor(mainSection, kinds)[0]?.id;
}

/**
 * Narrows a persisted/received category id to one that still exists in the table *and* is
 * reachable from a section's chip row. `standalone` ids fall back: the id this resolves is
 * `last_selected_category`, which the shop restores into a row that never contains them.
 */
export function resolveCategoryId(
  candidate: string | null | undefined,
  fallback: string,
  /**
   * Narrows to the categories one storefront sells. The shop passes `main-shop`, so a player whose
   * remembered chip was 特殊飾品 — a real, valid category that the ordinary shop stopped selling
   * when the 限時商店 became its own shop — opens on 帽子 instead of on an empty grid. Omitted by
   * the dressing room, which restores a rack of OWNED things and does not care who sold them.
   */
  channel?: DistributionChannel,
): string {
  const found = candidate ? CATEGORY_BY_ID.get(candidate) : undefined;
  if (!found || found.standalone) return fallback;
  if (channel && (found.channel ?? 'main-shop') !== channel) return fallback;
  return found.id;
}
```

## src/utils/debugOverrides.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * 測試用覆寫 — force a shop/inventory state for a session without touching the save.
 *
 * Why this exists: the storefront has states that only appear when you do NOT own something —
 * the 購買 button, the 經驗值 lock, the rarity treatment on a card you can't have yet. Once an
 * account has bought the item those states are unreachable, and the only ways back were editing
 * the player's Firestore document by hand or the 清空裝備 admin button, which wipes every
 * purchase, every worn item and every placed piece of furniture to inspect one card.
 *
 * Read once from the URL at load:
 *
 *   ?unown=pet-dog-shiba            treat that item as never bought
 *   ?unown=pet-dog-shiba,hat-beret  several, comma separated
 *   ?rarity=item-42:epic            render that item's card on a tier it does not have
 *   ?rarity=a:epic,b:mythic         several, comma separated
 *
 * `?rarity=` exists because the top of the ladder is deliberately scarce — 神話 is one item in the
 * whole game and 史詩 is capped at 12% of the catalog — so most cards can never be seen on those
 * tiers without buying the handful that carry them. It is also the quickest way to see the purchase reveal 史詩
 * and above trigger, on an item whose price you are not about to pay.
 *
 * Deliberately NOT behind 管理員測試模式 (unlike the features in constants/adminFeatures.ts):
 * admin mode is a setting stored on the account, and reading it needs React context, while this
 * has to answer inside `getOwnedCount` — a pure function the whole app calls. It is safe to leave
 * ungated because the override can only ever take ownership AWAY. It grants nothing, it is not
 * persisted, and a player who finds it can do no more than hide their own purchases until they
 * reload. Anything that could grant an item must not be added here.
 *
 * `?rarity=` passes the same test for the same reason, and it is worth spelling out because a
 * frame that says "mythic" sounds like it ought to be worth something: it changes the card's
 * PAINT and nothing else. Price, stock, ownership, unlock conditions and what the purchase
 * actually writes are all read from constants/items.ts, which this never touches — a player who
 * puts 神話 on a 600g budgie has an expensive-looking budgie and 600g less.
 *
 * That safety argument survived rarity becoming REQUIRED on every item, and it is worth checking
 * rather than assuming, because the tier now feeds a REWARD POOL (constants/rewardPools.ts) as
 * well as a card. Pools are resolved from `ALL_ITEMS` — the catalog — and never from this
 * override, so a faked 神話 cannot move an item in or out of a pool, and cannot change what a
 * reward hands over. If that ever stops being true, this file has to be re-examined before the
 * feature that changed it ships.
 */

import { DEFAULT_RARITY, Rarity, RARITY_SPECS } from '../constants/rarity';

function readList(param: string): ReadonlySet<string> {
  // Guarded for non-browser callers — the audit scripts in scripts/ import the catalog helpers
  // under tsx, where there is no `location`.
  if (typeof window === 'undefined' || !window.location) return new Set();
  const raw = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get(param);
  if (!raw) return new Set();
  return new Set(raw.split(',').map(id => id.trim()).filter(Boolean));
}

/** Item ids to report as unowned this session. Empty in every normal load. */
export const UNOWNED_OVERRIDE: ReadonlySet<string> = readList('unown');

/**
 * `id:tier` pairs from `?rarity=`. Unknown tier names are dropped rather than passed through —
 * an unrecognised value would reach `RARITY_SPECS[...]` as undefined and crash the aura, and a
 * debug switch that white-screens the shop on a typo is worse than no debug switch.
 */
function readRarityPairs(): ReadonlyMap<string, Rarity> {
  const pairs = new Map<string, Rarity>();
  for (const entry of readList('rarity')) {
    const [id, tier] = entry.split(':').map(part => part.trim());
    if (id && tier && tier in RARITY_SPECS) pairs.set(id, tier as Rarity);
  }
  return pairs;
}

export const RARITY_OVERRIDE: ReadonlyMap<string, Rarity> = readRarityPairs();

/**
 * The tier a card should be painted in — the item's own, unless this session is overriding it.
 *
 * Every surface that draws a rarity goes through this rather than reading `item.rarity` directly,
 * so the override reaches the shop card, the collection list, the build rail, the dressing room
 * AND the purchase celebration from one place. Reading the field straight is the bug this exists
 * to prevent: it works, and then the one screen that did it is the one screen the override
 * silently doesn't cover.
 *
 * Returns a `Rarity`, never `undefined`. Every item in the catalog is graded now
 * (constants/rarity.ts), so 「這件商品沒有稀有度」 is no longer a state any caller has to handle —
 * which is what let every `rarity ? … : …` branch come out of the shop, the wardrobe and the build
 * rail. The parameter still accepts an OPTIONAL `rarity` so a caller holding a partially-built item
 * (a test fixture, a preview) still type-checks; it falls back to {@link DEFAULT_RARITY}.
 */
export const getItemRarity = (item: { id: string; rarity?: Rarity }): Rarity =>
  RARITY_OVERRIDE.get(item.id) ?? item.rarity ?? DEFAULT_RARITY;

/** Whether any override is active, for the on-screen notice that says so. */
export const HAS_DEBUG_OVERRIDE = UNOWNED_OVERRIDE.size > 0 || RARITY_OVERRIDE.size > 0;

```

## src/utils/inventory.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { UserProfile } from '../types';
import { getItemKind } from './categoryUtils';
import { UNOWNED_OVERRIDE } from './debugOverrides';

/**
 * The Inventory System — one definition of "how many of this do I own, and how many are still
 * free to place".
 *
 * `profile.inventory` is a flat list of item ids where a **placeable** item appears once per
 * copy bought, and everything else (wearables, floors/walls, house styles) appears at most once.
 * Which of those two an item is comes from its category kind (utils/categoryUtils.ts), never
 * from an id prefix.
 *
 * Stock is derived rather than mutated: `available = owned − placed`, counting placements on the
 * island *and* inside the house, because one bought copy is one object in the world wherever it
 * ends up. Deriving it means putting an object down, moving it, retrieving it and buying another
 * can never disagree with each other — there is no second counter to keep in sync.
 */

/**
 * Items that stack — one inventory entry per copy bought. Two kinds do:
 *  - `placeable`, where each copy is one object you can put down;
 *  - `consumable` (特殊卡牌), where each copy is one use you can spend.
 * Everything else (wearables, floors/walls, house styles, pets, NPCs) is own-once.
 */
export function isStackableItem(itemId: string): boolean {
  const kind = getItemKind(itemId);
  return kind === 'placeable' || kind === 'consumable';
}

/** Total copies bought (1 = owned, for non-stacking items). */
export function getOwnedCount(profile: UserProfile | null | undefined, itemId: string): number {
  // ?unown=<id> — a test-only override that hides a purchase for the session so the shop's
  // not-yet-bought states can be inspected on an account that already owns the item. It hooks in
  // HERE, at the single definition of ownership, so every screen agrees the item is unowned
  // rather than the shop card saying one thing and the dressing room another. See
  // utils/debugOverrides.ts, including why it can only ever take ownership away.
  if (UNOWNED_OVERRIDE.has(itemId)) return 0;

  const inventory = profile?.inventory || [];
  if (!isStackableItem(itemId)) return inventory.includes(itemId) ? 1 : 0;
  return inventory.filter(id => id === itemId).length;
}

export function ownsItem(profile: UserProfile | null | undefined, itemId: string): boolean {
  return getOwnedCount(profile, itemId) > 0;
}

/** Copies currently standing somewhere — island placements plus interior placements. */
export function getPlacedCount(profile: UserProfile | null | undefined, itemId: string): number {
  const island = profile?.islandPlacements || [];
  const interior = profile?.interiorData?.placements || [];
  return (
    island.filter(p => p.itemId === itemId).length +
    interior.filter(p => p.itemId === itemId).length
  );
}

/**
 * Copies left in the backpack. Clamped at zero so a legacy profile whose seeded placements
 * predate the stock model can still never read as "negative stock" in the UI — the
 * reconciliation below is what actually repairs those.
 */
export function getAvailableStock(profile: UserProfile | null | undefined, itemId: string): number {
  if (!isStackableItem(itemId)) return ownsItem(profile, itemId) ? 1 : 0;
  return Math.max(0, getOwnedCount(profile, itemId) - getPlacedCount(profile, itemId));
}

/**
 * Whether a *new* copy can be put down right now. Moving an existing one never consumes stock.
 *
 * Asks for `placeable` by name rather than reusing {@link isStackableItem}: stacking and being
 * placeable stopped being the same fact when 特殊卡牌 arrived. A card stacks — you can hold five
 * 抽獎券 — but there is no flow that stands one on the island, so the stacking test alone would
 * have quietly answered yes for it.
 */
export function canPlaceItem(profile: UserProfile | null | undefined, itemId: string): boolean {
  return getItemKind(itemId) === 'placeable' && getAvailableStock(profile, itemId) > 0;
}

/**
 * Tops the inventory up so it accounts for everything already standing in the world.
 *
 * Placements used to be created without a matching inventory entry (a new player's preset living
 * room, an expansion room's auto-decorated furniture), which under the derived-stock rule above
 * would read as "you own fewer than you have placed" and silently deny a purchase's worth of
 * placements. This grants the missing copies once, so `owned ≥ placed` holds for every profile
 * from then on.
 *
 * Pure and idempotent: returns null when nothing is missing, so a healthy profile causes no
 * write. The caller decides whether to persist it.
 */
export function reconcileInventoryStock(profile: UserProfile): string[] | null {
  const inventory = profile.inventory || [];
  const placed = new Map<string, number>();

  for (const p of [...(profile.islandPlacements || []), ...(profile.interiorData?.placements || [])]) {
    if (!isStackableItem(p.itemId)) continue;
    placed.set(p.itemId, (placed.get(p.itemId) || 0) + 1);
  }

  const missing: string[] = [];
  for (const [itemId, placedCount] of placed) {
    const owned = inventory.filter(id => id === itemId).length;
    for (let i = owned; i < placedCount; i++) missing.push(itemId);
  }

  return missing.length > 0 ? [...inventory, ...missing] : null;
}
```

## src/utils/level.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import type { UserProfile } from '../types';

/**
 * 等級 — derived from cumulative XP, never stored.
 *
 * `profile.level` is written once, as `1`, when a save is created (AppContext) and is not
 * incremented anywhere in the game: there is no level-up write, and there never was one. Every
 * XP-granting path — a workout (FitnessView), 摸狗, the 島上互動, the 管理員測試補給 — only ever
 * does `currentXp: increment(n)`. So the LV badge sat on 1 forever while the XP bar, which draws
 * `currentXp % 100`, wrapped silently back to the same place.
 *
 * That is the whole of 「按了加經驗值沒有反應」: the 測試補給 button grants exactly 1000 XP, which
 * is ten whole levels' worth, so `currentXp % 100` lands on the identical pixel it started on and
 * the stored level cannot move. The write landed every time; nothing on screen was capable of
 * showing it.
 *
 * Deriving it here rather than adding a level-up write keeps ONE source of truth (the cumulative
 * XP that utils/unlock.ts already measures item unlocks against) and means an old save shows its
 * real level the moment it loads, with nothing to migrate. The doc comment in utils/unlock.ts
 * already described the game this way — 「等級是由 currentXp / 100 推導出來的」 — so this is the
 * code catching up with the rule, not a new rule.
 */
export const XP_PER_LEVEL = 100;

/** LV.1 at 0 XP, LV.2 at 100 XP, and so on. Never below 1, never fractional. */
export function levelFromXp(xp: number | undefined | null): number {
  const safe = typeof xp === 'number' && Number.isFinite(xp) && xp > 0 ? xp : 0;
  return Math.floor(safe / XP_PER_LEVEL) + 1;
}

/** How far into the current level the player is, in XP — the 0–99 the progress bar draws. */
export function xpIntoLevel(xp: number | undefined | null): number {
  const safe = typeof xp === 'number' && Number.isFinite(xp) && xp > 0 ? xp : 0;
  return safe % XP_PER_LEVEL;
}

/** The player's level for display. Reads the profile so call sites don't each repeat the field. */
export function profileLevel(profile: Pick<UserProfile, 'currentXp'> | null | undefined): number {
  return levelFromXp(profile?.currentXp);
}
```
