## src/utils/placementRules.ts

```ts
/**
 * Placement rules and collision resolution utilities for buildings and island decorations.
 * Designed and structured for clear expandability and future integration with a real-time
 * dynamic grid/placement system.
 */

import { HouseStyleFootprint } from '../constants/houseStyles';
import { PLAYER_COLLIDER_RADIUS } from '../constants/characterRig';

/**
 * The player's Home as an obstacle these rules must route around.
 *
 * Structurally compatible with ResolvedHome (hooks/usePlayerHome.ts) but declared locally so
 * this module stays free of React/three imports and can keep being called from imperative
 * solvers. `null` means the Home hasn't been placed yet, in which case the whole island is free.
 */
export interface HomeObstacle {
  position: [number, number, number];
  rotation: number;
  footprint: HouseStyleFootprint;
}

/**
 * The player's collision radius — how far their centre is held off anything solid.
 *
 * One number for the whole game: the interior walls and furniture, the island's props, and the
 * Home's solid box all inflate by exactly this, so "how close can I get" is the same answer
 * everywhere. `characterMovement.ts` reads it rather than keeping its own 0.35.
 *
 * Re-exported from the rig rather than declared here, because it is a measurement of the
 * CHARACTER and this file is about placement. Keeping it with the rest of the character's
 * dimensions makes swapping the model one file to review instead of a search for whichever
 * number each system happened to keep — see PLAYER_COLLIDER_RADIUS in constants/characterRig.ts,
 * which also explains why the collider is deliberately NOT derived from the model's mesh.
 * The name stays: it reads correctly at every call site and the value has not changed.
 */
export const PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS = PLAYER_COLLIDER_RADIUS;

/**
 * The **solid** half-extents of a Home: its footprint inflated by the player's physical radius.
 *
 * A Home is a completely closed box — there is no walk-through doorway, since the interior is
 * entered through the "進入我的家" interaction rather than by stepping into the mesh. This is the
 * single definition of "how big is the thing the player cannot pass through", used by the walk
 * collision (resolveHomeCollision) and by the model when it needs to know where the player will
 * be stopped (HouseModel's perimeter fence).
 *
 * Inflating by the player's radius is what makes the wall feel solid rather than absorbent:
 * collision moves the avatar's *centre*, so a box at the raw footprint stops that centre on the
 * wall plane and leaves half the body buried in the building. The margin also clears the deepest
 * eave any style draws (halfWidth + 0.30, on the hip roof), so the player is never stopped by
 * thin air under an overhang, nor able to walk through one.
 *
 * Every House Style shares one footprint, so this yields one collision rule for all of them.
 */
export function getHomeSolidHalfExtents(footprint: HouseStyleFootprint): {
  halfWidth: number;
  halfDepth: number;
} {
  return {
    halfWidth: footprint.halfWidth + PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS,
    halfDepth: footprint.halfDepth + PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS,
  };
}

/**
 * Is this world XZ inside the Home's solid box, plus `margin`?
 *
 * Extracted from `isPlacementAllowed` below when the ground-cover scatter needed the same test:
 * a grass tuft has no business running the furniture solver's spiral search, but it absolutely
 * must not stand inside the house, and re-deriving "inside the house" from the footprint is how
 * two answers to one question get into a codebase.
 *
 * Evaluated in the Home's LOCAL space, so a rotated Home keeps a correctly-oriented footprint —
 * the fixed-slot houses this replaced were always axis-aligned and used raw world deltas.
 *
 * Note what it does NOT include: the door lane. That is a rule about REACHING the house, which
 * matters for anything the player has to walk up to and not at all for grass.
 */
export function isInsideHomeKeepOut(
  x: number,
  z: number,
  home: HomeObstacle | null,
  margin: number,
): boolean {
  if (!home) return false;
  const rx = x - home.position[0];
  const rz = z - home.position[2];
  const cos = Math.cos(-home.rotation);
  const sin = Math.sin(-home.rotation);
  const localX = rx * cos - rz * sin;
  const localZ = rx * sin + rz * cos;
  const solid = getHomeSolidHalfExtents(home.footprint);
  return Math.abs(localX) < solid.halfWidth + margin && Math.abs(localZ) < solid.halfDepth + margin;
}

/*
 * DELETED: getVisualBounds / getCollisionBounds / getObjectBounds.
 *
 * A pair of name-keyed size tables — `if (name === '木製平台') halfWidth = 2.0` and so on for ten
 * decorations — describing the same objects as three other tables elsewhere in the app, in three
 * different sets of numbers, and called by nothing. Every one of them was wrong: the platform's
 * real half-extent is 2.64, not the 2.0 declared here, because BUILDING items are drawn at 1.32x
 * scale and a hand-typed table cannot know that.
 *
 * Placement bounds are measured off the model now (lib/furniturePlacement.ts), and the rules that
 * consume them live in lib/placementSurfaces.ts.
 *
 * DELETED: validateWalkablePassageBetweenBuildings / ensureMinimumBuildingGap — rules about
 * keeping a corridor between two houses, from the two-house era. There is one Home.
 */

/**
 * The radius of the walkable, flat Grass Terrain disc (matches Avatar.tsx's getTerrainInfo
 * and Island.tsx's grass mesh). Natural decorations are placed at a fixed Y, so they must
 * stay within this flat region — the sand ring beyond it is sloped and would leave them
 * floating above or sunk below the actual surface.
 */
export function getGrassTerrainRadius(islandScale: number = 1.0): number {
  return 5.7 * islandScale;
}

/**
 * Check if a point lies on the flat Grass Terrain (not on the sloped sand, water, or open sea).
 */
export function isValidTerrainPosition(x: number, z: number, islandScale: number = 1.0): boolean {
  const dist = Math.sqrt(x * x + z * z);
  const grassRadius = getGrassTerrainRadius(islandScale);
  return dist < grassRadius - 0.4; // leave 0.4 units safety margin from the grass/sand edge
}

/**
 * Draws a uniformly-distributed random point within the circular Grass Terrain area
 * (not a bounding square), so every candidate starts out on valid island ground.
 */
export function getRandomGrassTerrainPoint(islandScale: number = 1.0, margin: number = 0.4): [number, number] {
  const radius = Math.max(0, getGrassTerrainRadius(islandScale) - margin);
  const r = Math.sqrt(Math.random()) * radius;
  const theta = Math.random() * Math.PI * 2;
  return [r * Math.cos(theta), r * Math.sin(theta)];
}

/**
 * Find the nearest valid placement for an object when squeezed out by the player's Home.
 * Performs a spiral radial search for a location that is far enough from the Home and its door.
 * Includes explicit rulechecks:
 * - Must be on walkable, safe land (no deep ocean water)
 * - Must not overlap the Home or block its entrance
 * - Must not overlap other major collidable objects
 *
 * The old "keep the corridor between the two houses clear" rule is gone with the two-house
 * layout it existed to protect - there is exactly one Home now, so there is no corridor.
 */
export function findNearestValidPlacement(
  name: string,
  desiredPosition: [number, number, number],
  home: HomeObstacle | null,
  islandScale: number = 1.0,
  otherObjects: Array<[number, number, number]> = []
): [number, number, number] {
  const [origX, origY, origZ] = desiredPosition;

  // If it's already perfectly valid, keep it!
  if (isPlacementAllowed(name, [origX, origY, origZ], home, islandScale, otherObjects)) {
    return [origX, origY, origZ];
  }

  // Spiral search parameters
  const step = 0.35;
  const maxRadius = 12.0;

  for (let r = step; r < maxRadius; r += step) {
    // Scan angles
    const angleDivider = Math.max(8, Math.floor(r * 4));
    for (let k = 0; k < angleDivider; k++) {
      const angle = (k * Math.PI * 2) / angleDivider;
      const scanX = origX + Math.cos(angle) * r;
      const scanZ = origZ + Math.sin(angle) * r;

      if (isPlacementAllowed(name, [scanX, origY, scanZ], home, islandScale, otherObjects)) {
        return [scanX, origY, scanZ];
      }
    }
  }

  // Fallback return if we somehow can't find anything better
  return [origX, origY, origZ];
}

/**
 * Picks a valid spawn point for a naturally-scattered decoration (flowers, rocks, etc.).
 * Instead of sampling a rectangular box and hoping the point lands on the island, this
 * draws points directly from the circular Grass Terrain area and re-rolls a fresh random
 * point whenever a candidate can't be resolved onto valid land — it never falls back to
 * spawning at an out-of-bounds position.
 */
export function findRandomValidPlacement(
  name: string,
  home: HomeObstacle | null,
  islandScale: number = 1.0,
  otherObjects: Array<[number, number, number]> = [],
  y: number = 0.35,
  maxAttempts: number = 40
): [number, number, number] {
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < maxAttempts; attempt++) {
    const [x, z] = getRandomGrassTerrainPoint(islandScale);
    const resolved = findNearestValidPlacement(
      name,
      [x, y, z],
      home,
      islandScale,
      otherObjects
    );

    if (isValidTerrainPosition(resolved[0], resolved[2], islandScale)) {
      return resolved;
    }
    // Otherwise the spiral search couldn't resolve this attempt onto valid land — re-roll.
  }

  // Guaranteed-safe last resort: the island center is always on grass terrain.
  return [0, y, 0];
}

/**
 * Inner rules-check function to validate placement constraints
 */
function isPlacementAllowed(
  name: string,
  pos: [number, number, number],
  home: HomeObstacle | null,
  islandScale: number,
  otherObjects: Array<[number, number, number]>
): boolean {
  const [x, y, z] = pos;

  // 1. Must be on valid terrestrial land
  if (!isValidTerrainPosition(x, z, islandScale)) {
    return false;
  }

  // 2. Must clear the player's Home and the lane in front of its door. Evaluated in the Home's
  //    local space so a rotated Home keeps a correctly-oriented footprint and approach path -
  //    the old fixed-slot houses were always axis-aligned, so this used raw world deltas.
  if (home) {
    const fp = home.footprint;
    const rx = x - home.position[0];
    const rz = z - home.position[2];
    const cos = Math.cos(-home.rotation);
    const sin = Math.sin(-home.rotation);
    const localX = rx * cos - rz * sin;
    const localZ = rx * sin + rz * cos;

    // Measured against the SOLID box, not the raw footprint: a prop dropped in the shell between
    // the wall and the player's stop line is unreachable, since collision holds the player out
    // past it. Small scattered flora may hug that line more closely than furniture-sized props.
    const safetyMargin = name.includes('Flora') || name.includes('Flower') ? 0.3 : 0.6;

    if (isInsideHomeKeepOut(x, z, home, safetyMargin)) {
      return false;
    }

    // Keep the approach to the front door walkable.
    const isAtDoorX = Math.abs(localX) < fp.doorLaneWidth + 0.05;
    const isAtDoorZ = localZ > fp.halfDepth * 0.6 && localZ < fp.doorOffsetZ + 1.2;
    if (isAtDoorX && isAtDoorZ) return false;
  }

  // 3. Must not overlap too closely with other mapped props
  for (const other of otherObjects) {
    const dx = x - other[0];
    const dz = z - other[2];
    const distSq = dx * dx + dz * dz;
    const minObjectDist = 0.5; // Avoid clustered duplicate overlaps
    if (distSq < minObjectDist * minObjectDist) {
      return false;
    }
  }

  return true;
}

/*
 * DELETED: resolveObjectOverlap — a no-op that returned its own argument, and `PlacedObject`,
 * the type it took. Overlap between placed objects is decided by the measured-box rule in
 * lib/placementSurfaces.ts.
 */

/**
 * How big the i-th outcrop is drawn — the `scale` on its dodecahedron mesh.
 *
 * Shared because the rock is drawn in Three/Island.tsx and WALKED ON in Three/characterMovement.ts,
 * and both need the same size. They each had their own copy of this expression, which is the kind
 * of duplication that stays correct right up until someone resizes the rocks in one of them.
 */
export const getRockScale = (i: number): number => (0.5 + (i % 3) * 0.2) * 0.5;

/**
 * Ratio of a regular dodecahedron's INSPHERE to the circumradius three.js builds it at
 * (`dodecahedronGeometry(1)` puts its vertices on the unit sphere).
 *
 * The rock's walkable surface uses the insphere rather than the circumsphere because the two
 * mistakes are not equal: the insphere is entirely inside the solid, so the feet may end up a
 * few centimetres INSIDE a rock — invisible — where the circumsphere would hold them the same
 * few centimetres above one, which is the thing that reads as broken.
 */
export const DODECAHEDRON_INSPHERE = 0.7946544722917661;

/**
 * Resolves rock positions dynamically using the placement rules to avoid overlapping the Home.
 */
export function getResolvedRockPositions(
  islandScale: number = 1.0,
  home: HomeObstacle | null = null
): [number, number, number][] {
  const baseRocks: [number, number, number][] = [
    [3.5, 0.2, 2.5],
    [-4, 0.3, 3],
    [2, 0.25, -4.5],
    [-3.8, 0.2, -3.2],
    [5, 0.1, 0.5],
    [-1.5, 0.2, 5.2],
    [0.5, 0.3, -5.5]
  ];
  
  const resolved: [number, number, number][] = [];
  
  for (const rock of baseRocks) {
    const desired: [number, number, number] = [rock[0] * islandScale, rock[1], rock[2] * islandScale];
    const res = findNearestValidPlacement(
      '大石塊',
      desired,
      home,
      islandScale,
      resolved // prevent rocks from nesting directly on each other
    );
    resolved.push(res);
  }
  
  return resolved;
}
```

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { UserProfile } from '../types';
import { getItemById, ItemDefinition } from '../constants/items';

/**
 * 經驗值解鎖 — the one rule for items the player earns instead of buys.
 *
 * Most of the shop is bought with gold. A few items are 獎勵 rather than 商品: they cost nothing,
 * and the only way to get one is to have trained enough. 柴犬 is the first, at 100 XP.
 *
 * Two deliberate choices worth keeping:
 *
 *  1. **The requirement is a threshold, never a cost.** Reaching it unlocks the item and the XP
 *     stays where it is. `profile.currentXp` is cumulative and the player's 等級 is derived from
 *     it (`currentXp / 100`, see TopBar/AccountPanel), so spending XP would silently demote the
 *     player — an unlock that costs you a level is a punishment, not a reward.
 *  2. **An XP item is still bought through the Shop System.** It goes through the same
 *     `purchaseItem` write, the same confirmation dialog and the same inventory, only at a price
 *     of 0 with this check in front of it. That keeps ownership in one place; the unlock rule is
 *     a gate on the storefront, not a second way to own things.
 *
 * Marking an item as XP-unlocked is one `xpUnlock:` field in constants/items.ts (plus `price: 0`).
 * Nothing may re-derive the requirement from a price, a category or an id.
 */

/** The player's cumulative XP — the number every requirement below is measured against. */
export function getPlayerXp(profile: UserProfile | null | undefined): number {
  return profile?.currentXp ?? 0;
}

/**
 * How much XP this item demands, or 0 when it is an ordinary gold purchase.
 * Takes either the definition or its id, so callers holding one don't have to look up the other.
 */
export function getXpRequirement(item: ItemDefinition | string | null | undefined): number {
  const def = typeof item === 'string' ? getItemById(item) : item;
  return def?.xpUnlock ?? 0;
}

/** Whether this item is gated on XP at all. */
export function isXpUnlockItem(item: ItemDefinition | string | null | undefined): boolean {
  return getXpRequirement(item) > 0;
}

/**
 * Locked = gated on XP *and* the player hasn't reached it yet. Ordinary items are never locked,
 * so a caller can ask this about any item and get the answer it expects.
 */
export function isXpLocked(
  profile: UserProfile | null | undefined,
  item: ItemDefinition | string | null | undefined,
): boolean {
  const required = getXpRequirement(item);
  return required > 0 && getPlayerXp(profile) < required;
}

/** How much more XP is needed, for the "還差 N 經驗值" copy. 0 once unlocked. */
export function getXpRemaining(
  profile: UserProfile | null | undefined,
  item: ItemDefinition | string | null | undefined,
): number {
  const required = getXpRequirement(item);
  if (required <= 0) return 0;
  return Math.max(0, required - getPlayerXp(profile));
}

/** Progress toward the requirement as 0–1, for the lock's progress bar. */
export function getXpUnlockProgress(
  profile: UserProfile | null | undefined,
  item: ItemDefinition | string | null | undefined,
): number {
  const required = getXpRequirement(item);
  if (required <= 0) return 1;
  return Math.min(1, getPlayerXp(profile) / required);
}
```

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { WeatherType } from '../types';

/**
 * Wind sway multipliers shared by every swaying-foliage effect in
 * IslandDecorations (coconut palm leaves, garden zone plants, scattered
 * flora) — previously the same STORM/RAINY/SNOW/TWILIGHT table was
 * copy-pasted independently in three places.
 */
export function getWeatherSwayFactors(weather: WeatherType): { speedMult: number; swayAmt: number } {
  switch (weather) {
    case WeatherType.STORM:
      return { speedMult: 2.8, swayAmt: 2.5 };
    case WeatherType.RAINY:
      return { speedMult: 1.5, swayAmt: 1.3 };
    case WeatherType.SNOW:
      return { speedMult: 0.3, swayAmt: 0.2 };
    case WeatherType.TWILIGHT:
      return { speedMult: 0.6, swayAmt: 0.6 };
    case WeatherType.MIDNIGHT:
      return { speedMult: 0.45, swayAmt: 0.45 };
    default:
      return { speedMult: 1.0, swayAmt: 1.0 };
  }
}
```

## src/utils/zFightAudit.ts

```ts
/**
 * @license
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

/**
 * Scene-graph audit for depth conflicts (z-fighting).
 *
 * ## Why this is a runtime check and not a lint rule
 *
 * Every model in this project is procedural: a mesh's real world-space position
 * is the product of its own `position` prop and every `group` scale/rotation
 * above it, several of which are computed at render time from the territory
 * level or the player's saved placements. Reading the JSX cannot tell you where
 * a mesh actually ends up, so a static check can only enforce *conventions*
 * (that is `scripts/audit-zfighting.mjs`). This one measures the real thing:
 * it walks the live scene, resolves world matrices, and reports every pair of
 * surfaces close enough to flicker.
 *
 * ## What counts as a finding
 *
 * A pair of meshes is reported when all of these hold:
 *
 *   - both are opaque and both write depth (a transparent, `depthWrite: false`
 *     layer such as the ocean's foam cannot z-fight - it is sorted, not
 *     depth-tested against its own kind);
 *   - neither carries `polygonOffset` (a decal declaring itself a decal is
 *     doing the right thing - see DECAL_DEPTH_BIAS in constants/terrain.ts);
 *   - they present near-parallel faces along the same axis, separated by less
 *     than {@link MIN_SURFACE_SEPARATION};
 *   - their extents overlap in the other two axes by more than a sliver, so
 *     they genuinely cover each other rather than merely abutting.
 *
 * ## Usage
 *
 * In the browser console, at any time:
 *
 * \`\`\`js
 * __auditZFighting()          // audit every mounted scene, print a table per scene
 * __auditZFighting({ json: true })   // same, returned as data
 * \`\`\`
 *
 * EVERY mounted scene, because this game has two: the island's <Canvas> and, while the player
 * is indoors, BuildingInteriorView's own. They are separate renderers with separate scene
 * graphs, so an audit that only ever looked at one of them reported half the game as clean
 * without ever having looked at the other half. Each Canvas registers itself through
 * {@link installZFightAudit} (see Three/ZFightAuditBridge.tsx) and unregisters on unmount, so
 * the report always covers exactly what is on screen right now.
 */

import * as THREE from 'three';
import { MIN_SURFACE_SEPARATION } from '../constants/terrain';

/** Below this thickness a mesh is treated as a flat plate rather than a solid. */
const FLAT_EPSILON = 1e-3;

/**
 * Minimum overlap area (in world units squared) before an overlapping pair is
 * worth reporting. Two solids that merely touch along an edge share a hairline
 * of area and never visibly flicker; a genuine conflict covers real screen
 * space.
 */
const MIN_OVERLAP_AREA = 0.05;

export type ZFightFinding = {
  /** Axis along which the two faces are separated. */
  axis: 'x' | 'y' | 'z';
  /** Distance between the two faces. 0 means exactly coplanar. */
  separation: number;
  /** Overlap area of the two faces in the other two axes. */
  overlapArea: number;
  /** Identifies the two meshes involved, so one pair is reported once. Not for display. */
  pair: string;
  a: string;
  b: string;
  /** World coordinate of the shared plane, for locating it in the scene. */
  planeCoord: number;
};

type Plate = {
  object: THREE.Mesh;
  /** Position in the traversal, used to identify a pair. See the dedupe in the audit below. */
  id: number;
  name: string;
  box: THREE.Box3;
};

const AXES = ['x', 'y', 'z'] as const;

/**
 * A readable identity for a mesh: its own name if it has one, else the nearest
 * named ancestor plus the geometry type, which for procedural meshes is usually
 * enough to find the JSX that produced it.
 */
function describe(obj: THREE.Object3D): string {
  const parts: string[] = [];
  let cur: THREE.Object3D | null = obj;
  while (cur && parts.length < 3) {
    if (cur.name) parts.unshift(cur.name);
    cur = cur.parent;
  }
  const geo = (obj as THREE.Mesh).geometry?.type ?? 'Geometry';
  const trail = parts.length ? parts.join(' / ') : '(unnamed)';
  return `${trail} <${geo}>`;
}

/** A material (or every material in an array) that opts out of depth conflicts. */
function isExemptMaterial(material: THREE.Material | THREE.Material[]): boolean {
  const list = Array.isArray(material) ? material : [material];
  return list.every(
    (m) =>
      // Declared itself a decal - this is the sanctioned fix, not a defect.
      m.polygonOffset === true ||
      // Cannot fight: it never writes depth, so it is resolved by sort order.
      m.depthWrite === false ||
      // Not depth-tested at all.
      m.depthTest === false
  );
}

/**
 * IS THIS MESH A SLEEVE ALONG `axis` — a tube with no ends?
 *
 * `openEnded` cylinders and cones are the island's own terrain: the ground is a
 * `RingGeometry` cap at y = 0.30 sitting on an open-ended cylinder that runs y = -0.70 … 0.30,
 * which in turn is capped by a `CircleGeometry` at its bottom. That is a correct join — a lid
 * filling an open tube — but a bounding box cannot see the hole, so this audit was reading the
 * sleeve as a solid with a top face at 0.30 and a bottom at -0.70, and reporting both caps as
 * exactly-coplanar conflicts covering 130 and 187 square units.
 *
 * They were the two loudest findings in the whole report, and they were the two most obviously
 * correct pieces of geometry in the scene, which is the failure mode that teaches everyone to
 * stop reading the report. The parameter is right there on the geometry, so read it.
 *
 * Only the cylinder's OWN axis is exempted: a tube lying on its side still presents two real
 * silhouette faces across the axes it was not extruded along. Anything rotated off the world
 * axes has a bounding box that is not its faces anyway, which this audit has never claimed to
 * resolve.
 */
function openEndedAlong(mesh: THREE.Mesh, axis: 'x' | 'y' | 'z'): boolean {
  const params = (mesh.geometry as { parameters?: { openEnded?: boolean } }).parameters;
  if (!params?.openEnded) return false;
  // Cylinders and cones are extruded along their own +Y; find where that ended up in the world.
  const up = new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0).applyQuaternion(mesh.getWorldQuaternion(SCRATCH_QUAT));
  return Math.abs(up[axis]) > 0.99;
}

const SCRATCH_QUAT = new THREE.Quaternion();

/**
 * Overlap of two boxes in the two axes that are NOT `axis`, as an area.
 * Negative extent in either axis means no overlap at all.
 */
function overlapArea(a: THREE.Box3, b: THREE.Box3, axis: 'x' | 'y' | 'z'): number {
  let area = 1;
  for (const other of AXES) {
    if (other === axis) continue;
    const lo = Math.max(a.min[other], b.min[other]);
    const hi = Math.min(a.max[other], b.max[other]);
    const extent = hi - lo;
    if (extent <= 0) return 0;
    area *= extent;
  }
  return area;
}

/**
 * Walk a scene and report every pair of surfaces that can z-fight.
 *
 * @param root usually the R3F `scene`
 */
export function auditSceneForZFighting(root: THREE.Object3D): ZFightFinding[] {
  root.updateWorldMatrix(true, true);

  const plates: Plate[] = [];
  root.traverseVisible((obj) => {
    const mesh = obj as THREE.Mesh;
    if (!(mesh as any).isMesh || !mesh.geometry) return;
    if (!mesh.material || isExemptMaterial(mesh.material)) return;

    // Skinned/instanced meshes and anything animated per-frame in a shader
    // cannot be judged from a static bounding box, so they are out of scope.
    if ((mesh as any).isInstancedMesh || (mesh as any).isSkinnedMesh) return;

    const box = new THREE.Box3().setFromObject(mesh);
    if (box.isEmpty()) return;
    plates.push({ object: mesh, id: plates.length, name: describe(mesh), box });
  });

  const findings: ZFightFinding[] = [];

  for (const axis of AXES) {
    // Collect every candidate face: for a flat plate that is the plate itself,
    // for a solid it is its two extreme faces along this axis. The terrain bug
    // this module was written for was exactly a "solid's top face vs another
    // solid's top face" pair, which a flat-plates-only check would have missed.
    type Face = { plate: Plate; coord: number };
    const faces: Face[] = [];
    for (const p of plates) {
      const thickness = p.box.max[axis] - p.box.min[axis];
      if (thickness < FLAT_EPSILON) {
        faces.push({ plate: p, coord: p.box.min[axis] });
      } else if (openEndedAlong(p.object, axis)) {
        // A SLEEVE, not a solid — see openEndedAlong. Its bounding box has a top and a bottom
        // but the mesh does not, so neither end can fight anything.
        continue;
      } else {
        faces.push({ plate: p, coord: p.box.min[axis] });
        faces.push({ plate: p, coord: p.box.max[axis] });
      }
    }

    // Sort by plane coordinate so only nearby faces are compared: without this
    // the island scene's few thousand meshes would be a quadratic sweep.
    faces.sort((f, g) => f.coord - g.coord);

    for (let i = 0; i < faces.length; i++) {
      for (let j = i + 1; j < faces.length; j++) {
        const separation = faces[j].coord - faces[i].coord;
        if (separation >= MIN_SURFACE_SEPARATION) break; // sorted: no later j is closer

        const a = faces[i].plate;
        const b = faces[j].plate;
        if (a === b) continue;
        // A mesh's own two faces, and any parent/child pair, are modelling
        // decisions rather than conflicts.
        if (a.object === b.object) continue;

        const area = overlapArea(a.box, b.box, axis);
        if (area < MIN_OVERLAP_AREA) continue;

        findings.push({
          axis,
          separation,
          overlapArea: area,
          pair: a.id < b.id ? `${a.id}|${b.id}` : `${b.id}|${a.id}`,
          a: a.name,
          b: b.name,
          planeCoord: faces[i].coord,
        });
      }
    }
  }

  // Worst first: exactly coplanar and covering the most area.
  findings.sort((f, g) => f.separation - g.separation || g.overlapArea - f.overlapArea);

  // The same pair can be reported once per axis when two boxes are close in more than one
  // direction; keep only its worst axis.
  //
  // Keyed on WHICH TWO MESHES, not on what they are called. Every mesh in this project is
  // procedural and unnamed, so `describe()` returns the same '(unnamed) <BoxGeometry>' string for
  // all of them - and a name-keyed dedupe therefore collapsed every box-versus-box conflict in
  // the scene into a single row. The report came back with a handful of findings and read as
  // near-clean while hiding an unbounded number behind each one.
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  return findings.filter((f) => {
    if (seen.has(f.pair)) return false;
    seen.add(f.pair);
    return true;
  });
}

/**
 * Registers one scene with `window.__auditZFighting()`, and returns the function that
 * unregisters it again. Dev builds only - every caller is behind an `import.meta.env.DEV`
 * guard, and the whole module is dropped from production with them.
 *
 * `label` is what the report calls this scene ("island", "interior"), so a finding can be
 * traced to the Canvas it came from.
 */
export function installZFightAudit(label: string, getScene: () => THREE.Object3D | null): () => void {
  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return () => {};

  registry.set(label, getScene);
  (window as any).__auditZFighting = runAudit;

  return () => {
    registry.delete(label);
  };
}

/** Live scenes, by label. A Map so re-registering the same Canvas replaces rather than stacks. */
const registry = new Map<string, () => THREE.Object3D | null>();

function runAudit(opts?: { json?: boolean }) {
  const scenes = [...registry.entries()]
    .map(([label, getScene]) => ({ label, scene: getScene() }))
    .filter((entry): entry is { label: string; scene: THREE.Object3D } => !!entry.scene);

  if (!scenes.length) {
    console.warn('[z-fight audit] no scene mounted - is a 3D view on screen?');
    return [];
  }

  const all = scenes.flatMap(({ label, scene }) =>
    auditSceneForZFighting(scene).map((f) => ({ ...f, scene: label }))
  );

  if (opts?.json) return all;

  const scanned = scenes.map((s) => s.label).join(', ');

  if (!all.length) {
    console.log(
      `%c[z-fight audit] ${scanned} clean - no surface pair closer than ${MIN_SURFACE_SEPARATION} world units.`,
      'color:#2A9D8F;font-weight:bold'
    );
    return all;
  }

  console.groupCollapsed(
    `%c[z-fight audit] ${all.length} suspect pair(s) across: ${scanned}`,
    'color:#E8836A;font-weight:bold'
  );
  console.table(
    all.map((f) => ({
      scene: f.scene,
      axis: f.axis,
      separation: Number(f.separation.toFixed(4)),
      'overlap m²': Number(f.overlapArea.toFixed(2)),
      plane: Number(f.planeCoord.toFixed(3)),
      a: f.a,
      b: f.b,
    }))
  );
  console.info(
    'Fix by merging or deleting the redundant surface. If the pair is coplanar ' +
      'BY DESIGN (a decal lying on a floor), give it DECAL_DEPTH_BIAS from ' +
      'constants/terrain.ts instead - that also removes it from this report.'
  );
  console.info(
    'Note the overlap area is measured between AXIS-ALIGNED BOUNDING BOXES. Two round ' +
      'surfaces that only meet along a rim - an open-ended cone capped by a disc, say - ' +
      'share a whole square of bounding box and no actual area, and are reported here ' +
      'without being able to flicker. Check the geometry before moving anything.'
  );
  console.groupEnd();

  return all;
}
```

```tsx
/** Throwaway: every pet tile, to confirm the shared PetEyes/head change did not disturb the dogs

import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';

const IDS = [
  'pet-dog-dachshund', 'pet-dog-poodle', 'pet-dog-shiba',
  'pet-cat-orange', 'pet-cat-tabby', 'pet-cat-tuxedo',
  'pet-bird-budgie', 'pet-bird-javasparrow', 'pet-bird-canary', 'pet-bird-phoenix',

writeFileSync(process.argv[2], `<!doctype html><html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
 body{margin:0;padding:10px;background:#fff;display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;font:11px sans-serif}
 figure{margin:0}

 <div style="width:150px;height:150px;border:1px solid #eee">${renderToStaticMarkup(<QVersionIcon itemId={id} size={150} />)}</div></figure>`).join('')}</body></html>`);
```

## tmp-anomaly-scan.ts

```ts
/**
 * Diagnostic: sweep every outdoor placeable's REAL scene graph for the model defects that do not
 * show up in a mesh count — geometry under the ground, parts floating free of the model, and
 * decoration buried inside its own parent volume.
 *
 * Throwaway; delete with the pass.
 */
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { ALL_ITEMS } from './src/constants/items';
import { DISPLAY_CATEGORIES } from './src/utils/categoryUtils';
import { ISLAND_SCALE, buildModelObject3D } from './scripts/lib/measureFurnitureModel';

const byCat = new Map(DISPLAY_CATEGORIES.map((c) => [c.id, c]));
const scopeOf = (id: string) => { const c = byCat.get(id) as any; return c ? (c.placementScope ?? c.mainSection) : '??'; };

const ONLY = process.argv[2];

type Part = { name: string; box: THREE.Box3; centre: THREE.Vector3; radius: number };

for (const item of ALL_ITEMS) {
  if (scopeOf(item.shopCategory) !== 'OUTDOOR') continue;
  const cat = byCat.get(item.shopCategory) as any;
  if (!cat || cat.kind !== 'placeable') continue;
  if (ONLY && item.name !== ONLY && item.id !== ONLY) continue;

  const root = buildModelObject3D(item.id, ISLAND_SCALE);
  if (!root) continue;
  root.updateMatrixWorld(true);

  const parts: Part[] = [];
  root.traverse((o) => {
    const m = o as THREE.Mesh;
    if (!(m as any).isMesh || !m.geometry) return;
    // Same filter collision uses (lib/furniturePlacement's isSolidGeometry): a mesh that is
    // invisible, does not write depth, or is additively blended is a DRAWN EFFECT, not a part.
    // Their sizes are set per frame in useFrame, so their declared geometry is a unit sphere at
    // the origin and every test below reads it as a giant part swallowing the whole model.
    if (!o.visible) return;
    const mats = Array.isArray(m.material) ? m.material : [m.material];
    const solid = mats.some((mat: any) => mat && mat.depthWrite !== false && mat.blending !== THREE.AdditiveBlending);
    if (!solid) return;
    m.geometry.computeBoundingBox();
    m.geometry.computeBoundingSphere();
    const box = m.geometry.boundingBox!.clone().applyMatrix4(m.matrixWorld);
    const c = new THREE.Vector3();
    box.getCenter(c);
    const sph = m.geometry.boundingSphere!;
    const s = new THREE.Vector3();
    m.matrixWorld.decompose(new THREE.Vector3(), new THREE.Quaternion(), s);
    parts.push({
      name: (m.geometry as any).type ?? 'geo',
      box, centre: c,
      radius: sph.radius * Math.max(Math.abs(s.x), Math.abs(s.y), Math.abs(s.z)),
    });
  });
  if (!parts.length) continue;

  const whole = new THREE.Box3();
  for (const p of parts) whole.union(p.box);

  const notes: string[] = [];

  // 1. Under the ground plane. The origin is the surface a placed piece stands on.
  const sunk = parts.filter((p) => p.box.min.y < -0.02);
  if (sunk.length) {
    const deepest = Math.min(...sunk.map((p) => p.box.min.y));
    notes.push(`${sunk.length}/${parts.length} part(s) below ground, deepest ${(deepest * 1000).toFixed(0)}mm`);
  }

  // 2. Nothing touching the ground at all — the whole piece hovers.
  if (whole.min.y > 0.03) notes.push(`WHOLE MODEL FLOATS: lowest point ${(whole.min.y * 1000).toFixed(0)}mm up`);

  // 3. A part with clear air between it and every other part — a detached fragment.
  for (const p of parts) {
    let nearest = Infinity;
    for (const q of parts) {
      if (q === p) continue;
      const d = boxGap(p.box, q.box);
      if (d < nearest) nearest = d;
    }
    if (nearest > 0.12 && nearest < Infinity) {
      notes.push(`detached part (${p.name}) — ${(nearest * 1000).toFixed(0)}mm of air to the nearest other part, at y=${p.centre.y.toFixed(2)}`);
    }
  }

  // A "decoration buried in its own parent volume" test was tried here on both bounding boxes
  // and bounding spheres and thrown away: an elongated part (a palm frond's rib, a fountain's
  // pipe) has a bounding volume many times its own thickness, so both tests report every ring,
  // collar and rib in the catalog and bury the real cases in noise. That class of defect is found
  // by looking at the model (tmp-shrubfield.html), not by measuring its bounds.

  if (notes.length) {
    console.log(`\n### ${item.name} (${item.id}) — ${parts.length} meshes`);
    for (const nte of [...new Set(notes)]) console.log(`    - ${nte}`);
  }
}

function volume(b: THREE.Box3) {
  const s = new THREE.Vector3();
  b.getSize(s);
  return s.x * s.y * s.z;
}
function boxGap(a: THREE.Box3, b: THREE.Box3) {
  const dx = Math.max(0, Math.max(a.min.x - b.max.x, b.min.x - a.max.x));
  const dy = Math.max(0, Math.max(a.min.y - b.max.y, b.min.y - a.max.y));
  const dz = Math.max(0, Math.max(a.min.z - b.max.z, b.min.z - a.max.z));
  return Math.hypot(dx, dy, dz);
}
```

## tmp-artwork-preview.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * Throwaway harness for signing off 藝術品 — the models, and the wall/tabletop mounting.
 *
 * The house interior is NOT reachable on the guest path (a guest cannot place a Home, so no door
 * ever appears), which is why this exists: without it, a wall-mounted piece can only be checked by
 * reading arithmetic. Here a real room is built from the real interiorShell constants and every
 * piece is hung by the SHIPPING resolver (lib/interiorPlacement.ts) from a ray aimed at the wall —
 * the same call the drag ghost makes — so what the screenshot shows is what the game will do.
 *
 *   ?page=N     which slice of the catalog (0-based). Default 0.
 *   ?id=<id>    one piece, alone, filling the view.
 *
 * Publishes `window.__artwork` so a headless run can ASSERT the mounting (facing, standoff,
 * height) rather than only take a screenshot.
 *
 * Delete with tmp-artwork-preview.html once this is signed off.
 */
import { useLayoutEffect, useRef, useSyncExternalStore } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { Canvas } from '@react-three/fiber';
import { Environment, OrbitControls } from '@react-three/drei';
import * as THREE from 'three';

import { FurnitureModel } from './src/components/Three/FurnitureItem';
import { getFloorMaterial } from './src/components/Three/floorMaterial';
import { getWallMaterial } from './src/components/Three/wallMaterial';
import { ARTWORK_SPECS } from './src/constants/artwork';
import { HDRI_APARTMENT } from './src/constants/environmentMaps';
import { getItemById } from './src/constants/items';
import { getHangHeight, getPlacementMounts } from './src/constants/placement';
import { ROOM_GRID_SIZE, ROOM_HALF_SIZE } from './src/constants/rooms';
import {
  BASEBOARD_THICKNESS, CROWN_HEIGHT, CROWN_THICKNESS, CROWN_TOP_Y,
  INTERIOR_CEILING_Y, WALL_BASEBOARD_INSET, WALL_CROWN_INSET, WALL_THICKNESS,
} from './src/constants/interiorShell';
import {
  getFootprint, getFootprintVersion, measureFootprint, subscribeFootprints,
} from './src/lib/furniturePlacement';
import { buildMountableWalls, resolveInteriorPlacement } from './src/lib/interiorPlacement';
import type { PlacedItem } from './src/types';

const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const ONLY = params.get('id');
const PAGE = Number(params.get('page') ?? 0);

/** The interior draws every piece at 1.15 (BuildingInteriorView's FurnitureItem). */
const INTERIOR_SCALE = 1.15;

const ROOMS = [{ cx: 0, cz: 0 }];
const FACES = buildMountableWalls(ROOMS);
/** The two walls a camera inside the room, on the +x/-z side, is looking at. */
const N_FACE = FACES.find((f) => f.nz === -1)!;
const W_FACE = FACES.find((f) => f.nx === 1)!;

const WALL_PIECES = ARTWORK_SPECS.filter((s) => !s.outdoor && getPlacementMounts(s.id).includes('wall'));
const SURFACE_PIECES = ARTWORK_SPECS.filter((s) => !s.outdoor && getPlacementMounts(s.id).includes('surface'));
const FLOOR_PIECES = ARTWORK_SPECS.filter(
  (s) => !s.outdoor && getPlacementMounts(s.id).length === 1 && getPlacementMounts(s.id)[0] === 'floor',
);

const PER_WALL = 4;
const TABLE_ID = 'item-22';

/** One piece, rendered exactly as the interior renders it, and measured the same way. */
function Piece({ placement }: { placement: PlacedItem }) {
  const modelRef = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);
  const item = getItemById(placement.itemId);

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    if (modelRef.current) measureFootprint(placement.itemId, modelRef.current);
  }, [placement.itemId]);

  if (!item) return null;
  return (
    <group position={placement.position} rotation={[0, placement.rotation, 0]}>
      <group ref={modelRef}>
        <FurnitureModel name={item.name} item={item} scale={INTERIOR_SCALE} />
      </group>
    </group>
  );
}

/** The room shell: floor, two walls, their baseboards and crowns. Real constants throughout. */
function Shell() {
  const wallId = 'wall-white';
  const floorId = 'floor-oak';
  const baseboardOffset = WALL_BASEBOARD_INSET - BASEBOARD_THICKNESS / 2;
  const crownOffset = WALL_CROWN_INSET - CROWN_THICKNESS / 2;

  const wall = (x: number, z: number, rotation: number, sign: number) => (
    <group position={[x, 0, z]} rotation={[0, rotation, 0]}>
      <mesh position={[0, 2.5, 0]} receiveShadow>
        <boxGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE, 5, WALL_THICKNESS]} />
        <primitive object={getWallMaterial(wallId, '#f5efe3')} attach="material" />
      </mesh>
      <mesh position={[0, 0.15, sign * -baseboardOffset]}>
        <boxGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE, 0.3, BASEBOARD_THICKNESS]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#8d6e52" roughness={0.8} />
      </mesh>
      <mesh position={[0, CROWN_TOP_Y - CROWN_HEIGHT / 2, sign * -crownOffset]}>
        <boxGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE, CROWN_HEIGHT, CROWN_THICKNESS]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#fdf6e7" roughness={0.7} />
      </mesh>
    </group>
  );

  return (
    <group>
      <mesh rotation={[-Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} position={[0, -0.01, 0]} receiveShadow>
        <planeGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE, ROOM_GRID_SIZE]} />
        <primitive object={getFloorMaterial(floorId, '#c9a06a')} attach="material" />
      </mesh>
      {/* N wall (z = +6, inner face pointing -z) and W wall (x = -6, inner face pointing +x). */}
      {wall(0, ROOM_HALF_SIZE, 0, 1)}
      {wall(-ROOM_HALF_SIZE, 0, Math.PI / 2, -1)}
    </group>
  );
}

/**
 * Where every piece on this page ends up — resolved through the shipping rule, from a ray, on a
 * real wall face. Re-runs when a footprint lands, exactly as the view does.
 */
function useResolved() {
  const version = useSyncExternalStore(subscribeFootprints, getFootprintVersion);
  void version;

  const table: PlacedItem = { instanceId: 'table', itemId: TABLE_ID, position: [1.6, 0, -1.4], rotation: 0 };
  const out: PlacedItem[] = [table];
  const report: any[] = [];

  const wallPage = ONLY
    ? WALL_PIECES.filter((s) => s.id === ONLY)
    : WALL_PIECES.slice(PAGE * PER_WALL * 2, PAGE * PER_WALL * 2 + PER_WALL * 2);

  wallPage.forEach((spec, i) => {
    const face = i < PER_WALL ? N_FACE : W_FACE;
    const slot = i % PER_WALL;
    const s = ((slot + 0.5) / PER_WALL) * face.length;
    const target = { x: face.x1 + face.dx * s, z: face.z1 + face.dz * s };
    const y = getHangHeight(spec.id);
    const dir = new THREE.Vector3(target.x, 0, target.z).normalize();

    const r = resolveInteriorPlacement({
      itemId: spec.id,
      instanceId: `w-${spec.id}`,
      rotation: 0,
      ray: { origin: { x: 0, y, z: 0 }, direction: { x: dir.x, y: 0, z: dir.z } },
      faces: FACES,
      rooms: ROOMS,
      placements: out,
      excludeInstanceId: null,
    });
    out.push(r.placement);

    const fp = getFootprint(spec.id);
    report.push({
      id: spec.id,
      form: spec.form,
      mount: r.mount,
      ok: r.ok,
      reason: r.reason,
      rotationDeg: Math.round((r.placement.rotation * 180) / Math.PI),
      wallNormal: [face.nx, face.nz],
      // How far the piece's own back face ends up from the wall plane. The number the whole
      // "not sunk in, not floating" requirement reduces to.
      backGap: fp
        ? +(((r.placement.position[0] - face.x1) * face.nx + (r.placement.position[2] - face.z1) * face.nz)
          + (fp.cz - fp.halfD)).toFixed(4)
        : null,
      bottomY: fp ? +(r.placement.position[1] + fp.minY).toFixed(3) : null,
      topY: fp ? +(r.placement.position[1] + fp.maxY).toFixed(3) : null,
    });
  });

  const surfacePage = ONLY ? SURFACE_PIECES.filter((s) => s.id === ONLY) : SURFACE_PIECES.slice(PAGE * 3, PAGE * 3 + 3);
  surfacePage.forEach((spec, i) => {
    const x = table.position[0] + (i - 1) * 0.72;
    const r = resolveInteriorPlacement({
      itemId: spec.id,
      instanceId: `s-${spec.id}`,
      rotation: 0.4,
      ray: { origin: { x, y: 4, z: table.position[2] }, direction: { x: 0, y: -1, z: 0 } },
      faces: FACES,
      rooms: ROOMS,
      placements: out,
      excludeInstanceId: null,
    });
    out.push(r.placement);
    report.push({ id: spec.id, form: spec.form, mount: r.mount, ok: r.ok, reason: r.reason, y: +r.placement.position[1].toFixed(3) });
  });

  const floorPage = ONLY ? FLOOR_PIECES.filter((s) => s.id === ONLY) : FLOOR_PIECES.slice(PAGE * 2, PAGE * 2 + 2);
  floorPage.forEach((spec, i) => {
    const r = resolveInteriorPlacement({
      itemId: spec.id,
      instanceId: `f-${spec.id}`,
      rotation: 0.6,
      ray: { origin: { x: -3.4 + i * 1.8, y: 4, z: 2.2 }, direction: { x: 0, y: -1, z: 0 } },
      faces: FACES,
      rooms: ROOMS,
      placements: out,
      excludeInstanceId: null,
    });
    out.push(r.placement);
    report.push({ id: spec.id, form: spec.form, mount: r.mount, ok: r.ok, reason: r.reason, y: +r.placement.position[1].toFixed(3) });
  });

  (window as any).__artwork = report;
  return out;
}

function Scene() {
  const placements = useResolved();
  return (
    <group>
      <Shell />
      {placements.map((p) => <Piece key={p.instanceId} placement={p} />)}
      <Environment files={HDRI_APARTMENT} />
      <ambientLight intensity={0.75} color="#fffef4" />
      <directionalLight
        position={[6, 9, 4]}
        intensity={1.5}
        castShadow
        shadow-mapSize={[2048, 2048]}
        shadow-camera-left={-12}
        shadow-camera-right={12}
        shadow-camera-top={12}
        shadow-camera-bottom={-12}
      />
      <pointLight position={[0, 4.2, 0]} intensity={1.1} distance={16} decay={1.2} color="#ffdca8" />
    </group>
  );
}

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <Canvas
    shadows={{ type: THREE.PCFSoftShadowMap }}
    camera={{ position: [7.2, 4.4, -6.2], fov: 46, near: 0.3, far: 200 }}
    onCreated={({ camera }) => camera.lookAt(-1.4, 1.5, 1.6)}
  >
    <Scene />
    <OrbitControls target={[-1.4, 1.5, 1.6]} />
  </Canvas>,
);

// Height of the ceiling is not drawn here on purpose — an unroofed room is how the interior
// camera sees it, and a lid would black out the shot.
void INTERIOR_CEILING_Y;
```

## tmp-audio-audit.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * Throwaway harness: MEASURES what the island actually puts out, rather than trusting that a
 * gain of zero is silence.
 *
 * Every AudioContext the app creates gets its `destination` replaced by a tap gain feeding an
 * analyser, so the RMS of everything the audio layer emits can be read back. Each step drives
 * the real settings entry points and reports peak RMS over a real-time window.
 *
 * Results land on `window.__audio` for a CDP read. Delete with tmp-audio-audit.html.
 */

// --- The tap. Installed before anything asks for a context (soundUtils creates its
//     AudioContext lazily inside getSynthAudioContext, never at module scope). ---
const RealAC: typeof AudioContext = window.AudioContext;
let analyser: AnalyserNode | null = null;

const destDescriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(
  (window as any).BaseAudioContext?.prototype ?? RealAC.prototype,
  'destination',
)!;

class TappedAudioContext extends RealAC {
  constructor(...args: any[]) {
    super(...(args as []));
    const realDest = destDescriptor.get!.call(this) as AudioDestinationNode;
    const tap = this.createGain();
    const an = this.createAnalyser();
    an.fftSize = 2048;
    tap.connect(an);
    an.connect(realDest);
    Object.defineProperty(this, 'destination', { value: tap, configurable: true });
    analyser = an;
  }
}
(window as any).AudioContext = TappedAudioContext;
(window as any).webkitAudioContext = TappedAudioContext;

import {
  getSynthAudioContext,
  setAmbienceVolume,
  setAmbienceMuted,
  startBeachSurfAmbience,
  setBeachSurfIntensity,
  startSwimAmbience,
  setSwimActivity,
  stopBeachSurfAmbience,
  stopSwimAmbience,
  playStrokeSplash,
} from './src/lib/soundUtils';
import { configureBackgroundMusic } from './src/lib/backgroundMusic';

const buf = new Float32Array(2048);
function rms(): number {
  if (!analyser) return -1;
  analyser.getFloatTimeDomainData(buf);
  let sum = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < buf.length; i++) sum += buf[i] * buf[i];
  return Math.sqrt(sum / buf.length);
}

/** Peak RMS over `ms` of real time — a bed that only crashes every few seconds needs a window. */
async function peakOver(ms: number): Promise<number> {
  const end = performance.now() + ms;
  let peak = 0;
  while (performance.now() < end) {
    peak = Math.max(peak, rms());
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 25));
  }
  return peak;
}

interface Step { name: string; peak: number; expect: 'sound' | 'silence'; ok: boolean }
const results: Step[] = [];
const log = document.getElementById('log')!;

/** Anything under this is inaudible on any speaker; the point of the audit is that it is 0. */
const SILENCE = 1e-4;

/**
 * How long every fade in the audio layer is given to finish before measuring starts.
 *
 * Measuring from the instant of the change would report the FADE, not the result: the surf
 * takes 0.5s to wind down, the swim wash 0.3s, the music's master 0.6s. What the audit is
 * asking is "and then what", so it waits out the longest of those with room to spare and
 * measures only what is left.
 */
const FADE_SETTLE_MS = 1400;

async function step(name: string, expect: 'sound' | 'silence', ms: number, act: () => void) {
  act();
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, FADE_SETTLE_MS));
  const peak = await peakOver(Math.max(800, ms - FADE_SETTLE_MS));
  const ok = expect === 'silence' ? peak < SILENCE : peak > SILENCE * 10;
  results.push({ name, peak, expect, ok });
  log.textContent = results
    .map((r) => `${r.ok ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'}  ${r.name.padEnd(46)} peak=${r.peak.toExponential(3)}  want=${r.expect}`)
    .join('\n');
  (window as any).__audio = { done: false, results };
}

async function run() {
  const ctx = getSynthAudioContext();
  if (!ctx) { log.textContent = 'NO AUDIO CONTEXT'; return; }
  await ctx.resume().catch(() => {});
  log.textContent = `ctx state=${ctx.state} rate=${ctx.sampleRate}\n`;

  // ---- The sea ----------------------------------------------------------
  await step('surf, 海浪環境音 = 1', 'sound', 3500, () => {
    setAmbienceMuted(false);
    setAmbienceVolume(1);
    startBeachSurfAmbience();
    setBeachSurfIntensity(1);
  });
  await step('surf, 海浪環境音 = 0', 'silence', 4000, () => setAmbienceVolume(0));
  await step('surf, slider back to 1 (restarts)', 'sound', 3500, () => {
    setAmbienceVolume(1);
    startBeachSurfAmbience();   // Avatar's frame loop does this every frame
    setBeachSurfIntensity(1);
  });
  await step('surf, 全部靜音', 'silence', 4000, () => setAmbienceMuted(true));
  await step('surf, unmuted (restarts)', 'sound', 3500, () => {
    setAmbienceMuted(false);
    startBeachSurfAmbience();
    setBeachSurfIntensity(1);
  });
  stopBeachSurfAmbience();
  await peakOver(700);

  // ---- The water you swim in -------------------------------------------
  await step('swim wash, 海浪環境音 = 1', 'sound', 2500, () => {
    startSwimAmbience(0.3);
    setSwimActivity(1);
  });
  await step('swim wash, 海浪環境音 = 0', 'silence', 4000, () => setAmbienceVolume(0));
  await step('stroke splash while 海浪環境音 = 0', 'silence', 1200, () => {
    playStrokeSplash(0.4); playStrokeSplash(0.4); playStrokeSplash(0.4);
  });
  await step('swim wash, slider back to 1 (restarts)', 'sound', 2500, () => {
    setAmbienceVolume(1);
    startSwimAmbience(0.3);
    setSwimActivity(1);
  });
  stopSwimAmbience();
  await peakOver(700);

  // ---- The music --------------------------------------------------------
  await step('BGM, 背景音樂 = 0.5', 'sound', 4000, () =>
    configureBackgroundMusic({ source: 'builtin', builtinMood: 'island-dawn', volume: 0.5, muted: false }));
  await step('BGM, 背景音樂 = 0', 'silence', 4200, () => configureBackgroundMusic({ volume: 0 }));
  await step('BGM, back to 0.5', 'sound', 4000, () => configureBackgroundMusic({ volume: 0.5 }));
  await step('BGM, 全部靜音', 'silence', 4200, () => configureBackgroundMusic({ muted: true }));

  // ---- Everything at once, then off ------------------------------------
  await step('sea + music both on', 'sound', 4000, () => {
    configureBackgroundMusic({ muted: false, volume: 0.5 });
    setAmbienceMuted(false);
    setAmbienceVolume(1);
    startBeachSurfAmbience();
    setBeachSurfIntensity(1);
  });
  await step('全部靜音 with both running', 'silence', 4500, () => {
    configureBackgroundMusic({ muted: true });
    setAmbienceMuted(true);
  });

  (window as any).__audio = { done: true, results };
  log.textContent += `\n\n${results.filter((r) => r.ok).length}/${results.length} passed`;
}

run();

```

## tmp-beach-exit-check.ts

```ts
import {
  getTerrainInfo, nextSwimState, swimTransitionTimer,
  SWIM_TRANSITION_DURATION, SHORELINE_RADIUS, SwimState,
} from './src/components/Three/characterMovement';
import { SWIM_BODY_Y } from './src/constants/world';

const scale = 1;
const DT = 1 / 60;
const lerp = (a: number, b: number, t: number) => a + (b - a) * t;

/**
 * Replays Avatar.tsx's MOVING-branch height pipeline over a walk from open water up onto
 * the beach, and reports how far the body ever sank below the ground under it.
 *
 * `burial > 0` is the reported bug: the avatar rendered underneath the sand surface.
 */
function walkAshore(label: string, useFix: boolean) {
  let state: SwimState = 'swimming';
  let timer = 0;
  let worstBurial = -Infinity;
  let worstAt = 0;
  let maxJump = 0;
  let prevY: number | null = null;
  let sunkFrames = 0;

  // Walk inward from deep water (r=9) to well up the beach (r=5.2) at ~5.5 u/s.
  for (let r = 9.0; r > 5.2; r -= 5.5 * DT) {
    if (state === 'enteringWater' || state === 'exitingWater') {
      timer -= DT;
      if (timer <= 0) state = state === 'enteringWater' ? 'swimming' : 'walking';
    }
    const next = nextSwimState(state, r, 0, scale);
    if (next !== state) {
      timer = useFix ? swimTransitionTimer(state, next, timer) : SWIM_TRANSITION_DURATION;
      state = next;
    }

    const tInfo = getTerrainInfo(r, 0, scale);
    const ground = tInfo.targetY;
    const terrainY = ground + 0.05;
    const safeSwimY = Math.max(ground, SWIM_BODY_Y);
    const p = 1.0 - Math.max(0, timer / SWIM_TRANSITION_DURATION);

    let y: number;
    if (state === 'swimming') y = safeSwimY + Math.sin(r * 2.5) * 0.08;
    else if (state === 'enteringWater') y = lerp(terrainY, safeSwimY, p);
    else if (state === 'exitingWater') {
      // The one line under test: fixed blends up from safeSwimY, old blends up from raw -0.6.
      y = useFix ? lerp(safeSwimY, terrainY, p) : lerp(SWIM_BODY_Y, terrainY, p);
    } else y = terrainY;

    if (useFix) y = Math.max(y, ground); // the new hard floor

    const burial = ground - y;
    if (burial > worstBurial) { worstBurial = burial; worstAt = r; }
    if (burial > 0.02) sunkFrames++;
    if (prevY !== null) maxJump = Math.max(maxJump, Math.abs(y - prevY));
    prevY = y;
  }

  const ok = worstBurial <= 0.001;
  console.log(
    `${ok ? 'ok  ' : 'FAIL'}  ${label.padEnd(26)} ` +
    `worstBurial=${worstBurial.toFixed(3)} @r=${worstAt.toFixed(2)}  ` +
    `sunkFrames=${sunkFrames}  maxFrameJump=${maxJump.toFixed(3)}`
  );
  return ok;
}

console.log(`shoreline r=${SHORELINE_RADIUS}  SWIM_BODY_Y=${SWIM_BODY_Y}`);
console.log('burial > 0 means the avatar is rendered BELOW the sand surface\n');

const oldOk = walkAshore('before fix', false);
const newOk = walkAshore('after fix', true);

console.log(`\nold reproduces bug: ${!oldOk}`);
console.log(`new is clean:       ${newOk}`);
process.exit(!oldOk && newOk ? 0 : 1);

```

```tsx
/** Throwaway: the 3D 鳥 in flight, to check the spread wings and the shoulder join.
 *  `?before=1` puts the pre-change model beside each one. Delete when signed off. */
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { Canvas } from '@react-three/fiber';
import { PetModel } from './src/components/Three/Pets';
import { PetModelOld } from './src/components/Three/tmp-pets-old';

const IDS = ['pet-bird-budgie', 'pet-bird-javasparrow', 'pet-bird-canary', 'pet-bird-phoenix'];
const BEFORE = new URLSearchParams(location.search).has('before');
const VIEWS: Array<[string, [number, number, number]]> = [
  ['front', [0, 0.55, 2.2]],
  ['front-3/4', [1.2, 0.95, 1.9]],
  ['side', [2.2, 0.6, 0.15]],
];

function Tile({ id, cam }: { id: string; cam: [number, number, number] }) {
  const span = BEFORE ? 0.42 : 0;
  return (
    <div style={{ width: 280, height: 250, background: '#eef2f5', border: '1px solid #ccd' }}>
      <Canvas camera={{ position: cam, fov: 30 }} onCreated={({ camera }) => camera.lookAt(0, 0.5, 0)}>
        <ambientLight intensity={0.85} />
        <directionalLight position={[3, 5, 4]} intensity={1.5} />
        <directionalLight position={[-3, 2, -2]} intensity={0.5} />
        {BEFORE && <group position={[-span, 0, 0]}><PetModelOld itemId={id} /></group>}
        <group position={[span, 0, 0]}><PetModel itemId={id} /></group>
      </Canvas>
    </div>
  );
}

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <div style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(3, 280px)', gap: 6, padding: 6, font: '12px sans-serif' }}>
    {IDS.flatMap(id => VIEWS.map(([label, cam]) => (
      <div key={label + id}>
        <div>{id.replace('pet-bird-', '')} · {label}{BEFORE ? ' — left: before' : ''}</div>
        <Tile id={id} cam={cam} />
      </div>
    )))}
  </div>,
);
```

```tsx
const IDS = [
  'pet-bird-budgie', 'pet-bird-javasparrow', 'pet-bird-canary', 'pet-bird-phoenix',
  'pet-dog-shiba', 'pet-cat-tuxedo',
];

const tile = (id: string, px: number) => `
  <figure>
    <div class="tile" style="width:${px}px;height:${px}px">
      ${renderToStaticMarkup(<QVersionIcon itemId={id} size={px} />)}
      ${px > 100 ? '<div class="grid"></div>' : ''}
    </div>
    <figcaption>${id.replace('pet-', '')}</figcaption>
  </figure>`;

writeFileSync(process.argv[2], `<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { margin:0; padding:16px; background:#FAF3E6; font-family:system-ui, sans-serif; }
  .row { display:flex; gap:12px; align-items:flex-start; margin-bottom:18px; }
  figure { margin:0; text-align:center; }
  .tile { position:relative; background:#fff; border:2px solid #E8D9BE; border-radius:16px; overflow:hidden; }
  /* 64-viewBox landmarks scaled to 220: ground 55 -> 189, head centre 21.5 -> 74 */
  .grid { position:absolute; inset:0; pointer-events:none; }
  .grid::before, .grid::after { content:''; position:absolute; left:0; right:0; height:1px; }
  .grid::before { top:189px; background:#E8836A; }
  .grid::after  { top:74px;  background:#5B8FC9; }
  figcaption { margin-top:4px; font-size:12px; color:#6B5844; }
</style></head><body>
  <div class="row">${IDS.map(id => tile(id, 220)).join('')}</div>
  <div class="row">${IDS.map(id => tile(id, 64)).join('')}</div>
</body></html>`);
```

## tmp-birds-zoom.tsx

```tsx
/** Throwaway: the three 鳥 heads at 4x, to check the bill and face marks. Delete when signed off. */
import { renderToStaticMarkup } from 'react-dom/server';
import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { QVersionIcon } from './src/components/QVersionIcon';

const IDS = ['pet-bird-budgie', 'pet-bird-javasparrow', 'pet-bird-canary'];

const tiles = IDS.map(id => `
  <div class="zoom"><div class="inner">${renderToStaticMarkup(<QVersionIcon itemId={id} size={64} />)}</div></div>`).join('');

writeFileSync(process.argv[2], `<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { margin:0; padding:10px; background:#fff; display:flex; gap:10px; }
  .zoom { width:340px; height:340px; overflow:hidden; border:1px solid #ddd; }
  .inner { width:64px; height:64px; transform: scale(5.3) translate(-2px, -4px); transform-origin: top left; }
</style></head><body>${tiles}</body></html>`);

```

## tmp-birds.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * Throwaway harness for eyeballing the 鳥 icons (with a 貓 and a 狗 beside them, since all three
 * species have to read as one shelf). Run: npx tsx tmp-birds.tsx out.html
 * Delete once the birds are signed off.
 */
import { renderToStaticMarkup } from 'react-dom/server';
import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { QVersionIcon } from './src/components/QVersionIcon';

const OUT = process.argv[2];

const ITEMS: [string, string][] = [
  ['pet-bird-budgie', '虎皮鸚鵡'],
  ['pet-bird-javasparrow', '文鳥'],
  ['pet-bird-canary', '金絲雀'],
  ['pet-cat-tabby', '虎斑貓'],
  ['pet-dog-shiba', '柴犬'],
];

const tiles = ITEMS.map(([id, label]) => `
  <figure>
    <div class="tile">${renderToStaticMarkup(<QVersionIcon itemId={id} size={260} />)}</div>
    <div class="tile small">${renderToStaticMarkup(<QVersionIcon itemId={id} size={56} />)}</div>
    <figcaption>${label}<br><code>${id}</code></figcaption>
  </figure>`).join('');

writeFileSync(OUT, `<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { margin:0; padding:20px; background:#FAF3E6; font-family:system-ui, sans-serif; }
  .row { display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:14px; width:1420px; }
  figure { margin:0; text-align:center; }
  .tile { width:270px; height:270px; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center;
          background:#fff; border:2px solid #E8D9BE; border-radius:16px; overflow:hidden; }
  .tile.small { height:70px; margin-top:6px; }
  figcaption { margin-top:4px; font-size:12px; color:#6B5844; }
  code { font-size:10px; color:#9C8A72; }
</style></head><body><div class="row">${tiles}</div></body></html>`);
console.log('wrote', OUT);

```

```tsx
  .sm { width:64px; height:64px; background:#FDF6EC; border:1px solid #ddd; }
```

```tsx
/** Throwaway: the hippo butler's new formal outfit, close on the torso. Delete when signed off. */
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { Canvas } from '@react-three/fiber';
import { NpcModel } from './src/components/Three/Npcs';

const VIEWS: Array<[string, [number, number, number], [number, number, number]]> = [
  ['front torso', [0, 0.42, 1.15], [0, 0.36, 0]],
  ['front 3/4', [0.85, 0.5, 0.95], [0, 0.36, 0]],
  ['side', [1.25, 0.4, 0.05], [0, 0.34, 0]],
  ['back 3/4', [-0.9, 0.5, -0.95], [0, 0.3, 0]],
  ['back', [0, 0.4, -1.2], [0, 0.28, 0]],
  ['back low', [0, 0.16, -0.95], [0, 0.2, 0]],
  ['full front', [0, 0.55, 2.0], [0, 0.5, 0]],
  ['full back', [0, 0.55, -2.0], [0, 0.5, 0]],
];

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <div style={{ font: '12px sans-serif' }}>
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(4, 440px)', gap: 8, padding: 8 }}>
      {VIEWS.map(([label, cam, at]) => (
        <div key={label}>
          <div style={{ fontWeight: 700 }}>{label}</div>
          <div style={{ width: 440, height: 440, background: '#eef2f5', border: '1px solid #ccd' }}>
            <Canvas camera={{ position: cam, fov: 30 }} onCreated={({ camera }) => camera.lookAt(...at)}>
              <ambientLight intensity={0.85} />
              <directionalLight position={[3, 5, 4]} intensity={1.5} />
              <directionalLight position={[-3, 2, -2]} intensity={0.6} />
              <directionalLight position={[0, 2, -5]} intensity={0.7} />
              <NpcModel kind="hippoButler" />
            </Canvas>
          </div>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  </div>,
);

```

```tsx
/**

 * Delete once the poses are signed off.
 */
import { renderToStaticMarkup } from 'react-dom/server';
import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { QVersionIcon } from './src/components/QVersionIcon';

const OUT = process.argv[2];

const ITEMS: [string, string][] = [
  ['pet-cat-orange', '橘貓'],
  ['pet-cat-tabby', '虎斑貓'],
  ['pet-cat-tuxedo', '賓士貓'],
  ['pet-dog-dachshund', '臘腸犬'],
  ['pet-dog-poodle', '紅貴賓犬'],
  ['pet-dog-shiba', '柴犬'],
];

const tiles = ITEMS.map(([id, label]) => `
  <figure>
    <div class="tile">${renderToStaticMarkup(<QVersionIcon itemId={id} size={260} />)}</div>
    <div class="tile small">${renderToStaticMarkup(<QVersionIcon itemId={id} size={56} />)}</div>
    <figcaption>${label}<br><code>${id}</code></figcaption>
  </figure>`).join('');

writeFileSync(OUT, `<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { margin:0; padding:20px; background:#FAF3E6; font-family:system-ui, sans-serif; }
  .row { display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:14px; width:1140px; }
  figure { margin:0; text-align:center; }
  .tile { width:270px; height:270px; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center;
          background:#fff; border:2px solid #E8D9BE; border-radius:16px; overflow:hidden; }

</style></head><body><div class="row">${tiles}</div></body></html>`);
console.log('wrote', OUT);
```

```tsx
/** Throwaway: the three 貓 at card size with a ground line, for the anatomy pass. Delete when
 *  signed off. Usage: npx tsx tmp-cats3.tsx <out.html> */
import { renderToStaticMarkup } from 'react-dom/server';
import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { QVersionIcon } from './src/components/QVersionIcon';

const OUT = process.argv[2];
const IDS = ['pet-cat-orange', 'pet-cat-tabby', 'pet-cat-tuxedo'];

// 55 is LEG_BASELINE in the 64 viewBox, drawn in so paws can be checked against the ground.
const tile = (id: string, px: number) => `
  <figure style="margin:0">
    <figcaption style="font:12px sans-serif">${id}</figcaption>
    <div style="position:relative;width:${px}px;height:${px}px;border:1px solid #eee">
      ${renderToStaticMarkup(<QVersionIcon itemId={id} size={px} />)}
      <div style="position:absolute;left:0;right:0;top:${(px * 55) / 64}px;border-top:1px dashed #f0a"></div>
    </div>
  </figure>`;

writeFileSync(OUT, `<!doctype html><html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
 body{margin:0;padding:12px;background:#fff}
 .row{display:flex;gap:12px;align-items:flex-start}
</style></head><body>
<div class="row">${IDS.map(id => tile(id, 380)).join('')}</div>
<div class="row" style="margin-top:10px">${IDS.map(id => tile(id, 64)).join('')}${IDS.map(id => tile(id, 44)).join('')}</div>
</body></html>`);

```

## tmp-ceiling-light.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * Throwaway harness for signing off 燈具 — the ceiling mount, and the wall-switch integration.
 *
 * Same reason tmp-artwork-preview.tsx exists: the house interior is NOT reachable on the guest
 * path, so an interior change can otherwise only be checked by reading arithmetic. Here a real
 * room is built from the real interiorShell constants — floor, walls, ceiling plate AND the three
 * beams — and every fixture is placed by the SHIPPING resolver (lib/interiorPlacement.ts) from a
 * ray, which is the same call the drag ghost makes.
 *
 *   ?dark=1     start with the house lights OFF, to see which fixtures go out and which do not.
 *
 * Publishes:
 *   window.__ceiling   the resolved mounting of every fixture (mount, ok, top/bottom Y, the gap
 *                      to the ceiling above it) so a headless run can ASSERT rather than squint.
 *   window.__lights    { set(on), level() } over the real lib/interiorLights.ts.
 *
 * Delete with tmp-ceiling-light.html once this is signed off.
 */
import { useLayoutEffect, useRef, useState, useSyncExternalStore } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { Canvas, useFrame } from '@react-three/fiber';
import { Environment, OrbitControls } from '@react-three/drei';
import * as THREE from 'three';

import { FurnitureModel } from './src/components/Three/FurnitureItem';
import { getFloorMaterial } from './src/components/Three/floorMaterial';
import { getWallMaterial } from './src/components/Three/wallMaterial';
import { HDRI_APARTMENT } from './src/constants/environmentMaps';
import { getItemById } from './src/constants/items';
import { ROOM_GRID_SIZE, ROOM_HALF_SIZE } from './src/constants/rooms';
import {
  BASEBOARD_THICKNESS, CEILING_BEAMS, CEILING_BEAM_HEIGHT, CEILING_PLATE_THICKNESS,
  CEILING_PLATE_Y, CROWN_HEIGHT, CROWN_THICKNESS, CROWN_TOP_Y, INTERIOR_CEILING_Y,
  WALL_BASEBOARD_INSET, WALL_CROWN_INSET, WALL_THICKNESS, ceilingSurfaceAt,
} from './src/constants/interiorShell';
import {
  getFootprint, getFootprintVersion, measureFootprint, subscribeFootprints,
} from './src/lib/furniturePlacement';
import { buildMountableWalls, resolveInteriorPlacement } from './src/lib/interiorPlacement';
import {
  advanceInteriorLights, interiorLights, setInteriorLights,
} from './src/lib/interiorLights';
import type { PlacedItem } from './src/types';

const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const START_DARK = params.get('dark') === '1';

/** The interior draws every piece at 1.15 (BuildingInteriorView's FurnitureItem). */
const INTERIOR_SCALE = 1.15;

const ROOMS = [{ cx: 0, cz: 0 }];
const FACES = buildMountableWalls(ROOMS);
const N_FACE = FACES.find((f) => f.nz === -1)!;

/**
 * The fixtures, and where the player is imagined to be pointing when they place each.
 *
 * `z: 0` and `z: -3` are UNDER A BEAM; the others are under bare plate. Having both on screen at
 * once is the whole point — if the beams are not being seen, the two rows hang at the same height
 * and a screenshot shows a lamp buried in a beam.
 */
const CEILING_FIXTURES: { id: string; x: number; z: number }[] = [
  { id: 'light-crystal', x: -3.2, z: 0 },
  { id: 'light-industrial', x: -1, z: 0 },
  { id: 'light-modern', x: 1.4, z: 1.8 },
  { id: 'light-natural', x: 3.6, z: -3.0 },
];

/** The other three placement types, so all four kinds of 燈具 are in one picture. */
const TABLE_ID = 'item-22';

function Piece({ placement }: { placement: PlacedItem }) {
  const modelRef = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);
  const item = getItemById(placement.itemId);

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    if (modelRef.current) measureFootprint(placement.itemId, modelRef.current);
  }, [placement.itemId]);

  if (!item) return null;
  return (
    <group position={placement.position} rotation={[0, placement.rotation, 0]}>
      <group ref={modelRef}>
        <FurnitureModel name={item.name} item={item} scale={INTERIOR_SCALE} />
      </group>
    </group>
  );
}

/** The room shell: floor, two walls, the ceiling plate and the real beams. */
function Shell() {
  const baseboardOffset = WALL_BASEBOARD_INSET - BASEBOARD_THICKNESS / 2;
  const crownOffset = WALL_CROWN_INSET - CROWN_THICKNESS / 2;

  const wall = (x: number, z: number, rotation: number, sign: number) => (
    <group position={[x, 0, z]} rotation={[0, rotation, 0]}>
      <mesh position={[0, 2.5, 0]} receiveShadow>
        <boxGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE, 5, WALL_THICKNESS]} />
        <primitive object={getWallMaterial('wall-white', '#f5efe3')} attach="material" />
      </mesh>
      <mesh position={[0, 0.15, sign * -baseboardOffset]}>
        <boxGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE, 0.3, BASEBOARD_THICKNESS]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#8d6e52" roughness={0.8} />
      </mesh>
      <mesh position={[0, CROWN_TOP_Y - CROWN_HEIGHT / 2, sign * -crownOffset]}>
        <boxGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE, CROWN_HEIGHT, CROWN_THICKNESS]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#fdf6e7" roughness={0.7} />
      </mesh>
    </group>
  );

  return (
    <group>
      <mesh rotation={[-Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} position={[0, -0.01, 0]} receiveShadow>
        <planeGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE, ROOM_GRID_SIZE]} />
        <primitive object={getFloorMaterial('floor-oak', '#c9a06a')} attach="material" />
      </mesh>
      {wall(0, ROOM_HALF_SIZE, 0, 1)}
      {wall(-ROOM_HALF_SIZE, 0, Math.PI / 2, -1)}

      {/* Ceiling plate and beams, from the same constants BuildingInteriorView draws them from. */}
      <mesh position={[0, CEILING_PLATE_Y, 0]}>
        <boxGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE, CEILING_PLATE_THICKNESS, ROOM_GRID_SIZE]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#f7f2e8" roughness={0.9} side={THREE.DoubleSide} />
      </mesh>
      {CEILING_BEAMS.map((beam) => (
        <mesh
          key={`beam-${beam.offsetZ}`}
          position={[0, INTERIOR_CEILING_Y + CEILING_BEAM_HEIGHT / 2, beam.offsetZ]}
        >
          <boxGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE, CEILING_BEAM_HEIGHT, beam.width]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial color="#451a03" roughness={0.9} />
        </mesh>
      ))}
    </group>
  );
}

function useResolved() {
  const version = useSyncExternalStore(subscribeFootprints, getFootprintVersion);
  void version;

  const table: PlacedItem = { instanceId: 'table', itemId: TABLE_ID, position: [1.4, 0, 1.9], rotation: 0 };
  const out: PlacedItem[] = [table];
  const report: any[] = [];

  const record = (id: string, r: ReturnType<typeof resolveInteriorPlacement>) => {
    out.push(r.placement);
    const fp = getFootprint(id);
    const [px, py, pz] = r.placement.position;
    const surface = ceilingSurfaceAt(px, pz, ROOMS);
    report.push({
      id,
      name: getItemById(id)?.name,
      mount: r.mount,
      ok: r.ok,
      reason: r.reason,
      y: +py.toFixed(4),
      topY: fp ? +(py + fp.maxY).toFixed(4) : null,
      bottomY: fp ? +(py + fp.minY).toFixed(4) : null,
      ceilingHere: surface,
      // The number the whole "not sunk in, not floating" requirement reduces to.
      gapToCeiling: fp && surface !== null ? +(surface - (py + fp.maxY)).toFixed(4) : null,
      lighting: getItemById(id)?.lighting ?? null,
    });
  };

  // CEILING — aimed straight up from the floor, which is 「點天花板」.
  for (const f of CEILING_FIXTURES) {
    record(f.id, resolveInteriorPlacement({
      itemId: f.id,
      instanceId: `c-${f.id}`,
      rotation: 0,
      ray: { origin: { x: f.x, y: 1.4, z: f.z }, direction: { x: 0, y: 1, z: 0 } },
      faces: FACES, rooms: ROOMS, placements: out,
    }));
  }

  // WALL — 溫馨壁掛燈, aimed at the north wall.
  {
    const s = N_FACE.length * 0.3;
    const target = { x: N_FACE.x1 + N_FACE.dx * s, z: N_FACE.z1 + N_FACE.dz * s };
    const dir = new THREE.Vector3(target.x, 0, target.z).normalize();
    record('deco-wall-lamp', resolveInteriorPlacement({
      itemId: 'deco-wall-lamp',
      instanceId: 'w-sconce',
      rotation: 0,
      ray: { origin: { x: 0, y: 2.4, z: 0 }, direction: { x: dir.x, y: 0, z: dir.z } },
      faces: FACES, rooms: ROOMS, placements: out,
    }));
  }

  // SURFACE — 檯燈 dropped onto the table.
  record('furn-desk-lamp', resolveInteriorPlacement({
    itemId: 'furn-desk-lamp',
    instanceId: 's-desk-lamp',
    rotation: 0.5,
    ray: { origin: { x: table.position[0], y: 4, z: table.position[2] }, direction: { x: 0, y: -1, z: 0 } },
    faces: FACES, rooms: ROOMS, placements: out,
  }));

  // FLOOR — 弧形立燈 set down on the ground, and 螢光石燈 beside it (an `always` fixture, so it
  // is the one that must still be glowing after the switch goes off).
  record('furn-floor-lamp-arc', resolveInteriorPlacement({
    itemId: 'furn-floor-lamp-arc',
    instanceId: 'f-arc',
    rotation: 0,
    ray: { origin: { x: -3.6, y: 4, z: 3.2 }, direction: { x: 0, y: -1, z: 0 } },
    faces: FACES, rooms: ROOMS, placements: out,
  }));
  record('item-37', resolveInteriorPlacement({
    itemId: 'item-37',
    instanceId: 'f-glow',
    rotation: 0,
    ray: { origin: { x: -1.6, y: 4, z: 3.4 }, direction: { x: 0, y: -1, z: 0 } },
    faces: FACES, rooms: ROOMS, placements: out,
  }));

  (window as any).__ceiling = report;
  return out;
}

/**
 * The house's ambient light, driven by the REAL `advanceInteriorLights` — so the fixtures below
 * are reading the same eased `level` they read in the game, not a copy of it.
 */
function Ambience() {
  const ambientRef = useRef<THREE.AmbientLight>(null);
  const sunRef = useRef<THREE.DirectionalLight>(null);
  const { gl, scene } = (useFrame as any, { gl: null, scene: null }) as any;
  void gl; void scene;

  useFrame((state, delta) => {
    const level = advanceInteriorLights(delta);
    if (ambientRef.current) ambientRef.current.intensity = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(0.13, 0.7, level);
    if (sunRef.current) sunRef.current.intensity = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(0.16, 1.5, level);
    state.scene.environmentIntensity = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(0.05, 1, level);
    state.gl.toneMappingExposure = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(0.86, 1, level);
  });

  return (
    <>
      <ambientLight ref={ambientRef} intensity={0.7} color="#fffef4" />
      <directionalLight
        ref={sunRef}
        position={[6, 9, 4]}
        intensity={1.5}
        castShadow
        shadow-mapSize={[2048, 2048]}
        shadow-camera-left={-12}
        shadow-camera-right={12}
        shadow-camera-top={12}
        shadow-camera-bottom={-12}
      />
    </>
  );
}

function Scene() {
  const placements = useResolved();
  return (
    <group>
      <Shell />
      {placements.map((p) => <Piece key={p.instanceId} placement={p} />)}
      <Environment files={HDRI_APARTMENT} />
      <Ambience />
    </group>
  );
}

function App() {
  const [on, setOn] = useState(!START_DARK);

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    setInteriorLights(!START_DARK);
    (window as any).__lights = {
      set: (next: boolean) => { setInteriorLights(next); setOn(next); },
      level: () => interiorLights.level,
      on: () => interiorLights.on,
    };
  }, []);

  return (
    <>
      <button
        style={{
          position: 'fixed', zIndex: 10, top: 12, right: 12, padding: '10px 16px',
          font: '600 13px system-ui', borderRadius: 10, border: 0, cursor: 'pointer',
          background: on ? '#fde68a' : '#334155', color: on ? '#1f2937' : '#e2e8f0',
        }}
        onClick={() => { setInteriorLights(!on); setOn(!on); }}
      >
        {on ? '房間燈光：開' : '房間燈光：關'}
      </button>
      <Canvas
        shadows={{ type: THREE.PCFSoftShadowMap }}
        camera={{ position: [7.6, 3.2, -6.6], fov: 52, near: 0.3, far: 200 }}
        onCreated={({ camera }) => camera.lookAt(-0.5, 3.4, 1.2)}
        gl={{ toneMapping: THREE.ACESFilmicToneMapping }}
      >
        <Scene />
        <OrbitControls target={[-0.5, 3.0, 1.2]} />
      </Canvas>
    </>
  );
}

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(<App />);
```
