```tsx
/** Throwaway: legacy vs the imported authored parts, bare and dressed, to sign off the split. Delete when done. */
import { useRef } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { Canvas, useFrame } from '@react-three/fiber';
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { CharacterModel } from './src/components/Three/character';
import type { CharacterModelId, CharacterOutfit, CharacterRig } from './src/components/Three/character';
import { CHARACTER_ROOT_SCALE } from './src/constants/characterRig';
import { getHairSpec, AVATAR_SKIN_COLOR } from './src/constants/hair';

const BARE: CharacterOutfit = {
  hair: null, hat: null, outfit: null, pants: null, shoes: null,
  necklaceId: null, earring: null,
  hasGlasses: false, hasMask: false, hasShellNecklace: false, hasSkirt: false,
  hasSwimsuit: false, hasShirt: false, hasFallbackShirt: false, hasSleeves: false,
  specials: [],
  skinColor: AVATAR_SKIN_COLOR,
  bodyColor: '#718096',
};

/**
 * What a FRESH GUEST actually wears in the game, which is neither `BARE` nor `DRESSED`.
 *
 * `hasFallbackShirt = !isAnyShirtEquipped` (character/outfit.ts), so a player with nothing
 * equipped is still given a grey shirt and its sleeves — and no trousers at all. That is the
 * combination every screenshot of the running game is actually showing, and the one neither
 * preset here reproduced.
 */
const GAME_DEFAULT: CharacterOutfit = {
  ...BARE,
  hasFallbackShirt: true,
  hasSleeves: true,
  bodyColor: '#718096',
};

const DRESSED: CharacterOutfit = {
  ...BARE,
  hair: getHairSpec('hair-long') ?? null,
  hat: 'straw',
  outfit: 'jacket',
  pants: 'wide',
  shoes: 'sport',
  earring: 'jewel',
  hasGlasses: true,
  hasSleeves: true,
  bodyColor: '#4a5568',
};

function Rigged({ modelId, outfit }: { modelId: CharacterModelId; outfit: CharacterOutfit }) {
  const rig: CharacterRig = {
    head: useRef<THREE.Group>(null), torso: useRef<THREE.Group>(null),
    leftArm: useRef<THREE.Group>(null), rightArm: useRef<THREE.Group>(null),
    leftLeg: useRef<THREE.Group>(null), rightLeg: useRef<THREE.Group>(null),
    eyeL: useRef<THREE.Group>(null), eyeR: useRef<THREE.Group>(null),
    mouth: useRef<THREE.Group>(null), hairSway: useRef<THREE.Group>(null),
  };

  /**
   * What the CONTROLLER writes at rest, reproduced.
   *
   * Without this the harness renders the model as authored and is blind to a whole class of
   * bug — the one where the model is correct until Avatar's useFrame touches it. That is not
   * hypothetical: the imported eyes carried their own height, Avatar ASSIGNS `position.y`
   * rather than offsetting it, and the eyes flew 181 mm up in the game while every picture
   * taken here looked perfect.
   *
   * Only the resting values, and only the writes that are an assignment rather than an
   * animation — enough to catch "the controller overwrote what the model authored".
   */
  //  poses the legs at a walk-cycle extreme. Everything else here draws the
  // character standing still, which is exactly the state in which a leg that swings out of the
  // torso looks perfect.
  const swing = Number(new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('swing') ?? 0);

  useFrame(() => {
    if (swing) {
      if (rig.leftLeg.current) rig.leftLeg.current.rotation.x = -swing;
      if (rig.rightLeg.current) rig.rightLeg.current.rotation.x = swing;
    }
    for (const eye of [rig.eyeL.current, rig.eyeR.current]) {
      if (!eye) continue;
      eye.scale.y = 1;
      eye.position.y = 0;
    }
    if (rig.mouth.current) rig.mouth.current.scale.set(1, 1, 1);
  });

  return (
    <group scale={CHARACTER_ROOT_SCALE}>
      <CharacterModel modelId={modelId} rig={rig} outfit={outfit} />
    </group>
  );
}

type View = [label: string, cam: [number, number, number], fov: number, look: [number, number, number]];

// The character is 2.1638 world units tall with its feet on y=0, so every view below is framed
// on that: a full-body shot has to see y=0 (the sole rule) and y=2.16 (the crown rule) at once.
const VIEWS: View[] = [
  ['front', [0, 1.1, 5.2], 28, [0, 1.05, 0]],
  ['3/4', [3.2, 1.6, 4.0], 28, [0, 1.05, 0]],
  ['side', [5.2, 1.1, 0.02], 28, [0, 1.05, 0]],
  ['back', [0, 1.1, -5.2], 28, [0, 1.05, 0]],
  ['head', [0, 1.85, 2.0], 24, [0, 1.8, 0]],
  // The torso/hip seam: where a shirt's hem has to meet a trouser's waist. The two are fitted
  // by different mechanisms (a scaled socket vs. a lathe against a hard-coded leg radius), so
  // it is the one place on a re-proportioned body where bare skin can appear between them.
  ['waist seam', [0, 0.95, 1.6], 22, [0, 0.9, 0]],
  ['feet + ground line', [0, 0.18, 2.2], 24, [0, 0.25, 0]],
  // Poke-through hunting. Every one of these is a place where a wearable was lathed against a
  // number rather than mounted on a socket, so a re-proportioned body can come through it.
  ['zoom: shoulder', [0.75, 1.15, 0.95], 20, [0.25, 1.0, 0]],
  ['zoom: shirt hem', [0, 0.72, 1.15], 20, [0, 0.62, 0]],
  ['zoom: thigh front', [0, 0.62, 1.05], 20, [0, 0.5, 0]],
  ['zoom: thigh side', [1.05, 0.62, 0.06], 20, [0, 0.5, 0]],
  ['zoom: hem + shoe', [0, 0.30, 1.0], 20, [0, 0.18, 0]],
  // The two seams the body itself makes, bare: where the arm meets the torso and where the
  // legs leave it. Nothing is worn here — this is the MODEL's own silhouette.
  ['joint: shoulder front', [0, 1.02, 1.35], 22, [0, 0.98, 0]],
  ['joint: shoulder 3/4', [0.95, 1.15, 1.05], 22, [0.1, 0.98, 0]],
  ['joint: hip front', [0, 0.60, 1.25], 22, [0, 0.56, 0]],
  ['joint: hip 3/4', [0.9, 0.68, 1.0], 22, [0, 0.56, 0]],
  // The reported gap: shirt hem meets leg top, at the framing the screenshot was taken at.
  ['gap: shirt/leg front', [0, 0.70, 1.15], 22, [0, 0.64, 0]],
  ['gap: shirt/leg 3/4', [0.8, 0.76, 0.95], 22, [0, 0.64, 0]],
];

// One model + one outfit per page load: six live WebGL contexts is already near the browser's
// limit, and past it the oldest canvas is silently dropped and the screenshot shows an empty
// square that looks exactly like a part that failed to load.
const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const modelId = (params.get('model') ?? 'authored') as CharacterModelId;
const suit = params.get('suit');
const outfit = suit === 'dressed' ? DRESSED : suit === 'game' ? GAME_DEFAULT : BARE;
const only = params.get('views');
const SHOWN = only ? VIEWS.filter((v) => v[0].includes(only)) : VIEWS.slice(0, 7);
if (params.get('pants')) outfit.pants = params.get('pants') as never;
if (params.get('outfit')) outfit.outfit = params.get('outfit') as never;
if (params.get('shoes')) outfit.shoes = params.get('shoes') as never;
if (params.get('sleeves') === '0') outfit.hasSleeves = false;
if (params.get('top') === 'shirt') { outfit.hasShirt = true; outfit.hasFallbackShirt = false; outfit.hasSleeves = true; }

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <div style={{ font: '12px sans-serif', background: '#f4f1ea' }}>
    <div style={{ padding: '4px 6px', fontWeight: 600 }}>
      {modelId} · {params.get('suit') ?? 'bare'}
    </div>
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(5, 380px)', gap: 6, padding: 6 }}>
      {SHOWN.map(([vLabel, cam, fov, look]) => (
        <div key={vLabel}>
          <div style={{ padding: '2px 0' }}>{vLabel}</div>
          <div style={{ width: 380, height: 420, background: '#8fa9bd' }}>
            <Canvas camera={{ position: cam, fov }} onCreated={({ camera }) => camera.lookAt(...look)}>
              <ambientLight intensity={0.85} />
              <directionalLight position={[3, 5, 4]} intensity={1.5} />
              <directionalLight position={[-3, 2, -2]} intensity={0.5} />
              {/* The ground plane the sole is supposed to touch. */}
              <mesh rotation={[-Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} position={[0, 0, 0]}>
                <planeGeometry args={[6, 6]} />
                <meshStandardMaterial color="#7d9b6a" />
              </mesh>
              <Rigged modelId={modelId} outfit={outfit} />
            </Canvas>
          </div>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  </div>,
);
```

## tmp-cosmetic-preview.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * Throwaway harness for signing off the special cosmetic effect system.
 *
 * Two modes:
 *   ?mode=gallery                 all ten ornaments side by side, for the art pass
 *   ?mode=live&item=<itemId>      one ornament worn on a stand-in socket, emitting
 *
 * Live mode also publishes counts on `window.__fx` so a headless run can assert on the
 * pools rather than only on a screenshot: how many particles of each shape are alive, and
 * whether a creature is out.
 *
 * Delete with tmp-cosmetic-preview.html once this is signed off.
 */
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { Canvas, useFrame, useThree } from '@react-three/fiber';
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { AppProvider, useApp } from './src/context/AppContext';
import { WeatherType } from './src/types';
import { CosmeticEffectField, CosmeticSlot } from './src/components/Three/effects';
import { SPECIAL_COSMETICS, getSpecialCosmetic, resolveSpecialCosmetics } from './src/constants/cosmeticEffects';
import { playerBus } from './src/lib/playerBus';
import { LegacyCharacterModel } from './src/components/Three/character/legacy';
import { resolveCharacterOutfit } from './src/components/Three/character/outfit';
import {
  CHARACTER_ROOT_SCALE, LEGACY_ATTACHMENTS, LEGACY_SKELETON,
} from './src/constants/characterRig';
import { PetModel } from './src/components/Three/Pets';
import { getPetSpec } from './src/constants/pets';
import { petRootScale } from './src/constants/petRig';
import { ALL_ITEMS } from './src/constants/items';
import { QVersionIcon } from './src/components/QVersionIcon';

const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const MODE = params.get('mode') ?? 'gallery';
const ITEM = params.get('item') ?? 'fx-star-hairpin';
const MOVING = params.get('moving') === '1';
const NIGHT = params.get('night') === '1';
/**
 * `?slope=<dy/dx>` — a synthetic hillside for the ground-conforming check.
 *
 * The real sampler is the island's getSurfaceAt, which needs a profile and a territory level
 * this harness has neither of. A plane with a known gradient is better for the test anyway: the
 * ring's tilt has an exact expected value (atan of the gradient, clamped by maxTilt), so the
 * check is arithmetic rather than "does that look about right".
 *
 * FLOOR_Y matches where AvatarStand puts the feet, so the ring lands under them.
 */
const SLOPE = Number(params.get('slope') ?? '0');
const FLOOR_Y = -1.1;
const groundAt = (x: number) => FLOOR_Y + x * SLOPE;
/**
 * `?glow=<intensity>` — overrides every glow spec's intensity before anything renders.
 *
 * three 0.184 has no legacy light mode, so a point light's intensity is candela and its
 * irradiance is intensity/d^decay. That makes the right number something to MEASURE against the
 * scene it is lit into, not to reason out, and rebuilding the catalog file per value is both
 * slow and a CRLF trap.
 */
const GLOW_OVERRIDE = params.get('glow');
if (GLOW_OVERRIDE) {
  for (const def of SPECIAL_COSMETICS) {
    if (def.effect.glow) def.effect.glow = { ...def.effect.glow, intensity: Number(GLOW_OVERRIDE) };
  }
}

/** `?cam=x,y,z` — the framings above are per-mode, and a halo sits above every one of them. */
const CAM_OVERRIDE = params.get('cam')
  ? (params.get('cam')!.split(',').map(Number) as [number, number, number])
  : null;
const BOND = params.get('bond') === '1';

/**
 * Where the harness hangs each socket on its reference ball.
 *
 * NOT the real attachment points — those are stated relative to a head joint or a dog's body
 * origin, which this stand-in does not have. These put the ornament on the surface of a ball
 * so its own proportions can be judged; the real placement is checked in-game.
 */
const DISPLAY_POINT: Record<string, { position: readonly [number, number, number]; rotation?: readonly [number, number, number] }> = {
  hairPin: { position: [0.20, 0.13, 0.115], rotation: [0, 0.9, 0] },
  crown: { position: [0, 0, 0] },
  pendant: { position: [0, -0.18, 0.1] },
  back: { position: [0, -0.1, -0.2] },
  halo: { position: [0, 0.42, 0] },
  ankle: { position: [0, -0.24, 0] },
  aura: { position: [0, -0.3, 0] },
  petHead: { position: [0, 0.38, 0] },
  petCollar: { position: [0, 0, 0] },
  petBack: { position: [0, 0.34, 0] },
};

/** Counts live particles per shape by reading the per-instance alpha the runtime writes. */
const peak: Record<string, number> = {};
const raycastHits = { frames: 0, hits: [] as string[] };

function Probe() {
  const scene = useThree(s => s.scene);
  const camera = useThree(s => s.camera);
  const gl = useThree(s => s.gl);
  useFrame(() => {
    const perShape: Record<string, number> = {};
    let creatures = 0;
    scene.traverse((o) => {
      const im = o as THREE.InstancedMesh;
      if (im.isInstancedMesh) {
        const alpha = im.geometry.getAttribute('aAlpha');
        if (!alpha) return;
        let live = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < alpha.count; i++) if (alpha.getX(i) > 0.001) live++;
        // Shapes have no name, so key on the geometry's own vertex count + index —
        // enough to tell them apart for a smoke test.
        const key = im.name.replace('cosmetic-particles-', '');
        perShape[key] = live;
        peak[key] = Math.max(peak[key] ?? 0, live);
      }
      if (o.name === 'cosmetic-creature' && o.visible) creatures++;
    });
    peak.creatures = Math.max(peak.creatures ?? 0, creatures);

    // SECTION 五: an effect may not affect interaction. Fire a ray from the camera straight at
    // every live particle and every visible creature, and record anything the scene reports as
    // hit. A correct system reports NOTHING for those rays — the effect meshes opt out of
    // raycasting entirely, so they cannot swallow a click or occlude the interaction test.
    raycastHits.frames++;
    const cam = camera as THREE.PerspectiveCamera;
    scene.traverse((o) => {
      const im = o as THREE.InstancedMesh;
      const live = im.isInstancedMesh && im.visible;
      const creature = o.name === 'cosmetic-creature' && o.visible;
      if (!live && !creature) return;
      const target = o.getWorldPosition(new THREE.Vector3());
      if (live) {
        // An instanced pool's own origin is not where its particles are; aim at instance 0.
        const m = new THREE.Matrix4();
        im.getMatrixAt(0, m);
        target.setFromMatrixPosition(m);
      }
      if (target.lengthSq() === 0) return;
      const dir = target.clone().sub(cam.position).normalize();
      const ray = new THREE.Raycaster(cam.position, dir);
      for (const hit of ray.intersectObject(scene, true)) {
        if (hit.object.name.startsWith('cosmetic-')) {
          raycastHits.hits.push(hit.object.name);
        }
      }
    });

    // Wing pose, for the flap check: the two groups the runtime drives, found by the same
    // userData tag the runtime finds them by.
    const wings: Record<string, number> = {};
    scene.traverse((o) => {
      const tag = o.userData?.cosmeticPart;
      if (typeof tag === 'string') wings[tag] = o.rotation.z;
    });

    // The ground ring's WORLD orientation and height, for the conforming check. Read off the
    // world matrix rather than off local rotation, because the whole point of that socket is
    // that its local transform is the inverse of its parent's.
    let ground: { x: number; z: number; roll: number; pitch: number; y: number; err: number } | null = null;
    scene.traverse((o) => {
      if (o.name !== 'cosmetic-ground') return;
      const q = o.getWorldQuaternion(new THREE.Quaternion());
      const e = new THREE.Euler().setFromQuaternion(q, 'XYZ');
      const p = o.getWorldPosition(new THREE.Vector3());
      ground = {
        x: +p.x.toFixed(4),
        z: +p.z.toFixed(4),
        roll: +e.z.toFixed(4),
        pitch: +e.x.toFixed(4),
        y: +p.y.toFixed(4),
        // How far the ring's centre is above the plane it is meant to be lying on.
        err: +(p.y - (FLOOR_Y + p.x * SLOPE)).toFixed(4),
      };
    });

    // Every point light in the scene, so the glow pool's budget can be asserted rather than
    // eyeballed: how many exist, how many are actually contributing, and where they are.
    const lights: Array<{ on: boolean; i: number; y: number }> = [];
    scene.traverse((o) => {
      const l = o as THREE.PointLight;
      if (l.isPointLight) lights.push({ on: l.visible, i: +l.intensity.toFixed(3), y: +l.getWorldPosition(new THREE.Vector3()).y.toFixed(2) });
    });
    peak.litLights = Math.max(peak.litLights ?? 0, lights.filter(l => l.on).length);

    (window as unknown as { __fx: unknown }).__fx = {
      perShape, peak, creatures, wings, lights, ground,
      render: { calls: gl.info.render.calls, tris: gl.info.render.triangles },
      raycast: { frames: raycastHits.frames, hits: raycastHits.hits.length },
      t: performance.now() / 1000,
    };
  });
  return null;
}

/**
 * A stand-in wearer: a bare ball where a head or a collar would be.
 *
 * Player ornaments are authored against the character's 0.26 head; pet ornaments against the
 * dog's 0.4 half-width head in dog-local units. The group is scaled so both sit on a
 * same-sized reference ball, which is the only way to judge whether the two sets read as one
 * art direction.
 */
function Wearer({ itemId, position }: { itemId: string; position: [number, number, number] }) {
  const def = getSpecialCosmetic(itemId);
  if (!def) return null;
  const isPet = def.socket.startsWith('pet');
  const headR = isPet ? 0.4 : 0.26;
  const fit = 0.26 / headR;
  return (
    <group position={position} scale={fit}>
      <mesh>
        <sphereGeometry args={[headR, 16, 16]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#f3d9c0" roughness={0.8} />
      </mesh>
      <CosmeticSlot socket={def.socket} cosmetics={[def]} point={DISPLAY_POINT[def.socket]} rootScale={1 / fit} />
    </group>
  );
}

/** `?night=1` flips the app's weather, which is what EffectField derives `isNight` from. */
function NightDriver() {
  const { setWeather } = useApp();
  useEffect(() => {
    if (params.get('night') === '1') setWeather(WeatherType.MIDNIGHT);
  }, [setWeather]);
  return null;
}

/** Keeps the flags the `moving` trigger and the bond read set, without a real avatar. */
function BusDriver() {
  useEffect(() => {
    // Exposed so a headless driver can flip movement and take-off mid-run — the flap pose and
    // the jump burst are both about a TRANSITION, and neither can be seen in a static load.
    (window as unknown as { __bus: unknown }).__bus = playerBus;
    playerBus.playerIsMoving = MOVING;
    playerBus.dogIsMoving = MOVING;
    if (BOND) {
      playerBus.playerPos = new THREE.Vector3(-0.4, 0, 0);
      playerBus.dogPos = new THREE.Vector3(0.4, 0, 0);
    }
  }, []);
  return null;
}

function Gallery() {
  const spacing = 0.9;
  return (
    <>
      {SPECIAL_COSMETICS.map((def, i) => {
        const col = i % 5;
        const row = Math.floor(i / 5);
        return (
          <Wearer
            key={def.itemId}
            itemId={def.itemId}
            position={[(col - 2) * spacing, 0.9 - row * 1.1, 0]}
          />
        );
      })}
    </>
  );
}

const YAW = Number(params.get('yaw') ?? '0');

const CAMERA: Record<string, [number, number, number]> = {
  gallery: [0, 0.1, 6.4],
  // Roughly the game's third-person framing: the character is 2.16 world units tall.
  avatar: [0, 0.5, 3.4],
  dog: [0, 0.35, 1.9],
  live: [0, 0.15, 1.5],
  crowd: [0, 0.6, 3.6],
  bond: [0, 0.6, 4.4],
};

/**
 * The REAL legacy character model wearing the real sockets — the check the ball gallery
 * cannot make. Nothing is stubbed except the rig refs, which the controller would own.
 */
function AvatarStand() {
  const rig = {
    head: useRef<THREE.Group>(null), torso: useRef<THREE.Group>(null),
    leftArm: useRef<THREE.Group>(null), rightArm: useRef<THREE.Group>(null),
    leftLeg: useRef<THREE.Group>(null), rightLeg: useRef<THREE.Group>(null),
    eyeL: useRef<THREE.Group>(null), eyeR: useRef<THREE.Group>(null),
    mouth: useRef<THREE.Group>(null), hairSway: useRef<THREE.Group>(null),
  };
  const wanted = (params.get('items') ?? 'fx-star-hairpin,fx-forest-crown,fx-flame-charm').split(',');
  const equipped = ALL_ITEMS.filter(i => wanted.includes(i.id));
  const outfit = resolveCharacterOutfit(equipped);
  // ?pitch= tips the whole character the way swimming and crawling do. The ground socket has
  // to survive a rotated parent: a world-vertical offset becomes a local offset with x and z
  // in it, and reading that back is what used to make the ring wander off the wearer.
  const pitch = Number(params.get('pitch') ?? '0');
  return (
    <group scale={CHARACTER_ROOT_SCALE} position={[0, -1.1, 0]} rotation={[pitch, 0.6, 0]}>
      <LegacyCharacterModel
        rig={rig}
        skeleton={LEGACY_SKELETON}
        attachments={LEGACY_ATTACHMENTS}
        outfit={outfit}
      />
    </group>
  );
}

/**
 * The REAL companion model, wearing the real per-breed anchors — no stand-in geometry at all now
 * that pet cosmetics ride Three/Pets.tsx's PetModel. ?breed= picks which animal.
 */
function DogStand() {
  const breed = params.get('breed') ?? 'shiba';
  const species = ['orange','tabby','tuxedo'].includes(breed) ? 'cat'
    : ['budgie','javasparrow','canary','phoenix'].includes(breed) ? 'bird' : 'dog';
  const itemId = 'pet-' + species + '-' + breed;
  const spec = getPetSpec(itemId);
  const wanted = (params.get('items') ?? 'fx-pet-bow,fx-pet-star-collar,fx-pet-beehive').split(',');
  const cosmetics = resolveSpecialCosmetics(wanted, 'pet');
  if (!spec) return null;
  return (
    <group scale={petRootScale(spec)} position={[0, -0.55, 0]}>
      <PetModel itemId={itemId} cosmetics={cosmetics} />
    </group>
  );
}

function Rig() {
  const ref = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);
  useFrame(() => {
    // Fixed yaw rather than a turntable: a screenshot has to be reproducible, and two runs
    // at ?yaw= give the two angles a turntable would have.
    if (ref.current) ref.current.rotation.y = YAW;
  });
  return (
    <group ref={ref}>
      {MODE === 'gallery' && <Gallery />}
      {MODE === 'avatar' && <AvatarStand />}
      {MODE === 'dog' && <DogStand />}
      {MODE === 'live' && <Wearer itemId={ITEM} position={[0, 0, 0]} />}
      {/* `?mode=crowd&item=…&n=5` — several wearers of ONE item, spread in depth, for asserting
          a pooled resource's cap. The glow pool is the only effect whose budget cannot be seen
          with a single wearer on screen. */}
      {MODE === 'crowd' && Array.from({ length: Number(params.get('n') ?? 5) }).map((_, i) => (
        <Wearer key={i} itemId={ITEM} position={[(i - 2) * 0.75, 0, -i * 1.2]} />
      ))}
      {/* Both halves of a starlight pair, standing within BOND_RADIUS of each other. */}
      {MODE === 'bond' && (
        <>
          <group position={[-0.6, 0, 0]}><AvatarStand /></group>
          <group position={[0.6, 0, 0]}><DogStand /></group>
        </>
      )}
    </group>
  );
}

/** The shop/inventory icons, straight through QVersionIcon's real dispatch. */
function IconSheet() {
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexWrap: 'wrap', gap: 24, padding: 32, background: '#f6f3ec' }}>
      {SPECIAL_COSMETICS.map(def => {
        const item = ALL_ITEMS.find(i => i.id === def.itemId)!;
        return (
          <div key={def.itemId} style={{ width: 150, textAlign: 'center', font: '13px system-ui', color: '#264653' }}>
            <div style={{ background: '#fff', borderRadius: 18, padding: 12, border: '1px solid #dfe6e2' }}>
              <QVersionIcon itemId={def.itemId} size={96} />
            </div>
            <div style={{ marginTop: 8, fontWeight: 800 }}>{item.name}</div>
          </div>
        );
      })}
    </div>
  );
}

if (MODE === 'icons') {
  createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(<IconSheet />);
} else createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <AppProvider>
    <NightDriver />
    <Canvas camera={{ position: CAM_OVERRIDE ?? CAMERA[MODE] ?? [0, 0.15, 1.5], fov: 35 }}>
      {/* The hillside itself, drawn at exactly the gradient the sampler reports, so a ring that
          is conforming correctly sits flush against it and one that is not is obviously wrong. */}
      {SLOPE !== 0 && (
        <mesh position={[0, FLOOR_Y, 0]} rotation={[-Math.PI / 2, 0, -Math.atan(SLOPE)]}>
          <planeGeometry args={[16, 16]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial color="#6f8f68" roughness={1} />
        </mesh>
      )}
      {/* Night mode dims the harness's own key lights to roughly the island's midnight levels,
          because a 1.7 point light cannot be seen against a 1.1 ambient — which is the exact
          reason the glow spec is night-triggered in the first place. */}
      <ambientLight intensity={NIGHT ? 0.22 : 1.1} />
      <directionalLight position={[3, 5, 4]} intensity={NIGHT ? 0.18 : 1.4} />
      {/* A floor, so a light has something to land on. Without it "the ground is lit" has
          nothing to be true of. */}
      {NIGHT && (
        <mesh rotation={[-Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} position={[0, -1.1, 0]} receiveShadow>
          <planeGeometry args={[14, 14]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial color="#5e7a5a" roughness={1} />
        </mesh>
      )}
      <BusDriver />
      <CosmeticEffectField groundAt={SLOPE !== 0 ? groundAt : undefined}>
        <Rig />
      </CosmeticEffectField>
      <Probe />
    </Canvas>
  </AppProvider>,
);
```

```tsx
/**
 * Throwaway: the 每日登入 board, LIVE — press 領取 and the real celebration runs.
 *
 * This exists because the claim animation and its sound are unreachable in the app itself right
 * now: the panel only celebrates a claim that was actually written, and the write is being refused
 * (see firestore.rules — the update whitelist never learned the seven-day cycle's fields). The
 * animation was never broken; nothing was reaching it.
 *
 * So this page runs the same board with the same celebration and the same sound, against state held
 * in memory. Nothing here is a mock of the animation — `DailyLoginBoard`, `useCoinFlight`, the
 * `.daily-claim-*` CSS and `SoundEffect.COIN` are the app's own. The only thing replaced is where
 * the numbers live.
 *
 * Delete once the rules are deployed and the real panel can be watched instead.
 */
import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { Gift, RotateCcw } from 'lucide-react';
import './src/index.css';
import { DailyLoginBoard } from './src/components/UI/DailyLoginPanel';
import { buildSquares, resolveCycle } from './src/constants/dailyLogin';
import { PanelHeader, Button } from './src/components/UI/DesignKit';
import { playSound, SoundEffect } from './src/lib/soundUtils';

/** Day 3 of a round with days 1–2 already taken, so today's square is live and claimable. */
const cycle = resolveCycle('2026-03-10', new Date('2026-03-12T10:00:00+08:00'));

/** The panel's own count-up, reproduced here — it lives inside DailyLoginPanel and is not exported. */
function useCountUp(target: number, durationMs = 700): number {
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(target);
  const fromRef = useRef(target);
  useEffect(() => {
    const from = fromRef.current;
    if (from === target) return;
    const started = performance.now();
    let raf = 0;
    const step = (nowMs: number) => {
      const t = Math.min(1, (nowMs - started) / durationMs);
      setShown(Math.round(from + (target - from) * (1 - (1 - t) ** 3)));
      if (t < 1) raf = requestAnimationFrame(step);
      else fromRef.current = target;
    };
    raf = requestAnimationFrame(step);
    return () => { cancelAnimationFrame(raf); fromRef.current = target; };
  }, [target, durationMs]);
  return shown;
}

const CLAIM_FX_MS = 1100;

function Demo() {
  const [claimed, setClaimed] = useState<number[]>([1, 2]);
  const [balance, setBalance] = useState(4820);
  const [celebrating, setCelebrating] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const shownBalance = useCountUp(balance);

  const squares = buildSquares(cycle, new Set(claimed), true);

  // Exactly what DailyLoginPanel.handleClaim does after a successful write — the sound, the
  // celebration, and the balance moving. The write is the only thing missing.
  const claim = useCallback((day: number) => {
    const square = squares[day - 1];
    if (!square) return;
    playSound(SoundEffect.COIN);
    setClaimed(prev => [...prev, day].sort((a, b) => a - b));
    setBalance(prev => prev + square.prize.coins);
    setCelebrating(day);
    window.setTimeout(() => setCelebrating(null), CLAIM_FX_MS);
  }, [squares]);

  const reset = () => {
    setClaimed([1, 2]);
    setBalance(4820);
    setCelebrating(null);
  };

  return (
    <div className="min-h-screen bg-island-cream-2 p-4 flex flex-col items-center gap-4">
      <div className="w-full max-w-[980px] flex items-center justify-between gap-3">
        <p className="text-sm font-black text-island-navy">
          按下第 3 天的「領取」—— 金幣會飛進右上角的錢包，並播放 <code>SoundEffect.COIN</code>
        </p>
        <Button variant="secondary" onClick={reset} className="px-3 py-2 text-xs flex items-center gap-1.5">
          <RotateCcw size={13} strokeWidth={2.5} /> 重來
        </Button>
      </div>

      <div className="w-full max-w-[980px] bg-white rounded-3xl border border-island-line overflow-hidden shadow-xl">
        <PanelHeader icon={<Gift size={20} strokeWidth={2.5} />} title="每日登入獎勵" subtitle="每天回來看看，領取逐日增加的金幣！" />
        <DailyLoginBoard
          squares={squares}
          dayIndex={3}
          balance={balance}
          shownBalance={shownBalance}
          countdownMs={13 * 3600_000 + 41 * 60_000 + 7000}
          cycleId={cycle.cycleId}
          celebratingDay={celebrating}
          onClaim={(day) => claim(day)}
        />
      </div>

      {/* No second frame at a phone width here. The board's columns come from Tailwind's `md:`/`lg:`
          breakpoints, which measure the VIEWPORT and not the box the board is put in — a 390px-wide
          container on a desktop window still lays out eight columns and shows a squashed desktop
          board rather than the phone one. Narrow the window instead; the flight re-measures both
          ends on every claim, so its path is correct at whatever width it is watched at. */}
      <p className="text-xs font-bold text-island-navy-soft/70">
        想看手機版就把視窗拉窄再領一次 —— 金幣飛行會重新量測起點和終點。
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(<Demo />);
```

## tmp-daily-prizes.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * Throwaway: every kind of 每日登入 prize on screen at once, plus the 領取揭曉 stage for each.
 *
 * The real panel can only ever show ONE round, and a round shows at most four or five of the seven
 * prize kinds — so watching the feature in the app proves the day it happens to be and nothing
 * else. This renders several rounds' boards side by side (chosen so that between them they cover
 * 商品碎片, 金幣, 金幣＋碎片, 功能卡, 抽獎券, 商品 and 免費轉盤) against the app's OWN components:
 * `DailyLoginBoard`, `DailyClaimReveal`, the real `buildSquares` and the real prize roll.
 *
 * Delete once the round has been watched in the app across a full week.
 */
import { useState } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import './src/index.css';
import { DailyLoginBoard } from './src/components/UI/DailyLoginPanel';
import { DailyClaimReveal } from './src/components/UI/DailyClaimReveal';
import { addCivilDays, buildSquares, resolveCycle, CYCLE_LENGTH } from './src/constants/dailyLogin';
import { resolveDailyPrize, emptyAward, type DailyPrizeAward } from './src/constants/dailyLoginPrizes';

/** Rounds picked by `tmp-probe-daily.ts` so that between them every prize kind appears. */
const ANCHORS = ['2026-03-10', '2026-03-17', '2026-03-24', '2026-04-07'];

/** The award a claim of that day would produce, with nothing capped and nothing already owned. */
function awardFor(cycleId: string, day: number): DailyPrizeAward {
  const resolved = resolveDailyPrize(cycleId, day, []);
  const { prize } = resolved;
  return {
    ...emptyAward(prize.kind),
    coins: prize.coins,
    fragmentItemId: resolved.fragmentItemId,
    fragmentsKept: prize.itemFragments,
    tickets: prize.tickets,
    cardId: resolved.cardId,
    cardsGranted: prize.cards,
    itemId: resolved.itemId,
    spins: prize.spins,
  };
}

/**
 * `?round=2026-03-17&day=2` opens that day's 領取揭曉 on load.
 *
 * The reveal is a full-screen overlay, so unlike the boards it cannot be tiled — one screenshot
 * shows exactly one of them. A query parameter is how a headless pass gets through all seven
 * without a click script.
 */
function revealFromQuery(): { day: number; award: DailyPrizeAward } | null {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
  const round = params.get('round');
  const day = Number(params.get('day'));
  if (!round || !Number.isInteger(day) || day < 1 || day > CYCLE_LENGTH) return null;
  return { day, award: awardFor(`cycle-${round}`, day) };
}

/**
 * `?still=1` forces every reveal animation to its END state.
 *
 * Headless Edge advances TIMERS under `--virtual-time-budget` but runs CSS animations on the real
 * clock, so a screenshot taken 200ms after load catches the 結束 button (its line animation has no
 * delay) and misses the amount and the note (theirs are delayed ~1s) — both sitting at the
 * `opacity: 0` their keyframes start from. That reads as missing copy when the copy is fine.
 *
 * Overriding to the end state is the honest fix for a LAYOUT check: it is the frame the player ends
 * up looking at. It says nothing about the timeline, which is watched in the app instead.
 */
function StillFrame() {
  return (
    <style>{`
      .daily-reveal-dim { background-color: rgba(14, 10, 8, 0.9) !important; animation: none !important; }
      .daily-reveal-amount,
      .daily-reveal-line { opacity: 1 !important; transform: none !important; filter: none !important; animation: none !important; }
      .daily-reveal-spin { animation: none !important; }
      .daily-reveal-flash, .daily-reveal-burst, .daily-reveal-ring { opacity: 0 !important; }
    `}</style>
  );
}

function Demo() {
  const [reveal, setReveal] = useState<{ day: number; award: DailyPrizeAward } | null>(revealFromQuery);

  return (
    <div className="min-h-screen bg-island-cream-2 p-4 flex flex-col items-center gap-6">
      {new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).has('still') && <StillFrame />}
      {reveal && (
        <DailyClaimReveal
          day={reveal.day}
          isGrand={reveal.day === CYCLE_LENGTH}
          award={reveal.award}
          onDone={() => setReveal(null)}
        />
      )}

      {ANCHORS.map((anchor) => {
        // Day 3 of the round, days 1–2 already taken, so the board shows 已領取 / 已錯過 /
        // 今日可領 / 未開放 all at once as well as four different prizes.
        const cycle = resolveCycle(anchor, new Date(addCivilDays(anchor, 2) + 'T10:00:00+08:00'));
        const squares = buildSquares(cycle, new Set([1]), true);
        return (
          <div key={anchor} className="w-full max-w-[1000px]">
            <p className="text-xs font-black text-island-navy-soft/80 mb-1.5">{cycle.cycleId}</p>
            <div className="bg-white rounded-3xl border border-island-line overflow-hidden shadow-lg">
              <DailyLoginBoard
                squares={squares}
                dayIndex={3}
                balance={4820}
                shownBalance={4820}
                countdownMs={13 * 3600_000 + 41 * 60_000 + 7000}
                cycleId={cycle.cycleId}
                onClaim={(day) => setReveal({ day, award: awardFor(cycle.cycleId, day) })}
              />
            </div>
          </div>
        );
      })}
    </div>
  );
}

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(<Demo />);
```

## tmp-deckstand.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * Throwaway harness for the 2026-09 「玩家站上小型觀景平台會漂浮」 pass.
 *
 * Renders each standable piece with a player-height marker standing on it, placed by the REAL
 * surface lookup (`getSurfaceAt`, lib/placementSurfaces.ts) — the same call `footLevelAt` makes
 * for the character every frame. The left figure is where the player USED to be put (the model's
 * `maxY`), the right one is where the fix puts them (`standY`).
 *
 * ?ids=a,b   pieces to show (default: both standable items)
 * ?elev=14   camera elevation in degrees
 * ?before=0  hide the old position
 *
 * Delete with tmp-deckstand.html once the pass is signed off.
 */
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { Canvas } from '@react-three/fiber';
import * as THREE from 'three';

import { FurnitureModel } from './src/components/Three/FurnitureItem';
import { ALL_ITEMS, getItemById, getStandableSurface } from './src/constants/items';
import { getFootprint, measureFootprint } from './src/lib/furniturePlacement';
import { getSurfaceAt } from './src/lib/placementSurfaces';
import { PLATEAU_INNER_COLOR } from './src/constants/terrain';
import { LEGACY_SKELETON, worldHeight } from './src/constants/characterRig';
import { PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS } from './src/utils/placementRules';

const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const ELEV = Number(params.get('elev') ?? 14);
const SHOW_BEFORE = params.get('before') !== '0';
const ISLAND_SCALE = 0.85;
const PLAYER_H = worldHeight(LEGACY_SKELETON);

const DEFAULT_IDS = ALL_ITEMS.filter((i) => getStandableSurface(i.id)).map((i) => i.id);
const IDS = (params.get('ids') ?? DEFAULT_IDS.join(',')).split(',').map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);

/** A body of the player's real height and radius, standing with its SOLES at `y`. */
function Body({ x, y, z, color }: { x: number; y: number; z: number; color: string }) {
  return (
    <group position={[x, y, z]}>
      <mesh position={[0, PLAYER_H / 2, 0]} castShadow>
        <capsuleGeometry args={[PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS, PLAYER_H - PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS * 2, 4, 10]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color={color} roughness={0.9} transparent opacity={0.85} />
      </mesh>
      {/* A disc exactly at the soles, so "where are the feet" is a line, not a guess. */}
      <mesh rotation={[-Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]}>
        <ringGeometry args={[PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS * 0.75, PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS, 20]} />
        <meshBasicMaterial color={color} side={THREE.DoubleSide} />
      </mesh>
    </group>
  );
}

function Piece({ id, ox }: { id: string; ox: number }) {
  const item = getItemById(id)!;
  const fp = getFootprint(id);
  if (!fp) return null;
  const placement = { instanceId: id, itemId: id, position: [ox, 0, 0] as [number, number, number], rotation: 0 };
  // The shipping lookup, called exactly the way characterMovement's footLevelAt calls it.
  const hit = getSurfaceAt(ox + fp.cx, fp.cz, [placement] as any, 1);
  return (
    <group>
      <group position={[ox, 0, 0]}>
        <FurnitureModel name={item.name} item={item} scale={ISLAND_SCALE} instanceId={id} />
      </group>
      {SHOW_BEFORE && <Body x={ox + fp.cx - 0.85} y={fp.maxY} z={fp.cz} color="#e0503f" />}
      <Body x={ox + fp.cx + 0.85} y={hit.y} z={fp.cz} color="#38bdf8" />
    </group>
  );
}

function Scene({ ready }: { ready: boolean }) {
  const el = (ELEV * Math.PI) / 180;
  const PITCH = 7.5;
  const spanX = (IDS.length - 1) * PITCH;
  const dist = Math.max(11, spanX * 0.95 + 9);
  const target = new THREE.Vector3(0, 1.0, 0);
  return (
    <Canvas
      shadows
      style={{ width: '100%', height: '76vh', background: '#bfe3ef' }}
      camera={{ position: [0, target.y + Math.sin(el) * dist, target.z + Math.cos(el) * dist], fov: 35, near: 0.1, far: 200 }}
      onCreated={({ camera }) => { camera.lookAt(target); camera.updateProjectionMatrix(); }}
    >
      {/* Scene.tsx's lighting, verbatim. */}
      <ambientLight intensity={0.4} />
      <hemisphereLight intensity={0.5} color="#ffffff" groundColor="#4a4a4a" />
      <directionalLight
        position={[20, 20, 10]}
        intensity={1.2}
        castShadow
        shadow-mapSize={[2048, 2048]}
        shadow-camera-left={-20}
        shadow-camera-right={20}
        shadow-camera-top={20}
        shadow-camera-bottom={-20}
      />
      <mesh rotation={[-Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} receiveShadow>
        <planeGeometry args={[200, 200]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color={PLATEAU_INNER_COLOR} roughness={1} />
      </mesh>
      {ready && IDS.map((id, i) => <Piece key={id} id={id} ox={i * PITCH - spanX / 2} />)}
    </Canvas>
  );
}

function App() {
  const [ready, setReady] = useState(false);
  const [lines, setLines] = useState<string[]>([]);

  // The footprints have to be measured off a real scene graph before anything can be placed on
  // them, so build each model once into an offscreen group and hand it to the shipping measurer.
  useEffect(() => {
    const out: string[] = [];
    (async () => {
      const { buildModelObject3D } = await import('./scripts/lib/measureFurnitureModel');
      for (const id of IDS) {
        const obj = buildModelObject3D(id, ISLAND_SCALE);
        if (obj) measureFootprint(id, obj);
        const fp = getFootprint(id);
        const item = getItemById(id);
        if (fp && item) {
          out.push(
            `${item.name}: model top ${fp.maxY.toFixed(3)} · walking surface ${(fp.standY ?? fp.maxY).toFixed(3)}` +
            ` · drop ${((fp.maxY - (fp.standY ?? fp.maxY)) * 1000).toFixed(0)}mm`,
          );
        }
      }
      setLines(out);
      setReady(true);
    })();
  }, []);

  return (
    <div>
      <div style={{ padding: '4px 10px', fontSize: 12 }}>
        玩家身高 {PLAYER_H.toFixed(2)}・半徑 {PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS}・
        <b style={{ color: '#e0503f' }}>紅＝改版前（模型最高點 maxY）</b>・
        <b style={{ color: '#0284c7' }}>藍＝現在（量出來的可行走面 standY）</b>
      </div>
      <Scene ready={ready} />
      <div style={{ padding: '6px 10px', fontSize: 12, fontFamily: 'monospace' }}>
        {lines.map((l) => <div key={l}>{l}</div>)}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(<App />);

```

```tsx
import { renderToStaticMarkup } from 'react-dom/server';
import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { QVersionIcon } from './src/components/QVersionIcon';

const OUT = process.argv[2];
const IDS: [string, string][] = [
  ['pet-dog-shiba', '柴犬'],
  ['pet-dog-dachshund', '臘腸犬'],
  ['pet-dog-poodle', '紅貴賓犬'],
  ['pet-cat-orange', '橘貓'],
];

// Rendered at the real 64px the shop card uses, then blown up with nearest-neighbour so the
// pixels a player actually gets are what we are judging — not a clean 300px re-render.
```

## tmp-doorfollow-check.ts

```ts
/**
 * Throwaway: does the camera actually come through the doorway with the player, and does it do
 * it without a step?
 *
 * Restates the two lines the doorway branch of CameraController's solveCollisionFor now runs
 * (the repo's other tmp-*-check scripts do the same - the maths is inline in a useFrame and
 * cannot be imported), and walks a player from a doorway into the next room with the camera
 * trailing straight behind, reporting where the camera ends up each step.
 *
 *   npx tsx tmp-doorfollow-check.ts
 * Delete once the door-follow behaviour is signed off.
 */
import { CAMERA_COLLIDER_RADIUS } from './src/lib/cameraCollision';
import { ROOM_INNER_HALF_SIZE } from './src/constants/interiorShell';

/** CameraController's DOOR_FOLLOW_SPAN. */
const DOOR_FOLLOW_SPAN = 3.0;
/** BuildingInteriorView's DOOR_CLOSE_APPROACH - the door is shut further through the wall than this. */
const DOOR_CLOSE_APPROACH = 3.7;

const lerp = (a: number, b: number, t: number) => a + (b - a) * t;

/**
 * The rule. `standoff` is how far the pivot is in front of the doorway's face, `t` the distance
 * along the orbit ray to that face; both are what the segment loop already has.
 */
function doorLimit(standoff: number, t: number, desired: number): number {
  if (standoff <= 0.0001) return Infinity;
  const trail = lerp(desired, -CAMERA_COLLIDER_RADIUS, Math.min(1, standoff / DOOR_FOLLOW_SPAN));
  return Math.max(0, t * (1 + trail / standoff));
}

let failures = 0;
function check(name: string, ok: boolean, detail: string) {
  if (!ok) failures++;
  console.log(`${ok ? 'ok  ' : 'FAIL'}  ${name.padEnd(52)} ${detail}`);
}

// Geometry: the player walks north out of a doorway into the room beyond. The room's own face is
// at z = 0 here (the wall's inner surface); the wall centre - which is what the door's approach
// limit is measured from - is half a wall thickness back, and the player's distance from it is
// what closes the leaves.
const WALL_TO_DOOR_CENTRE = 0.5;

for (const desired of [7, 14, 6.36]) {
  console.log(`\ndesired arm = ${desired}`);
  let prevArm = desired;
  let prevCamera = -desired;
  let throughAt: number | null = null;
  let biggestJump = 0;
  for (let w = 0; w <= 8.001; w += 0.25) {
    // Camera straight behind: the ray is antiparallel to the face normal, so t === standoff.
    const arm = Math.min(desired, doorLimit(w, w, desired));
    const camera = w - arm;            // camera's own distance past the face (negative = still behind)
    if (throughAt === null && camera >= 0) throughAt = w;
    // A step in the arm is a step in the shot. Compare against how far the player moved.
    if (w > 0) biggestJump = Math.max(biggestJump, Math.abs(arm - prevArm) - 0.25);
    prevArm = arm;
    prevCamera = camera;
    if (w % 1 === 0) {
      console.log(`   player ${w.toFixed(2)} in   arm ${arm.toFixed(2)}   camera ${camera >= 0 ? '+' : ''}${camera.toFixed(2)} past the door`);
    }
  }
  check(
    `arm never steps (desired ${desired})`,
    biggestJump < 1.0,
    `worst extra movement in one 0.25 step = ${biggestJump.toFixed(2)}`,
  );
  check(
    `camera is through before the door shuts (desired ${desired})`,
    throughAt !== null && throughAt + WALL_TO_DOOR_CENTRE < DOOR_CLOSE_APPROACH,
    `through at ${throughAt?.toFixed(2)} in, door shuts at ${(DOOR_CLOSE_APPROACH - WALL_TO_DOOR_CENTRE).toFixed(2)}`,
  );
  check(
    `standing in the doorway is unconstrained (desired ${desired})`,
    Math.min(desired, doorLimit(0, 0, desired)) === desired,
    `arm at the threshold = ${Math.min(desired, doorLimit(0, 0, desired)).toFixed(2)}`,
  );
}

// Deep in a room, a doorway must behave like the wall it is in: the camera stays inside.
const deep = ROOM_INNER_HALF_SIZE; // 5.5, i.e. the player at the room centre
const armDeep = Math.min(7, doorLimit(deep, deep, 7));
check(
  'at the room centre the camera stays inside the room',
  deep - armDeep >= 0,
  `camera ${(deep - armDeep).toFixed(2)} from the face (>= 0 means inside)`,
);

console.log(failures === 0 ? '\nAll checks passed.' : `\n${failures} FAILED`);
process.exit(failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);

```

## tmp-doortrigger-check.ts

```ts
/**
 * Throwaway: the interior doors' trigger is now a box aligned to the doorway rather than a circle
 * around it, and the whole point of the change is that the two axes can be given different numbers.
 * This restates the test AutoDoor's useFrame runs (BuildingInteriorView.tsx - the maths is inline
 * in a useFrame and cannot be imported, same as the repo's other tmp-*-check scripts) and asks the
 * two questions the change has to get right:
 *
 *   1. Somebody walking PAST a doorway, along the wall it sits in, must not open it.
 *   2. Somebody walking INTO it must still find it open when they get there - for the player at
 *      full walk speed, and for the butler, who additionally refuses to step through anything
 *      less than 80% open (NpcWalker's DOOR_PASSABLE) and would visibly stall if he had to wait.
 *
 *   npx tsx tmp-doortrigger-check.ts
 * Delete once the door sensitivity is signed off.
 */
import { NPC_WALK } from './src/constants/npcs';

// --- the four limits under test (BuildingInteriorView.tsx) ---
const DOOR_OPEN_APPROACH = 2.6;
const DOOR_CLOSE_APPROACH = 3.7;
const DOOR_OPEN_OFFSET = 1.9;
const DOOR_CLOSE_OFFSET = 2.6;
const DOOR_SLIDE_RATE = 13;
/** Half the clear opening: DOORWAY_HALF_WIDTH, the jamb a walker actually has to aim between. */
const OPENING_HALF_WIDTH = 1.5;

/** Avatar.tsx: 3.8 * 1.2 * 1.2. */
const PLAYER_SPEED = 3.8 * 1.2 * 1.2;
/** NpcWalker: he will not step through a door that is less open than this. */
const DOOR_PASSABLE = 0.8;

/** The door's own test, given an offset resolved onto the doorway's two axes. */
function triggered(along: number, across: number, wasOpen: boolean): boolean {
  const alongLimit = wasOpen ? DOOR_CLOSE_OFFSET : DOOR_OPEN_OFFSET;
  const acrossLimit = wasOpen ? DOOR_CLOSE_APPROACH : DOOR_OPEN_APPROACH;
  return Math.abs(along) <= alongLimit && Math.abs(across) <= acrossLimit;
}

/** The leaf position after `dt` of holding a target, from `open`. Frame-rate independent. */
const slide = (open: number, target: number, dt: number) =>
  open + (target - open) * (1 - Math.exp(-DOOR_SLIDE_RATE * dt));

let failures = 0;
function check(name: string, ok: boolean, detail: string) {
  if (!ok) failures++;
  console.log(`${ok ? 'ok  ' : 'FAIL'}  ${name.padEnd(56)} ${detail}`);
}

/**
 * Walk a straight line past/into the door in 1/60s steps, running the real hysteresis and the real
 * slide, and report what the door did. `from`/`to` are [along, across] offsets from the door.
 */
function walk(from: [number, number], to: [number, number], speed: number) {
  const dist = Math.hypot(to[0] - from[0], to[1] - from[1]);
  const dt = 1 / 60;
  const steps = Math.ceil(dist / speed / dt);
  let open = 0;
  let wasOpen = false;
  let everOpened = false;
  /** Openness at the moment the walker reaches the wall plane (across crosses 0). */
  let openAtThreshold: number | null = null;
  let prevAcross = from[1];
  for (let i = 0; i <= steps; i++) {
    const t = Math.min(1, (i * dt * speed) / dist);
    const along = from[0] + (to[0] - from[0]) * t;
    const across = from[1] + (to[1] - from[1]) * t;
    wasOpen = triggered(along, across, wasOpen);
    if (wasOpen) everOpened = true;
    open = slide(open, wasOpen ? 1 : 0, dt);
    if (openAtThreshold === null && prevAcross > 0 && across <= 0) openAtThreshold = open;
    prevAcross = across;
  }
  return { everOpened, openAtThreshold, finalOpen: open };
}

console.log('--- 1. walking PAST the doorway, along the wall it sits in ---');
// Crossing right in front of an opening still opens it, and should: at that point you ARE in the
// doorway. What the change is about is how far down the wall the door starts reacting - the old
// 3.0 circle reached most of the way to the room corner, so a door announced itself for a walk
// that was never going to end at it. `lane` is how far out from the wall the walker is.
const OLD_RADIUS = 3.0;
for (const lane of [0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.6, 3.0]) {
  let firstAlong: number | null = null;
  for (let a = 8; a >= 0; a -= 0.01) if (triggered(a, lane, false)) { firstAlong = a; break; }
  const old = lane <= OLD_RADIUS ? Math.sqrt(OLD_RADIUS * OLD_RADIUS - lane * lane) : null;
  console.log(
    `   lane ${lane.toFixed(1)} out: reacts from ${firstAlong === null ? 'never' : firstAlong.toFixed(2) + ' along the wall'}`
    + `   (old circle: ${old === null ? 'never' : old.toFixed(2)})`,
  );
}
check(
  'hugging the wall, the door reacts later than it used to',
  Math.sqrt(OLD_RADIUS * OLD_RADIUS - 1.0 * 1.0) - DOOR_OPEN_OFFSET > 0.8,
  `at lane 1.0 the reaction point moved ${(Math.sqrt(OLD_RADIUS * OLD_RADIUS - 1) - DOOR_OPEN_OFFSET).toFixed(2)} closer to the opening`,
);
check(
  'a lane further out than the offset limit is ignored entirely',
  walk([-8, 3.0], [8, 3.0], PLAYER_SPEED).everOpened === false,
  'walking the length of the wall 3.0 out never touches it',
);
check(
  'a lane 2.0 out still opens it only near the opening',
  walk([-8, 2.0], [-OPENING_HALF_WIDTH - 0.4, 2.0], PLAYER_SPEED).everOpened === false,
  'approaching along the wall, stopping just short of the jamb, never triggers',
);
check(
  'the old circle would have opened it there',
  Math.hypot(OPENING_HALF_WIDTH + 0.4, 2.0) <= 3.0,
  `that spot is ${Math.hypot(OPENING_HALF_WIDTH + 0.4, 2.0).toFixed(2)} from the door, inside the old 3.0 radius`,
);

console.log('\n--- 2. walking INTO the doorway ---');
for (const entry of [0, 0.8, 1.4]) {
  const r = walk([entry, 8], [entry, -1], PLAYER_SPEED);
  check(
    `player head-on, ${entry.toFixed(1)} off centre, is not walking into a leaf`,
    r.openAtThreshold !== null && r.openAtThreshold > 0.97,
    `door is ${((r.openAtThreshold ?? 0) * 100).toFixed(1)}% open as they cross the wall`,
  );
}
// The butler's worst case is not head-on: his route can bring him at the doorway almost along the
// wall, which is exactly the direction the offset limit has narrowed. He stops NPC_WALK.arrive
// short of the gate and waits there until the door is DOOR_PASSABLE, so "does he ever wait" is
// the question, not "does he walk into it".
for (const [name, from] of [
  ['head-on', [0, 6]],
  ['diagonal', [4, 4]],
  ['almost along the wall', [6, 1]],
] as [string, [number, number]][]) {
  const r = walk(from, [0, NPC_WALK.arrive], NPC_WALK.speed);
  check(
    `butler arriving ${name} never has to stand and wait`,
    r.finalOpen >= DOOR_PASSABLE,
    `door is ${(r.finalOpen * 100).toFixed(1)}% open when he reaches the threshold (needs ${DOOR_PASSABLE * 100}%)`,
  );
}

console.log('\n--- 3. the boxes themselves ---');
check(
  'the close box strictly contains the open box',
  DOOR_CLOSE_APPROACH > DOOR_OPEN_APPROACH && DOOR_CLOSE_OFFSET > DOOR_OPEN_OFFSET,
  `open ${DOOR_OPEN_OFFSET} x ${DOOR_OPEN_APPROACH}, close ${DOOR_CLOSE_OFFSET} x ${DOOR_CLOSE_APPROACH}`,
);
check(
  'the offset limit still clears the opening',
  DOOR_OPEN_OFFSET > OPENING_HALF_WIDTH,
  `${DOOR_OPEN_OFFSET} vs a ${OPENING_HALF_WIDTH} half-opening - you can stand in the doorway and have it open`,
);
check(
  'the approach limit still buys more time than the slide needs',
  DOOR_OPEN_APPROACH / PLAYER_SPEED > 2 * (Math.log(10) / DOOR_SLIDE_RATE),
  `${(DOOR_OPEN_APPROACH / PLAYER_SPEED).toFixed(2)}s of walking vs ${(Math.log(10) / DOOR_SLIDE_RATE).toFixed(2)}s to 90% open`,
);

console.log(failures === 0 ? '\nAll checks passed.' : `\n${failures} FAILED`);
process.exit(failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);

```

## tmp-firefly-preview.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * Throwaway harness for eyeballing src/components/Three/Fireflies.tsx.
 *
 * The night ramp is a per-frame lerp, which SwiftShader never converges within a
 * --virtual-time-budget (see the headless-verify-limits note). So this pins the
 * material's uNight to 1 and its uTime to ?t=<seconds> AFTER Fireflies' own
 * useFrame has run - r3f runs same-priority callbacks in mount order, so the
 * override lands before the frame is drawn. That makes each screenshot a
 * deterministic sample of the swarm at a chosen instant, which is exactly what
 * the blink needs to be checked at all.
 *
 * Delete with tmp-firefly-preview.html once this is signed off.
 */
import { useRef } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { Canvas, useFrame, useThree } from '@react-three/fiber';
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { AppProvider } from './src/context/AppContext';
import { Fireflies } from './src/components/Three/Fireflies';

const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const FIXED_TIME = Number(params.get('t') ?? '4');
const NIGHT = Number(params.get('night') ?? '1');

/** Pins the swarm's uniforms so a headless capture is reproducible. */
function PinUniforms() {
  const scene = useThree((s) => s.scene);
  const found = useRef<THREE.Points[]>([]);

  useFrame(() => {
    if (found.current.length === 0) {
      scene.traverse((o) => {
        const m = (o as THREE.Points).material as THREE.ShaderMaterial | undefined;
        if ((o as THREE.Points).isPoints && m?.uniforms?.uNight) {
          found.current.push(o as THREE.Points);
        }
      });
    }
    for (const p of found.current) {
      const m = p.material as THREE.ShaderMaterial;
      m.uniforms.uNight.value = NIGHT;
      m.uniforms.uTime.value = FIXED_TIME;
      p.visible = NIGHT > 0;
    }
  });

  return null;
}

/** Stand-in for the island, so the swarm's height over the grass is judgeable. */
function GroundStub() {
  return (
    <group>
      <mesh rotation={[-Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} position={[0, 0.3, 0]}>
        <circleGeometry args={[5.7, 64]} />
        <meshBasicMaterial color="#16321f" />
      </mesh>
      <mesh rotation={[-Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} position={[0, 0.28, 0]}>
        <ringGeometry args={[5.7, 8.6, 64]} />
        <meshBasicMaterial color="#2a2b1e" />
      </mesh>
    </group>
  );
}

function App() {
  return (
    <Canvas
      camera={{ position: [13, 5.5, 15], fov: 30, near: 0.5, far: 2000 }}
      onCreated={({ scene, camera }) => {
        // Midnight-ish backdrop, matching SkyDome's MIDNIGHT bottom colour, so
        // the additive blend is judged against the sky it actually ships over.
        scene.background = new THREE.Color('#0d1834');
        camera.lookAt(0, 2.2, 0);
      }}
    >
      <GroundStub />
      <Fireflies count={40} />
      <PinUniforms />
    </Canvas>
  );
}

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <AppProvider>
    <App />
  </AppProvider>,
);

```

```tsx
/** Throwaway: the avatar wearing cross-slot combinations, to find clipping. Delete when signed off. */
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { Canvas } from '@react-three/fiber';
import { Avatar } from './src/components/Three/Avatar';
import { AppProvider } from './src/context/AppContext';

/** Each cell is one outfit: top + pants + shoes + hat + hair + necklace, in whatever mix. */
const COMBOS: Array<[string, string[]]> = [
  ['褲only 寬褲', ['pants-wide']],
  ['上only 夾克', ['top-jacket']],
  ['夾克+寬褲', ['top-jacket', 'pants-wide']],
  ['夾克+寬褲+靴', ['top-jacket', 'pants-wide', 'shoes-boots']],
  ['褲only 緊身', ['pants-skinny']],
  ['鞋only 高跟', ['shoes-heels']],
  ['緊身+高跟', ['pants-skinny', 'shoes-heels']],
  ['襯衫+錐形+歌劇鍊', ['item-1', 'pants-tapered', 'neck-opera']],
];

const VIEWS: Array<[string, [number, number, number]]> = [
  ['front', [0, 1.5, 6.4]],
  ['waist', [1.6, 0.95, 3.4]],
];

function Cell({ label, wear, cam }: { label: string; wear: string[]; cam: [number, number, number] }) {
  return (
    <div>
      <div style={{ font: '10px sans-serif', color: '#456', paddingBottom: 2 }}>{label}</div>

          <directionalLight position={[-3, 2, -3]} intensity={0.5} />
          <Avatar equippedOverride={wear} />
        </Canvas>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <AppProvider>
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(4, 232px)', gap: 6, padding: 6 }}>
      {COMBOS.flatMap(([label, wear]) =>
        VIEWS.map(([v, cam]) => <Cell key={label + v} label={`${label} · ${v}`} wear={wear} cam={cam} />)
      )}
    </div>
  </AppProvider>,
);
```

## tmp-footstep-audit.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * Throwaway harness: MEASURES each footstep surface instead of trusting the numbers in
 * FOOTSTEP_TONE. Renders one footfall per terrain through an OfflineAudioContext and reports
 * loudness, band split, spectral centroid and envelope granularity (how many separate little
 * peaks the step is made of - the "windowsill" of 窸窸窣窣).
 *
 * soundUtils caches one AudioContext at module scope, so each terrain gets a FRESH module
 * instance via a cache-busted dynamic import; that lets every step render into its own offline
 * context. Results land on window.__foot for a CDP read. Delete with tmp-footstep-audit.html.
 */

const SR = 48000;
const RENDER_SECONDS = 0.8;

type Metrics = {
  terrain: string;
  peak: number;
  rms: number;
  durationMs: number;
  centroidHz: number;
  bands: { sub: number; low: number; mid: number; hiss: number; air: number };
  envelopePeaks: number;
};

// --- radix-2 FFT (in-place, real input) ---
function fft(re: Float64Array, im: Float64Array) {
  const n = re.length;
  for (let i = 1, j = 0; i < n; i++) {
    let bit = n >> 1;
    for (; j & bit; bit >>= 1) j ^= bit;
    j ^= bit;
    if (i < j) {
      [re[i], re[j]] = [re[j], re[i]];
      [im[i], im[j]] = [im[j], im[i]];
    }
  }
  for (let len = 2; len <= n; len <<= 1) {
    const ang = (-2 * Math.PI) / len;
    const wr = Math.cos(ang);
    const wi = Math.sin(ang);
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i += len) {
      let cr = 1;
      let ci = 0;
      for (let k = 0; k < len / 2; k++) {
        const ur = re[i + k];
        const ui = im[i + k];
        const vr = re[i + k + len / 2] * cr - im[i + k + len / 2] * ci;
        const vi = re[i + k + len / 2] * ci + im[i + k + len / 2] * cr;
        re[i + k] = ur + vr;
        im[i + k] = ui + vi;
        re[i + k + len / 2] = ur - vr;
        im[i + k + len / 2] = ui - vi;
        const ncr = cr * wr - ci * wi;
        ci = cr * wi + ci * wr;
        cr = ncr;
      }
    }
  }
}

function analyse(terrain: string, x: Float32Array): Metrics {
  let peak = 0;
  let sumSq = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < x.length; i++) {
    const m = Math.abs(x[i]);
    if (m > peak) peak = m;
    sumSq += x[i] * x[i];
  }

  // Audible length: last sample above 2% of peak.
  let last = 0;
  for (let i = x.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    if (Math.abs(x[i]) > peak * 0.02) { last = i; break; }
  }

  // Summed magnitude spectrum over hann-windowed 2048 frames covering the whole step.
  const N = 2048;
  const spec = new Float64Array(N / 2);
  for (let off = 0; off + N <= Math.max(N, last + 1); off += N / 2) {
    const re = new Float64Array(N);
    const im = new Float64Array(N);
    for (let i = 0; i < N; i++) {
      re[i] = (x[off + i] ?? 0) * (0.5 - 0.5 * Math.cos((2 * Math.PI * i) / (N - 1)));
    }
    fft(re, im);
    for (let k = 0; k < N / 2; k++) spec[k] += Math.hypot(re[k], im[k]);
  }

  let total = 0;
  let weighted = 0;
  const bands = { sub: 0, low: 0, mid: 0, hiss: 0, air: 0 };
  for (let k = 1; k < N / 2; k++) {
    const hz = (k * SR) / N;
    const mag = spec[k];
    total += mag;
    weighted += mag * hz;
    if (hz < 300) bands.sub += mag;
    else if (hz < 1200) bands.low += mag;
    else if (hz < 2500) bands.mid += mag;
    else if (hz < 7000) bands.hiss += mag;
    else bands.air += mag;
  }
  const pct = (v: number) => Math.round((v / (total || 1)) * 1000) / 10;

  // Envelope granularity: smooth |x| over 1.5ms, count local maxima above 15% of the envelope
  // peak. One smooth decay -> 1. A bed of grains -> many.
  // Measured on the FIRST DIFFERENCE of the signal, i.e. through a crude 6dB/oct highpass: the
  // low body thump is one big smooth hump that otherwise sets the peak the 15% is taken from and
  // hides the very grain flutter this is here to count.
  const w = Math.floor(SR * 0.0015);
  const env: number[] = [];
  for (let i = 1; i + w < last + 1; i += w) {
    let s = 0;
    for (let j = 0; j < w; j++) s += Math.abs(x[i + j] - x[i + j - 1]);
    env.push(s / w);
  }
  const envPeak = Math.max(...env, 0);
  let peaks = 0;
  for (let i = 1; i < env.length - 1; i++) {
    if (env[i] > env[i - 1] && env[i] >= env[i + 1] && env[i] > envPeak * 0.15) peaks++;
  }

  return {
    terrain,
    peak: Math.round(peak * 1000) / 1000,
    rms: Math.round(Math.sqrt(sumSq / (last + 1)) * 10000) / 10000,
    durationMs: Math.round(((last + 1) / SR) * 1000),
    centroidHz: Math.round(weighted / (total || 1)),
    bands: { sub: pct(bands.sub), low: pct(bands.low), mid: pct(bands.mid), hiss: pct(bands.hiss), air: pct(bands.air) },
    envelopePeaks: peaks,
  };
}

async function renderStep(terrain: string, bust: string): Promise<Metrics> {
  const ctx = new OfflineAudioContext(1, Math.floor(SR * RENDER_SECONDS), SR);
  // soundUtils does `new AudioContextClass()` - hand it this offline context instead.
  (window as any).AudioContext = function () { return ctx; } as any;
  (window as any).webkitAudioContext = (window as any).AudioContext;

  const mod = await import(/* @vite-ignore */ `/src/lib/soundUtils.ts?fresh=${bust}`);
  mod.playFootstepThud(terrain, terrain === 'sand' ? 0.24 : 0.35);
  const rendered = await ctx.startRendering();
  return analyse(terrain, rendered.getChannelData(0));
}

(async () => {
  const out: Metrics[] = [];
  const terrains = ['grass', 'grass', 'grass', 'sand', 'wood', 'stone'];
  for (let i = 0; i < terrains.length; i++) {
    try {
      out.push(await renderStep(terrains[i], `${Date.now()}-${i}`));
    } catch (e: any) {
      out.push({ terrain: `${terrains[i]} FAILED: ${e?.message ?? e}` } as any);
    }
  }
  (window as any).__foot = out;
  const el = document.getElementById('log');
  if (el) el.textContent = out.map(m => JSON.stringify(m)).join('\n');
})();
```

## tmp-fpcheck.ts

```ts
/**
 * Throwaway: is the companion inside the first-person camera's frustum? Pure maths, no WebGL —
 * which is the point. The rendered harness (tmp-petfp.tsx) could not answer this because R3F kept
 * resetting the tile cameras, and a screenshot that shows nothing cannot distinguish "the pet is
 * off screen" from "the camera is not where I put it".
 *
 * Models exactly what CameraController does in first person: the camera sits at the owner's eye
 * (playerPos.y + 1.65) with FIRST_PERSON_FOV as its VERTICAL fov, looking along playerBus.cameraYaw.
 *
 * Run: npx tsx tmp-fpcheck.ts
 * Delete once the follow slot is signed off.
 */
import { FIRST_PERSON } from './src/components/Three/IslandPet';
import { AVATAR_BASE_SCALE } from './src/components/Three/Avatar';
import { PET_SPECS } from './src/constants/pets';

/** CameraController.tsx's FIRST_PERSON_FOV, and the eye height its first-person branch uses. */
const FOV = 68;
const EYE = 1.65;
/** Phone portrait is the meanest aspect the game ships in; anything wider only helps. */
const ASPECT = [0.56, 1.0, 1.78];
/** The player's own top speed on the island, which is what the follower has to keep up with. */
const PLAYER_SPEED = 5.5;

const halfV = (FOV / 2) * (Math.PI / 180);
const tanV = Math.tan(halfV);

/**
 * Where a point lands on screen, in normalised device coords: 0 is dead centre, ±1 is the edge of
 * the frame. Built from the camera's own axes rather than a matrix so the whole check stays
 * readable — forward is where it looks, right is +x on screen, up is +y.
 */
function project(camYaw: number, p: { x: number; y: number; z: number }, aspect: number) {
  // A camera looks down its own -Z, so yaw θ points it along (-sin θ, 0, -cos θ).
  const f = { x: -Math.sin(camYaw), z: -Math.cos(camYaw) };
  const r = { x: -f.z, z: f.x };
  const depth = p.x * f.x + p.z * f.z;
  const side = p.x * r.x + p.z * r.z;
  const rise = p.y;
  if (depth <= 0) return { depth, ndcX: NaN, ndcY: NaN };
  return {
    depth,
    ndcX: side / depth / (tanV * aspect),
    ndcY: rise / depth / tanV,
  };
}

/** The slot IslandPet puts the pet in, relative to the owner, in the same axes as ownerAxes(). */
function slot(kind: 'walk' | 'fly') {
  const ahead = kind === 'walk' ? FIRST_PERSON.walkAhead : FIRST_PERSON.flyAhead;
  const side = kind === 'walk' ? FIRST_PERSON.walkSide : FIRST_PERSON.flySide;
  return { ahead, side };
}

let failures = 0;

for (const [breed, spec] of Object.entries(PET_SPECS)) {
  const height = spec.height * AVATAR_BASE_SCALE;
  const kind = ['budgie', 'javasparrow', 'canary', 'phoenix'].includes(breed) ? 'fly' : 'walk';
  const { ahead, side } = slot(kind);

  // The pet's own vertical extent, as offsets from the EYE. A walker stands on the ground (1.65
  // below the eye) and rises by its height; a flyer hangs at flyHeight and is centred there.
  const feet = kind === 'walk' ? -EYE : FIRST_PERSON.flyHeight - EYE - height / 2;
  const crown = kind === 'walk' ? -EYE + height : FIRST_PERSON.flyHeight - EYE + height / 2;

  // A proportional follower settles SHORT of its slot by (owner speed / gain) whenever the owner
  // is moving, so "in frame standing still" is only half the answer — this is the distance the
  // player actually sees while walking, and it is the one that clips first.
  const lag = kind === 'walk' ? PLAYER_SPEED / FIRST_PERSON.gain : 0;

  for (const aspect of ASPECT) {
    // Camera yaw is irrelevant to the answer (the slot turns with it), so one sample proves the
    // family — but sweep anyway, because a sign error in the axes would only show at some yaws.
    for (const camYaw of [0, 1.1, 2.3, -2.9]) {
      const f = { x: -Math.sin(camYaw), z: -Math.cos(camYaw) };
      const r = { x: -f.z, z: f.x };
      const p = {
        x: f.x * (ahead - lag) + r.x * side,
        z: f.z * (ahead - lag) + r.z * side,
      };
      const lo = project(camYaw, { ...p, y: feet }, aspect);
      const hi = project(camYaw, { ...p, y: crown }, aspect);
      // "Visible" = the animal's own box overlaps the frame. Its feet may fall below the bottom
      // edge on a tall phone; what must never happen is the WHOLE animal being outside.
      const onScreen = lo.depth > 0.5
        && Math.abs(hi.ndcX) < 1
        && !(lo.ndcY > 1 || hi.ndcY < -1);
      if (!onScreen) {
        failures++;
        console.log(`FAIL ${breed} (${kind}) aspect ${aspect} yaw ${camYaw}: depth ${lo.depth.toFixed(2)} ndcX ${hi.ndcX.toFixed(2)} ndcY ${lo.ndcY.toFixed(2)}..${hi.ndcY.toFixed(2)}`);
      }
    }
  }

  // One representative readout per breed, at 16:9.
  const camYaw = 0;
  const f = { x: -Math.sin(camYaw), z: -Math.cos(camYaw) };
  const r = { x: -f.z, z: f.x };
  const p = { x: f.x * (ahead - lag) + r.x * side, z: f.z * (ahead - lag) + r.z * side };
  const lo = project(camYaw, { ...p, y: feet }, 1.78);
  const hi = project(camYaw, { ...p, y: crown }, 1.78);
  const pct = (n: number) => `${(50 - (n * 50)).toFixed(0)}%`;
  console.log(
    `${breed.padEnd(12)} ${kind}  h ${height.toFixed(2)}  dist ${lo.depth.toFixed(2)}  ` +
    `x ${(50 + hi.ndcX * 50).toFixed(0)}% across, y ${pct(hi.ndcY)}..${pct(lo.ndcY)} down`,
  );
}

console.log(failures === 0 ? '\nALL IN FRAME' : `\n${failures} FAILURES`);
```

## tmp-furniture-preview.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * Throwaway harness for signing off the 2026-09 furniture expansion — the new models, and the
 * eleven that were rebuilt after they turned out to be sharing one component.
 *
 * The house interior is not reachable on the guest path, and a guest cannot afford the new pieces,
 * so without this the only way to check a model is to read its arithmetic. Here every piece is
 * drawn by the SHIPPING `FurnitureModel` at the SHIPPING interior scale, on a floor, lit the way
 * the room lights it — so a screenshot is what the player will get.
 *
 *   ?set=lamps     the eight that used to be one grey cube
 *   ?set=seating   sofas and chairs
 *   ?set=tables    the eight tables
 *   ?set=bedroom   beds, dresser, vanity, mirror, coat rack
 *   ?set=kitchen   island, larder, microwave, oven, dish rack, dining chair
 *   ?set=study     shelves, filing cabinet, easel, globe, desk kit
 *   ?set=decor     the small things
 *   ?id=<item id>  one piece, alone, filling the view
 *
 * Delete with tmp-furniture-preview.html once this is signed off.
 */
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { Canvas } from '@react-three/fiber';
import { OrbitControls } from '@react-three/drei';

import { FurnitureModel } from './src/components/Three/FurnitureItem';
import { getItemById } from './src/constants/items';
import { getPlacementMounts } from './src/constants/placement';

const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const ONLY = params.get('id');
const SET = params.get('set') ?? 'lamps';

/** The interior draws every piece at 1.15 (BuildingInteriorView's FurnitureItem). */
const INTERIOR_SCALE = 1.15;

const SETS: Record<string, string[]> = {
  lamps: [
    'item-25', 'item-30', 'item-31', 'item-37',
    'light-crystal', 'light-industrial', 'light-modern', 'light-natural',
    'item-36', 'deco-radio',
  ],
  seating: [
    'item-21', 'sofa-rattan-single', 'sofa-linen-loveseat', 'sofa-l-shaped',
    'furn-beanbag', 'furn-armchair-wing', 'furn-rocking-chair', 'furn-dining-chair',
  ],
  tables: [
    'item-22', 'table-round-small', 'table-dining-square', 'table-dining-long',
    'table-coffee-round', 'table-side-rattan', 'table-folding', 'table-outdoor-teak',
    'desk-work-pine',
  ],
  bedroom: [
    'bed-single-wood', 'bed-canopy-tent', 'furn-dresser', 'furn-vanity',
    'furn-mirror-standing', 'furn-coat-rack',
  ],
  kitchen: [
    'furn-kitchen-island', 'furn-pantry-cabinet', 'furn-microwave', 'furn-oven',
    'furn-dish-rack', 'furn-tv-console', 'furn-display-cabinet',
  ],
  study: [
    'item-24', 'furn-bookcase-ladder', 'furn-filing-cabinet', 'furn-storage-basket',
    'furn-easel', 'furn-globe', 'furn-desk-lamp', 'furn-floor-lamp-arc',
  ],
  decor: [
    'deco-vase-ceramic', 'deco-photo-frame', 'deco-candle-set', 'deco-table-clock',
    'deco-cushion-set', 'deco-plush-toy', 'deco-whale-figurine', 'furn-book-stack',
    'furn-desk-organizer', 'deco-surfboard',
  ],
};

const IDS = ONLY ? [ONLY] : (SETS[SET] ?? SETS.lamps);
const COLS = ONLY ? 1 : Math.ceil(Math.sqrt(IDS.length));
const PITCH = ONLY ? 0 : 3.4;

function Piece({ id, x, z }: { id: string; x: number; z: number }) {
  const item = getItemById(id);
  if (!item) return null;
  // A ceiling piece hangs DOWN from its origin, so at y=0 it is under the floor. Lift it to the
  // room ceiling (constants/interiorShell.ts INTERIOR_CEILING_Y is 2.6) exactly as the room does.
  const lift = getPlacementMounts(id).includes('ceiling') ? 2.6 : 0;
  return (
    <group position={[x, lift, z]}>
      <FurnitureModel name={item.name} item={item} scale={INTERIOR_SCALE} />
      {/* A pad under each piece, so its footprint and its contact with the floor are both legible. */}
      <mesh position={[0, -0.005 - lift, 0]} rotation={[-Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} receiveShadow>
        <circleGeometry args={[1.5, 24]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#e9e2d6" roughness={1} />
      </mesh>
    </group>
  );
}

function App() {
  const rows = Math.ceil(IDS.length / COLS);
  // A single piece has no grid to size the camera from, so give it a fixed comfortable orbit.
  const span = Math.max(Math.max(COLS, rows) * PITCH, 4);
  return (
    <Canvas
      shadows
      camera={{ position: [span * 0.62, span * 0.5 + 2.4, span * 0.72], fov: 40 }}
      gl={{ antialias: true }}
    >
      <color attach="background" args={['#cfd8dd']} />
      <ambientLight intensity={0.85} />
      <hemisphereLight args={["#ffffff", "#8a7f6d", 0.7]} />
      <directionalLight position={[-8, 6, -4]} intensity={0.5} />
      <directionalLight position={[6, 12, 6]} intensity={1.5} castShadow shadow-mapSize={[2048, 2048]} />
      <mesh position={[0, -0.02, 0]} rotation={[-Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} receiveShadow>
        <planeGeometry args={[200, 200]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#b9b2a4" roughness={1} />
      </mesh>
      {IDS.map((id, i) => (
        <Piece
          key={id}
          id={id}
          x={(i % COLS) * PITCH - ((COLS - 1) * PITCH) / 2}
          z={Math.floor(i / COLS) * PITCH - ((rows - 1) * PITCH) / 2}
        />
      ))}
      <OrbitControls target={[0, 0.7, 0]} />
    </Canvas>
  );
}

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(<App />);
```

## tmp-hair.tsx

```tsx
/** Throwaway: every hairstyle in HAIR_SPECS on a real head sphere, lit exactly as Scene.tsx lights
 *  the island, so the new shading in legacy/hairShading.ts can be looked at rather than argued
 *  about. Delete when signed off.
 *
 *  Two rows of the same styles at two yaws: the front three-quarter that the shop thumbnail shows,
 *  and the back, because the highlight band and the occiput are both things you only see when the
 *  character turns.
 *
 *  `window.__hairReady` flips true once a frame has rendered, and any GLSL compile failure lands in
 *  the console as a three.js error - which is the whole reason this page exists before the app does.
 */
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { Canvas } from '@react-three/fiber';
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import type React from 'react';
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { HAIR_SPECS, HEAD_ANCHOR, AVATAR_SKIN_COLOR } from './src/constants/hair';
import { HairPiece } from './src/components/Three/character/legacy/wardrobe';

const STYLES = Object.values(HAIR_SPECS);
const GAP = 0.85;

function Head({ specIndex, yaw }: { specIndex: number; yaw: number }) {
  const sway = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);
  const spec = STYLES[specIndex];
  return (
    <group rotation={[0, yaw, 0]}>
      {/* The skull the hair is fitted to: HEAD_ANCHOR.radius is read straight off the rig. */}
      <mesh>
        <sphereGeometry args={[HEAD_ANCHOR.radius, 48, 32]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color={AVATAR_SKIN_COLOR} roughness={0.9} />
      </mesh>
      <FlatOverride>
        <HairPiece spec={spec} hat={null} swayRef={sway} />
      </FlatOverride>
    </group>
  );
}

function Row({ yaw, y }: { yaw: number; y: number }) {
  const span = (STYLES.length - 1) * GAP;
  return (
    <group position={[0, y, 0]}>
      {STYLES.map((s, i) => (
        <group key={s.id} position={[i * GAP - span / 2, 0, 0]}>
          <Head specIndex={i} yaw={yaw} />
        </group>
      ))}
    </group>
  );
}

const PARAMS = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
/** `?close=<index>` blows one style up across three yaws instead of showing the whole shop. */
const CLOSE = PARAMS.get('close');
/** `?flat=1` overrides every hair material with one unlit-ish grey. Shape only. */
const FLAT = PARAMS.get('flat') === '1';

const FLAT_MATERIAL = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: '#9aa3ad', roughness: 0.9 });

/** Replaces the material on every mesh under this group, after R3F has built them. */
function FlatOverride({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const ref = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!FLAT || !ref.current) return;
    ref.current.traverse(o => {
      const m = o as THREE.Mesh;
      if (m.isMesh) m.material = FLAT_MATERIAL;
    });
  });
  return <group ref={ref}>{children}</group>;
}

function CloseUp({ index }: { index: number }) {
  const yaws = [0.5, Math.PI * 0.55, Math.PI + 0.35];
  return (
    <group>
      {yaws.map((yaw, i) => (
        <group key={yaw} position={[(i - 1) * 0.78, 0, 0]}>
          <Head specIndex={index} yaw={yaw} />
        </group>
      ))}
    </group>
  );
}

function App() {
  const close = CLOSE === null ? null : Number(CLOSE);
  return (
    <Canvas
      orthographic
      camera={{ position: [0, 0, 10], zoom: close === null ? 210 : 620, near: 0.1, far: 100 }}
      gl={{ antialias: true }}
      onCreated={({ gl }) => {
        gl.setClearColor('#2b3a46');
        requestAnimationFrame(() => {
          (window as unknown as Record<string, unknown>).__hairReady = true;
        });
      }}
    >
      {/* Lifted verbatim from Scene.tsx's SceneLighting, because the highlight band is aimed at
          that directional light and would be meaningless under any other rig. */}
      <ambientLight intensity={0.4} />
      <hemisphereLight intensity={0.5} color="#ffffff" groundColor="#4a4a4a" />
      <directionalLight position={[20, 20, 10]} intensity={1.2} />
      {close === null ? (
        <>
          <Row yaw={0.6} y={0.42} />
          <Row yaw={Math.PI + 0.4} y={-0.42} />
        </>
      ) : (
        <CloseUp index={close} />
      )}
    </Canvas>
  );
}

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(<App />);
```
