## tmp-swimflip-check.ts

```ts
/**
 * Reproduces the "walks out of the sea and ends up upside down (feet up, head down)" bug by
 * driving Avatar.tsx's ACTUAL orientation pipeline over a scripted shore approach.
 *
 * What it models, frame for frame, is the one thing that matters here: Avatar.tsx writes the
 * group's orientation through TWO different representations - a quaternion while swimming
 * (applySwimOrientation) and raw Euler components while on land - and three.js keeps the two in
 * sync by DECOMPOSING the quaternion into XYZ Euler angles. A yaw*pitch quaternion does not
 * decompose to (pitch, yaw, 0); at a swim pitch of ~82deg it decomposes to something with a large
 * stray rotation.z. Whoever writes Euler components next inherits that z.
 *
 * Pass/fail is measured on the only thing the player can actually see: where the character's own
 * UP axis points. If its world Y goes negative the avatar is standing on its head.
 */
import * as THREE from 'three';
import {
  nextSwimState,
  swimTransitionTimer,
  swimPitchAllowance,
  getTerrainInfo,
  SWIM_PITCH_DEEP_Y,
  SWIM_TRANSITION_DURATION,
  SwimState,
} from './src/components/Three/characterMovement';

const DT = 1 / 60;
const scale = 1;

const UP_AXIS = new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0);
const RIGHT_AXIS = new THREE.Vector3(1, 0, 0);
const FORWARD_AXIS = new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 1);

// Verbatim from Avatar.tsx
function applySwimOrientation(group: THREE.Group, yaw: number, pitch: number, roll = 0) {
  const qYaw = new THREE.Quaternion().setFromAxisAngle(UP_AXIS, yaw);
  const qPitch = new THREE.Quaternion().setFromAxisAngle(RIGHT_AXIS, pitch);
  const composed = qYaw.multiply(qPitch);
  if (roll !== 0) {
    composed.multiply(new THREE.Quaternion().setFromAxisAngle(FORWARD_AXIS, roll));
  }
  group.quaternion.copy(composed);
}

interface Frame {
  /** Distance from island centre this frame. */
  r: number;
  /** Is a movement key held this frame? */
  moving: boolean;
}

function simulate(name: string, yaw: number, script: (t: number) => Frame, seconds: number) {
  const group = new THREE.Group();
  let state: SwimState = 'swimming';
  let timer = 0;
  let swimPitch = Math.PI / 2.2; // arrives at the beach mid-stroke, prone
  let moveWeight = 1;
  // Avatar.tsx's bodyYawRef / bodyTiltRef: the land pose's own record of the rendered angles.
  let bodyYaw = yaw;
  let bodyTilt = 0;
  let worstUpY = 1;
  let worstAt = 0;

  // Start the body where a swimmer actually is: quaternion-composed prone pose.
  applySwimOrientation(group, yaw, swimPitch, 0);

  for (let i = 0; i < seconds / DT; i++) {
    const t = i * DT;
    const { r, moving } = script(t);
    const pos = new THREE.Vector3(Math.sin(yaw) * r, 0, Math.cos(yaw) * r);

    // --- Avatar.tsx line ~821: isSwimming is snapshotted BEFORE the state machine runs.
    const isSwimming = state !== 'walking';

    // --- line ~920: transition timer ticks first and may complete the transition
    if (state === 'enteringWater') {
      timer -= DT;
      if (timer <= 0) state = 'swimming';
    } else if (state === 'exitingWater') {
      timer -= DT;
      if (timer <= 0) state = 'walking';
    }

    // --- line ~968 / ~1164: re-evaluate the state against the position
    const next = nextSwimState(state, pos.x, pos.z, scale);
    if (next !== state) {
      timer = swimTransitionTimer(state, next, timer);
      state = next;
    }

    // --- line ~1141 (moving) / ~1431 (idle): the position/scale block orients the body on land
    if (moving) {
      bodyYaw = yaw;
      bodyTilt = 0;
      group.rotation.set(bodyTilt, bodyYaw, 0);
    } else {
      bodyTilt = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(bodyTilt, 0, 12 * DT);
      let d = yaw - bodyYaw;
      while (d < -Math.PI) d += Math.PI * 2;
      while (d > Math.PI) d -= Math.PI * 2;
      bodyYaw += d * 8 * DT;
      group.rotation.set(bodyTilt, bodyYaw, 0);
    }

    // --- line ~1452: animation weights
    moveWeight = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(moveWeight, moving ? 1 : 0, 10 * DT);

    // --- line ~1699: "Bounce and Sway"
    const walkTilt = 0; // walkPhase-driven, +-0.05 max; irrelevant to the flip
    let targetRotX = walkTilt;
    let pitchRoom = 0;

    if (isSwimming) {
      const proneTilt = Math.PI / 2.2;
      const floatTilt = -Math.PI / 2.05;
      const tInfo = getTerrainInfo(pos.x, pos.z, scale);
      pitchRoom = swimPitchAllowance(tInfo.targetY);
      const isDeepEnough = tInfo.targetY <= SWIM_PITCH_DEEP_Y;
      const inWaterTilt = moving && isDeepEnough ? proneTilt : !moving && isDeepEnough ? floatTilt : walkTilt;

      if (state === 'swimming') {
        targetRotX = inWaterTilt;
      } else if (state === 'enteringWater') {
        const p = 1.0 - Math.max(0, timer / SWIM_TRANSITION_DURATION);
        targetRotX = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(walkTilt, inWaterTilt, p);
      } else if (state === 'exitingWater') {
        const p = 1.0 - Math.max(0, timer / SWIM_TRANSITION_DURATION);
        targetRotX = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(inWaterTilt, walkTilt, p);
      }

      swimPitch = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(swimPitch, targetRotX, Math.min(1, 5.5 * DT));
      const waveRoll = state === 'swimming' ? Math.sin(t * 0.55) * 0.06 * (1 - moveWeight) : 0;
      applySwimOrientation(group, yaw, swimPitch * pitchRoom, waveRoll * pitchRoom);
      bodyYaw = yaw;
      bodyTilt = swimPitch * pitchRoom;
    } else {
      bodyTilt = targetRotX;
      group.rotation.set(bodyTilt, bodyYaw, 0);
      swimPitch = targetRotX;
    }

    // --- Measure: where does the character's own UP axis point in world space?
    //
    // Only judged at/inland of the visible waterline, where there is no water to lie down in and
    // the character is unambiguously standing on sand. Out at sea a body near horizontal is the
    // correct pose, not a defect.
    const onDryGround = getTerrainInfo(pos.x, pos.z, scale).targetY >= 0.02;
    if (onDryGround) {
      group.updateMatrixWorld(true);
      const up = UP_AXIS.clone().applyQuaternion(group.quaternion);
      if (up.y < worstUpY) {
        worstUpY = up.y;
        worstAt = t;
      }
    }
  }

  // A walking character should be within a few degrees of upright. Anything below ~0.85 is a
  // visible lean; below 0 is literally inverted.
  const ok = worstUpY > 0.85;
  console.log(
    `${ok ? 'ok  ' : 'FAIL'}  ${name.padEnd(46)} yaw=${((yaw * 180) / Math.PI).toFixed(0).padStart(4)}deg  ` +
      `worstUp.y=${worstUpY.toFixed(3).padStart(7)} (tilt ${((Math.acos(THREE.MathUtils.clamp(worstUpY, -1, 1)) * 180) / Math.PI).toFixed(0).padStart(3)}deg) at t=${worstAt.toFixed(2)}s`
  );
  return ok;
}

let allOk = true;

// Swim in from deep water and walk straight up the beach, never letting go of the key.
for (const yaw of [0, Math.PI / 4, Math.PI / 2, Math.PI]) {
  allOk = simulate('walk ashore, key held', yaw, t => ({ r: Math.max(4.5, 9.0 - t * 1.2), moving: true }), 8) && allOk;
}

// The same approach, but the player releases the key on reaching the sand - which is what
// anybody actually does when they arrive somewhere.
for (const yaw of [0, Math.PI / 4, Math.PI / 2, Math.PI]) {
  allOk =
    simulate('walk ashore, release key at shore', yaw, t => {
      const r = Math.max(6.3, 9.0 - t * 1.2);
      return { r, moving: r > 6.31 };
    }, 8) && allOk;
}

// Release the key while still in the shallows, then stand there.
for (const yaw of [Math.PI / 2, Math.PI]) {
  allOk =
    simulate('stop in the shallows and idle', yaw, t => {
      const r = Math.max(7.0, 9.0 - t * 1.2);
      return { r, moving: r > 7.01 };
    }, 8) && allOk;
}

// Dense sweep: come ashore from every compass direction, releasing the key at the shore, and
// report only the failures. The original bug only fired past a quarter turn, so a handful of
// hand-picked headings is not enough coverage to call this fixed.
let sweepWorst = 1;
let sweepFails = 0;
for (let d = -180; d < 180; d += 5) {
  const yaw = (d * Math.PI) / 180;
  const group = new THREE.Group();
  let state: SwimState = 'swimming';
  let timer = 0;
  let swimPitch = Math.PI / 2.2;
  let bodyYaw = yaw;
  let bodyTilt = 0;
  let worst = 1;
  applySwimOrientation(group, yaw, swimPitch, 0);

  for (let i = 0; i < 8 / DT; i++) {
    const t = i * DT;
    const r = Math.max(6.3, 9.0 - t * 1.2);
    const moving = r > 6.31;
    const pos = new THREE.Vector3(Math.sin(yaw) * r, 0, Math.cos(yaw) * r);
    const isSwimming = state !== 'walking';

    if (state === 'enteringWater') {
      timer -= DT;
      if (timer <= 0) state = 'swimming';
    } else if (state === 'exitingWater') {
      timer -= DT;
      if (timer <= 0) state = 'walking';
    }
    const next = nextSwimState(state, pos.x, pos.z, scale);
    if (next !== state) {
      timer = swimTransitionTimer(state, next, timer);
      state = next;
    }

    // OLD=1 reinstates the pre-fix land pose (read tilt/yaw back off the group, never touch z),
    // so this sweep can be shown to actually discriminate rather than passing vacuously.
    if (process.env.OLD === '1') {
      if (moving) {
        group.rotation.set(0, yaw, 0);
      } else {
        group.rotation.x = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(group.rotation.x, 0, 12 * DT);
        let dy = yaw - group.rotation.y;
        while (dy < -Math.PI) dy += Math.PI * 2;
        while (dy > Math.PI) dy -= Math.PI * 2;
        group.rotation.y += dy * 8 * DT;
      }
    } else {
      if (moving) {
        bodyYaw = yaw;
        bodyTilt = 0;
      } else {
        bodyTilt = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(bodyTilt, 0, 12 * DT);
        let dy = yaw - bodyYaw;
        while (dy < -Math.PI) dy += Math.PI * 2;
        while (dy > Math.PI) dy -= Math.PI * 2;
        bodyYaw += dy * 8 * DT;
      }
      group.rotation.set(bodyTilt, bodyYaw, 0);
    }

    if (isSwimming) {
      const tInfo = getTerrainInfo(pos.x, pos.z, scale);
      const pitchRoom = swimPitchAllowance(tInfo.targetY);
      const isDeepEnough = tInfo.targetY <= SWIM_PITCH_DEEP_Y;
      const inWaterTilt = moving && isDeepEnough ? Math.PI / 2.2 : 0;
      let targetRotX = 0;
      if (state === 'swimming') targetRotX = inWaterTilt;
      else {
        const p = 1.0 - Math.max(0, timer / SWIM_TRANSITION_DURATION);
        targetRotX =
          state === 'enteringWater'
            ? THREE.MathUtils.lerp(0, inWaterTilt, p)
            : THREE.MathUtils.lerp(inWaterTilt, 0, p);
      }
      swimPitch = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(swimPitch, targetRotX, Math.min(1, 5.5 * DT));
      applySwimOrientation(group, yaw, swimPitch * pitchRoom, 0);
      bodyYaw = yaw;
      bodyTilt = swimPitch * pitchRoom;
    }

    if (getTerrainInfo(pos.x, pos.z, scale).targetY >= 0.02) {
      const up = UP_AXIS.clone().applyQuaternion(group.quaternion);
      worst = Math.min(worst, up.y);
    }
  }
  sweepWorst = Math.min(sweepWorst, worst);
  if (worst <= 0.85) {
    sweepFails++;
    console.log(`FAIL  sweep heading ${String(d).padStart(4)}deg  worstUp.y=${worst.toFixed(3)}`);
  }
}
console.log(
  `\n${sweepFails === 0 ? 'ok  ' : 'FAIL'}  72-heading sweep: ${sweepFails} failures, worst up.y across all headings = ${sweepWorst.toFixed(3)}`
);
allOk = sweepFails === 0 && allOk;

console.log(`\n${allOk ? 'ALL PASS - character stays upright' : 'SOME FAILED - character flips over'}`);
process.exit(allOk ? 0 : 1);
```

## tmp-swimstate-check.ts

```ts
import { nextSwimState, swimTransitionTimer, SWIM_TRANSITION_DURATION, SwimState } from './src/components/Three/characterMovement';

const scale = 1;
const sandRadius = 6.8 * scale;
const DT = 1 / 60;

/**
 * Drives the real state machine + the real timer bookkeeping from Avatar.tsx over a
 * scripted radius-vs-time path, and reports the worst transition progress the character
 * ever sits at while its state is a transition state.
 *
 * `p` near 0 while in exitingWater is precisely the bug: height is held at SWIM_BODY_Y
 * (-0.6) and pitch at the full in-water tilt, i.e. sunk into the sand face-down.
 */
function simulate(name: string, radiusAt: (t: number) => number, seconds: number) {
  let state: SwimState = 'walking';
  let timer = 0;
  let framesStuckLow = 0;   // frames in a transition with p < 0.15
  let longestTransition = 0;
  let curTransition = 0;
  let flips = 0;

  for (let i = 0; i < seconds / DT; i++) {
    const t = i * DT;
    const r = radiusAt(t);

    // Avatar.tsx: timer ticks first, may complete the transition
    if (state === 'enteringWater' || state === 'exitingWater') {
      timer -= DT;
      if (timer <= 0) state = state === 'enteringWater' ? 'swimming' : 'walking';
    }

    // then the state is re-evaluated against the position
    const next = nextSwimState(state, r, 0, scale);
    if (next !== state) {
      timer = swimTransitionTimer(state, next, timer);
      state = next;
      flips++;
    }

    if (state === 'enteringWater' || state === 'exitingWater') {
      const p = 1.0 - Math.max(0, timer / SWIM_TRANSITION_DURATION);
      if (p < 0.15) framesStuckLow++;
      curTransition += DT;
      longestTransition = Math.max(longestTransition, curTransition);
    } else {
      curTransition = 0;
    }
  }

  const stuck = longestTransition > 1.0;
  console.log(
    `${stuck ? 'FAIL' : 'ok  '}  ${name.padEnd(38)} ` +
    `final=${state.padEnd(13)} flips=${String(flips).padStart(4)} ` +
    `longestTransition=${longestTransition.toFixed(2)}s stuckLowFrames=${framesStuckLow}`
  );
  return !stuck;
}

console.log(`sandRadius=${sandRadius}  inner=${(sandRadius - 0.35).toFixed(2)}  outer=${(sandRadius + 0.35).toFixed(2)}\n`);

let allOk = true;

// Baseline: straight in, straight out. Must complete cleanly both ways.
allOk = simulate('walk straight out to sea', t => 5.5 + t * 1.0, 6) && allOk;
allOk = simulate('swim straight back to beach', t => 9.0 - t * 1.0, 8) && allOk;

// The reported bug: loitering exactly on the old shared threshold (sandRadius - margin).
allOk = simulate('park on the inner line', t => (t < 3 ? 5.5 + t * 1.0 : 6.45), 12) && allOk;

// Tangential shore walk: radius wobbles across the old shared line every ~0.4s.
allOk = simulate('wobble across inner line +-0.06', t => (t < 3 ? 5.5 + t * 1.0 : 6.45 + Math.sin(t * 15) * 0.06), 14) && allOk;

// Larger wobble, still inside the new 2*margin dead zone.
allOk = simulate('wobble across inner line +-0.25', t => (t < 3 ? 5.5 + t * 1.0 : 6.45 + Math.sin(t * 8) * 0.25), 14) && allOk;

// A genuine turnaround mid-exit must still be honoured (not deadlocked into walking).
allOk = simulate('exit then turn back out to sea', t => (t < 4 ? 9.0 - t * 1.0 : 5.0 + (t - 4) * 1.2), 12) && allOk;

console.log(`\n${allOk ? 'ALL PASS - every transition completes' : 'SOME FAILED - a transition never completed'}`);
process.exit(allOk ? 0 : 1);

```

```tsx
/**
 * Throwaway: the temple, up close, at the angles the complaint was about.
 *
 * One WebGL context for the whole grid (swiftshader will not hand out 12).
 * Open http://localhost:3000/tmp-temple.html?style=hair-buzz. Delete once signed off.
 */
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { Canvas } from '@react-three/fiber';
import { useRef } from 'react';
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { HAIR_SPECS, AVATAR_SKIN_COLOR, HairSpec } from './src/constants/hair';
import { HairPiece } from './src/components/Three/character/legacy/wardrobe';
import { LEGACY_SKELETON } from './src/constants/characterRig';

const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const only = params.get('style');
const STYLES = only ? only.split(',').map(id => HAIR_SPECS[id]) : Object.values(HAIR_SPECS);
const YAWS = (params.get('yaws') ?? '30,45,60,80').split(',').map(Number);
const ZOOM = Number(params.get('zoom') ?? 900);
/** Head-local point the camera is aimed at: the right temple. */
const FOCUS: [number, number, number] = [0, 0.03, 0];

const CELL = 0.62;

function Head({ spec, yaw, position }: { spec: HairSpec; yaw: number; position: [number, number, number] }) {
  const swayRef = useRef<THREE.Group>(null!);
  return (
    <group position={position}>
      <group rotation={[0, (yaw * Math.PI) / 180, 0]} position={[-FOCUS[0], -FOCUS[1], -FOCUS[2]]}>
        {!params.get('nohead') && (
          <mesh>
            <sphereGeometry args={[Number(params.get('headr') ?? LEGACY_SKELETON.head.halfWidth), 32, 32]} />
            <meshStandardMaterial color={AVATAR_SKIN_COLOR} roughness={0.7} />
          </mesh>
        )}
        <group position={[0, 0.035, 0.225]}>
          <mesh position={[-0.104, 0, 0]}>
            <sphereGeometry args={[0.036, 16, 16]} />
            <meshStandardMaterial color="#0d1117" roughness={0.1} />
          </mesh>
          <mesh position={[0.104, 0, 0]}>
            <sphereGeometry args={[0.036, 16, 16]} />
            <meshStandardMaterial color="#0d1117" roughness={0.1} />
          </mesh>
        </group>
        {/* Blush, so the corridor the hairline is solved against is visible. */}
        <mesh position={[-0.122, -0.029, 0.18]}>
          <sphereGeometry args={[0.056, 16, 16]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial color="#fda4af" transparent opacity={0.3} roughness={0.9} />
        </mesh>
        <mesh position={[0.122, -0.029, 0.18]}>
          <sphereGeometry args={[0.056, 16, 16]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial color="#fda4af" transparent opacity={0.3} roughness={0.9} />
        </mesh>
        <HairPiece spec={spec} hat={null} swayRef={swayRef} />
      </group>
    </group>
  );
}

function Sheet() {
  return (
    <>
      <ambientLight intensity={0.7} />
      <directionalLight position={[2, 4, 3]} intensity={1.2} />
      <directionalLight position={[-3, 1, -2]} intensity={0.4} />
      {STYLES.map((spec, r) =>
        YAWS.map((yaw, c) => (
          <Head
            key={`${spec.id}-${c}`}
            spec={spec}
            yaw={yaw}
            position={[
              (c - (YAWS.length - 1) / 2) * CELL,
              ((STYLES.length - 1) / 2 - r) * CELL,
              0,
            ]}
          />
        )),
      )}
    </>
  );
}

const width = YAWS.length * CELL * ZOOM;
const height = STYLES.length * CELL * ZOOM;

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <div style={{ display: 'flex', font: '13px sans-serif', background: '#f2f2f4' }}>
    <div style={{ width: 110 }}>
      {STYLES.map(s => (
        <div key={s.id} style={{ height: CELL * ZOOM, display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', fontWeight: 700 }}>
          {s.label}
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
    <div style={{ width, height, background: params.get('bg') ?? '#e9e9ee' }}>
      <Canvas orthographic camera={{ zoom: ZOOM, position: [0, 0, 6] }} gl={{ antialias: true }}>
        <Sheet />
      </Canvas>
    </div>
  </div>,
);
```

## tmp-wall-preview.tsx

```tsx
/**
 * Throwaway harness for signing off the procedural wall materials.
 *
 * The house interior is NOT reachable on the guest path (a guest cannot place a Home, so no
 * door ever appears), which is why this exists: without it, a wall shader can only be checked
 * by reading the GLSL. Here every style gets its own room on the real ROOM_GRID_SIZE lattice,
 * so the contact shading — which is keyed off world position, not mesh UVs — lands on the
 * corners in exactly the places it will in game.
 *
 *   ?style=<id>   one style, filling the view
 *   (no param)    every style in a row, for the art pass
 *
 * Publishes `window.__wall` so a headless run can assert the materials compiled rather than
 * only take a screenshot.
 *
 * Delete with tmp-wall-preview.html once this is signed off.
 */
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { Canvas, useThree } from '@react-three/fiber';
import * as THREE from 'three';

import { getWallMaterial } from './src/components/Three/wallMaterial';
import { getFloorMaterial } from './src/components/Three/floorMaterial';
import { FLOOR_STYLES, WALL_STYLES } from './src/constants/materialSwatches';
import { ROOM_GRID_SIZE, ROOM_HALF_SIZE } from './src/constants/rooms';
import {
  BASEBOARD_THICKNESS,
  CROWN_HEIGHT,
  CROWN_THICKNESS,
  CROWN_TOP_Y,
  WALL_BASEBOARD_INSET,
  WALL_CROWN_INSET,
  WALL_THICKNESS,
} from './src/constants/interiorShell';

const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const ONLY = params.get('style');
const ROOF = params.get('roof') !== '0';

/** Every wall style the shop sells, in shop order. */
const STYLE_IDS = Object.keys(WALL_STYLES).filter((id) => id !== 'default');
const SHOWN = ONLY ? [ONLY] : STYLE_IDS;

/**
 * Two walls of one room, meeting at a corner, plus its floor.
 *
 * Only the N (z = +6) and W (x = -6) walls are built: those are the two whose inner faces point
 * back at a camera placed high on the +x/+z side, so the room is open exactly the way the
 * interior camera sees it, with no near wall in the way.
 */
function RoomSample({ styleId, gx }: { styleId: string; gx: number }) {
  const cx = gx * ROOM_GRID_SIZE;
  const wallColor = WALL_STYLES[styleId] || styleId;
  const material = getWallMaterial(styleId, wallColor);

  const baseboardOffset = WALL_BASEBOARD_INSET - BASEBOARD_THICKNESS / 2;
  const crownOffset = WALL_CROWN_INSET - CROWN_THICKNESS / 2;
  const crownY = CROWN_TOP_Y - CROWN_HEIGHT / 2;

  return (
    <group position={[cx, 0, 0]}>
      <mesh rotation={[-Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} position={[0, -0.01, 0]} receiveShadow>
        <planeGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE, ROOM_GRID_SIZE]} />
        <primitive object={getFloorMaterial('floor-oak', FLOOR_STYLES['floor-oak'])} attach="material" />
      </mesh>

      {/* North wall, at z = +ROOM_HALF_SIZE. Its room side faces -z. */}
      <group position={[0, 2.5, ROOM_HALF_SIZE]}>
        <mesh receiveShadow>
          <boxGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE + 0.4, 5, WALL_THICKNESS]} />
          <primitive object={material} attach="material" />
        </mesh>
        <mesh position={[0, -2.35, -baseboardOffset]}>
          <boxGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE + 0.42, 0.3, BASEBOARD_THICKNESS]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial color="#8b5a2b" roughness={0.8} />
        </mesh>
        <mesh position={[0, crownY - 2.5, -crownOffset]}>
          <boxGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE + 0.42, CROWN_HEIGHT, CROWN_THICKNESS]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial color="#f6f1e6" roughness={0.55} />
        </mesh>
      </group>

      {/* West wall, at x = -ROOM_HALF_SIZE. Its room side faces +x. */}
      <group position={[-ROOM_HALF_SIZE, 2.5, 0]} rotation={[0, Math.PI / 2, 0]}>
        <mesh receiveShadow>
          <boxGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE + 0.4, 5, WALL_THICKNESS]} />
          <primitive object={material} attach="material" />
        </mesh>
        <mesh position={[0, -2.35, baseboardOffset]}>
          <boxGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE + 0.42, 0.3, BASEBOARD_THICKNESS]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial color="#8b5a2b" roughness={0.8} />
        </mesh>
        <mesh position={[0, crownY - 2.5, crownOffset]}>
          <boxGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE + 0.42, CROWN_HEIGHT, CROWN_THICKNESS]} />
          <meshStandardMaterial color="#f6f1e6" roughness={0.55} />
        </mesh>
      </group>

      {/* Ceiling plate and beams, so the crown can be judged against the two things it now has
          to sit under. `?roof=0` takes them away again. */}
      {ROOF && (
        <group>
          <mesh position={[0, 4.93, 0]} receiveShadow>
            <boxGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE, 0.12, ROOM_GRID_SIZE]} />
            <meshStandardMaterial
              color={`#${new THREE.Color(wallColor).lerp(new THREE.Color('#f6f1e6'), 0.82).getHexString()}`}
              roughness={0.9}
            />
          </mesh>
          {[0, -3.0, 3.0].map((bz) => (
            <mesh key={bz} position={[0, CROWN_TOP_Y + 0.06, bz]}>
              <boxGeometry args={[ROOM_GRID_SIZE, 0.12, bz === 0 ? 0.25 : 0.2]} />
              <meshStandardMaterial color="#451a03" roughness={0.9} />
            </mesh>
          ))}
        </group>
      )}

      {/* Reference sphere: a matte grey ball is the quickest read on whether the room's light
          is doing what it did before, independently of whatever the wall is up to. */}
      <mesh position={[0, 0.9, 0]} castShadow>
        <sphereGeometry args={[0.9, 32, 24]} />
        <meshStandardMaterial color="#d9d9d9" roughness={0.7} />
      </mesh>
    </group>
  );
}

function Rig() {
  const { camera } = useThree();
  useEffect(() => {
    const span = (SHOWN.length - 1) * ROOM_GRID_SIZE;
    const midX = span / 2;
    if (ONLY) {
      // INSIDE the room, aimed at the corner where the two walls meet. Judging a wall from
      // outside the room would miss the whole point of the contact shading, which only exists
      // to describe the corner and the floor line to a camera standing in the room.
      camera.position.set(4.6, 3.4, -3.2);
      camera.lookAt(-3.2, 1.9, 3.6);
    } else {
      // Far enough back that the whole row fits, high enough to see each floor.
      const dist = span * 0.75 + 26;
      camera.position.set(midX + dist * 0.42, dist * 0.52, dist);
      camera.lookAt(midX, 1.8, 0);
    }
    camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
  }, [camera]);
  return null;
}

/** Reports what actually compiled, so a headless run can assert rather than eyeball. */
function Probe() {
  const { gl, scene } = useThree();
  useEffect(() => {
    const id = setTimeout(() => {
      const programs = (gl.info as any).programs ?? [];
      (window as any).__wall = {
        styles: SHOWN,
        // One program per style is the whole point of the per-style cache key: without it
        // three hands every style whichever program compiled first.
        wallPrograms: programs
          .map((p: any) => p.cacheKey)
          .filter((k: string) => typeof k === 'string' && k.includes('wall|')),
        drawCalls: gl.info.render.calls,
        triangles: gl.info.render.triangles,
        meshes: (() => {
          let n = 0;
          scene.traverse((o) => {
            if ((o as THREE.Mesh).isMesh) n++;
          });
          return n;
        })(),
      };
    }, 2500);
    return () => clearTimeout(id);
  }, [gl, scene]);
  return null;
}

function App() {
  return (
    <Canvas shadows camera={{ fov: 45, near: 0.3, far: 400 }} gl={{ antialias: true }}>
      <color attach="background" args={['#1b2430']} />
      <Rig />
      <Probe />

      {/* Matches the interior's own lighting: one warm modelling light per room plus a soft
          ambient, so the materials are judged under the light they will actually ship with. */}
      <ambientLight intensity={0.55} />
      <directionalLight position={[18, 26, 14]} intensity={1.1} castShadow />
      {SHOWN.map((_, i) => (
        <pointLight
          key={`lamp-${i}`}
          position={[i * ROOM_GRID_SIZE, 4.2, 0]}
          intensity={1.0}
          distance={15}
          decay={1.2}
          color="#ffdca8"
        />
      ))}

      {SHOWN.map((id, i) => (
        <RoomSample key={id} styleId={id} gx={i} />
      ))}
    </Canvas>
  );
}

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(<App />);

```

## tmp-wallcam-check.ts

```ts
/**
 * Throwaway: does the interior camera still put a wall inside its own near plane when the player
 * walks into that wall and holds? That is 「室內移動視角破圖」 — the wall stops being drawn and the
 * player sees the outside of their own house.
 *
 * Pure maths, no WebGL. It reproduces the last three lines of CameraController's orbit branch —
 * the observation floor, the MIN_CAMERA_DISTANCE floor and the direction floor — against the real
 * exported helpers, for the one geometry that breaks: the player pressed against a wall, where
 * their own collision holds them PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS (0.35) off its face and the camera behind
 * them has 0.35 of room and needs 0.5.
 *
 * The measure of success is not a distance, it is a CLEARANCE: how far the wall ends up from the
 * lens, against the near plane that will clip it.
 *
 * Run: npx tsx tmp-wallcam-check.ts
 * Delete once the wall-clipping fix is signed off.
 */
import {
  applyObservationFloor,
  surfaceOverrunAllowance,
  CAMERA_COLLIDER_RADIUS,
  MIN_CAMERA_DISTANCE,
} from './src/lib/cameraCollision';
import { PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS } from './src/utils/placementRules';

/** The interior canvas' near plane (BuildingInteriorView.tsx) and the island's (Scene.tsx). */
const INTERIOR_NEAR = 0.3;
const OUTDOOR_NEAR = 0.5;
/** CameraController's MIN_ORBIT_DIRECTION_DISTANCE. */
const MIN_DIR = 0.02;

/**
 * The rendered distance, exactly as the orbit branch resolves it once the arm is already as short
 * as the geometry allows. `standoff` is how far the PIVOT is from the surface behind it.
 */
function renderedDistance(standoff: number, desired: number, near: number, fixed: boolean): number {
  // Stage 2 as the wall segment produces it: the intersection distance less the collider radius.
  const collision = standoff - CAMERA_COLLIDER_RADIUS;
  // Stage 3 snaps straight to the cap when something is in the way.
  let dist = Math.min(desired, collision);
  const overrun = fixed ? surfaceOverrunAllowance(near) : CAMERA_COLLIDER_RADIUS;
  dist = applyObservationFloor(dist, collision, desired, overrun);
  dist = fixed
    ? Math.max(dist, Math.min(desired, MIN_CAMERA_DISTANCE, collision + overrun))
    : Math.max(dist, Math.min(desired, MIN_CAMERA_DISTANCE));
  return fixed ? Math.max(dist, MIN_DIR) : dist;
}

let failures = 0;

function check(name: string, standoff: number, near: number) {
  const before = renderedDistance(standoff, 7, near, false);
  const after = renderedDistance(standoff, 7, near, true);
  // The wall is `standoff` from the pivot; the camera sits `dist` along the ray toward it.
  const clearBefore = standoff - before;
  const clearAfter = standoff - after;
  // The wall has to end up in FRONT of the near plane — unless the pivot itself is closer to the
  // surface than the near plane is to the lens, in which case no camera position on this ray can
  // manage it and the best available answer is "as far back as the ray allows".
  const achievable = Math.min(near, standoff - MIN_DIR);
  const ok = clearAfter >= achievable - 1e-9;
  if (!ok) failures++;
  console.log(
    `${ok ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'}  ${name}\n` +
    `        pivot ${standoff.toFixed(2)} off the surface, near ${near}\n` +
    `        before: camera at ${before.toFixed(3)} → ${clearBefore.toFixed(3)} of wall clearance` +
    `${clearBefore < near ? '  ← inside the near plane: 破圖' : ''}\n` +
    `        after:  camera at ${after.toFixed(3)} → ${clearAfter.toFixed(3)} of wall clearance`
  );
}

console.log('THE REPORTED CASE — walking into a wall and holding\n');
check('interior, player jammed against a wall', PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS, INTERIOR_NEAR);
check('interior, a hair further off the wall', PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS + 0.15, INTERIOR_NEAR);
check('interior, half a metre of room', 0.5, INTERIOR_NEAR);
check('interior, a metre of room', 1.0, INTERIOR_NEAR);

console.log('\nOUTDOORS — same rule, wider near plane\n');
check('outdoors, pressed against the Home shell', PLAYER_PHYSICAL_RADIUS, OUTDOOR_NEAR);
check('outdoors, a metre of room', 1.0, OUTDOOR_NEAR);

console.log('\nNOT A REGRESSION — an unobstructed orbit still gets what it asked for\n');
{
  const open = renderedDistance(99, 7, INTERIOR_NEAR, true);
  const ok = Math.abs(open - 7) < 1e-6;
  if (!ok) failures++;
  console.log(`${ok ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'}  nothing behind the camera: rendered ${open.toFixed(3)}, wanted 7.000`);
}

console.log(failures === 0 ? '\nALL PASS' : `\n${failures} FAILED`);
process.exit(failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);

```

```ts
import tailwindcss from '@tailwindcss/vite';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';
import path from 'path';
import {defineConfig} from 'vite';

export default defineConfig(() => {
  return {
    plugins: [react(), tailwindcss()],
    resolve: {
      alias: {
        '@': path.resolve(process.cwd(), '.'),
      },
    },
    build: {
      sourcemap: false,
      chunkSizeWarningLimit: 2000,
      rollupOptions: {
        output: {
          manualChunks(id) {
            if (id.includes('node_modules')) {
              if (id.includes('@mediapipe') || id.includes('tasks-vision')) {
                return 'mediapipe-vendor';
              }
              if (id.includes('firebase')) {
                return 'firebase-vendor';
              }
              return 'vendor';
            }
          }
        }
      }
    },
    server: {
      allowedHosts: true,
      // HMR is disabled in AI Studio via DISABLE_HMR env var.
      // Do not modifyâfile watching is disabled to prevent flickering during agent edits.
      hmr: process.env.DISABLE_HMR !== 'true',
      // The project lives under a OneDrive folder, where native file-system
      // events are unreliable: edits on disk never invalidated Vite's
      // transform cache, so the browser kept receiving stale modules even
      // after a full refresh. Polling sidesteps the missing events.
      watch: {
        usePolling: true,
        interval: 300,
      },
    },
  };
});
```
